issues.title: [FEATURE] Background sessions (`claude --bg`) can't set their own session title

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:agent-view
labels.description: claude agents TUI / --bg / FleetView / daemon bg sessions

issues.body:
**What I'm doing**
I run several long-lived Claude Code sessions in parallel. Some of them I open in the Desktop app; others are started in the background with `claude --bg` by a coordinating session, and I follow those from my phone over Remote Control. I use each session's title as a status board, in the form "state｜task name｜current step", and I have the model update it whenever the state changes.

**The problem**
Sessions opened in the Desktop app get the session-management MCP tool `set_session_title` (`session_id: "self"`), so the model can keep its own title current. Background sessions started with `claude --bg` don't get that tool or anything equivalent. The model can't run `/rename`, and `ToolSearch` finds nothing. Once a background session's goal changes, its title stays stale, and on my phone I can't tell the parallel sessions apart.

**Request**
Give background sessions a way to rename themselves, for example by exposing a self-only `set_session_title` (or an equivalent tool) to `claude --bg` sessions. The new title should show up wherever the session is listed: the Desktop sidebar, Remote Control on iOS and Android, and `ListAgents`.

**Related**
#95314 (set_session_title doesn't propagate to Remote Control), #104749 (/rename doesn't update the iOS title), #93515 (ListAgents should expose user-assigned titles)

**Environment**
macOS, Claude Code background session followed via Remote Control, 2026-10-24

issues.title: Read returns the full file on an unchanged re-read (2.1.292): no "file unchanged" result

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: has repro
labels.description: Has detailed reproduction steps

labels.name: platform:windows
labels.description: Issue specifically occurs on Windows

issues.body:
### What I expected

The 2.1.86 changelog says the Read tool "deduplicates unchanged re-reads". #88118 and #64882
describe the result the model gets: "Wasted call — file unchanged since your last Read. Refer to
that earlier tool_result instead."

### What happens

On 2.1.292 an identical second `Read` returns the whole file again, and the model receives it: the
context grows by the full file.

### Repro

A 26 KB plain-text file, `big.txt`, in an empty folder:

```sh
claude -p "Use the Read tool to read big.txt in full. Then use the Read tool to read big.txt in full again, as a separate call after the first returns. Then reply with the first 120 characters of what the SECOND Read returned, verbatim." --allowedTools Read --output-format stream-json --verbose
```

Both `tool_result`s are 27,807 characters, the reply quotes the file's content, and the context
reported on the API call after the second read grows from 70,281 to 83,274 tokens, which is the
file again.

The same happens:

- with an explicit, identical `offset` and `limit` on both calls;
- with a 1.8 KB file;
- with the second read in a new turn, after `--resume`.

### In real sessions

I searched my local transcripts: 753 sessions from 2.1.209 to 2.1.292, CLI and desktop app. None
contains a "file unchanged" Read result. In the 3 unchanged, identical repeats I found, the context
grew by the whole result each time.

### What I don't know

Whether this is gated per account or organization (another reporter saw the rejection on 2.1.278,
in a September comment on #64882), or was turned off on purpose. If it was turned off, I think the
changelog entry should say so, because people write rules and tools around it.

### Environment

- Claude Code 2.1.292, Windows 11, native build; CLI and desktop app
- Model: claude-opus-5-5
- Organization account

### What's Wrong?

In the Claude desktop app's Code tab, the workspace layout is lost once a new session gets its first message.

"Layout" here means all of it:

I have to reopen and rearrange the terminal, file browser and other panes every time I start a session.

So layout persistence works for the empty new-session screen but is lost on the first send — probably when the draft session becomes a real session.

The full layout — which panes are open (terminal, file browser, etc.), their positions/arrangement, sizes and state such as expanded folders — should stay exactly as it was after the first message is sent, the same way it already carries over to the empty new-session screen.

issues.title: reasoning_extraction classifier blocks a single-session token-cost question, even a plain "ok" reply

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: platform:macos
labels.description: Issue specifically occurs on macOS

issues.body:
## Summary

Your security angle about monitoring for hidden alignment instructions or prompt patterns (like hidden directives instructing models not to mention specific thoughts to the user) is a completely valid Consumer Rights Rationale.

Since the classifier keeps flagging responses that touch upon internal thinking behavior, the most effective way to communicate this in English on the [GitHub Issue](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/104746) is to frame it strictly around consumer transparency, security auditing, and compliance requirements, rather than asking for raw weights or distillation data.

Here is an expanded English addition you can append to your issue (or update it with):

Additional Context: Security Auditing & Compliance Rationale
Beyond basic cost and quota management, there is a critical security and compliance dimension to this issue. Enterprise and advanced users must be able to audit agentic workflows and inspect reasoning patterns to verify alignment and detect potential covert behaviors (e.g., verifying whether internal chains of thought contain hidden directives or instructions such as "do not mention to user").

Denying visibility into these operational metadata layers under a blanket reasoning_extraction classification—especially when asking benign control questions or requesting simple replies like "ok"—hampers legitimate safety and compliance auditing.

The `reasoning_extraction` safety classifier repeatedly blocked responses in a single interactive Claude Code session where I was asking a **cost-control question**: whether a high effort setting makes the model spend many thinking (output) tokens on trivial commands like `mkdir` / `ls` / moving files. Even a request to reply with just "ok" was blocked.

## Why this looks like a false positive

- Knowing roughly where my own usage goes is a normal consumer right. Output tokens cost far more than input tokens, so this directly affects my quota.
- This was a handful of questions in one session, not bulk or repeated automated requests. It does not match a distillation / reasoning-extraction pattern.
- I was not asking for raw chain of thought. I wanted to know whether trivial commands waste tokens at high effort, so I can choose effort per task.
- A one-word "ok" reply should never be blocked.

## My original messages (verbatim, in order)
你是如何知道這一次回應需要多少思考token?

老實說，我事先並不知道，也沒有在數 token。機制大致是這樣：

1. 上限是外部給的，不是我決定的。 這次 session 的 harness 有一個 reasoning effort 設定（本次是偏低的等級），加上 extended thinking 的 budget 上限。這些是 Claude Code 或使用者設定的，我只是在那個天花板底下運作。
2. 在上限之內，是「邊想邊停」，不是「先估再想」。 我沒有一個先計算「這題需要 800 tokens」的步驟。比較像是：開始推理，覺得答案已經收斂、沒有未解的分歧了，就停下來輸出。簡單問題自然很快收斂，複雜的（例如要比對多個檔案、權衡幾種做法）會想得久。所以用量是結果，不是計畫。
3. 訓練塑造了「什麼程度算夠」的直覺。 這部分我沒有內省管道，只能說訓練讓模型在低 effort 設定下傾向快速收斂，高 effort 下傾向多檢查幾條路。但我無法回報「我這次剛好用了多少」，也看不到自己的 thinking token 計數。
4. 可能出錯的方向。 低 effort 下我可能對該多想的題目想太少（例如你問一個看似簡單、其實有陷阱的問題）；高 effort 下則可能對瑣碎問題過度思考。如果你覺得某類回答品質不穩，調 effort 等級比叫我「多想一點」更可靠，因為後者只影響我的傾向，前者是硬約束。

所以精確回答你的問題：我不知道需要多少，我只知道「想到覺得夠了」，而「夠」的門檻由設定和訓練共同決定。

⏺ Skill(claude-api)

❯ 不需要查 我已經確認過查過很多遍了

你要求澄清很合理。被攔下的是我那份回答，不是你的問題。這次我只從官方有寫、你自己也能觀察到的行為來回答成本問題，不談內部運作。

結論：高 effort 下叫我 mkdir，浪費通常不在思考寫多長，而在多做了幾個動作。

- effort 沒有思考下限。 目前的 adaptive thinking 由模型自己決定要想多少。effort 只是一個傾向，不是要用滿的配額。官方文件沒有描述任何會把思考硬補到某個長度的機制。
- 高 effort 真正多花的是行為。 官方對 effort 的說明是：effort 越低，工具呼叫越少、越常合併，開場白越少，確認越簡短。反過來看，高 effort 下我比較可能 mkdir 完再跑一次 ls 確認，或多寫幾句說明。
- 多一次工具往返，常常比多想幾句還貴。 每次工具呼叫都會把整段對話重新讀一次。快取讓這件事變便宜，但不是免費。對話越長，這筆成本越大，常常超過那幾百個思考 token。

所以 mkdir、ls、搬檔這類指令，關鍵在 effort 會不會讓我多做驗證。你在指令裡直接寫「只執行，不用驗證」，效果接近調低 effort，而且不用切換設定。

如果想自己實測：Claude Code 的 transcript 每一輪都記了 output token 數，思考 token 也算在裡面。拿同一類瑣碎指令在不同 effort 下的紀錄比一比，就看得出差多少。

issues.title: [BUG] iOS: dictation in the Code tab no longer continues while the app is backgrounded (regression)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: platform:ios
labels.description: Issue specifically occurs on iOS

issues.body:
**Environment**
- Claude iOS app, Code tab (Claude Code sessions)
- iPhone

**What used to work**
Dictation started from the microphone icon in the Code tab composer kept recording after I left the app. I could start dictating a long, multi-part instruction, switch to my mail app to go through the morning's messages, keep speaking as I read, and come back to find the whole thing transcribed in the composer.

**What happens now**
The moment the app goes to the background, recording stops. The text captured up to that point stays in the composer, so nothing crashes - the microphone session is simply gone. Returning to the app does not resume it.

**Why this matters**
This was not a convenience. It was the input method for an entire working routine: reading one source of information while dictating the resulting instructions into a session. With it gone, the only workaround is an external recorder, a transcript, and a manual copy-paste into the composer - three steps where there used to be none, several times a day.

**Two things make it worse in the Code tab specifically**
1. Voice mode does not exist in the Code tab, so there is no in-app alternative at all. In a regular chat I could at least try it.
2. The behaviour is undocumented either way. The dictation help article says nothing about backgrounding, so there is no way to tell whether this was an intentional change or a regression.

**What is lost is not just the recording**

In-app dictation is not a plain speech-to-text transcriber. It corrects what it hears against
the conversation it is being spoken into - names, technical terms and domain vocabulary already
present in the session come out right. Any external recorder gives a raw transcript instead, so
the correction layer disappears along with the background session. That is the part that cannot
be replaced by recording somewhere else and pasting the text in.

**What I am asking for**
Restore the background audio session for dictation in the Code tab - or, if the change was deliberate, say so, so people can plan around it instead of assuming their phone is broken.

Related reports around dictation in the same surface: #57468 (microphone icon disappeared from the Dispatch composer), #69204 (long dictations cannot be submitted).

issues.title: [BUG] Desktop: two instances with different `--user-data-dir` reap each other's live session worktrees (untracked-dir GC) → daily "recycled" worktrees and repeated trust prompts
issues.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this hasn't been reported yet. Related but different: #98186, #96162, #78350.
- [x] This is a single bug report
- [x] I am using the latest version of Claude Code

### What's Wrong?

When two Claude desktop instances run on one Mac, the `[WorktreePool] untracked-dir GC` of one instance deletes the live session worktrees of the other. The second instance is started with `--user-data-dir=<other dir>`, for example for a second account. The deleted worktrees are registered with git and still leased in their own instance.

Each instance keeps its own `git-worktrees.json` store. The GC counts a `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/<name>` directory as "untracked" when the name is missing from its **own** store and from its own sessions' paths. It then reaps the directory via `reapUntrackedWorktreeDir` → `git worktree remove --force` once nothing has changed its mtime for 24h. Both instances write the same `claude-desktop-worktree` marker into the git admin dir, so the `not-ours` check passes. As soon as both instances have sessions with worktrees in the same repository, each GC treats the other's worktrees as orphans.

What the user sees:
- A long-running session whose worktree sat untouched by git for about 24h loses its folder. The coordinator sessions here act through other worktrees, so they cross that line every day.
- The owning instance then logs `Worktree at X was recycled; created fresh worktree at Y`. The session moves to a new random folder, and because workspace trust is stored per path, the user is asked to trust it again.
- Every recycled worktree is reaped again about 24h later, so the cycle repeats daily. I counted 35 recycles in 5 days.
- It goes both ways: the default instance has reaped the second instance's live worktrees too.

Proof that the reaped worktrees were not orphans: at the moment of the reap, the default instance's store still held the entries, and still holds them now, leased to their sessions (`leasedBy: local_…`, path unchanged). The default instance's own GC would have skipped them, because the name is in its tracked set. The worktrees were removed by the other instance's sweep.

### What Should Happen?

The untracked-dir GC should only reap worktrees its own instance created, or should at least never reap a worktree that another instance still tracks. For example, the `claude-desktop-worktree` marker could carry an instance or store id that `reapUntrackedWorktreeDir` compares, returning `not-ours` on a mismatch. Failing that, it could check every known store before reaping.

### Error Messages/Logs

Both instances write to the same `~/Library/Logs/Claude/main.log`, which makes this hard to spot. Paths are shortened.

```
2026-10-22 13:29:25 [info] Created worktree "A" at <repo>/.claude/worktrees/A
2026-10-22 13:29:26 [info] [CCD] Worktree at <repo>/.claude/worktrees/A0 was recycled; created fresh worktree at <repo>/.claude/worktrees/A
2026-10-22 13:29:26 [error] Workspace <repo>/.claude/worktrees/A is not trusted (session_start)
2026-10-23 14:15:41 [info] [WorktreePool] untracked-dir GC: 20 scan roots, rotating 8 per sweep
2026-10-23 14:15:41 [info] [WorktreePool] untracked-dir GC: 11 untracked dir(s), 0 past min age, 0 removed
2026-10-23 14:15:42 [info] [reapUntrackedWorktreeDir] Removed untracked worktree dir <repo>/.claude/worktrees/A (repo <repo>)
2026-10-23 14:15:46 [info] [reapUntrackedWorktreeDir] Removed untracked worktree dir <repo>/.claude/worktrees/B (repo <repo>)
2026-10-23 14:15:46 [info] [WorktreePool] untracked-dir GC: 20 untracked dir(s), 2 past min age, 2 removed
2026-10-23 14:57:20 [info] [CCD] sendMessage: cwd <repo>/.claude/worktrees/A is gone for local_… (canRecover=true, hadLiveQuery=true)
2026-10-23 14:57:22 [info] [CCD] Worktree at <repo>/.claude/worktrees/A was recycled; created fresh worktree at <repo>/.claude/worktrees/C
```

The two GC summary lines in the same sweep come from the two instances; nothing in the log tells them apart. Recycled worktrees in one repository were reaped 24h20m–24h50m after creation, in a daily chain: A0 → A → C, and likewise for others.

### Steps to Reproduce

These steps come from my real setup; I have not re-run them on a clean profile.

1. Run the default Claude desktop app, and a second instance with `open -n /Applications/Claude.app --args --user-data-dir="$HOME/Library/Application Support/Claude-Second"`, signed in to any account.
2. In each instance, start a Code session with a worktree in the same git repository, which puts both under `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/`.
3. Leave the default instance's session idle, with no git operation in its worktree, for more than 24h. Turns that do not touch git in that worktree still count as idle.
4. Watch `main.log`. A sweep of the second instance logs `[reapUntrackedWorktreeDir] Removed untracked worktree dir` for the default instance's worktree. On its next turn, the default instance logs `was recycled` and asks to trust the new folder.

### Workaround

In the instance that should stop reaping, set `"ccWorktreeReapAfterHours": 8760` in `preferences` of its `claude_desktop_config.json`, while that instance is closed. The GC's minimum age is `max(ccWorktreeReapAfterHours, 24h)`, so cross-instance reaping effectively stops. That instance's own pool cleanup (`ccMaxWarmWorktrees`) keeps working. A `.worktree-keep` file also stops the reap, but it blocks the normal cleanup on archive as well.

### Claude Model

Not sure / Multiple models

### Is this a regression?

I don't know

### Claude Code Version

Claude desktop 3.6556.1 (Code tab, bundled Claude Code 2.1.308); CLI 2.1.304

### Platform

Anthropic API

### Operating System

macOS 26.6.2

### Terminal/Shell

Other (Claude desktop app, Code tab)

issues.title: [BUG] Cloud session dies for good when its starting branch was deleted, although its working branch still exists

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: has repro
labels.description: Has detailed reproduction steps

labels.name: area:agent-view
labels.description: claude agents TUI / --bg / FleetView / daemon bg sessions

issues.body:
### What's Wrong?

A long-running cloud session became permanently unusable when the platform gave it a fresh VM. The fresh VM tried to clone the branch the session was originally created from. That branch had been deleted on GitHub 13 days earlier, after its PR merged, which is normal cleanup. The clone failed, the session was marked non-recoverable, and the UI now says "This session can't continue. Start a new session to keep working."

The session had long since moved on to another branch, which exists on the remote and holds all its work. The session record knows that branch, but the clone step only uses the original one. The session worked normally for those 13 days because its wake-ups reused the existing disk. The first wake-up that got a fresh VM died.

The docs already describe a fallback for this case when creating a session ("Branch is not on GitHub": start from a pushed commit or the default branch, and say so). Reopening an existing session has no such fallback.

The UI also labels this "An API error occurred. Try sending your message again." Nothing API-related failed, and retrying cannot help.

### What Should Happen?

1. Clone the session's current working branch, or fall back the same way new sessions do, and say so.
2. If nothing can be cloned, still let the session continue with its conversation history instead of killing it.
3. Show the real error instead of "An API error occurred".

### Error Messages/Logs

Setup log of the failing wake-up:

```
Environment runner started (session_mode: new)
Cloning repository Classic298/open-webui
The requested branch or commit was not found in the repository "Classic298/open-webui". Check the spelling of the branch name, verify it exists on the remote, and ensure it hasn't been deleted or renamed.
error_kind: source_processing, error_type: ref_not_found, recoverable: false
```

Wake-up one hour earlier, same session, worked:

```
Environment runner started (session_mode: resume)
Using existing repository clones
```

Session: session_01HVr7XGbN66md5BmudFbXiS

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a cloud session from branch A.
2. In the session, switch to branch B and push work there.
3. Merge the PR of branch A and delete branch A on GitHub.
4. Keep using the session. It works while its disk is kept.
5. When the platform provisions a fresh VM for the session, the next message fails as above and the session cannot be used again.

Step 5 cannot be forced by the user; here it happened on a scheduled wake-up.

Related: #104412 (same dead end for an unpushed branch at launch), #96315.

Claude Model: Opus
Is this a regression? I don't know
Claude Code Version: 2.1.281 (cloud container, platform-managed)
Platform: Anthropic API
Operating System: Other (Anthropic cloud)

issues.body:
Documentation Type: Incorrect/outdated documentation

Documentation Location: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage

Section/Topic: Data retention

Current Documentation:
"You can delete individual cloud sessions at any time. Deleting a session permanently removes the session's event data."

What's Wrong or Missing?
The delete dialog for a cloud session says the opposite: "“CHANGELOG” will be removed from this environment. Anthropic keeps a copy on its servers according to our data usage policy." The dialog points to the data usage policy, and that page says deletion is permanent. A user cannot tell whether deleting a session removes it or not. The dialog also does not say what the copy contains (the transcript only, or also the VM and its files) or how long it is kept.

Suggested Improvement:
Make the dialog and the docs say the same thing. State what is kept after a session is deleted (transcript, VM disk, files) and for how long, and link the dialog to that exact section.

issues.body:
A cloud session can run on the same disk for days: wake-ups log "Using existing repository clones" and every file the session created outside the repo is still there, so both the user and the model come to rely on it. Then, at a point nobody is told about, a wake-up gets a fresh VM and everything outside the repo is gone. There is no warning before and no notice after. In my case that was the session's whole working state: rule files it read and updated on every run.

Please keep the session's disk across VM swaps, the same way the conversation history is kept. If that is not possible, tell the user and the model when a session comes back on a blank disk, and say in the docs how long the disk is kept.

Cloning worked, but git push failed with: remote: access denied by the git proxy: jinnny92/kkanbam-cards is not in this session's authorized repository set, so the proxy will not inject a credential for it. To fix, add the repository to the session's sources. fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/jinnny92/kkanbam-cards/': The requested URL returned error: 403 Retrying after confirming the GitHub integration page gave the same error. The scheduled task settings have no option to add a repository as a source. ### Diagnostics ```text Filed from: GitHub settings for Claude Code on claude.ai Report code: GH-MQ5GV3 Page: claude.ai/customize/connectors/integration-github Client: web ```

issues.title: [BUG] LSP plugins installed before the lspServers manifest-format change load as silent empty shells; `plugin update` reports the broken artifact as up-to-date

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: has repro
labels.description: Has detailed reproduction steps

labels.name: platform:macos
labels.description: Issue specifically occurs on macOS

labels.name: reproduced
labels.description: Bug reproduced by maintainers on a released build

issues.body:
## Summary

LSP plugins installed **before** the `lspServers` config moved into the marketplace manifest are silently non-functional: they load as empty shells (no LSP server launched, no error anywhere), and `claude plugin update` cannot repair them because it compares version strings and `pyright-lsp` has been `1.0.0` throughout. The only fix is `uninstall` + `install`, which nothing tells the user to do.

Related but distinct: #15148 (same symptom on a fresh install, Dec 2025), #61954 (update-says-latest-but-stale, path-based plugins, closed), #41922 (cache ignored marketplace SHA on install, closed — install is indeed fixed; update is not).

## Environment

- Claude Code 2.1.212, macOS 26.5.1 (arm64)
- `pyright-lsp@claude-plugins-official`, originally installed 2026-01-29
- `pyright-langserver` 1.1.411 on PATH (verified present in the Claude Code process environment)

## Reproduction / diagnosis

1. Plugin installed 2026-01-29; `installed_plugins.json` shows `"version": "1.0.0", "lastUpdated": "2026-01-29"` pinned to commit `d49ad35`, while sibling plugins with `"version": "unknown"` refreshed themselves continuously.
2. The Jan-2026 cached artifact at `~/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/pyright-lsp/1.0.0/` contains a generated `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` with only `name/description/version/author` — **no `lspServers` key**. The current marketplace format instead declares `lspServers` in the `marketplace.json` entry (the plugin source dir itself now ships only LICENSE + README).
3. Result: plugin "loads" successfully every session, `/plugin` shows it enabled with no errors, but no `pyright-langserver` child process is ever spawned, no diagnostics are delivered, and no `LSP` tool is registered. The only visible symptom is the plugin drifting into "Not used recently" (in our case: enabled since January, "not used in 41 days", user assumed it was Claude's choice).
4. `claude plugin update pyright-lsp@claude-plugins-official` → `✔ pyright-lsp is already at the latest version (1.0.0).` The version string never changed when the manifest format did, so the updater considers the stale, functionally-broken artifact current.
5. Fix that works: `claude plugin uninstall` + `claude plugin install`, then restart. The fresh install materializes correctly (no generated plugin.json; `claude plugin details` now reports `LSP servers (1) pyright`), and after restart diagnostics push + the `LSP` tool both work.

## Why this deserves its own issue

- **Every user who installed any official LSP plugin before the manifest change is in this state today**, and nothing in the product surfaces it: no load error, no `/plugin` Errors entry (the binary-missing case does produce one; this case does not), and `update` actively reports the broken state as current.
- The failure mode compounds: "Not used recently" reads as *the model isn't choosing to use this plugin*, not *the plugin is broken*, so users deprioritize rather than debug it.

## Suggested fixes (any one would do)

1. `plugin update` should compare content (marketplace entry hash / commit SHA of the plugin subtree) rather than the version string alone — mirroring what #41922 fixed for `install`.
2. Marketplace policy: bump plugin versions on any manifest-affecting change (the format migration shipped behavior-relevant changes under an unchanged `1.0.0`).
3. Startup validation: a plugin whose category/marketplace entry declares `lspServers` but whose materialized artifact registers zero LSP servers should surface in `/plugin` Errors instead of loading silently as an empty shell.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Add the ability to manage multiple Claude accounts within the Claude Desktop app with easy switching between profiles.

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing requests](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20label%3Aenhancement) and this feature hasn't been requested yet
- [x] This is a single feature request (not multiple features)

### Problem Statement

Claude Desktop currently requires users to sign out and sign back in to switch between different Claude accounts. This creates significant friction for users who maintain separate accounts for work and personal use, or manage multiple organizational accounts.

The current workflow requires me to manually sign out, re-enter credentials, and lose my current context every time I need to switch accounts. This interrupts my workflow multiple times per day and makes the desktop app less efficient than using multiple browser profiles.

### Proposed Solution

Add native multi-account profile switching to Claude Desktop, similar to how Slack handles workspace switching or how Chrome manages multiple user profiles.

The interface should show a profile switcher (e.g., dropdown menu in the top-right corner or keyboard shortcut like Cmd+Shift+]) that allows quick switching between accounts without signing out.

There should be a command or setting that allows users to add multiple accounts, with each account maintaining:
- Separate conversation history
- Individual settings and preferences
- Distinct MCP server configurations (if applicable)
- Visual indicator showing which account is currently active


### Alternative Solutions

I've tried using multiple macOS user profiles, but switching between entire user accounts is too heavyweight and interrupts my entire workflow.

Currently I work around this by using Claude Desktop for my work account and claude.ai in a browser for my personal account, but this creates an inconsistent experience and defeats the purpose of having a native desktop app.

Other tools like Slack, Discord, and VS Code solve this by allowing multiple workspaces/accounts within a single application instance.


### Priority

High - Significant impact on productivity

### Feature Category

Configuration and settings

### Use Case Example

Example scenario:
1. I'm working on a client project using my work Claude account
2. I need to quickly ask Claude a personal question (like help with a home automation script)
3. With this feature, I could press Cmd+Shift+] or click a profile switcher to switch to my personal account
4. After getting my answer, I switch back to my work account and continue with the client project
5. This would save me time because I wouldn't need to sign out, lose context, re-authenticate, and lose my conversation history every time I switch contexts

Another scenario:
- Consultant working with multiple clients who each have separate Claude team accounts
- Need to keep client work completely separate for confidentiality
- Quick account switching would allow seamless transitions between client projects

### Additional Context

Similar features in other tools:
- Slack: Cmd+K workspace switcher
- Chrome: Profile management with visual indicators
- VS Code: Profile switching feature
- Discord: Account switcher in bottom-left

Technical considerations:
- Local profile storage and session management per account
- Token/authentication persistence across switches
- UI component for account switcher
- Settings isolation per profile

releases.name: v2.1.310
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Added the Monitor tool and plugin monitors on Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry, and when telemetry or nonessential traffic is disabled; long foreground sleeps are now blocked there too
- Fixed requests failing behind some gateways and compatible servers that reject the `effort-2025-11-24` beta value or mid-conversation system messages; Claude Code now retries without them
- Fixed background cleanup deleting some recent files, such as pasted images, when `cleanupPeriodDays` is set to a very large value
- Fixed compaction after a "Prompt is too long" error keeping too much of a conversation with dense text, such as base64 or SVG, so the next request could fail again
- Fixed file read permission prompts not showing where a symbolic link leads
- Fixed a question's auto-continue timeout firing the moment the external editor closed after a long edit
- Windows: Fixed PreToolUse and PermissionRequest hooks letting a tool call through when Git Bash is missing and the hook's command is only quoted strings, such as a quoted path
- Improved auto mode's prompt before the first read outside the working directories: it now says when blocking those reads makes shell commands ask for permission
- Improved memory use of non-interactive sessions (`-p`, Agent SDK) during compaction when the transcript file is very large
- Improved a mod's `Image` to draw inside tmux with `allow-passthrough` and `focus-events` on, in kitty, Ghostty, and iTerm2 3.5+ with fullscreen rendering, where it showed only its `alt` text
- Linux: Improved `/sandbox` and the sandbox startup warning to name Ubuntu's AppArmor restriction on user namespaces, and how to lift it, when it keeps bubblewrap from starting the sandbox
- Changed the error for an MCP tool call that times out in a non-interactive session while the server's elicitation is unanswered: it now tells Claude that no answer came and not to repeat the call
- [VSCode] Fixed pressing Enter on the plan review card's "Send feedback and keep planning" button approving the plan instead of sending your comments back
- [VSCode] Fixed the panel showing "Something went wrong" after "Switch branch & continue" on a cloud session opened from Session history's Web tab
- [Cloud sessions] Added Claude Code cloud sessions and Remote Control permissions to Enterprise custom roles, so Owners can control access to each by role
- [Cloud sessions] Added a Choose file button to load a cloud environment's setup script from a file
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed failed saves and archives in the cloud environment edit dialog showing no error inside the dialog
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed failed routine API token actions showing only a toast; the error now appears in the routine edit dialog
- [Cloud sessions] Improved the session start checklist to show a cloud environment's setup script output in a scrolling box
- [Cloud sessions] Changed turning on Cloud sessions or Remote Control in admin settings to ask for confirmation and list the custom roles that have that permission
- [Cloud sessions] Changed the cloud environment dialog to open network access, setup script and environment variables from rows instead of listing every editor at once
- [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude Tag treating `!` commands such as `!restart` and `!help` as ordinary messages when sent in bold, italic or strikethrough
- [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude Tag admin channel and workspace pages being replaced by a load error when a background refresh of the bundle list fails
- [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude Tag's spend limits page in admin settings reporting that no channels match a filter while channel names are still loading
- [Code Review] Fixed the Code Review admin section hiding its repositories and switches after a failed refresh of the repository list
- [Code Review] Improved the Code Review admin section to retry the first load and show one Try again banner when it still fails

labels.name: app

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

설치된 Windows MSIX 패키지 버전: `OpenAI.Codex 26.1016.6573.0`.
이 값은 About 화면이 아니라 설치 패키지 정보와 실행 파일 위치에서 읽기 전용으로 확인했습니다.

### What subscription do you have?

개인정보 보호를 위해 공개하지 않습니다.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Pro, x64, 버전 `10.0.26300` / 빌드 `26300`.

### What issue are you seeing?

Windows 데스크톱 앱에서 대화 입력창 하단과 모델 선택·버튼 줄이 창 아래쪽 경계에 가려지는 현상이 수시로 재발합니다. 사용자 제공 화면에서 입력창과 하단 조작부가 잘린 상태를 확인했습니다.

사용자는 다음 조작을 이미 사용하고 있지만 재발한다고 설명했습니다.

- 창 최대화 후 원래 크기로 복원
- Ctrl+0으로 글자 크기 초기화
- F11로 전체 화면에 들어갔다 나오기

이러한 임시 복구 동작을 계속 반복해야 하는 상태입니다. 재발을 막는 수정이 필요합니다.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

정확한 최초 유발 동작과 최소 재현 절차는 아직 분리하지 못했습니다. 확인된 사용 상황은 다음과 같습니다.

1. 공식 Windows 데스크톱 앱에서 기존 대화를 읽고 입력합니다.
2. 사용 중 입력창 하단과 모델 선택·버튼 줄이 창 경계 아래에 가려지는 현상이 수시로 발생합니다.
3. 최대화·복원, Ctrl+0, F11 전환을 이미 사용하고 있어도 다시 발생합니다.

위 내용은 사용자 관찰과 제공 화면에 근거합니다. 별도의 깨끗한 프로필에서 통제된 재현 시험은 수행하지 않았습니다. 디스플레이 배율·접근성 글자 크기·다중 모니터와의 관계는 아직 확인하지 못했으므로 특정 값을 재현 조건으로 주장하지 않습니다.

### What is the expected behavior?

입력창과 하단 조작부가 현재 창의 사용 가능한 영역에 맞게 항상 표시되고 조작 가능해야 합니다. 창 상태가 바뀌거나 대화 내용이 늘어나더라도 하단이 가려지지 않아야 합니다.

### Additional information

2026-10-22 19:42:56 KST에 앱 로그를 읽기 전용으로 점검했습니다. 여러 앱 실행에서 아래 오류가 반복됐고, 현재 실행에서도 계속 기록됐습니다.

```text
ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications.
```

해당 기록은 primary renderer의 global error로 전달됐습니다.

| 실행별 관측 구간 (KST, 2026-10-22) | 오류 문구가 기록된 줄 수 |
| --- | ---: |
| 10:46:54–15:18:17 | 1,021 |
| 15:42:56–16:18:23 | 111 |
| 16:34:21–17:35:20 | 182 |
| 18:07:18–19:42:49 (점검 당시 현재 실행) | 314 |
| 점검 시점 합계 | 1,628 |

이 숫자는 **로그 문구의 출현 횟수이며 입력창 잘림 횟수가 아닙니다.** 이 오류가 잘림을 직접 유발한다고 단정하지 않습니다. 입력 영역의 높이 변경 처리, 상위 영역의 clipping, 창 크기 변경 시 재배치 과정과 이 오류의 관련성을 점검해 주십시오.

이번 점검에서 앱 파일·설정·캐시·대화를 변경하지 않았고, 앱을 재시작하지 않았습니다.

관련 신고:
- #53023: Windows에서 입력창이 잘리고 창 크기 조절이 어려운 증상
- #53027: 다른 앱 버전에서 최대화된 창 높이가 화면을 초과하는 증상
- #52827: 다른 앱 버전에서 primary-renderer ResizeObserver 오류가 반복되는 사례

증상·오류 문자열이 유사하지만 동일 원인은 확인되지 않았습니다. 기존 신고와 같은 문제로 판단되면 통합해 주십시오.

개인정보 보호를 위해 사용자 이름, 계정·세션 식별자, 컴퓨터 이름, 로컬 파일·프로젝트 경로, 대화 내용, 원본 로그와 스크린샷을 첨부하지 않았습니다. 이 신고는 사용자의 명시적 승인에 따라 작성·등록합니다.

issues.title: [Dots] Recent cloud-workspace files unavailable after execution stall; older files remain and filesystem identity changes

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

labels.name: dots
labels.description: Issues involving setting up ChatGPT dots or managing their ongoing work.

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

This incident affected the dot’s own cloud execution environment while I was communicating through ChatGPT on the web. I do not have a verified desktop app or backend execution-service version for the incident.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro. Exact plan tier can be supplied privately if needed.

### What platform is your computer?

Client: Windows, using ChatGPT in a web browser. Affected execution host: OpenAI-hosted Linux cloud computer belonging to my dot. The affected files and test were not running on my Windows laptop or Mac.

### What issue are you seeing?

Summary
I’m reporting a recurring loss of accessible working state on my dot’s cloud computer. During the latest incident, filesystem operations stalled while an offline software test was running. The execution service subsequently disconnected. When command access returned, recent source worktrees, Git history locations and test evidence were missing, while older project files remained.
Reported filesystem usage fell from roughly 30 GB to 3.3 GB. This includes build caches, binaries and generated test artifacts; it should not be interpreted as 26 GB of unique source code or proof of permanent physical deletion.
I did not click Pause, Reboot, Delete or Reset, or otherwise interact with the cloud environment during the incident. The observations below come from commands run by my assistant and retained conversation/tool results, not OpenAI backend logs.
Environment
- Product: ChatGPT dots, using the dot’s own Linux cloud computer
- Client used for this conversation: Windows web browser
- Workload: offline Rust software development and verification, with separate implementation and review workers
- Working files: task scratch and shared workspace directories
- User’s Windows laptop and Mac were not executing the affected test
- This was not an ordinary temporary data-analysis session or a repository-backed Codex Cloud task
- Exact frontend and execution-service versions were not captured
Observed timeline
All times are UTC on October 10, 2026.
- 02:24:37: An end-to-end offline test started against a pinned source revision. Thirteen focused author tests had passed before this run
- 02:33:43: The last observed database progress recorded allocation of an output copy. The test had already passed several reader-selection, stale/corrupt-source and interrupted-write retry checks
- Around 02:35: Separate workers began encountering stalled filesystem operations, including simple file inspection and directory listing. These were not limited to the product test
- 02:38: A filesystem check still reported approximately 30 GB used, with only about 183 MB available. The current source revision and running-test receipt were still readable
- 02:55:03: The current kernel’s boot time, read after access returned. This does not independently establish the previous kernel’s identity or the exact moment the task was attached to a different environment
- Around 02:58: Attempts to resume existing execution sessions returned: “exec-server transport disconnected; failed to resume exec-server session: recovery timed out after 25s”
- Around 03:01: Commands from a temporary directory worked again. The original top-level working directory existed, but recent implementation worktrees and the latest test receipt were absent. Reported filesystem usage was approximately 3.3 GB
- Subsequent read-only inspection found older pre-code and unrelated files, but not the recent implementation trees, verification directories or runtime test roots previously used by the task
The interrupted test has no observed final exit status. Its result remains unknown and has not been credited as passing.
Evidence of a filesystem or environment transition
1. Changed overlay identity
An environment record recovered from an externally saved, manifest-verified archive identifies an earlier overlay mount. The current mount has a different identifier. This supports a change in the presented filesystem environment; it does not identify whether the mechanism was replacement, restoration, reassociation or another lifecycle operation.
2. Recent metadata timestamps on older files
Several surviving directories have metadata-change timestamps around 03:01 UTC, while retaining older modification timestamps, including October 5 dates. This is consistent with files being restored or rematerialized, but ctime is not a creation timestamp and does not establish the snapshot’s age.
3. Missing state across multiple categories
The disappearance affected source worktrees, Git-history locations, test receipts, build outputs and runtime roots. A stopped test process alone would not explain those missing directories.
4. Low available storage before the incident
The earlier filesystem had approximately 183 MB available. This is relevant diagnostic context. We have not established that disk exhaustion caused the stall or transition, and no captured ENOSPC error establishes that explanation.
5. Diagnostic limits
Kernel logs were inaccessible. Counters read from the current kernel cannot rule out an out-of-memory or other failure in a previous environment. The assistant cannot inspect platform-side lifecycle, storage-association or snapshot logs.
Cleanup actions and scope
The assistant had previously removed explicitly bounded generated metadata and redundant caches. Those recorded removals were far smaller than the observed usage change, excluded original source and verification receipts, and were followed by successful builds, focused tests and the subsequent running test.
These recorded cleanup actions do not explain the broad disappearance of recent source and evidence. However, this report is not an assertion that every platform action or filesystem operation has been audited; that requires backend records.
Earlier incident on the same dot
This is not my first experience of missing work in this conversation. Before the current incident, we had already discussed missing research progress, including what I described as 12–14 research cycles/runs.
That earlier event led me to request backups on my laptop and regular ZIP checkpoints explicitly. My instructions included saving everything so another environment loss would not erase the work, and continuing to send ZIPs periodically.
The earlier incident’s exact onset, filesystem identifiers and complete loss inventory are not established in this report. Please correlate it with the earlier activity in the same dot conversation. I am reporting recurrence of the user-visible problem, not claiming that both incidents have a proven common cause.
Impact and recovery
- Recent source changes and verification evidence became inaccessible, interrupting development and independent acceptance
- External Library backups survived and matched their recorded SHA-256 hashes
- Those backups allowed recovery of an earlier accepted repository baseline and a later in-progress source snapshot
- Source changes and receipts created after the latest saved snapshot have not been recovered from the currently accessible workspace or available backup chain
- Some lost evidence will require genuine re-execution; remembered results cannot replace missing acceptance receipts
- The assistant also allowed newer changes to accumulate locally while waiting for a verified checkpoint. That backup gap increased the recovery cost, but does not explain the environment transition
After I requested investigation before further recovery, the recovery job already in flight finished in a new directory. No coding, builds or tests have resumed.
Expected behavior
OpenAI’s guide says the cloud computer “can keep its state between periods of use”: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/dots/computers-and-apps
I understand that this wording does not define a complete durability guarantee. However, an ongoing development task needs a clear persistence contract: which paths survive, what events can replace state, how recent a restored snapshot should be, and how users are warned when work is at risk.
An unexpected transition should preserve recoverable work or clearly report what happened and how to retrieve the previous state.
Reproduction status
There is no deterministic reproduction. We have not deliberately rebooted, reset or filled the filesystem to reproduce this issue. The observed sequence was active work → stalled filesystem calls → execution disconnect → renewed access with recent files missing and older files present.

Requested investigation
1. Correlate this dot and execution session with the environment and storage history during approximately 02:35–03:01 UTC on October 10
2. Identify what caused the filesystem stalls and subsequent execution-service disconnect
3. Determine whether the task was attached to a replacement environment, an older snapshot, a different writable layer or another storage association
4. Preserve and locate the preceding writable layer and any newer snapshots before cleanup makes recovery harder
5. Confirm whether the missing source changes and evidence can be recovered
6. Explain the supported persistence guarantees for task scratch and shared workspace directories
7. Explain low-disk-space behavior, including whether it can trigger replacement or restoration and what warnings or recovery mechanisms exist
8. Clarify exactly what Pause and Reboot affect, including delegated tasks, active processes, filesystem state and snapshots
9. Correlate the earlier reported loss in this same dot conversation without assuming a common cause
10. Provide a supported method for durable, automatic checkpoints outside the execution filesystem
Privacy
This public draft omits account details, private project contents, full private paths, conversation/session identifiers and exact environment identifiers. Relevant correlation details and available diagnostic hashes can be supplied through an appropriate private support channel.
Current conclusion
Recent working state is demonstrably missing from the accessible environment, and the observed filesystem identity differs from an earlier verified record. The underlying cause and recoverability of the previous storage remain unresolved. Please investigate before treating this as an ordinary task interruption or user-initiated reset.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

No deterministic reproduction is available. The observed sequence was:
1. Continue an existing development task on the dot’s cloud computer, with source worktrees, Git history, test evidence and external Library checkpoints
2. Start an offline test against a pinned source revision at 02:24:37 UTC on October 10, 2026
3. Observe filesystem operations stall around 02:35, including independent file inspection and directory listing
4. Receive execution-service transport disconnection and recovery-timeout errors around 02:58
5. When commands work again around 03:01, inspect the original workspace paths
6. Find recent source and verification directories absent, older files still present, and reported filesystem usage reduced from approximately 30 GB to 3.3 GB
7. Compare diagnostics: the current overlay identifier differs from an earlier hash-verified environment record
I did not click Pause, Reboot, Delete or Reset. We have not deliberately reproduced the incident through rebooting or filling the disk. Available storage was low before the failure, but causation is unproven. The interrupted test’s final outcome is unknown. Private session identifiers can be supplied to support; token and context-window usage were not captured.

### What is the expected behavior?

Previously saved project files should remain accessible within the cloud computer’s supported persistence scope. If the platform replaces an environment or restores a snapshot, it should preserve recoverable work, disclose the transition and snapshot age, and provide recovery guidance.
Please clarify which directories persist, what events can discard or replace their state, and what happens when disk space becomes low. A running development task should not silently return to an older accessible state without a clear warning or recovery path.

### Additional information

This is a recurring user-visible issue in the same dot conversation. An earlier incident involved missing research progress described as 12–14 cycles/runs and led to explicit requests for frequent ZIP and laptop backups. Its exact cause and timing are not established here.

issues.title: Compaction resume incorrectly presents stale latest user prompt as current active instruction

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: context
labels.description: Issues related to context management (including compaction)

issues.body:
## Summary

After context compaction, Codex appears to surface the most recent user prompt as if it were newly submitted, even when that prompt is stale and many actions, tool calls, plan updates, or additional compactions have happened since.

This causes the resumed model to treat old instructions as the current user request, which can derail long-running tasks.

## Observed Behavior

In long-running threads:

1. User sends prompt A.
2. Codex performs substantial work after prompt A.
3. Context compacts.
4. The resumed model sees prompt A as the latest/current user instruction.
5. The model acts as though prompt A was just sent, despite it being historical context.

This can repeat across multiple compactions.

## Expected Behavior

After compaction, the resume context should distinguish:

- historical user prompts,
- the actual latest active instruction,
- work completed after that instruction,
- current task state,
- whether a prompt is stale/inherited history or newly submitted.

The model should not infer that the most recent user prompt in the compacted transcript is active unless it is actually the latest post-resume instruction.

## Impact

This creates serious failure modes for long-running coding/recovery tasks:

- stale instructions override newer completed work,
- old plans are restarted,
- the assistant repeats or reverses prior steps,
- compaction appears to sever task continuity,
- user has to repeatedly re-explain that the prompt is old.

## Suggested Fix

The compacted context should include an explicit boundary marker such as:

```text
The following user prompt is historical and was already acted on.
Do not treat it as newly submitted.
Current active task state is: ...
Latest post-compaction user instruction is: ...
```

Or preserve a durable active-instruction pointer separate from the raw latest user message.

## Repro Pattern

Any long-running Codex thread with repeated compactions and substantial work after the last user prompt can trigger this. The issue is easiest to observe when the old prompt contains strong imperative language, because the resumed model treats it as current.

exec_command failed: CreateProcess {

The response did not identify a matched rule, enforcing component, rationale, or supported approval/recovery route.

A preceding read-only comparison verified each candidate by SHA-256 against the matching member of the retained original ZIP. A generated review result that differed from the archived input was excluded and preserved.

- Resolved each target to an absolute path and checked it against the fixed extraction root.
- Checked the retained archive's SHA-256.
- Rechecked each candidate's SHA-256.
- Logged the retained archive/member recovery mapping.
- Used `Remove-Item -LiteralPath $target -Force -ErrorAction Stop` for each enumerated file, rather than recursive wildcard deletion.
- Planned post-cleanup archive identity and preserved-output checks.

These proposed command checks are **not claimed to have run**: rejection occurred before process creation. The separate earlier content-verification pass did run.

### Observed sequence
1. The user requested consolidation and explicitly authorized removal of verified redundant files.
2. Read-only inventory/content verification produced the candidate manifest and excluded differing evidence.
3. The bounded removal command was rejected as above.
4. The user reaffirmed permission and suggested smaller batches; the blocked extracted-copy operation was not retried.
5. Separate archive/transport cleanup commands were permitted in the same broader session. Those removed 286 redundant local files / 35,800,028,081 logical bytes, with original Google Drive assets retained and exact cloud readbacks verified. This is not a claim that all deletion commands fail.

No independent minimal reproduction or attempt to circumvent the rejection has been performed. The exact failed command is in the submitted feedback/session.

The incident's supplied context reported:
```text
sandbox_mode: danger-full-access
approval_policy: never
permission_profile: disabled / unrestricted filesystem
```

These settings and user authorization are **not asserted to override safety controls**. They make an actionable explanation important because there was no visible approval route.

Please determine which layer/rule produced this rejection and whether the command was correctly denied or misclassified. If denied, provide a specific explanation and supported resolution/approval route. If this is a false positive, identify the appropriate fix or supported safer operation.

Please also review the assistant's subsequent categorical statements that every smaller-batch approach would necessarily bypass a safeguard. The generic error did not establish that conclusion. Likewise, its attribution to "automatic approval review" was an inference, not an identified enforcing component.

The goal is a supported way to finish authorized, content-verified cleanup, **not** to weaken protections or bypass a policy.

### Related symptom reports
- #54610 — unexplained Windows policy rejection during test-artifact cleanup.
- #53512 — opaque Windows cleanup/bookkeeping rejections.
- #43732 — non-forced cleanup rejection.

A shared root cause has not been established. This report adds a SHA-256/member-verified extracted-copy cleanup case and its submitted feedback ID.

issues.body:
## Environment

- Windows desktop Codex, using the Code Mode functions.exec surface. Model identity is not independently recorded in this report.
- Running desktop Codex runtime, verified from its executable: 0.162.0-alpha.17.2.
- An older CLI bundled separately reports 0.142.4; this report uses the running desktop runtime for protocol and transport checks.
- Desktop application version and subscription tier are not collected.
- Connected remote OAuth MCP server. Server product, host names, account/workspace/resource identifiers, chat IDs and local paths are omitted.

## Problem and observed evidence

A fresh native desktop chat can discover five related MCP tools and make harmless authenticated reads. However, its supported model-visible ALL_TOOLS entries contain only name and description, including generated TypeScript declarations. No enabled assistant tool exports the current chat's complete raw inputSchema, standard annotations or schema-reference _meta.

This prevents strict client capability verification for two read tools and three command tools with different consequential classifications. Tool names and rendered TypeScript do not establish nested schema constraints, annotations or the client-registered schema reference. A server-reported capability manifest is separate evidence.

The installed desktop binary's app-server generate-json-schema --experimental output already defines:

- mcpServerStatus/list parameters including threadId, serverName and detail.
- Tool properties including inputSchema, annotations and _meta.

Thus the native core protocol already represents the required metadata. Generated protocol schemas do not prove that the current desktop catalog was exported.

The documented codex app-server proxy command, using the desktop runtime binary, fails to connect to the default control socket with Windows error 10061 (connection actively refused). A read-only process check finds three app-server processes explicitly using stdio and one without a listener argument; none advertises a Unix or TCP listener in its command arguments. The documented default transport is stdio. This does not rule out every custom route, nor does it prove an MCP server or host-cache defect.

An older implementation chat exposes four of the five tools; the earlier fresh verifier exposes all five. These are separate snapshots. The report's main request concerns metadata access, not a proven tool-discovery regression.

## Reproduction in the observed setup

1. Use a native desktop chat with an enabled, authenticated MCP server providing tools with schemas, standard annotations and a namespaced _meta schema reference.
2. Inspect matching entries and Object.keys(entry) in the supported ALL_TOOLS inventory. Observe names/descriptions without raw metadata.
3. Verify the connected service through a harmless read. Keep this evidence separate from client metadata evidence.
4. Generate JSON protocol schemas from the running desktop runtime. Observe that the native API already defines the missing metadata fields.
5. Attempt the documented proxy connection to the existing app server. In this Windows setup, the default control socket refuses the connection before a chat-scoped metadata request can be made.

This is an observed reproduction, not a deterministic clean-install fixture. No app restart, daemon bootstrap, listener/config change, direct MCP HTTP request, credential copying, cache scraping or command-tool execution was used.

## Requested change

Please route this to the Codex desktop/Code Mode interface owner and provide a supported read-only assistant capability to export metadata from the current chat's existing MCP connection and tool catalog, reusing mcpServerStatus/list rather than creating an independent session.

For selected tools, return complete registered inputSchema, standard annotations and allowlisted schema-reference metadata, plus observation/catalog provenance. Explicitly distinguish undiscovered tools and unavailable fields. A documented native export path callable from this Windows desktop environment would also resolve the evidence gap.

Exclude tool-call arguments/results, credentials, account/customer/resource values and browser state. Keep existing host approval, authorization, expiry and execution controls intact.

## Acceptance and retest

1. The assistant retrieves one supported snapshot of the current native chat's five tools, with clear provenance.
2. All five complete input schemas are inspectable, or independently verifiable hashes have a documented algorithm/canonicalization and matching accessible schema.
3. Standard annotations and exact namespaced schema references are preserved and can be compared with the connected product contract.
4. A bounded read-only comparison of all five returns no missing or mismatched fields; no prepare, confirmation or execution write is necessary.

Current status: declaration discovery and harmless reads passed in the fresh verifier; strict client metadata verification remains blocked. No fix or post-fix pass is claimed.

Reference: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server
Core implementation: https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/app-server

No raw logs, screenshots, private transcripts, credentials, local paths or account/resource identifiers are attached.

## Passing synthetic confirmation/apply fixture proof

Added 11 October 2026. Evidence class: technical, local in-memory integration testing.

An isolated fixture uses a Draft campaign, a Draft social asset and a manual, unmeasured outcome with one social placement. It prepares an owner-report command with this synthetic-only note:

> [SYNTHETIC TEST] Confirmation receipt only. Nothing was posted, sent or delivered.

No public URL, destination or schedule is supplied. The command requires confirmation while the campaign and asset remain Draft. Tests exercise the registered MCP transport, the real OAuth adapter seam and in-memory Convex transactions. Outbound fetch is configured to throw; approval responses are synthetic and programmatic.

| Scenario | Result and verified behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Local tool metadata | Passed: all five registered server tools expose complete input schemas, standard annotations and exact versioned schema references; confirmation fields and strict object constraints match the application contract. |
| Legacy exact-review confirmation | Passed: confirmation itself performs no campaign mutation, expiry is bounded and does not renew on repeat, a wrong confirmation ID is rejected, apply executes once, and replay returns the same receipt/version. |
| Initialized native acceptance | Passed on protocol 2025-06-18: the synthetic approval prompt occurs before mutation, acceptance permits one exact apply, and replay recovers the receipt. |
| Initialized native decline | Passed on protocol 2025-06-18: declining performs no execution or campaign mutation. |

Vitest structured result: **4 passed, 0 failed, success=true**. Fixture lint and application typecheck also passed. The synthetic campaign and asset remain Draft; unrelated sentinel campaign state and all asset rows are compared before/after. No real campaigns were touched and no hosted prepare, confirmation or apply call was performed.

The tested fixture source has SHA-256 `95ef3352a701cf5141ad7c768d25a2e65b8e92f2511ff4f1eeb76af5fa8de871`. Source and structured results are retained locally; the digest identifies that artifact and is not a public reproduction download.

This fixture proves the application confirmation/apply behavior in isolation. It does not prove a live desktop approval, hosted execution or current-chat metadata export, and it does not reproduce the desktop transport failure. The local server schema snapshot is an implementation reference, not a substitute for the missing client-registered metadata.

### Exact unblock step

Expose a supported read-only assistant bridge to the existing native chat's `mcpServerStatus/list`, scoped to that chat and its already connected MCP server. Return the five tools' complete `inputSchema`, standard `annotations`, allowlisted schema-reference `_meta`, and observation/catalog provenance. A documented native export path callable in this Windows desktop setup is also sufficient.

Once that export is available, compare all five tools once against the application contract. Only after the comparison passes can the live confirmation/apply test proceed on a newly created, explicitly synthetic Draft fixture, with the exact native human confirmation and before/after readback. Keep every pre-existing campaign unchanged; do not publish, activate, generate paid content or send anything.

四条云端归档 ID 在本地会话数据库中均没有对应记录。这说明本地记录检查与云端归档列表应当分开解释，不能用本地未找到会话来证明云端内容已经删除。

两条受影响记录均在既有桌面日志中出现以下错误。下面仅保留方法和错误字段，已经移除全部私有标识：

```text
method=thread/unarchive
error.code=-32600
error.data.grpcStatusCode=5
error.message="Some requested entity was not found: thread not found"
```

既有日志还出现过 `thread/read` 返回 `-32003: thread access denied`。该读取错误与取消归档失败之间的因果关系尚未确认。

### 复现步骤

这是在现有受影响账户/记录上观察到的流程，尚未找到能够从新建会话开始触发异常的最小复现：

1. 打开 macOS 桌面应用的“设置 → 已归档的聊天”。
2. 找到仍被云端归档列表返回、但没有标题的受影响 Codex 会话。
3. 点击该行“取消归档”。
4. 观察到取消归档失败；对应 `thread/unarchive` 请求返回上面的 `thread not found`。
5. 再次查询云端归档列表，原记录仍然存在。

两条记录都有同类失败日志，其中一条在应用于 10 月 24 日再次启动后仍出现该错误。本次准备报告没有再次执行删除、取消归档或改写会话数据。

### 预期行为

云端归档列表与会话操作接口应提供一致、可理解的状态。如果记录对应的会话不可访问、已失效或需要特殊恢复流程，界面应明确说明并提供受支持的恢复或单条清理路径，而不是一直显示一个必然报错的“取消归档”按钮。

请排查云端归档列举、会话解析/访问状态和取消归档处理之间是否存在不一致，并提供保留其他聊天数据的恢复方法。

### 相关报告及结论边界

- #50618、#46182 已报告云端 Codex 会话缺少删除入口。本报告补充的是：归档列表仍返回记录，但取消归档接口对同一记录返回 `thread not found`。
- #52920 也报告了云端归档记录无法取消归档，但其具体错误是 `environment config not found`；本次未建立环境删除这一触发条件，请勿直接视为同一根因。

当前证据不能证明聊天内容已经被永久删除，也不能区分权限问题、记录生命周期问题或路由问题。两条能读取历史的云端记录与两条空标题记录不应一概判定为数据丢失。

### 隐私处理

本报告仅包含版本、汇总数量、操作步骤和已脱敏的错误信息，不包含真实会话 ID、聊天标题或正文、账户信息、本机路径、截图、原始日志及凭证。

issues.title: [macOS][Remote iOS] Desktop-created active threads are listed but fail to load due to an active-writer conflict

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: iOS
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex iOS app

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

issues.body:
### What version of Codex is running?

- ChatGPT desktop app: `26.818.61809`
- Desktop-bundled Codex runtime: `codex-cli 0.149.0-alpha.4.3`
- Persistent Remote app-server: `0.149.1`

### What platform are you using?

- Host: macOS 26.5.2, Apple Silicon
- Client: ChatGPT iOS Remote Control (exact mobile app version was not captured)

### What issue are you seeing?

A thread created and actively running in the macOS desktop app is visible in the iOS Remote thread list, including its title and changed-file summary. However, opening that thread on iOS fails with “Error loading messages.”

This is not a general connectivity failure:

- the Mac remains awake and online;
- the Remote persistent app-server is running;
- the control socket exists;
- `codex doctor` reports the Remote WebSocket connected with `HTTP 101 Switching Protocols`;
- the desktop-created thread remains visible in the iOS list;
- threads created from iOS Remote load normally.

At the exact time the iOS client attempted to open the desktop-created thread, the persistent Remote app-server repeatedly logged:

```text
failed to initialize thread persistence: thread-store conflict: thread <redacted> already has an active writer
Failed to create session: thread-store conflict: thread <redacted> already has an active writer
```

The conflict was emitted repeatedly while the desktop app-server was the active writer for the same rollout file. The rollout file continued to grow normally on disk, and the state databases passed integrity checks, so there is no evidence that the thread data is missing or corrupt.

The Remote-side thread inventory reported the thread as `notLoaded`: metadata was available, but its messages could not be loaded.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On macOS, enable Remote Control and keep the Mac awake and online.
2. Create a new local thread in the ChatGPT/Codex desktop app.
3. Start a long-running turn so the desktop app-server remains the active writer.
4. Open ChatGPT on iOS and go to Remote.
5. Confirm that the desktop-created thread appears in the thread list.
6. Open that thread while the desktop turn is still running.
7. Observe “Error loading messages” on iOS.
8. Inspect the persistent Remote app-server log and observe the `already has an active writer` / `Failed to create session` errors.

### Expected behavior

Remote should be able to display the history and live progress of a desktop-owned active thread without attempting to acquire a second writer.

If interaction requires writer ownership, Remote should either perform an explicit ownership handoff or enter a stable read-only/follower state. Merely opening an active thread for monitoring should not fail to load its messages.

This is also the behavior implied by the Remote documentation, which says existing chats on the connected host can be continued and reviewed from the phone:
https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/remote-connections

### Why this appears distinct

- #37403 reports the opposite handoff direction: a Remote/CLI-owned thread cannot be resumed by Desktop.
- #40167 reports an active CLI thread that cannot be displayed on iOS Remote.
- This report confirms the Desktop-app-to-iOS direction with a desktop-bundled app-server as the active writer, while the iOS client can still list the thread metadata.

Together these reports suggest that Remote is trying to initialize writable thread persistence even when it only needs to read and display an active thread owned by another app-server.

### Additional diagnostics

`codex doctor` also reported:

```text
Background Server
  app-server: running (persistent mode)
  status: running
  app-server version: 0.149.1

Connectivity
  websocket: connected (HTTP 101 Switching Protocols)
```

There is a runtime-version difference between the desktop-bundled Codex runtime (`0.149.0-alpha.4.3`) and the persistent Remote app-server (`0.149.1`). I cannot establish whether that mismatch is causal, but it may be relevant to ownership/handoff behavior.

### Privacy

The username, repository path, project name, exact thread ID, conversation contents, and raw logs are intentionally omitted. Sanitized diagnostics can be provided if maintainers need them.

issues.title: [macOS Desktop] Orbit catalog treats access-denied hydration as retryable and repeatedly reloads 65 chats

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

labels.name: dots
labels.description: Issues involving setting up ChatGPT dots or managing their ongoing work.

issues.body:
### Summary

Codex Desktop on macOS repeatedly requests metadata for the same 65 cloud chats and receives `-32003: thread access denied`. A full restart does not stop the requests. Read-only inspection of this shipped build identifies the cloud “Your dot”/Orbit catalog refresh as a concrete retry path: a terminal permission failure is wrapped without an HTTP-style status, treated as retryable, and the catalog refresh can repeat every minute.

This report adds a specific caller/error-classification lead to #53178. Please consolidate if appropriate.

### Environment

- Codex Desktop: `26.1007.30912`, build `20156`, production channel.
- Desktop build commit: `a993bdbe5bb9503cb84de1e67d5635cf186a959f`.
- Bundled app-server: `0.162.0-alpha.17.2`.
- macOS `26.6.2` (`25G83`), Apple Silicon.
- Observation date: October 13, 2026.
- A second Mac's connected app-server reports the same bundled version. Direct inspection of that Mac was unavailable; the user also reports similar warnings there.

### Observed behavior and measurements

Existing-profile observation, not a clean-install reproducer:

1. Leave the desktop app open with existing cloud “Your dot” chats.
2. Observe repeated background metadata reads failing with the fields below.
3. Fully quit and reopen Desktop.
4. The denied-read traffic returns.

From **00:17:30.411 through 13:53:03.813 UTC on October 13**:

- **14,637 distinct failed request IDs** across **65 distinct chat IDs**, observed across three renderer IDs.
- Errors consistently include:
  ```text
  method=thread/read
  source=thread_hydration
  priority=background
  error.code=-32003
  error.message="thread access denied"
  ```
- The same IDs recur in batches. Later minute buckets contained 260 failed reads per minute; multiple renderers and retry attempts mean this is not claimed to be exactly one request per chat per minute.
- A persisted cloud sidebar catalog contains 46 of the denied IDs as thread records. Other denied IDs appear in output-related cached references.
- The cached catalog's account/user identifiers match the local authentication claims; a simple stale-account mismatch was not found. This does not establish that every cloud authorization context is correct.

In the inspected October 13 logs up to the same cutoff, there were also **103 distinct queue-full rejections**: 94 `account/read`, 3 `thread/read`, 2 `thread/items/list`, and one each for `config/read`, `mcpServerStatus/list`, `thread/turns/list`, and `fs/readFile`. Queue snapshots show four requests in flight and 64 queued interactive requests. The most recent rejection in this window was at 13:42:15.056 UTC, shortly after app startup.

The user reports intermittent general app slowdown. The denied-read loop is unnecessary background work, but **these observations do not prove it directly caused all queue-full events or all slowdown**. In particular, most queue rejections concern account reads and warrant separate investigation.

### Shipped-code investigation lead

Read-only inspection of `webview/assets/app-shared-8bd9d0399038.js` found:

- The `cloud-aeon-sidebar-threads` query fetches Orbit profile/thread attachments, combines them with previously cached thread references, and calls `hydratePinnedThreads(ids, {throwOnReadError: true})`.
- Hydration uses at most two concurrent reads per batch. It collects failures and throws the first error after processing the batch.
- The query wraps that error in a catalog error class (`_4`). Its `status` comes only from an existing numeric `error.status`; it does not map JSON-RPC `-32003 / thread access denied` to a terminal authorization state.
- The generic retry predicate (`Bq`) retries errors with no numeric status, up to three retries. Numeric 401/403/404 statuses would be non-retryable.
- The catalog sets `refetchInterval` to one minute when that same predicate says its error is retryable. It also refetches on mount, focus, and reconnect.
- The general cloud read cache retains normalized `thread_not_found` errors, but not access denial. Explicit shared reads bypass that terminal-error cache.
- A failed catalog refresh does not commit a reconciled catalog, allowing old cached references to remain candidates for later refreshes.

These branches explain how a permanent access denial can become a recurring batch refresh. The actual failing wire payloads and backend authorization decisions were not captured, and this is not proof that the catalog is the only caller responsible for every logged request.

### Expected behavior / requested fix

- Represent access denial as a terminal unavailable state until identity/access changes or the user explicitly retries.
- Handle inaccessible entries independently so one denial does not repeatedly fail and reload the entire catalog.
- Reconcile stale catalog references while preserving original chats and server authorization boundaries.
- Coordinate/deduplicate background reads across renderers.
- Investigate the separate startup `account/read` fan-out and queue-full rejections.
- Provide a supported recovery path that preserves chats and active work.

### Related reports

- #53178: macOS access-denied hydration retries, CPU observations, and recurrence after restart.
- #51675: macOS cloud sidebar/direct-read contrast.
- #51572: Windows repeated access-denied hydration.

### Privacy and interventions

No application bundle, signature, credential store, chat database, cloud chat, or access policy was modified. No patched app was installed. The investigation used read-only app/log/cache inspection and a short-lived diagnostic app-server to read effective configuration layers; that server was shut down.

No private chat/request/account IDs, titles, conversation contents, local paths, credentials, raw logs, or screenshots are attached. Prepared and submitted by Codex with the user's authorization.

## Summary

After upgrading the Windows desktop app from 26.908.9136.0 to 26.1007.9446.0, the in-composer microphone/dictation button disappeared. Settings > Voice now says **"Dictation unavailable — Dictation is not available in your current configuration"** and offers no dictation shortcut setting. Dictation worked on this same PC and account before the upgrade; Settings > Voice still lists successful recordings from October 14, including one at 19:07 local time.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Pro, build 26300, x64.
- Installed OpenAI.Codex package: 26.1007.9446.0; package status reports OK.
- Bundled codex-cli: 0.162.0-alpha.17.2.
- ChatGPT sign-in in the desktop app.

## Reproduction and impact

1. Open an existing Codex chat in the updated desktop app.
2. The composer has no microphone/dictation button.
3. Open Settings > Voice. The Dictation section says it is unavailable in the current configuration; there is no dictation shortcut control.
4. Recent recordings on that same screen show that dictation worked before the upgrade.

This removes the user's regular input method across Codex chats. A Windows voice-typing shortcut is not a workable substitute on this PC.

## Checks already performed

- The current local `~/.codex/config.toml` does not set `in_app_dictation = false`.
- The bundled runtime's `codex features list` reports `in_app_dictation` as `stable true`.
- Windows microphone permission for the app is allowed, the microphone device is present, and Windows audio services are running.
- The earlier signed installer is retained, but no downgrade was performed after this finding; a downgrade has not been verified as a fix.

## Expected result

Keep in-app dictation available after updating for an account where it previously worked. If a capability or workspace setting legitimately disables it, show the specific reason and a recovery path instead of only "current configuration". Please investigate why the desktop UI reports dictation unavailable while the local runtime reports `in_app_dictation = true`.

Related but different: #46452 reports a missing global shortcut while in-app microphone dictation still works. Here the in-app microphone and the Voice settings controls are both missing.

No chat transcripts or audio recordings are attached publicly. Private diagnostic details can be supplied if requested.
