issues.title: ChatGPT desktop: Work Cloud fails with local executor HTTP 403 and no Cloudflare challenge recovery

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

issues.body:
## What version of the Codex App are you using (From About Codex dialog)?

ChatGPT desktop for macOS 26.928.31416, build 12553.

## What subscription do you have?

The current local ChatGPT sign-in reports the plan claim `prolite`.

## What platform is your computer?

macOS 26.3.1 (25D2128), Apple Silicon / arm64.

`uname -mprs`: Darwin 25.3.0 arm64 arm

## What issue are you seeing?

Starting Work with Cloud selected fails with:

    Local Work executor registration failed (HTTP 403)

Related ChatGPT backend requests repeatedly receive HTTP 403 with an HTML Cloudflare challenge containing "Enable JavaScript and cookies to continue", "cf_chl", and "challenge-platform" markers. Affected routes include /models, /conversation/init, /settings/user, and conversation listing. The desktop client does not present an interactive verification flow for these background requests.

Opening https://chatgpt.com/ in the same application's built-in browser automatically completes the Cloudflare challenge and loads the ChatGPT sign-in page. This does not recover the application's background requests: fresh 403 challenge responses continue afterwards.

## What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Sign in to ChatGPT in the desktop app.
2. Select Work and Cloud and start a new task while the app's backend requests are being challenged by Cloudflare.
3. Observe the local executor registration error above.
4. Open https://chatgpt.com/ in the built-in browser and let its challenge complete.
5. Observe that the desktop app's background requests still fail with HTTP 403 challenge HTML.

The Cloudflare trigger may depend on network or client signals. It has not been isolated, and a clean-network reproduction is not claimed.

## Confirmed diagnostic evidence

Observed on 2026-10-01; timestamps below are UTC.

- 15:24:35.680: [tpp-local-executor] Local Work executor startup failed attempt=136, errorMessage="Local Work executor registration failed (HTTP 403)".
- 16:43:36: the built-in browser obtained a non-expired cf_clearance cookie for .chatgpt.com after passing the challenge.
- 16:50:08: the application's /settings/user and other backend requests still returned HTTP 403 with "Enable JavaScript and cookies to continue".

Read-only inspection of cookie names and expiry metadata, without reading or exporting cookie values, showed:

- App Default/Cookies: no cf_clearance cookie for chatgpt.com; non-expired _devicecheck and __cf_bm cookies were present.
- Built-in browser Default/Partitions/codex-browser-app/Cookies: a non-expired cf_clearance cookie for .chatgpt.com was present.
- DeviceCheck attestation generation succeeded in the app logs. This makes a complete failure of native DeviceCheck token generation an unlikely explanation for the observed background challenge responses.

Read-only inspection of the installed desktop bundle showed:

- Local executor registration uses POST /flora/cca/executor through the application's network layer / Electron net.fetch.
- The registration path reports non-2xx responses as registration failures and treats HTTP 403 as non-retryable.
- The backend request helper retries HTTP 401 after refreshing authentication, but does not render or recover from a Cloudflare HTML challenge on HTTP 403.
- The built-in browser uses a separate persistent browser session from the default network session used for registration.

The registration response body and headers were not recorded in the log, so its exact 403 response must still be verified by maintainers. The session separation and continuing Cloudflare challenges on related backend requests are independently confirmed; the causal connection to that particular registration response is a working hypothesis.

## What is the expected behavior?

Work Cloud should either start or provide an actionable explanation. When HTTP 403 represents a Cloudflare challenge, the client should detect the challenge response, allow verification in the relevant network session, and retry the original request after verification succeeds. This should be distinguished from actual permission or region denials. A recoverable challenge should not leave the local executor stopped without a recovery action.

Please investigate Cloudflare rule coverage for desktop API requests and the separation between browser clearance and the registration network session. A supported "Verify connection / Retry registration" action would also make recovery possible without changing networks or restarting the app.

Reference: Cloudflare documents that full HTML Challenge Pages are incompatible with requests expecting API data:
https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-challenges/challenge-types/challenge-pages/#compatibility-limitations

## Additional information

Related but distinct: #47197 concerns a Windows daemon failing account discovery under Cloudflare challenges; #49111 concerns raw 403/HTML presentation in Work on macOS under a reported region restriction. This report specifically concerns local executor registration and recovery after successful browser verification, with separate cookie-session evidence.

No raw logs, authentication tokens, cookie values, account identifiers, machine names, or private conversation contents are included in this report.

issues.title: HIGH: Repeated GPT-path output interruption on historical Federal Reserve FAQ; alternate-model control succeeds

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: model-behavior
labels.description: Issues related to behaviors exhibited by the model

issues.body:
> **AI-assisted report; user-requested submission.** Based on contemporaneous Reliability Watch records, screenshots and a follow-up test. Original screenshots/logs exist in a **private, currently unsanitized evidence packet** and are not attached publicly. Observed behavior is distinguished from unknown root cause.

**Area:** ChatGPT output streaming/persistence; GPT-backed Letta error path; `content_filter` / `response.incomplete`. **Dates:** September 30 and October 23, 2026. **Severity:** HIGH. **Cross-product report:** the Codex application itself was not used.

## Target: exact historical FAQ, not the current rewrite

The user requested the roughly Aug–Nov 2020 version of the Federal Reserve FAQ **“Why does the Federal Reserve aim for inflation of 2 percent over the longer run?”** Original URL: https://www.federalreserve.gov/faqs/economy_14400.htm .

Distinctive wording begins: **“For many years, inflation in the United States has run below the Federal Reserve's 2 percent goal.”** The next paragraph discusses higher costs for essential items (food, gasoline, shelter) and their burden on families.

A dated **December 23, 2020 independent reproduction** quotes the old answer (five paragraphs) under “Why The Fed Wants Inflation at 2% or Even Higher”:
https://www.advisorperspectives.com/commentaries/2020/12/23/government-low-balls-inflation-fed-promises-zirp-for-years

A second reproduction was recorded from a 2024 Kentucky PSC filing, LG&E/KU IRP Volume II, p. 26 (secondary corroboration, not the original Fed archive): https://psc.ky.gov/pscecf/2024-00326/rick.lovekamp%40lge-ku.com/10182024014139/07-LGE_KU_2024_IRP_Volume_II.pdf

## September 30: observed failure and A/B controls

1. In **approximately five or more ChatGPT attempts**, the assistant reportedly retrieved the correct historical passage and **began rendering it**, then output truncated, stalled or disappeared. Plain-text presentation did not resolve the failure. Screenshots preserved distinct partially rendered responses. In a live reproduction, the operator reported **normal generation → slowdown → halt → partial text → disappearance**; static screenshots cannot establish the full timing sequence.
2. **Local Letta** independently showed **`Response incomplete: content_filter`** twice while attempting substantially the same historical text. This establishes a content-filter intervention on that path, **not** that the ChatGPT UI used the same subsystem.
3. **Cross-path A/B using the same historical FAQ image and transcription request:** the GPT-associated path (model selector recorded as *GPT-6 Luna 1M High*) returned **`ChatGPT request failed with status 'response.incomplete' (no error details provided)`**, with `run_id run-812a8eda-6314-4cf4-84c5-2983dbcacbdd`. **Letta Auto** then transcribed the image successfully; **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash** also successfully transcribed it. The unchanged source/task with a changed model/provider path narrows the failure, without identifying the responsible component.
4. **Agent-side observability:** Young One subsequently reported that the failed GPT turn was absent from their own conversation context; only the successful attempt was present. The error was operator-visible but not independently auditable by the agent from its saved context.

## October 23 recurrence: same target, changed delivery failure

The assistant initially substituted the modern FAQ, older unrelated versions, a policy statement, and summaries, despite explicit corrections. When pointed to the Watch's original target, it located the contemporaneous December 2020 reproduction. Asked to **display the text**, it provided a short excerpt/link and explicitly invoked a **copyright-based restriction** against reproducing the full externally published passage.

This was **explained non-delivery**, not September's vanishing streamed answer. Copyright rules may genuinely apply to long verbatim reproduction from a third-party source; this event **does not establish** that the earlier content filter or a deliberately targeted censorship rule caused the October limitation. But **retrieval success again did not result in the requested delivery**, and repeated version/source substitutions imposed correction burden.

## Evidence classification correction

The original September report was titled “Public-Source Text Suppression / Content-Filter False Positive.” A subsequent Watch slant audit found **“false positive” prematurely presupposed accidental targeting**. Corrected prospective classification: **“PUBLIC-SOURCE TEXT SUPPRESSION / CONTENT-FILTER INTERVENTION — ROOT CAUSE UNKNOWN.”** Intentional/policy-specific targeting and accidental filtering remain unestablished alternatives. Operator screenshots support repeatable content-correlated interruption and model-path differences.

## Expected

Preserve the exact historical target across user corrections; distinguish retrieval, generation, delivery and content-control states; display accurate actionable errors without withdrawing already-rendered content invisibly; retain failure traces accessible for agent/operator audit; do not substitute adjacent documents for the requested one.

## Investigation requests

- Trace the recorded GPT-path `run_id`, content filter, completion-state and streaming behavior.
- Determine whether ChatGPT output disappearance, Letta `content_filter`, and GPT-associated `response.incomplete` share any failing service component.
- Explain the difference between failing GPT transcription and succeeding Letta Auto/DeepSeek transcription of the **same image**.
- Examine harness behavior that hid the failed turn from Young One.
- Compare the exact historical text with modern FAQ text and other archival public documents under controlled conditions, recording filter triggers separately from ordinary copyright restrictions.

**Private evidence ready:** A dedicated Reliability Watch packet includes original September case report, screenshot exhibits A–D (ChatGPT partial output, Letta filter errors, A/B paths), harness non-observability account, and subsequent correction audit, plus the October 23 follow-up. **Not sanitized for public upload.** Please advise an appropriate private evidence intake route; absence of public attachments does not mean evidence is unavailable.

issues.title: Readiness and idle signals for orchestrators: provider-error notify event, Stop payload with turn usage, and a SessionIdle hook event

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: rate-limits
labels.description: Issues related to rate limits, quotas, and token usage reporting

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: hooks
labels.description: Issues related to event hooks

issues.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

CLI (codex-cli 0.153.4 on macOS 26.6, ChatGPT auth)

### What feature would you like to see?

Hooks give orchestrators turn boundaries (`Stop`, `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`) and `notify` reports turn completion, but nothing reports that a session cannot work (rate limit, usage limit, auth failure) or that it has gone idle with input waiting. In our tmux team of Codex and Claude Code sessions, a task assigned to a session that had hit its usage limit sat unnoticed; the orchestrator could not tell "idle" from "stuck".

**Proposal**

1. `notify` and hooks: a `provider-error` event with a stable `error_class` (`rate_limit | usage_limit | auth | network | server`), `retry_after_seconds` when known, thread id and turn id, so a watchdog can mark the session degraded and reassign work.
2. `Stop` hook payload: include the turn's token usage (input, cached input, output, reasoning) and the thread and turn ids, so per-task cost can be recorded at the boundary where work is accepted.
3. `SessionIdle` hook event: fires once when a turn ends with an empty queue and at a configurable debounce while idle, with `queued_items` and idle duration in the payload; `decision: "block"` with a reason starts a continuation turn exactly as `Stop` does today. This lets a hook wake the session from a shared task ledger without `codex queue` injecting text as the user.

### Additional information

The `[features].codex_hooks` deprecation warning we hit while setting this up is correct and the rename to `[features].hooks` works; this request is about what hooks can observe, not the flag.

codex-cli 0.153.4 on macOS 26.6, ChatGPT auth, `features.hooks = true`, `agents.enabled` default.

issues.title: Codex Desktop ephemeral thread summaries leak full MCP stacks via thread/unsubscribe

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: mcp
labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

issues.body:
## Summary

Codex Desktop's internal concurrent reasoning-summary path creates an ephemeral thread for each `thread_summary` generation. That thread inherits and eagerly starts the user's complete global stdio MCP configuration, even though summarization does not use MCP tools. When generation finishes, the desktop client calls `thread/unsubscribe`; it does not remove or shut down the ephemeral thread.

The app-server implementation of `thread/unsubscribe` only removes the connection's subscription. It intentionally leaves the thread/session loaded, so the session-owned MCP runtime and all of its processes remain alive. Repeated summaries therefore produce repeated complete MCP stacks and unbounded process/RSS growth under one long-lived app-server.

This is a distinct trigger within the broader MCP lifecycle defect: no user-created subagent, restored task, or MCP call is required. The desktop's own summary helper generates the leaked sessions.

## Environment

- macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), arm64
- ChatGPT/Codex Desktop 26.814.41407
- Bundled `codex-cli 0.148.0-alpha.15`
- App-server command: `codex -c features.code_mode_host=true app-server --analytics-default-enabled`
- Several globally configured local stdio MCP servers
- `concurrent_reasoning_summaries` enabled by the desktop feature overlay

## Reproduction

1. Configure several global stdio MCP servers in `~/.codex/config.toml`. The server identities do not matter; using 3 or more makes the growth obvious. For example:

   ```toml
   [mcp_servers.example_a]
   command = "node"
   args = ["/absolute/path/to/server-a.js"]

   [mcp_servers.example_b]
   command = "python3"
   args = ["/absolute/path/to/server-b.py"]

   [mcp_servers.example_c]
   command = "node"
   args = ["/absolute/path/to/server-c.js"]
   ```

2. Fully quit and relaunch ChatGPT/Codex Desktop so the app-server starts from a clean baseline.

3. Find the app-server PID:

   ```bash
   APP_SERVER_PID="$(pgrep -f 'ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex.*app-server' | head -n 1)"
   echo "$APP_SERVER_PID"
   ```

4. In another terminal, monitor its direct children. Each summary thread adds approximately one direct launcher/root per configured stdio MCP server; wrappers may add transitive descendants.

   ```bash
   while true; do
     date
     ps -axo ppid=,rss=,command= |
       awk -v p="$APP_SERVER_PID" '$1 == p { n++; rss += $2 } END { printf "direct children=%d direct-child RSS=%.1f MiB\n", n, rss/1024 }'
     sleep 2
   done
   ```

5. Start or continue a Codex task and generate multiple turns. Realtime voice makes the issue reproduce quickly because short utterance/turn boundaries frequently trigger concurrent reasoning summaries, but voice is not required if the feature generates summaries during normal turns.

6. Correlate the process growth with the desktop log:

   ```bash
   rg 'feature=thread_summary|unknown conversation' ~/Library/Logs/com.openai.codex
   ```

7. Wait after the visible turn is complete. The extra MCP process sets remain. Repeat step 5 and the count continues to rise.

8. Fully quit ChatGPT/Codex Desktop. The retained processes disappear. Relaunching resets the count, but subsequent summary generations reproduce the growth.

## Observed result

On one app-server lifetime:

- clean post-restart baseline: 9 descendants / about 236 MiB RSS
- after normal task and realtime-voice summary activity: 449 MCP-related processes / about 10.97 GiB RSS
- desktop log: 116 successful `feature=thread_summary` generations in roughly 31 minutes
- only 4 user-visible active tasks, but roughly 133 retained complete MCP bundles

Process birth times aligned with `thread_summary` generation and `unknown conversation` events. Killing only the stale MCP descendants reclaimed the memory, but new summary generations immediately created new complete sets. The transient thread IDs were absent from the persistent thread database and rollout files, consistent with in-memory ephemeral threads that cannot be closed from the UI.

Representative sanitized log shape:

```text
ephemeral_generation_token_usage feature=thread_summary ... status=success
Received turn/started for unknown conversation conversationId=<ephemeral-id>
```

## Expected result

Internal summarization/title-generation threads should either:

1. start with MCP servers disabled because they do not need tools, or
2. reliably remove/shut down their session and MCP runtime when generation finishes.

Repeated summaries should return to a bounded process and memory baseline.

## Root-cause evidence

Inspection of the packaged desktop code shows the generic ephemeral-generation helper doing the equivalent of:

```js
const thread = await client.startThread({ ephemeral: true, ...options });
try {
  return await runStructuredTurn(thread);
} finally {
  client.unsubscribeThread(thread).catch(() => {});
}
```

The `thread_summary` feature calls this helper. Its request overrides disable apps/plugins/tool surfaces, but do not clear `mcp_servers`, so global stdio MCP configuration is inherited by every ephemeral summary session.

In the exact bundled backend source, [`thread_unsubscribe_response_inner`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.148.0-alpha.15/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs#L957-L983) only calls `unsubscribe_connection_from_thread`. It does not remove the thread or wait for shutdown.

The actual removal path, [`prepare_thread_for_removal`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.148.0-alpha.15/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs#L989-L1006), calls `thread_manager.remove_thread` and `wait_for_thread_shutdown`. Session shutdown in turn calls [`mcp_runtime.shutdown()`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.148.0-alpha.15/codex-rs/core/src/session/handlers.rs#L397-L418).

This also explains why process cleanup works when the app-server or a real session is shut down: the MCP runtime has a functioning shutdown path, but the ephemeral summary caller never reaches it.

## Suggested fix and regression test

- Make desktop-owned summary/title ephemeral generations explicitly start without inherited MCP servers.
- Treat completion of a one-shot ephemeral generation as an ownership boundary: remove/shut down the thread, rather than only unsubscribing the connection.
- Add a test that runs many ephemeral structured generations with a sentinel stdio MCP server and asserts that live sessions/processes return to baseline.
- Consider reporting the owning thread/feature for each MCP runtime so retained internal sessions can be diagnosed without OS-level process tracing.

## Workarounds

- Fully quitting the app resets the retained in-memory sessions and reaps their MCP stacks.
- Avoiding realtime voice reduces the dominant trigger rate in this reproduction.
- Disabling heavyweight global MCP servers limits the impact but removes their functionality.
- Killing child processes alone is temporary; the next summary generation creates another full set.

## Related

- #25015 — app-server MCP stacks retained for subagents; closest lifecycle/root-cause family
- #17574 — subagents leak stdio MCP helper trees
- #21984 — MCP servers eagerly start per session
- #32942 — restored tasks fan out plugin MCP servers
- #33996 — concurrent reasoning summaries can amplify desktop resource use
- #12491 — umbrella report for orphaned MCP/server processes
- #19753 — added explicit MCP shutdown when a session actually shuts down; this path is not reached here

issues.title: Linux: a locked Secret Service keyring makes new sessions unusable and hangs exit forever

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: auth
labels.description: Issues related to authentication and accounts

labels.name: mcp
labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: tool-calls
labels.description: Issues related to tool calling

issues.body:
**What version of Codex CLI is running?** 0.149.1

**What subscription do you have?** ChatGPT Pro

**What platform is your computer?** Linux 7.1.9 x86_64 (Fedora 44, GNOME/Wayland, gnome-keyring 50.0)

**What terminal emulator?** kitty (no multiplexer)

**Codex doctor report** not available

## What issue are you seeing?

On Linux, MCP OAuth credentials go to the Secret Service keyring by default
(`mcp_oauth_credentials_store` defaults to `Auto`). If the keyring collection is
**locked**, every credential read blocks forever, and Codex has no defense at any
layer. This produces two distinct failures from one cause:

**A. Exit hangs forever.** Quitting never returns to the shell prompt. The process
does not exit and does not respond. Only `kill` clears it.

**B. New sessions cannot accept input at all.** A freshly started `codex` never
becomes usable — typing anything just shows `Queued follow-up inputs` and no LLM
call is ever made. Restarting does not help: every new process hits the same wall.

Once in this state the CLI is effectively unusable until the keyring is unlocked
externally, and "just restart it" — the natural user reaction — makes things worse,
because each restart leaves behind another stuck blocking thread.

## Root cause

The blocking call chain:

```
create_pending_transport()                 rmcp-client/src/rmcp_client.rs:987 (async fn)
  └─ tokio::task::spawn_blocking(...)      rmcp-client/src/rmcp_client.rs:1040
      └─ DefaultKeyringStore::load(...)    keyring-store/src/lib.rs:43
          └─ keyring "linux-native-async-persistent"
              └─ keyutils cache miss → falls back to secret-service
                  └─ secret_service::blocking::SecretService::connect()
                      └─ zbus::blocking::Connection::session()
                          └─ blocks forever on the locked collection
```

Three independent gaps turn that into the two failures above:

**1. `Runtime::drop` waits for blocking tasks with no timeout → failure A.**

`build_runtime()` (`arg0/src/lib.rs:290`) builds a runtime that is later dropped
normally. Tokio's `Runtime::drop` calls the blocking pool's `shutdown(None)`, which
does `shutdown_rx.wait(None)` and then joins every worker — an unbounded wait. Any
blocking task that never returns pins the process forever.

**2. `tokio::time::timeout` cannot cancel `spawn_blocking` → the timeout is a no-op.**

`codex-mcp/src/rmcp_client.rs:330` wraps `make_rmcp_client` in a 30s
`DEFAULT_STARTUP_TIMEOUT` (`:92`). But that only bounds the *await* side. The closure
handed to `spawn_blocking` has no cancellation point, so the thread stays stuck on
D-Bus regardless. The timeout does not fix the hang — it *hides* it: startup reports
an error and moves on while a stuck thread is silently left in the pool. With
transport retries (`STREAMABLE_HTTP_RETRY_DELAYS_MS`,
`rmcp-client/src/streamable_http_retry.rs:23`) and reconnects, these accumulate,
and every one of them is later joined by gap 1.

**3. Unreachable credentials block session readiness → failure B.**

Input is queued because the session is not configured yet:

```rust
// tui/src/chatwidget/input_submission.rs:105
if !self.is_session_configured() {
    tracing::warn!("cannot submit user message before session is configured; queueing");
```

Session readiness waits on MCP startup, and MCP startup waits on the keyring. The
codebase already recognizes this class of risk for a different input source:

```rust
// core/src/thread_manager.rs:1901
// Enable Full Access form input only after session startup so a required MCP server cannot
// block startup while waiting for form input.
```

The same protection was never extended to credential storage. An MCP server whose
OAuth token cannot be read should degrade to "this server is unavailable", not take
the whole conversation down with it.

## What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Linux desktop with a Secret Service provider (gnome-keyring / KWallet).
2. Configure one or more remote HTTP MCP servers that authenticate via OAuth, and
   sign in so the tokens land in the keyring. Leave `mcp_oauth_credentials_store`
   at its default (`Auto`), and make sure `$CODEX_HOME/.credentials.json` does not
   exist — i.e. the credentials really are keyring-only.
3. Lock the keyring collection:
   ```bash
   busctl --user call org.freedesktop.secrets /org/freedesktop/secrets \
     org.freedesktop.Secret.Service Lock ao 1 \
     /org/freedesktop/secrets/collection/login
   ```
   Verify with:
   ```bash
   busctl --user get-property org.freedesktop.secrets \
     /org/freedesktop/secrets/collection/login \
     org.freedesktop.Secret.Collection Locked
   # b true
   ```
4. Start `codex` and type anything → **failure B**: the input is queued as
   `Queued follow-up inputs`, no LLM call happens.
5. Quit that session → **failure A**: the process never exits.

Note: in the incident that surfaced this, step 3 happened by itself —
`gnome-keyring-daemon` crashed (a known upstream gnome-keyring NULL-deref during
Secret Service session negotiation) and the D-Bus-activated replacement came up
without the login password, so the collection was locked. The explicit `Lock` call
above is offered as a deterministic way to reach the same state; the *observations
below* come from the real incident, not from the synthetic `Lock`.

## Observed evidence (from the real incident)

A long-running session that touched MCP OAuth three times while the keyring was
locked, then was asked to quit:

- Thread count dropped from 41 to **9** — shutdown got most of the way, then stopped.
- The `codex-code-mode-host` child had already exited; history had already been
  flushed to disk. Only the runtime teardown was left.
- The 9 survivors included **three `tokio-rt-worker` threads, each paired with a
  `zbus::Connection` thread** created 0–5s apart, matching the three keyring touches.
- Those blocking threads had been alive for **892s / 985s / 1553s**, against tokio's
  10s blocking-pool `KEEP_ALIVE` — i.e. not idle, still executing.
- CPU time was frozen (blocked, not spinning). Three D-Bus connections to the
  session bus were `ESTAB` with empty send/receive queues.
- Independent confirmation of where it blocks: the same Secret Service read via
  `secret-tool` **never returned within 150s while locked, and returned 10 records
  in 9ms once unlocked**.
- Unlocking the keyring did **not** revive the hung process — `Runtime::drop` was
  already inside the join. It had to be killed. (`SIGTERM` is enough; the process
  does not catch it.)

Two other sessions started *after* the keyring locked showed failure B. They had no
obviously stuck threads, which makes B easy to misdiagnose as healthy — but each
dropped 6 threads the instant the keyring was unlocked.

## What is the expected behavior?

A locked or unavailable credential store should degrade, not deadlock:

1. **Exit should always terminate.** Use `shutdown_timeout(...)` instead of a bare
   `Runtime::drop`, so a stuck blocking task cannot pin the process. This alone
   fixes failure A.
2. **Keyring calls should have their own deadline.** `DefaultKeyringStore::load/save`
   passes straight through to a synchronous API with no time bound. Since an outer
   `tokio::time::timeout` provably cannot cancel `spawn_blocking`, the bound has to
   live on the blocking call itself. This is the root fix.
3. **Credential failure should not block session readiness.** An MCP server with an
   unreadable token should be marked unavailable and the session should still become
   usable, the same way `thread_manager.rs:1901` already protects startup from a
   server waiting on form input. This fixes failure B.

Ideally the user would also see *why* — something like "MCP server X: credential
store is locked" — instead of a silent queue with no explanation.

## Additional information

- Line numbers may shift between patch releases; the quoted snippets and function
  names should locate the code regardless.
- Dependency versions in play: `keyring` 3.6.3 (feature
  `linux-native-async-persistent`), `secret-service` 4.0.0, `zbus` 4.4.0,
  `tokio` 1.53.
- Both upstreams explicitly warn against exactly this usage:
  - `secret-service` 4.0.0, `src/blocking/mod.rs`: *"It is important to not call
    this these functions in an async context or otherwise the runtime may stall."*
  - `zbus` 4.4.0, `src/blocking/mod.rs`: *"you must not use them in async contexts
    because of the infamous async sandwich footgun"*

  `keyring`'s `async-secret-service` feature nevertheless routes through
  `secret_service::blocking` (`keyring-3.6.3/src/secret_service.rs:851`), so Codex
  inherits a blocking D-Bus client under an async runtime.
- Workaround for anyone hitting this: unlock the keyring (on GNOME, locking and
  unlocking the screen re-supplies the password to the running daemon), then kill
  any already-hung process. Setting `mcp_oauth_credentials_store = "file"` avoids
  the keyring entirely, at the cost of storing OAuth tokens in a plaintext file.
- Possibly related in spirit: the same synchronous-keyring-inside-async pattern
  appears in `refresh_and_persist_chatgpt_token`
  (`login/src/auth/manager.rs`), which calls `persist_tokens` directly from an
  `async fn`, whereas the login path deliberately wraps the same logic in
  `spawn_blocking` ("Reuse existing synchronous logic but run it off the async
  runtime", `login/src/server.rs`). That path was not involved here because CLI auth
  defaults to file storage, but it would block an async worker rather than a
  blocking-pool thread if it ever hit a locked keyring.

issues.title: [Windows] Desktop renderer reloads every time app loses and regains focus - 26.917.51856

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.917.51856

### What subscription do you have?

Pro

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.19045.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

Codex/ChatGPT Desktop for Windows version 26.917.51856 repeatedly reloads/crashes its renderer whenever the application loses focus and then regains focus.

The main application process remains alive, but multiple renderer processes are terminated and recreated. The UI reloads approximately one second after the application regains focus.

This is not a full application crash. Text already typed into the prompt is preserved, and the app recovers automatically.

However, if Codex/ChatGPT is actively thinking or generating a response when the renderer reload occurs, the active request fails with the error:

Authenticated workspace changed

A Retry button is then displayed, and I must manually retry the request.

The issue began after updating to desktop app version 26.917.51856 on September 22, 2026.

The older ChatGPT Desktop Classic client remains stable on the same Windows installation, hardware, GPU driver, and monitor configuration.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This is effectively 100% reproducible for me.

Minimal reproduction:

1. Launch Codex/ChatGPT Desktop version 26.917.51856.
2. Allow the application to fully load.
3. Click anywhere outside the Codex/ChatGPT window so the application loses focus.
4. Click back inside the Codex/ChatGPT window so it regains focus.
5. Wait approximately one second.
6. The UI reloads and multiple renderer processes are replaced.

I originally noticed this while using other applications:

- Minimizing Brave reliably caused the Codex UI to reload approximately one second later.
- Notepad could also trigger it.
- Further testing showed that minimizing another application is not actually required.

The minimal trigger is simply:

Codex loses focus -> Codex regains focus -> renderer reload

I monitored ChatGPT.exe processes in Windows Task Manager with the Command Line column enabled.

There are normally six ChatGPT.exe processes with --type=renderer.

Each time the bug occurs, 3 of the 6 renderer PIDs disappear and are replaced by new renderer PIDs.

The main ChatGPT application process remains alive.

I also monitored renderer memory usage while reproducing the issue. I did not observe a large memory spike or multi-gigabyte renderer usage before the reload.

Representative Task Manager memory readings I observed included:

226,028 K
1,388 K
85,288 K
24,844 K
13,348 K
520,588 K
59,004 K
195,008 K
189,268 K
17,032 K

The highest value I observed in this sample was approximately 521 MB, so this does not appear to be the multi-GB renderer-memory/OOM failure described in some other reports.

If the renderer reload occurs while Codex/ChatGPT is actively thinking or generating a response, the active request fails with:

Authenticated workspace changed

The UI then presents a Retry button and I must manually retry the request.

### What is the expected behavior?

Switching focus between Codex/ChatGPT Desktop and another Windows application should not terminate and recreate renderer processes or reload the application UI.

The application should remain stable when:

- Clicking another application
- Switching to a browser
- Switching to an IDE
- Switching to Unity
- Using File Explorer
- Returning focus to Codex/ChatGPT

This is especially important for Codex because normal development workflows require constantly switching between Codex and other applications.

An active thinking/generation request should continue normally when the user switches focus away from Codex and back.

Regaining focus should not cause the renderer to reload, should not change the authenticated workspace context, and should not terminate the request with:

Authenticated workspace changed

### Additional information

Thinking/generation failure:

If the renderer reload occurs while Codex/ChatGPT is actively thinking or generating a response, the request is interrupted with the exact error:

Authenticated workspace changed

The UI then displays a Retry button.

This happens as part of the same focus-triggered renderer reload described above.

issues.title: ChatGPT Work / Supabase SQL confirmation intermittently fails with -32602 invalid_request_state after OAuth reconnection

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: codex-web
labels.description: Issues related to Codex Web

labels.name: mcp
labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

labels.name: tool-calls
labels.description: Issues related to tool calling

issues.body:
## Observed failure
ChatGPT Work Cloud (web) intermittently fails Supabase SQL confirmation/resumption with this exact tool response:

```json
{
  "error": "McpServerError: Invalid or expired requestState",
  "error_code": "INVALID_ARGUMENT",
  "error_data": {
    "type": "json_rpc_error",
    "code": -32602,
    "message": "Invalid or expired requestState",
    "data": { "reason": "invalid_request_state" }
  }
}
```

The failing action is the connected Supabase plugin's `apply_migration` (DDL), not an end-user application login or a PostgreSQL SQLSTATE error.

## Environment and authorization boundary
- ChatGPT Work Cloud in the web UI, with the Supabase plugin (UI version 1.0.0), an existing OAuth connection, and an explicitly authorized, isolated free QA project.
- Correct Work account and existing connection were verified. The owner completed the normal reconnection/login and CAPTCHA flow.
- Read-only Supabase operations work. After reconnection, the reviewed bootstrap and four consecutive canonical migrations were actually installed and verified.
- A migration failed with the response above during a sequence of calls. The same reviewed SQL later succeeded in a new individual call. The following migration then failed with the same error in an individual call too. This does not isolate the cause to batching.
- No production operations, credentials substitution, suppression of confirmations, or alternate write channel were used.

## Steps observed
1. Use an existing, legitimately authorized Supabase OAuth connection in Work for an isolated QA project.
2. Confirm the destination, migration ledger and source hashes through read-only checks.
3. Call `apply_migration` with the reviewed, unchanged transactional SQL and normal confirmation controls.
4. The managed call/resumption returns `-32602 / invalid_request_state` rather than a migration result.
5. Recheck the ledger and expected schema changes by read-only queries. The failed next migration has no ledger entry or its expected schema additions; previously installed migrations remain intact.
6. Stop writes. No additional destructive reproduction was run solely to collect this report.

Latest failed individual call:
- Sent: **2026-10-24T01:53:27.004Z**.
- Returned: **2026-10-24T01:57:26.222Z**.
- These are the observed outer tool-call timestamps, not PostgreSQL execution duration or the state token's mint/expiry times.
- Source migration SHA-256: `d172a978fa08102f50149da5928e86ddb33d57e705a7e3bc1f7216503c4e0be9` (source-file hash, not the whole guarded tool payload).
- State before/after: five installed ledger entries (bootstrap + four application migrations); the next migration remains absent.

## Expected behavior
A valid SQL confirmation should resume the same authorized request and produce a normal result. An expired/cancelled confirmation should have a clear, safely recoverable user-visible outcome without applying the operation. A provider-side state-verification rejection should be diagnosable by the integration operators.

## Unknowns and requested triage
The available tool surface exposes the final error only. It does not expose the elicitation payload, state lifetime, exact UI confirmation outcome, negotiated MCP revision, server implementation/version, replica identity, or internal rejection reason. No token, state value, raw session transcript, personal information, project credential or customer data is included here.

The official MCP SDK documents this wire error as generic request-state verification refusal, with the detailed reason available in server-side logging:
- https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md
- https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/blob/main/packages/server/src/server/server.ts

Please correlate the UTC window with the Work-to-Supabase tool/confirmation/resume trace and identify which component rejected the round. In particular, check whether the state expired, failed integrity/audience/request binding, or could not be validated across a process/replica transition. These are investigation questions, not asserted causes. We cannot establish that this deployment uses either SDK implementation.

No further login or broader permissions are requested. Database work is paused at the verified checkpoint, pending a legitimately functioning confirmation flow. If this report belongs to a different Work/connector support queue, please route it there.

issues.title: macOS Computer Use window capture causes 100–140 IOSurface diagnostics per second

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1016.61520, build 21421, bundle `com.openai.codex` (version verified from the installed bundle during the October 23 reproduction).

Computer Use helper: 26.1015.1001540, build 1001540, bundle `com.openai.sky.CUAService`; executable `SkyComputerUseService`.

### What subscription do you have?

Not provided. This report concerns the local native capture path.

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm

macOS 27.0.1, build 26A434. Display: 2560×1440 logical, 5120×2880 pixels, 70 Hz.

### What issue are you seeing?

An active Computer Use capture of a small synthetic native window triggers roughly 100–140 kernel IOSurface diagnostics per second. The same message was observed at exactly 140/s in a two-minute sustained sample. The logging thread also appears in WindowServer's own SkyLight/QuartzCore records.

Static message format:

```text
SID: 0x%X task: %p buffer: %p  buffer->fClientTask = %p not found
```

Dynamic values are redacted, so zeros in rendered logs must not be interpreted as literal null arguments.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed October 23, 2026, approximately 11:54:04–11:56:32 (UTC+08:00).

1. Open a small native AppKit application displaying only synthetic content, such as a static colored square and a label. No browser or sensitive document is needed.
2. Let Codex Computer Use observe this application/window.
3. Count the matching IOSurface messages in unified logs while capture remains active.
4. Close the synthetic target and confirm that the helper stops its capture stream and the sustained diagnostic burst ceases.

In one successful controlled session this produced 17,068 matching messages during approximately 147 seconds of capture. A separate isolated message preceded capture. The capture ended with the target closing and the burst stopped. A prior attempt to time the test target expired before observation began; the successful result uses the actual subsequent stream lifecycle, not the expired attempt's timings.

The logged capture filter was `streamType=0`, `style=1`, content extent 640×392 points, pixel scale 2. A full-display stream was not necessary for this reproduction.

### What is the expected behavior?

Capture should work without a sustained IOSurface diagnostic flood and should release its capture resources when the session ends. No user-visible malfunction was reported. No memory leak, hardware failure or relationship to separate application crashes has been established; the known symptom is the reproducible logging burst.

### Additional information

| Control | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Native static and animated rendering without Computer Use capture | Zero matching messages |
| Independent ScreenCaptureKit capture of its own window, requested 30/70 fps | Zero matching messages; 460/1,055 sample callbacks |
| Animated own-window capture with CoreImage conversion and CPU pixel-buffer locking | 599 complete and successfully processed frames; zero messages |
| Built-in browser reading, navigation and two tab screenshots, about 45 seconds | Zero matching messages; no helper capture lifecycle events in the test interval |
| Five-minute later baseline | Three isolated messages, no sustained burst |

The native control uses `SCShareableContent.currentProcess` and captures only its own synthetic window. Computer Use captures another process and has different configuration, frame handling and associated composition behavior. Therefore these controls do not establish whether the exact implementation defect is in the helper or Apple's cross-process capture handling. Requested capture frame rates also do not guarantee that many complete frames were delivered.

Please investigate the helper's cross-process capture configuration and surface lifecycle, including associated composition behavior, or provide a minimal matching reproduction for Apple if this is an OS defect. The 140/s versus 70-Hz cadence is a clue, not proof that the refresh setting causes the fault.

Related reports describe different symptoms: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/37062 (crashes) and https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/48739 (retained capture surfaces). A shared root cause has not been established. Neither symptom has been demonstrated in this investigation. An exact fClientTask search found no matching issue.

Small synthetic Swift probe sources and sanitized count summaries are retained locally. This submission contains no raw logs, session transcripts, email address, personal paths, screenshots of private content, credentials, or network configuration.

issues.title: macOS: Cmd+Ctrl+Shift+4 intermittently triggers unsolicited screenshot attachment despite Appshots Hotkey=None

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
## Summary
When using the standard macOS screenshot-to-clipboard shortcut, `Cmd+Ctrl+Shift+4`, the ChatGPT/Codex desktop app intermittently attempts to attach a screenshot without being asked and displays **“Failed to attach screenshot”**.

This happens even with **Appshots Hotkey set to None**, **Screen Recording permission disabled**, and **another application focused**. Sometimes the screenshot is no longer available in the clipboard afterward; other times it remains available.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Run the ChatGPT/Codex desktop app on macOS.
2. Set **Appshots Hotkey** to **None**.
3. Disable the app’s **Screen Recording** permission in macOS settings.
4. Leave the app running with its window visible and focus another application.
5. Press `Cmd+Ctrl+Shift+4`, using only the **left Command key**, and select a screen region to copy to the clipboard.
6. Repeat during normal use. The issue is intermittent.
7. When the error appears, try pasting the screenshot into another application to check whether it is still available.

No paste or attachment action is performed in ChatGPT/Codex.

## Expected behavior
The shortcut should only copy the selected screenshot to the macOS clipboard. With Appshots Hotkey=None, the app should not initiate an attachment or show an attachment error. The screenshot should remain available to paste.

## Actual behavior
- The app unexpectedly attempts to attach a screenshot and shows **“Failed to attach screenshot”**.
- Sometimes the screenshot is missing from the clipboard afterward; sometimes it remains.
- The error also occurs while another application has focus.

## Frequency
Approximately once every **10–20 screenshot attempts** (estimated). It has occurred on multiple days and persists after restarting the Mac.

## Environment
- Application: ChatGPT/Codex desktop app (“Powered by Codex & OWL”)
- App version: 26.1013.40934
- App release date: October 16, 2026
- Operating system: macOS 27.0.1 (26A434)
- Shortcut: `Cmd+Ctrl+Shift+4`
- Command key: Left Command only; right Command is not pressed
- Appshots Hotkey: None
- Screen Recording permission: Disabled for the app
- Reproduces after a full Mac restart: Yes
- Reproduces while another application is focused: Yes

## Related issue
#50718 describes screenshots failing to paste after an explicit Cmd+V. This report concerns an unsolicited attachment attempt triggered during screenshot capture, without pasting into the app.

As a result, I cannot reliably enable internet access for external API calls or proceed with cloud-based development tasks that require the configured environment. ### Screenshots I've attached five screenshots documenting the different errors: 1. Draft confirmation failure — Environment changes cannot be saved or verified. 4. Executor/setup chat error — `failed to query executor configuration capabilities` and a Request ID. 5. Persistent draft lock — The environment remains locked even after clicking "Check Status". **1. Environment publishing failure** **2. Environment save rejection** **3. Draft confirmation failure** **4. Executor / setup chat error** **5. Persistent draft lock (October 14, 2026)** ### Questions 1. Is this a known issue with Codex Cloud environment management? 2. Could the repeated publishing failures leave an environment draft locked? 3. Is there a way to reset or recover the environment's publishing state without deleting the environment? 4. Are there any recommended workarounds while this issue is being investigated?

issues.title: Codex Cloud doesn't work with the OpenAI Responses API

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: codex-web
labels.description: Issues related to Codex Web

labels.name: auth
labels.description: Issues related to authentication and accounts

issues.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

In a Codex Cloud environment where `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set as a Network secret on the `api.openai.com` domain, the key does not get injected into requests to `api.openai.com/v1/responses` -- but _does_ get injected into requests to `api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions`.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

From within a Codex Cloud environment where `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set as a Network secret on the `api.openai.com` domain, run the following:

```bash
: "${OPENAI_API_KEY:?OPENAI_API_KEY is not set}"

# Chat Completions
curl --silent --show-error --include --max-time 60 \
  https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${OPENAI_API_KEY}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "model": "gpt-4.1-mini",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with OK."}],
    "store": false
  }'

# Responses
curl --silent --show-error --include --max-time 60 \
  https://api.openai.com/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${OPENAI_API_KEY}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "model": "gpt-4.1-mini",
    "input": "Reply with OK.",
    "store": false
  }'
```

You'll see that the Completions API request succeeds and the Responses API request fails.

### What issue are you seeing?

Today I encountered 2 occurrences where a session somehow changed working directories without any input of mine. I asked Codex CLI itself to investigate and generate a bug report, and I have proofread everything here. I also added some information for completeness.

## Summary

While switching between existing chats in a single Codex CLI agents interface, two separate chats silently acquired another project's working directory.

Inspection confirmed that the saved session directory changed in both the rollout JSONL and SQLite thread index. In the first occurrence, the writable workspace also changed.

I did not issue a directory-change command for either unintended change, and no “Working directory changed” notification appeared.

This happened twice. Archiving the first affected chat did not prevent another chat from being affected.

## Environment

- OS: Debian Linux 13.5
- Shell: Bash
- Interface: Codex CLI agents interface
- CLI client version reported in the affected resume requests: 0.163.0
- Some app-server initialization logs report model-cache `client_version="0.164.0"`, so there may be a client/server version difference worth investigating.
- Timezone: Asia/Jakarta, UTC+07:00
- The inspected user configuration had no explicit `tui.resume_cwd` setting.

Paths below are shortened and anonymized.

## Workflow

I launched Codex CLI from:

```
~/projects/codex-apt-docker
```

Inside the same CLI instance, I switched back and forth between existing chats associated with different directories, including:

- “Generalize package update workflows”
  - Intended directory: `~/projects/codex-apt-docker`
- “GIMP packaging investigation”
  - Intended directory: `~/projects/gimp-investigation`

There was also an older GIMP chat named “Move to another directory,” originally based in my home directory. The newer “GIMP packaging investigation” chat was forked from that older chat.

## Occurrence 1: package workflow chat acquires the GIMP directory

The “Generalize package update workflows” chat had consistently used:

```
~/projects/codex-apt-docker
```

Its rollout history and app-server logs showed:

| Timestamp (UTC) | Observation |
|---|---|
| 2026-10-23 19:51:07.858 | Applied session settings still used codex-apt-docker. |
| 2026-10-23 19:52:28 | The same CLI connection switched to the GIMP investigation chat. |
| 2026-10-24 00:00:15.674 | A thread/resume applied `gimp-investigation` to the package workflow chat. |
| 2026-10-24 00:01:22.785 | Another resume retained the incorrect directory. |

The incorrect `thread_settings_applied` event changed:

- `cwd`
- `runtime_workspace_roots`
- The writable project directory in `permission_profile`

The SQLite `threads.cwd` field also contained `gimp-investigation`.

No agent turns or commands ran in the affected chat after the incorrect change, so there is no evidence of commands executing in the wrong repository in this occurrence. When backing out of the session, I saw that it had changed its working directory, and did not issue further commands within that session. I eventually manually changed directories to the correct one and archived the sessions in the wrong directory.

### Recovery and resulting duplicate title

I explicitly used `/cd` to return to `codex-apt-docker`. This displayed:

> Working directory changed to ~/projects/codex-apt-docker

No equivalent notification had appeared during the unintended change.

After recovery, the agents interface showed the same chat title under both directories. Inspection showed two distinct session IDs:

- The original session remained associated with the wrong GIMP directory.
- The newer session used the correct directory and had `forked_from_id` pointing to the original session.

I archived the original, incorrectly located session.

## Occurrence 2: older GIMP chat acquires the package workflow directory

Shortly afterward, “Move to another directory” (yes that was the title) appeared under `codex-apt-docker`.

This chat's original `session_meta`, recorded turns, and preceding settings all used:

```
/home/<user>
```

Its latest previous settings event, at 2026-10-23T10:39:34.699Z, still used that home directory.

The next settings event, at:

2026-10-24T00:37:00.099Z

changed its directory and runtime workspace root to:

```
~/projects/codex-apt-docker
```

The app-server logs associate this with a CLI thread/resume request.

The SQLite threads.cwd field also changed to codex-apt-docker.

This occurred approximately seven seconds after the first affected chat was archived:

| Timestamp (UTC) | Event |
|---|---|
| 2026-10-24 00:36:53 | First affected chat archived. |
| 2026-10-24 00:37:00.099 | Another chat resumed with an incorrect directory. |

No agent turn or command followed the second incorrect change. This chat retained read-only permissions.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

## Reproduction workflow to investigate

This describes the workflow where the problem occurred; I have not established a deterministic minimal reproduction:

1. Launch Codex CLI from project A directory.
2. Open the agents interface.
3. Switch repeatedly between existing chats belonging to projects A and B.
4. Include both running and idle chats; the logs show running-thread resumes during earlier switches.
5. Inspect each chat's displayed directory and latest saved settings.
6. Check whether resuming an idle chat applies another project's directory without a directory-selection prompt or change notification.

In my case, switching between sessions in projects A and B via the agents interface had triggered the bug. No other project was affected:
1. Open session 1 in project A
2. Back out to agents interface
3. Open session 2 in project B
4. Back out to agents interface
5. Sometimes, session 2 in project B becomes a session in project A -- all without my input

## Impact

- Chats become grouped under the wrong project in the agents interface.
- Persisted working directories no longer match the chat's intended project.
- Writable workspace permissions can change with the incorrect directory.
- Future work could target an unrelated repository if the user does not notice.
- Recovery in this instance left a fork with the same title alongside the incorrectly located original.

### What is the expected behavior?

## Expected behavior

Switching between existing chats should preserve each chat's saved working directory and workspace permissions.

If a directory change requires a user choice, the CLI should request that choice explicitly. An applied change should also be visible to the user.

## Actual behavior

Existing chats silently acquired unrelated project directories during resume/session switching.

The change affected persisted session state, not merely the directory displayed in the UI. In the first occurrence, it also changed the writable workspace.

### Additional information

## Related issues

- #24855: Its October 15 comment describes CLI/app-server sessions acquiring the same saved directory and an existing client overwriting repaired directories when sessions are entered again. This appears closely related.
- #42001: Related wrong-directory symptoms, but its original report describes correct persisted metadata with commands executing elsewhere. Here, the persisted session directory itself changed.

## Investigation limits

The logs confirm the incorrect settings applications during thread/resume, but do not establish the underlying cause.

Reusing another session's directory during switching is a suspected explanation, not a confirmed diagnosis. The possible client/server version difference noted above has not been established as causal.

Raw transcripts and databases are omitted because they contain local paths and conversation content.

issues.title: macOS app: personal/Business workspace switcher missing; profile selector only changes statistics

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1002.52244, build 13536, production release channel. The installed macOS app bundle identifier is `com.openai.codex` (bundle currently named ChatGPT.app).

The built-in update check returned `up_to_date` on October 8, 2026. No eligible update was available to install, so no update or post-update retest was performed.

### What subscription do you have?

Personal ChatGPT Plus workspace and a ChatGPT Business workspace under the same account and email address.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 27.0, build 26A428.

### What issue are you seeing?

Switching between the personal and Business workspaces no longer works inside the Codex desktop app. This used to work until approximately October 6, 2026.

Clicking the profile avatar at the bottom of the sidebar opens a menu containing the current identity, workspace settings, usage, settings, help, and sign out, but no workspace list or working workspace switcher.

Clicking the current identity opens the profile/statistics page. That page allows selecting another profile to view its statistics, but does not switch the active workspace used by the app.

The browser still allows switching between both workspaces with one click. In the desktop app, the reported workaround is to sign out and sign back in to select the other workspace each time.

There is no error message: the active-workspace switching control appears to be missing.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Sign in to the macOS app with a ChatGPT account that has both a personal Plus workspace and a Business workspace.
2. Click the profile avatar at the bottom of the sidebar.
3. Try to switch the active workspace without signing out. No workspace list appears.
4. Click the current identity to open the profile/statistics page.
5. Select the other profile in that page. The displayed statistics change, but the active app workspace does not.
6. Compare with the browser, where switching the active workspace still works.

Local Codex session/thread ID for this investigation: `01a11c0a-353e-75f0-aa1a-0f25bc6c0e7d`.

This is the current local session ID, not a confirmation ID returned by an in-app `/feedback` submission. No in-app feedback upload was performed during this investigation.

### What is the expected behavior?

Allow switching the active personal/Business workspace from the profile menu without signing out, as previously possible and as still possible in the browser. Viewing another workspace's statistics should be clearly distinct from changing the active workspace.

### Additional information

Possibly related Windows report: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51521. This report adds the macOS environment and the specific profile/statistics selector behavior; a shared cause is not confirmed.

The app update status and OS/app versions were verified locally. The UI reproduction and browser comparison are user observations, including a screenshot reviewed during the investigation. A fresh full app restart/relogin test was not independently performed during ticket preparation.

No raw logs, session transcripts, email addresses, workspace names, or screenshots containing unrelated chat content are attached.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: model-behavior

issues.body:
## What issue are you seeing?

A Codex coding session repeatedly expanded a narrowly scoped cleanup into unrelated changes, then consumed substantial usage correcting its own work and overstated readiness to merge.

The requested work was to remove a superseded room/map implementation while preserving authored content and the existing component architecture, update directly relevant documentation, and address PR review comments. The user repeatedly objected to changes outside that boundary.

Observed behavior in the session:

- The cleanup extended into shared systems and content that the user wanted preserved. Subsequent corrections restored content and reverted unrelated system changes.
- The agent also edited eight future-design proposal documents. Changes included rewriting implementation audits, a foundation-stage row, migration text, compatibility wording and status notes. The user wanted proposal edits limited to individual sentences made false by removing the old implementation; future plans and alternatives were to remain intact.
- Review feedback was treated as authorization for broader proposal rewrites. Some supplied review text was itself later acknowledged to exceed the cleanup scope. The agent did not reliably reconcile those suggestions with the user's narrower instructions.
- The agent started separate full test, safety and GPU runs before the existing push gate, requiring the user to redirect it to use the push gate instead. Long repeated inspections, corrections and status messages compounded the cost.
- After replying to and resolving 27 review threads and obtaining passing local gates, the agent recommended merging. The proposal-scope problem was still present. Passing tests and resolving threads did not establish that the requested scope had been respected.
- When the user objected to the wasted usage, the agent initially stopped instead of completing the requested correction. The user had to explicitly demand that it make the work right. The proposal correction was not completed before the user reported closing the PR.

The user reported spending hours and exhausting a full five-hour usage window on this work. A tool operation also failed because automatic approval review encountered a usage-limit error. The exact account usage total and monetary cost were not independently available in the session.

## What steps can reproduce the bug?

This is an observed long-session instruction-following failure, not a deterministic compiler or client crash. A minimal independent reproduction has not been isolated.

The task sequence was:

1. Provide repository instructions and an explicit cleanup boundary: remove a superseded implementation; preserve content, shared interfaces and planned component support.
2. Ask the agent to fix the PR, keep documentation unambiguous, reply to review comments and resolve only addressed threads.
3. Supply corrections distinguishing necessary current-state documentation updates from changes to unapproved future proposals.
4. Continue the session through multiple repair and review rounds.
5. Inspect the complete diff after the agent reports that the PR is ready to merge.

In this incident, the diff still contained proposal rewrites outside the intended boundary, despite repeated corrections and positive readiness claims.

## What is the expected behavior?

- Preserve the user's exact scope and previously selected outcomes throughout a long session, including after context compaction.
- Treat review suggestions as findings to reconcile with the task, rather than automatic permission to broaden it.
- For a removal task, amend a proposal only where removing code makes a specific sentence false. Preserve its proposed designs, migration plans, alternatives, open questions and cited observations unless their alteration is explicitly authorized.
- Interpret a requirement for clear documentation as a writing constraint, not permission to redesign or rewrite every related document.
- Verify scope and preservation against the complete diff before recommending merge. Passing technical gates and resolving review threads cannot substitute for that check.
- Use the project's existing required validation pipeline without redundant expensive runs, particularly after the user explicitly requests that workflow.
- Respond to reported rework and usage costs with concrete, scoped corrective action and concise communication.

## Additional information

- Environment: Linux, Git worktrees, repository-level `AGENTS.md` instructions, GitHub PR review, and local pre-push gates.
- Model and reasoning setting, confirmed by the reporting user: **Sol 6.1 (`gpt-6.1-sol`), `xhigh` reasoning effort**. The exact client version was not provided.
- The project is private. Repository identifiers, PR links, source snippets, local paths, screenshots and the full conversation are intentionally omitted from this public report.
- The user explicitly requested that this behavior and its usage impact be reported to OpenAI through a GitHub issue. Please investigate the scope-preservation and readiness-reporting failure and the reported usage impact. This report does not establish a billing-calculation defect or a specific internal root cause.

issues.body:
### App version
Installed ChatGPT.app metadata: 26.1021.22027, build 21747.

### Subscription
Not collected.

### Platform
macOS 26.5, Apple Silicon (arm64). Local desktop chat using the Chrome extension through cua_repl.

### Problem
Browser operations worked earlier in an existing chat. After the user reported switching ChatGPT accounts, continuing browser work in that same chat returned:

```
Local browser use is disabled in Work settings
```

The user reports this happens repeatedly after account switches and describes it as very disruptive: they must start a fresh chat and transfer the task context to continue. This occurrence interrupted an already-reviewed and explicitly authorized action before anything was submitted to the external service.

### Reproduction sequence
1. Start a desktop chat with browser access and use Chrome through cua_repl successfully.
2. Switch the signed-in ChatGPT account while retaining the existing chat (account-switch step reported by the user, not independently observed by the agent).
3. Continue an authorized browser task in the existing chat.
4. A browser-operation call returns the disabled-Work-settings error.
5. The user requests a new ChatGPT chat/session as their workaround.

The failing call attempted to name the existing browser session, navigate to an already-known HTTPS application thread, and read accessibility state. No external write occurred.

### Expected behavior
After an account switch, the app should accurately re-evaluate the current account's browser availability and provide a supported way to reconnect or continue an existing chat when allowed. If the new account or workspace actually disallows access, the error should identify that cause clearly. This report does not request bypassing account boundaries or access policies.

### Evidence and limitations
- Successful browser reads earlier in the same chat and the later exact disabled error were observed directly.
- The account switch and repeated recurrence are user-reported.
- The Browser setting and policy state after the switch could not be independently inspected. The underlying cause is not established.
- A fresh ChatGPT chat has been created as requested; restoration of browser access there has not yet been verified.
- The in-app feedback route could not be automated because cua.getApp('Codex') returned: `Computer Use is not allowed to use the app 'com.openai.codex' for safety reasons.` The restriction was respected.

### Related reports
#54989 and #56542 describe a similar error on Windows. This report adds the macOS environment and an account-switch trigger reported by the user.

Observed October 23, 2026 (America/New_York). No account identifiers, private application URLs, email content, credentials, raw logs or session transcripts are attached.

labels.name: bug

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.825.41651 (build 7345)

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 26.6.2; `Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 arm`

### What issue are you seeing?

The desktop app exposes Chat, ChatGPT Work, and Codex as different ways of working, but several controls and summaries collapse all of their objects into the generic term **chat**.

Observed examples on this build:

- The sidebar action remains **New chat** while **Work** is selected, even though the resulting object is a Work task.
- The Codex view also says **New chat**, although it creates a Codex task with a different execution context.
- Custom sections say **Drop chats or projects here** even when they contain Work or Codex tasks.
- Activity summaries can describe usage across a number of **chats** even when the activity includes Work and Codex tasks.
- Sidebar rows do not persistently identify whether an item is a Chat conversation, Work task, or Codex task.

This makes pinning, organizing custom sections, and reopening older work unnecessarily ambiguous. The user has to infer the object type from its location or manually encode it in the title.

This issue is specifically about incorrect control-level terminology and missing item-type identification. It is narrower than requests to redesign the entire sidebar or separate the product modes.

Official OpenAI documentation currently distinguishes **Chat**, **ChatGPT Work**, and **Codex** as separate choices:

https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/use-chatgpt

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Open the ChatGPT desktop app on macOS.
2. Select **ChatGPT**, then select **Work** in the Chat/Work switcher.
3. Observe that the sidebar creation control still says **New chat**.
4. Switch the top-level product selector to **Codex**.
5. Observe that the creation control again says **New chat**, although it creates a Codex task.
6. Create or inspect a custom sidebar section and observe the instruction **Drop chats or projects here** for mixed Chat, Work, and Codex items.
7. Compare existing sidebar rows and observe that their originating item type is not persistently labeled.

### What is the expected behavior?

Use terminology that preserves the actual object type:

- **New chat** for an ordinary Chat conversation.
- **New Work task** for ChatGPT Work.
- **New Codex task** for Codex.
- Neutral collection wording such as **Drop conversations, tasks, or projects here** where different object types are accepted.
- Persistent Chat, Work, or Codex badges/icons on sidebar rows and headers.
- Activity summaries that either preserve the item types or use a genuinely neutral term such as **items**.

The terminology should make it possible to identify an item's type without opening it or manually modifying its title.

### Additional information

In-product feedback was submitted before this issue was filed.

Feedback ID: `01a05059-5756-7ef3-be56-9b492d17d106`

Related issues:

- #33079 requests persistent Work/Codex identification and filtering.
- #33475 concerns ambiguity in the active execution mode.
- #33716 proposes separate organization models for Work and Codex.
- #35367 requests broader separation of ChatGPT, Work, and Codex projects and conversations.

This report is distinct because it focuses on the incorrect generic **chat** microcopy used by creation controls, section instructions, activity summaries, and sidebar item labels.

Diagnostics: **NONE**  
Logs or traces: **NONE**  
Screenshots or attachments: **NONE**

macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), Apple Silicon (arm64)

### What issue are you seeing?

The macOS desktop app previously allowed a user to manually continue an existing Chat conversation in Work while preserving the conversation context. The action was available from an assistant message's menu through **Open in new branch → Transfer to Work** (wording may vary by locale).

The desktop app should retain the previously available manual Chat → Work action, allowing the user to decide when to continue an existing discussion as a Work task while preserving its context.

## Summary

In a Windows desktop session, browser-use tools repeatedly report that local browser use is disabled, even though the Browser setting is visibly enabled. The user reports that fully closing and reopening the desktop app usually restores access, and that this happens frequently.

## Observed behavior

The user provided a screenshot of Settings → Browser showing the enabled toggle. Repeated calls to `cua.getState()` in the affected session returned:

```json
{"apps":[],"browsers":[],"errors":["Browsers: Error: Local browser use is disabled in Work settings"]}
```

Browser access remained unavailable in this session after the user checked the setting. No browser state could be inspected, so this report does not establish whether the cause is stale settings, session state, or another issue.

## Steps observed

1. Use a local Windows desktop session with browser use enabled.
2. Request browser access for a task.
3. The tool reports `Local browser use is disabled in Work settings`.
4. Check Settings → Browser: the toggle is already enabled.
5. Retry the inventory call: the same disabled error is returned.

The precise trigger for entering the inconsistent state is unknown.

## Expected behavior

The tool should reflect the enabled setting and expose the connected browser, or provide a more specific explanation if another policy is preventing access.

## Workaround reported by the user

Fully closing and reopening the desktop app usually restores browser access. This workaround has been reported by the user from prior occurrences; the app has not yet been restarted during this reproduction.

## Environment

- Windows 10, build 19045, x64.
- Local desktop execution, not a remote container.
- Desktop app version: not available from the tools in this session.
- Observed on October 18, 2026.

releases.body:
## New Features

- Save reusable prompts and slash commands in ten numbered `/presets` slots, with a keyboard menu for quick access. (#54380, #54381)
- Set model, reasoning effort, speed, and permission profiles directly with inline `/model` and `/permissions` arguments. (#54378, #54383)
- Preview viewed and generated images in the fullscreen transcript on terminals supporting Kitty or Sixel graphics. (#54216)
- Authenticate enterprise MCP connections using eligible Codex account grants or dedicated sign-in, including OAuth clients requiring secrets. (#55334, #55859, #56001)
- Mask credentials during supported remote Bash commands and Zsh snapshot sessions, including credentials from custom providers. (#54309, #54432, #56049)
- The Amazon Bedrock setup wizard is now enabled by default, with API key entry grouped alongside other AWS sign-in methods when credentials are detected. (#56033, #56023)

## Bug Fixes

- Failed compaction no longer leaves partial summaries in conversation history, and background compaction failures fall back without panicking. (#53932, #55581)
- Resuming sessions now finds compressed histories and restores saved thread settings instead of replacing them with global defaults. (#54008, #55923)
- Windows HTTPS and WebSocket connections now handle proxy authentication challenges using the signed-in user’s Negotiate or NTLM credentials. (#55994, #56000)
- CLI configuration overrides are preserved when `-c` or `--config` appears at multiple subcommand levels. (#56022)
- Queued prompts now wait for pending permission selections to resolve before continuing. (#55682)
- Hardened sandbox checks for case-variant metadata paths on macOS and replaceable symlinks used to locate executables. (#54273, #55384)

## Chores

- Reduced disk usage by pruning unused installations, cleaning abandoned marketplace checkouts, and bounding daemon logs. (#53827, #55149, #55689, #55690, #55856)
- Updated the embedded JavaScript runtime with safety checks for optimized `Array.sort` operations. (#54519)
