issues.title: Remote MCP (OAuth): active session keeps resending an expired access token instead of refreshing or prompting sign-in

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

A Copilot CLI session connected to a remote OAuth-protected MCP server keeps sending the same expired access token after its first HTTP 401. The client makes no request to the token endpoint and does not prompt the user to sign in again. The rejected requests repeat about every four minutes for hours.

We run the MCP server at `https://api.plori.ai/mcp` and observed this from the server side:

- Session A (`copilot-cli/1.0.99-2`): the server rejected one bearer token (same fingerprint on every request) 581 times as expired, from 2026-10-19 00:56 UTC to 2026-10-21 06:50 UTC.
- Session B (`copilot-cli`): successful MCP pings until 2026-10-20 19:38 UTC, which is one hour after the token was issued (our access tokens live one hour). From 19:42 UTC the server rejected the same expired bearer 82 times, about four minutes apart, until 2026-10-21 05:55 UTC. Between 19:30 and 20:00 UTC our authorization server received no token-endpoint request.

Every rejection is HTTP 401 with:

```http
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token", resource_metadata="https://api.plori.ai/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp"
```

The authorization server advertises `grant_types_supported: ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"]` and issues rotating refresh tokens when `offline_access` is requested. The token response sizes we logged before each session match a response that contains a refresh token, so we believe the client held one. We cannot inspect the client's credential store, so this is an inference.

### Affected version

`copilot-cli/1.0.99-2` (session A). Session B's user agent was `copilot-cli` without a version.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Add a remote MCP server whose authorization server issues one-hour access tokens and rotating refresh tokens (`offline_access` advertised).
2. Sign in through the CLI's OAuth flow.
3. Keep the session open past the access token's expiry, with the server connected (background pings or subscriptions running).
4. Watch the server logs: requests continue with the expired bearer and receive 401 `invalid_token`; no `refresh_token` grant reaches the token endpoint.

### Expected behavior

On a 401 with `error="invalid_token"`, the client uses its refresh token (RFC 6749 §6), stores the rotated credentials, and retries with the new access token on the active transport. If refresh is not possible, the client tells the user that the server needs authentication again, instead of resending the rejected token.

### Additional context

This looks related to #4203, which describes an expired access token at session start forcing interactive sign-in instead of a refresh. Here the token expires during an active session, and the client neither refreshes nor asks for sign-in; it keeps retrying the same token. We are happy to provide more server-side detail (timestamps, request counts) if it helps.

— Plori AI team

issues.title: Trusted folders silently auto-approve shell execution in manual mode, even for commands with unpredictable side effects (scripts, sqlcmd, curl)

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In `manual` permission mode, any shell command whose referenced file paths all lie inside a trusted folder is executed without any permission prompt. Path-based gating cannot determine what a command will actually do.

Concretely: the agent ran
```
powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\someScript.ps1
```
from inside a trusted folder. The session event log contains no `permission.requested` event for this execution - it went straight from tool request to execution. 




### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.102.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Add a folder to `trustedFolders` in `~/.copilot/config.json` (or accept the trust prompt with the persistent option).
2. Start a session in that folder with permission mode `manual`.
3. Ask the agent to run any script in the folder, e.g. a `.ps1` that connects to a local database or the network.
4. Observe: the command executes immediately; `events.jsonl` contains a `tool.execution_start` but no `permission.requested` event.

### Expected behavior


In `manual` mode, shell command execution should require approval regardless of folder trust.

At minimum, provide a setting that decouples the two, e.g. `"trustedFolderAutoApprovesShell": false`, so users can keep folder trust while retaining per-command prompts.

However, neither pure path-based nor pure command-based gating is sufficient on its own. Suggested combination, evaluated in order:

1. A built-in read-only tier: provably side-effect-free commands (`git show`, `git log`, `Get-Content`, `ls`, ...) never prompt, regardless of path or folder.
2. Per-folder command-pattern rules: `(folder, command-pattern) -> allow | ask | deny`, persisted via the existing per-folder structure of `permissions-config.json` and populated through the familiar "allow always (for this folder) / allow for session / deny" prompt choices.
3. Unclassifiable executions default to ask: invoking scripts or interpreters (`powershell -File *.ps1`, `cmd /c`, `bash`, `python`), database clients (`sqlcmd`, `psql`), service control (`systemctl`, `Stop-Service`), and network tools (`curl`, `Invoke-WebRequest` to URLs outside allowedUrls) always prompt unless explicitly allowlisted for that folder — their effect cannot be predicted from the command line.

Prior art: Claude Code uses per-command-pattern allow/ask/deny rules (folder trust does not grant execution); Codex CLI pairs auto-approval with OS-level sandboxing (network off, writes confined to the workspace) so unpredicted effects fail instead of succeeding silently; JetBrains Junie and VS Code agent mode prompt per terminal command with allowlists. Copilot CLI's "trusted folder implies unprompted shell" is the outlier among these.



### Additional context

**Environment**

- Copilot CLI 1.0.83 through 1.0.101 (long-lived session, behavior identical across versions)
- Windows, PowerShell tool
- permissionMode: `manual`, agentMode: `interactive`
- No entries for the folder in `permissions-config.json`; no `/allow-all`; no launch flags

issues.title: web_fetch fails DNS validation in proxy-only environments despite working native HTTP transport (1.0.102)

labels.name: area:networking
labels.description: Proxy, SSL/TLS, certificates, corporate environments, and connectivity issues

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

The built-in `web_fetch` tool fails for public HTTPS URLs in a corporate proxy-only environment where local DNS does not resolve public destination hostnames. The configured HTTP CONNECT proxy can resolve and fetch those destinations successfully.

Both `curl` and the same installed Copilot CLI native HTTP transport can retrieve the page through the existing proxy without local destination DNS resolution.

### Environment

- GitHub Copilot CLI: **1.0.102**
- OS: Linux on WSL2 / Windows
- Installation: npm (`@github/copilot`)
- System Node.js: **v24.18.0**
- Corporate HTTP CONNECT proxy: Zscaler
- `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, and lowercase equivalents are configured and inherited.
- `no_proxy` does not exclude the tested public destinations.
- `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` points to the trusted system CA bundle.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use an environment where public Internet access works through an HTTP CONNECT proxy, but local DNS returns `NXDOMAIN` for public destination hostnames.
2. Configure `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, and required CA trust.
3. Ask Copilot CLI to fetch `https://docs.github.com/` or `https://example.com/` using built-in `web_fetch`.
4. Compare with the following request from the same environment:

```bash
curl --fail --silent --show-error --location \
  --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 30 \
  -o /dev/null -w 'HTTP %{http_code}; TLS verify %{ssl_verify_result}\n' \
  https://docs.github.com/
```

### Actual behavior

Both tested destinations fail in `web_fetch` with:

```text
WebFetchBlockedUrlError: failed to lookup address information: Name or service not known
```

### Diagnostic evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Built-in `web_fetch` for GitHub Docs and example.com | DNS lookup error above |
| `curl` through configured proxy | HTTP 200; TLS verification result 0 |
| Local DNS lookup in WSL | Fails; A query returns NXDOMAIN |
| Windows `Resolve-DnsName docs.github.com` | DNS_ERROR_RCODE_NAME_ERROR |
| Direct query to configured corporate DNS | Authoritative NXDOMAIN for docs.github.com A |
| Installed CLI native HTTP transport through same proxy | HTTP 200, final URL https://docs.github.com/en |

For the last comparison, I loaded `runtime.node` from the installed CLI 1.0.102 package and invoked `networkFetchStreamStart` with a GET request, `redirect: "follow"`, `pinnedAddresses: []`, and `allowLocalhost: false`. The proxy environment was unchanged. This was a diagnostic transport probe, not a proposed replacement for URL validation.

This isolates the observed failure to local destination resolution in the built-in tool's validation path, rather than missing proxy variables, TLS trust, or a WSL-only DNS problem. The precise internal validation implementation has not been verified from source.

### Expected behavior

Please provide a supported, security-preserving way for `web_fetch` to work when the configured proxy handles destination DNS and local public-name resolution is unavailable.

If local destination DNS is an intentional prerequisite, please document that limitation and return an actionable error distinguishing it from proxy connectivity or TLS problems.

This is not a request to disable SSRF protection, allow private/loopback/metadata destinations, or bypass corporate network policy. Any solution needs appropriate destination and redirect validation.

### Related issues

- #5180: related conflict between local address validation and proxy-managed DNS, but concerns Fake-IP addresses rather than unavailable resolution / NXDOMAIN.
- #3948: previous proxy failures were marked resolved as of 1.0.88; this failure reproduces on 1.0.102.
- #4019: previous built-in web_fetch proxy support report.

### Workaround

Use shell `curl` through the configured proxy. No system DNS settings, CLI package files, TLS verification settings, or URL-safety checks were modified during investigation.

issues.title: TUI: a user-scrolled chat viewport shifts on every append (overflow-anchor forced to none)
issues.body:
**What happens**

Scroll up in the chat so you're reading something, then let the agent keep working. The text under your view marches upward — you have to chase it back down. It happens on every append, so with a streaming agent it's effectively impossible to read anything that was produced more than a few seconds ago.

This is *not* the auto-follow-to-bottom behaviour: that is correctly disengaged. The problem is that a user-scrolled viewport is anchored to the *bottom* of the scrollable content rather than to the content you're looking at.

**Why**

The chat message view builds its scroll hook with anchoring forced off:

```js
const Sn = e$e({ working: () => !0, overflowAnchor: "none" });
```

and the hook's setter takes that literally and returns early, so the dynamic branch is never reached for the chat:

```js
w = x => {
  const k = <overflowAnchor option>;
  if (k === "none") { x.style.overflowAnchor = "none"; return }   // ← taken
  if (k === "auto") { x.style.overflowAnchor = "auto"; return }
  x.style.overflowAnchor = o.userScrolled ? "auto" : "none"       // ← dead for the chat
}
```

With `overflow-anchor: none` the scroll container preserves `scrollTop` absolutely, so appending to the transcript shifts the visible content up by the height of each appended block.

Secondary, but related: `userScrolled` (which gates the auto-jump to the bottom) is only ever set from a `wheel` listener with `deltaY < 0`:

```js
y = x => { if (x.deltaY >= 0) return; ... p() }      // only wired to "wheel"
p = () => { ... o.userScrolled || (a("userScrolled", true), e.onUserInteracted?.()) }
```

There is no `scroll` listener on the container, so the `messages_page_up` / `messages_half_page_up` / `messages_line_up` actions never set it. That's a separate issue, but it's moot for the symptom above, because that view can never anchor at all.

**Environment**

- opencode 1.18.35
- kitty + zellij, Wayland
- Checked 1.19.4's release notes: no scroll/follow/viewport fix mentioned.

**What I verified locally**

The literal `overflowAnchor:"none"` occurs exactly once in the shipped binary, and `"none"` → `"auto"` is the same byte length, so I applied it as a 4-byte, single-site patch (no other byte changes; file size identical) to confirm the diagnosis rather than assume it. Result worth recording: **it substantially improves things but doesn't fully fix it.** Before, the view shifted every few seconds; after, it only shifts on very large appends (a big tool result landing at once). So browser scroll anchoring alone isn't sufficient here — which is the actionable part below.

**Suggested fix**

1. Stop forcing `overflowAnchor: "none"` for the chat: pass `"auto"`, or omit the option and let the dynamic `userScrolled` branch apply.
2. For large appends, don't rely on CSS anchoring alone. Measure `scrollHeight` before and after the append and compensate `scrollTop` by the delta when the user is not at the bottom. That is robust for a single very large block, where anchoring can fail (the anchor node itself may be replaced or re-keyed by the list render).

I'm not submitting a PR since I only have the minified bundle, but the call site is unique, so it should be easy to find in source: the `e$e({ working, overflowAnchor: "none" })` construction in the session/message view (the same object that calls `Sn.resume()` on session change), plus the `overflow-anchor` setter in the scroll hook.

issues.title: migration: sessions created via 1.19 /api/session lose all messages on v1->v2 migration (2.1.3)
issues.body:
## Description

Upgrading a 1.19.x database to 2.1.3 keeps every session created through 1.19's `/api/session` endpoint (the "next" session store, rows in `session_message`) but drops all of its messages. The session row survives; `GET /api/session/{id}/message` then returns `200` with an empty page — no error, no log line. Sessions created through the legacy routes (rows in `message`/`part`) migrate correctly.

Related but different from #58041 (that one covers v1 sessions created *after* the migration, which become malformed stubs and 500). Here the sessions existed before the migration, were already in the 1.19 `session_message` format, and come back empty.

## Measured (copy of a real 1.19.3 database, 832 sessions)

| | before (1.19.3) | after starting 2.1.3 on the copy |
|---|---|---|
| `session_message` rows / distinct sessions | 12,717 / 308 | 12,184 / 503 |
| legacy `message` rows / sessions | 11,737 / 502 | 11,741 / 503 |

Per session, via `GET /api/session/{id}/message` on 2.1.3:

- legacy-store sessions: 22 → 23, 18 → 19, 28 → 29, 2 → 2 messages (all present)
- 1.19 `session_message` sessions: 32 → **0**, 167 → **0**, 111 → **0**, 2 → **0**

`GET /api/experimental/migration/v1` reports `completed`; the server log shows only the schema migrations and no errors.

So the bulk migration appears to rebuild `session_message` from the legacy tables and discard the rows 1.19 had already written there for its own `/api/session` sessions.

## Steps to reproduce

1. With `opencode-ai@1.19.3`, `opencode serve`, then create a session with `POST /api/session` and send a couple of prompts with `POST /api/session/{id}/prompt`. Confirm `GET /api/session/{id}/message` returns them.
2. Stop the server. Copy the data dir.
3. Start `@opencode/cli@2.1.3` (`opencode serve`) on that data dir and wait for `/api/experimental/migration/v1` → `completed`.
4. `GET /api/session/{id}/message` for the session from step 1 → empty.

## Expected

Sessions already stored in the 1.19 `session_message` format keep their messages through the migration (they need no translation).

## Environment

- From: `opencode-ai` 1.19.3 (linux-x64), server mode
- To: `@opencode/cli` 2.1.3 (linux-x64, npm), `opencode serve`
- Provider: `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` custom provider

### Description On OpenCode Desktop, cold-boot project-copy refreshes can block session loading for minutes when the file watcher is enabled. With OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_DISABLE_FILEWATCHER=true, refreshes drop to ≤2.1 s and failed to subscribe errors go to zero. On my rotational disk this also amplifies a large-DB problem (separate issue: ). Environment Same as Issue 1: Linux Mint 22.3, kernel 7.0.0, ext4 on a rotational HGST 8 GiB RAM, OpenCode Desktop 1.19.0, SQLite 3.45.1/WAL.

Evidence

Metric | Cold reference | Plugin off | Watcher off -- | -- | -- | -- session-open refresh | 94.7 s | 0.7 s | 0.44–2.4 s subscribe errors | 4 | 4 | 0

M0 measurement (2026-10-19, three cold boots, 1 Hz /proc/diskstats + PSI):

  • Pathological refreshes: 203.0 s and 54.1 s on two workspaces, with 571–733 MB reads, await ≤813 ms, sda4 util ≤91%.
  • Watcher-off: all projects ≤2.1 s, 2.9 MB, zero failed to subscribe errors.

Log lines:

timestamp=... level=INFO message="project copy refresh started" projectID=...
timestamp=... level=INFO message="project copy refresh done" projectID=... updated=[] removed=[]
timestamp=... level=ERROR message="failed to subscribe" ...

Post-shrink note: after reducing the DB event table (Issue 1), watcher-on refreshes were 0.5–4.0 s and the 54–203 s stalls did not reproduce, so the DB bloat was a confound in later observations. The watcher-off A/B on 2026-10-19 remains valid.

Workaround

OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_DISABLE_FILEWATCHER=true on the launch path. The host already exports this automatically on WSL; the flag is supported by my build (verified against app.asar).

Requests

  1. Defer/serialize project-copy refreshes on session open; avoid git worktree list on every refresh.
  2. Honor a stable watcher setting and auto-disable on slow/rotational storage (not only WSL).
  3. Log refresh durations; add a guard so a refresh cannot block the session list.

issues.title: Desktop session loading freezes when the host event table grows unbounded (2.94 GB observed)
issues.body:
### Description


OpenCode Desktop freezes on session load when the host event table grows without bound. On my DB, 3.47 GB total / 2.94 GB (85%) was event (174,758 rows). The server uses better-sqlite3 synchronously; the session list took 4.2 s and two launches hung after booting location services. Offline .backup + DELETE FROM event + VACUUM reduced the DB to 519 MB, the list query to 3 ms, and three consecutive cold boots were clean.

Environment
OpenCode Desktop 1.19.0 (session records report version=1.19.0; app installed 2026-10-22), Linux Mint 22.3, kernel 7.0.0-38-generic, x86_64, 4 cores, 8 GiB RAM.
/dev/sda4 ext4 on a rotational HGST  (ROTA=1); SQLite 3.45.1, WAL, 4096-byte pages.
DB: ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode-desktop.db; 265 sessions.
Evidence
2026-10-22: DB 3.47 GB (848,540 pages, freelist 0); dbstat: event 2.94 GB, part 316 MB, message 179 MB; 174,758 events.
Session-list query: 4.2 s on 265 sessions.
Launches at 09:20:39 and 09:27:58 hung for 2–3 minutes after booting location services, with no plugin initPlugin line; 09:36:28 was usable after ~45 s.
Offline on a copy: .backup + PRAGMA quick_check + DELETE FROM event + VACUUM → 3.77 GB → 519.4 MB; 190,718 events deleted; 265 sessions / 17,804 messages / 79,181 parts intact; quick_check=ok.
After the shrink: list query 3 ms; three consecutive cold boots clean (0 subscribe errors, refresh 0.8–4.0 s); no freeze.
The table regrew to 2,767 rows within ~90 minutes of normal use.
Schema
CREATE TABLE `event` (
  `id` text PRIMARY KEY,
  `aggregate_id` text NOT NULL,
  `seq` integer NOT NULL,
  `type` text NOT NULL,
  `data` text NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY (`aggregate_id`) REFERENCES `event_sequence`(`aggregate_id`)
    ON DELETE CASCADE
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX `event_aggregate_seq_idx` ON `event` (`aggregate_id`, `seq`);
CREATE INDEX `event_aggregate_type_seq_idx` ON `event` (`aggregate_id`, `type`, `seq`);
The shipped app.asar contains this schema but no DELETE FROM event and no retention path. Rows are per-session append-only streams; the top aggregate IDs had 42,482 / 33,906 / 21,305 / 17,104 rows.

Reproduction / inspection
SELECT name, SUM(pgsize) AS bytes
FROM dbstat GROUP BY name ORDER BY bytes DESC LIMIT 10;

SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT aggregate_id) FROM event;

SELECT aggregate_id, count(*) AS c FROM event GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY c DESC LIMIT 5;
Then close the app, copy the DB, delete the event rows on the copy, VACUUM, and compare session-list latency.

Additional finding
The existing maintenance aborted 3× at 4.2–5.2 GB with backup quick_check failed (2026-10-14 and 2026-10-15), so no prune/VACUUM ever ran.

Requests
Add retention/compaction for event (prune completed sessions or enforce a max age/size; run in maintenance; compact safely).
Move heavy SQLite work off the server event loop / avoid synchronous checks on the boot path; add a large-DB guard.
Fix the maintenance backup quick_check failed abort.
Privacy
Paths/session IDs redacted. I can provide sanitized logs or a minimal synthetic DB, not the full private DB.

issues.title: npm 12 upgrade leaves the Windows executable stub
issues.body:
### Description

`opencode upgrade` can report success with npm 12 while leaving the published text stub in `bin/opencode.exe`. The next invocation fails on Windows because the file is not a valid executable.

The updater runs `npm install --global --force` without allowing the target package's lifecycle scripts. npm 12 can block postinstall and still exit 0, even with `ignore-scripts=false`. Adding `--allow-scripts=@opencode/cli` lets postinstall replace the stub.

I reproduced that policy behavior with a synthetic package in an isolated Windows install prefix using npm 12.0.2 and Node 24.21.0. The flag also preserved explicit `ignore-scripts=true`. This report covers the updater command; #48884 covers the broader packaging behavior when scripts are disabled.

### OpenCode version

Reported on the upgrade from 2.0.16 to 2.0.18.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start with a working npm installation of OpenCode 2.0.16 and npm 12.0.2, with `ignore-scripts=false` and no script approval for `@opencode/cli`.
2. Run `opencode upgrade 2.0.18` using the npm method.
3. Run `opencode --version`.

The upgrade reports success, but Windows rejects `bin/opencode.exe`. Running the installed package's `postinstall.mjs` manually repairs it.

### Operating System

Windows

issues.title: app: background shell stays "running" after exit; cannot dismiss and survives restart
issues.body:
## Summary

A background shell that has already exited keeps showing as `1 running` in the session header. The badge cannot be dismissed with `×`, and it survives an app restart. Runtime state shows no active shell at all, so this looks like a persisted status that is never finalized.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.1.4 (`opencode` CLI is not on PATH in this install)
- OS: Windows_NT 10.0.19045 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: desktop app (no TERM/TERM_PROGRAM set)
- Shell: C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: @tarquinen/opencode-dcp@latest

## Reproduction

1. In a session, start a background shell that writes output to a file and exits normally, e.g.:
   `cmd /c "py C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\<script>.py > out.txt 2>&1"` with `background: true`.
2. Wait until the script finishes (the output file is fully written, process is gone).
3. Look at the session header: it still shows `1 running`, tooltip `Shell  cmd /c "py C:\Users\..."` (command truncated).
4. Click `×` on the running task: nothing happens.
5. Quit and restart opencode, reopen the session: `1 running` is still displayed.

## Expected Behavior

- The running indicator should clear as soon as the background shell exits, even if the notification/output was not consumed.
- `×` should remove the task entry from the session.
- Restarting the app should not resurrect a task that has no live process.

## Actual Behavior

- The badge stays at `1 running` indefinitely (observed for more than a day across app restarts).
- `×` does not dismiss it.
- The runtime reports no active sessions: calling `shell.list_sessions` returns `"No active sessions"`.
- No related process exists on the machine: `tasklist` shows no `python.exe` / `mvn`; `netstat` shows nothing listening on the port used earlier (8086). The only `java.exe` is IntelliJ's `RemoteMavenServer36`, unrelated.
- The shell's output file is complete, so the process did exit normally.

## Additional Context

- The session had run several background tasks earlier (maven builds, a temporary server, python scripts). All of them exited or were killed; the badge nevertheless shows a single stuck `1 running` entry, always pointing at the same `cmd /c "py C:\Users\..."` command.
- Because restarting does not clear it, the state appears to be persisted (e.g. in `opencode.db` / `storage`) and re-read on load, rather than kept only in memory.
- Workarounds that did not help: clicking `×`, restarting the app.
- Not attempted: deleting the session, manually editing the persisted state.

issues.title: desktop: session pane renders blank after switching tabs until the tab is re-entered
issues.body:
## Summary

On OpenCode Desktop (v2.1.3, Windows 11), switching between tabs sometimes leaves the whole chat pane blank — no header, no transcript, no composer — and it stays blank indefinitely. Switching to another tab and back renders the session correctly with all messages intact. The session data is fine; this looks like a client-side mount/render failure in the pane.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.1.3 (desktop release). Bundled CLI reports `opencode v2.1.3`; `GET /api/info` returns `{"version":"2.1.3"}`. The updater had 2.1.4 downloaded and pending restart (`main.log`: `updater state changed { from: 'downloading', to: 'ready' }`).
- OS: Windows 11 Pro, build 26200, x64
- Terminal: Desktop app (Electron) — no terminal involved
- Shell: `%ComSpec%` = `C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe`; agent shell configured to PowerShell 7.6.6
- Install/channel: release desktop build under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\@opencodedesktop` (Electron, `app.asar` ≈178 MB)
- Active plugins: global plugin `~/.config/opencode/plugins/mnemon-summarizer.js`; MCP servers `windows-mcp` (local) and `rea` (local). No entries in the config `plugins` array.

## Reproduction

1. Open OpenCode Desktop with several tabs (I had 8: 6 session tabs, 1 file-preview tab, plus the active session; some sessions are 40k–80k tokens).
2. Switch tabs with `Ctrl+Tab` or by clicking a tab.
3. Sometimes the whole pane below the tab bar is white.

Not deterministic — roughly 3 of ~10 switches in one sitting. Once blank it stays blank: waiting 6+ seconds changes nothing, no spinner, no error UI.

4. Switch to any other tab, then back (`Ctrl+Tab`, then `Ctrl+Shift+Tab`).
5. The pane renders immediately and correctly, with the full transcript.

## Expected Behavior

Switching to a tab always renders that session's pane: header, transcript, composer. At minimum, show a loading state or an error instead of an empty white pane.

## Actual Behavior

The pane is entirely empty — session header, message list and composer are all missing; only the tab bar and window chrome remain painted. Nothing is logged when it happens: `renderer.log`'s last write was 3+ minutes before the failing switches, and its only entries are 329 `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications.` warnings plus one font-fallback message. No exception, no error boundary.

The data is intact: `GET /api/session/{id}/message?limit=80` returns the messages for the session that appeared blank, and re-entering the tab shows them all.

## Additional Context

- The same blank state also happened on a **non-session (file preview) tab** ("字幕相关"): blank, then recovered after switching away and back. That points at the shared pane/container rather than at session message loading.
- Timing: app started 2026-10-24 02:11, machine slept and resumed around 10:07; blanks were observed between 10:08 and 10:17.
- GPU/display: Intel Arc B580 + Intel iGPU, plus three virtual display adapters installed (Oray IDD, ToDesk, GameViewer). Hardware acceleration is on. A compositing/raster problem on this setup cannot be ruled out.
- Possibly related: #22323 (web/desktop renders no messages when the newest 80-message page is assistant-only). While checking the API I did find a session whose newest-80 page contains 0 user messages (0 user / 78 assistant), which matches that issue's trigger. In this repro, though, the pane recovered on re-mount and the affected session does contain user messages, so I believe this is a different (mount/render) failure.
- Workaround that works: switch to another tab and back. Reloading the window (`Ctrl+R`) or restarting the app should also clear it.
- Frequency: intermittent, several times per hour of tab switching.

### What

When writing a prompt, pressing newline at the end of a list item should continue the list.

`1. first item` + newline gives `2. `, `- item` + newline gives `- `, and newline on an empty item ends the list.

### Why

This is standard behavior in any text editor, GitHub comment box, and in Claude Code. Prompts often contain short numbered lists, and retyping every marker is unnecessary friction.

### Current behavior

OpenCode 1.19.3, macOS, TUI. After `1. first item` and a newline (`ctrl+j` or `shift+enter`), the new line is empty.

### Expected behavior

Same as a normal markdown editor: numbered lists increment, bullets repeat, empty item exits the list, indentation is preserved.

issues.title: Delegated subagent write silently denied on "ask" permission (works on v1, broken on v2)
issues.body:
### Description

## Description

A primary agent delegating a write to a subagent whose permission for that path is set to `ask` silently fails on OpenCode 2.0 — no prompt is shown anywhere (checked both the main session view and any secondary/subagent view in Desktop), and no approval occurs. The subagent simply reports it cannot write, with no further detail. On OpenCode 1.x, the identical config and identical delegated write succeeds with no prompt shown either — but the write actually lands.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a subagent with `edit` permission set to `ask` for a specific path (e.g. `"**/findings/**": "ask"`).
2. From the primary agent, delegate a write to that subagent, targeting a file under that path, using explicit delegation syntax (`@subagent-name — create a file at <path> containing <content>`).
3. Observe the result.

## Expected behavior

Either:
- The subagent's write succeeds (matching v1's observed behavior for the same config), or
- A permission prompt is shown somewhere in the session (main view or subagent view) that the user can approve, per the `ask` effect.

## Actual behavior

- On OpenCode 2.0 (CLI and Desktop, same config, same box): the delegated write is denied. No prompt appears in the main session view or any subagent-specific view in Desktop. The subagent reports it cannot obtain write approval.
- On OpenCode 1.x (same machine, same opencode.json, same permission rule): the identical delegated write succeeds silently — no prompt shown, but the write lands correctly.
- A write to the same path made directly by the primary agent (no delegation) succeeds silently with no prompt on v2.
- Tested three times across different, never-before-written file paths under the same `ask`-gated directory, to rule out a stale per-path approval. All three delegated attempts were denied identically; all three primary-agent direct writes succeeded identically.

## Environment

- CLI v2: 2.0.32
- CLI v1: 1.19.3
- Desktop: 2.0.32 (matches CLI exactly on this box — no version skew)
- OS: Windows 11
- Relevant permission config:
```json
  { "action": "edit", "resource": "**/findings/**", "effect": "ask" }
```

## Additional notes

This may be related to #4078 (subagent permission prompts not surfaced in the primary agent's view) — but in this case no prompt is generated at all, in any view, rather than being generated and simply hidden. It's also possibly related to the documented behavior of headless OpenCode auto-rejecting unattended permission asks — if that default now also applies to subagent sessions spawned from an interactive Desktop/CLI session, that would explain this, but that hasn't been confirmed from source.

Net effect: any `ask`-gated permission rule intended to gate a subagent's delegated writes is currently non-functional on v2 — it neither prompts nor silently allows, it just fails the write unconditionally.

prs.title: fix(core): skip no-op Azure model transform updates
prs.body:
## What it does

Stops the Azure model transform from deep-cloning and rewriting every Azure catalog model on each model state rebuild when no Azure resource is configured or when a model's `baseURL` has no resource placeholder.

## How it works

1. Skip the per-model loop when `resourceFor(item.provider)` is unset.
2. Read `item.models.values()` instead of `models.list(item.provider.id)` (which eagerly clones every model in the provider via `draft()`), and call `models.update` only when `expandResourceName` changes `model.settings.baseURL`.
3. Inside `models.update`, recompute the expanded `baseURL` from `draft.settings` so any earlier transform edits are preserved.

## Risk

Server/core model catalog transform for Azure. Azure models added via provider `models.set`/`add` with legacy settings are no longer re-normalized on this no-op path, matching every other provider. Configured Azure resources and deployment narrowing still run through the same expansion and update path.

## Proof

- Per-rebuild Azure model clones drop from `95 → 0` without a resource and `95 → 21` with a resource; full catalog `models.reload() + models.all()` drops from `2.84 ms → 2.00 ms`.
- `bun run script/test.ts test/plugin/provider-azure.test.ts` (22 pass)
- `bun typecheck` in `packages/core` (0 errors)

prs.title: fix(ai): tolerate unknown events and statuses in image protocols
prs.body:
I added a rule to `packages/ai/AGENTS.md` and applied it to the image protocols:

> **Tolerate unknowns.** Unknown provider events, statuses, and enum values must not fail a request: ignore them, or map them to an `unknown` value that keeps the raw data. Fail only on error-shaped frames, malformed known types, a missing terminal event, or when ignoring would silently drop output from an otherwise successful result.

## Problem

- OpenAI Images streaming decoded frames against a closed union, so any new stream event type failed the whole request with "OpenAI Images sent an invalid stream event".
- The shared queued-status helper failed the job on any status string it didn't know. A provider adding a new in-progress status would break every poll.
- Google Images reported a safety block with no image as `InvalidProviderOutput` instead of `ContentPolicy`.

## Change

| Where | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `openai-images` stream | unknown event type fails | ignored; `error` frames still classify, malformed known types still fail, no completed image still fails as incomplete-stream |
| unknown frame that looks like an error | n/a | decodes as the protocol's `error` event, so it fails with a classified reason instead of being ignored |
| `MediaProtocol.status` (shared) | unknown status fails | treated as `running`; polling continues and `poll.timeout` still bounds it |
| `bfl-images` | `No Card Generated` unmapped | mapped to `failed` (it's in BFL's documented status enum and is terminal) |
| `google-images` | no image + `promptFeedback.blockReason` or a policy finish reason → `InvalidProviderOutput` | → `ContentPolicy`, same diagnostic message and body. Other empty responses (e.g. `NO_IMAGE`) stay `InvalidProviderOutput` |

The unknown-type handling now lives in one place, next to `withUntypedFrames`:

```diff
 protocols/shared.ts
+  withUnknownTypes(event, known)
+    type in known                          -> event schema (malformed still fails)
+    has `error`, or type ends in error/failed -> decoded as { ...frame, type: "error" }
+    anything else                          -> { type: "unknown", rawType }
 openai-images.ts        + uses it
 openai-transcription.ts - local UnknownEvent  + uses it
 cohere-chat.ts          - local UnknownEvent  + uses it
 google-interactions.ts  - local UnknownDelta  + uses it
```

`google-interactions` keeps its own top-level `event_type` variant since that one is keyed on a different field.

The status helper is shared with the video and transcription queued routes (xAI video, Runway, fal, AssemblyAI). I checked each provider's documented status list and every terminal failure status is already mapped, and their result decoders treat a non-terminal status as "not finished yet", so an unknown status there now keeps polling instead of failing. `MediaProtocol.status` is now synchronous, so the callers lost a `yield*` and the unused `Output` type is gone. The video test that asserted an unknown status fails now asserts it resumes as `running`.

I checked the inline image routes (meta, xai, zai, alibaba, stability, cloudflare, fal results) and they already decode statuses, formats, finish reasons and filter levels as open strings, so nothing changed there.

## Out of scope

- `openai-speech` stream events are a closed union with no error variant.
- `openai-chat` fails on an unknown `finish_reason`.
- `google-interactions` ignores an unknown top-level `event_type` even when it carries an `error`.

prs.title: feat(core): add goal round driver and goal verification
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Part of the goal/todo series. **Stacked on #55744** (the endpoints) and #54799 (the durable contracts) — review those first.

### Type of change

- [x] New feature
- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Adds the goal round driver, the independent verification round, and the model-facing tools.

**No new loop.** A round is one synthetic inbox row plus one `SessionExecution.wake`. The only place a round is scheduled is the `session.execution.succeeded` subscription, and it re-checks before scheduling: the process-local arm, the durable phase, the verifier's verdict, the todo gate, `rounds < maxGoalRounds`, and no human item waiting. The upper bound is `maxGoalRounds` (default 8).

**The verifier is a second, independent LLM request** — the shape of `SessionTitle.generate`: no conversation history, its own prompt entry, its own `UsageRecorded{source:"goal-verify"}`. Its input is only three kinds of evidence: the session's file diff, the results of finished tool calls (exit code and output), and the todo rows' `acceptance` text. The assistant's prose never enters. The output is decoded from one `llm.stream`; anything that does not decode is `incomplete` (fail-closed).

**`completed` is the verifier's alone.** The model's todo tool cannot write `completed`, and the gate is in code: `todo.every(s => s === "completed" || s === "cancelled")`.

**The model cannot resume.** The goal tool's `action` set is `set|edit|pause|clear` — `resume` is not constructible.

**Fail-closed disarm list**: execution failure, shutdown interruption, a verifier throw, session move/fork, compaction failure. `armed` is process-local and never persisted, so a restart is always disarmed.

### Notes

- `SessionGoalVerify` is a global node with `verify(sessionID, context)` parameter injection — putting `SessionContext.node` in its requirements makes `Instance.Services` self-referential.
- The human-yield check uses `Session.inbox()` rather than `nextPromotable`, because `nextPromotable` only returns the head and would miss a user row queued behind a steer.
- Known limits: the verifier can be fooled by a model that edits tests or the diff; `armed` is process-local.
- If the loop should be reviewed on its own, this splits cleanly into the verifier + tools and the driver + disarm list.

prs.title: fix(core): serve the app timeline without read-tool image payloads
prs.body:
## What it does

Opening a session where the agent read images downloads every image's base64 in the message list, even though the desktop/web read card never uses those bytes: it loads the image from disk by path. On a slower link, that download is most of the time it takes to open the session. This PR serves the app's timeline from a new experimental route that leaves those bytes out.

This is step 1 of a plan for timeline images. Serving pasted images by URL comes next. It complements #58427 and #58560, which drop the same bytes in the app after they've been downloaded. This one stops them from being sent in the first place.

## How it works

1. New route `GET /api/experimental/session/:sessionID/timeline` (`experimental.session.timeline`, SDK `client.experimental.session.timeline`). It takes the same params and returns the same `SessionMessagesResponse` as `session.message.list`, through the same handler.
2. On that route only, the store removes `data:` files from completed or errored `read` tool results after decoding each message. If nothing else is left, the result gets the read tool's usual "Image read successfully" text. Execute and MCP images stay inline.
3. The app's timeline store calls the new route for message pages. Everything else keeps the stable routes: single-message reads, Revert, Fork, exports and model context.

The stable `GET /api/session/:sessionID/message` route is unchanged, and its OpenAPI entry is byte-identical. `client.message` still only has `list`.

## Risk

Low. The change only affects the desktop/web timeline. If a client rendered read images from `state.content` instead of by path, those images would disappear from the timeline. The read card in `session-ui` loads by path, so nothing changes on screen. Other clients (TUI, iOS, the SDK's `message.list`) never call the new route.

## Proof

Opening an image-heavy session (11 image reads, 2 pasted images). Production app build in headless Chromium on a Mac, against the real server, with a proxy that models the link. Medians of 7 runs.

| Link | | First page | Newest message painted | Scroll settled |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50 ms / 50 Mbit | before | 5.91 MB | 1336 ms | 1426 ms |
| 50 ms / 50 Mbit | after | 1.85 MB | 685 ms | 721 ms |
| localhost, cold server | before | 5.91 MB | 789 ms | 789 ms |
| localhost, cold server | after | 1.85 MB | 645 ms | 760 ms |

At 50 Mbit the runs don't overlap: 1274–1439 ms before, 567–762 ms after. Most of the remaining 1.85 MB is the two pasted images (1.79 MB), which this PR leaves alone.

The first page has 4 inline read-image payloads before and 0 after. In the same session, the read card on that page loads its image from disk in both builds, at full size (3092 px wide).

- `bun test test/promise.test.ts` (client): 40 pass
- `bun test test/message.test.ts test/persistent-pty.test.ts test/fetch.test.ts` (server): 19 pass. The stable list keeps read and execute media. The timeline drops read `data:` files, including the image-only fallback text, keeps execute media, and pages the same way.
- `bun test --conditions=solid … src/runtime/server/data.test.ts api.test.ts image.test.ts` (app): 49 pass
- `bun test test/solid-data.test.ts test/solid-refresh.test.ts` (client timeline store): 36 pass

prs.title: fix(core): drop bare remote names from branch lists and search remote branches
prs.body:
## What it does

Branch lists (the desktop new-session branch picker) showed bare remote names such as `origin` next to real branches. Searching also never found remote branches.

## How it works

- `VcsGit.branches` formats refs with `%(refname:lstrip=2)` instead of `%(refname:short)`. Git shortened `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` to `origin`, which slipped past the `/HEAD` filter; now it comes through as `origin/HEAD` and is dropped. The default-branch lookup uses the same format, so a tag that shares a branch's name can't turn it into `heads/<name>`.
- Search and limit now apply after that filter. `--count` ran before it, so the list could come up short. The `refs/remotes/*query*` globs couldn't cross `/`, so remote branches never matched a search; search is now a case-insensitive substring match on the shown name.

## Risk

Low. Branch listing now reads every ref and trims in process. The `committerdate` sort already reads every ref, so the cost barely changes.

## Proof

New `vcs.test.ts` case on a real repo with two remotes whose HEAD symrefs are set (plus a tag named `main`): lists `main, fork/main, origin/main`, respects the limit, and finds remote branches by search. `vcs.test.ts` passes; core typechecks.

prs.title: refactor(desktop): fork the legacy store import off the first window's path
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #54296

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The first window is shown as soon as Electron is ready (`windows/early.ts`), and the main bundle and the Effect layers are built on the same thread afterwards. The legacy store import reads and decodes the whole userData directory inside that build, holding the layers — and the IPC port — back.

The import is a one-time migration of files the renderer no longer writes, and the early snapshot already handles the pre-import state (`storage/window-snapshot.ts` checks for legacy files; `window-snapshot.test.ts` covers it). This forks it, so the layers and the port are handed out first.

### How did you verify your code works?

Measured with the repo's dev startup benchmark (`bun run bench:devex`), reading the main-process marks (`lifecycle/marks.ts`).

The window→layers block is **280ms** (median of 4 runs). Split: main bundle evaluation 152ms, storage 72ms, logging 34ms, onboarding 4ms. Inside storage: sqlite open + migrate 29ms, legacy import 21ms.

Forking the import takes the storage interval from **72ms to 42-47ms** (4 baseline runs vs 2 fixed runs, reproducible in the marks).

The benchmark's headline metric (`visibleWindowToHome`) does not resolve this: it is dominated by the dev-mode renderer (9.0-14.1s) and the isolated dev service (5.9-14.1s), and its `windowVisible` milestone is the adoption log *after* the layers, so the 280ms block sits outside it. Paired deltas were +101ms / −1459ms. The marks are the evidence here.

Two assumptions from the issue were measured and did not hold: theme resolution is 1.3ms (not "tens of milliseconds"), and onboarding is 4ms.

**Machine** (for comparability): AMD Ryzen 5 5600U (6C/12T), 13.8 GB RAM, AMD Radeon integrated graphics (driver 30.0.13044.0) plus a virtual display adapter, 1920×1080 @60Hz, Windows 11 Pro for Workstations build 26300, balanced power plan.

- `bun test src/main/storage` (`packages/desktop`): 29 passed, 0 failed.

### Screenshots / recordings

n/a

prs.title: fix(app): make desktop voice navigation and handoff match iOS
prs.body:
**What it does**

In a Desktop voice call, the assistant sometimes said it had switched to a session when the screen never moved. Sessions also showed the user's raw, disfluent transcript where the iOS app shows the request. Now `open_session` reports success only after the screen really shows the session. Search finds sessions by their spoken name. Voice delegations use the same handoff format as the iOS app. The delegator can also list and switch a session's model by voice.

**How it works**

- **Open:** The voice context selects the session's tab, or opens one, then navigates and waits up to 3 s for the route to change. If the route doesn't change, the tool says the screen did not move. The wait stops if the call ends or drops. Missing and archived sessions are refused.
- **Search:** Ported from the iOS app. Filler words are dropped and one-letter mishearings are tolerated. Results rank by match, then top-level sessions, then sessions with an open tab, then recency. A separate top-level server search stops subagents from crowding root sessions out. If no root session matches the phrase, it retries with the longest word.
- **Handoff:** Each delegation uses the iOS header and a sorted JSON body with `instruction`, `transcript_delta` (both sides of the call since the last delegation) and `context`. There is no `voice` field. Later delegations to the same session use the short continued header, and the full header returns after 30 minutes. The timeline still reads older Desktop messages, but stops showing their raw transcript as the voice framing.
- **Steering:** A steer first moves the session's running shells and subagents to the background, as typed steers and the iOS app do. It is tried once, with a short timeout.
- **Instructions:** Delegator and live wording is aligned with iOS. Open a session only when asked to switch; reading or messaging never moves the screen. Say only what the tools did; nothing happens unless the request is delegated. Never phrase an acknowledgement as already done.

**Risk**

The change is limited to the experimental Desktop voice call and the timeline's voice-message parsing. A real call wasn't tested; only unit tests and typecheck were run. If the route check is too strict on some setup, opening by voice would report a failure instead of a false success. iOS features not ported: pins, permissions and questions, queued-message tools, model favourites, switching servers, the call log, and the full header after compaction. The change got one independent model review, from a different model family, before push.

**Proof**

- `bun test --conditions=solid --isolate --preload ../ui/test/solid-jsx.ts --preload ./happydom.ts src/voice src/session/timeline/voice-delegation.test.ts` in `packages/app`: 40 pass
- `bun typecheck` in `packages/app`: clean

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Refs #27167. This is the first of four PRs; it does not close the request on its own.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The durable half of a session goal: a schema contract, `session_goal` / `session_todo` tables, four durable events, their projections and the read model. No endpoints, no UI, no round driver.

- `packages/schema/src/session-goal.ts` — `Phase` (`active | paused | blocked | complete`), `Snapshot` (with a `revision` CAS reference and `maxGoalRounds`), `TodoItem` / `TodoInput`, `Verdict`, and the `State` read model. The goal id is server-generated and validates the `goal_` prefix it emits.
- `session_goal` / `session_todo` follow the shape of `session_inbox` and `instruction_state`: `session_id` with `onDelete: "cascade"`, JSON columns, the shared timestamps.
- Four durable events: `session.goal.updated` / `.cleared`, `session.todo.updated` / `.verified`.
- Projections: the goal row is upserted with a revision guard (`excluded.revision > revision`), so replaying an event is idempotent; a clear deletes by `(session_id, goal_id)` and the id is never reused; the todo list is replaced wholesale in one transaction; a verification updates items by position and advances the round counter.

### Why it is split this way

The round driver is the only part with an autonomous loop, so it gets its own PR and can be rejected on its own. Even then, this PR plus the endpoints and the desktop indicator are a self-contained feature: a persisted goal, manual control, a todo list, and the indicator — and they already fix the class of defect in #48239, where the stop button did not stop the loop.

The 20MB `MAX_MEDIA_INGEST_BYTES` cap and the existing image/PDF/text paths are unchanged.

prs.title: refactor(session-ui): append to the markdown store by path
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #54305

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

A streaming delta only appends to the tail of a block, so the store can be updated by path instead of handing the whole tree to `reconcile`.

The renderer keeps the plain `parsed` tree, walks the tail by path, and writes only the changed node and the new children with `setNodes(...path)`. The live node is extended in place, so a grown word keeps its span. A delta that changes more than the tail (shorter tree, changed prefix, word/element swap) falls back to `reconcile`.

### How did you verify your code works?

Per-update cost for one paragraph growing by one word, mean of the last 100 updates, production build, chromium:

| scenario | base | first attempt | this |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1000 words | 4.64ms | 4.42ms | **0.97ms** |
| 3000 words | 16.80ms | 13.14ms | **3.37ms** |
| 299 short paragraphs + 3000-word tail | 30.31ms | 28.10ms | **6.54ms** |

The store walk alone (no store write, no DOM) is 0.05ms at 1000 words and 0.18ms at 3000 — near-constant. What remains is the parse (~0.9ms) and `For`'s DOM diff (~2.3ms), which the base pays too.

The first attempt handed `reconcile` a tree rebuilt from the store's own nodes. That moved the cost into the comparison: `reuseNodes` read the whole old tree through the store proxy (~5ms per update at 3000 words), and the live node was still rebuilt, so `reconcile` diffed all of its children (~7ms). Wrapping the writes in `batch()` also matters: without it, each `setNodes` re-diffs the block, and 3000 words goes from 3.4ms to 4.9ms.

- `markdown-solid.test.tsx` gains a streaming test: it appends a word at a time, asserts the existing spans keep their elements, and compares the result against a one-shot render.
- Behaviour was checked against the base across 16 scenarios (long words, `**` toggling, word/element swaps, inline code, links, new blocks, lists, code fences, shrink, headings): final DOM, span retention and `data-markdown-enter` counts all match.
- `bun test --conditions=browser src` in `packages/session-ui`: 250 passed, 0 failed. The test script gains `--conditions=browser` for the same reason `packages/app` has `test:browser`.

The end-to-end elapsed in the #54305 benchmark is dominated by the block's `innerHTML` re-parse (#54428), so the visible gain there is smaller than the per-update numbers above.

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

Scrolling a long session in the desktop app spends its main-thread time in layout and paint. A CPU profile of the scroll window puts `(program)` at 523ms of 1607ms sampled, with the app-side reads small next to it.

The timeline's row container sets `overflow: clip` but no containment, so every mounted row stays in the layout and paint path for the whole list. prs.title: fix(app): make the question dock keyboard-first and stop it flashing
prs.body:
## What it does

Makes the question dock work from the keyboard the way you'd expect, and stops it flashing. The arrows only move a highlight, Space marks an answer and Enter commits it and moves on.

- Pick one: nothing is picked when a question opens. Up/Down move the highlight, Space picks and stays, Enter picks and goes to the next question (or submits on the last), and 1–9 pick without advancing.
- Pick many: Space or 1–9 toggle on key down (no repeats, no double toggle from the trailing click), and Enter moves on with whatever is checked.
- Type your own answer: arrowing onto it only highlights it. Typing a character starts the answer with it and picks it, and Enter in the field moves on.
- Left/Right switch questions when focus isn't in the text field. ⌘[ / ⌘⏎ (Alt+← / Ctrl+⏎) still work.
- One highlighted card at a time; the pick shows only as the radio dot or check. The highlight, the answers box height and question changes move on a no-bounce spring instead of popping. Reduced motion gets a plain fade.

## How it works

Key handling lives in a pure `questionKey(event, { mac, zone, count })` in `question-keys.ts`, which maps one keydown to one intent (`move`, `activate`, `commit`, `type`, `number`…); RTL flips the arrows, and nothing fires during IME composition. The highlight is a roving tabindex: `store.focus` is the highlighted answer and holds the only tab stop, so screen readers announce it separately from `aria-checked`. Mouse hover moves the highlight too. It is drawn as one layer behind the cards that glides to the highlighted card by its `clip-path`, landing at once on a new question. The box height follows a ResizeObserver through a spring, and a question change slides 12px plus a fade via WAAPI.

## Risk

Low. Contained to the question dock. Roles and `aria-checked` are unchanged. Right Arrow on the last question does not submit; Enter, Next and ⌘⏎ do.

## Proof

Today (left) vs the first cut of this PR (right), keyboard only. This was recorded before the highlight model, so on the right ↓ still picks:

https://problems.kitlangton.com/media/Ub0fG5f_RsdLJyh08vCkxQ.mp4

- `question-keys.test.ts`: unit tests for every intent, including Enter, typing on the custom answer and IME composition
- `session-question-dock.spec.ts`: component tests for ↓ not changing the answer, Space marking, Enter advancing in both question types, typing into the custom answer, Left/Right and IME composition

prs.title: fix(app): fade sidebar contents only near closed and show hover actions instantly
prs.body:
## What it does

- The sidebar and side panel contents now stay fully opaque for most of a close and fade out only in the last 15% of travel. On open they appear almost at once, at the start. Peek uses the same rule.
- Ships Kit's settled timing: scale by distance stays on, 0.15–0.30 s (max was 0.45 s), reference width 480 px.
- Message hover actions show and hide instantly again: assistant copy/fork row, user message actions and meta, the message menu button, and tool row actions.

## How it works

- `panelOpacity` reads a new Knobs choice, **Contents fade**: Edge (shipped), Off, or Whole spring (the old fade down to 50%). **Edge fade** (a % of travel, default 15) replaces Fade floor and only shows for Edge. On a zero-bounce spring the last 15% of a close lasts about 70 ms on the 260 px sidebar. Opacity is still a function of spring progress, so a reversal mid-flight stays continuous.
- Removes the opacity transitions from the hover-revealed rows. #57653 had removed them, and #58089 (`2f96b1720e`, polish message footers) added `transition: opacity 200ms ease-out` back on `text-part-copy-wrapper`, `user-message-copy-wrapper` and `user-message-meta-tail`. Also drops the 150 ms fade on the per-message menu button (#58164) and on `basic-tool-action`.

## Risk

Low. The changes are limited to motion and CSS. Closed panels now rest at opacity 0 instead of 0.5, but they are 0 px wide and skipped by content-visibility. James mode doesn't change.

## Proof

Side-by-side, today vs new, captured frame by frame at 60 fps against a web build with mock data: [real speed](https://problems.kitlangton.com/media/aM9HdLu1YS355SZ5yAMoeA.mp4) · [0.25×](https://problems.kitlangton.com/media/sYZO4Bs5md3vBEJATeOgiA.mp4). Unit and browser tests cover the shipped durations, the edge fade curve and the knob visibility.

prs.title: fix(app): hide the side tab scrollbar, fade both edges, and even out the + gap
prs.body:
### What it does

Polishes the tab strip in the side panel:

- Tabs now fade out at both edges once there are more tabs past that edge, including under the "+" at the end. Before, only the start had a fade, and tabs ran straight under the "+".
- The gap between the last tab and "+" is now the same 8px as the gap between tabs, whether the tabs fit or overflow. Before, the "+" had an extra 12px after it when the strip overflowed.
- The strip still hides its scrollbar (`scrollbar-width: none`). Wheel and trackpad scrolling work as before.

### How it works

- `tabs.css` puts a `mask-image` on the side panel's tab list. One gradient fades each edge by `--tab-strip-fade-start` / `--tab-strip-fade-end` and stops at the sticky "+" (`--tab-strip-add`). A second layer keeps the "+" itself unmasked. There is a `:dir(rtl)` mirror.
- `createTabStripScroll` sets those three variables from a passive `scroll` listener and a `ResizeObserver`, so nothing runs per frame. Each fade is the distance scrolled past that edge, up to 24px, so it grows in instead of popping. It writes only values that changed.
- The sticky "+" loses its `padding-inline-end` and its old gradient `::before`, so it sits flush at the strip's end.

### Risk

Low. CSS and one scroll listener, scoped to the review and bottom panel tab bars.

### Proof

Overflowing, scrolled to the middle (before on top, after below):

Overflowing, scrolled to the end:

RTL mirrors both. `tab-strip-scroll.test.ts` and typecheck pass.

prs.title: fix(app): scroll natively with one shared scrollbar style
prs.body:
### Summary - **One scrollbar style for the whole app.** `packages/ui/src/styles/scrollbar.css` gives every native scroll container the `ScrollView` look: a 4px pill, at least 32px long, shown while you hover the container and darker while you hover or drag it. A plain `overflow-y-auto` now looks right on Windows. - **`ScrollView` is gone from 16 of its 18 call sites.** Dialogs, lists, settings, the composer, review, file, context and BTW panels all scroll natively now. It stays only where CSS cannot do the job: the session timeline and Home draw the thumb in an external track, and the timeline corrects it for virtualized rows. - **Two native-scrollbar leaks are fixed.** `scrollbar-width: thin` on the typeahead list and the directory picker tree made Chromium skip all `::-webkit-scrollbar` styling and draw the Windows scrollbar. - **The rules are written down.** The new Scrolling section in `packages/app/AGENTS.md` covers when to use a plain element, when to add a wrapper, `data-scrollable`, and the 8px gutter. ### What is still a `ScrollView`, and why | Call site | Needs | Native? | |---|---|---| | Session timeline (`session/timeline/virtualizer.tsx`) | Thumb in an external track; thumb corrected for virtualized rows (`verticalScrollAdjustment`, `onBeforeScroll`) | No | | Home (`home/route.tsx`) | Thumb in a track beside the centered session list, below the sticky search header | No | | The other 16 | Only a styled scrollbar | Yes, now native | ### Migration pattern ```mermaid flowchart TD A["<ScrollView>"] --> B{"Something must stay put
while the content scrolls?"} B -- "no (14 sites)" --> C["one div
overflow-y-auto + min-h-0 / max-h
data-scrollable"] B -- "edge fades in ::before / ::after (2 sites)" --> D["wrapper: relative flex flex-col min-h-0
inner: min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto
data-scrollable"] ``` ```tsx // Before (resultsRef = el)}>… // After
(resultsRef = el)}>…
``` - **Styles that targeted `> .scroll-view__viewport`** now target the container itself (composer fades, search-list fades, settings-search mask, review sidebar padding). - **`data-scrollable` stays on every migrated container.** The timeline, Home wheel containment and `createAutoScroll` use it to let an inner container scroll first, and the file list uses it to find its virtualizer's scroll element. - **Ref timing.** `viewportRef` ran in `onMount`, but a native `ref` runs before the children render. The context tab and the file view restored their scroll position in the ref, so they now defer it with `onMount`. - **Composer and settings search reserve the gutter.** They use `scrollbar-gutter: stable` and subtract the new `--scrollbar-size` variable from their end padding, so text does not rewrap when the content starts to scroll and keeps its inset. - **Dead CSS removed.** The `model-selector-scroll` rules in `app/src/index.css` had no element left. - **The question dock** now queries the timeline viewport by its slot, not the first `.scroll-view__viewport` in the document. ### How the shared style works - **Low priority.** It is in the `base` layer, so `no-scrollbar`, `scrollbar-width: none` and `ScrollView` still win. - **Pointer devices only.** It applies only under `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`. Touch devices keep their overlay scrollbars. - **Firefox.** It gets the same colors through `scrollbar-width: thin` and `scrollbar-color`, behind `@supports not selector(::-webkit-scrollbar)`. - **Hover repaint.** Chromium re-resolves scrollbar parts only when the owning element's style changes. A non-inherited registered property forces that change on hover, without restyling the subtree: ```css @property --scrollbar-hover { syntax: ""; inherits: false; initial-value: 0; } :hover { --scrollbar-hover: 1; } :hover::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb { background-color: var(--v2-border-border-muted); } ``` ### Trade-offs - **Native scrollbars take 8px of layout while they scroll.** CSS cannot overlay a native scrollbar. That is 7px less than the Windows scrollbar. On macOS, where the system overlay took no width, these containers now reserve 8px. - **No reveal from keyboard scrolling alone.** The thumb shows on hover. A wheel or trackpad scroll already hovers the container. - **Masked containers fade their thumb at the ends.** The composer, search-list and settings-search masks now also cover the scrollbar, so the thumb fades with the content edge. - **The review sidebar's horizontal thumb shows on hover.** It used to stay visible. The e2e test that dragged that custom thumb in RTL now checks the RTL scroll position directly. - **No thumb-drag e2e checks.** Headless Chromium hides native scrollbars, so the composer test no longer drags a thumb. A manual check in Edge confirmed that dragging the native thumb to the top scrolls to 0 and keeps the editor focused. ### The real search list (story `UI/Search List` > Long lists, Edge on Windows, list hovered) | | Before (`ScrollView`) | After (native) | |---|---|---| | Light | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8713d268-513d-465f-9085-811b32ddb1a8) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d36e76bd-1f32-482f-acda-e326b7805fc3) | | Dark | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/32a99d38-0299-45a9-ac93-9f360265b702) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/63b31ebf-58d9-44d0-b968-b81566b09373) | The thumb matches. The rows now end 8px before the edge instead of running under the thumb. ### Native scrollbar vs shared style (test page, Chromium on Windows) | | Light | Dark | |---|---|---| | Container hovered | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa5061a5-ccfd-4c0b-813c-573d9561be02) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2c8d71de-484e-423a-99cc-03634537d01c) | | Not hovered | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2c0f7fd3-7964-4227-838d-adba63e53ab2) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1d2668d8-7287-4ddb-b178-1128694f5b69) | | 5,000-line editor, 32px minimum thumb | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/96cda209-50d6-4067-9419-c752ebc1d227) | | ### Failing checks that also fail on `beta` - `e2e/regression/home.spec.ts:184`, `e2e/regression/timeline-stream.spec.ts:1958`, and `component-tests/composer.spec.ts:3` and `:268` fail the same way on `beta` (run 40046218839). - `:268` fails because `COMPOSER_SUGGESTION_TOP_PADDING` is 8 while the history menu has 6px padding (`p-1.5`). prs.title: fix(ai): classify OpenAI image moderation blocks as content policy
prs.body:
## Problem

When OpenAI's image safety system blocks a prompt, `@opencode/ai` didn't report it as `ContentPolicy`. I triggered a real block on `gpt-image-1-mini` and got this:

| Path | What OpenAI sends | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Image.generate` (generations and edits) | HTTP 400, `code: "moderation_blocked"`, `type: "image_generation_user_error"` | `InvalidRequest` | `ContentPolicy` |
| `Image.stream` | HTTP 200, then an `event: error` SSE frame with the same `error` object | `InvalidProviderOutput` ("sent an invalid stream event") | `ContentPolicy` |
| Vercel AI Gateway (generate and stream) | HTTP 400, OpenAI's message kept, code dropped, `type: "AI_APICallError"` | `InvalidRequest` | `ContentPolicy` |

The message in every case is "Your request was rejected by the safety system. ..."

## Change

```diff
 CONTENT_POLICY_CODES
+  "moderation_blocked"
 CONTENT_POLICY_TEXT
-  rejected as a result of our safety system
+  rejected (as a result of our | by the) safety system   # the gateway only keeps the message

 openai-images onEvent
+  if event.type === "error"
+    fail with classifyProviderFailure(frame)   # same as openai-transcription
```

The tests use the real bodies I captured (request IDs replaced). Both new tests fail on `dev` and pass with this change.

## Out of scope

- The Responses `image_generation` tool. I couldn't trigger a block there, since the main model rewrote the prompt into something milder. Its typed error code `image_content_policy_violation` is already classified.
- Other unknown OpenAI Images stream event types still fail as invalid output.

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Refs #43818 and #35765. Covers the same ground as #52629 (Chat Completions only), for every protocol OpenCode's own gateway speaks.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

OpenCode Console is going to tell clients what each request cost the user. It will send `usage.cost` in USD, the convention OpenRouter and LiteLLM already use. For Go, where a request is covered by the subscription and costs $0, it will also send `usage.opencode.allowance`: how much Go allowance the request used. This PR records both so the UIs can show them:

- `@opencode/ai`: `Usage` gets `cost` and `allowance`. Chat Completions, Responses, Anthropic Messages and Gemini read them from the response's usage. A malformed or negative value is ignored, and provider metadata still has whatever the endpoint sent. Some providers send a `cost` string, for example.
- core: `SessionUsage.record` uses a reported cost instead of the catalog price, and a reported 0 counts. It's projected onto the assistant message and a new `session_v2.allowance` column, and exposed as `Session.Info.allowance` and on `session.usage.updated`.
- client: `data.session.allowance(sessionID)` adds up a session family, like `cost()`.

Nothing changes for endpoints that don't report a cost. The UI changes are in the follow-up PRs for the TUI and the desktop app.

prs.title: fix(core): retry Azure deployment discovery after a transient failure
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #57690

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Discovery runs in exactly two places — once at plugin start and once on `Credential.Event.Switched` — and `refresh()` drops a failed result with `if (!found) return`. So a startup sync that fails while the machine has no network is not merely lost: nothing runs again until the connection switches or the process restarts, which is what the report describes when a laptop wakes before its modem or VPN.

This retries the discovery request instead of restructuring discovery. `deployments(...)` is wrapped in `Effect.retry` with a 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 30 second ladder capped at 8 attempts — about two minutes — and only a failure that can pass is retried: a transport error, a timeout, a 408, a 429, or a 5xx other than 501. A rejected key or an unmatchable body fails the same way however often it is asked, so it still logs `failed to sync Azure deployments` once and stops, as it does today.

Two details worth knowing:

- **The retry sits inside the call, before the `Effect.catch` that turns a failure into `undefined`.** Wrapping the retried effect rather than the call site is what keeps a retried attempt from being swallowed by the warning handler on the way out.
- **A switch still interrupts discovery through the existing fiber handle**, so a pending retry cannot answer the previous connection. The connection is re-read after the retry resolves and the result is discarded if it changed, so a retry that outlives a switch cannot publish the old account's deployments.

A timed-out attempt is included because Azure's own timeout can arrive before the client's, and that request may pass on the next attempt.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Added two tests in `packages/core/test/plugin/provider-azure.test.ts`, one per arm:
  - `retries a deployment sync that failed while the network was down` — the endpoint refuses the first attempt and answers the second; the deployments arrive without a restart.
  - `leaves a failure that cannot pass alone instead of retrying it` — a rejected key logs the warning once and the retry count stays at one.
- Verified red before green: with `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/azure.ts` reverted to the base and the new tests kept, the transient test fails (`22 pass, 1 fail`); with the change it passes (`23 pass`).
- `bun test test/plugin/provider-azure.test.ts` — 23 pass, 0 fail.
- `tsc -b tsconfig.json tsconfig.tests.json` in `packages/core` — clean.
- `oxlint` on both changed files — 0 warnings, 0 errors; `prettier --check` clean.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change.

prs.title: feat(app): hydrate user attachments on demand
prs.body:
## What it does

Opening a session with many pasted images downloads every image's bytes up front. The desktop/web timeline now loads them from a new experimental route, `GET /api/experimental/session/:sessionID/timeline` (`experimental.session.timeline`, SDK `client.experimental.session.timeline`; `client.message` is unchanged). It returns user attachments as `opencode-attachment:` references, and the app loads the originals near the viewport or on click.

**The stable API is unchanged.** `GET /api/session/:sessionID/message` has no new parameter, and its OpenAPI entry matches beta byte for byte.

## How it works

1. The timeline route takes the same paging params as the stable messages route and shares its handler. The only difference is that the store replaces inline user file bytes with `opencode-attachment:<sessionID>/<messageID>/<index>` and empty data. The response schema marks that format as experimental.
2. Only the app's timeline data store calls the new route. Revert, Fork, image hydration and single-message reads keep the stable routes and get full bytes. Exports and model context are untouched.
3. A per-server LRU (32 messages, 16 MiB) holds the originals for image display, Revert and Fork. Concurrent reads share one request, and a failed read can be retried.
4. `AGENTS.md` gets one line: new or uncertain API surface goes under `/api/experimental/` first.

#56989 is stacked on this PR and adds read-tool media omission to the same route.

## Risk

Desktop/web timeline only. If hydration fails, an image shows a sized placeholder and retries on its next intersection. Explicit clicks surface the error. Other clients never see references.

## Proof

200-prompt page on a HOME-shaped fixture: **9,920,082 → 145,676 B**. No reliable newest-paint improvement is claimed.

**What it does.** After pairing, a client knows only the server's address, so a newly paired computer shows up as an IP or a tailnet hostname. The JSON response from `GET /auth/connect/:code` now includes an optional `device: { name }` with the computer's own name (for example "Alex's MacBook Pro"), so clients can label the pairing with something a person recognizes.

**How it works.**
1. `ServerInfo.deviceName` reads the macOS Computer Name (`scutil --get ComputerName`, loaded only on darwin). Everywhere else, or if that fails, it uses `os.hostname()` without `.local`.
2. It never fails. When there's no name (for example on workerd), `device` is left out and pairing works the same as today.

The iOS app already reads `device.name` and ignores it if missing. It uses the name for a newly paired computer, and a name the user gave it still wins.

**Risk.** Small, server only. The field is additive and optional, so existing clients ignore it. Redeeming a code on macOS now runs `scutil` once, with a 1 s timeout. The workerd path isn't covered here beyond the existing workerd boot test.

prs.title: fix(core): patch Effect.fn stack frames that keep call arguments alive
prs.body:
The server heap snapshot (beta 21701, 11.7 h uptime) held **117 MB of message history**, 47 base64 screenshots, through `fiber.cache.stackFrame…stack → arguments[0].messages`. The cause is an `effect` bug: an `Effect.fn` call's stack frame keeps all of that call's arguments alive, and every fiber forked inside the call inherits the frame. - **Upstream:** issue https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/issues/9877, fix https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/9878 ```mermaid flowchart LR W["long-lived fiber
(watcher, plugin service, job notifier)"] --> F["inherited CurrentStackFrame"] F --> R["SessionRunner.runStep frame"] R --> A["arguments[0] = loaded conversation
every screenshot"] ``` | Fibers in the snapshot keeping a session's frames | Count | Frame chain kept | |---|---|---| | Plugin activation, config and folder watchers first started by a `move` tool call | 152 | `SessionMove.resolveDestination < SessionMove.move < Tool.execute < SessionStep.attempt < SessionRunner.runStep` | | `ShellTool.notifyWhenDone`, `Shell.wait` | 56 | `… < Tool.execute < SessionStep.attempt < SessionRunner.runStep` | - **Fix:** `patches/effect@4.0.1.patch` applies the upstream change. The frame is built by `makeCallFrame`, outside the traced function, so its `stack` closure can no longer reach `arguments`. Frames, names and stack output are unchanged. ```js return updateService(result, CurrentStackFrame, makeCallFrame(name, callError, definitionName, definitionStack)) const makeCallFrame = (name, callError, definitionName, definitionStack) => prev => ({ name, stack: callError ? fnStackCleaner(() => callError.stack) : constUndefined, parent: { name: definitionName, stack: definitionStack, parent: prev } }) ``` - **Test:** `packages/core/test/effect-fn-retention.test.ts` forks a detached fiber inside an `Effect.fn` call and asserts the argument is collected. It fails without the patch. - **Removing the patch:** drop it once `effect` ships the upstream fix. | Server heap | Before | After (expected) | |---|---|---| | History kept by `Effect.fn` frames | 117 MB | ~0 | ### Visual ```svg ``` --- _Added by the opencode bot (AI-generated)._ Related: #56058
