prs.title: fix(app): stop omitted tool images from keeping their payload alive
prs.body:
#58427 was meant to drop tool-result screenshots from the desktop store, but it did not free them. The overnight renderer snapshot (beta 21701, which includes #58427) still held **2.17 GB of `data:image/png` strings**, 1,173 of them, under `state.content[].uri`.

- **Cause:** `item.uri.slice(0, comma + 1)` returns a V8 *sliced string*. It is a view into the original string, not a copy, and it keeps the whole parent alive. In the snapshot, every stored `"data:image/png;base64,"` was a `(sliced string)` whose `parent` was the full 2–3 MB screenshot.
- **Fix:** the empty URI is now built from the item's `mime`, so it shares nothing with the original.

```ts
item.type === "file" && item.uri.startsWith("data:") ? { ...item, uri: `data:${item.mime};base64,` } : item
```

|---|---|---|
| `data:image/*` strings kept by the store | 2.17 GB (1,173) | ~0 |
| Renderer V8 heap | 2.48 GB | a few hundred MB |

issues.title: Codex: Use file references for image-heavy tool results
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

For Codex, decouple image storage from provider payload. Keep image bytes locally, but materialize outbound images as ChatGPT `file_id` references instead of replaying base64 on every request.

I have a local prototype and can implement this after we agree whether it belongs in the Codex provider or in a pi extension.

### Why?

On pi 0.84.2 with `gpt-5.6-sol`, five parallel png reads produced ~17MB of base64 and a ~23MB WebSocket request. The reads completed, then the session reported:

`WebSocket closed 1009 message too big`

The TUI repeatedly showed `Error: fetch failed` and eventually `Retry failed after 3 attempts: fetch failed`. Automatic SSE fallback resent the same history; later text-only turns remained stuck. I reproduced this from a copied session with extensions disabled.

An inline budget – as in _downample n images into payload budget p_ – potentially reduces visual context, while sequential reads lose parallelism and add model turns.

Related issues: #5369, #8351, #7330, and #4133

### How? (optional)

When constructing a Codex request, hash each image and cache by backend/account/content. On a miss:

1. `POST https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/files`
2. `PUT` the bytes to the returned signed `*.oaiusercontent.com` URL
3. Finalize `/files/{file_id}/uploaded`
4. Replace only the outbound block with `input_image { file_id, detail: "original" }`

Parallel tool results still upload concurrently and return in one follow-up request. Stable IDs preserve WebSocket continuation and should remain prompt-cache compatible.

Local bytes remain canonical, either inline or optionally in content-addressed sidecars. Expired IDs can be re-uploaded once; upload failures retain the bounded inline fallback.

Benefits:
- bounded requests
- parallel calls
- upload reuse
- continuation and
- stale-file recovery

Trade-offs and risks:
- an undocumented ChatGPT API contract
- upload latency/privacy
- remote-ID expiry and
- provider-specific core or extension complexity

issues.title: pi-durable: let durable tasks keep the conversation busy
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Kinda related to my previous #11141. I'd like a way for a task to keep the conversation busy (no new input while it runs).

My use case: at the end of a turn, I want to create a task that captures a git checkpoint snapshot of the whole repo. This task has two requirements:

1. It can't be cancelled by `Conversation.abort()`, otherwise it could produce corrupted snapshots
2. It has to keep the conversation busy: users shouldn't be able to prompt while it runs, because a new turn could write files mid-snapshot.

I can't find a way to do this in the current durable. The naive way to check whether a session is busy is to look at `live.run`: if it's defined, the session is busy (no more messages allowed); if it's undefined, it's idle.

This works fine, but tasks don't change `live.run`; only generation tasks do. So one could think: "I'll make my host's busy check look at both `live.run` and foreground (`background: false`) tasks". Only foreground, because background tasks should in fact stay in the background and not block. Then I'll create my checkpoint task as foreground.

This could work, but it raises two issues:

1. Foreground tasks are always cancelled by `Conversation.abort()`, with no way to opt out. I could live with that and make the checkpoint task handle its own abort.
2. It breaks manual compaction. Manual compaction should run in the background, yet it should be cancellable. How should it be classified? If it's `background: false`, then to keep conversing while it compacts, the busy check must NOT look at foreground tasks, otherwise the session is marked busy and you can't continue. If it's `background: true`, it's no longer cancelled by `abort()`, and idle waits stop including it.


### Why?

Without this, a host has to enforce busy itself while such a task runs, and other clients or extensions on the same session don't see it.

### How? (optional)

_No response_

issues.title: openai-codex Connection Reliability Issues

labels.name: inprogress
labels.description: Issue is being worked on

issues.body:
## Summary

`openai-codex` / `gpt-5.5` sometimes leaves the interactive TUI stuck on `Working...` with no streamed text, no tool call, and no visible error. The only way to recover is pressing Escape, which records an aborted assistant turn.

This has happened repeatedly over the last couple of days in normal interactive use.

## Environment

- pi: `0.75.5`
- Node: `v22.22.1`
- Provider/model: `openai-codex` / `gpt-5.5`
- Thinking level: `xhigh`
- No explicit `transport` setting in user settings
- Default tools/extensions enabled

## Observed behavior

When the issue occurs:

- TUI keeps showing `Working...` for minutes.
- No assistant text is streamed.
- No tool call is emitted.
- Pressing Escape aborts the turn.
- The saved session entry for that assistant turn has:

```json
{
  "role": "assistant",
  "stopReason": "aborted",
  "content": [],
  "usage": {
    "input": 0,
    "output": 0,
    "cacheRead": 0,
    "cacheWrite": 0,
    "totalTokens": 0
  }
}
```

I saw this pattern multiple times, including cases where the previous turn had completed normally and the next user message then hung before any provider usage was recorded.

This looks different from a long reasoning turn: there is no usage, no partial reasoning/text, and no tool call.

## Expected behavior

If the provider/transport stalls before the first event, pi should eventually surface a timeout/transport error or retry in a bounded way, instead of keeping the TUI in `Working...` indefinitely until the user manually aborts.

## Suspected area

From the installed `0.75.5` package:

- `SettingsManager.getTransport()` returns `"auto"` when no setting is present.
- The docs/settings table says the default is `"sse"`, so there may also be a docs/runtime default mismatch.
- For `openai-codex-responses`, `transport=auto` attempts WebSocket first.
- `retry.provider.timeoutMs` appears to be passed into `streamSimple()`, but the `openai-codex-responses` implementation does not seem to apply it to the Codex fetch/WebSocket wait path in the same way as SDK-based providers.
- The WebSocket event loop can wait for the first message/completion without an obvious idle timer.

So the likely failure mode is: Codex WebSocket/transport waits before the first event; no assistant event is produced; interactive UI keeps showing `Working...`; Escape finally records an aborted zero-usage turn.

## Suggested fix / mitigation

Possible fixes:

1. Add a hard idle timeout for `openai-codex-responses` WebSocket and SSE stream waits, especially before the first event.
2. Ensure `retry.provider.timeoutMs` or `httpIdleTimeoutMs` applies consistently to this provider path.
3. If `auto` is intended as the runtime default, update docs; if `sse` is intended, adjust `SettingsManager.getTransport()`.
4. Optionally show a clearer status/error when a provider turn has produced zero events for a long time.

Local workaround I am considering, but have not applied yet:

```json
{
  "transport": "sse",
  "httpIdleTimeoutMs": 120000
}
```

I can provide more sanitized session metadata if helpful, but I avoided attaching raw session logs because they contain private conversation/tool context.

issues.title: openai-codex: compaction retries never fall back to SSE after a mid-stream WebSocket disconnect

labels.name: inprogress
labels.description: Issue is being worked on

issues.body:
### What happened?

With `openai-codex` and the default `auto` transport, a WebSocket disconnect after `response.created` can exhaust every compaction retry without ever trying SSE:

```text
Auto-compaction failed: Summarization failed: WebSocket error
```

I reproduced the recovery failure with the installed package's `completeSummarization()` and native `streamSimple()`, without loading extensions or using real credentials. Both the SDK implementation and CLI bundle show the same behavior.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Call `completeSummarization()` with a Codex model, `reasoning: "high"`, a session ID, and retry enabled (`maxRetries: 3`, short backoff).
2. Replace WebSocket with an offline fake that opens, accepts `response.create`, emits `response.created`, then emits an error. Repeat this for each socket.
3. Provide a fake `fetch` returning a valid, completed SSE summary.
4. Count WebSocket and HTTP calls.

Observed: **4 WebSocket calls, 0 HTTP calls**, final `stopReason: "error"`. Expected: a retry can use SSE and return a complete summary.

Summaries set `cacheRetention: "none"`. The provider consequently sets `cacheSessionId` to `undefined`; `recordWebSocketFailure(cacheSessionId, error)` saves no fallback state. Retrying repeats the same transport. Using `options.sessionId` for fallback state while retaining `cacheSessionId` for caching fixes this repro: **1 WebSocket call, 1 HTTP call**, complete summary. Independent operations still start with WebSocket.

### Version

pi 1.3.0; Node 24.14.1; `openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol high`.

Related: #10781 covers transport-setting propagation. This repro uses default `auto` and specifically tests recovery after a stream has started.

issues.title: Allow `watchEvents` in pi-durable resume from the last seen entry
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Provide the ability for `watchEvents` to resume from a previously seen point by passing an entry id as a "last seen" argument .

When provided the returned `snapshot.entries` holds only the active entries with a higher ID, and includes `snapshot.after` to confirm this is a resumed stream. The rest of the snapshot (including partial message, tools, inbox, agent, usage) are still sent in full.

The client drops its entries before the marker's `head`. If the "last seen" is an unknown value the snapshot is returned in full without the `after` key.

### Why?

If a client disconnects or goes offline, on reconnection it would be ideal to only have to stream the events that happened since the reconnection rather than retransmitting the full stream.

This can be implemented in user land by discarding the earlier events but ideally it'd be built in.

### How? (optional)

Something like:

```ts
const stream = await watchEvents(harness, id, context, { after: lastSeenId });
```

Entries are already stored with increasing IDs. So ideally we'd check the `after` value then filter `snapshotOf(view).entries`.

An example of an expected stream including compaction.

 Fresh stream `watchEvents(harness, id, ctx)`

 ```jsonc
   {
     "type": "snapshot",
     "entries": [
       { "id": 214, "kind": "pi.compaction", "head": 180, "data": { "summary": "…" } },
       { "id": 180, "kind": "pi.user", "model": [{ "role": "user", "content": "Fix the flaky login test" }] },
       { "id": 181, "kind": "pi.assistant", "model": [{ "role": "assistant", "content": [ … ] }] },
       // … 30 more entries, 182–211 …
       { "id": 212, "kind": "pi.assistant", "model": [{ "role": "assistant", "content": [{ "type": "toolCall", "name": "bash", … }] }] },
       { "id": 213, "kind": "pi.tool-result", "model": [{ "role": "toolResult", "toolCallId": "call_9", … }] }
     ],
     "run": { "inputs": [41] },
     "generation": { "attempt": 1, "message": { "role": "assistant", "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "The test fails because" }] } },
     "tools": [], "nestedTools": [], "compactions": [], "inbox": [],
     "agent": { … }, "usage": { … }
   }
 ```

Resumed stream `watchEvents(harness, id, ctx, { after: 212 })`

 ```jsonc
   {
     "type": "snapshot",
     "after": 212,
     "entries": [
       { "id": 214, "kind": "pi.compaction", "head": 180, "data": { "summary": "…" } },
       { "id": 213, "kind": "pi.tool-result", "model": [{ "role": "toolResult", "toolCallId": "call_9", … }] }
     ],
     "run": { "inputs": [41] },
     "generation": { "attempt": 1, "message": { "role": "assistant", "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "The test fails because" }] } },
     "tools": [], "nestedTools": [], "compactions": [], "inbox": [],
     "agent": { … }, "usage": { … }
   }
 ```

 After the snapshot, both streams are the same:

 ```jsonc
   [{ "type": "message_update", "usage": { … }, "changes": [{ "type": "text_delta", "contentIndex": 0, "delta": " the session cookie" }] }]
   [{ "type": "message_update", "usage": { … }, "changes": [{ "type": "text_delta", "contentIndex": 0, "delta": " expires mid-test." }] }]
   [{ "type": "message_end", "entry": { "id": 215, "kind": "pi.assistant", … } },
    { "type": "turn_end" }, { "type": "run_end", "inputs": [41] }, …]
 ```

issues.title: codemode: long-running scripts in in-process subagents starve every other session (no per-session fairness, no holder info)
issues.body:
### What happened?

pi 1.4.0, Linux aarch64, default limit of 2 workers. One interactive session runs two in-process background subagents, and all three use codemode for every tool call. For about an hour, every codemode script in the parent session failed after its full 60 s wait:

```
No codemode worker became free within 60 seconds. All 2 workers, shared by every session in this process, are held by other scripts. Retry after they finish.

The script did not start.
```

Even a one-line `grep` failed this way, several times in a row. One subagent stopped its own work for the same reason. The parent could still reach the subagents through direct tools, but everything that needs bash, read or write goes through codemode, so it could do nothing. Nothing said which scripts held the workers, so there was no way to tell which subagent to steer or stop.

#11184 (fixed in 885a564b3) made the limit wait instead of failing, and `PI_CODEMODE_MAX_WORKERS` is the documented knob for in-process subagents (`docs/environment-variables.md`). That covers bursts. It does not cover long scripts. A worker keeps its slot from launch until exit (`packages/codemode/src/runtime/host.ts:30-38`), including while the script awaits a host tool such as a long `bash`. I understand from #10748 that this is intentional. Waiters sit in one FIFO with no session key (`execute.ts:72-105`). So any N long scripts from subagents hold every slot, whatever N is set to, and every other session in the process is locked out until they finish.

### What I'd like

1. **Per-session fairness at admission.** For example, a session that already holds a worker doesn't get the next free one while a session holding none is waiting, or one slot is kept back for sessions that hold none. With that, the interactive session always gets a worker within one script's run.
2. **Say who holds the workers.** The error at `execute.ts:567` gives only counts. Listing each holder's session id or label, its age, and the tool it is waiting on would let the user or the model stop or steer the holder instead of retrying blind.

### Steps to reproduce

Against 1.4.0's own `executeCodemode`, with a host tool that sleeps:

```js
import { executeCodemode } from ".../pi-coding-agent/dist/extensions/codemode/execute.js";
const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
const ctx = {
  tools: [{ name: "slow", description: "Waits N seconds", parameters: { type: "object", properties: { seconds: { type: "number" } }, required: ["seconds"] } }],
  executeTool: async (_n, a) => { await sleep(a.seconds * 1000); return { toolCall: { id: "c" + Math.random() }, result: { content: [{ type: "text", text: "ok" }], details: {} }, isError: false }; },
  sessionManager: { getBranch: () => [] }, modelRegistry: {},
};
const run = (id, code) => executeCodemode(id, { code }, undefined, undefined, ctx, {});
run("A", "return await tools.slow({ seconds: 130 })");
run("B", "return await tools.slow({ seconds: 130 })");
await sleep(2000);  run("C", "return 1");   // fails at 62 s
await sleep(61000); run("D", "return 2");   // fails at 123 s
await sleep(70000); run("E", "return 3");   // runs at 133 s, after A and B exit
```

Observed (`PI_CODEMODE_MAX_WORKERS` unset):

```
  2.0s C submitted
 62.0s C isError=true  No codemode worker became free within 60 seconds. ...
 63.0s D submitted
123.0s D isError=true  No codemode worker became free within 60 seconds. ...
130.1s A, B completed (host tool finished)
133.0s E completed in 0.0 s
```

The repro shares one context for all scripts, so it shows the pool behaviour, not separate sessions. In the real case, A and B were two in-process subagents and C, D and E were the parent session.

### Environment

- pi-coding-agent 1.4.0
- Linux aarch64
- Subagents run in-process (pi-subagents)

issues.title: perf(tui): full re-render causes scroll/typing lag in sessions with 800+ messages
issues.body:
## Problem

The TUI becomes noticeably slow (both scrolling and typing) when sessions grow large. Unlike OpenCode's OpenTUI which uses incremental cell-level diffing, Pi performs a full re-render of the entire scrollback on every interaction.

## Reproduction

- **Session:** 814 messages, 1.7MB JSONL file
- **Pi version:** 0.85.1
- **Terminal:** Kitty
- **OS:** Linux

### Symptoms
- Scrolling with mouse wheel feels laggy/not fluid
- Typing delay in the editor (visible lag between keypress and character appearing)
- Both issues appear progressively as session grows

## Root Cause Analysis

Pi's TUI does  re-render where  = total scrollback content:

```
Pi TUI render cycle:
  1. On every interaction (keypress, streaming chunk, tool result)
  2. Re-renders ENTIRE scrollback
  3. 814 messages = 814 messages to re-render every frame
```

This is documented in #5014 (auto-closed) and #6050.

### Comparison with OpenCode

OpenCode uses OpenTUI (Zig native renderer) which does incremental rendering:

```
OpenTUI:
  1. App mutates renderables
  2. Yoga computes layout
  3. Render traversal composes cells
  4. Native code DIFFS current vs next buffer
  5. Skips equal rows, only renders CHANGED cells
```

This gives OpenCode  per changed cell vs Pi's  per frame.

## What I've Tried

| Mitigation | Effect |
|------------|--------|
| `pi-render-cache` installed | Some improvement, but doesn't solve root cause |
| Regular mode (no fullscreen/sidebar) | More fluid, but loses sidebar UI |
| `/compact` | Helps but requires manual action |
| `Ctrl+O` collapse | Helps but requires manual action |

## Environment

- **Extensions:** gentle-pi 3.3.0, gentle-engram 0.1.14, pi-web-access 0.29.0, pi-mcp-adapter 2.34.0, pi-btw 0.5.0, pi-code-graph 0.16.0, pi-render-cache 1.2.0
- **Theme:** Gentleman-Sexy
- **tuiMode:** fullscreen
- **Terminal:** Kitty (Linux)

## Proposal

Consider implementing viewport-based or incremental rendering to avoid re-rendering the entire scrollback on every frame. The terminal cannot observe scroll position (POSIX limitation), but dirty-region tracking or row-level invalidation could significantly reduce the render cost.

## Related

- #5014 (auto-closed, same root cause)
- #6050 (full redraw clears scrollback)
- #4721, #4250, #369, #3785 (partial optimizations, not addressing O(n) scaling)

## Session Data

```
Session: inventario-tiendas
Messages: 814
File size: 1.7MB
Lines: 854
Pi version: 0.85.1
Node.js: 22.x
```

issues.title: Google: tool parameters using `const` are ignored by Gemini, then fail validation
issues.body:
> AI note: this report was written by Claude (an AI assistant) for @akirasosa. The behavior below was reproduced against the real Gemini API before posting.

### What happened?

On Gemini, a tool parameter declared with `const` (e.g. `Type.Literal("view")`) is unconstrained from the model's point of view. The model guesses a value (`"unknown"`, `""`), and `validateToolArguments` then rejects the call with `must be equal to constant`, every time.

The Google adapter sends the tool schema verbatim as `parametersJsonSchema` (`convertTools` in `packages/ai/src/api/google-shared.ts`). Gemini doesn't honor `const` there. The same value written as `enum: ["view"]` works.

gemini-3.8-flash, calling the API directly, 3 tries each:

- `{ const: "x" }`, `{ type: "string", const: "x" }`, `const` inside `anyOf`/`oneOf`, numeric `const`: ignored
- `{ enum: ["x"] }`, `enum` inside `anyOf`/`oneOf`, `pattern`, `minimum`/`maximum`: honored

So any `Type.Literal` or `Type.Union` of literals, and MCP schemas that use `const`, don't work on Gemini.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an `Agent` with model `google/gemini-3.8-flash` and a tool with `parameters: Type.Object({ origin: Type.Literal("zq-src-7") })`.
2. Prompt: "Call record_origin now."
3. The model sends `origin: "unknown"` and the tool result is `must be equal to constant`.

### Expected behavior

The Google adapter rewrites `const: v` to `enum: [v]` before sending (same meaning, and Gemini honors it). The comment on `convertTools` also says `parametersJsonSchema` supports `const`, which doesn't hold for current models.

### Version

1.3.0

issues.title: forkFrom copies sessions with one appendFileSync per entry, very slow on large sessions
issues.body:
### What happened?

`--fork` on a large session (73 MB, 3,322 entries) took over 30 s before pi answered any RPC, so our host timed out the handshake.

`SessionManager.forkFrom` copies the source with one `appendFileSync` per entry, so every entry reopens and closes the target file. On machines where open/close is expensive (here an endpoint security agent watching file events, ~10 ms per open/close) the fork cost becomes entries × open/close.

Same source file, the copy loop replicated standalone in Node 24 on macOS (no pi, no extensions):

- per-entry `appendFileSync` (current code): 33.5 s
- one `writeFileSync` of the joined lines: 0.19 s

With the security agent excluded for the sessions directory, the per-entry loop drops to 0.43 s, so the cost is per open/close, not data size.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Take a session with a few thousand entries.
2. Start pi with `--fork <id>` on a machine with an EDR/AV filesystem monitor.
3. The fork takes tens of seconds; nothing answers until the copy finishes.

### Expected behavior

Forking should cost about as much as loading the same file with `--session` (~1 s here). `_rewriteFile` already writes all entries through one fd; `forkFrom` could do the same, or join the lines and write once. Happy to send a PR.

### Version

issues.title: Support Stateless MCP (2026-07-28) the current latest version
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add dual-era support to `pi-mcp` for MCP 2026-07-28 over stdio and Streamable HTTP, while keeping existing servers working. 

The negotiation part is a little fiddly to get right (bad server implementations basically just require that you fail and fallback to old MCP fast - and ignore their weird responses). There is published guidance. I did this for Copilot agent runtime, and it was successful rollout, but had to be fairly thoughtful. 

AFAICT Pi currently only supports versions through 2025-11-25. With the breaking changes of the latest MCP specification we would upgrade to an optimistic server/discover probe, which is what I am proposing here.



### Why?

Support modern servers, no sessions in the new protocol, and MRTR statelessness is actually really nice once you grok it.

Selfishly, I am looking at finally supporting typed and structured outputs to GitHub MCP. We have some tools that are compound, and as the new revision also permits array and null structured results, we are gating it on the new protocol. I want Pi to be able to use it, and to use the modern protocol because we prefer it as server authors, and I really would love to make this work well for both of our sakes.


### How? (optional)

Follow the [[versioning and compatibility rules](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning).

Keep Pi’s existing result-envelope contract. Cover legacy fallback, probe timeout/late replies, modern result variants and array/null structured results/.

The [[tools specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools#structured-content)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools#structured-content) defines the output contract. [[Codex’s migration](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/44318)](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/44318) is one implementation reference.

MRTR is a little bit interesting also, to support it you need to allow for multiple requests - if you are supporting elicitation etc. it is required, but given you're primarily focused on code mode, I think you are not and so maybe you don't need MRTR at this stage.

Anyway, it'd be cool if this was supported. 🙏 

Couldn't be happier to see your announcement.

issues.title: TUI crash: unguarded undefined tool renderer child still kills Box.render in 0.83.0 (re-raise of #2627/#2934/#3209)

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What happened?

TUI crashed mid-session with `uncaughtException`, killing a ~2h session at turn 162:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'render')
    at Box.render (.../pi-tui/dist/components/box.js:62:33)
    at ToolExecutionComponent.render (.../pi-tui/dist/tui.js:99:38)
    at ToolExecutionComponent.render (.../pi-coding-agent/dist/modes/interactive/components/tool-execution.js:203:22)
    at Container.render (.../pi-tui/dist/tui.js:99:38)
    at TUI.render (.../pi-tui/dist/tui.js:99:38)
    at TUI.doRender (.../pi-tui/dist/tui.js:997:29)
```

Same crash class as #2627, #2934, #3209 — all closed, but **still present in 0.83.0**.

### The guard is still missing in 0.83.0

In `packages/coding-agent/dist/modes/interactive/components/tool-execution.js` (0.83.0), both the `callRenderer` and `resultRenderer` success paths still do:

```js
const component = callRenderer(this.args, theme, ...);
this.callRendererComponent = component;
renderContainer.addChild(component);   // no nullish guard
```

The `try/catch` only handles renderers that *throw*. A renderer that *returns `undefined`* (an extension bug, an async boundary, whatever) is pushed into `Box.children`, and the next `Box.render()` pass dereferences `undefined.render` — the whole TUI dies. As noted in #2627, we cannot hope every extension renderer is perfect; the framework should tolerate it.

### Suggested fix

In `tool-execution.ts` `updateDisplay()`: nullish-check renderer return values and fall back to `createCallFallback()` / `createResultFallback()` when the renderer returns `undefined`/`null`, not only when it throws. Optionally also harden `Box.addChild()` to reject non-Component children with a dev warning instead of crashing at render time.

### Environment

- pi 0.82.1 (crash) — verified still unguarded in 0.83.0 source
- macOS (Apple Silicon), Node bundled via npm global install
- Session context: turn 162, ~347k tokens context, several npm extensions loaded (pi-context-prune, pi-subagents, plannotator, pi-lsp-extension, etc.) — the offending renderer is likely extension-provided, but the crash should not be fatal either way
- Resume of the same session on 0.83.0 does **not** reproduce (crash happens at live render time, not during history replay)

Happy to test a patch — I have a session file that ran into this and can re-run extended sessions easily.

issues.title: env watch: a native watch dropped by the kernel (IN_IGNORED) is never re-armed when the directory keeps its inode

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Summary

On Docker Desktop for Mac bind mounts (fakeowner over virtiofs), the kernel can drop a native watch on a directory that still exists. It sends `IN_DELETE_SELF` + `IN_IGNORED`, apparently because the VM re-delivers the host's copies of events. Neither pi-durable's `NodeFileWatcher` (Linux, per-directory `fs.watch`) nor the pi-env daemon's watcher (`watch.rs`) re-arms such a watch. When they rescan, they find the same `dev`/`ino`, keep the `installed` entry and never re-add the watch, so later changes in that directory are never reported.

The root cause is in the Docker Desktop share, not in pi. But re-arming on that signal would make both watchers robust to this class of filesystem.

Seen with `@earendil-works/pi-durable` 1.2.0 and `@earendil-works/pi-env` 1.2.0.

## Where it shows up

pi-durable's env conformance case "watch follows a directory replaced at the same path", run against a pi-env daemon in a container whose cwd is a Docker Desktop bind mount, fails about 1 % of the time: `No change reported …/skills/a/y.md; got []`.

| Environment | Fails |
|---|---|
| macOS host, container tmpfs, container `/tmp` | 0 % |
| Docker Desktop bind mount, native mode | ~1 % (7/800, 3/300) |
| Same, `watch: { mode: "polling" }` | 0 % |
| Raw inotify in Python on the bind mount (script below) | 4–12 % |

Load does not matter.

## Minimal reproduction (no Node)

Run it in a container whose `/data` is a Docker Desktop for Mac bind mount: `python3 -I inotify-repro.py /data/r 300`. The script:

1. watches `skills` and `skills/a`;
2. renames `skills/a` to `skills-old`, then runs `mkdir skills/a`;
3. calls `inotify_rm_watch(old)`, then `inotify_add_watch(skills/a)`, as a snapshot watcher does;
4. writes `skills/a/y.md` twice.

A lost run shows `IN_DELETE_SELF`/`IN_IGNORED` on the new watch, and no event for the write.

<details><summary>inotify-repro.py</summary>

```python
# Issue #63 minimal reproduction, no pi-env, no Node: raw inotify in one process.
# Watches <base>/case/skills and <base>/case/skills/a; renames skills/a away, creates a new skills/a, watches it
# (as a snapshot watcher does once it sees the new inode), writes skills/a/y.md, and waits up to 3 s for an event
# on the new directory's watch. Usage: python3 -I inotify-repro.py <base> <runs> [delayBeforeWatch delayBeforeWrite]
import ctypes, ctypes.util, os, select, shutil, struct, sys, time, uuid

libc = ctypes.CDLL(ctypes.util.find_library("c") or None, use_errno=True)
IN_ALL = 0x00000FFF | 0x00000400 | 0x00000800  # all events incl. DELETE_SELF/MOVE_SELF
IN_NONBLOCK = 0o4000
fd_flags = IN_NONBLOCK


def add(fd, path):
    wd = libc.inotify_add_watch(fd, path.encode(), IN_ALL)
    if wd < 0:
        raise OSError(ctypes.get_errno(), f"inotify_add_watch {path}")
    return wd


def drain(fd, until, want_wd):
    """Read events until one for want_wd arrives (returns its latency start) or the deadline passes."""
    seen = []
    while True:
        left = until - time.monotonic()
        if left <= 0:
            return None, seen
        r, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], left)
        if not r:
            continue
        try:
            buf = os.read(fd, 65536)
        except BlockingIOError:
            continue
        i = 0
        while i < len(buf):
            wd, mask, cookie, ln = struct.unpack_from("iIII", buf, i)
            name = buf[i + 16 : i + 16 + ln].rstrip(b"\0").decode()
            seen.append((wd, hex(mask), name))
            i += 16 + ln
            if wd == want_wd and name == "y.md":
                return time.monotonic(), seen


def one(base):
    case = os.path.join(base, f"case-{uuid.uuid4()}")
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(case, "skills", "a"))
    with open(os.path.join(case, "skills", "a", "x.md"), "w") as f:
        f.write("x")
    fd = libc.inotify_init1(fd_flags)
    try:
        add(fd, os.path.join(case, "skills"))
        old_wd = add(fd, os.path.join(case, "skills", "a"))
        os.rename(os.path.join(case, "skills", "a"), os.path.join(case, "skills-old"))
        os.mkdir(os.path.join(case, "skills", "a"))
        time.sleep(DELAY_BEFORE_WATCH)
        # As the snapshot watcher does: see the new inode, drop the old directory's watch, watch the new one.
        os.listdir(os.path.join(case, "skills"))
        os.lstat(os.path.join(case, "skills", "a"))
        libc.inotify_rm_watch(fd, old_wd)
        new_wd = add(fd, os.path.join(case, "skills", "a"))
        os.listdir(os.path.join(case, "skills", "a"))
        time.sleep(DELAY_BEFORE_WRITE)
        worst = 0.0
        for content in ("y", "yy"):  # the case's step 3 (create) and step 4 (rewrite)
            t0 = time.monotonic()
            with open(os.path.join(case, "skills", "a", "y.md"), "w") as f:
                f.write(content)
            got, seen = drain(fd, t0 + 3.0, new_wd)
            if got is None:
                return None, [("lost write", content)] + seen
            worst = max(worst, got - t0)
        return worst, seen
    finally:
        os.close(fd)
        shutil.rmtree(case, ignore_errors=True)


DELAY_BEFORE_WATCH = 0.0
DELAY_BEFORE_WRITE = 0.0


def main():
    global DELAY_BEFORE_WATCH, DELAY_BEFORE_WRITE
    base, runs = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2])
    # Optional delays (seconds): between mkdir and the new watch, and between the new watch and the write.
    if len(sys.argv) > 4:
        DELAY_BEFORE_WATCH, DELAY_BEFORE_WRITE = float(sys.argv[3]), float(sys.argv[4])
    os.makedirs(base, exist_ok=True)
    lost = 0
    lat = []
    for i in range(runs):
        got, seen = one(base)
        if got is None:
            lost += 1
            print(f"run {i + 1}: LOST; events seen: {seen[-12:]}", file=sys.stderr)
        else:
            lat.append(got)
    lat.sort()
    p = lambda q: round(lat[min(len(lat) - 1, int(q * len(lat)))] * 1000, 2) if lat else None
    print(f'{{"base":"{base}","delays":[{DELAY_BEFORE_WATCH},{DELAY_BEFORE_WRITE}],"runs":{runs},"lost":{lost},"p50ms":{p(0.5)},"p99ms":{p(0.99)},"load":"{open("/proc/loadavg").read().strip()}"}}')


main()
```

</details>

## Suggestion

When a directory's watch is dropped (`IN_IGNORED`, libuv's `rename` for the watched path itself, or a watcher error) and a rescan finds the same entry, drop its `installed` record so reconcile re-adds the watch, then rescan once more.

## Our workaround

On VM-shared mounts (virtiofs statfs magic `0x6a656a63` or a `fakeowner` mount), we run a 1 s polling watcher next to the native one on the same targets.

issues.body:
### What happened?

With Claude models, `edit` calls on files containing Korean text fail very often, and occasionally corrupt a file. I have been tracking this for about three weeks. It keeps coming back and costs a lot of retries.

There are two symptoms, usually in the same sessions:

1. **Control characters instead of Korean.** The arguments contain C0 control characters where Korean characters were intended.
2. **Garbage calls.** An `edit` whose `oldText` is a few meaningless characters that exist nowhere in the file. Several in a row can occur.

Both usually fail safely as "Could not find ... oldText". Once, a corrupted `newText` was written to a file and had to be repaired by hand.

### The pattern behind symptom 1

It points to a `\uXXXX` escape whose `u` is missing in the tool-input JSON. When the next hex digit happens to be `b` or `f`, the result is still **valid JSON**: `\b` / `\f` followed by the remaining three hex digits. `JSON.parse` accepts it, so the tool runs with wrong strings instead of returning an error.

Illustration (synthetic): intended `\ub0b4` → emitted `\b0b4` → parsed as U+0008 + `0b4`.

### Evidence

Automated scan of my local session logs (edit arguments only, no file contents):

| Model | edit calls | errors | error rate | args with C0 control chars |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| openai-codex/gpt-6-astra | 398 | 9 | 2.3% | 0 |
| openai-codex/gpt-6-sol | 82 | 5 | 6.1% | 0 |
| xai/grok-4.7 | 27 | 3 | 11% | 0 |
| anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 | 212 | 86 | 40.6% | 15 |
| anthropic/claude-opus-5 | 34 | 20 | 58.8% | 8 |
| anthropic/claude-fable-5-1 | 20 | 8 | 40% | 2 |

- All control characters found in Claude edit arguments are U+0008 (`\b`) or U+000C (`\f`). 848 of 873 are followed by exactly three hex digits.
- An earlier manual classification over 20 days: 52 of 68 failed Opus 5.5 edits had lost their Korean text. GPT, Grok and DeepSeek had none.
- I found no case where `repairJson` turned an invalid escape into a literal backslash, so I don't think the repair path causes this. The corrupted cases are already valid JSON before any repair.

### What I ruled out

- **`eager_input_streaming`:** on vs off, 21 attempts each. One corrupted call in each group.
- **Session length:** I forked an affected session and ran four edits each with the default `edit`, a hash-anchored edit extension, and all extensions loaded. All 12 succeeded. On the same day, the original window failed 3 of 4.
- **Edit tool format:** the hash-anchored edit tool made no difference.
- **Encoding in general:** in the same failing window, shell edits, `write`, and a Node script inside the shell all wrote Korean correctly.

### A context effect

The failures cluster after corrupted strings have been visible in the context. In the original window, the broken calls closely resembled an example string that had just been displayed during analysis. Later, a fresh session reproduced it twice in a row right after reading notes that contained such an example. I also hit the garbage-call symptom about six times today in a long session, after the raw examples had already been removed from those notes, so removing them does not prevent it.

So this looks like a model-side tendency that feeds on its own output. I can't prove where the `u` goes missing from the client side.

### Why report it here

Even if the root cause is the model, the pi-side problem is that corruption is silent. A cheap guard would make it a normal retryable validation error:

- For `edit` / `write` (or any string tool args), reject C0 control characters other than `\t`, `\n`, `\r`, with a message like "argument contains control character U+0008; possible malformed \u escape".
- Or, in the Anthropic provider, flag `\b`/`\f` followed by hex digits in the raw `partialJson` before parsing.

If the context effect is real, the error should not echo the corrupted string back to the model. Naming the code point is probably enough.

I can write this guard as a local extension (a `tool_call` handler returning `{ block, reason }`). It seems worth handling in core, though, because every non-ASCII user on Claude is exposed to silent file corruption.

Related: #6278 (Claude tool-call schema errors, closed as model behavior). This case is narrower: non-ASCII content only, and it can corrupt files without any validation error.

### Steps to reproduce

Not deterministic. Using a Claude model, ask for several `edit` calls that replace Korean text in a UTF-8 file. It is much more likely once a corrupted string has appeared in the conversation. Failures show up as oldText mismatches whose arguments contain U+0008/U+000C, or as very short oldText values.

I can share the log-scanning script (counts only) if helpful.

### Version / environment

- pi 0.87.1 (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`), Windows, PowerShell 7
- Provider `anthropic`, Claude subscription login through the third-party `@gotgenes/pi-anthropic-auth` 3.3.2 extension. It only handles authentication, but I have not tested with an API key.

issues.title: Allow global and per-package overrides of native tool exposure in settings.json

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Let users override native extension tools’ exposure through `settings.json`, globally or per package/extension, using existing modes such as `direct`, `deferred`, and `codemode`.

In particular, let users choose **deferred by default**, with direct-exposure exceptions for selected packages. Tools should remain registered and discoverable through `tool_search` and codemode search.

### Why?

Installing a package can add substantial tool schemas and guidance to every session’s initial context, whether those capabilities are needed or not. Users cannot selectively override that exposure through standard settings; they must modify or disable the package, rely on package-specific controls, or use broad codemode-only presentation.

Users should be able to keep capabilities installed without accepting each package’s upfront context cost. A deferred-by-default policy would build on Pi’s existing tool discovery mechanisms: load schemas when needed rather than requiring every package author to opt into deferred exposure.

For example, locally changing process/debugger tools to `deferred` preserved discovery and execution without upfront declarations. That workaround is overwritten by package updates.

### How? (optional)

Apply a configurable global exposure default and per-package overrides when native tools register, including late registration and reload. Preserve `model-only` restrictions.

Related: #8583 and #9796. This request concerns user-controlled exposure, not merely disabling tools.

prs.title: fix(tui): crop boxed images scrolled above the fullscreen viewport
prs.body:
In fullscreen mode, a multi-row Kitty image inside a padded or colored `Box` disappeared completely once its first row scrolled above the viewport. It should keep showing its visible lower part, as unboxed images already do.

**Cause:** when the image line (the row with the image escape) is above the scroll window, `paintBox` in `packages/tui/src/layout.ts` walks backwards from the top visible row to find it, then draws a cropped placement. The walk stopped at the first row that was not exactly `""`. Inside a `Box`, the image's empty placeholder rows are padded with spaces and wrapped in background SGR codes, so the walk stopped before it reached the image line and nothing was drawn.

**Change:** the walk now treats a row as blank when it contains only whitespace and SGR codes.

**Testing**
- Added a test in `packages/tui/test/tui-alt-screen.test.ts`: a 3-row image inside `new Box(1, 0, bg)`, with content scrolled so the image line is above the viewport. The test checks that a cropped placement (`y=66,h=34,r=1`) is emitted. It fails without the change and passes with it.
- Ran `node --test test/tui-alt-screen.test.ts test/layout.test.ts test/terminal-image.test.ts`: 162 passed.
- `npm run check` passes.

Fixes #11271

prs.title: fix(ai): send const as enum in Gemini tool schemas
prs.body:
The Google adapters (`google-generative-ai`, `google-vertex`) sent tool schemas unchanged as `parametersJsonSchema`. TypeBox emits `const` for `Type.Literal` and for unions of literals, and the reporter found that Gemini ignores `const` there. The model then sends an arbitrary value, and argument validation rejects the call with `must be equal to constant`. According to the report, Gemini does honor `enum`.

The fix: `convertTools` in `packages/ai/src/api/google-shared.ts` now rewrites string and number `const` values to single-value `enum`s on the `parametersJsonSchema` path. Details:
- It works on a copy, so the tool's own schema, which is still used for validation, is unchanged.
- Keys inside name maps (`properties`, `$defs`, and so on) are left alone, so a property named `const` is not touched.
- Nodes that already have an `enum` are skipped.
- Boolean and null `const` values are left as they are, because Gemini documents `enum` for strings and numbers only.
- The doc comment that claimed `const` support is updated.

The legacy `parameters` path is unchanged.

Testing:
- Added a test in `packages/ai/test/google-shared-convert-tools.test.ts` covering top-level, `anyOf`, `oneOf`, `items`, a boolean `const`, and a property named `const`. It fails without the change and passes with it.
- `node ../../node_modules/vitest/dist/cli.js --run test/google` in `packages/ai`: all tests pass.
- `npm run check` passes.
- Before the change, `Type.Object({ origin: Type.Literal("zq-src-7") })` was sent as `{"type":"string","const":"zq-src-7"}`. After it, it is sent as `{"type":"string","enum":["zq-src-7"]}`.
- I could not check the model's behavior against the live Gemini API.

Fixes #11308

Requested by @davidbrai

prs.title: fix(ai): coerce JSON-encoded object and array tool arguments
prs.body:
## Summary

`validateToolArguments` recovers a tool argument the model delivered as a JSON-encoded string, for `object` and `array` parameters.

`arguments` already travels as a JSON string, so a model that mixes up the two encoding levels quotes a nested value one time too many: the outer parse succeeds and the inner value stays a string. `coercePrimitiveByType` already recovers that for every scalar type, but not for structures, so a tool whose parameter is an object or an array cannot be called at all by such a model — validation fails before the tool runs, once per `oneOf` branch:

```
Validation failed for tool "configure":
  - target: must be object
  - target: must be object
  - target: must match exactly one schema in oneOf

Received arguments:
{
  "action": "inspect",
  "target": "{\"kind\": \"agent\", \"name\": \"researcher\"}"
}
```

Reproduced on openrouter with `qwen/qwen3.8-flash`, 3/3 on two different object parameters. The scalars beside it arrive natively.

`parseStructuredString` sits next to the structural coercion rather than in `coercePrimitiveByType` — it reshapes a value instead of converting a primitive — and runs before the per-property descent so the parsed structure still gets the existing item/property coercion. It takes a string only when the schema asks for `object` or `array`, the string parses, and the result matches a type the schema accepts; otherwise the value is returned untouched and the original type error is still reported. A schema that also accepts `string` is left alone, so a caller's literal JSON-looking text is never rewritten. For example, with `type: ["string", "object"]` a JSON-encoded object stays a string, because it already matches the `string` arm; this is deliberate, so a model that sends serialized objects there keeps the string.

JSON-encoded strings on plain `properties`/`items` are decoded while optional nulls are normalized, before `Value.Convert`. The decoded structure gets the same optional-null handling as a native one, and a native TypeBox `Type.Array` does not wrap the encoded string into a one-element array. Strings decoded later inside `anyOf`/`oneOf` branches are normalized against the branch schema before descending. A union without a direct `type`, such as a native `Type.Union([Type.Array(...), Type.Null()])`, is decoded through the member that accepts the parsed structure, unless a member already accepts the string.

Refs #5697, #8757.

## Testing

- `npx vitest --run test/validation.test.ts` in `packages/ai` — 16 passed; the coercion, TypeBox array/object, native nullable-array union, and native-vs-encoded optional-null tests fail without the change
- `npm run check` — passes, rebased on current `main`
- `npx vitest --run` in `packages/ai` — same pass/fail set as `main`, plus the 6 new tests
- `npx biome check` on both changed files
- `npx tsgo --noEmit` — no new errors

prs.title: fix(tui,coding-agent): handle selection page keys in all scrolling lists
prs.body:
Fixes #7629. Supersedes #7680 by @muyiyr (co-author): same approach, rebased on current `main`, narrowed in scope, with a generic fullscreen capture flag instead of a page-key-specific one.

## Problem

`tui.select.pageUp` / `tui.select.pageDown` are configurable, but most lists ignore them:

- `SelectList` (slash commands, file autocomplete, theme/thinking pickers) and `SettingsList` (`/settings`) do not handle them.
- Editor autocomplete forwards only up/down to its list.
- Model, scoped models, auth, user message, llama search, and `/mcp` selectors have their own navigation without page keys.

In fullscreen mode there is a second problem: `tui.altScreen.pageUp/pageDown` default to the same keys and always scroll the transcript, so even a list that handles the keys never receives them.

With the remapping from the issue (`"tui.select.pageDown": "ctrl+v"`), Ctrl+V in an open autocomplete menu also pastes an image, because `app.clipboard.pasteImage` runs first.

## Changes

- `getSelectPageIndex()` (pi-tui): returns the index one page up/down, clamped to the list bounds. Used by `SelectList`, `SettingsList`, and the coding-agent selectors. Page keys clamp at the ends; up/down keep their existing wrap behavior.
- `Component.capturesViewportInput?: boolean`: while a component that sets it has focus, fullscreen viewport keys go to it instead of the transcript, the same rule focused overlays already follow on `main`. Transcript search and mouse wheel are unchanged. Set by `SelectList`, `SettingsList`, `Editor` (only while autocomplete is open), and the scrolling coding-agent selectors (session/tree selectors not while renaming or editing a label).
- `CustomEditor`: while autocomplete is open, page keys reach the menu before app actions, following the existing precedence exception for history keys.

Not set on `ctx.ui.select`, trust, first-time setup, and thinking selectors: they show every option, so there is nothing to page, and the transcript stays scrollable while answering an extension prompt (see #10769).

## Behavior change

In fullscreen mode, PageUp/PageDown (and the other viewport keys) move an open list or autocomplete menu instead of scrolling the transcript. Outside fullscreen mode, default bindings behave as before.

## Out of scope (follow-ups)

- Other selection keys vs app actions while autocomplete is open, e.g. `tui.select.up` remapped to Ctrl+P still cycles the model (#2133, #10408).
- `/resume` checks `app.session.*` before selection keys.
- Remaining hardcoded keys and key hints (scoped models Escape/Ctrl+C, `pi config` Ctrl+C, synthetic Enter in searchable submenus).
- #4748: extensions using their own pi-tui copy see default keybindings.

## Testing

- `npm run check`
- pi-tui: `SelectList`, `SettingsList`, editor autocomplete, and `TuiAltScreen` capture tests (all `node --test` pi-tui tests pass)
- coding-agent: model selector with remapped Ctrl+V/Alt+V, `CustomEditor` Ctrl+V paging vs image paste, `/mcp` menu capture

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): write forked session through one fd
prs.body:
`SessionManager.forkFrom` wrote the new header with `writeFileSync`, then called `appendFileSync` once for every copied entry. Each of those calls opens and closes the target file. Forking a 3,000-entry session therefore opened the new file about 3,000 times. Where open/close is expensive, for example under an endpoint security file monitor, a fork took tens of seconds. In the issue, a 73 MB session took over 30 s.

The change opens the new file once with `wx`, writes the header and all non-header entries through that fd, and closes it in `finally`. This is the same pattern `_rewriteFile` already uses. The `wx` flag still makes the fork fail if the target file already exists.

Testing:
- Added `test/session-manager/fork-from.test.ts`. It forks a 50-entry session and checks three things: the new file is opened for writing exactly once (`wx`), `appendFileSync` is never called on it, and the content is copied unchanged. The test fails without the fix and passes with it.
- All tests in `test/session-manager/` pass, and `npm run check` passes.
- Ran `strace -e openat` while forking a synthetic 3,000-entry session. Before the fix the target file was opened 3,002 times; after it, 2 times (one write, one load).

Fixes #11253

Requested by @davidbrai

prs.title: fix(ai): do not count faux cache writes as input tokens
prs.body:
With a `sessionId` (and `cacheRetention` other than `"none"`), the faux provider simulates prompt caching. It reported the tokens it counted as `cacheWrite` in `input` too, so `input + cacheRead + cacheWrite` came out larger than the estimated prompt. For example, a prompt of about 1002 tokens reported `input: 1002, cacheWrite: 1002` on the first request.

`withUsageEstimate()` now puts every prompt token in exactly one bucket. On the first request it all goes to `cacheWrite`. On later requests it goes to `cacheRead` for the cached prefix and `cacheWrite = promptTokens - cacheRead` for the rest. `input` is 0 while caching is simulated, which matches how real providers leave cache reads and writes out of `input`. Behavior without a session ID, or with `cacheRetention: "none"`, does not change.

**Testing**
- `packages/ai/test/faux-provider.test.ts`: the prefix-caching test now asserts the first request (`input: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 4`) and expects `input: 0` on later requests. Without the source change it fails; with it, all 24 tests pass.
- The issue's script, before: `{ input: 1002, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 1002 }`, then `{ input: 105, cacheRead: 1002, cacheWrite: 106 }` on a second turn. After: `{ input: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 1002 }`, then `{ input: 0, cacheRead: 1002, cacheWrite: 105 }`.
- `npm run check` passes.
- `./test.sh` has failures in `classifier-models`, `cloudflare-workers-ai-system-one` and `model-runtime-classifiers`. These files fail the same way on unmodified `main`.
- The durable files that use faux would not load until I rebuilt. After `npm run build`, the durable suite passes (1350 tests).

Fixes #11301

Requested by @davidbrai

prs.title: feat(coding-agent): show model names in model selectors when they add information
prs.body:
closes #5916

`/model` and `/scoped-models` listed only `id [provider]`, so a renamed override from `models.json` was invisible in the list:

```
minimax/minimax-m3 [openrouter]
```

Rows now show the name in parentheses when it adds information:

```
minimax/minimax-m3 (MiniMax M3 [rasmus@openrouter, parasail]) [openrouter]
claude-sonnet-4-5 [anthropic]
```

A name is shown only if it has a word the ID lacks. Ignoring case and punctuation alone was too noisy: 850 of the 1710 built-in models showed a name, mostly because IDs carry a namespace or version suffix the name drops (`eu.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0` vs "Claude Sonnet 4.5 (EU)"). With the word check, 152 show a name, mostly useful ones like `gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image (Nano Banana 2 Lite)` or `mistral-small-2603 (Mistral Small 4)`. Single-character words must match a whole ID word, so the `4` in "Mistral Small 4" is not covered by `2603`.

Other parts of #5916:
- Search by name was already in place (6d5ede31c).
- Ranking real matches above scattered ones was fixed in #11296.
- Scattered matches (`luna` matching sonnet) are still listed, below real matches. Hiding them can drop useful results, and with the fixed ranking they no longer push real matches down.
- The provider `extends` / `upstreamId` proposal is tracked separately in https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11346.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): exit with a clear error for unusable proxy URLs
prs.body:
## Summary

- An `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` value that undici cannot use, such as `socks5h://...`, a URL without a scheme, or a URL with a path, crashed startup with undici's `Invalid URL protocol` error and a Node stack. The same happened for the `httpProxy` setting.
- `configureHttpDispatcher()` now catches the error from `EnvHttpProxyAgent` and throws `Invalid proxy URL in HTTPS_PROXY. Use an http://, https://, or socks5:// URL without a path.` The CLI and RPC entry points, plus the startup path that applies the `httpProxy` setting, print it as one `Error:` line and exit 1.
- The message names the variable undici reads (a defined lowercase variable wins), or `the httpProxy setting` when that setting supplied the value. It omits the URL and undici's message. The original error can carry the URL with credentials, because `ERR_INVALID_URL` keeps it in `input`.
- undici still decides which URLs it accepts; pi does not validate proxy URLs itself, so anything undici accepts keeps working. `socks5://` already works through undici 8.10 and sends hostnames to the proxy, which covers what `socks5h://` is used for. I did not map `socks5h` to `socks5` or fall back to a direct connection, because either would silently change what the user configured.

Fixes #11195

## Validation

Before, on main:

```
$ HTTPS_PROXY=socks5h://127.0.0.1:8081 pi --version
node_modules/undici/lib/core/util.js:229
    throw new InvalidArgumentError('Invalid URL protocol: the URL must start with `http:` or `https:`.')
          ^

InvalidArgumentError: Invalid URL protocol: the URL must start with `http:` or `https:`.
    at parseURL (node_modules/undici/lib/core/util.js:229:11)
    ...
    at new EnvHttpProxyAgent (node_modules/undici/lib/dispatcher/env-http-proxy-agent.js:35:32)
    at configureHttpDispatcher (packages/coding-agent/src/core/http-dispatcher.ts:87:3)
    ...
  code: 'UND_ERR_INVALID_ARG'
```

After:

```
$ HTTPS_PROXY=socks5h://127.0.0.1:8081 pi --version
Error: Invalid proxy URL in HTTPS_PROXY. Use an http://, https://, or socks5:// URL without a path.

$ HTTPS_PROXY=socks5://127.0.0.1:8081 pi --version
```

prs.title: fix(examples): todo renderResult returns undefined on validation errors
prs.body:
A `todo` call that fails schema validation crashes the whole TUI in interactive mode.

For a validation failure `details` is `{}` (a truthy empty object), so `renderResult` skips both `if (!details)` and `if (details.error)`, then `switch (details.action)` has no `default` and returns `undefined`. `ToolExecutionComponent.updateDisplay()` then calls `addChild(undefined)`, and the next render pass throws:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'render')
    at Box.render (pi-tui/dist/components/box.js:62:33)
```

`pi -p` is unaffected (the agent loop recovers; only the TUI render crashes).

Add a `default` case to render the validation error:

```ts
default:
    return new Text(
        result.content[0]?.type === "text" ? theme.fg("error", result.content[0].text) : "",
        0,
        0,
    );
```

Scoped to the example; the framework-level "tolerate a renderer returning `undefined`" question is tracked in #2627 / #7291.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): preserve split UTF-8 output in pi.exec
prs.body:
Fixes #11312.

pi.exec() decodes each stdout and stderr chunk independently with Buffer.toString(). When a UTF-8 character spans chunk boundaries, "你好" becomes "���好" even though the command exits successfully.

This change gives stdout and stderr separate StringDecoder instances and flushes both before returning on success or error. This also handles waitForChildProcess() destroying inherited pipes without a normal stream-end event. The return structure, exit codes, and cancellation behavior remain unchanged.

Regression tests use controlled chunks rather than timing delays. They cover three- and four-byte characters, interleaved streams, BOM preservation, and incomplete trailing sequences.

Validation:
- All eight execCommand tests pass; the three chunk-splitting cases fail without the fix.
- npm run check passes.

Before #11326 was opened, I had already shared this fix and its branch in the issue discussion. PR #11326 plagiarized my code, and it was not submitted by me. This PR contains the fix from my original branch, with deterministic regression coverage. Please consider merging my version.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): decode pi.exec output across UTF-8 chunk boundaries
prs.body:
`execCommand()` (the function behind `pi.exec()`) decoded each stdout and stderr chunk on its own with `data.toString()`. When a multi-byte UTF-8 character was split across two pipe chunks, each half was turned into U+FFFD, so the result was corrupted. For example, `"你好"` came back as `"���好"` while the command still exited with code 0.

This change gives stdout and stderr each their own `StringDecoder("utf8")`. A decoder holds back incomplete bytes until the rest of the character arrives. Both decoders are flushed with `end()` before the promise resolves, on both the success path and the error path. `waitForChildProcess()` can resolve without a stream `end` event, so the decoders are flushed there and not in an `end` handler. The return shape, exit codes, and kill behavior are unchanged.

**Testing**
- Added a regression test to `packages/coding-agent/test/exec.test.ts`. The child process splits `"你好"` across two writes on both stdout and stderr. The test fails without the fix and passes with it: `node ../../node_modules/vitest/dist/cli.js --run test/exec.test.ts` reports 3 passed.
- `npm run check` passes.
- Reproduction from the issue: a child that writes the first byte of `"你好"` and then the rest 100 ms later. Before the fix the result was `{"stdout":"���好",...}`. After the fix it is `{"stdout":"你好","stderr":"","code":0,"killed":false}`.

Fixes #11312

Requested by @davidbrai

prs.title: fix(tui): stop nested blockquote rendering from growing exponentially
prs.body:
**Problem.** A line of many `>` characters makes `marked` produce one nested blockquote token per `>`. The blockquote branch of `Markdown.renderToken` renders its children at `Math.max(1, width - 2)` columns, then wraps each child line again at that width and adds a `│ ` prefix.

Once the nesting uses up the width (about 39 levels at 80 columns), the width stays clamped at 1. From then on, each child line (`│ x`, 3 columns wide) is wrapped into about 3 lines at every further level, so the output roughly triples per level. At 80 columns:

- 50 levels: 4096 lines, about 30 s to render;
- 55 levels: `push(...lines)` exceeds the JavaScript argument limit and throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`, which crashes pi. Reopening the session crashes it again.

**Fix.**
- When there is no room left for another border (`width < 3`), the blockquote branch now renders its child tokens at the same width without adding a border and without wrapping them again.
- Child lines are appended with a loop instead of a spread `push`.

Quotes that fit in the width render exactly as before.

**Testing.**
- Added a regression test in `packages/tui/test/markdown.test.ts`: 60 nested `>` rendered at width 80 give one line that keeps the content. Without the fix the test fails with the RangeError; with it, all 92 tests in that file pass (`node --test test/markdown.test.ts`).
- `npm run check` passes.
- Reproduction script rendering `">".repeat(n) + "x"` at width 80:
  - before: 50 levels gave 4096 lines in 29.5 s, and 55 or 60 levels threw a RangeError;
  - after: 40, 50, 60 and 200 levels each give 1 line in about 10 ms.

**Not covered.** A run of about 2000 `>` still overflows the stack inside `marked`'s own lexer, before pi's renderer runs. That is a separate limit and is not changed here.

Fixes #11272

Requested by @davidbrai

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): start when a configured package fails to install
prs.body:
## Summary

- A package configured in settings that cannot be installed no longer aborts startup. Resource resolution records the failure per source, skips that package the way offline mode does, and loads the packages that do install.
- The failure is reported through the extension warning channel: `Extension package "npm:...": failed to install (...). Run "pi remove npm:..." to remove it from settings.json.` Project entries point at `pi remove <source> --local`. Temporary `-e` sources are skipped the same way, with a hint to check the source.
- `--help` and `--list-models` now report runtime diagnostics, so the warning appears on every command the issue lists. Diagnostics go to stderr and exit codes are unchanged.
- A source that failed once is not retried for the rest of the process. Startup resolves packages twice when project trust is resolved, so without that a failing package cost a second npm attempt and printed npm's error twice.
- `pi install` and `pi update --extensions` still report the failure and exit non-zero. `pi config` prints the warning too, so a skipped package is not silently missing from the list.
- `docs/packages.md` documents the behavior.

Fixes #11088

## Validation

- Repro from the issue on unmodified main (936e5f40): `pi -p hello`, `pi --help` and `pi --list-models` all exit 1 with `Error: npm install @example/definitely-not-a-real-pkg-xyz --prefix /tmp/p/agent/npm --legacy-peer-deps failed with code 1` and a raw Node stack. With this branch: one warning line, startup continues, `--help` and `--list-models` exit 0.
- A healthy local package next to the broken npm entry still loads: its `--good-pkg-flag` appears in `--help`.
- `git:github.com/example/definitely-not-a-real-repo` warns, is skipped, and leaves no partial checkout under `<agentDir>/git`.
- `pi install npm:@example/definitely-not-a-real-pkg-xyz` and `pi update --extensions` still exit 1 with a single error line.
- With a trusted project and a failing project package the hint is `pi remove <source> --local`. An untrusted project never installs the package and prints nothing.
- Interactive startup shows the warning and continues.
- `npm run check`
- `node "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/node_modules/vitest/dist/cli.js" --run test/package-manager.test.ts test/resource-loader.test.ts` from `packages/coding-agent` (190 tests).
- `./test.sh` was run. The affected tests pass. Baseline failures in this environment, all present on unmodified main or environmental: `test/auth-storage.test.ts` "keeps a coalesced reload alive while another credential reader is waiting" (also fails on main), `packages/env` ssh suites (the Rust daemon is not built locally), and `packages/durable` timeouts under load (pass when rerun in isolation).

prs.title: Run a turn's tool calls one at a time from outside the loop
prs.body:
# Run a turn's tool calls one at a time, from outside the loop

## Problem

`AgentSession.prompt()` runs an entire turn: the model call, every tool call the model asked
for, and the next model call, all the way to a final answer. There is no way to run *one* tool
call and return to the caller in between.

That matters for durable execution. Temporal, for example, wants each unit of non-deterministic
work to be its own activity. With `prompt()` as the only entry point, either the whole turn is
one activity, or the tool calls are not durable at all.

```ts
// Today: all or nothing.
await session.prompt("read foo.txt and tell me what it says");
```

## Change

Two additions to `AgentSession`, no removals, no behavior change to `prompt()`:

| Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `getPendingToolCalls(): AgentToolCall[]` | The calls the last assistant message asked for that have no result yet, in the order the model asked for them. |
| `runToolCallById(toolCallId, options?): Promise<ToolResultMessage \| undefined>` | Runs one pending call by id through the same pipeline `prompt()` uses. Returns `undefined` if no pending call has that id, so a repeat is a no-op rather than a duplicate result. |

`runToolCallById` goes through argument preparation, schema validation, `beforeToolCall`,
execution, and `afterToolCall`, and emits the same `tool_execution_start` / `tool_execution_update`
/ `tool_execution_end` events. A turn driven one call at a time records the same transcript as
`prompt()`.

The first commit is a pure refactor of `packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts` that splits one loop
iteration into `runSingleTurn` and its phases into `runTurnModelCall`, `runTurnToolCall`, and
`sealTurnStep`. No behavior change; it makes the per-piece entry points readable.

## Usage

```ts
const pending = session.getPendingToolCalls();
for (const call of pending) {
  const result = await session.runToolCallById(call.id);
  console.log(call.name, result?.isError);
}
```

## What this does not do

- It does not make `prompt()` interactive. A caller that wants to drive a turn one call at a
  time still does its own model calls.
- It does not add anything Temporal-specific to the core. There is no new dependency, no new
  option, and no new event type.
- It does not change the session file format.

## Tests

- `packages/coding-agent/test/suite/agent-session-step-tool-call.test.ts` — a single call runs
  through the pipeline, an unknown id is a no-op, and pending calls are listed in model order.
- `packages/coding-agent/test/suite/step-driver.test.ts` — drives a two-call turn one call at a
  time and asserts the resulting order and that nothing is left pending.

```
$ npm run check        # passes
$ ./test.sh            # 48/49
```

The one `./test.sh` failure is `scripts/preview-packages.test.mjs`, which also fails on clean
`origin/main` and is unrelated to this change.

## Why this is the smallest useful seam

The alternative considered was a broader `prepareStep` / `sealStep` / `recordPrompt` API on
`AgentSession`. It turned out to be unnecessary: `runToolCall` was already exported from
`packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts` and already imported by `agent-session.ts`. The missing piece
was only the by-id entry point and the pending-call query, so that is all this adds.

issues.body:
## Problem

Main E2E uses ref-scoped concurrency that can replace older pending runs even when cancel-in-progress is false. A later tested tree includes earlier changes, but does not supply an independent result for each intermediate main SHA. The goal is to preserve per-SHA validation and failure attribution.

## Correction to the initial report

The title's “one merge in ten” and subsequent 11–21% coverage estimates are withdrawn. They used an incomplete repository-wide run page and, in some rounds, a stale local main denominator. A job record does not establish test execution; skipped and queued jobs must be distinguished. The claim that all sampled cancelled runs had zero jobs was also not verified for all of them.

The proposed reserved-runner remedy does not bypass workflow concurrency. For [39579111088](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/39579111088), the final job ended at 2026-10-21T10:17:11Z; [39580495703](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/39580495703) began Build for E2E at 10:17:15Z, four seconds later. That is consistent with serialization. Creation-to-first-job delay must not be reported as hosted runner queue time.

A few successful runs do not prove the failures tracked in #15022 are resolved. Failure diagnosis and scheduling coverage are separate questions.

## Proposed direction

Evaluate adding the main push SHA to the concurrency key while retaining non-cancellation of running main validations. Leave other event/ref semantics unchanged. This preserves independent scheduling opportunities; it does not guarantee immediate runner availability or successful tests.

Assess resource demand using actual job overlap and runner occupancy. Previous predictions that 2–4 lanes would create 20 queued jobs, or that a daytime idle snapshot makes the change safe, are withdrawn.

Investigate E2E step-level durations independently of the CI Test job. Shortening the E2E critical path may help; sharding and moving the hosted build are candidates only after measurement. Reserved self-hosted capacity alone cannot remove concurrency-group waiting. No sharding speedup or capacity benefit is assumed.

## Evidence and acceptance still needed

- Fully paginate this workflow's main push runs over a fixed time window; join by SHA and distinguish created jobs, allocated jobs, actual test execution, completed runs and success.
- Compare with an independently verified set of eligible main SHAs before publishing coverage percentages.
- Measure build and sandbox steps, runner occupancy and peak overlap. Retain the existing hosted build placement until a supported comparison warrants changing it.
- A later main push must not replace an earlier pending validation; running main validations remain intact. Results remain attributable to their SHA.

No main concurrency or branch-protection changes have been made. #14859 tracks broader capacity; #15022 tracks test failures; #12274 tracks artifact failures; #10254 records the separate merge-queue decision.

## Goal and corrected status

Track CI capacity and preserve independent validation opportunities for main pushes. This body replaces preliminary claims that mixed incomplete run samples, job records and actual execution. Earlier percentage estimates and slot forecasts in this thread should not be used for decisions.

## 1–2. Non-approval review gate work — fixed

#14857 merged and addresses #14854. Non-approval review events still create workflow runs and skipped checks; the guarded jobs do not execute. The earlier statement that the runs stop existing was incorrect. The claimed superseded-review totals and savings percentages were not adequately verified and are withdrawn.

## 3. Independent main validation — investigation / decision pending

Ref-scoped concurrency can replace an older pending run even when cancel-in-progress is false. Later successful trees include earlier changes, but do not provide an independent result for every intermediate SHA. The objective is per-SHA failure attribution, not merely a recent green tree. E2E is tracked separately in #15052.

Per-SHA main push grouping is the preferred candidate for preserving validation opportunities. Capacity must be measured separately; no concurrency change has been made. Test sharding is an option, not an established prerequisite. Preserve required check names and failure propagation if restructuring jobs; a branch-protection change is not inherently required.

The sampled CI run [39939451419](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/39939451419) had a Test job spanning approximately 70 minutes and Lint approximately 34 minutes. These are job durations, not isolated test execution times. Its creation-to-first-job gap does not establish runner starvation. CI Test and E2E sandbox jobs are different critical paths.

## 4. Hosted traffic — measure before rerouting

Collect hosted queued jobs across queued, pending and in-progress runs. Do not infer the account's concurrency entitlement from observed running jobs or treat queued-job started_at as a reliable queue-entry timestamp. Preserve untrusted-fork isolation; moving jobs to self-hosted runners requires a separate security and capacity assessment. Related: #10038, #14219.

## 5. Failure-report traffic — investigate trigger cost separately from issue deduplication

Main CI Failure Issue traffic can consume runner time. Existing failure-signature handling means this is not established as missing issue deduplication. Inspect triggers, existing signature handling and reporting guarantees before proposing concurrency or runner changes. Do not suppress valid failure reports.

## 6. Historical queued records — unresolved operational anomaly

Identify old records by actual run/job IDs and dates. Do not subtract fixed counts from future samples. Normal cancellation previously returned HTTP 409 for sampled old runs; cancellation is not a demonstrated remedy. No further cancellations are authorized here.

## 7. Review schedule and capacity

Day/night label allocation changes which jobs can run. Scheduled waiting remains user-visible queueing. Report online/busy/idle registrations by matching label; registrations and physical machines are not interchangeable. A single idle snapshot does not prove spare sustained capacity.

## Next work and acceptance

- Fully paginate each workflow over a fixed window and join main push runs by head SHA. Distinguish job records, allocated execution, actual test steps, completion and success; do not report per-merge coverage without a verified denominator.
- Inspect step-level durations separately for CI and E2E, then assess runner-minutes and peak overlap before selecting an optimization.
- Evaluate per-SHA grouping against the requirement that a later main push must not replace an earlier pending validation. Keep running validations intact and preserve failure attribution.
- No main concurrency, branch-protection or merge-queue policy changes are made by this tracking update.

Related: #14854 / #14857 (fixed gate work), #15052 (E2E), #14743 / #14912 (SDK Java lock work), #14392, #10254 (merge queue decision).
