### Architecture and ownership

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    UI[WebShell / product client] -->|Product REST and SSE| J[Java control plane]
    J -->|Session / Prompt / Resume| Q[qwen serve]
    Q --> L[Legacy engine / ACP]
    Q --> H[Managed TS Harness]
    H --> M[Model service]
    H -->|Tool requests and results| B[Embedded Runtime Broker]
    B -->|Java-initiated HTTP and SSE| R[On-demand Tool Runtime]
```

The Broker is embedded in the Java service in the hosted reference deployment. `qwen serve` keeps the common Session protocol and hosts the Legacy/Managed engines; the Harness owns the single model loop, context, compaction, and tool orchestration. The Runtime owns files, Shell, and admitted tool-side effects. It receives neither the user Prompt nor model credentials. Local Managed uses a local Runtime provider and does not require Java.

Hosted deployment starts with one Java instance plus a `qwen serve` sidecar and a default Session-exclusive Runtime process/Pod; #14435 adds separately gated Workspace residency. Model inference uses a pre-published immutable AgentBundle while Runtime provisioning proceeds in parallel; only tool execution waits for readiness. Multiple Sessions may share the Harness process without sharing their model context or permission view.

### Proposed decisions

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Area | Proposed behavior | Detailed design |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Engine selection and identity | Persist Legacy/Managed ownership before the first side effect. Managed failure never reruns through Legacy. Use one RFC UUID `sessionId` across public API, qwen authority, Harness, transcript, and Broker scope. | [Engine selection][engine], [architecture][architecture] |
| Admission and interaction | Keep the existing Harness-confirmed product admission (named `harness_confirmed` in the in-repo contract and `qwen_confirmed` in the pinned reference design). The opt-in `java_durable` input/cancel profile landed in #14470 after durable delivery and original-command reconciliation; other operation/Turn fields retain their declared status. Retries retain identity; approvals/questions resolve through the original arbiter. | [Admission, Actions, lifecycle][contracts] |
| Ordinary tools | Preserve prepare, approval, preflight, execute, original-execution query, result commit/ACK, and file-history settlement. An ambiguous side effect blocks recovery instead of being replayed on a new Runtime. Cancellation is complete only with physical stop evidence. | [First release][first], [tool integration][tools] |
| Workspace and cwd | At creation, select an authorized registered Workspace and optional relative directory, defaulting to `.`. Commit the binding with the creation receipt. Broker resolves the physical mount from that binding; refresh, retry, default changes, and restart do not rebind the Session. | [Workspace: English][workspace-en] / [中文][workspace-zh] |
| Storage and live delivery | Accept bounded event batches and source progress in one SQL transaction, then immediately push committed events through Java SSE. Async materialization builds Items/Snapshots. Reconnect uses Session sequence plus snapshot/tail recovery; GC needs settled consumers and recovery/reader retention checks. | [Storage and events][storage], [delivery contracts][contracts] |
| Database and MQ adapters | Keep business transaction semantics behind storage interfaces: MySQL first, PostgreSQL as another implementation. Use SQL-only delivery initially; an optional EventTransport can use RocketMQ or Redis Streams for notifications/async distribution. MQ is not on the synchronous frontend path or the authority for model history. | [Storage boundaries][storage] |
| Runtime and Harness recovery | Persist Broker binding/execution facts, reconcile and attest physical Runtime identity, and fence old writers. Persisting metadata alone does not prove recovery. Full shared Session authority/checkpoint storage and replaceable Harness belong to stage G. | [Broker persistence][broker], [Session storage][session-storage], [recovery][recovery] |
| Full tool output and artifacts | Keep captured bytes, exact model-consumed results, and public previews distinct. Persist large bytes as immutable objects/segments with digests and receipts; SQL holds metadata/previews. WebShell reads bounded ranges/downloads. Execution success and capture/delivery completeness are separate states. | [Tool results: English][outputs-en] / [中文][outputs-zh] |
| Public API and WebShell | Version Session/list/query, Prompt/cancel, Actions, Turns/Items, events/replay, Workspace discovery, and artifact reads. Preserve the browser-to-Java boundary. Generate compatible DTOs from the reviewed OpenAPI and enable capabilities only after contract tests. | [API contract][api], [OpenAPI v1.12][openapi] |
| Extensions | Harness remains the model-loop owner. Add durable domain records and task projections before migrating MCP, Hooks, background Shell/Monitor, child agents/workflows/teams, Channels, and automation. Each feature needs its own admission, receipt, cancellation, quota, and recovery checks. | [Extension runtime][extensions] |

The event path is **Harness SSE → Java bounded batch → SQL commit → Java SSE → browser**. SQL delivery/Outbox work can separately notify MQ consumers and materialize history. SQL failure therefore blocks new event acceptance; this proposal does not promise unlimited buffering through a database outage. Full tool bytes do not belong in token-event rows, SSE frames, or MQ payloads.

### Initial release boundary

The first hosted validation slice uses a single Java/sidecar deployment, immutable published configuration, a Session-exclusive Runtime, and Read/Write/Edit/foreground Shell. Member collaboration is not a release prerequisite for this slice. Board #13928, peer messaging #13955 and plan approval #13974 have landed upstream; plan enablement and collaboration deployment promotion remain optional and behind their own acceptance gates. Approval, durable results/file history, cancellation cleanup, and safe continuation after clean Runtime reclamation remain required. Existing product SSE/history can serve this slice; the full public API, multi-instance takeover, and extension migration have separate gates.

W0 adds Workspace selection and fixed cwd. W1 restore/backfill/verified mount relocation and W2 controlled same-Workspace cwd changes have landed within their recorded boundaries. Later authorized directory creation/registration is implemented by the Workspace/SSH slices above. Arbitrary server-path registration, clone/worktree creation, and changing existing Sessions' directories are outside W0. Sessions using the same Workspace share files, so their tool turns need the existing Workspace lease/settlement discipline.

Accepted recovery/support policy for the first release is one Java control plane on one trusted Linux host, with sequential compatible Hosted Harness replacement only for supported and accepted states. Public CSI/Pod qualification, two surviving control planes and cross-host takeover retain independent gates. The experimental server/embedded-Broker archive is implemented in #14176, while publication and formal support remain separate. Parent-close active child cancellation is implemented by #14218. Stream liveness is completed by #14512 (`46bf492d05`); deployment wait/retention/capacity values still need measured acceptance.

### Delivery plan

These are capability stages, not one mandatory linear mega-change. A/C/E, the shared B ownership/no-fallback guarantees, and the necessary F checks form the first runnable Hosted slice; completing all of D or promoting the optional ordinary-host Managed engine is not a prerequisite for that slice.

| Stage | Deliverable and exit gate |
| --- | --- |
| A | Freeze identities, contracts, ownership, and baseline latency measurements. |
| B | Persist engine ownership and reject runtime engine fallback. Paired-host B2 and M1–M6 are implemented, with M6 registration in #14483 behind `--experimental-paired-engines`; #12737 is closed; default enablement and full local acceptance remain separate. |
| C | Integrate Broker binding/execution repositories, leases, Runtime transport, and original-execution lookup. |
| D | Deliver the public Agent API, durable admission profile, projections, replay, and compatible client contracts. |
| E | Run the hosted sidecar profile with inference/provisioning in parallel and no local-tool fallback. |

Workspace implementation is split into **W0a contracts/Registry → W0b durable creation → W0c execution-directory wiring → W0d WebShell → W0e restart/reclamation validation**. Full-output delivery is **O1 capture/reference contracts → O2 hosted persistence/receipt recovery → O3 API/tool cards → O4 retention and admitted extensions**. These refine the stages above rather than creating competing roadmaps.

### Acceptance criteria

- The adopted staged path-independence matrix is a release gate: Hosted proves its bounded scope with ordinary local-only state unreachable; local now requires its M6 exit acceptance under the opt-in; shared dependencies are inventoried before the run. No existing component or recovery report substitutes for this gate.
- With Runtime startup delayed by 15 seconds, published-configuration model output starts first; a no-tool Turn can finish, and a tool Turn waits and continues in the same model context.
- Sessions retain their engines after restore; a Managed failure causes no Legacy replay. Ordinary-host Legacy/Managed coexistence is an acceptance gate for local support promotion, not the first Hosted slice.
- Lost create/Prompt/execute/ACK responses resolve through original identities without duplicating side effects. Unknown outcomes remain explicitly blocked.
- Two Workspaces and different child directories execute Read/Write/Shell in the intended locations. A retry after changing defaults keeps the original binding; missing mounts or revoked access never fall back to another directory.
- Java restart and clean Runtime reclamation retain the Session binding; physical identity is verified before reuse, and old writers cannot mutate a newer binding.
- Committed SSE replay and Snapshot-plus-tail recovery preserve order without duplicate content. MQ delay cannot block local post-commit SSE; SQL unavailability is surfaced with bounded backpressure.
- Large output can be read/downloaded after Runtime cleanup. WebShell distinguishes tool outcome, partial/missing capture, delivery failure, and truncated preview; storage failure never causes tool re-execution.
- Cancellation settles admitted tools and descendant processes. Production enablement additionally requires actor/tenant isolation, capacity limits, and the fault gates for the selected deployment profile.

## Why is this needed?

Hosted execution should not make the first model response wait for a tool container. Splitting the model loop from tools, however, creates ownership and recovery boundaries: a selected directory must survive process changes, an ambiguous tool call must not run twice, and a browser reconnect must recover committed progress. Permanent per-fragment storage also grows without a retention/materialization plan, while Runtime-local output disappears when the environment is reclaimed.

This proposal joins those boundaries into one implementable contract while preserving Qwen's existing agent semantics and local deployment. It gives reviewers a scoped rollout and observable exit gates instead of treating an experimental branch or a passing component test as the finished product.

### 架构与职责

链路为：产品前端 → Java 控制面 → qwen serve → Legacy 或 Managed Harness；Managed Harness 调用模型，并通过 Java 内嵌 Runtime Broker 调用按需 Tool Runtime。Java 主动发起到 Runtime 的 HTTP/SSE。上方架构图展示同一链路。

Java 内嵌 Broker；qwen serve 保留统一会话协议与双引擎；Harness 负责唯一模型循环、上下文、压缩及工具编排；Runtime 负责文件、Shell 和已准入的工具副作用，不接收用户 Prompt 或模型凭据。本地 Managed 使用本地 Runtime provider，不依赖 Java。

托管首版采用单 Java + qwen serve Sidecar + 默认 Session 独占 Runtime 进程/Pod；#14435 增加独立门禁下的 Workspace 常驻。模型使用预发布不可变 AgentBundle，与环境启动并行；只有工具执行等待环境就绪。多个 Session 可共享 Harness 进程，但不共享模型上下文或权限视图。

### 首版范围

首版采用单实例、预发布不可变配置、Session 独占 Runtime，验收 Read/Write/Edit/前台 Shell。成员协作不作为该首版交付前置；board #13928、成员消息 #13955 与计划审批 #13974 均已在上游合入，计划启用与协作部署开放继续可选并遵循各自验收门禁；审批、结果/文件历史持久保存、取消清理、干净回收后的续轮仍是必需项。可复用既有产品 SSE/历史；完整公共 API、多实例接管和扩展迁移各有独立门槛。

W0 支持创建时选择 Workspace 并固定 cwd；W1 恢复、存量回填、可验证挂载迁移，以及 W2 同 Workspace 内受控切换目录已按各自边界合入。后续授权目录创建/注册已由上方 Workspace/SSH 切片实现。W0 不提供任意服务器路径注册、clone/worktree 创建或已有 Session 目录编辑。同 Workspace 的会话共享文件，工具轮次需要遵守 Workspace 租约与结算规则。

首版已接受的恢复/支持策略为单 Java 控制面、同一可信 Linux 主机，仅在已支持且验收的状态下顺序替换兼容 Hosted Harness。公开 CSI/Pod 资格、两个存活控制面与跨主机接管保留独立门禁。实验 Server/嵌入式 Broker 归档已在 #14176 实现，公开发布与正式支持独立。父关闭主动取消 child 已由 #14218 实现；流存活检测已由 #14512（`46bf492d05`）收尾，部署等待/留存/容量数值仍需实测验收。

### 验收标准

- 已采纳的分阶段路径独立性矩阵是交付门禁：Hosted 在普通本地专属状态不可达时证明限定范围，本地路径现在需在 opt-in 下完成 M6 退出验收，运行前列出共享依赖；既有组件或恢复报告不能替代该门禁。
- Runtime 延迟 15 秒时，使用预发布配置的模型输出先返回；无工具轮次可完成，有工具轮次等待后继续同一模型上下文。
- 会话恢复后引擎不变，Managed 失败不经 Legacy 重放。普通宿主的 Legacy/Managed 共存属于本地支持提升的验收门槛，不是首个 Hosted 闭环的前置条件。
- 创建、Prompt、执行或 ACK 响应丢失时按原身份查询，不重复副作用；未知结果明确 blocked。
- 两个工作区和不同子目录的 Read/Write/Shell 位置正确；改变默认值后的重试仍保持原绑定，目录失效/撤权不回退其他目录。
- Java 重启与 Runtime 干净回收后保持 Session 绑定，复用前验证物理身份，旧 writer 不能修改新绑定。
- 已提交 SSE 与 Snapshot+tail 恢复保持顺序且不重复内容；MQ 延迟不阻塞本机提交后推送；SQL 不可用时有界背压并呈现失败。
- Runtime 清理后大输出仍可读取/下载；工具结果、部分/缺失捕获、交付失败及预览裁剪分别展示，存储失败不触发工具重跑。
- 取消能结算已准入工具并清理后代进程；生产开放前另验收 actor/tenant 隔离、容量限制及所选部署的故障门槛。

## 为什么需要

托管工具容器的启动不应阻塞模型首输出，但分离模型与工具后，目录归属、执行恢复和客户端续传必须有清晰边界：所选目录要跨进程保留，不确定的工具不能重复执行，断线客户端要找回已提交进度。永久逐片段保存会持续膨胀，Runtime 本地输出也会随回收丢失。

本提案在保留现有 Agent 语义和本地部署的基础上，把这些边界整理为可实施契约，并提供分阶段开放及可观察的验收门槛，避免把实验分支或单项测试当作完整产品。

#12827/#12952 仍为 OPEN umbrella；#14122、#14166、#12737、#14211、#14047、#14460、#13333、#14850 已 CLOSED。#14765/#14656/#14657/#14658/#14708/#14806/#14726/#14821/#14829/#14848/#14853/#14730/#14833/#14812/#14478/#14207/#14777/#14843/#14851/#14857/#13678 已 MERGED，从原 open head 表移除。源码默认值与各配置验收仍是权威。

### 评审决策与待定部署参数

**2026-10-12 采纳的策略，已对账到 2026-10-24 实现。** [分发决定](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/12380#issuecomment-6117059631)和[其余决策记录](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/12380#issuecomment-6117130998)保留原范围。

1. **实验 Java 分发：** #14176 已交付独立于 npm CLI 的归档、兼容源码 manifest、启动器、文档与受保护 workflow。#14277 后 Server 在 `packages/managed-agent-server` 内含嵌入式 Broker，SDK 独立。build/verify 已有，公开发布、精确当前产物验收和正式支持独立。
2. **首版与生命周期：** 保留普通工具、W0 固定绑定和各能力门禁；单 Java 控制面/同一可信 Linux 主机仍为首版支持边界。父 CLOSE/DELETE 方案 B 已由 #14218 实现，#13875 已关闭；G3 首版恢复已实现，#12952 的双存活 owner/跨主机阶段和 #14481 剩余矩阵仍开放。D7 input/cancel 已由 #14470 提供 opt-in `java_durable`，默认仍是 Harness-confirmed。
3. **部署策略，实测数值待定：** GC 或扩大流量前，记录事件/快照/输出留存，task/Session/tenant 字节及并发，恢复目标和有界模型/工具/Turn 等待。回收受 reference/reader/snapshot 与 ownership 检查约束。已采纳的心跳加独立操作预算策略，基础 keepalive/watchdog 已在 #13314 实现，#14512（`46bf492d05`）补齐协商/类型化结果/打包存活证据，并关闭 #14135。#13654 默认关闭的异步 publication 吞吐问题独立，不因流心跳而解决；MQ 仍可选。
4. **路径独立性，验收仍欠：** 固定 engine owner、不运行时 fallback，不要求跨引擎迁移 Session。M6 已实现，本地一行转为可以开展自身验收，不再因缺少注册而阻塞。

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| 路径 | 门禁与当前状态 |
| --- | --- |
| Hosted Managed | 让普通本地双引擎宿主机制和仅本地 Managed 状态不可达，在固定产物上证明已启用的 Hosted 创建/Turn/恢复；既有恢复/组件测试不替代该矩阵。 |
| 普通本地 Managed | 在现有 opt-in 和兼容配置下，让 Hosted 专属调用不可达，证明本地 select/create/tool/cancel/close/restart；#14488 已合入，M5 限制与完整本地验收仍保留，默认支持提升未认证。 |
| 共享依赖 | 运行前列出有意共享的身份/认证、配置、推理、Workspace/Runtime、Session/transcript 权威、产物存储和恢复/迁移。 |

5. **任务面板演进：** #13936 交付原来采纳的 child-only v1，#14415 已扩展为全部 task kind；仅按 `actionCapabilities` 提供取消，服务端鉴权仍权威。#14413 已提供按权限读取 child Session 输出。最终文本作为 task Artifact 发布、更丰富的 input 控制和跨 boot attach 仍独立。取消 operation 完成不等于 task 终态或物理 stop 认证。

</details>

issues.body:
## Background

qwen-code's current TUI is built on **ink 7 + React 19** with a heavily patched renderer
(`patches/ink+7.0.3.patch`, ~1037 lines) and a custom Virtual Viewport (VP) mode. In real-world
use this has produced a set of structural problems that are hard to fix within ink:

- **Flicker / repeated full-frame redraws** on Warp, Tabby and Windows PowerShell. ink's write
  pattern is "eraseLines + full-frame rewrite" every frame; enabling ink's `incrementalRendering`
  was measured to **not** fix Warp (still flickers + re-renders), because the erase-then-write
  structure remains.
- **Mouse is not a first-class citizen**: selection/copy and click interactions are weaker than a
  native terminal, and the VP mouse path has known parity gaps.
- **Renderer maintenance burden**: the ink patch and the hand-rolled `VirtualizedList`
  (~920 lines) are expensive to maintain and block rendering improvements.

A source-level study of five terminal UIs (kimi-code, pi, qwen-code, opencode, OpenTUI) — with a
byte-level PTY comparison — shows that **OpenTUI's renderer (Zig native core: row memcmp fast-path
+ cell-level diff + run coalescing, zero erase sequences, DEC 2026 synchronized output) eliminates
the flicker class by construction**. A local POC (`bun` + `@opentui/react`) confirmed **0 erase
sequences vs ink's ~749/6s** and no flicker on Warp/Tabby.

The full implementation was developed on #8677 and passed 5 review rounds there (all 56 round-1
Critical findings resolved, with regression tests). It is now being landed onto main
incrementally, in reviewable batches tracked below.

## Rollout phases

1. **Land the code (current phase)** — merge the implementation to main batch by batch. OpenTUI
   stays **opt-in** via `QWEN_TUI_RENDERER=opentui` on a runtime that can load it (Bun, or Node
   with `node:ffi`). The default renderer remains ink throughout this phase.
2. **Manual real-device validation** — folks enable the flag locally and exercise the TUI on real
   terminals.
3. **Flip the default** — a small PR switches `DEFAULT_RENDERER` to opentui after validation
   passes.
4. **Remove ink** — delete the legacy renderer once opentui is the default and stable.

## PR tracking

Implementation PRs are listed here as they are created. Batches below reflect the current landing
plan; the list will grow and be re-cut as the work proceeds (it is a plan, not a fixed count).
Estimated sizes are from the source diff and will drift as batches are finalized.

| Batch | Scope | Est. size (source / test) | PR |
|-------|-------|---------------------------|----|
| Infra | `@opentui` deps, ~~ESLint rules for opentui JSX~~ (deferred to the Foundation-modules batch — first batch carrying opentui JSX sources; recorded in PR #10134), dependency-direction arch test, framework-neutral streaming model | ~0.8k / ~0.3k lines | #10134 (merged) |
| Foundation modules | theme family, a11y (screen-reader, plain-text), clipboard, key-map, mouse-hit/caret, link-click/osc8, early-input, exit-guard/lifecycle, kitty negotiation, event-adapter, item-projection, slash-dispatch, commands-context/output, help-content, input-history, dialog scaffolding + theme dialog (pulled forward from the Dialogs & commands batch — later dialogs build on the scaffolding; recorded in PR #10146) | ~5.9k / ~5.3k lines | #10146 (merged) |
| Live-session & input | live-session stream fold, message rendering, transcript adapter + resume/session-switch, sticky-todos, composer input, mouse rows/scrollbar/selection, multi-click-select, diff-render, session-compaction | ~5.7k / ~5.1k lines | #10368 (merged) |
| Dialogs & commands | dialog family, dialog-data, folder-trust gate, session-rewind, slash-command registry/dispatch, help-overlay | ~11.3k / ~5.7k lines | #10383 (merged) |
| Backend composition root | thin composition root: command-bridge (host + dispatcher + gateway), dialog-mount, error-boundary, runtime-sidecar passthrough; transcript view and model-turn exposed as seams | ~1.5k / ~1.2k lines | #10696 (merged) |
| Renderer activation | renderer dispatch + runtime gate (this batch introduces the `QWEN_TUI_RENDERER` read itself — no code references it today) + entry, startInteractiveUI wiring, small shared exports. It owns the mount site, so the composition-root contracts land here: stable callback identities (U-8), a real confirmation UI in place of the deny stub, and fatal render-error parity (U-10). The runtime fixes originally listed in this row — Bun memory flags, goal-runtime startup timeout — shipped early in #10128. Default renderer stays ink | ~0.5k / ~0.5k lines | #10739 (merged 2026-09-02) |
| Build & CI | bundle asset pipeline (opentui runtime assets), CI legs (e2e, tui-parity), renderer-matrix integration tests, parity tooling (codemod, tui-parity harness), opt-in Bun standalone flavor (`--runtime=bun`; classic Node packaging stays the default) | ~4.1k / ~2.6k lines | #10770 (merged 2026-09-02) |
| Submit & exit parity | OpenTUI mid-turn submit and exit behave the way ink's do: the whole quit family normalizes ahead of the mid-turn gate, every OpenTUI exit signals the client before cleanup, steered text is resolved the way an idle submission is (expansion, read deadline, queue restore), the prompt-side vision bridge runs on both hops, and the offline parity gate requires its base defect. Closes U-15, U-21, U-22, U-23, U-24, U-25 | ~0.4k / ~1.1k lines | #10883 (merged) |
| Transcript visibility | OpenTUI shows what a command did: every recorded history item becomes a transcript row at record time, `/clear` clears the screen as well as the history (and no longer throws doing it), a message typed mid-turn appears as its own row when the turn accepts it, and an unreadable image format is disclosed on both prompt hops. Closes U-12 (visible half), U-27, U-28, U-29, U-30 | ~0.2k / ~0.6k lines | #10947 (merged 2026-09-04) |
| Chrome restore | The banner, the bottom status line and the responding indicator the pre-batch implementation had but no batch ever carried: gradient logo + info panel (title/version, auth|model, directory, custom-banner tiers, narrow-terminal collapse), status line (project, session, git branch, model, context % used, approval-mode row with the mid-turn steer hint and queue count), and the spinner + witty phrase + elapsed seconds + cancel hint above the composer. Also fixes two defects in the restored source (missing percent sign on the context label; a dead approval-mode colour branch) and aligns the spinner to the 80ms rate ink and the compaction spinner both use | ~0.5k / ~0.3k lines | #11437 (open) |

Additional follow-up PRs (default flip, ink removal, packaging) will be added to this table when
their phase starts.

**Related merged PRs** (not batch PRs, but part of the migration effort):
- #10343 — migration design and architecture notes (merged)
- #9885 — npm per-platform packaging for OpenTUI runtime (merged)
- #10728 — **open issue** (not a PR): deferred review items from the pre-Batch-5 batches (test hardening, dead-code cleanup, packaging follow-ups); filed 2026-09-01 because they had no owner anywhere

## Parity gaps from real-device validation

Confirmed while testing Preview 3 ([v0.21.11-preview.3](https://github.com/chiga0/qwen-code/releases/tag/v0.21.11-preview.3)); each needs a fix before the default flip. These are functional gaps that predate the review fixes, not regressions from them. **All items below must be resolved before Phase 3 (default flip).**

| # | Gap | Ink behavior | OpenTUI status | Root cause |
|---|-----|--------------|----------------|------------|
| G-1 | First-run auth onboarding dialog | With no provider configured, the auth dialog auto-opens at startup (startup auth check fails → auth-error wiring opens the dialog); same when an auth error occurs at init | Does not open; the user lands in the composer and only hits a failure on first prompt | The OpenTUI entry receives no initialization result (no `authError` / `shouldOpenAuthDialog` wiring), and the OpenTUI backend has no `onAuthError` path — the auto-open branch of the auth flow was never ported |
| G-2 | Follow-up prompt suggestions | After a completed turn, a model-generated follow-up suggestion appears as the composer placeholder (ghost text) | Not implemented | No follow-up / prompt-suggestion code exists anywhere in the OpenTUI tree; the ink hook plus the suggestion-generation integration on turn completion were never ported |
| G-3 | Update-check notification placement | Update check failures and available-update info render in a dedicated notification bar above the composer (persistent while relevant) | **Slot reserved, still unfilled.** The composition root renders a persistent banner below the transcript (hidden while a dialog is open, ink `DefaultAppLayout` parity), but nothing populates it | No entry passes an update-info value yet: the update-check → shell wiring lands with the renderer-activation batch, which owns the mount site |

### Registered 2026-09-09 — chrome the batches never carried (G-4)

Confirmed on the v0.23.1 preview standalone build (the Bun-flavoured archive, which defaults to the OpenTUI renderer), not on Preview 3. Kept separate from the table above so that table's provenance stays intact: these are not functional gaps found while exercising the TUI, they are the absence of the entire surrounding chrome, and the mechanism is different too — nothing was removed, it was never carried across.

| # | Gap | Ink behavior | OpenTUI status | Root cause |
|---|-----|--------------|----------------|------------|
| G-4 | Startup banner, bottom status line, and responding indicator all absent | Banner at startup (gradient logo + bordered info panel with title/version, auth|model, directory, custom-banner tiers, narrow-terminal collapse); a permanent status line at the bottom (project, session, git branch, model, context % used, approval-mode row with the mid-turn steer hint and queue count); a spinner + rotating phrase + elapsed seconds + cancel hint above the composer while a turn is in flight | All three missing — the renderer opens straight into the transcript, gives no visible indication that a turn is running, and shows no status line. Restored by #11437 | Verified by pickaxe over main's OpenTUI tree: the banner, status-line and responding-indicator symbols each return **zero commits**, so they were never carried into any batch PR rather than dropped after landing. They exist only in the pre-batch implementation branch the migration was cut from; the split into modules left them behind. Note the compaction spinner is unrelated and has been present since #10368 — it is a different component with the same frame set, which is why the frames looked ported while the responding spinner was not |

**Consequence for the phase gates:** G-4 made the opt-in renderer unusable for the real-device validation phase — a chrome-less screen cannot be compared against ink meaningfully, and the degraded appearance masked any genuine parity signal. It is a prerequisite for Phase 2, and it is the reason "Phase 1 complete" could not be read as "the renderer looks like ink": landing every batch is not the same as having carried every piece of the UI across.

## Unresolved items for upcoming batches

Discovered during implementation review (2026-09-01). Each item is assigned to the batch PR where it should land.

### Land in Batch 5 (Backend composition root)

| # | Item | Location | Outcome |
|---|------|----------|---------|
| U-1 | `OpenTuiDialogRequest` type | `commands-registry.ts` | **Resolved (predates this batch).** The exhaustive dialog-request union already lives on main from the Dialogs & commands batch; the dialog mount consumes it. |
| U-2 | ink ErrorBoundary not reusable | `opentui-error-boundary.tsx` | **Delivered in Batch 5.** Own `@opentui/react` implementation, no `ink` import. |
| U-3 | AppContainer state replication | `opentui-app-shell.tsx` | **Resolved by design — no replication.** The composition root assembles the command-bridge, dialog mount, error boundary and runtime sidecar and exposes the transcript view + model turn as seams. The 50+ AppContainer hooks are deliberately *not* reorganized: the OpenTUI-native state machinery (streaming-model fold + host) landed with the Live-session batch, so a 1:1 AppContainer copy would fork state and create two sources of truth. |
| U-4 | slash-dispatch feature stubs | `slash-dispatch.ts` / `commands-dispatch.ts` | **Already live; dead path removed.** `load_history`, tool results, `goal_control`, confirm dialogs and stacked skills are implemented in `OpenTuiSlashDispatcher` (reached via the gateway). The stubbed `executeSlashCommand` chain was test-only (no production caller) and is dropped in the Batch 5 PR — `slash-dispatch.ts` now exports only `loadInteractiveCommands`. End-to-end dispatch verification rides with Batch 6. **Amended by the Batch 8 audit (2026-09-03):** "already live" described dispatch wiring, but every command echo and its `info`/`warning`/`error` output lands in `host.history`, which nothing renders (U-28) — commands take effect without ever showing feedback, and no case had crossed a command's visible output, which is how this survived six batches. |
| U-5 | G-3 update notification bar | `opentui-app-shell.tsx` layout | **Slot reserved.** A fixed banner slot sits below the transcript and hides while a dialog is open (ink `DefaultAppLayout` parity); the update-check wiring that fills it stays gated behind G-3. |

### Land in Batch 6 (Renderer activation)

| # | Item | Location | Details |
|---|------|----------|---------|
| U-6 | G-1 auth dialog auto-open | entry wiring (`startInteractiveUI`) | **Deferred past Batch 6.** The entry landed and receives `initializationResult`, but the auth auto-open flow is not implemented; stays on the G-1 gate. **Verified 2026-09-04 at `9c320cb0cc`: smaller than registered** — the auth dialog is already mounted (`dialogs-auth.tsx` via `opentui-dialog-mount.tsx:330`, exhaustive switch with compile-time check); what is missing is only the *trigger*: ink auto-opens from `useInitializationAuthError` (`AppContainer.tsx:1674`), while the shell's sole `setDialog` writer is the slash-dispatch outcome (`opentui-app-shell.tsx:360`) and `start-opentui-ui.tsx:302` still takes `_initializationResult` unread. Threading the auth error into the shell as an auto-request is the whole change. Slated for Batch 10 |
| U-7 | G-2 follow-up suggestions | composer + turn-complete hook | **Deferred past Batch 6.** The turn-completion point exists (live-turn drives turns to completion), but suggestion generation is not wired; stays on the G-2 gate. **Verified 2026-09-04 at `9c320cb0cc`:** zero consumers of `useFollowupSuggestions` under `ui/opentui/` (ink: `InputPrompt.tsx:29,430` `useFollowupSuggestionsCLI`, gated at `AppContainer.tsx:3518`); the composer already has a `placeholder` slot (`input-prompt.tsx:188`, default `:212`) but the shell's `OpenTuiInputPrompt` site passes no `placeholder`, so the ghost-text slot is unfed. The work is turn-complete wiring plus an acceptance interaction decision (how ghost text is accepted under this renderer). Slated for Batch 10 |
| U-8 | Composition-root callback identity | app shell mount site (`startInteractiveUI`) | Batch 5 review (P3): the shell's host memo and dispatcher effect key on the raw callback props (`getSessionStats`, `onToggleVim`, `onTranscriptReset`), so the mount site must pass **stable** identities (refs). Inline callbacks would recreate the host and re-run the full interactive command loader on every render. **Delivered in Batch 6:** the entry passes stable identities to the shell (stable `useCallback` seams + the stats-ref pattern), so the host memo and dispatcher effect do not re-run per render |
| U-9 | Settings sub-dialog routing and composer owner | `opentui-dialog-mount.tsx` | Batch 5 review (R1-3): two dialog actions need seams this batch does not own. (a) The settings rows `ui.theme` / `general.preferredEditor` / `fastModel` / `visionModel` route into sub-dialogs in ink (`DialogManager.tsx:285-306`), which the mount cannot express — it takes `onClose` and has no channel to change `request`. (b) The arena model picker starts a session by writing `/arena start …` into the composer, owned by the entry layer. Batch 5 made both dead ends visible (each reports through `notify`) and wired the parts that were pure persistence (working-directory add/remove). **Verified 2026-09-04 at `9c320cb0cc`: the mount-side seams now exist and are unfed** — `opentui-dialog-mount.tsx:119` `fillInput?` and `:311` `props.onSelectSetting(...)` are wired through to fallback `notify` dead-ends (`:312`, `:515-518`), but the sole production call site (`opentui-app-shell.tsx:537-548`) passes neither prop, and the mount still cannot change `request` (`onClose` only, `:544`). Landing this is: pass the two props from the shell, give the mount a dialog-change channel, and decide what the settings apply callback owes the row. **Deferred past Batch 6** — both dead ends remain visible via `notify`. Slated for Batch 10 | 
| U-10 | Fatal render-error parity at the mount | `opentui-app-shell.tsx` mount site + entry teardown | Found while reviewing what Batch 5 left as seams. The shell wraps its subtree in `OpenTuiErrorBoundary` **with no props**, while the ink call site (`startInteractiveUI.tsx:262-274`) passes `recordForExitEcho` and an `onError` that logs `[FATAL_RENDER_ERROR]` and schedules a graceful exit (the fallback unmounts the keypress/Ctrl+C providers, so under the Kitty protocol Ctrl+C is a keypress, not SIGINT). On the OpenTUI side `consumeLastRenderError()` has no production reader either, so a caught render error would be echoed to neither the debug log nor the main screen. Batch 5 cannot verify any of it — the exit chain and the cleanup timer live in the entry this batch does not touch. **Delivered in Batch 6:** the mount passes `recordForExitEcho` + `onError` (`[FATAL_RENDER_ERROR]` debug log + scheduled graceful exit), and the entry's cleanup chain echoes the render error after teardown and fires the SessionEnd hook (ink parity) |

### Deferred from the Batch 6 review (registered 2026-09-02)

The merged cut opened as one PR, one commit per item. Dispatching U-31 first turned the Batch 9 prediction into measured fact: the OpenTUI leg hung on the first prompt (U-36), the MCP confirmation asked no question (U-37), a whole-batch cancellation sent a second model request where ink sends none, and a confirming card re-rendered as its own surface on every token — all fixed inside this batch rather than deferred, because the harness leg cannot go green while any of its five scenarios hangs or floods. Design doc: `docs/design/2026-09-04-opentui-batch10-parity-closeout.md`.

**Review rounds 1–3 disposition (2026-09-07):** the three `/review` rounds raised 45 distinct findings across 55 threads. Round 3 landed in `74a7b56eb0` + `ce22a87f9d`: all 12 Criticals and 18 Suggestions fixed with pinned tests; 15 Suggestions deferred to U-39 (row below); every thread answered and resolved. Per-thread replies and the accounting: [round-3 summary](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/11152#issuecomment-5565786584).

| # | Item | Outcome |
|---|------|---------|
| U-31 | The mem0-write spec self-spawns its PTY and exercises ink on the OpenTUI leg | **Delivered.** The spec resolves the renderer matrix like every matrix-aware spec and keeps its own PTY harness (it drives scenarios `InteractiveSession` cannot express); the OpenTUI leg carries the strict no-fallback guard, so a silent ink boot fails instead of passing as a false green. Its flow-gating assertions moved to screen reconstruction — the raw-PTY channel is unfaithful on a cell-diff renderer (four scenarios timed out on strings the same code path had rendered) |
| U-36 | First OpenTUI prompt dies with "Chat not initialized" when command loading owns the `initialize()` flight | **Delivered.** Config initialization is a shared once-guard — first caller wins, everyone awaits the same settlement, and a genuine failure reaches the screen instead of being swallowed. The turn waits for the chat an in-flight flight creates, and readiness means tool declarations, not chat existence (`startChat()` assigns the chat before the SessionStart hook and `setTools()`) |
| U-37 | The MCP confirmation shows title + names but never ink's question line | **Delivered.** The question line ink renders is ported; the wired spec gates on exactly this row |
| U-13 | Long confirmation bodies: ink keeps the head and offers ctrl-s, OpenTUI kept the tail and offered nothing | **Delivered, scope widened from the registered one-liner.** Head window + hidden-tail indicator + one-way ctrl-s expand (ink's ShowMoreLines has no collapse either), with a physical-height-aware window so a single wrapped JSON row still triggers it |
| found by the harness | Rejecting the only confirmation with Esc made OpenTUI send a second model request | **Delivered.** A whole-batch cancellation ends the turn — cancelled responses go to history only, no follow-up request |
| found by the harness | A confirming tool card re-rendered as its own surface on every stream token | **Delivered.** The confirmation renders as one surface; the transcript cap is the interim bound |
| U-6 / G-1 | The auth dialog never auto-opens | **Delivered.** The missing trigger is threaded; the dialog itself was already mounted |
| U-9 | Settings sub-dialog routing and the composer fill owner | **Delivered.** Both dead ends (sub-dialog routing, `fillInput`) are fed from the shell |
| G-3 | The update-notification banner slot unfilled | **Delivered.** The wiring was mostly present; the gap was flush-on-idle |
| U-7 / G-2 | No follow-up suggestions | **Delivered.** Generated at the entry, consumed at the composer as a ghost placeholder |
| U-32 | Steered messages visible but not recorded for /resume | **Delivered.** The steering hop writes to the chat recording |
| U-11 | Mid-turn queue Esc-restore | **Delivered.** The whole queue pops back into the composer, joined with ink's blank-line separator |
| U-34 | Four command kinds project to nothing | **Delivered.** Structural rows replace the null arm for the four kinds |
| U-33 | No `!` shell mode despite the help advertisement | **Delivered.** Empty-buffer `!` toggles in both directions, Esc exits before other escape behaviors, mid-turn submissions defer as tagged entries and drain in submission order, and a thin executor over the core shell service streams child-process output as throttled deltas into a synthetic `run_shell_command` card that injects into model history. ink's persistent shell-command history (up/down recall, reverse search) is deliberately deferred |

### Deferred from the Batch 10 review (registered 2026-09-06)

| # | Item | Location | Why deferred |
|---|------|----------|--------------|
| U-38 | No automated guard against a `<text>` nested inside a `<text>`. The OpenTUI reconciler throws `TextNodeRenderable only accepts strings, TextNodeRenderable instances, or StyledText instances` and the session dies, so one label fragment written the wrong way is a crash with nothing in CI to catch it. PR #11152 removed six such sites found by a reviewer's comment-stripped scan (`dialogs-mcp`, `dialogs-permissions` ×3, `dialogs-settings`, `dialogs-theme` — all six present on main); the scan itself was never committed, so the next one can land silently. Two candidate implementations, both measured by the reviewer: (a) the ~20-line comment-stripped static scanner under `scripts/tests/`, running at PR time on the existing `test:ci` tail with no new lane; (b) a real mount through `@opentui/react/test-utils` in the existing bun lane (`tui-parity.yml` already installs bun and runs `bun packages/cli/scripts/opentui-*.tsx`). (a) is cheaper and should land first; (b) is the half that also proves the `<span>`-in-`<text>` pattern safe, which the transcript's arena rows use at 13 sites | `packages/cli/src/ui/opentui/dialogs-*.tsx`, `transcript-view.tsx`; guard would live under `scripts/tests/` or the bun lane | Deferred out of #11152 under AGENTS.md's "don't let review rounds balloon the PR" — it is new test infrastructure, not a defect in that diff, and the diff itself is clean. **Wanted before Phase 3**, which is not approved, so it gates nothing today. Discriminator the reviewer measured under `testRender` (60×6): plain `<text>` → frame `hello`; `<text>` with a `<span>` child → `hello world`; nested `<text>` → empty frame (renders nothing); `<box><text/><text/></box>` → `hello world`. So one non-empty `captureCharFrame()` assertion per dialog label fragment kills both the nested-text crash and the false-confidence case. Note jsdom cannot stand in for this: the box→div / text→span harness has no reconciler to throw |
| U-39 | Fifteen Suggestion-level deferrals from #11152 review rounds 1–3 (auth auto-open trigger set; settings sub-dialog return; arena resume replay; two-text recording pin; child_process interim output; initialDialog/initialError mount tests; U-34 row render tests; early keystrokes behind a boot dialog; `!` cancel affordance; PR-gating integration coverage; `user_shell` projection dead case; fillComposer poll witness; theme-diff derived-count assertion; permission scope-row join pin) plus the R1-39 two-phase-settle follow-up on top of the landed minimal abort re-check | Various `packages/cli/src/ui/opentui/*`; full per-item ledger in the [U-39 comment](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/8662#issuecomment-5565748874) | Deferred under AGENTS.md's review-round balloon rule — all 12 Criticals were fixed in #11152 (`74a7b56eb0` + `ce22a87f9d`); these are test-pinning and scoped-parity items queued for Batch 11 |
| U-40 | The `onSubmit` gate comment over-promises: `opentui-app-shell.tsx` :515-518 says a running `!` command "holds the same gate", but the branch only defers shell-mode entries and commands the dispatcher marks `mustDeferDuringStreaming` — an ordinary prompt typed while a shell command runs still reaches `onSubmitPrompt` immediately. That is the ordering ink's own gate permits, and the damage the finding was about (a command's LLM-history write racing into a live turn's chat) is separately bounded by the `chatAtStart` guard (R1-43), so the code is not defective; the fix is to tighten either the comment or the gate | `packages/cli/src/ui/opentui/opentui-app-shell.tsx` (onSubmit gate) | Raised by the round-4 verification review at head `ce22a87f9d` (2026-09-07) as non-blocking. **CLOSED 2026-09-07 — superseded by the round-7 R5-5 fix** (`de12b19c6d` in #11152): while a `!` command runs, a plain prompt now queues behind the shell lane and is routed to the prompt turn when it finishes, pinned by `routes a prompt held behind a running shell command to the turn seam (R5-5)` and mutation-verified; the over-promising comment was replaced with the gate's actual contract |
| U-41 | **Resolved upstream — entry corrected 2026-09-07 after the round-6 discriminator.** The OpenTUI dispatch leg failed `context-compress-interactive` (`rig.waitForText('einstein')` seed-completion probe timed out 190s ×2 retries; runs 34107930678 and 34114500559). The discriminating experiment the round-6 review demanded (word present → oracle bug; word absent → renderer regression) returned **word absent** — but a pure-main failure at the PR's own merge-base ([run 34043372845](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/34043372845) at `4dbfc0c1c1`, zero PR diff, same signature) pointed to a third case: the #11175 seed was a single ~7,000-char response (~88 wrapped rows in the 80×30 pty), and the OpenTUI renderer writes only viewport-visible rows to the pty stream, so the seed's own end marker never reached the byte stream — the leg had been red on every main run since `62d22cd48a` (tracked upstream in #11191). The earlier attribution in this cell ("cell-diff drops mid-prose tokens; raw-PTY text waits are the wrong instrument") was wrong, and with it the screen-based-instrument fix plan: the raw-stream wait is fine for viewport-fitting content, and the ink legs always passed because ink appends completed rows to scrollback. The "pre-existing since Batch 9" framing was also wrong — the Batch 9 dispatch miss (33830499451) was a different assertion and the red-streak began with the #11175 seed | `integration-tests/interactive/context-compress-interactive.test.ts` (the seed is server-side in the spec's `runInteractiveWithFakeModel`) | Root cause is the seed, not the spec's waits: fixed upstream in #11199 (`f33c40a6af`, Sep 6 17:01Z, fixes #11191) by shrinking the seed to `repeat(100)` (~11 rows). #11152's merge-base predated the fix by ~75 minutes, which is why both PR heads ran the pre-fix spec deterministically while post-fix main runs were green; the branch merged `origin/main` at `602c5d7e7f` to pick the repair up — no change needed in the PR itself |
| U-42 | R1-7b from the round-5 review at head `f461edeaf1` ([comment](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/11152#discussion_r3949420172)): partially-streamed `!` output where a throttle tick lands on a chunk ending in a newline and more output arrives before the result — `emittedText.trimEnd()` drops the tracked trailing newline, so `tail = mainContent.slice(emittedTrimmed.length)` starts one character early and re-introduces the stripped newline; the card renders one extra blank line. Reproduced (`emittedText="abc\n"`, output `"abc\nline2\n"` → card `"abc\n\nline2"`); the three shell-mode pins (fully-streamed, non-streamed, empty-tail-with-status) all miss this variant. Candidate fix: split against raw `res.output` first (`res.output.startsWith(emittedText)` → slice + trimEnd), then fall back to the current trimmed comparison, else full content — the fallback must stay so results that drop a final newline the stream already carried keep deduping | `packages/cli/src/ui/opentui/shell-mode.ts` (result tail split, :171-175) + a pinning test in `shell-mode.test.ts` | Reproduced but cosmetic: content is complete and deduped, the damage is one blank line under a narrow timing window (result within the 1s throttle window after a newline-terminated tick), and the review itself labels it "Not a blocker"; #11152 is merge-ready after five review rounds, so per AGENTS.md's review-round balloon rule only Criticals land — queued for the next shell-mode batch with a mutation-verified pin |

## Progress

### Phase 1 — land the code
- [x] Infra batch (merged via #10134)
- [x] Foundation modules batch (merged via #10146)
- [x] Live-session & input batch (merged via #10368)
- [x] Dialogs & commands batch (merged via #10383)
- [x] Backend composition root batch (merged via #10696)
- [x] Renderer activation batch (opentui reachable via flag; default renderer = ink; merged via #10739)
- [x] Build & CI batch (merged via #10770)
- [x] Submit & exit parity batch (PR #10883)
- [x] Transcript visibility batch (PR #10947, merged 2026-09-04 as squash `9c320cb0cc`)
- [x] Parity closeout merged batch (PR #11152, merged 2026-09-08 — dialogs/entry/composer + transcript/recording/resume + the e2e harness fix)
- [ ] Chrome restore (PR #11437 — banner, status line, responding indicator; see G-4)
- [x] #8677 closed as superseded (2026-10-24); source branch and reviews retained, with remaining obligations explicitly tracked in https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/8662#issuecomment-6378659691

### Phase 2 — real-device validation
- [ ] Flag-driven validation on real terminals (Warp / tmux / VSCode / etc.) — **blocked on G-4 (#11437)**: without the banner, status line and responding indicator there is nothing to compare against ink, and the v0.23.1 preview attempt surfaced exactly that
- Preview builds published for hands-on testing: preview.1–preview.3 (latest [v0.21.11-preview.3](https://github.com/chiga0/qwen-code/releases/tag/v0.21.11-preview.3)); first confirmed parity gaps tracked above

### Phase 3 — default flip
- [ ] `DEFAULT_RENDERER` → opentui

### Phase 4 — remove ink
- [ ] Delete ink renderer, ink patch, and VirtualizedList/VP mode

## Acceptance criteria (per landing PR)

- `npm run build` (all workspaces) and `tsc --build` clean
- ESLint clean; Prettier clean on touched files
- Full `packages/cli` vitest suite green
- Default (ink) path unchanged: launching the CLI without `QWEN_TUI_RENDERER` behaves exactly like
  main — batches that add flag-gated code touch zero reachable ink code paths
- The activation batch additionally smoke-tests `QWEN_TUI_RENDERER=opentui` under Bun (boot,
  dialog, live turn, exit drain)
- The build/CI batch additionally runs the opentui e2e leg green on CI — the leg was withdrawn
  before it ever passed and is restored by #10831, green on a dispatched run; see "OpenTUI
  interactive e2e leg withdrawn from CI, then restored" below (U-17…U-20 closed)

## Notes

- All 56 Critical findings from the round-1 bot review of #8677 are already fixed on the source
  branch; the fixes land with the batch that carries their files.
- The npm per-platform packaging PR (#9885) has been merged to main.
- Track-2 (`@opentui/solid`) and the M4 A/B evaluation from the original proposal remain deferred.

## Accepted trade-offs (documented, unchanged)

mermaid degrades to code block for now; legacy terminal-scrollback mode dropped (single scrollbox);
iTerm2 inline image not supported (kitty/sixel/blocks only); screen-reader support to be evaluated.

issues.body:
### What happened?

**R1-1** comes from the review of #13109 (Hosted MCP release and recovery). In that case a Hosted Session with MCP could not finish closing after its owner release was lost and the Broker was then replaced. It was measured on a real stack and called "a regression against the base", but #13109 merged without the fix, and no issue tracked it. The review thread that carried R1-1 no longer resolves, so the record below comes from the comments that quote it.

**Whether it still happens on current `main` is unverified.** Spring now closes every active MCP Session through lifecycle v2, and on that path the replaced Broker probably answers the retry by itself (see below). Nothing has run that sequence.

**Round 1** ([comment](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13109#issuecomment-5915334486)):
- **Rig.** Ubuntu 24.04, JDK 21, MySQL 8.4.11, `durable-local-process=true`. The rig called the Harness's `/session/:id/detach` directly, with no lifecycle authority.
- **Sequence.**
  1. The per-configuration drain receipts are committed.
  2. A proxy answers the owner release with 503, so it never reaches the Broker.
  3. The Broker JVM is killed and restarted. The worker survives with the same PID.
- **Results:**

  | Build | Detach after the restart | Broker requests |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | base | 204 | release 503 `runtime_reconciliation_required` → status 404 → acquire 200 → status settled → release 200 |
  | #13109 | 503 on 5 attempts (3 by the same Harness, 2 after a new Harness loaded the Session); the holder is kept | release 503 `runtime_reconciliation_required`, nothing else |
  | #13109 + the suggested retry | 204 | release 503 → acquire 200 → release 200 |

- **No way out through the API.** A prompt to the stuck Session was refused with `503 hosted_mcp_recovery_required`.

**Round 2** ([comment](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13109#issuecomment-5918102084)) measured the same wedge with no restart, when a second Broker instance on the same host took over from one that died. It also measured it when the recovering Harness ran on another host, with a Broker restart between the two phases.

The [approving review](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13109#pullrequestreview-5373220473) said: "It should still be fixed before merge; this approval does not resolve that thread."

**What `main` looks like now (`c7a6e5c2d5`):**
- **The Harness's release line is unchanged.**
  - `HostedMcpSession.closeResources()` commits every configuration `drained`, then makes a bare `await this.broker.release()` (`packages/cli/src/serve/hosted-mcp-session.ts:933-934`).
  - `HostedWorkspaceBroker.release` sends one request and throws on any unconfirmed answer (`hosted-workspace-broker.ts:839-860`).
  - No test covers `runtime_reconciliation_required` there.
  - What changed is the request around it. The lifecycle headers came with #13354, and #13931 wired the MCP Session's Broker to them. So while a lifecycle authority is set, the release carries the lifecycle operation id and claim generation (`hosted-workspace-broker.ts:905-918`). That matters below.
- **The close path has changed.**
  - Since #13931, an active MCP Session closes only through lifecycle v2 (`WorkspaceToolProfiles.java:26-33`, `ManagedAgentStore.java:2286-2290`).
  - When the Harness does not advertise v2 for the profile, the close is refused at admission with `409 workspace_unavailable` (`ManagedAgentStore.java:2302-2306`). It does not fall back to the old path.
  - Both v2 for MCP and the MCP profile itself are opt-in. `QWEN_HOSTED_LIFECYCLE_V2_PROFILES` defaults to empty (`hosted-harness-contract.ts:38-42`). `hosted-workspace-mcp/1` must also be added to `QWEN_MANAGED_AGENT_DEFINITION_TOOL_PROFILES` (`packages/managed-agent-server/README.md:1510`, `:1512`).
  - Spring still calls the Harness's `/session/:id/detach`, as the last step of a v2 close (`SessionLifecycleCoordinator.java:740`). That call carries a lifecycle authority. It comes after `settle_resources` has already run the owner release, when the head is already `DRAINING`.
  - The rig's request is different: a detach with no authority and no drain before it. Nothing marks the head `DRAINING` on that path, so the wedge still reproduces there statically. Spring never sends that request, but the SDK still supports it: the authority-less `HostedHarnessClient.detachSession` (it sends the `X-Qwen-Client-Id` header but no lifecycle authority) is the example in the README's Hosted Harness private API section (`packages/sdk-java/qwencode/README.md:158`), so a control plane built directly on the SDK can take that path.
- **On v2, the replaced Broker probably answers the retry by itself** (static reading):
  - Spring's effects phase marks the head `DRAINING` in the database before `settle_resources` runs (`WorkspaceLifecycleStore.java:257`; `SessionLifecycleCoordinator.java:686`, then `:709`).
  - The claim check runs first (`requireLifecycleRelease`, `RuntimeBrokerService.java:2382-2388`). It should pass: the re-claimed operation is copied onto the `DRAINING` head (`ManagedAgentStore.java:3601-3626`), and the Harness sends the current claim.
  - #13673's branch (`RuntimeBrokerService.java:2486-2493`) then needs all of the following:
    - a still-active Runtime Session;
    - a managed-context binding;
    - a matching generation;
    - a binding that is `READY` or `DRAINING`;
    - a Harness head that is `DRAINING` (`isHarnessDraining`).
  - The periodic recovery scan (every 5 s) leaves a Session-isolated binding alone once the head is not `OPEN` (`RuntimeBrokerService.java:4211-4222`), so the binding should still be `READY`.
  - `releaseSavedSession` and `releaseSession` must then pass too (`:740-745`, `:778-784`, `:3004-3015`, `:3027-3071`):
    - the saved lease, seed and handle are present;
    - the isolation key and scope match;
    - the Broker runs on the worker's host and boot (`LocalProcessRuntimeProvisioner.java:754-756`);
    - a live reconcile of the durable worker matches the saved lease and registers it again;
    - the parent binding is `READY` or `DRAINING`;
    - the Runtime Session has no active control, execution or background row;
    - the worker confirms the release (`RuntimeBrokerService.java:818-822`).
  - If all of that holds, the bare retry gets `released: true`, and the Broker adopts the worker itself; no Harness-side acquire is needed.
  - `RuntimeHarnessDrainTest.java:262-280` pins only the Broker half. It runs on H2 with a fake provider, a v0 drain fence (`requestHarnessDrain`) and no lifecycle authority.
- **If one of those checks fails, the close is re-driven as blocked.** The Harness passes only five refusals back as a 503 carrying the Broker's code: `workspace_lifecycle_claim*`, `workspace_lifecycle_authorization*`, `workspace_close_identity_unverified`, `workspace_close_execution_unsettled` and `runtime_admission_closed`. It re-answers every other failure as `503 workspace_lifecycle_resources_unsettled` (`hosted-harness-session.ts:6240-6256`). What Spring does next depends on that code:
  - **The claim check fails** (a head that is not `DRAINING`, or a claim that no longer matches or has expired). The Broker answers `409 runtime_admission_closed`. Spring rethrows it (`SessionLifecycleCoordinator.java:718-725`), and the next claimant re-drives.
  - **The branch is not taken** (no binding, another generation, a binding neither `READY` nor `DRAINING`, a Runtime Session no longer active, or one that is not managed-context).
    1. The Broker answers 503 `runtime_reconciliation_required` (`RuntimeBrokerService.java:2522-2524`).
    2. The Harness answers `503 workspace_lifecycle_resources_unsettled`.
    3. Spring hands that to its stopped-worker fallback for MCP. Under the default Session isolation, the fallback refuses a live worker with `409 workspace_close_identity_unverified` (`:457`).
  - **The branch is taken, but a check in the release refuses.** An identity mismatch, another host or boot, or a non-retryable refusal such as `runtime_session_busy` all become `409 workspace_close_identity_unverified` (`:779-785`, `:800-806`). A retryable failure, such as `runtime_session_release_failed` when the worker does not confirm (`:818-822`), becomes `workspace_lifecycle_resources_unsettled` at the Harness. Either way Spring reaches the same fallback, which gives the same 409.
  - **The retry budget does not end it.** After 40 attempts (10 retries × 4, `SessionLifecycleCoordinator.java:346-353`), a close fails only once the Session's journal writer has stopped (`:356-373`). Here the Harness still holds the Session, and its writer is sealed only by the v2 detach (`hosted-harness-session.ts:10137`), which Spring sends only after `settle_resources` succeeds (`SessionLifecycleCoordinator.java:703-740`). So the close stays a budget-exempt `recovery_blocked` wait, and `closeWorkspace` never runs, while that Harness holds the Session and the original worker stays alive. On the worker's own host and boot, a worker death lets the stopped-worker fallback complete the close (see #14503). A Broker on another host still cannot prove the worker stopped.
- **Half of R1-1's precondition is now the default.** #13211 made `durable-local-process` and `trusted-local-reboot-recovery` default on (`ManagedAgentProperties.java:996-997`), so the Broker that can adopt a worker is the default. MCP and MCP-on-v2 remain opt-in.

### What did you expect to happen?

After a lost owner release and a Broker replacement, a retried close should release the original owner and complete, with the holder cleared, as the base did.

**Run the v2 sequence on a real stack.** The setup:
- MCP on lifecycle v2;
- the owner release refused before it reaches the Broker;
- Spring and its embedded Broker restarted;
- then a retried close.

Use the real durable reconcile, not a fake provider. That is the R1-1 cell of FG12d in #14447. A same-host multi-instance failover, the one round 2 measured, would be an addition to that cell. A failover to another host takes the branch, but the release inside it refuses another boot with `409 workspace_close_identity_unverified`.
- **If the close completes,** R1-1 is closed on v2 by #13673. Pin it with that test.
- **If it stays blocked,** the fix depends on which check refused. Note that the review-time [candidate patch](https://github.com/wenshao/qwen-code/blob/eaffceda4c19499f5e309d0dfc4aaeb7e262302b/pr13109/candidate/candidate-r1-1-and-tests.patch) covers only the rig's direct detach. On 503 `runtime_reconciliation_required` it acquires once and releases again. On v2, though:
  - the acquire goes through `acquireRecovery` (`RuntimeBrokerHttpServer.java:261-265`);
  - that is stricter than the branch: it needs a `READY` binding at the same generation, a saved Session that is `READY`, and a live `READY` observation (`RuntimeBrokerService.java:913-926`);
  - the other v2 failures are 409s, which the patch's catch does not match.

  No v2 case was found in which the patch helps. A v2 fix would more likely sit in the Broker or in Spring's MCP fallback.

### Client information

Not client-specific: the Hosted Harness and the embedded Runtime Broker (`packages/managed-agent-server`) on `main` at `c7a6e5c2d5`, with the default durable `local-process` provisioner, and with MCP and MCP-on-lifecycle-v2 enabled.

### Anything else we need to know?

- **#14447.** This answers that tracker's open decision on "whether to file R1-1 as its own bug". FG12d's R1-1 cell stays the runtime check.
  - **A correction to its [triage comment](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/14447#issuecomment-6231453014).** The comment says #13673's branch "does not put a retry on the Harness path that throws first". But the Harness's next attempt *is* the bare release the branch answers. The comment's gate list also leaves out `record.isActive()` (mentioned only in its prose) and the claim check before the branch.
  - **Line drift.**
    - The branch moved from `RuntimeBrokerService.java:2414-2420`, as cited in the #14447 body and doudouOUC's comment, to `:2486-2493`.
    - The `DRAINING` update moved from `WorkspaceLifecycleStore.java:253` to `:257`.
    - `HostedWorkspaceBroker.release`, which the triage comment cites as `:757-778`, is now at `hosted-workspace-broker.ts:839-860`.
- **R2-1, from the same review, matters little now.**
  - Under v2, the legacy 409 fallback is off entirely: every acquire failure rethrows under lifecycle authority (`hosted-mcp-session.ts:858-867`).
  - Round 2 also measured that a restarted Broker that cannot adopt answers the acquire after about 121 s with 503 `runtime_broker_reconcile_timeout`, while the Harness gives up after 30 s.
  - It also needs records written by a pre-#13109 writer. Only the `v0.24.7-nightly.20260930.57e720bc97` prerelease has #12946 without #13109.
- **The H1 design** (`docs/design/2026-09-28-managed-mcp-runtime.md:49`) says a reload "retries only that owner release, including after a lost Broker acknowledgement". That line does not mention a replaced Broker.
- **Related:** #12766 and #13040, both about the non-durable provisioner, whose restarted Broker cannot adopt a worker.
- **Not verified.** Everything above about current `main` is a source reading; nothing was built or run.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

### 发生了什么?

**R1-1** 出自 #13109（Hosted MCP 的释放与恢复）的评审。在那个场景里，一个带 MCP 的 Hosted Session 的 owner 释放丢失，随后 Broker 被替换，这个 Session 就无法完成关闭。它在真实栈上实测过，被称为"相对 base 是回归"，但 #13109 合入时没有修，此前也没有 issue 跟踪。承载 R1-1 的那条评审线程如今已无法打开，下面的记录来自引用它的评论。

**它在当前 `main` 上是否仍会发生，尚未验证。** Spring 现在通过 lifecycle v2 关闭所有活跃的 MCP Session，而在这条路径上，被替换的 Broker 很可能会自己接住那次重试（见下文）。还没有人跑过这个序列。

**第 1 轮**（[评论](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13109#issuecomment-5915334486)）：
- **环境。** Ubuntu 24.04、JDK 21、MySQL 8.4.11、`durable-local-process=true`。测试装置直接调用了 Harness 的 `/session/:id/detach`，没有带 lifecycle authority。
- **步骤。**
  1. 各配置的排空回执已提交。
  2. 代理以 503 应答 owner 释放，所以它从未到达 Broker。
  3. 杀掉并重启 Broker JVM。worker 以同一个 PID 存活。
- **结果：**

  | 版本 | 重启后的 detach | Broker 收到的请求 |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | base | 204 | release 503 `runtime_reconciliation_required` → status 404 → acquire 200 → status settled → release 200 |
  | #13109 | 5 次都是 503（同一个 Harness 3 次，新 Harness 加载 Session 后 2 次）；holder 一直保留 | release 503 `runtime_reconciliation_required`，此外没有任何请求 |
  | #13109 + 建议的重试 | 204 | release 503 → acquire 200 → release 200 |

- **无法通过 API 脱困。** 向卡住的 Session 发 prompt 被以 `503 hosted_mcp_recovery_required` 拒绝。

**第 2 轮**（[评论](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13109#issuecomment-5918102084)）实测：完全不重启、只是同一台主机上的第二个 Broker 实例接管了死掉的那个，也会出现同样的卡死。负责恢复的 Harness 在另一台主机上运行、两个阶段之间重启了 Broker 时，也一样。

[批准该 PR 的评审](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13109#pullrequestreview-5373220473)写道："It should still be fixed before merge; this approval does not resolve that thread."

**现在的 `main`（`c7a6e5c2d5`）：**
- **Harness 的释放那一行没有变化。**
  - `HostedMcpSession.closeResources()` 先把每个配置提交为 `drained`，然后裸调一次 `await this.broker.release()`（`packages/cli/src/serve/hosted-mcp-session.ts:933-934`）。
  - `HostedWorkspaceBroker.release` 只发一次请求，任何未确认的应答都抛错（`hosted-workspace-broker.ts:839-860`）。
  - 那里没有任何测试覆盖 `runtime_reconciliation_required`。
  - 变化的是它所在的请求。lifecycle 头部随 #13354 引入，#13931 把 MCP Session 的 Broker 接上了它们。所以只要设置了 lifecycle authority，释放请求就会带上 lifecycle 操作 id 和 claim generation（`hosted-workspace-broker.ts:905-918`）。这一点在下文很重要。
- **关闭路径变了。**
  - 自 #13931 起，活跃的 MCP Session 只能通过 lifecycle v2 关闭（`WorkspaceToolProfiles.java:26-33`、`ManagedAgentStore.java:2286-2290`）。
  - 如果 Harness 没有为该 profile 通告 v2，这次关闭会在准入阶段被以 `409 workspace_unavailable` 拒绝（`ManagedAgentStore.java:2302-2306`），不会回退到旧路径。
  - MCP 走 v2 与 MCP profile 本身都需要显式开启。`QWEN_HOSTED_LIFECYCLE_V2_PROFILES` 默认为空（`hosted-harness-contract.ts:38-42`）；`hosted-workspace-mcp/1` 还必须加进 `QWEN_MANAGED_AGENT_DEFINITION_TOOL_PROFILES`（`packages/managed-agent-server/README.md:1510`、`:1512`）。
  - Spring 仍会调用 Harness 的 `/session/:id/detach`，作为 v2 关闭的最后一步（`SessionLifecycleCoordinator.java:740`）。这次调用带着 lifecycle authority，而且发生在 `settle_resources` 已经执行过 owner 释放之后，此时 head 已经是 `DRAINING`。
  - 测试装置发的请求不一样：不带 authority，之前也没有 drain。在那条路径上没有任何东西会把 head 标为 `DRAINING`，所以静态看卡死在那里仍会复现。Spring 从不发这种请求，但 SDK 仍支持它：不带 authority 的 `HostedHarnessClient.detachSession`（它带 `X-Qwen-Client-Id` 头，但不带 lifecycle authority）是 README 中 Hosted Harness private API 一节的示例调用（`packages/sdk-java/qwencode/README.md:158`），所以直接基于 SDK 构建的控制面可以走到这条路径。
- **在 v2 上，被替换的 Broker 很可能会自己接住那次重试**（静态阅读）：
  - Spring 的 effects 阶段在 `settle_resources` 运行之前，就在数据库里把 head 标为 `DRAINING`（`WorkspaceLifecycleStore.java:257`；`SessionLifecycleCoordinator.java:686`，然后 `:709`）。
  - claim 检查先运行（`requireLifecycleRelease`，`RuntimeBrokerService.java:2382-2388`）。它应当能通过：重新 claim 的操作会被同步到 `DRAINING` 的 head 上（`ManagedAgentStore.java:3601-3626`），而 Harness 发送的是当前的 claim。
  - 接着，#13673 的分支（`RuntimeBrokerService.java:2486-2493`）需要以下条件全部成立：
    - Runtime Session 仍然 active；
    - binding 是 managed-context 的；
    - generation 一致；
    - binding 为 `READY` 或 `DRAINING`；
    - Harness 的 head 为 `DRAINING`（`isHarnessDraining`）。
  - 周期性的恢复扫描（每 5 s 一次）会在 head 不再是 `OPEN` 之后放过 Session 隔离的 binding（`RuntimeBrokerService.java:4211-4222`），所以 binding 应当仍是 `READY`。
  - 随后 `releaseSavedSession` 与 `releaseSession` 也必须通过（`:740-745`、`:778-784`、`:3004-3015`、`:3027-3071`）：
    - 保存的 lease、seed 与 handle 都在；
    - 隔离键与 scope 一致；
    - Broker 与 worker 在同一台主机、同一次启动上（`LocalProcessRuntimeProvisioner.java:754-756`）；
    - 对 durable worker 的一次实时 reconcile 与保存的 lease 一致，并重新登记它；
    - 父 binding 为 `READY` 或 `DRAINING`；
    - 该 Runtime Session 没有进行中的 control、execution 或后台记录；
    - worker 确认了这次释放（`RuntimeBrokerService.java:818-822`）。
  - 如果这些都成立，裸重试会得到 `released: true`，由 Broker 自己接管 worker；Harness 一侧不需要 acquire。
  - `RuntimeHarnessDrainTest.java:262-280` 只钉住了 Broker 这一半。它跑在 H2 上，用的是假的 provider、v0 的 drain fence（`requestHarnessDrain`），也没有 lifecycle authority。
- **只要其中某项检查失败，这次关闭就会以 blocked 状态被重新驱动。** Harness 只会把五类拒绝以 503 加 Broker 原码的形式回传：`workspace_lifecycle_claim*`、`workspace_lifecycle_authorization*`、`workspace_close_identity_unverified`、`workspace_close_execution_unsettled` 和 `runtime_admission_closed`。其他任何失败都会被改答为 `503 workspace_lifecycle_resources_unsettled`（`hosted-harness-session.ts:6240-6256`）。Spring 接下来怎么做取决于这个码：
  - **claim 检查失败**（head 不是 `DRAINING`，或 claim 已不匹配、已过期）。Broker 回答 `409 runtime_admission_closed`。Spring 会把它重新抛出（`SessionLifecycleCoordinator.java:718-725`），由下一个 claim 者重新驱动。
  - **没有走进分支**（没有 binding、generation 不同、binding 既不是 `READY` 也不是 `DRAINING`、Runtime Session 已不再 active，或者不是 managed-context 的）。
    1. Broker 回答 503 `runtime_reconciliation_required`（`RuntimeBrokerService.java:2522-2524`）。
    2. Harness 回答 `503 workspace_lifecycle_resources_unsettled`。
    3. Spring 把它交给针对 MCP 的 worker 已停止兜底。在默认的 Session 隔离下，该兜底会以 `409 workspace_close_identity_unverified` 拒绝存活的 worker（`:457`）。
  - **走进了分支，但释放中的某项检查拒绝了。** 身份不匹配、主机或启动不同，或者 `runtime_session_busy` 这类不可重试的拒绝，都会变成 `409 workspace_close_identity_unverified`（`:779-785`、`:800-806`）。可重试的失败，例如 worker 没有确认时的 `runtime_session_release_failed`（`:818-822`），会在 Harness 处变成 `workspace_lifecycle_resources_unsettled`。两种情况下 Spring 都会进入同一个兜底，得到同样的 409。
  - **重试预算并不能结束它。** 40 次尝试之后（10 次重试 × 4，`SessionLifecycleCoordinator.java:346-353`），只有在 Session 的 journal writer 已经停止时，关闭才会失败（`:356-373`）。而这里 Harness 仍持有 Session，它的 writer 只会在 v2 detach 中被封存（`hosted-harness-session.ts:10137`），Spring 又只在 `settle_resources` 成功之后才发这个 detach（`SessionLifecycleCoordinator.java:703-740`）。所以只要那个 Harness 仍持有 Session、原 worker 仍然存活，这次关闭就会一直停在一个不计预算的 `recovery_blocked` 等待上，`closeWorkspace` 也不会运行；在 worker 自己的主机与同一次启动上，worker 一旦死亡，worker 已停止的兜底就能让关闭完成（见 #14503）。另一台主机上的 Broker 仍然无法证明 worker 已停止。
- **R1-1 的前提有一半现在是默认配置。** #13211 把 `durable-local-process` 与 `trusted-local-reboot-recovery` 设为默认开启（`ManagedAgentProperties.java:996-997`），所以能接管 worker 的 Broker 是默认配置。MCP 与 MCP 走 v2 仍需显式开启。

### 期望是什么?

owner 释放丢失、Broker 被替换之后，重试的关闭应当释放原 owner 并完成，holder 被清空，就像 base 那样。

**在真实栈上跑一遍 v2 序列。** 设置如下：
- MCP 走 lifecycle v2；
- owner 释放在到达 Broker 之前被拒；
- 重启 Spring 及其内嵌 Broker；
- 然后重试关闭。

要使用真实的 durable reconcile，不能用假的 provider。这正是 #14447 中 FG12d 的 R1-1 那一格。第 2 轮实测过的同主机多实例故障转移，可以作为这一格的补充。故障转移到另一台主机时会走进这个分支，但分支中的释放会以 `409 workspace_close_identity_unverified` 拒绝另一次启动。
- **如果关闭完成，** R1-1 在 v2 上已由 #13673 修复。用这个测试把它钉住。
- **如果仍然阻塞，** 修法取决于是哪项检查拒绝了。注意，评审时的[候选补丁](https://github.com/wenshao/qwen-code/blob/eaffceda4c19499f5e309d0dfc4aaeb7e262302b/pr13109/candidate/candidate-r1-1-and-tests.patch)只覆盖测试装置那种直接 detach：遇到 503 `runtime_reconciliation_required` 时 acquire 一次再 release。但在 v2 上：
  - acquire 走的是 `acquireRecovery`（`RuntimeBrokerHttpServer.java:261-265`）；
  - 它比分支更严格：需要同一 generation 的 `READY` binding、`READY` 的已保存 Session，以及一次实时的 `READY` 观测（`RuntimeBrokerService.java:913-926`）；
  - v2 下其余的失败都是 409，补丁的 catch 匹配不到。

  没有找到补丁在 v2 下能起作用的情形。v2 的修复更可能落在 Broker 或 Spring 的 MCP 兜底里。

### 客户端信息

与客户端无关：`main` 上 `c7a6e5c2d5` 的 Hosted Harness 与内嵌 Runtime Broker（`packages/managed-agent-server`），使用默认的 durable `local-process` provisioner，并开启了 MCP 与 MCP 走 lifecycle v2。

### 还需要知道什么?

- **#14447。** 本 issue 回答了该 tracker 中"是否把 R1-1 单独开成 bug"的待决问题。FG12d 的 R1-1 那一格仍是运行时的检验。
  - **对它的[分诊评论](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/14447#issuecomment-6231453014)的一处更正。** 该评论说 #13673 的分支 "does not put a retry on the Harness path that throws first"。但 Harness 的下一次尝试，正是该分支所应答的那次裸 release。该评论的条件列表也漏掉了 `record.isActive()`（只在正文里提到）和分支之前的 claim 检查。
  - **行号漂移。**
    - 分支已从 `RuntimeBrokerService.java:2414-2420`（#14447 正文与 doudouOUC 的评论所引）移到 `:2486-2493`。
    - `DRAINING` 更新已从 `WorkspaceLifecycleStore.java:253` 移到 `:257`。
    - 分诊评论引用为 `:757-778` 的 `HostedWorkspaceBroker.release`，现在位于 `hosted-workspace-broker.ts:839-860`。
- **同一评审中的 R2-1，现在已不太重要。**
  - 在 v2 下，legacy 的 409 兜底完全不起作用：在 lifecycle authority 下，每个 acquire 失败都会被重新抛出（`hosted-mcp-session.ts:858-867`）。
  - 第 2 轮还实测到：一个不能接管 worker 的重启后 Broker，要约 121 s 才以 503 `runtime_broker_reconcile_timeout` 回答 acquire，而 Harness 30 s 就放弃了。
  - 它还需要由 #13109 之前的 writer 写下的记录。只有 `v0.24.7-nightly.20260930.57e720bc97` 这个预发布版本包含 #12946 而不含 #13109。
- **H1 设计**（`docs/design/2026-09-28-managed-mcp-runtime.md:49`）写道，重新加载会 "retries only that owner release, including after a lost Broker acknowledgement"。这一行没有提到 Broker 被替换的情形。
- **相关：** #12766 与 #13040，二者都是关于非 durable provisioner 的：它重启后的 Broker 无法接管 worker。
- **未验证。** 上面关于当前 `main` 的一切都是源码阅读，没有构建或运行任何东西。

</details>

prs.title: fix(ci): file new main CI failure signatures as their own issues
prs.body:
## What this PR does

`main-ci-failure-issue.yml` used to record every red `main` run as a comment on one open aggregate issue per workflow. This PR splits that routing by whether the run named its failing tests:

- A run with identified failing tests now files or reuses a **per-signature issue**. Recurrence is matched by the `qwen-main-ci-failure-test:<key>` markers the filing embeds in the issue body (the analyzer already emits them), scanned across the workflow's open bot-owned issues inside the serialized writer job. A certified miss creates a new issue titled `Main CI failed: <workflow> — <shortened test>`, labeled `type/bug` + `status/needs-triage`. When a run's failure set grows, the markers that joined later are accreted onto the tracking issue's body (best-effort, after the comment is posted).
- A run with no test identity keeps the aggregate route unchanged, except the aggregate's title is now refreshed to `Main CI failed: <workflow> — no test identified (latest: <run date>)` whenever it carries a machine-shaped title, so the shared issue stops looking frozen at its filing date. The legacy label retirement (stripping `status/ready-for-agent`/`autofix/approved`) now skips issues whose body already carries the workflow marker, so a retitled aggregate is no longer misread as an adopted single-failure issue.

Three boundaries got explicit screening in the same step (found in review):

- Aggregate adoption is body-checked: a legacy-shaped family candidate whose body carries only test markers is a per-signature issue and is skipped (an already-adopted aggregate carries the workflow marker and stays selectable); the closed-issue reopen lookup applies the same body filter, so a resolved per-signature issue is never reopened and converted.
- The signature route also scans the bodies of bot-owned open issues whose titles no longer match the family (a human retitle), mirroring the aggregate route's marker fallback, before certifying a miss and filing a new issue.
- Fail-safe reading: a corrupt open-issue listing aborts the step loudly instead of reading as an empty family; a body that cannot be read leaves labels untouched rather than being stripped on uncertainty. Candidate read failures make the signature route uncertifiable, so the run falls back to the aggregate — precision is lost, never the record.

Lookup, dedupe, and write stay inside the existing per-workflow concurrency group, so two near-simultaneous failures of the same new signature cannot file twice.

## Why it's needed

After #15256, even a brand-new regression was only a comment on a months-old aggregate issue whose title still described the first failure it ever recorded — e.g. run 40021993132's new `peer-messaging.test.ts` failure landed as comment #6375057677 on #12714 (title frozen at a September `llm.test.tsx` failure), invisible in the default issue list and to every label filter. The aggregate comment stream is the right home for unidentified per-commit noise (that was #15166's fix), but a named regression deserves its own triageable, assignable, closable unit.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Read the writer step's routing branches in `main-ci-failure-issue.yml` against the meta-test scenarios: the suite spawns the step's real bash with a mocked `gh` and covers new-signature creation, marker-hit recurrence, marker accretion, retitled-issue body scan, per-signature adoption refusal (open and closed), body-read fallbacks, the dated retitle, and marker-aware legacy adoption. `npx vitest run scripts/tests/main-ci-failure-issue-workflow.test.js --config scripts/tests/vitest.config.ts` (94 tests) plus `scripts/tests/ci-platform-lanes.test.js`, `scripts/tests/workflow-size.test.js`, and `node .github/scripts/ci/main-failure-signature.test.mjs` all pass locally. The next real red main run after merge is the end-to-end confirmation: an identified failure should produce a fresh `Main CI failed: … — <test>` issue, and an unidentified one should comment on the aggregate with a retitle.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — CI routing only; the behavior change is which GitHub issue receives the failure record.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |  N/A   |

### Environment (optional)

Local vitest + node:test harnesses only; no runtime environment involved.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a new signature now opens a new issue; a test whose name varies run to run could file more than one issue before triage renames merge them. Marker dedupe is unchanged from the pre-aggregate design, and the per-workflow concurrency group keeps the check-and-create atomic.
- Not validated / out of scope: no live exercise against GitHub (the writer needs a real failed run); the optional "close a green aggregate after N days" idea from the issue is not in this PR.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: the workflow file grows past its recorded size baseline; `.size-baseline` is updated here because the writer job deliberately checks out nothing and cannot move its script into `.github/scripts/`.

## Linked Issues

Resolves #15398

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

`main-ci-failure-issue.yml` 之前把 main 上每一次 CI 失败都记录为每个 workflow 共享的汇总 issue 下的一条评论。本 PR 按"能否识别失败用例"拆分路由：

- 能识别失败用例的 run 改为新开或复用按签名去重的 issue。复用匹配靠的是落盘时写进 issue 正文的 `qwen-main-ci-failure-test:<key>` marker（分析器本来就产出），在按 workflow 串行化的 writer job 内扫描该 workflow 所有 bot 所有的 open issue。确认无匹配时新开标题为 `Main CI failed: <workflow> — <缩短后的测试名>` 的 issue，打 `type/bug` + `status/needs-triage`。失败集合后续变大时，新加入的测试 marker 会增补进跟踪 issue 的正文（尽力而为，且在评论发布之后）。
- 识别不了测试的 run 保持汇总路由不变，唯一区别是汇总单的标题会在每次记录时刷新为 `Main CI failed: <workflow> — no test identified (latest: <运行日期>)`（仅限机器格式的标题），避免汇总单看起来永远停在创建那天。退役旧路由时摘除 `status/ready-for-agent`/`autofix/approved` 标签的动作，现在会跳过正文已带 workflow marker 的 issue，避免把已改名的汇总单误判成被收编的旧单。

同一步里还为三条边界加了显式筛查（来自评审发现）：汇总收编按正文把关——legacy 形状标题但正文只带测试 marker 的是签名 issue，一律跳过（已收编的汇总单正文带 workflow marker，仍可被选中）；closed issue 重开查找应用同一正文过滤，已解决的签名 issue 永远不会被重开改造成汇总单。签名路由在确认未命中前，还会像汇总路由的 marker 兜底一样，扫描标题已掉出 family 的 bot open issue 正文（防止人工改名后重复开单）。读取失败一律走安全方向：open 列表无法解析时响亮中止而不是当空 family 处理；正文读不出来时不摘任何标签。候选正文读不到时，该 run 回落到汇总单——损失的是精度，不是记录本身。

查找、去重、写入都留在原有的按 workflow 串行的 concurrency group 里，两个几乎同时失败的同签名 run 不会重复开单。

动机：#15256 之后，哪怕是全新的回归也只是月份久远的汇总单下的一条评论，标题还停在第一次失败的指纹——例如 run 40021993132 的 `peer-messaging.test.ts` 新失败只落成了 #12714 的评论 #6375057677，在默认 issue 列表和一切标签过滤里都不可见。汇总评论流适合收容识别不了的按 commit 噪音（那是 #15166 的修复目标），但有名有姓的回归应该有自己可分诊、可指派、可关闭的单子。

Reviewer 验证：对照 meta-test 场景读 writer 步骤的路由分支——测试用 mock `gh` 驱动真实 bash，覆盖新签名开单、marker 命中复用、marker 增补、人工改名 issue 的正文扫描、签名 issue 防收编（open 与 closed 两侧）、正文读取失败回落、按日改名、以及感知 marker 的旧单收编。本地通过：`main-ci-failure-issue-workflow.test.js`（94 项）、`ci-platform-lanes.test.js`、`workflow-size.test.js` 与 helper 的 node:test（62 项）。合并后下一次 main 变红即为端到端验证。

风险：新签名会新开 issue；测试名逐 run 变化的场景可能在人工归并前开出多张单。marker 去重与聚合化之前的设计一致，按 workflow 的串行组保证查重与开单原子。workflow 文件超出记录的大小基线，`.size-baseline` 随之更新——writer job 刻意不 checkout 仓库，脚本无法外置到 `.github/scripts/`。

Resolves #15398

</details>
