prs.title: feat(core): skip re-injecting an unchanged UserPromptSubmit hook context block
prs.body:
## What this PR does

A `UserPromptSubmit` hook that returns `additionalContext` has that text appended to the user's message, wrapped in a reserved tag, on every turn. When the payload the hook returns is byte-identical to one already appended earlier in the same session, the change detects the earlier copy in the shallow conversation history and does not append it again; the turn also stops recording the hook context as coming from this turn, so the stored transcript matches what the model actually received. A payload that differs in any byte — different results, a different order, a changed similarity score — still appends, so there is no state that can expire or go stale. Identical bytes alone are not treated as proof: the injector stamps the block it appends with an in-process receipt, and a stored transcript, an IDE-supplied prompt block, or model output cannot reproduce that stamp, so tagged text that merely appears elsewhere — in a model turn, as a whole user message, or as a caller-authored copy of the injection shape — does not suppress a fresh delivery. Because a stamp cannot survive serialization, a resumed session re-derives it from the per-turn hook provenance the injector recorded alongside the message; where no such provenance exists, as for a block delivered to an IDE session, the block is injected again rather than trusted.

## Why it's needed

The appended block becomes a permanent part of session history, so a hook whose payload repeats is paid for again on every subsequent request: the resent tokens grow on the order of T² over a session. The bundled retrieval extensions make this easy to hit, because their auto-recall hooks render a bounded, newest-first window — with a stable upstream result set the rendered bytes are identical turn after turn. The earlier copy is still in the conversation, so the information is not lost; what is removed is the duplicate.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Point a `UserPromptSubmit` hook at a command that prints a constant `additionalContext` (for example a one-line Node script that writes the same hook JSON every time), then send three prompts in the same session, continuing that session between sends. Read the session transcript for the run and, for each recorded user message, note whether the reserved tagged block and the recorded hook-context provenance are present. Expected: the first user message carries both; later user messages carry neither. Then ask the model to repeat the extra context block it was given — it should still return it verbatim, which shows the deduplication removed a repeat rather than the content.

Count only user records, and only as a presence check. Unrelated records in the same file (telemetry, the auto-memory extractor) can quote the payload back, so a raw substring count over the whole file is not a usable metric.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before, on the released CLI (v0.25.0), a constant-payload hook over three turns in one session: all three user records carried both the tagged block and the hook-context provenance.

After, running from source on this branch, a constant-payload hook over three turns in one session where the second and third turns were separate processes continuing the same session: only the first user record carried the block and the provenance; the second and third carried neither, even though each of those turns rebuilt its history from the stored transcript — the path where the receipt has to be re-derived rather than carried in memory. On the previous revision, a fourth turn asked the model to output the extra context block from its history and it returned the block verbatim, confirming that what is dropped is the duplicate and not the content.

Independent [local verification at `7102b967`](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14129#issuecomment-6305250452) reports 2,430 passing unit tests (hooks 24, session API history 48, core client 517, llm-chat 579, ACP session 1,262), plus wire/transcript checks of three-turn interactive and resumed sessions. The model-bound requests retain one hook block on every turn; the base accumulates one, two, then three. The hooks tests cover receipt validation and forged-text rejection. Resume re-stamping at the history-rebuild call site is demonstrated by the differential wire test, but is not pinned by the committed session-history suite; Turn-level option forwarding is also a remaining non-blocking test gap. The subsequent `8adb7e8e` revision changes tests only, adding a non-compacting-send control and requiring exactly one wrapped rescue block; it leaves the production behavior exercised by that report unchanged.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

The before run used the globally installed `qwen` (v0.25.0); the after run used `node scripts/dev.js` from this branch, which executes the TypeScript sources directly with `DEV=true`, in a scratch directory containing only the test hook and its settings.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a hook that deliberately repeats a fixed block on every turn — a standing or pinned instruction — now appears only on the first turn of a session, and the hook output schema has no field to opt out of that. Any change to the payload re-injects it on the next turn, and suppressing a repeat never removes the text from the conversation.
- Not validated / out of scope: the headline scenario from the linked issue — an external memory recall hook whose items restate content that core already injected from local memory files — is **not** fixed by this change. Core holds no identifier that matches an external recall item against a local memory block, so that comparison cannot be expressed at delivery time; this PR only removes the byte-identical repeat. The cross-source case stays open in the issue, as does putting a size bound on hook context.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. No configuration, protocol field, or package API is added, and hooks whose payload varies per turn behave exactly as before.
- Design documents: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/14089-hook-context-dedup/docs/design/user-prompt-submit-context-dedup.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/14089-hook-context-dedup/docs/design/user-prompt-submit-context-dedup.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Related to #14089. This does not close it: the issue's headline case, where recalled external memory duplicates content core already injected from local memory files, needs an identity that core owns on both sides and is left open.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

返回 `additionalContext` 的 `UserPromptSubmit` hook，其文本会在每一轮被追加到用户消息后面，并用保留标签包裹。当 hook 返回的载荷与同一会话中此前已追加过的某一份逐字节相同时，本次改动会在浅拷贝的会话历史中识别出此前那一份，不再重复追加；同时本轮也不再记录该 hook 上下文来源于本轮，使落盘的会话记录与模型实际收到的内容一致。只要载荷有任何字节不同——结果不同、顺序不同、相似度分数变化——仍会照常追加，因此不存在会过期或失效的状态。仅字节相同并不被当作证据：注入点会给自己追加的块盖上一个进程内的凭据，而落盘的会话记录、IDE 传入的提示块或模型输出都无法复制这个凭据，因此仅仅出现在别处的带标签文本——模型回合里、作为整条用户消息、或调用方自己拼出的注入形状——都不会抑制一次新的投递。凭据无法经由序列化保留，所以恢复会话时会依据注入点随消息一并记录的逐轮 hook 来源信息重新盖上；在没有这类来源信息时（例如投递给 IDE 会话的块），会照旧注入而不是信任它。

## 为什么需要

被追加的块会成为会话历史的永久组成部分，因此载荷重复的 hook 会在之后每一次请求中再付一次代价：重发的 token 量随会话轮数呈平方级增长。本仓库自带的检索扩展很容易触发这一点，因为它们的自动召回 hook 渲染的是一个有界、最新优先的窗口——只要上游结果集稳定，渲染出的字节就逐轮完全相同。此前那一份仍留在对话里，信息并没有丢失，去掉的是重复。

## 评审验证方案

### 如何验证

让 `UserPromptSubmit` hook 指向一个每次都打印相同 `additionalContext` 的命令（例如一行 Node 脚本，每轮输出同一份 hook JSON），然后在同一会话中发送三次提示，每次之间延续该会话。打开该次运行的会话记录，逐条用户消息查看保留标签包裹的块与本轮记录的 hook 上下文来源信息是否存在。预期：第一条用户消息两者都有，之后的用户消息两者都没有。随后让模型复述它拿到的额外上下文块，它应当仍能原样给出，这说明去重去掉的是重复而非内容。

只统计用户记录，且只做有无判断。同一份文件里不相关的记录（遥测、自动记忆抽取器）会把载荷原样引用回来，因此对整个文件做子串计数不能作为指标。

### 证据（修复前后）

修复前，在已发布的 CLI（v0.25.0）上，载荷恒定的 hook 在同一会话中跑三轮：三条用户记录都同时带有标签块和 hook 上下文来源信息。

修复后，从源码运行同一场景，三轮同一会话，其中第二、三轮是延续该会话的两个独立进程：只有第一条用户记录同时带有标签块和来源信息，第二、三条都没有——尽管这两轮都在从落盘的会话记录重建历史，也就是必须重新推导凭据的那条路径。此前一版还额外让第四轮要求模型输出它历史中的额外上下文块，它原样返回，证明去掉的是重复而非内容。

独立的[本地验证报告（`7102b967`）](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14129#issuecomment-6305250452)记录了 2,430 项单测通过（hooks 24、session API history 48、core client 517、llm-chat 579、ACP session 1,262），并验证了三轮交互式会话及跨进程恢复会话的请求体和记录。候选每轮请求都保留一份 hook 块，基线则累积为一、二、三份。hooks 单测覆盖凭据校验与伪造文本拒绝；恢复会话时历史重建调用点的重新盖凭据由线级差分验证证明，但提交的会话记录单测尚未钉住它，Turn 层参数转发同样仍有非阻塞测试缺口。后续 `8adb7e8e` 仅修改测试，增加不触发压缩时的对照，并要求救援块有完整包装且恰好一份；上述报告实测的生产行为未变。

### 测试环境

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️  |

### 运行环境（可选）

修复前为全局安装的 `qwen`（v0.25.0）；修复后为在本分支上运行 `node scripts/dev.js`，它以 `DEV=true` 直接执行 TypeScript 源码，工作目录是一个只包含测试 hook 及其配置的临时目录。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：有意每轮重复某个固定块的 hook——例如常驻或钉住的指令——现在只会在会话第一轮出现，而 hook 输出 schema 没有可供退出该行为的字段。载荷一旦变化，下一轮就会重新注入；抑制重复也从不把文本从对话中移除。
- 未验证／超出范围：关联 issue 的核心场景——外部记忆召回项与 core 已从本地记忆文件注入的内容重复——**并未**被本次改动修复。core 不持有能把外部召回项与本地记忆块对应起来的标识，因此在投递时刻无法表达这种比较；本 PR 只消除了逐字节重复。跨来源去重仍留在该 issue 中，给 hook 上下文加长度上限同样如此。
- 破坏性变更／迁移说明：无。没有新增配置、协议字段或包 API，载荷逐轮变化的 hook 行为与之前完全一致。
- 设计文档：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/14089-hook-context-dedup/docs/design/user-prompt-submit-context-dedup.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/14089-hook-context-dedup/docs/design/user-prompt-submit-context-dedup.zh-CN.md)

## 关联 issue

关联 #14089，但不关闭它：该 issue 的核心场景（召回的外部记忆与 core 已从本地记忆文件注入的内容重复）需要 core 在两侧都持有的标识，因此保持开启。

prs.title: fix(ci): run the sdk-java suite before taking the host lock
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The self-hosted SDK Java test lane now seeds a job-local Maven repository from the host cache, runs the SDK suite, the SDK install, and the Managed Agent suite from that copy without the per-host lock, and takes the ticketed host lock only for the final cache write-back. The write-back's `mkdir` and bounded `find`/`cp` children close fd 9 so a cancelled job's survivor cannot retain the lock. Both lock sites in the workflow now follow the same write-back-only rule, and the cache loop is unchanged.

## Why it's needed

Run 39771949573's fast-tier job failed in `Run Java SDK tests (self-hosted)` on both attempts, each time after exactly 5400 seconds, with the annotation `sdk-java host lock not acquired within 90 minutes as queue ticket 223 (fast)`. The job was waiting, not testing: the full-tier Java 21 leg of run 39754414693 ran for 89 minutes on the same host range, and the fast job failed five seconds after that leg ended. #15128 scoped the MariaDB lane's lock to its cache write-back, but the test job still serialized its whole suite on the same lock. A loaded host can therefore consume the entire fast-tier budget before Maven starts. This change removes that failure mode for the fast tier and shortens the test job's own hold to the write-back.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Inspect the self-hosted test step: the job-local repository seed and every Maven command should appear before the `source .../sdk-java-lock.sh` acquisition, and the write-back should follow it with `mkdir ... 9>&-` and the bounded `find ... 9>&-` copy. Run `npx vitest run --config ./scripts/tests/vitest.config.ts sdk-java-workflow workflow-size` from the repository root and expect 351 passed, 1 skipped. On the next ECS pool run, the `Run Java SDK tests (self-hosted)` step should start Maven without a `Waiting for the sdk-java host lock` line; any lock wait is now limited to the final write-back.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — CI-only change; no user-visible interface.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🐧 Linux | ✅ tested |

### Environment (optional)

Node 22.23.2 on Linux. Java and Maven are not installed in the sandbox, so the Java suites were not run locally; the workflow and its Node pins were verified.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the test job's Maven suites now run concurrently with other pool jobs instead of serializing on the host lock. This follows #15128's write-back-only scoping for the MariaDB lane; the host-shared Maven cache is still protected by the seed/write-back lock, and the write-back children close fd 9.
- Not validated / out of scope: the Maven suites themselves on a real ECS host (CI owns that), and any change to the 5400 s budget or the job ceilings.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The `lock not acquired within` signature, the bare-lock fallback for older release tags, and the tier priority are unchanged.
- Design docs: [English](docs/design/2026-10-20-sdk-java-fair-lock-queue.md) · [简体中文](docs/design/2026-10-20-sdk-java-fair-lock-queue.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15242

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

self-hosted 的 SDK Java test 通道现在从宿主机缓存播种一个 job 本地 Maven 仓库，SDK 套件、SDK install 和 Managed Agent 套件都从该副本运行且不持每宿主机锁，只在最后的缓存写回时获取票据锁。写回的 `mkdir` 和有界 `find`/`cp` 子进程会关闭 fd 9，避免被取消 job 的幸存进程继续持有锁。workflow 的两处取锁点现在都遵循“只锁写回”的规则，缓存循环保持不变。

## 为什么需要

Run 39771949573 的 fast 档 job 两次 attempt 都在 `Run Java SDK tests (self-hosted)` 失败，每次恰好 5400 秒，annotation 为 `sdk-java host lock not acquired within 90 minutes as queue ticket 223 (fast)`。它是在等待，不是测试：run 39754414693 的 full 档 Java 21 leg 在同一宿主机范围运行了 89 分钟，而 fast job 在该 leg 结束后 5 秒失败。#15128 已把 MariaDB 通道的锁收缩到缓存写回，但 test job 仍把整套测试串行在同一把锁上。负载高的宿主机因此可以在 Maven 启动前耗尽 fast 档的全部预算。本改动消除 fast 档的这一失败模式，并把 test job 自身的持锁缩短到写回。

## Reviewer 测试计划

### 如何验证

检查 self-hosted test 步骤：job 本地仓库的播种和所有 Maven 命令都应出现在 `source .../sdk-java-lock.sh` 取锁之前，写回应在其后，并带有 `mkdir ... 9>&-` 和有界 `find ... 9>&-` 复制。在仓库根目录运行 `npx vitest run --config ./scripts/tests/vitest.config.ts sdk-java-workflow workflow-size`，预期 351 通过、1 跳过。下一次 ECS 池运行时，`Run Java SDK tests (self-hosted)` 步骤应当不再打印 `Waiting for the sdk-java host lock` 就开始 Maven；任何锁等待现在都只可能发生在最后的写回。

### 证据（Before & After）

N/A —— 仅 CI 改动，没有用户可见界面。

### 测试环境

| OS | 状态 |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ⚠️ 未测试 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未测试 |
| 🐧 Linux | ✅ 已测试 |

### 环境（可选）

Linux 上的 Node 22.23.2。沙箱未安装 Java 和 Maven，因此 Java 套件未在本地运行；已验证 workflow 及其 Node pin。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：test job 的 Maven 套件现在会与其他池 job 并发运行，而不是在宿主机锁上串行。这遵循 #15128 为 MariaDB 通道确立的“只锁写回”范围；宿主机共享 Maven 缓存仍由播种/写回锁保护，且写回子进程会关闭 fd 9。
- 未验证 / 范围外：真实 ECS 宿主机上的 Maven 套件本身（由 CI 负责），以及 5400 秒预算或 job 上限的任何改动。
- 破坏性改动 / 迁移说明：无。`lock not acquired within` 签名、旧 release tag 的裸锁回退和档位优先级都保持不变。
- 设计文档：[English](docs/design/2026-10-20-sdk-java-fair-lock-queue.md) · [简体中文](docs/design/2026-10-20-sdk-java-fair-lock-queue.zh-CN.md)。

## 关联 issue

Fixes #15242

</details>

prs.title: fix(ci): skip stale main CI failure issues after main advances
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The main-CI failure tracker now skips a post-merge push run whose tested head is no longer the tip of main. The newer push run owns that result. The check still reports when the head is current, when main's tip cannot be read, and for scheduled or manual runs.

## Why it's needed

Run 39777472391 on commit 06e59666 failed on the sdk-java host-lock timeout that #15128 had already fixed and merged. By the time the failure-issue analyzer ran, main had advanced to 3d65e23 and that head's own push run later passed, but the analyzer still filed #15259 for a head main had replaced — asking autofix to repair code main already contained. Without this guard, every slow failure-issue analysis on a moving main can create the same kind of stale repair issue.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the focused workflow suites and confirm 304 tests pass with 1 skipped. To observe the behavior directly, execute the `live` step's shell with `EVENT_NAME=push`, `HEAD_BRANCH=main`, and `HEAD_SHA=<old>`, using a `gh` stub whose `commits/main` result differs from the head; the step should print `superseded=true` and the "main is now" warning. Make the stub return the same sha and it should print `superseded=false`. Set `EVENT_NAME=schedule` and the step should not query `commits/main` at all. Because `superseded=true` gates the destination, log download, infrastructure classification, and issue planning steps, the stale run produces no issue, comment, or rerun.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — CI workflow change with no user-visible surface.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Node.js 22.23.2 and Vitest 3.2.7. The sandbox home is read-only, so the checks ran with `COREPACK_HOME=/tmp/corepack-qwen`.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a real failure could go unreported if the newer tip's push run never completes. Mitigation: main pushes get independent per-commit gate runs, scheduled and manual runs are excluded, and an unreadable tip fails open.
- Not validated / out of scope: a live GitHub Actions dispatch — the sandbox cannot dispatch workflows. Further sdk-java lock hardening is already covered by the merged #15128 and open #15242/#15257, so this PR does not duplicate them.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The workflow-size ratchet is updated for the 20 added workflow lines.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15259

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

main CI 失败跟踪器现在会跳过这样的合入后 push 运行：它测试的 head 已经不再是 main 的 tip。更新的 push 运行负责该结果。当 head 仍然是当前 tip、main 的 tip 无法读取，以及定时或手动运行时，仍然会正常报告。

## 为什么需要

提交 06e59666 上的运行 39777472391 因 sdk-java 主机锁超时失败，而 #15128 已经修复并合入了该问题。等到失败 issue 分析器运行时，main 已经前进到 3d65e23，且该 head 自己的 push 运行后来通过，但分析器仍然为 main 已经替换的 head 创建了 #15259——要求 autofix 修复 main 已经包含的代码。没有这个保护，main 每次前进时的缓慢失败 issue 分析都可能创建同类的过期修复 issue。

## 审查者测试计划

### 如何验证

运行聚焦的 workflow 测试套件，确认 303 个测试通过、1 个跳过。要直接观察行为，可用 `EVENT_NAME=push`、`HEAD_BRANCH=main` 和 `HEAD_SHA=<old>` 执行 `live` 步骤的 shell，并使用 `commits/main` 返回值与 head 不同的 `gh` 桩；该步骤应打印 `superseded=true` 和 “main is now” 警告。让桩返回相同的 sha，则应打印 `superseded=false`。设置 `EVENT_NAME=schedule` 后，该步骤根本不应查询 `commits/main`。由于 `superseded=true` 会关闭目标选择、日志下载、基础设施分类和 issue 规划步骤，过期运行不会产生 issue、评论或重跑。

### 证据（修改前与修改后）

不适用——这是 CI workflow 改动，没有用户可见界面。

### 测试环境

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ⚠️  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅  |

### 环境（可选）

Node.js 22.23.2 和 Vitest 3.2.7。沙箱 home 目录只读，因此检查使用 `COREPACK_HOME=/tmp/corepack-qwen` 运行。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：如果更新的 tip 的 push 运行一直不完成，真实失败可能不会被报告。缓解措施：main push 有独立的按提交 gate 运行，定时和手动运行被排除，且 tip 读取失败时会放行。
- 未验证 / 范围外：真实的 GitHub Actions 调度——沙箱无法派发 workflow。进一步的 sdk-java 锁加固已由已合入的 #15128 和开放的 #15242/#15257 覆盖，因此本 PR 不重复这些工作。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。workflow 大小棘轮已按新增的 20 行更新。

## 关联 issue

Fixes #15259

</details>

issues.title: CPU Usage Regression: v0.9.12 (idle) → v0.9.13 (moderate) → v0.10.0 (heavy)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: tui
labels.description: Terminal UI behavior, rendering, or interaction

labels.name: performance
labels.description: Runtime/render performance

issues.body:
**Platform**: FreeBSD 15.0 (x86-64)
**Binaries analyzed**:

* `cw00912` — Codewhale v0.9.12 (82 MB ELF, dynamically linked)
* `cw00913` — Codewhale v0.9.13 (89 MB ELF, dynamically linked)
* `cw01000` — Codewhale v0.10.0 (90 MB ELF, dynamically linked)

All three binaries are Rust executables (ELF 64-bit LSB pie, compiled for FreeBSD).

## Observed Behavior

<!-- linear:table-colwidths:200,200,200,200 -->
| Version | Idle CPU (top) | Threads | event_loop.rs size |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| v0.9.12 | \~1% (uwait) | 17 | \~4264 lines |
| v0.9.13 | \~5-8% | \~25-30 | \~7323 lines |
| v0.10.0 | \~8-15% | \~30+ | \~7323 + dispatch |

`uwait` state = waiting on user event (interrupt-driven). Later versions show active polling.

## Root Cause Analysis

### Between v0.9.12 and v0.9.13 (+7 MB, major CPU increase)

The event loop grew from \~4264 to \~7323 lines (+70%). Multiple **background polling workers** were added:

1. **@-mention discovery worker** (`crates/tui/src/tui/mention_completion.rs`)
   * Background thread `codewhale-mention-discovery` that continuously scans the workspace for @-mention candidates
   * Polls filesystem even when user is idle
2. **LSP (Language Server Protocol) integration**
   * New modules: `crates/tui/src/lsp/mod.rs`, `lsp/client.rs`, `core/engine/lsp_hooks.rs`, `tools/lsp.rs`
   * Spawns `lsp-writer`, `lsp-reader`, `lsp-dispatcher` threads
   * Supports rust-analyzer, gopls, typescript-language-server, clangd, etc.
   * Background language analysis runs continuously, even with no files open
3. **Runtime event tap / store monitoring**
   * `runtime event tap lagged; a store-failure notice may have been missed`
   * Polls runtime store state periodically
4. **Thread goal stall monitoring**
   * `failed to initialize durable goal stall schema`
   * Tracks `stalled_ms`, `pause_reason`, `repeated_gap_count`, `last_gap_fingerprint`
   * Continuously checks if threads are stalled
5. **Engine tick & telemetry bucket aggregation**
   * `engineTick` increments every iteration, bucket aggregation every 12 ticks
   * Telemetry events with timestamps, agent IDs, tool tracking
6. **Session persistence polling**
   * Polls `session_index.jsonl` for job status changes
   * Periodic SQLite queries for thread status (`SELECT id, rollout_path, preview...`)
7. **File frecency tracking** (`crates/tui/src/tui/file_frecency.rs`)
   * Background tracking of file access frequency
8. **[Models.dev](<http://Models.dev>) live fetch** (`crates/tui/src/models_dev_live.rs`)
   * Periodic HTTP fetch of model catalog

### Between v0.9.13 and v0.10.0 (+1 MB, additional CPU)

1. **Fleet manager** (`crates/tui/src/fleet/manager.rs:1338`)
   * Fleet worker coordination with active polling
   * `Fleet worker coordination is not currently admissible`
2. **Background hooks**
   * `background hooks cannot deny tool calls because they exit immediately with no result`
   * Hooks run for every tool call/event
3. **Dispatch completion mailbox**
   * `dispatch completion mailbox is unavailable/full/closed`
   * Polls mailbox for dispatch results
4. **VM thread management**
   * `VM thread exited without reporting a result`
   * `VM admission gate closed`
5. **Agent profile permissions** (`AgentProfilePermissionsToml`)

## Architectural Shift

**v0.9.12** uses an **interrupt-driven** event loop: it sleeps on `kevent`/`kqueue` and wakes only on user input. The TUI event loop had \~4264 lines.

**v0.9.13+** switches to a **polling-driven** architecture: background workers wake periodically regardless of user activity. The event loop grew to \~7323 lines with runtime tap lag detection, persistence health checks, and session validation — all running on every iteration.

## Impact

* Significant battery drain on laptops
* Unnecessary CPU contention on shared/small VPS
* Background LSP scanning may be redundant with external editor LSP

2026-10-08 Codex continuation: [owner.rs](<http://owner.rs>) now stops world advancement and periodic saves after viewer/producer/audio leases expire, with authenticated /v1/frame wake messages on its existing bounded queue and a frame-deadline wait replacing 2 ms polling. Existing archives and active producer/audio semantics are retained. Exact checkout: engine-0102, local 80e1d2a9be plus owned changes. Focused native validation is starting at one build job and lower CPU priority. This addresses an orphaned-companion cause seen on macOS; it does not yet establish the reported FreeBSD idle/focus behavior or installed acceptance. No new tests or code comments, no new branch.

issues.body:
Founder reconfirmed the complete `MODELS_DEV_REPAIR_CHECKLIST.md` as required for **v0.10.2** on 2026-10-08. All 14 implementation items and the installed-candidate acceptance below are release requirements, not a post-release deferral. Source artifact: `/Volumes/VIXinSSD/CW/artifacts/ratatui-pet-main-20261008/followup/space-recovery-20261009/MODELS_DEV_REPAIR_CHECKLIST.md`. Continue this existing issue and ownership; do not create a second queue.

## Required 0.10.2 work: repair the existing [models.dev](<http://models.dev>) integration

Founder-requested implementation checklist, added 2026-10-08. **Continue the existing 0.10.2 work and current ownership. Repair the existing integration; do not create a new crate, repository, database, service or second catalog.** This section defines the current model-catalog repair and supersedes older statements below that defer these correctness defects wholesale to 0.11. The broader consolidation issue retains its follow-up scope; private billing migrations and invoice reconciliation are not prerequisites for this repair.

The read-only audit at Engine `c54be26ec8ddcacb0d054831209025b531e605f9` confirmed four remaining defects: sparse provider rows shadow rich metadata; live [models.dev](<http://models.dev>) rates are explicitly rejected; the parser misses current identity/pricing fields; and different consumers use competing readers. Remote fetching, bounded caching and generated offline seed support already exist. Recheck drift and continue rather than restarting that investigation. Preserve the active implementer's claimed paths and progress below. This checklist is requested work, not evidence of implementation or acceptance.

### Implementation checklist

- [ ] Establish a reproducible baseline and claim the existing work.

  Work in canonical main. Coordinate dirty files before editing. Compare relevant stranded changes by content against main before recovering anything; preserve backups and inventory, and never use an old checkout as a new development lane. Use the Core execution plan and codewhale-hq/Codewhale#6396 for ownership/evidence. Capture one fetched catalog with timestamp/hash and the matching Codewhale raw JSON/list/picker/runtime outputs. Record the actual provider/endpoint/auth mode and active config overrides without secrets. This gives an exact before/after comparison without depending on a changing upstream website.
- [ ] Define which facts each source owns.

  [Models.dev](<http://Models.dev>) supplies public model facts and provider-offering specifications/prices. The selected provider/account supplies actual access, route identity and any account-specific metadata. Explicit Codewhale configuration supplies user overrides and effective operating settings. Preserve these distinctions within one resolver: a catalog listing is not proof the account can call the model, and a published price is not an invoice. Keep supported, configured, available, deprecated and unknown states distinct. Do not automatically switch the selected model, account or billing route when a catalog refreshes.
- [ ] Parse the generated upstream schema completely for the features Codewhale uses.

  Read the combined catalog, including canonical models and provider offerings. Consume `canonical_model_id` from generated JSON, retaining legacy `base_model` compatibility where needed and rejecting conflicting identity claims rather than guessing. Preserve display names/families, distinct context/input/output limits, capability booleans, modalities, reasoning controls, interleaving, lifecycle status, provider/model transport hints and pricing structure. Preserve descriptive metadata needed by existing views; unknown optional fields must not break all ingestion. The generated provider row already incorporates upstream inheritance and overrides: do not reconstruct a different result or refill intentionally removed fields. Invalid required values must produce a bounded visible diagnostic rather than silently erasing the entire previous good catalog.

  Owner: `crates/config/src/models_dev.rs` and its projection in `crates/config/src/catalog.rs`. Several fields parse today but are lost in downstream projection, so follow each required field to the final consumer. References: [current upstream schema](<https://github.com/anomalyco/models.dev/blob/dev/packages/core/src/schema.ts>) and [API/identity/inheritance documentation](<https://github.com/anomalyco/models.dev#api>).
- [ ] Correct model identity and availability joins.

  Keep canonical model ID separate from the exact provider wire ID sent on a request. Normalize provider aliases consistently and preserve distinct endpoint/account/auth scopes. Use explicit upstream canonical relationships instead of name prefixes, family guesses or flattening gateway IDs. Same-named models on direct Anthropic, a gateway and a custom endpoint can have different limits and rates. Metadata-only entries may be shown in discovery without inventing a callable route. Check pagination and completeness of provider discovery before absence in a response is treated as removal; preserve configured custom models through existing explicit policy.
- [ ] Replace whole-row shadowing with field-aware resolution.

  An ID-only provider response states that a model exists; it does not state that context, capabilities and prices became unknown. Enrich that row from the exact compatible [models.dev](<http://models.dev>) provider offering. Preserve explicit provider values, false, zero and empty values with meaningful upstream semantics; fill only genuine absence. Scope signed corrections and user overrides to the facts/routes they actually name. Track where each resolved fact came from so a provider roster cannot relabel a [models.dev](<http://models.dev>) price as provider-confirmed.

  Repair both merged-list and exact-route paths in `crates/tui/src/provider_lake.rs`, plus any used `CatalogCompiler::compile` path in `crates/config/src/catalog.rs`. Both currently insert whole rows. Keep the source of ID-only offerings in `crates/tui/src/client.rs` honest; do not replace missing provider facts with invented defaults there. A single resolver should own this merge rule wherever consumed.
- [ ] Accept live [models.dev](<http://models.dev>) rates as published-price estimates.

  Remove the blanket capabilities-only rejection in `crates/tui/src/pricing.rs`. Its current `verified_catalog_offering` path replaces live [models.dev](<http://models.dev>) pricing with bundled rates or strips it. Update existing assertions that demand that obsolete behavior. Live catalog rates should refresh displayed estimates; Codewhale-managed billable rates, provider-reported charge receipts, enterprise terms and subscription quotas retain their own explicitly identified basis. Missing price is unknown, not free. An unpriced portion must not disappear from a total presented as complete.
- [ ] Preserve and evaluate the actual price structure.

  Support input/output, cache read/write, context tiers and relevant separately priced reasoning/audio token classes. Normalize the legacy `context_over_200k` representation with `tiers` when encountered, without counting both. Apply the tier threshold and usage definitions for the actual serving route. Do not silently flatten an unsupported tier/mode into the cheapest base rate; make the unsupported estimate explicit. Preserve provider-specific schedules and pricing modes already supported, instead of losing them in the merge. Avoid double-counting cached input or reasoning tokens that are subsets of total output.

  Reuse `crates/config/src/pricing.rs` for a shared quote calculation, with precise amounts/rounding and explicit currency/units; retire duplicate TUI calculations as their last consumers migrate. Four optional f64 fields in `ModelsDevCost` cannot express the upstream pricing structure. Do not introduce another parallel quote engine. Preserve sufficiently small rates without rounding them to zero.
- [ ] Make price freshness and history truthful.

  Distinguish source fetch time, upstream update metadata, any actual rate effective time and cache expiry. A fresh download alone is not an invoice verification or a provider's declared effective date. Show whether a current estimate is live, cached, stale or unavailable. Keep offline facts available under an explicit fallback policy; do not silently advertise an expired fallback price as current. Persist the quote used for each dispatch in the existing receipt path. Never apply today's refreshed rate retroactively to old usage or discard authoritative historical amounts.
- [ ] Fix context/output budgeting through the entire runtime.

  Use resolved limits for the picker, request validation, output ceiling, compaction and context percentage. Preserve advertised context, separate max input/output, configured output budget and effective usable context as distinct values. Respect explicit user/route overrides and any applicable endpoint constraint. When effective capacity is smaller than the catalog maximum, show the reason. Remove stale hardcoded fallbacks where an actual fact exists. For genuinely unknown limits, preserve a labeled conservative policy rather than presenting a guess as a published maximum. Do not set every Claude model to 1M: the dated snapshot includes both 1M models and Haiku 4.5 at 200K.

  Trace `crates/tui/src/config.rs`, `crates/models/src/lib.rs`, `crates/config/src/catalog/reviewed.rs`, route-budget/compaction consumers and the picker/footer. A correct picker number with an old runtime denominator does not complete the repair.
- [ ] Fix capability labels and request settings together.

  Distinguish reasoning supported, unsupported and unknown from the current reasoning selection. Preserve supported toggle/effort/token-budget options and their actual values; do not collapse every provider into one low/medium/high set. Display unknown as unknown, not “off”. Make supported tools, image/file/audio/video input, structured output and temperature controls agree with the resolved offering and Codewhale's implemented transport. Only send parameters the selected route supports. Preserve prior user settings when valid, explaining a now-invalid setting rather than silently changing route or account.
- [ ] Make every relevant consumer use the same resolved facts.

  Cover both `codewhale models` and `codewhale model list`, model resolve/set, the TUI picker/detail views, defaults/fallback selection, runtime planning/compaction, parent and delegated model selection, status/usage/cost views, and Engine API/client projections. The singular CLI command still constructs `ModelRegistry::default()`, while other paths consume the provider lake. Remove separate live-ignorant decisions in agent ModelInfo, bundled intrinsic helpers, constants and generated web facts as their consumers migrate. Keep exact user-selected model IDs and existing persisted config/session compatibility. Do not build a resolver with one caller and leave the rest on the old system.
- [ ] Complete refresh, persistence and offline behavior without adding another fetcher.

  Reuse `crates/tui/src/models_dev_live.rs`: it already supplies background fetching, TTL, bounded responses, disk caching and atomic writes. Ensure all catalog entry points initialize/use it consistently; successful refresh invalidates every derived snapshot and visible projection. Provide a working explicit refresh/retry action through existing controls. Keep input responsive, avoid per-card network requests and repeated parsing, and preserve the last good snapshot on timeout/parse failure. Handle old cache formats through the existing migration/invalidating path; do not tell the user to delete all configuration or credentials. Check source override isolation, empty/partial responses and restart persistence. Pin each active request to coherent facts while allowing later requests to see new metadata.
- [ ] Regenerate the fallback and remove catalog drift.

  Use the existing generated offline seed pipeline from [models.dev](<http://models.dev>); do not paste new model values into Rust match arms. Ensure its documented coverage meets supported cold-start behavior and does not accidentally freeze an obsolete six-model list. Keep any seed-size subset intentional and visible. Shrink `catalog_corrections.json` and other local overrides to current, sourced exceptions. Data-only corrections belong upstream when practical; transport/account policy belongs in Codewhale. Unknown new providers may be discoverable without claiming an unimplemented transport is callable. Existing supported providers should gain new model facts through data refresh, without another binary release.
- [ ] Make mismatches explainable and verify the finished behavior.

  Through existing model detail/diagnostic output, expose the selected provider and exact wire ID, canonical ID, relevant source/fetch time, config override, effective limit and price basis. Keep the ordinary picker compact. Produce a bounded comparison of one upstream snapshot against resolved Codewhale output; every difference must be an explicit route/config/policy difference or an identified defect. This is a direct verification artifact, not a new permanent audit service.

  Required checks: Anthropic ID-only refresh retaining its metadata; current 1M rows and a 200K control; reasoning unknown versus disabled; cache/tier-edge estimates; a gateway override and custom endpoint with the same model spelling; a subscription route with no fabricated per-token bill; refresh during use; offline first start; stale/corrupt cache; historical cost stability; consistent values across both CLIs, picker, context usage and Engine API. Verify that model changes reach the installed candidate and that responsiveness/idle CPU do not regress. Run existing focused checks, update obsolete expectations and run required repository gates. Add no new unit/integration tests or code comments without an explicit task request. Report real nonzero counts; direct execution, tests, provider acceptance and installed behavior are separate evidence.

### 0.10.2 acceptance and handoff

- [ ] Capture one catalog snapshot with timestamp/hash and compare the same provider/endpoint/model against Codewhale before and after. Explain every remaining mismatch.
- [ ] Demonstrate that an Anthropic ID-only refresh retains prices, context, output limits and capabilities; both CLI model commands, picker, runtime context usage and Engine API agree.
- [ ] Demonstrate tier/cache pricing, supported versus enabled reasoning, route/account isolation, offline/stale/corrupt-cache behavior and frozen historical costs.
- [ ] Qualify the installed candidate with exact source identity, installed version/hash, actual nonzero existing-check counts and responsiveness evidence. Do not infer provider/invoice/physical-terminal acceptance from unit checks.
- [ ] Update existing help/feature/release documentation and this issue's evidence; clearly identify the completed 0.10.2 slice and broader consolidation work still open.

Use canonical `codewhale` on `main` under the current workspace instructions; preserve peer changes and reconcile older checkout work before editing. Do not add new unit/integration tests or code comments without explicit task authorization; run existing checks and update obsolete expectations. Config pricing is currently floating-point: reuse its provenance/quote ownership while correcting precision, rather than assuming an exact-money implementation already exists.

The related [ChatGPT authorization repair #6925](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6925>), [xAI authentication inspection #6926](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6926>), responsiveness and every-shell inspection work remain separate active requirements; this checklist does not replace them. Release visibility: [0.10.2 planning tracker #6094](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6094>).

---

## Earlier scope, implementation history and active ownership

> **Status at 0.10.1** (re-triaged 2026-10-08): partly done. Filed against 0.10.0 (filed 2026-09-22, the day v0.10.0 was tagged; body cites 0.10.0 commit 2dca7fcdda).
>
> **What remains**
>
> * Pricing: fold crates/tui/src/pricing.rs (5,888 lines, f64) into the provenance model in crates/config/src/pricing.rs - integer micros, sourceRef/checkedAt/expiresAt per rate, one quote function, golden vectors for DeepSeek time-of-day and tier edges
> * Catalog: move aliases and supports_tools out of crates/agent/src/lib.rs ModelInfo into the catalog; retire the remaining match tables in crates/models/src/lib.rs and the consts in crates/config/src/provider_defaults.rs
> * Reconcile the three price authorities (TUI [pricing.rs](<http://pricing.rs>), platform rate cards, cwc_usage_rate_cards) and diff rates against real provider invoices
> * Upstream thin vendors (AICraft, MiMo, SenseNova, StepFun, DashScope, command-code) to [models.dev](<http://models.dev>) and shrink crates/config/assets/catalog_corrections.json accordingly
>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
>
> * Slice A done: crates/config/src/catalog.rs:448-487 at v0.10.1 enumerates namespaced top-level `catalog.models` keys as offerings after provider rows (comment cites #6396)
> * Slice B done: commits cbfbcb699c 'upstream-keyed canonical entries join offline (#6396 slice B)', 6227825dd7 'generate the offline seed from a reviewed spec and a lock', cd5e643512 'regenerate the offline seed from [Models.dev](<http://Models.dev>)'; CHANGELOG.md:834-841 'The offline model list is now generated from [Models.dev](<http://Models.dev>) instead of edited by hand'
> * Bundled seed now carries upstream-shaped keys: crates/config/assets/models_dev.bundled.json at v0.10.1 has models keys xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro and xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-flash plus `_meta`/`_reviewed`
> * Slice C partly done: `git grep -w ApiProvider v0.10.1 -- crates` matches only a test-local enum (crates/tui/src/config/tests.rs:16519) and `git grep KIND_LOOKUP v0.10.1` is empty; crates/models/assets/model_catalog.bundled.json no longer exists; crates/tui/src/config/models.rs is down to 34 lines / 6 consts
> * Slice C still open: crates/agent/src/lib.rs:29-35 still owns ModelInfo aliases (21 supports_tools hits); crates/tui/src/pricing.rs is still 5,888 lines; crates/config/src/provider_defaults.rs and web/lib/facts.generated.ts still exist
> * Pricing partly done: unknown-is-a-value exists as UnpricedReason (crates/tui/src/pricing.rs:1197) and provenance-carrying rows in crates/config/src/pricing.rs:1-19, but [pricing.rs](<http://pricing.rs>) still has 56 f64 lines and there are two Rust pricing modules; CHANGELOG.md:823-833 and :842-845 record the 0.10.1 price corrections

---

Supersedes #4173, which was opened from a 2026-07 architecture doc with counts that have since drifted (it says 81 models / 31 providers; both are now far larger). Its acceptance criterion was "there is an inventory of which registries are product contracts vs generated/catalog data vs internal implementation." That inventory now exists and is below, so the old issue is closed in favour of this scoped one.

## Root cause, verified

`offerings_from_models_dev` (`crates/config/src/catalog.rs:344`) enumerates catalog offerings from `catalog.providers[*].models` **only**.

[models.dev](<http://models.dev>) deliberately splits facts *about a model* from facts *about a provider serving it*. We implemented one half. A model that exists only in the top-level `models` map therefore produces no offering and can never be listed — so we are structurally late for **every** vendor, not just the one that surfaced it.

Two precisions worth recording, because they change the fix:

1. The top-level map is not entirely unread — `crates/config/src/models_dev.rs:86` reads it for reasoning-support enrichment. The defect is in *enumeration*, not deserialization. The fix is "enumerate from the union", not "read a field nobody reads".
2. `ModelsDevModel` (`models_dev.rs:199`) carries **no provider field** — `id`, `name`, `family`, capabilities, `limit`, `modalities`, and nothing naming who serves it. The join must therefore come from the map key (`xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro`). That works against live upstream data, but our bundled snapshot keys models bare (its only two entries are `deepseek-v4-pro`, `deepseek-v4-flash`). So the ingestion fix alone does **not** repair offline/first-boot until `crates/config/assets/models_dev.bundled.json` is regenerated in upstream shape.

Consequence for 0.10.0: commit `2dca7fcdda` (hand-seeded MiMo 2.6 rows) is a human doing the join the code refuses to do, and it stays load-bearing for cold offline start. Retire it when the seed is regenerated, not when the ingestion fix lands.

## Inventory: seven independent declarations of the same model facts

<!-- linear:table-colwidths:266,266,266 -->
| \# | Source | Size |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | `crates/models/src/lib.rs` match tables | \~150 ids |
| 2 | `crates/models/assets/model_catalog.bundled.json` | 56 entries |
| 3 | `crates/config/assets/models_dev.bundled.json` | 99 rows / 21 providers |
| 4 | `crates/agent/src/lib.rs` `ModelInfo` | 155 entries — the only home for aliases + `supports_tools` |
| 5 | `crates/config/src/provider_defaults.rs` | 169 consts, duplicated verbatim in `crates/tui/src/config/models.rs` |
| 6 | `crates/tui/src/pricing.rs` | 5,920 lines, 287 price match arms |
| 7 | `web/lib/facts.generated.ts` | 50 providers / 77 models |

Plus two parallel provider enums — `ProviderKind` (52) and `ApiProvider` (53) — bridged by a fixed-size `KIND_LOOKUP: [_; 53]` in `crates/tui/src/config.rs`.

Adding one provider today costs \~14 hand edits across `provider_kind.rs`, `provider.rs`, `lib.rs`, the TUI enum and that fixed-size array. That cost is why vendors go missing: adding one is a code change, so it competes with feature work and loses.

## Slices

**A — model-only ingestion.** Enumerate offerings from the union of `providers[*].models` and namespaced top-level `models` keys. \~30 lines plus a test. Stops every vendor being late. Land first, independent of everything else.

**B — regenerate the offline seed in upstream key shape**, so A also fixes cold start, then retire the hand-seeded rows.

**C — collapse to one authority.** Migrate the last consumer of each of the seven, deleting as you go; move aliases + `supports_tools` out of `crates/agent` into the catalog (their only home today); collapse `ApiProvider` into `ProviderKind` so `KIND_LOOKUP` dies. Large blast radius — exhaustive matches across two crates — so it is deliberately not a release-window change.

**D — upstream the thin vendors to [models.dev](<http://models.dev>)** (AICraft, MiMo, SenseNova, StepFun, DashScope, command-code). It is a public repo; the live refresh then picks them up with no infrastructure, and every other tool benefits. Keep a local overlay only for what [models.dev](<http://models.dev>) structurally cannot carry: transport facts and prices we bill against.

## Pricing: hold it to billing standard before billing exists

Display-only today, but `PRODUCT_PRD.md:220` commits to "an evidence-backed model catalog". A wrong cost number is a false product claim regardless of whether money moves.

There are currently **three** pricing authorities: `pricing.rs` (display), the platform rate cards (`CWC_MANAGED_MODEL_RATE_CARDS_JSON`), and `cwc_usage_rate_cards` (Postgres). When they disagree we show one number and would charge another. Managed inference is gated off today, so fixing the divergence now costs nothing; after it is enabled it means migrating historical charges.

The rate-card shape in `wrangler.jsonc` is already the professional one — `revision`, `sourceRef`, `pricingPolicy`, `checkedAt`, `expiresAt`, integer micros, customer vs provider rates, `CWC_RATE_CARD_MAX_AGE_DAYS`. The work is propagating it, not inventing it:

1. Integer micros end to end, never `f64`.
2. `sourceRef` / `checkedAt` / `expiresAt` on every rate; past expiry reads unpriced, never stale-priced.
3. Unknown is a value, not zero — `Quote::Unpriced { reason }` as a type, so no surface can render a guess as `$0.00`. The MiMo seed already gets this right in data; make it unrepresentable to get wrong.
4. Separate rate data (catalog rows) from billing-surface detection (credential logic, stays local) from rate rules (time-of-day, context tiers) as a few typed variants over data rather than 287 arms.
5. Freeze the quote at dispatch and persist it in the receipt; a later refresh must never reprice history. Already correct on the cloud-facts path — generalize it.
6. One quote function, one stated rounding rule, an audit trail per number.
7. Golden vectors: `(route, usage, timestamp)` → exact amount, covering the DeepSeek time-of-day windows and the 512k/272k/200k tier edges.
8. **Reconcile against real invoices.** The evidence file records invoice reconciliation as "unqualified". 287 arms nobody has diffed against a bill are 287 guesses, however tidy. This is the only item that needs something we do not already have, and it is the one that separates professional from merely organized.

Items 1–7 are engineering. Item 8 is ground truth, and no amount of 1–7 substitutes for it.

2026-10-08 Codex /root takeover (local 0.10.2 candidate, no push): claimed crates/config/src/{models_dev.rs,[catalog.rs](<http://catalog.rs>),[pricing.rs](<http://pricing.rs>)}, existing related tests/literals, crates/tui/src/{provider_lake.rs,provider_catalog_live.rs,[pricing.rs](<http://pricing.rs>),tui/model_picker.rs}, and crates/cli/src/lib.rs for current [models.dev](<http://models.dev>) schema, sparse-roster completion, scoped/frozen estimates, and CLI agreement. Source confirms config pricing is currently floating-point; the earlier handoff's claim of an existing exact-money implementation was inaccurate. Broader invoice and managed-billing consolidation remains open. No new test cases or code comments under current operator instructions; existing cases will be adapted where behavior changes.

issues.title: v0.11: Model refresh can still drift — 24 unseeded remote providers, unreachable non-text rows, unflagged stale pins, no scheduled job

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: providers
labels.description: Model providers, routing, auth, catalogs and pricing

issues.body:
**Why this matters.** The founder reported that the OpenAI/ChatGPT models were visibly out of date and concluded the model-updating system had failed. The user-visible symptom had a real cause (see "What was fixed"), but investigating it surfaced four systemic gaps that keep any route able to drift silently: 24 remote providers have no offline seed facts, non-text-output rows are unreachable, a stale-but-present pin is never flagged, and the scheduled refresh exists only as prose. Each is independently checkable, so they are tracked here as one body of work rather than four vague wishes.

## What was fixed (evidence, verified against the shipped binary)

The refresh pipeline was healthy; the installed binary was older than the catalog it read.

- `codewhale models --provider openai` on the installed release binary showed `source=models_dev_cache status={"state":"fresh"}` with 51 rows.
- `~/.codewhale/catalog/models-dev-catalog.json` held 230 providers / 8,849 rows, `python3 scripts/catalog_models_dev.py seed age --max-days 30` → 0.0 days.
- Stale ChatGPT-plan rosters at launch were fixed in `c869044358`.

So "OpenAI is stale" was a stale *binary*, not a dead updater. The gaps below are what remains.

## Gap 1 — 24 remote providers have no offline seed block

`crates/config/assets/provider_descriptors.json` declares 52 providers; `scripts/catalog/models_dev_seed.toml` has 23 seed blocks. Four uncovered entries are loopback (`custom`, `ollama`, `sglang`, `vllm`) and one is a disabled legacy route (`antigravity`), leaving 24 remote providers with no pinned offline facts:

`atlascloud, codewhale, concentrate, csdn, deepinfra, deepseek-anthropic, edenai, huggingface, longcat, mistral, modelscope, nvidia-nim, ollama-cloud, openai-codex, opencode-go, opencode-zen, openmodel, qianfan, sakana, siliconflow-CN, telecomjs, volcengine, wanjie-ark, zenmux`

With no network, or with `CODEWHALE_DISABLE_MODELS_DEV_FETCH=1`, those routes browse only the generic bundled set. `openai-codex` is the notable one, because the ChatGPT-plan roster is exactly the surface that was reported stale.

## Gap 2 — non-text-output rows are unreachable by any path

`xai`'s `grok-imagine-*` image/video models are dropped before the picker sees them. `codewhale models --provider xai` lists 13 rows and none of them, although the live cache holds:

```
xai/grok-imagine-image -> {"type":"image","modalities":{"input":["text","image"],
  "output":["image"]},"limit":{"context":16000,"output":0}}   // no "cost" key
```

`google/gemini-3-pro-image` survives because `modalities.output` is `["text","image"]`, `limit.output` is 32768, and `cost` is present. The drop happens in the catalog/lake projection, not in `model_picker.rs`. The live cache holds 453 non-language rows across 53 providers (`vercel` 155, `poe` 31, `digitalocean` 16, `google` 14, `edenai` 12, `nvidia` 12).

Product question to settle first: should a chat-model picker list image/video-only models at all? If yes, this is a catalog projection change; if no, the drop should be deliberate and documented rather than incidental.

## Gap 3 — a stale-but-served pin is never flagged

`crates/tui/src/tui/model_picker.rs:2275-2305` reacts only when a pinned model id vanishes from the catalog. A pin that still exists but is three generations behind renders as normal and healthy, which is precisely the shape the report took from a user's seat: nothing is broken, the model is just old.

## Gap 4 — the scheduled refresh is prose only

`docs/CATALOG_REFRESH.md` carries a "Recommended scheduled job (not shipped yet)" section. Until it ships, "the model updating system" refreshes when someone runs it by hand. Wiring it needs a maintainer token, which is a founder decision.

## Desired behavior

1. Every remote provider in `provider_descriptors.json` either has a seed block or an explicit, justified exemption recorded in the seed spec, and `seed render --check` / `defaults audit --spec` stay green.
2. Non-text-output rows are handled deliberately: either projected with their modality visible in the picker, or dropped by an explicit rule with a test naming the rule.
3. A pinned model that is materially older than the catalog's newest generation for that provider is surfaced in the picker (a chip or notice), without changing the selection.
4. A scheduled catalog refresh exists as a runnable job with a documented token source, or the doc states plainly that refresh is manual and removes the "not shipped yet" section.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `python3 scripts/catalog_models_dev.py seed render --check` and `defaults audit --spec` pass with no provider listed in Gap 1 left unaccounted for.
- [ ] `codewhale models --provider xai` shows `grok-imagine-*` rows, or a test asserts the exact predicate that excludes them.
- [ ] A picker test pins an outdated-but-present model and asserts the staleness flag renders; a healthy pin renders without it.
- [ ] `docs/CATALOG_REFRESH.md` describes a job that exists in the tree, or no longer promises one.

## Evidence

Full writeup and commands: `CW/artifacts/model-refresh-20261023/MODEL-REFRESH-GAP.md` (local artifact). All claims above were produced by running the shipped binary and reading the on-disk catalog.

## Related

- #6396 — pricing authority; the price tables and `CatalogCompiler` bypass are tracked there, deliberately out of scope here.

🤖 Filed from a live investigation on `main` @ `ec45097d01` with the installed binary and catalog in place.
— Written by deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 (AI agent) on behalf of the maintainers.

issues.title: Deferred-toolbox eviction is economically net-negative under provider prompt caching: full-prefix re-prefill + write premiums, permanent stale recovery notes, wire-byte-blind budget
issues.body:
### What happened? 发生了什么？

The bounded deferred-tool toolbox (`ToolActivationCache`, 8 names / 16 KiB, `crates/tui/src/core/session.rs:17-19` at HEAD `008d21d69`) is **cost-blind**, and under current provider prompt-cache pricing its eviction path is economically net-negative. Concretely:

**1. Eviction invalidates the entire downstream prefix — the one toolbox operation with no offsetting benefit.**
The prefix fingerprint is `SHA256(system) + SHA256(tools wire array)` with order load-bearing (`crates/tui/src/prefix_cache.rs`), and tools sit at the front of the rendered prompt on every provider. Any admission/eviction mutates the tools array, so system + tools + the **entire conversation history** re-prefills at miss price. `docs/CACHE.md` calls this "an expected, one-request miss" (lines 39-40) — wording written when cache writes were free:

| Provider/API | Cached-input read | Write premium | Tool-change invalidation |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenAI Chat/Responses | 0.1x | 1.25x (GPT-5.6+) | prefix from that point (tools are first) |
| Anthropic Messages | 0.1x | 1.25x (5m) / 2x (1h) | **any tool change invalidates the entire cache** (tools are block 1) |
| DeepSeek | 1/30 – 1/50 | none | prefix-based |
| Moonshot Kimi k3 | 0.1x | 1x (5m) / 2x (1h) | prefix from that point |

Break-even for evicting one ~400-token schema from a session with H tokens of history: pay ≈ 0.9–2.25 × H once, save ≈ 0.9 × 400 per later request → needs ~75 further tool-free requests at H = 30K. Real conversations run 6–40 requests. Admission at least unlocks a needed capability; **eviction only pays when the session is about to end anyway**. LRU position alone is the eviction trigger today — no hysteresis, no cost term, and two alternating overflowing searches would re-prefill the full prefix every round.

**2. The eviction→recovery cycle multiplies the loss (relevant to the in-flight reporting work).**
Reporting evictions (as the Pinvou fork's open PR #101 does) is necessary for correctness — silent eviction caused a live incident where a model fabricated tool results for tools that had vanished from its `<functions>`. But the recovery contract ("re-search to re-activate") completes a cycle whose full cost stack, for one eviction of 4 browser tools (~460 tokens of schema) in a 30K-token history with 20 requests remaining (0.1x reads, 1.25x writes):

| # | Cost item | Tok-eq |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Eviction invalidation (re-prefill + write premium) | ~34,500 |
| 2 | Eviction note in history (≈72–147 tokens/event; rides the result forever; 1 + 19×0.1x) | ~427 |
| 3 | Recovery re-search round trip | ~3,050 |
| 4 | Search-result payload becomes history | ~1,160 |
| 5 | Re-activation invalidation (tools array changes again — second re-prefill + write) | ~34,500 |
| | **Total vs never evicting** | **≈ 73,600 (~2.5× the entire history)** |

Two structural gaps in the reporting design: (a) **notes are never retracted** — ride-time netting (`render_toolbox_eviction_notes`) only trims the note at the moment it attaches to a result; once in history it is permanent, and the only "compaction" that removes it is generic conversation compaction; (b) **re-activation carries no supersession marker** — the re-admitting search result is byte-identical to a first-time hit (`tool_references` list only), so after recovery the model's history permanently contains "these tools are no longer callable" next to a tools array that has them again. (Compare: the direct-call hydration path does emit an explicit "was deferred and has now been loaded" receipt.)

**3. The headline saving is first-turn-only, and the budget does not measure wire bytes.**
The historical justification ("reduce catalog tokens 73%") measures a first-request, native-tools-only, `bytes/4`-estimated ratio — no provider, no tokenizer, no MCP, caching never modeled. Under caching, both an eager stable header and the deferred header are hit-priced after request 1; the durable steady-state saving is ~0.1x-scale. Separately, the 16 KiB toolbox budget is measured in engine-side serde bytes (`ToolActivationCache::serialized_bytes`), while the same tool serializes differently per wire family (Chat Completions wrapper ~69 B/tool, Anthropic ~40 B, Responses ~71 B) and per-provider sanitizers (Moonshot MFJS, root-level `oneOf/anyOf` flattening) change schemas further — so the budget is a proxy that matches no provider's actual token accounting.

**4. In practice the mechanism survives by accident.**
Across five real sessions on k3/DeepSeek (93–94% hit ratios with heavy `tool_search` churn vs 92.5% baseline without), activation happened at request 1 (short history) and the surface then stayed stable within turns. The measured re-prefill drivers were skill loading and engine restarts — not tool_search. The one live failure (mid-task silent eviction) is exactly the case with no offsetting saving.

### Expected 期望

Surface-change decisions — especially LRU eviction — should be cost-aware or at least cost-attributed, and the eviction-recovery loop should not leave permanent stale statements in history:

1. **Hysteresis / eviction economics**: a minimum activation lifetime, or an eviction cost term once current re-prefill size exceeds a few multiples of the evicted schema. Pure LRU position makes mid-task eviction the default worst case.
2. **Update `docs/CACHE.md`**'s "expected, one-request miss" for the write-premium era, and reconcile observed `cache_hit_tokens`/`cache_miss_tokens` against declared `change:<what>` re-pins — today telemetry and decisions never meet (`calculate_cache_savings` is `#[cfg(test)]`-only).
3. **Supersession semantics for recovery**: when a reported-evicted tool is re-activated, emit an explicit restored/re-admitted marker (hydration-receipt style) so the history's "no longer callable" note is not left as the last word; consider bounding note persistence (e.g. drop after the next successful activation of the named tools, or fold into compaction).
4. **Evaluate append-in-context injection** for dynamic tools (Moonshot's documented pattern: keep the top-level `tools` array stable, append dynamic declarations as a trailing system message inside `messages`) — zero prefix invalidation by construction, which sidesteps items 1 and 5 of the cost stack entirely.
5. **Measure the toolbox budget in wire-shaped bytes** (or tokenizer tokens) per active wire format rather than engine serde bytes.

### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

Economic issue rather than a crash; the observable sequence:

1. Start a conversation that activates ≥8 deferred tools (e.g. a browser task: `tool_search` for browser tools, then a second search for page-management tools).
2. Observe the second search silently evicting earlier activations from the request tools array (no model-visible signal at HEAD `008d21d69` — `delta.evicted` is consumed by `remove_evicted_cache_activations` in `execute_tool_search_inner`, `tool_catalog.rs:1546-1551`).
3. Watch `/cache stats` + provider usage: the next request reports a miss covering the full history; on Anthropic routes the write premium applies; re-searching to recover triggers a second full miss + write.
4. Cross-check the arithmetic against `calculate_turn_cost_from_usage_with_prision`-billed totals for the session.

### Codewhale version 版本

`008d21d69` (workspace 0.10.2; latest tag v0.10.1) — verified at this HEAD on 2026-10-13; the mechanism is unchanged from v0.9.12 through HEAD. Observed live via the Pinvou downstream (fork pinned at v0.9.12 + maintenance), engine-level, platform-independent.

### Where did it happen? 在哪里出现？

Engine — affects all surfaces (TUI / CLI / Desktop / Web) and all providers with prefix caching, which in 2026 is all of them.

### Before you start 前置确认

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。（recent 100 issues swept for tool/cache/deferred/eviction — no overlap）

issues.body:
## Problem (user report against 0.10.1 and the 0.10.2 candidate)

With many successful `run` cards, a long completed output collapses to `N lines omitted ⌥V:output`. A still-running silent recursive search shows `run running · stale · no output 2m 07s`. After newer cards arrive, the user cannot reliably open the operation that is still running, or the exact completed call they picked. Whether the control is unreachable, selects the wrong operation, shows only a snapshot, or loses the record has not been established. Reproducing that is the first step.

## Scope

Every shell route Codewhale starts or tracks in a session, using the existing tool-call, job, session and agent identifiers:

* foreground Bash / `run` (the visible label is not the backend identity; inventory the real tool names and aliases first)
* commands moved to the background, and commands started in the background
* named PTY / terminal sessions
* shell work owned by delegated agents

States where supported: queued or waiting, running with output, running silent, completed, failed, cancelled, refused.

## Acceptance

1. Option+V / Alt+V and mouse click open the exact operation, including while a silent command runs and newer cards arrive. A new card never takes over the target.
2. The inspector shows the full command and working directory (existing redaction rules), owning agent, truthful state, elapsed time, last output, retained stdout/stderr and exit result when known. Silent running work says "no output yet". Silence is never shown as failed, completed or hung.
3. Expanding a grouped success card exposes each constituent call.
4. Refresh uses authoritative events or bounded reads, without consuming the model's output cursor. Follow mode stops when the user scrolls back. Scroll and copy work. Esc restores the composer draft, scroll position and selection.
5. Stop or cancel acts only on the selected live operation, under the existing ownership and authorization checks. Closing the inspector or moving on in the conversation never stops a process. Inapplicable controls are disabled.
6. Compact default presentation, plus a reachable list of current work.
7. Proof: focused tests with real nonzero counts, and controlled PTY journeys on the installed candidate at normal and narrow sizes. Local tests alone do not establish the interaction.

## Relation to existing issues

* codewhale-hq/Codewhale#6912 (GitHub #6912): PTY Terminal view in the work dock. Covers PTY sessions only.
* codewhale-hq/Codewhale#6909 (GitHub #6909): detach a blocked shell wait with Ctrl+B or steering. Already in the local 0.10.2 line.
* codewhale-hq/Codewhale#6899 (GitHub #6899): one terminal board with approve, reply and attach. v0.11, not required for 0.10.2.
* codewhale-hq/Codewhale#6436: optional running-command line on foreground shell cards.

This issue is the bounded 0.10.2 inspection requirement. It must not add a second task store or execution loop.

## Status

Filed 2026-10-09 during the 0.10.2 takeover. No implementation and no code claim yet. Candidate paths, to be claimed exactly before any edit: crates/tui/src/tui/ui/activity_detail.rs, crates/tui/src/tui/app.rs, crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs, crates/tui/src/tui/mouse_ui.rs, crates/tui/src/tui/work_surface/{model,input,interaction}.rs, crates/tui/src/commands/groups/utility/jobs.rs, crates/tui/src/tui/ui/handlers.rs, crates/tui/src/tools/shell.rs, crates/tui/src/tools/terminal_session.rs.

issues.body:
The installed Codewhale 0.10.1 ChatGPT sign-in fails before login with HTTP 400 and `invalid_authorize_request`. Continue the active 0.10.2 login repair.

Recorded anonymous initial-authorization probes on 2026-10-08 isolate an extra query parameter:

* Documented dynamic-client parameters: HTTP 302 to the login page.
* The same parameters plus `prompt=login`: HTTP 302.
* The same parameters plus `originator=codewhale`: HTTP 400, `invalid_authorize_request`.
* Both extras, as the installed client sends: HTTP 400.

These receipts establish initial request acceptance/rejection only. They do not establish completed authentication, token exchange, catalog access or inference.

A local, uncommitted patch in `crates/tui/src/oauth.rs` already sets `CHATGPT_OAUTH_PARAMS.originator` to `None` and updates the URL test. Continue and validate it; review the retained originator constant and its compatibility comment against actual consumers. No passing test or installed 0.10.2 acceptance is claimed for this patch.

Acceptance:

* Omit the unsupported originator parameter for this provider flow while retaining the documented Codewhale dynamic-client contract, PKCE S256, state, nonce, loopback callback, issuer/signature validation, granted scopes and account/workspace binding.
* Do not substitute another application's identity, import credentials without consent, or fall back to API-key billing.
* Add focused regressions for request construction and retained security properties; preserve returning-account/registration behavior.
* Verify fresh initial authorization separately from a user-completed browser login. Record test counts, candidate SHA and installed-binary evidence; leave unavailable live checks explicit.
* Preserve existing login/responsiveness/pet work in the active 0.10.2 checkout. No worktree or push/publication is part of this repair brief.

Related completed integration: codewhale-hq/Codewhale#6816 / GitHub #6816. This issue tracks the newly observed authorization regression, not a repeat of that migration.

Official contract: [https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/sign-in](<https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/sign-in>)

2026-10-08 Codex /root takeover (chat 01a11eb8-f97c-75e0-992e-fd4418d26ec3): continuing the founder-supplied 0.10.2 handoff in the existing engine-0102 checkout at local 80e1d2a9be. C17/C19/C21 first slice claims crates/tui/src/tui/pet_watch/{owner,avatars,mod}.rs, crates/tui/src/oauth.rs, crates/tui/src/commands/contract/debug_operations.rs, crates/tui/src/tools/subagent/tests.rs, crates/tui/src/tui/model_picker.rs, the three existing config_panel goldens, docs/features.toml, CHANGELOG.md and crates/tui/CHANGELOG.md. Preserve the local pet merge and login/CI repairs, remove only the inherited temporary metadata probe, inspect daemon idle/retention behavior, and validate one coherent batch using existing checks. No new worktrees or PR branches. Contributor reviews and remaining catalog/shell inspection are part of the continuing takeover; add exact path claims before their edits. Hosted, installed and physical-terminal results remain separate. No deployment/tag/publication.

issues.body:
**0.10.2 candidate update (2026-10-13).** The complete strict no-upload preflight passes for all **29** workspace crates at [6e72400bbb](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/6e72400bbb5182473e6971abcd18bd8953c2f4cc), including the new saved-DeepSeek-key correction. Every package built from its packaged source with dirty inputs disallowed; all archives carry that exact clean Git SHA, and 1,319 non-generated payloads match committed blobs with no unexpected/mismatched files. TUI is **9,431,125 bytes / 8.994222 MiB** (956 files), below the 10,485,760-byte cap, with no installed Node dependency payload. All29 pass; no Codewhale crate was uploaded. The preceding7bf pass and its29 archives are retained as historical evidence.

The audit also found and fixed two preflight defects in [2750a5d124](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/2750a5d124): Cargo’s separate build directory was being ignored, so the checker measured stale target-directory archives, and four ignored installed Node dependency files entered the TUI tarball. The checker now selects the active build directory, and the manifest explicitly excludes those installed dependencies. The frozen vendored `codewhale-ratatui` 0.1.2 dependency was [published with founder approval](https://crates.io/crates/codewhale-ratatui/0.1.2) and its downloaded bytes match the verified dry-run package.

This establishes candidate packaging readiness, with final-main freeze, RC/dist acceptance and actual all-29 registry/install readback still required before closing this issue. It does not repair or relabel the historical 0.10.1 packages. The original failure record follows.

Founder followup2026-10-09: Cargo should be0.10.1 and updatewinget. Fresh cache-busted registryreadback verifies26/28 packages published0.10.1; TUI+CLI still0.10.0. Independently rehashed frozenfead51ee TUIcrate is12,504,591bytes SHA2560dc03f1fa6d2dd977477051745dca2770bc8c2ea1ac2e1b796f8187391edefd6, exceeding10MiB and matching recordedHTTP413; CLI depends onTUI. Current0.10.2 contains packagingtrim+beforefirstuploadsizeguard, but it doesnot fill0.10.1 retroactively. No tags changed and no packages published inthisfollowup. Missing stableTUI/CLI publication needs historical packaging/provenance resolution; do not relabel dirty0.10.2as0.10.1. All29 0.10.2 tarballs+actualregistry/installreadback remain releaseacceptance gates. Winget0.10.1 alreadyexists in microsoft/winget-pkgs#448554 at1aaee6b99689: hashes/manifest/schema/scanpass, installationNEUTRAL/Validation-Executable-Error andMicrosoftreviewrequired. Parenthas noMicrosoftmergeauthority; no duplicatesubmission/comments. Verified3-manifest/x64binarypacket andCargo sourceevidence: artifacts/packaging-repair-20261009/winget-0.10.1/EVIDENCE.md. Rootowns publicationreconciliation and claims existingissue ratherthannewqueue.

**What happened (2026-10-08, v0.10.1).** The [crates.io](<http://crates.io>) publish uploaded 26 of 28 crates and then failed:

```
error: failed to publish codewhale-tui v0.10.1 to registry at https://crates.io
Caused by: the remote server responded with an error (status 413 Payload Too Large): max upload size is: 10485760
```

The packaged tarball was 11.9 MiB compressed ("Packaged 1796 files, 53.9MiB (11.9MiB compressed)"). 0.10.0 was 8.94 MiB, so the crate crossed the 10 MiB cap in one cycle. `codewhale-tui` and its dependent `codewhale-cli` never reached [crates.io](<http://crates.io>) for 0.10.1; The missing TUI/CLI versions leave the older published CLI available until a complete later release is published; 0.10.2 has not shipped yet.

**Why the existing gates did not catch it.** `cargo publish --dry-run` cannot see the limit — it is enforced server-side, and the dry run passed cleanly. The 413 surfaces only during the real upload, after all 28 crates have been packaged and verified (\~40 minutes in), which is also where it strands the release half-published.

**Proposal.** After the preflight packaging (the dry run already writes every `target/package/<crate>-<version>.crate`), stat each tarball and fail before any upload when one exceeds 10,485,760 bytes compressed, naming the crate and pointing at `exclude`/`include` in its `Cargo.toml`. A warning threshold around 9.5 MiB would give notice as a crate grows toward the cap.

0.10.2 already carries the content fix for `codewhale-tui`: `exclude` in `crates/tui/Cargo.toml` trims test sources from the published package (1796 → 1176 files; 11.9 → 9.5 MiB compressed, verified with `publish-crates.sh dry-run`).

**Receipts.** Publish log lines quoted above; `scripts/release/check-published.sh 0.10.1` lists `codewhale-tui`/`codewhale-cli` as not published; [crates.io](<http://crates.io>) size history for `codewhale-tui`: 8.42 MiB (0.9.13) → 8.94 MiB (0.10.0) → 11.9 MiB (0.10.1, refused).
