prs.title: fix: recover PostgreSQL startup during schema publication
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes intermittent PostgreSQL Gateway startup failures reporting missing physical-schema or state admission while a sibling worker publishes a first-use schema.

## User Impact

Startup can recover from a brief gap between a schema commit and delivery of its replacement admission facts. A gap longer than the one-second budget still fails visibly with the original typed error. Cancellation, owner failure, earlier caller deadlines, and all schema and authority checks remain in force.

## Why This Change Was Made

The one-shot read retry from #181837 could refresh before replacement facts reached the host. Live proof also exposed an uncovered connection-opening check and the standalone feature-schema ensure path. Both are reproduced deterministically.

One helper owns the bounded failure-only backoff and current-fact exchange. Reads retain the no-callback/no-imported-snapshot guards. Connection opening retries only initial fact acquisition, before metadata reads or caller work. Standalone feature-schema ensures replay only their own schema transaction after rollback; raw fragment checks inside arbitrary caller transactions remain unretried. Both state-admission checks use the existing typed error. No new publication registry, settlement contract, protocol, config, or lock changes were introduced.

CI exposed a narrower publication window: physical facts can arrive before version facts. The original typed error on exhaustion hid subsequent version-admission failures. An explicit retry refresh now exchanges even when physical facts are already valid, so it can receive the remaining publications. Ordinary reads do not poll. This keeps the cheap bounded mechanism rather than adding a publication-settlement contract.

## Evidence

The original read race was RED on main. On the first PR head, new tests were RED at the exact connection-opening and fragment-ensure throw sites, while the seven previous cases stayed green. The strengthened publication barrier is RED on 3f1edaef7166 with the exact CI signature: 10 transactions, 3 admission exchanges, zero callbacks, and the original typed error after 1,037 ms. It holds version publication until the reader retries with physical facts already delivered.

With the correction, all ten cases pass on the pinned Bun runtime, including both #181837 snapshot cases, the startup ledger, OPEN, standalone ensure, raw-transaction refusal, bounded exhaustion, cancellation, and an earlier deadline. All five publication cases also pass on CI's Node 24.22.1. Core and infra-test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, the runtime build, and independent P0–P3 reviews pass. The per-reader loop is replaced by one shared policy owner; the final correction was simplified to one refresh condition plus the stronger existing fixture.

Final head: bba066dcd34d1a957d13147ad292363100736d3b. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards executed and passed in [CI run 40056882588](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40056882588). Fresh PGLIVE5 cron proof passed 30/30 direct and 30/30 relay starts, with zero admission failures of either message and no third admission failure. The relay adds 15 ms per direction. Runtime source hashes were verified unchanged through the loop. No performance claim is made.

Local native provisioning proof previously had two 120-second timeouts. Their equivalent Linux CI cases passed in 10.6 and 8.3 seconds on the inventory-correction head; the local failures remain recorded as investigated rather than claimed fixed. CI also caught the new helper missing from the copied wrapper source inventory; the one-line inventory correction has its own clean review and passing closure proof.

Change size against the base: production +103/−37, tests +698/−28, docs +10/−4, wrapper inventory +1.

prs.title: fix: queued messages show no typing indicator while they wait behind a live run
prs.body:
Closes #162547

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a direct message that queues behind a live run shows no typing indicator for the whole wait, even though `docs/concepts/queue.md` says typing still fires on enqueue.

## User Impact

User impact: on Telegram and other channels whose turns carry an adoption lifecycle, a message queued behind a busy session keeps showing "typing…" until its own run starts and replies. Typing stops when the queued item finishes, is cancelled, or is dropped from the queue. Messages that do not queue are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The enqueue path already signals typing when a follow-up queues behind a live run, and the follow-up runner keeps the same typing controller. But the buffered dispatcher that handled the inbound message then returns. Its dispatcher idle callback and its `finally` (`markRunComplete` and `markDispatchIdle` in `src/auto-reply/dispatch.ts`) seal that controller and call the channel's `onIdle`, which closes the channel typing loop for good. So typing starts and stops within the same ~360 ms dispatch the issue's log shows (`message dispatch completed ... duration=363ms`).

Related: #92287 starts typing when a queued turn begins to execute (#92267). This change covers the wait before that, and keeps the controller that run would use from being sealed when the inbound dispatch returns.

This follows the direction in the ClawSweeper review: the queued item owns typing from enqueue to settlement.

- `createReplyDispatcherWithTyping` returns a new internal `onTypingHandoff` reply option. It lives in `InternalReplySessionOptions` next to `onReplyOperationOwned`, not in the public `GetReplyOptions`, and `publicReplyOptions` strips it from plugin-supplied options. Core builds these reply options itself in `dispatchReplyWithBufferedBlockDispatcher`, so Telegram still gets the handoff. After it is called, the dispatcher no longer completes the typing controller. When typing comes only from `typingCallbacks`, their `onIdle` (typing teardown) is deferred, and the queued item's typing cleanup runs `onCleanup` and then that `onIdle` once. The handoff state lives in `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher-typing-handoff.ts`.
- A channel that passes its own `onIdle` gets no `onTypingHandoff`, so its whole typing lifecycle is unchanged. That `onIdle` can do more than stop typing: Feishu's (`extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts:1232`, `queueIdleSideEffects`) finalizes streaming delivery and closes the card preview. Deferring it made finalization wait on itself (ClawSweeper revision 3). Running it while the handed-off controller kept ticking let the next tick's `onReplyStart` reopen the closed preview (revision 5). So Feishu does not get typing through the queued wait. Channels that pass only `typingCallbacks`, such as Telegram, do.
- `runReplyAgent`, on the enqueue-behind-a-live-run path, closes typing from the queued item's `turnAdoptionLifecycle.onSettled`. Queue completion calls that for a run that finished, a cancelled item, a cleared queue, and the sources of a collected batch.
- The handoff happens only when the follow-up has an adoption lifecycle and queued typing actually started (`typing.isActive()` after `signalToolStart`). Without a lifecycle nothing would settle the typing. In `message` typing mode typing does not start before text, so the controller's `cleanup` never calls `onCleanup` and a deferred `onIdle` would never run. Both cases keep today's behavior. That keeps a dropped item from leaving a typing loop running forever.
- The dispatcher exposes `onTypingHandoff` only when the channel supplied a cleanup callback, because the deferred `onIdle` runs from that callback.
- Each queued `FollowupRun` now carries the typing controller of the dispatch that queued it (`typing`), and the follow-up runner completes that one (`queued.typing ?? defaults.typing`). The queue keeps only the latest runner per key, so before this an earlier queued message, when it finished, completed the later message's controller and sealed it before that message's own turn (ClawSweeper revision 6).

`waitForReplyDispatcherIdle` moved to `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher-idle.ts` with main's current body (including its `abortSignal` handling), the queued item's `onSettled` wrap lives in `bindQueuedFollowupTyping` in `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-typing.ts`, and the two queued-typing cases moved to `agent-runner.runreplyagent.queued-typing.cases.ts`, so the line-cap ratchet holds for `reply-dispatcher.ts`, `agent-runner-run.ts`, and the runner e2e file.

## Evidence

- New `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-utils.test.ts` case drives a real `createReplyDispatcherWithTyping`, `createTypingController`, and `createTypingCallbacks` (channel TTL off, as on Telegram) through handoff, dispatcher idle, `markRunComplete`, and `markDispatchIdle`. On the test commit the channel `start` runs 0 times in the next 60 s. On the fix it runs 30 times, `stop` is not called during the wait, and `stop` runs once after the queued run settles.
- New `agent-runner.runreplyagent.queued-typing.cases.ts` case: a follow-up with a lifecycle queued behind a live run calls `onTypingHandoff` once and keeps typing open, and `completeFollowupRunLifecycle` on the queued item cleans typing up once. On the test commit `onTypingHandoff` is called 0 times.
- Channel with its own idle (ClawSweeper revisions 3 and 5, fixed in 0f720c428ae). The `reply-utils.test.ts` case with distinct `onReplyStart`, `onIdle`, and `onCleanup` callbacks uses fake timers: it calls the handoff option if offered, completes the run and the dispatcher, then advances 5 s. On 4f0fc716970 it fails: the controller never cleans up (`["idle"]` instead of `["cleanup", "idle"]`) and keeps calling `onReplyStart`, which is the call that reopens a Feishu preview. On 0f720c428ae it passes: cleanup and `onIdle` run once at dispatcher idle, and `onReplyStart` is not called again. It replaces the case that raced finalization against a real 50 ms timer.
- Message typing mode. New `queued-typing.cases.ts` case: a follow-up queued behind a live run in `message` mode never starts typing, so it must not take over idle. On 10d05599818 `onTypingHandoff` is called once. On a0ebdb83961 it is called 0 times. The existing handoff case now marks the mock controller active when its typing loop starts, as the real controller does.
- Two messages queued behind one live run (ClawSweeper revision 6, fixed in 2c7c47c9acd). New `followup-runner.test.ts` case runs a queued item that carries its own controller through a runner whose default controller belongs to a later message. On 0f720c428ae it fails: the item's own `markRunComplete` runs 0 times and the later message's controller is completed instead. On 2c7c47c9acd it passes: the item's own controller is completed once and the later one is untouched. The queued-typing handoff case now also checks that the enqueued run carries the dispatch's controller.
- On 2c7c47c9acd: `followup-runner` 30/30, `src/auto-reply/reply/queue` 75/75, `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` 226/226 with the e2e config, `dispatch-from-config.delivery.test.ts` 294/294, `extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts` 79/79, `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass.
- On 0f720c428ae: `reply-utils` and `reply-flow` 74/74, `extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts` 79/79, `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` exit 0, `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files clean. `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` (226/226 on 4f0fc716970) was not rerun: this commit does not touch the runner, and its queued-typing cases pass a mock `onTypingHandoff`.
- CI on 0f720c428ae: `checks-node-changed-1` failed in `src/agents/model-fallback.reply-entry.e2e.test.ts` and `checks-node-changed-5` in `dispatch-from-config.delivery.test.ts` ("delivers deferred Telegram text when generation fails after a block"). Both assert the old error copy ("API rate limit reached", "Authentication failed", "Something went wrong") that main changed in d0b48d63efb (#163381) after this branch's base. CI's merge ref picked up the new copy. Main updated the delivery test in 08eb496e2c6. The model-fallback e2e on main still expects the old strings. On this branch's base the delivery file passes locally (294/294) and the model-fallback e2e passed 10/10 in an earlier pass. This PR does not touch the error copy.
- Earlier, on a0ebdb83961: rebased onto upstream/main 836087a89a4 (green CI); `src/agents/model-fallback.reply-entry.e2e.test.ts`, red in an earlier CI run and on main at that time, passed 10/10 locally.

On 8afd852ac2d: `followup-runner`, `reply-flow`, and `reply-utils` 103/103, `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` 226/226 with the e2e config, `pnpm tsgo:core` exit 0. The other suites listed above were not rerun after the rebase.
- 2026-10-06: rebased onto upstream/main d8a62a83f37 after main's #166085 deleted `reply-dispatcher-observers.ts` and made `invokeReplyDispatcherObserver` local to `reply-dispatcher.ts`. 242a714b8d8 resolves it: `createReplyDispatcherWithTyping` wraps the channel idle in that observer guard once and passes it to `createTypingHandoff`, which no longer imports anything. Commit ids in the bullets above name the head they were measured on; the 2026-10-09 line below gives the current ones. ### Test cost

Measured on an Apple Silicon laptop.

This PR does not change that cost: its three queued-typing cases take 1 ms each, and the file's slowest existing cases take 2.1 to 3.7 s each. CI seconds are not in yet.

### Live Telegram proof

A third party (nissl24) ran this head (8afd852ac2d) on production Telegram, not the Test Server flow, and posted Bot API timelines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/162684#issuecomment-6014674015. The agent itself did not run it. It has no access to the Convex credential broker that the `telegram-e2e-userbot` skill leases Test Server credentials from, so it could not drive a Test Server DM or capture screenshots. The visible typing state is covered by the channel-callback tests above, not by a real chat. prs.title: improve: speed up PostgreSQL memory vector search
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL semantic memory search currently reads every float32 embedding, so lookup time grows linearly with large memory stores.

## User Impact

Memory vector search becomes approximate by default with no new configuration: **approximate results accepted (Peter, 2026-10-24)**. A binary Hamming prefilter selects eight times the requested result count, followed by exact cosine reranking. Model, source, exclusion and candidate-ID scopes remain enforced; small candidate-ID scopes stay exact. SQLite stays exact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The generated binary projection reduces the scanned embedding payload by roughly 32× and avoids an HNSW build during startup. Zero-vector eligibility and returned rows remain unchanged. PostgreSQL requires pgvector 0.7+; weekly PG16/PG18 images pin 0.8.7. There are no iterative scan settings or per-query capability probes.

## Schema migration (standing approval 2026-10-14)

Agent schema 32→33 backfills the nullable generated bit column on each admitted native vector projection, using its own dimensions (1–16000). Existing migration transactions and deadlines remain in force. Canonical embeddings stay unchanged; derived sketches are omitted/rebuilt under the existing backup/port rule.

The preregistered gates are structured recall@10 ≥0.95 including filters, at least 5× p50 speedup at 50k, backfill within 90s SQL/120s bridge deadlines, and reported write cost (flag full reindex above ~2×). Uniform random data is a reported non-gating worst case. No paid APIs, downloads or private data are used.

### Structured corpus — initial native-SQL qualification

Shared Mac, PG17.11/pgvector 0.8.7, Node 24.22.1. These are native joined-SQL timings, not Testbox or Gateway claims. Frozen 256-cluster Gaussian mixture, 32D latent basis embedded in 1536D, anisotropic noise, unit normalization, independent query stream. 60 distinct queries per scope, 240 per size; exact and candidate alternate on the same draw, with five warmups. All 720 searches completed without errors, underfill or scope leakage.

Default HNSW 200k construction timed out at 90.048s; stronger 20k at 90.013s. Default 50k built in 30.128s, but its short diagnostic chose exact execution and is not ANN recall evidence. These are host/settings-specific results. The existing migration owner has no concurrent/background build lifecycle; binary prefilter meets the registered gates without adding one. Oversampling 4/8/16 was compared; 8 retains more recall margin than 4 at 200k. The 40-ID diagnostic favored exact (1.40ms vs 1.52–1.69ms), which remains the production shortcut.

### Remaining qualification — in progress

Random 20k/50k/200k recall/latency/backfill tables, production publication/reindex paired measurements, one Testbox A/B, PG16/18 execution and final 3-shard conformance will be filled before landing. Historical 20k publication/full-reindex context: #181957: 22.538s/91.997s and #181860: 31.680s/107.660s; these are different-host comparisons, not paired evidence.

## Evidence

Current candidate: 3dfab69ad211. Focused engine/admission/port/memory worker proof 28/28 passes, including hybrid and backup reconstruction; schema/metadata/port 17/17 and historical/Doctor 32 regressions pass. Core and targeted memory production/test TSRS, changed lint/format, wrapper-inventory regression pass. Fresh P0–P3 autoreview is scoped-clean; pr-simplify retains one projection/query/migration owner. Generated DDL was regenerated.

A native PostgreSQL PANIC occurred during an earlier failure-recovery test on the shared Mac and auto-recovered; affected cases and the complete memory worker suite passed on replay. No root-cause repair is claimed. Full final-head conformance is still required.

Reproduce with the committed `scripts/perf/bench-postgres-ann-decision.mjs` and `scripts/perf/bench-postgres-ann-publication.mjs`; each documents environment inputs. Distribution and queries were frozen before measurement. Later mechanical lint changes preserve 48 representative draws byte-for-byte and preserve the publication AST after style normalization.

Change size: 2019 additions/94 deletions over 35 files, mostly reproducible benchmarks. No scheduler, config option or write-lock change.

Fixes model preparation reading a stale owner when overlapping configuration refreshes replace its pending publication, and repairs the runtime/onboarding CI fixtures exposed during the dependency-sweep follow-up.

prs.title: fix(sqlite): size the worker store budget from the configured agent roster
prs.body:
Related: #162497

## What Problem This Solves

`SqliteWorkerBroker` caps concurrent SQLite worker stores at a hard-coded `MAX_STORES = 64`, and the broker is a **process-global singleton** (`resolveGlobalSingleton(Symbol.for("openclaw.sqliteWorkerBroker"), ...)`). Every agent in one Gateway process shares that single budget, and the count only grows with the number of distinct agents the Gateway has touched.

A Gateway with more than 64 agents therefore refuses new store opens for the tail of the fleet. The rejection is `SQLite worker store capacity reached` with code `overloaded`, so it is treated like a provider overload: the fallback chain runs and the user sees "The model provider returned a temporary internal error before replying". Nothing in the message points at the real cause, and the advice in the error text ("run openclaw doctor --fix ... and restart") names the wrong target — the agent databases are healthy.

There is also no knob. The cap is a literal in `src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker.ts`, and the same literal bounds the pending-open queue (`maxPendingOpens`), so a fleet larger than 64 is refused during startup preparation as well as during normal turns.

This change makes the store budget configurable and sizes the default from the configured agent roster, so a Gateway can serve a fleet larger than 64 without editing `dist/`.

## User Impact

- A Gateway with more than 64 configured agents stops refusing store opens for the tail of the fleet. The budget now defaults to `max(64, 2 * configured agent count)`.
- Operators can set an explicit bound with `database.sqlite.maxStores` when the automatic size is not what they want.
- A single-agent Gateway keeps the historical limit of 64, so resource use on small installs is unchanged.
- The budget is read from the published runtime config on each open, so a config reload can raise it without restarting the Gateway. Lowering it stops new stores until the live count falls below the new value; stores that are already open are not force-closed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The merged reclamation fix (#164477) releases idle shared-state handles, and the startup retry candidate (#173994) stops a temporary rejection from becoming a terminal degradation. Neither of them changes the bound itself: the live store count still grows monotonically with the number of distinct agents touched inside one Gateway process, so the 65th distinct agent is refused no matter how many stores were reclaimed in between.

Deriving the budget from the configured roster removes the fleet-size cliff without removing the bound, and the explicit override gives operators a deterministic handle when the automatic size is wrong. The pending-open queue follows the same budget, because a fleet that cannot open stores cannot start its agents either.

## Evidence

- The budget is read from the same process-global broker that produces the failure: `MAX_STORES` gated both the store reservation (`reserveSqliteWorkerClient`) and the pending-open admission.
- New unit coverage in `src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-sizing.test.ts` pins the default (64 without config), the derived size (220 for a 110-agent roster), the explicit override (192), and the rejection of invalid limits.
- New broker coverage in `src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker.capacity.test.ts` opens two stores against a broker limited to two and asserts that the third open fails with `SQLite worker store capacity reached` / `overloaded`.
- New config coverage in `src/config/zod-schema.database.test.ts` accepts `database.sqlite.maxStores` and rejects out-of-range values.
- Focused tests: `pnpm test src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-sizing.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker.capacity.test.ts src/config/zod-schema.database.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 7 + 13 + 22 tests, all passing.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — clean. `pnpm lint` — clean.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a fresh human follow-up in a completed task session cannot resume automatically after a Gateway restart because its recovery source was discarded.

## User Impact

Already-authorized follow-up work can resume from its saved history without another instruction or approval. Current identity, permissions, revocation checks, and the original completion destination remain enforced. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain the follow-up’s fresh operator source in the existing registry owner, targeting the exact child session and task rather than borrowing the completed parent’s grant. Restore that source through the child’s session store; preserve the existing parent-target recovery path and completion routing. Add the requested one-line restart-continuation rule to AGENTS.md.

This reuses existing recovery state and admission instead of introducing a second recovery route. Production code grows by 28 net lines; the additional integration coverage checks admission, durable recovery, unrelated-source rejection, and a second restart. Identity-rotating compaction remains a separate, pre-existing limitation; this change does not claim to fix it.

## Evidence

- Authenticated chat admission, cold registry reload, exact-source rejection, and a second restart preserving the task identity are covered through production owners with fixed model I/O.
- The new recovery regression fails on the unmodified production code because the persisted operator source is undefined; the same cases pass with this fix.
- 119 focused tests pass across the registry restart, detached recovery, steer/restart, and chat-custody suites.

prs.title: refactor(canvas)!: retire A2UI widgets and content-kind hooks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A2UI duplicates the HTML widget path and retains the last Lit renderer dependency. This retires that format and its otherwise-unused plugin API in favor of HTML widgets.

## User Impact

HTML widgets, native plugin widgets, and MCP Apps keep their existing behavior.

**Breaking change:** stored A2UI widgets are deleted during Doctor/update after a fresh standard database backup. Doctor reports the number removed and explains that they can be recreated as HTML widgets. Other widgets survive. The candidate's Doctor performs this repair, so an already-installed update driver does not need to understand it. Calls using `show_widget(kind: "a2ui")` fail at argument validation with `A2UI widgets were removed; use kind "html"`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Removing both Canvas renderers, their HTTP route and build pipeline, and the generic `registered` board-content path leaves one HTML rendering path.

The closed board schema removal advances the wire protocol to v5. General clients use v5; nodes and probes retain the v4 window. The client retry path preserves the v4 pairing envelope instead of applying its retired v3 transformation. Approved v4 nodes retain plugin capabilities, commands, and hosted surface URLs. Linux operators and the Rust node host consume the canonical protocol constants; the Rust host starts at v5 and retains v4 fallback. It treats `hello.protocol` as the server version and preserves the selected v4 session protocol when an accepted v4 connection reaches a v5 server. Older source-built Rust binaries require rebuilding; this does not retrofit already-compiled clients.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Canvas entry tests | Passed: 3 tests |
| UI typecheck | Passed on final source (`pnpm tsgo:ui`) |
| Doctor backup/deletion regression | Passed: fresh backup, both legacy markers, 3 surviving widget kinds, count warning, idempotence |
| Production Knip | Passed on the repaired head (`pnpm deadcode:knip`) |
| Same-machine startup comparison | Strict check passed: 280,645 → 280,626 B gzip (−19 B), 7 JS requests; CSS 40,215 B, 1 request unchanged |
| Targeted lint | Passed; one redundant-spread finding corrected |
| Docs MDX / internal links / glossary | Passed: 1,391 pages, 15,868 links |
| `pnpm why @a2ui/web_core lit` | Empty |
| v4 protocol repair | Node policy: 21 passed. Rust: node-session 10, lifecycle 1, external signing 1, device-token recovery 1 passed. Final independent review passed at P0–P2. |
| Full CI | Replacement head `8e6d5a2b5a2` requested with `ci:full`; pending. Earlier full runs are prior-head evidence. |
| CI repair tests | 21 widget unit tests and 12 mobile-survivor tests passed; corrected protocol shard passes CI; local setup timeout recorded below |
| Hosted-web QA | Passed the changed HTML document capability probe on the repaired head |

The Doctor regression seeds both legacy markers, an earlier same-version backup, and surviving HTML, MCP, and plugin widgets; it checks the fresh backup, deletion, count warning, and repeat-run behavior. Hosted-web QA now serves real persisted HTML documents while retaining wrong, expired, revoked, and retired capability checks. The remaining UI change removes retired-format recognition and its label override; surviving markup, styles, and layout are unchanged.

The first full CI run passed all 9 UI E2E shards and both real-Gateway shards. Hosted review subsequently identified old v3 feature filtering accidentally applied to v4 nodes and stale Rust client constants; those findings are repaired, with a real-Gateway regression for v4 plugin URL access and invocation. It exposed stale protocol fixtures, a missing generated config-doc hash, the reduced environment-variable budget, and a shadowed test variable; these are fixed in the replacement head.

A targeted local rerun passed 21 widget tests and 12 mobile-survivor tests. The node control-plane suite timed out in its 180-second setup hook during isolated target-config convergence, after Doctor completed; all 5 cases were skipped. This remains an investigated local setup failure. The exact repaired head passed all five node control-plane cases in hosted CI job 120764135947. No timeout or assertion was relaxed. Baseline reproductions are limited to unmatched failing CI cases. No local Docker was run.

Independent Codex review completed clean at P0–P2 on the current-main integration; a fresh review of the subsequent protocol repairs also completed clean at P0–P2. It reviewed the full diff plus unchanged backup, Doctor/update, and protocol-client owners. The resolved merges retain main's dependency updates. The final integration conflict was limited to the lockfile: it was regenerated with pnpm from main, and `pnpm why @a2ui/web_core lit` remained empty. Reviewed production/test changes were unchanged by that integration. UI typecheck, the Doctor regression, production Knip, and the startup comparison were repeated after that integration.

## Removal and compatibility notes

Against the integrated main base, counting touched TS/JS/JSX and native source files: production source LOC 31,787 → 28,807 (−2,980); test/fixture source LOC 26,886 → 24,797 (−2,089). No startup budget was raised. The lockfile drops `@a2ui/web_core`, `lit`, `lit-element`, `lit-html`, `@lit/reactive-element`, `@lit/context`, `@lit-labs/ssr-dom-shim`, `@preact/signals-core`, `redos-detector`, `regjsparser`, `validate-color`, and the unused `zod-to-json-schema` Zod-3 variant. Canvas no longer depends on Solid, DOMPurify, or marked; their other owners retain them.

Public Plugin SDK usage inspection observed no matching references, with incomplete coverage (2,062 complete / 2,469 eligible packages; 407 incomplete and 621 unresolved references). A source search found Canvas as the only direct bundled caller on the base. A bounded Inspector run completed 3 of 175 plugins; its retained checkpoint is incomplete and is not used as a finished inventory or a zero-consumer claim. The removal proceeds under the explicit maintainer decision to retire this API.

Intentional A2UI mentions remain in Doctor/validation regression code, retirement and historical release documentation, native path-rejection tests, and the frozen command inventory of the released iOS upgrade-survivor fixture. That fixture never executes the retired commands.

The source repository no longer carries documentation translation memories. Control UI translation memory is regenerated by the existing post-merge **Control UI Locale Refresh** workflow; CI deliberately separates generated locale PRs from source changes. A canonical-generator preview confirmed one obsolete help segment per 21 locales, with no added translations.

prs.title: fix(agents): pin legacy default agent workspace on load to prevent silent per-agent move
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A `default: true` agent with **no explicit `workspace`** (inheriting `agents.defaults.workspace`) silently changes its resolved workspace from `<workspace>` to `<workspace>/<agentId>` on upgrade. The new per-agent directory is scaffolded with a blank default identity, and the agent's `memory/` and `outputs/` move to the empty subdir — a silent identity + memory reset, with no error or prompt. Fixes #127802.

## Root Cause

`resolveAgentWorkspaceDir` returns `agents.defaults.workspace` for the legacy default agent only when `tryResolveInheritedWorkspaceAgentId` identifies it. That relies on `getRetainedLegacyDefaultAgentId` — a process-local `WeakMap` keyed by the config object, seeded during the roster migration that strips `default: true`. Across config re-materialization on the read/load path, the config object resolved against is not the one the retention was seeded on, so the retention is lost, `inheritedWorkspaceAgentId` is `undefined`, and resolution falls through to `path.join(defaults.workspace, agentId)` → `<workspace>/<agentId>`.

The write path (`io.write.ts`) already pins the workspace via `materializeWorkspace: true`, but a config that is never rewritten after upgrade (e.g. a read-only mounted config) never receives that pin — so the read path must not depend on the fragile in-process retention.

## Fix

`migratePersistedImplicitMainRoster` now defaults `materializeWorkspace` to `true` when it processes a legacy default agent (callers can still pass `false`). Retiring the `default: true` marker therefore also pins the legacy default agent's workspace into the config **data** on every read path (load, snapshot, validation) — mirroring the write path — so resolution stays correct regardless of `WeakMap` object identity. The pin only applies to a legacy default agent that has no explicit `workspace` (an agent with an explicit workspace is untouched), and it resolves to `agents.defaults.workspace` (its historical value), so behavior is preserved rather than changed. No on-disk config is rewritten on read.

## Evidence

Added a regression test in `legacy.roster.test.ts`: loading a config with `main: { default: true }`, a sibling agent with an explicit `workspace`, and `agents.defaults.workspace` set now yields `entries.main.workspace === defaults.workspace` (previously `main.workspace` was absent, which produced the `<workspace>/main` fallback). Confirmed the failing behavior on latest `main` (`resolveAgentWorkspaceDir` and its `// Read-time migration removes default:true before write-time workspace pinning can run.` comment are unchanged).

prs.title: fix(workers): preserve cloud commits on reclaim
prs.body:
Fixes #110498

## What Problem This Solves

Reclaiming a cloud worker currently keeps its files but drops unpushed worker-authored commits.

## User Impact

Stop and reclaim now preserve worker commits in Gateway-source managed worktrees when they can fast-forward safely. Dirty working files and unrelated staged changes survive. Divergent worker history, a moved Gateway branch, or conflicting staged changes keep file reconciliation and produce a visible transcript note. Older workers and Gateways retain v1 behavior; repository-only restoration and publication behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capability-negotiated result upload v2 carries worker HEAD, ancestry metadata, and a Git pack capped at 256 MiB. The existing staged result retains the imported history until reclaim verifies ancestry and advances the branch with an expected-old-value ref update. A two-tree index merge preserves staged-only content. Ordinary turn reconciliation and recovery remain file-only.

The change stays within the existing transfer, staging, and reclaim owners. Both native and SSH transports use the same history capture and adoption policy. Production: +708/-59 lines; tests: +707/-5; docs: +6/-2. The necessary growth covers negotiated transport and reclaim together, without adding a state store.

## Evidence

Final validation used Node 24.22.1 with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` and `--maxWorkers=1`.

- CI follow-up: reproduced the missing transfer-protocol dependency in the trusted PR-wrapper closure, then moved the v2 constant and shared history schema into existing inventory owners. `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt` is unchanged.
- Follow-up `pnpm test test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **19/19 passed**, **144.33 s** wall, including both previously failing wrapper extraction checks. The pre-fix inventory regression failed as expected in **27.65 s**.
- Follow-up inventory, connection, real native v1/v2 HTTP transfer, negotiation, upload-reader, tunnel, Git-history and SSH tests: **117 passed, 1 existing platform skip**, **291.27 s** wall across 8 files. Format, type-aware lint, `tsgo:core` (**6.00 s**) and independent review passed.
- `pnpm test workspace-result-history.test.ts placement-reclaim-history.test.ts`: 8 passed, **323.08 s** wall. Covers retained ancestry through Git GC, adoption, dirty edits, staged-only content, moved/divergent fallback, and empty commits.
- Focused transport/reconciliation/recovery run: **197 passed, 1 existing platform skip**, **508.90 s** wall. Its sole failure was the new SSH status assertion encountering deliberately invalid submodule metadata in the fixture. Scoped that assertion to ignore submodule status; `pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-sync-tunnel.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` then passed **11/11**, **48.64 s** wall, including the 1,800-file round trip.
- That focused run included `node-worker-transfer-client.git`, `connection`, `node-worker-result-negotiation`, `node-workspace-upload-reader`, `placement-dispatch-reclaim`, `placement-reclaim-history`, `worker-workspace-recovery-transcript`, `workspace-reconcile`, `workspace-result-staging.reads`, `workspace-local-reconciliation`, `node-worker-tunnel`, and `node-worker-tunnel.device-folder`. It proves real v1/v2 HTTP uploads, pack bounds, visible notes, and all three lifecycle cases: direct reclaim and reclaim recovery adopt before destruction; ordinary recovery leaves HEAD unchanged.
- Red-on-base proof at `094bbd6b153`: the new reclaim lifecycle regression fails at the pre-destroy HEAD assertion, **308.33 s** wall. The fixed lifecycle cases pass.
- Changed-file `oxfmt --check`, type-aware `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`, `pnpm run tsgo:core` (**5.91 s** final wall), and `git diff --check` passed.
- An earlier default-runtime Bun attempt hit the 60-second large-workspace timeout and a large-upload worker heap limit before being interrupted. Both cases passed under the required Node runtime; that preliminary attempt is not counted as final validation.

prs.title: fix(browser): preserve literal download and trace output paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Browser downloads and trace exports silently change an explicitly supplied filename when it has leading or trailing whitespace. This can write to a neighboring file, reject an otherwise valid destination, or make browser-node file transfer fail.

## User Impact

Quoted output paths such as `" report.pdf "` retain their literal spelling. Managed output roots, symlink and non-regular-file rejection, and Windows path protections remain enforced. Blank-path defaults and required-path errors are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing nonblank string reader at filename boundaries and preserve the returned path during node transfer. The shared route resolver passes the literal destination through `fs-safe`'s whitespace-preserving default-name branch, which applies the same writable-path checks. There is no duplicate filesystem validator or new configuration.

The original fix is by @SunnyShu0925; contributor commits are retained. The revision consolidates coverage into existing tests and reduces the original +254 net lines to +39: production +11, tests +26, documentation +2. The small production increase is imports and the shared-resolver explanation; further reduction would require unrelated cleanup.

## Evidence

- Baseline `7b71c2379764`: seven expected regression failures across CLI parsing, route admission, literal file writing, and node transfer. The file-write check fails because the literal file is missing; the trimmed neighbor is protected by the final assertion.
- Revised branch, integrated with `094bbd6b153b`: all 105 tests pass across the seven focused browser, CLI, trace, cancellation, and transfer suites. Combined cold run: 210.92 seconds, primarily worker preparation; CLI, route, writer, and trace test execution each stays below one second. The existing node-transfer suite took 16.65 seconds on this host.
- Real headless Chromium: clicked and waited downloads fail literal-path equality on baseline and preserve the exact path and payload with the fix. The ref-based denied-host case also passes.
- Targeted oxlint and oxfmt pass. Oxlint ran on the exact candidate files in the independent tooling checkout because linked dependencies prevent the PR checkout's declaration preflight. Broad typechecking is left to PR CI.
- Independent Codex autoreview: no actionable P0–P2 findings. ClawSweeper also found no introduced code defects on `67d2914f8a12`; its request to restore the prior CLI/Gateway transcript is addressed below.
- Exact-head CI for `67d2914f8a12` passed: [run 40053992608](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40053992608). The native watcher reports GREEN; older superseded checks do not describe this result.
- The optional broader `check-changed` run reached the expected shared-install typecheck refusal (`Declaration input escapes checkout`); targeted checks above and CI provide the applicable validation.

The complete CLI → Gateway → Chromium chain and Windows whitespace filenames were not rerun; they require additional environment setup beyond the existing Chromium proof. The optional denied-waiter Chromium scenario times out with an unhandled `SsrFBlockedError` on both the unchanged baseline and this branch. The allowed clicked/waited literal-path scenarios pass with the fix; the separate denial-scenario failure remains unresolved.


<details>
<summary>Retained contributor CLI/Gateway evidence</summary>

The following transcript was supplied by @SunnyShu0925 in the original PR body for contributor head `d751edc32c69876e7f877134b28a44fadf2f7418`. It is restored here for provenance and was not rerun as a complete CLI/Gateway chain in this revision; independently rerun baseline/head evidence is summarized above.

Real patched CLI + real Playwright chromium (isolated dev Gateway, loopback HTTP server, `browser.ssrfPolicy.dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork=true` for the harness):

```text
$ openclaw browser download e2 " report.pdf "
downloaded: /tmp/openclaw/downloads/ report.pdf        # literal trailing space preserved
$ ls -la "/tmp/openclaw/downloads/ report.pdf "        # literal file exists, content correct
-rw-rw-r-- ... /tmp/openclaw/downloads/ report.pdf
$ ls "/tmp/openclaw/downloads/report.pdf"              # trimmed neighbor absent
ls: cannot access .../report.pdf: No such file or directory

$ openclaw browser waitfordownload " wait.pdf "        # waitfordownload literal preserved
downloaded: /tmp/openclaw/downloads/ wait.pdf
$ openclaw browser trace stop --out " trace.zip "      # trace output literal preserved
TRACE:/tmp/openclaw/ trace.zip     (Zip archive; trimmed neighbor trace.zip absent)
```

Admission regressions (real CLI, rejected before dispatch — route 400, no download event):

```text
$ openclaw browser download e2 "escape-link/existing/report.pdf"   # parent symlink escapes root
GatewayClientRequestError: Invalid path: must stay within downloads directory

GatewayClientRequestError: Invalid path: must stay within downloads directory
```

prs.title: fix(codex): chats wait after reloading an already-closed thread
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes chats remaining at “Waiting for turn to start…” after a plugin reload when their old thread already closed and another chat keeps the retired worker alive.

## User Impact

Affected chats can resume without waiting for unrelated chats to release the retired worker. A still-loaded thread continues to block handoff, and stopping the waiting chat cancels its read without closing sibling sessions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The closure receipts introduced in #180204 cannot recover an event received before receipt tracking was installed. When no receipt exists, query the exact old client once and accept only the matching thread with `notLoaded` status. Existing native persistence writer locking still fences resume; closure, worker exit, and cancellation clean up the pending read.

Stacked on #182104 because this was found while investigating its queued-startup failure path. That PR fixes terminal accounting; this follow-up addresses the separate startup wait. The comparison contains only this three-file follow-up.

## Evidence

- The missed-closure regression fails on base `34b632ccf4ad6deff945c7c2c889fd5cbb39f1a4` and passes with this change.
- Handoff suite: 11 passed, including already-closed recovery, wrong-thread rejection, still-loaded waiting, cancellation, and closure/read races.
- Shared-client lifecycle suites: 158 passed.
- An isolated backport onto the affected live gateway's source revision passed all 16 handoff and configured-MCP ownership tests and built the Codex plugin package.
- Formatting, syntax lint, diff checks, and an independent AutoReview completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings.

Draft while verification gaps remain: type-aware lint was blocked by the declaration-generation guard against borrowed dependency symlinks. The patched native startup flow has not been proven end to end: the older running host rejected an external replacement for its reserved bundled Codex runtime, so that attempted deployment was rolled back. The affected live chat was recovered separately by recycling a retired worker after confirming its retained threads had completed; that recovery does not prove this patch was deployed.

prs.title: fix(claude-cli): classify rejected resume checkpoints as an expired session
prs.body:
Fixes #181254

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the first turn of a checkpointed Claude CLI fork being classified as an unknown model failure when the parent compacted away its saved checkpoint.

## User Impact

The requested Claude CLI runtime can use its existing fresh-session recovery when the rejected checkpoint is identified and account-authorized history and retry budget are available. Recovery remains unavailable without those prerequisites. The recorded fork point, account-history boundary, and retry limits are unchanged; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Claude Code reports `No message found with message.uuid of: <checkpoint>`. The existing classifier recognized only an unsupported resume option, and the structured-result path bypassed that classifier. This change passes the requested checkpoint separately from the option name and recognizes its rejection on both structured-result and process-exit paths, including a result received after CLI activity. Unrelated errors and a different checkpoint remain unchanged.

The existing recovery owner handles the resulting `session_expired` error. The patch does not remove `--resume-session-at` or fork from the parent's newer state. Thanks to @mushuiyu886 for the implementation and regressions; contributor commits remain in this PR.

## Evidence

- Main-source confirmation: `src/agents/cli-runner/exit-error.ts:44` requires the option name and unsupported-option wording; `src/agents/cli-runner/execute-process.ts:119` uses generic structured-result classification. Neither recognizes the reported missing-checkpoint message. `runCliRecovery` rejects unknown failures under the backend's invalidated-only policy.
- Contributor regressions exercise `executePreparedCliRun` with the reported error record on nonzero and clean process exits and after observed activity. On the base, the expected `session_expired` classification would instead be `unknown`. Independent controls retain unsupported-option classification and reject unrelated or mismatched-checkpoint errors. The contributor reported red/green results and a real-process runner/recovery demonstration using a stub Claude executable; that is harness evidence, not a live Claude Gateway result.
- Live Gateway/channel E2E, leases, broad local suites, and local execution of contributor code were skipped per maintainer policy. PR CI supplies broad execution proof. No after-fix live Claude claim is made; existing account-history and retry-budget prerequisites remain in force.
- Maintainer source review and `pr-simplify`: **LAND-AS-IS**, retaining the contributor implementation and history. Fresh main `377c0fcb1f106b6ebda3f069d554d1d64732998b` still has the defect and has no intervening change to the affected classification or recovery owners; no main merge is needed for this patch.
- Local static checks: `git diff --check`, oxlint with the core config, and `oxfmt --check` passed for all four changed files. Contributor code and tests were not executed locally. Prescribed isolated Codex autoreview: **scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings**.
- Exact-head [PR CI 39976248918](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39976248918) succeeded for `4d8dd32fb08b5b8c2cf2c16ce5a27d93e990074d`, including lint, production/test types, test lanes, and `openclaw/ci-gate`.
- Exact diff totals: production +43/−11 (net +32), tests +167/−0, docs +0/−0. The small production growth carries the checkpoint value to both classification surfaces. The two duplicate positive matcher cases are nonblocking cleanup under review-first mode.

prs.title: fix(agents): detect sustained same-target write churn
prs.body:
Related: #122577

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an agent can repeatedly overwrite one file with different successful contents while never producing a final response. Because every write has different arguments and reports `changed: true`, current loop detection treats the sequence as ordinary progress indefinitely.

This PR proposes a conservative behavioral boundary for maintainer review. The issue is currently marked as requiring a product decision; this PR does not claim that decision has already been made.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change keeps successful writes classified as real mutations and adds a separate, warning-first run-liveness signal for a contiguous tail of content-changing writes to one resolved target. Target identity excludes document content and is stored only as a hash.

The existing loop warning threshold is reused. The warned write remains allowed. Continuity clears when the run changes tools (including read/verification), changes targets, repeats an earlier argument variant, or completes/replaces its lifecycle. If churn remains continuous through the existing stale-run boundary, owner-bound recovery can abort only that run whether or not follow-up work is queued.

The behavior is limited to the built-in `write` result contract (`details.changed === true`). It is not tied to a provider, model, transport, channel, or reported private document. No new configuration or default surface is added.

## Batch and Liveness Semantics

A whole assistant batch is admitted before its calls have outcomes. This revision therefore keeps warning and liveness behavior aligned at both lifecycle boundaries:

- successful write-mutation liveness stays inactive below the shared warning threshold;
- a sequential batch emits the same run-scoped warning before the threshold-crossing write implementation starts;
- a post-outcome fallback covers parallel or out-of-order batch completions;
- the shared warning bucket prevents duplicate pre- and post-outcome warnings;
- the existing stable no-progress classifier still includes the just-recorded outcome and activates on its original boundary.

## Scope

The write-churn changes remain in the agent loop owner. A separate memory-core test commit stabilizes the unrelated provenance-repair assertion that failed hosted CI: it holds the detached repair open while asserting that automatic candidates remain hidden, then releases and verifies the repaired result. The test moved into the existing candidate-repair suite to satisfy the line-cap ratchet. No memory-core production behavior changed.

A subsequent agent fix resets the reverse write-variant scan at the newer occurrence of a repeated variant, retaining only post-repeat writes. A replacement regression uses actual `changed: true` outcomes at the shared warning threshold and verifies that a fresh post-repeat streak can warn again.

## User Impact

Runaway same-file rewrite sequences become bounded without immediately blocking normal edits. Short rewrite sequences, multi-file work, write/read/write verification, repeated identical content, and successful writes outside the sustained same-target pattern retain their existing behavior. The latest file state and session remain available after recovery.

## Policy Status

ClawSweeper marked #122577 as requiring a maintainer product decision and disabled automated fix-PR queueing. This PR implements one conservative proposal for review; it does not claim that maintainers have approved the warning, escape, or recovery boundary. It is ready for maintainer review of that decision, but does not claim approval or merge readiness.

## Evidence

Behavioral incident baseline: `v2026.7.2-beta.7` (`dabe1915362e20c25704af91612a32a8f4c96e83`). The beta is provenance only; the patch and tests are bound to the recorded branch head and integrated base below, not an unqualified current-main merge.

Negative controls observed before their fixes:

```text
same-target detector: expected warning, received { stuck: false }
below-threshold liveness: active=true after the second distinct changed write
embedded sequential batch: 11 successful writes, warning event list empty
stable no-progress boundary: sixth completed outcome still reported active=false
default-parallel batch: warning emitted, first churn lease remained absent
loop detection omitted/disabled: changed-write churn emitted a warning
CI dependency scan: three internal helpers were exported but unused
```

## Current revision and verification

Head: `f72242e6faf82f8608abd704b16d868d8a034ada`. The branch's integrated main merge-base remains `d45155d6c51169ac10890445418a9144395d1697`; it has not been integrated with current main.

- Revision 34's staged-write-target lifecycle P2 is fixed in the shared wrapper settlement `finally`, with run-scoped cleanup on success, errors, late cancellation, source-guard refusal and disposal. Batch final-target precedence is retained. The follow-up adds three production lines and +132 net test lines across two files.
- Five regressions failed on the preceding wrapper and passed after the fix. At this exact clean head, the focused detector, warning, write-target, admission and real-Agent sequential/default-parallel suites passed 169 distinct tests across five files. This is native wrapper/Agent lifecycle evidence, not a current-head Gateway recovery proof.
- Production `tsgo:core`, the canonical `core-test-agents-root` compiler graph, focused type-aware lint, formatting, line-cap ratchet and whitespace checks passed. The changed-graph selector stopped on the pre-existing 721-root/advisory-720 budget check; no config or test inventory changed, and the named graph was compiled separately. No full all-graph check claim.
- Independent read-only review found no actionable defect in the lifecycle fix. The full branch surface against its integrated base is source +475 and tests +1503 across 23 files; the added production state remains limited to target-aware detection, batch reconciliation and existing liveness ownership.
- Prior-head hosted CI failed one subagent-registry shard at `subagent-registry.test.ts:5160`, with dependent failure/cancellations; this unrelated failure was not repaired. Local passes are not a new-head hosted-CI pass.
- A merge-tree against main `3f12395208355949832da16c882e83cc5726c560` reports ten conflicting paths. Integration remains explicitly unqualified.

[The final follow-up comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/122631#issuecomment-5974613163) contains the exact commands, checked-in proof links and captured terminal excerpts. No new isolated-Gateway result is claimed.

### Historical isolated Gateway proof (`27b24258c8`)

The real gateway, authenticated loopback agent RPC, embedded runner, built-in write/read tools, diagnostic heartbeat, and owner-bound recovery were exercised using a deterministic loopback model transport. No outbound-channel delivery or live-provider claim.

```text
canonical warning: argument_churn / warn / count 10 (seq 197)
later warning: argument_churn / warn / count 20 (seq 302)
continuous churn duration: 378645 ms
session.stalled: age 376954 ms, model_call (seq 361)
recovery requested: abort, same age (seq 362)
recovery completed: abort_embedded_run / aborted / embedded_run (seq 367)
healthy concurrent control: passed
post-recovery control: passed
same-session file readback: passed
target-file digest readback: matched
artifact verifier: passed, no failures
```

This trace is historical: subsequent target-hash, repeat-continuity and staging-cleanup changes have not been qualified through the isolated Gateway at the current head. No rerun is in progress or claimed; final Gateway qualification is deferred until a maintainer chooses the policy and the branch is integrated. The synthetic harness at the proof head selected the latest marked prompt because runtime context could follow it as another user-role message; no production timing constants were changed for that historical proof.

The [historical proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/122631#issuecomment-5746076190) contains the sanitized event evidence and artifact digests. Raw logs, runtime identifiers, local paths, credentials, and provider configuration are intentionally not published.

## Remaining decisions

prs.title: perf(agents): avoid duplicate selected operator authority checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway tool caller guard can invoke the same operator access authority twice when the selected participant is the caller.

## User Impact

No intended permission or user-visible behavior change. Each effect still checks live authority, and revocation between asynchronous steps still blocks the next effect. Distinct selected and calling participants keep both checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

The selected participant already owns its operator assertion. Skip the second assertion only when its admitted authority object is exactly the caller's authority. There is no cross-await answer cache and no change to plugin scope lifetime.

Production delta: +3 lines; the identity conditional preserves the distinct-participant contract. Test delta: +56 lines.

## Evidence

- Shared-source regression: 2 live source calls before, 1 after per guard (-1, -50%). This is owner-boundary work-count evidence, not whole-turn performance.
- Baseline focused file: 1 failed / 24 passed; the failure observed 2 calls where 1 was required.
- Candidate focused file: 25/25 passed, including shared-source and either distinct-source revocation after an await. Wrapper wall time 48.25 s, dominated by cold worker preparation; individual new cases 12/2/2 ms. CI time pending.
- Changed-file oxfmt and repository lint passed; git diff --check passed.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable P0/P1/P2 findings. The configured review helper refused the requested provider route before inference; configuration was not changed.

Draft: required v5.4 benchmark evidence is pending. No allocation/turn, CPU, loop-p99, GC, promotion, or whole-cron-turn improvement is claimed. The benchmark host's shared safety guard blocked execution. Do not merge until the required calibrated measurements are complete.

The separate scope-reuse proposal remains unresolved: current public Gateway scope views are mutable and invocation-local. A same-registry/same-identity reuse experiment failed the existing sibling-isolation regression and was removed. Reusing those views requires a compatibility decision; this change preserves them. Cross-await policy-result caching remains outside this PR.

prs.title: fix: make Daybreak independent of retiring model aliases
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Daybreak workflows rely on Blue/Red aliases retiring October 28, 2026, and must retain automatic recovery through authorized Access configuration without changing the selected model or processing speed.

## User Impact

The chat menu uses segmented Access choices matching Speed and shows **Access above Effort above Speed**, but only when the active account/model/runtime explicitly advertises a Daybreak program. Unavailable options are absent; unknown or empty capabilities hide Access entirely. There are no requested/reported status or explanatory paragraphs below Access. **Use model default** clears the session override; Standard is an explicit selection. If account capabilities no longer expose Access, **Clear saved Access** remains available in the model menu. Clearing is explicit; unavailable program choices and explanatory Access paragraphs remain absent.

The advisory Doctor check reports configured retiring aliases without rewriting models or account pins. **Automatic cyber recovery retries the same model once with authorized Blue Access**, without changing the saved session selection. Exact model pins and an empty model-fallback list do not disable this configuration retry. Ordinary configured cross-model fallbacks remain separate. Review saved session overrides and scheduled jobs separately before retirement.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the aliases retire. A replay-safe, structured cyber refusal in Standard/default mode can retry the same provider/model/runtime/account with Blue Access. Existing Blue/Red requests are not retried or downgraded, and `cyberFailover.mode=off` remains authoritative. Current account/credential/route grants are required before submission; there is no entitlement inferred from a model name, auth type, or another account. Run `openclaw doctor --fix` to remove retired `cyberFailover.model` fields through the existing core/plugin migration owners; explicit mode/cooloff settings and ordinary primary/fallback model configuration are preserved. Program selection (`standard`, `daybreak_blue`, `daybreak_red`) remains independent of Fast/Ultrafast. Empty model configuration (`accessPrograms: {}`) leaves selection unspecified; null is invalid.

Authenticated ChatGPT model discovery supplies caller-specific program metadata. The Gateway projects it as optional `availableAccessPrograms.cyber` on each account/model/runtime choice, preserving unknown versus explicitly empty results. The existing account/catalog lifecycle owns invalidation; no new cache or state store is introduced. Saved session overrides are checked again at execution, and native Codex verifies the same client/account model catalog before its turn starts.

This OpenClaw integration supports the native Codex turn-scoped parameter with ChatGPT authentication and rejects explicit programs with native API-key authentication before submission. This is the integration’s current scope, not an upstream limitation: pinned Codex 0.162.1 rejects API-key programs when its separate feature is disabled and forwards them when enabled. **Platform API-key discovery now reads explicit caller-specific program metadata from the official Codex models endpoint, using the same selected key.** Public `/v1/models` remains the model-inventory authority; metadata cannot add an unlisted model. No model-name, plan, or approval-label inference and no billable Responses probe is used. Custom routes and header overrides cannot inherit official grants. The existing selected-account refresh now reaches the HTTP cache and publishes changed outcomes to open UI consumers. Native Codex API-key execution remains unsupported by this integration; official Platform and ChatGPT Responses endpoints remain separate. The 60-second HTTP-cache lifetime is not a polling timer or instantaneous revocation guarantee. Selected profile/key and route isolate observations; project/organization request-header overrides are ineligible for default-route grants. Missing, empty or failed metadata hides Access while ordinary inventory remains usable.

References: [Daybreak](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/daybreak), [Fast](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/fast-mode), [Ultrafast](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/ultrafast-mode).

## Evidence

Prior-head proof is not relabeled as current-head CI. **Current-head [CI 39734744199](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39734744199) is successful: 107 successful and 20 skipped jobs, zero failures; all PostgreSQL shards and openclaw/ci-gate passed.** [ClawSweeper revision 40](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177812#issuecomment-6279630547) completed for this exact head with **no findings and no before-merge items**, confirming the prior conflict is resolved. prs.title: fix(agent-core): bound runaway loops with turn/error-batch/idle-repeat guards (#120962)
prs.body: Closes #120962 [AI-assisted] ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where a worker agent could enter an unbounded retry loop inside the native runLoop: an external service returning HTTP 429 (masked inside a "successful" tool output) drove 219 assistant turns / 177 tool calls / ~15M tokens over 6h42m, stopped only by the global `stuckSessionAbortMs` timeout rather than by any active guardrail. ## Why This Change Was Made Adds three opt-in hard cutoffs to the agent-core runLoop, each activating independently when set to a positive integer in `tools.loopDetection`: - **`turnLimit`** — max assistant turns per run; ends gracefully with a terminal message instead of another provider request. - **`maxConsecutiveErrorBatches`** — max consecutive all-error tool batches; any success resets the streak. - **`maxIdleRepeatCalls`** — max consecutive identical tool calls (same name + args); catches errors hidden inside successful output. Steering-skipped calls are excluded. `enabled: true` alone does not engage hard cutoffs (preserves upgrade contract). `enabled: false` disables both layers. Resolved config propagates through sessions, compaction, and worker launch descriptors. The launcher fences guard-enabled turns on worker bundles lacking the `worker-loop-guard-v1` capability; configless and `enabled:false` turns are unaffected. ## User Impact Operators who want the guardrails set at least one guard key (e.g. `turnLimit: 200`) in a `tools.loopDetection` block. Existing configurations gain no new hard termination behavior unless a guard key is explicitly set. Public package consumers see no change unless they opt in. ## Evidence **Focused tests (all pass):** - `packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.guard.test.ts` — 23 tests: maxTurns, error-batch, idle-repeat, steering-skip exclusion (sequential + parallel), steering requeue - `src/agents/sessions/agent-session-loop-guard-transport.test.ts` — real `AgentSession` through local HTTP/SSE transport, 3 repeated calls → graceful termination, no 4th request - `src/agents/tool-loop-detection-config.test.ts` — 9 tests: per-key activation, `enabled:false` kill switch, per-agent cascade - `src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-launcher.loop-guard.test.ts` — 6 tests: launcher fence, serialization, guard-off compatibility - `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/worker-admission.test.ts` — 25 tests: loop-guard capability in worker protocol features

prs.title: fix(ios): session drawer downloads the full session list on every session event
prs.body: Closes #167729 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: the iOS drawer downloads the full session roster for every session event, even when the event already contains the changed row. ## User Impact User impact: drawer rows stay current while downloading **46.9% less session-roster data** in the real-Gateway simulator run: **476,148 → 252,997 bytes** for the same event sequence. ## Why This Change Was Made Known, identified, active-scope rows use the shared row updater. Missing, deleted, archived, malformed, or stale rows request a coalesced roster refresh. The drawer and shared sidebar queries use the same refresh coordinator. Known child lifecycle and subagent-status events still request a coalesced authoritative refresh: child-only deltas cannot clear omitted activity flags on ancestors. Ordinary label patches remain local. The original shared session-change projection is preserved: partial event rows merge field by field; omitted fields retain loaded metadata, explicit null clears a field, and supplied arrays replace it. This preserves model selection and thinking capabilities when Gateway lifecycle events omit them. A model, provider, or runtime change invalidates stale thinking capabilities; a new session incarnation replaces retained state. Complete roster snapshots remain authoritative. Event encoding preserves omission and explicit null through replay. Row changes received during a load accumulate the projected row so a later partial lifecycle event cannot erase an earlier model update. They are replayed without resurrecting rows invalidated afterward. Newer held metadata and matching observer receipts survive older roster snapshots; foreign global observer receipts are cleared. Connection, pull, and sequence-gap refreshes remain immediate. ## Evidence ### Partial-event metadata regression - The new regression fails with the pre-fix row replacement: 17 assertion issues across 7 tests. - Patched focused run: **161 tests in 7 suites passed**, including omitted thinking/model metadata, explicit null clearing, event replay, model/provider/runtime changes, session replacement, sidebar queries, refresh coordination, Gateway decoding, and reasoning visibility. - SwiftFormat and strict SwiftLint pass on all six changed Swift files: **0 violations**. ### In-flight roster replay regression (ae3267c84fb) The iPhone 17 simulator on iOS 26.5 runs the same nine `RootSidebarModelSessionEventsTests` against the old partial-event buffer and the cumulative projection fix. A model-selection update is followed by a lifecycle update omitting the model while a roster response is held. - Red, reverting only the buffer fix: **1 test fails, 8 pass**, exit 65. The held-load regression reports `Expectation failed: (model.sessions.first?.model → nil) == "new-model"`. - Green, restoring the fix: **9 tests in 1 suite pass**, exit 0 (`** TEST SUCCEEDED **`). The selected model survives both updates and the older roster response, without another fetch. - All six tested source-file SHA-256 hashes match the submitted files. The shared **161 tests in 7 suites** and strict six-file lint pass on those same sources. ### Known helper completion regression (current revision) - Red control uses the exact reviewed `ae3267c84fb` drawer source with the new tests. Both `lifecycle` and `subagent-status` cases fail: `hasActiveSubagentRun → true` remains set and `loads.rosters → 0` instead of 1; xcodebuild exits 65. - Green: **11 tests in 2 suites pass** on an isolated iPhone 17 / iOS 26.5 simulator (including both parameterized completion cases), exit 0, **TEST SUCCEEDED**. Eight child events coalesce to one roster load, the parent's helper flag clears, and ordinary label updates still perform zero roster loads. The 20-event burst still requires only one load. - Shared native validation: **300 tests in 24 suites pass**, including the existing finished-helper lifecycle/subagent-status regression and `ChatSessionSidebar` tests. This result is reused only under matching source hashes. - SwiftFormat, strict SwiftLint on all six Swift files, and docs formatting pass. All seven submitted source/doc hashes match the tested tree. - The client contract now documents identified nested wire rows as partial deltas; authoritative roster snapshots retain replacement semantics. ### Real Gateway: rendered drawer and measured traffic The iPhone 17 Pro simulator on iOS 26.5 runs base `fddee787e37` and head `e001c9d8447` through the normal iOS Gateway adapter. Each run starts with six sessions, performs 16 label patches, creates two sessions, and deletes two sessions. Both deliver **22 `sessions.changed` events**. Initial connection and roster loads are excluded. Counts and payload bytes come from the Gateway response log for the app operator connection, independently matched to passively captured WebSocket frames. | Measured result | Base | Fixed | |---|---:|---:| | Delivered session events | 22 | 22 | | Drawer roster responses during 16 label patches | 16 | 0 | | Drawer roster responses, whole sequence | 22 | 3 | | All session-roster responses on app connection | 40 | 21 | | Session-roster response payload bytes | 476,148 | 252,997 | **223,151 bytes saved (46.9%)**. Both UI runs pass: four renamed rows and two newly created rows appear; both deleted rows disappear. The fixed drawer applies all 16 label updates without its full-roster reload and uses three roster responses for the create/delete sequence. Receipts and connection-filtered Gateway logs: [base](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/c77a87bd476c692f4b32b873eec7e2f674b26bff/before/receipt.json), [fixed](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/c77a87bd476c692f4b32b873eec7e2f674b26bff/after/receipt.json), [base log](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/c77a87bd476c692f4b32b873eec7e2f674b26bff/before/gateway-filtered.log), [fixed log](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/c77a87bd476c692f4b32b873eec7e2f674b26bff/after/gateway-filtered.log). Behavior proof commit: `e001c9d8447` on main `fddee787e37`. The same 20-event burst through the production drawer event handler performs **20 roster loads with the source change reverted, then 1 with the fix**. The red assertion is `Expectation failed: (loads.rosters → 20) == 1`; setup loads are excluded. - Red: 4 tests in 2 suites, 3 failures and 9 assertion issues; exit 65. Metadata replacement and observer-retirement assertions fail along with the load count. - Green: **170 tests in 9 suites pass**, including local metadata updates with zero roster loads, one trailing invalidation, no overlapping event-driven loads, in-flight row replay, deleted-row absence, stale-roster rejection, observer ownership, cancellation/replacement of debounced waits, and immediate sequence-gap recovery. - Full shared-kit `swift test --jobs 2 --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit`: **2,308 Swift Testing tests in 195 suites and 59 XCTest tests pass**. - Both iOS simulator build-for-testing runs pass. SwiftFormat 0.63.1 and strict SwiftLint 0.65.1 pass on all eight changed Swift files; oxfmt passes on `docs/gateway/clients.md`. AI-assisted (Claude and OpenAI Codex).

prs.title: fix(gateway): report active unmanaged restart startup accurately
prs.body:
Closes #119958

## Summary

Fixes the unmanaged SIGUSR1 restart path that reports a 60-second health timeout even when the same gateway process has accepted the restart and is still progressing through startup.

## Root cause

The CLI sends SIGUSR1 and then polls only listener health. An in-process restart can retain its PID while the listener is intentionally absent, so PID and port state cannot distinguish active startup from a dead restart.

## Fix

The gateway loop owns a short-lived renewable startup-progress lease while awaiting each startup. The unmanaged listener waiter accepts a typed `still-starting` result only when that lease is fresh, belongs to the signaled gateway process, and began after this restart request. The normal 60-second listener window is not extended. Missing, stale, expired, or non-progressing lease evidence still fails the restart.

## User impact

A bounded still-starting result tells operators to run `openclaw gateway status --deep` instead of treating a healthy slow boot as failed and applying destructive recovery.

## Validation

Run the focused lifecycle, listener-health, run-loop, and lease regressions; then `git diff --check` and `pnpm check:changed`.

## Credit

Thanks @islandpreneur007 for the source reproduction in #119958.
