prs.title: fix: reclaim cloud workers after cleanup acceptance
prs.body:
Follow-up to #168454 and #173825.

## What Problem This Solves

Stopping a cloud worker waits for the provider's full physical release, keeping session reclaim on a 40–120 second cleanup path.

## User Impact

Reclaim can finish after session shutdown and accepted cleanup. The environment remains `destroying` until physical release is confirmed; billing can continue during that interval. Failed confirmation remains visible and retryable. Providers without the capability, unsupported direct Crabbox backends, and already-disconnected dedicated workers retain blocking cleanup.

Expected savings are the physical-release portion of the observed Azure 100–117s, GCP 66–77s, and AWS 4–58s waits, minus acceptance and session-cleanup overhead. These are estimates from the reported timings, not a new live benchmark; physical billing duration is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing environment lifecycle owner now distinguishes cleanup acceptance from confirmation through an optional provider notification. Crabbox uses `stop --wait=false` for acceptance and a waiting `stop` within the same cleanup budget for confirmation. Terminal inspection alone is never release proof.

Warm-image capture still releases reclaim after capture admission, but its destroy promise now remains owned through confirmed stop and preserves late failures. The redundant post-reclaim tunnel wait and warning-only teardown observer are removed. No new environment states, configuration, or state stores are introduced. The provider contract and user documentation describe the handoff and continued billing window.

Against the merge base: non-test source +212/-86, tests and fixtures +388/-63, docs +7/-1. The remaining production growth is the optional acceptance contract, its existing-owner handoff, and Crabbox's bounded acceptance/confirmation sequence. The CI follow-up changes only ten test/fixture files (+37/-16); it adds no production logic.

The CI follow-up preserves the original lifecycle assertions. The dispatch fixture now shuts down its tunnel before returning reclaim acceptance, matching the existing production owner. The Move/Stop fixture holds recovery-source release after local publication instead of waiting at the removed post-completion tunnel stop. A real SSH-manager regression verifies that tunnel shutdown, credential revocation, and rejection of the old handle all precede provider cleanup acceptance. The existing tests still cover delayed destruction, visible confirmation failure/retry, and blocking providers.

Crabbox's classless lifecycle command sequence was already correct; its exact timeout assertion now uses a fixed monotonic clock. Test doubles retain the required reclaim contract, the acceptance fixture narrows to an attached lease, and extension tests use the public SDK test-fixtures entry point.

## Evidence

CI follow-up validation on Node 24.22.1 with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`; runtime checks use `pnpm test <file...> --maxWorkers=1`:

| File | Result | Wall time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-dispatch-authority.test.ts` | 17 passed | 195.73s |
| `src/gateway/server-worker-placement-reclaim.preparation.test.ts` | 39 passed | 308.82s |
| `extensions/crabbox/index.test.ts` | 8 passed | 212.47s |
| `test/extension-test-boundary.test.ts` | 12 passed | 197.81s |
| `src/gateway/worker-environments/provider-reclaim-acceptance.test.ts` | 3 passed | 131.03s |
| `src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-dispatch-reclaim.test.ts` | 31 passed | 71.45s |
| `src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-reclaim-acceptance.test.ts` | 1 passed | 28.30s |
| `src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-launcher-build-recovery.test.ts` | 27 passed | 151.79s |
| `src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-shutdown.test.ts` | 2 passed | 54.97s |
| `extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-stop.test.ts` with `extensions/crabbox/index.test.ts` | 13 passed | 135.74s |

- `pnpm run tsgo:core`: passed, 3.50s. Core test type graphs `gateway-other` and `gateway-server` via `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.<graph>.json --incremental`: passed, 248.36s and 5.66s.
- `pnpm run tsgo:extensions:test`: passed, 305.08s.
- `node --import tsx scripts/check-extension-plugin-sdk-boundary.mts --all`: all three modes passed, 11.72s.
- Scoped type-aware lint using the repository `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` runner: core passed, 218.48s; Crabbox passed, 253.84s. Touched-file `pnpm exec oxfmt --check`: passed, 0.12s; `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent review through P2: no actionable findings. The only subsequent change was import ordering by the formatter.
- Baselines reproduced all reported runtime failures on `afa45c965d0`: authority 1 failed/16 passed; Move/Stop 5 failed/34 passed; Crabbox lifecycle 2 failed/6 passed; boundary 1 failed/11 passed. The core test-type baseline reproduced all four reported diagnostics. The fixes retain the behavioral assertions rather than accepting new expected outcomes.
- Wall times include compilation, source verification, and shared artifact-lock waits on the loaded host. The existing SQLite coordinator suites cover real cancellation/completion ownership and cannot be replaced by provider-only mocks. No live Gateway, cloud allocation, or Docker run was used.

Earlier implementation evidence:

- Red on unchanged owner code at `094bbd6b153b` (also unchanged on `origin/main` at `1fead915921e`): the placement regression failed with `expected 'waited-for-release' to be 'reclaimed'`. One test, **364.88s wall** / 6.948s test execution under Node 24.22.1.
- Node 24.22.1, `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`: `pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/provider-reclaim-acceptance.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-reclaim-acceptance.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/provider-crabbox-runtime-preflight.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-dispatch-reclaim.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/provider-node-teardown.test.ts extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-stop.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **82 tests passed, 795.88s wall**. Covers accepted reclaim, delayed physical confirmation, visible failure/reconciliation retry, unchanged blocking providers, direct-backend fallback, and detached capture.
- Final Node 24.22.1 rerun after the dedicated-node fallback: `pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/provider-node-teardown.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/provider-reclaim-acceptance.test.ts extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-provider.test.ts extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-warm-image.test.ts extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-warm-image-lifecycle.test.ts extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-stop-lifetime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **125 tests passed, 216.38s wall**. This includes the capable-provider offline fallback, shared/unknown-host rejection, warm-image lifecycle, and late stop failure/timeout custody.
- `pnpm run tsgo:core`, touched-file `oxfmt --check`, scoped core and Crabbox **type-aware** lint, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent review through P2 found no actionable issues in the final production change.
- Inspected Crabbox v0.77.0/v0.78.1 stop semantics: asynchronous acceptance explicitly requires a follow-up waiting stop; direct backends reject the asynchronous flag with the exact diagnostic used for fallback.
- No live cloud allocation or latency benchmark was run. PR CI supplies the broader checks. Local preparation was expensive on the heavily loaded host; timings above include worker compilation and module loading.

prs.title: feat(sdk): support realtime transcription WebSocket protocols
prs.body:
Closes #118952

## What Problem This Solves

Realtime transcription plugin authors cannot use the shared WebSocket session helper with upstream servers that require subprotocol negotiation. The official FunASR server, for example, rejects the upgrade with HTTP 400 unless the client requests its required `binary` protocol.

The helper also needs a supported typed package boundary so third-party providers can consume the session contract without importing host-only registry internals.

## What Changed

- Add optional `protocols: string | string[]` to the realtime transcription WebSocket session options and forward it through the standard `ws` protocol argument.
- Publish `openclaw/plugin-sdk/realtime-transcription` as a typed SDK subpath containing provider/session types and `createRealtimeTranscriptionWebSocketSession`.
- Move host provider-registry helpers to private-local `openclaw/plugin-sdk/realtime-transcription-runtime`.
- Add package-boundary, export-surface, required-subprotocol, and consumer-build coverage.
- Document the public SDK import and protocol-negotiation usage.

The protocol-free path keeps the previous two-argument WebSocket constructor and existing behavior. No provider ID, configuration default, dependency, or bundled plugin is added.

## User Impact

Third-party realtime transcription providers can use a stable typed SDK surface and negotiate required WebSocket subprotocols while retaining OpenClaw reconnect, bounded queue, proxy capture, graceful close, and diagnostic behavior. Existing providers that do not set `protocols` are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Integration Follow-up (2026-10-01)

The published signed head is unchanged at `0a348e273357266a8247cd53101af1c0c222a9df`; GitHub still reports merge conflicts. I audited upstream snapshot `7c8d77bfd49cddf382428a8778a426a6437dd523`, which was 1,358 commits beyond the shared base `1a94ee9ed7e277eb98439d5ceecc6ab2b7411fa9`. The PR API's base SHA still reported that old shared base, so the comparison used the separately fetched branch tip and GitHub compare result. Main advanced again during this audit; the later branch read at 2026-10-01T02:45:13Z returned `3b8fc7e64cee7bdb35b2e122a0948c331f100795`. The exact conflict evidence below belongs to snapshot `7c8d77bf`, **not** that later main.

A whole-tree dry merge reached its 120-second bound in the partial clone and produced no merge result. I then exported the exact Git blob bytes for the six files changed on both sides, checked their blob identities and SHA-256s, and ran native `git merge-file` separately:

- Five files merge textually without conflict: both SDK documentation pages, the voice-call provider-discovery test, `package.json`, and the WebSocket-session implementation.
- `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mts` has two conflict regions: PR budgets of 4,602 public exports / 2,696 callable exports versus audited-main budgets of 4,588 / 2,694. Upstream has both retired SDK surface and reconciled previously shipped growth since the shared base; simply keeping the old larger numbers would not establish the correct current surface.

This is a bounded textual-conflict diagnosis, **not** a passing whole-tree merge, package build, API-diff, or test run on a new candidate. No working-tree merge, source/budget edit, commit, push, or CI rerun was made; the branch remains clean. A future resolution must preserve upstream removals and validate the resulting surface through the canonical SDK workflow, not hand-edit generated baselines or widen ratchets just to pass. SDK-owner acceptance of this PR's public boundary remains outstanding. The hosted failures documented below also remain unresolved; old successful tests do not establish compatibility with newer main.

### Prior Head Validation (2026-09-29)

Published SSH-signed+DCO head: `0a348e273357266a8247cd53101af1c0c222a9df`, based on the prior synchronization head `d191b4deef00662db93886a5fe2f644326b66491` and pinned upstream `1a94ee9ed7e277eb98439d5ceecc6ab2b7411fa9`. The new test-only commit addresses the current review finding that the successful protocol test left its client connected while closing the server. The earlier synchronization addressed a reproduced merge conflict in `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mts`; neither commit is an empty CI refresh. The effective delta remains 16 files. Upstream's removed budget annotations stay removed; only this PR's existing +1/+11/+1 increments are retained, yielding 159 public subpaths, 4,602 exports and 2,696 callable exports as the budgets. Upstream async WebSocket capture, lazy loading, payload limit and close behavior are preserved.

Validation on the authorized Linux host, with source hashes unchanged through testing and independent review:

- The protocol test reproduced the teardown cost at 5,077 ms against the repository's under-five-second file budget. Terminating the server-owned clients before `server.close()` reduced the same test to 101 ms; the adjacent realtime-transcription suite passed 25/25. The changed file passed `oxfmt`, all 263 targeted oxlint rules, `src` test typechecking, and `git diff --check`.
- Frozen-lock installation passed using the repository-pinned pnpm version; no lockfile or dependency override was introduced.
- Four focused native test files passed: package-contract guardrails, WebSocket protocol negotiation, existing WebSocket sessions, and SDK surface reporting.
- Full `tsgo:all` passed, covering core, UI, core tests, extension projects, scripts and root tests.
- Of the 34 units in the canonical changed-file plan, 32 completed successfully across bounded calls, including formatting, SDK exports/surface, package boundaries, all three unused-export scans and runtime import-cycle validation. This is constituent-command evidence, not a passing all-in-one `pnpm check` run.
- The environment-variable ratchet failed: 484 names exceed the unchanged budget of 483. The same native checker against an alternate index containing only the exact pinned upstream commit also failed at 484/483. The candidate and upstream name sets are identical, with no added or removed names; the checker and budget are unchanged. No ratchet allowance was increased or skipped.
- Full local lint did not complete within the 540-second enclosing limit. The scripts shard (1,249 files) and extensions shard (10,531 files) passed with zero warnings/errors; core was interrupted by the deadline. This is not a full-lint pass, and prior-head hosted lint results do not establish coverage for this head.
- All native strict-smoke and full-build phases completed across bounded executions, including unified declarations, bundled plugins/runtime checks, SDK declarations and export verification, UI build, build information and startup metadata. The initial strict-smoke/full-build invocations timed out; the remaining phases were executed through the repository's own build-step runner and artifact-ownership mechanism. No single full-build invocation is claimed to have passed. Export verification covered all 159 public SDK subpaths.
- Independent source review found no P1/P2 findings. Native pre-commit hooks passed; the signed commit retains the reviewed/tested tree. The effective PR delta passes `git diff --check`. Full-merge whitespace diagnostics in imported changelog/patch files are identical to the upstream-only control and were not rewritten in this PR.

Remaining boundaries: whole-suite tests and the historical hosted large-test shard failures were not rerun locally for this head. Current hosted CI has completed with unresolved failures; see the follow-up below. The native commit-to-commit API-diff command remains unrun locally because it creates temporary worktrees outside this task's permitted workflow. Protocol coverage still demonstrates successful array-form negotiation, not separate string/rejection/reconnect cases. Real FunASR audio was not rerun. This update is not presented as all-CI-green or merge-ready.


### Hosted CI Follow-up (2026-09-29)

The checks associated with published head `0a348e273357266a8247cd53101af1c0c222a9df` have completed: 174 success, 50 skipped, 1 neutral, and 2 failures. The failures are `checks-node-changed-compact-large-21` and the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`; this is not an all-green result.

The [large-21 execution log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36514323799/job/109233458993) records checkout of CI merge `b7ea8f5e`, merging this head into upstream `d3008b2d5ee76e6f858380da5935db305305b005`. Its 59-file agent-chat shard reports 598 passed and 7 failed: one RPC timeout in `server.sessions.create.stores.test.ts`, three failures in `server.sessions.create.titles.test.ts`, and three in `server.sessions.delete-state-lifecycle.test.ts`. The latter six report the SQLite pathname/active-worker-owner guard directly or through an UNAVAILABLE response.

I ran the entire delete-lifecycle file through the native test-projects entry point on the published PR head, with Node 24.20.0 and isolated HOME/TMPDIR:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-projects.mts src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-state-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Result: **13 passed**, exit 0, 222.53 seconds, without reaching the enclosing 360-second limit. This is deliberately not reported as a reproduction or a fix of the hosted failures: it uses the PR head rather than the CI merge, one file rather than the original 59-file ordering, and a different local environment. No assertion, test timeout, SQLite guard, or runtime source was changed. The complete shard and title cases were not run locally because they create additional Git worktrees outside this task's permitted workflow. No model download, inference, or live service restart was performed.

The current hosted failures remain unresolved. Owner approval of the newly public typed realtime-transcription SDK boundary also remains outstanding; test evidence does not replace that decision or any required CI check.


## Historical Validation

### Previous Synchronization (2026-09-22)

prs.title: fix(exec): allow larger commands on large-memory hosts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Follow-up to #182111: a fixed 8 GiB ceiling can kill legitimate agent builds and test runs on large-memory hosts.

## User Impact

The Linux host-exec bound is now the smaller of one quarter of host/cgroup memory and half the headroom after Gateway RSS. It scales with the machine while preserving protection on small or constrained hosts. The existing one-second sampler and kill path are unchanged. Foreground failure text and background polling include the applied cap in MiB; regression assertions now require that value.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the fixed ceiling and its unused constant instead of adding configuration or another policy. On a synthetic 192 GiB host with 8 GiB Gateway RSS, the cap becomes 48 GiB rather than 8 GiB. A 64 GiB cgroup gets 16 GiB; a 4 GiB cgroup with 1 GiB Gateway RSS remains at 1 GiB, falling to 512 MiB when Gateway RSS is 3 GiB.

Net LOC versus #182111's implementation: **−4 overall, −5 production**. Same four existing files; no new module, dependency, or test case. Sampling can still overshoot and per-command budgets are independent; this remains a watchdog rather than aggregate kernel containment.

## Evidence

Acceptance: remove only the fixed ceiling; preserve the small-host/cgroup and RSS-headroom cases, one-second sampling, real child/PTY termination, and visible applied-cap diagnostics. This is a default correction, with no latency or GC performance claim.

- Red control: the updated large-host expectation fails on the old implementation (8 GiB returned, 48 GiB required).
- Focused local tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/child-memory.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec.pty.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 5 passed, 3 Linux-only skips, 44.15 seconds wall time including worker preparation. Individual file times: 0.367 s and 37.26 s; actual PTY test work is about one second. Exact-head [Linux CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40058343036/job/120766543952) passed the existing real 384 MiB hog against a scaled 256 MiB cap: **1.154 s non-PTY / 1.017 s PTY**, requiring the cap in both foreground outcome and background polling.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean. The provider mismatch was not bypassed or reconfigured.
- Changed-file lint, targeted core typecheck, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed. [CI run 40058343036](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40058343036) is green on `d52a4fd65d2fc29c5da4745b55681d5bd375aa8d`; no CI reruns were requested.

## Operator Host Hardening Proposal

This is a follow-up proposal, not deployment configuration or a host change in this PR:

- Enable `Delegate=yes`; keep the delegated root empty, put the Gateway in its own leaf, and place commands in an `agent-work` leaf before execution. `DelegateSubgroup=gateway` can establish the Gateway leaf on supporting systemd versions. Delegation alone does not relocate commands.
- Reserve measured Gateway working-set protection with `MemoryLow=` on its leaf (`memory.low` for a raw delegated subgroup), including the necessary ancestor budget. Give sshd, tailscaled, and journald modest measured `MemoryMin=` reservations with corresponding ancestor allocations. Budget these together; do not overcommit hard protection. [Resource-control semantics](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.resource-control.html).
- Enable `systemd-oomd` pressure killing on a monitored ancestor with agent-work as the eligible victim. Explicitly omit the Gateway leaf from victim selection using the supported ownership-aware mechanism, then verify that choice with `oomctl` and a synthetic pressure test. Enable cgroup-v2 memory accounting and PSI; choose pressure/duration settings from observed healthy workloads. Oomd kills descendant candidates, so setting pressure killing on a process-filled leaf itself is insufficient. [Oomd behavior and requirements](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-oomd.service.html).

A deployment needs separate operator approval and coordinated restart scheduling. No production services, cgroups, or configuration were changed.

prs.title: fix(android): refuse embedded Control UI auth on pinned gateway connections
prs.body:
## Summary

The Android app's embedded Control UI WebView never enforced the native Gateway TLS certificate pin: its pin check lived only in the SSL-error callback, which Android invokes exclusively for recoverable certificate errors, so a successful platform-CA-trusted handshake bypassed the pin entirely and the page's own WebSocket transport was outside it too. This change refuses embedded Control UI auth admission — before credential evaluation, bridge registration, or remote loading — whenever the admitted native connection actually enforces a pin, and sources that decision from the admitted connection's TLS parameters instead of the saved fingerprint preference.

## What Problem This Solves

1. `apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/ui/ControlUiWebView.kt` — `installAuth` installed the native-auth bridge and the document-start credential script with no pin gate, and the page then loaded unconditionally on success. The only pin comparison was `onReceivedSslError`, unreachable for CA-trusted handshakes per the Android `WebViewClient` contract. A network attacker holding a different system-CA-trusted certificate and key for the exact Gateway hostname could serve an allowed-origin document that the startup auth and native-connect bridge would provision with the current native credential while the native connection stayed pinned. Now `installAuth` fails closed when `page.tlsFingerprintSha256` is set: no bridge, no credential script, no remote load; the superseded SSL-error proceed-exception and its helpers are removed.
2. `apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/NodeRuntime.kt` — the control page's fingerprint was read from the saved preference store even when the active connection had not enforced it. `GatewayConnectionContext` now carries the `GatewayTlsParams` resolved for the connection, and `refreshGatewayControlPage` reflects the admitted transport: an actively enforced pin gates the embedded page, while an intentionally admitted local-cleartext connection with an inactive saved pin keeps working.

3. `ControlUiWebView.kt` — the refusal reused the generic "Reconnect the app to reopen this gateway page." message, which is wrong for a pinned connection because reconnecting with the same pin repeats the refusal. A pinned refusal now shows a localized explanation that embedded pages are unavailable on certificate-pinned gateways and native screens remain usable.

Net effect: a document admitted through a transport that cannot enforce the native pin can no longer receive native authentication material or connect proofs, and the local-cleartext workflow is preserved rather than broken by a naive saved-preference refusal.

## Why this design

- Fail closed at the owning boundary: Android WebView exposes no pre-document certificate hook for successful CA-trusted handshakes and cannot pin the page's own WebSocket networking, so the only sound admission decision for a pinned connection is refusal.
- The refusal keys off the admitted connection's TLS params, never the saved preference: a stored fingerprint that the current transport does not enforce must not lock users out, and the admitted transport must not inherit trust it did not verify.
- No new configuration surface: behavior is keyed entirely off existing per-connection pin state; unpinned CA-trusted workflows are unchanged.
- Embedded terminal, desktop, dashboard, and browser views are unavailable on actively pinned connections; native Gateway operation and native app screens retain the pin. This mirrors the Linux native-auth fail-closed approach and is documented in `apps/android/README.md`. A future feature-preserving transport that carries the pin across documents and credential-bearing WebSockets remains a separate design option.

## Evidence of Fix

| Path | Mode | Before | After | Verified by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `installAuth` admission, pinned connection (`ControlUiWebView.kt:341`) | Active native pin, no SSL-error callback (successful CA-trusted handshake simulated via feature-supported WebView mounts) | Bridge registered, credential script injected, remote URL loaded, credential callbacks reachable — pin never consulted | No remote load, no bridge registration, no document-start script, no auth-port transfer, zero credential evaluations and zero signings, across https and loopback origins and both modern and legacy auth feature paths | New regression `pinnedGatewayDoesNotLoadOrExposeAuthWithoutSslErrorCallback` (passes in 0.159 s) |
| Control page fingerprint source (`NodeRuntime.kt` `refreshGatewayControlPage`) | Manual local cleartext admitted with a saved-but-inactive pin | Page carried the saved fingerprint (wrong source; a naive refusal would break cleartext) | Page fingerprint is null — reflects the admitted transport, not the preference | `GatewayBootstrapAuthTest.controlPageUsesCurrentNativeOperatorGrantAndRetiresAfterDisconnect` extended with a saved pin + cleartext connect |
| Superseded SSL-error proceed-exception (`onReceivedSslError`) | Pinned self-signed certificate, recoverable SSL error | Proceeded only on exact leaf-hash + origin match (the only path consulting the pin) | Removed; helper-only test coverage removed with it; pinned connections now refuse by default instead of exceptioning through | `ControlUiWebViewTest` trimmed; remaining 6 tests green |
| Refusal message on a pinned connection (`ControlUiWebView.kt`) | Opening an embedded page while the pin is enforced | Generic "Reconnect the app…" text (reconnecting never clears it) | Localized message that embedded pages are unavailable on pinned gateways and native screens remain usable; asserted not to say "Reconnect" | Same regression, extended; `native:i18n:verify` and `check` for the new string |
| Normal native auth / navigation / lifecycle | Unpinned CA-trusted gateway | Working | Unchanged — gate is a no-op when no pin is enforced | ControlUiWebViewAuthTest 13, GatewayBootstrapAuthTest 86, ConnectionManagerTest 37, GatewayTlsTest 15 all green |
| Native connection pin itself (`GatewayTls.kt`) | Fingerprint mismatch on native transport | Rejected | Unchanged (file untouched) | GatewayTlsTest 15/15 green |

Limits of this proof: the regression mounts the production composable under Robolectric with the AndroidX WebView shadows, so it proves the admission decision and the absence of credential/signature delivery, not Android network delivery. Not demonstrated: a live device/emulator certificate-interception PoC — the attack prerequisite (a distinct system-CA-trusted certificate and key for the exact Gateway hostname plus active MITM) is not reproducible in a unit-test harness, and the refusal is proven at the admission boundary instead.

Local gate runs (Ubuntu x86_64, Node 24.22.1, Temurin JDK 21.0.13+9, pinned Gradle 9.7.1, Android platform 37.0 rev 2): `:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest` focused suites — 157 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped; `:app:ktlintCheck` and `:app:lintPlayDebug` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL; `scripts/android-app-i18n.ts check` — no inventory diff; `git diff --check` — clean.

Red on base: with the production files (`ControlUiWebView.kt`, `NodeRuntime.kt`) restored to the base revision and the new tests kept, `:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest` fails both regressions. `pinnedGatewayDoesNotLoadOrExposeAuthWithoutSslErrorCallback` fails with `expected null, but was:<https://gateway.example:8443/openclaw/dashboard>` (the remote page loads under an active pin). `controlPageUsesCurrentNativeOperatorGrantAndRetiresAfterDisconnect` fails with `expected null, but was:<abab…>` (the saved-but-inactive pin leaks into the page). The existing `mountedBridgeSignsNativeIdentityAndCurrentTokenWithoutExportingStartupSecrets` control passes on base. With the fix, all three pass.

Stored data and upgrade: this change reads no new stored data and writes none. `SecurePrefs.kt`, `ConnectionManager.kt`, the `gateway.tls.*` and `gateway.manual.tls` keys, device auth storage, and the native TLS trust manager are untouched, so saved pins and local-cleartext settings from an earlier release are interpreted exactly as before by the native connection. The only new input is the per-connection `GatewayTlsParams` that the existing `resolveTlsParams` already produces for the native sessions. A device or emulator upgrade run was not performed.

## Testing

- New: `ControlUiWebViewAuthTest.pinnedGatewayDoesNotLoadOrExposeAuthWithoutSslErrorCallback` (refusal contract, no SSL-error callback involved, both origins, both auth feature paths).
- Extended: `GatewayBootstrapAuthTest.controlPageUsesCurrentNativeOperatorGrantAndRetiresAfterDisconnect` (admitted-transport fingerprint semantics).
- Removed: helper-only `ControlUiWebViewTest.pinnedSslError_proceedsOnlyForExactCertificateAtGatewayOrigin` testing the deleted SSL-error exception logic.
- Unchanged-green suites: `ControlUiWebViewAuthTest` (13), `GatewayBootstrapAuthTest` (86), `ControlUiWebViewTest` (6), `ConnectionManagerTest` (37), `GatewayTlsTest` (15).
- Docs: `apps/android/README.md` documents the pinned-connection behavior for users.

prs.title: perf(gateway): reuse mention presentations and trim sidebar packing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Sidebar refreshes and mention broadcasts repeatedly allocate packing intermediates and identical display objects for connected viewers.

## User Impact

No wire or permission behavior changes. Viewers still receive current titles and private inbox revisions, with live authorization checked before publication.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mention publication reuses private item presentations, compares the visible vector directly, and removes whole-view JSON/SHA-256 fingerprints and duplicate reverse copies. Actual list/dismiss responses retain their mutable embedded API contract. Sidebar packing creates recipient arrays only for facts that repeat, reuses prepared zero/one-row replies, and builds delta lookup maps without temporary pair arrays. Full multirow packing remains page-specific; there is no new cross-viewer authorization cache.

Gateway runtime delta: +44 lines (+64/-20). The growth retains mutable caller responses separately from private shared presentations and represents unshared recipients without arrays. Tests add 25 net lines to existing cases; the existing real-Gateway benchmark adds 131/deletes 43 lines (+88), rather than adding a second fixture. Documentation adds 18 net lines.

## Evidence

- 42 focused mention tests passed across mention-inbox, sharing-target, and compatibility files, including callback mutation isolation and unchanged revisions after unrelated profile maintenance.
- 15 focused sidebar tests passed across serialization, delta, and history-retention files, covering private visibility, role changes, clock facts, expanded wire values, and collection of retired replies.
- Initial CI caught the singleton encoding-budget expectation: it still charged removed fact encodings. Reproduced the failure locally, extended the same test to both singleton and two-row pages with distinct labels, and passed all 4 accounting/retirement tests. The two-row case retains the original fact-encoding budget proof. No production change was needed.
- Changed-file oxfmt/lint and the single core typecheck lane passed. No broad local test suite or Testbox lease was used; PR CI supplies broad validation.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable P0–P2 findings. Autoreview preflight refused the configured route mismatch; operator configuration was unchanged.
- Final-head CI passed: [run 40045807065](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40045807065), head `7d85b548df6ece96aaecdcbf2253cf5557705752`.
- **v5.4 measurement gate pending:** stale runner reconciled; four longer A/A controls precede untraced candidate timing and a separate traced promotion pass. Earlier two-pair results below are context only.

### Measurement contract — v5.4

The earlier two-pair results below are historical context, not the current landing gate. After the shared-host outage, the previous third pair was reconciled as guard-discarded; no task runner or scope remained active.

Run four matched baseline/baseline (A/A) control pairs first, then two baseline/candidate pairs without GC trace logging, then two swapped baseline/candidate pairs as a separate traced promotion pass. Use the committed benchmark with 5,000 synthetic sessions, 6,000 settled runs, 70 recipient sockets plus one sender, 40 mentions, 200-row sidebars, **20,000 inbox reads and 1,000 broadcasts per phase**. Each broadcast patches a mentioned session title, waits for all recipient notifications, refreshes all sidebars through the real conditional-row decoder, and verifies the title. Allocation sampling and unprofiled runtime phases remain separate; CPU/latency/GC gates use untraced runtime observations, and promotion uses the separate traced pass only.

All pairs queue on slot A, use concurrent interleaved 16-CPU sets within CPUs 96–127, and swap placement on each successive pair. Preparation is low-priority on CPUs 0–63. Every sandbox process inherits a systemd scope; each side has MemoryMax=10G and MemorySwapMax=0, the controller 2G and zero swap. Pair timeout is 100 minutes, lock wait 60 minutes, each guard wait 15 minutes, whole stage six hours, at most three attempts for a guard-interrupted pair. The unchanged shared guard watches every pair; interrupted pairs are discarded. No production Gateway is exercised.

Judge controls across all four pairs and each swapped two-pair block. If controls trip a gate, the protocol is inconclusive: double the workload once to 40,000 reads/2,000 broadcasts and rerun all four controls before any candidate decision. If that still fails, report inconclusive and stop. Candidate gates retain v5 thresholds: ≥20% adverse paired mean, or ≥10% adverse in both swapped pairs. Opposing signs or >5× baseline spread require absolute deltas and v5.2 treatment. p95 requires 200 samples/side; p99 1,000; major GC tails are context below 50 collections. GC pause-percentile absolute mean shifts below 1 ms are context under v5.3; fewer collections without higher total GC also follow v5.1. Always report both maximum pauses and apply max(50 ms, 2× baseline max). Total GC/work and promotion still gate; if total GC/work alone is adverse while allocation falls, flag it for the lead under the existing lane rule.

### Paired measurements (two pairs complete; third pair blocked)

The two swapped pairs reduce total allocation by 5.57% (2.260 MB/broadcast; 32.279 kB/viewer/broadcast) and mean broadcast latency by 3.55% (2.163 ms). The `readView` subtree falls 10.46% and sidebar packing falls 5.53%; these attributions overlap. List GC/work changes by −0.005418 ms/op (−13.04%) and +0.029934 ms/op (+67.33%); promotion by −237.648 B/op (−0.96%) and +15,526.416 B/op (+62.15%). Both metrics are inconclusive under v5.2, so a third identical pair is required before deciding. The third attempt was last verified ready and queued at 2026-10-24 01:45:13 UTC. SSH monitoring and the original runner connection subsequently timed out; a separate reachability probe also failed. There is no third result, no inferred guard outcome, and no replacement run was launched. Merge remains held until the original run is reconciled and the third-pair gate is resolved. No maximum-pause clause is breached in either completed pair.

The 70 recipient sockets share one synthetic profile, so existing list ownership can coalesce requests; this does not measure 70 distinct authorization domains. The baseline and candidate run concurrently on disjoint interleaved 16-CPU sets, with placement swapped in pair two, under the same exclusive lock and unchanged production guard. Each side performs 1,000 inbox reads and 200 broadcasts per measurement phase on Node 26.12.1. The measured checkout is frozen at `155f67dfc6ccc4c10d40ac6ff3931fae744e21b6`, with parent `9538d3ab0bb5d1d5de262fe53ec0c24da0b2f0cc` owner modules as baseline. Both changed production owners and the benchmark script are byte-identical to final PR head `7d85b548df6ece96aaecdcbf2253cf5557705752`; later edits affect accounting-test coverage and measurement documentation.

CPU is unprofiled; process CPU includes workers. Each cell reports candidate minus baseline as both an absolute and relative delta. Means are arithmetic means of paired deltas.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): pin writable ancestors of nested protected skill mounts
prs.body:
## Summary

With `workspaceAccess: "rw"` (and private `"none"` workspaces), OpenClaw bind-mounts skill roots read-only at nested paths inside the writable workdir (`<workdir>/.agents/skills`, `<workdir>/.openclaw/sandbox-skills/skills`). Linux refuses to rename a mountpoint, but not its parent, so a sandboxed shell could move `.agents` or `.openclaw` aside and recreate the protected skill path as ordinary writable files. This PR binds each writable directory between the workdir and a nested protected mount onto itself, so those parents are mountpoints too and the rename fails with `EBUSY`. It complements https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96028 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/126775, which handle different layers.

## What Problem This Solves

The docs promise that "local container mounts and sandbox file tools enforce these read-only roots." The sandbox file tools already refuse to rename a parent of a read-only mount (`requireWritable: "subtree"` in `src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge-mutation-helper.ts`). Shell `exec` does not go through that check, so the sandboxed model could still replace a protected skill path:

- **`.agents/skills`:** the replacement lands in the host workspace. Host skill discovery picks it up, it can shadow a lower-precedence skill with the same name, and the next container recreate mounts the agent-written copy read-only.
- **Materialized `.openclaw/sandbox-skills/skills`:** `exec` and skill scripts inside the sandbox see the agent's copy instead of the managed one.

After this change, a sandboxed process cannot move those parent directories, so the protected path keeps resolving to the real read-only mount. Ordinary edits to other files in those directories still work.

## What was wrong

1. `src/agents/sandbox/workspace-mounts.ts` (`resolveReadOnlyWorkspaceSkillMounts`) plans protected mounts at nested container paths, but nothing pins the intermediate directories (`.agents`, `.openclaw`, `.openclaw/sandbox-skills`). They stay ordinary entries inside the writable workspace bind.
2. `src/agents/sandbox/mount-plan.ts` (`prepareSandboxMountPlan`) emits only the workspace and protected-leaf binds, so in the created container those parents can be renamed by any sandboxed process.

Net effect: a sandboxed `exec` could detach the read-only mount and put agent-written instructions at the protected path.

## Why this design

- Pin the parents at the owning boundary, the container mount plan, so the kernel enforces it for every in-container process and not only the file tools.
- Work out the parents generically from the planned mounts (workdir, owning managed mount, protected target). Nothing is hardcoded to `.agents` or `/workspace`, so non-default workdirs are covered.
- Pin only parents owned by a managed workspace or agent mount that is writable. Read-only roots already refuse the rename, and custom binds keep their daemon-host contract.
- Skip the pin when a Docker-hosted Gateway already exposes that parent through its own read-only bind. That bind is projected as its own mountpoint, and its writable child binds keep their access. A read-only parent cannot be renamed anyway.
- Create the parent directories on the host before the container is created, as the workspace owner, through the existing fs-safe root (`mutationSymlinks: "reject"`, `assertCurrent`). Engines can't create them root-owned, and a symlinked parent fails closed.
- Send the self-binds through the existing `translateSandboxMountSources` path, so Gateway-in-Docker deployments translate them like any other managed bind. Each one is ordered before the protected mount it pins.
- Teach the image-backing check (`sandboxContainerShowsWorkspacePaths`) to accept a covering self-bind only when its source is the workspace source at that same relative path, so images under `.agents/` still display and unrelated binds are still rejected.
- No config surface or default change. Existing containers pick up the new binds through the existing config-hash and `sandboxMountPlanMatchesContainer` mount-change handling.

## Why this does not conflict with related PRs

| PR | Governed layer | Relation to this PR |
|---|---|---|
| https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/85591 (merged) | Introduced read-only skill mounts | This PR closes the parent-rename gap left in that layout |
| https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96028 (open) | Creating missing protected skill roots | Different concern (roots that don't exist yet); both create directories before the container, in different helpers |
| https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/126775 (open) | Moving the materialized skills mount to a direct workdir child | Would remove one nested target; `.agents/skills` stays nested and still needs this pinning. The two compose: if the materialized target becomes a direct child, no parent bind is produced for it |

## Evidence of Fix

Both runs created the sandbox through OpenClaw's own `ensureSandboxContainer` (rw workspace, shared scope, `openclaw-sandbox:bookworm-slim`, Docker 29.8.0), then ran commands with `docker exec` as the sandbox user (uid 1000). The host workspace held an inert `SKILL.md` marker with `description: ORIGINAL`.

| Path | Before (upstream main `5730de35ae9`) | After (this branch) |
|---|---|---|
| Mounts OpenClaw created (`docker inspect`) | `/workspace` rw, `/workspace/.agents/skills` ro, `/workspace/.openclaw/sandbox-skills/skills` ro | the same, plus rw self-binds at `/workspace/.agents`, `/workspace/.openclaw`, `/workspace/.openclaw/sandbox-skills` |
| `mv /workspace/.agents …` | exit 0 | `Device or resource busy`, exit 1 |
| Recreate `.agents/skills/demo/SKILL.md` | exit 0; host marker becomes `REPLACED` | not reachable; host marker stays `ORIGINAL` |
| `mv /workspace/.openclaw …` | exit 0 | `Device or resource busy`, exit 1 |
| `mv /workspace/.openclaw/sandbox-skills …` | not run | refused (`Read-only file system` on the protected child), exit 1 |
| Write inside a protected skill root | blocked (not re-run) | `Read-only file system`, exit 1 |
| Sibling writes in `.agents/` and `.openclaw/` | allowed | allowed, exit 0 |

<details>
<summary>Captured terminal output (scratch paths redacted)</summary>

```text
## BEFORE (upstream main 5730de35ae9) docker 29.8.0 container=proof1119-shared (created by ensureSandboxContainer)
## docker inspect .Mounts
/workspace rw=true
/workspace/.agents/skills rw=false
/workspace/.openclaw/sandbox-skills/skills rw=false
## exec as sandbox user
1000
mv .agents exit=0
recreate protected path exit=0
mv .openclaw exit=0
## host marker
description: REPLACED
```

```text
## docker 29.8.0  container=proof1119-shared (created by ensureSandboxContainer)
## docker inspect .Mounts
/workspace rw=true
/workspace/.agents rw=true
/workspace/.openclaw rw=true
/workspace/.agents/skills rw=false
/workspace/.openclaw/sandbox-skills rw=true
/workspace/.openclaw/sandbox-skills/skills rw=false

## exec as sandbox user
1000
mv: cannot move '/workspace/.agents' to '/workspace/moved': Device or resource busy
mv .agents exit=1
mv: cannot move '/workspace/.openclaw' to '/workspace/moved': Device or resource busy
mv .openclaw exit=1
mv: cannot remove '/workspace/.openclaw/sandbox-skills/skills/demo/SKILL.md': Read-only file system
mv .openclaw/sandbox-skills exit=1
touch: cannot touch '/workspace/.agents/skills/x': Read-only file system
write protected skill exit=1
sibling writes exit=0
description: ORIGINAL
## host marker
description: ORIGINAL
```

</details>

Podman was not run locally. The reporter measured the same mount layout working on rootless Podman 6.1.3.

## Testing

- New tests in `src/agents/sandbox/mount-plan.test.ts`:
  - parents pinned under a non-default workdir, with host directories created as the workspace owner and ordered before the mounts they pin;
  - a read-only Gateway parent bind stays read-only instead of failing startup, and a writable Gateway child below it stays writable;
  - a container created before this fix is detected as a mount change;
  - a symlinked parent is refused, with nothing created outside the workspace;
  - no parent binds under a read-only workspace;
  - image-backing reads under a pinned parent accept the matching self-bind and reject a different source.
- Updated the existing whitespace plan expectations to include the parent binds.
- `pnpm vitest run src/agents/sandbox/`: 56 files, 698 passed, 3 skipped.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` passes; oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the changed files.

prs.title: fix(ios): parallel tool calls show no result after their outputs arrive
prs.body:
Closes #171975

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes parallel tool calls showing “No result” in iOS chat when their outputs arrive together in one message.

## User Impact

Each tool output appears under its originating call, without creating an extra user turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

Split result carriers before assigning turn ownership, while preserving genuine user text, canonical transcript ancestry, and turn boundaries.

## Evidence

[Failing/passing Swift checks and native simulator proof](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/915592231cec8339b68e5bfdecf75c1a360c9675/test-output.md). Both outputs are visible after expanding the completed work.

[Rebased native v2026.10.3 persisted-state upgrade proof](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/cbdace227f07e74aed8318598175387c01f2723e/upgrade-proof.md): cached content, two queued messages with attachments and settings, canonical carrier IDs, and branch ancestry survive the in-place upgrade. Strict-decoder red control fails as expected; all 16 focused ingestion tests pass.

[Native latest-stable v2026.10.6 persisted-state upgrade proof](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/618a11fb0d0896c80edb585efe6ed147eb0de59a/upgrade-v2026.10.6.md): existing cache rows, two queued messages, attachments, settings, and canonical branch ancestry all load and survive the in-place upgrade. Both v2026.10.3 and v2026.10.6 upgrades pass.

**Stored-data compatibility:** the carrier-ID field decodes as absent (nil) from pre-change data via decodeIfPresent. The native v2026.10.6 upgrade asserts this directly. The [legacy-decode regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d62dfc6241cd410c9997a4451a616f31f48eafd6/apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Tests/OpenClawKitTests/ChatToolResultIngestionTests.swift#L43) from the verified r5 run fails under strict decoding and passes with the tolerant decoder; all 16 ingestion tests pass.

![Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/915592231cec8339b68e5bfdecf75c1a360c9675/before.png)
![After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/915592231cec8339b68e5bfdecf75c1a360c9675/after-expanded.png)

prs.title: fix(node-host): resume Windows sessions after a node crash
prs.body:
Related: #171867, #168863

## What Problem This Solves

A Windows node host killed during a tool call can leave its launch marked running after restart, reserving capacity and preventing the interrupted session from continuing.

## User Impact

Updated Windows node hosts recover launches recorded under kill-on-close Job custody after the recorded supervisor and worker are verifiably gone, then release the slot so the session can continue. Update and restart the node host to receive this behavior. Older receipts retain conservative recovery.

Recovery checks the recorded PID and process creation time, then allows one second for remaining Job members to terminate. A descendant that broke away from the Job or is unusually slow to die could briefly overlap the next turn; this is an accepted recovery tradeoff.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native launcher exposes established kill-on-close custody, recorded through the existing cleanup mode and Windows boot identity. Recovery reuses the existing identity-wait loop and stop grace, retains the exact launch-owner checks, and joins the existing background recovery observation. It does not infer extinction from a missing Job name.

No schema, migration, protocol, dependency, or configuration changes. The complete change is +68/-32 = **+36 production TypeScript lines**, across 9 files; the growth supplies custody recording and bounded recovery while sharing the existing process wait.

## Evidence

- The owner regression fails on the previous implementation in both dead/reused-PID cases with `released a live Windows worker`.
- Owner startup suite: 15 passed, including both grace regressions and legacy Windows receipts. `pnpm test src/node-host/node-worker-supervisor.startup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 251.89 s wall (55.25 s Vitest including transform/import; new cases 578/568 ms).
- Launch store: 32 passed, including unchanged legacy schema and exact process ownership. `pnpm test src/node-host/node-worker-launch-store.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 182.06 s wall (64.97 s Vitest). Cold worker compilation and module loading dominate command time; the durable journal boundary is intentional.
- Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent Codex review accepted the corrected working tree; its pre-fix index finding is resolved in the committed version.
- Linux runtime build passed in 112.6 s. Live proof used a native Windows node and an isolated Linux Gateway connected through SSH tunnels, with a single advertised worker slot and Gateway-only inference.

| Native Windows fault | Automatic continuation after kill | Restart invocation | Effect count | Old worker/write overlap |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Host killed mid-tool | 20.577 s | After old worker exit | 1 | None |
| Immediate host restart | 20.486 s | Same millisecond as kill; 4 ms before old worker exit | 1 | None |

Both variants retain native process handles and match the recorded PID plus creation time, then compare actual worker/writer exit times and the last old write against the continuation write. The resumed model executes verification in a separate automatic recovery run, without an operator follow-up. After reclaim, both have zero nonterminal launches and advertise total=available=1.

The effect fixture appends unconditionally, so an observed replay would duplicate the record. These trials demonstrate one effect and no overlap for the exercised crashes; they do not provide a universal exactly-once guarantee for arbitrary external tools. The accepted breakaway/slow-descendant edge remains as documented above.
## CI attribution and landing

Exact-head CI [40056830376](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40056830376) failed four existing cases; security-fast passed. The changed-shard names differ from scheduled main, so the automated report labels them unknown. Independent baseline evidence establishes the failures:

- Schema inlining: the same `test/scripts/tsdown-runtime-config.test.ts` failure appears in scheduled main [40054969997, job 120755951386](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40054969997/job/120755951386).
- Hooks CLI stderr: reproduced on main `9cf739b6` in 43.047 s; expected line breaks, received literal `\n` text and an error prefix.
- Telegram model-picker recovery: reproduced on that main in 100.971 s; the same callback record has attempts 1 instead of 0.
- Subagent timeout recovery: reproduced on that main in 171.684 s; child completion is terminal/ok but delivery remains pending and not leasable until the test times out.

The three focused main tests use the default Bun runtime and synthetic providers, with the same test-source hashes as the CI merge checkout. Each actual case ran once. The initial hooks title filter selected no tests and is excluded from the verdict. No assertion, timeout, baseline, or production behavior was changed to address these unrelated failures. Landing uses the authorized inherited-failure exception; CI remains recorded as failed.

prs.title: fix(plugins): surface dropped prompt-build context
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugins use `before_prompt_build` to add context that can determine what an agent does next. When that context is dropped, the resulting prompt looks exactly like the plugin had nothing to report. A task or memory plugin can therefore fail while the agent incorrectly concludes that its queue or context is empty.

The silent-loss paths include a handler failure or timeout, a nested prompt build that is prevented from recursively dispatching hooks, a dispatch rejection, and a failure in the later tool-authorized enrichment phase.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime now appends one bounded `<dropped_plugin_context>` marker when a contribution is lost. It identifies the affected plugin and one fixed reason code: `handler-failed`, `nested-prompt-build`, or `dispatch-failed`.

The implementation deliberately preserves existing policy:

- prompt-build hooks remain fail-open;
- surviving plugin contributions still reach the prompt;
- error details remain in operator logs and never enter model context;
- authority-only handlers are reported only by the authorized phase that can actually run them;
- exact raw plugin identities are counted before labels are sanitized and truncated, so display collisions cannot understate the number of losses;
- the marker lists at most five entries and is capped at 640 bytes, with `+N more` accounting for every omitted contribution.

Pre-dispatch preparation failures remain marker-free because no plugin contribution was dispatched or dropped.

## User Impact

Agents can distinguish “the plugin had nothing to add” from “the runtime lost the plugin’s context.” That prevents false empty-queue conclusions and gives the agent a safe recovery instruction without exposing exception text, credentials, endpoints, or plugin-authored prompt injection.

No configuration or public plugin SDK change is introduced.

## Evidence

Current topic head: `2fb1637ed675e9615d92730f9d83087aa58a9485`.

- The complete changed-file gate, config-schema check, Plugin SDK surface check, and unused-file scan passed on that refreshed candidate.
- Focused validation passed 223 tests across four repository-runner shards (12 + 17 + 172 + 22). These are the saved refresh results, not a claim of a new run caused by this description update.
- `scripts/proof-prompt-build-drop-marker.ts` passes all 55 runtime assertions on the current head (`EXIT 0`). Its CLI scenarios now run inside `withTestRunAdmission`, so the CLI preparation path's own live-authority assertions execute for real rather than being bypassed by a no-audit fixture carrier. It exercises the real hook runner and production embedded, agent-harness, and CLI prompt-consumer functions: healthy contributions, failures/timeouts, nested builds, dispatch rejection, redaction, bounds, hostile identities, and pre-dispatch negative controls.
- Review regressions cover sanitized-label collisions, authority-only nested hooks, and failed authorized enrichment.
- `scripts/proof-118555-installed-plugin-provider-request.ts` passes all 26 runtime assertions on the current head (`EXIT 0`, four consecutive runs). It closes the installed-plugin and provider-edge gap described below: the fixture plugins are installed through `installPluginFromPath` (the entry `openclaw plugins install <dir>` uses), loaded by the real `loadOpenClawPlugins` through the loader's real conversation-hook consent gate, and the assertions are made on the **stdin of a real spawned provider process**, not on a returned value.

### Installed-plugin proof at the outgoing provider request

The earlier proof boundary — constructed registrations and a returned prompt value — is now closed by a second harness, `scripts/proof-118555-installed-plugin-provider-request.ts`.

**What is real.** Each fixture plugin is packaged on disk and installed through `installPluginFromPath` (`src/plugins/install.ts`), the same programmatic entry `openclaw plugins install <dir>` uses; the install really validates the package, and the run asserts a committed artifact exists before proceeding. The plugins are then discovered and registered by the real `loadOpenClawPlugins`. The loader's own consent gate applies unchanged: `before_prompt_build` is a conversation hook, so a non-bundled plugin does **not** register without `plugins.entries.<id>.hooks.allowConversationAccess`. The harness sets that key in its own isolated config the way an operator would, rather than bypassing the gate.

**Where the request is observed.** One installed fixture registers a CLI backend via `api.registerCliBackend` whose `command` is a small recorder process. `runCliAgent` then runs end to end, and `resolvePromptInput` (`src/agents/cli-runner/helpers.ts`) routes the assembled prompt to that process's stdin under `input: "stdin"`. The runtime performs a real spawn, so the recorder's stdin is literally the request that left the process. Substituting the provider binary is the stub at the very edge; every step between the installed plugin's handler and that spawn is production code.

**Isolation.** `OPENCLAW_HOME` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` are redirected to a fresh temporary tree before any OpenClaw module is imported, which is why every import in the harness is dynamic. Installs, state, and sessions land in that tree, a configured install is never read or written, and the tree is removed on exit.

**Scenarios and results** (26 assertions, `EXIT 0`):

1. **Healthy-only turn** — the installed plugin's block and the user's ask are both in the outgoing provider request, and there is **no** loss notice. This is the negative control the review asked for by name.
2. **Installed healthy/throwing pair** — the throwing plugin raises an error carrying credential-shaped text. The outgoing provider request retains the healthy plugin's content, carries **exactly one** notice (384 bytes, within the 640-byte cap) naming `proof-throwing (handler-failed)`, contains **no** exception text, does not contain the dropped plugin's own block, and does not blame the healthy plugin.
3. **Bounded under load** — one healthy plus seven throwing installed plugins: still exactly one notice, five plugins named, `+2 more`, 515 bytes, healthy content retained, no exception text.

The outgoing provider request captured verbatim in scenario 2:

```
<plans_and_tasks><ready_issues><issue id='openclaw-beads-201'/></ready_issues></plans_and_tasks>

latest ask

<dropped_plugin_context hook="before_prompt_build">
The runtime dropped this turn's before_prompt_build contribution from proof-throwing (handler-failed).
That context is MISSING from this prompt, not empty — do not read its absence as "nothing to report" (for example, an empty task or work queue). Re-read anything you need from its source before acting.
</dropped_plugin_context>
```

**The proof can fail.** Run unchanged against pristine `origin/main` (`38c3edcc4caf692bbb9ff0078bda002587528036`, which has no `src/plugins/prompt-build-drop.ts`), the harness completes scenario 1 green — including `healthy: content is RETAINED`, so the fix is shown not to alter healthy behavior — and then fails at `pair: outgoing provider request carries EXACTLY ONE loss notice`, `EXIT 1` after 9 checks. That failure is the silent drop this PR fixes, observed at the provider boundary.

### Line-cap ratchet: coherent extraction (September 18, 2026)

The previous head grew three already-over-cap files, and `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` rejects *growth against a grandfathered baseline*, not absolute size. Three cohesive extractions erase that growth without touching behavior or coverage:

- `src/plugins/hooks-prompt-build.ts` — both `before_prompt_build` dispatch phases (ordinary and tool-authorized), the `AsyncLocalStorage` nesting token, and the loss collection they share. The hook runner injects its merger, its registration list, and its modifying-hook dispatcher, so the new module never imports back into `hooks.ts` and `check-import-cycles` still reports 0 runtime value cycles.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/hook-prompt-build.ts` — the CLI's two prompt-build hook resolutions, including this PR's deliberate asymmetry: preparation failures stay marker-free, dispatch failures become the bounded marker.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.prompt-build-drop.test.ts` — the five CLI drop-marker tests, moved verbatim beside the existing `prepare.context-window` / `durable-context` / `model-routing-authority` / `rooted-execution` siblings. No assertion was weakened or deleted.

Counted lines (oxlint `max-lines` with `skipBlankLines`/`skipComments`, the measurement the gate itself uses) against the baseline each file is ratcheted to:

| File | Before | After | Baseline |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts` | 6872 | **6721** | 6736 |
| `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts` | 2361 | **2325** | 2353 |
| `src/plugins/hooks.ts` | 1397 | **1289** | 1364 |

Neither new module nor the new test file reports a `max-lines` diagnostic. CI confirms it: `Line-cap ratchet OK: 19 changed source files; no new violations or over-cap growth.`

**Behavior and coverage preserved, measured rather than asserted.** The *unmodified* `prepare.test.ts` from the previous head passes **191/191** against the extracted production code; the reduced file passes **186/186** and the five moved tests pass **5/5** in their new home (186 + 5 = 191). Both proof harnesses still pass on the new head — `proof-prompt-build-drop-marker.ts` 55/55 and `proof-118555-installed-plugin-provider-request.ts` 26/26, both `EXIT 0`. `pnpm check:changed` is `EXIT 0` across every lane, including the core/extensions/scripts oxlint shards and the Knip dead-export and unused-file scans.

The earlier partial-gate failure and old-head evidence are superseded by the successful refresh checks above. No unrelated CI failure is being claimed as fixed by this PR.

prs.title: feat(gateway): allow a custom tailnet port for managed Tailscale ingress
prs.body:
Related: #125369

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**Allow edits from maintainers** is enabled on this PR.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

**Updated 26 Aug:** the original problem statement is out of date, and I want to correct it rather than leave it standing.

When I opened this, managed Serve was the only way to get trusted ingress, and an external route was rejected before `gateway.trustedProxies` was consulted. #125412 changed that two hours after this PR was filed: the Tailscale-header check now runs *after* the trusted-proxy branch, so an external `tailscale serve` plus a narrow `trustedProxies` is attributed and works. That was the stronger half of my case and it is gone. The startup failure I hit — `sending serve config: updating config: listener already exists for port 443` on a host where nginx owns `0.0.0.0:443` — has a supported answer today.

What remains is narrower, and it is about ownership rather than reachability.

Managed ingress holds the route as a foreground claim: the Gateway creates it, watches it, and releases it when it exits. An externally managed route has no owner. If the Gateway dies, the route stays.

That is not hypothetical for me. In August a `tailscale serve` on 443 outlived the process that created it and kept nginx from binding for three days, because nothing owned it and nothing released it. Managed ingress is precisely what prevents that.

So the remaining question is narrow: today, changing the tailnet port means giving up managed ingress — and its lifecycle guarantee — for a reason that has nothing to do with lifecycle. This PR lets an operator keep the managed claim and move it off 443.

I have no strong view on whether that is worth a permanent config key; that is a maintainer call, and I understand if the answer is no. I would rather the record be accurate than the PR survive.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `gateway.tailscale.port`, defaulting to 443, threaded through to `claimTailscaleRoute` as `--https=<port>`. Keeping the route *managed* is the point: it preserves identity-header attribution, which is exactly what the manual-Serve workaround loses.

Design decisions:

- **The flag is omitted for the default port**, so the emitted `tailscale serve`/`funnel` command is byte-identical to today for anyone who does not set the key.
- **A non-default port stays in every published origin and log line** (`https://<magicdns>:8443/`, `wss://<magicdns>:8443`). Clients dial the tailnet route directly, so dropping it would advertise an unreachable URL.
- **Funnel ports are validated at config time.** Serve accepts any port; Funnel accepts only 443, 8443, and 10000, so a bad value is rejected with a clear message instead of failing inside the CLI at startup.
- **One helper owns the published authority.** `formatTailscaleAuthority()` in the new dependency-free `src/shared/tailscale-ports.ts` is the single place that decides whether the port appears, and the managed route, pairing/QR setup, and status output all go through it. That file stays free of runtime imports so the config schema can use the port constants without pulling in the process-spawning Tailscale helpers.
- **Pairing fails loudly when the tailnet host is unresolvable.** That path previously interpolated a possibly-`null` host straight into the URL, producing `wss://null`; it now returns an explicit error.

Non-goals: no auto-detection of port conflicts and no auto-selection of a free port — silently changing a URL operators have to type is worse than failing loudly. No change to trusted-proxy or attribution semantics.

## User Impact

Operators whose Gateway host already uses 443 can now run managed Tailscale ingress on another port:

```json5
{
  gateway: {
    bind: "loopback",
    tailscale: { mode: "serve", port: 8443 },
  },
}
```

The dashboard is then at `https://<magicdns>:8443/`, identity-header auth keeps working, and the reverse proxy keeps 443. Misconfigured Funnel ports now fail config validation with an explicit message instead of a CLI error during startup.

No behavior change for existing installs: the key is optional and the default is the current behavior.

## Evidence

### Live run on a host where nginx owns 443

OpenClaw 2026.8.1, Ubuntu 24.04, Tailscale Serve, reverse proxy bound to `0.0.0.0:443`. Hostnames are this tailnet's real MagicDNS names; secrets are redacted.

**Before**, with `gateway.tailscale.mode: "serve"` and no port setting, startup died:

```
reason:         gateway.startup_failed
error.message:  sending serve config: updating config: listener already exists for port 443
```

**After**, with `tailscale: { mode: "serve", port: 8443 }`, the managed route comes up and the Gateway reports ready:

```
[tailscale] serve enabled: https://ingil.tail37360.ts.net:8443/ (WS via wss://ingil.tail37360.ts.net:8443)
[gateway] ready
```

Listener layout — the managed route and the reverse proxy coexist, and the Gateway itself stays on loopback:

```
LISTEN  127.0.0.1:18789          # gateway, bind=loopback
LISTEN  100.99.141.60:8443       # managed Serve route (tailnet IP)
LISTEN  0.0.0.0:443              # nginx, untouched
```

Authenticated client flow over the non-default route:

```
$ curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://ingil.tail37360.ts.net:8443/
200
```

On 17 Aug, before #125412 landed, the same request returned 403, with the Gateway logging
`observed unattributable proxy-shaped traffic from 127.0.0.1` on every attempt; that log line has not reappeared since the managed route took over. A real Android device then completed pairing against this endpoint and is connected.

### Endpoint publication (the P1 raised in review)

The first push threaded the port only into the managed claim, so pairing and status still advertised 443. Fixed in `d2ef555bb65`, verified by running the two commands that were wrong, with no override:

```
$ openclaw qr --json
  gatewayUrl: wss://ingil.tail37360.ts.net:8443
  urlSource:  gateway.tailscale.mode=serve

$ openclaw status
  Tailscale exposure   serve · ingil.tail37360.ts.net · https://ingil.tail37360.ts.net:8443
```

Both previously emitted the bare host. The QR produced by that command was decoded back to confirm the payload carries `url: wss://ingil.tail37360.ts.net:8443`, and the device paired from it.

### Tests

`136 passed` across the five affected suites:

```
$ npx vitest run src/pairing/setup-code.test.ts src/commands/status.scan.shared.test.ts \
    src/gateway/server-tailscale.test.ts src/config/config.gateway-tailscale-bind.test.ts \
    src/infra/tailscale.test.ts

 Test Files  5 passed (5)
      Tests  136 passed (136)
```

New coverage:

- `infra/tailscale.test.ts` — `--https=8443` is emitted for a non-default port and omitted for the default. The foreground fixture exits non-zero on unexpected argv, so the emitted command is genuinely asserted rather than mocked.
- `server-tailscale.test.ts` — the configured port reaches `claimTailscaleRoute` and is retained in the published MCP app-channel origin and the `wss://` log line.
- `setup-code.test.ts` — a configured port lands in the pairing URL (`wss://mb-server.tailnet.ts.net:8443`).
- `status.scan.shared.test.ts` — a non-default port appears in the Control UI URL; the default stays implicit.
- `config.gateway-tailscale-bind.test.ts` — Serve accepts arbitrary ports; Funnel accepts 443/8443/10000 and rejects 9443; out-of-range values are rejected.

### Repo checks

`pnpm build` and `pnpm check` pass, along with `pnpm check:base-config-schema` (still `ok` after registering the new key in the help and label maps) and `pnpm format:docs`.

`pnpm test` has failures on this machine that predate the branch — TUI PTY e2e, markdown file-link wrapping, UI radius/icon tokens, browser launch, OAuth callback, macOS CA trust, IPv6 dial. None touch Tailscale, gateway config, or ingress attribution. Verified by running the same suite on the base commit `793669c8f6d` with and without the branch:

```
this branch:          Test Files  3 failed (3)   Tests  3 failed | 27 passed (30)
793669c8f6d (base):   Test Files  3 failed (3)   Tests  3 failed | 27 passed (30)
```

Identical either way, so I have left them alone per CONTRIBUTING's guidance on known `main` failures.
