prs.title: fix(channels): add opt-in multi-bot storm protection
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The existing loop guard budgets each unordered bot pair independently. In a conversation with three or more bots, traffic can rotate across pairs so no pair reaches its limit even while the conversation runs away.

This happened in a production Slack deployment: four OpenClaw agents in one thread replied at roughly 15-second intervals for hours. Six independent pair buckets each stayed below the existing 20-events-per-minute limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an **explicitly opt-in** conversation-wide burst budget to the existing shared guard:

- `maxConversationBotEvents` enables a 10-minute rolling budget for one conversation and receiving bot.
- Suppression requires at least two peer bots to be actively posting, so ordinary two-bot relays and one-off integration messages remain governed by the pair budget.
- Provider replays are deduplicated by stable Discord, Matrix, Slack, Feishu, and Google Chat event identities in both the pair and bounded conversation buckets before either budget mutates.
- Native conversation boundaries are preserved, including separate Slack threads.
- The accepted limit is bounded to 1–500, with fixed memory retention.
- Existing configurations that omit the new field remain pair-only.

The feature stays at the existing pre-record/pre-dispatch enforcement boundary, so supported channels share one policy and one suppression result.

## User Impact

Operators with multi-agent channels can opt into protection against N-party reply storms without changing existing pair-loop behavior. A sustained storm is dropped before session recording or model dispatch, preventing channel flooding and unnecessary model spend.

The new setting is available through shared defaults and channel/account/room overrides where supported. Documentation now covers Buzz, ClickClack, Discord, Feishu, Google Chat, Matrix, and Slack.

## Evidence

### After-fix production turn-kernel proof

The proof drives the real `runPreparedChannelTurn` boundary with redacted mock-channel facts:

```json
{
  "optInBurst": {
    "verdicts": ["dispatch", "dispatch", "dispatch", "drop:bot-loop-protection"],
    "dispatchCount": 3,
    "skipped": ["botLoopProtection"]
  },
  "existingPairOnlyConfig": {
    "verdicts": ["dispatch", "dispatch", "dispatch", "dispatch"],
    "dispatchCount": 4,
    "skipped": []
  }
}
```

This demonstrates both required outcomes: the opted-in multi-bot burst is suppressed before dispatch, while the same traffic under an existing pair-only configuration is unaffected.

### Replay boundary proof

The adapter tests now forward each transport's stable replay identity and exercise the actual Discord preflight boundary. Replaying the same Discord message ID leaves the conversation budget unchanged; only the fifth unique event triggers suppression. Focused guard regressions also cover the harder cases: a retry of an event first suppressed by the pair guard does not consume another conversation slot, and replay identity cannot bypass an already-active conversation cooldown.

### September 8 adapter-retry repair

Feishu and Google Chat now forward their existing message IDs into the same shared guard. The new regression targets retries after an earlier processing failure, not only ordinary webhook deduplication: an event that reached admission once must not consume another conversation-budget slot on retry.

`scripts/proof-117734-conversation-burst-replay.ts` exercises real Feishu ingress and Google Chat's durable SQLite ingress queue with **20 passing assertions**. Four unique bot events remain admitted despite retry; the fifth unique event is suppressed. Without the new setting, pair-only behavior remains unchanged. The proof simulates the downstream turn runner; provider JWT verification and actual outbound channel delivery are outside its scope.

The changed Feishu/Google Chat suites pass **136 tests**. The replay proof typechecks, and the reconciled scoped review has no P0/P1 findings. The generated config baseline records the existing opt-in setting (+18 entries) following explicit operator approval; this does not substitute for upstream maintainer approval of a new shared setting.

Exact published head and completed gate/supplement results are recorded in the publication update below. Earlier review-round results remain historical evidence rather than current-head claims.

### Published refresh — September 8, 2026

Signed, GitHub-verified head at that refresh: [`4834367ab5e9`](https://github.com/zeroaltitude/openclaw/commit/4834367ab5e9cfb3239241fcf38ae52b7599641b). Superseded by the September 9 round below.

- The refreshed candidate's local validation gate, schema consistency, SDK surface check, and full-tree unused-file scan pass.
- Topic proofs and test counts above describe their stated boundaries; the fresh scoped review is clean at P0/P1.
- Final deployment integration is being validated separately. This does not claim the combined tree is deployed or that a hosted-provider/channel restart test has passed.
- The relocated Google Chat replay regression retains all 33 Google Chat assertions; together with Feishu, the adapter total remains 136.

### Slack channel isolation + ephemeral-Gateway proof — September 9, 2026

Prior round head, signed and GitHub-verified: [`8aa2154cc09a`](https://github.com/zeroaltitude/openclaw/commit/8aa2154cc09a836025ba54c045d64c36ba052b27). Superseded by the round below; this section's claims describe that head.

**Fix.** `resolveSlackBotLoopProtection` now keys the conversation identity on `` `${channel}:${thread_ts}` `` when a thread timestamp exists, falling back to the bare channel for top-level messages. Slack guarantees timestamp uniqueness only within a channel, so the previous bare `thread_ts` key merged distinct channels whenever their thread timestamps collided under the same account and receiving bot, sharing one burst budget and one pair cooldown. The new shape matches `buildSlackDebounceKey`'s thread branch, the in-repo precedent; that helper is now the only other Slack key of this kind, and no remaining call site keys on a bare `thread_ts`.

**New proof: real transport, real Gateway, real guard singleton.** `scripts/proof-117734-slack-gateway-isolation.ts` spawns an OpenClaw Gateway with its own state dir, config and loopback port, then posts signed Slack event envelopes over HTTP to the Gateway's real Slack webhook route. Real on the path: the plugin HTTP route, Bolt's `HTTPReceiver` signature verification, the Slack event and message handlers, `dispatchChannelInboundTurn`, core's `runPreparedChannelTurn`, and the process-wide `channelBotPairLoopGuard` singleton — not a fresh `createPairLoopGuard()`. Only two edges are stubbed, both on loopback HTTP: the Slack Web API through the production `SLACK_API_URL` seam, and an OpenAI-completions model endpoint. Admission is read from the model endpoint, because the guard drops a suppressed event before any agent dispatch; the harness asserts the slowest measured admission is at least 4x inside the suppression deadline in the same run, so a broken pipeline cannot read as suppression.

`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/proof-117734-slack-gateway-isolation.ts` — **18/18 assertions pass**:

```
pair-budget-only (maxConversationBotEvents ABSENT, maxEventsPerWindow 2)
  C_FIRST/pa1=admitted  C_FIRST/pa2=admitted  C_FIRST/pa3=suppressed  C_SECOND/pa4=admitted
conversation-burst-budget (maxConversationBotEvents 3, maxEventsPerWindow 100)
  C_FIRST/cb1=admitted  C_FIRST/cb2=admitted  C_FIRST/cb3=admitted
  C_FIRST/cb4=suppressed  C_SECOND/cb5=admitted  C_SECOND/cb6=admitted
```

`pa4`, `cb5` and `cb6` differ from the suppressed events only by channel: same account, same peer bot, same receiving bot, same `thread_ts`. Admitted latencies were 306-1112 ms against a 20 s deadline. Controls in the same harness: a bad-signature event is rejected `401` at the real HTTP boundary and never reaches an agent turn, and `auth.test` is observed against the loopback Web API before any scenario runs.

**Ablation.** With the single production expression reverted to the pre-fix `thread_ts ?? channel` and `dist` rebuilt, the same harness fails at exactly that point — `C_SECOND pa4` observed suppressed, `model requests: 2`, second channel never dispatched. The unit suite behaves the same way: 7/7 with the fix, 4 failed / 3 passed reverted. The three that still pass reverted are the pair-only compatibility control, the channel-fallback branch and the `eventId` assertion, none of which can be sensitive to the key shape.

**What this proof does not establish.** It never contacts Slack's servers, so it makes no claim about real signing secrets, Socket Mode, rate limits or delivery semantics; the Slack Web API and the model are loopback stubs. It covers Slack only. It does not exercise multi-account or Enterprise Grid installations, and it does not claim any combined integration tree is deployed.

**Gate on this head**, against `origin/main` `7e701b1208e`, every step with a terminal exit marker: `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, `tsgo:scripts`, `tsgo:test:root`, `config:schema:check`, `plugin-sdk:surface:check`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, `git diff --check` (worktree and range), `deadcode:unused-files` with both Knip scans at 0 entries, `deadcode:exports`, `build`, and a cold-cache repeat of all six `tsgo` lanes. Focused suites: slack bot-loop 7/7, slack debounce-key 7/7, `pair-loop-guard-runtime` 28/28, `run-channel-turn.finalize` 20/20, slack provider transport credentials 4/4. Both proof harnesses pass. `check:changed`'s one failing lane, `plugin boundaries`, is inherited: a pristine `origin/main` worktree and the branch tree both exit 1 with normalized captures that are byte-identical, md5 `72b2184817e68494943215b5935f016c`.

**Open, and maintainer-owned.** Upstream acceptance of the shared config and public SDK addition; the granularity question below; and the reported merge conflict (`mergeable=false`, `mergeable_state=dirty`, confirmed on two polls) which needs a rebase this round did not perform. On granularity: `main` keys Slack on the bare channel, this PR keys on the thread, and this round makes that thread key channel-qualified. Cross-channel bleed is therefore gone, but a deployment that sets nothing still moves from one channel-wide pair budget to one per thread. If strict pre-change behavior is wanted when `maxConversationBotEvents` is absent, gating the thread scoping on the setting is a small change and can be re-proved through the same harness.

### Cooldown deadline correctness — September 9, 2026 (round N+1)

Prior round head, signed and GitHub-verified: [`4d0ed5e42e1a`](https://github.com/zeroaltitude/openclaw/commit/4d0ed5e42e1a0423c29a40bf49f10dac72d1a472). Superseded by the round below; this section's claims describe that head. That round addressed one finding only, the `[P2]`.

**Fix — `[P2] Return the latest active cooldown deadline`** (`src/plugin-sdk/pair-loop-guard-runtime.ts:408-410`). An event can sit inside the pair cooldown and the conversation burst cooldown at the same time. `recordAndCheck` returned the pair deadline unconditionally and discarded `burstResult`, so callers were told suppression ends earlier than it actually does. A new `latestActiveCooldown()` merges the two verdicts and reports the later deadline whenever both suppress. It is applied at both sites in `recordAndCheck` that report a pair cooldown: the already-active branch the review cited, and the trip-now branch, where a config reload can shorten `cooldownSeconds` underneath a longer conversation cooldown that is still running. The replay path and the clean path already returned `burstResult` and are unchanged.

**Why the value matters.** Both consumers of `cooldownUntilMs` render it as remaining suppression time — Discord's preflight verbose log and ClickClack's inbound warn each compute `ceil((cooldownUntilMs - Date.now()) / 1000)`. An understated deadline tells an operator the storm has cleared while the guard is still suppressing.

**Red before green, on the review's exact scenario.** Pair limit 1, conversation limit 4, 5,000 ms cooldown, unique events A1/A2/B1/B2/A3 at 0/1/2/3/4 ms. A3 trips the conversation budget at t=4 (deadline 5,004) while bot-a's pair cooldown from t=1 is still active (deadline 5,001). Before the fix the new coverage failed with exactly the reported number:

```
AssertionError: expected { suppressed: true, …(1) } to deeply equal { suppressed: true, …(1) }
-   "cooldownUntilMs": 5004      (expected)
+   "cooldownUntilMs": 5001      (received)
```

**Coverage.** `src/plugin-sdk/pair-loop-guard-runtime.test.ts` gains the scenario above plus the config-reload case for the trip-now site. A new `src/channels/turn/bot-loop-protection.test.ts` runs the same scenario through `recordChannelBotPairLoopAndCheckSuppression` — the real process-wide `channelBotPairLoopGuard` singleton that channel adapters actually share, and the real `windowSeconds`/`cooldownSeconds` config resolution — rather than a locally constructed `createPairLoopGuard()`.

**Discrimination is per changed line**, measured by reverting in a scratch copy and restoring to a verified checksum:

| Production state | `pair-loop-guard-runtime` | `bot-loop-protection` |
|---|---|---|
| fix present | 30 passed (30) | 1 passed (1) |
| both sites reverted | **2 failed** / 28 passed | **1 failed** (1) |
| already-active site reverted alone | **1 failed** / 29 passed | **1 failed** (1) |
| trip-now site reverted alone | **1 failed** / 29 passed | 1 passed (1) |

Neither changed line is redundant. The trip-now row is also the honest limit of the shared-guard test: it exercises the already-active site only, so it passes when the trip-now site alone is reverted, and it is not claimed as coverage of that line.

**Honest proof limit.** The ephemeral-Gateway harness cannot observe this fix, because Slack never reads `cooldownUntilMs` — it consumes only `suppressed`. The harness was still run on this head against a rebuilt `dist` and passes 18/18, which establishes the change is non-regressive at the real signed-HTTP ingress boundary, not that it proves the deadline. The deadline value is proven at the shared-guard entry point above; a live Discord or ClickClack log capture is not part of this round.

**Gate on this head**, against `origin/main` `7e701b1208e`: **53 lanes with terminal exit markers, 50 EXIT 0.** All seven `tsgo` lanes warm *and* cold (`.artifacts/tsgo-cache` moved aside), `config:schema:check`, `plugin-sdk:surface:check`, `oxlint` (plain and the `--tsconfig` form), `oxfmt --check`, `git diff --check`, `deadcode:unused-files` with both Knip scans at 0 entries, `deadcode:exports`, `build`, and all 20 `check:changed` lanes recovered via `--dry-run` and run individually. Nine focused suites, each its own invocation, counts predicted before running and reconciled after: 30, 1, 3, 20, 7, 100, 1, 32, 103 — every delta from the raw `it(` count is `it.each` table expansion. Both `proof-117734` harnesses EXIT 0. The committed tree `cafb1114aeb3` is the gated tree, and the push was fast-forward and non-force (`8aa2154cc09..4d0ed5e42e1`).

**The one failing lane is inherited, re-demonstrated this round.** `plugin boundaries` exits 1 on a pristine `origin/main` worktree at `7e701b1208e` and on this tree, with normalized 14-line captures that are byte-identical, md5 `72b2184817e68494943215b5935f016c` (`eligibleForRemoval=1`, `plugin-sdk-media-understanding-public-demotion`, window 2026-09-30). The throwaway worktree was removed.

**Not addressed in this round, deliberately: `[P1] Preserve Slack's pair budget when burst protection is unset`.** That is a product decision about default scope — whether a deployment that sets no burst config keeps channel-wide pair accounting — and it is left to a maintainer rather than self-decided. The concrete alternative remains the one named in the previous round and recommended by the review: gate the thread scoping on the effective burst setting, including shared-default and channel overrides, and cover the cross-thread upgrade case. It is a small change to one expression and is re-provable through the existing Gateway harness.

### Slack pair budget preserved when the burst budget is unset — September 9, 2026 (round 27)

Current signed, GitHub-verified head: [`efaa6ee7074`](https://github.com/zeroaltitude/openclaw/commit/efaa6ee7074571055ad9257c2c6281e3048c0089). This round addresses the one remaining actionable finding, the `[P1]`.

**Fix — `[P1] Preserve Slack's pair budget when burst protection is unset`** (`extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/dispatch-helpers.ts:40-42`). The branch replaced Slack's bare-channel bot-loop conversation key with a channel-qualified thread key *unconditionally*, and the guard's config is resolved separately and afterwards, so an installation that never set `maxConversationBotEvents` still got the narrower key — silently splitting one channel's pair budget across its threads. Thread scoping now rides the opt-in conversation burst budget: with the budget absent, Slack keeps the shipped channel-wide key, so the upgrade is behavior-preserving.

**The setting is resolved as the guard resolves it, not as a field-presence test.** The gate calls `resolvePairLoopGuardSettings({ config, defaultsConfig, defaultEnabled: true })` — the same runtime resolver the guard itself uses — and asks whether the *effective* `maxConversationBotEvents` is defined. A bare `!== undefined` on the configured field would have been wrong in both directions: it would miss an opt-in that arrives through `channels.defaults`, and it would treat out-of-range values the guard rejects (`0`, `501`) as opt-ins. Shared defaults, account settings and channel overrides are therefore read exactly as the guard will read them.

**Red before green, on the review's own numbers.** `dispatch-helpers.bot-loop.test.ts` fails **11 failed / 24 passed (35)** against the pre-fix production file and passes **35 passed (35)** after — the same file, the same 35 cases, only the production expression changed. | `cross-thread-upgrade-compatibility` | absent | `xu1` admitted | `xu2` admitted | **`xu3` suppressed** | — |
| `cross-thread-opt-in-scope` | `maxConversationBotEvents: 50` | `xo1` admitted | `xo2` admitted | `xo3` admitted | **`xo4` suppressed** |

The first row is the behavior the review said must be preserved: with nothing configured, the third message in a *different* thread still exhausts the one channel-wide pair budget. The second row shows the opt-in budget is genuinely per-thread and still enforced inside the thread, not merely wider. `All 31 runtime assertions passed.`

prs.title: fix(update): restore direct updates from extended-stable 2026.9.33
prs.body:
## Blocked Before Landing

The required published-driver matrix is incomplete. The exact candidate built and the published 2026.9.33 updater completed successfully (exit 0, `status: ok`, 352.78 s), including the real Doctor migration. Afterward, Gateway startup failed because the installed `@opentelemetry/api` directory was empty.

A separate plain-install reproduction now identifies a bundled-peer trigger in npm 11.19.1: a bundled package declaring `@opentelemetry/api` as a peer, alongside `@anthropic-ai/sdk` 0.135.0 requiring that dependency, produces an empty API directory while npm exits 0. Both optional and required peer variants fail; deleting the bundled peer edge passes with the same SDK/API/npm versions and makes the SDK tracing import succeed. The private bundled `@openclaw/ai` manifest retains that peer metadata after its dependency list is removed. This reproduction uses no OpenClaw updater, so the trigger is independent of the installed 2026.9.33 driver.

The approved separate packaging repair is #182168: remove the `@opentelemetry/api` peer declaration and its optional peer marker from the privately bundled AI copy while preserving the standalone AI manifest and every dependency version, with package and installed-tree regressions. Peter approved the dependency-metadata change on 2026-10-23. That PR must land first; the final candidate for this PR will contain both fixes. A clean install of the full exact candidate and the 2026.10.5 updater comparison remain unrun. This PR stays draft until the packaging repair and all final-candidate update/rollback cells pass.

## What Problem This Solves

Direct updates from extended-stable 2026.9.33 can fail during database migration and refuse automatic rollback even when the captured data has not changed.

## User Impact

Users can update directly from 2026.9.33 to a release containing this fix, with database migration and verified rollback supported. Older candidates still need the documented intermediate 2026.10.5 update. Changed databases continue to block automatic restoration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The digest owner computes the 2026.9.33 physical format after the same stable-source and native-integrity checks. Doctor selects it only after the entire captured inventory matches exactly and keeps that selection through migration, native close, and settlement. Unmarked worker requests use the physical format only when the current recorded 2026.9.33 producer matches the live parent identity. Candidate-produced captures explicitly request committed-content fingerprints. Mismatches still refuse restoration; no schema or public configuration changes.

Update the troubleshooting guidance introduced in #179349: direct updates work with candidates containing this fix; retain the intermediate 2026.10.5 route for older candidates.

## Evidence

- The 2026.9.33-format migration and unmarked rollback-request regressions fail on base `b7b7415ae65`; changed-source rejection passes there. All three pass with this fix.
- Existing migration coverage: 12 unchanged cases passed in the complete file run. The initial new positive fixture bypassed the close observer by capturing its disposer before registration; corrected to explicit observed close and revalidated.
- `pnpm test src/infra/update-doctor-migration-attribution.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 193.34 s wall time including cold worker compilation and the fixture failure; corrected three-case run: 146.68 s wall time, 12.26 s test execution. Baseline negative control: 236.73 s.
- All 21 existing digest integrity tests pass (`pnpm test src/infra/update-database-generations.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 195.51 s wall time).
- Changed-file format/lint and `git diff --check` pass. Independent Codex review reports no actionable P0/P1 findings.
- Exact candidate `91c4956b509767bd9e51d83046de42afe149ba78` built with the canonical package recipe. Published 2026.9.33 native update completed in 352.78 s with exit 0 and `status: ok`; the real Doctor migration and post-plugin lint passed. Final Gateway restart failed on the missing mandatory dependency described above, so this is not an end-to-end pass.
- Pending before landing: complete 2026.9.33 retained-state/reconnect acceptance, forced database rollback, and 2026.10.5 success cells; required PR CI. No latency claim.
- Legacy captures retain exact physical-fingerprint matching. A read-only probe that changes fingerprinted WAL-header metadata can still be rejected. The suggested empty-reader alternate was declined because broadening legacy equality is outside this adapter's approved exact-match contract.

## Production Size

Net **+94 production lines** in 9 files (139 added / 45 removed); **+130 test lines** and **+7 documentation lines**, 11 changed files total. Approved budget: at most +150 production lines.

Growth by responsibility: +52 lines at the digest/producer owner, +22 in private worker transport, +12 for migration/native-close propagation, and +8 for admission/settlement. These cover five necessary parts: the exact legacy digest at the existing owner; private worker transport for the selected format; one-time whole-inventory admission; retaining that format through migration, native close and settlement; and recognizing the old parent's unmarked request from the active run plus verified parent identity. The options type moves beside the digest contract to keep its caller within the existing file-size limit. The existing digest, migration, and restore owners remain authoritative; no new durable state.

prs.title: fix(heartbeat): end the turn after heartbeat_respond is accepted [2026.10.6]
prs.body:
Fixes #180833 (follow-up to #86324). Supersedes #177679.

## Why this targets `release/2026.10.6`

`main` retired `heartbeat_respond` in #180192, so there's nothing left to fix there. Released 2026.10.x still ships the tool, and the loop reproduces on stock 2026.10.6 (evidence in #180833). This is a port of #177679 onto the `release/2026.10.6` branch (`fe06181`). Please retarget or relabel it if you'd rather carry it as a named backport.

## Change

- An accepted `heartbeat_respond` now ends the turn (it terminates the tool round). A rejected duplicate can no longer keep the run going until it errors out or hits `timedOutByRunBudget`.
- Tool-loop detection and incomplete-turn resolution treat the accepted heartbeat as a completed turn.
- Diagnostic wording: "three consecutive identical failures" is now "3 consecutive failures of the same tool call", and the recovery guidance is kept.
- New `heartbeat-response-tool.loop.test.ts` covers repeating models (duplicate, invalid response and invalid schema cases), plus updated unit tests.

## Verification

- `vitest`: 6 files, 95 tests passed (heartbeat-response-tool, heartbeat-response-tool.loop, error-text, compaction-and-tool-summaries, tool-loop-detection, incomplete-turn-resolution)
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: clean
- `oxlint` on touched files: 0 warnings, 0 errors
- Live run in an isolated install (gemini-3.8-flash via an OpenAI-compatible shim, `messages.visibleReplies: message_tool`):
  - stock 2026.10.6: run with 4 `heartbeat_respond` calls, 3 rejected as `already accepted`, about 87k tokens, `session.ended status=error`
  - this branch: 4 of 4 heartbeats made 1 accepted call each, `session.ended status=success`, about 22k tokens each, `timedOutByRunBudget=false`

prs.title: feat: remove saved personal model accounts from Profile and CLI
prs.body:
Related: #178803

## What Problem This Solves

Saved personal model accounts cannot be removed through Profile, the CLI or a supported Gateway operation, leaving duplicate or obsolete credentials in the account list.

## User Impact

Owners can explicitly remove their own saved account from this Gateway through Profile or `openclaw models accounts remove <account-id>`. This deletes the local credential record, not access at the provider. `clear-default` still keeps credentials.

This is a **draft implementation for product review**, not a claim that the proposed lifecycle contract has been accepted. It does not yet show the number of affected chats before confirmation. Live incognito current/rollback pin cleanup now has focused native-worker coverage. Fallback behavior across every runtime remains unverified.

### Known gaps — why this is a draft

- **Pinned-chat count:** confirmation explains what removal does, but does not count or list affected chats. The reporter requested that count; it is not implemented here.
- **Incognito:** this update covers existing live memory owners, including agents without a durable session store, current/rollback pins, no durable persistence, and truthful partial cleanup/retry. This is bounded native-worker proof, not a claim about every runtime or provider.
- **Fallback coverage:** the native runtime resolves Gateway credentials in the tested synthetic scenario. No claim is made that every runtime behaves identically. Product acceptance of this lifecycle contract is still pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

Removal uses the existing admitted credential transaction and retirement publication. It clears exact current and rollback account pins across discovered agent session stores without changing unrelated accounts or model choices. An already-open account picker refreshes instead of retaining a deleted row.

Credential deletion can succeed while chat cleanup fails. In that case, Profile offers a cleanup retry and the CLI reports partial completion with a nonzero exit status. Retrying the same account ID never restores its credential. Administrators cannot use this operation to delete another person's account, and shared credentials are outside its scope.

There is no provider-side revoke, schema migration or new background service.

Pre-publication overlap check: no PR referencing #178803 or implementing `users.removeModelAccount` was found. The merged #157745 handles existing credential-removal cleanup/recovery, and #174904 changes provider/shared-account controls; neither adds this personal-account removal operation. This change reuses the existing cleanup owner rather than replacing those flows.

## Evidence

### Incognito and transport/upgrade follow-up (2026-10-24)

- Incognito cleanup uses the existing memory session owner; it neither creates a new owner nor persists incognito sessions. Unrelated account/model selections and rollback metadata are retained.
- Independently rerun local checks: state removal 7/7; incognito/worker suite 8/8; real local Gateway transport and stable-upgrade suites 7/7; targeted gateway-methods types, changed-file lint and format checks passed. These are local synthetic results, not hosted CI or production acceptance.
- Regression negative control: omitting the incognito cleanup call makes the live-incognito test fail at the retained account pin; restoring the implementation passes. No mutation is retained.
- Transport coverage includes owner removal, foreign-admin denial, revoked writer and disconnected-client scenarios before/after credential commit. The transport is real local TLS/WebSocket with deterministic operation holds; no real provider or real account is used.
- Upgrade input is generated by the clean stable checkout pinned to `fe06181dc5ecc01cf8904abbfc26925925efefbc`; the test requires that exact supplied commit and rejects a dirty source checkout. It exercises Doctor, removal and restart while checking unrelated state preservation.
- Independent autoreview of the follow-up delta against `999bfccdb7d522398876697a3e106c33bd9b8512` returned `scoped-clean` at P0–P2. It reviewed source, did not execute the project, and explicitly lacked unchanged implementation contracts. Local runtime checks above are separate evidence; this is not a new ClawSweeper rank.

Reproduce the follow-up with Node 26.12.1 and the repository test runner:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/model-account-removal.worker.test.ts src/state/user-model-account-removal.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
B1_UPGRADE_SOURCE_CHECKOUT=/path/to/clean/stable-checkout B1_UPGRADE_SOURCE_COMMIT=fe06181dc5ecc01cf8904abbfc26925925efefbc node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-methods/model-account-removal.authority.integration.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/model-account-removal.upgrade.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-methods.json --incremental
```

Pinned-chat count, broad fallback coverage, CLI/Control UI live-Gateway end-to-end coverage and maintainer acceptance of the lifecycle remain open. This PR intentionally stays draft.

### Original candidate evidence (commit 999bfccd)

- Native SQLite: 33 tests passed, covering existing account behavior and seven removal cases. The foreign-owner guard was deliberately removed: its regression failed; restoring the guard passed.
- Gateway worker/handler: four tests passed, including retained-authority retirement, current and rollback pins across two agents, preservation of unrelated accounts, partial cleanup and retry. An existing synthetic chat resolved Gateway credentials after removal through the real RPC handler and native storage path.
- Profile/picker: 37 tests passed. CLI: 16 tests passed. The browser scenario covers cancel, confirmed removal, partial cleanup, retry and preservation of the other account.
- Production and selected test types, protocol registry/generation/native contracts, changed-file formatting/lint, and an independent final-diff review were checked locally. Hosted CI is reported separately in the PR checks; these local results are not a claim that hosted CI is green.

Local evidence is for commit `999bfccdb7d522398876697a3e106c33bd9b8512`, based on `4a5eef31765e801a2425afe35e5c9b05d57d5216`. The independent full-diff review reported no actionable P0–P2 findings; a separate fresh-context review covered the final equivalent exact-link loop simplification. Review was source-based, not an additional runtime test. No new manager, schema, background service, dependency or provider-revocation mechanism was introduced; the additional code wires the existing credential owner into Profile, CLI and RPC consumers and tests those boundaries.

<details>
<summary>Reproducible local commands and observed results</summary>

Run from the repository root in an isolated, dependency-installed checkout, with Node 24.20.0 and `CI=true OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`. Tests use synthetic identities and credentials.

```sh
# Native storage: 33/33 (26 existing cases + seven removal cases).
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts --configLoader runner src/state/user-model-account-removal.test.ts src/state/user-model-accounts.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

# Gateway worker/handler: 4/4; final run 106.41 seconds.
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-database-workers.config.ts --configLoader runner src/gateway/model-account-removal.worker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

# Browser flow: 1/1; final run 39.96 seconds, including setup/build.
OPENCLAW_CAPTURE_UI_PROOF=1 PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE_PATH=/usr/bin/chromium node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/model-account-removal.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

# Final affected canonical type graphs after file extraction: all four passed.
node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --ci-graphs-json '["core","core-test-gateway-root","core-test-state-logging","core-test-ui-e2e"]'
```

Additional focused suites: `ui/src/pages/profile/model-accounts.test.tsx` plus `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-session-controls.test.tsx` — 37/37; `src/commands/models/accounts.test.ts` — 16/16. These counts include existing regressions, not only new tests.

Ownership negative control: temporarily removing the exact credential-owner guard caused the foreign-owner/shared-ID regression to fail (`expected function to throw`). Restoring it passed all seven removal cases. No weakened guard remains. The final loop-only simplification was subsequently covered by those seven native tests, lint and the separate review; the type result above predates that equivalent simplification.

The native path exercises committed credential retirement, exact current and rollback pins across two agents, an unreadable-store partial result, and same-ID retry. The browser flow exercises cancel → no removal; confirm → credential removed, cleanup pending; retry → complete, with the other account preserved.

</details>

The browser capture uses the built Control UI and a **mocked Gateway with synthetic accounts**. The native handler test uses real state workers and SQLite, but is not a WebSocket/full-Gateway or real-provider test. No real account or provider token was removed or revoked. These are bounded WIP proofs, not production acceptance.

### Before and after the removal action

These inspected captures show the **candidate UI**, not a base-versus-patch visual comparison. Built Control UI in Chromium 156, mocked Gateway, two synthetic accounts. No private account or desktop content is shown.

Before confirmation — both saved accounts remain:

![Candidate UI before removal: two synthetic saved accounts](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8e894c93-4e34-4f83-80da-7477a8601a9f)

After removal and successful cleanup retry — only the unrelated account remains:

![Candidate UI after removal: the other account remains and completion is explicit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/799d6b10-4fb6-4bd6-aafb-6e7e3b759eaf)

<details>
<summary>Confirmation and truthful partial-completion state</summary>

![Confirmation separates local credential deletion from provider revocation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/df5336db-d224-4e26-8594-91ccb0e7a941)

![Credential already removed, with a retry for pending chat cleanup](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1948f16b-73a0-4e5b-894f-83065b6575b8)

</details>

prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/96692.

Slack currently writes the requested `threadTs` into text and Block Kit receipts when `chat.postMessage` omits `message.thread_ts`. This makes an unconfirmed threaded placement look confirmed to durable terminal delivery.

This repair keeps generic Slack send canonicalization intact while recording receipt thread evidence only from Slack's returned `message.thread_ts`. It adds regressions for missing and mismatched confirmation through terminal reconciliation, retains valid child-to-root canonicalization, and leaves media behavior unchanged.

prs.title: fix(setup): preserve the current model when activating saved auth
prs.body:
Related to #167381

## What Problem This Solves

Activating a previously saved auth profile failed with `The candidate route does not match the selected model` when the saved credential's starter model differed from the current agent model. The activation path staged the stored starter model instead of the model the agent was already using, so route verification rejected the candidate. If the models happened to match, activation could also overwrite the user's current model with the starter model. Discovery had the same mismatch: Model Setup forwards the discovered candidate model explicitly, so fixing activation alone was bypassed by the normal UI flow. Provider-qualified aliases such as `openai/Fast` must also be resolved to their canonical model identity or the same route check rejects a valid current model.

## Why This Change Was Made

Saved-auth discovery and `stageSavedAuthCandidate` now share the same model-selection decision:

1. An explicitly supplied `modelRef`.
2. The canonical current agent route model, when it belongs to the same provider as the saved credential.
3. The saved credential's stored model, preserving the existing cross-provider fallback.

Both paths call `resolveCurrentModelRefForSavedAuth`, which uses the existing setup route resolver. Configured aliases therefore resolve to the same concrete model identity used by the model-selection updater, and discovery advertises that canonical current model to Model Setup. The trailing auth-profile suffix is removed before comparing providers. API-key header configuration is applied to the provider of the resolved model rather than always using the saved starter model's provider. Credential and auth-profile binding behavior is unchanged.

## User Impact

Users can switch back to a saved sign-in without a spurious route mismatch, and activation no longer resets their current model to the provider's starter model. Cross-provider saved credentials retain the previous fallback behavior.

## Evidence

- Full target test file: `42 passed` on the final head, including both `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` and the configured `openai/Fast` alias.
- Discovery-to-activation regression: both cases call `setup.detect()`, assert the saved-auth candidate advertises the canonical current model, activate that candidate as Model Setup does, and verify the persisted model and inference call.
- Discovery base-red: with the previous discovery selection restored, both cases advertise `openai/starter-model` and fail before activation.
- Discovery unit suite: `19 passed` in `setup-inference-detect.test.ts`.
- Type-safety hardening: the API-key header target uses the resolved model provider when a model is present and otherwise falls back to the saved provider, so `parseInferenceRef` never receives an optional model reference. The final-head model regressions pass (`2 passed | 40 skipped`).
- Formatting: `oxfmt --check` passed for all changed files; `git diff --check` passed.
- Logs: `167381-vitest.log`, `167381-base-red.log`, `180832-full-vitest.log`, `180832-alias-base-red.log`, `180832-p2-typefix-vitest.log`, `180832-discovery-vitest.log`, `180832-discovery-base-red.log`, `180832-detect-vitest.log`, and `180832-full-vitest-final2.log` under `contributions/pr-evidence-20261023/` in the contributor workspace. Upgrade readback logs: `stable-doctor.log`, `stable-baseline.json`, `candidate-doctor.log`, `candidate-activation.log`, `candidate-followup.json`, `requests.jsonl`, `schema-before-after.json`, and `upgrade-verification.json` under `180832-live-proof/upgrade-20261023e/`.

### Real CLI behavior proof

On 2026-10-23 I exercised the shipped `openclaw` CLI in an isolated state directory against a local loopback OpenAI Responses provider. The state had an active `openai:baseline` credential and a saved replacement `openai:saved-proof` credential whose recorded model was `openai/starter-model`; the current agent model was `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`.

- A baseline `openclaw agent --local` turn authenticated with the baseline credential and returned `LIVE_PROOF_REPLY_1` on `gpt-5.4-mini`.
- `openclaw models auth activate openai:saved-proof --agent main` printed `Inference verified: openai/gpt-5.4-mini` and `Sign-in verified and saved.` It authenticated the probe with the saved credential, not the baseline credential.
- A subsequent `openclaw agent --local` turn returned `LIVE_PROOF_REPLY_3` from `gpt-5.4-mini` and used the saved credential.
- Persisted config after activation: `agents.defaults.model.primary` remained `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`, while `agents.entries.main.model` became `openai/gpt-5.4-mini@openai:saved-proof`.
- The saved profile remained present in the migrated auth store with its original key; only its consumed setup marker was cleared.

Provider-side request sequence, with keys redacted:

```text
baseline warmup   Bearer <baseline>  gpt-5.4-mini     LIVE_PROOF_REPLY_1
activation probe  Bearer <saved>     gpt-5.4-mini     LIVE_PROOF_REPLY_2
follow-up turn    Bearer <saved>     gpt-5.4-mini     LIVE_PROOF_REPLY_3
```

The discriminating latest-stable run used the published `openclaw@2026.10.6` package with the same fixture. It activated the saved credential as `openai/starter-model` and persisted `agents.entries.main.model = openai/starter-model@openai:saved-proof`, reproducing the reported drift. The head above instead persisted `openai/gpt-5.4-mini@openai:saved-proof`.

### Existing-state compatibility

The fixture initially used the legacy `auth-profiles.json` layout. The reviewed head's `doctor --fix` migrated it to the current state SQLite database, retained both profile IDs and credentials, and the CLI listed and activated both afterwards. This PR adds no persisted-format change.

### Latest-stable upgrade readback

The readback was verified on `a8b7787e`, rebased onto current `main` (reports `2026.10.6`). The branch was then rebased once more to `e3d624de` solely to pick up upstream `82c46546`, a test-fixture typecheck fix; the source diff is unchanged. I seeded an isolated state with the published `openclaw@2026.10.6` (fe06181) package: its `doctor --fix` migrated the legacy store and stamped `meta.lastTouchedVersion=2026.10.6` with schema v20, and one baseline turn ran against that state (`LIVE_PROOF_REPLY_1`, baseline credential, `gpt-5.4-mini`).

The candidate head then opened the same state. Its `doctor --fix` advanced schema v20 -> v31 and retained pre-migration SQLite backups. `models auth activate openai:saved-proof --agent main` printed `Inference verified: openai/gpt-5.4-mini` and `Sign-in verified and saved.` with no downgrade-guard warning. The follow-up turn returned `LIVE_PROOF_REPLY_3` on `gpt-5.4-mini` using the saved credential. After the upgrade, `agents.defaults.model.primary` remained `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`, and only `agents.entries.main.model` became `openai/gpt-5.4-mini@openai:saved-proof`.

Machine-checkable result: `upgrade-20261023e/upgrade-verification.json` (13/13 checks), with logs in `upgrade-20261023e/` under `contributions/pr-evidence-20261023/`.

Command:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts \
  src/system-agent/setup-inference-activate.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

`tsgo` could not be run on this host because the available glibc is older than the installed TypeScript native binary requires, so this PR does not claim a local typecheck result.

## CI note

`check-test-types-core-1` failed only in `src/hooks/loader.cache-invalidation.test.ts` (`managedHooksDir`), which this PR does not touch; it is a pre-existing failure on `main` already fixed by upstream `82c46546`. The final rebase includes that fix.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted implementation and test preparation. The contributor reviewed the diff, ran both the focused regression and base-red checks, and verified the final patch.

prs.title: improve(ui): offer guests starter prompts they can act on
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Guests signed in through Visitor Access see empty-chat and New Session starter prompts such as "Help me configure a channel" and "Check system health", which need operator permissions their role does not have.

## User Impact

User impact: guests (session-scoped grants without `operator.write`) now see starter prompts that fit their access: asking what Roboclaw can do, touring OpenClaw's code and docs, investigating an issue in a sandbox, and fixing a bug in a draft PR. Operators and admins keep the same four prompts as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The welcome block shared by the empty chat and the New Session page rendered one fixed prompt list. It now picks the list from the connected principal's `hello.auth` grant with the existing `hasOperatorWriteAccess` check. The Visitor Access guest policy grants only `operator.sessions.write` (or `operator.sessions.read`), never `operator.write`, so guests get the session-scoped list. Missing auth keeps the operator list, the same way `operator-access.ts` treats legacy snapshots.

Unchanged: the welcome block still shows prompts only when there are no recent chats on that agent.

## Evidence

- Unit (`ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-welcome-suggestions.test.tsx`): operator prompts are unchanged for missing auth, `operator.write`, and `operator.admin`; an `operator.sessions.write` grant gets the guest prompts, and clicking one sends its text.
- Browser E2E (`ui/src/e2e/new-session-page.responsive-welcome.e2e.test.ts`, bundled build, mocked Gateway with `operatorScopes: ["operator.sessions.write"]`): fails with the base `chat-welcome.tsx` (operator prompts shown) and passes with this change. The existing desktop-only suggestions scenario still passes.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, oxfmt check and oxlint on the changed files: clean (one existing warning on an unchanged line).

Screenshots: New Session page, 1280×800, light theme, mocked Gateway with a guest grant (`operator.sessions.write`) and no recent chats.

Contributor credit: requested by @jalehman as part of the guest onboarding project.

prs.title: fix(packaging): preserve required SDK API installation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A fresh npm install can report success while leaving `node_modules/@opentelemetry/api` empty. The Anthropic SDK requires that package, so the installed Gateway then fails to start. This also blocked direct update acceptance after an otherwise successful 2026.9.33 update and Doctor migration.

## User Impact

The privately bundled AI runtime no longer advertises the redundant API peer that triggers npm's missing extraction. Installed-package verification rejects an unresolved API dependency when the installed SDK requires it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The package owner already removes dependency declarations from the private AI copy because the root owns its runtime dependencies. Remove only `@opentelemetry/api` from that copy's `peerDependencies` and `peerDependenciesMeta` too. Keep unrelated peers, the standalone AI manifest, all dependency versions, overrides, and the npm lock mirror unchanged.

Peter approved this exact package-side metadata change on 2026-10-23. It addresses npm behavior reproduced on 11.19.1, with additional coordinator-confirmed reproductions on 11.21.1 and 12.2.1; upgrading npm does not avoid the defect.

## Evidence

- Three serial clean-prefix probes on Node 24.22.1 / npm 11.19.1 used the same SDK 0.135.0 and selected API 1.10.0. Optional and required bundled-peer variants both exited 0 but left an empty API directory and failed the SDK tracing import. Removing the bundled API peer installed the API files and made the import pass.
- Both regressions fail on the baseline for the intended reason: the private artifact retains the API peer, and installed-tree verification accepts the empty required dependency.
- Both regressions pass after the fix. The complete installed-tree test file passes all 12 cases (3.29 s wall). The combined focused package/installed-tree run took 16.24 s wall; the package case used 11.98 s, predominantly transformation. No timers, retries, limits, or versions changed.
- Changed-file format/lint, independent review, and fresh candidate install/Gateway smoke are being completed before landing.

## Production Size

+24 lines in packaging and verification scripts, +30 net test lines, +4 documentation lines; 5 files. Runtime production files under `src`, `extensions`, `packages`, and `ui`: 0 changed lines. The script growth stays within the approved +30 production/config budget: five lines remove the private peer metadata, and nineteen add required-dependency resolution to the existing installed-tree walk.

prs.title: feat(visitor-access): retain invitation onboarding metadata
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Guest invitations need durable inviter and setup metadata so first-sign-in welcome sessions can be created once and recovered after a restart.

## User Impact

Invitations record the authenticated inviter when available, and renewals preserve existing notes and onboarding progress. Older grants continue to work without these fields. This is item 1 of guest onboarding: note tool input, welcome-session creation, and guest UI changes are separate follow-ups.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses the existing SQLite-backed grant store and its service mutation queue instead of introducing another store or setup owner. New invitations start pending. Plugin-internal lookup and compare-and-set methods let setup reserve a stable welcome-session key before creation; pending-to-pending updates advance their comparison timestamp even within one millisecond. Inviter attribution uses the trusted Gateway users.self request, never tool input or session ownership.

The simplification pass kept grant decisions in the existing service and moved record/input definitions out of the near-limit service file. Against the base: production +267/−71 lines; tests and test support +300/−4; documentation +31. No SQL schema migration or access-policy change.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/visitor-access --maxWorkers=1`: 103 tests passed, including registered-plugin SQLite persistence/restart/renewal, legacy grants, concurrent onboarding reservations, and caller-lifetime rejection.
- Stable-to-head upgrade with Doctor: a `v2026.10.6` checkout (`fe06181dc5ec`) recorded one email and one GitHub grant via the registered plugin's `visitor_invite` into an isolated SQLite state directory. On a copy, this head's built CLI ran `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` (isolated `HOME`/state/config; exit 0, pre-migration backup saved, state schema 31 with 0 pending). This head's registered plugin then started on the migrated database and:
  - loaded both grant values unchanged, admitted the email visitor, and returned both from `findActiveInvitation`;
  - reserved onboarding with compare-and-set from `null` (`pending`, stable session key);
  - renewed the email grant through `visitor_invite` (30 days, reservation preserved);
  - after a service stop and restart, still admitted the visitor, returned the renewed grant with its reservation and the unchanged GitHub grant, and advanced the reservation to `ready` with compare-and-set.
- Before Doctor, the unmigrated copy loaded and read correctly but core refused writes pending `openclaw doctor --fix`; that is the existing core upgrade step.
- The committed registered-plugin test seeds the exact recorded email grant and covers admission, lookup, compare-and-set from `null`, and renewal.
- Production and test extension typechecks passed.
- Targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Codex AutoReview (P0–P2): no actionable findings in the supplied change. It did not independently execute the integration tests.
- External identity/provider I/O used fixtures. No production invitation, live Cloudflare change, or end-to-end guest sign-in was performed; full onboarding proof is a later project item.

Requested by @jalehman.

- [Original discussion with @jalehman](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4ff43853-805b-4ab6-932c-1622ab5bb1d8)

prs.title: improve(ui): keep delegated work inline with its originating turn
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Delegated-work progress is pinned above the composer instead of staying with the conversation turn that launched it.

## User Impact

Tasks now appear inline: one to five helpers use a compact expandable row, while larger active batches expand with progress and task details. Completed work stays at its original turn, leaving the composer clear.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the footer-only swarm renderer with a transcript-owned activity row. Accepted launch receipts establish exact placement; live collector state and persisted collection results update that same row. Missing historical outcomes are explicitly unavailable, never assumed successful or still running.

The existing transcript remains the storage owner. Compact receipts preserve existing result-size limits; no new store, RPC, retention policy, or browser cache. Ordinary announced helpers without a retained terminal identity use the unavailable historical fallback after their live record expires.

Simplification: removed the old footer renderer, duplicate rendering tests, and the obsolete footer diagnostic.

## Evidence

- Built Control UI desktop and mobile lifecycle tests: live progress, compact completion, exact turn placement, and reload after child/registry removal.
- Focused tests cover one/five/six/thirty helpers, partial failure, missing outcomes, child navigation, composer draft/focus preservation, and no extra descriptor requests during live updates.
- Producer tests cover native accepted launches, collector outcomes, ordinary/nested persistence caps, and prompt-prefix stability.
- Targeted type-aware lint, core/UI/scripts typechecks, generated-validator consistency, formatting, and docs checks.
- Independent frozen-input review: no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- CI integration repairs verified locally: 19 wrapper import-closure tests, 22 focused UI tests, 31 activity tests, and 3 built desktop/mobile/history E2E scenarios. English source catalog, affected test types, lint, formatting, cursor policy, and CSS budget checks pass; exact-head hosted CI run [40057764621](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40057764621) passed (79 successful jobs, 21 skipped).
- Real-model Gateway E2E was not run: this execution context cannot use the attributed Gateway agent-input route. UI captures use the real built application with a mock Gateway; producer tests exercise the production projection/persistence boundary.

prs.title: fix(meta): Muse subscription sign-in cannot be finished from chat and turns are rejected after sign-in
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `/login meta` in chat can never start the Muse device-code subscription sign-in (it always hands off to Control UI guided setup), and even after a successful sign-in every turn on `meta/muse-spark-1.3` fails — first with missing-auth errors on the wrong runtime, then with `Requested agent harness "muse" does not support meta/muse-spark-1.3`.

## User Impact

User impact: users can add and authorize Meta Muse models end-to-end in Telegram (device-code in the browser, no API key or secret handling in chat), and signed-in models actually run. Control UI guided setup behavior is unchanged. Security boundaries are preserved: nothing starts in chat without the plugin's explicit `channelLogin` opt-in (the same mechanism GitHub Copilot, xAI, MiniMax, and Codex device-code already use), API-key entry still hands off to secure setup, and no credentials pass through chat.

## Why This Change Was Made

Four stacked gaps, each fixed at its layer:

1. The `muse-code` choice never declared `channelLogin`, so chat could not start it.
2. `projectChannelChoice` only computed a login kind for `credentialOnly` choices; harness-owned sign-ins (no credential profile saved — the credential lives in the Muse CLI) always projected to setup-only even with an explicit chat opt-in.
3. Credential-only login persistence dropped the auth result's declared `agentRuntimeId`, so the model kept resolving to the default API runtime. It now stages the same per-agent model runtime policy guided setup writes (`prepareSetupModelRuntime`), scoped to the signing-in agent and the login's own default model, ignored for the default `openclaw` runtime.
4. Prepared native routes carry a blank `baseUrl`, which masked the configured official Meta endpoint in harness support facts while `endpointOverrides` was derived from that same config — the Muse harness therefore rejected every turn. Blank prepared baseUrls now fall back to the configured endpoint (live diagnostic before the fix: `rt=muse provider=meta transport=none endpoint=present baseUrl= api=openai-responses`).

## Evidence

Live verification on a real Telegram + gateway install, before/after on the same account:

- Before: `/login meta` → "Meta API key needs provider setup. Open Control UI…"; after out-of-band sign-in, turns failed with missing-auth on the API route, then with the harness rejection above (gateway journal, runs at 17:40 and 19:35, 2026-10-21).
- After: Muse Spark and Muse Wonder Full turns succeed through the gateway (`probe ok`, `wonder ok`, and a Russian translation), with the session reporting the Muse runtime.

Focused tests on this branch (all passing, 147 tests):

- `src/plugins/provider-login-options.test.ts` — channelLogin-declared harness sign-in starts in chat; the API-key sibling still resolves to setup handoff; no opt-in still means setup.
- `src/commands/models/auth.test.ts` — declared runtime staged for credential-only harness sign-ins; nothing staged for the default runtime.
- `src/agents/harness/selection.test.ts` — configured endpoint preserved when a prepared native route has a blank baseUrl.
- `extensions/meta/muse-login.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/model-provider-capabilities.test.ts` — Control UI still offers Meta API key + Muse device sign-in through guided setup.

`tsgo` core clean; oxlint/oxfmt clean on touched files.

Evidence gaps: fresh-account device-code completion in Telegram was exercised on the author's already-signed-in account (re-login short-circuits in the Muse CLI); the staging write is covered by unit tests. On a host where the Muse runtime plugin is not installed, chat sign-in completes but model selection still goes through the normal runtime-install/consent path; the declared model now reaches runtime-plugin repair, matching other login paths. Usability note: `/login meta` now starts the Muse device-code flow directly (single chat-capable route); the API-key route stays available as `/login meta/meta-api-key`.

Cross-review: independently reviewed with Claude Code (Opus 5.5, xhigh); full review in `claude-review.md`. The blocking contract issue was addressed in `docs/plugins/manifest/setup-and-auth.md`: `channelLogin` no longer "requires `credentialOnly`" — harness-owned sign-ins may declare it alone, with the narrowed persistence behavior documented. prs.title: fix(qa-lab): stop child log buffering from exhausting memory
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A QA suite runner can retain unbounded child output when its debug-log file stops draining. The recent text tail was already bounded, but each stdout/stderr event appended another Buffer to the file stream's pending-write queue.

## User Impact

QA now stops its owned Gateway with a `log backlog exceeded` diagnostic before either stream queues more than 4 MiB. This limits pending writes, not total log size. An unusually large burst during a slow disk can therefore fail a suite; check the output disk before retrying.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing pipe-failure monitor and lifecycle remain responsible for termination and bounded log finalization. Removing the extra `Buffer.from` also avoids copying every incoming chunk. Production delta: +13/-2 lines (+11 net); the growth supplies an actual queue bound and error path, without a cache, configuration option, new timer, or containment layer.

This fixes a reproduced stalled-sink defect. **It does not establish the cause of the originally reported OOM.** A silent stopped child timed out normally rather than reproducing that incident.

## Evidence

Synthetic local source-owner runs used the pinned Bun 1.4.4 fork and Node 26.12.1, isolated state, and loopback ports. An external watchdog sampled aggregate runner/descendant RSS every 0.5 seconds and killed every observed owned process group at 4 GiB or a fixed wall cap. Runs were serial. The blocked-sink workload emits 64 KiB chunks for 10 seconds while its file write callback is held.

| Runtime | Pending bytes before → after | Aggregate RSS peak before → after | RSS samples before / after | Outcome |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Bun | 274,464,768 → 4,194,304 (−98.47%) | 932.83 → 547.48 MiB (−385.34 MiB; −41.31%) | 53 / 22 | Baseline wall-stopped at 30 s; fixed runner exited in 11.48 s |
| Node | 274,989,056 → 4,194,304 (−98.47%) | 1,354.73 → 1,216.00 MiB (−138.73 MiB; −10.24%) | 129 / 55 | Baseline wall-stopped at 70 s; fixed runner exited in 29.86 s |

One run per cell; RSS includes source import/preparation and is context, not a timing/GC performance claim. The deterministic acceptance condition is the pending-byte bound and visible failure/child termination. An active blocked write may retain the bounded queue until completion/GC; the fix does not promise immediate reclamation.

Bun `bun:jsc.heapStats()`/`process.memoryUsage()` showed buffer/external growth matching the pending queue. A separate Node allocation profile including collected objects traced allocations through the child output callback and bounded-tail decoding. Silent stopped-child source-owner runs exited at their 120-second startup deadline: Bun 596.72 MiB peak / 232 RSS samples; Node 1,285.45 MiB peak / 258 samples.

The full suite entry (`gateway-restart-inflight-run`, concurrency 1, stopped child before Gateway entry) also completed both startup attempts and the built-in infrastructure retry without runaway growth: Bun 248.60 seconds / 936.42 MiB peak / 455 RSS samples; Node 294.15 seconds / 1,723.13 MiB peak / 538 RSS samples. This tests startup/retry plumbing; no scenario steps execute while its child is stopped.

Validation:

- Changed-file oxfmt, changed-file type-aware oxlint, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Standalone real-owner / real corked-file-stream assertion: **red on base, green on fix for stdout and stderr**. Base retained all 8,388,608 bytes per stream (exit 1); fixed runs admitted at most 4,128,768 bytes, reported the backlog error, confirmed child termination and destroyed the sink (exit 0). Two cases per revision; 3.85 s base / 3.36 s fixed. This is separate from the Vitest execution below.
- Added one owning-boundary regression parameterized over stdout/stderr, using a real corked file stream and real child: checks queued bytes, surfaced error, process termination, and sink cleanup.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'log sink stops draining'`: worker prerequisite preparation crossed the mandatory 4 GiB aggregate cap and was killed before tests ran. The supported Node runtime with a 1 GiB heap budget hit the same preparation limit. No cap was raised.
- Supported `--native-bun` alternative: the file's existing `vi.hoisted` mocks are unsupported; no tests ran. These local attempts did not execute tests; candidate Vitest coverage was subsequently verified in PR CI below. Base/fix red-green evidence comes from the separate owning-boundary assertion above.
- PR CI [run 40056002230](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40056002230) is green on `ec20ee9552373a3249c4d2434ceb7879bea327fb`, including the final `openclaw/ci-gate`, production/test types, lint, docs, changed-test shards, and all four QA smoke profiles. No CI retries were needed.
- [The QA unit-test shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40056002230/job/120759358182) explicitly passed all 21 `gateway-child-lifecycle.test.ts` cases, including both new stdout/stderr backlog cases. Its sibling `gateway-child`, artifacts, auth-handoff, auth-profiles, bootstrap, drain, env, process, and runtime-selection files also passed. [The E2E shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40056002230/job/120759358192) passed gateway-kill-restart-send and managed-gateway-service-lifecycle, alongside the selected hook/account/subagent coverage.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): scoped clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. The helper refused the requested provider route because it did not match operator configuration; no configuration was changed.

All memory reproductions ran locally; no production state or Team/Testbox hosts were used. No Gateway/exec containment or systemd changes. Please leave this PR open for the coordinating maintainer to verify and merge.

prs.title: fix(lmstudio): send binary on/off reasoning efforts to binary-thinking models
prs.body:
Closes #181888

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: the native LM Studio route sends graded `reasoning_effort` values (`medium`, `xhigh`, ...) to models that only support binary on/off reasoning, so LM Studio warns and silently falls back to its own default instead of honoring the requested thinking level.

## User Impact
Selecting any thinking level on a binary-thinking LM Studio model (for example Gemma 4 12B) now delivers the intended semantics: every enabled level sends `on`, and turning thinking off sends `off`. No more "Reasoning setting 'medium' is not supported" warnings with a fallback the user never chose. Graded-native models are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made
Discovery normalized binary `on/off` capability metadata into the graded OpenAI-compat ladder for the catalog, but the compat effort map still carried graded target values, and the shared completions transport passes the requested graded level through for non-OpenAI providers — so the wire carried a value the endpoint rejects. Binary-capability models now keep the graded ladder for the catalog while their compat map carries on/off wire tokens, and the LM Studio stream wrapper rewrites outgoing `reasoning_effort` through that map (graded-native models stream through unpatched).

## Evidence
- `models.test.ts`: discovery of a model reporting `allowed_options: ["off","on"]` now yields the graded supported ladder plus the binary wire map (`minimal..xhigh → on`, `off/none → off`); red on base, which produced graded map values. Graded-native and off-only discovery cases unchanged.
- `stream.test.ts` (real wrapper pipeline with payload capture): thinking `medium` on a binary-map model sends `reasoning_effort: "on"` (red on base: sent `medium`), thinking `off` sends `"off"`, and a graded-native model still sends `medium` untouched.
- Suites: lmstudio stream + models + setup, 99/99 (node 24.19, direct vitest against the `extension-providers` shard config).
- Not run locally: a live LM Studio server (none available); CI covers typecheck and lint lanes.

prs.title: feat: expose final worker prompts to admission hooks
prs.body:
Fixes #170118

## What Problem This Solves

Plugins cannot inspect the final system prompt in `before_agent_run` for worker-placed sessions. The worker supplies the host-local prompt, but the Gateway must own the other hook fields and enforce admission itself: trusting worker-provided input or worker call order allows rejection-before-persistence to be bypassed.

## User Impact

Updated workers report their final system prompt while the Gateway supplies the authoritative prepared triggering prompt, history, and identity. Approval is bound to the exact turn claim and required before input persistence, transcript commits, proxied inference, Gateway tools, and content-bearing live events. Rejection persists only the redacted block message; cleanup receipts omit unapproved worker content. Older workers retain the original Gateway gate without `systemPrompt`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The worker remains the sole owner of final prompt assembly. The negotiated `worker-turn-admission-v1` transport preserves existing prompt bytes and the base protocol version. Worker-provided prompt/history fields are ignored by the gate. The existing turn owner records approval for its captured Gateway input; pending-result finalization retains that same decision after execution closes.

The full PR adds/removes 530/136 production lines, 629/42 test lines, and 20/6 documentation lines versus its merge base. This follow-up accounts for 117/34 production lines; it reuses the existing claim owner and introduces no state store.

The Gateway cannot verify host-local prompt bytes. A compromised worker can misreport `systemPrompt`, so the hook documentation explicitly says that field is not a trust boundary.

## Evidence

Validation uses Node 24.22.1 and `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`, with `--maxWorkers=1` for tests.

- `pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-admission.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 8 passed, **186.63 s** wall time. Covers exact gate/model system-prompt equality, both persistence owners, blocked input redaction, old-worker allow/block fallback, forged prompt/history, and skipped-admission effect boundaries.
- `pnpm test` for `worker-turn-rpc.transcript`, `worker-turn-rpc.inference-publication`, `worker-turn-rpc.inference-reconnect`, `worker-turn-rpc.gateway-tools`, `worker-turn-rpc.live-ack`, `worker-turn-rpc.computer`, and `src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts`, with `--maxWorkers=1`: **37 passed, 346.23 s** wall time.
- `pnpm test src/worker/worker.runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'runs and replays an embedded turn|revokes an active native provider'`: **3 passed, 150.54 s** wall time.
- Negative control restoring the pre-fix worker-event forwarding: the forged-input regression failed because the hook received the forged prompt/history, **173.00 s** wall time. The script restored the fixed source byte-for-byte afterward; the same focused case then passed, **196.59 s** wall time.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json <changed source/tests>`: type-aware lint passed, **37.82 s** wall time; the final fixture-only check passed in **42.36 s**.
- `pnpm run tsgo:core`: passed, **39.73 s** wall time including local artifact-lock wait.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-other.json --incremental`: passed, **5.10 s** wall time. Worker test types also passed in **6.17 s**. This corrects the admission fixture type errors reported on the prior PR head.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check <changed files>`, `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent Codex autoreview of the follow-up diff: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. Follow-up fixture type corrections and a lint-only variable rename preserve the reviewed behavior.

The admission regression uses real Gateway placement, admission, transcript storage, and worker prompt assembly with a synthetic model boundary. No live model was called. PR CI remains the broad proof; the prior head also had progress-card test failures outside this admission path.

The separate P2 review about the admission RPC's default timeout is unchanged by this P1 repair.

prs.title: fix(doctor): PostgreSQL state Gateways cannot start after a host replacement loses local credentials
prs.body:
Closes #180344

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Gateway whose state uses PostgreSQL cannot start again after its host is replaced and the host-local client credential store is lost, when no backup of that file exists.

## User Impact

Operators running PostgreSQL state on ephemeral hosts, such as containers or replaceable VMs, can recover with `openclaw doctor --client-credentials --repair --non-interactive --rebind-missing-credentials`. Clients on that host get new device identities and must pair again; devices that kept their own credentials stay paired, because the Gateway's pairing records live in the PostgreSQL state store. Nothing changes unless the operator passes the flag: Gateway startup never rebinds, SQLite state is unaffected, and present, mismatched or corrupt local stores keep their existing refusals. Legacy `identity/*.json` files kept from an earlier import stay retired: the repair cannot bring an old private key or a removed token back.

## Why This Change Was Made

With PostgreSQL state, `client/credentials.sqlite` stays on the host and its receipt binds it to the shared state store's identity and anchor file. When only that local file is missing, preparation can only refuse today. The new flag lets the existing PostgreSQL recovery path bind a fresh local store to the current state store the same way a first bootstrap does, writing the same complete receipt for the existing store identity and anchor file. That receipt seals every legacy import claim, as a new local store does, so the legacy identity and token importers that run in the same preparation skip retained JSON instead of reading it as unimported. Later boots and anchor replacement then follow the normal path. It is an explicit doctor option rather than an environment variable, so it stays a deliberate operator repair and adds no `OPENCLAW_*` name.

## Evidence

**Upgrade with existing data.** PostgreSQL state is not in a stable release yet: `openclaw@2026.10.5` rejects the configuration with `Unrecognized key: "database"`. The run therefore starts from upstream `main` before this PR (`333b38de877`, `pnpm build`) and upgrades to this PR's head (`6ecfb2de77b`, rebased on `8c5918e8f83`), on PostgreSQL 18 (`pgvector/pgvector:pg18`) with Node 24.22.1. The pre-PR Gateway stores a cron job in PostgreSQL state; the host then loses `client/`. The upgraded build refuses without the flag, repairs with it, and its Gateway starts on the same store and serves the same job. The state store identity is unchanged throughout.

<details>
<summary>Upgrade transcript (cron JSON condensed to job identity; paths, token and connection string redacted)</summary>

```text
before: OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (333b38d)
pr:     OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (6ecfb2d)  commit 6ecfb2de77bfa5718cf9850ff11e795be627595a
== 1. upstream main before this PR creates PostgreSQL state, its anchor and the local credential store
  state anchor: {"engine":"postgres","store_id":"392c621f-4ab1-470c-8458-60d743e19ae6"}
  client/credentials.sqlite present
== 2. upstream main before this PR Gateway stores shared state in PostgreSQL
  [before] gateway healthy on loopback after 10s

$ [before] openclaw cron add --name upgrade-proof-job --every 1h --message upgrade proof --json
  job 56ed343e-32a2-475c-8d11-7bfc706af9cd "upgrade-proof-job" every 60m
exit=0

$ [before] openclaw cron list --json
  job 56ed343e-32a2-475c-8d11-7bfc706af9cd "upgrade-proof-job" every 60m, status idle
  (+ 1 managed job: Memory Dreaming Promotion)
exit=0
  gateway stopped
== 3. host replaced: local client credential store lost; PostgreSQL state, anchor and settings kept
  state anchor: {"engine":"postgres","store_id":"392c621f-4ab1-470c-8458-60d743e19ae6"}
  client/credentials.sqlite absent
== 4. upgraded build: preparation refuses without the explicit repair

$ [pr] openclaw doctor --client-credentials --repair --non-interactive --json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "Local credentials are missing; restore the matching client credential backup."
  }
}
exit=2
== 5. upgraded build: explicit repair

$ [pr] openclaw doctor --client-credentials --repair --non-interactive --json --rebind-missing-credentials
Local client credentials were missing and have been re-created for the existing PostgreSQL state store (--rebind-missing-credentials). Clients on this host have new device identities and must pair again; devices that kept their own credentials stay paired.
{
  "ok": true
}
exit=0
  state anchor: {"engine":"postgres","store_id":"392c621f-4ab1-470c-8458-60d743e19ae6"}
  client/credentials.sqlite present
== 6. upgraded build: Gateway starts on the existing PostgreSQL state and serves the before-created job
  [pr] gateway healthy on loopback after 14s

$ [pr] openclaw cron list --json
  job 56ed343e-32a2-475c-8d11-7bfc706af9cd "upgrade-proof-job" every 60m, status idle
  (+ 1 managed job: Memory Dreaming Promotion)
exit=0
  gateway stopped
  state anchor: {"engine":"postgres","store_id":"392c621f-4ab1-470c-8458-60d743e19ae6"}
  client/credentials.sqlite present
```

</details>

**Base-red regression.** The PR's tests run against the unfixed base, current `main` `8c5918e8f83`:

| Suite | Base | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `startup-client-credentials.postgres.test.ts` (conformance harness, PostgreSQL 18) | 3 failed, 2 passed | 5 passed |
| `register.maintenance.test.ts` | 9 failed, 37 passed | 46 passed |
| `startup-client-credentials.test.ts` (SQLite) | 21 passed | 21 passed |

On base, the rebind, retained-legacy and later-boot cases fail and every new-flag CLI case fails; the existing refusals and the SQLite suite pass unchanged, which is the intended compatibility boundary.

**Retained legacy credentials.** "keeps retained legacy credential files out of a rebound store" writes a legacy `identity/device.json` (Ed25519 identity) and `identity/device-auth.json` (operator token) beside the lost store, rebinds, then boots again without the flag. It expects no device identity, no operator token, and both files byte-for-byte unchanged. On the previous head `03aee56d4a4` it fails: the retained `device.json` identity is imported into the rebound store. It passes on this head.

**Data-model compatibility.** The repair writes the receipt a first bootstrap writes: format 1, a canonical PostgreSQL source with the existing store identity, the current anchor file identity, and every legacy import claim sealed. No schema, table or stored format changes.
