prs.title: fix(doctor): recover lost PostgreSQL client credentials with --fix
prs.body:
Closes #180344

Supersedes #180345 (thanks @ceckert).

## What Problem This Solves

A replacement or ephemeral Gateway host can retain its PostgreSQL state while losing `client/credentials.sqlite`. Previously, preparation refused and required a matching local backup, with no recovery path when that backup was unavailable.

`openclaw doctor --fix` now reports the absent local credentials and asks before creating new identities. `--fix --yes` (or `--repair --yes`) accepts the repair without prompting. `--non-interactive` without `--yes` leaves identities unchanged and reports the exact next step: `openclaw doctor --fix --yes`. Gateway startup only points to `openclaw doctor --fix`; it never performs the rebind. There is no new CLI option, and the existing narrow `--client-credentials` operation remains unchanged.

The simplification follows Peter's review question, “could we not make that simpler?” The recovery design is the coordinator's.

## Identity tradeoff and ownership

Clients on this host receive new identities and must re-pair. Paired remote devices keep working, with their pairing records preserved in PostgreSQL. Doctor explains this before consent. The existing recovery owner writes a complete first-bootstrap receipt bound to the retained PostgreSQL store identity and current anchor, sealing all six retired legacy imports. It runs inside Doctor's maintenance owner. Pre-cutover PostgreSQL credentials still migrate without identity changes or recovery consent, and replacement anchors continue through existing receipt recovery. SQLite and present, mismatched, corrupt, unsafe, or incomplete store refusals remain protected; no schema or identity protocol changes.

Release-note context: ordinary Doctor repair now recovers from lost host-local PostgreSQL client credentials with explicit consent, local re-pairing, and protection against reviving retired imports.

Simplification scope against the merge base: production/tooling +143/-8 lines, tests +385/-1, docs +20. Remaining growth covers the missing-store owner operation, Doctor consent, and compiled entry-point regressions.

## Evidence

- Final head `16610fe1d787ce53f2c01495547aef631784a22c`: [CI run 40056730579](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40056730579) passed. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards actually executed and passed; shard 1 passed all seven compiled Doctor CLI regressions. Type, lint, docs, security and the remaining required checks are green.
- Trusted-main RED reproduction: the compiled ordinary Doctor CLI failed with `client/` removed against Homebrew PostgreSQL 17.
- Real terminal `doctor --fix` confirmation passed against Homebrew PostgreSQL 17: accepted the prompt, recreated the credentials, and exited 0. Local compiled CLI proof also covers the pre-cutover identity/token-preserving migration and the healthy PostgreSQL / unchanged SQLite refusal paths.
- 69 focused credential lifecycle/budget, startup preparation and CLI registration tests passed. Runtime build, formatting and diff checks passed.
- Full isolated Codex review and fresh reviews of the migration-order and assertion corrections are clean through P3. The pre-cutover regression found and fixed a real ordering issue: the existing backed-up migration owner now runs before ordinary state repair.
- An earlier loaded-host full CLI run hit its 120-second process guard; subsequent scoped proof completed in 43 seconds without changing that guard. The initial delay remains unexplained and is not claimed fixed. Final-head CI and the scoped local proofs passed. The earlier full run also detected source changes and is not counted as completed final-head proof.

Fixes the managed Crabbox minimum remaining at 0.77.0 instead of 0.79.2.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw still accepts and installs Crabbox 0.77.0 instead of the approved minimum, 0.79.2.

## User Impact

Workers, Crabbox sandboxes, and local proof commands prepare a verified 0.79.2 distribution when the selected CLI is missing or older. Existing operator binaries and settings are preserved. Restricted hosts need to supply Crabbox 0.79.2 or newer.

Upstream upgrade considerations: explicitly configured Static SSH ports no longer fall back to port 22, and coordinator connectivity uses native TLS/proxy configuration rather than curl-specific workarounds. Legacy direct Azure checkpoints without a recorded snapshot identity require manual reconciliation instead of deletion by name.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing managed-binary owner: its minimum determines the release URL, archive name, installation directory, and version admission. Align the separate protected PR-gate workflow and its published Linux amd64 checksum, test fixtures, repair guidance, and documentation. No installer manifest or separate managed checksum table exists to update.

Reviewed release notes for [0.78.0](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/releases/tag/v0.78.0), [0.78.1](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/releases/tag/v0.78.1), [0.79.0](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/releases/tag/v0.79.0), [0.79.1](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/releases/tag/v0.79.1), and [0.79.2](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/releases/tag/v0.79.2), then checked the 0.79.2 source against OpenClaw's consumers:

- Inspect JSON and lifetime fields remain compatible.
- Stop still waits by default and accepts `--wait=false`; accepted release remains distinct from confirmed cleanup.
- Run cleanup events use `cleanup`/`leaseStopped=false` for unconfirmed cleanup, already handled by the gate publisher. Command exit codes retain their existing meaning, including exit 4 with `lease_id_conflict:` for fixed-lease conflicts (#177497).
- Checkpoint create/inspect/fork fields and `captureEstablished` remain compatible with the existing attestation and pending-image handling.
- Checked the newer ownership checks, environment-cleanup reporting, native TLS recovery, and explicit SSH-port behavior. No provider adapter changes were required.

The CI follow-up corrects the publisher test's old asset/hash and explicitly exercises the retained-checkpoint wait with a reserve capture. Updating the shared fixture to 0.79.2 enables the existing nonblocking first-session path; reserves still wait for capture completion. The test keeps its enrollment, single-capture, cleanup, and timeout-budget assertions. Production behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- CI follow-up on Node **24.22.1**, using `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`: both reported failures reproduced locally. The publisher baseline had **1 failed / 73 passed, 18.40 s wall**; the project baseline had **1 failed / 52 passed, 276.67 s wall**, with the reported `checkpoint_pending` capture error.

- Follow-up checks on Node 24.22.1: type-aware lint via `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` for the extension test and publisher test passed (**247.66 s** and **37.13 s**); `pnpm run tsgo:core` passed (**3.38 s**); `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` passed (**0.22 s**); `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet` passed (**2.73 s**); `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Codex review of the two-file follow-up: no actionable P0–P2 findings. The patch adds no production code or test helper API.

- Before changing the production floor, the focused admission/upgrade regression failed in 5 cases (5 passed, 28 skipped), **287.50 s wall**. It exposed acceptance of 0.77.0, 0.78.1, 0.79.1, and the 0.79.2 prerelease, plus retention of an outdated configured binary.

prs.title: fix(agents): preserve ACP lifecycle ownership
prs.body:
## Summary

- keep spawned ACP runs under their canonical `acp` task owner while retaining a topology/control observer in the subagent registry
- stop ACP observer rows from creating duplicate `subagent` task projections, terminal delivery obligations, or child-session cleanup authority
- upgrade persisted legacy ACP mirrors during normalization and use the active ACP turn or canonical durable task as observer liveness
- emit a specific ACP owner-loss reason and preserve one-shot session state until a later corroborating maintenance pass

Fixes [GEN-6353](https://linear.app/genhealth/issue/GEN-6353/openclaw-loses-active-shrimp-acp-backing-sessions-after-the-legacy).

## What Problem This Solves

An ACP spawn created the canonical `runtime=acp` task, then the shared spawn pipeline registered the same run as a native subagent. The mirror's sweeper checked `getAgentRunContext`, which never represented external ACP liveness, so it false-failed after the stale grace and ran session-scoped cleanup. Task maintenance later treated only the process-local ACP turn marker as backing evidence, marked the canonical task lost after its grace, and could close the one-shot session in that same pass.

The observed production intervals match those two grace periods plus sweep cadence.

## Design

Patterns found and retained:

- the shared spawn registry remains the source for child topology, admission caps, status, and control
- the ACP manager/task registry remains the canonical lifecycle, progress, delivery, and cleanup owner
- observer ownership is persisted in the existing forward-compatible payload JSON; no SQLite schema change is required
- legacy ACP rows are recognized by their canonical ACP session key and normalized into observer-only state

Patterns intentionally not used:

- native subagent restart recovery and native `AgentRunContext` liveness, because Codex/ACP has a separate durable thread/session identity and resume contract
- deleting ACP rows from the subagent registry, which would regress topology and child controls
- immediate session deletion after declaring loss; cleanup now requires a later pass and rechecks the active turn

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-delivery-state.test.ts src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-run-launch.test.ts src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-sweeper-recovery.test.ts src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-run-liveness.test.ts src/agents/subagents/spawn/acp-spawn.test.ts src/tasks/task-registry.test.ts`
  - 239 tests passed across 3 Vitest shards
- `pnpm tsgo`
- `pnpm tsgo:test`
- scoped `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check`

`pnpm check:changed` could not run because the local Crabbox binary failed its built-in version/help sanity check; the equivalent scoped formatting, lint, type, and focused test checks above passed.

prs.title: feat(gateway): let Gateway-authored agent messages mention people
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway features cannot add an agent message that @mentions a person. The planned guest welcome message needs to mention the inviter so they get an Inbox entry and the welcome session shows up under **Involving me**, but today only a human's own typed chat message can carry a mention, and the Control UI only renders mention chips in human messages.

## User Impact

No visible change on its own. This adds a trusted, Gateway-internal way to insert an agent message that mentions people on behalf of a signed-in profile, for the guest-onboarding welcome message (item 4) to use. When that runs, the mentioned person gets an Inbox entry ("<Guest> mentioned you") and the session appears in their Involving me list, and the agent's message shows the same person chip as a typed mention. No client or guest can request these messages, and who can create mentions from the client is unchanged.

This is item 5 of guest onboarding. Session creation, the welcome text and the first-sign-in trigger are separate PRs.

## Why This Change Was Made

`injectAssistantMessageWithHumanMentions` (`src/gateway/assistant-human-mentions.ts`) is called by Gateway code only, with no RPC method. It reuses the existing owners instead of adding a new mention path:

- Spans are checked with the same normalizer `chat.send` uses. A mention of the sender and incognito sessions are rejected before anything is written.
- The row is written through the existing `chat.inject` implementation, with `__openclaw.humanMentions` like a human message. That implementation moved unchanged into `chat-inject.ts` so both callers share it. It returns a result instead of responding, and it skips the live broadcast on an idempotent replay.
- After the write, the committed row goes to the existing Mention Inbox. The Inbox applies the current recipient policy (the recipient can read the session, is not the sender, and the session is not incognito) and records involvement and the Inbox entry, with the on-behalf-of profile as sender.
- The caller's idempotency key becomes both the transcript idempotency key and the Inbox source id. A retry replays the same row. If an earlier attempt stopped before Inbox delivery, the retry finishes it, without a second row, broadcast or alert.

In the Control UI, a chat bubble now accepts structured mentions on assistant rows as well as user rows. It uses the same span validation and the same person-reference component.

Accepted edge case: if a recipient can't read the session when the message is inserted, the message still keeps the chip in its text, but that person gets no Inbox entry or involvement. This is the same delivery-time check the Inbox already uses for typed mentions.

## Evidence

- New `src/gateway/assistant-human-mentions.test.ts` (real SQLite transcript, session store and Mention Inbox; 9 tests). It checks one assistant row with `humanMentions`, one Inbox entry from the on-behalf-of profile, recorded involvement, and a chat broadcast that carries the mention metadata. A retry returns `replayed` with no new row, broadcast or alert. An interrupted delivery is completed on retry. A recipient who can't read the session gets nothing. Self-mention, a span without an `@label`, no mentions, untrimmed text, a missing key and incognito sessions are all rejected before writing.
- `chat-message-markdown.test.tsx`: a Gateway-authored assistant row now renders the person chip. It rendered none on `origin/main`, where this case expected no chip. Tool results still render none. Existing `chat.inject` suites (`chat.directive-tags`, `chat.inject.parentid`) pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, plus oxlint and oxfmt on the touched files, all pass. An independent review (autoreview, branch vs `origin/main`) found no actionable issues.

- Test-only change in `chat-send-message-injection.isolated-gateway.test.ts`: the durable-steer test bounded its first `chat.send` at 1s, and that call timed out twice in Bun CI shard `agentic-gateway-methods-hosted-7` (its Gateway import alone took 27s). The other five tests in the file passed in the same process. The test now uses the default RPC timeout. It still fails if the acknowledgement waits for injection, because the older input is retired only after both sends. On a quiet local machine, the first `chat.send` took 4058ms and 1152ms on `origin/main`, against 1129ms and 515ms on this branch, so 1s is too tight on main as well. Importing `server-methods/chat.ts` under Bun took 1442–2149ms with this split and 1504–2104ms on the base, so the `chat-inject.ts` extraction does not slow loading. After the change the whole file passes 6/6 under both Node and Bun.

Screenshots: mocked Control UI, a Gateway-authored welcome message for guest Sam that mentions inviter Josh (synthetic data).

![Agent message on origin/main: @Josh is plain text](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ef77ecf4-ff85-49b9-9b93-4ecdbe7fd61b)

After

![Agent message with this change: @Josh renders as a person chip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/28dc4d86-2eec-471e-821a-4a6a858357e1)

Related: #167266. Parent: #171666. Followed by activation #168399; UI #171710 is a sibling on the backend.

Consume a saved answer in one native continuation under the original caller’s current authority. Claim custody at native admission, before execution; retain write-only completion receipts after an outage, and never repeat an uncertain admitted run. Restart recovery recognizes exact question-owned runs without suppressing a later ordinary turn or replacement session.

Head `031daa2bcd7cdb96ef5f342305bc3c8b7a76e8f2`, on backend `cea37a2cbdbdf36be0bc8672db3f5df20b77344c`; **41 paths, +4,306/−290**. Worker envelope classification lives in main’s current error owner; scalar retry classification is unchanged.

A real authenticated-member regression exposed an execution authority gap: a queued continuation could run after the original member became a viewer while a newly configured same-key store granted membership. The fix supplies the existing `executionSource` contract with retained mutation facts from the original physical conversation, checks its current membership and session generation through native effects, and applies current policy. Retained execution holders keep both facts and restored authority alive. Once execution ends, only write-only terminal receipt persistence remains. No worker API or schema was added.

The accepted final-status finding remains fixed: a nonthrowing `error` or `timeout` native final produces an interrupted receipt rather than false success. The answer stays saved; the user can start a new turn, and the attempt is not automatically replayed.

Validation: the preceding implementation passed **505 native cases** across continuation/readiness, worker errors, restart/admission, facade/operator authority and startup. After the execution repair, all **31 dispatcher cases** pass, including membership revocation after claim, allowed original-store access across a configured-store change, and retained owner lifetime. The revoked original member has an interrupted receipt, zero provider requests, no marker and zero final events despite B’s grant; the answer stays in A. Crash/lost-ACK also passes. The clean exact assembly passed strict readiness before/after and all owned processes joined.

The native Telegram recovery path retains its existing linked administrator contract; the authenticated non-admin member proof uses Gateway RPC. No broader channel authority is introduced. Fresh Telegram Test Server proof remains tracked on #168399; the current broker authentication prompt timed out before any lease was acquired. Earlier channel traces remain supporting evidence, not a fresh run of this head. Hosted CI must be assessed on this head. prs.title: fix(pr): keep in-flight landings working after dependency refreshes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native PR landings becoming stranded when main refreshes dependencies after their workflow binding was created. #182065 and #182046 were bound to main with dotenv 18.0.7; after #182010 installed 18.0.8, their next commands stopped at `the trust anchor requires 18.0.7` before acquiring a lock.

## User Impact

Maintainers can continue an admitted review or landing after a dependency refresh without downgrading a shared checkout or replacing its workflow binding. Exact-version checks and the original trusted workflow remain in force.

## Why This Change Was Made

The old recovery in `scripts/pr:533` (`pr_materialize_dependencies`) could only fast-forward and reinstall a separate tooling checkout. That cannot satisfy an older anchor. The wrapper now prepares an isolated frozen installation from the authenticated anchor commit, verifies the extracted source before lifecycle hooks execute, rechecks exact package versions, and pins the resolved package directories as before. It atomically publishes complete cache entries, reuses them, and sweeps old entries whose recorded consumers have exited. The forward-only refresh is removed; explicit tooling-root validation remains.

The cache key includes the full source tree, platform, architecture, and Node ABI. Using the full tree covers workspace manifests, patches, and install-hook inputs, at the cost of less sharing between source revisions with identical lockfiles. Concurrent first installs may duplicate work; only one complete entry survives. PID reuse can delay cleanup.

## Evidence

- The older-anchor regression fails on the baseline wrapper and passes with this fix. It asserts one install across two commands, including explicit and default tooling roots.
- All four new regression cases pass: older-anchor install/reuse, overlapping creators, changed manifest, and extra package hook. The workspace-only dependency case also fails before the staging-projection correction and passes with it.
- Targeted tooling typecheck, lint, formatting, shell syntax, and line-cap ratchet pass. The actual pre-commit hook passes on the exact staged candidate.
- Independent Codex reviews: no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- An unchanged workflow-retention test exceeded its existing 120-second limit in two local attempts (261 and 359 seconds under heavy host load). No timeout or test expectation was changed; broad validation remains with PR CI.

Production delta: +145 / −60 lines (net +85); tests: +153 / −100 (net +53). The added bootstrap owns frozen-install recovery; no new eager import is introduced.

Real historical-anchor proof completed against main commit `7b71c23797646bed71dc869b83a1c51764c267a6`: the normal frozen install reused 1,592 packages, including lifecycle scripts. On the final committed head, `scripts/pr ls` then exited 0 using the completed cache without reinstalling. The cached dotenv is 18.0.7; both the task checkout and shared tooling remain at 18.0.8.

CI is green on `f70c1ce062be4eb2cb564f5c6618da1dc1eaaf47`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40057330854. The exact-head watcher accepted eight superseded checks; current required gates succeeded.

Validation commands:

```sh
pnpm test test/scripts/pr-wrappers.test.ts test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'older anchor|creators overlap|unverified frozen install|keeps the admitted workflow after|PR wrapper inventory'
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.tooling.json --incremental
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json test/scripts/pr-wrappers.test.ts test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts scripts/pr-lib/materialize-dependencies.mjs
bash -n scripts/pr
```

The focused test command passed all four new cases and the import inventory; its exit was nonzero solely for the investigated local timeout described above. Typechecking, lint, syntax, formatting, line-cap ratchet, and pre-commit checks passed.

prs.title: fix(ci): await progress refresh steering before ending active work
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes scheduled compact CI failures when the progress-card test ends an active turn before its refresh has actually been steered.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The fixture exercises accepted steering and duplicate retries under the existing asynchronous acknowledgment contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

The handoff's #175837 attribution is unproven. The concrete race is at the fixture's active-run lifecycle: it awaits two refresh ACKs and immediately calls `finishDispatch()`, which completes the original operation. #181953 (`9434e42d61217cf263ee2d6d5e173fa55da4a38f`) moved steering admission after the ACK: “Durable custody precedes ACK; detached dispatch retains FIFO, current authority, refusal settlement, and exactly-once delivery.” Its raw parent-relative patch removes pre-ACK injection and starts it in detached dispatch instead. The queue-steering documentation explicitly says an ACK does not mean the runtime consumed the input.

When the fixture completes the operation first, steering correctly falls back to the standalone refresh. The dispatch stub writes no new card, so retry correctly returns `PROGRESS_CARD_REFRESH_TERMINAL`. This does not establish a product regression in #175837, nor an exact historical first-bad replay.

Wait for the backend's actual queue-acceptance signal before ending its operation. Preserve the accepted-retry, one-injection, no-question-answer, no-cancellation, no-chat, and no-standalone-dispatch assertions for both confirmed and unconfirmed receipts. No polling, timeout, retry, production changes, or new test-only production seam.

## Evidence

- Saved scheduled-main signature: [run 40050785381, compact-large-12](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40050785381/job/120742996833), also present in run 40047705637.
- Base `c19a52bf52b76c3982b0f44c3afa741b211523c2`, default pinned Bun: both `unconfirmed=false/true` cases reproduce the exact terminal-response assertion failure. All seven other progress tests pass.

Production delta: +0/-0. Test delta: +4/-0; no assertions removed or relaxed. The existing two receipt cases cover this fixture regression; no redundant test is added.

```sh
pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-list-persisted-worker.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/progress-card-refresh.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/progress-card-refresh.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-methods.json --noEmit
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-methods.json src/gateway/server-methods/progress-card-refresh.integration.test.ts
pnpm format:check src/gateway/server-methods/progress-card-refresh.integration.test.ts
git diff --check
```

Targeted tsrs typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Focused replay: **9/9 passed**, including both formerly failing receipt cases; 17.39 seconds of test bodies / 149.46 seconds wrapper wall time. Independent Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P1. PR CI supplies broad proof; CI seconds are pending. No merge requested.

prs.title: feat(liquid): add native Decision model provider
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/177044

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot select Liquid AI's native d1 or d1 Ultra Decision models with their Liquid credentials.

## User Impact

Adds a full `liquid` provider plugin with credential-only setup, model discovery, native text/JSON and single-image decisions, and documentation. Connecting it does not select or replace a chat model.

This is an unpublished development candidate. Authenticated hosted inference is not yet verified because no Liquid credential is available. Source merge and publication are separate: the first-party plugin must ship with a host release containing Decision V2 and the shared codec exports; this PR does not authorize independent publication.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider owns Liquid authentication, metadata and endpoint policy. It reuses the Decision V2 host, API-key onboarding and pooled provider HTTP transport. A shared SystemOne codec replaces OpenRouter's duplicate decoder without changing its wire contract. No new third-party dependency or core provider-specific routing is introduced.

Caller-prepared credentials, route prefixes, proxy/TLS policy, cancellation and authority checks remain intact. Undeclared endpoint overrides cannot inherit native capabilities. Unsupported inherited parameters are rejected. Native distributions and scores are preserved; missing costs are not invented.

The integration is resolved against pinned main `7b71c23797646bed71dc869b83a1c51764c267a6`. Package, catalog and host compatibility metadata align with that development revision. Generated inventory/config baselines and SDK export counts reflect the actual plugin surface.

Contract sources: [Liquid API](https://docs.liquid.ai/lfm/models/d1), [Decision models](https://docs.liquid.ai/lfm/models/decision-models), [TypeSafe wire types](https://github.com/typesafe-ai/typesafe-sdk-js/blob/main/src/types.ts).

## Evidence

- Current signed head: `10567484f1cdcc2a669a4dcc2d410c51dcb9a0c3`, tree `2a133c10d8bb36d84ff324d5d96792a352d4a79f`. Relative to the tested source below, only the two canonical generated baseline files changed. The configured commit hooks passed in the task-owned full checkout.
- [Blacksmith Testbox build and focused proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40055970712): source `124b7d9f7a908d2acfb831347be5792374b4a610`, tree `f49c9a8bc83326794dd5b721d85be479e79a9b8c`, lease `tbx_01m5nx5j5q567xp3bswp06y1f6`. Wrapper exit 0; cleanup settled.
- `pnpm build`, `pnpm config:docs:gen` and `pnpm config:docs:check` passed. The two tracked config baselines are the exact generated artifacts from this run, not hand-written hashes.
- Focused test wrapper passed four shards in 60.48 seconds: Liquid adapter/setup, registered-plugin HTTP integration, manifest catalog, shared codec, Decision validation/compatibility/admission/preparation.
- The registered real plugin, SQLite auth profile and guarded HTTP transport dispatched the authorized request with its expected native body, bearer credential and declared prefix. Forbidden callers, undeclared routes and revocation before physical dispatch produced no additional completed HTTP request. Chat selection remained unchanged. This is real local-server boundary proof, not authenticated hosted inference.
- Adapter cases cover both configured models, image/body bounds, inherited parameters, prepared credentials/custom transport, revocation, HTTP failures, bounded responses and awaited cancellation. Shared-codec cases preserve OpenRouter behavior.
- Independent full-diff P0-P2 review: scoped-clean, no actionable findings, confidence 0.83. The merge audit found and repaired the catalog compatibility-floor mismatch. Exact-head hosted CI remains pending for the updated commit.
- Production TypeScript: net +260 lines; SDK accounting tooling: net +2. Tests: +803. Growth implements the native provider and shared public codec; 93 duplicated OpenRouter decoder lines were removed.

### Review Follow-Through

Prior SDK accounting, config baseline, route/SSRF, credential-only setup and registered transport requests are covered by source and the focused proof above. The release-floor concern is handled through coordinated host/plugin publication, not an invented future version. Authenticated inference remains an explicit unclosed evidence gap. Current vendor docs also list d1.1; continued hosted acceptance of the older d1 identifier needs live catalog qualification. No throughput, latency or model-quality claim is made.

Release note: add native Liquid AI d1 and d1 Ultra Decision models with separate credentials and no chat-default changes.

## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in chat or dashboard deep-link reload repeatedly recalculates unchanged sidebar styles.

**Experiment rejected: both native-style timing primaries fail. Do not land this experiment.**

## User Impact

No change is landing. The candidate met the diagnostic count target, but not the declared timing confidence required for a reload performance change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native invalidation trace identifies two avoidable sources: inherited scroller-mask intermediates and five managed-background selectors containing a universal descendant compound. The candidate removes both inherited intermediates and scopes the background condition to the actual chat surfaces. Production delta: +22/−20, net **+2 LOC**, preserving the two-layer scrollbar mask and RTL placement. No new state, cache, config option, or scheduling owner.

## Evidence

One AWS c7a.4xlarge, lease `cbx_6054bc1f4c52`, 16 vCPUs (AMD EPYC 9R14), approximately 31 GiB usable RAM; one comparison at a time. Node 26.12.1, pnpm 12.15.0, repo Playwright 1.64.1 / headless Chromium 156.0.8078.4. Gate-start host loads and per-run load averages are retained. No other campaign runs shared the lease.

Pinned measurement base: `777007b662d0` (full SHA in downloaded/head.txt). Candidate: the archived combined.patch applied to that base. Its three production CSS file hashes match the experiment commit; the public branch was rebased before push and also includes newer unrelated main changes. These numbers qualify the pinned comparison, not a later full-head build.

Production Team-scale UI and synthetic mock-Gateway transport served through the existing benchmark; warmed HTTP and scoped browser state, service workers blocked, 1719×1179 viewport, literal full-UUID chat and dashboard deep links pinned before every reload. This does not measure real authentication/proxy/server latency. No real account, operator browser, Gateway state, or private Team capture was used.

Primary acceptance was recorded before comparisons: ≤2.5 sidebar-row resolutions per final element (diagnostic target), and native RecalcStyleDuration improves on BOTH routes in 11 unprofiled interleaved baseline/candidate pairs, with favorable non-overlapping IQRs OR ≥9/11 negative paired deltas with median paired delta <0. Secondary regression: adverse non-overlapping IQRs OR ≥9/11 adverse pairs and median rise >max(10 ms, 3%). No rule was relaxed after measurement.

The timing gate uses committed `--latency-profile live-fast`: challenge floor 439 ms, connect 41 ms, chat.startup 220 ms, message subscription 183 ms, resolve 216 ms, plus the other committed per-method floors. These are browser-delivery floors, not isolated server timings. Earlier 340/50 diagnostic captures are retained separately for L184/L187 comparison.

Main-target native Performance.getMetrics counters were sampled around reload without tracing or profiling during the 44 gate runs. Separate debug-selector/invalidation captures establish scope; their timestamps and durations are heavily inflated, alter races, and are not performance results.


All values below are milliseconds, median [Q1–Q3]. Paired Δ is candidate minus baseline; its median need not equal the difference of medians.

Chat first-paint medians move 808 → 1008 ms while the paired median is −16 ms: the distributions are bimodal, IQRs overlap, and pair signs are mixed. This is disclosed, not smoothed or excluded. No secondary meets the declared regression rule. Neither native timing result proves an inherent performance floor or that the CSS correction has zero effect; it fails the predeclared confidence rule.

## Resolution counts and causal owners

| Route | Baseline resolutions | Candidate resolutions | Final sidebar elements | Resolutions/element |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| chat | 7,394 | 2,986 | 1,548 → 1,548 | 4.78 → 1.93 |
| dashboard | 7,452 | 3,054 | 1,548 → 1,548 | 4.81 → 1.97 |

Diagnostic count target: PASS on both routes. Counts include native pseudo-style resolutions; final element counts exclude pseudo-elements. The denominator follows L187 and includes only final sidebar-row elements. It is not the number of distinct node lifetimes: cached/live construction replaces some descendants. Every raw resolved node ID and ancestor mapping is retained in passes.json. Narrow animation/avatar counts differ between captures because profiling changes scheduling.

The baseline has three inherited-mask passes, with 897 + 783 + 1,851 = 3,531 row resolutions, plus a background-marker pass with 930. The correction removes the two inherited mask intermediates and moves the five managed-background ancestor conditions outside the universal descendant compound. Native invalidation explicitly named all five original selectors and `allDescendantsMightBeInvalid: true`; a controlled native reproduction falls 329 → 6 total style computations with identical computed chat paints. The mask reproduction falls 66 → 2, with no descendant computation.

The remaining large passes construct cached rows and then live row children. Smaller passes update needed row control attributes, avatar pending/fallback presentation, and running indicators. No virtualization, content-visibility, cache, state, or scheduling layer was introduced. No additional row-wide pass in these captures is established as a hover/focus, media/container-query, or late-stylesheet-attachment problem; the native reasons and stacks, rather than coincident network arrivals, drive the classification.


### Proof and stop decision

Two focused native Chromium regressions passed locally and on AWS. Background work-count regression is red on original CSS (329 computations) and green on the correction; controlled work is 329 → 6 with identical computed chat paints. The mask reproduction is 66 → 2. Remote pnpm command wall times: background 7.23 s; mask 3.33 s. Combined Codex autoreview is clean through P2. Both production builds passed.

Production files: `ui/src/styles/chat/grouped.css`, `ui/src/styles/chat/composer-surface.css`, `ui/src/styles/layout.css`. Regressions: `ui/src/styles/background-invalidation.node.test.ts`, `ui/src/styles/sidebar-scroll-mask.node.test.ts` (+108 test LOC).

Stopped after the primary failure: zero-diff screenshot matrix, sidebar keyboard e2e, affected background e2e, full UI e2e, and changed-file/typecheck checks were not run. CI on head `4bcc01ff393192218a812f3965e0a8f4a5ae7267` was skipped because this remained a draft; it is not green CI. No executed CI reds need classification against main. No screenshots, private captures, or real account data were uploaded.

Measurement base: `777007b662d0`; the same three candidate CSS file hashes were verified against the experiment commit. AWS lease `cbx_6054bc1f4c52` is released, independently verified `state=released`, `hasHost=false`. No local Gateway was started. The initial setup omitted a required probe and failed before measurement; it was supplied and all accepted samples used the same lease. Failed setup contributes no samples.

The combined candidate remains parked under the predeclared reload gate. L184 can proceed independently under its steady-state scroll count contract. No merge or gate exception is requested.

prs.title: fix(ci): wait for active progress refresh steering to settle
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes CI failures when the progress-card refresh fixture ends an active run before its accepted steering input finishes persisting.

## User Impact

Internal test repair; no runtime behavior change. Both confirmed and unconfirmed steering cases retain their existing retry, visibility and cancellation assertions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The refresh ACK precedes native steering completion. Ending the incumbent immediately invalidates the in-flight input's authority and caches a terminal error. Wait for the accepted source to settle before completing that run.

## Evidence

- Reproduced both failures from [scheduled main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40050785381/job/120742996833) on the unchanged base.
- All 9 progress-card refresh integration tests pass with this repair.
- Gateway-methods test typecheck, targeted lint, formatting and diff checks pass.
- Independent review found no actionable issues.

prs.title: feat(session-share): filter by person and open original sessions
prs.body:
Closes #156697

## What Problem This Solves

Session Share needs a way to narrow selected shared groups to one person's sessions and return from a read-only shared transcript to its writable original.

## User Impact

Source operators must select nonempty exact `share.groups`. Optional `share.involvingProfileId` narrows those groups to sessions with that canonical owner or a profile participant; mentions alone never qualify. Missing or invalid selectors publish nothing. **Person-only configuration does not publish sessions.** Existing private/draft/spawn exclusions remain.

On the receiver, configure `nodes.<nodeId>.controlUiOrigin` and, when applicable, `controlUiBasePath` to offer **Open original** in the shared-session menu and transcript. It opens the exact source session in a separate tab without URL credentials, opener, or referrer. Source sign-in, permissions, and queues remain authoritative; Session Share remains read-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The approved publication boundary is selected groups AND optional canonical owner/participant matching, not Activity mention matching. The source rechecks current configuration and session identity across asynchronous list/read boundaries; the receiver withdraws stale fresh-only rows while refreshes are pending. Existing bounded snapshot scheduling and sidebar window ownership are preserved.

The receiver owns the validated source origin/base path. Canonical session routing preserves literal main/workspace/global keys and raw-global source-agent identity. Original navigation now lives in the maintained Solid catalog-menu owner, with its existing action validation, reactive translations, focus and disposal behavior. No new remote write command or protocol-version change is introduced.

This PR interaction is not inherited-main red or hosted Bun27 proof.

prs.title: fix(ci): align persisted session checks with live child control
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes scheduled compact CI failures in `sessions-list-persisted-worker.test.ts` after #181117.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The worker tests enforce the intended distinction between durable parent lineage and live execution control.

## Why This Change Was Made

#181117 states that “terminal and unowned controller snapshots do not confer control.” Its merge commit `4e26493aafd06079dc94195f03b871bba6c3c618` changed `resolveSessionChildOwners` to obtain control only from a current executor/reservation. This fixture contains a terminal run whose requester differs from its controller, without stored lineage to that controller. Expecting that controller's `childSessions` to contain the child was stale.

Assert `childSessions: undefined` explicitly rather than omitting the assertion. Preserve the exact swarm totals, current metadata, privacy, pagination, payload-redaction, embedded Gateway/TUI, and concurrent plugin-state-write checks. No production changes or new test machinery; test delta +3/-2 lines.

## Evidence

- Saved scheduled-main signature: [run 40050785381, compact-small-25](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40050785381/job/120742996954), also present in the two older handoff runs.
- Reproduced on base `c19a52bf52b76c3982b0f44c3afa741b211523c2` using the default pinned Bun runtime: both session-list assertions fail exactly as CI; its privacy case passes. The same command also reproduces the separate progress-refresh failure, which is excluded from this PR.

```sh
pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-list-persisted-worker.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/progress-card-refresh.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-list-persisted-worker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

pnpm format:check src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-list-persisted-worker.test.ts
git diff --check
```

Focused replay: **3/3 passed**, 6.94 seconds of test bodies / 183.22 seconds wrapper wall time (worker graph preparation dominates). Targeted tsrs typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Independent Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P1. PR CI supplies broad proof; CI seconds are pending. No merge requested.

- `@solidjs/web@2.0.0-rc.16`: move the shared select-insertion callback to module scope so it cannot share the first select's closure context. Keep lazy activation, immediate selection, option-arrival handling, and the microtask retry.
- `@solidjs/signals@2.0.0-rc.16`: include staged computations in the existing disposal scheduling condition. The ordinary coalesced drain clears retired pending owners; no synchronous flush, per-disposal queue scan, or Workboard workaround is added.

Both packages were published from `solidjs/solid` branch `next`, commit `b0ad1df505b835058a4b3750ab37d6576bb18c01`. Patch removal gates are recorded in `patches/README.md`. These are retention counts, not a latency benchmark or a claim of an unlimited-session memory plateau.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the two Windows fixture cleanup cases in `openclaw-test-state.test.ts` that reach the 120-second test timeout after #180495.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. State fixture cleanup keeps unrelated databases alive without leaving a reopened SQLite database behind. Timeouts, retries, and existing assertions are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sibling auth seed used the active fixture's environment even though its agent database lived under the sibling directory. Its retained agent lease therefore belonged to the fixture's shared database. After the fixture was removed, closing that sibling auth database reopened the fixture's shared database to release the lease. macOS can unlink the open database; Windows cannot, leaving recursive removal retrying against live SQLite files.

The incorrect seed environment predates #180495. That consolidation exposed it by replacing explicit handle cleanup, which closed the reopened shared database afterward, with scoped sibling cleanup. Scope auth seeding to the same environment used by the other sibling handles. Extend both existing cases to assert that sibling cleanup never recreates the removed fixture root.

The pr-simplify pass kept this to one test file: 6 added / 2 removed lines, zero production changes, and no additional test cases or cleanup abstraction.

## Evidence

- Saved Windows evidence: [last passing run 39763877916](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39763877916), head `240a90ef9f95`, has the two cases at 382 / 355 ms. prs.title: fix(cli): restore archived sessions
prs.body:
Closes #124491

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the CLI, Gateway lifecycle contract, focused tests, public docs, and a real isolated Gateway run.

## What Problem This Solves

Headless users could archive a session with the stock CLI but could not restore it. Once archived, a fixed routing key rejected new work and told the operator to restore it, while the CLI offered only destructive deletion.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `openclaw sessions restore <keys...>` to the existing lifecycle command family. It calls the same `sessions.patch` operation used by the Control UI with the caller-observed session identity and `archived: false`; no new Gateway protocol, persistence, compatibility path, or configuration is introduced.

Restore supports the existing agent, Gateway credential, timeout, JSON, multi-key, and dry-run options. Active sessions return `already_active`, and an archived row without durable identity is refused before mutation. The Sessions CLI reference now documents the non-destructive restore flow alongside archive and delete.

## User Impact

CLI and SSH operators can resume archived sessions safely under the same routing key without deleting transcripts or invoking raw Gateway RPC.

## Evidence

Focused validation after rebasing onto current main:

```text

Tests: 52 passed (52)
```

Documentation validation:

```text

```

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes turns that remain busy when OpenAI Responses repeatedly sends bookkeeping events without advancing output.

## User Impact

Responses now uses a fixed 15-minute no-progress ceiling, or the effective idle budget when larger. Real output or reasoning progress resets it; ordinary network silence keeps the existing idle budget. This selected tradeoff gives legitimate hidden-reasoning phases a long window while bounding recovery from a permanently nonproductive stream. No configuration or migration is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

prs.title: fix(workboard): finalize running execution on terminal status transitions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workboard dispatch slots could be permanently starved by stale execution state and uncleared dispatch claims, blocking follow-up work for the same owner agent.

Two related bugs caused this:

1. **Stale running execution on terminal transitions**: When a card left `running` status via `releaseClaim`, generic `updateCard`, `move`, or `reassign` (paths that don't pass an explicit execution patch), the execution record stayed `running`. The dispatcher's capacity predicate then counted the card as occupying the owner's slot indefinitely.

2. **Dispatch claim not released on lifecycle success**: `syncLifecycle` mapped the card to `review` and execution to `review` on lifecycle success, but did not clear `card.metadata.claim`. `workboardCardConsumesOwnerSlot` still counted the active (non-expired) claim against the owner's capacity, so the next ready card for that owner was blocked until the claim's TTL expired (30 minutes by default).

Closes #122911.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Fix 1: Finalize running execution on terminal status transitions only

`updateCard` (`store-core.ts`) is the shared owner for execution lifecycle. It already had logic to sync session keys, but lacked the symmetric finalization for execution status. The fix adds a finalization step: when a card transitions from `running` to a **terminal** status (`done`/`review`/`blocked`) without an explicit execution patch, the execution status is closed to match the card's terminal state. `done`/`review` are successful outcomes (attempt succeeds, `failureCount` resets); `blocked` is an explicit failure or abandonment path.

Non-terminal statuses (`todo`, `backlog`, `triage`, `scheduled`, `ready`) preserve execution occupancy so a worker moved aside can still complete successfully. The original broad condition (`status !== "running"`) incorrectly finalized executions for non-terminal moves, causing `completeDirect` to retain `blocked` on later successful completions (ClawSweeper P1 re-review).

The dispatcher's unguarded `card.execution?.status === "running"` capacity arm was removed — with execution now finalized at the owner, legacy stale rows no longer need a downstream guard.

### Fix 2: Release terminal review claims before capacity counting (ClawSweeper P1)

`syncLifecycle` (`store.ts`) is the lifecycle owner that transitions the card to terminal-for-dispatch status (`review`/`blocked`). The claim must be released at this boundary so the owner's slot is freed immediately, not after claim TTL expiry. Without this, `normalizeMetadata`'s fallback preserved the stale claim, and `workboardCardConsumesOwnerSlot` counted it against capacity.

The fix clears `card.metadata.claim` in `syncLifecycle` when the card transitions to any non-running, non-done status. `workboardCardConsumesOwnerSlot` (`store-constants.ts`) additionally excludes `review`/`blocked` claims as defense-in-depth, covering legacy rows where `syncLifecycle` did not clear the claim before this fix shipped.

### Production LOC delta

- `store-core.ts`: +19/-1 (execution finalization at the shared owner, terminal-only)
- `store.ts`: +15/-0 (claim release at the lifecycle owner)
- `store-constants.ts`: +7/-4 (defense-in-depth capacity exclusion)
- `dispatcher.test.ts`: +12/-4 (updated review-slot test)
- `dispatcher-ownership.test.ts`: +5/-2 (use non-terminal status for claim-expiry test)

Production: +41/-5 net +36 across 3 lifecycle owners. Tests: +703/-6 net +697.

Each change lives at its architectural owner — `updateCard` owns execution lifecycle, `syncLifecycle` owns claim lifecycle, `workboardCardConsumesOwnerSlot` owns capacity semantics. The terminal-only narrowing absorbs the ClawSweeper P1 finding without expanding the production surface: the broad `status !== "running"` condition and `finalizedExecutionStatus` ternary were replaced by a direct terminal-status check, keeping net production LOC proportional to the three owners repaired.

## User Impact

Workboard dispatch recovers immediately when a worker finishes or fails — no 30-minute starvation window. Follow-up cards for the same owner agent dispatch as soon as the lifecycle transition completes. Legacy cards with stale claims (from before this fix) also no longer hold slots. Moving a running card aside to a non-terminal status (e.g., `todo`) no longer corrupts the execution record — the worker can still complete successfully and the attempt is recorded as `succeeded`. This is a default-path fix: every operator using workboard dispatch was affected.

No config, API, default, protocol, or schema change; existing operator behavior is unchanged except that stale executions are now finalized and stale slots are released.

## Evidence

Linux, Node 22 (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` wrapper).

Rebased onto current main. The dispatcher's unguarded `card.execution?.status === "running"` capacity arm is removed at its canonical helper location in `store-constants.ts`, so both `dispatcher.ts` and `sqlite-store.ts` call sites are repaired in one change.

### Focused proof (two files, 46 tests)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/workboard/src/dispatcher-ownership.test.ts \

prs.title: fix(sessions): drain archive retention across bounded pages
prs.body:
Closes #181722

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `doctor` keeps reporting retention-deleted transcript archive copies as missing when archive retention spans more than one 256-row page.

## User Impact

Operators no longer see permanent stale `Missing ... canonical transcript archive file(s)` warnings after ordinary retention. Later eligible rows are no longer starved by an older retained prefix.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retention previously read one 256-row page and filtered it after selection. It now walks bounded pages, advances only past rows intentionally retained, and drains each page in 16-row write batches. Both worker and native SQLite paths accept the page offset. Doctor warnings for genuinely unexplained missing copies and cold-storage history are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Reproduction through the production retention path

The proof seeds a 300-row retained prefix with published files, then 20 later retention-eligible rows with no file. It closes the database, runs the production `sweepCronRunSessions()` owner with `resetArchiveRetention: "1h"` and cron retention `1ms`, then runs `openclaw doctor --fix` and reads the archive table again.

```text
sweepLogs=["[object Object] cron-reaper: pruned 1 expired cron run session(s)"]
sweep {"swept":true,"pruned":1}
after code=0
[state-migrations] Auto-migrated legacy state:
- Migrated canonical transcript archive media in .../openclaw-agent.sqlite: 300 archive(s).
rows total=301 retained=300 expired=0
```

Doctor scanned the remaining 300 archives and emitted no `Missing ... canonical transcript archive file(s)` warning. The 300 retained-prefix rows remain; the 20 later missing rows were drained. One additional row is the cron trigger archive created while exercising the reaper.

### Issue dataset

The `tre1d` measurement from #181722: an earlier weekly archive held 822 copies, one day contributed 762, and the later archive held none of those 822. There were 605 manifest/blob rows with missing files (234 / 326 / 45 per agent); every publish recorded success. Rebuilding all 605 files produced 605 writes and 0 SHA-256 mismatches.

### Regression coverage

- **Base-red (`7845dd3e`):** new regressions fail with `expected 256 to be 258` and `expected 0 to be 20`.
- **Head-green (`7e053421`):** both regressions pass; the full retention file passes `8/8`.
- **Acceptance set:** 6 affected suites pass, 83 tests total (`session-history-archive-retention`, archive-pruning admission, page-reclamation binding, session reaper, cleanup missing-file handling, and transcript-directive migration).
- `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`, `oxlint`, and `oxfmt --check` pass.
- `pnpm build:runtime`: TypeScript runtime and tsdown phases completed. The final UI phase failed because this host lacks the unrelated `libdeflate` package.

No UI changes.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted implementation and validation under contributor direction and review.

prs.title: fix(agents): report an exhausted structured_output retry budget instead of the stale error
prs.body:
Closes #181442

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a collector child that has spent its one `structured_output` retry gets the previous attempt's validation error back for every later call, even when the new payload is schema-valid, so the model reads a stale verdict as a rejection of the payload it just sent.

A collector child (`sessions_spawn collect=true` with `outputSchema`) gets one corrective retry. Once that retry is spent (`invalidAttempts >= 2`), the exhausted branch in `src/agents/tools/structured-output-tool.ts` returned the stored `schemaError` before validating anything. In the reporter's batch, 5 of 5 collector runs ended `failed` this way after the child had produced valid output.

## User Impact

User impact: a collector child that keeps calling `structured_output` after its retry budget is spent is now told that the budget is exhausted and that the call was not evaluated, instead of being shown an error that describes an earlier payload. Parents see no change: `agents_wait` completions, the two-attempt limit and the stored validation state are identical.

## Why This Change Was Made

The exhausted branch now says what actually happened: the retry budget is spent, this call was not evaluated, and the run completes without a structured result. The reply keeps the last validation error as context inside the message but no longer presents it as `schemaError` for the new call.

```json
{
  "status": "rejected",
  "success": false,
  "reason": "retry_budget_exhausted",
  "error": "structured_output retry budget exhausted: this call was not evaluated and the run completes without a structured result. Last validation error: <previous schemaError>"
}
```

Unchanged on purpose: the two-attempt limit, the frozen registry state (`invalidAttempts`, `schemaError`), the registry publication guard, and the collector completion that reports `schemaError` through `agents_wait`. No state is written on the exhausted path before or after this change. The documented recovery contract in `docs/tools/swarm.md` gains one sentence describing the exhausted reply.

## Evidence

- `src/agents/tools/structured-output-tool.test.ts` ("nudges once then freezes schemaError"): the valid third call must carry `reason: "retry_budget_exhausted"`, an `error` saying it was not evaluated, no `schemaError` field, and leave the frozen state untouched. Red on the base (5 parameter rows fail: the base reply has `schemaError` and no `reason`), green with the fix (16 passed).
- Consumer tests green with the fix: `agents-wait-tool.test.ts`, `agent-tools.collector.integration.test.ts`, `swarm-tools.integration.test.ts`, `subagent-spawn.profiles.production-boundary.test.ts` (exercises the real spawned tool through the production tool construction path, including the one-retry rejection), `openclaw-tools.swarm.test.ts`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `git diff --check`: see the CI lanes on this head.

### Live run with a real model (real Gateway, fix vs. fix reverted)

Setup: an isolated Gateway from this source tree; the parent agent runs on a scripted local model that only does `sessions_spawn collect=true` with the issue's `outputSchema` and then `agents_wait`; the collector child runs on **anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5** (a separate `worker` agent) with the task "call `structured_output` three times with these arguments, in this order". The worker's tool calls and tool replies below are read from its transcript store after the run. Same run on the base with only `structured-output-tool.ts` reverted.

Child transcript, base (fix reverted):

```
#6  text  I'll execute this tool-behavior test by making the three structured_output calls in order.
#6  call  {"result":"x"}
#7  reply {"status":"error","tool":"structured_output","error":"structured_output validation failed: <root>: must be object. Retry once with a corrected final result."}
#9  call  {"result":{"result":"x"}}
#10 reply {"status":"rejected","success":false,"schemaError":"findings: must have required property 'findings'; already_declared: must have required property 'already_declared'; excluded: must have required property 'excluded'"}
#12 text  I'll now make the third call with the complete schema:
#12 call  {"result":{"result":"x","findings":1,"already_declared":0,"excluded":0}}
#13 reply {"status":"rejected","success":false,"schemaError":"findings: must have required property 'findings'; already_declared: must have required property 'already_declared'; excluded: must have required property 'excluded'"}
#15 text  DONE
```

Child transcript, fix (calls and replies 1 and 2 identical to the base):

```
#12 call  {"result":{"result":"x","findings":1,"already_declared":0,"excluded":0}}
#13 reply {"status":"rejected","success":false,"reason":"retry_budget_exhausted","error":"structured_output retry budget exhausted: this call was not evaluated and the run completes without a structured result. Last validation error: findings: must have required property 'findings'; already_declared: must have required property 'already_declared'; excluded: must have required property 'excluded'"}
#15 text  DONE
```

Parent `agents_wait` completion, identical on base and fix apart from run ids and usage:

```
{"completed":[{"runId":"…","status":"failed","result":"DONE","schemaError":"findings: must have required property 'findings'; already_declared: must have required property 'already_declared'; excluded: must have required property 'excluded'","sessionKey":"agent:worker:subagent:…","usage":{"inputTokens":259,"outputTokens":1045}}],"pending":[]}
```

The same scenario with a scripted stand-in for the child (deterministic, no provider) gives byte-identical tool replies; it is kept in the author's bench scripts and was the first version of this proof.

prs.title: fix(cron): follow-up wait drops subagent results or overruns when the wall clock jumps
prs.body:
Related: openclaw/openclaw#175040, openclaw/openclaw#171097 (merged monotonic-clock precedents); complements open PR openclaw/openclaw#180554.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: cron follow-up replies from subagents are silently dropped, or a finished cron run keeps holding its gateway execution slot, when the host wall clock jumps while the run is waiting for descendant subagent results.

## User Impact

User impact: scheduled-task follow-up output survives wall-clock corrections (NTP sync, VM suspend/resume) instead of vanishing, and cron runs no longer exceed their configured wait budget after a backward clock jump.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cron isolated-agent follow-up derives its descendant-wait deadline from `Date.now()` and compares the wall clock against that deadline in every loop (drain loop, grace polling, gateway timeout clamp, catch path). A forward jump makes `Date.now() >= deadline` true immediately, so the wait is abandoned before subagent results are collected; a backward jump keeps the wait alive far past `timeoutMs`. The deadline is a pure in-process duration budget, so it is now measured with the monotonic clock (`performance.now()`), and the remaining budget is handed to `waitForAgentRunsToDrain` as a duration (`timeoutMs`) instead of a wall-clock epoch. The drain's own contract is unchanged; open PR #180554 converts the drain internals separately, and the two changes compose in either order.

## Evidence

### Before fix

Clock-jump reproduction (fake timers, never-draining yielded descendant, 1000ms budget) on `origin/main`:

- Control: wait gives up at ~1000ms as budgeted.
- Forward jump (+60s) after 100ms: wait abandons at ~300ms of monotonic time — subagent results are dropped.
- Backward jump (-60s) after 500ms: wait is still holding the run after 4000ms of monotonic time against the 1000ms budget.

The two new regression tests fail on the base commit:
- `does not abandon the wait when the wall clock jumps forward mid-wait` — settles early (`settled === true` after the jump).
- `does not extend the wait when the wall clock jumps backward mid-wait` — still waiting after 400ms of a 300ms budget (`settled === false`).

### After fix

- `subagent-followup.test.ts`: 24/24 pass, including the two new clock-jump regression tests (forward jump no longer abandons the wait at 250ms of a 300ms budget; backward jump no longer extends it past 400ms).
- `run-oxlint.mjs` on both changed files: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `oxfmt --check`: clean.
- `tsgo` core lane: 0 errors in the changed files (the lane reports pre-existing, unrelated `src/tui`/`src/process(darwin)` errors in this environment; unchanged by this diff).
- Sibling cron tests (`subagent-followup.worker.test.ts`, `delivery-dispatch.*.test.ts`) fail in this environment with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` from missing native/dev packages; verified the identical failure class on a clean `origin/main` worktree, so it is a pre-existing environment gap, not a regression.

### What was not tested

- Real VM suspend/resume or live NTP step (simulated via fake-timer clock jumps).
- Gateway e2e (the change is pure in-process duration-budget logic covered by the unit regressions).

prs.title: fix(goals): count tokens from post-creation baseline
prs.body:
## Summary

- start Goal token-budget accounting from the first fresh post-creation token snapshot instead of importing earlier session usage
- accumulate subsequent usage from a persisted cursor, rebasing safely across counter resets and saturating at safe-integer bounds
- advance Goal accounting from CLI session finalization while preserving concurrent durable Goal changes
- keep `/goal status` and `get_goal` projections read-only and align scoped/global session-store routing
- reject token budgets that are not positive safe integers

## What Problem This Solves

A new Goal could inherit cumulative token usage from before Goal creation. For example, a fresh post-creation snapshot could be compared with an older or stale creation-time value and immediately exhaust a new budget.

The session token total is a snapshot that can cross accounting epochs (including compaction/reset), so repeatedly subtracting one absolute `tokenStart` is not reliable.

## Approach

`SessionGoal` now carries an optional `tokenCursor`:

1. The first persisted fresh snapshot after Goal creation establishes `tokenStart` and `tokenCursor` with zero charged usage.
2. Later fresh snapshots add only positive deltas from the cursor.
3. Equal snapshots are idempotent; lower snapshots rebase the cursor without reducing accumulated usage.
4. Legacy Goals reconstruct a cursor from `tokenStart + tokensUsed` where safe.
5. Goal resume/reset opens a new accounting window at the current fresh snapshot when one is available.

CLI session finalization projects accounting after fresh usage metadata is assembled and before concurrent snapshot reconciliation, allowing compatible token metadata to advance without overwriting concurrent Goal edits, completion, replacement, or clearing.

## Regression coverage

- stale/missing creation baseline followed by fresh snapshots
- incremental charging (33,107 → 33,124 charges exactly 17)
- duplicate and decreasing snapshots
- safe-integer validation and saturation
- legacy Goal migration and resume charging
- read-only status/tool projections
- global and scoped session-store routing
- CLI persistence and concurrent durable Goal changes

## Evidence

- `src/agents/command/session-store.test.ts` + `src/agents/tools/goal-tools.test.ts`: 67 passed
- `src/config/sessions/goals.test.ts`: 19 passed
- `src/tui/embedded-backend.test.ts`: 60 passed
- `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-goal.test.ts`: 10 passed
- `oxfmt --check`: passed
- type-aware `oxlint --deny-warnings`: 0 warnings/errors
- core `tsgo`: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed

## Scope

This is intentionally limited to Goal accounting and its persistence/status surfaces. It does not change global context/token limits or redesign session usage accounting.

## Redacted live behavior proof

An isolated live session was exercised against a deployed patched OpenClaw `2026.7.1-2` runtime implementing this accounting path. Identifiers, local paths, endpoints, and deployment hashes are omitted. This demonstrates the after-fix behavior; it does not claim that this PR head is already shipped upstream.

```text
Goal created after the session already had historical usage:
  session totalTokens: 32987 (fresh)
  Goal tokenStart: 0
  Goal tokenStartFresh: false
  Goal tokensUsed: 0
  Goal tokenBudget: 30000

First fresh post-creation snapshot:
  session totalTokens: 33110
  Goal tokenStart: 33110
  Goal tokenCursor: 33110
  Goal tokensUsed: 0

Next fresh snapshot:
  session totalTokens: 33133
  Goal tokenCursor: 33133
  Goal tokensUsed: 23
  observed charge: 33133 - 33110 = 23

Later fresh process readback:
  session totalTokens: 33339
  Goal tokenStart: 33110
  Goal tokenCursor: 33339
  Goal tokensUsed: 229
  cumulative charge: 33339 - 33110 = 229
```

The same acceptance also verified:

- `/goal status` and `get_goal` returned the same accounting state.
- Direct read-only status calls left the persisted Goal unchanged before vs. after the calls.
- A separate process reread the same persisted `tokenStart`, `tokenCursor`, and `tokensUsed` values.
- Focused regression tests cover legacy cursor reconstruction/resume behavior and concurrent durable Goal replacement/completion/clear preservation; the live transcript above specifically proves post-creation baselining and later delta charging.

prs.title: fix(update): verify Windows Doctor-restored Gateway readiness
prs.body:
Refs #170956. Thanks @Rene-F for the detailed Windows repair follow-up.

## What Problem This Solves

Windows `openclaw update repair` can say the restored Gateway's readiness was not verified after only 60 seconds, while that Scheduled Task is still starting normally.

## User Impact

Doctor restoration now uses the same Windows cold-start allowance as Gateway start/restart. Explicit timeouts and attempt limits, other platforms, and definitive failure checks retain their behavior. No configuration, dependency, or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor already called the shared readiness owner, but supplied no budget. Start/restart supplied the canonical Windows budget, while the shared owner's fallback still used 60 seconds. The fallback now consumes the existing Windows timing owner.

Current main already acknowledges abandoned history without a target build after successful repair (#153291, with further repair-driver settlement in #178292). The original failed outcome remains recorded; acknowledgment retires Doctor's repair prompt. The second Doctor repair pass is already conditional on plugin changes, deferred model retirement, or unfinished plugin migrations. The reporter's unfinished plugin migrations require that fresh convergence pass, so this PR keeps it. Repair does not yet share the transcript scan receipts introduced in #177933, because it does not supply the database-generation evidence those receipts require; that performance follow-up is outside this bounded readiness fix.

## Evidence

- New Node regression: old code returned `starting` at 60 seconds; fixed code returns `ready` when the Scheduled Task Gateway becomes healthy at 90 seconds. The regression runs with a fake monotonic clock (23 ms), without increasing a test timeout.
- Final focused Node readiness file: 16/16 passed. Missing-target repair-history suite: 9/9 passed. Conditional fresh-Doctor cases: 4/4 passed.
- Live proof on macOS with an isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, profile, and loopback Gateway on a verified free port: seeded the reported run ID as `failed` / `abandoned`, with empty `target` and `after`. `pnpm openclaw --profile upd-l1885 update repair --json --yes --timeout 45` returned `status: "ok"`, `coreUpdate: "completed"`, `restart: false`, and the seeded ID in `reconciledRuns`. Read-only ledger inspection retained the original failure and empty target, with completed `reconcile:acknowledged`. A subsequent `pnpm openclaw --profile upd-l1885 doctor --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions` completed successfully without repeating the abandoned-update warning. `/readyz` returned HTTP 200 and `ready: true`. Only the task-owned Gateway was started/stopped. Native Windows Scheduled Task execution was not available; its readiness timing is covered through the production wait owner on Node.
- Cross-lane Node consumer proof: `rg -l 'restart-health' --glob '*.test.ts' src extensions packages test` selected 60 files, passed in that order to `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ... --maxWorkers=1` with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` and isolated HOME/state/cache. All six wrapper shards passed: **59 files / 1,502 tests passed; one file / 15 tests skipped by existing guards**. Total wrapper time 1,576.85 seconds.
- Production and service-test typechecks, targeted oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and Madge (0 cycles) passed. Independent Codex review found no actionable P0/P1 findings.
- Existing slow-file follow-up: `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-original-service.test.ts` passed 48 cases with about 283 seconds of reported test time. Its per-case fresh A/B roots, real state/lease owners, and snapshot/schema verification account for repeated database worker and filesystem work; individual cases stayed below 30 seconds. `update-command-lease.test.ts` also passed 54 cases in 218.93 seconds (fresh Doctor children and real state/lease setup); `update-command-rollback.test.ts` passed 46 cases in 134.21 seconds (snapshot/config/restore matrix). These existing aggregate costs were recorded under the campaign exception, without timeout/retry changes.
- Full `check:changed` SQLite inventory was not run under the campaign's local gate budget; PR CI provides broad proof.
- Production LOC +7/-1; tests +20/-0; docs +3/-0. The change adds no new policy owner or state.

prs.title: perf(control-ui): avoid restyling sidebar rows when scroll fades change
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Scrolling a long Control UI sidebar changes the top/middle/bottom fade class. Its mask custom properties inherit into every session row, although only the scroller consumes them. A native Chromium reproduction with 64 unchanged children performs 66 style computations for one top → middle transition.

## Why This Change Was Made

Set the two mask layers directly on the scroller and change its non-inherited `mask-image` for each scroll state. Remove the unused `--sidebar-body-mask` and `--sidebar-scroll-edge` tokens; preserve the opaque native scrollbar strip and RTL positioning. No new state, options, dependencies, or stored shapes.

## User Impact

Sidebar scrolling avoids descendant restyling when its fades change. Appearance is unchanged. This is a steady-state scroll fix: the earlier reload experiment did not establish a LoAF improvement, and no reload improvement is claimed.

## Evidence

The pre-declared deciding gate is ≤2 style computations per sidebar state change, with 64 unchanged children. The committed native regression fails on base (66) and passes with the fix (2: scroller plus its pseudo-element; no descendant restyle).

Seven interleaved baseline/candidate pairs on one quiet AWS `c7a.4xlarge`, repository Playwright Chromium, actual `createSidebarScroll`/`observeScrollState` owners, production CSS, and 64 synthetic sidebar rows. Each sample uses 20 native wheel steps through top → middle → bottom → middle → top, five times; all 14 samples verify the exact 20 state transitions and offsets. Timings use native `RecalcStyleDuration` counters without tracing and are report-only; the deterministic count gate decides.

| Style recalculation, 20 wheel steps | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median (ms) | 34.797 | 3.139 |
| IQR (ms) | 34.679–35.127 | 3.095–3.197 |
| Layout (ms), every sample | 0 | 0 |

AWS lease `cbx_5d30fbea4d00`, fixed `c7a.4xlarge`; [run context](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_d062c3d0decf1f96813e98941c8dfce0). Production CSS: **15 additions / 15 deletions, net 0 LOC**. Files: `ui/src/styles/layout.css`, `ui/src/styles/sidebar-scroll-mask.node.test.ts`.
