prs.title: fix(agents): system prompt advertises /update and /reasoning even when commands are disabled
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #181956

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where deployments that disable chat commands (`commands.restart: false`) still get a system prompt that tells the model the owner can send `/update` and `/restart` in chat. The model then recommends commands the deployment rejects ("`/update` is disabled (commands.restart=false)"), sending users into dead ends.

- **Related:** #145527 (introduced the unconditional `/update` recommendation for discoverability) and #145573 (restored tool-based updates while keeping the chat fallback); this keeps the default guidance and only removes it where the command cannot run. Fix signal labels on the issue: `clawsweeper:queueable-fix`, `clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear`, `clawsweeper:source-repro`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The config-aware prompt facade now passes `isRestartEnabled(config)` to the renderer, and the `/update`/`/restart` chat guidance follows it: with `commands.restart: false` the prompt drops the "owner can send `/update`" sentence, the "`/restart` in chat" clause, and the "direct the user to `/update`" fallback (replaced by Control UI/operator guidance). This gate is exactly the check the `/restart` and `/update` command handler enforces, so it is correct in every configuration. Default deployments keep identical guidance.

The `/reasoning` and `/status` hint is intentionally left unconditional (addressing the review findings on the first revision): whether a native-capable surface actually parses commands is resolved inside channel adapters at connection time (per-account `commands.native` overrides such as `channels.discord.accounts.work.commands.native=true`, and channel-specific single-command routes such as Slack's `channels.slack.*.slashCommand.enabled` route), none of which is visible from the core configuration. Hiding the hint from an incomplete view would suppress guidance for command paths that actually work; suppressing it needs account-resolved availability published by the channel owner.

- **Intended outcome:** with `commands.restart: false`, the prompt no longer mentions the chat `/update` or `/restart` routes and falls back to Control UI/operator update guidance; all other guidance unchanged.
- **Out of scope:** command execution/gating logic (already correct), surface-dependent suppression of the `/reasoning`/`/status` hint (needs channel-owner-published command availability).
- **Highest-risk area:** none identified for the shipped gate — it mirrors the exact runtime check the command handler performs.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** regressions cover disabled restart with and without the gateway tool, the no-tool fallback, and unchanged defaults; prompt stability/prefix tests pass unchanged.

## User Impact

Operators who disable `commands.restart` no longer get a model that directs users to a command the deployment rejects. Default deployments see no prompt change.

- **Success criteria:** configured-prompt regressions pass for disabled update/restart commands and unchanged defaults; `pnpm tsgo:core` clean.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/agents/system-prompt-config.ts` (fact derivation), `src/agents/system-prompt-command-guidance.ts` (conditional guidance lines), and the fixtures in `src/agents/system-prompt-config.test.ts` / `src/agents/system-prompt.commands.test.ts`.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** local checkout on branch `feat/issue-181956-system-prompt-commands` (rebased on `origin/main` @ 491b03c8751), Node v26.7.0; rendered the prompt through the real `buildConfiguredAgentSystemPrompt` facade with zero mocks, and additionally captured the provider-bound system prompt through the shipped Gateway-to-agent entry point (`chat.send` on a real gateway server with an anthropic-messages provider bound to a local recording endpoint).
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts src/agents/system-prompt-config.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/system-prompt.cache-prefix.test.ts src/agents/system-prompt-stability.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts src/auto-reply/commands-registry.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-update.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/helpers.system-prompt.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-system-prompt.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-system-prompt.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/pr181956-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts   # provider-bound capture through the real gateway
  pnpm tsgo:core
  node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs render-prompt-evidence.mts   # before/after prompt probes
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:** provider-bound capture through the shipped gateway (`test/pr181956-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts`): a real gateway server serves a session whose provider is an `anthropic-messages` endpoint bound to a local recording server; `chat.send` → `agent.wait` runs the full gateway-to-agent turn and the probe reads the system prompt from the actual `POST /v1/messages` request body:
  ```json
  [
    {
      "case": "default config (commands.restart defaults to true)",
      "capture": { "transport": "POST /v1/messages", "api": "anthropic-messages" },
      "guidance": {
        "updateChatGuidance": true,
        "restartInChatClause": false,
        "reasoningToggleHint": true,
        "gatewayUpdateGuidance": true,
        "controlUiUpdateFallback": false,
        "directUserToUpdate": false
      }
    },
    {
      "case": "commands.restart=false",
      "capture": { "transport": "POST /v1/messages", "api": "anthropic-messages" },
      "guidance": {
        "updateChatGuidance": false,
        "restartInChatClause": false,
        "reasoningToggleHint": true,
        "gatewayUpdateGuidance": true,
        "controlUiUpdateFallback": false,
        "directUserToUpdate": false
      }
    }
  ]
  ```
  The default session exposes the `openclaw` tool alongside `gateway`, so its config-read line takes the `openclaw` variant and the `/restart`-in-chat clause stays with the gateway-tool-only profile (covered by the facade regressions). With the same zero-mock facade script before the patch (files restored to `origin/main`), the identical disabled config rendered `"updateChatGuidance": true` and `"restartInChatClause": true`.
- **Observed result after fix:** through the real gateway, `commands.restart: false` removes the "owner can send `/update`" sentence, the "`/restart` in chat" clause, and the "direct the user to `/update`" fallback from the provider-bound prompt (the gateway tool keeps its `update.run` guidance); the reasoning hint and default-config output are unchanged.
- **Before evidence (optional, visual changes encouraged):** same facade probe on unpatched `origin/main` reported `updateChatGuidance: true` for every config, matching the issue report.
- **What was not tested:** a live channel account connected to the gateway (the e2e provider is a local anthropic-messages recording endpoint); surface-dependent command-route resolution inside channel adapters (see Why This Change Was Made). CI lanes pending.
- **Proof tier:** L2
- **Proof limitations:** none for the shipped gate — L2 via the provider-bound prompt capture through the real gateway plus focused regressions; no live channel credentials available in this environment.
- **Review state:** Awaiting CI + maintainer review; first-review P2 findings addressed by deferring surface-dependent suppression; the requested gateway-to-provider proof is added as `test/pr181956-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts`; the low-value direct-renderer suite was removed per review. CI lanes pending.

prs.title: fix(agents): allow file edits in registered linked worktrees of the same repository
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Subagent fleets commonly spawn children with `cwd` set to the repository and have each child create its own `git worktree add <repo>-wt/<name>`. OpenClaw's file tools (edit, write, apply_patch) then refused every edit inside those sibling worktrees as outside the workspace. This was the single most common cause of incomplete fleets in live stress runs: children burned their replacement budget on "Path escapes sandbox root" / "worktree edit-scope denials". Guidance-only wording did not change model behavior in an A/B.

## User Impact

Host file tools can edit registered linked worktrees of the same repository. Git metadata is now refused, and container sandboxes and Codex-native sandbox boundaries are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Root cause

`agent-tools.ts` selects one containment root (the spawn `cwd`), and `sandbox-paths.ts` enforces it lexically. Writes and patches pin that root (`agent-tools.read.ts`, `apply-patch-file-ops.ts`) with no knowledge of git's linked worktrees.

### Fix

Approved direction (maintainer decision): host file tools allow writes inside a git **linked worktree of the same repository** as the admitted root. The new `workspace-write-scope.ts` selects the boundary per write, at the point of effect, from current git registration:

- the candidate's `.git` file must point into the root repository's common dir under `worktrees/<id>`;
- the registration's `gitdir` backpointer must resolve to that exact `.git` file;
- paths are realpath-resolved, and the scope is rechecked at mutation time.

Forged `.git` pointers, worktrees of other repositories, escaping aliases and unregistered directories stay refused. Container sandboxes are unchanged.

Behavior change: git metadata is now refused. On base, file tools could write the root repository's `.git` internals (for example `.git/config`); they now refuse any `.git` path and the common/git dirs. That closes a path where a file-tool write to `.git/hooks` or `core.hooksPath` could run code on a later, separately approved git command. Agents still operate git through commands.

The Codex app-server harness enforces its own native sandbox (`writableRoots: [cwd]` captured at turn start). It's unchanged here, and `docs/plugins/codex-harness.md` now says so. Making it registration-aware needs upstream Codex support for dynamic writable roots: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/config-options.ts`, `turn-params.ts`; Codex `core/src/tools/handlers/apply_patch.rs`, `hooks/src/schema.rs`. Docs updated in `docs/concepts/agent-workspace.md` and `docs/tools/subagents/tool-reference.md`. A small helper extraction keeps `agent-tools.read.ts` under its line cap.

## Evidence

- New `core-coding-tools.linked-worktrees.test.ts`, red on base (2 failed: a registered-worktree write is rejected while `.git/config` stays writable) and green twice with the fix. The containment suites pass: sandbox, sandbox-paths, workspace mutations, root guard, workspace paths, workspace outside, apply-patch, root lifetime, lazy root and host-write integrity.
- Live on a Crabbox AWS host with real OpenAI models, in a build combining this with three sibling fixes: 6 embedded fleets (8 children each), 0 write denials, 6/6 complete. Main's 12-fleet run on the same box had 2 distinct embedded write denials. Codex-runtime children still see denials in sibling worktrees, as documented.
- Landing CI found an exported-name collision between the extracted host writer and an existing test helper. Renamed the host writer to `writeHostWorkspaceFile`; the export-name collision guard, changed-file formatter, and lint pass locally. The change is naming-only.
- A later baseline-ratchet gate rejected an unchecked errno cast in the new registration resolver. Replaced it with the existing `hasErrnoCode` predicate for the same `ENOENT`/`ENOTDIR` cases. Assertion-safety, formatting, lint, and independent review pass. An additional local regression rerun could not reach test execution because the borrowed worktree dependencies lack several workspace package links; exact-head GitHub CI remains the broad proof.
- Final exact-head CI is green at `b3ea68b06dd5348efa7e6e70b74f51097d9eb123`: [CI run 40057027149](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40057027149). The run completed successfully with no failed jobs.

prs.title: fix(feishu): retry once on token-invalid errors 99991663/99991664 with cache invalidation (fixes #97287)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #97287.

When the cached `tenant_access_token` becomes invalid (e.g. clock drift, server-side revocation, or Feishu token expiry), the plugin cannot send messages. Error code `99991663 Invalid access token` is returned, but the plugin does not automatically refresh the token and retry. Users must manually restart the gateway to recover.

## Changes Made

- `extensions/feishu/src/comment-shared.ts`: Added `addFeishuTokenCacheClearer` / `clearFeishuTokenCaches`. `getFeishuTokenInvalidCode` detects 99991663/99991664. `requestFeishuApi` retries once on token-invalid (`retriedTokenInvalid` flag, independent of rate-limit budget). Fulfilled token-invalid bodies handled.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.ts`: `createFeishuClient` creates a plugin-owned `Lark.Cache` via `buildSdkTokenCache()`. `clearClientCache` expires `CTenantAccessToken` in the private cache by appId namespace.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.ts`: getter pattern — `opts.getClient()` inside request closure, ensures fresh client after cache clear.
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.ts`: `clearFeishuTokenCache` registered. CardKit create retry on 99991663/99991664. Guarded-fetch release on non-JSON response.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.test.ts`: NEW — client cache isolation tests.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.retry.test.ts`: NEW — token-invalid + rate-limit retry sequence tests.
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts`: NEW/UPDATED — card streaming tests including retry and guarded-fetch release.
- `extensions/feishu/src/token-retry-proof.test.ts`: NEW — end-to-end recovery proof tests (99991663/99991664 detection, cache clearing, getter pattern).

## Evidence

### 1. Production requestFeishuApi auto-retry on real 99991663 (7/7 passed)

Loads the ACTUAL `comment-shared.ts` module via `tsx` and exercises `requestFeishuApi` with a real 99991663 error. The production code automatically detects the token-invalid code, clears caches, and retries — all through the same code path that ships in the plugin.

```
 PRODUCTION requestFeishuApi AUTO-RETRY PROOF — PR #97295
 Host: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
 Time: 2026-07-08T06:01:43Z
 Commit: 83830f71ec

─── 1. Real Feishu API: get token ───
  ✅ GET TOKEN: code=0
  ✅ BOT INFO:  code=0

─── 2. requestFeishuApi auto-retry on 99991663 ───
  ✅ Real API returns 99991663 with tampered token
  ✅ requestFeishuApi called 2x (1st=99991663, 2nd=success)
  ✅ Cache clear callback invoked (via addFeishuTokenCacheClearer)
  ✅ Recovered: result.code=0

─── 3. Cache isolation proof ───
  ✅ Fresh client after cache clear (different instance)

  RESULTS: 7/7 passed

  Production module exercised:
    extensions/feishu/src/comment-shared.ts
      → requestFeishuApi() — auto-retry on 99991663
      → getFeishuTokenInvalidCode() — detects 99991663/99991664
      → addFeishuTokenCacheClearer() — registers cache clearers
    extensions/feishu/src/client.ts
      → createFeishuClient() — builds SDK client
      → clearClientCache() — evicts CTenantAccessToken by namespace
```

### 2. Retry path steps (production code flow)

```
send() → 99991663 thrown
  → getFeishuTokenInvalidCode() detects 99991663
  → clearFeishuTokenCaches() → addFeishuTokenCacheClearer callbacks
  → clearClientCache() evicts CTenantAccessToken
  → retriedTokenInvalid = true (prevents infinite retry loop)
  → requestFeishuApi() RETRIES → SDK/fetch gets fresh token
  → send succeeds → code=0
```

### 3. Unit tests (113/113 passed)

```
 Test Files  5 passed (5)
 Tests       113 passed (113)
```

**Cache storage model**: All token caches are in-memory (Map + Lark.Cache), not persisted. No migration needed.

(Proof scripts run locally and deleted — not committed.)

prs.title: fix(exec): stop runaway Linux host command memory usage
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A runaway Linux Gateway exec child can exhaust host memory before the global OOM killer intervenes. Existing OOM-score adjustment changes victim preference, but does not bound allocation.

## User Impact

Linux Gateway-hosted foreground, background, and live PTY command trees get an RSS-plus-swap watchdog. The default limit is the smallest of **8 GiB**, **one quarter of physical/cgroup-constrained memory**, and **half the memory remaining after the Gateway's resident usage**. A sample over the bound immediately requests the existing tree-kill operation and returns `memory-limit`, observed usage, the bound, and recovery advice. Background polling/logs retain that explanation. No new config, dependency, or service changes.

This is sampled protection, not hard containment. The one-second interval allows overshoot; concurrent commands have independent budgets and shared pages may be counted repeatedly. Non-PTY commands retain a descendant owner. Reparented PTY daemons are outside the live ancestry monitor; use supervised non-PTY background execution for long-running work. Remote `host=node`, Codex-native shell commands, non-Linux hosts, and sandbox backends are outside this watchdog.

## Design and Simplification

The existing supervisor owns cancellation, background lifetime, cleanup, and now memory sampling. The service relay exposes its retained tree root so the monitor includes adopted descendants. Procfs sampling avoids subprocess polling and virtual-address limits that interfere with V8/Go runtime reservations. Cgroup containment requires delegation and spawn-time placement; this safeguard requires neither. RLIMIT_AS/RLIMIT_DATA do not provide a tree RSS bound, and RLIMIT_RSS does not provide a modern Linux RSS bound ([getrlimit](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/getrlimit.2.html)).

Production LOC: **+155 (324 added / 169 removed)**; test LOC: **+196**. Growth implements the missing watchdog and failure propagation. Outcome shaping and its types now live together in the existing output owner; the duplicated diagnostic failure union and obsolete max-lines exemption are removed. No second execution owner or cache was added.

The retained owner already reports uncertified cleanup and fences the supervisor when admission is revoked before command launch. The launch-policy regression explicitly asserts both denial of execution and that cleanup failure. This behavior already applied to service-hosted execution; distinguishing confirmed local refusal from uncertain launch delivery remains a separate lifecycle repair.

## Proof

- Exact-head [Linux exec CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40056137055/job/120759764323), `a256dc489d9b38b5e562e34865404ede1d0aadd7`: a real descendant allocating 384 MiB under a scaled 256 MiB default is killed before its 8-second timeout, returns `memory-limit`, and retains background guidance. Whole-test times: **1.200 s non-PTY / 1.041 s PTY**. Actual terminal selection is asserted. Existing PTY/OOM-score behavior and all 11 launch-policy cases pass. These are reliability results, not latency/GC performance claims.
- Red control: the child/PTY supervisor regression fails with the original production code (no kill), then passes with the change; sandbox exclusion passes on both. Budget, nonleader-thread descendant, swap, and sampler-retirement tests pass.
- Local focused exec/process tests, changed-file lint/format, targeted core typecheck, export-name guard, and required import-closure/planner tests pass. Closure/planner proof: 178 tests. No local full test suite or Testbox lease.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean, including the repair and rebase conflict resolution. Autoreview's route mismatch was not bypassed or reconfigured.
- First CI found three attributable issues: stale max-lines baseline, a type-import cycle, and launch-policy tests intercepting only the former spawn path. Repaired together; their exact-head CI jobs now pass. Required rebase onto main `38bf89ccf774` preserved the upstream error formatter in an import-only conflict; range-diff confirms no other patch changes.

## Remaining CI Failures: Attributed Baseline / Unrelated

[Final CI run 40056137055](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40056137055) has three non-aggregate failures; security-fast and all changed execution-owner checks pass. The CI gate is red because of these failures. No CI reruns were requested.

| Failed job | Attribution |
| --- | --- |
| [checks-node-changed-2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40056137055/job/120759764282) | `test/clawrouter-managed-gateway.e2e.test.ts:109`: catalog returns `count: 0`, missing the configured model. Reproduced identically on unchanged main `1fead915921e307018bdb7b8d2a2e7d80c9d8d4a` using that revision's official CI runtime and matching packaged plugins from [main run 40054969997](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40054969997). Failure occurs before the agent turn; fixture CLI uses the unchanged managed-child owner. |
| [checks-node-changed-12](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40056137055/job/120759764355) | `test/gateway.multi.e2e.test.ts`, scheduler-disabled Gateway edit: cron.add rejects the fixture's model override against its single-model allowlist. Same exact rejection reproduced on unchanged main `1fead915921e` with the same official artifacts. The fixture and model-selection owner are unchanged by this PR. |
| [checks-node-changed-compact-small-18](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40056137055/job/120759764261) | `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-message-injection.isolated-gateway.test.ts:220`: a 1-second chat.send timeout. Initial focused PR run reproduced it; then **five main-parent runs (`38bf89ccf774`) and five PR-head runs passed**, six tests each. This synthetic steering flow does not execute a shell child; diagnostic-events changes are type-only. Meets the lane's explicit unrelated-flake criterion; the original failures remain recorded, not claimed fixed. |

Baseline E2E commands used the supported `OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1` mode, one worker, and only the failing file/case. Artifact build-info matched the checked-out main SHA; original generated directories were preserved and restored. An earlier attempt omitted that flag and began automatic build preparation; it was stopped (143) and excluded from evidence, then official artifacts were restored afresh. No Team production changes or sandbox writes.


## Actual Codex HTTP and fallback wire evidence

Unmodified released Codex0.164.0 Linux ARM64 ELF SHA256 `8813c8d8a4cea2eeba271b72ab22f49628b184b24ab18dbef06b4ce41e9a8d39`; source `6aaac694803004a63c6f393d153c96d22521a6b9`. Historical CA bundle SHA256 `c3aa6ce83618c247fdeb0afad3a4eb1d01da2eb9035defe70f74c4bbaaca986f`. Consumers reuse this evidence only where their selected ELF matches exactly.

A pass-through CONNECT recorder observed the unchanged CLI, without TLS termination, interception, certificate substitution, decryption, request-payload recording or real credentials. It parsed record lengths and ClientHello/ServerHello fields. Each run had isolated state and a synthetic key. The negative oracle is natural connection closure and complete client-flight records, never timeout or process cleanup.

| Mode | Hosts | Connections | Actual client observation |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Default HTTP |14|14|Plaintext fatal unknown_ca48; no encrypted client flight|
| CODEX_CA_CERTIFICATE historical store, HTTP |14|14|CCS + one19-byte encrypted record, then clientEOF|
| SSL_CERT_FILE historical store, HTTP |14|14|Same19-byte flight and clientEOF|
| Actual WebSocket failure → HTTP fallback, historical store |14|42|Typed WebSocket CertDistrusted then POST diagnostic; all3connections/host have same19-byte flight and clientEOF|

All84incident connections select TLS1.3/cipher0x1302 (AES256GCM/SHA384), with no PSK or early-data offer. All client streams parse completely, with zero trailing bytes. All close before the diagnostic process cleanup signal; zero observation bounds and zero unsettled connections. Four server streams have partial trailing bytes after client abort; this does not truncate the client records.

Inference from the recorded protocol: with this negotiated cipher a client Finished needs at least69protected bytes (48verify data +4handshake header +1inner type +16tag). The only encrypted19-byte flight cannot contain Finished. With no early-data offer and natural closure, the tested conforming CLI cannot have sent an authenticated HTTP request. The19-byte record was not decrypted and is not represented as a decoded alert or typed HTTP CertDistrusted. See [RFC8446 §2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446.html#section-2), [§4.4.4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446.html#section-4.4.4), [§5.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446.html#section-5.2).

Actual legitimate controls: custom-private-CA HTTP and custom-private-CA WebSocket→HTTP fallback each receive a synthetic authenticated `/v1/responses` POST. Ordinary public HTTPS reaches HTTP405. Unknown private CA and wrong hostname do not reach private HTTP. Two0.160.0 predecessor controls against incident destinations emit Finished-sized and subsequent large encrypted records; remote reset prevents claiming a successful remote HTTP response. Predecessor ELF SHA256 `50b06603bdcdac39b714f5c3e68583c002b8ad8779ebfdaaf4932ff016b379c0`.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

This is an **unmeasured synthetic investigation, not a merge candidate**. It tests whether short chat-event frames are needlessly recompressed for identical WebSocket recipients when the complete frame reaches 1 KiB but each owned segment is smaller.

## User Impact

No production performance improvement is claimed. This diagnostic-only commit must never be merged. It contains a temporary baseline owner and a synthetic measurement workload; a justified fix would remove both and receive fresh review and exact-head validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The candidate reuses the existing immutable-byte compression owner for this gap. Negotiated window sizes, no-context-takeover requirements, per-recipient projection, ordering, and mutable-buffer behavior stay authoritative. The baseline carrier is byte-identical to the compression owner at `d355f2fd148dd68486d863aba8b510adfa8005c2` (SHA256 `50ee2affc2bde1a6baa955c48a87a32e8ee29861090993dc597fae856c4069ff`).

Earlier whole-frame reuse was closed without incremental proof in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175039; this investigation tests the remaining small-segment case against the later segment-reuse and 1 KiB-threshold implementation.

## Evidence

### Acceptance rule — recorded before the first run

- Workload: the real Gateway broadcaster, client registry, compression codec, transport, and negotiated loopback WebSocket receivers. Eight equal-profile recipients; a synthetic 1,000-byte chat-final payload; every encoded segment below 1,024 bytes and the complete frame at least 1,024 bytes.
- Six interleaved baseline/candidate pairs, alternating which version starts each round. Each pair measures a new broadcaster's first frame (owner-cold), a 30-frame warm burst with fresh frames, and one-recipient control. Native zlib/process state is retained: owner-cold is not process startup.
- Required improvement: native deflations fall from eight to one per shared broadcast, with at least a 10% reduction in warm synchronous dispatch median.
- Reject a candidate with any comparable dispatch, process-CPU, or end-to-end delivery median/p95 at least 20% worse, including the single-recipient control. Report smaller adverse changes rather than hiding them.
- Require identical decoded JSON, ordering, sequence and wire-byte totals. Verify window-10 separation, uncompressed delivery, and repeated mutation of bare buffers. Report distinct output backing buffers/bytes and exact-sized cached storage; this is not a retained-process-heap measurement.
- Report raw samples, median/p95/range, host load, source hashes, native/fallback compression counts, and test cost. The observer itself is included in dispatch/CPU measurements equally on both sides.

The selected test must be `src/gateway/server/ws-shared-frame-latency.test.ts`; an aggregate green check without its actual measurement output is insufficient. Intended focused command: `pnpm test src/gateway/server/ws-shared-frame-latency.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.

No dependency-backed tests have run locally. Normal PR CI is the authorized proof route. Formatting and whitespace checks pass. Independent source review verified the owner and real transport/counter contracts; AutoReview found no actionable P0–P2 issue, and fresh AutoReview of the final balanced-order revision also found no actionable P0–P2 defects. The selected probe completed successfully; results below reject this candidate.

Reviewed probe SHA256: `ee4d517cf0552f1777be33604d111b6f4d72189c7b49c0f244125663b17f6717`. Candidate owner SHA256: `b78c9971e6f7937d471924df80535e24a11af29a5f54d497cded51fc08a77dc3`.

## Result — rejected, diagnostic closed without merge

The candidate does not meet the predeclared acceptance rule. It removes repeated compression and improves warm fanout, but owner-cold and single-recipient process-CPU medians exceed the 20% adverse threshold. No production regression or causality is inferred from these small synthetic CPU samples. Independent result review confirmed rejection; no measurement rerun or threshold change is used.

Exact head: `49e4ae04ef2330e537bf0502fa12294d515c820d`. [Executed probe and raw samples](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40057217204/job/120763168149), `agentic-gateway-core-3-hosted-1`; selected test passed in **107 ms**. The job reports Node `v26.3.0`, Linux x64, 8 CPUs, load averages `1.53, 0.67, 0.26`. Source hashes match the reviewed candidate/baseline above. The focused command was not run locally; this is actual selected PR-CI execution, not aggregate-green inference.

Each timing cell is **median / p95 [min–max] ms**, six samples. At n=6, the nearest-rank p95 is the maximum.

prs.title: fix(secrets): accept config-owned env markers in models.json audit
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Custom model providers configured with env SecretRefs write bare env-name markers into agent `models.json` (for example `"apiKey": "FACTCHAT_API_KEY"`). That is the intentional serialization contract. `openclaw secrets audit` only treated a fixed list of built-in env markers as non-plaintext, so an unregistered custom marker was reported as `PLAINTEXT_FOUND` even when `openclaw.json` owned the same provider with the same env SecretRef id. Operators then saw a false security finding that regenerating models.json could not clear.

Ownership must follow the models.json writer. The writer normalizes the complete provider map, then inspects the winning apiKey. Exact canonical spelling wins over aliases regardless of credential source or insertion order. A losing alias such as `OpenAI` with `LOSING_ENV` must not suppress `PLAINTEXT_FOUND` when the canonical `openai` winner is another env id, a file or store SecretRef, a literal credential, or an absent apiKey.

## Evidence

Live `node scripts/run-node.mjs secrets audit --json` against an isolated state dir on head `2d9f413b8ad15b8cc295268d59291f52428397a5`. Never `~/.openclaw`. Config and models files lived under `PROOF_HOME` and `STATE`.

Owned custom marker. Config owns `custom-factchat-cloud-mindlogic-ai.apiKey` as env SecretRef id `FACTCHAT_API_KEY`. Production writer `ensureOpenClawModelsJson` wrote that bare marker into models.json. Audit is clean:

```console
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=STATE OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=PROOF_HOME/openclaw.json node scripts/run-node.mjs secrets audit --json
{
  "status": "clean",
  "plaintextCount": 0,
  "modelsJsonFindings": []
}
```

Writer-collision control. Config has both `OpenAI` (`LOSING_ENV`) and `openai` (`WINNING_ENV`). models.json `openai.apiKey` is `WINNING_ENV`:

```console
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs secrets audit --json
{
  "status": "clean",
  "plaintextCount": 0,
  "modelsJsonFindings": []
}
```

Same env-versus-env config with models.json marker set to `LOSING_ENV`:

```console
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs secrets audit --json
{
  "status": "findings",
  "plaintextCount": 1,
  "modelsJsonFindings": [
    {
      "code": "PLAINTEXT_FOUND",
      "jsonPath": "providers.openai.apiKey",
      "provider": "openai"
    }
  ]
}
```

Mixed-source collision on this head. Canonical `openai.apiKey` is a file SecretRef; alias `OpenAI.apiKey` is env `LOSING_ENV`. models.json `openai.apiKey` is `LOSING_ENV`:

```console
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs secrets audit --json
{
  "status": "findings",
  "plaintextCount": 1,
  "modelsJsonFindings": [
    {
      "code": "PLAINTEXT_FOUND",
      "jsonPath": "providers.openai.apiKey",
      "provider": "openai"

}
```

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** secrets audit accepts a models.json bare env-name marker only when the writer-winning models.providers apiKey is that env SecretRef. Losing alias `OpenAI`/`LOSING_ENV` cannot hide plaintext when the canonical winner is another env, a file or store SecretRef, a literal, or an absent apiKey.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS Darwin 25.6.0 arm64, Node v26.8.2, OpenClaw worktree at `2d9f413b8ad15b8cc295268d59291f52428397a5`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` under `/tmp/oc-proof-state-121578` (not `~/.openclaw`).

- **Observed result after fix:** generated config-owned custom env marker is accepted. Writer-winning canonical env marker is accepted. Losing-alias marker stays plaintext when the canonical winner is env or file.
- **What was not tested:** live gateway model call that regenerates models.json on a Windows host with a real FACTCHAT key; exec SecretRef mixed-source collision on the production CLI.

## Summary

Follows ClawSweeper fix shape for #121543: keep the models.json env marker writer contract; select the owner from the complete provider map; inspect only the winning apiKey.

prs.title: fix(agents): stop recommending disabled update commands
prs.body:
Related: #181956

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the agent's system prompt recommends `/update` and `/restart` when `commands.restart=false` makes those commands unavailable.

## User Impact

Disabled update/restart commands are no longer recommended. The prompt keeps the Control UI/operator-terminal update fallback and preserves default guidance. Working WebChat `/reasoning` and `/status` hints remain available.

This addresses the restart-setting portion of #181956. It does not change channel/account-specific text or native command availability, execution permissions, or configuration defaults.

## Why This Change Was Made

The configured prompt builder now uses the same `isRestartEnabled` decision as command execution. The control-guidance section lives in a sibling renderer because the existing prompt file is already above the repository's line cap. All prompt callers continue through the existing configured builder; no new configuration or state is introduced.

## Evidence

### Current-head Gateway-to-provider capture

Replayed on **`8ff98abc85369861b88bb8c95712629d22ddeb62`**, after the control-section extraction and branch rebase. Both build stamps recorded this exact SHA. The checkout stayed clean; this follow-up changes only PR evidence.

Environment: macOS arm64 with Node 24.22.1 as launcher. Built through `pnpm --silent openclaw --help`, then used the repository's isolated Gateway fixture and its stamped production `dist/index.js` entrypoint. Each case started a fresh home/state/workspace and Gateway, with plugins disabled, tools denied, and a local Responses-compatible endpoint. The endpoint recorded the actual incoming provider request and returned a fixed plain-text confirmation; it did not construct or inject the system prompt.

Procedure for each fresh instance: run `openclaw agent --session-key <isolated-session> --message 'Reply with a short confirmation.' --json --timeout 60`; capture the request's system instructions at the HTTP endpoint; select the `OpenClaw Control` section; verify successful completion; shut down the Gateway and remove its isolated state. No update/restart command, external model service, operator credential or existing Gateway was used.

| Observed in actual provider request | `commands: {restart:false,text:false,native:false}` | Default command configuration |
|---|---|---|
| Requests received | 1 | 1 |
| CLI exit | 0 | 0 |
| Confirmation returned | Yes | Yes |
| `/update` recommendation | Absent | Present |
| Operator terminal fallback | Present | Present |
| `/reasoning` and `/status` hints | Present | Present |

The retained reasoning/status hints are intentional for WebChat/text-only surfaces. The tools-denied live fixture does not exercise the Gateway-tool `/restart` branch; the configured-prompt regressions cover it. The native/channel-specific portion of the broader issue remains outside this PR.

<details>
<summary>Actual disabled-config provider-bound control section</summary>

```text
## OpenClaw Control
Do not invent commands.
For the Gateway hosting this session: For an update request, use the Control UI or ask the operator to run `openclaw update` in a terminal. Missing chat ownership needs owner setup in the Control UI or help from the Gateway operator. Never run openclaw update, npm install -g openclaw, swap installations, or stop/restart the gateway service via exec or detached jobs.
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Actual default-config provider-bound control section</summary>

```text
## OpenClaw Control
Do not invent commands.
For the Gateway hosting this session: In a connected chat, the owner can send `/update` with commands.restart enabled (the default), regardless of the agent's tool profile. For a chat update request, direct the user to `/update`. Outside chat, use the Control UI or ask the operator to run `openclaw update` in a terminal. Missing chat ownership needs owner setup in the Control UI or help from the Gateway operator. Never run openclaw update, npm install -g openclaw, swap installations, or stop/restart the gateway service via exec or detached jobs.
```

</details>

These are captured request excerpts, not reconstructed expected output. Unrelated prompt sections, host identifiers, local paths, listener addresses, tokens and request headers are omitted. Both runs completed successfully and all task-owned services/state were cleaned up.

### Regression and static checks

- Both new configured-prompt regressions failed on the base because disabled prompts still contained `/update`; the cases cover prompts with and without the Gateway tool, including `/restart` guidance.
- Prior implementation validation: 149 focused tests across eight files passed in 49.66 seconds wall time. Core typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, diff checks and the line-cap ratchet passed. The four repair files are byte-identical after the rebase; the current-head live capture above supersedes the earlier pre-extraction capture.
- One independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 findings before the behavior-preserving section extraction. The focused tests and static checks were rerun after extraction; no extra local review round was run.
- Current-head CI: broad CI is skipped while this remains a draft. The [Auto response job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40040625038/job/120710595396) failed in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'owner')`; it did not run candidate product tests. This patch does not change that automation, and no green result is claimed for it.

Simplification: command execution remains the policy owner, and the prompt consumes its result. Production delta: +48/-19; regression coverage: +17 lines.

prs.title: fix(ui): transcript search opens the selected historical message
prs.body:
Closes #118560

AI-assisted with Codex. I reviewed the implementation and validation results.

## What Problem This Solves

Transcript-search results from before a main-session reset could open the current visible transcript tail instead of the selected historical message. Same-session invalidations, terminal events, resets, route changes, pane lifecycle transitions, and failed anchored requests could also replace, strand, or retry the temporary historical projection before the selected message was visibly centered.

## What Changed

- Carry the selected hit's typed `sessionId` and `messageId` as one-shot internal navigation state.
- Keep exact anchor ownership through the anchored history request, render commit, and selected-message centering attempt.
- Park and coalesce ordinary history loads behind that owner, preserving caller options and promise completion instead of allowing a live refresh to invalidate the anchor.
- Defer terminal `session.message`, applied `sessions.changed`, reset, and other passive refresh paths until visible anchor completion; unavailable recovery still owns exactly one canonical fallback.
- Reconcile exact-run terminal Gateway events while the historical projection is isolated, so local run/stream lifecycle completes without replacing the selected historical messages.
- Preserve the historical projection during a deferred reset while invalidating its canonical cache, and block older-page loads throughout anchor isolation.
- Keep the pane retry guard through a failed anchor's parked canonical recovery, then consume the one-shot anchor without starting a third history request.
- Fence asynchronous pane work by state, session, connection generation, pending token, and pane attempt; route/destructive cancellation and disconnect settle parked work without leaking it into a new owner.
- Expand collapsed dashboard work groups, await their render, measure the expanded row, and center the actual matched message element.
- Keep historical projections pane-owned so ordinary navigation restores the canonical current tail, and show a dismissible notice when the selected message is unavailable.

The change adds no schema version, configuration surface, fallback path, or changelog entry.

## Rebase And Current-Head Validation

- Published head: `f79a38f6531b541a2317c549378192fbdfbaf5cb`.
- Rebased the complete 21-commit branch onto `main` `a3817e987483765dd339f9d584ae5d1580d5981e`, resolving shared chat event ownership, refresh ownership, and transcript virtualizer overlaps while preserving current-main behavior.
- `main` advanced to `dbc2356abc9a10c3c9e2b7f5b7f14d9a4fc229be` during publication; the merge simulation remains clean and the intervening upstream changes do not overlap this history path.
- The previous hosted bundle failure is not reproducible after the required rebase. Exact-head `pnpm ui:build` passes with 11 startup JS requests and 334002 gzip bytes, below the unchanged 335415-byte baseline-plus-tolerance limit. No performance baseline or tolerance was changed.
- Initial anchored-history transport failure now performs exactly one guarded canonical recovery, keeps the retry guard until settlement, consumes the route anchor, and has a dedicated lifecycle regression.
- An anchored terminal now retires acknowledged steer chips and attachment ownership into the canonical cache without admitting the live tail into the historical projection.
- SQLite active-event regression: 13/13 passed.
- Focused Control UI/Gateway history-anchor and terminal regressions: 181/181 passed after the final rebase.
- Isolated virtualizer and collapsed-work-group centering regression: 9/9 passed.
- Gateway chat-history regression: 101/101 passed.
- Browser transcript-search E2E: 6/6 passed with fresh local screenshots. It opens the selected historical match and clears its one-shot route state before ordinary reload returns to the canonical tail.
- Isolated real-Gateway Control UI transport E2E: 2/2 passed; generated evidence confirms both Gateway and proxy ports closed after cleanup.
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:test:ui`, Control UI i18n verification, focused UI boundary lint, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- `pnpm check:changed` was not rerun because the local Crabbox runner previously failed its own basic sanity check before dispatch. No source failure was bypassed.

## Evidence Boundaries

- Browser proof uses local, isolated fixtures and contains no credentials or public artifact URL.
- The real-Gateway transport proof uses ephemeral local state and confirms cleanup; it does not claim a live third-party channel result.
- All rebased commits are authored and committed as `Sami Rusani <samgithub@pm.me>`.

## What Problem This Solves

Measured clone groups leave repeated preparation, projection, and private policy tables across otherwise independent runtime owners.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change, migration, configuration change, or new SDK export. Security checks, transcript durability, existing protocol shapes, and plugin boundaries remain intact. The standalone session-memory backend is untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse existing error/response and wire-type owners; share session query bindings, conversation-match allocation, publication facts, committed-snapshot checks, and patch preparation. Within individual plugins, model-picker receipt fields, environment-key subsets, and canonical stop words have one implementation. The workspace dotenv block policy is unchanged: two literal rows were already covered by existing token rules. The explicit ClawHub rows remain because the security scanner requires them in addition to the prefix guard.

The original 150-line candidate retains four explicit security-inventory rows and drops seven files from an inconclusive UI failure's import graph. This is a bounded campaign accumulator, not a claim that every instance of a structural group is interchangeable.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- No security, durability, concurrency, or authority guard is removed. Shared helpers retain the original checks and call ordering.
- Existing error coercion performs one additional `instanceof Error` observation for exotic Proxy inputs; ordinary thrown values retain their messages. Side-effecting Proxy observation counts are not a supported error contract.

Browser actions repeat a DNS policy check while preparing the response URL, even when that same address was admitted earlier in the request.

## Why This Change Was Made

The action route opts in to reuse its admitted address only for response URL projection, with an exact URL and complete navigation-policy match. Changed URLs, changed policies, missing admission and cancellation retain validation. Execution and navigation guards remain authoritative. There is no cross-request cache, new setting or protocol change.

Five serial baseline/candidate pairs used fresh processes; all 30 actions per revision returned identical page data and response URLs. All ten `about:blank` controls performed zero hostname lookups.

`config patch --dry-run` can report success when a large provider-catalog reduction will be rejected by the real write's size-drop guard, misleading deployment preflights.

## User Impact

Structured config previews now fail early with a `write-safety` error and the same size-drop reason as the writer, plus its existing recovery guidance. The preview leaves config bytes unchanged and creates no backup or rejected-payload file. If persistence preparation refuses the change, JSON output retains the assignments, input modes, completed checks, and counters; plain-text output retains the original refusal. Existing write protection remains enabled; this does not add a public size-drop override or change value-mode's documented limited validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preview and commit share preparation of the authored, metadata-stamped payload and its canonical size baseline. Include-only mutations retain their existing write route instead of applying the root-file guard to an expanded config. The writer continues to own runtime activation, rejection artifacts, auditing, publication, and rollback.

The related roster-retention preview work in #153069 does not evaluate the serialized-byte guard. The public override requested in #166718 remains a separate product decision, so this PR does not close the entire issue.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the registered-CLI regression fails because the large-shrink preview succeeds; moderate-shrink and include-owned controls pass.
- Real CLI proof uses the normal `pnpm openclaw config patch --file <patch> --replace-path models.providers.bounty.models` entry point in isolated task-owned home/config/state, with 409 synthetic provider models and no provider calls or credentials. The original live failure was reproduced at `2b988ee83444` (the affected owner code is unchanged at this PR's base `80322af5c7e5`).
- Committed candidate `9982d96b8c1d` results: 409→32 root preview and actual write both reject with `size-drop`; the preview preserves original bytes and creates no artifact. 409→300 root and 409→32 include-owned changes pass preview and persist the exact requested model count. Include-owned writes preserve the root file. A real provider-builder shrink also rejects in both preview and commit; its preview has `checks.schema:false` and still returns `write-safety`, directly proving the review correction.
- `pnpm test src/cli/config-cli.integration.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 99 passed; 51.68 s runner wall time. The materially changed integration file has 34 tests and takes 29.83 s Vitest wall time; the cases reuse its existing real config-command fixture.
- Unchanged writer/reference coverage, run at `9982d96b8c1d`: `pnpm test src/config/io.write-config.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.reference-values.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 130 passed; 62.96 s total. Covers existing canonical-format/BOM sizing, references, include ownership, refusal, and rollback contracts.
- The supported CLI wrapper completed the production build for live proof. Core and core-test typechecks and changed-file lint passed. The aggregate changed check stopped at the unrelated existing `observePlacementAuthority` unused export in `src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-turn-authority.ts`; this file and its references are unchanged by the patch. The subsequent ready-for-review CI result and current follow-up are documented below.
- Follow-up `9b8e17b2b06`: parser-validated builder/batch inputs and thrown persistence refusals have registered-command regressions that failed before their corrections. For the empty-roster refusal, the old JSON path returned `operations:0`, empty `inputModes`, and false checks; its text-output control already passed. The corrected real CLI returns `operations:1`, `inputModes:["json"]`, all completed checks true, preserved counters, and the original schema refusal. It exits 1, leaves config bytes unchanged, and creates no backup/rejected file. The matching non-JSON regression preserves the exact original diagnostic.




### CI and conflict follow-up (2026-10-10)

Integrated main `0c94b6966078` to resolve the real `src/config/io.write.ts` import conflict. Both intents are retained: upstream `composeConfigWriteAssertions` and this PR's shared payload preparation. The PR delta against the new base remains the same nine files; no Doctor test, timeout, assertion, or CI workflow was changed.

The previous CI run [37805483456](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37805483456/job/113409493434) failed on `runs legacy state migrations in yes mode without prompting` at 30.228 s (30 s limit), causing the aggregate gate to fail. Diagnosis did not reproduce that failure:

- Exact old PR source `9b8e17b2b064`: original seven-file shard order, separate file processes, macOS arm64 / Node 26.4.0: all 87 tests passed; the named test took 10.582 s. A standalone diagnostic retained all assertions and the deadline, observed maintenance admission in 65 ms and overall completion in 12.939 s, and was removed afterward.
- Same old source in a credential-free Linux arm64 container, Node 24.19.0, 2 CPUs / 8 GiB: all five Doctor-file tests passed; the named test took 18.558 s. This matches the CI Node version and resource limits but not its Linux x64 hardware. The container was removed after diagnosis.
- Conflict-resolved candidate: original seven-file shard, all 87 tests passed; the named test took 12.338 s. Config CLI and writer suites passed 202 tests (34 integration, 65 CLI, 103 writer), 67.86 s combined runner wall time; integration file 27.12 s Vitest wall time.

The original CI timeout remains unattributed. These passing replays are not presented as a timeout fix; no retry logic, longer deadlines, weakened assertions, or speculative production changes were added. The subsequent CI run [38082056748](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38082056748) passed all 86 jobs on `64e6949e85a3`; this is prior-head evidence.

Final local validation on `64e6949e85a3`: types, targeted lint, formatting, and all remaining selected guards pass. The aggregate check stops at 17 Knip findings; the same canonical scan on a separately installed, clean `0c94b6966078` worktree reproduces the identical set (15 authentication/runtime exports, one Solid lint export, one UI test-helper export). They are inherited rather than introduced by this PR.



### Review guidance and async conflict follow-up

Commit `3687439fae0` reuses `createConfigWriteSafetyRejectionError` for actionable recovery guidance in both JSON and text previews, retaining the size-drop reason. The existing registered-command case failed before the message repair and now verifies both output formats and unchanged config/files. No new test fixture or production abstraction was added.

Integrated main `c6d71fae0ed` to resolve the writer conflict from #168481: topology preparation is now asynchronous, so the preview and writer await it and the shared payload type consumes its resolved value.

Validation: 202 tests passed across config CLI integration (34), CLI (65), and writer (103); 101.20 s runner wall time. Integration-file Vitest wall time: 46.38 s. No hosted CI timing for this new head yet.

Final local checks: production types, all core-test type groups, scoped lint, formatting, and the selected ratchets passed. The aggregate changed check stops at four Knip unused exports outside the PR diff: `stripClaudeCliGeneratedUserPrefixes`, `createChannelApprovalHandlerAsync`, `GitHubConnectionsContent`, and `reconnectGateway`. Their defining files match the integrated base; no clean-base Knip replay was run for this head. These findings remain recorded, not suppressed.



### Conflict refresh (2026-10-11)

Integrated main `0ff0202128f` for the new writer conflict. Preserved upstream's agent-deletion authority check before publication and awaited metadata recording. Applied upstream's payload cleanup in the extracted shared preparation function; audit metadata remains computed by the writer. No new behavior, tests, or dependencies were introduced by this conflict repair. The prior head `3687439fae09` had a successful [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38109291576); that remains prior-head evidence.

Conflict-resolved head `963d92c985b`: 137 tests passed (34 CLI integration, 103 config writer), 121.12 s runner wall time; CLI integration 61.12 s and writer 42.78 s Vitest wall time. Core types, scoped lint, formatting, and diff whitespace checks passed. New-head CI is pending.

prs.title: fix(sqlite): avoid holding plugin-state writer during initial admission
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin-state writes can hold the shared SQLite writer while waiting for the Gateway to authorize them, blocking unrelated state writes even though the plugin mutation has not begun.

## User Impact

Plugin state no longer reserves the writer during initial host admission. Session authority, commit checks, and approval replacement behavior remain intact; no configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the initial, source-qualified admission before each write transaction. Keep current-row predicates, commit admission, and publication receipts inside the transaction, including both transactions used to revoke and replace an entry.

This completes the plugin-state path alongside [the common shared-state repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181604). Restart receipts, session-event writers, and upstream-link writers are separate follow-ups because they have distinct caller contracts. Production growth is two explanatory comment lines.

## Evidence

- One real-worker regression exercises ordinary writes, compound operations, both replacement transactions, and refusal of the second replacement grant. An independent SQLite connection checks writer availability before each initial grant and contention at commit.
- Targeted formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Exact-head PR CI passed all 13 plugin-state operation tests and all 18 plugin-state worker tests on Bun. The new writer-lock regression passed in 12 ms; sibling coverage includes source-qualified single and compound session claims. [Operation tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40055346232/job/120757330164), [worker tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40055346232/job/120757330104).
- Independent scoped review found no actionable issue. Production changes are three admission moves and two comment lines; current-row checks, commit admission, publication, read-only behavior, and replacement revocation remain at their existing owners.
- Blacksmith Testbox [allocation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40054256837) queued and was stopped before payload execution; no pre-fix failing run is claimed.
- This repairs a source-level contention defect. It does not identify the lock holder behind a production incident or establish a deployed performance improvement.

prs.title: chore(ci): qualify selective compiler backports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The previous compiler candidate lost generic arguments in value import queries such as `typeof import("./factory").fn<T>`, producing a real Slack test failure. This draft pins the repaired candidate and adds explicit graph profiles, independently auditable synthetic cache checks, and isolated admission through the canonical CI wrappers. The repository compiler selection stays unchanged.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/175541
Stack base: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175567

## User Impact

The repository compiler selection is unchanged. This opt-in qualification workflow and all compiler fixes remain drafts; landing and adoption require explicit owner approval.

## Why This Change Was Made

Candidate `vincentkoc/tsc-ts@a80cd9190942d16286a8483f1f51d9a68037324f` includes four stacked repairs: [uniform-union narrowing](https://github.com/vincentkoc/tsc-ts/pull/1), [recursion/identity relations](https://github.com/vincentkoc/tsc-ts/pull/2), [no-emit exit semantics](https://github.com/vincentkoc/tsc-ts/pull/3), and [generic import-query instantiation](https://github.com/vincentkoc/tsc-ts/pull/4). It remains a selective 7.0.2-based candidate.

The separate capacity profile preserves four CPUs, no swap, immutable inputs, original flags/Go policy, deadlines and cleanup rules, while raising the two large plugin graphs' hard limit from 12GiB to 24GiB. The other 36 graphs retain 12GiB. Profile identity is recorded and audited; the failed 12GiB controls remain failed. Memory diagnostics retain raw traces but cannot qualify as benchmark samples.

[Linux 6.6.141](https://github.com/gregkh/linux/blob/v6.6.141/Documentation/admin-guide/sysctl/net.rst) can create inactive fallback tunnels inside a network namespace; Docker's [null network driver](https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/v28.0.4/libnetwork/drivers/null/null.go) does not make a one-device inventory a valid contract. The shared collector/auditor validator replaces the incorrect one-device assertion with exact documented device name/type pairs, all non-loopback devices down, matching sysfs/proc inventories, distinct namespaces, all five capability sets zero, `NoNewPrivs=1`, complete loopback-only route inventories, and observed TCP `ENETUNREACH`. Unknown or incomplete facts fail admission before compiler invocation. The artifact retains the receipt for independent replay; EROFS, resource, deadline and cleanup enforcement remain in place.

Synthetic cache checks use one fresh container per call, bounded cache-only transport, immutable producer snapshots and fresh receiver controls. The wrapper proof uses the seven canonical row commands and scheduling, with an identical experiment-only CLI overlay in both arms. API/declaration consumers remain pinned. Frozen cgroup snapshots, descendant accounting, row-level outcomes, generated-input hashes and exact cleanup are recorded before a pair can qualify; a rejected pair stops later row admission.

## Validation

**38/38 canonical graphs qualify across the two declared profiles. All 576 planned trials were attempted and accepted; none were rejected or missing.**

| Resource profile | Run (attempt 1) | Verified result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4 CPUs / 12GiB / no swap | [36 graphs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39203865485) | 549/549 trials accepted |
| 4 CPUs / 24GiB / no swap | [Two plugin graphs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39203857098) | 27/27 trials accepted |

Candidate and pinned compilers typecheck cleanly with equivalent, stable outcomes in all 44 repository graph/mode comparisons (396 trials). All 180 canary trials are valid, with candidate/pinned diagnostic and exit parity and matching configured expectations. The 7.0.2 reference completes with stable outcomes, including known version-specific diagnostics; it is not a clean-reference result.

All 38 artifact ZIP digests and actual pinned-auditor replays were independently verified. Checks cover source/run/attempt, immutable producer and compiler identities, the common 108-library manifest, input equality, resource profiles, raw isolation receipts, EROFS/deadline/exit smokes, terminal non-OOM trial state, process/GNU-time exits, output hashes and joined cleanup.

These results cover compiler/typechecking, including test-source graphs. Application runtime and E2E test execution are outside this run. The separate 24GiB profile does not replace or turn the earlier failed uniform-12GiB controls into a pass.

Historical graph workload: `37ceb90e289b181af83c0c58a74caa1dceec2a5a`. At that head, hosted tooling passed 63 tests, both tooling typechecks, lint, formatting and workflow checks. The [isolation-only diagnostic](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39203243739) passed without compiler invocation; its ZIP digest and actual validator replay were independently verified.

[Full compiler CI](https://github.com/vincentkoc/tsc-ts/actions/runs/39267848429), attempt 1, passed all 69 selected units on their first attempts, with no omitted, skipped or quarantined selected units. The workflow branch was `614c02692c886460780faa77d54dbd942d5571b7`; the actual PR checkout `33c70ec2cc345fcb199566883e783898cc24112e` was verified tree-equivalent. Compiler semantics remain those of `a80cd919`. Existing internal exclusions remain: 29 excluded CLI cases; 263 parser-only boundary cases reported separately from 4,982 comparisons per arm; resolver exclusions in each of three modes; and threshold-based emit/declaration sampling. This is not exhaustive compiler equivalence. The selected native-watch unit passed all 10 tests on their first attempts; the earlier retry is historical evidence. The earlier 67/69 fixture-failure run remains historical failed evidence.

The [synthetic cache run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39290478743), attempt 1, collected all 56 planned calls at collector `0998c17442a86369272fd043e1bec71021f0cca5`. Its original auditor rejected upstream-valid bare standard-library names. The strict manifest-based correction at auditor `2d66b712cfc6c9156926152e9a831551a6cc62ab` was independently replayed against the same digest-verified artifact `12206310576`, with no compiler recollection: 56/56 outcomes, 26 seeded transitions, 59 cache files (396,996 bytes), fresh controls, immutable handoff seeds, diagnostics, hashes and cleanup all pass. ZIP SHA256: `f5fd7aceff885b0a4ab8d102d89d28e3654078f2dfae73c693d6640ed4d997f7`. [Corrected-auditor tooling](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39294007254) passed. The original run remains failed; this is a separately attributed successful replay, with `performanceEligible=false`. Truncated-cache cases do not establish actual interrupted-write recovery.

[Separate package qualification](https://github.com/vincentkoc/tsc-ts/pull/5) passed seven targets, 14 Node 24.16/26.1 observations and 98 checks: six non-Windows targets from [run 39284302977](https://github.com/vincentkoc/tsc-ts/actions/runs/39284302977), and Windows from [run 39290103425](https://github.com/vincentkoc/tsc-ts/actions/runs/39290103425) after the portable archive-path repair. The original Windows harness failure remains recorded. Those package binaries and their 107-library manifest `2261994e4ef466f5e79bcc81f81de2b3798b1d3bb3e398fd98a9a97e774e620d` differ from the qualified raw binary `9785e87d…` and 108-library manifest `b13ee3a6…`; semantic qualification does not transfer between them.

**Canonical-wrapper correctness passed under the declared four-CPU / 24GiB / no-swap profile** in [run 39308750952](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39308750952), attempt 1, at harness `04c2ea15fe62ed3d71f71dd6e9e70a7654ac35a5`. All nine mandatory smokes, seven row pairs / 14 arms and 76 checking calls passed; both parent-row exits and all checking outcomes are clean and equivalent. The independent audit verified all 23 row-profile container cleanups, frozen lifecycle evidence and zero OOM events on actual rows, and replayed the exact `04c2ea15` auditor with the same verdict as hosted CI. Artifact `12217109269` (11,911,885 bytes), ZIP SHA256 `b10bb78778f8a55a06ed985946e018fe23671c3fcce1d68df22b31c659884fce`, binds the immutable workload `37ceb90e289b181af83c0c58a74caa1dceec2a5a`, baseline `2330ea6c0951273da91489db91af768d214f93c71583a377a327363a6828e72e`, candidate `9785e87da1650d3a4007d234bc194c63b640524c010497884e4b93161c7bb149` and common 108-library manifest `b13ee3a64a0d52a1bffd5b509cdfd56552444b4295dd258463edf46cb58e9133`. Collector accounting is 76 checking calls plus two explicit compiler-version queries: 78 native CLI calls. Provenance hashing/extraction performs no native call; CLI discovery, API sessions/operations and declaration emission are zero in this collector route. The separate tooling prerequisite adds two explicit pinned typechecks, giving 80 explicit native calls across these identified routes. Dependency installation/setup is outside the collector inventory; no zero-call or whole-CI total is asserted for it. All 76 build-info hash/size and input receipts were validated; raw build-info bytes were intentionally not retained under this proof plan. The proof preserves each canonical row's commands and inner scheduling, with a serial outer pair loop; it is not normal 16-CPU CI, a whole-CI timing comparison, a speedup or adoption proof.

The two earlier wrapper attempts stopped before any compiler version/provenance or checking invocation. [Run 39302907626](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39302907626) failed the first smoke on scratch-directory `EACCES`; effective ownership/mode on that failed runner was not recorded. [Run 39305749476](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39305749476) proved the corrected 0700 scratch owner and first five smokes, then rejected the deliberate child-OOM control because Docker correctly reported `OOMKilled=true` while the harness expected false. Both artifacts prove exact cleanup and 0/76 checking calls. Only that designated positive control now expects the true flag; ordinary controls and actual rows still require false and zero OOM counters.

Exact harness `04c2ea15` passes [117 focused tests, both tooling typechecks, lint, formatting and workflow checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39307807756). Earlier tooling-only failures remain recorded: [argv narrowing](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39300369139) and [lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39301038909); both skipped comparison with zero compiler calls.

The original native producer, run `39162206911`, attempt 1, artifact `12149466946`, expired on 2026-10-21. The historical behavioral evidence above remains attributed to its original harness and artifact identities.

[Producer-only restoration](https://github.com/vincentkoc/tsc-ts/actions/runs/40055744106), attempt 1, rebuilt immutable compiler source `a80cd9190942d16286a8483f1f51d9a68037324f` at producer workflow `e256fcaca159a4bada953b27430157a71831a657`. Independently audited artifact `12545079224` expires `2026-11-23T02:52:19Z`; ZIP SHA-256 `bc7e7ab2562ba84e1c55b85ea70155bb35d44d1670cfa716f2c2b6188d5b27d7`, tar SHA-256 `a435f15e1fd1c7f20e9732823e43c82a0c0fa0a27674b39f234b50c66d404c75`. The restored compiler exactly matches SHA-256 `9785e87da1650d3a4007d234bc194c63b640524c010497884e4b93161c7bb149`; the separately restored 108-library manifest exactly matches `b13ee3a64a0d52a1bffd5b509cdfd56552444b4295dd258463edf46cb58e9133`. The [first restoration attempt](https://github.com/vincentkoc/tsc-ts/actions/runs/40054706699) failed an added post-build content guard on npm workspace-launcher mode normalization and retained no native bytes; it establishes neither a binary match nor mismatch.

Consumer transport refresh `782b3a63c288a0661c7009626cb28c48b6da1f91` changes only seven run/artifact/hash/expiry literals or comments (+7/-7). Compiler source and binary, libraries, workload, sandbox and qualification logic are unchanged. Exact-diff independent review, collector syntax, scoped formatting and workflow syntax checks pass. [Current-head PR tooling](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40056653030), attempt 1, passed the focused boundary tests, both tooling typechecks, lint, formatting and workflow checks; its comparison job was skipped with zero steps. [Workflow Sanity](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40056653034) also passed. No graph, cache or wrapper campaign was redispatched. The completed behavioral proof remains at `04c2ea15fe62ed3d71f71dd6e9e70a7654ac35a5`, not a fresh run at the transport head. No moving-build fallback.

## Limits and Follow-ups

- The [historical ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175991#issuecomment-6244599337) covers `04c2ea15fe62ed3d71f71dd6e9e70a7654ac35a5`, with no actionable findings or before-merge requests. It used REST/linked-artifact evidence; the separate audit above performed receipt replay. It is not an exact-head review of the transport refresh, which received separate bounded independent review. Landing remains subject to explicit owner approval.
- The [previous 38-graph run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39144853163) attempted 576 trials: 567 valid, nine explicitly OOM-killed/rejected at 12GiB, none unattempted. Those results and all 180 passing canaries remain historical evidence for the previous compiler head.
- The [six-trial memory diagnostic](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39181890646) completed candidate trials at both soft targets; all four pinned/reference controls OOM-killed at 12GiB. Different CPU models prevent attributing timing/GC differences to the soft target.
- Synthetic cache correctness and the seven-target packaged-launcher smoke are bounded proofs, not general warm-build performance or raw/package equivalence. Canonical-wrapper correctness is now admitted only under its declared profile; whole-CI performance and actual interruption recovery remain unproven. Per-graph timings do not establish a whole-CI improvement.
- Follow-up: surface the first failed admission-smoke cause directly in job logs, without requiring artifact inspection.
- Full PR delta against stack base `476fbb2663c1b6e2c67d14e3a8b26cb793e9fc05`: tooling/workflow +3,109/-144 (**+2,965 net**), tests/fixtures +1,095/-0; no product runtime changes. The positive tooling delta owns bounded cache transport and lineage audit, runtime staging, actual-row isolation, cgroup barriers, terminal outcome and cleanup receipts. These are required to distinguish complete compiler/wrapper proof from a collector-only green result. Independent source reviews and scoped autoreviews closed the identified admission defects; hosted execution remains separately reported above.
