prs.title: fix: preserve paragraph breaks in streamed replies
prs.body:
Closes #42106

AI-assisted with Codex. Validation and independent code review were performed by agents.

## What Problem This Solves

Streamed source line breaks can disappear between independently delivered blocks. This affects both embedded replies and ACP replies: a forced ACP flush of `First.\n` followed by `Second.` must reconstruct `First.\nSecond.`, and paragraph boundaries must survive every shared normalization stage.

The chunker now retains source line/paragraph boundaries across drains and checkpoints when the boundary and visible text fit the cap. Coalescing respects an existing leading source line break instead of adding another joiner; ordinary text retains the configured joiner. A private `streamedSourceBoundary` fact carries an established continuation through presentation, coalescing, dispatch preparation and routing. The sanitizer skips only leading-empty-line removal for that fact on block replies; first blocks, suppressed output, errors, internal-context filtering, tool replies and final replies retain their normal cleanup.

ACP establishes that fact in its existing serial pipeline callback only after an earlier source block was accepted by delivery. Both routed preparation and the real `routeReply` normalization consume it. Async admission order, source cursors and fence handling remain with their existing owners. A direct import from the canonical payload type also avoids the type-only barrel cycle caught by CI. No public configuration/protocol fields or channel-rendering changes are introduced.

## Candidate and integration

Candidate: `5847aff32fb96bd45484fadde6bbc02195789440`.

Merge commit `f475a3adf14862e7c7cc34ede09c1fea4304520e` incorporates frozen main `5f357b747802439b4878dea48a78bb91957b7ff5`. That merge commit’s tree matches the recorded conflict-free `git merge-tree` result, and its frozen-lockfile install passed. The current candidate descends from that verified merge. Against that base: 20 files; production +160/-29 (net +131), tests +771/-15 (net +756).

## Evidence

- On the merged candidate, **954 tests passed across 21 distinct affected/sibling files**. This includes the chunker, actual embedded presentation/dispatcher/coalescing path, ACP projection and delivery, real routing, sanitizer controls, source checkpoints, fences, BTW and channel delivery.
- Chunker regression: the old branch source failed 5 of the 70 cases; the repair passes all 70, including single-LF, split paragraph and source-cursor contracts.
- The six new ACP source-reconstruction cases failed with the old branch normalizers, after the independent chunker repair. They pass after the cutover. The 12-case suite exercises the real projector → coordinator → preparation → direct dispatcher or real `routeReply` → durable wrapper, with the **outbound delivery boundary mocked**. Controls cover a suppressed first source, status output and marked blocks reused as final/tool replies.
- The 17-case embedded composition suite covers both single-LF and paragraph prefixes, metadata copies and media-caption coalescing, plus lane/filter/cache controls. Its new real chunker → presentation → coalescer → dispatcher matrix checks one forced drain producing multiple source boundaries; only the two single-LF categories fail on `f475a3adf1`, and all four categories pass after the one-line joiner repair. Existing ordinary-text configured-joiner cases remain green.
- The complete `check-changed --base 5f357b747802439b4878dea48a78bb91957b7ff5 --head HEAD`, exact `pnpm check:architecture`, `git diff --check`, scoped lint/format and owner type checks all passed. The clean private-QA runtime build passed, with temporary observation code absent.
- Independent reviews covered the chunker and ACP changes, including their real callers and the final proof below. A separate independent agent reviewed the complete `5f357b7478..5847aff32f` source diff, including source accounting, chunk limits and fences, delivery lifecycle, metadata propagation, direct/routed normalization and filtering, and reported no actionable finding. The earlier bundled autoreview helper produced no validated report; it is not counted as a successful review.

### Actual Gateway evidence

The original matched experiment is retained separately: with identical scenario and log-only instrumentation, the pre-presentation-fix `a32bf3f44c` production overlay produced `["First", "Second"]`, while `5a50d8b762` produced `["First", "\n\nSecond"]`. This established the earlier embedded-path repair.

The current candidate `5847aff32f` was then rerun as a **regression confirmation**, using the same stable mock stream, signed local Slack ingress, real Gateway/Slack plugin and local Crabline API. Its source and dependencies differ from the old pair, and diagnostic field bindings were renamed; this is not presented as a new strictly paired experiment against that old baseline.

Temporary log-only observation immediately after shared sanitization and before the channel transform produced:

```jsonl
{"text":"First","applyChannelTransforms":true,"hasChannelTransform":true,"transformAlreadyApplied":false}
{"text":"\n\nSecond","applyChannelTransforms":true,"hasChannelTransform":true,"transformAlreadyApplied":false}
{"text":"First\n\nSecond","applyChannelTransforms":false,"hasChannelTransform":false,"transformAlreadyApplied":false}
```

All three records were retained. The frozen predicate `applyChannelTransforms && hasChannelTransform && !transformAlreadyApplied` selects exactly two nonempty blocks within the 20-character cap; their concatenation exactly equals the emitted SSE source `First\n\nSecond`. The third record is internal final normalization with no channel transform. All `reply_payload_sending` records were exactly two block deliveries; native API logs contained exactly two `chat.postMessage` calls (`First`, `Second`) and no extra final/fallback send, update or delete.

The instrumentation and scenario copy were restored before the clean runtime rebuild and final checks. This proves the observed shared source boundary in an isolated, instrumented Gateway. Slack's existing channel transformation/rendering remains unchanged; no live external-channel result is claimed.

## CI

[CI run 34807553901](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34807553901) completed successfully for `5847aff32fb96bd45484fadde6bbc02195789440`. Its completed-check snapshot recorded 169 SUCCESS, 44 SKIPPED and 1 NEUTRAL, with no failed or pending checks.

[ClawSweeper Revision 18](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/125340#issuecomment-5317656663) reviewed this exact head, found the prior ACP/coalescing findings addressed and no remaining actionable defect, and marked it ready for maintainer review. Maintainer review and merge remain pending.

prs.title: fix(gateway): isolate scheduled runs from worker refresh scope
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Workboard automation nudges fail with "Plugin runtime changed" when a script-payload cron job runs after the worker that nudged it has ended.

In plain terms, a card-completion event could schedule the board's owner job, but that job inherited a permission lifetime from the worker that had just finished. The job therefore started and immediately lost permission to call its first tool. Scheduled and manually started runs were unaffected.

## User Impact

Event-driven Workboard automations now start with their own scheduler-owned lifetime instead of inheriting the ended worker's refresh scope. Scheduled runs, manual runs, tool restrictions, cancellation, and stale-tool rejection keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scheduler already replaces Gateway caller, plugin registry, and request scopes, but it intentionally preserved unrelated ambient async context. One of those inherited contexts was the agent plugin-runtime refresh owner, so a queued run captured the closing worker's owner and every tool call rejected it.

The scheduler boundary now clears only the plugin-runtime refresh field before running detached work. A real agent run still creates its own refresh owner through the existing embedded-runner path.

## Evidence

Base-red behavior probe using the production refresh and scheduler owners:

```text
refresh_assert=Error: Plugin runtime changed. Continue with the refreshed tool catalog; do not repeat completed actions.
```

Head-green with the same probe:

```text
refresh_assert=ok
```

Focused regressions:

```text
src/gateway/scheduled-run-gateway-context.test.ts                    2 passed
src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.plugin-runtime-refresh.integration.test.ts  17 passed
```

The new regression holds the scheduled callback until the originating refresh owner closes, then verifies the callback no longer inherits that closed owner. The adjacent integration suite verifies real agent runs still reacquire generations and preserve run authority, committed work, and terminal results.

- `pnpm test src/gateway/scheduled-run-gateway-context.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.plugin-runtime-refresh.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/agents/plugin-runtime-refresh.ts src/gateway/scheduled-run-gateway-context.ts src/gateway/scheduled-run-gateway-context.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/agents/plugin-runtime-refresh.ts src/gateway/scheduled-run-gateway-context.ts src/gateway/scheduled-run-gateway-context.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

Focused typecheck remains unavailable in this container because the pinned `tsrs` binary requires `GLIBC_2.34`; the host loader fails before project checking starts. A full Workboard card lifecycle was not run against a live Gateway, but the regression and production probe exercise the exact scheduler/refresh boundary that produced the reported error.

## AI Assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Codex). The scope came from #170985 and was validated against the real scheduler and refresh owners. No production data, credentials, or external services were used.

Closes #170985

prs.title: fix(secrets): secure captured contracts and reference docs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

SecretRef credential reference files could drift from the source target registry because they were maintained separately, while external channel-contract loading needed a deterministic captured-source boundary that remains compatible with existing native admission receipts.

## Changes

- Generate both SecretRef reference artifacts from the canonical registry and enforce drift checks in the documentation gate.
- Load bundled source manifests and channel contracts through captured source while failing closed on malformed manifests, blocked candidates, incomplete discovery, mutable configuration, and escaped targets.
- Preserve supported exact, wildcard, inherited `baseUrl`, in-root symlink, extensionless module, and unrelated extensionless asset behavior.
- Capture executable contract dependencies by canonical path, including static imports and bound literal `require` aliases.
- Bound capture entries and bytes, revalidate source descriptors, and reject unowned hardlinks before executable loading.
- Upgrade legacy managed-native receipts only when the installed and captured names still account for the complete inode link inventory.
- Use private native copies for strict runtime captures, replace hardlinked or source-referencing recovery namespaces, and preserve selected-host validation.
- Keep OpenClaw-owned private admission sharing while rejecting external links, late source replacement, and non-missing source-resolution errors.
- Preserve admission-owned native-link inventories when recovery retains an input after the original installed source is removed.
- Resolve channel security surfaces from each collected source root so documentation checks remain deterministic when ambient bundled-plugin discovery is disabled.

## Evidence

At signed head `6b42e60d4e277b26ad6f7bed1b75ba9135251472`:

- Native recovery after package removal passes for standalone and package-export variants, including the file-symlink fallback path.
- Recovery-link inventory propagation is covered across multiple same-inode members after an original source is removed.
- An additional external hardlink remains rejected after recovery-link propagation.
- Source-directory `EACCES` and other non-missing realpath errors fail closed; only confirmed missing paths are skipped during retained recovery.
- Strict native captures resolve to private `nlink=1` inodes rather than the installed source inode.
- Legacy receipts with exactly the admission-owned names are upgraded, while late hardlinks and pathname substitution remain rejected.
- With `OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=1`, the SecretRef generator still loads source-owned channel security surfaces and reports the generated artifacts as current.
- Independent correctness and security reviews found no remaining actionable findings.

## Validation

Current-head validation:

```bash
OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/generate-secretref-docs.ts --check
# passed: SecretRef reference docs are up to date.

pnpm test test/scripts/secretref-docs-file.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# passed: 1 file, 8 tests

pnpm check:bundled-channel-config-metadata
# passed

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.scripts.json --incremental
# passed

pnpm exec oxlint scripts/generate-bundled-channel-config-metadata.ts test/scripts/secretref-docs-file.test.ts
# passed

git diff --check
# passed
```

Native recovery validation:

```bash
pnpm test src/plugins/plugin-module-loader-recovery.test.ts src/plugins/plugin-native-namespace.legacy-hardlinks.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# passed: 2 files, 20 tests

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.plugins-platform.json --incremental
# passed
```

Post-merge validation before the CI follow-up:

```bash
pnpm test src/plugins/plugin-native-namespace.legacy-hardlinks.test.ts src/plugins/plugin-generation-artifact.admission.test.ts src/plugins/plugin-generation-executable-capture.test.ts src/plugins/plugin-generation-source-inspection.test.ts src/plugins/plugin-source-file.copy.test.ts src/secrets/channel-contract-api.external.test.ts src/secrets/credential-matrix-docs.test.ts src/secrets/target-registry-data.current-snapshot.test.ts src/secrets/target-registry.docs.test.ts test/scripts/ci-workflow-planning.test.ts test/scripts/secretref-docs-file.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# passed: 11 files, 707 tests
```

Earlier behavior-bearing validation:

```bash
pnpm build
pnpm check:secretref-docs
pnpm check:assertion-safety
pnpm check:docs
pnpm exec oxfmt --check
pnpm exec oxlint src/plugins/plugin-generation-artifact.ts src/plugins/plugin-generation-capture-budget.ts src/plugins/plugin-generation-source-lookup.ts src/plugins/plugin-instance-module-loader.ts src/plugins/plugin-native-admission.ts src/plugins/plugin-native-namespace.ts src/plugins/plugin-native-namespace.legacy-hardlinks.test.ts
```

## Limitations

- No external provider behavior was required or claimed; proof is deterministic and repository-local.
- The security-sensitive-path gate requires fresh maintainer approval for this head.
- The persisted native-link inventory compatibility decision remains maintainer-owned.
- The preceding hosted run also exposed production/core-1 type failures reproduced on current main and unrelated flaky Telegram, Gateway, Discord, Codex DB, UI, and Feishu tests.
- Hosted CI and automated review have restarted for this head.

Disclosure: AI was used to understand the codebase and review the fix.

prs.body:
Related: #182106

## What Problem This Solves

Workshop learning reviews can report only “Completed-turn transcript anchor changed” when the failure is an unavailable transcript index, leaving operators unable to distinguish it from a genuine anchor mismatch.

## User Impact

Operators get a bounded reason and observed review phase for supported source-bound refusals. This is diagnostics only: it does not recover failed reviews, attribute historical incidents, or change which reviews run. Current-main learning/admission policy is preserved; no propose-mode restoration or release compatibility is claimed.

**Draft / unvalidated.** Receiving revision: `b7b7415ae65bb230632a31ee5bcc302d23cf31a2`. Original candidate: `11ca9540509de9f3f81b7580a839aa5cf56733d2`; corrected head: `ec84f20956f81092b2138dc347b1db28b62dec9f`. Required CI evidence is still pending. No production deployment is proposed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Classify the existing failure using readiness/anchor predicates at the existing read point; transport only narrowly validated, source-bound diagnostic detail using existing task correlation through the current transcript-worker error owner; and emit bounded Workshop failure metadata. Existing generic refusal messages remain intact. Unknown, malformed, unrelated or unbound detail falls back to the existing generic error.

No retry, waiting, rescheduling, anchor recapture, reconciliation, recovery, cancellation/admission policy or mutation changes. No schema, dependency, release-policy or workflow changes. The shared generic worker runtime is not modified.

The older 2026.9.3 patch in the issue is reference evidence, not this port. Related foreground reports #152511 and #159692 are not verified duplicates or established repairs for this diagnostic-loss path.

## Evidence

- Pinned-source applicability inspection confirms the current domain fence codec discards this distinction; the separate projection-unavailable error type does not repair the anchor-fence path.
- Focused regressions cover the actual transcript worker, anchor mismatch/index unreadiness, qualifying and malformed metadata, accessor rejection, source binding, privacy, and Workshop refusal before fake-provider entry. They are not claimed passing before hosted execution.
- Original baseline CI: https://github.com/jarvis1982oc/openclaw/actions/runs/40054783668 (unchanged receiving SHA). Locale parity failed with catalog fallback baseline drift. The custom iOS screenshot job did not start, with GitHub's billing/spending-limit annotation. Those are baseline/environment failures, not candidate failures.

The diagnostic helper is unused by original production code; regressions assert the original refusal before missing-detail expectations. Candidate results will be updated here with immutable revisions and actual outcomes. Prior 9.3 local test counts are not receiving-branch proof.
- Original published candidate content was read back: all 16 file hashes match the reviewed source port. Initial independent static review found no remaining scoped logic defect (superseded by the exact-head upstream findings below); patch apply check passed. These are not runtime test passes.
- No local dependency tree was installed or borrowed. No real model calls or live production state were used.

The held-lock `worker.execute` path retains generic refusal behavior and does not receive this ordinary transcript-worker diagnostic adapter. This draft does not claim universal worker-path diagnostic coverage. Full current-main type/lint/build/fake-provider E2E results remain pending. All four runs use the unchanged `ci.yml`, `test_runtime_policy=node`, default runner/shape, full validation, no release-gate override. **Node-only:** no Bun parity or later-main/merged-head validation claim. The original pinned main is not the later moving PR base.

prs.title: fix(anthropic): fail over on Claude CLI session limits
prs.body:
Closes #118793

Credit to @germankovacevic-lab for the report and exact error text.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users relying on a configured model fallback chain would get a terminal `surface_error` instead of trying the next model when Claude CLI reported that the account or session usage limit had been reached.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Anthropic provider now maps the observed Claude CLI usage-limit prose to the existing `rate_limit` failover reason while preserving the current structured Anthropic error mappings. The prose matcher is gated to the `claude-cli` backend so unrelated providers and unrelated session-limit errors retain their existing behavior.

The shared classifier now dispatches directly to an already-loaded, explicitly matched provider hook through leaf process-global registry slots and retains full provider discovery as the fallback. The build also exposes the existing full provider runtime at a stable package-internal entry, so the lazy source/dist bridge no longer resolves outside the package after bundling. The leaf scope-key and failover-context contracts keep this synchronous path out of gateway/plugin import cycles.

## User Impact

Claude CLI subscription exhaustion can now advance through the configured model fallback chain instead of stopping the run immediately.

## Evidence

- Controlled process-level replay on exact final head `1c1725ed277b3d210fd6843fc2b5102d063ae3a9`: [`reason=rate_limit`, `status=429`, fallback succeeds](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/118835#issuecomment-5171471700).
- Added focused regression coverage for the reporter's exact `You've hit your session limit` message and Anthropic's current `You've hit your limit` wording, plus negative coverage for other providers and unrelated Claude CLI session limits.
- Added unmocked CLI-output-to-provider-hook wiring coverage and a built-bundle singleton smoke that resolves a hook alias through the production classifier.
- Focused Vitest: 4 shards, 6 files, 125 tests passed; after the final lint-only cleanup, the 2 directly affected shards were rerun with 7/7 passing.
- Exact final-head architecture gate: `Madge import cycle check: 0 cycle(s)`.
- Exact final-head unified production build and built plugin singleton smoke: passed.
- Targeted `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` on the final change: passed.
- Mandatory external Codex autoreview against the exact final Git tree: clean, no accepted/actionable findings (`patch is correct`, confidence `0.98`).
- TruffleHog scan of the review bundle: clean.
- Upstream wording contract: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/54750

prs.title: feat(nodes): prefetch worker archives before first session
prs.body:
Fixes #140425

## What Problem This Solves

The first session on a persistent node after a Gateway update still has to acquire the new worker archive, even when the node has been connected and idle.

## User Impact

Capable persistent paired nodes now prefetch and verify the current pinned archive in the background. A session preempts an unfinished prefetch or reuses its completed archive. Failed prefetch and older nodes retain normal session-owned installation. Extraction, worker publication, prewarm, and activation remain owned by the session; this does not eliminate all first-start preparation time. No new configuration option is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

This deliberately revisits the background-installation boundary from #140449 using a negotiated archive-only mode in the existing bundle RPC. Prefetch never extracts or executes worker code, so it cannot publish or prewarm a runtime under a superseded enrollment owner. Downloads and verification are cancellable; foreground installation aborts background work before taking the node's installation queue. Gateway preparation is bounded to one attempt per node, connection, and build, is cancelled on disconnect, enrollment takeover, transport replacement, and shutdown, and warns on failure without a retry loop.

Maintenance pins the current hash before prefetch. The archive occupies the existing hash directory without an installation receipt and follows normal bounded bundle retention; no second cache, state store, dependency, or retention policy is introduced. Each session verifies staged bytes and falls back to acquisition if staging is absent or corrupt. Optional capability negotiation preserves older-node and older-Gateway behavior and excludes disposable cloud hosts.

## Evidence

- Node 24.22.1, frozen dependency installation. 147 distinct focused tests pass across the native installer, bundle protocol, Gateway installer, retention coordinator, connection negotiation, and inventory suites.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/node-workspace-retain-coordinator.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/node-worker-bundle-installer.test.ts src/node-host/connection.test.ts src/infra/node-runner-inventory.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 96 passed, 299.81 seconds wall time including the first compiled worker-cache preparation.
- Final rerun after mechanical lint corrections: `pnpm test src/node-host/node-worker-bundle-installer.test.ts src/worker/node-bundle-install-protocol.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/node-workspace-retain-coordinator.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 90 passed, 21.51 seconds wall time. The earlier native/protocol run also passed all 51 tests in 19.51 seconds.
- The archive-staging regression fails against the original installer as intended (7.85 seconds wall time), then passes with this change (8.53 seconds). Real HTTP and filesystem fixtures prove one acquisition total across prefetch plus first session, foreground progress while the prefetch response is held, failed/corrupt-prefetch fallback, disconnect cancellation, and normal archive cleanup. Coordinator tests cover warning-only failure, enrollment/shutdown cancellation, old-node fallback, independent maintenance, and current-build pins.
- Core typecheck, scoped type-aware lint through the repository wrapper, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 findings; subsequent changes only correct mechanical lint issues.
- No current deployment-latency claim: #140449's historical 31.97-second cold versus 7.79-second warm activation is not a measurement of this archive-only change. Live Gateway/paired-node upgrade testing was not run; PR CI supplies broader proof.

prs.title: fix(telegram): ignore native commands from senders the DM policy rejects
prs.body:
Closes #181955

## What Problem This Solves

With `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`, a normal message from a sender who is not on the list is dropped. The same sender's native command (`/status` and the rest of the menu) got the reply "You are not authorized to use this command." That tells a stranger a bot is listening.

## User Impact

Senders the DM policy does not admit get no reply to native commands, the same as for ordinary messages. A sender who is admitted but is not allowed to run the command still gets the refusal. Pairing still replies, so a first contact can finish the challenge. `commands.allowFrom` denials are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

#131408 made the refusal text deliberate for a channel-admitted sender who lacks command permission. This path was also used when `dmPolicy` itself rejected the sender. The command authorization result now carries that distinction, and the native-command dispatch returns without sending when the denial is `dm_policy_not_allowlisted` or `dm_policy_disabled`.

## Evidence

Regression in `src/channels/message-access/telegram-native-owner.test.ts`: a native command as sender 300 with `dmPolicy: "allowlist"` and `allowFrom: ["999999"]` must not call the handler and must not send a message. The existing owner-admission cases still expect the refusal text.

I could not run the OpenClaw suite on this machine. CI is the run that counts.

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

prs.title: feat: resume requesters after deferred sessions_send replies
prs.body:
Closes #112372

## What Problem This Solves

Adds opt-in `wakeOnReply: true` behavior to `sessions_send`. The tool returns after target dispatch, then resumes the exact requesting session incarnation and captured ingress route when that target run succeeds or fails.

## Why

An agent can currently delegate work and return from the tool call, but it cannot durably express “my user is waiting for this particular result.” Legacy A2A announce behavior is not correlated to one target run or pinned to the exact requester route, so the user may not hear the result until another inbound turn wakes the requester.

## Changes

- Add opt-in `wakeOnReply` tool contract
- Register completion before target dispatch
- Persist terminal payload before target settlement
- Replay prepared and interrupted dispatches at startup
- Reuse one stable continuation idempotency key
- Retire dispatch only after transcript persistence
- Hand accepted restarts to session recovery
- Pin session incarnation and complete delivery context
- Require explicit captured channel account
- Lazily add deferred state on existing databases
- Suppress legacy A2A flow for opted-in calls
- Preserve all omitted-option behavior

## Safety And Recovery

The model cannot provide a return destination. OpenClaw captures the requester session ID and normalized `DeliveryContext` from trusted runtime state. Registration fails if the external origin does not contain an explicit `channel`, `to`, and `accountId`; continuation dispatch therefore cannot substitute a provider-default account.

The target terminal payload is written while the registration remains `pending`, before the target is allowed to settle. After settlement, dispatch changes the row to `dispatching`. Gateway acceptance does not complete that row. The row is retired only after the continuation's user turn is durably written to the exact requester transcript.

Gateway startup reconciles both prepared `pending` rows and interrupted `dispatching` rows. If the exact requester session incarnation owns the continuation run ID and its transcript contains that run's user turn, deferred recovery retires its row without another gateway call and leaves the existing main-session recovery system as the sole post-restart continuation owner. If no transcript turn exists, deferred recovery replays the dispatch with the same continuation ID. Durable-ownership inspection failure suppresses dispatch and leaves the row available for a later recovery attempt.

Persistence failure before target settlement prevents settlement. Ambiguous continuation dispatch failure remains durable and restart-replayable. Completed, expired, explicitly cancelled, or mismatched state produces no new continuation. Required delivery and `expectedExistingSessionId` prevent route or incarnation fallback.

This is not a general durable outbound outbox. It provides durable target-result correlation and coordinates accepted continuation ownership with OpenClaw's existing main-session restart recovery for this opt-in `sessions_send` path.

## Evidence

Current head `16ccee3e2f2b`, rebased onto `openclaw/main` at `9faf34d3bcb`:

- `pnpm test src/agents/sessions-send-deferred.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts src/gateway/server-startup-post-attach.test.ts`
  - Passed 168 tests across three repository-routed Vitest shards in an isolated Node 24 container.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`
  - Passed the production source typecheck.
- Focused test typecheck for the three changed test files
  - Passed against the repository test tsconfig and ambient declarations.
- `pnpm format:check <changed files>` and `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <changed files>`
  - Passed with zero formatting errors, lint errors, or warnings.
- `node scripts/generate-kysely-types.mjs --verify` and `git diff --check`
  - Passed after the rebase.

The previous head also passed `check:changed`, the build, the full test type graph, and 363 focused agent/gateway tests. Those broader results predate the current-main rebase; current CI is the broad validation source for this head.

Regression coverage includes:

- prepared completion recovery after restart
- claimed dispatch recovery after restart
- accepted-before-retirement handoff to session recovery
- exactly one post-restart model continuation admission
- claim without transcript remains replayable
- gateway transcript persistence retires the dispatch
- stable idempotency after ambiguous dispatch failure
- pre-settlement persistence failure blocking settlement
- startup replay after gateway methods become available
- lazy table creation on an existing current-schema database
- explicit account preservation and no default substitution
- exact requester session ID and route capture
- target success and terminal failure
- duplicate, mismatched, cancelled, and expired state
- concurrent requester origins
- incompatible tool options
- omitted-option compatibility
- legacy A2A suppression for opted-in calls

Not yet run: a live two-agent channel round trip using `wakeOnReply`. This remains a draft for external design review before live proof.

<details>
<summary>Redacted AI-assisted decision transcript</summary>

This PR is AI-assisted. The author reviewed the implementation and validation and can explain the code.

**User need:** “We do not want to destroy wake in the channel you asked. We want a setting for ‘my user is expecting me to come back with an answer.’”

**Agreed contract:** make the behavior opt-in on `sessions_send`; return after the target run is accepted; do not expose the target result to the initiating turn; resume the exact requester session incarnation and ingress route on target success or terminal failure; suppress legacy A2A ping-pong/announce only for that call; never use a fallback destination.

**Review corrections:** persist the completion payload before target settlement; reconcile both prepared and interrupted dispatches after restart; reject external origins without a canonical account so ordinary delivery cannot choose a provider default; and keep an accepted dispatch durable until transcript persistence transfers restart ownership to the existing main-session recovery system.

The optional `autoreview` skill was not run. Direct diff review and the repository gates listed above were run instead.

</details>

## Review Focus

- Whether pre-settlement persistence plus startup reconciliation is the correct durability boundary.
- Whether transcript persistence plus the exact restart-recovery claim is the correct ownership-transfer boundary after gateway acceptance.
- Whether the feature-local lazy table lifecycle is the correct additive upgrade path.
- Whether requiring an explicit captured account is appropriate for every external ingress adapter.

prs.title: fix(telegram): drop native commands from DM senders dmPolicy does not admit
prs.body:
Closes #181955

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: with `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`, a stranger's ordinary DM is dropped silently, but their builtin native command (`/think`, `/login`, ...) gets the reply `You are not authorized to use this command.` — confirming to an unknown sender that a bot is listening.

## User Impact
Unadmitted DM senders are now ignored for native commands exactly as they are for messages, so a Telegram bot under an allowlist policy no longer reveals itself to strangers who probe the command menu. Owners and allowlisted senders are unaffected.

## Why This Change Was Made
The builtin native-command lane always dispatches with `requireAuth: true` and answered every unauthorized sender with the refusal text, without distinguishing why authorization failed. Ordinary-message admission drops a sender the effective dmPolicy does not admit without any reply. The dispatch now applies the same distinction before refusing: in a DM under an allowlist policy, a sender who is in neither the effective allowlist (wildcards respected) nor the owner list nor the commands allowFrom configuration is dropped silently with a verbose log. Senders that dmPolicy admits but who only lack command permission keep the deliberate refusal introduced by #131408, as does every group-command rejection.

## Evidence
- Regressions in `bot-native-command-dispatch.routing.test.ts`, run against the real bot pipeline: `/think` from a sender outside the allowlist sends no message and starts no turn (red on base — the refusal was sent to the stranger), and an allowlisted sender excluded by `commands.allowFrom` still receives the refusal. `/status` already fell through ordinary admission and stays silent.
- Neighbors stay green: the full routing suite 16/16 plus `bot-native-command-dispatch.delivery` and `.concurrency` 20/20 (node 24.19, direct vitest against the `extension-database-workers` shard config that owns these files).
- Not run locally: live Telegram traffic (no credentials) and project typecheck/lint lanes (CI covers).

prs.title: fix(ci): refresh stale security review publishers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes blocked native landing when an unchanged PR's Security Review result was published by outdated workflow sources. The existing dispatch replay is not accepted by older retained native workflows.

## User Impact

Maintainers can request a fresh review of a specific PR head with `/refresh-security-review <full-current-head-sha>`. This refresh grants no approval, reruns no CI, and leaves failed checks subject to the existing landing rules.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing comment resolver accepts the standalone command only on a new comment from a human with current repository maintain/admin access. It checks the live PR and exact head, then schedules the existing head-only review job. Approval commands, revocations, workflow permissions, and enforcement remain unchanged.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177485

## Evidence

- Both valid-role regressions failed on the unchanged resolver, then passed with the fix.
- All 166 event, workflow, and admission cases passed; the existing failed-CI publication regression also passed. Native runner wall times: 7.74s and 2.21s. [Exact-head hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40056139255) passed at `2df2af897612666ef0d29d2dc04e8773f5f47a31` (33 successful jobs, 28 skipped, no failures).
- Targeted type-aware lint, tooling test types, formatting, and native workflow validation passed.
- Fresh independent P0–P3 review completed with no findings.
- Live use of the refresh command requires this protected-main workflow change to land first.

prs.title: fix(ui): preserve mounted plugin catalog detail routes on startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Fixes plugin catalog detail links opening chat instead when the Control UI is mounted below a path and must infer its mount at startup.

## User Impact
Mounted catalog links and reloads keep the requested detail, query and hash.

## Why This Change Was Made
- Preserve mounted plugin catalog detail URLs when startup must infer its mount from the current pathname (no injected base path).
- Register the existing catalog-ID classifier alongside the other dynamic route matchers. No offline admission or Gateway-owned HTTP namespace changes.

## Reproduction and behavior
Open `/ui/plugins/ch_bWF0cml4?probe=1#catalog` without an injected mount. Before this patch the application infers the root mount and rewrites to `/chat/main`. Afterward it renders Matrix detail under `/ui`, including on reload, retaining query and hash.

## Evidence
### Tests and cost
- Route unit suite: 37 passed; removing the matcher produces 2 intended failures (35 pass). Latest complete run 10.40s wall / 5.42s Vitest.
- Real Control UI source-server Chromium regression: before 1 failed with actual `/chat/main` vs expected mounted catalog path (39.74s); after 1 passed (22.79s total, case 10.786s). Reload, visible Matrix level-1 heading, pathname, query/hash, and absent injected mount are asserted.
- New source-server test is registered in the serialized private-server group. Mount accessor deliberately ignores fixture injection independent of init-script order.
- Focused oxlint, formatter, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent read-only review approved production matcher and regression; final fixture/registration corrections reviewed separately.

## Browser evidence
Synthetic fixed fixtures only: actual application routing/rendering with mocked Gateway/catalog responses through a local mounted reverse proxy. This is source-server proof, not a packaged build, real Gateway, live catalog, installation, or provider connectivity test. Chromium only; WebKit not run for this routing patch.

![Before: startup incorrectly renders chat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AmelioMansour/openclaw/proof/ui-catalog-mount-20261023-1956/catalog-before.png)
![After: mounted Matrix detail survives reload](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AmelioMansour/openclaw/proof/ui-catalog-mount-20261023-1956/catalog-after.png)

## Scope and limitations
One-line production fix plus route and application regressions. No credentials, live Gateway/config changes, provider calls, or installs. Dependency overlay reuses existing local artifacts; full local typecheck is unavailable under the repository external-declaration safety guard. CI must verify the complete checkout; skipped/cancelled jobs are not claimed green. Fresh bounded open-PR title search for catalog mount found no duplicate.

prs.title: feat(kimi): show code quota in usage status
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Adds Kimi Coding five-hour and seven-day quota windows to the existing provider usage pipeline, including `openclaw status --usage` and the Control UI. The previous revision checked only root configuration, so an agent-authored `models.json` proxy could be overlooked and its credential sent to the official quota endpoint.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Kimi plugin owns endpoint policy, usage credential selection, HTTP requests, and response parsing. Core prepares the selected agent's effective model routes through the existing model registry and shares one lazy snapshot between usage authentication and fetching.

- All Kimi credential-sharing aliases are checked together. Custom, mixed-region, mixed-proxy, missing, or malformed routes skip Kimi usage authentication; explicitly supplied usage auth still passes the same fetch gate.
- Reused model publications must match the requested configuration. Cold route preparation uses the existing read-only model-catalog owner and manifest-declared default models, including when another provider is the agent's primary model.
- Credential-free model preparation skips ambient/synthetic credential discovery and native auth-store preparation. The existing core credential-source eligibility check is unchanged; the no-auth regression assertions concern the Kimi credential-resolution callbacks and the new cold route-preparation boundaries.
- Only one official `api.kimi.com` or `api.kimi.ai` coding endpoint is accepted. URL credentials, query strings, fragments, and redirects are rejected before credential-bearing HTTP can reach another destination.
- Managed ratio windows and reset timestamps are parsed. The earlier absolute `usage`/`limits` response shape remains supported; successful responses with no readable quota window produce an explicit error. Response bodies retain the bounded reader and unread-body cleanup.
- Gateway API-key usage eligibility uses the prepared manifest usage capability instead of a hardcoded provider list. CLI `models status` keeps its existing OAuth/token selection; the incorrect promise of Kimi API-key quota there is removed.

No new user configuration, environment option, dependency, protocol version, or SQLite schema is introduced. Normal inference routing and credential precedence are unchanged.

## User Impact

Existing Kimi API-key credentials can supply quota windows when the selected agent's effective Kimi model routes all resolve to one official managed coding endpoint. Agent model overrides and provider aliases participate in this check. Custom proxy and mirror configurations do not trigger official quota requests.

Current upstream response reference: [MoonshotAI/kimi-code managed usage implementation](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code/blob/21406fb4/packages/oauth/src/managed-usage.ts). The upstream ratio-format change was introduced in [bb0c66a15b77](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code/commit/bb0c66a15b77af5185a9d44428c87310fa358394). Its inspected caller uses OAuth; the authenticated API-key check below independently confirms the current endpoint response shape.

## Evidence

Repaired head: `026efed04ae34aaa7c8379ec545ac9891719748f`, incorporating main `623d8e02a5d87997b9378b7b4b2980fff8bc11cf` and resolving all seven conflicts. Exact-head CI: [37646624067](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37646624067), **completed successfully: 56 successful jobs, 24 scope-skipped jobs, no failed or pending jobs**. Functional tests, production/test types, lint, docs, the Node test-runtime build, and SDK declaration checks passed. A full package/artifact build was scope-skipped, not claimed as tested. The separate maintainer security-approval statuses remain blocked as described below.

- Independent Node 24 probes ran the actual Kimi hook/parser source with controlled SDK/auth/fetch boundaries. The original revision resolved a credential and requested the official endpoint for an overridden proxy; the repair performs zero Kimi credential-resolution callbacks and zero HTTP requests for custom, mixed-alias, and unknown routes. Official-route controls still resolve credentials and fetch with redirects disabled.
- Independent source probes checked alias-family aggregation, current-publication/config mismatch, one route capture per collection, and caller-supplied auth passing the fetch gate.
- Exact-head CI passed all nine route unit cases and all four cold-owner integration cases. The unit cases use the real model registry for root/agent/model-level precedence, replace mode, malformed inventory, and mixed aliases. The integration cases use the real prepared runtime with a non-Kimi primary, plus alias/provider/model proxy overrides and ambient/native-auth read backstops. The snapshot-replacement fixture explicitly gives the replacement model its proxy endpoint and asserts that the old publication is not consumed. Kimi hook and parser regressions also passed. Vitest was not run successfully on this host; this dynamic proof comes from CI.
- Focused Vitest invocation was attempted and stopped before collection because the isolated worktree has no matching dependencies. The available host Vitest is 4.1.10 versus this checkout's 5.0.1. No worktree dependency reconciliation or test-config workaround was used. Blacksmith is unauthenticated and the local Docker command is unavailable.
- `pnpm docs:list`, pinned oxfmt 0.68.0 formatting, exact-version oxlint 1.83.0 line-cap ratchet across all 17 changed source files, and `git diff --check` passed. The canonical plugin inventory generator updated the Kimi reference and its check passed. No unresolved merge entries remain.
- The complete repair diff received clean Codex medium autoreview at the helper's default P0 threshold (correctness 0.98; 83,402-byte bundle). Subsequent catalog-route and fixture/documentation corrections each received clean medium delta review (0.97 and 0.99); TruffleHog passed each final bundle. Independent reviews covered the routing and credential boundaries beyond that reporting threshold.

Production TypeScript versus current main: +454/-48 (net +406); the manifest adds 3 lines. Original PR production TypeScript was +248/-1 (net +247), so the repair adds net 159 production lines. Growth implements effective-route ownership, credential-free preparation, and the updated endpoint response contract. Tests/helpers: +741/-73; docs: +23/-2.

### Historical evidence and remaining verification

The previous PR body recorded an authenticated API-key probe on **2026-07-18**, with the official `/coding/v1/usages` endpoint returning 5h and 7d windows. It also recorded 145 focused tests and type/SDK checks on an earlier repaired revision. This is retained as historical evidence, not represented as a rerun on the current head.

On **2026-10-07**, a bounded read-only check found one existing API-key profile belonging to an agent whose Kimi routes were confirmed official. The key stayed in memory. Using that installation's existing literal proxy settings and Node 24's documented `--use-env-proxy` flag, the official `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1/usages` request returned **HTTP 200**. The response contained both legacy `usage`/`limits` fields and `usages.limit_5h` / `usages.limit_7d` with `used_ratio` and `reset_time`. The current production usage module parsed two windows (`5h`, `7d`), both with finite percentages and reset timestamps, with no error. No raw account payload, key, or quota percentage is included here.

This is authenticated endpoint and current-parser proof using controlled SDK bindings and real Node fetch, **not** full Gateway RPC or SDK bounded-reader end-to-end proof. An initial direct Node attempt lacked the installation's proxy environment and timed out without an HTTP response; the successful check kept the same 10-second budget and did not alter product timeouts, TLS policy, Gateway configuration, services, or databases.

Before merge, obtain maintainer acceptance of default automatic polling for managed Kimi routes. The current revision also requires maintainer security-review approval: the effective `security-sensitive-review/ci-gate` status says "A maintainer must approve the current PR revision." This update does not merge the PR or waive these gates.

Related: #67593 and the narrower Kimi Coding direction following #20343.

prs.title: refactor: keep single-consumer preparation with its owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Single-consumer internal modules and helper frames expose implementation details that belong with the code using them.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior, text, configuration, CLI, protocol, public package or Plugin SDK contract changes. Lazy imports, security and approval checks, resource bounds, persistence and shutdown settlement remain. The standalone session memory backend is untouched.

## What Changed

Keep playback codec policy, desktop PCM playback, Nostr relay subscription lifecycle, QA result projection and WhatsApp envelope preparation with their existing owners. Localize one-use TTS, media, terminal, status, diagnostics, Markdown and Gateway-status preparation, plus three erased UI prop aliases. Shared operations remain shared. Useful private-helper assertions move to the actual public owners rather than keeping test-only production exports.

Net production reduction: **152 lines across 22 paths** (535 additions / 687 deletions against the branch base). Moved bodies count as additions. Tests grow by 51 net lines across 18 paths to exercise the real boundaries. One mock-baseline entry disappears with its retired leaf mock; no allowance is transferred or increased.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

No rare-failure guard or supported behavior is removed. Function/profiling frame identity is not preserved. A private test that reused the same stopped PCM queue instance is retired because the public audio owner clears that queue and creates a new one for the next capture; reset implementation and fresh-capture sample/cleanup coverage remain. No race, security, durability or realistic-concurrency concession is introduced.

## Evidence

Every changed owner has focused tests and targeted native types, typed lint, format and line-cap proof. Migrated cases passed on unchanged production before cutover. Final focused packets include 40 TTS fallback cases, 29 media-context cases, 6 terminal-note cases, 43 QA cases, 27 status cases, 54 playback/staging cases, 52 Nostr cases, 27 desktop audio/panel cases, 33 diagnostics/Markdown cases, 43 WhatsApp cases, 45 Gateway-status cases and 22 UI cases. Tests run serially with one worker and isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG state; no timeout, retry, skip or suppression is added.

The Nostr negative EOSE migration waits a microtask before shutdown so shutdown cannot mask the failure it protects. WhatsApp proof uses the real reply boundary and formatter, retaining filtered-quote privacy, audio and content-free diagnostics assertions. Gateway TLS network output and human header assertions were proved before folding. UI alias changes leave runtime bodies and markup unchanged.

Final structural guards pass: format parity, assertion safety, lint suppressions, mock exports, wrapper/eager-import closure, frozen updater bindings, prompt-prefix stability and line caps. Runtime and static import cycles are both zero. Whole-candidate independent review through P2 has no accepted actionable findings. Hosted exact-head CI is the broad proof. No local build, broad suite, whole-graph typecheck, live provider/channel, pixel, performance or native-device verification is claimed. The changed WhatsApp E2E file is type/lint checked locally; its remaining E2E cases are left to hosted CI. Existing unchanged desktop panel strict-read warnings and dependency/tooling warnings are recorded, not suppressed or claimed repaired.

prs.title: fix(mcp): allow SecretRef values in mcp.servers env and headers [AI-assisted]
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Core `mcp.servers` credentials could not safely use structured SecretRefs across every runtime path. A missing secret for one static MCP server could affect other servers, OAuth-managed transports could attempt to resolve a static `Authorization` value they replace, and CLI probe paths could construct transports from the unresolved source config.

This PR makes MCP env/header SecretRefs resolve at the owning server boundary and ensures unavailable static credentials never create that server's transport.

Closes #76493.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Register `mcp.servers.*.env.*` and `mcp.servers.*.headers.*` as supported SecretRef targets in config, audit, configure, and runtime collection.
- Fence `mcp:<server>` before static transport construction, emit a safe diagnostic for that server, and keep healthy MCP servers available.
- Do not fence requester-scoped connection overrides, because the override replaces the static command, environment, and authentication surfaces.
- Use one OAuth/auth-profile predicate in transport construction and SecretRef collection so managed authentication neither delivers nor resolves a replaced static `Authorization` header.
- Resolve command-scoped MCP targets before every CLI-created probe runtime (`mcp probe`, `mcp doctor --probe`, add-time probe, and configure-time probe).
- Limit those probe targets to authored structured SecretRef objects and unresolved braced source facts so scalar `$NAME`, escaped `$${NAME}`, and raw CLI flag values are never offered to `secrets.resolve`.
- Recover unavailable authored `${NAME}` MCP credentials from config-resolution facts so active transports resolve or isolate before launch, while bare and escaped literals retain their existing meaning.
- Keep Doctor's preliminary raw-config inspection silent so a valid structured SecretRef does not produce a false "env ignored" warning before the resolved probe succeeds.
- Keep structured SecretRef acceptance root-MCP-only; `nodeHost.mcp.servers` retains its scalar env/header schema and TypeScript contract because Node Host does not own secret resolution.
- Merge `upstream/main` through `91fb03223afdf8b6e1dba89ba088474d6236b9fd` without content conflicts.

## User Impact

- A healthy MCP server remains usable when another server's SecretRef is unavailable; the unavailable static server is not started.
- A requester-scoped connection can work without a stale static env/header secret blocking it.
- OAuth MCP no longer requires an unused static `Authorization` secret; active non-authorization headers such as `X-Tenant` still resolve.
- `openclaw mcp probe` and `openclaw mcp doctor --probe` deliver resolved env/header strings to the real transport instead of dropping SecretRef objects during coercion.
- Existing MCP scalar values retain the documented config semantics: bare `$NAME` is literal, `${NAME}` uses standard config substitution, and escaped `$${NAME}` reaches the MCP child as literal `${NAME}`.
- An unavailable authored `${NAME}` credential is no longer delivered as a literal placeholder: it must resolve through its source fact or block the affected MCP transport before launch.
- Doctor no longer emits a misleading blocked-env warning for a valid structured MCP SecretRef.
- Node Host rejects structured env/header SecretRefs at config validation instead of accepting them and silently dropping their object values during transport coercion.

## Risk and Rollback

This touches an authentication/credential boundary, so the primary risk is resolving too much or starting a transport whose active secret is unavailable. The collector tests cover selected vs inactive transports, OAuth replacement, requester overrides, and per-server degradation.

- **Downgrade compatibility:** existing scalar configurations remain valid, but an older OpenClaw release cannot parse a structured MCP SecretRef after an operator saves one. Downgrading requires converting those values back to supported scalars first.
- **Stdio trust boundary:** a resolved stdio SecretRef is intentionally delivered to the configured MCP child process. Operators must trust that server with the credential, just as they must when configuring the equivalent scalar environment value.
- **Node Host scope:** structured SecretRefs remain unsupported under `nodeHost.mcp.servers`; supporting them later requires a Node Host-owned resolution boundary and execution proof.

Rollback is the PR revert; there is no data migration or stored-format rewrite.

## Evidence

AI-assisted: yes. Exact proof head: `32f0b9e3e63baf99b4f9ffbfbaf2e61feacf774e` (merged with upstream `f5553a8fee0efcb87757a65d24a3899f50529b3c`).

### Real behavior proof — PASS

This was run against disposable real OpenClaw configs and standalone local stdio MCP processes outside the test suite, on Node `v24.18.0`. The probe process exits unless its child environment simultaneously contains the fake proof value as a resolved `PROOF_MATERIALIZED_VALUE`, preserves bare `$OPENCLAW_PR69417_PROOF_VALUE`, and preserves escaped `$${OPENCLAW_PR69417_PROOF_VALUE}` as literal `${OPENCLAW_PR69417_PROOF_VALUE}`. Only after all three assertions does it expose the tool `secret_ref_materialized`. A separate Doctor process writes a mode-0600 marker only after the SecretRef is materialized and Doctor enumerates its real tool schema. No third-party service, real credential, or HAL configuration was used.

Steps and expected outcomes:

1. Configure `mcp.servers.proof.env.PROOF_MATERIALIZED_VALUE` as an env-backed SecretRef.
2. Start the exact-head CLI through `scripts/run-node.mjs`, which rebuilt the stale dist for the recorded Git head.
3. Run `mcp probe proof --json`; expect the child to accept the resolved structured ref plus both literal assertions, one connected server, tool `proof__secret_ref_materialized`, and no diagnostics.
4. Run `mcp doctor proof --probe --json`; expect the same child assertions, the server and report to be `ok: true`, and no false blocked-env warning.
5. Run `openclaw doctor --non-interactive --allow-exec` with a single-purpose real MCP process; expect local SecretRef resolution and a marker written only after `tools/list` reaches that process.
6. Run standalone `agent --local` with an unavailable authored `${NAME}` credential and an executable MCP process that writes a marker if started; expect secret resolution to fail and verify the marker remains absent, proving transport launch was not attempted.

Bounded, redacted terminal result:

```text
$ git rev-parse HEAD
32f0b9e3e63baf99b4f9ffbfbaf2e61feacf774e

$ node scripts/run-node.mjs mcp probe proof --json
[secrets] ... gateway secrets.resolve unavailable ... resolved command secrets locally.
{
  "servers": { "proof": { "tools": 1, "codexApprovalMode": "auto" } },
  "tools": ["proof__secret_ref_materialized"],
  "diagnostics": []
}

$ node scripts/run-node.mjs mcp doctor proof --probe --json
[secrets] ... gateway secrets.resolve unavailable ... resolved command secrets locally.
{
  "ok": true,
  "servers": [{ "name": "proof", "ok": true, "issues": [{ "level": "info", "message": "Codex approval mode: auto; tools have no safety annotations; calls will require interactive approval" }] }]
}

$ node scripts/run-node.mjs doctor --non-interactive --allow-exec
[secrets] doctor runtime tool schemas: ... resolved command secrets locally.
$ cat doctor-materialized-32f0b9e3.marker
tool-schema-enumerated

$ env -u OPENCLAW_PR69417_MISSING_PENDING_VALUE node scripts/run-node.mjs agent --local --message "standalone source-fact fence proof" --json --timeout 5
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "agent: failed to resolve secrets from the active gateway snapshot ..." }
}
$ test ! -e standalone-transport-started.marker
PASS: standalone transport was not launched

Overall: PASS
```

### Regression and validation evidence

- The new CLI regression failed before the fix with SecretRef objects reaching both probe runtimes, then passed with resolved strings.
- A second regression failed on Doctor's false `API_TOKEN ... blocked` warning, then passed after using silent read-only transport inspection.
- The Gateway-path scalar regression failed before the fix because all four probe callers invoked `secrets.resolve` without path restrictions, then passed with zero Gateway calls for scalar-only configs.
- The pending-template regressions failed before the source-fact repair: runtime collected zero assignments and CLI probe/Doctor delivered literal `${OPENCLAW_MCP_PENDING_TEMPLATE}`. They pass after the repair while bare and escaped literals remain unchanged.
- The Node Host schema regression failed before the scope repair for both `env` and `headers`, then passed after restoring root-only SecretRef acceptance and a scalar-only Node Host config type.
- ClawSweeper's Node Host acceptance suite passed **124/124 tests** on the exact final head.
- The unrelated console-routing test tweak, gateway test timeout increase, and branch-only Talk-secret behavior/tests were removed; the core secret collector now differs from upstream only by the MCP collector import and invocation.
- The hosted root-test typecheck initially caught three E2E fixture maps still declared with the broader root MCP type. Those scalar-only fixture builders now declare `McpServerConfig<string | number | boolean>`; the exact failing `pnpm tsgo:test:root` command passes on the exact final head.
- `pnpm check:changed` passed with the schema, config regression, Node Host test, and both affected config-type files; its production and core-test typechecks, lint, dead-export scans, metadata checks, and runtime guards all passed.
- Exact final head: `src/cli/mcp-cli.test.ts` plus command-resolution coverage, **48/48 passed**.
- MCP owner suites: collector **5/5 passed**, runtime **101/101 passed**, and isolated transport **13/13 passed** with localhost enabled.
- ClawSweeper's exact acceptance command passed all 3 Vitest shards, **120/120 tests passed** on the exact proof head.
- Exact merged-head focused acceptance passed all 5 Vitest shards, **244/244 tests passed**; `pnpm tsgo:test:root` and the expanded `pnpm check:changed` also exited 0.
- Full focused selection: **13 test files, 413/413 tests passed** on authored head `b1b4665ba80626a7b4669a11460902fa0d19e538`; the subsequent upstream-only UI merge did not overlap the MCP patch.

[Exact-head GitHub Actions run 32620894894](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/32620894894) completed against current-upstream head `32f0b9e3e63baf99b4f9ffbfbaf2e61feacf774e` with **184 jobs passed**, 14 skipped, and two red check names from one unrelated flaky test plus the aggregate gate. `check-lint`, `check-test-types`, all five core test-type stripes, the managed-image shard, and all MCP acceptance paths passed. `checks-node-compact-large-6` repeated the unrelated `src/audit/audit-event-writer.test.ts` event-loop threshold flake (262.77 ms versus 250 ms); 1,936 tests passed, one skipped, and one failed in that shard. prs.title: fix(gateway): distinguish queued chats from completed empty replies
prs.body:
Closes #124447

Related: #50298, #116649, #31346, #33016

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Gateway clients submitting a chat turn while a session is busy under `collect` would receive an empty successful `final` indistinguishable from an ordinary completed empty reply, even though the prompt had instead been accepted for a later queue drain.

This is the independently fixable classification part of #50298. It does not claim to correlate the initiating run with a later aggregate run.

## Why This Change Was Made

Queued client runs keep their existing terminal `final`, preventing older request clients from waiting forever, but now carry the backward-compatible literal `queued: true`. The marker is emitted only after successful queue admission, including the post-admission dispatch-error path; ordinary successful finals retain their exact existing payload.

The change adds no queue owner, worker, retry, or lifecycle behavior. It extends the shared protocol schema and regenerated Swift model, then marks the two existing queue-admission terminal producers.

## User Impact

Gateway clients can now distinguish “your requested run completed” from “your prompt was retained for later processing.” Existing clients can continue treating the event as a terminal final, while clients that understand the optional marker can avoid reporting the queued turn as a completed empty reply.

Clients still need a future resolution of #50298 if they must correlate the initiating run with the later aggregate response.

## Evidence

- Red before the production change: the focused direct Gateway regression expected `queued: true` on the accepted follow-up final and failed on the unchanged payload; the other 101 tests in that file passed.
- Protocol schema tests: 6 passed, including acceptance of literal `true`, rejection of `false`, and unchanged ordinary finals.
- Direct Gateway server chat tests: 102 passed, covering normal queue admission and the post-admission dispatch-error path.
- Chat terminal broadcast tests: 6 passed, including exact ordinary-final payload compatibility.
- Real authenticated Gateway WebSocket regression over loopback with an isolated session store and mock OpenAI Responses SSE: 1 selected collect/FIFO test passed (4 skipped); it observed `queued: true` before the retained prompt drained in FIFO order.
- `tsgo:core`, changed core-test/root-test TypeScript checks, targeted Oxlint/Oxfmt, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Protocol registry, JSON generation, Swift generation check, Kotlin generation, protocol-since guard, and generated-file cleanliness: passed.
- Tested under the repository-supported Node.js 22.23.1 toolchain. The optional `$crabbox` wrapper was not available in this environment, so these were repository-native local lanes; GitHub CI remains the independent containerized check.
- Exact-head GitHub CI on `ca61005f2bff82a647d39e75ac9b1736c53bc1d1` passed the protocol, Gateway boundary, security, lint/type, Node matrix, iOS debug/release build, and focused iOS lifecycle lanes. One unrelated shard is red: [`checks-node-compact-large-9`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/31930838182/job/95125328789) observed `776` instead of an exact `777` ms in `workspace-sync.test.ts`; this PR does not touch worker workspaces or timeout budgeting. That test passed once in its full 7-test file and 10/10 additional focused repetitions locally. Contributor permissions cannot rerun the upstream job.

AI-assisted: Codex helped investigate prior art, implement the focused patch, and run the validation above. I reviewed the diff and evidence. Maintainer edits are enabled.
