prs.title: fix: bound repeated transient model fallback failures
prs.body:
Closes #119711

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with a healthy configured fallback still pay an intermittently degraded primary attempt on later turns. Existing auth-profile cooldowns handle unavailable profiles, but they do not bound repeated provider/model failures when transient failures are interleaved with successes.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a process-local circuit per agent, provider, and model route. Five transient failures in 10 minutes open the circuit for 2 minutes, then one half-open recovery probe decides whether to close it or double the open period up to 15 minutes.

Only `rate_limit`, `overloaded`, `server_error`, `timeout`, and `empty_response` count. State is TTL-pruned and capped at 256 routes.

**The circuit is opt-in and off by default.** It changes which configured routes are attempted across turns, so it should not alter existing deployments implicitly:

```json
{ "agents": { "defaults": { "model": {
  "primary": "openai/gpt-5.5",
  "fallbacks": ["anthropic/claude-opus-4-7"],
  "circuitBreaker": { "enabled": true }
} } } }
```

With it disabled the fallback runner keeps its current per-run cooldown and skip behavior untouched, and the gate is never called. The circuit is process-global, so the switch is accepted only on `agents.defaults.model`; setting it on a per-agent, subagent, or tool model chain is a config error rather than a silent no-op.

An open route is skipped only when a later candidate can **actually reach transport**. A candidate that would be rejected before any provider call does not justify the skip. When every remaining candidate is blocked, the open route is attempted anyway as a last-runnable-route recovery probe, so a turn can never fail with zero provider attempts because of the circuit.

`timeout` failures are not counted while the local event loop is saturated (rolling utilization >= 0.9, 5s sample). On a saturated host, in-flight provider calls get classified as timeouts regardless of provider health; counting them opens circuits for healthy routes exactly when the host is least able to afford losing them. Other reasons still count, so a genuinely degraded provider trips the circuit even on a busy host.

This targets current `main` and supersedes the older approach in #84072. It does not change image fallback.

## User Impact

Operators who opt in get fallback answers without repeatedly waiting for a known-degraded primary. Routes still recover automatically, single-model or explicitly strict selections continue trying their only candidate, and the circuit can never leave a turn with no route at all. Operators who do not opt in see no change.

## Config surface

This adds 2 core config paths (`agents.defaults.model.circuitBreaker` and `.enabled`), so the core budget in `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` goes from 2512 to 2514. The switch is opt-in on purpose: the circuit changes which routes are tried across turns, so existing setups keep their current routing. It is accepted only on `agents.defaults.model`, where the process-global circuit is honored; other model chains reject it.

## Previous review findings, repaired

All three P1 findings came from the circuit gate re-deriving candidate eligibility instead of reusing what the fallback runner already computes. Both paths now call one implementation (`model-fallback-candidate-facts.ts`), which removes the class of defect rather than patching each instance. Two further divergences surfaced while doing that:

| Finding | Repair |
|---|---|
| Skip cache queried without an auth scope | Shared helper always passes the resolved scope. The cache keys on `(sessionId, provider, model, authScope)`, so a marker for one profile no longer answers for every profile |
| Auth profile order resolved without `forModel` (not previously reported) | Shared helper matches the runner |
| User-locked profile not promoted to the front (not previously reported) | Shared helper matches the runner |
| Agent-harness route counted as runnable without its preflight | Routes needing an unverified harness no longer justify skipping an open route. Runtimes that reach transport on the normal provider path are still allowed |
| Overlapping recovery probes carried no identity | Attempts capture the route state generation, and a successful probe closes the route in place instead of deleting it, so a superseded completion is detectable rather than looking fresh |

## Evidence

### Real transport-boundary trace on the exact head `72eac2b5865`

Re-captured after merging current `main`. Two local OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoints are served over the production `openai-completions` transport client, driven through a Gateway process built from this head (`pnpm build`, then `openclaw gateway run`) with an isolated state dir. The fault endpoint returns HTTP 503 (overloaded) until it is switched to healthy. No failures are injected through the fallback callback. Turns were sent through the Gateway with `openclaw agent --agent main --session-id <id> --message "say hi"`.

Config under test:

```json
"model": {
  "primary": "faultprov/fault-model",
  "fallbacks": ["okprov/ok-model"],
  "circuitBreaker": { "enabled": true }
}
```

Phase 1, degraded primary and fallback serves (turns 1 to 5, one shown). Each turn makes 8 or 9 primary transport calls because the runtime retries the 503 inside the attempt; the circuit counts one failed fallback attempt per turn:

```text
11:47:23.555 [model-fallback/decision] decision=candidate_failed requested=faultprov/fault-model candidate=faultprov/fault-model reason=overloaded next=okprov/ok-model detail=503 The server is currently overloaded
11:47:23.760 [model-fallback/decision] decision=candidate_succeeded requested=faultprov/fault-model candidate=okprov/ok-model reason=unknown next=none
```

Phase 2, the fifth failure opens the circuit, and turn 6 skips the primary with **no transport call to the open route**:

```text
11:53:00.616 [model-fallback] Model circuit open for faultprov/fault-model for 120s after overloaded
11:54:53.948 [model-fallback/decision] decision=skip_candidate requested=faultprov/fault-model candidate=faultprov/fault-model reason=overloaded next=okprov/ok-model detail=Model circuit open after repeated overloaded failures (retry in 7s)
11:54:54.033 [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] start provider=okprov api=openai-completions model=ok-model
11:54:54.035 [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=okprov api=openai-completions model=ok-model status=200
```

Phase 3, the endpoint is healed and the open window expires: turn 7 sends one probe, it succeeds, and the circuit closes. The answer comes from the recovered primary:

```text
11:55:23.568 [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] start provider=faultprov api=openai-completions model=fault-model
11:55:23.570 [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=faultprov api=openai-completions model=fault-model status=200
11:55:23.594 [model-fallback] Model circuit closed after recovery for faultprov/fault-model
```

Counted from the Gateway log of the same run: primary transport starts per turn were 9, 8, 8, 8, 8 (turns 1 to 5), **0** (turn 6, circuit open) and **1** (turn 7, recovery probe). Between the circuit opening (11:53:00.616) and the probe (11:55:23.568) there were 0 primary transport starts. Left running, the same Gateway later re-opened the route after five more failures (12:02:37) and skipped it on the next turn.

CLI readiness cannot be staged over HTTP endpoints, since a CLI route resolves through a registered backend rather than a provider URL. That path is covered by unit regressions: `keeps a model-configured CLI runtime runnable and exempt from provider cooldown` and `keeps a direct CLI route runnable and exempt from provider cooldown`.

### Control run with the switch removed (default behavior)

Same scenario, same head, fresh Gateway and endpoints, `circuitBreaker` deleted from config:

| | Circuit enabled | Default (off) |
|---|---|---|
| Circuit log lines | opens, skips, closes | **0** |
| `skip_candidate` decisions | 1 (turn 6) | **0** |
| Primary transport starts | 42 across 7 turns, 0 while open | **56 across 7 turns** (7 to 9 every turn) |
| Turn outcome | fallback, then recovered primary | fallback every turn |

With the switch absent the primary is attempted on every turn and no circuit state is created, which is the pre-change behavior.

### Regressions

New tests cover each repaired path:

- profile-scoped eligibility: a marker recorded for another profile does not block a candidate, and one matching the resolved scope does
- auth facts: profile order and skip-cache scope, including user-locked promotion
- harness preflight: a route needing an unverified harness is not runnable; runtimes that reach transport normally are
- overlapping probes: a stale failure cannot re-open a route a newer probe closed, and a stale success cannot erase a newer re-open
- existing coverage retained for last-route probe, runnable-fallback skip, and the host-saturation guard
- after merging current `main` (`model-fallback.circuit-breaker.test.ts`): a fallback the live operator model policy denies does not justify skipping an open route, a chain-stopped result releases the recovery lease without closing the circuit, circuit skips carry `MODEL_FALLBACK_SKIPPED_CODE`, and routing is unchanged with the switch off

### Host-saturation guard, production motivation

On a production OpenClaw 2026.6.11 deployment running this policy as a backport, a gateway event-loop saturation incident (heap 9.1 GiB, event-loop utilization 1.0, p99 loop delay 1.5s) caused every in-flight provider call to be classified `timeout` while both providers were answering HTTP 200 in 2-12s. All six configured routes opened within ~100ms of each other, exhausting the chain and surfacing hard errors. Those self-inflicted timeouts are no longer counted, while non-timeout reasons still count on a saturated host.

### Prior evidence (context)

A production OpenClaw 2026.6.11 incident recorded about 140 failed primary attempts before healthy fallback answers during a nine-hour intermittent degradation. Replaying 144 recorded failures against the rolling policy prevented 103 attempts while preserving recovery probes.

## Integration with current `main`

The branch was re-fitted to the current fallback owner rather than merged mechanically:

- config types are derived from the zod schemas on `main`, so the switch lives only in `AgentDefaultModelSchema` (used by `agents.defaults.model`)
- the shared candidate auth facts follow the runner's current auth selection (pending OAuth refresh, user-locked profile, `resolveFallbackAuthScope`); the async subscription reprobe stays on the attempting path, so the circuit gate stays read-only
- the gate treats a candidate the live operator model policy denies as unreachable, matching the runner's per-candidate re-check
- the gate reads the live candidate list after context-fit reordering
- circuit skips use `MODEL_FALLBACK_SKIPPED_CODE` like other local skips, so reply copy does not treat them as new backend attempts
- chain-stopped results (terminal timeout, abort) release a half-open lease instead of closing the circuit

## Validation on `72eac2b5865`

- CI on this head: all required checks green, including `ci-gate`, `check-docs` and `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`
- focused Vitest for the circuit, runner, candidate-facts, chain-stop, context-overflow, operator-model-policy, probe and config schema suites: 112 passed
- `pnpm tsgo:prod`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test` (shards covering the changed files), lint, `oxfmt --check`, `pnpm check:max-lines-ratchet`, `pnpm check:architecture`, `pnpm check:base-config-schema`, `check:docs`, the mock-exports ratchet and `config:docs:check`: clean for the changed files
- the two new circuit-breaker regressions fail when their behavior is removed (operator policy check, chain-stop release)
- no `.oxlintrc.json` max-lines exception; the runner stays within the standard budget

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the state machine, fallback ownership, failure classification, eligibility gating, and safety boundaries.

prs.title: fix(gateway): plugin reloads hang when config changes during Gateway startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a `plugins.reload` (or other plugin install/update/reload) request sent while the Gateway is still starting never answers when the config file changed during startup. The client times out (300 s in the reported run), and the Gateway recovers only when its config watcher gives up waiting for the plugin lifecycle lease after 10 minutes.

## User Impact

Plugin lifecycle requests that arrive during startup now complete. They also apply the config edit that was pending at startup, and startup finishes after them. Later config edits keep hot-reloading through the watcher as before. There is no config change, migration, or new option.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin request holds the plugin lifecycle lease and then waited for the config reloader's full startup readiness. Since #172266, readiness also drains the reload that initial reconciliation queues for an edited file, and that watcher reload needs the same lease. The request waited for the reload, and the reload waited for the request.

The config reloader stays the single owner; its startup is now split into two stages. Plugin application waits only for **preparation**: the startup baseline, watcher start, and initial reconciliation. The existing `running` flag already serializes it against watcher reloads. It reads the current file, so the pending startup edit is applied together with the plugin change, and the queued watcher reload later sees only its echo. Because the baseline is published before the application reads or commits anything, startup cannot overwrite an applied mutation.

**Readiness** still means nothing is in flight. The startup drain now also waits while an application is running, and the application wakes the drain when it finishes, because it may have consumed the reload timer the drain was waiting on. The startup guarantee documented with #172266 still holds: initial config publication cannot race the first request after startup. No timers, polling, retries, or config were added.

<details>
<summary>Source chain and layout</summary>

1. `src/gateway/server-methods/plugins-mutations.ts` takes the plugin lifecycle lease (`waitMs: 0`) and runs the mutation under it.
2. `src/plugins/management-mutations.ts` calls runtime application, `applyPluginLifecycleChange` in `src/gateway/config-reload.ts`.
3. That application awaited `ready`; `ready` drained the reload queued by initial reconciliation.
4. The watcher's `startTrackedReload` acquires the same lease outside the caller's context, so it waits for the request.

The behavior change is about 20 lines in `src/gateway/config-reload.ts`. That file is over its line cap, and the cap ratchet forbids growth, so five pure candidate-settlement helpers (`isConfigReloadSuperseded`, `candidateApplications`, `settleCandidateApplications`, `transferCandidateApplications`, `createObservedCandidate`) move unchanged into `src/gateway/config-reload-candidates.ts`. Net: `config-reload.ts` +27/−84, `config-reload-candidates.ts` +82. For the same reason, the regression lives in `config-reload.lease-retry.test.ts`, next to the other lease-admission cases.

Docs: `docs/gateway/configuration/hot-reload.md` now describes plugin lifecycle requests during startup.

</details>

## Evidence

- **Field report:** a local-model campaign lane (macOS, isolated Gateway, 2026-10-22) sent `plugins.reload {"plugins":[{"pluginId":"memory-core"}]}` at initial listening while its config had changed during startup. The Gateway log showed `[scheduler] running config:reload` followed by `Waiting for plugin lifecycle lease core:plugin-lifecycle/global held by …`, and the RPC client was killed after 300 s.
- **Regression** `applies a leased plugin change while startup reconciles a config edit` (`src/gateway/config-reload.lease-retry.test.ts`) uses the real plugin lifecycle lease. The plugin change enters under the lease during deferred startup preparation while a disk edit is pending. The test asserts the plugin receipt, that the startup edit was applied with the plugin lifecycle, that full readiness completes, and that a later watcher edit still applies.
  - main's reloader (`f04709b78a04`) with the new test: **fails** at the 120 s test timeout; on shutdown the stuck application rejects at its `await ready`.
  - this branch: **passes** in 0.7 s; the whole lease-retry file passes 17/17.
- **Affected suites:** all 13 reloader, startup-admission, and plugin-lifecycle suites (`config-reload*.test.ts`, `server.hooks-admission`, `plugins.lifecycle-contention`, `plugins.reload-readonly`, `server-plugins.lifecycle`, `server-reload-handlers`, `server-reload-managed-secrets`, `server-kernel.config-activation`): 13 files, **398/398 passed** on the final tree.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs` for `tsconfig.core.json` and `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-root.json`: clean. `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and the line-cap ratchet on touched files: clean.
- **Live isolated Gateway:** in progress (main baseline and this fix on fresh isolated state, own ports); results will be added here before this leaves draft.

prs.title: fix(agents): clarify intentional yields in native harness transcripts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On the Codex app-server harness, every `sessions_yield` is recorded in the native Codex thread as `<turn_aborted> The user interrupted the previous turn on purpose…`. OpenClaw ends the native turn with `turn/interrupt` after returning the yield tool result, and Codex persists that wording for every interrupt. Models permanently carry a false claim that the user interrupted them, which looks like a cancellation or Stop.

## User Impact

Native-harness continuations now explicitly identify intentional yields as agent-requested pauses, so work can continue when the expected follow-up arrives. Real interrupts, Stop and restart are unchanged. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Root cause

OpenClaw interrupts the native turn after a yield (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-lifecycle-controller.ts`). Codex persists the interruption marker (`codex-rs/core/src/tasks/mod.rs`) with fixed user-interruption wording (`codex-rs/core/src/context/turn_aborted.rs`). The app-server protocol in the shipped Codex 0.162.1 has no client-requested normal completion. `turn/interrupt` takes only thread and turn IDs (`app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs`), and `DynamicToolCallResponse` has no completion flag (`…/v2/item.rs`). A supported non-abort path doesn't exist.

### Fix

No native history rewrite. The persisted OpenClaw yield context for native-harness transcripts (`appendSessionYieldContext` in `src/plugin-sdk/session-transcript-runtime.ts`) now says the pause was agent-requested, not a user interruption. It also says that a Codex `<turn_aborted>` marker for that yield describes OpenClaw's interrupt mechanism, not a Stop or cancel. The embedded runtime's yield context is unchanged, since it never receives that marker. Real interrupts, Stop and restart are unchanged. `docs/plugins/codex-harness.md` documents the limitation; removing the marker needs an upstream completion or per-interrupt reason contract.

## Evidence

- `run-attempt.native-hook-relay-retention.test.ts` (Codex yield context, red on base) and `attempt-prompt-error.test.ts` (embedded context unchanged) pass. The lifecycle-controller (44), steering (11), plugin-refresh (5), native-process-authority (13) and `agent-tools.prefix-stability` (8) suites pass.
- Live on a Crabbox AWS host with the Codex harness: in a build combining this with three sibling fixes, 2/2 Codex fleets complete and both parents' rollouts carry the new yield context.

prs.title: fix(agents): tailor private completion guidance to requester routes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Private completion wakes (announce and requester-settle) always told the requester: "If the original request requires a user-facing update, send it through an available, permitted messaging tool; do not rely on your final reply for delivery." A requester with no conversation target, such as a parent started with `openclaw agent` (Gateway agent RPC), then called `message(action=send)` and got "Action send requires a target. This turn has no current conversation". In live fleets that was one wasted tool call per fleet; parents reported "an earlier report-send attempt failed because no conversation target".

## User Impact

Channel-less requesters record private completion outcomes in their session without attempting a target-less message send. Channel and WebChat guidance is unchanged. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Root cause

`src/agents/subagents/completion/subagent-completion-instructions.ts` exported one unconditional instruction string, used by both announce and settle wake producers without considering the requester's delivery route.

### Fix

`buildSubagentPrivateCompletionInstruction(requesterOrigin)` keeps the messaging sentence only when the requester has a deliverable target: WebChat, or a target the message tool would resolve implicitly. It reuses `resolveImplicitMessageActionTarget`, the message tool's own predicate. Channel-less requesters are told their final reply is recorded in the session and no messaging send is needed. Both producers pass the requester origin. Channel and WebChat wording is unchanged. This is wake input text (per-turn), not system prompt; `docs/tools/subagents/announce.md` documents it.

## Evidence

- Regressions, red on base and green twice: `subagent-announce.test.ts` (base: 2 failed / 15) and `subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.private.test.ts` (base: 4 failed / 7), asserting a channel-less requester gets no messaging-tool instruction and a channel requester keeps it. `embedded-agent-runner.prompt-cache.test.ts` and `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` pass, and `pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen` shows no diff.
- Live on a Crabbox AWS host, in a build combining this with three sibling fixes: channel-less fleet parents made 0 failed target-less sends across 8 fleets. The prior campaign observed such failed sends in about half of restarted channel-less parents. After #181420, which stopped advertising "send to this conversation", the main baseline in this run also had 0, so the regression tests are the targeted proof.

prs.title: improve: verify installed package recovery after interruption
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/143917
Follow-up to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176125

## What Problem This Solves

The published-package survivor tests do not cover the current packaged recovery helper while the installed CLI is missing, or interruption during retirement. The new lane must also preserve useful, sanitized evidence when its owned updater fails.

## User Impact

Test and harness coverage only; zero product runtime changes in this PR. Published 9.8/9.9 survivor cells stay unchanged. Complete installed-recovery proof is still pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

The isolated `package-installed-recovery` lane installs the exact current package, interrupts the real live-package move, joins the original writer, and runs its printed helper twice using external Node. It checks the package, launcher and complete config bytes, then exercises seven retirement cuts, completed-receipt inspection through a helper from the same artifact, and a real next update.

The current correction checks the package owner's actual permission contract. At previous-package displacement and the first candidate repair, every regular file and directory must have exactly its prior mode with group/other permissions removed. Already-private entries naturally remain unchanged; symlink modes stay exact. Complete entry inventories include the root and hidden npm files. Bytes, raw link targets, kind, UID/GID, owner/special bits and direct-rename inode/hardlink identity remain strict. The observed post-transition inventory becomes the exact baseline for status, repeated repair and retirement. Limits fail explicitly; only displayed relative path/field differences truncate. No cache exclusion, timeout increase or permission masking.

Failure capture runs before container teardown. The command owner records the selected cut and log coordinates before launch, preserves rejection without inventing a successful join or numeric exit, and closes its descriptors. Existing capture and host sanitization publish bounded, current-attempt logs and selected checkpoint fields. Both the trusted overlay and isolated test copier carry the required observation dependency.

This cell tests process interruption, not power-loss durability or arbitrary escaped-descendant cleanup. Only tests requiring actual self-SIGKILL, strict process-tree verification or Bash are gated on Windows; portable parser, summary, SQLite and diagnostic projection checks remain enabled.

## Evidence

### Current candidate

- Signed head `0b368d6d1efed686e1674169053445f236245899`, tree `cca92a5ee622d5f3874cfa01ef0aca9ce98e452e`. The native successor integrates fixed baseline `f3c3c9b68d2460a90b0ee43dfc45b68c9773b96a`, which includes the canonical [image resource-bound repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177642). That owner restored the finite-positive fallback; this supersedes the earlier stale-test-only interpretation. No bespoke media fix or failed-CI waiver is included.
- Independent integration review verified the prior 15 non-package PR blobs unchanged and the same single package-script addition. Publication/integrity/activation/filesystem owners retain the reviewed permission contract.
- Independent exact review cleared the four-path permission-witness delta `58db0909d0f9298a5519619e734474ee3ae2f6ac0d9203e82dfc6a13ae7a8070` (20,445 bytes); its scoped autoreview completed one clean pass, exit 0. The subsequent mechanical sorting correction has independent exact review: delta `906e5a6577763709071446a6527ad645655b2a37d98b5341b07146c43e4573f1` (1,310 bytes). Both dense string arrays now use nonmutating explicit code-unit ordering, preserving traversal and difference-report order. Full current diff against the fixed baseline: SHA-256 `50c016525d591f84c542074498d44c63b7a98ecded3d68d33b11ca78f66305e2` (85,295 bytes).
- The exact physical regression body passed once under external Node 26.7.0 on macOS arm64: real rename, hardlink identity, exact permission tightening, and mode/content/cache/link/add/remove/budget negatives. Source guards matched before and after; the child joined, its group was absent, and its owned fixture was removed. This is focused observer proof, not full Vitest or installed Docker proof.
- Targeted formatting, syntax, diff/privacy checks and ordinary signed-commit hooks passed. The native publication gate records GitHub proof as pending; it does not stamp local CI/build success.
- **Pending:** fresh exact-head ordinary CI, full current-source build/canonical pack, complete installed-recovery Docker execution and the task-required exact-head ClawSweeper review. The f3 runtime baseline requires a fresh package; historical package evidence does not qualify it.

### Retained historical evidence

- [caf ordinary CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40053581642), source `caf86dc9a086e9a87094b22f3527a4f02bdf1561`, tested merge `2cca022efa0b375dccf5be37874276d2ffa85b9b` over base `47ce38735155506c56228a017f548b5b356ecde5`: installed-recovery **18/18** and docker-build-helper **142/142** passed, including the complete permission witness and both copied fixtures. Build, seven type jobs, guards and ratchets passed. Overall CI failed: the owned sorting lint is corrected here; three separately inherited E2E failures remain unwaived (hooks human-output newline expectation, Telegram prepared-gateway attempt accounting, subagent completion handoff). The four diagnostics/migration/recovery-phase/assertions files were not bound in this run; prior-head evidence below is not relabeled as current proof.

- Initial full-candidate and later scoped reviews found real defects: Node SQLite row prototypes, platform process contracts, inherited lane environment, buffered extraction, diagnostics lifecycle and copied dependency closure. Their raw finding verdicts remain unchanged. Each correction received independent exact-source review; the current clean scoped review does not relabel those reports.
- [481 ordinary CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39310242301) tested merge `2462c1918f9fae13705a204d645a14cd712657fe` over base `b413bdc277ecd8b7758ba6d7ac0454dec8721e52`. The four complete recovery suites passed 143/143 with zero skips; `docker-build-helper` passed 142/142, including both corrected sqlite/historical capture-and-publish rows. Types, lint, build and ratchets passed. Overall CI failed on the image-cap assertion and aggregate. These are historical results, not caf proof.
- [Original Package Acceptance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39267616122) passed normal full build, canonical pack, integrity and installation for historical source `1db9f46b53e2bf3808df33b7967f0b021ddb357e`; its lane-admission failure was fixed. [The first artifact retry](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39288737000) exposed the subsequently fixed buffered extraction error. A real 2,097,225-byte extraction regression then passed exact bytes, exclusive-file preservation, partial-output removal and descriptor closure.
- [The 30c artifact attempt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39295459150) hit the unchanged 180,000 ms updater watchdog without useful child evidence. The diagnostics correction addressed that evidence loss. Neither an updater defect nor the timeout's cause was established by that receipt.
- [c350 current-writer Package Acceptance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39307016356) passed a normal full build in 5m43.4s, canonical pack, integrity and npm 12 installation. Its package/workflow/harness source was `c350f037ea76df4cfdfc8aa936b3b797b79a9ef2`. Artifact `12215081507` contains `openclaw-current.tgz`, version `2026.10.5`, SHA-256 `d7e1bba9f5ce8d533112a2573d92504cbc5cb9300d030bde476f83293114340a`.
- That Docker attempt reached actual displacement: the original writer returned 137 with `treeJoined: true`, the journal matched, and both live package and CLI were absent. The old opaque full-mode digest assertion then failed before the first recovery call. Sanitized evidence was published, but no per-entry inventory existed, so permissions alone are **not** a proven explanation. The new witness must expose any remaining path, content, ownership or mode drift. Helper repair, retirement and next-update assertions have not passed.

Only `package-installed-recovery` is selected for the next fresh-source Package Acceptance run, with registry image publication and Telegram/live lanes disabled (`shared_image_policy=no-push-artifact`). Landing still requires actual required CI, review and installed recovery proof.

The earlier recovery PR remains open until this distinct proof and landing complete. Relative to the fixed baseline, this PR changes 1,862 lines across 16 harness/test/command paths, with zero product runtime changes.

Updates `github/codeql-action/init` from 4.38.3 to 4.39.1
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.39.1

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

v4.39.0

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

prs.title: fix: distinguish publication policy refusals from credential failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes misleading publication recovery advice when a contributor inspects a bot-authored PR or OpenClaw refuses changes to GitHub Actions workflows.

## User Impact

Contributors can distinguish a linked-author check or an OpenClaw requester-permission refusal from broken publisher credentials, without reconnecting a working account or broadening token permissions unnecessarily. No authorization, identity, private-repository access, or workflow-write policy is relaxed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The own-PR inspection path now explains that it checks the requesting person's linked authorship, not the managed publisher's credentials, and points to the existing `edit` or `publish` action as appropriate. Private or unverified PRs keep the existing nondisclosing failure. The workflow refusal names OpenClaw's full operator-write requirement rather than leaving the failure open to interpretation as missing GitHub token scopes.

The tool description and GitHub identity guide explain the same boundaries. This does not enable importing another conversation's bot-authored PR, change inherited-workflow handling, or change contributor-credit provenance.

## Evidence

- Reproduced both misleading diagnostics through the admitted tool/Gateway boundary with synthetic fixtures before changing their owners; the new assertions failed on the old diagnostics and pass with the fix.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/github-publication-inspect.test.ts src/gateway/github-publication-workflows.test.ts src/gateway/github-repository-publication-workflows.test.ts src/agents/tools/github-publish-tool.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **116 tests passed** across five files (174.36 seconds). Coverage includes raw and agent-tool inspection, unchanged private-access failures, no writes or session mutation after rejection, real temporary Git worktrees, inherited target workflows, and requester/publisher revocation checks.
- Targeted TypeScript, lint, formatting, documentation MDX, and diff checks pass. Independent full-context Auto Review reported no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- No live participant branches, credentials, or configuration were changed. Remote GitHub behavior is represented by synthetic transport fixtures; no live credential-failure experiment was needed for these diagnostic-only changes.

## Worked on by

- @steipete

prs.title: improve: make session lists faster on large stores
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where session lists, filters, facets, and session-id lookups parsed every persisted session blob and repeated filtering and ordering in JavaScript, even though the v14 agent schema already promotes and indexes those fields.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway now treats `entry_json` as the canonical record and promoted SQLite columns as the indexed read surface. List selection, counts, creator facets, lineage predicates, ordering, and current-session-id lookup run through Kysely before surviving rows are parsed. Derived titles are projected into `session_nodes.display_name` at write time and backfilled once at startup. Runtime continues to assume the doctor-enforced canonical-key contract; no alias, compatibility, or fallback reader was added.

Pending `entry_valid` rows are intentionally excluded from indexed pages until a canonical writer rewrites them or `openclaw doctor --fix` repairs them. This accepts transient count/facet skew during a mixed-version writer window, as explicitly accepted by the maintainer, instead of retrying or reconciling on the read path. The maintainer also approved the additive title/index surface without a schema-version bump.

## User Impact

Large session sidebars and filtered session views load substantially faster while preserving pagination, visibility, creator facets, projected titles, and moved-child lineage behavior. Operators with pre-canonical stores must run `openclaw doctor --fix`, matching the runtime contract established by #116703.

## Evidence

### Performance

Seeded Testbox SQLite database: 12,000 canonical `session_nodes`, 2 KiB JSON payload per row, 25% archived, promoted interaction timestamps, and `entry_valid = 1`. Both paths were warmed, then measured as the median of five runs: the prior full-cache parse/filter/sort/slice path versus the promoted-column query with `limit = 100`.

| Path | Median |
| --- | ---: |
| Full blob scan + JavaScript selection | 70.27 ms |
| Indexed SQLite selection | 12.00 ms |
| Speedup | **5.9x** |

Final post-rebase perf proof: Testbox run 30674426726.

### Validation

- Final post-rebase focused proof: Testbox run 30669963436 passed 564 tests across Gateway session listing and lineage, accessor/conformance, SQLite query plans, TUI, and embedded-agent surfaces. This includes 94 accessor tests, 55 conformance tests, and the 12,000-row performance test.
- Exact post-rebase changed gate: run 30669963436, green, including the wizard lint shard, extension typecheck/lint, and 0 runtime import cycles.
- Post-rebase build: run 30669963436, green; no `INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT` warning.
- The first hosted head exposed an unrelated Madge cycle already fixed on moving `main`; current-main Testbox run 30669830915 proved 0 Madge cycles, and the branch was rebased onto that fix before the final proof above.
- Final title-projection leaf proof: run 30672101033 passed the full architecture gate with 0 Madge/runtime cycles plus 255 focused title/accessor tests.
- Final compile proof: run 30672730954 passed prod/test typechecks, all 125 extension package boundaries, and targeted lint; run 30673587220 passed the 100-test agent database fixture.
- Final conflict-surface proof: run 30673771719 passed architecture, production types, catalog-prewarm reconciliation, additive-schema repair, and the seeded performance test.
- ClawSweeper rank-up move applied: `pinned_at <= 0` is included in the unpinned indexed page, and the regression asserts both the zero-valued and NULL-valued rows remain visible. Run 30674426726 passed 95 accessor/query-plan tests.
- Final branch autoreview against current `origin/main`: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- SQLite schema baseline and query-plan assertions are green; no schema-version bump.

### Protocol verdict

`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/sessions.ts` changes documentation only. No field was added, removed, or retyped, so the protocol surface is compatible and no Swift/Kotlin regeneration is required.

### LOC accounting

Final GitHub diff: 59 files, **+3,587 / -1,703**. GitHub file stats classify this as production **+1,938 / -902** (net **+1,036**), tests **+1,636 / -800**, and generated **+13 / -1**.

| Deleted or trimmed | Why the cut is safe |
| --- | --- |
| `session-list-order.ts` and the synchronous list projection | SQLite owns canonical ordering; async bounded enrichment is the only list path. |
| JavaScript include-lineage chunk merge and byte-sort reimplementation | Producers switch to residual selection above 400 keys; bounded SQL sets fail loudly. |
| Pagination retry-exclusion threading | Canonical-invalid rows fail earlier; visibility retains the simpler retry-once contract. |
| Admin profile-specific work keys | Admin list visibility is profile-independent. |
| `"__row-context__"` sentinel and alias loop | `lineageKeys` is a first-class predicate and canonical opaque keys are authoritative. |
| Repeated retained-window tombstone probes | One shared helper owns the exception. |
| Read-side `entry_valid` settle/retry machinery | Writers set validity and doctor repairs; indexed reads exclude pending rows. |

Named tradeoff: the net +1,036 production LOC buys indexed selection/count/facets, exact `current_session_id` lookup, bounded child hydration, title projection plus streamed backfill and cache coherence, invalid-row-safe pagination, partial indexes, embedded/prewarm parity, and one leaf title-projection owner that keeps schema bootstrap acyclic. The residual combined-store deletion lands only with the goal-3 federation decision; this PR does not add a second path.

## Follow-ups

Goal 3 remains deferred exactly as ruled: either persist the current runtime controller into canonical lineage, changing today’s runtime-only ownership design, or redesign multi-store federation so indexed per-store queries compose without a materialized combined store.

prs.title: fix(ui): export complete conversation history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`/export` and `/export-session` previously downloaded only the currently loaded transcript window. Opening a long conversation and exporting without scrolling silently omitted its older questions and answers.

## User Impact

Conversation Markdown downloads include all history pages, independently of how far the reader has scrolled. Failed or changing reads do not produce misleading partial files.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing complete-history reader from the session-menu copy action, preserving chronological order, overlap deduplication, and snapshot consistency. The pane export now uses that reader rather than its rendered `chatMessages`; asynchronous errors use existing visible feedback and preserve the draft. Switching conversations retires an in-flight export. No Markdown presentation or server-side export changes.

## Evidence

Full HTTP-served Control UI through the actual composer and real Chromium download, with a synthetic 160-message mock Gateway conversation. Startup shows the newest80; no upward scroll and no `chat.send`. This is source-served application proof, not a production-bundle/live-Gateway/provider claim. Node24.22.1, Chromium156.0.8078.4.

| Actual served browser scenario | Observed result |
|---|---|
| Baseline: `/export` immediately after opening | Download contains80/160 messages; earliest marker absent; zero export history reads |
| Fixed: same action | Download contains all160 markers exactly once and chronologically, including earliest/newest; history offsets0,80 then tail consistency read |
| Older-page request rejected | Visible error, `/export` draft retained, zero partial downloads |
| Sidebar switches conversation during deferred older page | Old export retires before tail verification/download |

All successful fixed proofs recorded zero page errors. Unit regressions cover full-page ordering, failed reads, session/connection/instance/pane retirement; existing sidebar-copy overlap/snapshot tests remain.

## Validation

- Canonical focused UI unit owner:80tests/4files passing,16.32s.
- UI production and changed-regression TypeScript graphs pass.
- Focused type-aware lint:0warnings/errors,292rules; format and diff checks pass.
- Initial reviewed revision bundled-Control-UI E2E:8/8passing (including both `/export` and `/export-session` paginated downloads),97.35s. Initial two failures were an overbroad marker selector matching101–160; corrected to the exact earliest message, without changing production code or weakening the missing-old-message assertion.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Tlon group sends returned a fabricated `~ship/<unix-ms>` message ID instead of the provider-native dotted `@ud`. Reusing that delivery receipt for a reply targeted the wrong group post. Direct messages use a separate `~ship/<@ud>` contract and are unaffected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Tlon send owner now formats timestamps once with `scot("ud", da.fromUnix(sentAt))`. Group sends return that bare provider-native ID, while direct messages continue to prepend the sending ship. This repairs the producer boundary instead of rewriting IDs later in receipt or reply routing.

## User Impact

Agents and operators can reuse a sent Tlon group message receipt as the reply target, preserving native thread routing for both text and media sends. Direct-message IDs and existing numeric reply-ID formatting remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Before the repair: 3 of 8 focused send-owner tests failed, covering group text/media receipts and root-to-reply target reuse.
- After the repair: focused Tlon send-owner tests pass 8/8; the full Tlon suite previously passed 285/285.
- Fresh publication check: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tlon/src/urbit/send.test.ts` passes 8/8, and `git diff --check` is clean.
- Extension type, lint, format, package-boundary, and architecture checks passed during validation.
- Direct dependency proof: `@urbit/aura` 3.0.0 declarations and implementation show `da.fromUnix(number): bigint`; `scot("ud", bigint)` renders decimal digits grouped with dots.
- Scope: exactly `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/send.ts` and `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/send.test.ts`. Production `+6/-3` (net +3); tests `+74/-2`.
- Exact-head CI is terminal green, including `openclaw/ci-gate`.
- AI-assisted; the patch was inspected and validated. No agent transcript is included.

**Review required: live Tlon group root-to-reply roundtrip unavailable; do not merge until supplied.** No authorized live Tlon ship and disposable group channel were available. The deterministic poke-boundary test verifies the exact outgoing reply target, but it is not a live external-provider roundtrip.

prs.title: fix(sessions): log unreadable transcript probes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: session activity monitoring silently ignores an unreadable transcript, so operators cannot tell a persistent permission or locking failure apart from an idle conversation.

When the transcript file cannot be opened for a reason other than "missing", the probe is now reported through the existing `plugins/session-catalog` logger. It remains retryable and is still not classified as missing.

## User Impact

Operators can see why activity detection has stopped working for an adopted Claude or Pi session, while healthy sessions and missing-transcript cleanup continue to behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared JSONL activity reader intentionally keeps non-`ENOENT` failures distinct from a missing transcript because marking them missing could eventually remove a recoverable upstream link. It previously returned `undefined` without logging, which made that deliberate distinction invisible.

The change adds only a bounded warning at the existing catch site. It does not change the activity result, retry policy, marker, or link lifecycle.

## Evidence

Base-red with the new regression test: `EACCES`, `EPERM`, and `EBUSY` all return `undefined` with zero warnings.

Head-green:

```text
src/plugins/session-catalog-jsonl-activity.test.ts  4 passed
```

Real behavior probe with a `chmod 000` transcript on Linux:

```text
[plugins/session-catalog] failed to read session catalog transcript /tmp/openclaw-173080-.../unreadable.jsonl: Error: EACCES: permission denied
result=undefined
```

The same probe on `origin/main` prints only `result=undefined`, confirming the missing diagnostic.

- `pnpm test src/plugins/session-catalog-jsonl-activity.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/plugins/session-catalog-jsonl-activity.ts src/plugins/session-catalog-jsonl-activity.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/plugins/session-catalog-jsonl-activity.ts src/plugins/session-catalog-jsonl-activity.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

Focused typecheck could not run in this container because the repository-pinned `tsrs` binary requires `GLIBC_2.34`; the host loader reports the missing version before project checking starts. The reported Windows permission failure was not reproduced locally; Linux `EACCES` exercises the same open-failure branch.

## AI Assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Codex). The change was scoped from #173080, verified against the current source, and validated with the commands above. No production data, credentials, or external services were used.

Closes #173080

prs.title: fix(cli): reject doctor --force without repair mode
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `openclaw doctor --force` would be told that aggressive repairs were enabled even though Doctor remained in inspect-only mode unless `--repair`, `--fix`, or `--yes` was also supplied.

## Why This Change Was Made

`--force` remains a modifier for an explicit repair mode. The CLI now rejects the ineffective standalone combination with exit code 2 and points users to `openclaw doctor --fix --force`; help and public docs describe the same contract. JSON-producing Doctor modes retain structured error output.

## User Impact

Operators no longer get a successful-looking no-op when they intend to run aggressive repairs. Valid `--repair --force`, `--fix --force`, and `--yes --force` invocations are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Pre-fix CLI regression: `doctor --force --non-interactive` dispatched Doctor with `{ repair: false, force: true }` and left an aggressive repair finding untouched.
- Focused regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/program/register.maintenance.test.ts` — 41/41 passed.
- Core test typecheck: `pnpm tsgo:core:test` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- src/cli/program/register.maintenance.ts src/cli/program/register.maintenance.test.ts docs/cli/doctor.md` — passed on exact head `757a4d4cd5d6691c12ac15e058104c6d9b316493`.
- Exact-head CI [run 32441106349](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/32441106349) — green.
- ClawSweeper exact-head review found no actionable correctness or security finding and independently passed the live exit-2 behavior proof; it classified the observable exit-code change as requiring maintainer compatibility acceptance before merge.
- Autoreview bundle preparation and TruffleHog scan passed; the isolated Codex reviewer could not run because this executor has no valid Codex authentication (HTTP 401).

Provenance: the force/repair CLI split was introduced by commit `2d4ec35e1c3f4e2fd9af0d6946673cbc28b37f5f` on 2026-01-08 (author/committer `@steipete`; no associated PR found).

AI-assisted: Amp. The implementation and owner path were reviewed directly, and the focused behavior was reproduced before and after the fix.

prs.title: fix(github): open reconnect flow from active sessions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent's managed GitHub OAuth credential expires, `github_identity_status` can diagnose the state but cannot get the operator into the masked reconnect flow from the active session. Long-running release work must stop and wait for the operator to find the agent's Tools settings manually.

## Why This Change

- Adds a capability-negotiated `screen` action, `github_identity_settings`, that routes only the requesting Control UI to the current agent's Tools panel.
- Keeps the OAuth flow entirely inside the existing masked Control UI; no token, code, or callback data enters model context.
- Makes `github_identity_status` direct the model to open that flow and re-check identity health afterward.
- Requires an action-specific client capability in both tool construction and Gateway routing, so older or cross-origin Control UIs fail closed instead of silently ignoring the command.
- Computes reconnect guidance after effective deployment tool/action policy, preserving manual Settings guidance when `screen` or `github_identity_settings` is filtered out.

## User Impact

An active release session can diagnose an expired GitHub identity, open the correct reconnect surface for the requesting operator, and verify recovery without losing the session or exposing credentials.

## Evidence

- 50 focused tests passed across registration, identity status, and Gateway tool policy, including tool-denied, action-denied, and action-allowed reconnect guidance.
- Focused `oxlint` passed with 0 warnings/errors.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Earlier branch evidence: 91 targeted tests across Gateway routing, screen/status tools, tool registration, Control UI capability negotiation, and UI navigation; `pnpm tsgo:core`; `pnpm tsgo:ui`; `pnpm protocol:check`; `pnpm format`; `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`.

## Limits

This opens the existing operator-owned reconnect flow; it does not move OAuth handling into the model or auto-authorize GitHub access.

prs.title: fix(agents): respect stop requests during final reply delivery
prs.body:
Related historical context: #128008 and merged #128695. Current-main integration: #127836.

## Status: non-landable, test-first cancellation baseline

This revision integrates the complete twelve-file diagnostic candidate onto pinned main `b5946cfcc1623f0b423c556126ddfe960f9d3fce`, preserving all31 Session regression cases and upstream's dedicated Gateway runtime shard. Session Base/Prompting production remains byte-identical to the published `caf02b3b8035880b1431598b4582a0149fa8d721` baseline; the unpublished logical-controller repair is not applied. Four original-order defects have actual failing CI evidence, while three additional boundary reproductions and two first-reason controls remain unexecuted. Do not merge this diagnostic baseline.

## Ownership boundary and test change

The independent #127836 integration remains intact: one logical prompt stays active across retry and compaction gaps, public terminal facts drive exact steering-occurrence cancellation, and deferred-flush failure does not suppress finalization. No upstream test or queue policy is discarded.

Actual baseline failures show that an early handoff snapshot misses cancellation during awaited `agent_end` callbacks, a failed continuation can settle while a foreign core successor is active, and aborting an idle retry delay can still permit queued continuation. The unchanged Gateway fixture separately records B's failed disposition. These remain production blockers, not successful repair claims.

The existing retry table now also covers real disposal with queued input and synchronous public abort from `auto_retry_start`. It keeps the original 503 response, ten-second fake-clock delay, normal retry and empty-queue controls. The queued/disposal rows establish provider, active-retry, core-idle and queue facts before interruption. The unqueued retry-start callback instead records provider1 and core-idle; it does not require retry-controller or queue state at that notification. Disposal must leave the exact queued input dormant without a second provider request; it must not emit to listeners it has already removed. The reentrant abort case requires the original prompt to fulfill before any ten-second clock advancement, with fulfillment and rejection observation installed beforehand. Its cleanup joins the actual prompt, abort and observer before restoring real timers.

The existing post-compaction table adds a real direct-core successor acquired by the public settlement listener. It proves that B is distinct, live and unaborted, then checks that A does not publish an extension settlement into B's lifecycle. Both public and extension terminal assertions remain. The new first-reason table uses real `agent_end` and a pre-registered `waitForIdle` reaction: A retains its first handoff reason, while a later independently acquired B receives its own caller's stop reason. It does not fabricate an awaited flush; final flush is synchronous.

Source prediction on unchanged production is seven failing and 24 passing cases. The three incremental predicted failures are disposal with queued retry input, abort at retry-start notification, and public-to-extension successor reentry. Both first-reason controls are expected to pass. Those numbers are not an execution result. A strengthened public-terminal assertion may fail before the historical extension assertion in the pre-public successor case; prior later-assertion execution is not assumed.

A parked intermediate implementation exposed a new predecessor-to-successor reason-transfer regression during review. It was not published. Both production files were restored exactly to the public baseline before this test-only candidate. All source, review findings and preservation records remain retained. No public API, SDK, authorization, configuration, persistence or protocol change, production seam, timeout increase or forced replay is introduced.

The already-proved private deferred-manager repair remains unchanged: record cancellation, restart or supersession on the exact existing ReplyOperation before aborting the derived signal. Canonical methods preserve first reason, upstream, terminal, frozen, stale-expiry and retired-successor behavior; command callers without an operation remain supported.

Relative to pinned main b594, the PR has twelve changed files: runtime +27/-21 (net +6), prerequisite tooling +6, tests +1367/-66. The main integration adapts the planner test and carries upstream changes; it adds no new Session production repair. This is diagnostic staging, not acceptance of the final production shape.

## Canonical main integration

Published `d025f0e9232844ff8fe3bcfca3014214c735c9fc` could not attach CI because its test-planner expectation conflicted with current main. An older pinned preview was clean, but the actual server main b594 had one concrete planner-test conflict; no test failure or GitHub fault is inferred from that attachment state.

Upstream `ef18511a0a56bda63bc7dad8097d87ed0d3975ff` makes one dedicated Gateway runtime shard prepare the runtime, instead of doing that in each ordinary stripe. This integration preserves that canonical planner and consumer discovery. The test now keeps three strict ordinary stripes without runtime preparation and one strict dedicated-runtime entry with an independent literal inventory: active-memory, concurrent-streams and terminal-cancellation. The full/compact inventory also includes gateway-support-export-runtime. Completeness, uniqueness, and preparation checks remain; the expected inventory is not derived from the production resolver. The unchanged Gateway fixture must execute in that actual runtime shard on the new hosted candidate.

The initial resolved merge and all old public history were preserved, then all twelve candidate changes were reconstructed on a real b594 parent. The complete resulting Git tree is byte-identical to the saved resolved merge, including every upstream file. This is a clean-parent representation, not a partial index or sequencer/hook override; normal precommit checks must still scan every introduced file. No alternate index, fabricated sequencer marker, narrowed guard scan or hook override is part of this reconstruction.

## Actual public-baseline evidence

[CI33225898567](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33225898567) executed merge `6ece55f65705e30142b509cfbc08e3e4b3f322f9`, parents `9b1bc3bb93e6a004a534c4f485f26d34c911b02a` and `caf02b3b8035880b1431598b4582a0149fa8d721`. The complete run had 163 successful jobs, 17 skipped and three failures: the Session shard, Gateway shard and aggregate gate.

The [Session shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33225898567/job/99029643854) ran the previous 26-case file: 22 passed and four failed. The newly established idle-retry abort-with-queued-input case failed provider count, two instead of one, after real public abort and original-prompt join. Later dormant-queue, transcript, retry-ended and settlement assertions did not execute. Normal retry and abort-without-queued-input passed; the three prior late-callback/foreign-successor failures remained. The selected group had 2,337 passing, four failing and two skipped tests. Real handoff adoption passed.

The [Gateway core-3 shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33225898567/job/99029643771) failed the unchanged 135-second B-disposition bound; the whole fixture took 146,469 ms. Normal control delivered two intended replies. Aborted A reached its typed native-lane join and intended third reply. B was skipped after a missing exact pending-entry cancellation and accepted-unconfirmed warning; the wire remained at three intended replies, without an extra generic error. B's later final/history/provenance and strict-four-wire assertions were not reached.

A possible hidden continuation after the embedded observer unsubscribes could remove B's queued occurrence before transcript cleanup rejects its write. That sequence is source-inferred, not directly observed in the raw log. One logged embedded start cannot rule out a later unobserved core loop. The conservative no-replay policy and every Gateway assertion remain unchanged; eventual recovery must be demonstrated by that same fixture.

The exact executed object and parents were inspected. Critical Session/core/retry/transcript owners and the executed test sources match the published caf02/previous 26-case baseline, not the new 31-case test file. Thirteen other context/metadata deltas, including the actual runner/dependency changes, were separately read and qualified; this is not an all-package or entire-checkout parity claim.

## Review state

The fresh complete twelve-file diagnostic-integration P2 review completed eleven default automatic passes with exit0, no findings in any raw report, and helper status scoped-clean for that selected diagnostic-integration scope. Minimum confidence was 0.61. All eleven reports explicitly retained cross-batch owner limitations: the first specifically validated the ordinary/dedicated Gateway inventory, while still lacking complete ReplyOperation-to-native-abort and build-admission-to-worker relations; other batches could not independently verify complete planner or Session/Core relationships. These are complementary source assessments, not eleven complete integrated reviews or a production-completeness certificate. All reports and limitations are preserved. The243 whole-file inputs and all276 bindings, complete candidate tree and historical records were unchanged after review, and the recorded owned processes were gone. Known production cancellation blockers remain; the31-case fixture has not run.

Before this review, the genuine default formatter check passed on all twelve complete files using32 threads (201ms reported formatting time); pre/post source and relevant configuration stayed unchanged. This check made no source edits and does not substitute for normal commit guards, hosted tests or runtime proof.

AI-assisted. Independent source review accepted the complete 31-case test and its public-baseline contracts. The historical narrow test-authoring review completed three default automatic passes with exit0 and no findings in any raw report; the helper recorded scoped-clean only for the complete actual one-file test-authoring delta. Minimum confidence was 0.35. The first pass reviewed the supplied lifecycle source and found no authoring defect; the second and third explicitly lacked the complete test/fixture/Session/Core owners within their complementary batches and could not independently validate those boundaries. Those limits and all reports remain preserved, not promoted into a whole-PR certificate. That historical packet contained 101 whole-file semantic evidence inputs, and all 134 bindings plus preserved earlier artifacts were rechecked unchanged afterward. The full PR remains nonclean and non-landable; the final production repair still requires fresh whole-PR review and actual hosted proof.

Earlier complete reviews remain intact. The immediately preceding eight-pass review produced 22 raw findings, 19 after exact duplicate grouping, with exit1 and minimum confidence 0.93. Its disposal, retry-start, foreign-reason and public-to-extension findings were retained and source-adjudicated; they motivated these test-first controls and the withdrawal of the unpublished reason-transfer implementation. The prior seven-pass review retained 22 production findings, and the older eight-pass baseline review retained its three findings, including a source-disproved concurrent-test hang prediction. No report has been erased, filtered into a clean certificate or cosmetically rerun.

Older [882/cb7 CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33217391928) passed all 166 successful/17 skipped jobs, seven manager controls, seven cancellation-composition cases and the strict four-reply Gateway flow. That success is historical after material upstream integration. Earlier [0eb failures](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33208597601) and [e464's cleanup-test authoring mistake](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33213762584), subsequently corrected and passing at882, remain disclosed.

## Limits and next proof

The five added cases and strengthened public-terminal oracles are unexecuted. After an authentic hosted baseline, the combined Session owner repair needs complete independent/static review, unchanged Gateway recovery, all sibling regressions, exact-head green CI and normal maintainer preparation.

The Gateway evidence uses the real built Gateway with local provider and Telegram HTTP fixtures, not an authenticated live account or video. B's immediate ACK alone does not establish acceptance. Native prompt/abort join is not every outer cleanup. A single immediate `agent.wait` snapshot reported `status: ok`; final cancellation projection remains a separate producer-fact follow-up, not a consumer-status remapping.

prs.title: fix: paired Mac cleanup fails and hides native errors
prs.body:
> **Lifecycle-only split; draft pending real native-input proof.** Depends on #137821 (completed CLI actions replay after session saving fails). Receipt compatibility is #137755 (successful input fails with older Mac nodes); acknowledged worker outcomes are #137828 (cleanup failures lose their cause after a reply). Those changes are no longer duplicated here. Historical combined-head evidence is not a green claim for this split.

Closes #135944 (paired Mac cleanup hides its native cause), after this lifecycle repair and its prerequisite land with the required proof.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users automating a paired Mac could finish an action but fail to close its execution, leave held input or private references attached to the wrong lifetime, or lose the useful native failure during cleanup. Stateful tools created for HTTP/RPC requests, CLI/MCP captures, and Copilot attempts did not consistently live—and close—with the caller that owned them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native Peekaboo binds input and references to the exact execution UUID and original live Gateway route. Close fences admission, reuses canonical invocation cancellation, drains work, releases only owned input, and retires private references. Stale or wrong closes cannot affect a successor. Closing a never-acquired execution truthfully reports that nothing was closed without initializing services or inventing released resources. CUA remains separately owned.

Managed callers carry cleanup through final settlement. HTTP/RPC requests await their request-owned tools before responding. CLI/MCP executable tools belong to the exact capture/configuration/admitted run, not a metadata TTL or refreshed node inventory; predecessor cleanup survives warm transfer. Copilot constructs through the existing placement-bound host surface, retires direct/catalog/Code Mode tools at attempt settlement, and drains cleanup before releasing the active run.

**Why these pieces remain atomic:** native-first would let previously unbound callers strand newly exclusive execution ownership; placement-bound callers first would require a close command the older native owner does not support. The implementations were developed and verified in separate worktrees, then integrated as one landing unit rather than introducing a transitional shim or fake close acknowledgement.

Removed paths include duplicate native queue/generation ownership, TTL-driven executable reconstruction, unissued base-bearer/header-derived authority, the test-only Copilot constructor route, and stale CLI metadata plumbing. The result-retention/no-replay owner comes from the prerequisite rather than being reimplemented here. No protocol-version bump, schema/material-store change, new configuration, dependency change, global release, or product-timeout increase is introduced.

## User Impact

This repairs **paired Mac execution, not only cloud sessions**. Managed callers close their own tools. Raw clients must reuse one execution UUID and close it in `finally`, including after failed actions. **Update the Gateway and Mac companion together.** The stricter ownership boundary is intentional; older companions do not implement this close lifecycle. Cleanup failure does not undo earlier input, so inspect effects before retrying.

Already-landed Talk drain, Android reconnect ownership, and sibling reroute reporting are excluded. The optional additional Android held-Room test remains archived as a coverage follow-up, not an unproved production change in this PR.

## Evidence

Lifecycle-only commit `52eee478605fa38cc8e4f9ccba70ebd0ff7d5594` changes 80 files on results prerequisite `41bc333bd6b2794e78f8ef7a960bb3100a4e85fe`. The PR is temporarily still based on `main` because the client blocked the base change, so its displayed diff also includes that prerequisite. Keep it draft; do not land this combined ancestry before the results PR. All **98 integrated source files** were hash-verified against the tested and independently reviewed input; no integration fixes were required. Lifecycle-only patch SHA-256: `008bfd04ed044be01f212e6e7e79fd4f98b55a0cf81ffdfa24a0379de1441d60`.

**TypeScript boundary proof:** 2,277 passed across 75 unique files, zero failures or discovered skips. This includes all 655 Copilot plugin tests, both placement-bound host lifecycle cases, aggregate cleanup failures, managed HTTP/MCP/CLI request and capture lifetimes, Code Mode siblings, and command/channel/cron/result overlaps. Previously dependency-blocked or excluded cases are included in this integrated run. Five additional doctor-contract tests passed inside the changed gate.

**Static/build proof:** all 39 checks in the actual 78-path non-Swift gate passed, including production/test types, formatting, lint, boundary/storage guards, dead exports and import cycles. The complete 98-path dry-run is retained; the 20 Swift paths were deliberately not run as host native suites. The full package build passed with four dependency EVAL warnings and no ineffective-dynamic-import warnings.

```bash
pnpm build
```

**Current-source native proof:** the frozen native archive's 1,043 members, file modes and symlink targets were verified before extraction into the owned Mac VM. On macOS 26.4 / Xcode 26.5 / Swift 6.3.2, all 107 selected Mac ownership tests passed, both focused shared suites passed 84 tests, and the full shared package passed 1,629 tests across 124 suites. The 84 focused tests are included in the full shared count, not additional distinct coverage. No failures, exclusions or skips; source hashes were unchanged afterward and VM shutdown was independently verified.

**Independent review:** fresh isolated Codex autoreview covered the complete integration in two bounded chunks and returned P0 scoped-clean. This is not an all-priority correctness certificate. Direct Codex call/binding contracts were inspected in upstream `codex-rs/core/src/mcp_tool_call.rs:430–610` and `codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/binding.rs:145–394`.

**Live proof remains a blocker for this PR.** The prerequisite has real stock-CLI/provider before/after proof, but that does not prove native input. Native tests, a synthetic SDK peer, compile success, and signature verification are not being relabeled as live native behavior. The preview launcher still reads an older worktree's configuration, so no correctly owned isolated Gateway has been launched for this flow. An existing guest-native Peekaboo capture route and matching Foundation signing identity are available; the current signed companion package, guest Bridge/TCC readiness, and guest capacity still require verification. No personal desktop or operator Gateway is used, and no protection is bypassed to obtain a screenshot.

Exact-head CI, current review disposition, live native proof, and the repository-native prepare/merge flow remain mandatory after the prerequisite lands and this stack is retargeted to main.

**LOC relative to prerequisite:** production **+577**; tests **+2,389**; test support **+358**; tooling **+24**; docs **+40**; shrink-only assertion ratchet **−1**. The production growth supplies missing exact native-route and request/capture/attempt lifetime ownership. CLI result-builder relocation is counted net, not as a new 468-line capability.

Operator docs: [computer use](https://docs.openclaw.ai/nodes/computer-use), [CLI backends](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/cli-backends), [HTTP tool invocation](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/tools-invoke-http-api), and [Copilot](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/copilot).

prs.title: fix(agents): reuse warm prefixes for single-chunk compaction
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes cold compaction requests when the same Anthropic Messages or OpenAI Responses route already has the conversation prefix cached. Eligible single-request summaries reuse the foreground system prompt, tool declarations, and verified native history. Invalid native summaries and genuinely changed history retain serialized fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

The embedded live scenario on the previous head completed with `paths=serialized usageRecords=1` and no cache read. A deterministic replay now drives two real embedded runs and on-demand manual compaction with mocked streams, large stable prefixes, and the same model alias and 512-token target budget.

The no-tool case captured 1 then 3 foreground messages. Prefix resolution successfully matched the 2-message summary source against the last 3-message request. A later core eligibility check then planned hypothetical safeguard chunks against the capped 512-token context and discarded the verified prefix. Core compaction actually emits one history-summary request. Removing that redundant check restores reuse without changing budgets, split-turn handling, or actual safeguard chunking.

The tool case captured 1, 3, 5, then 7 messages. Its 4-message summary source failed at assistant index 1: replay had normalized the tool-call ID from `read-1` to `read1`. Prefix resolution now reuses the captured foreground ID-normalization policy and replay tool allowlist. It first checks the original projection for same-attempt turns; either projection must match every dispatched message fingerprint exactly. No transcript fields are ignored, and no transcript bodies or executable tools are retained in the bounded session cache.

## User Impact

Matching routes can reuse warm prefixes during compaction without new configuration. Changed history, missing snapshots, split turns, actual multi-chunk summaries, and previous-summary redistillation retain fallback. Foreground tools are never executed by summarization. Native output must satisfy the existing summary heading contract; provider rejection or malformed output triggers serialization.

Per-request usage diagnostics now include a serialization reason: missing snapshot, history length, digest mismatch with index and role, changed route/source, missing heading contract, or rejected/failed prefix request. Exception text is excluded. Both completed requests are accounted for when a native response is rejected. See `docs/concepts/compaction.md`.

## Evidence

- 450 focused tests across seven files passed, including real embedded execution, core/session compaction, safeguard, format propagation, and hook/accounting behavior.
- Both full embedded regressions failed before the repairs and now require exactly one `foreground-prefix` request. Final assertions compare the entire native history prefix and tool declarations with the real foreground request.
- Fallback cases verify changed-history index/role diagnostics, overlong history, changed model, actual chunking, rejected native output, and a throwing prefix request.
- The live compaction fixture now requires a final `foreground-prefix` request and positive cache read, rather than passing on serialization alone.

Follow-up head: `69378adab6bfed3ad4152bc4f961d1dd950b9717`. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed, including production/test typechecks, lint, ownership/state guards, and zero runtime import cycles. Fresh P1 autoreview on the final diff is scoped-clean with no accepted/actionable findings. The five affected embedded/accounting cases also passed after moving usage collection into the existing diagnostics owner. Exact-head [CI run 34143177283](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34143177283) completed successfully. The canonical watcher exited 0 with `pending=0` and `GREEN` after reconciling six superseded checks; no workflow rerun was needed. The requested [ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/141114#issuecomment-5573398520) was posted after pushing. No live provider calls were made for this follow-up. Mocked request reuse is proven; a warm live cache hit remains for the coordinator to verify. No OpenAI live result is claimed.

Coordinator rerun with provider credentials supplied through the existing live-test setup:

```sh
OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 OPENCLAW_LIVE_CACHE_TEST=1 \
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.live.config.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.cache.live.test.ts \
  -t 'preserves cache-safe shaping across compaction followup turns'
```

This PR remains open. No prepare or merge operation is requested.

Status/Doctor guidance and supported legacy readiness compatibility remain required. Owner: #145169, with #156298 supplying only bounded receipt persistence.
