## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where updating from 2026.9.2 could leave the Gateway unusable after rollback: target Doctor migrated persistent state, package rollback restored the old binary, and that binary failed with `no such column: workspace_dir`. It also fixes no-op updates stopping healthy Gateways, completed legacy captures blocking later updates, and repair capture overhead growing with every inventory entry.

## Why This Change Was Made

This implements the [accepted lossless-capture contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/140339#issuecomment-5614409997) and [transaction-scoped lifecycle decision](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/140339#issuecomment-5614508856). Peter's explicit 2026-09-10 approval: “update should always work. It's best effort. If there are minor hiccups we add that in the warning log. We should backup things before, and rollback restores the backup.”

### Capture, restore and retirement

Before protected mutation, existing backup machinery captures config/include files, shared and per-agent SQLite, Skill Workshop and inventoried plugin resources. SQLite uses online backup; recovery captures remain unsanitized, without delivery-row or TTL pruning. One immutable manifest binds numbered resources by size and SHA-256; the terminal outcome is separately write-once.

Sets live at `<stateDir>.update-captures/<captureId>/` with private ancestors and owner-only permissions. The shared privacy marker excludes them from ordinary backup/support exports, including explicit containing/nested selections. User archives retain their existing behavior. Capacity admission covers capture, package/recovery staging, growth and reserve; insufficient space preserves live data and earlier sets.

Generic JSON/plan adapters and custom bundled migration owners enumerate inputs through existing collectors. The optional read-only `requireLocalResources` collector argument rejects remote resources when complete local capture is required; it is not configuration. Missing declarations refuse protection.

Rollback restores package files and captured state, then verifies the previous managed Gateway. State-only finalization restores its capture without inventing a package transaction. Database-directory restore removes migration-created files only within the declared boundary; reopened LanceDB verifies captured schema, rows and version. The shared copy helper clears restored `state_leases` and `agent_database_leases`: process leases cannot survive copying. Captures remain lossless.

Both finalizer Doctor phases share one verified capture and config-write receipts. Mutating children settle before restoration. Manual recovery retains protection through subsequent Doctor/bootstrap writes, restores again if continuation fails, and closes reopened stores. Standalone repair never starts the Gateway. Data failures are hard errors; reporting failures after verified recovery are advisory.

There is no count, age or capacity-pressure pruning. Existing terminal owners retire captures only after durable, identity-bound success and settled recovery dependencies. Admission reconciles completed prior transactions through Doctor's resolution owner, requiring confirmed matching runtime/version/build and successful Doctor/Gateway verification. Explicit false readiness fails; missing newer fields remain compatible with 9.2. Nonterminal, restored, failed-restoration and unverified sets are not automatically adopted.

### No-op and tagged-upgrade contracts

Convergence requests protection only for actual plugin/config mutation, using facts already available inside its existing lease. Unchanged baseline publication and repeated failure of an already-disabled plugin preserve their no-change result. Real enablement, alias and slot changes remain mutations. Exact target identity is always validated; an already-current core uses its installed schema/runtime metadata. Lease ordering, publication fencing and `--no-restart` semantics are unchanged.

Admission checks capacity and independent writers before shutdown. A late pre-mutation refusal restores the original service, including with `--no-restart`. Native parent/launcher identity and Gateway-lock checks distinguish a supervised Gateway child from unrelated writers. Capture callbacks now check live executor/maintenance fences; full recovery admission runs before and after capture, avoiding repeated SQLite snapshots per resource.

The named **tagged 2026.9.3/2026.9.4 rehearsal contract** accepts their disposable copies only with the existing update-in-progress marker, exact private environment/config/data layout, observed live parent chain and matching copied-ledger identity. It verifies local resources, OAuth paths, SQLite companions, ownership and links under existing maintenance authority. Identity-bearing driver/capture calls remain strict. Admission emits a typed `legacy-driver-rehearsal` fact and warning. Remove this compatibility path when those tags cease being supported upgrade sources.

Inline Git RPC remains explicitly unprotected, recorded in its parent run and reflected in result/status: “This Gateway-initiated update is not protected by a recovery capture. Run `openclaw update` from a terminal for a protected update.” The external drain/stop/capture continuation is [#144422](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/144422).

This builds on @fuller-stack-dev's #143693, #143799 and #143899, and reuses @vincentkoc's cleanup fencing (#143791) and terminal settlement (#143921). Package activation stays with #143750/#143752. Please keep maintainer edits enabled.

### Data-model compatibility

No SQLite schema/column, protocol, configuration option or dependency change. One recovery-set kind and existing run metadata hold config receipts, restoration facts and unprotected RPC identity. No ratchet increased; the upstream environment-variable budget passes at **492/492**.

prs.title: fix: keep task recovery working across shared Gateway updates
prs.body:
Do not merge this combined PR. It remains a draft preserving the original branch and source-bound evidence while focused replacements land.

The replacement update design is stop-first: refuse replacement while another Gateway uses the installation and tell the operator to stop it first. Automatic sibling updates are no longer part of that design. Session-identity work is being split into smaller storage, Doctor, runtime, and wire-boundary changes; the current direction uses qualified logical identities while retaining existing physical addresses and explicit adapters for published clients and durable data.

The historical landed checkpoint contains **53 named focused PRs**. It originally reported **1,824 fewer application lines**, **105 additional production-tooling lines**, and **1,719 fewer application-plus-tooling lines**. A subsequent reconstruction resolved all 53 canonical landings unambiguously and remeasured each actual first-parent diff using the same explicit classifier as the later accounting: **1,813 fewer application lines**, **103 additional tooling lines**, and **1,710 fewer application-plus-tooling lines**. Tests/support add 8,837 lines and docs add 91 under that classifier. The original per-file accounting is unavailable, so the nine-line application/tooling discrepancy remains unattributed; both figures are preserved rather than silently combined.

This historical subtotal is not the current replacement-series total, and the **overall net-negative goal is not yet established for the surviving series**. The broader campaign merge count is not this umbrella’s replacement set. A separate actual-parent measurement of 16 subsequently named landings records +5,677 application, +1,376 production-tooling, +22,006 test/support and +228 documentation lines. Another bounded measurement of #160203, #160472, #160663, #160718 and #161110 records +3,648 application, +718 tooling, +6,720 test/support, +78 docs and one explicit unclassified configuration line. Those two later sets add 7,053 and 4,366 application/tooling lines respectively. They are partial named sets, not a complete series or overall repository LOC claim.

Recent verified landings are updater runtime (#153764), chat identity cleanup (#155664), selected-session queue protection (#155714), failed-steer UI ownership (#155746), registry fixture migration (#155727), TUI/CLI session ownership (#155872), registry dependency retirement (#155796), stored-session address preservation (#155886), prepared lookup-key reuse (#156035), explicit Doctor migration policy (#156034), native restart ownership (#155355), and session-method policy consolidation (#156071). The updater-runtime landing has source-bound build, compiled-worker, binding, sealed-smoke, and published-driver qualification. Its original failed outer proof and unattributed timeout remain recorded; recovered inner evidence and diagnostic CI reruns do not relabel those failures.

Registry retirement #155796 removed 121 application lines and 13 test/support lines while preserving the existing runtime owners. Its original profile-merge test failure remains unattributed. The authorized exact-head rerun passed the target and all 152 cases in its state group on different GitHub-hosted hardware; no production fix or unrelated-flake verdict is claimed. Native merge, main ancestry, and cleanup are verified.

Stored-session address preservation #155886 landed after exact-head CI, independent review, the exact candidate package, and both actual published `2026.9.4` updater cells passed. The proof preserves session IDs, lifecycle revisions, lineage, projected history-window ownership, and transcript bytes; repeated Doctor leaves the entire captured agent state identical. The legacy `session.mainKey` field remains accepted but ignored. Its conflict case preserves canonical main while the existing repair quarantines the divergent retired-main claim. The Testbox hosting run was intentionally cancelled after successful proof and lease cleanup; it is not relabeled as green CI. The actual landed delta is +83 application, +553 test/support, and +19 documentation lines, byte-identical to the qualified candidate. Native receipt, main ancestry, and cleanup are verified.

Prepared lookup-key reuse #156035 removes 12 application lines by carrying one ordered key plan through store reads and returned targets. Its 31 focused cases passed. Initial CI timed out in two existing Doctor/config fixtures and reported a subsequent cleanup-order failure; the cause remains unattributed. One unchanged-source rerun of the original five groups passed 3,280 cases with eight skips, followed by verified native landing and cleanup. No product fix or flaky-test verdict is claimed.

Doctor migration policy #156034 makes the existing removed-default-agent choice explicit at the Doctor boundary. The landed patch adds 15 application and 49 test lines, with 19 focused cases, green exact-head CI, and both actual published `2026.9.4` updater cells passing against the exact candidate package. Repeated Doctor preserves the captured agent state. Retired-agent sibling placement is proved at the canonical-repair boundary; whole-update migration can move or quarantine retired-main claims, and whole-config byte idempotence is not claimed. The hosting run was intentionally cancelled after successful proof and verified cleanup; it remains separate from green CI.

Native restart ownership #155355 removes 752 application lines and one tooling line by using the installed Gateway CLI and verifying every attempted restart. Known-empty native metadata and retained PATH ordering now preserve eligible service rebinds without weakening authority or definition checks. Its 354 selected tests, retained 76-case owner proof, exact-head CI, exact candidate package, native candidate-to-same-candidate rebind, and genuine published `2026.9.2` upgrade are qualified. The retained recovery cases use real orchestration with simulated native manager, HTTP, and package transport; no native failed-activation recovery is claimed. Original failed acceptance, the optional continuation-row diagnostic, and cleanup warnings remain recorded. Actual-parent delta, receipt, main ancestry, and cleanup are verified.

Session-method policy consolidation #156071 removes 79 application lines from one file. One per-method map supplies the existing targeting, profile, approval, and run-start predicates with their conditional rules intact. All 31 selected existing tests passed before and after; 7,452 equivalence assertions, selected changed checks, independent review, and exact-head CI passed. The landed patch is byte-identical to the qualified delta. Native receipt, main ancestry, and cleanup are verified.

Requirement disposition (bounded updates through September 29):

- **Managed service discovery and source-build protection are landed.** [#151608](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/151608), merge `244d4419`, owns the registered-service inventory and strict Windows reader. #151463 was closed as superseded with its unique contracts and failed platform history explicitly transferred. [#152875](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/152875), merge `d09ffd22`, owns the live physical-dist build fence and selected-service failed-build recovery. Its final conflict composition passed 456 receiving cases, one existing skip, full changed checks and independent review. The maintained administrative route recorded its independently reproduced pre-existing CI planner overflow; skipped jobs were not called passing. Existing real Linux published-source-shell and Windows restoration/reassignment/disabled-start receipts retain their exact source/package identities. These establish the bounded build/recovery behavior, not whole shared-install admission.
- **Startup-only Windows discovery landed in [#151674](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/151674) (`733ceac1`).** Its exact CMD/VBS binding, private profile provenance, aggregate inventory deadline and bounded Startup state read preserve diagnostic-only discovery and never confer Scheduled Task control authority. Its landed source exactly matches the reviewed candidate and carries the landed Upper prerequisite. Native recovery and cleanup completed, preserving the original base-modified refusal. Fresh-install, explicit-start and authority component receipts remain source-bound; none is relabeled as a whole published-driver campaign pass.
- **TUI, saved-pane and bounded client identity requirements are qualified.** [#158240](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158240) (`df5e316a`) keeps the selected agent/session owner consistent; [#158639](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158639) (`3bdec389`) preserves saved-pane identity and leaves an ownerless raw-global pane unbound until explicit choice. [#158845](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158845) (`bc84e282`) closes the old remembered-session/pointer-clear SQLite gap through awaited worker reads/writes/scan/CAS and joined normal shutdown, including awaited Doctor cleanup. Forced exit is not a persistence guarantee. [#159166](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159166) (`ccf4edde`) qualifies exact existing-row precedence, shipped Home fallback, immediate-send readiness and physical history/send/reply/persistence. It preserves the public alias contract; the obsolete #152895 unconditional exact-main dialect is not being revived. [#154069](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154069) (`e0d80000`) supplies the landed projection/readiness owner work. None of these is a whole-product async-completion claim.
- **Wire and media evidence have precise boundaries.** Retained real browser→real Gateway evidence proves delayed/expired ACK handling, reconnect, successor ACK, retained selection and row update; the existing 18-case protocol/session-capability boundary additionally proves observer-versus-operation error ownership and clearing. Generic authenticated request/result/targeted-event payload preservation is separately proved. The stronger exact-event-label refinement failed amid a sessions.list/model-catalog readiness fault; that failure, unobserved label assertion and lost additional private diagnostic remain disclosed and separately routed. No observer-error banner or all-specialized-formatter claim is made. Source-bound before/after pairs for the TUI and saved-pane replacements were delivered and rendered in both destinations. All six attention images for landed #151412 were recovered, inspected and delivered in the originating task and verified rendered in the PR; historical first-delivery/capture-location uncertainty is not misrepresented as a new UI run.
- **Runtime, cancellation and exactly-once work is partly landed and partly active.** [#159632](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159632) (`0269af6f`) owns worker reply admission/FIFO/generation custody and joined release. [#159807](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159807) (`15bb24e3`) fixes mutable SessionManager rollback/view parity. [#159943](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159943) (`1fea5ee1`) preserves correlated completion custody and marker→await-onSettled→terminal ordering; [#160238](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160238) (`da51d9ed`) moves durable archive discovery/preflight to existing workers. [#160035](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160035) (`1ac31be0`) retains the shipped conditional ACP cancellation contract. [Native Stop #160203](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160203) has now landed as `fd1467d4`, qualifying the file-backed registered Stop path, source/session replacement and unknown-write custody through the existing worker. [Requester wake #160472](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160472) landed as `10e951e8`, retaining known-commit reconciliation without replay, surviving-sibling retry, restore fencing and marker→await-onSettled→terminal ordering. Both have verified complete native receipts and cleanup. [Initial requester transfer #160778](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160778) has also landed as `437572e2`, with matched merge parent/tree, all 92 reviewed postimages and complete native cleanup. Its independently attributed fixture failures and cancelled CI coverage remain explicit; this does not close ordinary announcement or Incognito work. Ordinary announcement bookkeeping, native/Incognito-only branches, prepared deletion/reset discovery, unqualified ACP/reset/conditional SDK cleanup, synchronous atomic replacement, and full retained/Incognito/session-storage execution still have named active owners and outstanding proof. The intentionally retired Tasks/TaskFlow domain is not restored. Partial worker proofs do not close remaining caller SQL, pending-input, Cron-descendant or compatibility obligations.
- **Atomic recovery remains with its dedicated owner.** Landed #158491 does not fully supersede originals [#144005](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/144005) and [#145169](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/145169). Complete config/includes, database, Workshop/plugin-resource recovery and recovered-generation publication preserving later writes/configuration/history remain under that owner’s current work. Its retained proof-loss disclosure is not erased. The separate stale-release follow-up [#160288](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160288) landed as `95414356`, with its official 2026.9.6 installed-update cell and complete native receipt; that bounded repair does not close the broader rollback requirements. This umbrella does not duplicate that implementation or close those originals.
- **Observed shared-install publication protection landed in [#160663](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160663) (`e694fa75`).** It checks known managed consumers before stopping the selected Gateway and again at publication, preserves package `--no-restart`, and grants no sibling controls. Known untouched preparation refusals retire safely so a later update can proceed; retained runtimes exclude activation control journals; common finalization adopts a recorded delegated Doctor stop. Exact-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36536818555), receiving tests, independent review, native merge and cleanup passed. Linux proof covers early live-sibling refusal, successful publication to an exact healthy target, untouched disjoint peers, and a published 2026.9.6 manual lifecycle upgrade. The strict native Doctor-adoption cell remains unqualified because a watcher-owned restart left that branch unexercised; controlled producer/finalizer proof is separate. macOS GUI proof preserves actual loaded-job observation across plist changes without granting selected-service authority; positive live System-domain proof remains absent. This is bounded observed physical overlap, not exhaustive discovery of every consumer. **The reference source-update script repair landed in [#161110](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161110) (`8953498f`).** Its existing Git runtime transaction prepares privately before stopping and publishing source/dependencies/output; the last observed-consumer check follows private Git import. Exact candidate `cfe94b1e` passed 200 receiving cases, full changed checks and independent review. [Native run 36547729748](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36547729748) qualified stop refusal with the original installation intact, restoration before restart after a controlled publication fault, and ordinary success at the exact resulting target. All 80 command receipts joined and the task-owned service/account/lease were cleaned. The native administrative merge preserved three independently proved pre-existing workflow-fixture failures, the failed gate and all 67 cancelled jobs; canonical repair `c7e89bc6` is separate from product qualification. Genuine [released 2026.9.6 source proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36564324421) now establishes the exact old-script limitation and supported manual path. Actual `eb377` main/non-fast-forward and detached/locale-conflict refusals preserved PID 9387, native snapshots, all 141,282 runtime/dependency entries, and the seeded state. Neither old invocation reached dependency install or the three-argument adapter. The separate manual recovery stopped the installed-old service before selecting/building exact `cfe`; the manual build stayed stopped, Doctor restored the service, and explicit start confirmed already-running PID 14546. Real RPC build identity moved from `eb377` to `cfe`, the selected unit/environment/root/database identities stayed fixed, and the authored disabled automation, scratch and workspace were unchanged while shared schema migrated 18→19 with integrity passing. All 131 receipts joined normally and owned cleanup/provider completion passed. This closes the genuine source-installation follow-through for those exact refusals and manual recovery; it is not automatic old-script success, a published npm-tarball cell or all-state migration proof. Immediate pre-refusal source files were checked by the bound fixture but not separately exported; retained initial/post inventories and native snapshots support independent comparison. The [original setup attempt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36557495387) remains failed; the corrected preparation used ordinary complete history and unchanged bounds. Required one-worker follow-through also passed all seven full changed test files (194 cases), with [exact costs and limits](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161110#issuecomment-5887919665) recorded separately from earlier sharded measurements. These changes cannot patch already-running shipped scripts, and the whole stop-first umbrella requirement is not closed. Positive-live macOS System-domain proof also remains unavailable: two isolated task-owned guest attempts were cleaned, with the final attempt unable to obtain maintained guest execution because Parallels Tools were unavailable; GUI component evidence retains its narrower scope.
- **Published Windows completion and series accounting remain open, with explicit recovery continuity now proved.** The old 2026.9.3 parent still failed the unchanged command settlement bound; the loaded-addon/residual observation does not identify its active syscall or transfer backup authority. The separate [actual 2026.9.4 recovery run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36436325852), tooling `5388562f` and candidate `a68299da`, completed public repair → disabled-task public start → selected/peer continuity. Repair reconciled the run and left the Task stopped/disabled; public start restored the exact candidate RPC/root. Selected start-time config/launcher/XML checks and peer PID/build/definition/install checks passed, all 16 commands joined, and fixture cleanup succeeded. This closes the post-disabled-start continuity gap only: the original automatic update still exited 1, and no whole-driver or full-matrix pass is claimed. A later bounded [native diagnostic](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36464960676), tooling `a5f20aad` against the same `a68299da` candidate, source-binds a newer-content rejection in the shipped 9.4 `getUpdateRun` callback during Windows recovery handoff, after the capability check and before normal finalizer launch. The original noninstrumented first exception was not retained; the diagnostic does not establish the earliest exception of the whole invocation or the exact rejected schema number. Its per-command/fixture cleanup passed, while outer Vitest descendant cleanup remained unverified. All original red campaigns remain red. Early containment has now landed in [#160718](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160718) (`0703c215`). [Native run 36526721185](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36526721185) qualified the explicit package-lifecycle refusal before activation: selected and peer native identities, RPCs, files, prefixes and canaries stayed unchanged, as did shared versions 17/17, all 334 preexisting schema objects and all prior rows. The sole exception was the exact shipped updater’s first-use four-object ledger bootstrap and one run-bound row. That is safe containment, not automatic 9.4 completion. The Windows owner retains original-parent completion and the 9.3 diagnosis; no schema-version lie, old-reader weakening, or blind matrix retry is authorized. Actual-merge-parent application/tooling/test/docs accounting remains limited to named replacements; the historical 53-PR subtotal and broader campaign tally do not establish the final net-negative goal.

The old native restart helper branch #153643 is closed as superseded by #155355. Its [closure disposition](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153643#issuecomment-5822012122) records the exact owner/caller removal and preserved restart-outcome suite; it explicitly does not claim new native Windows qualification. That resolves the historical helper disposition, not the remaining platform or whole-update contracts above.

The combined branch stays unmerged and must not be used as the next implementation base. The historical 53-PR subtotal and original source-bound evidence below remain retained; no new full-series LOC or completion claim is made. This umbrella stays open until the surviving requirements above have verified dispositions.

No production deployment or release is claimed.

The twelve recent landings above join these 41 earlier verified replacements:

#151416, #151430, #151450, #151607, #151447, #151432, #151435, #151840, #151842, #151836, #151892, #151652, #152107, #152116, #152195, #152795, #153387, #153596, #151412, #152466, #153637, #153749, #153838, #153947, #153868, #154219, #154669, #154790, #153814, #154863, #154867, #154972, #154776, #155058, #155125, #154985, #155157, #155098, #155307, #155291, #155120.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Historical description and evidence for the original combined branch</summary>

The following describes the original branch only. Its automatic multi-Gateway behavior, LOC figures, and proof do not describe the replacement candidates or clear their remaining gates.

Related: #92241

## What Problem This Solves

Tasks can fail on missing runtime modules, remain waiting after interruption, or show another conversation's pending question or approval when Gateways share an installation or recover across updates.

## User Impact

One updater coordinates the Gateways sharing an installation while preserving each profile's service, configuration, runtime intent, verification, and decision to remain stopped. Interrupted work resumes from its latest execution transcript, equivalent completion delivery stays idempotent, and questions and approvals stay with their originating conversation. Foreground replacement survives slow startup and releases agent database leases before candidate repair.

Published 2026.9.3/2026.9.4 updaters retain their first-hop limitations: let active work finish, stop sibling Gateways sharing the installation before that initial upgrade, then restart and verify them afterward. Their original shutdown path can cancel work still active when its drain expires. Same-install system services require their deployment owner to coordinate replacement. Out-of-band package replacement while Gateways run remains outside this repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

Shared runtime publication and rollback have one owner; service policy and task state remain profile-specific. Only the origin publishes the final update result. The audit removes superseded update/Doctor paths, duplicate finalization decisions, session adapters, plist parsers, and private forwarding exports. Published-driver contracts and settlement of write-capable processes remain intact. Rotated runtime credentials reach the correct service refresh, explicit Responses strict-mode compatibility settings reach the provider, and recoverable plugin-path warnings remain in durable update history and JSON output.

Service discovery now includes macOS system/global consumers and binary plists, using one native decoder over captured bytes. External definitions retain their exact identity without granting native-service authority. Loaded or unverifiable external consumers remain protected. Malformed unrelated LaunchAgent plists no longer block updates; selected or recognizable Gateway definitions and captured OpenClaw/Clawdbot branding still require inspection when decoding fails. Positive system ownership blocks code replacement at update admission; Doctor retains its existing authority for state-only repair.

At `5dc7317102c8`, product source is reduced by **33 lines**. Including production tooling, the net reduction is **12 lines** against main `1e6ca9fe6e39`: 6,295 additions and 6,307 deletions. Tests, test support, documentation, and generated inventory are counted separately. Application deadlines and size limits are unchanged. Live ownership and write-settlement checks remain enforced. This change introduces no SQL schema migration. Published-driver upgrade evidence below covers the existing migration path. Changelog generation remains release-owned.

## Evidence

The candidate passed the native discovery/publication, Doctor ownership, systemd target, and caller-cutover regressions. The main integrations passed 216, 122, and 227 focused cases, respectively. The malformed-plist regression failed before the fix; 108 discovery, native decoder, and service-ownership cases pass afterward, with nine existing platform skips. Two complete independent P0–P2 reviews passed before the final mechanical merge; the merge resolutions and automatic overlaps were independently checked. A further focused P0–P2 review passed for the plist fix. The `5552fbe1acec` package build, tarball integrity/import graph, and exact-tarball macOS CLI/config/Gateway smoke passed with owned-process cleanup. The refreshed Linux shared-install live proof passed at `5552fbe1acec`. Full changed checks passed there; the final focused changed checks also passed at `b14038c40620` in a checkout with physical dependencies. Current-head [CI run 35292975843](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35292975843) passed at `5dc7317102c8`, including the corrected Node and UI E2E scenarios.

Retained real-provider evidence proves held-child recovery during shared-install updates, tool-result preservation across two cold restarts without command replay, duplicate-completion delivery, stale-replay refusal, and foreground replacement with all profiles preserved. Each result retains its original source and package identity; these are not described as fresh runs of the final candidate.

<details>
<summary>Live and integration evidence, including original failures</summary>

- The subsequent UI E2E failure came from a lifecycle waiting hint without a registered approval. The fixture now follows the Gateway registration order and retains every original assertion. Main independently landed the same repair plus a deferred-snapshot race check; the merge keeps that exact test. Browser-free ACK/approval controls passed 26 cases, and focused review was clean. The unchanged browser assertions passed in current-head hosted CI.
- CI at `b14038c40620` exposed four stale test expectations in one Node shard: an eager-loader forwarding name and an optional refusal argument. `57ffca32627d` repairs only those two tests; all 15 direct cases, targeted lint/formatting, and focused P0–P2 review pass. Production code is byte-identical to `b14038c40620`.
- Fresh Blacksmith Testbox proof at `5552fbe1acec`, [run 35287758231](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35287758231), durable update `22799417-a9ae-4c7f-8562-336a053ed788`: foreground and native-service profiles were replaced, the stopped profile stayed stopped, real provider replies worked before/after, and the foreground replacement survived a measured 12,000.466 ms startup delay. The wrapper exited 0, its 70-file evidence export verified, native cleanup reported zero errors, and the lease is completed. This retains its original source identity; the later main merge and macOS-only plist repair have separate focused proof.
- Installed-driver update at `6654812bf6af`: real provider replies, both running profiles replaced, held child resumed, one parent final, stopped profile and channel policies preserved. Published 2026.9.4 upgrade to that candidate verified removal of the old ACP chunk. Earlier published 2026.9.3 and system-service ownership cells also passed.
- The native active-child test exposed ordinary stop cancelling waiting work after drain expiry. The repair writes the existing profile- and PID-bound restart intent before the authorized stop and clears it if stopping fails. Regression failed before the fix and passed afterward; ordinary stop behavior is unchanged.
- Foreground Git update at `d96f72612042` failed with durable `doctor-failed` because the closed Gateway retained an agent database lease. Four real-server regressions failed before the final-owner retirement repair and passed afterward, including sibling ownership, pending resources, incognito handles, and fatal close failures. Doctor's lease guard is unchanged.
- Repaired foreground update at `8c76a1b06fca`, run `6db32ec4-ce99-430e-af3e-be2897963765`: durable `succeeded`, real provider replies before/after, all three profiles preserved, owned services cleaned up. Its initial fixture process exited 1 because it expected absolute receipt paths instead of the ledger's `~` home prefix. Corrected exact-path assertions and every remaining recorded assertion were independently replayed against retained, hashed inputs. The original startup-delay function passed unchanged: 12,000.916 ms preload delay, matching process identities/arguments, 20 observations of unavailability. The replay made no new live requests and does not turn the original fixture exit into a pass.
- Cold-restart proof at `932c148c5cc7`: all 9,925 runtime files matched its Linux tarball; real provider requests across two cold restarts preserved recovered tool output, produced one parent final, and rejected stale hard-kill replay without another provider dispatch.
- Published 2026.9.2 to `932c148c5cc7`: automatic migration before standalone Doctor, survival, missing-path config-byte preservation, dependency cleanup, and readiness/status passed. Initial baseline startup deliberately requested one fresh process after installing migration plugins, before candidate execution. The bounded fixture now follows that exact published protocol, retains the first log, and rejects unrelated or repeated failures; candidate assertions are unchanged.
- Historical `7be29196eb22` package: full build, integrity/import graph, exact-tarball macOS CLI/config/readiness/RPC, eight served UI assets, and owned-process cleanup passed. CI [35189876458](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35189876458) passed on verified merge `60777822a4f7`, parents `c49879668263` and `7be29196eb22`.
- The `91799f` main integration passed 188 updater/startup-duration cases, 171 task/startup cases, selected changed checks, and independent P0–P2 review. The `4c8032` integration passed 96 browser-free UI attention/identity cases. Native decoder/discovery/publication proof passed 390 cases with nine platform skips; install-helper proof passed 111. The registered systemd reader/boundary group passed 121; the forwarding cutover passed 98 distinct selected cases. Focused regressions preserve original red results and unchanged expectations.

</details>

The original combined-branch [before capture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150153#issuecomment-5708708546) and its historical missing-after checkpoint remain part of the retained evidence. They do not qualify this obsolete combined branch for merging. The separately landed user-visible replacements have their own source-bound before/after delivery and rendering records, including the recovered six-image #151412 attention set described above; no screenshot waiver or new combined-branch UI run is claimed.

</details>

prs.title: fix(ci): price compact jobs for measured worker capacity
prs.body:
> **Code PR — head `b080de324cf7b661aff356d54e80af47fde10e39`.** The measured payload is isolated in [the stacked data PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155585), head `18e6decf719514d88f141de7a56b9f289ff0e5de`. No cap changes or auto-merge. Code P2 review is `scoped-clean`; native acceptance of the repaired code remains unresolved. No standalone native dispatch is part of this publication request. Splitting data does not conceal full-stack capacity or establish acceptance.

## Cap options

Caps remain **130 PR Node / 90 compact / 70 push Node**. At 130/90 the complete repair is refused; retaining the earlier underpriced layout would retain the measured tails. The hypothetical 145/100 option fits all three profiles with the headroom below. These are broad-PR simulations of the same workload at code head `b080de324cf7b661aff356d54e80af47fde10e39`, including the exact 353-observation payload.

| Profile | Rows at 130/90 | Rows at 145/100; free rows | Smallest fitting caps preserving existing limits | Extra rows above 130 at minimum: hosted / Blacksmith | Extra at 145/100: hosted / Blacksmith |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| hybrid | 143/98 — refused | 143/98; 2/2 free | 143/98 | 0 / 13 | 0 / 13 |
| github | 139/94 — refused | 136/91; 9/9 free | 135/90 | 5 / 0 | 6 / 0 |
| blacksmith | 131/86 — refused | 131/86; 14/14 free | 131/90 | 0 / 1 | 0 / 1 |

Pairs mean **PR Node / compact**. Blacksmith's raw minimum is **131/86**; 131/90 preserves the current compact limit. Physical routing is the canonical, trusted first-attempt PR route: hybrid's constrained 4/8-class jobs are Blacksmith, and the GitHub profile uses GitHub-hosted runners. GitHub packing depends on the cap: 134/89 refuses with 141/96 demand, 135/90 fits exactly, and 145/100 repacks to 136/91. The 201-evaluation replay preserves declared coverage and changes no repository policy.

Code-only rows at 145/100 are **124/79 hybrid, 136/91 GitHub, 119/74 Blacksmith**. Code-only hybrid and Blacksmith also fit the unchanged caps; GitHub needs 135/90. Adding the data at the common 145/100 policy adds **19 Blacksmith rows on hybrid, no GitHub rows, and 12 Blacksmith rows on Blacksmith**. This shared workload comparison does not predict the data-only PR's targeted matrix.

## What Problem This Solves

Compact packing underprices work when child partitions or worker allocations change. The original five-main-run cohort contained 11 two-CPU jobs above 12 minutes despite forecasts of at most 360 seconds. Later native proof exposed an additional tooling-reader defect: retained `toolingFileSeconds` were not being used consistently. `b080de324cf7b661aff356d54e80af47fde10e39` fixes that reader path, preserves the tooling longest-file floor, honors compatible command worker suffixes, and keys cached prices by the merged job/group environment.

## User Impact

This changes CI pricing and packing, with no product behavior change. Coverage, timeouts, runtime worker policy and all row caps stay intact. The minimal `config/ci-test-timings.json` shape retains the base legacy maps and an **empty worker-observation array**. It does not include the regenerated 353 records.

The historical native criterion still **fails**: PR 121s → 797s and dispatch 357s → 777s. Those runs predate the repairs in `b080de324cf7b661aff356d54e80af47fde10e39` and use the earlier published code/data combination. They neither certify `b080de324cf7b661aff356d54e80af47fde10e39` nor prove the complete stack can pass under unchanged caps.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR owns all planner/refit-reader/schema/executor/test/doc changes. It preserves compatible measured work before repartitioning, prices the actual runner/worker allocation, keeps cold CLI and indivisible-command-file floors, and requires compatible observations before replacing serial floors. The tooling reader consumes the retained file map while preserving its longest-file floor. Command pricing retains compatible worker-suffix lookups. Price-cache identity includes the merged job/group environment so distinct executions do not share an estimate; companion assertions exercise these owner contracts.

The refit preserves memory metadata even when seconds stay unchanged and detects metadata-only changes. Log sampling retains untimestamped environment continuations; the frozen execution adapter carries its complete dependency closure. Empty stripes are removed, compatible serial tooling tails share an existing budget, and immutable pricing is memoized. No new timing multiplier, timeout, retry or cap increase is introduced.

The paired data PR contains only the regenerated config payload and provenance. Its full historical baseline and sampling tables live there; the complete published-head native job/step evidence and original-workload successor comparisons remain below in this code PR.

## Evidence

- Exact-head PR CI: [35703601380](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35703601380), source `b080de324cf7b661aff356d54e80af47fde10e39`; in progress at publication. This is not a new acceptance claim.

- Final rebased `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`, formatting, docs sanity and `git diff --check`: **passed**. The code PR is **+2,790 / −457** across 28 files; its timing config diff is only **+2 / −1**.

- Focused repair proof: **42 tests passed in 28.76s**. The additional environment regression was reproduced red, then **28 worker-cost tests passed in 1.29s: one environment test plus 27 existing cases**. These are separate runs, not a combined unique-test count.
- Final cap replay on the rebased code: **201 evaluations in 354.12s**, exact passing minima and lower refusals retained; source fingerprints unchanged. The prior 280.55s replay is preserved separately.
- Full code P2 review for `b080de324cf7b661aff356d54e80af47fde10e39`: **`scoped-clean`**. The rebase onto `2b943452054b57a8e1267014defee11a504b9e69` retained all nine patch entries unchanged; the earlier `e2b1eab…` review remains historical.
- Native acceptance for `b080de324cf7b661aff356d54e80af47fde10e39`: **unresolved**. No standalone dispatch is part of this publication request. Historical matrices below predate the repairs, with failed jobs and wall violations preserved.

## Historical Native Evidence — Published e2b1eab

**The primary criterion fails once in each attempt:** PR small-52 predicts **121s** and takes **797s**; main-shaped large-5 predicts **357s** and takes **777s**. PR [35689705064](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35689705064), attempt 1, completed with failure: 83 compact jobs, 81 successful and 2 failed. Main-shaped [35690200152](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35690200152), attempt 1, has 66 terminal compact jobs, 65 successful and 1 failed; the overall manual workflow was running at collection and later completed with failure (06:15:49Z).

The PR source is `e2b1eabf5dd2bb16b6192c414e2b71154e56fa17`; its actual merge checkout is `dbcb18237ed4a4792224615b61f64b96fb9b7353`, merging into `44559eb315e09528aa287878494583e32ad9582e`. It uses `bun-compatible` policy. Dispatch source/checkout is `e01ad070f46fedd99c2d82b1cdcc2a3c7e81b734`, a workflow-only proof derivative of the published candidate, using Node. Both are unfrozen. Descriptor matching and child pricing use those exact historical sources and predate the repairs in `b080de324cf7b661aff356d54e80af47fde10e39`.

The workflow emits nondist rows only. Planner totals 85/67 include 2/1 dist selectors, giving **83/66 actual named compact jobs**; no delayed dist jobs exist. The earlier 85/67 expected-job audit is superseded and retained. Dist selection is consumed by `build-artifacts` through core-support boundary and conditional proof-tier PTY flags. PR build-artifacts succeeded (283s whole / 95s check step); dispatch build-artifacts succeeded (923s / 622s). Conditional canaries are not counted as additional compact jobs.

PR failures: command-planner assertions (S55) and `gateway-codex-delivery-cache.test.ts` (S39). Dispatch S4 failed `server-reload-handlers.test.ts` argument expectations. The command assertions are fixed in `b080de324cf7b661aff356d54e80af47fde10e39`; those historical failures remain recorded, and the other failures remain unresolved. A Linux Gateway singleton diagnosis hit a Testbox source-sync timeout before setup/build/test; its lease was stopped.

PR tooling-6/9 outer native walls are **222.07s + 496.16s = 718.23s**, wrappers 722.834s, executor 724.38s, whole 797s. A nested fixture's 0.720s summary is excluded from the already-inclusive outer run. The parser selects a final summary only for a declared one-config child with an outer one-shard completion; all 11 original child measurements and true multi-config durations remain intact. Dispatch large-5 has native work 678.10s, wrappers 690.089s, executor 691.55s and whole 777s.

The tooling forecast was exactly `(78 + 43) files × 2s / 2 workers`: retained file measurements were never read. `b080de324cf7b661aff356d54e80af47fde10e39` fixes that reader and preserves the tooling longest-file floor through the existing scheduler. Main large-5 remains a workload-projection/calibration gap; methods/security history already has two effective workers, so an 8→2 multiplier is unsupported.

### Published-head class/job/step results

Both nondist matrices are complete with zero parser gaps: PR 83 jobs / 265 children; main-shaped 66 jobs / 237 children. Every native descriptor matches its exact-source diagnostic (83/83 and 66/66). No scratch tooling-reader patch or 451-record refit contributes to these measurements.

| push | blacksmith-8vcpu / 2 / 2 / 1 | 21/0 | 5253 | 3998.68 | 0.76× | L2: 498 / 586 | 0 |

The initial two-CPU class ratio was 1.72× native work/prediction. Current two-CPU ratios are 1.02× PR and 0.76× main-shaped, with changed source, workload and placement; these are not controlled speedups. For concurrent children, native sums are work totals, not elapsed wall. Resource ceilings remain distinct from effective child pins/fallbacks.

All following values are seconds. `S`/`L` identify small/large compact job suffixes within the named run. P=prediction, V=outer Vitest work, E=executor, W=whole job; C=checkout, N=Node setup, B=runtime build, R=Run Node test shard, O=all remaining steps, U=outside recorded steps. C+N+B+R+O+U=W. CI S/F means successful/failed job; criterion violations are separate.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes scheduled CI reporting the documented worker graph benchmark and its worker as unused files after #181962.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. The worker benchmark remains available to maintainers and participates in the existing dependency audit.

## Why This Change Was Made

The benchmark is invoked by path in `scripts/perf/README.md`, so no application import reaches it. Register its executable entry in the existing Knip owner; its static import makes the worker reachable without an ignore rule or a second entry.

Net production LOC: **0** (two tooling configuration lines added; one file changed).

## Evidence

- Scheduled main run [40050785381, check-dependencies](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40050785381/job/120742998181) lists both `scripts/perf/worker-module-graphs-measure.mjs` and `scripts/perf/worker-module-graphs-worker.mjs` under unused files.
- The documented command and static worker import were inspected; the real configuration loads and contains the new executable root.
- Formatting, targeted type-aware lint, and `git diff --check` passed. No tests changed; test-file wall time is not applicable.
- Required PR CI passed on reviewed head `7ba4573b7cbbb2c7172207880e073aa86ed764c5` ([run 40055342366](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40055342366)).
- Ordinary PR CI deliberately excludes the dependency scan. The pinned manual run [40055674514, check-dependencies](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40055674514/job/120758344691) completed all three deadcode commands: both worker benchmark findings disappear and full-tree unused files drop from 14 to 12, with no new unused-file finding. The overall job remains red on unrelated findings. Comparing every reported file/export diagnostic with scheduled main [40054969997, check-dependencies](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40054969997/job/120755950612) at the exact base `1fead915921e307018bdb7b8d2a2e7d80c9d8d4a` yields exactly the two removed worker-file findings and zero new diagnostics. prs.title: fix: paired clients time out behind queued connection metadata
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An update could pass its private Doctor rehearsal without copying the legacy session index that the serving-state migration would later read. The update now discovers those inputs through Doctor's existing target owners, captures the selected transcripts and their source environment, and checks the copied bytes before rehearsal. Configured stores and completed-import receipts are projected into private state without replaying stale history over canonical edits or deletions. Required inputs that cannot be represented safely fail before activation; omitted optional historical archives produce a bounded warning.

Registry, deletion and completed-update facts come from the captured shared database. The shared image is captured once, before agent copies need its session paths and receipts. Raw Doctor targets retain their alias semantics; a companion map carries resolved physical paths. Cold ownership inspection of unregistered agent stores also reads a private image, preserving the serving database's WAL family. Existing snapshot publication and cleanup own the whole operation, including failures. Inventory retains its private database through measurement; the obsolete wrapper and fallback source reread are removed.

Serving import, archive recovery, retained-receipt verification and the Codex plugin's legacy-index reader use the same existing JSON/JSON5 parser as rehearsal. File identity, original hashes, shape validation and ownership checks remain authoritative. Canonical SQLite rows, binding sidecars and JSONL keep their strict parsers. Rehearsal capacity includes retained inputs and prospective SQLite working space as an estimate; the already-staged shared image is accounted for once.

Paired clients can also time out before hello when optional connection metadata waits behind queued state work. The Gateway completes authenticated hello before that observation, while node work and event delivery retain exact connection and pairing checks through final handoff. Destructive pending-work operations keep their admission owner. Offline and capacity refusals now carry fixed, actionable public guidance through the existing trusted preflight-error contract; arbitrary diagnostic text stays hidden, and these failures do not retry another model.

The Control UI waits for the visible pane to accept route drafts, then carries the loader's resolved session through URL cleanup using its original connection. Reconnects, repeated renders and hidden panes cannot rebind that resolution to a new client. Sidebar focus restoration follows the render and connection lifecycle.

The upgrade harness records one verified published baseline identity before Doctor or scenario mutations. Positive fixtures use the supported `modelProvider` field and independently check canonical delivery metadata after the real normalizer runs. The unsupported-input fixture uses `room` without `groupChannel`, preserving main’s Doctor repair for the July provider aliases; the fixture helper explicitly types authored session entries before normalizing them. Related repairs align terminal-result and Watch-history fixtures with their admission owners and make the release verifier's canonical coercion import work from temporary directories.

Candidate: `fd5b466b1bb848c79010387978fe187dba7bd73d`, incorporating pinned [main ee578bc73257](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ee578bc73257aa228561c350417b96010dec87fa). Main supplies canonical Doctor expectations, model-picker focus and compatibility review metadata. The authored change adds no database schema, configuration option or default surface.

## Evidence

- [Exact fd5b ordinary CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37038983179) completed successfully: 112 jobs passed and 15 were skipped, including the aggregate CI gate and published-driver update. The separate queued event-transport proof request remains unrun; this result does not substitute for that evidence.
- The latest two-file test compatibility correction passes all six real-Doctor cases and root-script types both on the candidate and on exact ordinary-CI merge `81de703214a9` with its frozen dependencies. Candidate formatting/lint and independent P2 review are clean. It changes three test lines in and three out, without production, dependency or upgrade-harness changes.
- [Ordinary CI for 30b645a4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37030433183) ended with 108 successful jobs, 15 skipped and four failures (three root jobs plus the aggregate). The two test failures caused by main’s intentional Doctor alias/overload changes are corrected above. Eight worker-abort cases failed before reaching abort; their executed worker-admission/transcript path is unchanged from the tested main baseline and does not invoke the changed NodeRegistry/pairing owner. This is source attribution, not a baseline-only failing reproduction; the underlying transcript exception was suppressed by the fixture and remains unresolved.
- [Protected proof for 30b645a4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37030472289) passed install, package build and types, then stopped at six strict max-lines violations. Each failing file and the command/configuration inputs are unchanged from the candidate’s pinned main baseline. No protected final test stage ran. The coordinator accepted worker release, but physical cleanup was still pending in the terminal evidence.
- [Package Acceptance for exact 30b645a4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37030892504) passed both published-2026.9.7 updater/manual cells on their first attempts: base 50/50 phases in 1,054 seconds and legacy 45/45 in 1,474 seconds, with no retry, timeout or recovery. Exact source/package/build identity, base installed-identity checks, legacy schema/restore and serving checks passed; scheduler cleanup joined and all clients closed. The successor changes only two tests absent from the tested tarball; all 51,562 other tracked entries are identical. This preserves the 30b behavior evidence, not an fd5b package build, installed-payload result or merged-main package claim.
- The final UI test alignment accepts main's retirement of two redundant agent/face combinations and retains both idle and pending-draft checks with fresh context/location per iteration. All 19 file cases, selected checks and independent P2 review pass; all 13 real-Page/loader/stale cases are byte-identical. This is test-only, with no production or visual change.
- The final one-file baseline-order alignment adopts main's installed Cron-SDK fixture while retaining the real delivery normalizer and every existing migration/negative assertion. All 11 candidate cases and the selected staged checks pass; independent P2 review is clean. Formatting and a genuine three-way merge against observed main `553c6bde` pass. Production and dependency bytes are unchanged. The candidate prepares that SDK fixture; main's newer volume seeder consumes it, so ordinary merged-head CI still owns proof of that composition.
- The final CI correction has genuine failing-before/passing-after cases for source WAL/SHM preservation, lone-agent legacy alias projection, and offline/capacity guidance. The original 58 snapshot, cleanup and independent-WAL-writer cases pass with their copy-count and cleanup assertions intact. The final 20 session-input, external-selector and retained-receipt cases pass. The complete pure reply-owner file passes 25/25, including its existing rejection of foreign `userMessage` properties. Its wrapper took 34.17 seconds including 20.3 seconds of compiler preparation; the two added assertions took 10 ms and less than 1 ms. Independent P2 reviews are complete with no accepted findings. One follow-up claim about ownerless registries was rejected after source/history verification: [the upstream July support-window change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163036) already rejects that shape before normalization, and the original Doctor lookup uses the same gate. The final wrapper-removal addendum passes 17 affected inventory, session and online-WAL cases. Core and all 27 test type graphs passed before that deletion; the affected types, all three unused-export scans, targeted lint, formatting and remaining invariant/import-cycle checks passed on the final source. The final one-line explicit-field projection preserves the raw target and the complete physical-target shape.
- [Package Acceptance for exact earlier candidate 0b2b733c](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37009562047) passed both published `2026.9.7` updater/manual cells on their first attempts: base 50/50 phases in 1,066 seconds, legacy 45/45 in 1,452 seconds, with no timeout or recovery. Candidate/package identity, schema assertions, Gateway checks and legacy isolated backup/restore passed. Both first-update outputs bind the published baseline to the exact 0b2 build. Two deferred Doctor validation scopes were checked successfully later. This is earlier-head evidence, not a claim that the successor package has run.
- [Ordinary CI for 0b2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37009129582) completed with six failed jobs. The correction addresses the exported-helper collision, snapshot/source-artifact failures and inherited loss of offline guidance; its published-driver job passed. The later 30b run and its remaining limits are recorded above; exact successor CI has passed as recorded above. The 0b2 protected proof request was rejected before allocation when main advanced; it is not successful candidate execution evidence.
- The preceding resolved-main composition passed 264 targeted cases: upgrade tooling 222, Gateway events nine, retained-session rehearsal seven, session-input rehearsal six, keyed queue six, SQLite seven and real Chromium UI seven without skips. Its frozen installation and planned type, export, lint, formatting, style and invariant checks passed. Three test-only integration corrections preserved assertions: a supported per-agent default fixture, safe optional access before a positive assertion, and removal of an identical duplicate mock.
- The two-file harness alignment passed 11 baseline-order cases, 14 selected metadata cases and seven scoped static checks. It retains both model checks while removing their trivial helper and uses the real legacy-index reader for baseline admission, incorporating overlapping fixture behavior from [#163404](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163404). Main's canonical keyed queue and shared GitHub icon replace duplicate implementations. Both SQLite result contracts remain represented. Automatic pre-agent root-store discovery stays retired; explicitly configured stores use Doctor's canonical owner.
- Retained current-driver proof covers omitted default/external inputs, transcript selection under the private environment, JSON5 serving import, historical archive adoption, receipt equivalence, and Codex binding ownership. The preceding complete Codex Doctor file passed 37/37; its comment-only index regression separately failed with the original parser and passed with the fix while preserving the authored bytes. The canonical generated plugin leaf and SDK declaration/closure checks passed within those recorded scopes.
- Earlier connection/UI proof includes composed UI integration, the complete route file, Doctor history, terminal-result/close, Watch transport in original order, release verifier/workflow and loader tests. These remain scoped historical evidence. The [earlier dc48 package run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36961440005) passed legacy/manual but failed base/manual after incomplete rehearsal missed an unsupported fixture field; that failure is retained and superseded by the successful parent run above.

Published `2026.9.7` resolves its installed snapshot worker and does not consume the new store projection. Those first-hop cells cannot prove the new capture logic; current-driver source-worker and real Doctor tests provide that separate evidence. The exported package evidence omits raw installed file maps and complete post-core outputs. Legacy schema assertions passed after candidate plugin/config probes, so they do not exclusively attribute migration to the first Doctor call. Backup database inventories describe the baseline and isolated restore, not raw upgraded rows. Optional historical archives remain unrehearsed with a warning; required source/receipt conflicts fail before activation.

The additional registered-Gateway/native trace for queued foreign revocation or reassignment was **not run**. The CI offline failure was investigated through source and pure presentation regressions without a manual replay of that wire scenario. Existing ordinary negative tests and prior native allowed-delivery evidence cover their stated scopes. The earlier Bun closed-pane collection failure remains unexplained; its named case passed in [parent CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36957178928), without a claimed causal GC repair. The cancelled superseded `9363abbd` and `bd6d132b` protected runs likewise remain incomplete evidence.

Against pinned main, the complete authored diff has 162 paths: production net +1,592, tests/support +3,386, harness/tooling +6 and documentation +36. Growth supplies connection-owned observation, retained pairing admission, immutable invocation capture, bounded UI handoffs and private legacy-input/receipt projection. The final correction adds 97 production lines for captured-fact discovery, artifact-preserving ownership inspection, explicit shared-first orchestration and curated runner guidance; it reuses existing capture, cleanup and admission primitives. Pure moves do not add to these totals, and prepared-fact consolidation removed 52 production lines from the earlier correction draft.
