prs.title: fix(state): complete async SDK auth and plugin discovery cutovers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cold discovery, model policy and whole-store auth saves still reached native SQLite through synchronous contracts. Bundled callers now prepare through existing worker owners and derive policy from captured facts. Released SDK APIs remain available with bounded deprecation warnings and documented async replacements. Internal discovery requires preparation; named native adapters serve boot, offline administration and deprecated compatibility. This follows #169580 and changes no schema, format, retention or dependency.

`saveAuthProfileStoreAsync` preserves whole-store replacement, including removal of omitted profiles and bookkeeping, and waits for committed-state publication. It captures input before awaiting; the auth owner retains shared/local ownership and external-profile filtering. Use `updateAuthProfileStoreWithLock` for partial mutation. Credential callbacks prepare before writer admission and then consume the transaction-current store. Synchronous saves retain one bounded deprecation warning.

Model policy carries the pinned account's prepared provider. Discovery carries captured metadata through loader awaits and scopes facts by state root. Concurrent same-key loads queue through the existing loader; effect owners retain credential, activation and execution authority. Supplied config skips cold default capture; otherwise `resolvePluginRuntimeLoadContextAsync` awaits `captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader()` and carries that exact config into the metadata owner. No new cache or authority guard is introduced.

Provider hooks, TTS/speech, embeddings, media, web tools, Gateway and CLI consumers await existing metadata/registry owners. Model parsing offers an awaited one-shot API and prepared resolver. Bundled callers reuse their prepared result; internal cold fallbacks are removed. Native incognito removal is preserved.

The final cold-path fixes prepare the existing runtime owner before agent-command execution, channel discovery/install setup and Workshop work. Security audit remains config-only with manifest normalization disabled. Provider-auth input and Doctor install-candidate preparation carry their exact environment into the existing owner; helper lifetimes keep those prepared facts alive through consumption. These are supported entry-point repairs, with no added warm-path SQL claimed and no new measurement. Later cold-path fixes initialize the provider singleton through the existing default runtime, prepare the secrets-audit metadata scope, await the existing `addDoctorLegacyIssues` owner and Doctor catalog collection, and migrate the bundled node-native caller to `snapshotAsync`. These later fixes are unmeasured; no additional T1 or per-turn saving is claimed.

## SDK migration

| Subpath | Deprecated synchronous API | Awaited replacement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agent-runtime` | `saveAuthProfileStore` | `saveAuthProfileStoreAsync` |
| `agent-runtime` | `parseModelRef` | `parseModelRefAsync` / `prepareModelRefResolver` |
| `agent-runtime` | `resolveModelRefFromString` | `prepareModelRefResolver(...).resolveModelRefFromString` |
| `model-session-runtime` | `applyModelOverrideWithAuthProfileCompatibility` | `applyModelOverrideWithAuthProfileCompatibilityAsync` |
| `session-transcript-runtime` | `createSessionCatalogSourceActorProjector` | `prepareSessionCatalogSourceActorProjector` |
| `session-transcript-runtime` | `createSessionCatalogGitHubLinker` | `prepareSessionCatalogGitHubLinker` |
| `media-runtime` | `resolveAutoMediaKeyProviders` | `resolveAutoMediaKeyProvidersAsync` |
| `media-runtime` | `resolveDefaultMediaModel` | `resolveDefaultMediaModelAsync` |
| `provider-catalog-runtime` | `resolvePluginProviders` | `resolvePluginProvidersAsync` |
| `memory-core-host-engine-foundation` | `resolveMemorySearchConfig` | `resolveMemorySearchConfigAsync` |
| `realtime-voice` | `getRealtimeVoiceProvider`, `listRealtimeVoiceProviders`, `canonicalizeRealtimeVoiceProviderId`, `resolveConfiguredRealtimeVoiceProvider` | Corresponding `Async` operations |
| `realtime-transcription` | `getRealtimeTranscriptionProvider`, `listRealtimeTranscriptionProviders` | `getRealtimeTranscriptionProviderAsync`, `listRealtimeTranscriptionProvidersAsync` |
| `provider-http`, `provider-model-shared` | Endpoint/request-policy helpers | `prepareModelProviderRequestRouteFacts` and captured `providerMetadataOwners` |

The transcription sync pair is deprecated with bounded warnings and consumes already loaded providers; its async replacement pair owns cold provider preparation. Bundled callers await those replacements.

Legacy auth-save, model-reference, provider HTTP and realtime-voice signatures, immediate results and mutation timing remain available until a later stable release, including their named cold native adapters. Generic provider-catalog, speech and embedding discovery APIs consume an already prepared registry; their async replacements own cold discovery. Calls use the existing bounded `DEP_PLUGIN_SDK` warning per plugin/capability family. The async save does not accept a native transaction handle; transaction-local kernels retain their owner API. Media callers can supply a prepared registry. The catalog preparation helpers already existed; this change documents and registers the old factories' deprecation. Bundled callers use the async APIs. External plugins use the typed-public `agent-runtime` exports; bundled callers may use the existing private `model-ref-parse` seam. The earlier five public declarations and two deprecations, plus the two new public provider/memory pairs, have explicit named surface allowances. The shipped release snapshot is unchanged.

## Removed checks and accepted edges

- Pending status-read freshness: main #169581 (`5b242`) retired held pending-read freshness; the retained delayed-read scaffolding is removed. Status preparation racing completion may require a refresh. Confirmation checks the live receipt before effects, and direct terminal-confirmation/no-extra-commands regression coverage remains.
- Pairing preparation: concurrent unawaited calls using different adapter-preparation routes may reach writer admission in readiness order during a cold lookup. Writer FIFO begins at admission, and post-await effect authority remains intact.
- Native discovery cache-miss fallbacks: an unprepared internal caller gets a preparation error; explicit native admission remains in the named boot, offline administration, test-fixture and deprecated SDK compatibility owners.
- Discovery getter's cache-retirement `AbortSignal` recheck: a derivation racing retirement may finish with its captured policy; real-effect owners retain current authority checks.
- Single-slot root replacement and its repeat policy read: admitted roots retain facts until the metadata lifecycle invalidates them; out-of-owner live database edits are outside the ownership contract.
- Repeated model alias discovery in synchronous expressions: the resolver keeps its selected manifest source; a caller adopts later metadata by preparing again. Credential and execution authority remain with effect owners.
- Implicit credential-provider reload in synchronous session policy: policy uses the provider recorded during preparation; the next preparation observes later changes, and authentication still uses its credential owner. No compensating generation or reread was added.
- Immediate index-preparation assertions in config-wide metadata, metadata snapshots, persisted-index reads and install-record publication: preparation already checks the fact and the following derivations contain no await; a later receipt is observed by the next read. Activation and effect guards remain.
- Immediate installed-index currency assertion: `preparePluginCacheFact` has already asserted the same fact with no intervening await; its returned guard still runs after async work at activation/effect boundaries. No SQL saving is claimed.
- Registry publication retry/current checks are retained exactly from root `339e4f7`, with both supported-write and cross-database tests. The returned witness feeds destructive survivor/file planning and final sharing guards, so this is a real user-data/disclosure boundary. No check or SQL reduction is claimed for it.
- Duplicate outer fallback-notice validation is removed; the lower owner guard remains authoritative. Prepared metadata, including an explicit null result, is carried into fallback rows.
- Repeated metadata selection during one request/setup interaction: the invocation retains its selected metadata and prepared plugin callbacks through completion; config/install changes appear on the next invocation. Credential and execution authority checks remain at their real effect boundaries.

## T1 accounting

The discovery cutover removes **two transitive native fallback branches**. Its directly inventoried SQLite primitives remain **0 → 0**. Moving a shared SQL kernel behind its worker is not a statement saving.

Across the original 23 state files and their successors, this follow-up is **T1 26 → 26** and **worker expressions 38 → 38**. The parent state lane's scoped inventory has 25 T1 expressions in original filenames plus one relocated row reader, versus 33 on the source-aware `63a034f` baseline and 54 in the original campaign census. The original comparison includes 21 classification corrections and seven removals/cutovers; it does not mean 28 fewer queries per turn. This follow-up does not claim an additional direct primitive reduction.

Remaining mixed kernels serve workers, released synchronous SDK contracts, native administration, or credential authority at a real effect. Boot admission, migrations, Doctor/CLI one-shots, and lock primitives remain allowed synchronous paths. Synchronous auth-save/model-policy, model-reference, HTTP-policy and realtime-voice compatibility remains through explicit native adapters. Generic provider-catalog/speech/embedding discovery consumes prepared facts and has no internal cold fallback. The lane does not claim zero native runtime SQL or count classification changes as eliminated statements.

## Measurement

One live baseline/candidate pair under RELAXED TESTING v6, using isolated state and the shared harness. Base `63a034f64e3af869a5affb0968d0d3a199121358`; measured candidate `1d4c0e3d1ab5d9655d6a3c00c35beb0cb154e70e`.

| Metric | Base | Measured candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Warmed all-thread statements/turn, median [min–max] | 343 [303–489] | 456.5 [424–549] |
| Warmed requests/turn, median [min–max] | 95.5 [82–116] | 113 [105–123] |
| Warmed MAIN statements/turn, median [min–max] | 0 [0–2] | 0 [0–2] |
| Whole-workload statements | 10096 | 11817 |
| Whole-workload requests | 1943 | 2176 |
| Whole-workload MAIN statements | 1995 | 2104 |

The raw increase is real inherited work, not a saving or unexplained noise. Main commit `7aae49e8677b18ca992b72a49221e1b6de4b45e4` (#169660) added a transcript-triggered usage-cost sidecar: **122 SQL / 18 requests per warmed turn**, plus **3 SQL / 3 plugin-state requests**. Its new unscoped cache writes invalidate the session actor. This state lane adds no warmed owner-operation SQL or requests. Later type/fixture/conflict fixes preserve the measured ordinary SQL paths; a cold Dev-update fix removes a read, for which no saving is claimed.

Required shared-family means per warmed turn:

| Family | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Exact-entry facts SQL | 11.4 | 10.1 |
| Actor hydration SQL | 5.3 | 6.5 |
| Entry-cache snapshot SQL | 1.2 | 1.2 |
| Row-facts SQL / requests | 26.5 / 5.3 | 26.5 / 5.3 |
| Watermark SQL | 7.3 | 6.3 |

The hydration increase is explicitly attributed: nine new borrowed-read and nine delivery-settlement hydrations follow usage-cache writes on the same writer thread; one follows an unchanged memory write; transcript-append hydrations fall by seven. Net: +12 across ten turns. The usage operations use the pre-existing unscoped write transaction, which bumps the revision used by all actor residency tokens. For example, turn 03 usage rollup at monotonic `481807197171208` precedes borrowed hydration at `481807222625583`. This is a separate usage-owner optimization; no claim of a lane hydration saving is made.

Whole-workload state operation SQL/requests: machineState.read 0/0→5/5 (cold worker admission); userModelAccounts.links 8/2→4/1; config health/snapshot operations and profile authority/attribution reads unchanged; userProfiles.ensureOwner 34/1→37/1 (cold admission). Registry-deletion snapshot samples fall 60/9→48/7 because a startup maintenance sweep was skipped, so that drop is not credited.

Both runs completed 13 turns, the child flow, cron, compaction and shutdown with exact SQL count conservation. There were zero missing SQL contexts or duplicate sends; request send/receive tracing has two unmatched records on base and three on candidate. On the heavily loaded host, the candidate's first attempt exceeded readiness before any turns. The successful retry used the same build and only raised the copied harness readiness deadline from 300 to 900 seconds; the shared harness and workload deadlines stayed unchanged. No latency claim is made.

Limitations retained: one candidate startup maintenance sweep logged “Agent database registry changed during discovery” and skipped; the later cron workload passed. The existing guard protects deletion/retention against an invalidated registry snapshot and remains. Candidate Workshop review reached an existing synchronous transcript effect guard (130 MAIN SQL during cron/compaction), while base scheduled that same review but rejected its stale anchor before admission. Scheduler, review and guard sources are unchanged; the metadata-preparation await may affect timing, so this is reported as background-flow placement variation rather than zero whole-Gateway MAIN. Warmed MAIN outliers are unchanged secret-store timer work, outside this lane.

## Evidence

Current pushed SDK head is `d9c110158faeeea8eeddf89ef3e6625957e93182`, based on root `8bf0a9ca0b7e75a7ba36cee505646ada2014cd44`. The merge adopts main's `isTtsProviderConfiguredAsync` readiness helper and passes the existing prepared speech registry (6 additions/15 deletions); one deprecation comment also changes. No database operation, cache, request or owner design is added, and no SQL saving is claimed. Current static and behavior gates remain pending; prior results below are not final-head clearance.

| Gate | Source-pinned evidence and current limit |
| --- | --- |
| Current `d9c1101` | CI, static and behavior results pending; no mergeability or final-head pass claimed |
| Prior production CI | `db9c7b4`, [38325886820](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38325886820): 7/7 types, 6/6 lint, source/export contracts, Madge, T1/dialect/worker ratchets and runtime API PASS |
| Prior SDK API/surface | API diff 115064594072 PASS; surface 115064348735 PASS: public 154 entrypoints / 3,748 exports / 2,198 callables / 216 deprecated exports / 157 deprecated callables |
| Prior Knip | SDK 115064594962 matches main `5cf` 115053329496 by exact message: UI findings only, no new findings at that source |
| Security review | Not eligible while based on the root branch; retargeting to main after root lands must trigger actual review |
| Published-driver update | `db9c7b4` [38325882261](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38325882261) includes the cold-ingress owner hunks; actual survivor result remains pending. Both merges wait for it. |

LOC at these exact current pins: **1,744 files, +21,756/−10,564** (net +11,192). Production: 605 files +9,369/−4,542; tests: 1,117 +11,918/−5,801; docs: 8 +228/−7; tooling: 14 +241/−214. Test/support/harness files count as tests. Prior `00cede88` update [38318174296](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38318174296) passed in 1,302s but is historical, not current qualification.

Two Codex review rounds are complete for their recorded scopes; the lane owner reviewed later fixes. The orphaned synchronous registry-ownership helper is removed; its awaited parent guard remains. The ACP assertion keeps exactly two terminal/cancelled records and actor-release barriers. The handoff lock remains unresolved: main passed the matching test, and source identity does not prove behavioral inheritance. No additional direct T1 saving is claimed for late repairs.

prs.title: refactor(plugin-sdk): remove synchronous APIs deprecated by stable v2026.10.2
prs.body:
## Draft: removal timing remains Peter's decision

This refresh keeps the synchronous SQLite SDK removal proposal current with main and limits it to contracts whose deprecations shipped in stable v2026.10.2 or earlier. **Keep this PR draft; do not merge until Peter decides the compatibility period is over.** Beta releases do not count, and this is a later normal release removal, not a version-policy change.

The previous draft removed several APIs whose deprecations had not shipped in stable. Those contracts and their live dependencies are restored. Eligible removals use the existing awaited owners; synchronous paths used exclusively by removed contracts are deleted. Shared kernels still required by retained APIs, worker execution, offline maintenance, or real authority checks remain explicitly classified.

## Stable removal inventory

Owning declarations and public exports were checked in stable tags; compatibility-record dates and introduction dates were not treated as proof. Release links establish deprecation history, not a removal deadline. Supporting migration details are in `docs/plugins/sdk-migration/deprecated-sqlite.md`.

| Deprecated API | Replacement | First stable deprecation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `readAcpSessionEntry`, `AcpSessionManager.resolveSession` | Await `readAcpSessionEntryAsync` and `resolveSessionAsync`. | [v2026.9.7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.9.7) |
| `SessionBindingService.touch`, `resolveByConversation`, `resolveRuntimeConversationBindingRoute` | Await `touchAsync`, `resolveByConversationAsync`, and `resolveRuntimeConversationBindingRouteAsync`. | [v2026.9.6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.9.6) |
| `setIdleTimeoutBySessionKey` and `setMaxAgeBySessionKey` on `ChannelConversationBindingSupport` and `api.runtime.channel.threadBindings` | Await the corresponding `Async` setter. | [v2026.9.6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.9.6) |
| Discord `setThreadBindingIdleTimeoutBySessionKey`, `setThreadBindingMaxAgeBySessionKey`; Telegram `setTelegramThreadBindingIdleTimeoutBySessionKey`, `setTelegramThreadBindingMaxAgeBySessionKey` | Await the corresponding `Async` setter. | [v2026.9.7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.9.7) |
| `OpenClawPluginNodeHostCommandContext.acquireManagedWorkspace` | Await `acquireManagedWorkspaceAsync`; release its lease in `finally`. | [v2026.9.7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.9.7) |
| `loadArchivedSessions`, `resolveMemorySessionTargets` | Await the corresponding `Async` reader from `memory-core-host-engine-sessions`. | [v2026.10.1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.1) |
| `buildWatchedSessionsHarnessContext` | Await `prepareWatchedSessionsHarnessContext` with current host authority. | [v2026.10.1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.1) |
| `captureNativeSessionGenerationAuthority`, `resolveNativeSessionBinding`, `reclaimNativeSessionGeneration`, `NativeSessionGenerationOperations` | Use `prepareNativeSessionGenerationAuthority`, `resolveNativeSessionBindingWithAuthority`, and `reclaimNativeSessionGenerationWithAuthority`. | [v2026.10.1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.1) |
| `SessionManager.open`, `openBounded`, `openDetachedBounded`, `setSessionTarget`, `reloadPersistedTranscript` | Await the corresponding `Async` method. | [v2026.9.6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.9.6) |
| `SessionManager.appendMessageToTranscript` | Await `appendMessageToTranscriptAsync`. | [v2026.9.7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.9.7) |
| `SessionManager.appendMessage`, `appendMessageWithTranscriptAnchor`, `appendCompaction`, `appendResetBoundary`, `appendCustomEntry`, `appendSessionInfo`, `appendCustomMessageEntry`, `appendLeafControl`, `appendLabelChange`, `branch`, `branchWithSummary`, `removeTrailingEntries`, `persist`, `prepareTranscriptRewrite`, `openModelContext` | Await the corresponding `Async` method, including completion of a prepared rewrite commit. | [v2026.10.1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.1) |
| `ExtensionAPI.appendEntry`, `setSessionName`, `setLabel`; `AgentSession.setSessionName` | Await the `Async` methods; supply `ExtensionActionsV2` and `ExtensionRuntimeV2` through `bindCoreAsync`. | [v2026.10.1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.1) |
| `ProviderPlugin.sanitizeReplayHistory`, `ProviderReplaySessionState`, `ProviderReplaySessionState.appendCustomEntry`, `ProviderSanitizeReplayHistoryContext` | Use `sanitizeReplayHistoryAsync`, the V2 replay context, and `appendCustomEntryAsync`. | [v2026.10.1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.1) |
| `sanitizeGoogleGeminiReplayHistory` | Use provider-local replay hooks; the awaited helper is `sanitizeGoogleGeminiReplayHistoryAsync`. | [v2026.5.12](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.5.12) |
| Mention Inbox `list`, `dismiss`, `recordCommittedInput`, `invalidate` | Await the corresponding `Async` method. | [v2026.10.1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.1) |
| GitHub publication `deferOrphanedRequests` | Await `deferOrphanedRequestsAsync`. | [v2026.10.1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.1) |
| Gateway placement `listPendingWorkspaceResults`, `getWorkspaceResultReconcilingSessionIds` | Await the corresponding `Async` method. | [v2026.10.1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.1) |
| `ensureAgentWorkspace.beforePersistentApply` | Prepare database inputs first; retain SQL-free `guard.assertHost` at the effect. | [v2026.10.1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.1) |
| `DebugProxyCaptureReader`, `DebugProxyCaptureStore`, `getDebugProxyCaptureStore`, `acquireDebugProxyCaptureStore`, `closeDebugProxyCaptureStore`, `createDebugProxyCaptureReader`, `initializeDebugProxyCapture`, `captureHttpExchange`, `captureWsEvent`, `finalizeDebugProxyCapture`, `DebugProxyCaptureContext.captureWsEvent` | Acquire `acquireDebugProxyCaptureStoreAsync`, await capture operations, and release the lease. | [v2026.9.7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.9.7) |

The original `ExtensionActions`, `ExtensionRuntime`, and `ExtensionRunner.bindCore` remain for retained capabilities: they never shipped a stable deprecation. `readAcpSessionMeta` was an internal wrapper, never exported by the public ACP facade, and had already disappeared on main; it is not counted as a new removal here.

## Retained contracts and shared kernels

- First stable deprecation **TBD**: raw SQLite callbacks/helpers; newer authentication/profile/provider/TTS/capability APIs; single-session memory metadata and session context/statistics/catalog/upstream readers; model-account and observer APIs; channel ingress/allowlist/command helpers; transcript and approval callbacks; newer native binding/factory/inspection APIs; Matrix native idle/max-age setters; pending-input and reply-visibility APIs; remaining placement/publication methods. The migration document names the individual families and replacements.
- Plugin-state synchronous keyed stores and opaque `update`/`deleteIf` shipped deprecated in **v2026.9.5**, but bundled Codex, ClickClack, Discord, Telegram, Matrix, Reef migration, and cache owners still consume them. Several calls enforce current revocation or disclosure authority. Their owner cutovers are prerequisites; deleting exports alone would not retire the kernels.
- Legacy `SessionBindingAdapter.resolveByConversation` and `touch` shipped deprecated in **v2026.9.6**, but retained registration/factory/inspection contracts still require them. The 11 removed generic and Discord/Telegram wrappers therefore retire **zero raw binding T1 calls** by themselves.
- Shared native session and ACP kernels remain where live callers still require them. No worker-only classification is claimed from a filename or an SDK export deletion alone.

## Cancellation and check removal

Fast abort calls the cancellation owner immediately instead of performing the retired synchronous ACP existence read. This preserves the owner's synchronous snapshot of accepted turns, so an async pre-read cannot capture a successor. Only fast abort opts into `ignoreMissing`; other cancellation callers retain the existing error contract. Accepted edge case: a session with no ACP metadata produces a no-op, while stale metadata and runtime failures are still reported. The existing command-authority assertion is passed to the cancellation effect.

The replay cohort fixture no longer attempts a write while it holds the admission that the queued write needs. Accepted case: writes wait for replay consumption under the existing owner; closure/revocation still invalidate consumption, and separate tests reject mutations before model dispatch.

No real credential, approval, tool/command, external-effect, or disclosure guard is removed. Compatibility-only checks disappear with the retired APIs. An external plugin still using a removed API must migrate to the named awaited replacement. No schema, durability, retention, or update-format change is included.

## Evidence and current blockers

Main merged: `9c4b1a9b9f610512069069e35399d0b6df531a2c`. The final refresh was triggered by GitHub reporting `CONFLICTING`; its only manual resolution keeps main's paused performance clock and this branch's lifecycle-based prompt delivery wait in the question-refresh fixture. Current candidate: `9c6a8924938bcbe1fd49ed4a9e4dbd5829ab9816`. Fixture commit `3547b7fe40d2a` repairs test ownership/routing, awaits real async writes, preserves stale-read and lost-update assertions at deterministic async boundaries, and corrects a retired compatibility-test reference. The tested CI comparison has a shrink-only mock baseline change: 9,713 → 9,699 entries.

[CI run 38374734058](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38374734058) tests the earlier head `4c3972081c4c7e60c598244f3a1a6c4f035addc6`. Production types, source contracts, the SDK API report, and baseline ratchets passed. The final job snapshot has 154 passes, 30 failures, 11 skipped jobs, and eight cancelled jobs. The remaining superseded-head jobs were cancelled after preserving their evidence. These results are not presented as a full pass for the fixture follow-up or final main merge. No new broad run was started while the explicit removal prerequisites below remain unresolved.

| Inventory | Frozen CI base | Tested candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| T1 | 453 | 452 |
| T1-compat | 9 | 9 |
| Dialect mechanical | 0 | 0 |
| Dialect design | 0 | 0 |
| Dialect engine-maintenance | 4 | 4 |

The ratchet job is 115221281006; its frozen comparison base is `fada6e0812ce163dfc39d4ca19dacf0acc3a4c1b`. This differs from the merged-main revision, so the aggregate count does not attribute every intervening change to this PR. The one retired T1 site is the prepared-workspace kernel `find`: after deleting `findSync`, its only runtime caller is `node-worker-journal.worker.ts`. The old approximately 199-site census estimate is not achieved: retained SDK contracts and shared live-authority consumers still keep those kernels alive. These are static call-site counts, not executed SQL statements. No warmed-path performance claim is made; no SQL harness was run under compute conservation.

The SDK API report passed in [run 38374734058](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38374734058), head `4c3972081c4c7e60c598244f3a1a6c4f035addc6`: **0 added/removed entrypoints; 16 removed exports; 1 signature change; 215 reachable-declaration changes**. The signature spells out unchanged parameters of `prepareWatchedSessionsHarnessContext` instead of referencing the removed function. Removed exports are the watched-session builder, conversation-route resolver, two replay types from each of `core` and `plugin-entry`, and ten proxy-capture exports. Method removals appear in reachable declarations. Artifact `plugin-sdk-api-diff-38374734058-1`, digest `5080a410eea9a552e87e833fd175a2bb574a620b545709e7383322e36b4af7a5`. This report predates the fixture-only follow-up and final main refresh.

Diff against merged main: **583 files, +7,778 / −12,083 lines (net −4,305)**.

Scoped lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed on the fixture repairs. After the final main refresh, the normal lint wrapper stopped before lint because plugin-SDK boundary declaration preparation exceeded its 300,000 ms deadline. This is recorded as incomplete preparation, not a passing check; no broad retry was started. The resolved fixture passed formatting and direct syntax lint (one file, 258 rules, zero diagnostics); this does not replace the incomplete declaration preparation. Codex autoreview completed in two rounds; its actionable ACP fixture type finding was fixed. No third round was run. Focused replays passed all five previously failing model-admission cases (Vitest 254.29 s; 577.03 s whole runner) and all six selected hydration cases (Vitest 245.28 s; 515.50 s whole command). Those include cold worker/transform preparation; assertions remain intact. The two selected lifecycle identity-observer cancellation cases also passed (Vitest 89.63 s; 161.78 s whole runner with warm compiled artifacts). The question-refresh rerun produced no result and was stopped when the required main refresh brought a new deadline-clock fix for that same fixture. It is not counted as passing. No broad local suite was run. No update/Doctor/migration/plugin-loading/service-lifecycle behavior changes, so no published-driver update cell is required.

### Removal prerequisites

1. **Removal timing:** the shipped-SDK surface test requires qualified removal records with a reached `removeAfter` date. Peter has not approved the timing. Job 115221288427 (`test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts`) confirms the watched-session, replay, and proxy-capture records still fail this gate. No date was invented/backdated and no guard was weakened. This failure is not inherited.
2. **Explicit incognito-path hydration:** `SessionManager.openAsync` fails for an existing incognito sentinel path paired with an ordinary session key. Job 115221288265 reproduces this in `session-manager-model-context.test.ts` → `keeps model reads non-persisting (path)`. The replaced synchronous opener supported this case. `prepareSessionTranscriptHydration` recognizes its legacy native route only by session key; the explicit sentinel is consequently sent to a worker as a nonexistent durable file. Recognizing the path in that branch would invoke `readInProcess` and add a main-thread SQLite path. The fix needs the canonical incognito actor binding, not a synchronous fallback. The regression test remains intact; this call is stopped under the lane's owner-redesign escape hatch.

### CI failure attribution

- **Confirmed inherited Knip diagnostic:** unused `interruptedChatRunId` in `ui/src/test-helpers/interrupted-chat-history.ts`, current job 115221283923; same diagnostic on the prior merged-main [run 38365062007](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38365062007), job 115188496004. The final main refresh imports its upstream fix (the helper is no longer exported).
- **Confirmed inherited runtime failure:** `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-transcript-corpus.test.ts` → `reads worker content revisions without claiming an agent database lease`, current job 115221288466; same test/error/stack (`Runtime config is not prepared`) on scheduled-main [run 38371740449](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38371740449), head `4dd4b8ef9c8fd0c8dd9286f70f98b0842efca758`, job 115210402430.
- **Confirmed inherited screenshot failure:** `chat-collapsed-reply-reveal.e2e.test.ts` times out at `page.screenshot` after 30 s, current job 115221280966; identical test/error/stack on main [run 38359584345](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38359584345), job 115170476315.
- **Follow-up after the two review rounds:** `abort.test.ts` → `does not abort the caller source lane for an unbound explicit ACP target`, job 115221288373, still expects the old cancellation argument object. The source lane remains active; the assertion rejects the added `agentId`, effect-authority callback, and `ignoreMissing: true`. Update the expectation without restoring an awaited ACP existence read. This test failure is not inherited.
- **Repaired, awaiting CI confirmation:** worker-project routing for provider auth/session fixtures; Alibaba awaited auth seeding; approval deferred lint; compatibility test reference; hydration positive control and replacement seeding; guarded review-evidence writes; model retarget fixture context; committed initial-message receipt; async context/retry mutation ordering; question-delivery fake-timer polling. The deleted final-read rewrite case attempted a reentrant write inside the reader's own retained admission; independent writers cannot enter that gap. Owner closure/replacement and later-read visibility tests remain.
- **Unclassified runtime failures:** first-sign-in (90 s), reconnect/dedup (120 s before listening), Telegram join-intro (120 s), workspace-node-files (180 s), required-native same-session completion, and the Prometheus event-loop metric's missing first sample. No matching main failure is established. Source equality is not treated as inherited proof.
- **Unclassified platform/UI failures:** Windows native CLI returned PONG but did not exit before 120 s; position-rail and reply-preview recovery timed out; Incognito draft update recovery timed out waiting for `domcontentloaded`; sidebar roster restoration expected two groups and observed one. The latest downloaded scheduled-main run passed its mocked UI E2E shards and Swift tests. These failures remain unclassified.

**This draft is not green or ready to merge.** Removal timing, the incognito actor-binding prerequisite, and unresolved failures remain explicit. No merge or release is authorized by this refresh.

prs.title: perf(sqlite): transfer lexical maintenance authority
prs.body:
## Status: parked after bounded attribution

The bounded attribution pass completed on the unchanged published head `c9805a2c3e8f6adee32146400cb5e1dd96879431` and latest ordinary CI's exact main parent `3b850b5627febaac239451cf5a6008af28dfa81e` (run 38482964437, tested merge `43641bb668362b04b79f4c75e7af0970f4a83a70`). **This PR is parked and is not ready to land.** No production edit, new commit, push, CI rerun, or merge was made during this pass.

| Original full-file Team comparison | PR head | Exact main parent | Original CI signature observed |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `src/gateway/server-plugins.startup-error.test.ts` | 10/10 passed | 10/10 passed | 0 on either revision |
| `ui/src/e2e/model-picker-search.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` | 10/10 passed | 10/10 passed | 0 on either revision |

All 40 original-file attempts ran the expected cases (60 passing cases total), with unchanged assertions/deadlines, `--maxWorkers=1`, zero timeouts and zero unhandled errors. Both clean `sourcePerformance` Gateway builds passed. Synthetic Team state, private directories, loopback ports and the required CPU/memory/priority scope were used. Exact source/build pins and 360 evidence payloads were independently verified. These results are bounded nonreproduction: neither the original startup physical-admission invalidation nor the model-picker lifecycle operation/cleanup failure has a proven baseline match or established repair. Their changed-path attribution remains unresolved.

The Mac comparison built the Gateway from this exact PR head and used the original native test methods. **Live pairing/chat/relaunch passed 5/5; the keyboard case passed 0/5 and failed all five attempts at the original line 836, `latestSeededReply.isHittable`, before opening the keyboard.** Xcode 27.0/27A266a and iPhone 17 Pro/iOS 27.0 match the failed CI configuration; local Node was 24.19.0. The original 6,772-byte keyboard method hash is `9bfa6cb73fee4158551df2c146cf93616dfc7c8883c3adb4fd36107027ecb3e1`. All 19,221 built Gateway file hashes stayed unchanged. The task-owned adapter selects the candidate runtime and preserves the canonical lifecycle: the live case exercises the candidate Gateway, then Gateway shutdown precedes the keyboard case's app-local long-chat fixture. A synthetic failed capture shows the marker rendered on screen despite XCTest reporting it unhittable. This narrows the failing boundary; the required five keyboard passes were not achieved. Preparation failures were preserved separately and are not counted as test attempts. All five owned Simulators and fixture processes were cleaned up.

ACK and writer CPU measurements remain 750.28→788.57 ms and 290.33→309.41 ms/turn, with the previously reported uncertainty. No established speedup or tight noninferiority result is claimed. The physical-read implementation remains on an unpublished local branch. The Team sandbox was deleted after an empty owned-process scan. The local park report retains the exact remaining gaps; the program stops here pending attribution.

---

## What Problem This Solves

Writer admission still depends on Gateway-thread lexical maintenance state. This requested prerequisite transfers scope and accepted-work lifetime through canonical shared cells, so later admission-service cutover can enforce current maintenance authority without a host callback.

## User Impact

Draining scopes refuse new outside work while their exact accepted frames retain cleanup and receipt-settlement custody. A scope that fails cleanup reopens; a successfully closed scope, retired claim, or completed cleanup frame never revives. Mixed production admission, final host COMMIT authorization, and receipt settlement retain their existing owners. There is no schema, persistent-state, configuration, dependency, or update migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scope owner replaces its local closed/active flags and claim-identity checks with shared scope, frame, and resource-claim lifetimes. It publishes revocation before mutation. Admission captures the original caller's async context before queue/capacity waits; ports remain dispatch-owned. Native and service checks consume the same exact descriptors, including after a host grant and after awaited backend-module loading immediately before fallback native open. Explicit resource-claim callbacks, policy, physical identity, and process/schema custody remain host-owned.

The adjacent placement-reader repair uses the existing retained reader while worker setup progresses across an awaited acquisition. It preserves all final session, lifecycle, service, input, and source checks and leaves durable admission with the existing worker claim writer. Regression-fixture cleanup fixes join their owned work and snapshots without weakening behavioral assertions.

Production/config LOC is **+220**: this is the explicitly requested transferable contract prerequisite. Superseded local authority state is removed; the new descriptors and real effect-boundary checks account for the necessary growth. The service transport remains unbound to mixed production admission.

## Evidence

Published head: `c9805a2c3e8f6adee32146400cb5e1dd96879431`, base `5082c9bc4625402707cbaeb22fe63dea837e24e7`, complete review patch SHA-256 `c615d472b50f773a44849421897433c93f954df1bd73a18d7d3bd3ea2ac04083`. A fresh independent reviewer received only the complete diff and architecture design; no actionable P0–P2 findings remain. The candidate fixes the preceding head's test-only floating-promise lint error by retaining the maintenance scope's returned promise. Both native-open regressions pass in **14.99 seconds wrapper**; formatting and focused repository syntax lint pass. **The reviewed test-only correction is pushed. Exact-head ordinary CI completed with both lint jobs green and two runtime failures now matched to main.**

Prior head `5942de340cecd2a493139f19affdd5959349229b` and this head have identical production source. [Ordinary CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38475468833) completed with 71 successful and 24 skipped jobs; the sole root failure is the corrected test lint diagnostic. The aggregate also failed. All seven Security High jobs passed. Ordinary CI tested merge `0e74cfe10e72b6e5562cace650871d412b3d9bff` against main `98a5def17ecea4c3da8c8e4578ef0f63d51eade0`. Elapsed CI was 1,068 seconds, with 21,175 summed parallel job-seconds.

The required native same-session case passed all eight turns/four pairs in **86.239 seconds case / 98.32 seconds wrapper**, with all cleanup stopped. The one explicitly requested [full-tier run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38475524235) executes prior head `5942de340cecd2a493139f19affdd5959349229b` directly. It ran **all four SQLite store files, 42 cases, green**, and **all seven admission-service cases, green**, including crash/restart, late registration after retirement, and accepted maintenance-frame drainage. All **241 cron files** ran: **1,932 cases passed and one failed**; the unchanged exact baseline reproduces that cleanup failure. The full run’s iOS build/tests passed; the separate iOS qualification failure remains below. The Docker tail’s last cached observation was running; present completion is unverified. The attribution table below distinguishes completed comparisons from unresolved failures. No unchanged CI rerun or duplicate full dispatch was requested.

Review dispositions: queued fallback admission now captures the original caller before enqueue; generated identity-open admission uses that caller context; each cleanup-attempt frame retires before either successful close or failed-close reopening; fallback native open checks authority after module loading, immediately before the factory. The proposed binding of close admission to the actor’s opening scope is declined: actor scope alone does not confer an accepted frame, and retirement must drain accepted work after ordinary access revocation under separate cleanup and receipt custody. A fresh complete diff/design review covers the resulting contract.

Adversarial proof covers revocation before mutation, failed-close reopening, permanent retirement, original caller custody across queued dispatch, native rollback after a host grant, accepted-frame drainage, and stale descriptors after service replacement. The native-open regression pauses real module loading against an existing synthetic database: old production wrongly opens after revocation; the repaired full file passes 10/10 cases in 33.85 seconds wrapper. Omitting the broker's maintenance descriptor commits the guarded write; restoring it refuses and leaves the table empty. The stale cleanup-attempt regression grants on old code and refuses after the owner retires that exact frame. The placement-reader negative control fails on original production at the real restart-recovery boundary and passes the repair without persisting staged input or doing caller-thread data SQL.

Local checks remain changed-file format/lint and focused single files. Export collisions and PR-wrapper source closure pass. Three eager-import bootstrap cases refuse the shared local installation's `fs-safe` 0.26.2 versus required 0.26.3; this environment mismatch is retained, and shared dependencies were not changed. No normal-validation lease or Windows diagnostic host was used.

Current-head [ordinary CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38482964437) tested merge `43641bb668362b04b79f4c75e7af0970f4a83a70` against exact main parent `3b850b5627febaac239451cf5a6008af28dfa81e`: 72 successful jobs, 24 skipped, two runtime root failures and the aggregate failure. Types, both lint jobs, all seven Security High partitions, PR context/evidence, and review status gates passed. The required native same-session case passed all eight turns/four pairs in 65.855 seconds (77.62 seconds wrapper), with cleanup complete. Current-head ordinary CI elapsed 932 seconds, totaling 19,665 parallel job-seconds. The two runtime failures are `current-conversation-bindings.test.ts` fixture removal (`ENOTEMPTY`, [job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38482964437/job/115590257031)) and `session-row-projection.topology.test.ts` federated lookup recursion ([job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38482964437/job/115590256909)). The original head files passed: bindings 20/20 in 19.071 seconds; topology 17/17 in 40.524 seconds. [Latest executed main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38484533627/job/115595038906) reproduces the exact topology case and recursive stack, establishing that failure as inherited. Source audit identifies a foreign-root memory-owner recursion in nine byte-identical exact-main-parent/merge modules and fixtures. The queued diagnostic was cancelled. [Latest main CI also fails the bindings file](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38484533627/job/115595038909) with the same shared `afterEach` cleanup error: `ENOTEMPTY` removing `openclaw-current-bindings-*/state`. Main fails after the legacy-binding migration case, while this PR fails after the touch-write case; the PR’s touch-write case passes on main. This establishes an inherited shared-fixture cleanup defect, not an identical individual-case failure. The fixture removes files after synchronous close without awaiting worker retirement. The original local file passes 20/20 on both head (19.071 seconds) and exact main parent (37.340 seconds); these passes are not the attribution evidence. No cleanup patch or extra push was made. Both current-head runtime roots are therefore attributed to main, while the three full-tier gaps below remain unresolved.

### Current failure attribution

Original single-file comparisons use prior head `5942de34` and exact full-run baseline `5082c9bc`, with unchanged assertions and deadlines. Built-runtime comparisons use a synthetic Team sandbox, CPU set 64–127, 64 GiB limit, private state, and loopback-only ports. Source tests run one file at a time locally with `--maxWorkers=1`. Matching baseline failures are distinguished from the requested five-passes-per-revision flake criterion. Passing replay alone is not a fix.

| Root | Classification | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/infra/sqlite-worker-store.existing.test.ts` | fixed in current head; both lint jobs pass | [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38475468833/job/115566116776) — typescript(no-floating-promises): Promises must be awaited, add void operator to ignore. |
| `src/commands/onboard-browser-handoff.test.ts` | inherited | [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38475524235/job/115565581756) — Exact baseline original file reproduces same CI assertion; parent verified raw hashes. |
| `src/gateway/worker-environments/project-preparation-environment.test.ts` | unrelated-flake | [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38475524235/job/115565582087) — Five original-file passes on each exact version; copied Node/Corepack fixture path excludes changed admission runtime. |
| `src/gateway/server-plugins.startup-error.test.ts` | unattributed | [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38475524235/job/115565581936) — Startup failed: required secrets are unavailable. Error: OpenClaw state database read admission changed |
| `Knip unused exports` | inherited | [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38475524235/job/115565567759); [matching main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38478278963/job/115574544966) — Latest executed scheduled main dependency job reproduces all5same production exports and3same full-tree exports, plus additional main-only unused symbols. |

The failing case uses a deferred catalog with an unscoped null client and unchanged synchronous auth SQL; other cases in the file use database infrastructure, but this failing case does not use changed admission code. |

The failing case exercises unchanged in-memory queue/logger timer bookkeeping; no changed admission path. |

| `src/auto-reply/dispatch.block-streaming-recovery.test.ts` | inherited | [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38475524235/job/115565596444) — Exact base and head original file reproduce the CI unhandled Session history database read was revoked error in the fallback-ambiguous case. The lint failure is corrected by the reviewed test-only change in the current head. Four timer files (status Git, models, session diagnostics, sidecars) each passed five original-file runs on each exact revision; all 40 log hashes were checked. The unchanged-path conclusion is scoped to each failing effect, not unrelated database setup elsewhere in a file.

The auth recovery original fails identically on both built revisions: 70.412 seconds base, 82.608 seconds head, with `GatewayStateOwnerContentionError` at owner acquisition → schema lease → credential fixture replacement. The history dispatch original passes all 13 cases on both but reproduces the same unhandled revoked-history read; head additionally encountered a local process-exit timeout, retained as separate uncertainty. The missing-ripgrep original reproduces all seven prerequisite failures in an explicit environment-faithful PATH replay on both versions.

The real model-picker remains **unattributed**. Its [failed CI capture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38475524235/artifacts/11856175245) shows a successful config command, no catalog-change event, and a prior plugin lifecycle operation/cleanup error leaving a five-minute lease. Original built comparisons pass in 54.026/53.322 seconds; a bounded nested-cause diagnostic pair using four CPUs also passes in 94.118/91.617 seconds. No assertion, deadline, or authority guard was weakened. These passes do not establish inheritance or a fix.

Plugin startup’s physical-admission invalidation also remains **unattributed**: the original pair passes, while a test-only diagnostic head run encountered a different later RPC timeout (1 passed/1 failed, 67.115 seconds) and its baseline passed (2/2, 73.440 seconds). Neither diagnostic reproduced the original physical-admission error. The fleet HTTP reset meets the requested unrelated-flake criterion: all five original-file baseline runs and all five head runs passed 13/13 cases. Baseline wrapper times were 199.253, 173.084, 187.891, 218.527, and 211.660 seconds; head times were 180.240, 209.298, 185.087, 182.231, and 153.573 seconds. All ten raw log hashes were checked. The failing HTTP probe/response/socket-close production path is unchanged; broader database setup does use the changed broker, so this classification is specific to the reported transport reset, not the whole fixture.

The iOS qualification failure is a seeded-reply visibility assertion against a published stock Gateway. A complete comparison of newer candidates in the 100-run main dispatch inventory found 36 newer runs that skipped or lacked qualification. The latest executed [main qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37416434257/job/112116126374), October 6 at `2983dfcfb319ea5b600d20ee94b68f28014e9d52`, passed the exact keyboard case in 85.307 seconds and pairing/relaunch in 174.759 seconds. Its 6,772-byte keyboard test method is identical to this head. The uploaded proof hash was verified. That baseline used stock Gateway 2026.9.8; this failed run used 2026.10.3. The passing baseline does not establish inheritance or identify a repair. **Plugin startup, real model-picker publication, and iOS qualification remain unclassified and block the inherited-only landing exception.**

Team attribution source/runtime/capture capsules and the diagnostic addendum were independently hash-verified (132 and 42 payloads). All sandbox processes drained; the attribution sandbox was deleted and absence verified. Build prep used the supported `sourcePerformance` profile after the ordinary artifact build failed its unchanged declaration-size guard; no artifact qualification success is claimed.

## Measurement

Four preselected balanced ABBA/BAAB blocks per protocol completed on the Team sandbox: **320 ACK sends and 800 writer turns per version**, plus 3,200 history reads and 800 updates/probe rounds per version. Base is `343ce2e20b5c0a7189712520eec9d2eb710ec700`; measured candidate is CI merge `67e746e454f1e96d2eed2a0b6c532c208adafe37`, containing the production owner and placement-reader repairs. No legs were discarded or retried.

| Metric | Before | After | Paired block ratio and interval |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| ACK mean | 750.28 ms | 788.57 ms | 1.050 [0.760, 1.452] |
| ACK p50 / p99 | 662.07 / 1,743.69 ms | 663.52 / 1,768.73 ms | — |
| Writer CPU | 290.33 ms/turn | 309.41 ms/turn | 1.065 [0.942, 1.205] |
| Writer queue p50 | 117.16 ms | 130.50 ms | — |
| Writer hold p99 | 38.53 ms | 45.11 ms | — |
| FIFO occupancy | 94.74% | 95.85% | — |
| Transaction delivery | 1.189 ms | 1.293 ms | 1.088 [0.966, 1.225] |
| Throughput | 3.126 turns/s | 2.895 turns/s | 0.928 [0.797, 1.081] |

This is a neutral prerequisite result with substantial uncertainty, **not an established speedup or tight noninferiority result**. CPU was worse in three of four blocks; intervals include both directions. Execution-descriptor coverage also varied between writer variants, a retained confound. There were zero endpoint failures, refusals, or unclean exits. All stress probes reported degraded status on both versions while endpoints succeeded. Every native start carried broker custody; maintenance/read descriptors and service RPCs were zero in these warm workloads.

The final production delta from the measured candidate is the fallback factory-entry assertion. Frozen broker-event audit found no actor open or overlapping open-to-settlement interval in any of the 32 measured windows; all observed opens settled at least 12.5 seconds before load. These measurements therefore cover the retained warm path. Cold-open cost and final-binary identity are not claimed. All runtime and harness hashes were checked. The main proof capsule and recovered ACK-capture addendum were verified before deleting the completed benchmark sandbox; no data was reconstructed. The process-sampling observer's transient empty environment/argv samples remain a documented measurement limitation.

## Risks and Follow-up

This transfers one authority owner and adds no service round trip to production. Shared physical read admission is the next separate owner PR; process/schema custody follows it. Complete off-thread admission still requires the remaining authority contracts, and host COMMIT/ACK publication can still wait on the Gateway thread.

Historical investigations included nonreproduced native discovery, pre-ACK placement, Trash cleanup, and automation timing failures. Later actual ordinary CI passed those selected paths, but those passes are not retrospective claims that every original failure was explained or fixed. Current unresolved failures remain explicit above and are not classified by those historical passes.

prs.title: feat(control-ui): request declared session row fields
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link can progress through fourteen visible states; the cold-load campaign measured a 643 KB sidebar first page. Fixed row presets make consumers fetch unrelated session facts. This is the UI half of the approved selectable-row-fields contract, stacked on `steipete/coldload-session-row-fields` (L42). The lane is rebased onto current main as required by the campaign; until L42 refreshes its early base, GitHub also displays intervening main commits. The UI change is [commit 1a452088fa5d](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1a452088fa5dcb454c3470e1c9c4e0a7657b1a68).

## Change

Sidebar, dashboard gallery, agent cards, Sessions, command palette, Activity history and current work declare renderer/controller fields beside their owning modules. Row types derive from those declarations. Requests use `fields` when hello advertises `sessions.rowFields` and otherwise use the matching preset. The grouped sidebar and its new-session picker share the sidebar projection; standalone agent cards use their narrower projection. Selected chat descriptors stay full because composer, transcript, settings, header and menus share them.

The session cache merges by coverage, preserves unknown facts, and permits covered omissions or explicit delta tombstones to clear. Describe request keys distinguish projections. Shared-session and Activity reconciliation handle ordinary deltas following projected reads. Canonical protocol presets replace the local omission branching. The parent-owned live sidebar handoff from current main is preserved. Mock replies use the protocol resolver, and the bench has an opt-in capability flag.

## Dependency and measurement limits

L42 currently publishes the early protocol commit, not its Gateway projection implementation. Its opaque projection ID repeats the complete field-index list on every row. That encoding needs to shrink before landing this stack. Real Gateway payload and main-thread CPU proof remain dependent on L42.

The final Team-scale mock census has six `sessions.list` responses both before and after. The 200-row grouped-sidebar and selected-agent first pages each grow from **152,685 to 185,802 bytes (+21.7%)**. The grouped-sidebar continuation grows from 81,699 to 98,342 bytes. Owner-count and child-window replies are unchanged. Total list responses grow from **552,282 to 635,159 bytes (+15.0%)**. The baseline mock does not project legacy presets, so these are mock wire counts, not real Gateway preset-versus-fields savings.

Fixed-time, 200-row synthetic content estimates exclude projection markers/descriptors, shared facts, response envelopes and compression:

| Consumer | Preset row bytes | Selected row bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Sidebar | 125,417 | 125,417 |
| Dashboard gallery | 95,841 | 95,841 |
| Agent cards | 143,023 | 85,833 |
| Sessions | 143,023 | 86,331 |
| Command palette | 143,023 | 71,277 |
| Activity history | 143,023 | 83,125 |
| Current work | 143,023 | 60,525 |

The fixture has no extra populated sidebar/dashboard facts to remove. Renderer counts in the paired run were sidebar 53→59, roster 60→66, and chat pane 58→57; these are single-run observations, not a demonstrated CPU improvement. Loaded-host wall times are noisy. The browser mock supplies no Gateway main-thread samples.

## Evidence

Focused unit files passed serially: field-selection/cache boundary (3), provenance (8), describe (19), mock projection (2), roster transport (16), roster activity (4), palette search (8), Sessions route (4), Activity controller (12), Activity reconciliation (16), sidebar feedback (6), and sidebar projection memo (6).

Changed/new test wall times using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1`: field-selection/cache 5.50s on the pushed head, provenance 6.87s, mock projection 9.15s, Activity controller 2.83s, Activity reconciliation 3.54s, sidebar feedback 14.99s, sidebar projection memo 17.77s, Sessions list-filter e2e 36.08s, and capability-enabled sidebar roster e2e 47.24s.

Affected e2e files also passed individually: Activity current work (2 cases, 23.92s), agent-switch roster (1, 18.08s), command-palette first open (4, 59.12s), and the unchanged sidebar cold-load regression (2, final rebased run 32.98s). That cold-load test exposed a transient handoff on the earlier base; current main's parent-owned roster fix was retained during rebase and the test now passes. UI bundles build, all 67 changed files pass formatting, and diff whitespace checks pass.

No Testbox IDs: remote capacity is blocked. The full UI suite is waived under the campaign capacity policy. Local broad suites/typecheck were not run; CI is the broad gate. The published-head CI result and timings are recorded below. Autoreview addressed projected-read/delta coverage in both cache consumers; the final review is clean with no accepted/actionable P0–P2 findings.

## CI on the published head

Head: `1a452088fa5dcb454c3470e1c9c4e0a7657b1a68`. **Blocked; broad UI checks did not run.**

- [CI preflight](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38362118755/job/115178532857) failed after 45 seconds: the old stacked base makes the PR diff include main's generated locale artifacts alongside source edits. This UI commit contains no generated locale edits. L42 needs to refresh its base (or land) before the normal diff-scoped CI gate can proceed.
- [Declaration build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38362118548) fails on `SessionObserverHealthSchema` and `SessionObserverPlanProgressSchema`: L42 moved the definitions to `sessions-observer.ts` but `sessions.ts` still refers to them locally in type exports without importing them.
- [macOS protocol generation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38362118568/job/115178854559) and [shared-kit indexing](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38362118543/job/115178855469) fail because generated Swift references `SessionRowFields` without a corresponding generated type. This is in the early protocol dependency.

The [PR context and evidence gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38362878167) passes after correcting its required headings. Failed logs were fetched once; these deterministic dependency failures were not rerun. UI CI seconds: zero, because preflight stopped lane selection. Local scoped proof is above; the full UI suite remains waived under the capacity policy. L42 also needs compact projection IDs and its Gateway projection implementation/CPU proof before this stack is ready to land.

## Size and release-note context

UI-only production delta under the requested test/docs exclusions: **+821/-169, net +652**. The required main-to-head comparison includes L42’s early protocol dependency: **+1,330/-221, net +1,109**. The pattern includes census/mock support. Growth implements explicit typed consumer declarations, per-view query ownership, and coverage receipts. Superseded preset omission branching is removed.

Control UI can request its rendered session facts while preserving cached metadata across partial reads and live events. The attached before/after captures contain only synthetic fixture data and were inspected in full.

![Before: synthetic preset fallback](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee0497b1-29ea-456d-be30-e339f7aa44cc)

![After: synthetic selected fields](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f0c8fa93-4979-4621-91b6-f10fafa4c85a)

prs.title: feat(macos): archive bundled runtime resources
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fresh copies of OpenClaw.app carry tens of thousands of individually sealed runtime files. This change packages non-native runtime content in one ZIP while keeping native signing targets loose. Packaging traverses a runtime directory without assuming a node_modules layout, so the same container can carry a compiled runtime's resource sidecar.

## User Impact

The app verifies the archive's SHA-256 and format version from signed Info.plist metadata, extracts into an unpublished sibling directory, validates the completed runtime, then atomically publishes the build. Missing, corrupt, unsupported, or unextractable archives produce typed errors directing the user to reinstall; the selected runtime remains usable.

A Sparkle update from the loose layout seeds the new archive on first launch. Rolling back to an older app reuses its retained seed or seeds again from its loose bundle. Runtime packaging does not change configuration or the terminal CLI path; database downgrade compatibility follows the existing rollback rules.

Private helpers prepare a runtime without adopting the terminal CLI or changing its ownership. Helper retention now keeps current/previous helper builds, Gateway-selected builds, and live executable references; it also handles a profile whose terminal CLI remains on one older build. Cleanup uncertainty defers deletion, and helper bookkeeping failures warn instead of preventing a verified helper launch. The macos-app install-owner marker remains part of the payload. Elevation-host and cloud-worker bundles keep their existing loose layout.

## Validation

- Production archive encoder and macOS ditto round-trip documentation, executable resource modes, pnpm-style directory links, native aliases, and signed manifest fields; Mach-O/native payloads remain loose. Regression failed before the repair; final focused test passes (4.98 s test / 22.84 s command wall, including epoch-normalized timestamp coverage).
- Sandboxed Swift owner harness: 13 test functions passed across archive verification/failure, atomic publication, build changes/reuse, loose-layout upgrade/rollback, helper retention, existing CLI ownership, live-executable retention, recovery, and cloning (10.986 s test / 11.212 s wall). It compiles actual runtime/CLI/retention owners with isolated application adapters; this is not whole-app release proof. Pre-fix archive and retention failures were captured.
- Touched Swift format/strict lint, targeted script lint, docs format, line-cap, assertion safety, timeout-race, mock-export, config-docs, plugin-inventory, native-protocol/localization, shell/Python syntax, and diff-whitespace checks passed.
- Max-lines passed, but its inherited environment-name budget fails at 455/454; the counted source and budget are byte-identical to the integrated main. Targeted typechecking encountered stale local proc-safe 0.2.0 against the pinned 0.3.0. A fresh pinned-dependency rerun remains pending with the signed build; dependency declarations were not changed.
- Independent Codex branch review at `9fc2de679c1af0f1ccd5eb126020cd30223f31c7`: scoped clean at P0–P2. The previous review's normalized-timestamp defect was reproduced and fixed.
- Diff against integrated main: production +366/-119, tests +310/-15, docs +43/-8. The added production code owns archive integrity/extraction and helper retention; no compiled-runtime builder changes.

## Release Proof Hold — Keep Draft

Main was integrated at `d02330deba0e`. Signed Release validation is queued on the required shared macOS build lock. The comparison baseline is a separately built, signed main app with the loose runtime; the archive app uses its own test bundle identifier. Both use isolated profiles. No operator Gateway or installed app is modified, and nothing is submitted to Apple.

Initial representative extraction times (DEFLATE6 41.945/70.877/133.527 seconds; ditto ZIP 30.263 seconds; stored ZIP 87.518 seconds) are too costly and too affected by changing host load to justify selecting by archive size. Format selection remains provisional. A three-round benchmark through the actual Swift seeding owner compares loose APFS seeding, ZIP alternatives, and raw/LZFSE AppleArchive with parallel extraction, including hashing, cloning, validation, Bun probe, and publication.

Before ready, require at least three interleaved fresh-copy launches per signed app, measuring both rendered dashboard readiness and `[gateway] ready`, with load and observation intervals recorded. Overall first-use time is the later of those two boundaries. If the archive does not improve end-to-end first use, retain this proof hold and report the measurements.

Still pending: final format selection; signed candidate build; paired first-use and repeat-launch measurements; app ZIP/profile sizes; verified notarization-ready ZIP for the maintainer's Apple submission; and exact-head ClawSweeper re-review. Exact-head CI run `38607739757` skipped `openclaw/ci-gate` and broad jobs while draft; this is not passing CI evidence. Do not land this PR.

Release-note context: macOS can prepare its bundled runtime from an integrity-checked archive while preserving CLI ownership and bounding old helper copies.

prs.title: fix: preserve updater and gateway observation lifetimes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Runtime replacement could retire the updater's own code before recovery capture finished, causing a late `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` and rollback.

## User Impact

Updates keep recovery code and admitted worker work alive until their owners finish. Gateway shutdown stops passive observers promptly while joining work already admitted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Backup owners now load before replacement, and the shared worker-pool factory captures worker code before detached work can lose its generation. A matching native owner drains admitted domain work, retires all its pools, then joins its supervisor and broker before releasing code. This includes pools created during the drain and owners without custom pool cleanup; independently owned native siblings retain their behavior.

CI exposed two related lifecycle defects. A credential-only refresh could publish an unchanged configuration epoch and reject an already-admitted hook; the configuration owner now permits reuse only when recorded runtime/source values and detached provenance still match. Generic publication invalidation and the hook's exact publication fence remain intact. Passive observations stop at request-entry closure while accepted work remains joined by its connection owner. Main's scheduler fence is preserved through the same close handler, and execution retirement and approval-listener ordering remain unchanged.

The repair also removes unused internal exports and obsolete diff wrappers, keeps meaningful pairing assertions through the existing state reader, and renames a private snapshot-read constant incorrectly counted as an environment variable. No configuration, schema, migration, storage representation, protocol, or public SDK contract is added. Existing main's Users-label fixture repair from Vincent Koc is preserved. The sidebar keyboard fixture now parks inherited pointer input before mounting hover controls, preventing a separate rail tooltip from polluting the picker occlusion trace.

The session-link reconnect fixture also uses the existing atomic request cursor to separate prior title-decoration reads from navigation. This preserves the eager off-roster title capability added in #172558 (thanks @Patrick-Erichsen), while still requiring exactly one interrupted navigation request or two requests when reconnect retries it.

## Evidence

Original failures were reproduced before edits. The final eight-case real Worker test fails three cases on the original published producer and passes unchanged after the phased native repair. Focused coverage also includes native supervisor/broker custody and pool preparation, nonempty SQLite snapshot/restore and rollback, credential/provenance drift, the original failed CI files in their original order, held-work drainage, internal observation, pairing/preparation, and diff unit/browser layout. Refreshed-main coordinator/scheduler-fence and received-execution shutdown proof passes. Narrow types, lint, formatting, architecture, environment-budget, SDK, and hard-zero dead-export checks pass. Independent complete-candidate review found no actionable P0–P2 issue. Hosted CI must qualify the exact published head before landing.

The UI CI failure was reproduced in the original 14-case order at real native tooltip completion boundaries: the retained pointer opened a rail tooltip before late pointer parking, yielding the same extra occlusion cycle. Moving the existing parking step before mounting passes that same probe and all 14 original cases; 29 real-browser tooltip and three geometry siblings also pass. The original CI trace did not identify its first shadow surface, so the independently captured rail-tooltip reproduction is not presented as its exact surface identity. The final test-only move changes no assertions, timing budgets, mocks, tooltip behavior, or geometry policy; all task-private diagnostics were removed. Scoped independent review, lint, and formatting pass.

The exact failing reconnect file reproduced both CI count failures before the change. Ordered caller diagnostics showed two title requests before the click; those could also satisfy the old navigation wait before its deferred request existed. The cursor correction passes both original cases with all route, history, startup and deferred-response assertions unchanged. Fifty existing title, atomic-deferral and route-recovery sibling cases, focused lint/formatting, and independent P0–P2 review pass. A roster-only attempted correction still failed and was discarded.

Against the refreshed main baseline, production changes total +28 lines and tests/support +418, discounting pure owner moves. Remaining growth provides missing code-generation closure ownership, owner-proven publication reuse, accepted-observation drainage, and the private domain→pool→physical retirement phase. The latter replaces competing peer cleanup without requiring a new public callback contract. Duplicate construction, ambient first-registration lifetime binding, unused exports, and retired wrappers were removed.

Limits and follow-ups: the native cancellation reproduction qualifies the generic explicit same-generation source contract; actual snapshot staging constructs its prebound pool in a detached context, so production staging cancellation is not claimed. PostgreSQL bootstrap/control reaches the intended connection refusal, not a successful external backup. The compiled SQLite bootstrap fixture has no databases; nonempty preservation is covered separately. Unmanaged file-descriptor warnings remain a native-lifecycle follow-up. A prior-head diagnostic observed a synchronous cold GitHub source-facade load blocking client receipt; built-distribution impact remains unqualified. Vite's native configuration loader also reports an existing JSON import-attributes warning, retained as a tooling follow-up. Two pre-click title reads were observed, but whether their distinct owner scopes require both remains an unqualified follow-up; this test correction does not change that behavior. No timeout, prewarming workaround, or CI waiver is included.
