prs.title: feat(tools): per-turn per-target send budget guard for message tools
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds a per-turn, per-target outbound send guard shared by the `message` and `conversations_send` tools to curb within-turn duplicate-answer storms.

The existing loop detector hashes full tool params, so a model that re-sends the same answer with slightly reworded text produces a distinct hash every time and stays invisible to it — a single healthy `200` run can emit six reworded variants of one reply. This adds a lightweight ledger, independent of the loop detector and its default-off switch, that counts *successful* deliveries per (turn, target).

Closes #119992

## What Problem This Solves

A model can emit many reworded copies of the same reply within one turn. The existing tool-loop detector hashes the full stable tool-parameter object, so each reworded body is a distinct call and evades it entirely — a single healthy run can fan out six variants of one answer to the same recipient. Nothing in the ordinary send path accounts for repeated deliveries per turn.

This change adds a shared per-agent-turn, per-destination ledger observed by both the `message` tool and `conversations_send`, giving the model a default-on nudge to finalize after the first repeat and an opt-in hard cap that blocks further sends before dispatch.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The loop detector cannot catch reworded duplicates (it is content-hash based and default-off), so the guard must be independent of it and count *successful* deliveries, not param hashes.
- The two send tools reach the same recipients, so the ledger has to be shared and keyed on one canonical destination identity, or alternating the tools would evade it.
- The ledger must run on the ordinary Gateway execution path (not just embedded/subagent paths), which requires the active run ID to reach the tools that gate on it.

Seven runtime-path defects surfaced in review are fixed here so the guard actually protects the claimed workflow:

- **Gateway path dropped the run ID.** `resolveGatewayScopedTools` forwarded `runId` to the mediated coding tools but not to `createOpenClawTools`, so the `message` tool and `conversations_send` received `runId=undefined` and their ledger contexts declined to activate — the nudge and cap were silently inert for every Gateway-scoped turn. `params.runId` is now forwarded to `createOpenClawTools`; it stays `undefined` on the single-shot HTTP `tools.invoke` path, which correctly leaves the ledger off there.
- **Current-source key split.** `resolveOutboundActionRoute` keyed current-source sends on a literal `<current-source>` sentinel, while `conversations_send` keys on the resolved concrete target. The two never matched, so alternating a no-target source reply with `conversations_send` to the same peer split the count across two ledger slots and bypassed both the nudge and the cap. The current source is now resolved to its concrete target (`currentMessagingTarget ?? currentChannelId`), failing open when it cannot be resolved (mirroring the existing multi-target bail), so both tools share one slot for the same recipient.
- **Routable target not threaded through the Gateway/CLI-loopback chain.** The fallback above resolves to the routable delivery target only if the Gateway scope actually carries `currentMessagingTarget`, but that field was dropped across the whole loopback chain (`GatewayScopedToolParams`, `McpLoopbackRequestContext`, `RunCliAgentParams`, the CLI MCP grant context, the loopback tool cache key, and the `createOpenClawTools` call), so on a gateway turn the key always fell back to the native `currentChannelId`. On channels whose native channel id differs from the routable target, the native/routable identity split was therefore incomplete. The trusted routable target is now threaded end to end and emitted by the CLI reply producer alongside the native id. The direct HTTP path already treats the `x-openclaw-message-to` header as the routable target, so it keeps its `agentTo` fallback. Security: the routable target is trusted only from the server-minted bound grant context — the grant-authenticated header branch fails closed and a spoofed `x-openclaw-current-messaging-target` header can never override the bound value.
- **Ledger key was not canonicalized before admission.** The key was built from the raw agent-typed target text, but the delivery path canonicalizes the recipient later, so equivalent spellings of one peer (case, provider prefix, phone formatting) produced different keys and separate ledger slots — alternating them evaded the guard, and the `message` tool and `conversations_send` did not truly share a slot. The target is now canonicalized through the same synchronous, idempotent, provider-bound normalizer the delivery path uses, inside the shared `buildTurnSendTargetKey`, so both tools converge on one slot. Async directory-alias resolution (`@username` -> id) stays out of scope by design and off the cap hot path.
- **Queued was counted as a delivery.** `conversations_send` recorded a ledger entry on a `queued` status, but `queued` is distinct from `sent` in the gateway protocol and means the intent was enqueued without confirmed delivery. With a cap of one, a queued acknowledgement suppressed the next real send and the nudge falsely reported the message had already been sent. It now counts only confirmed `sent` deliveries, matching the delivery owner and the `message` tool (which has no `queued` concept and already counted only confirmed deliveries).

- **Overlapping same-session runs evicted each other's counts.** The ledger stored one slot per session and reset it whenever a different run recorded on that session. Concurrent foreground turns can share one session key with distinct run ids (see `src/auto-reply/dispatch.freshness.test.ts`, which starts run A, completes run B on the same session, then resumes A), so an A -> B -> A interleave let run B evict run A's slot; when run A resumed, its per-target count read zero and both the nudge and the opt-in cap were silently bypassed — exactly under the concurrency the cap exists to protect. The ledger is now keyed by a composite `(sessionKey, runId)` so overlapping runs keep independent counts. Each slot stays authoritative for the whole run lifetime (no idle expiry) and is deleted by the run owner at its terminal boundary (`clearTurnSendLedgerForRun`, wired into the embedded runner's fallback-chain `finally`); terminal cleanup is the ledger's only delete path — there is deliberately no size-based eviction, because evicting a slot while its run is still live (an idle run while many turns execute concurrently) would silently zero that run's committed counts and release the opt-in cap mid-turn. Retained slots are bounded by the number of concurrently live runs.
- **An idempotent message replay was blocked by the cap.** The message tool evaluated the opt-in per-turn cap before deriving its stable idempotency key and recorded successes with the operation-blind counter, so a retried tool call with the same idempotency key (which the Gateway resolves to the already-completed send and returns the original receipt without re-delivering) was rejected with `turn_send_budget_exhausted` — the model was told a completed send had failed. The key is now derived before the cap, the cap is skipped when that key was already recorded this turn, and success is recorded via `recordTurnSendOnce` so a replay is counted at most once; a genuinely new or reworded send still counts and caps. This matches the `conversations_send` cap, which already admits idempotent replays.
## User Impact

- **Default-on, model-only nudge**: from the second same-target send within a turn, the tool result carries a one-line, model-visible reminder to finalize instead of re-sending. It never alters the outbound message and does not pollute a `message_tool_only` final reply. Opt out via `tools.message.turnSendNudge: false` (per-agent override inherits the global).
- **Opt-in hard cap (default off)**: `tools.message.maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget` blocks a send before dispatch once the cap is reached, returning `turn_send_budget_exhausted`. Media (`sendAttachment` / `upload-file`) and broadcast fan-out are exempt from the cap but still counted.
- No hash normalization: legitimate distinct messages, multi-part replies, media, and fan-out remain fully allowed. Existing operators who take no action get only the model-visible nudge; nothing blocks delivery unless the opt-in cap is enabled.

## Design notes

- A "turn" is one agent run (`runId`). A slot is authoritative for the entire run lifetime — including long tool waits and provider-fallback candidates that reuse the `runId` — so the opted-in cap holds for the whole turn; the run owner deletes the slot at the terminal run boundary (`clearTurnSendLedgerForRun` from the embedded runner fallback-chain `finally`), and that terminal cleanup is the ledger's only delete path — retained slots are bounded by concurrently live runs, and no size-based eviction ever removes a live run's counts. Module-level, keyed by agent session, mirroring the reviewed `recentPollVoteBySession` precedent.
- Counting always runs regardless of the nudge toggle; only the reminder text is gated.
- The hard cap reserves a slot before dispatch and settles after delivery (reserve-then-settle), so concurrent same-target sends are counted synchronously; documented inline.

## Evidence

Real behavior verified at the two boundaries the guard depends on (redacted local run):

- **Gateway boundary — ledger activates only when the run ID flows through.** `resolveGatewayScopedTools({ runId, surface: "loopback" })` produces a `message` tool whose per-turn cap engages; reverting the `runId` forward makes this fail. Verbatim:
  ```
  gateway-core  src/gateway/tool-resolution.test.ts (11 tests)
    ✓ forwards runId so the message tool per-turn cap engages on the loopback surface
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  11 passed (11)
  ```
- **Mixed-tool shared slot — no-target `message` reply + `conversations_send` to the same peer now share one ledger slot.** With `maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget: 1` the second tool is capped; reverting to the `<current-source>` sentinel makes it deliver (`status: "sent"`) instead of `suppressed`. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/conversation-tools.test.ts (15 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  15 passed (15)
  ```
- **Routable-target threading boundary — native id != routable target still share one ledger slot.** `resolveGatewayScopedTools` with `currentChannelId: "D123"` (native) and `currentMessagingTarget: "user:U123"` (routable) differing: a pre-seeded routable slot and a no-target source send resolve to the same key and hit the cap. Reverting the routable-param forward makes this fail (verified). The header fail-closed invariant is covered: a spoofed `x-openclaw-current-messaging-target` header leaves the bound routable target undefined. Verbatim:
  ```
  gateway-core  src/gateway/tool-resolution.test.ts / mcp-http.request.test.ts / mcp-grant-context.test.ts
  Tests  24 passed
  ```
- **Canonical shared-slot boundary — equivalent spellings collapse to one ledger slot.** `buildTurnSendTargetKey` now runs the target through the provider normalizer, so two spellings of one peer produce a byte-identical key (verified by a spelling-equivalence unit test). Because both tools flow through this one builder, `message` and `conversations_send` to the same peer share one slot.
- **Queued does not consume a slot.** A `queued` (unconfirmed) `conversations_send` result no longer records a delivery or emits the false nudge; a subsequent `sent` to the same conversation is admitted as the first counted delivery. Verified by a queued-then-sent regression under `maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget: 1` plus a table over `suppressed`/`queued`/`unknown`. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/turn-send-ledger.test.ts / conversation-tools.test.ts
  Tests  27 passed
  ```
- **Overlapping-run isolation boundary — interleaved runs on one session keep independent counts.** With the ledger keyed by `(sessionKey, runId)`, an A -> B -> A interleave keeps run A's count climbing (`record(A)=1`, `record(B)=1`, `record(A)=2`, `peek(A)=2`, `peek(B)=1`) and per-run operation-id isolation holds; the A -> B -> A regression fails on the pre-fix single-slot code (the resumed run A reads a reset count of 1 instead of 2). The new tests are anchored to the concurrent-same-session behavior proven in `src/auto-reply/dispatch.freshness.test.ts`. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/turn-send-ledger.test.ts (16 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  16 passed (16)
  ```
- **Idempotent-replay-past-cap boundary — a retried send at the cap reaches delivery dedup.** With `maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget: 1`, a first send is admitted and counted, a replay of the same tool call (same idempotency key) is not cap-blocked and returns the completed receipt without double-counting or a false nudge, and a genuinely different send is still capped. The regression fails on the pre-fix code (the replay came back `suppressed`/`turn_send_budget_exhausted`). Delivery-layer dedup here applies to Gateway-routed sends (the `conversations.send` `operationId` store); direct-mode channels do not yet dedup on the idempotency key at the delivery layer — tracked in #125824.
- Both regressions were confirmed to have teeth by reverting each production change and observing the corresponding test fail.
- Full suite for the feature: `turn-send-ledger.test.ts` + `message-tool.test.ts` + `conversation-tools.test.ts` pass; `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` exit 0; changed files pass `oxlint --type-aware`.
- Rebased onto latest `upstream/main`; clean.




- **Live-run budget retention boundary — the cap survives long idle waits and provider fallbacks.** The 10-minute idle TTL is deleted: a `(sessionKey, runId)` slot now lives for the whole run and is removed only at the run's terminal boundary. Regressions (fake timers): a capped run stays `exhausted` after an idle interval far past the old TTL (this fails on the pre-fix TTL code — verified by temporarily restoring the prune), a committed operation is still admitted as a `replay` across the same idle wait, and `clearTurnSendLedgerForRun` deletes only the exact `(session, run)` slot (siblings on the same session and same-runId slots on other sessions stay intact; missing scope/slot is a no-op). Run-entry tests prove the budget survives the fallback boundary and is cleared on both success and throw paths. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/turn-send-ledger.test.ts (28 tests)
  embedded-agent-runner  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run-entry.test.ts (22 tests)
  Test Files  passed   Tests  50 passed
  ```
- **Direct-mode replay cap guard — a duplicate model-emitted tool-call id is disambiguated into a distinct cap-blocked send, not admitted as a replay.** The discriminating regression drives the real streaming normalization (`wrapStreamFnTrimToolCallNames` -> `normalizeToolCallIdsInMessage`): a model response emitting the same `message` tool-call id twice with byte-identical arguments is rewritten to two distinct ids, so the copies derive different idempotency keys and the second is cap-blocked with a schema-valid `turn_send_budget_exhausted` result while the runner is invoked exactly once. This guards the exact mechanism that keeps the replay-admission branch unreachable from a real model turn on direct channels (the delivery-layer dedup gap for an admitted replay is tracked separately in #125824). Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/message-tool.test.ts (253 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  253 passed (253)
  ```

- **Route-aware replay admission boundary — a replay is only admitted past the cap when the selected delivery route dedups it.** The message tool resolves the actual gateway-vs-direct delivery route BEFORE reserving and hands the operationId to the ledger only when delivery relays through the Gateway backend (whose completed-result store dedups the repeated operationId). On direct in-process routes a repeated operation is treated as an ordinary new send: cap-blocked when a cap is set, honestly counted otherwise — closing the hole where an admitted replay on a direct channel would re-deliver because the delivery layer does not dedup idempotency keys there (tracked in #125824). Route detection fails conservative: when unsure it withholds the operationId, which cap-blocks a replay rather than re-delivering it. Regressions drive the REAL delivery path (actual outbound adapter call counts): a direct-route replay is suppressed and delivers exactly once, and a Gateway-routed replay is admitted without re-delivering or double-counting. Both fail on the pre-fix unconditional replay admission. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/message-tool.test.ts (254 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  254 passed (254)
  ```
- **Run-terminal budget release boundary — a reused runId starts the next turn with a fresh budget, and fallback candidates never lose committed counts mid-chain.** `prepareCliRunContext` records the exact ledger slot (agent/session/run) the loopback grant mints; CLI settlement deletes only that slot, and only at the true terminal — success or the FINAL fallback attempt's failure. A non-final failure hands off to the next candidate, which must inherit the committed counts, so settlement defers; a dispatched CLI candidate (no `isFinalFallbackAttempt`) defers to the embedded runner's fallback-chain owner, keeping exactly one cleanup owner per terminal. The threw state is derived from real control flow (a `completedNormally` flag), not from `runError`, so a `settleCliAuthProfile` throw after a successful non-final candidate defers exactly like a non-final run failure instead of wiping the budget mid-chain (discriminating regression: the pre-fix `runError` proxy fails it). Cron's isolated-agent finally adds a bounded, idempotent safety net keyed identically to the loopback grant (same `canonicalizeMainSessionAlias` composition, durable session id as runId), so a chain that throws before any candidate settles still releases the slot. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-support  src/agents/cli-runner/cli-run-settlement.test.ts (18 tests)
  cron            src/cron/isolated-agent/run.turn-send-ledger.test.ts (1 test)
  agents-tools    src/agents/tools/turn-send-ledger.test.ts (28 tests)
  Test Files  3 passed (3)   Tests  47 passed (47)
  ```

### Real delivery-boundary proof (mock provider + mock channel, ephemeral Gateway, in a container)

Added `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/per-turn-send-budget.e2e.test.ts`: a real-behavior proof that boots an ephemeral Gateway child with the mock-openai provider and the `qa-channel` synthetic transport, then exercises the shared per-turn send ledger at the real delivery boundary (Gateway + qa-channel outbound bus), not by stubbing `callGateway`. It was run inside a clean `node:24-bookworm` container with container-local Linux dependencies (not just a host unit run). All scenarios pass and the run emits a machine-readable verdict:

```
test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/per-turn-send-budget.e2e.test.ts (8 tests)
  ✓ sanity: a plain qa-channel DM turn delivers one outbound reply
  ✓ scenario 1: second confirmed message send in one turn nudges and both deliveries land
  ✓ scenario 2: hard cap returns a schema-valid suppressed conversations_send result
  ✓ scenario 3: a suppressed message send does not charge the per-turn budget
  ✓ scenario 4: idempotent conversations_send replay does not re-deliver or double count
  ✓ scenario 5: two concurrent distinct-op sends to one target admit exactly one under the cap
  ✓ scenario 6: a model-repeated direct message send under the cap is disambiguated and cap-blocked (exactly-once delivery) — proves the cap-block path, NOT idempotent admission
  ✓ scenario 7: a spoofed attach-grant principal is refused before any delivery I/O (authority chain)
Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  8 passed (8)
```

Verdict (`pass: true`), summarized per scenario:

- **Soft nudge counts confirmed deliveries** — two confirmed `message` sends to one target land on the qa-channel bus; the second tool result carries the model-visible "already sent 2 messages to this target this turn" nudge. `deliveriesRecorded: 2`, ledger `{ "qa-channel:qa-operator": 2 }`.
- **Hard cap returns a schema-valid suppressed result** — with `maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget: 1`, only one delivery reaches the bus; the second `conversations_send` returns `status: "suppressed"` with details that pass `Value.Check(ConversationSendResultSchema, details)` (only `status`, `conversationRef`, `channel`; no `reason`/`message`) and the block explanation in the result text. `deliveriesRecorded: 1`.
- **Only visible deliveries charge the budget** — applying the production `deliveredNothing` predicate: `suppressed` and `failed` do not count (`0`), `partial_failed` counts (`1`, a visible partial reached the peer), plugin/gateway `undefined` counts (`1`), `sent` counts (`1`); no false "sent" nudge is emitted for a non-delivery.
- **Idempotent conversations_send replay** — replaying the same `operationId` returns the Gateway's completed `sent` receipt without a second bus delivery, is not cap-blocked, and does not double-count. `deliveriesRecorded: 1`, ledger stays at `1`.
- **Concurrent distinct-op sends under the cap (reserve-then-settle)** — two parallel `conversations_send` calls with distinct operationIds (NOT a replay) to the same conversation under `maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget: 1`: the first in-flight reservation counts toward the cap synchronously, so the second call is exhausted before it reaches the Gateway — exactly one delivery lands on the bus and the ledger commits exactly one send. This is the core concurrency regression for #119992 (the old peek→await→record path let both peek 0 and both deliver).
- **Cap-blocked model-repeated direct send (cap-block proof, NOT idempotent admission)** — the mock provider emits the SAME direct `message` send twice in one model response (identical planned call id and byte-identical args). The runtime disambiguates the duplicate model-emitted ids into two distinct tool-call ids, so the copies derive different idempotency keys: the first delivers, and the second is cap-blocked before dispatch with a schema-valid `turn_send_budget_exhausted` result fed back to the model. Exactly-once delivery is asserted on the RECEIVE side — the qa-channel outbound bus carries exactly one copy of the marker, and a re-delivered copy would surface as a second. This proves end-to-end cap enforcement for the direct `message` tool at the real delivery boundary; it proves the cap-block path, not the idempotent-admission path (a duplicate model-emitted send is always disambiguated upstream and can never be presented as an idempotent replay).
- **Authority chain — an unauthorized principal is refused before any delivery I/O (scenario 7).** The harness's own `attach.grant` method mints a real non-owner grant; the test then drives the REAL MCP loopback HTTP entry with that grant plus spoofed delivery-authority headers (`x-session-key`, message channel, account id, current channel id, and `x-openclaw-current-messaging-target` pointed at a registered conversation) — every hop is the genuine defense, with no mocked resolver output: `validateMcpLoopbackRequest` → `resolveAttachGrant` → `resolveMcpRequestContext` (grant branch forces every spoofable header, including the routable target, to undefined) → owner-only tool deny. Asserted: `tools/list` does not advertise `conversations_send` for the grant principal; a `tools/call conversations_send` attempt is refused; and zero deliveries reach the qa-channel bus. Positive control on the same lane: the legitimate owner-bound path (real Gateway `conversations.send` → qa-channel bus, as scenarios 2/4/5) delivers exactly one — so the zero above is a real refusal, not a dead harness. Verdict entries carry no tokens.

Full unit suite for the feature (`turn-send-ledger.test.ts` + `message-tool.test.ts` + `conversation-tools.test.ts` + `cli-run-settlement.test.ts` + cron `run.turn-send-ledger.test.ts`) passes; `tsgo:core`/`tsgo:extensions`/`tsgo:test:root` exit 0; changed files pass `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check`. Rebased onto latest `upstream/main`; clean.

### Final-head validation (HEAD `782540cd69f`)

Second upstream catch-up: the published branch was brought up to current `upstream/main` via an ordinary merge commit that merged main `36537b21828`. No published commit was rewritten, so the branch stays a descendant of its published head `97eb46dc643` and an ordinary fast-forward push applies. This second merge only resolved the generated config-documentation baseline conflicts (`docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` / `.sha256`, core option count settles at 2450) alongside the auto-merged code; the CHANGELOG Unreleased section is byte-identical to the merged upstream parent.

Re-verified on this final head `782540cd69f`:

- **Real qa-lab per-turn-send-budget E2E: 8/8 passing.** All eight stable scenario outcomes are pre-registered and fail-closed — the run asserts no missing, duplicate, unknown, or unsuccessful outcome; every registered scenario reports its expected result and the machine-readable verdict is `pass: true`.
- **Typecheck green:** `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, and `tsgo:test:root` all exit 0.
- **Focused tests: 759 passing** across the feature's unit and integration suites, plus proof 9/9.
- **Config docs / lint / format / diff check green:** config docs generation, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` are all clean.
- **Autoreview (honest scope note):** the final PR-tree fresh autoreview was scoped-clean with 0 P0–P2 findings on the predecessor head `97eb46dc643`, run over the PR tree against that merge commit's second parent `8e1f02805f66` (exact `upstream/main`). This second catch-up merge (`782540cd69f`) only resolved the generated config-baseline conflicts and did **not** receive a new fresh autoreview on `782540cd69f`.

Note: the Telegram (D5) live-channel proof from earlier revisions was not rerun on this final head; the validation above covers the qa-lab delivery-boundary E2E, typecheck, focused tests, config/lint/format/diff, and the prior scoped-clean autoreview.



### CI line-cap ratchet remediation (HEAD `4bcae80db14`)

CI job `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` failed at `782540cd69f`: the send-budget work pushed eight grandfathered files past their `check:line-cap-ratchet` baseline (deterministic against the merge base `36537b21828`). No cap was raised, no rule disabled, and no coverage trimmed — each file drops back to or below its base counted-line count by relocating cohesive helpers and the new send-budget test group into focused sibling modules:

- `message-tool-execution.ts` → `message-tool-turn-send-budget.ts` (turn-send-budget resolve/reserve/settle/nudge orchestration).
- `message-tool.test.ts` → `message-tool.turn-send-budget.test.ts` for the per-turn-send-budget group; `createChannelPlugin` and the runner-input type shared via `message-tool.test-support.ts`. The tool-assembly wiring assertion stays where its `createOpenClawTools` mocks live.

Validation on this head (`4bcae80db14`):

prs.title: fix(media): retry against the original file when Wikimedia rejects a thumbnail width
prs.body:
Closes #119684

## What Problem This Solves

Users asking an agent for a Wikimedia image received **nothing at all — not even the text portion of the reply** — when the agent picked a thumbnail width Wikimedia hasn't pre-rendered for that file. Wikimedia's thumbnail servers only serve a whitelist of widths per file and reject anything else with `HTTP 400 "Use thumbnail sizes listed on ..."`; the media-fetch failure took down the whole reply.

## The Fix

When a media fetch fails with **HTTP 400** and the URL is a rewritable `upload.wikimedia.org` thumbnail URL, retry once against the original (non-thumbnail) file, which Wikimedia always serves:
`.../wikipedia/<project>/thumb/<a>/<b>/<file>/<width>px-<file>` → `.../wikipedia/<project>/<a>/<b>/<file>`.

Key properties (directly addressing the earlier review):

- **Reachable on the real path (was the P1).** The trigger keys off **status + URL shape, not the response body.** The managed-media store path (`saveRemoteMediaForStore`) drains non-OK response bodies (`store.remote.runtime.ts`), so a body-text predicate (`"thumbnail sizes"`) never matched in production — the first revision's fallback was dead exactly where it mattered.
- **Covers both fetch entry points.** The fallback is shared (`withWikimediaOriginalFallback`) across `saveRemoteMedia` (managed-media store write) **and `readRemoteMediaBuffer`** — the path Telegram reply delivery actually uses (`loadWebMedia → readRemoteMediaBuffer`), the exact route the bug report described.
- **Exact host match.** `hostname === "upload.wikimedia.org"` (the previous `endsWith("wikimedia.org")` also accepted `evilwikimedia.org`). The original URL is derived purely from the same file's path, so it can never point at another origin.
- **Rewrites only genuine renditions.** The last path segment must be a `<width>px-<sourcefile>` rendition (contains a `\d+px-` width token and the source filename); an incomplete thumbnail-shaped URL whose tail is not a real rendition is left alone, not rewritten.
- **Safe failure.** If the original file also fails, the **original** error is surfaced — error reporting is unchanged for genuine failures.
- **No new lint suppression.** The logic lives in `src/media/wikimedia.ts` (fallback + URL rewrite) and `src/media/remote-filename.ts` (filename decoders split out of the grandfathered-oversized `fetch.ts` to satisfy the `max-lines` ratchet without a suppression).

## Tests

Unit (`src/media/wikimedia.test.ts`): thumb→original rewrite, non-Wikimedia and `evilwikimedia.org` host rejection, original-error propagation.

Integration (`src/media/fetch.test.ts`), for **both** `saveRemoteMedia` and `readRemoteMediaBuffer`:
- `retries against the original file even when the 400 response body was drained` — mocks a body-less `Response(null, { status: 400 })`, the exact shape the store wrapper produces, proving the fallback fires on the production path.
- `does not rewrite non-upload.wikimedia.org hosts (guards the endsWith overmatch)`.
- `surfaces the original thumbnail error when the original file also fails`.

## Evidence

Real deployment: an agent asked for a dog photo, picked `.../thumb/e/e7/007_American_Pit_Bull_Terrier.jpg/800px-...jpg`, got the 400, and the reply never reached the user.

The drained-body reachability tests are the in-repo proof that the fallback now fires on the production (store + Telegram-reply) paths; a live redacted delivery screenshot would require a running deployment.

## Real Behavior Proof (real transport client over a real socket)

Drove the **real `readRemoteMediaBuffer`** — the path outbound web media / Telegram reply delivery uses (`loadWebMedia → readRemoteMediaBuffer`) — with **no `fetchImpl`, no mocked `globalThis.fetch`, and no runtime-deps override**. Because a pinned dispatcher is attached and nothing is stubbed, `fetch-guard.ts` takes the runtime path (`shouldUseRuntimeFetch === true`) and a **real `undici` client opens a real TCP connection**. The Wikimedia host is DNS-pinned to loopback (`lookupFn → 127.0.0.1`) and the SSRF policy is opened for the private network (`ssrfPolicy: { allowPrivateNetwork: true }`), so the real client connects to a **real local HTTP origin server** standing in for `upload.wikimedia.org`. That server returns a genuine HTTP **400** (with the real `"Use thumbnail sizes listed on ..."` body) for the out-of-whitelist thumbnail width, then a genuine **200 + image bytes** for the original file. The only thing "mocked" is which machine answers — the transport, the request, the status codes, and the bytes are all real.

### Before — fallback removed from the buffer path (the bug)

```
REAL TCP requests received: [ "/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/88/007_American_Pit_Bull_Terrier.jpg/800px-...jpg" ]
readRemoteMediaBuffer THREW: MediaFetchError code=http_error status=400
  "...HTTP 400 Bad Request; body: Use thumbnail sizes listed on ..."
```

The buffer read aborts — the reply/attachment would be lost.

### After — with the fix

```
REAL TCP requests received by the origin server:
  #1 (thumbnail 400) -> /wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/88/007_American_Pit_Bull_Terrier.jpg/800px-...jpg
  #2 (original 200)  -> /wikipedia/commons/8/88/007_American_Pit_Bull_Terrier.jpg
readRemoteMediaBuffer resolved: contentType=image/jpeg, bytes=3
PASS: real undici client recovered the original file over a real socket
```

The recovery is driven entirely by the real guard/dispatcher/undici pipeline reacting to a real 400 — no stub can influence which URL is fetched or how the SSRF/redirect logic runs. The store-write path (`saveRemoteMedia`) shares the same fallback and is additionally covered by the drained-body integration tests (the managed store delivers non-OK responses with an empty body, which the status-based predicate handles).

prs.title: feat(whatsapp): add poll_vote_received hook
prs.body:
Related: #119254 (closed as not planned; it did not establish sponsorship for this public contract).

## What Problem This Solves

WhatsApp plugins can passively observe decoded votes and retractions on polls accepted through the OpenClaw Gateway. The opt-in `poll_vote_received` event avoids separate WhatsApp polling or another agent turn.

## Behavior and lifecycle

The hook is limited to polls recorded from an accepted Gateway send. A `fromMe` echo alone does not establish ownership. Ownership is bound to the exact WhatsApp account monitor lifetime; queued `poll_vote_received` and sibling `message_received` callbacks revalidate that scope immediately before plugin dispatch. The scope is disposed when the monitor exits, before socket shutdown, so callbacks queued by a retired monitor cannot disclose data after an account slot is reused.

The observation cache remains process-local, bounded to 500 entries, and expires after ten minutes. A restart or eviction ends observation of older polls; no persistent vote data or SQLite schema is added.

## Contract and compatibility

`channels.whatsapp.pluginHooks.pollVoteReceived` and the account-level override are optional booleans. Omitted means disabled; the account value overrides the channel value. Existing configs remain valid, the schema tests cover both levels and omission, and the generated bundled channel metadata includes the field. No migration is needed because the new value is optional.

This is a public plugin contract that exposes voter, conversation, poll, and selected-option data. A listed WhatsApp/plugin maintainer still needs to sponsor that disclosure scope and explicitly accept the ten-minute process-local lifetime, including expiry, eviction, and restart.

## Evidence and validation

- Conflicts with current `main` through `fecba819ef2e67952e52896501278dc9bee72d4b` are resolved. The integrated SDK budget preserves upstream's retired exports and the PR's poll-event allowance; both `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` and `pnpm check:assertion-safety` pass. Current PR head: `cb00a538bebf117576e244d0f7ec36fb45a59d74`.
- Final-effect tests assert no plugin callback for a linked-device poll without an accepted Gateway send, an opt-out applied while a vote is queued, a poll from a prior account lifetime after slot reassignment, and a queued vote after owner revocation. The sibling queued `message_received` path asserts both plugin and internal callbacks remain at zero after its monitor closes.
- Full local validation passed on the integrated tree: 72 focused tests, lint, formatting, regenerated artifacts, production/test type checks, and SDK surface checks. The assertion-safety ratchet also passed.
- Local `autoreview` on the source repair reported no accepted actionable P0/P1 findings; the final `main` merge changes no runtime behavior.
- Manual live positive evidence at candidate `3136032aca05908ff5a3b9e0579f50abc9f16f00` showed an isolated Gateway poll, a real WhatsApp vote, one matching `poll_vote_received` fixture event, hashed identifiers, candidate cleanup, and a healthy production Gateway. That run predates the monitor-lifetime repair, so it is not exact-head live proof for the new lifecycle binding.
- Reviewed net change against current `upstream/main`: +725 production lines, +2,729 test/support lines, and +81 documentation/generated/tooling lines. The production growth is the new hook/config capability and shared hook contract; the lifecycle repair adds 92 net production lines to bind both queued callbacks to one monitor owner boundary, with 189 net test/support lines.

## Remaining before merge

ClawSweeper's final-effect rank-up move is covered by the tests above. Its separate maintainer-decision move remains open: a listed plugin/channel maintainer must sponsor the contract and observation lifetime. `.github/CODEOWNERS` has no matching WhatsApp path, so the repository's CODEOWNERS rule does not identify that sponsor. Exact-head GitHub CI and the fresh ClawSweeper review are pending. Do not merge until CI is green and the sponsor decision is recorded.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Contributors preparing security-sensitive branches have no optional worktree-local guard that binds an explicit reviewed path set, branch identity, and exact head before a push. The repository's hosted CI and canonical `scripts/pr` landing controls remain authoritative, but they do not provide that additional pre-publication convenience at the contributor worktree.

## What This Change Does

Adds an **opt-in, worktree-local publication preflight** for contributors who want an additional local check before pushing a reviewed branch. It does not replace hosted CI, branch protection, or the maintained `scripts/pr` landing controls; those remain authoritative.

Current `scripts/pr prepare-push` synchronizes an already-open PR head under lease and ancestry checks. It does not cover this branch's distinct before-first-publication contributor use case. The standalone lane therefore retains unique behavior, but the PR stays draft while maintainers decide whether OpenClaw wants that optional convenience surface.

## Review findings repaired

- Preserves the existing automatic `git-hooks` installation during package `prepare`, including the maintained pre-commit hook.
- Enables the optional pre-push gate only after explicit opt-in, recorded in the current worktree's Git metadata rather than shared repository config.
- Documents both supported opt-ins: `--install` for manual setup and exact-value `OPENCLAW_INSTALL_GIT_HOOKS=1` for non-interactive setup. Other values do not enable the preflight.
- Accepts the documented `git push origin HEAD` form while still requiring one exact branch update at the current reviewed SHA.
- Rejects empty/multiple ref updates once enabled and retains fail-closed behavior for missing preflight state.
- Collects all open PRs and all changed files through `gh api --paginate --slurp`; malformed, truncated, or incomplete response shapes fail closed.
- Includes added, copied, modified, renamed, **and deleted** paths in both staged and committed-range allowlist checks, so an unapproved tracked-file deletion cannot bypass the exact path set.
- Makes the default CONTRIBUTING command runnable: it now uses the authenticated complete live inventory instead of requiring a nonexistent placeholder file. The optional `--inventory-file` path is documented only for trusted tooling that supplies a complete canonical snapshot, never a partial hand-written list.
- Exercises the accepted pre-push update through a real local bare-remote `git push`. This avoids a Windows test-harness dependency on whichever incompatible `bash` happens to resolve first while preserving the direct multi-ref rejection assertion.
- Requires `update_existing` to select an actual overlapping PR on the current feature branch, rejects a wrong-branch selection, and fails closed when any additional overlap is undeclared. The same complete-overlap requirement applies to `supersede_existing`.

## Evidence

Reviewed head: `d9700ba75ebc76c0be6198b483d02f6f033d8cdb`

Frozen upstream base merged for this validation: `d91b3970b47f3df9ebd36bb93c5074b24515dd82`

### Inspectable real hook behavior

The focused suite uses temporary Git repositories and real local bare remotes. On native Windows, the final exact-head run passed **11/11**, including:

```text
✓ keeps automatic maintained-hook setup transparent until explicit opt-in
✓ invokes the configured hook for an allowed push and rejects an unallowlisted commit
✓ rejects an unallowlisted tracked-file deletion through the real hook
✓ prepares, checks, approves, and accepts the exact pre-push update
✓ fails closed before approval
```

Those tests exercise real `git push` behavior and prove:

- normal package preparation retains the maintained hook path without enabling the optional pre-push policy;
- an unopted real push succeeds;
- after explicit opt-in, `git push origin HEAD` at the approved exact SHA succeeds;
- later unallowlisted additions and deletions are rejected;
- an additional unreviewed ref in the same push is rejected.

### Pagination proof

The regression fixture supplies multiple PR pages and multiple file pages, proves every PR/path is retained, asserts every request uses `api --paginate --slurp`, and verifies malformed page/file shapes fail closed.

A prior read-only live GitHub API shape check returned:

```json
{"pages":22,"pulls":2191,"allPagesArrays":true}
```

This confirms the former 100-PR limit was materially incomplete and that the implemented page-array contract matches the observed response shape.

### Current exact-head checks

- Latest overlap-declaration regression suite: **13/13 passed**, including the valid single-update path, wrong-branch rejection, additional-update overlap rejection, and additional-supersede overlap rejection.
- Latest repair gates passed: `pnpm tsgo:scripts`, type-aware Oxlint (with only the branch's inherited test-line-48 conversion rule allowed), Oxfmt, and `git diff --check`.
- Mandatory exact-branch repair review: TruffleHog clean in **6.6 seconds**; **5,875-byte**, one-pass Codex `gpt-5.6-sol` high-reasoning bundle; findings `[]`; `patch is correct` at **0.98 confidence**; reviewer exited **0**.
- Focused real-Git suite for the preceding portability repair: **11/11 passed**.
- Repository-selected changed-file plan: all conflict, attribution, registry, wildcard-export, duplicate-coverage, coercion, dependency-pin, format, and patch guards passed.
- Root test-source type check passed.
- Full script lint selected by the changed-file plan passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Preceding exact-branch review on `a69400bb79e2f50b3d3c4ba3176351f1a3a88bf6` against the frozen base: TruffleHog clean in 6.5 seconds; 58,581-byte one-pass Codex `gpt-5.6-sol` high-reasoning bundle; findings `[]`; `patch is correct` at **0.99 confidence**; terminal result `autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported`.
- Fresh draft-safe hosted checks for `d9700ba75ebc76c0be6198b483d02f6f033d8cdb` are attached at [run 31502685750](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/31502685750). The substantive CI matrix is intentionally skipped while the PR remains draft; light repository checks are monitored separately.

## Limitations and hosted proof

- The configured Crabbox changed-gate helper failed its binary sanity check before dispatching any remote workload. The identical repository-selected plan was run locally on Windows using the helper's documented remote-child mode; this is local proof, not a claim of remote execution.
- The bundled `pnpm` launcher reported Node 24.14.0 below the repository's current engine floor, while the direct runtime and `pnpm exec node` were Node 24.18.0. All selected gates completed successfully, but hosted exact-head CI remains authoritative for a supported clean runner.
- The frozen validation base is intentionally fixed. By the final lease check, current main had advanced beyond it; this update did not chase later main after review.
- The test-temp report remains warning-only for four raw temporary-directory helpers already present in this feature diff; the portability repair adds no new raw temporary directory.

## Maintainer decision

This branch provides a contributor pre-publication surface that current `scripts/pr prepare-push` does not. Please decide whether to retain that optional standalone convenience or reject the product policy in favor of no local pre-publication layer. No merge, ready-for-review transition, or claim that a bypassable local hook is the repository's security boundary is requested by this update.

prs.title: fix(agents): prioritize skill-creator over direct skill_workshop calls for skill creation
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes #104104 The model non-deterministically routes between invoking the `skill-creator` skill and calling the `skill_workshop` tool directly when a user requests skill creation. This happens because the system prompt presents two competing, unprioritized directives at the same level: 1. **Skills section** — lists `skill-creator` and instructs the model to load it when applicable 2. **Skill Workshop section** (`skill-workshop-prompt.ts`) — unconditionally directs: "Route durable skill work through `skill_workshop`" When `skill_workshop` is chosen directly, the `skill-creator` workflow (validation rules, structure conventions, edit workflow) is bypassed entirely. ## Why This Change Was Made The Skill Workshop prompt section now includes explicit routing priority: "When the `skill-creator` skill is available, load it first — it owns the creation workflow and will route to `skill_workshop` when ready." This establishes a single unambiguous routing path: user request → `skill-creator` → `skill_workshop`. The change is a one-line edit to `skill-workshop-prompt.ts` with no function signature changes, no new parameters, and no caller modifications. When `skill-creator` is unavailable, the directive becomes a natural no-op. ## User Impact Users creating skills via chat will consistently get `skill-creator`'s structure and validation guidance before the proposal reaches `skill_workshop`, resulting in higher-quality skill proposals. ## Evidence - `pnpm test src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts` — 94/94 pass (including "instructs models to use skill_workshop only when the tool is available") - Change: 1 file, 1 line (`src/agents/skill-workshop-prompt.ts:11`) - After the modification, when creating a skill, it can reliably trigger skill-creator first, and then trigger skill workshop.

prs.title: fix(release): hand Windows-node a self-contained candidate
prs.body:
## Problem

Release Checks' Windows-node lanes (`main`, `stable`, `prerelease`) hand the external `openclaw/openclaw-windows-node` harness exactly one candidate tarball, which it installs inside WSL with every other dependency from public npm. Release-shaped candidates keep `@openclaw/ai` unbundled because it publishes alongside core, so an unpublished candidate fails `install-cli`:

```
npm error code ETARGET
npm error notarget No matching version found for @openclaw/ai@2026.10.10-beta.4.
```

Seen on every Windows-node lane of the 2026.10.10-beta.4 FRV (release checks run 40051233511, jobs 120744992818 / 120744992871 / 120744992859) and on the earlier beta.4 FRV. Main hides the defect only because its version (2026.10.6) is already on npm, so main's lane installs the *published* `@openclaw/ai` rather than the candidate's.

## Solution

- `scripts/self-contained-candidate-package.mjs`: for each core `dependency` entry in `scripts/lib/npm-core-release-packages.json` that is not already bundled and has an exact-version tarball in the verified prepublish registry, extract it into `package/node_modules/<name>`, validate its dependency alignment with the existing `validateBundledPackageDependencyAlignment`, strip its nested deps (same shape as `package-openclaw-for-docker`), add it to `bundleDependencies`, repack, and rewrite `package-candidate.json` with the new sha256. With no registry or nothing to bundle the tarball passes through byte-identical.
- `openclaw-release-checks.yml`: when Windows-node is scheduled, `prepare_release_package` verifies the prepublish registry, builds a Windows-node-only candidate artifact, and feeds its name/sha256 to the three Windows-node jobs. Every other lane keeps the unmodified release package.
- Tests (`test/scripts/self-contained-candidate-package.test.ts`, updated `package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts`) and a docs note in `docs/reference/full-release-validation/release-checks.md`.

## Impact

Windows-node release validation can qualify unpublished candidates (beta/stable) instead of failing at CLI install. No change to published bytes or other validation lanes.

## Evidence

- Root cause reproduced locally: `npm install -g --dry-run` of the FRV candidate artifact → `notarget ... @openclaw/ai@2026.10.10-beta.4`.
- The script on the real beta.4 artifact + prepublish registry produced a candidate that `npm install -g` installed from public npm; `openclaw --version` → `OpenClaw 2026.10.10-beta.4 (4575d28)`; `@openclaw/ai` and `@openclaw/ai/providers` import from the installed package.
- New tests (3) plus workflow/release test files (802 tests), `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, oxlint, format, `pnpm check:workflows` pass locally.
- Not yet proven: a hosted Windows-node run with the new artifact (next beta.4 Full Release Validation will exercise it after backport).

prs.title: feat(cron): run scheduled children in their parent conversation's workspace and sandbox
prs.body:
Builds on #178933, #179834, #178965, #179011 and #179062 (all merged).

Related: #178812
Related: #178811

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a scheduled child of a conversation runs in the agent's default workspace, not the workspace, working directory or managed worktree its parent conversation is bound to. A child of a sandboxed conversation can also run without a sandbox.

## User Impact

User impact: an automation created from a conversation that is bound to a workspace, working directory or managed worktree now runs its child sessions there, with that conversation's ownership checks.
- If the parent conversation requires a sandbox, the child does too, including when the job's cron session already existed before this change. A child never runs looser than its parent.
- If the parent is reset (`/new`) or removed while the child runs in its workspace, the run ends: the child's next OpenClaw tool effect is refused, and a CLI backend's process is stopped so its own file tools cannot keep writing there. It never keeps working in the former conversation's workspace.
- If the parent's bound worktree is gone, the job pauses with a notice naming the path (the #178965 pause). It never falls back to the agent workspace.
- A parent that was already reset when the occurrence is admitted does not pause, and the child gets none of these: that occurrence runs unbound, in the run session's own workspace, as before this PR.
- In-session (`session:<key>`) jobs, operator jobs and unbound jobs keep their current workspace selection.
- File scope stays `root`: a child automation is limited to its own workspace and does not get its parent conversation's file scope. Josh decided this on 2026-10-21 ("Keep root."; design row 36, resolved decision 9).

## Why This Change Was Made

- **One parent read.** The occurrence admission from #179834 already reads the parent row once per occurrence. For a child run whose parent is current and not paused, it now also returns `occurrence.childParent`: the parent row when it persists a workspace binding, its sandbox requirement, and `assertCurrent`, which fails once the parent resets or the occurrence settles. Run preparation and workspace selection use it and don't read the parent again. The parent row's workspace uses the same persisted-binding rule run preparation applies (`resolveIngressWorkspaceOverrideForSessionRun`).
- **Workspace.** `prepareCronSessionWorkspace` applies the existing ownership and worktree checks to the parent's row, not the run session's row, and every workspace step checks the parent. The in-session target path is unchanged.
- **Live parent authority.** When the child runs in its parent's bound workspace, the prompt executor passes the parent check as the admitted run's source assertion. Embedded tool authority runs that assertion before every tool effect, so a parent reset mid-run refuses every later read and write. A CLI backend's native file tools never reach that check, so admission also watches committed changes to the parent row while a bound child runs (`parent-reset-watch.ts`) and aborts a signal once the parent stops being current; the CLI run's abort signal includes it, so the process ends with the parent.
- **Sandbox.** The creator-role sandbox still wins. Otherwise a parent with `sandbox: "required"` makes the child sandboxed. An existing cron root keeps its row and never takes creation metadata, so the CLI host-placement check also receives the occurrence's inherited requirement directly.
- **File scope.** The execution context now records `root` for child runs, matching what runs today; only in-session runs record their session's scope. No consumer reads this field yet, so behavior is unchanged.
- **Fail-safe.** If the parent read fails, the occurrence is unadmitted and carries no `childParent`, so the run keeps the legacy run-session workspace instead of failing, and the minted context fails closed for grants that only the parent gets.

## Evidence

- **Real cron service, sessions and tools** (`run.session-workspace-authority.test.ts`): a job created through the automations tool from a bound conversation runs through the real cron service with persisted session rows.
  - An isolated child reads its parent's workspace (plain and managed worktree).
  - After a real `/new` reset of the parent during the run (`resetSessionEntryLifecycle`), the admitted run's assertion refuses, and nothing is read from the former workspace.
  - Archived parents pause, and foreign, escaping and mismatched bindings are refused, as before.
- **Sandbox, real CLI process** (`run.sandbox-admission.test.ts`): with an existing persisted, unstamped cron root and the agent's sandbox mode off, a child whose parent requires a sandbox fails closed before the CLI process launches; the same root with an unsandboxed parent launches the real CLI stub. Without the placement fix the first case launches the CLI on the host.
- **Admission:** `execution-context-admission` covers removed and archived parents (pause), a reset parent (runs, no binding), a missing worktree (pause naming the path), a child getting its parent's bound row, sandbox requirement and live check (which fails after a parent reset and after the occurrence settles), an unbound parent's child getting only its sandbox requirement, an in-session job keeping its own binding, a failed read (no pause), and the notice.
- **Parent reset watch** (`execution-context-admission.test.ts`): a bound child's signal aborts with the parent's failure on a change to the parent row, ignores other rows, stays live while the parent is current, and stops after the occurrence settles.
- **Docs:** `docs/automation/cron-jobs/payloads.md` now describes which detached runs inherit the creating conversation's workspace and what a reset does mid-run.
- **Related suites** (execution context, admission, occurrence, workspace authority, sandbox admission, fast mode, PR automation, memory audience): pass.
- **Checks:** `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test` and `tsgo:test:src` are clean; type-aware oxlint and oxfmt are clean; the line-cap and mock-export ratchets pass.
- **Autoreview (Codex, P0–P2):** the two P1s from the previous review were confirmed fixed by the new commit; a stale admission-test expectation it found was updated.

### Live behavior proof (real Gateway, code at head `4618fc07eb9`)

A QA scenario creates conversations with `sessions.create` bound to a working directory (`cwd`) that holds a marker file, schedules child jobs from inside them, and force-runs the jobs on a real Gateway child process (`mock-openai`). The CLI lane uses a local fake CLI backend that reports its launch directory and writes files with its own (native) file I/O, so those writes never pass OpenClaw's tool check. The scenarios, the fake CLI and the gated probe tool are local proof tooling only, not part of this PR.

| Scenario | This PR | `main` / previous head |
|---|---|---|
| Embedded child reads `QA_PARENT_WS_MARKER.txt` | pass: reads `PARENT-WS-MARKER` from the parent's directory | `main` (`ddbf65c9215`) fails: `File not found: <qa-suite>/workspace/QA_PARENT_WS_MARKER.txt` (agent default workspace) |
| CLI child launch directory | pass: `cwd=<parent dir> marker=PARENT-WS-MARKER` | — |
| Parent reset while an embedded child is parked mid-run | pass: run ends `source execution authority is no longer active`; no tool result after the reset reaches the model | — |
| Parent reset while a **CLI** child is mid-run (native file writes before and after a gate) | pass: write before the reset lands; the CLI process is already gone right after `sessions.reset`; the write after the gate never happens; run ends `source execution authority is no longer active` | previous head `d1920578643` fails: process still alive after the reset, writes `QA_CLI_HOLD_AFTER.txt` into the parent's directory, run reports `ok` |

<details><summary>CLI reset case, before and after the fix</summary>

```text
d1920578643 (before):  before=true after=true  aliveAfterReset=true  status=ok
4618fc07eb9 (after):   before=true after=false aliveAfterReset=false status=error
                       "source execution authority is no longer active | SESSION_DELIVERY_GENERATION_REVOKED"
```
</details>

### Upgrade proof (latest stable `2026.10.6` → this PR)

On an isolated state directory, `2026.10.6` creates a conversation bound to a working directory, a job linked to it and an unlinked job, then stops. This PR's `doctor --fix` runs on the same state, and this PR's Gateway starts on it.

- Both jobs are byte-identical before and after the upgrade. The only job change is Doctor's existing conversion of the built-in heartbeat job.
- The parent conversation's saved `workspaceDir`, `spawnedCwd`, label and session id are unchanged.
- The pre-upgrade linked job runs in the parent's directory (`cwd=<parent dir> marker=PARENT-WS-MARKER`); the pre-upgrade unlinked job runs in the agent workspace (`marker=missing (ENOENT)`); a linked job created after the upgrade also runs in the parent's directory. All three runs use the CLI runtime.
- A conversation's required sandbox can only be set through an identified operator's role policy, not over the token connection used here, so the live upgrade does not cover it. The stored `sandbox` field is read unchanged; its inheritance is covered by `run.sandbox-admission.test.ts` against a real CLI process.

prs.title: fix: recover large session histories without worker memory failure
prs.body:
Closes #182060

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes restart recovery failing with `ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY` when a session has a large SQLite-backed history.

## User Impact

Users can recover the complete history without increasing the worker heap or truncating the conversation. Existing atomicity, lifecycle checks, and successor linking are preserved; no configuration or schema changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recovery currently materializes every decoded event, then filters and spreads additional whole-history arrays. The canonical reader now supports scoped synchronous iteration; recovery passes a lazy replacement-header/body stream to the existing bounded append owner inside the same transaction. Existing array consumers retain their contract and share query, decoding, hot-snapshot admission, and cursor cleanup.

This removes recovery-wide decoded/filter/spread arrays, not the existing array API. Production delta is +68/-47 lines (net +21), with +94 test lines for the memory boundary and partial-write rollback. PostgreSQL buffering and the cost of an individual event are unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Red on the exact base:** the new compressed-history regression reaches the production recovery command after successful setup, then fails with `ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY` under the default 512 MiB worker limit (60.162 s wall).
- **Green with the fix:** the real-worker recovery suite passes 12/12, including >512 MiB decoded compressed history with 601 successor events and an intact last payload/tombstone link. A separate malformed late row rolls back the partial clone and source metadata, and a repaired retry succeeds.
- Recovery-suite command: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/session-accessor.recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (equivalent repository test wrapper; 56.996 s wall, about 23 s test time; large-history case 13.647 s). The actual worker heap boundary cannot be established by a parser mock. CI seconds are not yet available.
- Six directly affected reader/append/fork/rewind/lifecycle/mirroring suites: 77/77 pass (263.981 s wall, including 103.318 s initial worker compilation).
- Focused TypeScript check, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. Simplification pass complete; fresh independent P0/P1 review is scoped-clean.

The fixture is entirely synthetic. This is production-worker proof, not yet proof of recovery through a serving Gateway. Broader checks are left to PR CI.

prs.title: fix(agents): preserve tool timeout recovery checkpoints
prs.body:
## Summary

- preserve `tool_execution` watchdog phase through canonical terminal settlement
- persist tool timeouts as durable interrupted recovery checkpoints with explicit unknown-side-effect guidance
- force replay-safe continuation, reject CLI runtimes that cannot enforce it, and preserve legacy Claude recovery markers
- ignore duplicate terminal events after a checkpoint is settled so stale timeouts cannot resurrect recovery

## Tests

- targeted terminal normalization, watchdog settlement, lifecycle checkpoint, startup recovery, explicit recovery, CLI safety, and Claude history import regressions
- `pnpm tsgo`
- targeted `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check`

`pnpm tsgo:test` was also run; relevant shards passed, with an unrelated current-main UI test type error in `chat-details-output-intent.test.tsx` where `artifactsLoading` is not in `ChatOutputsDesktopProps`.

## Exact-head authority and compatibility proof

Exact head: 4cab71c426bea36494435cad57750ea8f570c271 (current main merged cleanly).

Redacted terminal receipt (no credentials, endpoints, phone numbers, or private data):

```text
PASS restart-safe automation inspection (8/8)
✓ reads the owner recorded status through the restart-safe dispatcher catalog
✓ rejects global status and every automation mutation at the owner even with open admission
✓ rejects a hook rewriting an allowed read into a mutation at final execution
✓ requires caller identity for recovery reads and owner authority for normal writes
```

prs.title: fix(sessions): recover large transcripts without loading the whole history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #182060: **Resume in new session** can terminate the SQLite worker with `ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY` when the source conversation has a large compressed transcript.

Supersedes #182073, thanks @diregoblin (Pavel Zun) for the report and reference implementation. Reimplemented on main without checking out or executing contributor code.

## User Impact

Recovery preserves the complete transcript, including inactive branches, while copying large SQLite histories without retaining the entire decoded conversation. The successor and source tombstone link still publish atomically. A failed copy rolls back and can be retried.

No schema, configuration, CLI, dependency, retention, or worker-heap-limit changes are required. Release-note context: session restart recovery no longer exhausts the worker heap on large SQLite transcripts; fixes #182060, supersedes #182073, thanks @diregoblin.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recovery worker eagerly decoded every event and then constructed another filtered array before appending. The existing append owner already handles iterables in batches bounded by 1 MiB or 512 events. Recovery now consumes a scoped native cursor through that owner within the original synchronous transaction. Cursor cleanup stays inside the fenced read snapshot, including early header discovery and failure; existing array readers retain their behavior.

The simplification pass removed whole-history buffering and reused the existing transaction, append batches, and publication owner. Necessary growth is **+23 net production lines** for the scoped cursor and streaming clone, **+78 net test lines**, and **+4 documentation lines**. Sharing the existing read-option declarations avoids duplicating that contract. No staging store or extra recovery owner was introduced.

## Evidence

- Node 26.12.1, production SQLite-worker limits unchanged (512 MiB old generation, 32 MiB young generation). The new 544 MiB decoded-history regression fails on the untouched base with `ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY` and passes with this fix. The recovery file passes all 12 tests, including a malformed row after a flushed batch: no successor rows or tombstone link survive, and repair followed by retry succeeds.
- Additional contract suites: 143 tests passed; four existing mixed-engine tests skipped because their PostgreSQL fixture is not configured.
- Completed all **132 selected direct-import, one-barrel, contract, and recovery files** across stable-source runs. All runnable selected cases pass after the recorder repair below; **27 existing environment-gated cases** were skipped. The final remaining-file invocation passed all five shards, including 230 reply-agent E2E cases.
- All 24 additional one-barrel consumer files passed: 375 tests. Sibling testing also exposed a timestamp conformance test reading `sourceSQL` after its native statement was finalized, after the timestamp itself had returned correctly. The test now captures SQL through the existing execution observer without weakening its assertions; its full 42-test file passes. An earlier broad invocation was discarded because a type-only edit invalidated its frozen source snapshot; validation was repeated against stable source.
- Existing slow-suite observation: `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` passed 230 cases in 160.47 s wall time, approximately 136 s of test time. Its fixture creates separate SQLite stores and joins recovery-owner release plus database close after each case; this is existing per-case persistence/lifecycle cost, not the new large-history regression (4.5 s). Recorded under the campaign's pre-existing-slow-suite continuation rule; shared fixture optimization belongs in a dedicated follow-up.
- Production and session-test typechecks, touched-file oxlint and oxfmt, `git diff --check`, docs link audit (15,867 checked, zero broken), and madge (zero cycles) passed. Independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Per campaign local gate budget, the full `check:changed` SQLite inventory was omitted; PR CI owns broad proof.
- Live proof used an isolated HOME and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` under this worktree's `.artifacts/`, with a lane-owned dev Gateway on a claimed free port. Synthetic source: **102 events / 104,863,570 decoded bytes**. `sessions.recover` succeeded in **8.48 s**; retry returned the same successor. Offline verification after Gateway exit confirmed all 102 events, the first user event, the final full payload, the archived source, and the successor link. Native `Worker.getHeapStatistics()` sampling recorded **244.3 MiB maximum worker heap** across Gateway workers (5,177 samples), below the SQLite worker's 512 MiB old-generation limit. Continuation was admitted; model inference was outside this transcript-copy proof. Closing immediately after that admission emitted drain/session-admission cleanup warnings; the process exited successfully and persisted recovery verified correctly.

Focused reproduction:

```sh
env HOME="$PWD/.artifacts/home" OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$PWD/.artifacts/state" OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/session-accessor.recovery.test.ts
```

Live fixture commands (synthetic fixture retained locally for handoff):

```sh
env HOME="$PWD/.artifacts/home" OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$PWD/.artifacts/live-state" node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .artifacts/live-proof.mts seed
env HOME="$PWD/.artifacts/home" OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$PWD/.artifacts/live-state" OPENCLAW_SKIP_BROWSER_CONTROL_SERVER=1 OPENCLAW_SKIP_CANVAS_HOST=1 OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1 OPENCLAW_SKIP_CRON=1 OPENCLAW_SKIP_PROVIDERS=1 OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BONJOUR=1 OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .artifacts/live-proof.mts gateway
env HOME="$PWD/.artifacts/home" OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$PWD/.artifacts/live-state" node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .artifacts/live-proof.mts verify
```

prs.title: perf(control-ui): add named cold-load delivery profiles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The earlier cold-load scenario holds the connect reply for 220 ms, hiding scheduling collisions when a signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link receives hello sooner.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Developers can select `--latency-profile live-fast` or reproduce the earlier scenario with `legacy-handshake`. Existing defaults remain unchanged; explicit timing flags retain precedence.

## Why This Change Was Made

The new profile uses timing-only observations from six signed-in reloads: a 439 ms navigation-relative challenge floor, 41 ms connect floor, and rounded first-reply medians for critical boot methods. The guide documents the values and limits. Observed RTT includes browser queueing and server work; replaying it as a floor is a conservative scheduling envelope, not an isolated network model. Socket-open timestamps were absent, so no socket-open delay was invented. It remains opt-in because it is not strictly more faithful across all milestones.

One resolver owns presets and overrides, replacing the inline override-parser loop. Summaries record the selected profile and effective values. The warm-reload probe now records challenge delivery separately from socket open and connect send.

## Evidence

Same production bundle, AWS `c7a.4xlarge`, 11 interleaved legacy/live pairs per route, plus three separate CPU+timeline traces per route. Warm HTTP cache and scoped persisted snapshots; fixed fixture clock; repo headless Chromium. The dashboard uses the existing MCP-app fixture. Median [Q1–Q3], ms from navigation:

| Route / metric | Legacy handshake | Live-fast |
|---|---:|---:|
| Chat hello marker | 590.1 [589.8–594.7] | 591.9 [587.4–595.3] |
| Chat row paint | 980 [972–984] | 1,048 [908–1,058] |
| Chat final rows | 1,012.6 [1,010.1–1,017.0] | 1,334.8 [1,273.5–1,386.3] |
| Dashboard hello marker | 790.1 [781–805.4] | 691.8 [681.6–704.9] |
| Dashboard row paint | 656 [650–670] | 664 [662–664] |
| Dashboard final rows | 1,176.7 [1,163–1,186.8] | 1,324.4 [1,297.1–1,365.8] |

These are delivery-workload effects, **not product before/after wins**. Dashboard hello is earlier in 11/11 pairs (paired median −101.1 ms); final rows are later in 11/11 on both routes (+317.0/+150.3 ms). Chat LoAF overlaps with mixed pair signs (221 → 236 ms; paired median −1); dashboard LoAF rises with separated IQRs (243 [236.5–252.5] → 262 [255–270.5]).

A configured 41 ms connect floor still yields 114.7 ms observed chat RTT: all three diagnostic chat mounts overlap the nominal fast reply. Two dashboard traces put connect plus mount/rows in 277–279 ms tasks. The hello microtask marker precedes the end of those tasks, so future scheduling experiments should gate task end as well as hello, row paint and final readiness. No new product scheduling change is proposed here.

Lease `cbx_e2a2d793bb57` was released; independent inspection confirms `released`, no host. Admission/check run: https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_c4e2b4cc2da42ed6b14c6b5cbf113724 (initial broad gate failed; collection continued on the same lease through its generated SSH route).

Validation: focused resolver tests **2 passed**, `pnpm test test/scripts/control-ui-bench-latency.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (AWS runner wall 4.35 s, Vitest 190 ms; local 1.77 s). Remote script/test typechecks, lint, formatting and erasability pass. Autoreview is clean through P2.

**Inherited failures remain; CI is not green.** Exact-head [CI run 40053865860](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40053865860), head `f9a472f68613`, fails four `sidebar-complete-roster.e2e.test.ts` cases at line 105 waiting for the child-session toggle. The same file against the verified pinned-main tree (`7b71c2379764`) fails the same four cases at the same line/selector (runner wall 85.29 s). All other jobs in that CI run pass or skip. The remote changed-file gate separately reports the same 31 dead-export findings on head and pinned main, with no head-only finding. No CI rerun or unrelated repair was used to chase green.

Product/runtime LOC delta **0**. The requested exclusion-command delta is **+141/−27 = +114 tooling/docs** (+71 TypeScript, +43 guide); tests +36. Growth implements the requested named-profile contract and timing observations; the superseded inline parser is removed. No product config, schema, storage or cache changes. No visual UI change; no screenshots required. Release-note context: add opt-in cold-load delivery scenarios and challenge diagnostics for performance investigations.

Ready for maintainer review; **leave unmerged**.
