prs.title: chore: trim redundant Control UI browser coverage
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

UI CI spends browser time repeating presentation-only assertions and Cartesian theme variants that do not protect additional behavior.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Remove 42 E2E invocations from automatic UI runs while retaining every real-Gateway persistence, reconnect, RPC/auth, ordering, and documented regression contract audited in this lane.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Session-entry geometry: 48 → 24 cases. Keep every entry path × history size × viewport × motion preference; sample both themes across history sizes instead of crossing theme with every row. The first-paint regression from #150516 stays protected.
- Pending session creation: 16 → 8 cases. Keep every content type × viewport × motion preference; sample dark Markdown and light JSON. Rejection, draft/attachment restoration, retry, and held chat-module/thinking rollback proof remain.
- Publication availability: move eight display-only rows into the existing mounted Environment component suite, using the real publication owner. Keep the changed-account browser case because it refreshes through RPC. Availability copy, native-publisher enablement, absent account chooser, and no accidental writes remain asserted.
- Delete the sole-personal publication E2E duplicate. `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-github-publication.test.ts` → `keeps a sole personal account unselected until its labeled publish button is clicked` already mounts the real action and owner and asserts the exact selected identity.
- Delete the test-only installation-gate self-test and its unused expected-request parameter. Actual service-worker activation, reconnect, draft preservation, and terminal restoration remain in the same E2E suite.

The census covered all 51 files in the real-Gateway inventory and the 15 slowest historical mocked files, plus five additional files from fresh CI's top 15. No real-Gateway case qualifies for deletion or new release-only demotion. Existing release-only selection already contains long compositions. No new shards, ignores, production seams, or production changes.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Passed |
| Mounted publication component suite | 32 passed; 8.52 s command wall time (5.74 s Vitest) |
| Changed-file format | Passed |
| Changed-file lint | Passed after renaming one shadowed test variable |
| Production Knip + export/file scans | All findings match scheduled main exactly: 15 production exports/types, 14 full-tree files, 44 detailed export entries. Production unused-file scan: zero. |
| Independent preservation review | Clean through P2; all selected changes assessed |
| Full UI PR CI | [40053007339](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40053007339): success, all 14 UI jobs green, maximum 660 s |

No local E2E/build: this is test-only and keeps runtime/startup bytes unchanged. Browser proof runs in PR CI under the migration compute budget. Touched test/support LOC: 2,693 → 2,702; production LOC: 0 changed. The nine-line growth moves eight browser cases into the existing component harness; total test count falls by 34.

### CI wall-time baseline

The order's successful [run 39982924090](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39982924090) is retained for context. Fresh [scheduled main 40047705637](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40047705637), at `d955b40e46e0b3650d84ec6d52c89f6beb24fc5a`, already reflects earlier speed work. prs.title: fix(ios): restore the last chat, send voice to the chat on screen, keep command drafts
prs.body: Related: #163153 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: on iOS, relaunching the app forgets the chat you were in; Talk, push-to-talk, Watch start and wake word can send to a different chat than the one on screen; child sessions are not nested under their parent in the sidebar; and a failed `/new`, `/reset` or `/compact` deletes the typed command. ## User Impact User impact: users reopen the app in the chat they left (per Gateway and agent), can rely on voice input going to the visible chat, see child sessions under their parents in the sidebar, and keep the typed command when a local command fails. ## Why This Change Was Made - **Last chat:** focus is saved per Gateway through the existing settings owner and restored before the first frame. Changing agent, or a roster refresh that removes the selected agent, clears both active and saved focus through the same selection transition, so a retired agent's chat cannot keep routing chat or Talk. Forgetting a Gateway erases its saved focus with the other per-Gateway preferences, so re-pairing the same Gateway does not reopen the forgotten chat. Reset Onboarding, which forgets every Gateway, erases their saved focus the same way. - **Talk routing:** Talk follows the presentation's current chat; callbacks from a replaced chat model are ignored; launch, enable, foreground, Watch start and wake word synchronize to the visible chat. - **Sidebar:** ancestry is resolved from child metadata before pin/group placement. - **Local commands:** `/new`, `/reset` and `/compact` report whether they ran. The draft is cleared only after the command ran, and only if it is still the draft that was submitted (same composer session, same revision, same text). `main` cleared it before running, so any failure lost the typed command. A stale compaction result is still dropped rather than applied to the chat the user moved to. ### Navigation parity Restore the saved chat on cold launch and prioritize child-side ancestry. This brings iOS into line with the Control UI, which [loads the saved Gateway-scoped chat](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e28a63d8b99e7fc11d6392d8fa3ae475584a5164/ui/src/app/settings.ts#L403-L422) and [uses it for initial navigation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e28a63d8b99e7fc11d6392d8fa3ae475584a5164/ui/src/app/bootstrap.ts#L238-L253). The macOS Dashboard uses the same Control UI with a [persistent per-profile WebKit data store](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e28a63d8b99e7fc11d6392d8fa3ae475584a5164/apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/DashboardBrowserSessionStore.swift#L113-L130). The web sidebar [places children under their parents](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e28a63d8b99e7fc11d6392d8fa3ae475584a5164/ui/src/components/app-sidebar-session-tree.ts#L100-L142) and [prioritizes child-side ancestry over parent-owned child lists](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e28a63d8b99e7fc11d6392d8fa3ae475584a5164/ui/src/components/app-sidebar-session-parent.ts#L18-L80); iOS should preserve that same placement when a parent roster no longer lists the child. ## Evidence ### Maintainer validation of the published candidate The startup approval repair keeps remembered chat focus separate from configured approval authority: a delivered Watch decision stays in durable custody until its actual Gateway route is configured. The sidebar conflict with main is resolved by retaining child depth and main's per-render selection/category inputs and alias caching. Published candidate: **a562c32100fde2a70e74aa58bcb6389bee48caa3**; effective source tree `60acc6d777af9e275e90c832f1ca993b4645006f`, composed with main `cb2dbda93738f84f6b25c974c6d0b2d50698b76b`. Focused local validation on that exact tree: - macOS shared sidebar/command checks: **69/69 top-level cases**, 123 parameter-expanded invocations; normal Mac OpenClaw product compile passed. - iOS simulator: **22/22 top-level cases**, 25 invocations, zero failures/skips; normal app/test build and strict formatting/lint phases passed. Both cached and uncached startup regression inputs executed. - Independent integration review and structured publication review completed; exact results retained in the local handoff. - The prior same-oracle startup red control, 56 focused passes on repair tree `1397bdf4efbd35fceb2b2131a9c5a3accc677a8b`, and supported uncached wire custody proof remain separately attributed and preserved. They are not relabeled as this integration run. Mac tests ran in an audited OS sandbox; no operator Gateway or physical phone was used. iOS results retain two AVAudioSession main-thread warnings. After successful test completion, Xcode's optional simulator diagnostic collector stalled; only that collector was stopped, partial diagnostics retained, and the xcresult finalized Passed with xcodebuild exit 0. No test rerun, relaxed assertion, or timeout extension was used. The following contributor evidence is historical and retained. Local checks do not replace required hosted checks on the published head or owner acceptance. **Do not merge yet; auto-merge remains off.** ### Earlier contributor evidence - Shared kit suite: 2337 tests in 196 suites passed. - The iOS app builds for the simulator, and the app suites this change touches passed there: 365 tests in 5 suites (`GatewayConnectionControllerTests`, `NodeAppModelInvokeTests`, `RootTabsSidebarRegressionTests`, `TalkVisibleSessionTests`, `ChatLaunchRestoreTests`). - Strict SwiftLint is clean on the changed source files. Red → green: - **Command finishing after a chat switch** (new here, measured on `main` `bbaabd6ced1`): `command finishing after a chat switch consumes the draft it was typed in` fails for all three commands on the first version of this change, where a successful command that finished after the reader switched chats reported "did not run" (the typed command stayed in the old chat's draft; 3 issues), and passes once the result means "the command ran". An independent review of the first carve found this; the same gap was in #163153 as filed. - **Failed commands:** `failed local command keeps its draft` (3 commands) and `failed reset fallback keeps new command draft` fail on `main` (4 issues, measured on `bbaabd6ced1` with only these tests added), which clears the draft before running the command, and pass with the change. - **Talk routing:** 7 functions / 9 cases; 6 failed on the original pre-fix baseline (retired model refocused Talk onto a cron chat; cold launch, Watch start and wake word used stale keys). Measured for #163153. - **Roster removal:** `roster removal of the selected agent forgets its saved chat` fails without the fix (focus, saved focus and relaunch selection all keep `alpha`) and passes with it. Measured for #163153. - **Reset Onboarding:** `onboarding reset forgets saved chat focus for every paired gateway` fails without the fix (the saved chat survives the reset and reconnecting either Gateway reopens it; 4 issues) and passes with it. - **Forget Gateway:** `forget gateway erases only its saved chat focus` fails without the fix and passes with it; another Gateway's saved focus is kept. Measured for #163153. - **Agent switch:** `agent switch forgets the previous agent's saved chat` fails without the fix (2 expectation failures) and passes with it. Measured for #163153. - **Sidebar nesting:** six failing assertions on the original pre-fix baseline, plus a pinned-tree depth check. Measured for #163153. ### Cold launch against a real Gateway (simulator) The app, signed in to a scratch Gateway that holds synthetic chats, opens a non-main chat, is terminated, and is launched again as a new process. Nothing is mocked and no preference is seeded; the same UI test drives `main` `b1f3eac43cf` and this change. | | Before terminate | After relaunch | First `chat.history` request after relaunch | |---|---|---|---| | `main` | | | `agent:main:main` | | This change | | | `agent:main:dashboard:traffic-amber` | The request lines were recorded at the Gateway: [cold-history-requests.jsonl](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/fd4cd088fe742ea46d117635c9e3b96da87adf11/ios-sessions/cold-launch/cold-history-requests.jsonl). ### Upgrade from the latest stable build (simulator) The latest stable release (v2026.10.1) is installed and paired with a scratch Gateway; the agent picker selects a second agent ("Proof Worker") and a saved chat is opened. The app is then replaced in place by a newer build, with no uninstall, erase, re-pairing or seeded preference, and launched. | Installed over stable | Gateway connects without re-pairing | Selected agent after launch | Saved chat | |---|---|---|---| | Stable again (relaunch) | yes | Proof Worker | listed, opens with its history | | `main` `b1f3eac43cf` | yes | Proof Worker | listed, opens with its history | | This change | yes | Proof Worker | listed, opens with its history | Stable, `main` and this change read the selected agent from the same key in the same defaults suite (`gateway.selectedAgentId.v2.`), and the saved chat focus this change adds is a new key beside it. | Stable, before | Stable relaunched | `main` over stable | This change over stable | Saved chat opened after the upgrade | |---|---|---|---|---| | | | | | | Gateway-side request lines for each case (connect, session list, history of the saved chat): [native-request-receipts.jsonl](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/1485a517841de5cea29c76b45d318d342b657da4/ios-sessions/upgrade/native-request-receipts.jsonl). Test results: [native-test-results.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/1485a517841de5cea29c76b45d318d342b657da4/ios-sessions/upgrade/native-test-results.txt). ### Talk into a non-main chat after a relaunch (physical iPhone, real Gateway) On an iPhone running a build that carries these changes, a new chat (`agent:main:ios-01b3f936-…`, not the main chat) is opened and the app is force-quit. The recording starts on the phone's Home Screen (its upper half is blurred): the app is opened and comes back in that chat while it is still connecting to the Gateway, Talk is started, and the spoken request and the spoken reply appear in the chat on screen. The Gateway stores both in that chat's transcript. | Relaunch: the chat is back before the Gateway connects | Talk listening in the chat | The spoken turn in the same chat | |---|---|---| | | | | Recording, Home Screen to spoken turn (video only): [voice-relaunch-visible-chat.mp4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/0641f6f9200869b295200ddf89188c3e99b7d848/ios-sessions/voice/voice-relaunch-visible-chat.mp4). The composer placeholder names the agent (`main` until the roster loads), not the chat. - Gateway log lines: the app's connections close at 02:07:16Z and a new one opens at 02:07:19Z; `talk.session.create` follows on that connection at 02:07:24Z, and Talk session `092ede0b-…` completes its first turn at 02:07:35Z. [voice-gateway-receipts.jsonl](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/0641f6f9200869b295200ddf89188c3e99b7d848/ios-sessions/voice/voice-gateway-receipts.jsonl) - The chat's transcript as stored by the Gateway: rows 3 and 4 are the spoken request and reply, with `provenance.kind` `realtime_voice` and the ID of that Talk session. [voice-transcript-rows.jsonl](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/0641f6f9200869b295200ddf89188c3e99b7d848/ios-sessions/voice/voice-transcript-rows.jsonl) ### Sidebar nesting and a failed command (simulator, synthetic fixture that is not part of this PR) Three simulator UI tests on a synthetic chat were run on `main` `c1b9f4ec91e` and on this change (fresh simulator each time, `OpenClawUITests` scheme). The fixtures and tests are local-only evidence code, not in this PR: a parent chat with a child and a grandchild reported child-side, and a fixture whose `/compact` and `/reset` fail. | Test | `main` | this change | |---|---|---| | Sidebar shows the child under its parent and the grandchild under the child | fails (`CHILD_NOT_NESTED`: the child sits at the parent's indent, so the rows are a flat list) | passes | | A failed `/compact` keeps the typed command | fails (`DRAFT_LOST_AFTER_FAILED_COMMAND`: the composer is empty after the error) | passes | | A successful `/compact` clears the draft | passes | passes (consumption is unchanged) | | Sidebar on `main` | Sidebar with this change | |---|---| | | | | Failed `/compact` on `main` | Failed `/compact` with this change | |---|---| | | | The "before" command screenshot also shows a simulator system banner ("Ready for Apple Intelligence") that has nothing to do with the app. Physical iPhone (builds carrying these changes together with the rest of #163153): last-chat restoration was accepted on device. AI-assisted (Claude).

prs.title: fix(telegram): preserve business identity in lanes and pairing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram Business updates need to stay business-scoped all the way through lane selection and pairing/access decisions. Without that boundary, Business traffic can collapse into plain chat-id lanes or lose its `business_connection_id` before downstream handling can make a safe distinction between ordinary bot DMs and secretary-mode messages.

## Summary

This is the focused business-identity slice from the Telegram Business Connect review work around #114087 / #20786.

It fixes two business-mode routing boundaries:

- business updates now use business-scoped sequential lanes instead of collapsing into plain chat-id lanes
- pairing/access decisions preserve `business_connection_id` when a Telegram Business message enters the DM access path

## Evidence

Tested locally after rebasing on current `openclaw/openclaw:main`:

- `pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/dm-access.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/sequential-key.test.ts` -> 2 files, 71 tests passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` -> passed
- `git diff --check origin/main..HEAD` -> clean

prs.title: fix: settle interrupted subagent completions after cleanup
prs.body:
Closes #182062. Related: #142224, #182046, and #181184.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a completed requester turn leaving its interrupted child's durable wake dispatching after legitimate cleanup retires the child's transient recovery marker.

## User Impact

The same interrupted task can finish completion bookkeeping after cleanup, including when a follow-up already owns the child session. Changed runtime, task, requester, child incarnation, kill state, or terminal result still refuses settlement.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/agents/subagents/completion/subagent-completion-admission.store.ts:280` on the inspected main rejected any `terminalOwner` change. `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-lifecycle-bookkeeping.ts:166` legitimately clears `interrupted-recovery` after recording cleanup and the sticky session-effects fence. A retained requester completion therefore lost settlement solely because cleanup succeeded.

The existing admission owner now recognizes that one-way transition only with the cleanup receipt, sticky fence, and identical interrupted terminal timing/outcome. It retains the surrounding owner and requester checks, then commits through the existing registry/SQLite path. Late provider and yield results remain fenced.

Team relevance is bounded: the sanitized journal correlation in merged #181184 records a recovered parent/requester-settle session `fa35e3ac`, a later yield-cleanup timeout at boot-log line 3744, stale reports at 4113/4265, and six queued-without-run reports at 4542/4635/4928/5435/6569/8395. Those logs establish a related cleanup wedge, but do not identify its retained barrier or prove this exact marker mismatch. This PR fixes the independently reproduced settlement defect; it does not claim to repair every Team cleanup timeout.

## Evidence

Maintainer validation uses main `7b71c23797646bed71dc869b83a1c51764c267a6` merged into the original contributor commit, without rebasing or changing the two-file patch.

- Red on main: with unchanged main production code and the regression test overlaid, the same-terminal case fails at `currentCompletionOwner` with `Subagent completion owner changed before mutation`; all 13 changed-state controls pass. The real cleanup controller creates the cleanup state, and the test reopens SQLite to verify durable settlement or unchanged rejected rows. Baseline: 1 failed / 13 passed, 167.82 seconds wall time (158.46 seconds reported by Vitest, dominated by compilation).
- Fixed head `426650184280128f24b5ae72558cc137804c85cc`: all 67 completion/storage cases passed (51 requester-wake, 16 storage/admission), followed by all 3 late-provider/yield controls. The two-file run took 362.21 seconds including cold worker compilation; the changed file reported 59.09 seconds, of which 57% was test execution. The three filtered lifecycle controls took 97.61 seconds including cache validation; skipped cases are not claimed as executed.
- Core production types passed; changed-test types passed (`agents-sessions`, 6.9 seconds). Focused typed lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Codex autoreview: `scoped-clean`, no actionable P0–P2 findings on the committed branch. The review covers the patch; executed behavior is established separately above.
- Exact-head CI watcher: **GREEN** for `426650184280128f24b5ae72558cc137804c85cc`, [run 40053463881](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40053463881). Ten superseded same-lane checks are excluded by the native policy. No rerun or inherited-failure exception was needed.

Production delta: +31/-2 lines (net +29). Tests: +119/-0. The added code is the narrow predicate needed to distinguish legitimate marker retirement from a different terminal winner; no new owner, retry loop, schema, config, or authority is introduced. Thanks @ericcaiwx-star; the contributor's commit and patch are preserved.

Accepted limits: this is completion bookkeeping, not requester-source admission (#182046) or pending-parent continuation source recovery (#182043). No live Team/Gateway or real channel was touched. The contributor reported separate combined-patch synthetic Gateway proof, but maintainer acceptance here rests on the executed owner/SQLite regression and final-head CI; it makes no standalone live-provider or business-side-effect claim.

<details>
<summary>Focused validation commands</summary>

```sh
pnpm test src/agents/subagents/completion/subagent-completion-admission.requester-wake.test.ts src/agents/subagents/completion/subagent-completion-admission.store.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm test src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'keeps a cleaned legacy recovery winner|persists interrupted recovery before task projection'
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --changed-paths-json '["src/agents/subagents/completion/subagent-completion-admission.requester-wake.test.ts"]' --concurrency 1
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/agents/subagents/completion/subagent-completion-admission.store.ts src/agents/subagents/completion/subagent-completion-admission.requester-wake.test.ts
pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/agents/subagents/completion/subagent-completion-admission.store.ts src/agents/subagents/completion/subagent-completion-admission.requester-wake.test.ts
```

Node 26.12.1; repository-selected Bun test runtime. The baseline uses the first test file with `-t 'settles a cleaned interrupted winner'` against the unmodified main owner. Skipped cases from filtered runs are not counted as executed.

</details>

prs.title: feat(telegram): support copy-text presentation buttons
prs.body:
## Merge Brief

- **Problem:** plugins cannot express a portable copy-to-clipboard control through message presentation.
- **Demand:** continues the missing capability first explored in #36105; current `main` still has no equivalent portable action or Telegram encoder.
- **Value:** Telegram gets a native `CopyTextButton`; channels without native support keep a safe, readable manual-copy fallback.
- **Smallest complete fix:** add one capability-gated shared action, Telegram encoding, and fallback behavior at every affected channel boundary.
- **Scope:** presentation payloads, shared limits, Telegram, and existing Discord/Slack/Feishu fallback owners; no raw Telegram button input.
- **Risk:** public additive SDK surface and message-delivery behavior; exact-value privacy, select budgets, mentions, locations, and edits are regression-covered.
- **Proof:** exact-head focused suites pass **127/127**; core and extension production/test typechecks, changed-file format/lint, assertion ratchet, and merge simulation pass.
- **Gap:** native Telegram Test Server send → tap → clipboard proof remains externally blocked on authenticated broker access.
- **Non-goals:** no callback reinterpretation, provider-keyboard takeover, Gateway/config change, or production activation.
- **Maintainer ask:** accept the additive portable `copy-text` contract and review the repaired exact head.

## What Problem This Solves

Add a portable typed `copy-text` presentation action. Telegram renders it as a
native Bot API `CopyTextButton`; channels without native support keep a readable,
safe manual-copy fallback.

This updates the existing contribution first explored in #36105. It does not
reintroduce the retired raw Telegram button input.

## Current maintenance head

- **Exact head:** `d3c9ca87eb7ce42243ff9f65796f474f8e8c6007`
- **Frozen base:** `cd57bc91d991ba1350009e935caaf21e70c09c89`
- **Shape:** one signed semantic commit, 45 files, +2,636/-343.
- **Merge simulation:** clean against the frozen base.

The frozen base has no equivalent portable `copy-text` presentation action or
Telegram `copy_text` encoder. Existing inline-code tap-to-copy behavior is a
separate rendering path and does not expose this capability to plugins.

## Behavior

- The message tool schema exposes a typed `copy-text` action with a required
  string value.
- The shared presentation adapter preserves the action only when a channel
  declares `copyTextButtons`; unsupported channels render readable manual-copy
  fallback while callback payload values remain private.
- Telegram emits `InlineKeyboardButton.copy_text` only for values satisfying
  the Bot API's 1–256-character contract. Values that cannot be encoded safely
  remain visible as escaped fallback instead of being silently rewritten.
- Native controls share Telegram's existing 100-action budget, including every
  option in a select that Telegram renders as an individual button. Every
  native select row is reserved before Discord-sized button selection.
- Direct Telegram sends retain authored select prompts while excluding native
  copy values from visible text.
- Standalone location sends never receive a synthetic text anchor.
- Provider-owned and usable legacy keyboards retain precedence; unusable legacy
  controls do not falsely displace a valid presentation keyboard.
- Drop-time copy identity keeps duplicate labels paired with the correct value
  when an action falls back after planning.
- Markup-only edits do not synthesize replacement body text. If a rejected,
  over-budget, or shadowed copy control needs readable fallback, the action
  returns a recoverable result requiring explicit content or caption.
- Discord long-copy fallback uses a complete collision-safe fence in every
  independently rendered fragment. Mention suppression derives from the exact
  rendered fallback text, including enabled and disabled labels.

## Evidence

Exact-head focused behavior suites pass **127/127** across the 14 changed test
files:

- shared payload, message-tool visibility, and presentation limits: **13**
- Discord delivery/fallback/mention boundaries: **93**
- Telegram native/fallback/direct-action paths: **19**
- Slack fallback: **1**
- Feishu fallback: **1**

The PR-wrapper runtime-closure suite also passes **19/19** after adding the new
payload fallback helper to the wrapper's explicit trusted inventory. This
repairs the only branch-owned failure found by the first hosted run.

Exact-head static gates:

- core production typecheck: pass
- core test typecheck shards: pass
- extension production typecheck: pass
- extension test typecheck: pass
- changed core/extension/script lint: pass
- changed-file Oxfmt and `git diff --check`: pass
- assertion-safety ratchet: pass; the branch shrinks the
  `outbound-components.ts` baseline from two assertions to one
- merge tree against the frozen base: clean

The canonical changed-check also reports two full-tree failures already present
unchanged in the frozen base: three pre-existing UI `max-lines` suppressions are
absent from their baseline, and the database-first guard flags two pre-existing
retired-runtime migration files. This PR does not touch those files. Hosted PR
CI is the authoritative broad gate for the published head.

The isolated worktree was hydrated with the frozen lockfile to run the pinned
toolchain. No lockfile or dependency declaration changed; no Gateway, runtime
configuration, credential, or production state was touched.

## Live proof state

No exact-head live Telegram send/tap/clipboard claim is made. Historical branch
proof is not used as a substitute for current-head evidence. Remaining live
proof requires an authenticated Telegram Test Server/broker route to send the
native button, tap it in a Telegram client, verify exact clipboard bytes, and
exercise invalid-value/edit fallback. That route is currently unavailable to
the contributor environment.

## Maintainer decision

This intentionally keeps `copy-text` as a portable, capability-gated
presentation action rather than a Telegram-local input. Maintainer acceptance
of that public SDK surface remains the upstream product gate.

AI-assisted implementation and tests.

prs.title: feat(tasks): follow background task progress from the CLI
prs.body:
Closes #123488

## What Problem This Solves

Operators can inspect durable background tasks from the CLI, but they cannot stay attached to one task without repeatedly polling `tasks show`. Gateway logs are too broad for this job, and the Control UI does not cover every remote, headless, or shell-first workflow. As a result, operators can miss progress transitions and may not know whether execution finished while completion delivery is still pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds `openclaw tasks follow <lookup>` with human-readable and JSON Lines output. The viewer reuses the `tasks show` lookup contract, connects with `operator.read`, projects existing bounded task summaries and visible session history, filters the existing task event stream to one task, and replays durable state after event gaps or Gateway reconnects. Stable record identifiers suppress replay duplicates, execution and delivery remain separate, and Ctrl-C closes only the viewer.

The change is read-only. It adds no task or session persistence, protocol schema, cancellation, notification, delivery, or restart-recovery owner.

## User Impact

Operators can follow one subagent, ACP, cron, or CLI task from a terminal until both execution and completion delivery reach a terminal state. `--json` supports line-oriented consumers with bounded, redacted records and duplicate-safe identifiers. Existing `tasks show`, Control UI, task execution, and delivery behavior remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `e5c7ebd3143c014fdb0412043c71b10bf66737f5`, based on `6bd21a11222af41e7c758739c0e0cd2994dee445`.
- Focused CLI, command, and Gateway callsite-guard tests: 44/44 passed, covering human output, JSONL, bounded and redacted visible history, hidden reasoning and tool-result exclusion, `operator.read`, ordered updates, event gaps, duplicate suppression, reconnect, separate execution and delivery terminal behavior, Ctrl-C viewer-only behavior, lookup failure, and the production `GatewayClient` allowlist.
- `pnpm check:changed` passed all selected core, core-test, and docs lanes. Crabbox 0.41.6 matched the current stable release but had no ready remote provider, so the repository used its documented local fallback.
- `pnpm build` passed through the rebased CLI invocation, including CLI bootstrap imports, runtime post-build module loading, bundled plugin assets, and the Control UI build.
- Built CLI help exposes `openclaw tasks follow [options] <lookup>` and `--json` as JSON Lines.
- AutoReview loop 3 reviewed the exact rebased 37,028-byte bundle with `gpt-5.6-luna` at maximum thinking. TruffleHog passed and the review reported no accepted or actionable findings.
- The original `check-lint` failure had no lint finding. Every core shard completed, then the GitHub-hosted runner received a shutdown signal while linting extensions and exited 143. The new head retriggers that infrastructure-cancelled job.

### Live Gateway transcript

This proof used a loopback-only development Gateway and a dedicated temporary state root. It did not read or operate the normal Gateway. The controlled task had finished execution while delivery was still queued, so the viewer stayed attached. I stopped the isolated Gateway, completed delivery in the same SQLite-owned task row while it was down, and restarted it. The existing viewer emitted one disconnect marker, reconnected, replayed the durable terminal state, and exited 0. The task identifier below is redacted; the event order, timestamps, state, and exit status are unchanged.

```console
$ openclaw tasks follow proof-task --json

{"id":"connection.reconnected:861f5a0dd801ecd00d09","cursor":"connection.reconnected:861f5a0dd801ecd00d09","timestamp":"2026-08-14T05:44:24.517Z","taskId":"proof-task","runtime":"cli","kind":"connection.reconnected","state":{"message":"Gateway reconnected; replaying durable task state"}}

prs.title: fix(minimax): match CN host on a dot boundary for region detection
prs.body:
## Summary

fix(minimax): bind CN region detection to the `minimaxi.com` host on a dot boundary, so look-alike hosts such as `notminimaxi.com` no longer route web search to the CN endpoint

## What Problem This Solves

The MiniMax web search provider infers the region (`cn` vs `global`) from `MINIMAX_API_HOST` or the configured provider base URL, and picks the search endpoint accordingly (`https://api.minimaxi.com/v1/coding_plan/search` for CN, `https://api.minimax.io/v1/coding_plan/search` for global).

**代码证据**: in `extensions/minimax/src/minimax-web-search-provider.runtime.ts`, `isMiniMaxCnHost` used:

- `new URL(trimmed).hostname.endsWith("minimaxi.com")` — matches any host that merely *ends* with the string, e.g. `notminimaxi.com` or `evilnotminimaxi.com`.
- `trimmed.includes("minimaxi.com")` as the fallback for scheme-less values — a pure substring check that also matches look-alike hosts.

So a misspelled or maliciously crafted host like `MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://notminimaxi.com` was classified as CN, and search traffic (including the query and the `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header) would be sent to the CN search endpoint derived from that wrong classification.

Trigger condition: any host value that ends with the literal string `minimaxi.com` without being `minimaxi.com` or a subdomain of it.

## Root Cause

- Violated invariant: region inference is a security-relevant routing decision (it selects which endpoint receives queries and credentials), but the host check was a suffix/substring match instead of a dot-boundary host match.
- `endsWith("minimaxi.com")` has no label boundary: `notminimaxi.com`.endsWith(`minimaxi.com`) is `true`. The scheme-less fallback `includes(...)` is weaker still.

## Why This Fix

- Option A: keep `endsWith` but prepend a dot (`endsWith(".minimaxi.com")`). Handles the URL-parseable path but leaves the scheme-less substring fallback untouched.
- Option B (chosen): extract a single `isCnHostname` predicate — `hostname === "minimaxi.com" || hostname.endsWith(".minimaxi.com")` — and use it for both paths; for scheme-less values, prepend `https://` so only the host is inspected (never the path or query), and return `false` if the value still cannot be parsed.
- Not chosen: a regex over the raw string — duplicates URL parsing logic and still mixes host and non-host content.

## User Impact

- Affected scenarios: users setting `MINIMAX_API_HOST` or a provider `baseUrl` to a host that shares the `minimaxi.com` suffix (typo'd or look-alike domains).
- Before: such hosts were classified as CN and search requests were routed to the CN endpoint.
- After: only `minimaxi.com` and its subdomains classify as CN; everything else falls back to global.
- Behavior change: legitimate CN endpoints (`https://api.minimaxi.com`, `https://minimaxi.com`, `https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic`) are unaffected — still classified as CN.

## Real Behavior Proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** look-alike hosts sharing the `minimaxi.com` suffix were classified as CN, routing MiniMax web search to the wrong (CN) endpoint.
- **Real environment tested:** worktree `wt-minimax-cn-host-boundary` on latest `origin/main`, Node v24.19.0, importing the real `extensions/minimax/src/minimax-web-search-provider.runtime.ts` via tsx and calling the exported `testing.resolveMiniMaxRegion` / `testing.resolveMiniMaxEndpoint` with `MINIMAX_API_HOST` set per case. No mocks of the functions under test.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  $ node node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs minimax-cn-host-boundary.proof.mjs
  $ npx vitest run extensions/minimax/src/minimax-web-search-provider.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix (8/8 PASS):**
  ```bash
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://api.minimaxi.com -> region=cn
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic -> region=cn
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://minimaxi.com -> region=cn
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://api.minimax.io -> region=global
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://notminimaxi.com -> region=global
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://evilnotminimaxi.com/v1 -> region=global
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=notminimaxi.com -> region=global
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://example.com/redir?u=minimaxi.com -> region=global
  RESULT: ALL PASS
  ```

**Before (on main, same script, exit code 1):**

```bash
FAIL MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://notminimaxi.com -> region=cn (expected global), endpoint=https://api.minimaxi.com/v1/coding_plan/search
FAIL MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://evilnotminimaxi.com/v1 -> region=cn (expected global)
FAIL MINIMAX_API_HOST=notminimaxi.com -> region=cn (expected global)
RESULT: 3 case(s) show WRONG region/endpoint
```

- **What was not tested:** a live search request against the real MiniMax endpoints (requires valid credentials); the proof exercises the real region/endpoint resolution code paths end to end.

## Tests and Validation

- `npx vitest run extensions/minimax/src/minimax-web-search-provider.test.ts` — 23/23 passed, including new regression cases: apex CN domain still classifies as CN; `https://notminimaxi.com`, `https://evilnotminimaxi.com/v1`, scheme-less `notminimaxi.com`, `https://minimaxi.com.evil.com`, and a query-string-only mention all classify as global.
- `npx oxlint --deny=warn` on both changed files — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Before/after real-behavior proof logs are embedded above.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: unit tests on the real exported `resolveMiniMaxRegion` / `resolveMiniMaxEndpoint` (via the module's `testing` surface), with `MINIMAX_API_HOST` as the input vector.
- Target test file: `extensions/minimax/src/minimax-web-search-provider.test.ts`
- Scenario locked in: suffix-sharing look-alike hosts (`notminimaxi.com`, with scheme, with path, scheme-less) and non-host mentions (query string) never classify as CN, while the real CN hosts (`api.minimaxi.com`, apex `minimaxi.com`) still do.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: it pins the exact predicate that makes the routing decision, using the exact inputs that previously misclassified.

prs.title: fix(cron): warn when an explicit allowlist suppresses configured MCP tools
prs.body:
Related: #120385

## What Problem This Solves

A cron automation with a finite explicit `toolsAllow` can silently prevent configured MCP tools from materializing. The job runs, the MCP runtime never starts, and nothing tells the operator why their MCP tools are missing. This is the policy foot-gun behind the "Unknown tool id" class of cron failures.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cron preflight now records a warning when a non-empty explicit finite allowlist omits every configured MCP selector, naming the concrete remedies (`bundle-mcp`, `group:plugins`, an exact `<server>__<tool>` selector, or `*`).

Established semantics are deliberately preserved: intentional deny-all `[]`, omitted policy, wildcard, plugin-group, and MCP selectors all behave exactly as before and produce no warning.

**Compatibility fix:** `resolveCodexMcpToolOverridesForAgent` is now applied only when `agentRuntime === "codex"`. It was previously applied to every cron run, which let Codex-specific MCP filtering distort static server resolution for non-Codex runtimes. Non-Codex coverage is included.

Preflight diagnostics are now accumulated and merged rather than early-returned, so an allowlist warning and a `web_search` provider warning can both surface from a single run instead of the first one silently masking the second.

This PR is AI-assisted. I reviewed the implementation and validation results and understand the shipped behavior.

## User Impact

Operators get a durable, actionable warning in cron run history when their explicit allowlist is the reason configured MCP tools are absent, instead of silently missing tools. Non-Codex cron runs no longer inherit Codex-specific MCP filtering.

## Scope Note

This is the second half of a deliberate split of #121488. This PR carries the `merge-risk: compatibility` surface; the cron run-history diagnostic ships separately.

## Evidence

### Exact head and current-main integration

- Branch parent: `2753351abe63260f9f4a3381754c63fb5ed93b7d`
- Exact head: `a60f73872c59634e54ca6e5f6d2283cee97b80b0`

### Credential-free hosted real-Gateway proof

[Exact-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/32464597590) completed successfully on `a60f73872c59634e54ca6e5f6d2283cee97b80b0`: 184 jobs passed, 14 intentionally skipped, and none failed. Across all exact-head checks, 209 passed and 38 were skipped with no pending or failing checks.

The hosted [`docker-seed-e2e` job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/32464597590/job/96718568074) selected only `cron-mcp-cleanup` and passed the credential-free real-Gateway lane. It uses the existing Docker E2E stack, a local stdio static MCP probe, and the repository's mock OpenAI-compatible provider; no private credentials are involved. The exact-head client hard-fails unless all of these boundaries hold:

1. **Finite core-only cap:** `toolsAllow: ["read"]` completes with persisted history status `ok`, exposes no MCP namespace or MCP tool, starts no MCP probe, and persists the actionable suppression warning.
2. **Matching exact selector:** `toolsAllow: ["cronCleanupProbe__cleanup_probe"]` exposes and successfully calls only `cronCleanupProbe__cleanup_probe`; `secondary_probe` remains absent, no warning is persisted, and the spawned MCP process exits.
3. **Non-Codex scoped-server control:** an OpenClaw-runtime cron with `toolsAllow: ["bundle-mcp"]` sees and successfully calls both static tools even though the server has `codex.agents: ["research"]`; no false warning is persisted and the MCP process exits.
4. **Cleanup boundary:** the follow-on subagent cleanup control verifies that every observed MCP probe process exits.

There is no permissive fallback and no test-only production seam. The already-merged memory-flush schema subproblem is untouched.

prs.title: feat(workboard): receipt-backed closeout tracking
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds an optional, receipt-backed Workboard closeout flow on current `main`.

- records one durable closeout generation before sending
- sends through the existing authenticated `conversations.send` Gateway operation
- confirms only from a platform-backed message receipt or an authenticated operator-admin confirmation
- classifies definitive pre-I/O Gateway rejection separately from ambiguous delivery
- prevents blind resend and blocks completion without evidence
- keeps persisted tracker state JSON-safe and bounded

This is the narrow mainline successor to #120537. It intentionally excludes the release-branch session-reset, command-queue, ended-run, and design-document changes from that branch.

## What Problem This Solves

An agent can currently report an external closeout as sent without retaining enough transport evidence to distinguish a platform receipt from a locally prepared identifier. If a send result is interrupted or ambiguous, blindly retrying can duplicate the external message; treating the ambiguous result as success can falsely complete the work. This change records the closeout before I/O, reuses a durable Gateway operation per stored generation, and permits completion only after platform-backed or authenticated operator evidence.

## Evidence

- **147 focused tests passed** across the Workboard tracker/adapters, Gateway send projection, plugin-origin propagation, agent tool output, protocol schema, boundary guards, and the exact-head in-process path.
- The exact-head test executes Workboard → plugin runtime → in-process Gateway → authenticated `conversations.send`, and proves a `platform` receipt confirms while a `prepared` identifier remains uncertain.
- Full build, core/extension/root typechecks, targeted lint/format checks, protocol checks, Plugin SDK API baseline check, and package-boundary checks passed.
- The in-process proof replaces the final transport owner with a deterministic test seam; it does not send a live message.

## Architecture

- **Gateway owns transport facts:** `conversations.send` returns the platform message identifier separately from queue/fallback identifiers.
- **Workboard owns closeout policy:** the tracker persists state transitions and only allows completion from `confirmed` or `manually_confirmed`.
- **Plugin runtime owns trust propagation:** bundled plugin origin is preserved across tool factory and callback scopes so the Workboard adapter can request the required operator-admin Gateway scope.
- **Operator confirmation is authenticated:** user identity is preferred; paired clients are attributed by `client.connect.device.id`, not by shared client type.

## Exact-head boundary proof

`test/workboard-closeout-in-process.test.ts` executes the bundled Workboard adapter through the Workboard public runtime barrel:

`createRuntimeConversationSend` → plugin runtime Gateway request → trusted bundled-plugin scope → real in-process Gateway router → authenticated `conversations.send` handler.

The transport owner is replaced with a deterministic test seam, so this proves the exact current-head boundary without sending a live recipient message. The test verifies the receipt-bearing result and the owner-authorized Gateway invocation.

## Verification

- focused tests: **147/147 passed**
  - Workboard tracker and adapters
  - Gateway conversation send and exact-head in-process path
  - plugin tool origin scope
  - agent conversation tool output
  - protocol schema and plugin/core boundary guards
- `pnpm tsgo:core`
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`
- targeted oxlint: 0 warnings/errors
- targeted oxfmt: clean
- plugin/extension boundary checks: clean
- Swift protocol generation check: clean
- protocol event coverage and registry checks: clean
- Plugin SDK API baseline regenerated and verified
- full `pnpm build`: passed
- local `check:changed`: all reached feature gates passed; the remaining full-tree dead-export scan reports two pre-existing current-main exports from #121005
- `git diff --check`: clean
- added-line secret/injection/private-identifier scan: clean

## Scope and review notes

- Merged current `main` without force-pushing.
- Six commits including current-main merges; 20 changed files.
- Production: +736/-5; tests: +890/-4; docs: +53; generated contracts: +41/-37.
- No live message was sent for exact-head verification.
- No private recipient, conversation, or platform message identifiers are included.

## Maintainer decision

This adds an optional Workboard tool and one additive Gateway result field. Maintainer sponsorship of that mainline product surface remains the final product decision.

prs.title: feat(media-understanding): shared structured extraction for image-capable providers
prs.body:
Closes #119772

> AI-assisted PR. Written with Claude Code; I have reviewed the change and understand what it does. See **Evidence** for validation.

**Rescoped on 6 September.** The previous head of this branch bundled two fixes. The provider-resolution half landed on `main` as #139231 (`18733285112b`), rewritten by @steipete at the shared catalog owner — I am not carrying a second version of it here. What remains is the other half, now filed as the feature it is rather than a bug fix, at +220/−11 production lines instead of +336/−27.

## What Problem This Solves

Logbook's `visionModel` is effectively single-provider. On current `main`:

- `extensions/codex/media-understanding-provider.ts` is the only `extractStructured` implementation in the repository.
- Registry hydration binds `describeImage` and `describeImages` from the shared image runtime for every image-capable provider (`src/media-understanding/provider-registry.ts:44-45`) but never `extractStructured`.
- So `extractStructuredWithModel` throws `Provider does not support structured extraction: <id>` (`src/media-understanding/runtime.ts:372`) for any non-Codex provider — after #139231 made that provider resolvable, it resolves and *then* throws.

The `extractStructured` contract shipped in May with Codex as its only implementer; the docs already say other providers "do not currently expose" it. This PR gives them one.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Owner:** the registry hydration and the shared image runtime that already own the `describeImage`/`describeImages` defaults.

**Canonical fix.** Hydration binds `extractStructured: provider.extractStructured ?? extractStructuredWithImageModel` next to those defaults; providers with their own hook (Codex) keep it. `src/media-understanding/structured-extraction.ts` runs one completion through `completeImagesWithModel` with the extraction instructions — including a no-secrets rule — as the prompt, supplemental text inputs as `userText` in the user message, and the reply parsed and schema-validated the same way the Codex extractor does it. It never routes through a provider's bespoke `describeImages`. Replies are parsed strictly first; a fenced or prose-wrapped reply falls back to the first balanced JSON object or array via normalization-core's `extractBalancedJsonPrefix`, so a model that ignores "no Markdown fences" does not fail the whole batch — Codex's own extractor does a raw `JSON.parse`, so the shared path is now the more tolerant of the two. A reply with no JSON in it is still a controlled error.

**The delivery gate, and what it deliberately is not.** The output is persisted, so the instructions must reach the model as an instruction, not as user text beside a screenshot. `promptDelivery: "system-required"` makes the runtime refuse — before any stream is registered or request sent — exactly the routes on which the runtime *itself* decides to demote the prompt into user content: `shouldPlaceImagePromptInUserContent` (the GitHub Copilot, OpenRouter, and Alibaba Model Studio endpoint classes) and both MiniMax VLM branches. Those get a named batch error.

The previous head instead carried an allowlist of transport names. That was wrong in both directions — it refused Ollama on its `api` string even though Ollama's plugin stream sends `Context.systemPrompt` as a `role: "system"` message (`extensions/ollama/src/stream.runtime.ts:740`), and it admitted plugin streams on a declared name it could not verify. The gate now records only the one decision the runtime owns. The trust boundary for a plugin stream that demoted `systemPrompt` is the plugin install — such a plugin would break every agent turn on that provider — and I have left that as a question for maintainers rather than a promise in code.

**`agentDir` default.** The shared extractor defaults an empty `agentDir` to the configured default agent dir (`structured-extraction.ts`). The dispatcher is unchanged and still passes `""` through, so a bespoke extractor such as Codex — which uses a non-empty `agentDir` as its thread `cwd` and loads project-local configuration from it (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/bounded-turn.ts:125`) — sees no change at all. On the shared path that value is the key for prepared-model owners, and `""` matches none of them on a long-lived gateway; Logbook never passes one. An earlier revision of this head put the default in the dispatcher, which would have changed Codex's working directory for existing installs — the review caught it, and it is fixed here.

**Removed versus the previous head**, so reviewers who saw it know what went where: the by-id resolver (superseded by #139231); the transport allowlist and `KnownApi` inspection (above); `imagePayloadTransform` and the opencode rewrite (opencode-only and separable — opencode is now hydrated with the shared hook without its reasoning-strip transform, which I am naming as a follow-up rather than carrying an SDK-adjacent field for one plugin). `runtime.ts`, `runtime.test.ts`, and all three opencode files are byte-identical to `main`.

## Maintainer decision requested

**Hydration now supplies `extractStructured` to every image-capable provider that lacks one — including providers whose `describeImage`/`describeImages` are bespoke.** That is a change to the provider-plugin capability contract, and I would rather state it than have it found.

What it does and does not do: the shared extractor never calls a provider's describe hooks — it runs its own completion through `completeImagesWithModel`, the same stream path `describeImage` takes when a provider does not override it. So a provider with bespoke description hooks that previously returned a visible `Provider does not support structured extraction` error now either extracts, or returns a visible provider error recorded on the batch. The delivery gate applies either way. On current `main`, the only bundled provider with bespoke hooks and no extractor of its own is opencode (its reasoning-strip transform is the named follow-up); Codex keeps its own.

I looked for a narrower rule and there isn't a correct one expressible from hook shape: deepinfra assigns the shared functions by reference, openai wraps the shared function in a lazy-import closure, and anthropic/google/ollama leave the hooks undefined — presence or identity checks each exclude a provider that is plainly on the shared path. The alternatives are therefore **(a)** this behavior, documented as above, or **(b)** an explicit opt-in on the provider contract, which is SDK surface and a maintainer call. I am asking for (a) and will implement (b) if that is the decision.

## User Impact

- Logbook works with any image-capable provider for which the shared runtime delivers the prompt as a system instruction. `visionModel` becomes a real choice.
- The Copilot, OpenRouter, and Model Studio endpoint classes and the MiniMax VLM endpoint are refused with an error naming the route, recorded on the batch, instead of running with a weaker boundary. `docs/plugins/logbook.md` and the `visionModel` help text state this rule and nothing broader.
- No behavior change for providers with their own `extractStructured`, for audio/video-only providers, or for plain `describeImage`/`describeImages` — only `promptDelivery: "system-required"` consults the gate.

## Evidence

**Regression tests fail on pre-fix code**, captured by removing the relevant line and re-running:

- Hydration line removed → `provider-registry.test.ts`: `expected undefined to be [AsyncFunction invoke]` on "hydrates structured extraction from the shared runtime".
- `promptInUserContent` refusal removed → `image.test.ts`: the Copilot case reaches `complete()` (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'stopReason')`), the MiniMax case resolves `"portal ok"` instead of rejecting — i.e. the request went out.
- `agentDir` default removed → `structured-extraction.test.ts`: `''` received where the configured default agent dir was expected.
- Fence fallback removed → `structured-extraction.test.ts`: a ` ```json ` -wrapped reply fails with `Structured extraction returned invalid JSON: anthropic`.

**Boundary tests.** `image.test.ts` asserts the exact `Context` handed to `complete` — system prompt equals the instruction, user message holds the caller text and image only — and that refused routes make no stream registration, no `complete`, and no `fetch`. `structured-extraction.test.ts` covers prompt assembly, text-input placement, JSON parsing, and schema validation. `provider-registry.test.ts` covers hydration identity and bespoke-hook preservation.

**Ran locally on this head:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` over `image`, `provider-registry`, `runtime`, `structured-extraction`, `image-tool.provider-loading`, and both opencode suites — all green; `oxfmt`, `oxlint` on changed files; `git diff --check`; `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` (no new SDK exports); `check:assertion-safety`; `check:coercion-helpers`; `config:docs:check` after regenerating `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` for the help-text change, as that check's own message instructs; an independent `$autoreview` pass at P2, which produced one finding — the fenced-JSON hard failure above — fixed in this head.

**Left to CI on purpose:** `pnpm build`, the `tsgo` typecheck lanes, and the full suite. My development machine cannot run those lanes, so this PR's CI on the exact head is the authority for them.

### Real-behavior proof (this head)

Isolated dev gateway on an x86-64 Linux box (Node v24.19.0), own `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, own port, never the operator's gateway. Logbook capture is macOS-only, so two synthetic JPEGs (a mock editor window; no real screen content) were seeded as frames — extraction, provider resolution, and the batch pipeline are all real; only the screenshot source is not.

Head `ce8458199cf95c85703fa1c884943e3541a552e1`; base `dd3faf5f`. Built dist self-reports `OpenClaw 2026.9.2 (ce84581)`. Vision model: `qwen2.5vl:7b` on local Ollama — a plugin stream with no bespoke `extractStructured`, which the previous head's allowlist would have refused on its `api` string.

#### 1. Accepted route completes (Ollama)

`visionModel: ollama/qwen2.5vl:7b`

```
$ openclaw gateway call logbook.analyze.now
{ "started": true }
$ openclaw gateway call logbook.status
lastBatch: { "id": 1, "day": "2026-09-06", "status": "done", "endMs": 1788750180139 }
todayCards: 2
```

`logbook.timeline` returns two cards built from the seeded frames:

```
{ "title": "Drafting release notes",
  "detail": "Added a short paragraph about how the extraction prompt travels in the system channel",
  "category": "coding", "keyframeId": 1 }
{ "title": "Re-read runtime dispatcher", "category": "coding", "keyframeId": 2 }
```

`batches` row: `{id:1, status:"done", error:null, frame_count:2, model:"ollama/qwen2.5vl:7b"}`. Gateway log: `[plugins] loading ollama from <dist>/extensions/ollama/index.js`.

**The prompt reaches the model in the system channel.** A logging pass-through proxy in front of Ollama recorded the extraction request:

```
POST /api/chat  bytes=87752
  model='qwen2.5vl:7b' stream=True
  messages[0].role='system' text="You are OpenClaw's bounded structured-extraction worker.
    Return only the requested extraction. Do not include secrets such as passwords, API keys,
    tokens, or credentials, even when they are visible in the input. ..."
  messages[1].role='user' images=2 text=''
  -> upstream 200
```

That is `STRUCTURED_EXTRACTION_INSTRUCTIONS` verbatim as `role: "system"`, images in the user message — the property `promptDelivery: "system-required"` exists to protect.

#### 2. Refusal happens before extraction I/O

`visionModel: minimax/MiniMax-VL-01`, with that provider's `baseUrl` pointed at a local listener that logs every TCP connection.

```
$ openclaw gateway call logbook.analyze.now      # 23:20:56
$ openclaw gateway call logbook.status
lastBatch: { "id": 1, "status": "error",
  "error": "Provider does not accept system instructions for image requests: minimax/MiniMax-VL-01 (the prompt is delivered as user content)" }
```

Listener log, complete file:

```
23:20:39 LISTENER-START port=19001
23:20:41 CONNECT from ('127.0.0.1', …)   first-bytes b'GET /listener-self-test HTTP/1.1…'
```

The single entry is a `curl` self-test proving the listener records. **Zero connections after the trigger** — the route was refused before any request was built.

Same refusal on the OpenRouter class against the real `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` with a dummy key, terminal in 5s (a key that reached OpenRouter would return 401 instead):

```
lastBatch: { "id": 3, "status": "error",
  "error": "Provider does not accept system instructions for image requests: openrouter/qwen/qwen2.5-vl-7b-instruct (the prompt is delivered as user content)" }
```

#### 3. Existing route (Codex) is untouched

```
$ git diff HEAD~1 -- src/media-understanding/runtime.ts extensions/codex/media-understanding-provider.ts
$ echo $?
0
```

Empty. Neither file is in the commit's changed set, and the dispatcher still passes `agentDir: params.agentDir ?? ""` unchanged (`src/media-understanding/runtime.ts:387`), so the bespoke Codex extractor keeps receiving `""` as its thread cwd. No OpenAI/Codex credentials were available for a live Codex run; the diff is the proof offered.

#### 4. Before/after on the same batch

Base `dd3faf5f` built separately in its own checkout, same state dir and frames:

```
BEFORE (dd3faf5f)  lastBatch: { "id": 4, "status": "error",
                     "error": "Provider does not support structured extraction: ollama" }
AFTER  (ce845819)  lastBatch: { "id": 4, "status": "done", "endMs": 1788751260139 }
```

Identical frames, identical batch id, only the checkout differs.

**Complete diagnostics** — the full proxy and listener logs, every gateway batch/refusal/plugin-load line, RPC captures, and redacted configs — are in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/119773#issuecomment-5565102396).

#### Limits of this proof, stated

- **The `github-copilot` class could not be exercised.** That provider validates its token against GitHub before any inference (`extensions/github-copilot/runtime-auth.ts:83-96`) and derives its API base URL from that response, so without valid Copilot credentials the batch fails at `Copilot authentication failed: HTTP 401` before the gate runs. With valid credentials the classification is the same as OpenRouter's and the gate applies; I have no Copilot account to show it live. The OpenRouter and Model Studio branches are classified from `baseUrl` (`resolveProviderRequestCapabilities`), so they cannot be aimed at a local listener — hence OpenRouter was proven against its real host and MiniMax carried the zero-I/O proof.
- **Pre-existing Logbook behavior found on the way, not this PR's:** card synthesis (`reviseCards`) runs on the agent default model, not `visionModel`. With no `agents.defaults.model` configured, extraction succeeds and the observations are written, but the batch is then marked `error` by the synthesis step. Worth its own issue; I can file it.

**Production LOC:** +220/−11 across four files (`image.ts` +55/−8, `provider-registry.ts` +9/−2, `image-runtime.ts` +8/−1, `structured-extraction.ts` +148). Tests +347/−3. Docs and manifest +36/−19. The growth is the capability; about 35 lines of `structured-extraction.ts` mirror Codex's parse/validate and could be shared through the SDK later, which would need a surface-budget decision I am not making here.

prs.title: fix(trajectory): session.ended timestamp matches model.completed before cleanup
prs.body:
Closes #102014

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where trajectory exports showed `session.ended` with the same timestamp as `model.completed`, so cleanup duration looked like zero even when teardown took real wall-clock time.

## Why This Change Was Made

`session.ended` was recorded at finalize time, right after model completion, so its timestamp preceded session teardown. This PR captures the terminal payload at finalize and records `session.ended` only after attempt cleanup completes, on both the embedded runner and the Codex app-server. No new event types or exporter knobs; payload fields are unchanged, only emit timing moves from finalize into post-cleanup.

Rebased note (2026-08-26): the original branch predated the embedded-attempt lifecycle rewrite, so this was re-implemented onto current `main` (`attempt-finalize.ts` / `attempt-session-settle.ts` / `attempt-settle.ts` on the embedded side, `run-attempt-finalize.ts` / `run-attempt-cleanup.ts` / `run-attempt-turn-start.ts` for Codex). Review findings from the previous round are addressed:

- P1 "Guarantee terminal recording when Codex cleanup throws": `cleanupCodexAttempt` now records `session.ended` (captured payload, or the derived fallback) inside its `finally` block as the `codex-trajectory-terminal` step, followed by a terminal flush, so a teardown failure can no longer skip terminal recording.
- P2 "Finish startup-failure teardown before ending the session": the Codex turn-start failure path now captures the payload and records it only after binding clear, thread unsubscribe, route release, sandbox release, and shared-client lease release all finish.

## User Impact

Operators reading trajectory traces can measure real session end time versus model compute time, including cleanup latency.

## Evidence

Verified at head `0d46a743604` (current `origin/main` `636e21b1985` plus these two commits), Windows 11, Node v24.15.0.

Embedded runner tests:

```
npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-session-cleanup.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-execution-settle.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-execution-phase.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-stream-finalize.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-result.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-finalize.media.test.ts

Test Files  16 passed (16)
     Tests  141 passed (141)
```

Codex app-server tests (new ordering coverage: `session.ended` recorded after `thread/unsubscribe` and after the one-shot client `closeAndWait`, on both the success path and the startup-failure path):

```
npx vitest run extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts -t "session.ended"

Tests  2 passed | 146 skipped (148)
```

Full `run-attempt.test.ts` A/B on this machine: 13 failures are `EBUSY: resource busy or locked, unlink *.sqlite` temp-dir cleanup flakes that reproduce identically on unmodified `origin/main` (13 failed / 133 passed baseline vs 13 failed / 172 passed with this PR's files in the same run); the failure set is identical test-for-test, so they are pre-existing Windows-only flakes, not regressions.

Revert-red check: with only the production hunks stashed, the new Codex ordering tests fail (2 failed) and the new/updated embedded cleanup tests fail (12 failed); all pass with the hunks restored.

Repo checks: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` all clean. `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files. `pnpm check` guards pass, including the assertion SAFETY comment ratchet (the one new field uses a typed spread instead of an `as` assertion).

### Live embedded trajectory artifact (2026-08-26, this head)

Ran on this PR head (`0d46a743604`), Windows 11, Node v24.15.0, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, embedded `openclaw agent --local --json`, model `mistral/mistral-small-latest` (no Telegram / Vertex / gateway secrets).

Runtime event order from `trajectory_runtime_events`:

```
seq=0 session.started      2026-08-26T10:52:02.672Z
seq=1 trace.metadata       2026-08-26T10:52:02.680Z
seq=2 context.compiled     2026-08-26T10:52:02.741Z
seq=3 prompt.submitted     2026-08-26T10:52:02.746Z
seq=4 model.completed      2026-08-26T10:52:05.364Z
seq=5 trace.artifacts      2026-08-26T10:52:05.364Z
seq=6 session.ended        2026-08-26T10:52:05.371Z
```

`session.ended` is recorded after `model.completed` and after `trace.artifacts` (7ms delta on this short no-tool turn), matching the fixed ordering: the terminal event now carries the post-cleanup wall-clock time instead of sharing the `model.completed` timestamp.

### What was not tested

- `pnpm test` full suite and `pnpm build` artifacts beyond the local build used for the live run above (targeted suites only, per above).
- Codex app-server live run (its ordering is covered by the new harness tests instead).

## AI-assisted

Yes. Authored with Cursor/Grok assistance. Human: Stan Shih (stantheman0128). Rebase onto current main, review-finding follow-up, and live proof also Cursor.

prs.title: fix: start typing for queued followup turns and honor configured typingMode for Telegram room events
prs.body:
Fixes #92267

## Problem

`agents.defaults.typingMode: "instant"` is silently ineffective for message-tool delivery setups — the configuration the ambient-room-events docs recommend (`unmentionedInbound: "room_event"` + `visibleReplies: "message_tool"`). Two independent gaps:

**Gap 1 — queued/steered turns never start typing.** `createFollowupRunner` builds the typing signaler but never calls `signalRunStart()`; its only trigger is streamed renderable text, which `message_tool` turns never produce (their streamed final is the silent token). With `messages.queue.mode: "steer"` and long-running sessions, most real inbound messages take this path — observed in production as a full day of Telegram traffic with 42 `sendMessage` operations and **zero** `sendChatAction` calls, in DMs and groups alike. `runReplyAgent` already signals run start for fresh turns; the docs define `instant` as "start typing as soon as the model loop begins, even if the run later returns only the silent reply token", with no queued-turn exception.

**Gap 2 — Telegram hardcodes `suppressTyping` for room events.** `bot-message-dispatch.ts` sets `suppressTyping: isRoomEvent` unconditionally while simultaneously setting `sourceReplyDeliveryMode: "message_tool_only"` — the exact mode `resolveTypingMode()` deliberately maps to `"instant"`. The suppression check runs first, so that mapping and any explicit operator-configured `typingMode` are unreachable for unmentioned group turns.

## Fix

- `followup-runner.ts`: call `typingSignals.signalRunStart()` at follow-up run start, mirroring `runReplyAgent`. The signaler gates on mode internally, so `message`/`thinking`/`never` semantics are unchanged; existing `markRunComplete`/`markDispatchIdle` teardown already handles cleanup (silent turns drop typing promptly).
- `bot-message-dispatch.ts`: suppress room-event typing only when the operator never configured a typing mode — `isRoomEvent && resolveConfiguredTypingMode(cfg) === undefined`. The new resolver (session override, then `agents.defaults`) mirrors how `get-reply` resolves the effective mode. Default installs keep today's quiet ambient-room behavior.
- `plugin-sdk/config-contracts.ts`: re-export `TypingMode` for the resolver's signature.

## Tests

- `followup-runner.test.ts`: queued turns start run-start typing under `instant`, and do not under `message` (regression for gap 1).
- `agent-config.test.ts` (new): resolver precedence (unset → undefined, defaults, session override) plus a guard on the existing reasoning-default fallback.

`vitest run` on both touched suites: 79 passed. `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:extensions` clean; oxlint/oxfmt applied.

## Verification beyond tests

Both changes were first applied to a live 2026.6.5 deployment (as dist patches with identical semantics) and verified by the affected user: typing restored in DMs (gap 1 path) and in unmentioned group-topic messages (gap 2 path), with message-tool final delivery unchanged.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Telegram typing indicator (`sendChatAction: typing`) now appears during agent runs for both queued/steered turns and unmentioned group `room_event` turns with `typingMode: "instant"`, where previously neither path ever issued a `sendChatAction`; it still stops when the message-tool reply lands.

**Real environment tested:** Production OpenClaw 2026.6.5 on a macOS gateway (LaunchAgent), Telegram channel polling, Codex app-server runtime, `agents.defaults.typingMode: "instant"`, `messages.queue.mode: "steer"`, `messages.groupChat: { unmentionedInbound: "room_event", visibleReplies: "message_tool" }`; both fixes applied to the live deployment with semantics identical to this PR and the gateway restarted.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** (1) restart gateway with both fixes applied; (2) send a DM to an agent whose session is mid-run (follow-up/steered path); (3) send an unmentioned message in an always-on group topic (room_event path); (4) observe the Telegram client and audit gateway logs for `sendChatAction`.

**Evidence after fix:** Telegram client visibly rendered the "typing…" indicator within ~1–2s of the inbound message on both the DM and the group-topic turn and held it through each run until the message-tool reply was delivered (operator-observed live); before the fix, a full day of runtime logs showed 42 `sendMessage` operations and 0 `sendChatAction` entries, and a direct Bot API `sendChatAction` returned `{"ok":true}` and rendered — isolating the gap to the run pipeline. Screen recording from the live deployment available on request.

**Observed result after fix:** Both previously-dead typing paths show live typing through the full run and stop on message-tool delivery; silent (`NO_REPLY`) turns tear typing down promptly; message-tool final delivery, mentioned-group, and fresh-DM behavior unchanged.

**What was not tested:** `typingMode: "thinking"` under this setup (needs streamed reasoning); heartbeat turns (excluded by design in the signaler); other channels sharing the room-event pattern (e.g. Discord's analogous flag, out of scope for this PR).

prs.title: fix(update): keep the in-Gateway refusal code for update repair runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw update repair` launched inside the managed Gateway's process tree correctly refuses to stop its parent, but records a generic `repair-failed` reason and `Error` fact. The Updates page and recovery notices lose the actionable refusal code.

Fixes #182054. Thanks @coygeek for the detailed report and reproduction evidence.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor's maintenance inspection now forwards the managed-service failure facts, and update failure results retain those Doctor facts instead of replacing them with a generic error. Existing finalization can then keep the specific refusal reason. This also preserves sibling service-membership, ancestry, triage-tree, and service-definition refusal codes.

The shared recovery guidance directs context-refused repairs to an external terminal. Update-failure heartbeat notices explicitly tell the agent that stop-requiring repair must run outside the Gateway process tree.

## User Impact

Repair history, failure reports, and update status retain `inside-gateway-process-tree` and the other typed refusal codes. Operators get the external-terminal `openclaw update repair` action instead of generic triage advice for caller-context refusals. The maintenance guard and nonzero refusal exit remain intact.

## Evidence

- Node 26.12.1: **154 tests passed across six files**, covering repair finalization, sentinel notices, reports, recovery guidance, diagnostics, and prompt-prefix stability; 135.26 seconds total wall time.
- **Seven red-before regression cases**: six managed-service refusal codes lost their facts on the base, and the heartbeat notice lacked the external-terminal restriction. All pass with the fix. Existing generic repair-failure and deferred-maintenance controls also pass.

Each prepares three successive Doctor contexts to prove initial deferral, durable convergence, and idempotence; those serial passes account for the repeated setup cost. Docker was unavailable. The clean-machine Testbox never became ready (`hydrating`, `ready=false`, no host) and was stopped. No managed-Gateway live reproduction is claimed. The host's real Gateway and service were not modified or restarted.
