prs.title: fix(ui): correct Turkish language removal label
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Turkish accessibility label for removing an additional Talk language calls that language a server.

## User Impact

Language removal now announces “remove the {name} item.” The shared MCP-server removal label and tooltip use the same neutral wording. Visible button text and removal behavior stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The canonical grouped translation at `ui/src/i18n/.i18n/tr.tm.jsonl:8981` serves both `configPage.deviceTalk.removeLanguage` (`ui/src/pages/config/talk-device.tsx:237`) and `mcpServers.removeNamed` (`ui/src/components/mcp-servers-card.tsx:333`). Both English strings are “Remove {name}”; the Turkish translation incorrectly specialized them to servers.

This changes only that row’s translated value from `{name} sunucusunu kaldır` to `{name} öğesini kaldır`. The entry identity, source hash, alias, timestamp, and all unrelated current-main translations are preserved. This is the supported isolated generated-output correction: normal refresh reuses canonical memory, and locale artifact fan-in invalidates stale worker data when canonical memory changed. No glossary or parallel override is needed.

## Evidence

- The actual catalog materializer fails on pinned main `c20b504a` because both shared labels contain the server-specific wording; it passes after the correction for both labels.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, `pnpm ui:i18n:check --locale tr`, and `git diff --check`: pass. The full parity check and Turkish-only check pass on pinned base `c20b504a` and with the correction. The old draft’s stale-catalog failure on its September base no longer applies.
- One generated line changed (+1/-1); production logic +0/-0, tests +0/-0. No implementation-mirroring test was added for a wording-only change.
- Independent Codex P0–P2 review: scoped-clean, no actionable findings.
- No live Gateway, native bridge, screen-reader, or model proof was run; canonical materialization checks the changed labels, and exact-head PR CI supplies broad validation.

Historical synthetic component captures below are from original PR head `346882a302e5e347699856d397189f056fd43abb`, inspected again for this refresh. Their visible button text is identical (“Kaldır”); the original component proof reported computed accessible names changing from “Türkçe sunucusunu kaldır” to “Türkçe öğesini kaldır.” These are not current-head captures and do not independently display the accessibility name.

![Before: synthetic Talk language-removal control](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/798c56c0-b1c2-4a52-be3e-08f870408a0a)

![After: the same synthetic control with corrected accessibility label](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0f4a2ad4-7551-49cc-bb74-291b5d485a6a)

CI follow-up: run `39566396225` tested merge `106f5899` against newer main `4e6f52e0`; `control-ui-i18n` job `119109918998` passed source verification but failed locale parity with “control-ui catalog fallback baseline drift detected.” Running that exact command on unmodified `4e6f52e0` reproduces the identical failure; its English composer catalog extraction (`4fa2da58`) followed the last locale refresh. No unrelated locale artifacts were regenerated. Scheduled main run `39563487228`, head `4fa2da58`, reproduces the identical locale-parity error in job `119100314441` at 07:40:43 UTC. That job’s outer result is success because scheduled main permits locale drift; its parity command exits 1. The automatic classifier compared an older passing main run (`39557777617`), so its “new” job-level label does not reflect this newer matching step-level evidence. This is an inherited main catalog-metadata failure; no rerun or unrelated locale repair was performed.

prs.title: fix: preserve requester recovery source for native subagents
prs.body:
Closes #182042. Related: #182043, #182065.

## What Problem This Solves

Native subagents started by a channel requester can lose their completion after a Gateway crash because command admission never saved their original requester source.

## User Impact

Native children now retain the admitted requester facts needed by registry recovery. Recovery still checks the current child, requester incarnation, Gateway lifetime, and permissions before continuing. Existing runs with no saved source remain blocked; transcript text and delivery routes cannot recreate authority.

## Why This Change Was Made

The exclusion at [`agent-command.ts:304`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/de0b7ffc0c98e9254add882052b879343d224b67/src/agents/agent-command.ts#L304) prevented native keys from reaching the existing claim producer. `restoreChannelSubagentCompletionSource` already consumes that private child claim and independently reauthorizes it. Removing the exclusion repairs that producer/consumer contract; main-session recovery still excludes delegated sessions.

Eric Cai's implementation and regression are unchanged. The maintainer integration only merges main `d355f2fd148dd68486d863aba8b510adfa8005c2`, preserving the original commit. Production: +3/-7 (net -4); tests: +16/-4 (net +12). No schema, configuration, or public API change; existing restart-recovery documentation already describes the intended behavior.

**#182043 remains separate.** Its missing source is on the parent settlement turn. Native launch capture omits the existing `retainRequester` opt-in, batch authority compares operator source/scopes rather than channel principals, and announce dispatch omits `agentToolCaller`. That is a capture/batch/settlement ownership question, not this child's claim producer. Selecting a requester for a mixed-principal batch is outside this fix. The contributor's combined crash reproduction also remains red for #182043. Cleanup settlement is separately owned by #182065. No unconditional resend or uncertain-send success is introduced here.

## Evidence

Maintainer verification on integration head `de0b7ffc0c98e9254add882052b879343d224b67`:

- **Red on current main:** the expanded regression with production `agent-command.ts` from `d355f2fd148d` produced **1 failed / 5 passed**. The native-key case retained `previous-child-command` instead of `next-child-command`; this was an assertion failure at real command admission/SQLite claim persistence, not a fixture setup failure.
- **Green with the fix:** `pnpm test src/agents/agent-command.recovery-source.test.ts src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-detached-recovery.restart-integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed **17/17 tests**: 6 command regressions and 11 registry recovery cases. The native case proves main-recovery exclusion and terminal source cleanup; the registry suite covers restored channel sources, missing/mismatched sources, and requester reset. Per-file wall times were 59.85s and 164.15s on the loaded host, dominated by import/transform and existing worker-backed fixtures; cold worker preparation was separate. These tests exercise real admission, persistence and recovery owners with model/transport doubles.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and all **29 affected test type graphs** passed. Targeted typed lint, two-file format check, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh committed-branch **Codex autoreview: scoped-clean**, no actionable P0–P2 findings. Personal source review covered admission, claim preparation, registry restoration, source lifetime and the sibling settlement path.
- Exact-head CI: [run 40053286039, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40053286039) completed with **39 successful jobs, 31 skipped, and one failing test job plus the downstream aggregate**. `security-fast` passed. The two failures are the existing replaced-session metadata and off-page controller/collector assertions in `sessions-list-persisted-worker.test.ts` ([job 120750780484](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40053286039/job/120750780484)); both also fail in original [run 40046482472](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40046482472). The CI merge `47f3db8778b989d14460223bdff369559178d391` has main baseline `0d49ef7bd1c6fa024d76e962995a0f37aa93c74e` and this exact PR head as parents. Its diff from baseline is only this PR’s two files; the failure fixture, list/read/projection owners and registry are byte-identical. Those seeded list/describe tests never execute changed command admission. The classifier had no comparable scheduled-main job and reported unknown; inspected source and original-run failures establish them as inherited. The maintainer then ran only these two cases with production command code from main `d355f2fd148d`: **both failed with the same assertions** (2 failed, 1 unselected/skipped); the fixed module was restored and the worktree is clean. Landing uses the authorized inherited-failure exception; CI is not relabeled green.

Audit context: the restart analysis covered 61 Gateway starts and recorded 985 interrupted subagent waits and 110 direct-announcement failures. Journal lines 254140–254141 and 254444 illustrate this recovery surface. Those counts are not an attribution of every event to this bug; the synthetic regression above establishes this defect. No live Gateway or Team state was touched.

The contributor's inspectable full-process, replacement-rejection and latest-stable upgrade evidence follows. Those runs retain their original SHAs and limitations; they are not represented as new maintainer executions.

<details>
<summary>Contributor runtime and upgrade evidence</summary>

### Inspectable existing source-recovery behavior evidence

**Scope and pinned inputs:** the standalone source fix is `e13f9030214a1654d1eb55dc2ad89d9dac2e4f65`, based on `2fc557a9fb060befdb5443db5d3963fa2cd082bc`. Combined integration commit `0a38fe2ad20e5c1b60051ee42159dffcc24abef5` contains that source fix plus the independent cleanup-settlement repair from #182065 (`9aabdbf9fd73965afe18fdded712a93ae1289f6c` on its own branch). Standalone source recovery, standalone downstream settlement failure, and combined settlement success are reported separately below.

This section contains actual archived driver/Gateway output and explicitly labeled selected audit fields. Newly executed final-effect and latest-stable upgrade evidence follows in the next section. No IPs, keys, phone numbers, non-public endpoints, or local usernames/checkout paths are published here. All retained IDs are synthetic fixtures.

**Real entry path:** the built `openclaw.mjs gateway run --port <isolated-loopback-port>` runs on Node 26.12.1 / macOS arm64 under an OS sandbox, with a fresh isolated HOME, state, workspace, and TMPDIR. Non-loopback outbound traffic and user-home reads/writes are denied. Only `rehearsal-channel` is loaded. `rehearsal.ingress` queues an inbound synthetic message; the channel lifecycle calls `finalizeInboundContext` → `recordInboundSession` → `dispatchReplyWithBufferedBlockDispatcher`. A controllable loopback HTTP `openai-completions` model supplies responses to the real host `sessions_spawn`, `sessions_yield`, and `sessions_send` tools. The test `sendText` implementation records its outbound effect and returns a synthetic platform message ID.

The driver invocation shape was `python3 reproduce.py --source <source-or-integration-checkout> --scenario normal|active --label <fixture-label> --port <isolated-loopback-port>`. prs.title: experiment(control-ui): keep unchanged catch-up rows idle [do not merge]
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link can rewrite cached transcript rows during startup even when their contents have not changed. The campaign's original baseline had 14 visual states over roughly 15 seconds; this experiment targets one remaining catch-up reconciliation task.

## Why This Change Was Made

History reconciliation already retains equal message objects and groups. Unconditional browser-tab, reaction, reply-lookup and question-draft dependencies still invalidate ordinary rows. The candidate narrows these dependencies at the transcript projection owner, with no renderer change, new cache, stored shape, or configuration option.

## User Impact

**Experiment stopped: the pre-declared reload gate failed. This PR is closed without merging.** The isolated no-op contract improves, but overall reload performance does not meet the required evidence threshold.

## Evidence

Baseline `d355f2fd148dd68486d863aba8b510adfa8005c2`; candidate `7fc82c0afad40db83e4b763c07989379523e82dd`. Quiet AWS Crabbox `cbx_9b6e76f6fc4e`, c7a.4xlarge (16 AMD EPYC cores, 32 GiB class), 11 interleaved unprofiled pairs per route. Team-scale benchmark; connect not-before 340 ms, connect reply 220 ms, ordinary RPC delay 20 ms, resolve/describe 195 ms. These retain the L179 workload for comparison; the separately running latency-fidelity lane is outside this experiment.

Pre-declared acceptance: unchanged-row catch-up writes approach zero; chat final rows and LoAF improve with non-overlapping IQRs or at least 9/11 better pairs and a negative paired median. Secondary regressions require separated IQRs or at least 9/11 worse pairs with a paired rise above max(10 ms, 3%). **Primary FAIL; secondary PASS.**

The fully cached idle fixture retains 80/80 message objects. At the first catch-up publication, six equal prepared-row arrays/footer actions are recreated on the baseline. The candidate removes that redundant mutation batch: message-ID writes 6 → 0 and action-row writes 3 → 0. Across the entire catch-up interval, including independent descriptor/identity updates, message-ID writes are 18 → 12, action-row writes 9 → 6, and style mutations 18 → 18. Those later updates remain real presentation changes.

With one edited message, 79/80 message objects and five of six visible groups remain equal. The original broad vector still re-prepares all six; only the edited row's prepared content and footer differ. The regression verifies idle rows stay untouched while edits, reactions, deletion, and new messages render; existing activity coverage protects run-status updates.

Focused regression: 13/13 tests, `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-transcript-projection-scale.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, **9.71 s wall time** remotely. The new no-write assertion fails on the original production code. Four sibling files (warm startup, reply previews, reactions, question drafts): **83/83 pass**. Autoreview is clean through P2. Broad changed-file checks, native UI e2e and full UI e2e were intentionally not run after the failed performance gate. Draft CI is skipped; there is no broad-CI-green claim.

Runtime LOC: **+15/-7 = +8** across two production files; +58 test lines. Five unconditional invalidations are deleted. Growth preserves per-message reaction updates while narrowing invalidation. No production change is landed.

Setup attempts were excluded: one accidentally captured temporary diagnostic code; one allocation substituted t3.small and was stopped before work; another used incompatible HTML/MCP readiness flags and timed out during baseline warm-up. The successful comparison uses clean pinned source and the corrected L179 MCP invocation. Every lease is released; no live Gateway or real account was used.

prs.title: fix: disconnection watchdog in provider lifecycle owner
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the Discord gateway disconnects and an event-loop stall prevents the reconnect timer from firing, the gateway stays in 'reconnect scheduled' state indefinitely and goes deaf to Discord. The existing lifecycle owner (provider.lifecycle.ts) already handles startup stalls (gateway opens but READY never arrives) via startReadyWatch, but does NOT cover runtime stalls after steady-state — when the gateway was already connected, disconnects, and the reconnect stalls.

## The Fix: Disconnection Watchdog in the Lifecycle Owner

Extended createGatewayStatusObserver in provider.lifecycle.ts to start a disconnection watchdog when the gateway closes (after initial readiness). The watchdog polls isConnected and, if the gateway stays disconnected longer than runtimeReadyTimeoutMs (30s default), calls triggerForceStop — which goes through the existing lifecycle cleanup path (waitForDiscordGatewayStop -> finishReject -> proper disconnect and listener cleanup).

Key design:
- Only arms after `markRuntimeReady()` (after initial `waitForGatewayReady` completes)
- Arms on both "Gateway websocket closed" AND "Gateway reconnect scheduled" (covers Invalid Session, server RECONNECT, heartbeat timeout, failed IDENTIFY)
- Deadline preserved across reconnect cycles (startDisconnectWatchdog is no-op if already running)
- Grace period: if a reconnect is in progress (socket CONNECTING/OPEN) when the watchdog fires, it defers and grants another runtimeReadyTimeoutMs
- Stopped on READY/RESUMED dispatch, on dispose, and when lifecycle is stopping

## Evidence

**Live transport proof, CONNECTING-at-cap branch (head `3acb82dec3b`, 2026-09-03):**
```
[+      0ms] graceful ws.close(1000), reconnectAttempts preset → backoff 16000ms
[+    ~100ms] reconnect-scheduled: 16000ms → watchdog rearmed to min(21000, cap−elapsed)
[+  16108ms] RESUME dial stranded on a stuck TCP server — socket readyState=0 (CONNECTING)
[+  21105ms] watchdog fires → grace 1/2, rearm capped to remaining budget 3895ms (< T)
[+  25105ms] watchdog fires → grace 2/2, remaining budget 0
[+  25107ms] force-stop at cumulative cap: elapsed 25005ms vs cap 25000ms, socket still CONNECTING
[+  ~25200ms] supervisor recovery → fresh READY → inbound MESSAGE_CREATE delivered
```
Full redacted log: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/124162#issuecomment-5525733609

**Live transport proof (runDiscordGatewayLifecycle public entry point, prior head `9cb5b13ebd2`):**
```
[+     9ms] proof: connecting to Discord gateway
[+   317ms] gateway.debug: Gateway websocket opened
[+   820ms] proof: gateway READY (isConnected=true)
[+  2821ms] proof: terminating gateway websocket; reconnect disabled
[+  2823ms] gateway.debug: Gateway websocket closed: 1006
[+ 32828ms] runtime.error: discord gateway: disconnection watchdog fired after 30004ms — force-stopping lifecycle
[+ 32830ms] proof: PASS — disconnection watchdog force-stopped the real lifecycle
```

Exercised the REAL `runDiscordGatewayLifecycle` — the public exported entry point — with a live Discord gateway connection. Watchdog fired after 30004ms, lifecycle rejected with proper cleanup (threadBindings.stop called).

**Unit tests (provider.lifecycle.test.ts):**
- "force-stops the lifecycle when the gateway stays disconnected past the ready timeout"
- "does not force-stop when the gateway reconnects before the watchdog threshold"
- "defers force-stop when a reconnect is in progress at the watchdog threshold"

**ClawSweeper review:** Zero code findings, proof: sufficient, patch quality: platinum hermit (4/6), status: ready for maintainer look.

## Changes

- **provider.lifecycle.ts** (+76): startDisconnectWatchdog, clearDisconnectWatchdog, wired into onGatewayDebug (close + reconnect-scheduled), dispose, markRuntimeReady, grace-period deferral for in-progress reconnects
- **provider.lifecycle.test.ts** (+73): three tests covering force-stop, quick-reconnect, and grace-period deferral
- **gateway.ts** (-35): removed old gateway-level watchdog (shouldReconnect=false in maxAttempts kept)
- **gateway-lifecycle.ts** (-39): removed GatewayConnectionWatchdog class
- **gateway.test.ts** (-149): removed old watchdog tests

Net: +149 -224 = -75 lines

Closes #122950

prs.title: feat(slack): opt-in intro turn when the bot is added to a channel
prs.body:
Closes #122370

## What Problem This Solves

When a Slack bot is added to a channel, OpenClaw records only a passive `member_joined_channel` system event, delivered on the next heartbeat tick. Agents with long heartbeat intervals greet long after the invitation; agents with the heartbeat disabled never react at all. Being invited to a channel is an explicit human action directed at the bot, but there is no supported way for the agent to respond to it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an opt-in Slack account config, `channels.slack.selfJoinIntro: { enabled, prompt }`, default **off**. When enabled and the join event is about the bot itself, the members handler dispatches an immediate agent turn through the normal message pipeline — a synthetic inbound message attributed to the inviting user, with an explicitly automated instruction text (`prompt` overrides the default introduction request). The message lane was chosen over a heartbeat wake so the behavior is independent of heartbeat configuration and reuses the exact ingress path (auth, dedupe, routing, threading) every real mention takes; a bot-authored sender would be dropped by self-message/allowBots filtering, which is why the turn is attributed to the inviter. The synthetic message carries a fresh ts because the join's own `event_ts` can repeat across leave/re-invite cycles and would collide with inbound dispatch dedupe.

Boundaries: other members' joins are untouched; the channel must pass the same access checks as any other system event; when Slack omits `inviter`, behavior falls back to the passive system event. No new scopes or event subscriptions (`member_joined_channel` is already in the recommended manifest).

## User Impact

Operators can opt an agent into greeting and introducing its capabilities within seconds of being added to a channel, with an optional custom instruction (e.g. "read recent history and offer concrete help, in a thread"). Existing deployments see zero behavior change unless they set `selfJoinIntro.enabled: true`.

## Evidence

- `extensions/slack/src/monitor/events/members.test.ts`: 6 new cases — intro dispatch attributed to the inviter (fresh ts, mention + automated prefix, `wasMentioned`), custom prompt override, passive fallback when disabled / no inviter / no handler wired, and other-members' joins unchanged.
- `extensions/slack/src/config-schema.test.ts`: `selfJoinIntro` absent by default, valid at root and account level, rejects wrong types/unknown keys.
- Targeted run: 62/62 tests pass across both files. `pnpm config:channels:gen` regenerated bundled metadata.
- The mechanism (synthetic inviter-attributed turn on self-join) has been running in production on a 2026.7.1 deployment since 2026-08-10: invite → greeting in ~21 s → threaded capabilities briefing.
- Failures currently on `main` (streaming preview-fallback rendering, Mattermost gateway-auth contract parity, slash `/think` menu, Enterprise Grid allowlist, exec-approvals binding, durable-ingress retry) reproduce identically with this change stashed — none are introduced or touched by this PR.

prs.body:
## Proof follow-up

**Tip SHA:** `c6acabd113623d601863ffe6f3b5b6a877bc8601`

### DIRTY rebase

Rebased onto current `main` `16eb38cf9725b073bec2cf89842c28d59509231d` from starting SHA `a947649ada7a98e10f5fddadcd8d51607cba9b02`. Published with `--force-with-lease`.

- **Production files:** auto-merged. Native ChatGPT builder still distinguishes omitted vs explicit-null summaries and defaults summary-only effort to `medium`. Shared and generic builders keep the same undefined-vs-null contract.

### ClawSweeper findings — this revision

- [x] **[P2] Assert the resolved generic transport effort** — `packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-params-internal.test.ts` asserts `{ effort: "high", summary: null }` for the gpt-5.5 summary-only fixture (omitted-effort default is `high`, not `medium`).
- [ ] **[P1] Verify native endpoint acceptance for null summaries** — still blocked: this environment has no OpenAI / ChatGPT-authenticated credentials. Local native tests still capture the request body via `onPayload` and stop before dispatch. Public SDK types allow `summary: null`; that is not `/codex/responses` acceptance proof.

### Before-merge checklist

- [x] Focused Vitest on the three owner test files after rebase (3 files, 142 tests)
- [x] Generic-transport proof text corrected from `medium` to `high`
- [x] oxfmt, oxlint (touched files), `tsgo:core`, and packages test-types
- [ ] Live OpenAI / ChatGPT-authenticated endpoint proof — **not available** (no credentials)

### Focused test transcript (exact head)

```text
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts
 ✓ |unit| packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-params-internal.test.ts > buildOpenAIResponsesCompactSystemMessage > uses the developer role for reasoning models that support it
 ✓ |unit| packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-params-internal.test.ts > buildOpenAIResponsesCompactSystemMessage > falls back to the system role for xAI's native route, which disables the developer role

 ✓ |unit| packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-params-internal.test.ts > buildOpenAIResponsesParams reasoning summary > preserves null reasoning summary with explicit effort
 ✓ |unit| packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-params-internal.test.ts > buildOpenAIResponsesParams reasoning summary > preserves null reasoning summary without explicit effort
 ✓ |unit| packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-params-internal.test.ts > buildOpenAIResponsesParams reasoning summary > defaults omitted reasoning summary to auto
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  142 passed (142)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 17.25s
```

Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-params-internal.test.ts packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.test.ts packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts --reporter=verbose`

### Wire payload proof (exact-head, redacted)

Path-local omitted-effort defaults remain intentionally different:

```text
=== exact-head builder proof: reasoning.summary:null without explicit effort ===
HEAD_SHA=c6acabd113623d601863ffe6f3b5b6a877bc8601
transport.buildOpenAIResponsesParams (gpt-5.5 fixture) => {"effort":"high","summary":null}
shared.applyCommonResponsesParams / native ChatGPT builder => {"effort":"medium","summary":null}
LIMIT: no live OpenAI or /codex/responses proof; payload construction is covered locally.
```

---

Closes #121443

## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Responses payload builders coerced `reasoning.summary: null` to `"auto"`. The OpenAI SDK allows `summary?: 'auto' | 'concise' | 'detailed' | null`, so callers that pass `reasoningSummary: null` to disable summaries silently still requested auto summaries.

### Before (broken)

```ts
{ reasoningEffort: "medium", reasoningSummary: null }
```

became:

```ts
{ reasoning: { effort: "medium", summary: "auto" } }
```

because defaults used `|| "auto"` / `?? "auto"`, both of which treat `null` as missing.

Affected builders:

- `applyCommonResponsesParams` (`openai-responses-shared.ts`)
- Responses params-internal transport builder
- Codex Responses payload assembly (`openai-chatgpt-responses.ts`)

## Why This Change Was Made

Default `"auto"` only when the field is **omitted** (`undefined`):

```ts
summary: options?.reasoningSummary === undefined ? "auto" : options.reasoningSummary
```

Adjacent matrix:

- explicit `null` → `summary: null`
- omitted → `summary: "auto"`
- Codex Responses `onPayload` path preserves `null`

## User Impact

Clients that disable reasoning summaries via `null` now send `summary: null` on the wire instead of accidentally requesting auto summaries (token waste / unwanted reasoning exposure). Omitted summary still defaults to `"auto"`.

## Evidence

### Before vs after (payload projection)

| Case | Before tip | After tip `c6acabd113623d601863ffe6f3b5b6a877bc8601` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{ reasoningEffort: "medium", reasoningSummary: null }` | `summary: "auto"` | `summary: null` |
| `{ reasoningEffort: "medium" }` (omitted summary) | `summary: "auto"` | `summary: "auto"` (unchanged) |
| Generic transport `{ reasoningSummary: null }` (gpt-5.5, omitted effort) | coerced to `auto` | `effort: "high"`, `summary: null` |
| Shared / native `{ reasoningSummary: null }` (omitted effort) | coerced to `auto` | `effort: "medium"`, `summary: null` |
| Codex Responses `reasoningSummary: null` | coerced to `"auto"` | `summary: null` on captured payload |

```text
result=3 files passed; 142 tests passed
```

Live OpenAI and ChatGPT-authenticated `/codex/responses` calls with `summary: null` against production endpoints (payload construction covered in unit tests). Native tests still throw from `onPayload` before dispatch.

prs.title: fix: preserve queued startup failures and cancellations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: queued replies can lose their original startup failure or cancellation and instead finish with `Terminal accounting session changed` after the same turn claims its session writer.

## User Impact

Users receive the startup failure's intended error reply, and cancelled turns remain cancelled rather than becoming accounting failures. Execution is not replayed. Genuine session, lifecycle, writer, and reply-operation replacement checks remain unchanged. No configuration, schema, or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the runtime's already-recorded writer facts through early rejected and aborted outcomes, including terminal normalization, and let queued completion consume those facts just as it does for settled results. This removes the settled-only handoff restriction without introducing another state owner or weakening finalization's guards.

Thanks @jjjhenriksen for the report and reproduction direction.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/fb2548de-8e54-4f34-a3f1-ff4203259127)

## Evidence

- Reproduced through the real follow-up queue, writer admission, embedded orchestration, accounting, and source delivery. Only harness startup is replaced by a deterministic failure/cancellation fixture; no model request is made.
- Both regression cases fail on base `59e9f2ece84cc7ba6c0f157b81125e14b4c89967`: the source receives empty payloads and `Terminal accounting session changed` instead of the intended startup failure or cancellation. Both pass with this patch; startup executes exactly once.
- **128 tests pass across six focused suites**, including queued custody, terminal completion, cancellation, and real session/lifecycle/writer replacement guards. The new regression cases took 9.2 seconds of test time in the final six-suite run (107.6 seconds total invocation wall time). CI timing is not available yet.
- Core and messaging-test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent Auto Review: scoped clean at its default P0 severity.
- A later standalone `pnpm test` invocation timed out during worker compilation around a Gateway interruption, before producing a test verdict. The successful 128-test proof above used the repository's supported direct `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` entrypoint. No test process remains running.
- Scope: three production files (+16/-6 lines), one existing lifecycle assertion, two new production-boundary regression cases, and native-database test-lane registration. Necessary test growth exercises the full handoff rather than fabricating writer receipts.

**Not claimed:** this does not explain or fix the reported six-minute Codex startup stall, nor does it change Codex startup-cancellation diagnostics. The error-replacement defect is in the shared queued-turn finalization path.

## Worked on by

- @jjjhenriksen

prs.title: fix: MEDIA leak, large-video aspect, steered webchat takeover
prs.body:
Closes #113014
Closes #97826
Closes #113194

## What Problem This Solves

Block-streamed replies can expose raw `MEDIA:` paths while attachment extraction is deferred. MP4 buffers whose metadata follows their video data can produce zero video dimensions through non-seekable ffprobe input.

## Why This Change Was Made

The conflict resolution ports the remaining media fixes to current owners: `parse-output.ts` strips streaming directives while final delivery still owns attachments, and `media-probe.ts` writes a temporary workspace and calls the existing seekable-descriptor probe. Existing protocol restrictions, descriptor cleanup, rotation, sample aspect ratio, and older-ffprobe fallback stay in the canonical probe.

The old Gateway active-run helper and post-dispatch owner were retired upstream. This integration keeps the current Gateway turn-adoption lifecycle and its `acceptedMessageInjection` early return rather than restoring those retired paths. The earlier direct-run adoption finding is therefore not validated by the removed helper tests.

## User Impact

Streamed captions hide media directives while retaining paragraph spacing, indentation, and fenced examples. MP4 dimensions can be read when the metadata is at the end of a full buffer.

## Evidence

October 4 validation used Node 26.5.0 and the pinned lockfile with pnpm 12.5.1. Against upstream `cc43c8c53cfeaede21a68fedc553d7c322574ffb`:

- Native parser suite: 202 tests passed, 1.37 seconds shard wall time. The four added streaming regressions fail against the unmodified upstream parser while the other 198 tests pass.
- Native media-probe suite: 28 tests passed, 4.81 seconds shard wall time. This includes descriptor cleanup, fd protocol compatibility, rotation, sample aspect ratio, and bounded probing behavior. The changed descriptor regression took 28 milliseconds.

prs.title: feat(ui): add setting to opt out of right-click message actions
prs.body:
Related: #106765

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI chat thread binds a `contextmenu` handler that calls `preventDefault()` on every message bubble to show the message actions menu. There is no way to get the browser's native context menu back on a message, so users who rely on native Copy, Search or spell-check on chat text have no escape hatch.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an explicit opt-out rather than changing the default: a **"Right-click message actions"** setting under Settings → Appearance → Chat, **enabled by default** so existing behaviour is unchanged. When it is turned off, `handleChatContextMenu()` returns before `preventDefault()` and the native menu opens normally.

The setting follows the existing `composerHoldToRecord` pattern — a browser-local preference persisted only when explicitly disabled. No gateway config schema change, and no change to the actions menu itself.

**Relationship to #106765 and #107137.** #106765 asks for native-menu access on *selected text* and lists three options; #107137 already implements option 2 (a Copy selection entry in the actions menu) and is further along. This PR is option 3 and is deliberately complementary, not a competing fix: it does not change selection behaviour at all, so it can land alongside #107137 or on its own. I am happy to close this if maintainers would rather keep the surface to one change.

Non-goals: no new menu entries, no change to selection handling, no change to link handling (which already falls through).

## User Impact

- Users who want the browser's native context menu on chat messages can turn off **Right-click message actions** in Settings → Appearance → Chat.
- Everyone else sees no change: the setting defaults to on and the actions menu behaves exactly as before.

## Evidence

Real-browser proof captured headless with `OPENCLAW_CAPTURE_UI_PROOF=1`.

### Screenshots

**1. Default — the actions menu opens on right-click**

![Actions menu opens on right-click by default](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tangotrick/openclaw/pr-proof-assets/04-actions-enabled-default.png)

**2. The new setting, Settings → Appearance → Chat (on by default)**

![The new Right-click message actions setting, enabled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tangotrick/openclaw/pr-proof-assets/05-setting-on.png)

**3. Setting switched off**

![The setting switched off](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tangotrick/openclaw/pr-proof-assets/06-setting-off.png)

**4. After opting out — no custom menu, native menu restored**

![Right-click after opting out shows no custom menu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tangotrick/openclaw/pr-proof-assets/07-actions-disabled-native-menu.png)

### Tests

New e2e case in `ui/src/e2e/chat-message-actions.e2e.test.ts` covering the whole chain in Chromium: the menu opens by default, the Settings toggle is clicked in the real UI and `aria-checked` flips to `false`, and the thread then leaves the event untouched. Suppression is read from `dispatchEvent()`'s return value, which is `false` only when a listener called `preventDefault()` — a browser-level fact rather than an assertion about internals.

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner \
  ui/src/e2e/chat-message-actions.e2e.test.ts -t "restores the native context menu"   → 1 passed

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts                        → passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/config/config-page.test.ts                    → passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/app/settings.node.test.ts                           → 38 passed
oxfmt --check / oxlint / git diff --check                                              → clean
```

Two notes in the interest of full disclosure:

- The pre-existing case `offers Reply inline and mirrors every assistant action in the context menu` fails in my environment on a tooltip assertion. I verified it **fails identically on an unmodified `main` checkout**, so it is not caused by this change.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:check` exits non-zero, but it also does so on unmodified `main`, and none of the reported keys are the two added here.

I could not run a full-repo `tsc --noEmit` locally — it exhausts memory on my machine — so type checking on the changed surface is covered only by the test runs above and CI.

prs.title: fix(workboard): clearing card selection loses keyboard focus
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Clearing Workboard card selection removes the focused toolbar button and drops keyboard focus to the page body. Restore focus to an already-rendered selected card within the invoking board before removing that toolbar.

## Evidence

Built production Gateway and Control UI together in secretless Linux Docker with Node 24.22.1. Main `094bbd6b153bbf4387644abdc1b488fc7eab31d2` and candidate `26ae90e463020c8356cd66b33bfd04c7b00bc8e3` each ran twice. No mocked Gateway, card rows or authored database state: shipped setup/config commands enabled bundled Workboard, and `workboard create 'Review release notes' --json` created the card.

Actual Tab navigation reaches the card; Shift+Enter selects it; Tab reaches Clear selection; Enter activates it. DOM focus observations after the toolbar disappears:

| Arm | Selected styling | document.activeElement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main | cleared | BODY |
| Candidate | cleared | same rendered ARTICLE card |

Both arms leave the card data unchanged (`workboard list --json` before/after) and retain independently selected state in a second real board instance. This does not claim a new solution for all-filtered/collapsed targets. Screenshots and accessibility snapshots accompany direct DOM focus assertions; media scrolls the card into view only after sampling focus, without focusing it.

Focused Chromium E2E regression, formatting and lint pass. Exact-head live provider gate passes with openai/gpt-5.4-mini and LIVE_PIN_OK; credential removed.

Inspected and render-checked comparison images with DOM focus evidence: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182020#issuecomment-6378689818

Whole-diff simplification retains the existing handler and its board scope: production +4/-1; tests/runner registration +54. No new state, scheduler, fallback target or SDK/config contract.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert fully restores prior behavior; no persisted state or schema migration. Blast radius is keyboard focus after Clear selection in Workboard. Card mutation behavior is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(ci): streamline desktop staging and enforce Windows test failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Desktop staging passes a nameless archive to npm, which fully extracts it just to discover its package name before the normal manifest and installation extractions. Its Windows test also observed the fixture registry over an HTTP control request after synchronous npm children; that request failed with `ECONNRESET`, and the following successful Cargo command hid Node's failure.

## User Impact

Desktop packaging avoids one redundant core-archive extraction while retaining the fresh archive install, dependencies and lifecycle policy. Windows CI now fails immediately when its Node boundary tests fail.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use npm's supported `openclaw@file:<archive>` spec and validate the installed manifest name before plugin stamping, ownership metadata or resource publication. The supplied name can otherwise alias a differently named package. Installation flags, private home, absolute-archive script policy and download-cache reuse remain intact.

Read the test registry's counter through its existing Worker IPC channel, with the listener registered before the request. Actual tarball HTTP traffic and cache, freshness, lifecycle and isolation assertions remain. Check PowerShell's `$LASTEXITCODE` immediately after Node, matching the existing native-power fixture guard.

Runtime: +3/-1 (net +2), justified by package identity before mutation. Workflow: +1. Tests: +58/-7. No dependencies or cache layer added.

## Current Refresh
Current signed head: `b54c69dbde97f51511cc63283a848fe997ee07c8`, integrating fixed baseline `aa9ddb7357396dee7f92959bbdd944882c880b29`. Current main had refactored the workflow test, causing one genuine content conflict; its shared helpers and all 15 existing cases remain, with the step-specific failure-propagation assertion added. The other three fix blobs are unchanged from the earlier reviewed head.
The refreshed source requires newer Node and pnpm. Task-isolated official Node 26.12.1 and pnpm 12.15.0 were checksum/integrity verified without changing host defaults. On this source, the Node staging file covered all seven distinct cases successfully: four initially passed; three release-tag fixtures failed only under the operator's signed-tag setting, then those exact three passed with command-scoped `tag.gpgSign=false`. Real commit signing and hooks remain enabled. Targeted formatting, scoped `git diff --check`, independent final-diff review and fresh complete autoreview passed.
Fresh exact-head proof is complete:
- [Core CI 39761953704/1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39761953704) passed: 29 successful jobs, 30 skipped, no failures. Actual hosted output in [job 119768691192](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39761953704/job/119768691192) confirms all **16 workflow cases passed**, including the exact Node/exit-guard/Cargo order.
- [Desktop 39761953533/1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39761953533) passed all three platforms. Actual [Windows output](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39761953533/job/119768026673) confirms the named cache fixture passed (10862.9726 ms), wrong-identity fixture passed (8.4284 ms), Node **14 passed, 0 failed, 1 expected platform skip**, Cargo **288 passed**, and native-power **1 passed**. Node 24.22.1/npm 11.19.1/pnpm 12.15.0 retained; real fresh npm installation, same-commit staging (970,578,625 package bytes / 975,886,854 resource bytes) and NSIS passed. [Installer artifact 12421375625](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39761953533/artifacts/12421375625): 396,534,103 bytes, SHA-256 1300ec32b26a3df038a8d8036e412e889d973df6a139086494ab9d8ecae4216e. Linux actual Node **25/25**, Rust **330 passed / 3 ignored** and native-power **1 passed**; macOS Rust **318 passed** and native-power **1 passed**.
- [Full ClawSweeper revision 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177474#issuecomment-6272237271) reviewed exact b54c69dbde97f51511cc63283a848fe997ee07c8: no findings, before-merge requests or remaining rank-up moves. Its pending-at-review Windows packaging observation is resolved by the completed run above.
Earlier evidence below remains historical. No elapsed-time or billing savings are claimed.
## Evidence

- Wrong-identity regression fails against the original staging owner and passes with the guard, without changing build-info, owner metadata or output resources.
- Actual npm 11.19.0 and 12.2.0 probes independently compare the same archive within each version, fresh prefixes/private homes and initially empty caches: core archive extractions **3 → 2**, final installed extraction **1 → 1**. Complete installed file/directory/link hashes and modes, lifecycle marker and package lock match.
- The real-install fixture covers a spaced archive argument, executable permissions, script-policy matching, isolated homes, all cache aliases and fresh archive bytes with unchanged version/source identity.
- Before this baseline refresh, revised Node staging/runtime/envelope tests: **15/15 pass**. The workflow exit-order regression fails without the guard (**1 failed, 15 passed**) and the corrected focused suite passes **16/16**. Scoped lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass; formatting intentionally excludes `apps/`. Release-tag fixtures used process-scoped `tag.gpgSign=false`; real commit signing remains enabled.
- Earlier [Windows run 39285084531/1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39285084531/job/118168638571) built and uploaded the real installer, but its Node tests had **13 passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped**. Its green job is **not** successful fixture proof. The observed failure was the parent counter fetch; an idle pooled socket is a likely mechanism, and one blocked-parent diagnostic did not reproduce it. This change removes that HTTP observation path without retries or timeout increases.
- Independent full-source review and fresh staged autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 defects.
- Previous-head `b7c838a2` [desktop run 39295809609/1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39295809609) passed all three platforms. Its actual [Windows log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39295809609/job/118207897776) shows the named cache fixture passed (9194.2221 ms), wrong-identity fixture passed (38.9871 ms), Node **14 passed, 0 failed, 1 existing platform skip**, Cargo **288 passed**, and native-power **1 passed**. Node 24.21.0/npm 11.19.0 retained; real package validation, fresh npm installation of 368 packages, same-commit staging and NSIS all passed. The [installer artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39295809609/artifacts/12212046584) uploaded successfully (386,985,345 bytes). Linux's actual Node **25/25** plus Rust **330 passed** and macOS Rust **318 passed** also passed. This completes the latest ClawSweeper review's Windows proof move. No elapsed-time savings claim is made.
- Previous-head `b7c838a2` [core CI 39295808958/1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39295808958) remains **failed**: 27 jobs succeeded, 29 skipped, and the baseline-ratchet job plus its downstream aggregate failed. That run's sole root failure is a stale `config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt` tuple for `extensions/acpx/register.runtime.test.ts`: [#177499](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177499) removed the recorded closed mock without removing its ledger entry. The actual tested merge includes all four PR files; the test, baseline, scanner and dependency inputs are byte-identical to its protected-main parent. Complete logs and 58-job accounting were independently checked; security passed. That inherited-only attribution was retained and independently reviewed; it is not reused as fresh-head CI admission, and failed CI is not relabeled green.
- Earlier core run 39285084818/1 had a different main-owned missing-command mock failure, covered separately by [#177501](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177501). That history is not used to attribute the final run's stale-ledger failure.
- Historical ClawSweeper revision 2 (retained in the [review history](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177474#issuecomment-6272237271)) covered `b7c838a2` with no findings or before-merge requests; its sole Windows proof move is completed above.

Related follow-up: the Docker installer's bare npm archive installs can have the same discovery cost, but their global-install and script-policy contracts need separate proof.

prs.title: feat(memory-core): optional cross-encoder rerank stage for memory search
prs.body:
## Summary

OpenClaw's builtin (sqlite-vec) memory search does first-stage hybrid retrieval (dense `vec0` ∥ FTS5 BM25, fused) → temporal decay → MMR diversity, but has **no second-stage relevance reranker**. MMR reuses the frozen first-stage score and measures only lexical (Jaccard) redundancy — it cannot re-judge query↔document relevance, so a genuinely-best passage that first-stage scoring underranks is dropped before the model sees it.

This adds an **optional, vendor-neutral cross-encoder rerank stage** to the builtin backend, as a plugin-SDK capability:

- New `MemoryRerankProvider` seam: `rerank({ query, candidates, signal }) → { ref, score }[]`. Candidates are passed by **core-assigned `ref`** and the provider returns scored refs (not full results), so it cannot drop/duplicate/fabricate rows; scores are normalized `[0,1]` written to a separate `rerankScore` field (the fusion `score` stays intact for `minScore`/telemetry).
- Registered via `api.registerMemoryRerankProvider`, gated by a `memoryRerankProviders` manifest contract (mirrors the embedding-provider contract). **Single exclusive slot** — a second registering plugin is rejected.
- `MemoryManager.search` runs the reranker on the **wide pre-MMR pool**, then MMR diversifies, then `minScore`/trim. **Fail-open**: an aborting deadline wraps the call; on timeout/error it returns the pre-rerank order.
- **Observable, not fail-silent:** `status().custom.rerank` / the search `debug.rerank` field reports `disabled` (no reranker) / `active` (scores applied) / `degraded` (registered but returned no scores — failing, timed-out, or plugin-disabled), with a latched warn on the active→degraded transition.

**No new core config** — opt-in is registration-based. Core ships **no concrete reranker**; a TEI/`bge-reranker` implementation is a separate plugin.

Intentionally out of scope: the concrete reranker plugin; the **qmd** backend (it delegates ranking to its own server-side reranker — noted inline at the insertion point and in docs).

Reviewers should focus on: the fail-open path in `MemoryManager.search` (must never throw), the `MemoryRerankProvider` refs→scores contract, the `memoryRerankProviders` gate, and the `disabled/active/degraded` observability.

## Linked context

Related #89477 (the RFC; the seam-surface decision lives there — a maintainer closes it on decision).
Related #82985 (a complementary, independent optimization — keep open; see below).

**Relationship to #82985 (`engineCandidates` passthrough) — complementary, not superseded.** The two are easily conflated as competing rerankers, but they solve different problems and can land independently:
- **This PR** adds a *reranking stage* on the **wide pre-MMR pool** (`candidateMultiplier`-expanded, up to ~4× `maxResults`) — so it can promote a passage that first-stage scoring underranked *before* the trim, and MMR then diversifies on the cross-encoder's relevance.
- **#82985** forwards `manager.search()`'s **already-trimmed** output to the existing `MemoryCorpusSupplement.search` so a supplement skips a redundant `manager.search()` roundtrip (#82984). Running *after* the pipeline, it can reorder the surviving top-N but cannot rescue a dropped passage.

So the supplement contract is the wrong *stage* for true reranking, but a fine fit for #82985's roundtrip goal. This seam gives reranking a first-class home (a plugin no longer *needs* the supplement-reranker pattern), yet it does **not** deliver #82985's roundtrip-efficiency benefit for other supplement types — so **#82985 stays open on its own merits**. The two currently overlap textually on `src/plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-runtime-core.ts` and `src/plugins/memory-state.ts`; a rebase resolves that.

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner? — Proposed RFC-first via #89477. Implementation is complete, expert-reviewed, rebased on latest `main`, and fully green, so this is marked **ready for review**; the one open item is the maintainer surface decision in #89477 (the new public SDK API + `memoryRerankProviders` contract).

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior addressed:** the `memory_search` tool now **preserves the manager's composed rerank→MMR order**. The prior tool-boundary code re-sorted results by `rerankScore`, which could **undo MMR's diversity reordering** (ClawSweeper [P1]). The fix removes the tool-boundary re-sort entirely — ordering ownership stays in `MemoryManager.search`; `corpus=all` block-interleaves the two corpora (their score scales are incomparable). With no reranker registered, order is unchanged (fusion-`score` descending). Active/degraded/disabled observability is unchanged.
- **Real environment tested:** OpenClaw built from this branch (the `mergeMemorySearchCorpusResults` change), run in an **isolated** home (`OPENCLAW_HOME=/tmp` throwaway; production `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` mtime unchanged before/after). A companion plugin implementing `MemoryRerankProvider` registered against a live TEI **bge-reranker-v2-m3** cross-encoder; **bge-m3** base embeddings; a local OpenAI-compatible **Qwen3.6-27B** drove the `openclaw agent --local` turn. Self-hosted tailnet endpoints; no cloud. (A dense-weighted hybrid first stage — `query.hybrid.vectorWeight:1` — was used only to stage a first-stage order that diverges from the cross-encoder; the fix itself is a config-independent ordering *preservation*.)
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** indexed a 5-doc corpus, then `openclaw agent --local --json` invoking `memory_search` for *"rotate the signing key in the vault"* **with MMR enabled**, then again with the plugin's kill-switch on.
- **Evidence after fix:** MMR ordering preserved at the tool boundary (terminal capture):
  ```
  debug: {"backend":"builtin","rerank":"active","hits":5}
  #0 near-dup.md   score 0.687  rerankScore 0.977
  #1 decoy.md      score 0.706  rerankScore 0.823
  #2 answer.md     score 0.682  rerankScore 0.967
  #3 access.md     score 0.426  rerankScore 0.000
  #4 runners.md    score 0.453  rerankScore 0.000
  (rerankScore-descending order would be: near-dup, answer, decoy, runners, access)
  ```
  MMR demoted `answer.md` (a near-duplicate of `near-dup.md`, `rerankScore` 0.967) **below** the diverse `decoy.md` (`rerankScore` 0.823) for diversity. The tool output **preserved** that order: it is **neither `rerankScore`-sorted** (which would put `answer` at #1) **nor raw-`score`-sorted** (which would put `decoy` at #0) — it is the manager's composed order. The prior re-sort-by-`rerankScore` would have re-promoted `answer` to #1, undoing MMR.
- **Evidence — degraded (kill-switch on):** same query → `debug.rerank:"degraded"`, no `rerankScore` on any result, fail-open to the base order (observable, not a false `"active"`).
- **Regression test:** `tools.test.ts` *"preserves the manager's rerank+MMR order (no re-sort by rerankScore or raw score)"* — verified to **FAIL** on the prior re-sort and **PASS** after the fix (the manager order disagrees with both a `rerankScore` sort and a raw-`score` sort).
- **Observed result after fix:** MMR demoted the near-duplicate `answer.md` (`rerankScore` 0.967) below the diverse `decoy.md` (`rerankScore` 0.823), and `memory_search` **preserved** that composed order — neither `rerankScore`- nor raw-`score`-sorted — so MMR's diversity reorder reaches the tool output; the prior re-sort would have re-promoted `answer`. Kill-switched, the search fails open to the base order (`degraded`).
- **What was not tested:** the qmd backend (out of scope — its own server-side reranker).
- **Limitations:** isolated dev home + local tailnet model, not the production gateway.

## Tests and validation

Which commands did you run?
- `pnpm tsgo:all` → exit 0 (whole monorepo; note `tsgo:core` excludes `extensions/`)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core` → 852 passed
- **Linux Node 24 re-verification** (CI runtime) — committed tree piped via `git archive` into an isolated `node:24` container (no host mount): `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` + `extensions/memory-core` **852 passed** + `tsgo:extensions` prod & test, all green.
- `pnpm test:contracts:plugins` → 935 passed
- `pnpm check:docs` → clean

What regression coverage was added or updated?
- `manager.rerank.test.ts`: rerank reorder, fail-open-on-throw, deadline→abort, invalid-ref reject, empty-return→degraded, no-reranker→disabled.
- `memory-rerank-provider.contract.test.ts` + `loader.runtime-registry.test.ts`: contract reject (undeclared) / allow (declared) / exclusive-slot conflict.
- `memory-state.test.ts`: exclusive-slot register/clear + snapshot round-trip (warm-restart guard).
- `mmr.test.ts` (relevanceScore drives ranking), `hybrid.test.ts` (merge no longer applies MMR), `tools.test.ts` (**rerank+MMR order preserved at the tool boundary** + `debug.rerank` passthrough), `tools.citations.test.ts` (`corpus=all` block-interleave order).

What failed before this fix, if known? N/A (new capability). Unit/contract tests are supplemental to the live proof above.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? **Yes** — a new opt-in stage; no change when no reranker is registered.
Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? **No** — opt-in is registration-based; no new core config; no migration.
Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? **No in core** — core makes no network calls; the (separate) reranker plugin owns its endpoint/auth.
What is the highest-risk area? The fail-open path in `MemoryManager.search` and the new public SDK surface (`MemoryRerankProvider` on `memory-core-host-runtime-core` + the `memoryRerankProviders` manifest contract).
How is that risk mitigated? Aborting deadline + total catch → pre-rerank order on any failure; honest `disabled/active/degraded` state on `status().custom.rerank` + latched warn so a failing reranker is observable, not silent; the ref-based contract makes dropped/duplicated/fabricated results unrepresentable. Branch rebased on latest `main`; `tsgo:all` + memory-core + plugin-contract lanes + `check:docs` all green.

## Current review state

What is the next action? Maintainer review — the implementation is complete, reviewed, rebased on latest `main`, and CI-ready. The remaining open item is the product decision on the new public SDK surface (tracked in #89477).
What is still waiting? Maintainer buy-in on the new public plugin-SDK surface + manifest contract (the direction decision tracked in #89477); the concrete reranker plugin remains a separate deliverable. (#82985 is a complementary, independent optimization — not a competing reranker.)
Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed? ClawSweeper findings addressed across rounds — most recently the **[P1] tool-boundary ordering**: `memory_search` now preserves the manager's composed rerank→MMR order instead of re-sorting by `rerankScore` (which could undo MMR diversity), via a `corpus=all` block-interleave, an MMR-inversion regression test, and the refreshed live proof above ([P2] docs aligned). Earlier rounds: the gate-bypass via the public barrel export (removed), the degraded-reason ordering, the test-API noop, the score-contract completeness, and the `memoryRerankProviders` manifest-gate docs.

prs.title: fix(update): keep repair refusal reason in update history
prs.body:
Closes #182054

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update repair` records only the generic `repair-failed` reason when Doctor refuses to stop a Gateway ancestor process.

## User Impact

User impact: update history keeps the actionable refusal code (for example, `inside-gateway-process-tree`) while reports still identify the failed operation as a repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor now carries the managed-service failure facts it already receives into the maintenance refusal. The report renderer derives repair operation identity from the existing retained `repairing` phase, keeping operation identity separate from the specific failure reason. Generic repair failures remain compatible, and ordinary update failures still render as update failures.

## Evidence

- Dependency-free source-path oracle reproduced the base failure: the producer and finalizer carried failure facts, but Doctor did not forward them.
- The same oracle passes at `a3a842fb584c112f0743d6735059724ded01887e`: Doctor forwards the facts, the retained `repairing` phase identifies a repair, and generic `repair-failed` compatibility remains.
- `git diff HEAD^ HEAD --check` passed.
- Exact-head autoreview completed with no findings (`patch_correctness_confidence: 0.99`), and an independent verifier reported CLEAN through P2 / best-fix.

## Summary

- preserve `blockFailureFacts` through the Doctor refusal boundary
- keep repair/update operation identity separate from the specific refusal code
- cover standalone repair history, ordinary Doctor callers, and renderer controls

## Issue

Closes #182054

## Root cause

`PreManagedServiceStop` recorded the authoritative failure facts and update finalization already collected them, but `assertDoctorMaintenanceInspection` rebuilt `DoctorMaintenanceRefusalError` without forwarding those facts. Once the specific reason was preserved, the report renderer also exposed a coupled assumption: it inferred repair identity only from `reason === "repair-failed"` instead of the retained repair phase.

## Verification

- Before-fix oracle: `doctorForwardsInspectionFacts=false`, exit 1.
- After-fix oracle: `doctorForwardsInspectionFacts=true`, `rendererUsesRepairIdentity=true`, `rendererUsesReasonOnly=false`, `genericRepairCompatibility=true`, exit 0.
- `git diff HEAD^ HEAD --check`: passed.
- Focused Vitest and changed checks were attempted but did not collect because dependencies were unavailable; details are in **Not tested**.

## Before / after

Before: the refusal was saved as `repair-failed`, losing the actionable `inside-gateway-process-tree` fact. A report could only identify repair from that generic reason.

After: the refusal's specific fact is saved, and the existing failed `repairing` phase independently preserves the operation identity. Generic repair failures continue to render as repair failures.

## Risk and scope

Low and bounded to update maintenance refusal propagation/reporting. This uses existing ledger fields and lifecycle phases; it adds no schema, config, protocol, or migration. Production delta is +8/-2 lines; tests are +110/-0 lines.

## Not tested

- Focused Vitest did not collect: `node_modules` was absent, and `pnpm install` failed twice because `@pnpm/macos-arm64@12.15.0` was unavailable from both the configured mirror and the official npm registry.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs ...` likewise stopped before checks because dependencies were absent.
- Blacksmith Testbox did not start because the host had no `blacksmith` binary.
- No packaged or live Gateway run was performed.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**

Preserve the concrete managed-service refusal code through Doctor into update finalization, while continuing to report standalone repair runs as repairs.

**Real environment tested**

An isolated macOS source checkout at exact head `a3a842fb584c112f0743d6735059724ded01887e`, using dependency-free source-path assertions. This was not a live Gateway environment.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**

```bash
node -e 'const fs=require("fs"); const report=fs.readFileSync("src/infra/update-run-report.ts","utf8"); const checks={specificReasonPreserved:/failureFacts:\\s*inspection\\.blockFailureFacts/.test(fs.readFileSync("src/commands/doctor-maintenance-inspection.ts","utf8")),repairIdentityRecorded:/this\\.ownsRepairRun\\s*\\?\\s*"repairing"/.test(fs.readFileSync("src/cli/update-cli/update-finalization-lifecycle.ts","utf8")),rendererUsesRepairIdentity:/steps\\.some\\([\\s\\S]{0,160}step\\.step === "repairing"/.test(report),rendererUsesReasonOnly:/run\\.reason === "repair-failed" \\? "repair" : "update"/.test(report),genericRepairCompatibility:/run\\.reason === "repair-failed" \\|\\|/.test(report)}; checks.fixed=checks.specificReasonPreserved&&checks.repairIdentityRecorded&&checks.rendererUsesRepairIdentity&&!checks.rendererUsesReasonOnly&&checks.genericRepairCompatibility; console.log(JSON.stringify(checks,null,2)); process.exit(checks.fixed?0:1);'
git diff HEAD^ HEAD --check
```

**Evidence after fix**

The oracle printed all required booleans as `true` and `fixed=true`, then exited 0. The diff check produced no output and exited 0. Exact-head autoreview returned `findings: []`.

**Observed result after fix**

The specific refusal code crosses the Doctor owner boundary, and the report derives repair identity from the retained `repairing` phase. The existing generic `repair-failed` path remains supported.

**What was not tested**

No focused Vitest, changed-check lane, Testbox run, packaged CLI run, or live Gateway run completed; the precise environment blockers are listed above.

prs.title: fix(ui): clarify imported insights cluster tabs
prs.body:
Fixes #80301.

## Summary

- Turns the Imported Insights cluster chips into a labeled, more prominent horizontal tab bar.
- Adds cluster counts directly to each tab so users can scan chats, sensitive clusters, and candidate signals before switching.
- Adds ARIA tab semantics with roving focus and keyboard navigation, plus focused Dreaming view regressions.

## Problem summary

Dreaming -> Diary -> Imported Insights already exposed cluster navigation, but the controls were small label-only chips. The useful counts were only visible after selecting a cluster, which made the row easy to miss and hard to scan in large imports.

## Root cause

`renderDiaryImportsSection` reused the generic diary day-chip style and rendered only `cluster.label` in each control. The memory-wiki import insight payload already carries the relevant counts, but the view did not surface them in the navigation row or provide stronger selected/focus semantics for this cluster-switching control.

## Architectural reasoning

This stays entirely in the Control UI presentation layer. The memory-wiki plugin remains the source of cluster data and ordering, the Dreaming controller contract is unchanged, and the view only formats the existing `WikiImportInsightCluster` fields. The patch does not alter runtime behavior outside the Dreaming UI, gateway/session flows, concurrency, cleanup logic, API behavior, or plugin contracts. Sort controls are intentionally not included because the issue discussion calls the exact sort dimensions a product/UX choice; preserving backend order keeps this PR narrow and reviewable.

## Testing performed

Local proof on refreshed head `ab1d6b0f92865eac250049059de1364a459b6480`:

- `pnpm test ui/src/ui/views/dreaming.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed: 16/16.
- `pnpm format:check -- ui/src/ui/views/dreaming.ts ui/src/ui/views/dreaming.test.ts ui/src/styles/dreams.css`
- `pnpm check:changed`
- `pnpm ui:build`
- `git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD`

GitHub Actions on `ab1d6b0f92865eac250049059de1364a459b6480`:

- Workflow Sanity #201587: success
- CI #207301: success

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Imported Insights cluster navigation is now visually prominent, labeled as `Filter by cluster`, shows useful counts in each control, and exposes correct tab selection/focus semantics.

Real environment tested: Local Windows checkout on branch `Hemant/improve-imported-insights-tabs`, Node `v22.15.0` with pnpm running under the repository install and the repo's existing engine warning. The branch was rebased onto upstream/main `11d7499db107f7669d89ead56bf2c5f5187bfe73`, and GitHub reported the PR mergeable after push.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Ran the Dreaming view Vitest file after the rebase with `pnpm test ui/src/ui/views/dreaming.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose`, then ran formatting, changed checks, diff whitespace checks, and the Control UI production build with `pnpm ui:build`. The refreshed GitHub PR checks then passed on the current head SHA.

Evidence after fix: The Dreaming view test asserts the Imported Insights cluster tab label, count-rich tab text, `role="tablist"`/`role="tab"`, `aria-selected`, `aria-controls`, roving `tabIndex`, `role="tabpanel"`, and ArrowRight keyboard navigation from Travel to Health. The production Control UI build also completed successfully, and GitHub Actions passed on the pushed head.

Observed result after fix: The focused Dreaming view test passed with 16 tests, including the keyboard navigation regression. Formatting, changed checks, whitespace checks, Control UI Vite production build, Workflow Sanity, and CI all passed.

What was not tested: I did not attach a live browser screenshot or recording from a real imported ChatGPT dataset. The visual behavior was verified through the jsdom view test harness and production Control UI build; a maintainer or contributor with screenshot upload access should attach redacted UI proof if required by review automation.

## Risk analysis

- Runtime behavior: Limited to Control UI rendering for Dreaming -> Diary -> Imported Insights.
- Concurrency/session/gateway flows: No changes.
- Cleanup/lifecycle handling: No changes.
- API behavior: No public API, gateway protocol, plugin manifest, or controller payload changes.
- Tests: Adds focused coverage for the new tab label/count semantics and keyboard navigation.
- Backward compatibility: Existing memory-wiki data contracts and backend cluster ordering are preserved.
- Developer ergonomics: The count formatter is typed against `WikiImportInsightCluster` and keeps the display logic local to the view.

## Backward compatibility

Backward compatible. Existing Imported Insights data renders through the same `wikiImportInsights.clusters` payload; this only changes presentation and accessibility semantics for the cluster selector.

prs.title: fix(codex): avoid premature post-tool turn timeouts
prs.body:
Related: openai/codex#32659

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running trusted or heavy Codex app-server turns could have a still-running post-tool continuation interrupted after five quiet minutes when the upstream stream had not exposed observable progress.

## Why This Change Was Made

Raises the existing post-tool completion-idle default from 300,000 ms to 600,000 ms while preserving the bounded watchdog and all explicit configuration overrides. The shorter final-assistant release timeout and the 30-minute terminal guard are unchanged.

This PR was prepared with AI assistance; I reviewed and understand the change.

## User Impact

Codex app-server turns now get up to ten quiet minutes to finish post-tool synthesis before OpenClaw interrupts them, reducing premature mid-turn termination without allowing turns to hang indefinitely.

## Evidence

- Redacted production timeline and matching upstream source analysis: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/32659#issuecomment-5018598981
- The affected OpenClaw runtime recorded the following redacted state:
  - Last tool result: `T+0`.
  - Last visible post-tool item completion: `T+25s`.
  - Completion-idle timeout: `300001 ms` later with `timeoutMs=300000`, `completionIdleWatchArmed=true`, `activeAppServerTurnRequests=0`, `activeTurnItemCount=0`, `assistantCompletionIdleWatchArmed=false`, and `terminalIdleWatchArmed=true`.
  - This proves the post-tool guard was armed for the partial-custom-tool gap. The generic completion guard is 60 seconds; the observed 300-second override was the post-tool default changed by this PR.
- Lifecycle source proof:
  - A tool handoff persists in `turnCrossedToolHandoff`, and later reasoning progress or the final non-assistant item arms the post-tool override: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7c39776115fcf8d757fde75356b2a06f92592367/extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-notification-state.ts#L133-L192
  - A completed dynamic-tool response also arms that same override: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7c39776115fcf8d757fde75356b2a06f92592367/extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-server-requests.ts#L331-L345
  - Existing end-to-end tests exercise tool handoff followed by raw/streamed reasoning and assert that the post-tool timeout, not the generic or terminal timeout, is selected: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7c39776115fcf8d757fde75356b2a06f92592367/extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.turn-watches.test.ts#L2770-L2905
- Re-ran the four focused lifecycle cases (`uses the post-tool timeout after...`): all passed.
- Focused timeout resolver tests: 7/7 passed.
- Codex app-server config tests: 126/126 passed.
- Exact-head GitHub CI is green, including `openclaw/ci-gate`.
- Full local changed-file validation passed, including formatting, production/test type checks, extension lint, plugin boundaries, dependency guards, database compatibility, and import-cycle checks.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- OpenClaw's prescribed autoreview was attempted twice; both runs failed inside the Codex review engine before producing structured review output. A manual adjacent-path review found no mismatch across runtime default, manifest schema/help, tests, and docs.

prs.title: chore(ui): retain evidence for descendant PR hydration failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The real-Gateway case “shows three persisted descendant PRs while keeping the parent branch unpublished” intermittently times out with durable receipts present but no hydrated PR metadata. The failures on #181477 and #181868 did not identify which awaited stage stopped progressing.

Related: #181868.

## User Impact

No UI behavior, timeout, assertion, subscription policy, or publication policy changes. The next failure of this one case carries the missing diagnostic evidence in its existing, CI-uploaded `failure.public.json` report.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse Node diagnostic channels and the existing E2E failure-facts recorder. An opt-in Gateway channel marks loader import, checkout context, branch cache/facts, receipt and metadata reads, snapshot publication, and broadcast. The test combines these with the existing Gateway RPC and Git-operation channels and its already-decoded WebSocket messages.

Each stage retains at most 128 Gateway events and 128 subscription frames, with timestamps and eviction counts. The failure-only browser read records the session owner's PR summaries and roster membership for the parent and three descendants, plus badge/card/link projection state. Session keys become indexes (0 = parent, 1–3 = descendants); PR numbers are restricted to the fixture. Titles, URLs, paths, credentials, frame IDs, and payload content are omitted.

Passing runs add only bounded in-memory observations: no extra RPC, browser probe, wait, log, or artifact write. Production channels are inactive without subscribers. The watched-state type moves beside its base type to keep the subscription module within its existing line cap.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Prior investigation, unchanged main | 0/160 local/Linux failures; no root cause claimed |
| Temporary forced failure through the actual case | CI-uploaded public failure report contained 86 Gateway events, 12 subscription frames, four UI session records, and three rendered descendant links; temporary failure removed |
| Unchanged real-Gateway case, both initial and restarted stages | PASS; public-attachment correction was subsequently proved with the forced failure |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` and `pnpm tsgo:core` | PASS |
| Madge import-cycle guard | PASS (0 cycles); CI caught a type-only diagnostic dependency cycle, removed before landing |
| UI E2E typecheck leaf | PASS |
| Scoped oxlint and formatting; `git diff --check` | PASS |
| Independent autoreview, P0–P2 | No actionable findings |
