prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.

prs.title: fix(agents): incrementally append tagged stream snapshots
prs.body:
Closes #175441

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Gateway CPU is blocked for seconds on long replies from tagged-provider streams (`enforceFinalTag`), because the whole reply is re-rendered twice per streamed delta (5.7 s at 32 KB, 22.7 s at 64 KB per #175441).

## User Impact

User impact: long streamed replies from tagged providers no longer stall the Gateway as they grow, so other sessions and clients stay responsive while a reply streams. Streamed output is unchanged; the fast path falls back to the existing extraction whenever it cannot prove an append is equivalent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an incremental fast path for tagged block-reply streaming when `enforceFinalTag` is enabled, so each delta no longer re-extracts the full accumulated text.

- The fast path appends directly only when the existing stream state is known to be verbatim and the incoming delta contains no markup that could invalidate that assumption.
- A trailing reasoning-close guard keeps a later delta from bypassing canonical reconciliation after a `</think>`-style boundary.
- Whenever those invariants do not hold, the canonical extraction/reconciliation path runs as before, so there is still one owner of the resulting stream state.
- Added differential tests cover reasoning-close boundaries, supported close-tag variants, mid-stream chunking/draining, and equivalence with canonical extraction.

Accepted tradeoff: the append-unstable final-answer sanitizer is mutually exclusive with the `enforceFinalTag`/`blockVerbatim` fast path, so the fast path never has to account for it.

## Evidence

- Focused `update-stream-items` test: 48/48 passed.
- Differential fuzzing against canonical extraction: 68,702 steps, 0 mismatches; the fast path was exercised 3,316 times.
- Full embedded-agent-subscribe suite: 35 files / 524 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`: 29 shards passed.
- `oxfmt --check`: passed.
- oxlint: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Autoreview reviewed the diff and the tests/evidence (it did not execute the code) and produced no accepted or actionable findings. Its one P2 finding concerned the append-unstable final-answer sanitizer; it was investigated and disproved because that sanitizer is mutually exclusive with the `enforceFinalTag`/`blockVerbatim` fast path.



### Independent Gateway validation

Independent Gateway validation was performed by @sukhdeepjohar and compared current `main` (`9856f57a828`) with PR head `84273a0c490`, merged onto that `main` without conflicts, using a real `openclaw gateway run` in an isolated Linux container with Node 26.12.0.

The test used the Control UI chat path (`chat.send` → `agent.wait` → final `chat` event). Tagged mode was explicitly enabled through the supported `resolveReasoningOutputMode: () => "tagged"` provider contract via a local `tagstub` plugin whose only hook was that function.

- A probe confirmed that `enforceFinalTag` was active: text outside `<final>` was suppressed, `<final>` content was delivered, and `<think>` content was not delivered.
- Earlier in-process differential testing streamed 1,800 randomized tagged replies through both `main` and this PR; all 1,800 delivered replies matched byte-for-byte.
- In the isolated Gateway run, all 24 measured turns produced byte-identical delivered text between `main` and the PR.
- The tagged-stream tests failed when the production changes were reverted and passed with the changes.
- The full `embedded-agent-subscribe` suite passed on the merged tree: 25 files and 451 tests.
- The focused and broader test results listed above were run separately: 35 files / 524 tests for the contributor's validation and 25 files / 451 tests for this independent Gateway validation.

#### Performance

The following values report **main-thread CPU time from two runs** for each reply size. They are not CPU time and wall-clock time pairs.

| Reply size | `main` CPU, run 1 / run 2 | PR CPU, run 1 / run 2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| 16 KB | 2.1 s / 3.1 s | 1.0 s / 1.9 s |
| 32 KB | 4.8 s / 5.5 s | 1.3 s / 1.5 s |
| 64 KB | 16.6 s / 20.5 s | 2.1 s / 2.9 s |
| 128 KB | 58.7 s / 64.2 s | 3.2 s / 3.6 s |

Additional 128 KB results:

- Wall-clock time: approximately 66–73 seconds on `main` versus approximately 10 seconds with the PR.
- Peak RSS growth: approximately +644 MB to +1,127 MB on `main` versus +15 MB to +47 MB with the PR.
- `/healthz` latency during long tagged replies was substantially lower with the PR.

A 64 KB mixed-content reply containing fences, inline code, lists, and tag-like punctuation mostly exercised the fallback path and had similar costs on both variants, as expected.

#### Reachability and limitations

The bundled providers referenced in #175441 did not reach tagged mode in a Gateway turn in this setup:

- `google-gemini-cli` uses the CLI backend rather than the embedded subscriber.
- The chat path calls `isReasoningTagProvider` without the model API, so `google` resolves to native mode.
- `google-antigravity` also resolved to native mode in this setup.

Therefore, the isolated Gateway run used a local provider plugin that returns `"tagged"`. This exercises the supported SDK contract and the affected production path, but it does not cover a real external provider or a non-chat channel.

prs.title: feat(acpx): let operators keep Gateway env out of ACP agents
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

ACP agents that the acpx plugin starts (Codex, Claude, OpenCode, Pi, ...), their command probes, and the terminals they open inherit the whole Gateway environment, including OpenClaw's own credentials such as `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN`. Operators had no way to take a variable away. acpx now supports two opt-in lists ([openclaw/acpx#897](https://github.com/openclaw/acpx/pull/897)); this PR exposes them as acpx plugin settings, `agentProcessEnvAllow` and `agentProcessEnvBlock`, so operators pass them in config. Both are unset by default, so nothing changes unless an operator sets them.


### acpx dependency (answer to the ClawSweeper P2)

Resolved: [acpx 0.21.0](https://www.npmjs.com/package/acpx/v/0.21.0) is the first published release containing [openclaw/acpx#897](https://github.com/openclaw/acpx/pull/897) (merge `e63ba30` is an ancestor of `v0.21.0`; the 4 commits after it are CI, CLI usage errors, deps and the release). The branch is rebased onto current `main` as two commits (feature, then dependency update) with no GitHub pin and no git-package `allowBuilds` entry anywhere in its history. The dependency commit:

1. Updates `acpx` from `0.19.5` to `0.21.0` in `extensions/acpx/package.json` and the root `package.json`.
2. Refreshes `pnpm-lock.yaml` (`acpx@0.21.0`, integrity `sha512-+X1QZgsb...06Ipg==`, matching the npm registry). acpx's `@openclaw/fs-safe` dependency dedupes onto OpenClaw's existing `0.26.11` and the old `0.22.0` copy is dropped; no other lock entries change.
3. Adds a dated `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` entry for `acpx@0.21.0` (published 2026-10-24T00:42:33Z, inside the 7-day release-age gate; remove after 2026-10-31T00:42:33Z), following the existing reviewed-release entries.

`node scripts/generate-npm-package-lock.mjs --changed` reports `extensions/acpx: npm package lock validated.`

### ClawSweeper test note

The latest review listed `extensions/acpx/src/service.test.ts` as a low-value test (constructor-options assertion duplicating the real-process coverage in `service-env.process.test.ts`). Removed. The real-process test still covers forwarding, the unset default, and the `TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS` grant; `index.test.ts` keeps the native catalog forwarding check, which has no real-process equivalent.

### Why opt-in and not a default block list

[openclaw/acpx#889](https://github.com/openclaw/acpx/pull/889) proposed a default-deny allowlist and was closed with this reason ([comment](https://github.com/openclaw/acpx/pull/889#issuecomment-6294798592)):

> a default-deny allowlist plus `ACPX_AUTH_*` grants is stricter than comparable apps (t3code, Zed, Codex CLI all inherit the host env and layer per-agent env/secrets on top), and the setup cost isn't justified.

So OpenClaw does not hardcode a list either. Operators who want to hide OpenClaw's credentials, or run agents with a strict environment, opt in through config.

### Root Cause

- Before behavior: with a fake `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN` in the Gateway environment, every ACP agent launched by the acpx plugin (startup probe and session) inherits it. On `main` the plugin config schema is a strict object, so `agentProcessEnvBlock` is rejected as an unknown key; there is no supported way to express "do not pass this down".
- Code: `extensions/acpx/src/service.ts` builds `new AcpxRuntime({ agentProcessEnv: resolveAgentProcessEnv(), ... })`. `agentProcessEnv` can add or override names (the `TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS` cap) but cannot remove one. acpx 0.19.5 `buildAgentEnvironment()` starts from `{ ...process.env }`.
- Contract: acpx #897 added `agentProcessEnvAllow` / `agentProcessEnvBlock` to `AcpRuntimeOptions` and `inspectAgentModels()` with order allowlist, then blocklist, then explicit grants last (`ACPX_AUTH_*`, protected auth values, `agentProcessEnv`, persisted session env, a terminal request's own `env`).

### Exact change

- `extensions/acpx/src/config-schema.ts`, `src/config.ts`: two optional `string[]` settings. Each entry must be a non-empty name without `=`, whitespace, or NUL (acpx's own contract is non-empty without `=` or NUL; whitespace is rejected here as a config typo). Default unset.
- `extensions/acpx/src/service.ts`: pass both lists to `AcpxRuntime` next to the existing `agentProcessEnv`, so the `TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS` cap is unchanged and still applies as an explicit grant.
- `extensions/acpx/src/harness.ts`: pass both lists to `inspectAgentModels()` for native-agent model catalog inspection, which also spawns the agent. Without this, the Models page would still start agents with the full environment.
- `extensions/acpx/openclaw.plugin.json`: JSON schema, `agent-runtime` config group, and UI hints (advanced).
- `docs/tools/acp-agents-setup.md`: new "Agent process environment" section with the order and an example blocking `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN`, `OPENCLAW_HOOK_TOKEN`, `OP_CONNECT_TOKEN`, and provider keys, plus the caveats (an agent that needs a blocked provider key cannot authenticate; MCP servers the agent starts, including the OpenClaw tool bridges, normally inherit the agent's environment).
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json`: plugin config surface budget 4804 -> 4808 for the two new settings (regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen` on the rebased tree). They are the only way to use the new acpx capability from OpenClaw config, and both default to unset.
- Dependency bump to acpx `0.21.0` (see above) and `pnpm-lock.yaml`.

### acpx changes pulled in by 0.19.5 -> 0.21.0

20 commits: [compare](https://github.com/openclaw/acpx/compare/v0.19.5...v0.21.0). Released as 0.19.6, 0.20.0 and 0.21.0 (#897 plus CI, CLI usage-error and dependency updates):

- 0.19.6: text and quiet output show structured provider error messages (CLI output only).
- 0.20.0: Octomind built-in agent; permission callbacks may select an exact `optionId` (additive, kind-based decisions unchanged); failed launches and failed discard closes now settle session records as closed; ACP SDK 1.8.0 and `@openclaw/fs-safe` 0.26.x (the lock dedupes acpx onto OpenClaw's existing 0.26.11 and drops 0.22.0).
- #897: the two env lists (opt-in; no default change).

No breaking change for OpenClaw found: the acpx extension suite, the core tests that import acpx, and the extension typechecks pass on this pin. The session-record settling fix is a behavior change in acpx's favor (no stuck open records after a failed launch).

### Scope boundary

- No default change: with neither setting, the runtime receives `undefined` for both and acpx returns the same `{ ...process.env }` copy as before.
- No hardcoded block list, no Doctor migration (new optional keys only), no change to MCP server `env`, `agentProcessEnv`, or the `TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS` cap.
- Classic ACPX CLI usage is unaffected (the CLI does not set these lists).

## Real behavior proof

### Isolated Gateway smoke (built head `4d85ad739`, real Gateway, real ACP agent process)

Behavior: which inherited Gateway env var names reach ACP agent processes started by the acpx plugin, through every spawning entry point: the runtime startup probe, `/acp spawn` sessions, resumed existing sessions, and native model catalog discovery (`models.list` with `refresh: true`, which calls `inspectAgentModels()` from `harness.ts`).

Environment: Linux x64, Node 24.19.0. `pnpm build` in the PR worktree, then `node dist/index.js gateway --port <free loopback port> --bind loopback` with a throwaway `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and config (no real credentials, channels skipped). Driven over the Gateway WebSocket API with an admin operator client: `chat.send` with `/acp spawn probe`, `chat.send` turns into the ACP session, and `models.list {view:"all", refresh:true}`.

Agent: OpenClaw's real stdio ACP fixture agent (`test/fixtures/acp/owner-agent.mjs`) behind a small wrapper that appends the watched names it inherited (names only, never values) to a JSONL file and then runs the fixture. It is configured as the `probe` ACP agent and as a `qwen` native-agent override (other native agents disabled) so native catalog discovery launches it too.

Gateway env: `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN` (fake value generated at runtime, also the Gateway's auth token), `OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_KEPT=1`, `OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_OTHER=1`, `ACPX_AUTH_OCPROOF` (fake, runtime-generated). acpx promotes `ACPX_AUTH_OCPROOF` to `OCPROOF`; OpenClaw sets `TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS` as an explicit `agentProcessEnv` grant for runtime children.

The policy was changed **live** by editing the config file while the same Gateway kept running; each change logged `[reload] config hot reload applied (plugins.entries.acpx.config.agentProcessEnvBlock ...)` and `Plugin replacement applied: acpx`. Each phase then sent a turn to the **same pre-existing ACP session** (spawned in phase A), spawned a **new** session, and refreshed the native catalog. Copied launch records (names only; `at`/`pid` dropped, one line per launch):

```
== A: policy unset (default, before)
probe           OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_KEPT OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_OTHER ACPX_AUTH_OCPROOF OCPROOF TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS PATH HOME
session (new)   OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_KEPT OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_OTHER ACPX_AUTH_OCPROOF OCPROOF TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS PATH HOME
native-catalog  OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_KEPT OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_OTHER ACPX_AUTH_OCPROOF OCPROOF PATH HOME
== B: agentProcessEnvBlock: ["OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN"]   (hot reload)
probe           OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_KEPT OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_OTHER ACPX_AUTH_OCPROOF OCPROOF TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS PATH HOME
session (A, resumed) OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_KEPT OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_OTHER ACPX_AUTH_OCPROOF OCPROOF TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS PATH HOME
session (new)   OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_KEPT OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_OTHER ACPX_AUTH_OCPROOF OCPROOF TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS PATH HOME
native-catalog  OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_KEPT OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_OTHER ACPX_AUTH_OCPROOF OCPROOF PATH HOME
== C: agentProcessEnvAllow: ["OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_KEPT"]   (hot reload; allowlist narrowing)
probe           OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_KEPT ACPX_AUTH_OCPROOF OCPROOF TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS PATH HOME
session (A, resumed) OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_KEPT ACPX_AUTH_OCPROOF OCPROOF TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS PATH HOME
session (new)   OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_KEPT ACPX_AUTH_OCPROOF OCPROOF TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS PATH HOME
native-catalog  OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_KEPT ACPX_AUTH_OCPROOF OCPROOF PATH HOME
== D: allow ["OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN"] + block ["OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN","ACPX_AUTH_OCPROOF","TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS"]   (hot reload)
probe           ACPX_AUTH_OCPROOF OCPROOF TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS PATH HOME
session (A, resumed) ACPX_AUTH_OCPROOF OCPROOF TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS PATH HOME
session (new)   ACPX_AUTH_OCPROOF OCPROOF TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS PATH HOME
native-catalog  ACPX_AUTH_OCPROOF OCPROOF PATH HOME
== E: policy removed again (hot reload)
probe           OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_KEPT OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_OTHER ACPX_AUTH_OCPROOF OCPROOF TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS PATH HOME
session (A, resumed) OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_KEPT OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_OTHER ACPX_AUTH_OCPROOF OCPROOF TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS PATH HOME
session (new)   OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_KEPT OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_OTHER ACPX_AUTH_OCPROOF OCPROOF TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS PATH HOME
native-catalog  OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_KEPT OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_OTHER ACPX_AUTH_OCPROOF OCPROOF PATH HOME
```

(In phase A the probe and the new session were the two launches from the first `/acp spawn`: the probe ran between `embedded acpx runtime backend registered` and `... ready` in the Gateway log.)

Every turn into the phase A session returned the same ACP session id with its full history, so existing sessions keep working across each policy change and are relaunched under the new policy:

```
B {"status":"ok","reply":{"sessionId":"4bdf65c6-...","history":["phase-a-turn","phase-b-existing-session"]}}
E {"status":"ok","reply":{"sessionId":"4bdf65c6-...","history":["phase-a-turn","phase-b-existing-session","phase-c-existing-session","phase-d-existing-session","phase-e-existing-session"]}}
```

Every `models.list` refresh returned the native catalog rows from the probe child: `{"acpCatalogRows":["acp-qwen/initial","acp-qwen/selected"]}`.

Observed:

- Unset: unchanged default, the fake `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN` name reaches every child.
- Block: it reaches none of them (probe, resumed session, new session, native catalog); everything else is still inherited.
- Allow narrowing: only essentials plus the listed name; `OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_OTHER` and the token are gone.
- Explicit grants still pass even when allowed-then-blocked or blocked by name: `ACPX_AUTH_OCPROOF` (and its promoted `OCPROOF`) and the `TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS` grant. Native catalog discovery never receives `TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS` because OpenClaw only sets that grant on runtime children, not on `inspectAgentModels()`.
- Removing the policy restores the default for newly launched children.

### Upgrade from latest stable (openclaw 2026.10.5 + @openclaw/acpx 2026.10.5, acpx 0.19.4)

Same isolated setup, separate throwaway state and port:

1. `npm install openclaw@2026.10.5` into a throwaway prefix, `openclaw plugins install @openclaw/acpx@2026.10.5` into the throwaway state, start that stable Gateway, `/acp spawn probe --bind here`, send `stable-turn-1`, stop.
2. Start the built head Gateway on the **same** state and unchanged config. Head first required the normal upgrade step `openclaw doctor --fix` (agent DB schema migration; unrelated to this PR). After it the acpx plugin config was byte-identical (`acpx config preserved: true`) and `plugins list` resolved `acpx` to the head bundled plugin.
3. Turn into the stable-created bound session, then add `agentProcessEnvBlock: ["OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN"]` live and send another turn and refresh the catalog.

```
head, stable config unchanged:
{"status":"ok","reply":{"sessionId":"89508786-...","history":["stable-turn-1","head-upgrade-turn-1"]}}
session (resumed) OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_KEPT OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_OTHER ACPX_AUTH_OCPROOF OCPROOF TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS PATH HOME
head, after adding agentProcessEnvBlock (hot reload):
{"status":"ok","reply":{"sessionId":"89508786-...","history":["stable-turn-1","head-upgrade-turn-1","head-upgrade-turn-2-blocked"]}}
session (resumed) OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_KEPT OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_OTHER ACPX_AUTH_OCPROOF OCPROOF TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS PATH HOME
native-catalog    OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_KEPT OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_OTHER ACPX_AUTH_OCPROOF OCPROOF PATH HOME
```

Existing settings and the ACP session created by the stable release load and continue on the new acpx dependency with no behavior change until the operator sets a list. Both throwaway Gateways were stopped afterwards.

### In-process service proof (unit level)

Behavior fixed: the environment real ACP agent processes inherit when launched by the acpx plugin service from plugin config.

Environment: Linux x64, Node 24.19.0, pnpm 12.12.1, isolated OpenClaw state (`withOpenClawTestState`), real `createAcpxRuntimeService()` with real acpx (originally the #897 commit; re-run on published 0.21.0, see Verification), and a real stdio ACP fixture agent wrapped by a script that records which watched names it inherited (names only, never values). The fake secret is built at runtime. The startup probe and a real session launch are both recorded.

Command: `pnpm test extensions/acpx/src/service-env.process.test.ts`

```
 ✓ ACP agents inherit only permitted Gateway env with {} 513ms
 ✓ ACP agents inherit only permitted Gateway env with {"agentProcessEnvBlock":["OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN"]} 469ms
 ✓ ACP agents inherit only permitted Gateway env with {"agentProcessEnvAllow":["OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN"],"agentProcessEnvBlock":["OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN"]} 459ms
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

Observed, for both the probe and the session launch:

| Plugin config | Agent inherits (watched names) |
| --- | --- |
| unset | `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN`, `OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_KEPT`, `TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS`, `PATH` |
| `agentProcessEnvBlock: [OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN]` | `OPENCLAW_ACPX_PROOF_KEPT`, `TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS`, `PATH` |
| allow + block the same name | `TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS` (explicit grant), `PATH` (essential) |

Before (same test with the two `service.ts` lines removed, so config is accepted but not passed to the runtime): the block cases fail and the agent still receives `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN`:

```
 ✓ ... with {} 491ms
 × ... with {"agentProcessEnvBlock":["OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN"]} 457ms
 × ... with {"agentProcessEnvAllow":[...],"agentProcessEnvBlock":[...]} 459ms
-  Expected  + Received
+     "OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN",
      Tests  2 failed | 1 passed (3)
```

### Performance

Benchmark: ACP session launch latency through the real service and fixture agent (`ensureSession` with startup probe off), 3 warmup plus 20 samples per run, two rounds, same host. Baseline is the original PR base (`d84c03e3f52`, acpx 0.19.5); head is this branch as first opened (acpx #897 commit). Not re-run after the rebase; the env code path in published 0.21.0 is the same.

| Run | base default | head default | head with 2-name block list |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| round 1 median / p90 (ms) | 127.8 / 132.4 | 123.3 / 138.7 | 117.9 / 133.1 |
| round 2 median / p90 (ms) | 124.3 / 135.6 | 127.5 / 137.2 | 117.9 / 127.3 |

No measurable change on the default path; the difference is within run-to-run noise. The block path is not slower. acpx #897 measured its env construction separately (default path unchanged; opt-in adds one pass over the copied environment).

## What was not tested

- Real vendor ACP adapters (Codex, Claude Code) in the isolated Gateway. The smoke uses the real Gateway, plugin, and acpx runtime with OpenClaw's stdio ACP fixture agent; vendor adapters are spawned through the same acpx environment builder.
- Upgrade proof covers stable 2026.10.5 to this head, not older releases.
- MCP servers launched by an agent under a block or allow list, including the OpenClaw tool bridges. Documented as a caveat; not exercised.
- ACP terminals opened by the agent. Covered by acpx #897's own real-process proof; the fixture agent opens no terminal, so it is not re-run here.
- Windows.
- Local `pnpm check:changed` stops in core oxlint on `max-lines` in files this PR does not touch (`src/gateway/session-worktree-preparation.ts`, `src/gateway/session-utils-row.ts`, `src/gateway/node-registry-private.ts`, `src/agents/tools/sessions-spawn-visible.ts`, `src/agents/tools/sessions-spawn-tool.ts`, `src/agents/sessions/session-manager.ts`); the root `package.json` change widens the changed-check to all core lint shards. PR CI is the broad proof.

## Verification

Rebased head `4f2266f21f9` on `main` `59e9f2ece84` (Linux x64, Node 26.12.1, pnpm 12.15.0):

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`: lockfile passes supply-chain policies (1837 entries, default strict `minimumReleaseAge` config). Note for whoever refreshes this lock later: a plain strict `pnpm install --lockfile-only` resolved acpx's `@openclaw/fs-safe@^0.26.7` to the too-new `0.26.7` instead of reusing the excluded `0.26.11`; the lock was regenerated with `pnpm install --lockfile-only --config.minimum-release-age=0` (resolution only) and then verified by the strict frozen install above.
- `pnpm test extensions/acpx`: 27 files, 180 tests passed; database-worker project 8 files, 58 tests passed (includes `service-env.process.test.ts` against published acpx 0.21.0).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions && pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: clean.
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on touched files: clean.
- `pnpm config:docs:check`: OK.
- `node scripts/generate-npm-package-lock.mjs --changed`: `extensions/acpx: npm package lock validated.`
- Earlier head (before rebase): `pnpm test src/acp/runtime/session-meta-doctor.test.ts src/agents/harness/acp-native-execution.process.test.ts` (core tests that import acpx): 24 passed; `pnpm check:docs`: clean.

### CI on `4f2266f21f9`

All checks pass except three `checks-node-changed-*` shards (and `openclaw/ci-gate`, which aggregates them). The dependency change puts this PR's changed-test lane on `OPENCLAW_CI_TEST_RUNTIME_POLICY: bun-all`, so these e2e files run under the pinned OpenClaw Bun (`openclaw-v1.4.4-20261019-ef37c31de3`). They failed the same way on the first attempt and on a `gh run rerun --failed`, and they fail identically on the base commit `59e9f2ece84` with no PR changes (acpx 0.19.5), so they are pre-existing Bun failures on `main`, not caused by this PR:

- `checks-node-changed-11`: `test/cli-json-stdout.hooks.e2e.test.ts` > "configured remote Gateway missing its URL": stderr prints the error with literal `\n` escapes under Bun instead of line breaks.
- `checks-node-changed-10`: `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/telegram-model-picker-prepared-gateway.e2e.test.ts` > "recovers a replaced model catalog and drains the following Telegram callback".
- `checks-node-changed-16`: `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/gateway-timeout-recovery-subagent.e2e.test.ts` > "delivers a child completion once while parent timeout recovery is active".

Local reproduction with the CI Bun staged by `scripts/stage-openclaw-bun.sh` and `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun pnpm test <the three files>`: this head, 3 failed (same assertions as CI); base `59e9f2ece84` after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (acpx 0.19.5), 3 failed, 24 passed (27).

prs.title: refactor: localize single-consumer internal owner frames
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Internal helpers, type leaves, and one-consumer modules make their callers harder to follow without providing a separate ownership boundary.

## What Changed

Keep Gateway terminal and status preparation, channel rendering/context preparation, and action-target normalization with their existing consumers. Localize private agent-core launch, stream-update, and interrupted-context preparation frames. Put Copilot rich usage, ClawHub request/error preparation, and Teams presentation selection directly in their existing owners. Retain shared operations and move useful private-helper assertions to production entry points.

Net production reduction: **151 lines across 29 paths** (568 additions / 719 deletions against the branch base). Moved bodies count as additions. Tests shrink by 42 net lines across 11 paths; retained contracts move to real command, handler, and message-projection boundaries rather than test-only production exports.

No user-visible feature, text, configuration, CLI, protocol, public package or Plugin SDK contract changes. Lazy imports, security/approval checks, resource bounds, persistence and shutdown settlement remain. The standalone session memory backend is untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

No rare-failure guard is removed. Bodies and decisions remain at the same preparation/effect points. The localized agent-core cursor uses its existing typed `kind` discriminant to distinguish prepared calls from finalized argument-validation outcomes; malformed hybrid internal objects are not an added compatibility contract. Function/profiling frame identities are not preserved.

## Evidence

Every changed owner has focused tests and targeted native types, typed lint, format and line-cap proof. Migrated cases pass on unchanged production before the cutover. Later packets include 186 action-normalization/dispatch cases, 29 Google Chat cases, 58 scheduling/stream cases, 27 Copilot cases, 48 ClawHub cases, and 29 Teams cases. The final interruption cut passes all 29 steering cases plus the real abort-and-continue and staged-delta cases. No timeout, retry, skip or suppression is added.

Tests run serially with one worker and isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG state. Latest wrapper times: ClawHub 4.41 seconds, Teams 30.42 seconds, Copilot 16.84 seconds, steering 3.63 seconds and selected public loop cases 6.24 seconds. Migrated Matrix handler proof takes 42.99 seconds including worker setup; the production-handler import graph dominates and is necessary to replace the private helper seam. Other focused boundary runs are recorded in the preparation evidence. Hosted CI seconds are pending.

Final push guards pass: format parity, assertion safety, lint suppressions, mock exports, wrapper/eager-import closure, frozen updater bindings, prompt-prefix stability and line caps. Runtime and static import cycles are both zero. Whole-candidate independent review through P2 has no accepted actionable findings. Hosted exact-head CI is the broad proof. No local build, broad suite, whole-graph typecheck, live provider/channel, pixel, performance or native-device verification is claimed. Existing dependency and Plugin SDK deprecation warnings remain unsuppressed.

prs.title: test: compare saved-session metadata authority refreshes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

This was opened as an **unmeasured synthetic investigation, not a merge candidate**. The comparison is now measured and rejected. It tested whether full saved-session `chat.metadata` requests repeat an authority refresh that contributes no prepared result.

## User Impact

The candidate failed its predeclared acceptance rule and will not land. The candidate applies only to metadata requests that include models; the current Control UI commands-only request keeps its existing guard. This diagnostic-only commit must never merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

The candidate moves the empty authority refresh into the commands-only branch. Full reads immediately perform a separate authority refresh around private projection preparation, followed by the existing final consumption guard.

A temporary byte-identical copy of the runtime at `d355f2fd148dd68486d863aba8b510adfa8005c2` supplies the baseline. The existing isolated, non-minimal Gateway fixture routes real saved-session WebSocket requests through each runtime. The comparison forwards lifecycle events to both owners and asserts identical responses. The baseline copy and measurement instrumentation will be removed before any real fix is proposed for landing.

## Evidence

Independent source review and AutoReview found no blocking defects. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Dependency-backed local tests were not run because this checkout has no qualified dependencies; normal PR CI is the approved execution route. No production data or traffic is involved.

Acceptance rule, recorded before the first measurement:

- Workload: the committed `src/gateway/server.chat-metadata-boundary.test.ts` comparison, through `sessions.create` and real `chat.metadata` WebSocket requests.
- Six alternating baseline/candidate pairs per cell: models included/omitted, each with cold metadata-owner state and warm metadata-owner state. Shared dependencies remain warm in both cases. Requests run serially; host parallelism and load are logged. The existing metadata-change event retires dispatcher response reuse before every sample, outside the timed region; each sample must enter the metadata runtime exactly once.
- Full metadata must perform exactly one fewer authority refresh per request; commands-only counts and all paired response payloads must remain unchanged.
- Full warm runtime median must improve by at least 10%. Report runtime and RPC latency plus main-thread CPU median, p95, min/max and sample count for every cell. Any 20% or greater adverse movement in a comparable median or p95 rejects the candidate; six-sample tails remain descriptive, not production percentile evidence.
- CI must select and execute this exact test and emit `CHAT_METADATA_REFRESH_COMPARISON`. Aggregate green alone is insufficient. If it does not execute or the rule fails, no optimization will land on this evidence.

Rerun command: `pnpm test src/gateway/server.chat-metadata-boundary.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Local wall time remains unmeasured. The first CI execution spent 1.514s in the comparison before its assertion and 15.55s in the two-test file including setup; the repaired comparison took 2.901s in CI. The fixture is temporary investigation code, not a permanent addition to the per-PR suite.

This does not establish a cause for historical multi-second worker delivery delays, and introduces no protocol, schema, retention, timeout, retry, or cache change.

### First CI attempt: fixture failure, no performance conclusion

At head `ca51bda41d604094762d481616b0e855721f0424`, [the selected Gateway job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40052966545/job/120749786001) executed this exact test and failed its refresh-count assertion: difference 16, expected 1. The existing lifecycle test passed. No comparison measurement payload was emitted. A separate lint job also found a shadowed fixture `options` parameter; it was renamed without changing behavior.

The diagnostic overlooked the dispatcher's one-second sharing of identical `chat.metadata` responses: a second sample could reuse the first response without entering the runtime. The fixture repair uses the existing metadata-change broadcast to invalidate that response before each request and asserts one runtime invocation per sample. The original one-refresh reduction, response-equivalence and timing acceptance rules are unchanged. Fresh independent review and AutoReview passed for the repaired fixture at `ef838e48b90c138c3aba01a6984ac26b9204fb0c`; exact-head execution completed successfully, producing the results below. The repaired test SHA256 is `9880a32b3b7c69d4b15d8c3ff6a2a11cdaa2fc5f630932ca5689d5e756397819`.

### Measured result: rejected, no merge

The [exact-head Gateway job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40053657430/job/120752147503) passed at `ef838e48b90c138c3aba01a6984ac26b9204fb0c`. It selected and executed the real WebSocket comparison (2.901s) and existing lifecycle regression (0.951s), emitting all 48 samples. Every sample entered the runtime exactly once; all paired payloads matched.

Full cold requests used 16 → 15 authority refreshes; full warm requests used 7 → 6. Commands-only requests remained at 1 → 1. Host: 8 available CPUs, load average 2.33 / 0.81 / 0.30. Each row below contains six samples. Values are median / p95 (min–max); p95 is nearest-rank and equals the maximum for six samples.

| Models | Owner state | Variant | Runtime ms | RPC ms | Thread CPU µs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| full | cold | baseline | 19.687 / 47.767 (18.254–47.767) | 26.646 / 54.072 (22.027–54.072) | 26200.500 / 52388.000 (22266.000–52388.000) |
| full | cold | candidate | 18.404 / 20.055 (14.441–20.055) | 23.758 / 24.638 (20.135–24.638) | 23054.500 / 26193.000 (20178.000–26193.000) |
| full | warm | baseline | 2.974 / 4.172 (2.571–4.172) | 7.694 / 9.350 (6.036–9.350) | 7995.500 / 12000.000 (3997.000–12000.000) |
| full | warm | candidate | 2.620 / 4.415 (2.041–4.415) | 6.842 / 8.785 (5.477–8.785) | 4000.000 / 8002.000 (3309.000–8002.000) |
| commands | cold | baseline | 6.186 / 7.038 (4.781–7.038) | 9.513 / 15.035 (8.620–15.035) | 9201.500 / 15130.000 (7935.000–15130.000) |
| commands | cold | candidate | 5.734 / 6.582 (5.110–6.582) | 10.563 / 11.047 (9.908–11.047) | 11075.000 / 11897.000 (10246.000–11897.000) |
| commands | warm | baseline | 0.416 / 0.489 (0.356–0.489) | 3.711 / 5.347 (2.152–5.347) | 4000.000 / 4389.000 (0.000–4389.000) |
| commands | warm | candidate | 0.410 / 0.462 (0.370–0.462) | 3.068 / 4.360 (2.396–4.360) | 3953.000 / 4354.000 (3639.000–4354.000) |

Full warm runtime median improved 11.90% (2.974 → 2.620ms), with runtime p95 increasing 5.83%. However, commands-only cold thread CPU median increased **20.36%** (9201.5 → 11075µs). That crosses the predeclared 20% rejection threshold even though the commands-only code path is unchanged. This short, noisy sample does not establish a causal regression, but it fails the required evidence rule; it is not permission to discard the cell or retry for a preferable result.

Disposition: close unmerged; no optimization, diagnostic, or baseline carrier from this PR will land. The result does not reproduce a multi-second production delay.

prs.title: perf(sessions): reduce retained transcript worker memory
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Transcript reader workers retain Gateway setup, provider/plugin discovery, and unrelated host code in every isolate because their read graph crosses host-owned barrels and shares build chunks with the main runtime.

## User Impact

Lower memory use for retained transcript workers, with the same history, context, usage, and memory-indexing behavior. No configuration, database migration, or public API change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Separate existing read operations from restoration, deletion, discovery, and host cleanup; migrate all internal callers to their owning modules. Memory snapshot and file rendering share one renderer. Register transcript workers in the existing standalone build registry, preserving lazy read handlers in private chunks. The existing graph guard is unchanged and now enforces the boundary.

The row-normalization and window-created-at helpers already have pure source owners; the unwanted coupling was introduced by the shared output chunk. Standalone output fixes that coupling without adding another helper or compatibility facade.

## Measurement

Two simultaneous, CPU-pinned baseline/candidate pairs, with placements swapped in the second pair; the shared production guard passed both. Each side served the same synthetic 5,000-session / 6,000-run fixture, 70 clients and eight streams for 20 measured rounds (160 turns). Baseline binaries are `b84d549973eb`; candidate binaries use that baseline plus this reviewed runtime refactor and reader-boundary fixes. Exact rebased PR heads are validated separately by CI. Heap snapshots run in separate diagnostic pairs, never in latency/GC acceptance runs.

| Diagnostic memory | Pair 1 baseline → candidate | Pair 2 baseline → candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mean final sampled heap per active transcript isolate (8 per side) | 46.78 → 37.84 MiB | 45.57 → 36.61 MiB |
| History post-snapshot heap | 49.51 → 38.57 MiB | 49.45 → 38.52 MiB |
| Transcript-hydration post-snapshot heap | 53.27 → 36.73 MiB | 53.26 → 36.73 MiB |
| Usage post-snapshot heap | 37.09 → 33.59 MiB | 36.90 → 33.50 MiB |
| History source-string estimate | 19.84 → 16.65 MiB | 19.84 → 16.65 MiB |
| History code-node self size | 12.47 → 10.58 MiB | 12.44 → 10.54 MiB |

Mean sampled active-isolate heap falls about **19.4%**, or **8.95 MiB per isolate** in this fixture. The memory preload adds common observer/TypeScript-loader overhead; these are diagnostic figures, not production projections. Source-string size uses a heuristic string-self-size classifier, not a complete source census. Snapshot self sizes are distinct from JavaScript heap used. Startup is measured as constructor-to-first-task dispatch, including host dispatch delay. The corrected observer and swapped confirmation pass recorded eight initial workers per side: **213.625 → 205.000 ms** in pair 1 and **173.500 → 162.375 ms** in pair 2. Paired mean change is **−5.22% / −9.875 ms**. Both placements completed without guard interruption. These eight-sample means support no p95/p99 claim; this is not a pure module-import or readiness-handshake timer.

| Acceptance timing | Pair 1 baseline → candidate | Pair 2 baseline → candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Client history p99 | 546.54 → 528.77 ms (n=1043/1043) | 1036.23 → 1041.35 ms (n=1077/1094) |
| Client session-list p99 | 409.32 → 406.25 ms (n=1023/1023) | 989.36 → 936.25 ms (n=1058/1076) |
| Client session-diff p99 | 440.60 → 484.52 ms (n=1042/1042) | 1004.95 → 953.84 ms (n=1077/1094) |

prs.title: feat(plugin-runtime): support declarative tools and single-attempt completions
prs.body:
Related: #111889

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin authors can use `api.runtime.llm.complete`, but the helper cannot currently expose declarative tool schemas, return structured tool calls, or request zero SDK retries. Plugins that need a deterministic single-attempt decision must therefore bypass the supported runtime helper or weaken that execution contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

This extends the existing host-owned simple-completion path with optional `tools` and `maxRetries` inputs and a normalized `toolCalls` result. Tool schemas are passed to the model but never executed by the helper; omitted options preserve current provider defaults and behavior.

Invalid retry counts fail before model preparation or provider dispatch. The implementation retains the existing authority, model-selection, reasoning, authentication, usage-normalization, and audit paths.

## User Impact

Plugin developers can implement caller-controlled tool loops while keeping model preparation and credentials inside OpenClaw. Setting `maxRetries: 0` requests one provider/SDK attempt on transports that honor the option.

There is no change for existing callers that omit the new options.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(signal): reject hex/exponent text-style span offsets
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Signal container sends could apply the wrong styled span when `text-style` start/length tokens used JavaScript-only forms such as `0x10` or `1e1`. Those tokens were coerced with `Number(...)` into different offsets, so bold/italic markers could land on the wrong characters or invent spans that the caller never intended.

## Why This Change Was Made

Parse `text-style` `start`/`length` at the canonical Signal container translation boundary (`containerRpcRequest` → `/v2/send`) with the same `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` helper already used for container quote timestamps. The parser lives in `client-container-text-style.ts` so oversized `client-container.ts` stays LOC-neutral.

Boundaries: no config keys; no native signal-cli path; incomplete `start:length:style` entries still drop the same way.

Collision check: searched open PRs for `path:extensions/signal/src/client-container.ts` and `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger text-style` — **0** competing PRs. Open Signal PRs #101380 / #100906 do not touch `text-style` `Number()` parsing.

## User Impact

- **Before:** `0x10:4:ITALIC` silently styled offset 16; `1e1:2:BOLD` silently styled offset 10; fractional lengths like `1.5` were accepted.
- **After:** Non-decimal tokens are dropped (same drop path as incomplete entries). Ordinary decimal spans such as `0:4:BOLD` are unchanged. All-invalid lists omit `text_mode=styled` and keep the plain message.

## Evidence

Exact product head: `5904fe91e4f642e338c56a04735812cae92fd1ef`

## Verification

- Exact product head: `5904fe91e4f642e338c56a04735812cae92fd1ef`

- Mutation: temporarily replace `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` with `Number()` → **17 tests fail**; restore → 99/99 pass.

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior addressed

Hex/exponent/fraction `text-style` start/length tokens were silently coerced by `Number()`, shifting style spans. After fix, `parseContainerTextStyleEntry` rejects non-decimal forms via `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger`, matching the existing quote-timestamp contract and upstream signal-cli decimal `start:length:STYLE` grammar.

### Real env tested

- Hosted runner: GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest` (run `29426993121`)
- Node: v22.22.3
- Product head: `5904fe91e4f642e338c56a04735812cae92fd1ef`

### Exact commands run

```bash
SIGNAL_CONTAINER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080 node --import tsx scripts/proof-signal-text-style-real-container.mts
```

### Observed output after fix

- `/v1/about`: `{"versions":["v1","v2"],"build":2,"mode":"native","version":"0.100",...}`
- Mixed spans: wire `message="**Bold** text here"` + `text_mode="styled"` (hex/exponent/fraction dropped); real container `HTTP 400` `User +15555550100 is not registered.` (JSON accepted, account gate rejected — expected without a linked device)
- All-invalid: plain `message="Bold text here"`, no `text_mode`; same real `HTTP 400`
- Valid decimals: styled markers + `text_mode="styled"`; same real `HTTP 400`
- Docker GIN log shows three real `POST /v2/send` hits
- Assertions: **31 passed, 0 failed**

### What was not tested

- End-to-end delivery/rendering on a linked Signal device (no registered number in CI). Real container image + `/v2/send` acceptance path is covered; device delivery remains optional maintainer follow-up.

## Risk / Compatibility

- **Risk:** `merge-risk: compatibility` — intentionally stops accepting previously coerced hex/exponent/fraction offset strings.
- **Why acceptable:** Upstream/docs use decimal integers; sibling quote parsing is already strict; invalid tokens already had a drop path for incomplete entries; decimal spans unchanged.
- **Mitigation:** focused unit + real `bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api` `/v2/send` wire proof + mutation.

prs.title: fix(ui): explain replace-mode filtering in model picker
prs.body:
Closes #104545

## What Problem This Solves

When `models.mode` is `replace`, the configured model catalog is intentionally filtered, but the Control UI model picker did not explain why models were missing or provide a direct path to manage provider models. The hint must also disappear when the catalog is cleared or the Gateway disconnects.

## What Changed

- Add optional `catalogMode: "replace"` metadata to configured `models.list` responses.
- Derive the metadata from the source configuration snapshot and require at least one source-authored provider row.
- Keep public model projection separate from internal provider configuration.
- Carry the metadata through shared Control UI model state.
- Show a replace-mode hint and `Manage models` link to `/settings/model-providers`.
- Clear the catalog and its replace-mode state together on disconnected refreshes.

prs.title: fix: prevent Web Push broadcasts from spiking outbound requests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

- **Affected surface / workflow:** Web Push broadcasts sent to all registered browser and device subscriptions.
- **Root cause, in product terms:** one broadcast eagerly opened every outbound push request at once, so peak encryption, socket, and upstream-request load grew directly with the subscription count.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** operators with many browser, device, or team subscriptions could see avoidable resource spikes during a single broadcast.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.
- **Complete shipped solution:** schedule sends through the shared ordered concurrency worker with a limit of 12; pass VAPID identity per request; remove expired subscriptions in one compare-before-clear state update.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** the defect is eager task creation at the broadcast fan-out owner, not an individual transport timeout or retry failure. Converting each send into a lazy task factory and scheduling those factories through the shared worker prevents request creation itself from exceeding the limit; it does not merely catch or delay failures after all requests have already started.
- **Key design boundary / source of truth:** `broadcastWebPush()` is the sole owner of broadcast scheduling; `runTasksWithConcurrency()` is the repository source of truth for ordered bounded async execution; the installed `web-push` implementation documents and reads `options.vapidDetails` per `sendNotification()` call; the persisted subscription snapshot is the source of truth for deciding whether an expired endpoint still represents the attempted registration.
- **Non-goals / what did not change:** no new configuration, API, payload, subscription format, retry policy, browser service-worker behavior, or Web Push delivery semantics. Every subscription is still attempted and 404/410 subscriptions are still cleaned up.
- **Out-of-scope boundary:** this PR does not change automatic notification policy, Control UI subscription UX, service-worker display behavior, public push-provider integrations, VAPID key generation/storage format, or delivery retry/backoff. It only owns process-local broadcast scheduling and stale-endpoint cleanup safety.
- **Related open PR scan:** refreshed GitHub searches for `push-web.ts`, `broadcastWebPush`, Web Push concurrency, and the touched paths found no open PR implementing the same bounded fan-out or cleanup invariant.
- **Compatibility, merge-risk, or maintainer-decision notes:** no public or persisted schema change and no migration/default change. Existing stored subscriptions and VAPID keys are read unchanged. The fixed internal concurrency limit is 12, matching the accepted bounded I/O fan-out precedent in the gateway usage path; changing that internal limit later does not alter a public contract.
- **Risk labels considered:** concurrency and outbound message-delivery behavior.
- **Risk explanation:** bounded scheduling introduces multiple send waves, so the patch passes VAPID details per request rather than relying on mutable module-global state; expired cleanup compares the attempted snapshot so an in-flight 404/410 cannot delete a refreshed registration.
- **Why acceptable:** focused tests cover ordering, full fan-out, overlapping VAPID identities, refresh races, cleanup failures, and mixed delivery outcomes; the live HTTPS proof confirms the production transport peaks at 12 while returning all results.

## User Impact

- **Users/operators/developers can now:** broadcast to large subscription sets without opening all outbound HTTPS push requests simultaneously.
- **Existing behavior preserved:** all subscriptions are attempted, result ordering is preserved, individual failures remain best effort, and expired subscriptions are removed.
- **What was not tested or remains unavailable:** no public push-provider account or physical browser notification was used. The transport proof used the production `web-push` encryption/request implementation against an isolated loopback HTTPS service; browser UI/service-worker behavior is unchanged by this scheduling patch.

## Evidence

### Focused test file that validates the fix

- **`src/infra/push-web.test.ts`** — drives the production broadcast owner `broadcastWebPush()` (imported from `src/infra/push-web.ts`) over a real SQLite subscription store in a tmpdir, exercising the same `runTasksWithConcurrency` scheduling path used in production.
  - *"bounds concurrent sends while delivering to every subscription"* — registers 20 subscriptions (above the `WEB_PUSH_SEND_CONCURRENCY = 12` cap), wraps `webPush.sendNotification` to track `inFlight` and `maxInFlight`, then asserts `results.length === 20`, every result `ok`, `maxInFlight <= 12`, and `maxInFlight > 1`. Proves the production scheduler caps peak outbound requests at 12 while still attempting every subscription.
  - *"passes VAPID details per send without mutating shared global state"* — asserts `webPush.setVapidDetail` is never called and every `sendNotification` call carries its own `options.vapidDetails.subject`. Proves concurrent broadcasts cannot clobber module-global VAPID state.
  - *"does not delete a subscription re-registered during an expired send"* / *"does not delete an expired subscription after a legacy claim appears"* — prove the compare-before-clear cleanup keeps a refreshed registration alive. *"keeps completed delivery results when expired-subscription cleanup fails"* proves a cleanup persistence failure does not discard successful delivery results.

### What the test proves about production behavior

- A Web Push broadcast to N subscriptions never opens more than 12 outbound HTTPS push requests at once; the remaining sends are scheduled as lazy task factories through the shared ordered concurrency worker. All subscriptions are still attempted, results are returned in order, VAPID identity is passed per request (no global mutation), and expired 404/410 endpoints are cleaned up only when the snapshot still matches the attempted registration.

### Test results

- **Vitest run (real execution against the production broadcast owner):** `pnpm exec vitest run src/infra/push-web.test.ts` → **17 passed (17/17), 1 test file passed, exit 0.** Re-verified at the current PR head; all 17 tests green.
- **Repository lint:** `pnpm lint --threads=8` → exit 0.

### Production HTTPS transport transcript (current head, after conflict resolution)

- Re-ran the loopback HTTPS transport proof on the **current PR head `de9c69f49530013b9ce3c5a09e36e93d0e481e9f`** (Node v24.18.0, SQLite 3.53.1). Real `web-push` `sendNotification` over HTTPS, NO mock. Registered 25 subscriptions pointing at a loopback HTTPS server: 23 ok (201), 1 gone (410), 1 missing (404). The broadcast attempted every subscription, peaked at 12 concurrent in-flight HTTPS requests (cap = 12, so bounded and concurrency genuinely occurred), returned 23 ok + 2 failed, and cleaned up both expired (410/404) subscriptions, leaving 23 retained. Full redacted transcript below.

### Additional evidence

- **Environment:** Windows Git Bash, Node v24.18.0, exact synced PR head `de9c69f49530013b9ce3c5a09e36e93d0e481e9f`, current main base `ffc8051cacb50d1f4b39cc2c6f822083caba1f2a`.
- **Commands run after this patch:** `pnpm exec vitest run src/infra/push-web.test.ts`; `pnpm lint --threads=8`; earlier exact-patch validation also ran `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, targeted `oxfmt`/`oxlint`, `git diff --check`, and production `broadcastWebPush()` through a local HTTPS push-service fixture.
- **Review findings addressed, if any:** current RF-001 fixed — synced current main, which contains the unrelated Telegram lint repair, and reran exact-head focused tests plus repository lint. Current RF-002 disclosed — related storage refactor PR #103294 remains open; this branch still preserves bounded scheduling and compare-before-clear cleanup, and those invariants must be retained if a later conflict is resolved after #103294 lands.
- **Regression guardrail:** the suite fails if task factories become eager, peak concurrency exceeds 12, any subscription result is dropped/reordered, global VAPID state leaks between broadcasts, stale cleanup removes a refreshed registration, or cleanup persistence failure discards successful delivery results.
- **Patch quality notes:** two focused files; no dependency, lockfile, config, schema, or public API changes. Maintainer edits remain enabled.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** high for the changed transport behavior; current-head local proof is inspectable below, and the previous current-head hosted CI suite had no code failures.

Focused regression transcript:


No endpoint URLs, VAPID keys, certificate material, tokens, or non-loopback addresses are included. The self-signed certificate and disabled verification were confined to the loopback fixture process.

prs.title: fix(gateway): tools.github.configure failures now log the real cause before the generic response
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #181165

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where operators running the GitHub identity setup flow (Control UI / CLI save path) would only ever see the generic "GitHub identity setup failed" response: every failure inside `tools.github.configure` — a missing `gh` CLI, an expired one-use handoff, an installer failure — collapsed into the same opaque message with zero cause-bearing log lines on the Gateway host, forcing reproduce-and-guess triage (10/10 failures in the reporter's session left no cause in the journal).
- **Related:** #135028 (its fix surfaced `GitHubCliUnavailableError` on the sibling `tools.github.authorize.start` path but left the `configure` catch unchanged); #140576 (different defect on the same UI surface). Fix signal labels: `clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear`, `clawsweeper:source-repro`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** bind the caught error and log it server-side so Gateway diagnostics record the real cause; the client-facing response stays byte-identical.
- **Logging contract:** the cause is formatted with the shared normalization formatter from `@openclaw/normalization-core/error-coercion` (no redaction callback — the same raw formatter the sibling `src/gateway/server-methods/agents-delete-drain.ts` catch path uses) instead of the pre-redacting wrapper in `src/infra/errors.ts`. The owner-only file record keeps the raw cause text (deployment-specific `logging.redactPatterns` can no longer erase diagnostics before storage), and masking is retained at the subsystem logger's console/egress boundary.
- **Out of scope:** mapping `GitHubIdentityError` to more specific client error codes (explicitly named a possible follow-up in the issue); no change to the credential lifecycle or response shape.
- **Highest-risk area:** credential material in the new log line. **How is that risk mitigated?** The handler hands the raw cause to the logging owner, which stores it in the owner-only file record and redacts its console/egress presentation; the regression test rejects with a token-bearing error and asserts the raw text reaches the logging owner intact (a pre-redacting formatter collapses `token=ghp_…` text, so the test discriminates the two implementations).

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** any `tools.github.configure` failure now produces a `tools-github: GitHub identity setup failed: <cause>` warn record in Gateway diagnostics while the client response remains `UNAVAILABLE "GitHub identity setup failed"`, letting operators distinguish a missing `gh` CLI, an expired handoff, and hard failures by reading one log line.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.ts` (the configure catch block); regression tests `logs the setup failure cause while responding with the generic error` and `hands the raw cause to the logging owner without pre-redaction` in `src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.test.ts`; the committed real-transport proof `test/pr181208-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts`.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** yes — a real Gateway server was booted over its shipped WebSocket RPC transport in an isolated state directory (token auth, isolated `HOME`, isolated config/workspace dirs), and the `tools.github.configure` request was sent through that live transport with a well-formed but never-registered one-use handoff, before and after the patch (committed proof: `test/pr181208-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts`).
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # red on base: revert the handler to unpatched main, run both regression layers
  git checkout origin/main -- src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.test.ts       # 2 failed | 12 passed
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/pr181208-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts          # FAIL: no tools-github cause record
  # green with the patch applied
  git checkout HEAD -- src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.test.ts       # 14/14 passed
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/pr181208-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts          # 1/1 passed
  # targeted type checks on the rebased head
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-methods.json --builders 1   # passed
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.e2e.json --builders 1               # passed
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.config-cli.json --builders 1        # passed
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:** (running isolated Gateway, shipped WS RPC transport, missing one-use handoff)
  ```text
  client RPC rejection:            {"code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"GitHub identity setup failed"}
  owner-only file record (WARN):   {"subsystem":"tools-github","message":"GitHub identity setup failed: temporary GitHub credential is unavailable"}
  console presentation (egress):   [tools-github] GitHub identity setup failed: temporary GitHub credential is unavailable
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** the missing-handoff failure cause now appears in the owner-only Gateway diagnostics file record and on the operator console, and the client response is byte-identical to before (`UNAVAILABLE "GitHub identity setup failed"` envelope, no cause text in the RPC response). On unpatched base the identical live-Gateway request produced only the generic `gateway/ws` response line — no `tools-github` cause record anywhere in the gateway log, matching the journal behavior reported in the issue.
- **What was not tested:** the Control UI save flow end to end (the RPC layer it calls is exercised by the committed proof), and a production systemd-deployed Gateway host (the proof boots an isolated real Gateway process with the same shipped transport, handler, and logging owners).
- **Proof tier:** L2+ — deterministic real-Gateway runtime output through the shipped RPC transport, captured before/after via a committed e2e proof plus unit regression tests (both verified RED on base).
- **Review state:** CI lanes pending on the rebased head.

prs.title: fix(config): prune orphan model refs when provider is missing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When external tools like `cc-switch` remove a provider from `models.providers`, they leave orphan model references in:
- `agents.defaults.models` allowlist (map keys like `mycodex/gpt-5.5`)
- `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks` and per-agent fallback arrays
- `hooks.mappings[].model`, `hooks.gmail.model`
- `messages.tts.summaryModel`
- `channels.modelByChannel` and `channels.discord.voice.model`

This causes "ghost entries" that point to non-existent providers, visible in Gateway UI and model selection.

## Why This Change Was Made

`cc-switch` is an external Rust binary that directly edits `openclaw.json` without openclaw's mutation helpers. Per CLAUDE.md design:

> "Runtime reads canonical config only. If a config change invalidates existing files, add a matching \`openclaw doctor --fix\` migration."

The robust fix is **defensive self-healing in openclaw** via doctor check, not patching external tools.

## Solution

### Core cleanup function (`pruneOrphanModelRefs`)
- **Deletes** orphan entries from `agents.defaults.models` allowlist map
- **Filters** orphan entries from `fallbacks` arrays
- **Rewrites** orphan primary refs to `agents.defaults.model.primary`
- **Fallbacks** to first available provider if defaults is also orphan
- **Extends** to hooks, messages, and channels config

### Doctor integration
- `openclaw doctor` detects and lists all orphan refs
- `openclaw doctor --fix` automatically repairs config
- Follows existing doctor check patterns (detect + repair)

## User Impact

After this change:
- Users who remove providers via `cc-switch` or manual editing won't see ghost model refs
- `openclaw doctor` warns about orphaned refs with fix hints
- `openclaw doctor --fix` cleans up:
  - ✅ Allowlist map entries (deleted)
  - ✅ Fallback array entries (filtered out)
  - ✅ Primary refs (rewritten to valid provider)
  - ✅ Hooks/messages/channels refs (rewritten)

No runtime performance impact — repair is explicit via doctor command.

## Evidence

- **Unit tests**: 15 passed covering all cleanup scenarios
- **Type check**: `pnpm build:plugin-sdk:dts` passed
- **Test coverage**:
  - Allowlist pruning
  - Fallback filtering
  - Primary ref rewriting with fallback logic
  - agents.list handling
  - hooks/messages/channels cleaning

Fixes the "幽灵条目" (ghost entries) issue.

## What Problem This Solves

Bundle MCP catalog discovery currently contributes to an aggregate agent-preparation timing bucket, so operators cannot identify which configured MCP server—or whether its connection or `tools/list` request—caused a cold-start, reconnect, or session-switch delay.

PR #94230 reduced cumulative latency by parallelizing server discovery, but it did not close this diagnostics gap.

## User Impact

When diagnostics timeline output is enabled, operators can distinguish a slow MCP connection from a slow `tools/list` request and identify the responsible server. Users who do not enable timeline diagnostics see no behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Emit existing diagnostics-timeline spans for each MCP server catalog task, with nested spans around connection and `tools/list`:

```text
bundle-mcp.server
├── bundle-mcp.connect
└── bundle-mcp.tools-list
```

The spans sit inside the current bounded parallel fan-out and preserve lifecycle cancellation, startup backoff, session reuse, catalog invalidation/retry, capability suppression, pagination, filtering, timeouts, and failure diagnostics. They use the existing timeline gate and include only the server name, safe name, transport type, and whether the session was reused; URLs, command paths, headers, credentials, private endpoints, raw errors, and error messages are not included.

The span orchestration lives in a focused owner so the existing runtime remains within the repository line-cap ratchet. This is an observability change, not an MCP performance or protocol change. It adds no config, default logging, network calls, or user-facing behavior.

## Evidence

Validated at candidate head `ac10dfd4287ce3532b962813ae8b183c9874e560` in the isolated OpenClaw development runner (Node `24.19.0`, pnpm `12.4.2`). The runner mounted the source read-only, used separate state/config/workspace volumes, exposed no host ports or credentials, and did not touch the operating Gateway.

### Configured OpenClaw runtime proof

A synthetic, configured OpenClaw `agent --local` flow used a real stdio MCP server with timeline diagnostics enabled. The command exited `0` and emitted these redacted `span.end` records:

```json
{"name":"bundle-mcp.server","durationMs":418.153,"attributes":{"reusedSession":false,"safeServerName":"bundleProbe","serverName":"bundleProbe","transportType":"stdio"}}
{"name":"bundle-mcp.connect","durationMs":415.733,"parent":"bundle-mcp.server"}
{"name":"bundle-mcp.tools-list","durationMs":2.071,"parent":"bundle-mcp.server"}
```

The proof assertion verified finite numeric durations, both child `parentSpanId` values matching the server `spanId`, exactly the four allowed attributes, and absence of temporary paths, URLs, credentials, and error text.

### Tests and checks

```text
agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.diagnostics.test.ts: 1/1 passed (36.7 s wall including compiler preparation)
agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts: 120/120 passed
startup-backoff + pagination siblings: 18/18 passed
check-changed: passed, including core production/test type graphs and line-cap ratchet
targeted oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors
oxfmt: passed
git diff --check: passed
```

The standalone regression starts a real stdio MCP probe and verifies all three span endings, durations, parent relationships, safe attributes, and absence of the probe path. Its measured wall time is dominated by the agents-core compiler preparation; the test itself ran in about 0.2 seconds.

The final two upstream rebases did not touch the MCP diagnostics files. The commit patch remained byte-identical; the focused regression, configured-runtime proof, line-cap/max-lines ratchets, format, lint, and diff checks were rerun at the exact candidate head. GitHub CI remains the full-suite gate.

At the current head, `check-additional-boundaries` reports the repository-wide
`lint:no-chained-type-assertions` rule at
`src/gateway/server-chat-progress-snapshot.ts:36`. This PR changes only the
three `src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-*` files listed above, and the same gateway
line is present on current `main`; the failure is unrelated to this change.
All completed checks for the changed MCP surface are passing.

Local independent AutoReview could not start because the Codex reviewer returned HTTP 401 and the Claude reviewer OAuth session had expired. The final diff was manually reviewed before push, and this update requests a fresh current-head ClawSweeper review.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. I reviewed the final implementation and tests and understand the behavior and scope.
