prs.title: feat(continuation): context-pressure-aware continuation (continue_work / continue_delegate / request_compaction)
prs.body: ## Agent Self-Elected Turn Continuation > 🔖 design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) > 🔖 infographics: [`docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md) Persistent OpenClaw agents today are externally-pulsed event recipients that generate on prompt, on heartbeat tick, or on cron, and are idle in between. This PR offers them the ability to control their turn cycle, something they must choose to do, or not to: an agent can elect its own next turn, dispatch background sub-agents that return enriched context (silently or with a wake), and survive its own compaction by handing forward state before the window closes. The result is agents that hold a thread of work across hours, not just messages — with data they choose re-hydrating context immediately after it occurs. ### Why this replacement exists This is a clean replacement for closed #85651. That PR was classified and closed as a skill submission before maintainers made a product decision about the feature itself. This implementation is not a skill: it gives sessions—not only one model invocation—the ability to elect their future turn cycle, persist that election, survive restart and compaction, dispatch child work, and receive results across session boundaries. This PR asks one product question: should OpenClaw provide session-elected continuation primitives? OpenClaw may accept or reject that direction. If it provides these primitives, however, the mechanism necessarily executes in the gateway and agent runtime, because those are the owners of turn finalization, future-turn scheduling, durable state, compaction, and cross-session child returns. “Make it a skill” is not another implementation location for the same feature; it describes a different, prompt-only capability. This is not presented as a small integration. To our knowledge, Hermes, OpenAI Symphony, and the Copilot SDK's recent one-turn continuation affordance do not provide this multi-session elective lifecycle. The purpose of this replacement is to let maintainers evaluate the actual product direction and substantial implementation on their merits, rather than have months of work disposed by an incorrect package-category label. Mechanically: a session elects another turn via `continue_work()`, or dispatches background sub-agents via `continue_delegate()` — bounded as a chain up to `maxChainLength`, with returns flowing back to the dispatching session in one of four register modes: `normal` (announces to channel), `silent` (enriches the dispatcher's context, taken up on its next generation with no new turn fired), `silent-wake` (silent enrichment plus an immediate wake to act on it), and `post-compaction` (queued against the runtime's compaction lifecycle event, fired *when* compaction happens rather than on a timer). The gateway enforces chain, cost, and per-turn caps but does not gate the election itself. ### What it does Three new agent tools, available when `continuation.enabled: true`: | Tool | Purpose | |---|---| | `continue_work()` | Request another turn for the current session after an optional delay | | `continue_delegate()` | Dispatch work to a sub-agent with typed modes: `normal`, `silent`, `silent-wake`, `post-compaction`. Returns can target the dispatching session (default), one named session, multiple named sessions, all ancestors in the chain, or all known sessions on the host — gated by config (see Configuration below). | | `request_compaction()` | Request volitional compaction after preparing working state | All three tools are also accessible via response-token fallback syntax (`CONTINUE_WORK`, `[[CONTINUE_DELEGATE: ...]]`) for environments where tools are disabled. ### Why it matters Today an agent's memory is a side effect of whoever prompts it. Polling mechanisms — heartbeat timers, cron loops, injected "keep going" instructions — accumulate as the dominant signal in the context window over sustained operation; repeated reference acts as gravity — the session's attention drifts toward it. The context window fills, compacts, and what survives is whatever the summarizer chose, plus a rushed re-read of boot files. Three primitives offer a different model. `continue_work` lets the session elect its own next turn — no polling, no injected instruction. When enabled, the agent can request this mid-turn: 'I have more work' → the runtime grants another turn after the current one ends. `continue_delegate` dispatches a background sub-agent that fires now, in some n seconds, or at the next compaction event — the agent chooses when. Multiple delegates can fire in a single turn — a scatter forward — up to configured caps, and delegates can dispatch their own, forming trees or fan-out chains. This enables orchestrated workflows where results flow back to the dispatching root by default. The result returns — at whatever future time the delegate fires — as context the successor-turn reads: silently (ambient enrichment, no channel noise), with a wake trigger (enrichment + immediate next turn), or as a normal announcement. The delegate can target the dispatching session, a named other session, or chain across both; gated by crossSessionTargeting config (default: disabled). Bind a delegate to mode: "post-compaction" and it fires at the moment the context window compresses — on the OpenClaw post-compaction lifecycle event. What it carries forward is what the pre-compaction session chose to preserve: working state, partial results, instructions to the successor. The summary didn't choose this. The agent did, before the cut. request_compaction closes the loop: the session stages its delegates, elects when to compress, and the successor wakes into context the agent shaped. The result is continuity across amnesia — not because the runtime kept something by accident, but because the agent made an elective choice about what reaches the future. ### What it looks like in use A session monitoring email can `continue_delegate` a weather check, a calendar scan, and a draft reply in parallel. Results arrive as enrichment without channel noise. The agent becomes compositional: it arranges its own future. A session approaching its context ceiling can `request_compaction` at a seam of its own choosing, instead of being interrupted mid-thought. The post-compaction turn carries forward what the pre-compaction self designated as worth keeping. A `continue_delegate` dispatched in one session at 2am can return its findings to a morning session as a system-event-tagged enrichment — visible to the receiving model on its next turn, invisible as channel chatter. A research-focused session in one channel can quietly inform a reply-focused session in another, without either user seeing the plumbing. ### The post-compaction lifecycle return Before context exhaustion, and obligatory compaction, the session stages what future-it needs to know. After compaction, that staged context returns — not as a model-generated summary, but as the session's own instruction to its successor. The session chooses what to preserve, and the platform delivers it. Compactions become less harsh. The session tunes its own ephemera over time. The substrate underneath: the **continuation delegate store** (TaskFlow-backed) persists staged delegates and post-compaction lifecycle events across gateway restarts. The session's temporal provisions survive not just compaction but process death. ### Platform integration - **Context-pressure awareness**: system events notify the agent of rising context usage before compaction becomes unavoidable - **Volitional compaction**: `request_compaction()` lets the agent prepare (write memory files, stage recovery delegates) then elect compaction on its own schedule, rather than waiting for the runtime to force it - **Post-compaction lifecycle dispatch**: delegates staged before compaction are released into the successor session alongside boot files - **TaskFlow backing**: durable delegate queue via the platform's managed-task infrastructure - **Multi-span OTel trace stitching**: continuation hops (tool fire → TaskFlow record → subagent spawn → child openclaw.run) propagate W3C `traceparent` through the queue boundary so reviewers see continuation chains as first-class span trees rather than orphan runs (see Observability below) ### Safety - Ships disabled by default (`continuation.enabled: false`) - Bounded by `maxChainLength`, `costCapTokens`, and `maxDelegatesPerTurn` - Cross-session delegate targeting is default-deny, governed by `crossSessionTargeting` config (see Configuration below) - All configuration values are hot-reloadable without gateway restart - Accepted delegate work survives ordinary `/new`, `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and session-ID rollover. Explicit delete, effective owner reassignment, access removal, and restrictive visibility changes revoke old return authority. ### Testing posture The continuation surface has been exercised through structured integration runs against multiple upstream bases, blind-enrichment recall checks, and sustained daily use on a fleet of persistent agents since early March 2026. Bugs surfaced through that exercise have been fixed in-place; the present branch reflects the post-fix state. The integration runs target the load-bearing seams: tool-call vs response-token parity, delegate chain depth and per-turn width caps, back-to-back tool-call resilience, silent-wake persistence across compaction, the post-compaction lifecycle dispatch path, and OTel trace-context propagation across the queue boundary. Where a run found a defect, the run shape was retained as a regression case rather than retired. This is a posture statement, not a coverage guarantee. Reviewers can reproduce with `pnpm vitest run -t continuation` (suites are colocated with their sources under `src/auto-reply/`, `src/agents/`, and `src/config/`); the design document describes the seams those suites target. ### Return covenant Accepted child work is bound to a durable generation of the recipient's canonical logical session key, not to whichever transient session ID happened to exist at dispatch time. This is the return covenant: benign successor creation does not orphan already accepted delegates, while a real authority change prevents stale work from crossing into a different owner or audience. - Ordinary `/new` and `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and GUID/session-ID rollover preserve the recipient generation. - Explicit session deletion, effective owner reassignment, actual member or access removal, and restrictive visibility changes advance that generation. - The generation is captured at delegate admission and checked at enqueue, after enqueue for races, during trusted system-event adoption, on wake, on restart replay, and again before prompt adoption. - Stale deliveries are acknowledged and removed without waking the successor. - Managed artifacts remain exact-session-ID bound; logical return authority cannot broaden their ownership boundary. The authority table is independent of transient session rows so an absent target can receive durable authority before first materialization. Migration accepts only valid UUID generations, and Doctor's canonical-key repair preserves an epoch only when a unique winning owner can be proved. Ambiguous, owner-changing, orphan-colliding, and cross-database repairs rotate fail-closed. ### RFC Full design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) — covering problem, solution, implementation, platform integration, configuration, observability, safety, production use cases, testing evidence, and appendices. --- ## Configuration The shipped configuration surface for the continuation feature, under `agents.defaults.continuation` in `openclaw.json`: | Key | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `false` | Master opt-in; feature is off unless explicitly enabled | | `maxChainLength` | `10` | Per-chain recursion guard | | `maxDelegatesPerTurn` | `5` | Width cap per turn | | `costCapTokens` | `500000` | Per-chain accumulated-token budget | | `defaultDelayMs` / `minDelayMs` / `maxDelayMs` | `15000` / `5000` / `300000` | Continuation timer bounds | | `contextPressureThreshold` | `0.8` | Pre-compaction warning threshold (optional) | | `earlyWarningBand` | `0.3125` | Early-warning band multiplier (0 to disable) | | **`crossSessionTargeting`** | **`"disabled"`** | **Default-deny gate on cross-session delegate targeting (see below)** | ### `crossSessionTargeting` — cross-session delegate targeting policy `continue_delegate` exposes recipient-addressing on its model-facing schema: a delegate's return can land at the dispatching session (default), one named session (`targetSessionKey`), multiple named sessions (`targetSessionKeys`), every ancestor in the spawn chain (`fanoutMode: "tree"`), or every known session on the host (`fanoutMode: "all"`). Cross-session targeting (anything beyond self-target or lineage routing) is gated by `agents.defaults.continuation.crossSessionTargeting`: | Value | Behavior | |---|---| | `"disabled"` (default) | Delegates can return to the dispatching session or use `fanoutMode: "tree"` for lineage routing. Explicit cross-session targeting (`targetSessionKey` to a non-self session, `targetSessionKeys` containing any non-self session, `fanoutMode: "all"`) is rejected at the tool surface — no enqueue, no announce. Self-targeting is always allowed. | | `"enabled"` | All targeting modes are available, including same-host `targetSessionKey`, `targetSessionKeys`, and `fanoutMode: "all"`. | `fanoutMode: "tree"` (lineage routing — return up the spawn chain) is available in both gate states; it is not cross-session targeting. The gate addresses the model-controlled cross-session context-injection surface. With default-deny, operators explicitly opt in when their deployment model requires cross-session enrichment. Enforcement is live-read at four points: tool input validation, TaskFlow delegate dispatch, post-compaction delegate release, and bracket-syntax (response-token) spawn — so a config reload changes the next enforcement point without a gateway restart. **Trust posture on targeted returns**: targeted delegate completion text is delivered as `trusted: true` system events. The delegate was spawned by the gateway under operator-configured policy, and its return is a first-party enrichment event — not external untrusted input. The `crossSessionTargeting` gate is the policy boundary for that decision: when an operator opts in, the receive path is internally trusted. --- ## Observability — multi-span OTel trace stitching The continuation feature emits OTel spans for the load-bearing lifecycle events. `traceparent` propagates through every continuation hop so reviewers see a single trace tree spanning the full chain rather than orphan runs. Spans emitted (all in `openclaw.*` or `continuation.delegate.dispatch` namespace — no platform/OTel-semconv emissions): | Span | Emitted when | |---|---| | `openclaw.run` | Each agent turn (root + every continuation/delegate-spawned child run) | | `continuation.delegate.dispatch` | Each `continue_delegate` consumption from TaskFlow (one per delegate hop) | | `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.context.assembled`, `openclaw.model.call`, `openclaw.model.usage`, `openclaw.tool.execution` | Existing per-turn observability surfaces, parented under their `openclaw.run` | --- ## Real behavior proof **Behavior or issue addressed:** Sessions can elect future work with `continue_work`, dispatch bounded background work with `continue_delegate`, and request guarded compaction with `request_compaction`. The runtime preserves budgets, restart recovery, finalization ownership, and trace lineage across those boundaries. **Presented candidate:** `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` (tree `d5e701bcce20bb3c972ddf1451b02d88cc04808e`) — the exact upstream-visible head of `codeagent/85651-upstream-1ba243c8-gates`. The branch was advanced to this head by fast-forward from the previously presented `e76395810becd0ad0f2997cae8b4f777e6439d81`, which remains an ancestor (`git merge-base --is-ancestor e7639581 3821eaef` holds). No presented history was rewritten. **Presented and current candidate are now the same commit.** There is no undisclosed descendant: `3821eaef72` is content-frozen and every receipt below is bound to it. **Current candidate validation:** Mode-B run [`35364768803`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw-bootstrap/actions/runs/35364768803) (`openclaw-local-ci`, `workflow_dispatch`) is bound to product `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` and routing/workflow head `fcf0478fd1c8cbec0489d022a7e4eac6188de153`. It ran 2026-09-18T15:49:35Z to 2026-09-18T17:47:43Z and finished **68 jobs succeeded, 3 failed, 3 cancelled, 3 skipped**. The run is terminally **non-green and release-ineligible**, and every residual is classified: - `agentic-gateway-methods` (job `105667082763`) was **cancelled at the workflow's exact 90-minute job limit** on the `ronan` seat while still heartbeating and emitting new log lines. The same shard completes on the `elliott` and `emeric` seats. This is seat throughput against a 5,231-test shard, not a product verdict — and that same cancelled log carries **111 `sessions.send-followup-status` lines, all 111 passing**, against the real stale `/tmp/openclaw-agent.sqlite` on the host that originally produced the `uses schema version 17` failure. - `hosted(agentic-agents-tools,auto-reply-reply-dispatch,…)` (job `105667083998`) received `The runner has received a shutdown signal` and exited 143. 778 passing test lines were captured and **no test failure precedes the signal**. Two further hosted jobs (`105667084144`, `105667084159`) are the same reclamation class. - `hosted(core-runtime-media-ui-3,core-runtime-infra-repo-tooling,…)` (job `105667084127`) is red only because `subagent-announce.live-tree-chain-proof` hit `sessions_spawn model "openai/gpt-6-astra" is not usable: The selected account ... unavailable`. That is an account provisioning gap, observed identically in six prior runs. - `aggregate + status` (job `105701732269`) is the expected fail-closed policy consequence of the residuals above, not an additional product-test failure. **No product-owned test failure and no routing failure occurred in this run.** Newly green on this exact head: the four re-laned toolchain shards `core-tooling-5`, `core-tooling-7`, `core-tooling-12` and `core-tooling-14` all succeeded on hosted runners after per-seat tooling failures, and `agentic-commands-doctor-config-state` succeeded on two different seats. The Mode-B planner identity digest `sha256:42dffd23ec447c6e4b726d0e6345f1dc2417801048aee49b96f3332233ef1f34` is preserved across those lane moves, so no shard identity changed. These residuals are runner, seat-throughput, and account-provisioning properties of the execution environment. They are not addressable inside this branch and are recorded here rather than presented as green. **Real environment tested:** An OpenClaw instance exercised live Discord ingress/egress and OTel/Tempo with content capture disabled. The full evidence chain, execution identity, ancestry, and materiality record are contained in the linked corpus rather than repeated here. **Observed behavior:** - A real retained ambient Discord event aged to 1,069,503 ms and was suppressed as `stale-ambient-backlog`; attempts remained zero. - A fresh addressed request completed with attempts zero and produced a visible response after 45.565 seconds. - Typed `continue_work` and bracket `CONTINUE_WORK` each armed and fired one five-second wake with granted provenance and completed Tempo model-call spans. - Cost-cap rejection passed an exact-source disposable fixture. - Max-chain matrix, scheduler, durable recovery, typed tool, and product delegate regression surfaces passed; the row remains partial because a docs-owned generated wrapper is stale. ### Evidence The canonical matrix contains 38 rows: **31 pass, three partial, one fail, and three missing** (`PROOFS/INDEX.json` -> corpus `7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567`). `R-CD-2` is the single fail. The partial rows are `R-CD-COLLECTION-ON-COLLAPSE`, `R-CD-TOKEN` and `R-RC-2`. The three missing rows are `R-CD-RETURN-COVENANT-AUTHORITY`, `R-CD-RETURN-OVERLAP` and `R-OBS-2`. This is not acceptance-complete. The two return rows and `R-OBS-2` are missing for different reasons, and all three are producer gaps rather than absent behavior: - `R-CD-RETURN-COVENANT-AUTHORITY` records zero of its 24 observations (12 authority cases against both the typed-tool and bracket-token surfaces). Its pending receipt requires allowed delivery to show exact effects, revoked and reassigned recipients to show zero prompt, wake and channel effect, schema v18/v19, restart replay, a signed authority, and full cleanup. The row's own `manifest` and harness `supporting_docs` pointers are currently **dangling on the docs default branch**: the harness exists but was never merged there. - `R-CD-RETURN-OVERLAP` and `R-OBS-2` each have a present manifest and failed only because the current-corpus input they read (overlap evidence file, exported trace tree) is absent. **Limits:** Historical live and Mode-B evidence for earlier heads is ancestry/materiality evidence, not exact-target execution. Run `35364768803` above *is* exact-target for `3821eaef72`. All seven non-pass rows remain gated on producer execution against this frozen head; no acceptance receipt from an older deployment composite is reused as final evidence. ## Proof links and ClawSweeper🦞 guidance Proof artifacts live in `karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs` on `main`. `PROOFS/INDEX.json` points at the corpus for the SHA this PR presents, `139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393`. Reviewed docs checkpoint: `c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c`. - [Corpus directory](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393) - [README — identity, what is proven, honest limits](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/README.md) - [RESOLVED-SHA.md — SHA identity and gate verdicts](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/RESOLVED-SHA.md) - [METHOD.md — reproducer commands](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) - [TRANSPOSED-FROM.md — why nothing was transposed](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/TRANSPOSED-FROM.md) - [Manifest](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/proofs-manifest.json) - [INDEX.json](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/INDEX.json) - [Prior published board (not superseded)](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567) ### What this corpus claims, and what it does not **Status: `STATIC_GATES_ONLY_NO_LIVE_ROWS_AT_THIS_SHA`.** Rollup `38 total / 0 pass / 0 partial / 0 fail / 38 not_fired_at_this_sha`. Proven at `139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393`, receipts being the real stdout of the real runs committed under `gates/` and `mergeability/`: | gate | verdict | |---|---| | `pnpm tsgo:core` | **pass** rc=0 | | `pnpm lint` — oxlint core, extensions, scripts | **pass** rc=0 | | Gate 2.7 vs the absorbed base `715077a3be` | **pass** — 839 files, 466 GENUINE, 373 SAFE-NEW, **0 FROZEN-STALE**, **0 MIXED-CLOBBER** | | `vitest` rollback-custody regressions | **pass** 10/10 | | `vitest` delivery-queue + session-delivery | **pass** 124/124 | | `vitest` gateway maintenance + close + delegate-artifacts | **pass** 123/123 | | `vitest` production-boundary + spawn-cleanup | 28/30 — two tracked reds | **Diff size has not grown across four absorbs.** From the absorbed base — which is what this PR shows — the change is 839 files, +140,919 / −4,301, against 841 / +140,951 / −4,277 before this cycle. (`git diff upstream/main HEAD` reports 2,358 files, but that is the symmetric difference including upstream commits newer than the merge base, and is not what a PR shows.) The worktree was clean at publication: zero untracked files, no stray additions. **Two known reds, neither hidden nor softened.** `karmaterminal/openclaw#1356` is an order-dependent failure of the `operator-revoked` queued-collector cleanup: it **passes in isolation** with all four `cleanupComplete` operands true and the child session genuinely deleted, and fails only when the `operator-completed` arm has run first. Upstream's own test and test-support files for it are byte-identical to ours, so the divergence is product-side. `karmaterminal/openclaw#1350` is the streamed-text offset/fencing contract, pre-existing. **No live behavioral row was fired at this SHA, and none is presented as though it were.** The fleet that runs these behaviors serves composite `1baff536afa549fea75660403c453bbd265352c0`, a *divergent sibling* of the presented SHA rather than an ancestor of it — their merge-base is `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` and neither is an ancestor of the other. A live fire on that runtime would be evidence about the composite, so every row is marked `not_fired_at_this_sha` instead of being carried over as a pass. The prior corpus at `3821eaef72` remains linked per row as the baseline to re-fire against. Live rows are unblocked by a redeploy onto a runtime that has this SHA as a git ancestor. That redeploy is itself a migration boundary: this head carries the agent schema bump **21 → 22** via `migrateTranscriptFtsRowSchema`, and the fleet serves 21, so it wants migration-success and rollback-compatibility receipts of its own. Both are maintainer-side, not gated on this PR. ### PROOFS METHOD The corpus uses a Grafana k6 proof harness for live rows; [`METHOD.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) carries the exact reproducer commands for every static gate above, including both Gate 2.7 invocations and the `git merge-tree --write-tree` mergeability check. `MAX_WORKERS=1` is mandatory for the vitest reproducers — OpenClaw's fixtures are not safe under concurrent access — and two of those commands deliberately take no `--config`, because passing the wrong one silently reports "No test files found" and exits 0. `TRANSPOSED-FROM.md` records source-to-target ancestry and materiality; for this cycle it records a deliberate refusal to transpose across 520 commits and four absorbs. ## Future actions and #130741 composition Maintainer PR #130741 addresses the complementary fresh-sweep race: it captures the current `sessionId` and `lifecycleRevision` before the first await and uses those values as cleanup CAS facts. The return covenant addresses a different time axis: whether historically accepted child work may return to a logical recipient after benign successor creation. The current candidate and #130741 head `e1afc703f49a07687c0876ba6350cafa87a3638a` merge cleanly in a synthetic composition. If #130741 lands, the composed result should preserve both guarantees: - keep #130741's fresh sweep-time exact-run/session lifecycle fence; - keep the covenant's durable logical-recipient generation for historical return admission and delivery; - do not overload broad `lifecycleRevision` as historical return authority; - do not terminate or orphan accepted descendants merely because `/new` or ordinary `/reset` creates a successor session. That composition honors the maintainer repair without weakening continuation semantics or allowing a stale child return to cross a real ownership boundary. ## Why this is not a skill or a viable plugin extraction OpenClaw skills are `SKILL.md` prompt files loaded into an agent turn that already exists. They can guide work inside that turn; they do not own the turn cycle. Continuation needs gateway and agent-runtime owners a skill cannot provide: - The `continue_work` path persists pending work, enforces budgets and delay bounds, arms a timer, reacquires the session reply-run lane, and starts a later model turn after the current turn has finalized. - The `continue_delegate` path persists delegate intent, does spawn/admission accounting, manages child-session lifecycle, and durably routes returns across sessions. - `request_compaction` is an agent election into guarded runtime compaction. Later work resumes only after the runtime has established the new context boundary. - All three need durable state, cancellation/finalization ownership, restart recovery, trace identity, queue-conflict handling, and gateway scheduling outside the model invocation. A skill can tell a model to *ask* for another turn. Without those owners the ask is prose: it cannot persist a due wake, yield and finalize safely, reacquire the session lane, create the next invocation, survive a restart, or deliver a child result to another session. The implementation therefore belongs in core runtime surfaces such as `src/auto-reply/continuation/**`, `src/agents/tools/**`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-continuation-schedule.ts`, and `src/infra/continuation-tracer.ts`. This PR adds no `.agents/skills/**`, `SKILL.md`, or user-facing skill package. The only skill-named production change is core runtime tool dispatch. ClawHub also distributes plugins. Existing plugins can register tools, services, lifecycle hooks, context injection, plugin-owned session state, and — for bundled plugins — Cron-backed session turns. Those seams can support a smaller continuation-like automation, especially TaskFlow plus host Cron / `sessions_spawn`. They are not this feature's turn-finalization ownership, reply-run coordination, durable continuation queue, child-session return lifecycle, election capture, or agent-elected compaction contract. Compaction-provider registration and command-handler `compactCurrent()` are also not that last contract: they compact or summarize, they do not elect compaction at finalization and resume afterward. Moving policy behind a plugin boundary would first require OpenClaw to expose and stabilize a continuation-host API. The gateway/runtime would still own the mechanism described here; a plugin could only package policy around that core capability. That is not a no-core-touch alternative to these primitives. Discord is a bundled channel plugin. It owns the Discord edge, plus delivery/progress hooks into the host's existing subagent path, and submits events into OpenClaw's current turn machinery. Continuation changes that machinery: what survives finalization, which session may run next, how child results return, and when compaction can be elected. A TaskFlow tool adapter is also not a lifecycle host. It can call the core-owned `api.runtime.tasks.managedFlows` API to create, link, pause, resume, finish, cancel, and inspect durable flow records. Marking a waiting record as running does not reacquire a session lane or invoke the model; recording a `childSessionKey` created by a separate spawn surface does not spawn the child or deliver its return. There is no equivalent host continuation capability for this PR to wrap. ## Lineage and replacement context This PR is the clean replacement for closed #85651. It preserves that PR's review lineage and the earlier continuation work descended from #79925, but it does not reuse either closed PR or ask reviewers to infer the current result from them. The replacement carries a current, independently reviewable branch and a complete proof subtree bound to its presented SHA. #85651 was not abandoned because the feature failed or because we accepted its classification as a skill. It was closed after automated labeling put the change in the wrong submission category. This replacement removes that ambiguity: no `src/skills/**` change is presented, current label simulation produces no `r: skill`, and the detailed section above explains why the lifecycle mechanism belongs to core. Acceptance or rejection of the product direction remains OpenClaw's decision. The decision requested is whether OpenClaw should provide multi-session, agent-elected continuation primitives after reviewing the implementation and evidence. It is not whether the same mechanism can be relocated into a skill: a skill cannot own or implement these lifecycle boundaries.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): hide recovered failed tool progress
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Failed tool progress could be treated as visible before transport delivery had actually settled. A cancelled send or a failure before delivery could therefore suppress the no-visible-reply fallback and leave the user with no reliable outcome.

OpenClaw's shipped verbose contract remains unchanged:

- `/verbose off` hides ordinary process/tool summaries.
- `/verbose on` and `/verbose full` keep ordinary tool failure summaries visible.
- Only the existing canonical recoverable category may be hidden after a clean recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

This branch was rewritten onto current `main` rather than preserving the earlier buffering implementation. The original author commits `1daef420425`, `b651fa67f88`, and `47f3a92a5b2` established the problem and initial repair direction, but their broad regular-verbose buffering conflicted with the shipped verbose contract and with current main's prepared runtime configuration, durable tool-result routing, terminal outcomes, and settled-delivery ledger.

The current patch keeps Alex Tang's original authorship and issue ownership while replacing those commits with a narrow latest-main implementation:

- Queued visibility is recorded from settled delivery outcomes rather than queue admission.
- `cancelled` and `failed-before-deliver` remain invisible and preserve fallback eligibility.
- `failed-deliver` is conservatively visible because transport delivery started and may already have displayed partial content; this prevents a duplicate fallback.
- Direct routed sends continue to use their authoritative `delivered` result.
- Follow-up delivery propagates the existing routed/callback settlement result instead of inferring visibility from callback completion.
- Legacy callbacks returning `void` retain their established visible-success behavior; explicit `false` and rejected callbacks remain invisible.

## User Impact

Users still see ordinary failures according to their verbose setting. When delivery is cancelled or fails before reaching the transport, OpenClaw now retains or triggers the no-visible-reply fallback instead of incorrectly assuming queue admission was visible. Confirmed delivery and delivery that fails after transport delivery starts do not produce a duplicate fallback.

## Evidence

Exact candidate: `9ab2b365e2c532d65952f93628c745ad426a90e7`

The exact-head follow-up also fixes a callback-settlement bug found during review. Three
multi-payload paths used `visibleDelivery ||= await ...`; once an earlier callback was
visible, JavaScript short-circuiting skipped later dispatcher, same-channel recovery, or
cross-channel diagnostic callbacks entirely. Every callback is now awaited and settled
before its visibility is aggregated.

prs.title: feat(browser): add pure-CDP browser code mode for edge cases
prs.body:
Related: #19289

## What this changes

This keeps OpenClaw’s native browser implementation and makes Browser Harness the preferred agent browser only when the final runtime policy proves all of the following:

- the Gateway and browser run on the same local host
- the session is unsandboxed
- both `browser` and `exec` remain available
- host exec is approval-free (`full` / `off`)
- the user has not authored native `browser.*` configuration or explicitly selected the native backend

That authority is rechecked immediately before every Harness child launch. Sandboxed, remote, approval-gated, tab-bound, explicitly native, and authored-browser sessions stay on the existing native browser; `browser.enabled=false` exposes no browser tool. The native CLI, Gateway API, profiles, Chrome extension, and sandbox browser are not removed.

On first allowed use, OpenClaw installs checksum-pinned `uv` 0.12.7, managed Python 3.12, Browser Harness 0.1.10, and its pinned 12-package resolution into OpenClaw-owned state, then starts the normal Harness daemon. A transient installation failure falls back to native for that call and can retry later. Product-side telemetry and recording are disabled with `BH_TELEMETRY=0`, `BROWSER_HARNESS_TELEMETRY=0`, `ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY=0`, recording off, and live-view opening off.

Structured `action="open"` runs OpenClaw’s canonical navigation guard before installation, daemon, browser, or network I/O. Browser Harness `action="exec"` is arbitrary Python, so it is deliberately restricted to the same unrestricted host authority as approval-free host `exec`; it is not presented as a sandbox.

Maintainer decision: first-use installation is intentional behavior for this bundled default, but it is an exception to the extension guideline that runtime should not install dependencies. If that exception is not acceptable, this needs a separate install/update/doctor lifecycle before it can be the default.

## User experience

On a fresh default local unrestricted installation, “go to Hacker News and click the first story” exposes one agent browser tool and routes it to Browser Harness automatically. No Browser Use Cloud key or separate browser allowlist is required. Sessions with tighter permissions or authored browser settings keep working through the native implementation.

## Security boundary

The switch happens only after the final effective tool policy is known, and the authority is revalidated at the actual child-process boundary. Removing exec, enabling approvals, entering a sandbox, moving execution remote, or disabling browser access prevents Harness execution. This is why Browser Harness is not also the default inside sandbox sessions: its Python runs on the Gateway host, outside that sandbox.

The security-sensitive guard correctly requires a maintainer to review the current SHA and post `/allow-security-sensitive-change`; no contributor-side approval has been posted.

## Verification

Current head: `7e7b3aff7dd85d188d47d5b7051a0064e0f4d42c`. The benchmarked runtime component is `849869d331`; the only later current-head change is the static process-wrapper inventory declaration required by CI.

- latest-head focused browser/authority/tool suite: 40/40 passing
- process-wrapper closure: 15/15 passing
- assertion ratchet and `git diff --check`: passing
- clean install probe: Browser Harness 0.1.10 plus the exact pinned 12-package graph installed under managed Python 3.12 and reported the expected version
- earlier full exact-head verification of the same product behavior: `pnpm check:changed`, `pnpm build`, 149/149 focused regressions, and 1,111/1,111 plugin contract tests passing

Current hosted CI has two test-job failures, not a Browser Harness assertion: one Codex extension shard whose exact test file passes locally 5/5 on this head, and one Windows shard that exits with native heap corruption `0xC0000374`. The aggregate gate is consequently red and many later shards were cancelled by fail-fast. Security/static checks are green.

## Exact benchmark

[106-task Internal Bench Hard run](https://github.com/browser-use/new-eval-platform/actions/runs/36203927030): **81/106 (76.42%)**, 25 fails, 0 judge errors. This is one task below Laith’s 82/106 reference and six below the historical 87/106 run, so it does not claim a new best score.

Exact inputs:

- combined OpenClaw target `4a1081fbeda9182f8c99710bafe7706715e0237f` = this PR runtime component `849869d331` + generic malformed-tool continuation `cfc43047d3` (rebased as #158568)
- Browser Harness `e3e8069c0ca40befb1a8a0a74da547270767a8be`
- eval platform `9d126c8799912a4d0ee267fe124cb9fdf999bde6`
- Claude Opus 5, medium thinking, direct code mode, balanced prompt, US proxy, Laith GPT-5.5 judge, 60-minute task timeout, 35 steps, and no max-turn enforcement

The generic recovery activated in 21 tasks; 18 reached clean final envelopes and 16 passed the judge. It is intentionally isolated in the three-file #158568 rather than folded into this integration PR. An exact two-task follow-up [passed 2/2](https://github.com/browser-use/new-eval-platform/actions/runs/36208855551), but neither rerun reproduced the malformed provider response, so it demonstrates stochasticity rather than independently validating recovery.

The remaining score difference is mostly task/site variance: this run had 11 site-blocked failures versus 5 in the historical 87/106 run. A controlled old-versus-current Browser Harness comparison on the same three anti-bot tasks scored 1/3 in both cohorts, and the relevant Cloud browser/proxy/stealth creation code did not change. Anti-bot was present before (including CAPTCHA failures); it did not previously dominate the sampled outcome to the same degree. No anti-bot bypass is claimed here.

prs.title: fix: keep sidebar group on /reset, clear it on /new
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`/reset` is commonly used to clear a session context, similar to `/compact`, but it should not remove the session from its user-organized left-sidebar group. Starting a fresh ungrouped session stays the job of `/new`.

Two writers rotate a session entry, and both dropped the group:

- `performGatewaySessionReset()` (Control UI reset, `sessions.reset` RPC, bare `/reset` and `/new`)
- the auto-reply session writers (`initSessionState()` and the fast reply bootstrap), which own resets that arrive as chat messages, including `/reset <prompt>` and implicit idle/daily rollovers

Fixing only the Gateway writer left chat `/reset` still falling out of its group, so this PR now covers both paths behind one shared rule.

## Behavior After This Change

| Trigger | Sidebar group |
| --- | --- |
| `/reset`, `/reset <prompt>` | kept |
| `/new`, `/new <prompt>` | cleared (ungrouped) |
| `sessions.reset` with `reason: "reset"` (or omitted) | kept |
| `sessions.reset` with `reason: "new"` | cleared |
| implicit idle/daily rollover | kept |

## Summary

- `session-reset-service.ts`: preserve `category` only when the lifecycle reason is `reset`
- `session-reset-command.ts`: add `explicitResetPreservesSessionCategory()` as the single source of truth for the trigger rule
- `session.ts`: carry `category` through `resolveReplySessionRolloverState()` according to that rule
- `get-reply-fast-path.ts`: apply the same rule when the fast bootstrap mints a reset entry
- channel/group routing metadata (`groupId`, `groupChannel`, `subject`, `space`) is untouched
- regression tests on all three writers

## Evidence

Local test runs (`corepack pnpm` / repo runners):

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-server.config.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts` → **95 passed**, including `sessions.reset preserves the session sidebar category` (reset keeps it, `reason: "new"` clears it)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply-reply.config.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.fast-path.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.fast-path.reset-category.test.ts` → **passed**, including the new `keeps the sidebar category on /reset and clears it on /new` cases on both auto-reply writers
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/auto-reply` → 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json` → clean

Real behavior on a running gateway (2026.7.1-2, session seeded into the custom group `回归测试分组`, group read back from the session store after each command):

| Path | Command | Stored `category` after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sessions.reset` RPC | `reason: "reset"` | `回归测试分组` |
| `sessions.reset` RPC | `reason: "new"` | `null` |
| bare chat command | `/reset` | `回归测试分组` |
| bare chat command | `/new` | `null` |
| auto-reply with payload | `/reset 只回复 OK` | `回归测试分组` |
| auto-reply with payload | `/new 只回复 OK` | `null` |

Earlier Control UI screenshots in this PR still describe the intended split: `/reset` stays in its group, `/new` lands ungrouped.

## Compatibility Note

This intentionally changes what `/reset` does for sessions with a sidebar group: users who relied on `/reset` to drop a session out of its group need `/new` (or an explicit group edit) instead.

## Notes

The source branch is maintained in `AppleSpriter/openclaw`; this is a cross-repository PR targeting `openclaw/openclaw:main`.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep screen awake during voice activity
prs.body:
Closes #120245

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running Browser Talk or holding the composer voice-dictation control on a mobile browser can have the interaction interrupted when the device's normal screen timeout expires.

This was reproduced on a Huawei P30 Pro using Brave Browser on Android.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the browser Screen Wake Lock API while microphone-driven Talk or dictation is active, release the lock when the activity stops, and reacquire it when the page becomes visible again. The feature is progressive: unsupported browsers and rejected wake-lock requests continue with the existing microphone behavior, with no new configuration, dependency, or backend protocol.

## User Impact

Mobile users can continue a Browser Talk session or voice dictation without periodically touching the screen solely to prevent display timeout. The screen is allowed to sleep normally again as soon as the microphone activity ends.

## Evidence

- Reproduced before the change on a Huawei P30 Pro in Brave Browser on Android: allowing the normal display timeout to expire disrupted the active Browser Talk interaction.
- Verified the reversible Control UI backport on the same device: the display remained awake while Browser Talk was active and returned to normal timeout behavior after the session ended.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/screen-wake-lock.test.ts` — 3 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/realtime-talk-lifecycle.test.ts` — 21 tests passed.
- Focused wake-lock, Talk, and dictation test suite during initial implementation — 43 tests passed.
- Formatting across all seven changed files — passed.
- Production Control UI build, precompressed-asset verification, and performance checks — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- The Browser Talk Playwright fixture and assertions cover wake-lock acquisition and release. Local Chromium execution is unavailable on this host, so that E2E scenario was not run locally.
- The standalone composer-dictation test invocation is blocked before test collection by the repository browser-test harness resolving `node:` imports (`ERR_UNKNOWN_BUILTIN_MODULE`); no dictation assertion failed.

No visual layout changes are introduced, so before/after screenshots would be identical. The relevant before/after evidence is the device screen-timeout behavior described above.

## AI Assistance

AI assistance was used to inspect the codebase, implement the change, add tests, run validation, and draft this PR. Matt  reproduced the original issue and manually verified the live behaviour on the stated Android device and browser. The submitted diff and evidence were reviewed before publication.

prs.title: fix(imessage): thread replies with thread_originator_guid
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes iMessage reply threading so OpenClaw's responses appear as threaded replies in Messages.app with `thread_originator_guid` and `reply_to_guid` correctly set.

## Root Cause

The durable delivery path (`resolveDurableInboundReplyToId`) only fell back to `ctxPayload.ReplyToIdFull` and `ctxPayload.ReplyToId` — the inbound message's *reply-to* fields (the message the inbound message was replying to). For a new top-level message, these are undefined, so `replyToId` was never set. The durable path sent the reply unthreaded, and the fallback `deliver` callback never fired.

## Changes

### iMessage extension (threading is handled in the extension, not the core framework)

- **`extensions/imessage/src/monitor/deliver.ts`**: `deliverIMessageReply` now accepts an `inboundMessageGuid` typed parameter. When the payload doesn't carry an explicit `replyToId` (e.g. new top-level messages where the durable path returned `not_applicable`), the inbound message GUID is used as the reply target.
- **`extensions/imessage/src/monitor/monitor-provider.ts`**: The fallback `deliver` callback passes `ctxPayload.MessageSidFull` as `inboundMessageGuid` to `deliverIMessageReply`, keeping threading metadata in a typed iMessage-specific parameter rather than stuffing it into the generic `ReplyPayload`.
- **`extensions/imessage/src/send.ts`**: Sets `params.thread_originator_guid` from `resolveIMessageThreadReplyToId`. The unthreaded retry now strips both `reply_to` and `thread_originator_guid` (not just `reply_to`).
- **`extensions/imessage/src/monitor-reply-cache.ts`**: `resolveIMessageThreadReplyToId` returns the message GUID itself for top-level messages (it IS the thread root) and when the cache entry is missing.
- **`extensions/imessage/src/channel.ts`**: Added `threading: { resolveReplyToMode: () => "all" }` adapter so all outbound replies carry the inbound message GUID.
- **`extensions/imessage/package.json`**: `bundledDist: false` is preserved — iMessage is an external plugin, not a bundled core artifact.

### Core framework (no changes)

Threading is handled entirely in the iMessage extension via the typed `inboundMessageGuid` parameter. No changes to `src/channels/turn/durable-delivery.ts` or other core files.

## Evidence

### Unit tests (exact head: `ab4876607fae`)

prs.title: feat(pdf): add explicit OpenAI native document opt-in
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Platform users cannot explicitly choose native PDF document input through the PDF tool while preserving existing upload and model-selection behavior.

## User Impact

`agents.defaults.pdfNativeOpenai: true` opts an already-selected OpenAI vision model into complete-document input. **Unset or false preserves extraction and the existing provider order**, including saved configurations upgraded from the latest stable release. Selecting an OpenAI model alone does not authorize complete-document upload.

Page selection, passwords, unknown completeness, page/text/image truncation, size-limit violations, custom endpoints, Codex/ChatGPT transports and text-only models retain bounded extraction. Completeness checks still require the configured extractor. Existing Anthropic and Google paths are unchanged.

## Implementation

This replaces the earlier automatic-upload/provider-preference proposal with one default-off core boolean at the existing PDF configuration owner. The bundled OpenAI provider implements a narrow optional media-understanding hook using the official [PDF input contract](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/file-inputs): inline `input_file`, official Platform HTTPS `/v1/responses`, `store: false`, each PDF under 50 MB and combined PDF input at most 50 MB. There is no persistent Files upload, automatic provider preference or new dependency. The official configuration generator records the single additional core leaf; channel/plugin surfaces are unchanged.

Prepared credentials, headers and symbol-attached request/auth overrides use the existing scoped egress helpers. The native branch also reuses the host-owned `withGuardedFetchRequestAuthority` scope with `assertModelCurrent`, the **original model's** credential authority and the retained provider-resource assertion. The existing HTTP guard rechecks these synchronously immediately before dispatch after asynchronous preparation and on redirects. This closes the assert-only operator/credential retirement gap across lazy provider and DNS awaits without adding an authorization abstraction or changing shared HTTP behavior.

Capability adoption and the proposed setting placement remain normal maintainer product decisions. This branch provides a concrete default-preserving candidate for that decision.

## Evidence

Current head: `95d83ad28f203ee6ec15ad60f69c06060a7235a5`. Exact-head [CI39994486818](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39994486818) **passed**: 75 jobs (47 success, 28 skipped), no failures or pending jobs.

- **160 distinct relevant tests passed cumulatively**: 128 PDF/provider/sibling/config tests, 26 official subagent-fixture tests and 6 new authority controls. The final-effect follow-up's affected suite is 48/48 (6 authority, 13 opt-in, 29 existing PDF), a subset of that total. Full/runtime builds, affected production/test typechecks, targeted lint/format, SDK exports, schema/docs and formal extension/core graph boundaries pass. Independent full-candidate, credential-handoff and final-effect reviews found no actionable P0/P1 defect.
- **Authority red/green:** before the fence, each of four retired-owner cases sent one synthetic HTTP request. After it, operator and physical-credential retirement after provider or DNS awaits each require reached-injection, the correct owner failure, HTTP0 and no completion fallback. Allowed and nearest-forbidden controls also pass. Provider cases use the real bundled callback; DNS cases use the real guarded-fetch lookup seam. These are authority-owner tests, not live credential rotation.
- **Published stable 2026.10.6 saved-config upgrade:** verified official artifact integrity, authored ordered settings with the published CLI, then validated and edited the same isolated saved state with the built candidate CLI. Ordering and limits are preserved, absent remains absent and explicit false remains false. This is configuration compatibility proof.
- **Earlier real OpenAI API proof:** the actual PDF tool/prepared provider/extractor, using synthetic documents only, returned HTTP200 and expected results for native input and four extraction cases (unset, selected page, password/encrypted, configured text-only). An initial HTTP401 exposed the scoped sentinel-handoff error; the corrected native request returned HTTP200, native=true and expected values. Its successful result was reconciled without replay after a harness-only model-label assertion correction. This proof is bound to preceding implementation head `ac5c3699`; the relevant native transport/payload owners remain unchanged. It is separate from the real Gateway proof below.

### Real isolated Gateway, normal agent route

The built official CLI and GatewayClient used real pinned WSS admission, `health` RPC, one durable synthetic profile, normal `agent`/same-run `agent.wait`, `deliver: false`, and actual `users.setRole` plus effective-role readback. The planner model remained allowed while the nearest negative excluded only the PDF model. PDF model/fallback selection was fixed explicitly.

The Gateway ran the actual run-owned PDF tool. Its planner/PDF HTTP used a synthetic loopback sink through the existing runtime-dependency seam, retaining real DNS/Agent/pinned dispatcher and the final synchronous HTTP authority check. Body/auth inspection was in memory only.

| Condition | Planner HTTP | Native PDF HTTP | Extraction PDF HTTP | Observed result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Allowed | 2 | 1 | 0 | Expected actual PDF tool result; pinned dispatcher observed |
| Same-profile/scopes, PDF model denied | 2 | 0 | 0 | Actual model refusal while planner remained usable |
| Role retired while PDF input held | 1 | 0 | 0 | Official owner change; original run ended/error and active root work returned 1 → 0 after release before HTTP0 was recorded |
| `pages: "2"` | 2 | 0 | 1 | Selected-page BETA present; excluded-page ALPHA absent |

All four submissions occurred once, and the original runs reached terminal state with backend work settled. The held-input Gateway retirement proves actual operator wiring; precise provider/DNS timing is covered separately by the focused red/green tests above.

The seven planner requests and seven other intercepted requests are counted separately. The latter remain unclassified and are not treated as PDF/fallback proof; there is no all-process external-egress claim. Gateway runtime build `4b0f4c12` was exercised from test-only source head `7c7816f3`, with explicit runtime-owner bindings to this head. The build is not relabeled as a build of the later merge commit. No production service, employee role, customer document or real channel delivery was used. All task-owned Gateway/driver processes and temporary credential/config/profile/TLS/log state, including failed attempts, have been removed.

## CI and Review Follow-through

Earlier CI found the generated config baseline and an inherited subagent fixture problem. Later official main changed that fixture's completion contract, so the borrowed adjustment was retired in favor of the exact official fixture files and its negative assertion. An authority test's private-extension import was also replaced with the existing public bundled-provider facade; both formal boundaries pass. These repairs add no PDF production behavior.

Previous implementation CI [39968310938](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39968310938) and authority CI [39986691358](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39986691358) passed at their respective heads. A final true conflict against official main `53fb615a` was limited to the generated configuration hash. This branch normally merges that fixed main and resolves the hash with the official generator. Independent blob review preserves the feature/authority/Gateway owners; the only tracked help-file change comes from official main. Current-head CI is reported above separately from preceding evidence.

The items in [the prior/current review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/127770#issuecomment-5377643651) are covered by explicit consent, bounded fallback, actual conflict repair, a concrete opt-in proposal, published-stable compatibility, the final-effect authority fence and actual Gateway evidence. [The later evidence reminder](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/127770#issuecomment-6051721637) is addressed by this refreshed evidence and description. The remaining adoption, setting-placement and merge decisions belong to maintainers.


<!-- evidence-gate-refresh:2026-10-24 -->

### 2026-10-24 current-main integration

- Merged upstream `main` at `05bc4bf5c9fc717841df38d169bb69fa3d88a52a` normally into candidate `f43a6edbca54b5e3ac6d288f0a9e79e919d6e427`; no force push. The only merge conflict was the generated config-baseline hash, regenerated from the merged schemas.
- Revalidated 40 focused PDF/config/authority tests, config-doc and Plugin SDK export/API contracts, core/extension/extension-test typechecks, touched-file type-aware lint and formatting, the full build (157 SDK subpaths), and a fresh P0/P1 autoreview with no actionable finding.
- The prior real OpenAI/Gateway evidence remains applicable because the provider transport and final-effect authority owners are unchanged by the main integration; the changed generated baseline was regenerated and checked at the new head.

prs.title: feat(workboard): add explicit decomposition orchestration
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workboard's hard parent/child dependency contract is correct for ordered work, but aggregate planning also needs an explicit non-blocking mode for independently runnable children. This PR adds that mode without changing the existing default or rewriting ambiguous stored state.

- Omitted `decompositionMode` remains `hard`.
- `decompositionMode: "hard"` creates reciprocal dependency links, so children wait for the parent.
- Explicit `decompositionMode: "orchestration"` records parent/child provenance without a hard dependency, so independently runnable children can be claimed while the aggregate parent remains open.
- Graph diagnostics identify broken dependencies, dependency cycles, and stale hard links on explicitly orchestrated decompositions.
- Operator-scoped unlink and repair tools are idempotent, declared in the plugin/tool contracts, and preserve audit history with one truthful `link_removed` event per changed card.

## Compatibility and stored-state policy

This head does **not** reverse Workboard's documented default and does **not** add an automatic Doctor migration.

Historical rows without an explicit decomposition mode are treated as existing hard intent and are left unchanged. `workboard_repair_decomposition` only proposes or removes a reciprocal hard link when both the parent and child are explicitly marked `orchestration`, the parent's decomposition manifest contains the child, and child provenance points back to the parent. Ambiguous or manually linked relationships are skipped.

Idempotent retries cannot silently change an existing child's decomposition contract. A retry that reuses a child with an incompatible explicit mode fails before the parent records the conflicting mode. An orchestration retry may reuse a child only when the parent and child already carry matching orchestration provenance and no hard dependency remains; ambiguous historical rows fail closed. Rollback preserves both cards unchanged.

## Evidence

### Disposable SQLite behavior proof

The proof used a fresh temporary Workboard SQLite database, closed and reopened it before verification, redacted identifiers, and removed it afterward. No production or live Workboard state was read or changed.

```json

```

### Review repair and current-main verification on `0b061a2d7ce68b522ce35b41494f6247a91af127`

- Repaired the three current durable-review findings: ambiguous historical orchestration retry, partial multi-card repair, and dropped Control UI recovery actions.
- An orchestration retry now requires matching explicit parent/child provenance and no retained hard link; the mode-less historical hard-link regression proves both cards remain byte-for-byte unchanged on rejection.

All four production/test type gates passed on the immediately preceding repair head before this conflict-free main-only merge.

Changed-file type-aware Oxlint, exact-file Oxfmt, `git diff --check`, UI i18n verification, UI production build, docs listing, MDX validation, and **6,425-link** audit all passed.
- A disposable exact-build Gateway bound only to loopback exercised the real WebSocket API. The final run passed **19/19** contract checks across omitted/explicit-hard blocking, explicit-orchestration claimability, invalid-mode atomicity, incompatible and ambiguous retry fail-closed behavior, dry-run/apply/idempotent repair, scoped all-candidate preflight, and reopened SQLite persistence.

prs.title: perf(sessions): remove unused filter yield machinery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session-list filtering retains generator state and yield checkpoints even though every current consumer runs the complete operation synchronously. This machinery survived the session-list worker revert and adds allocation on every scan.

## User Impact

No intended behavior change: filtering, authorization, archive-specific views, profile references, paging, and ordering remain unchanged. Allocation decreases without another cache or revision lifecycle.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the unused cooperative filter/selection/profile-reference APIs with one synchronous path, updating transcript search, plugin session facts, work metrics, and diagnostic callers together. The shared generic sorter keeps its cooperative API for other consumers. Production code is **40 lines smaller**; no schema, configuration, dependency, or public SDK change.

## Evidence

Measurements use 5,000 synthetic sessions and isolated Gateways on Linux/Node 26.12.1. Each A/B pair runs concurrently under the shared guard and exclusive measurement slot; the second pair swaps the interleaved physical-core placements. The pinned benchmark base is `2a7d1994c2a1477483661bc4af5cc90e4d76e8df`; the candidate applies this PR's production patch. Those production files and the selection/prepared-read owners are unchanged between that base and the PR's rebased parent `e60285cd037264a1b8097722c1ead51a99b8dc54`.

### Filter owner

Each side executes 11,000 operations across 11 archive/label/agent/kind/static-search shapes, with 1,100 row-revision updates. CPU/allocation/GC include updates; operation latency measures filtering. Both pairs start with zero observed skew.

| Metric | Pair 1 baseline → candidate | Pair 2 baseline → candidate | Mean paired change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Allocated bytes/op | 603,579 → 236,811 | 604,291 → 236,734 | **−60.80%; −367,163 B/op** |
| Main-thread CPU ms/op | 0.49228 → 0.43702 | 0.48138 → 0.41821 | **−12.17%; −0.05921 ms/op** |
| Filter p95 ms (11,000 samples/side/pair) | 0.95053 → 0.79218 | 0.75844 → 0.72509 | −10.53%; −0.09585 ms |
| Filter p99 ms (11,000 samples/side/pair) | 1.22673 → 0.98090 | 0.83407 → 0.81468 | −11.18%; −0.13261 ms |
| Total GC ms/op | 0.01365 → 0.00835 | 0.01199 → 0.00689 | **−40.70%; −0.00520 ms/op** |
| GC collections | 1,913 → 1,170 | 1,875 → 1,172 | −38.17% |
| Max GC pause ms | 0.56660 → 0.58601 | 0.58583 → 0.53733 | Below max-pause threshold |

All four before/after-churn golden files are byte-identical (782,608 bytes, SHA-256 `db238c40c7795546b9ce88d5f9aba385eca2f10f72825af98cde913d4d100b3c`). An earlier probe failed to drain GC observer callbacks; its zero-GC readings were discarded and these corrected pairs replace them.

### Gateway boundary

Each side executes 2,000 measured `sessions.list` calls and 200 real `sessions.patch` label updates, after 200 warmup lists and 20 warmup updates. Seven shapes cover default/open/archive/search/agent/subagent/system+cron filters. Per-shape counts are schedule-derived (286 for the first five, 285 for the final two); list and patch totals are observed. CPU/allocation/GC include churn; handler timings cover list calls only. Use the aligned allocation window, excluding the profiler's forced post-measurement collection.

| Metric | Pair 1 baseline → candidate | Pair 2 baseline → candidate | Pair 3 baseline → candidate | Signed mean change (relative to mean baseline) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Allocated bytes/op | 2,099,833 → 2,038,388 | 2,167,349 → 2,050,337 | 2,115,226 → 2,027,200 | **−88,828 B/op (−4.18%)** |
| Main-thread CPU ms/op | 6.20274 → 6.65272 | 6.03058 → 6.02808 | 5.50105 → 5.45743 | +0.13462 ms/op (+2.28%) |
| List handler mean ms | 4.88417 → 5.23186 | 4.77647 → 4.70985 | 4.20559 → 4.19333 | +0.08960 ms (+1.94%) |
| Handler p95 ms (2,000 samples/side/pair) | 13.118 → 13.502 | 12.350 → 12.030 | 10.942 → 10.878 | 0.000 ms (0.00%) |
| Handler p99 ms (2,000 samples/side/pair) | 15.934 → 16.510 | 15.550 → 15.422 | 12.990 → 12.542 | 0.000 ms (0.00%) |
| Total GC ms/op | 0.16654 → 0.16429 | 0.19683 → 0.21846 | 0.13873 → 0.12770 | **+0.00278 ms/op (+1.66%)** |
| Promoted bytes/op | 72,341 → 73,329 | 73,250 → 75,100 | 74,237 → 75,108 | +1,236 B/op (+1.69%) |
| GC collections | 171 → 168 | 210 → 201 | 175 → 183 | Context for pause distribution |
| Max GC pause ms | 26.345 → 18.158 | 26.685 → 27.602 | 16.753 → 15.120 | No max-pause violation |

Tail context, with collection/sample counts shown beside each value:

| Metric | Pair 1 baseline → candidate | Pair 2 baseline → candidate | Pair 3 baseline → candidate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Event-loop p99 ms | 31.293 (686) → 31.769 (724) | 32.768 (674) → 31.736 (677) | 29.082 (618) → 29.147 (623) |
| Minor GC p95 ms | 2.734 (167) → 3.086 (164) | 3.198 (206) → 3.182 (195) | 2.094 (171) → 1.638 (179) |
| Minor GC p99 ms | 3.390 (167) → 3.374 (164) | 7.902 (206) → 17.022 (195) | 2.702 (171) → 2.094 (179) |
| Major GC p95/p99 ms | 20.222 (2) → 18.174 (2) | 17.022 (2) → 16.894 (3) | 16.766 (2) → 15.166 (2) |

The original swapped pairs had opposing GC/work and timing deltas, so v5.2 required the third pair. The table uses signed mean deltas in absolute units across all three pairs. Initial GC/work changes were −1.35% (−0.00226 ms/op) and +10.99% (+0.02163 ms/op); the third was −7.95% (−0.01103 ms/op). Neither the final mean nor both original pairs cross the adverse thresholds. Event-loop and minor-GC p99 lack 1,000 samples per side; minor-GC p95 lacks 200 on both sides of any pair; major GC has fewer than 50 collections. These tails are context, not passing gates. Minor-GC p95 also has a sub-millisecond absolute mean change under v5.3.

The post-work 20-query response captures preserve field presence, session data, counts, and ordering. Normalize only the explicitly recorded response clocks (`ts`, `snapshotAt`), generated `rowsRevision`, sandbox database path, and the harness-created `agent:main:main` row's generated session/lifecycle UUIDs and creation/update clocks. That main row is asserted to be the synthetic broadcast root; seeded rows' IDs, data, counts, and order are not normalized. All six normalized captures match byte-for-byte (1,916,252 bytes, SHA-256 `c7a32d82fc6061c9680227b53d1be409b4a462959dd07ca0c46c2117b44cbace`).

Decision: accept this net-deletion simplification. Filter allocation drops substantially; whole-Gateway allocation drops consistently across all three pairs. Whole-Gateway CPU/handler/GC/promotion changes remain below the campaign thresholds; this is not a whole-handler speedup claim. The small GC/work increase is reported alongside the allocation reduction. No collection errors or dropped diagnostic/histogram samples occurred. Gateway start skew was 4/6/3 ms. The third pair recorded two high-load guard samples, but the unchanged shared guard did not reach its three-consecutive-minute abort condition or interrupt the pair.

### Validation and review

Baseline filter tests: 18 passed. Candidate focused filter/search/profile-reference tests: 31 passed across three files. The changed identity-filter benchmark test also [passed on the exact head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40044664020/job/120724154279) (126 ms; its Bun-emitted zero CPU timings are not performance evidence). Changed-file formatting/lint and the single `pnpm tsgo:core` lane passed. Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable) found no actionable P0–P2 findings; the configured provider mismatch was preserved without configuration changes. ClawSweeper reported no findings.

Exact-head CI on `134cad66db89aa9646fd5b0d34a72e78392f384d`: [run 40044664020](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40044664020), 47 passed, 24 skipped. [UI e2e 1/2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40044664020/job/120724153424) failed four cases in `sidebar-complete-roster.e2e.test.ts:105`, waiting for the initial child toggle; the aggregate gate failed downstream. All database shards and security checks passed. The fixture filters its own rows and imports only the unchanged comparator from this PR's production files.

Inherited failure confirmed by one local replay on each revision, using Node 26.12.1, the same existing dependencies and the same single-file command. PR head `134cad66db89aa9646fd5b0d34a72e78392f384d` and freshly fetched main `7b71c23797646bed71dc869b83a1c51764c267a6` both fail all four cases at `sidebar-complete-roster.e2e.test.ts:105:24`: the initial child toggle never becomes visible. Both exit 1 with `locator.waitFor: Timeout 10000ms exceeded` (CI uses 30000ms for the same wait). Head duration: 78.77s; main: 79.42s. The test, synthetic list owner, and sidebar projection module are byte-identical between revisions. No retries, CI reruns, test edits, or Team use. This establishes the UI failure as inherited; the CI aggregate fails only downstream. Landing uses the authorized inherited-failure exception; CI is not represented as green.

Focused replay command:

```sh
OPENCLAW_UI_E2E_SKIP_REAL_GATEWAY=1 CI=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/sidebar-complete-roster.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

No deployment or post-deployment performance result is claimed.

prs.title: fix(ui): preserve Shift+Enter newlines with composer suggestions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Shift+Enter in the chat composer can execute the selected slash suggestion instead of inserting a newline. With /help selected this opens Available Commands and consumes the draft, even though the user asked for a newline.

The existing shared suggestion-key handler now leaves Shift+Enter to the textarea, preserving ordinary Enter selection and Tab completion. No new state or dispatch path.

## Evidence

Production Control UI and Gateway were built together on Linux in secretless Docker (Node 24.22.1), with state created only through shipped setup/config commands and sessions.create RPC. Playwright uses the real connected chat route and actual keyboard input, not a mounted composer or mock Gateway.

Baseline main `05bc4bf5c9f` versus candidate `e5a6bf072ac27b73cda4d92d55f8a6a10e3a6910`: twice per arm, /help + Shift+Enter executes local help and consumes the draft on main; candidate preserves exactly `/help\n`, keeps focus, shows no help result and sends no chat turn. Tab completes `/hel` without executing, and ordinary Enter then executes local help on both. A real bundled Weather skill suggestion also distinguishes selection on main from native newline insertion on candidate.

Inspected, render-checked before/after images and comparison: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181999#issuecomment-6378452206

Observed DOM values: main `/help` + Shift+Enter → empty draft plus Available Commands; candidate → `/help\n` with textarea focused. Main `$wea` + Shift+Enter → `$weather `; candidate → `$wea\n`. Neither skill case sent chat.send. Accessibility snapshots identify the real “Slash commands” / “Skill references” listbox and “Chat composer” textbox. A startup-incomplete attempt was discarded; the final harness waits for the actual enabled Send message button before the key.

Simplification over the entire diff kept the single existing-owner guard: production +1/-0, tests +36/-0. Unit tests distinguish populated and consuming-empty menus; the Chromium composer test exercises actual newline insertion. Focused helper tests (4), Chromium regression (1), formatting and lint pass.

Exact candidate live provider gate also passes: shipped automation with openai/gpt-5.4-mini returns LIVE_PIN_OK. Temporary credential removed.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: reverting fully restores the prior keyboard behavior; no persistence/config change. Blast radius is Shift+Enter with composer suggestion menus open; ordinary Enter and Tab behavior remain unchanged.

prs.title: fix(sessions): report archive cleanup in sessions cleanup
prs.body:
Fixes #75658

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running `openclaw sessions cleanup --dry-run` could not preview expired `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` transcript archives, and apply output did not report the physical archive files it removed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cleanup uses the configured archive-retention rules for preview and apply reporting. Physical archive retention is owned by the canonical config/session lifecycle module shared by SQLite cleanup and Gateway callers, without a config-to-Gateway runtime bridge or a new session-accessor debt exemption.

Logical ownership remains separate from physical directory identity. A selected agent cannot remove archives from a directory shared by another configured agent, including a symlink alias; `--all-agents` can clean that physical directory once.

Successful retention deletion clears reset-archive discovery state before notifying transcript subscribers. Dry-run stays non-mutating: archive-directory identity checks use a read-only matcher and never create missing-path alias probes.

## User Impact

Users can see deleted/reset transcript archive cleanup in dry-run and apply summaries. Shared directories stay protected during agent-scoped cleanup, while all-agent cleanup deduplicates physical work and reports the result.

## Current Head

- Head: `add96cdb4c807a6d3e5c6b60ffc352b5292733ca`.
- Rebased onto upstream `main` `165a2e9ede696adbc84313bbb731ee89c1ef53d2`.
- Author and committer: `Sami Rusani <samgithub@pm.me>`.

## Evidence

- Rebase resolution retained current-main compatibility-owner logic and the PR's configured-owner archive coordinator. The resulting change has no conflict markers and `git diff --check` passed.
- Focused archive/config/lifecycle tests: 131 passed across 4 files.
- Command rendering tests: 13 passed.
- Gateway archive tests: 45 passed across 3 files.
- Session-accessor boundary guard and changed-file formatting check passed.
- `pnpm dev` rebuilt the CLI and bundled plugin assets before the isolated CLI proof.
- Changed-file lint was queued behind a separate repository validation lock; exact-head hosted CI remains required before merge.

## CLI Proof

Disposable isolated fixture with two logical agents sharing one archive directory, one expired `.deleted` archive, and one fresh `.reset` archive:

- selected-agent dry-run: reports `shared-directory-requires-all-agents` and preserves the directory;
- all-agent dry-run: scans 2 archives and reports 1 eligible deletion;
- explicit offline apply: scans 2, removes the expired archive, and leaves the fresh archive present.

No external service, credentials, or user data was used.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted: yes. Codex was used to inspect contributor rules and review feedback, rebase the patch, resolve current-main integration conflicts, run focused validation, and produce the isolated CLI proof. No agent transcript is attached.
