prs.title: perf(cron): reuse source validation at transcript target checks
prs.body:
## Outcome: rejected by the GC max-pause gate

Do not merge this candidate. The first valid concurrent timing pair hit the v5.1 maximum-pause gate: **107.27 ms baseline → 1,110.91 ms candidate**, above `max(50 ms, 2 × 107.27 ms) = 214.55 ms`. The main-isolate raw trace independently reports 1,110.79 ms. The guard did not interrupt the pair. Remaining measurements were stopped; there is no swapped-pair mean or allocation estimate, and the green CI/review do not override this performance gate.

The assertion reduction is verified, but this measurement does not establish that the change caused the long pause. It establishes that this candidate has not met the agreed landing criterion. The branch preserves the implementation, regression tests, and reusable cron instrumentation for a future investigation.

## What Problem This Solves

Authenticated cron turns repeatedly traverse recovered operator authority during transcript target checks, bookkeeping, and synchronous tool registration. Prior diagnostic evidence in #182002 observed about 38,550 availability checks per turn.

## User Impact

Completed-output accounting and trajectory recording retain their exact run lifetime without repeating operator policy validation. Tool execution, approvals, credentials, and delivery retain full live-source validation, including synchronous policy-callback revocation.

## Why This Change Was Made

A prepared transcript target repeated a full source traversal already performed by its attempt controller. Use the controller’s source check, then verify the captured run binding. Recheck exact attempt ownership after source callbacks, since a synchronous callback can close or replace an attempt without closing its admitted run. Keep the final transcript commit assertion.

Receipt composition dropped its inputs' existing lifetime-only assertions, forcing bookkeeping back through full authority checks. Preserve that contract at the receipt owner, use it for bookkeeping/prepared data, and run one composed check during tool registration. No cache, new configuration, or state migration. Production delta: +31/-26 (net +5). The existing lifetime-only contract must survive receipt composition, and the attempt owner needs an explicit post-callback ownership check; those correctness requirements account for the small net growth.

The existing Gateway benchmark now creates an authenticated same-conversation scheduled job through the real automations tool, executes its tools, verifies its receipt, and attributes assertion calls by stack. The cron workload is adapted from #182002.

## Evidence

- 38 existing recovered-operator tests passed, including synchronous policy-callback revocation (62.10 seconds including compilation).
- The new bookkeeping/revocation test failed on the original policy check and passes with the change. It exercises the real admitted caller and host, records completed output after policy revocation, and verifies the next bound tool does not execute.
- Focused host lifetime/environment, tool authority, host capability, and Gateway caller tests pass. Final follow-up: 111 tests, 40.97 seconds including compilation. Earlier focused pass proved the 10 source-lifetime and 2 environment tests; three registration error-order failures were fixed and the affected file rerun.
- Both new synchronous callback regressions (close attempt / replace attempt) fail on the original attempt owner and pass with the fix. Dispatch-owner and lane-controller tests: 58 passed in 43.44 seconds. Transcript lifecycle and original controller coverage: 76 passed before the final ownership fix.
- Changed-file lint, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable P0–P2 findings. No operator configuration changes. Hosted Codex review also completed on `d30a3133c2c856e1587840287827f81e49fb521c` without findings.
- Exact-head PR CI on `d30a3133c2c856e1587840287827f81e49fb521c`: 81 successful checks, no failures; CI gate and security-sensitive review passed.
- Count-only diagnostic on the revised transcript path: 38,807 → 29,170 availability checks, 13,565 → 10,213 recovery assertions, and 23,821 → 17,957 source assertions per turn (three tool completions, five message appends). All six candidate owner snapshots were attested as loaded. The first timing pair failed the maximum-pause gate; subsequent timing/allocation measurements were stopped. No Testbox lease used; broad validation belongs to PR CI.

### Measurement acceptance rule

Use an isolated Gateway and synthetic loopback model: four fixture sessions, one active cron turn, five stream chunks, real tool callbacks, successful same-conversation receipt, no session reset. Counts use a separate instrumented pass and never supply timing evidence. Compare at least five turns per side in each of two concurrent, exclusively locked pairs, swapping interleaved CPU placement. One source installation, separate state/ports, and attested baseline/candidate owner overlays.

Report assertions, allocation, CPU, and latency per turn; GC total/promotion per work unit; maxima and tail sample counts. Apply v5.3: reject ≥20% adverse paired mean or ≥10% in both pairs. Opposite signs or >5× baseline spread are inconclusive, require absolute deltas and a third gating pair. p99 requires 1,000 samples, p95 200, major-GC tails 50 collections. Sub-1 ms paired pause-percentile shifts are context. Fewer collections ≥20% with nonincreasing total GC makes pause percentiles context. Candidate max pause >max(50 ms, 2× baseline max) retains its gate. Discard guard-interrupted pairs.


### Caller classification

One baseline diagnostic turn: 38,853 availability checks, partitioned by first meaningful caller (179 distinct locations; no overlapping stack-substring counts). The final same-base count comparison above uses a later diagnostic turn, so incidental scheduling counts differ slightly. The workload performs three real tool completions, commits five message appends, and delivers its scheduled result.

| Caller group | Availability checks | Classification and action |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Session target settings validation | 9,978 | Current policy/target validation nested in authority; retain peer-adjacent owner. |
| Attempt controller `isCurrent` | 7,021 | Retain full validation as the prepared target’s single source check; recheck exact ownership after callbacks. |
| Prepared target’s explicit active assertion | 6,970 | Repeated synchronous validation; replace with final exact scope check. |
| Transcript lifecycle commit | 6,919 | State mutation boundary; retain prepared source validation. |
| Plugin construction/caller guards | 1,224 | Source/caller admission; retain. |
| Other target capture/admission | 1,009 | Original caller/source capture; retain. |
| Watchdog validity/attachment | 918 | Lifecycle bookkeeping (901) and attachment admission (17); unchanged, scope-only follow-up possible. |
| Tool construction preparation | 527 | Source-bound caller preparation; retain. |
| Exec/process/client-tool dispatch | 705 | Privileged effects; retain. |
| Session-tool operator authority | 114 | Privileged session-tool authority; retain. |
| Session state readers/writers | 313 | Storage/source boundaries; retain. |
| Native registration | 155 | Retain ownership; deduplicate synchronous active traversals in registration callback. |
| Audit owner binding | 102 | Owner bookkeeping across asynchronous binding; retain exact owner capture. |
| Runtime/model/workspace preparation | 1,717 | Mixed admission, credential/model policy and bookkeeping; unchanged. |
| Reply orchestration/policy/delivery | 883 | Mixed admission, delivery and terminal bookkeeping; unchanged. |
| Session admission/mailbox/tool snapshot | 129 | Source admission/ownership; retain. |
| Cron capture/settlement/heartbeat | 135 | Mixed occurrence admission, settlement and bookkeeping; unchanged. |
| Provider rate-limit stream | 34 | Request/authentication after awaited rate limit; retain. |
| **Total** | **38,853** | |

The built-in workload does not directly call host output-token/trajectory bookkeeping. Those scope-only changes are proven by the focused admitted-host revocation test; the count reduction principally demonstrates transcript-target and registration changes. The mixed residual buckets are not a claim that every remaining assertion is necessary. No global authority memoization or fail-open fallback is introduced.


### Recorded measurement and limits

One valid concurrent pair, 20 completed cron turns per side, interleaved slot-B CPUs (baseline even 64–94; candidate odd 65–95), separate synthetic state and loopback ports. prs.title: fix(gateway): stop publication footer stripping from backtracking
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The publication description stripper used

```
(?:\s*---\s*\n\[View the OpenClaw team session\]\([^\r\n)]*\)\s*)+$
```

The trailing `\s*` sits **inside** the repeated group, so whitespace between two
footers has two possible owners — the previous unit's trailing `\s*` or the next
unit's leading one. Once the body ends in anything the pattern cannot consume,
the engine walks every split of that ambiguity before failing.

## Evidence: real publication, before and after

The production-path proof uses unmocked `runCommandBuffered`, real `git`, real `gh`,
and real draft pull requests in a throwaway public repository. It runs through
`coordinator.requestForSession` into `executeGitHubPublication`; no publication
transport or PR-creation response is mocked.

With the fix, a 1,103-byte description containing 28 unfinished footer-shaped units
published successfully in 18,213 ms as
[lzhan011/openclaw-publication-proof#3](https://github.com/lzhan011/openclaw-publication-proof/pull/3).
The resulting 1,271-byte body preserved the incomplete units and appended exactly
one canonical session footer.

With only the regex restored to `main` and the same input/setup, publication failed
with `OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_LOST`: synchronous backtracking held the thread long
enough for the publication state lease to expire before commit.

A prior real 26-unit pair was inconclusive because variable `git push` and GitHub API
latency exceeded the regex-cost difference (37,952 ms before versus 47,038 ms after);
both runs published. On that exact input, isolated pattern timing was 16,154.5 ms on
`main` versus 0.1 ms with the fix, with byte-identical output.

The focused regression test uses mocked command transport so it can assert a stable
five-second bound in CI. Its 90 ms local and 364 ms CI measurements validate the
same coordinator path but are not claimed as end-to-end GitHub timings. The real
proof above covers identity resolution, commit, branch update, push, and pull-request
creation; it drives the coordinator directly rather than through a running Gateway
server.

## Why This Change Was Made

`row.body` is supplied by the caller of the publication request — the
`github-publish` agent tool (`src/agents/tools/github-publish-tool.ts:42`) or the
Gateway protocol method — and reaches this line unchanged:
`input.body` (`github-publication-coordinator-methods.ts:167`) →
`requestForClaim({ body })` → `body: request.body ?? null`
(`github-publication-store.ts:186`) → `row.body`.

The fix hoists the trailing `\s*` out of the group:

```
(?:\s*---\s*\n\[View the OpenClaw team session\]\([^\r\n)]*\))+\s*$
```

Whitespace between footers now has exactly one owner. The language is unchanged:
a differential run of the two patterns over **400,000 random strings** assembled
from footer-shaped fragments (`---`, newlines, tabs, spaces, CR, the link label,
parens, complete footers, plain text) found **0 differences**.

## Review items addressed

- **Proof through the production executor.** The numbers above come from
  `coordinator.requestForSession` running to pull-request creation, not from the
  pattern in isolation.
- **Test consolidation.** The earlier revision exported a
  `stripPublicationDescriptionFooters` helper purely so a unit test could reach
  it. That export is gone; the fix is inline again and the regression test lives
  in `github-publication-attribution.test.ts` alongside the other
  published-output assertions. Production delta is now **+5 / -1**.

## Checks

`oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on both changed files — clean.
`vitest run src/gateway/github-publication-attribution.test.ts
src/gateway/github-publication.test.ts` — 23/23 passed.

**Pre-existing failure, not from this change.** `pnpm tsgo:core` fails on
`src/infra/install-package-dir.ts(551,15): error TS2353`, inherited from `main`.

## How This Was Found

CodeQL `js/redos` over a `src/` database. The reachability of `row.body` and the
8 KiB cap were traced by hand, and every number above was measured.

## Diff accounting

- production: +5 / -1
- tests: +43 / -0

prs.title: fix(slack): accept thread follow-ups before the first reply
prs.body:
Closes #139152.

## What Problem This Solves

A human adds an unmentioned clarification to an accepted Slack request while its first response is still running. The clarification is skipped because delivered-reply participation does not yet exist.

## User Impact

With thread participation enabled, accepted human work temporarily makes the same thread eligible for human follow-ups before the first visible reply. Eligibility ends with the existing publisher/queued-work lifetime; delivered participation is still persisted only after actual delivery.

This expands the documented activation contract for installations already using thread participation. **Maintainer acceptance of that policy remains required; no previously working release is claimed.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing active Slack publisher registry. Current main's extracted thread-mention owner resolves eligibility, preserving its bot-owned-thread policy, explicit mention settings, sender restrictions, and thread/account/monitor boundaries. Bot/control/abort inputs cannot open temporary human participation. No new store, scheduler, timeout, retry, or production runtime patch is introduced.

Integrated fixed official main `228b5e9e7df8b978a85a0f3f3aa249b705f383aa` with an ordinary merge to repair actual preparation-owner conflicts. Main retains a single `prepareSlackMessage` owner. Existing in-flight human eligibility is carried into its inline conversation shape; retired context/authorization helper frames are not restored. Existing mention decision and unchanged source classification live together in the existing thread-mention sibling. The shrink-only line-cap contract passes without an exception.

Removed the duplicate in-process scripted-agent pipeline and its helper (436 lines). The actual Gateway proves model/final delivery, focused prepare tests own policy/isolation, and existing dispatch tests now verify human eligibility through first-mode and queued settlement. Failure and cleanup coverage remains in the existing dispatch owner.

## Evidence

Candidate: `d8c6f0427d056988a288c34f63839db6c4e0aa02`; ordinary merge parents are the previous accepted head `637a18c3417d663940f2dda43f808adc1786f743` and fixed official main `228b5e9e7df8b978a85a0f3f3aa249b705f383aa`.

The corrected Evidence-heading check [39897416741](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39897416741) passes; its earlier failed run remains historical. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Sessions transcript search unconditionally consumes Escape, removing the focused input even when the key belongs to a modified shortcut or an active composition. Keep ownership in the existing input handler, matching the neighboring roster search.

## Evidence

Built Gateway and Control UI from the same checkout in secretless Docker, Node 24.22.1. State was created through shipped config commands and sessions.create RPC; Playwright drove the real connected /sessions page. Baseline main 2777bd87e9c64d93771b5bc16528567a8884076f and candidate 1bc7f647344e7966616d71e3864726da1784c768 each ran twice.

- Decisive real keyboard red/green: Ctrl+Escape, Alt+Escape and Shift+Escape each remove the input on main; each leaves it connected and focused on candidate.
- Browser-level composition proof: CDP Input.imeSetComposition followed by Input.dispatchKeyEvent delivers key=Escape with isComposing=true. Main collapses search; candidate retains it. This is browser-level composition, **not an OS-native IME red**. The IME fix targets platforms delivering key=Escape with isComposing=true.
- Linux IBus/libpinyin native control: xdotool types a real composition and cancels it. Escape arrives as key=Process/keyCode=229; main already behaves correctly, as does candidate. This is a non-reproducing control, not evidence of an OS IME regression.
- Ordinary Escape still collapses search, returns focus to the trigger, and reopening preserves the query on both arms.
- Screenshots and accessibility snapshots capture the built connected page before/during/after composition. No fake history or source-only app server.
- Exact candidate real-provider gate passed: OpenAI gpt-5.4-mini completed the shipped automation run with LIVE_PIN_OK; its temporary credential file was deleted.

Simplification: one existing key handler remains the sole owner; no listener, state, abstraction or SDK change. Whole diff: production +10/-1; tests +62, covering rendered focus ownership and the browser component boundary. Remaining growth is the explicit keyboard-ownership predicate.
Images (uploaded and render-checked), with the comparison evidence: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181991#issuecomment-6378160186


## Merge danger

Two-way door: revert fully restores the prior key handling; no persisted state or config migration. Blast radius is Escape handling in Sessions transcript search only.

prs.title: fix(reply): log dispatcher observer failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reply-dispatcher observers could fail without leaving any diagnostic. A rejected `onIdle` callback also prevented `onSettled` from running, so deferred delivery cleanup could be skipped during an otherwise completed turn.

The dispatcher now reports observer failures through its subsystem logger. Idle cleanup attempts `onSettled` even when `onIdle` fails, while preserving the original idle failure for the observer boundary.

## User Impact

Operators now get an actionable warning when an `onIdle`, `onSettled`, or `onError` observer fails instead of silent loss. Settlement cleanup is no longer skipped solely because the idle callback threw.

Delivery ordering, reply counts, and cancellation behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`invokeReplyDispatcherObserver` intentionally isolates failures so delivery bookkeeping can finish, but its default reporter was a no-op. The typing wrapper also awaited `onIdle` before `onSettled`, which let a throwing idle observer bypass settlement cleanup.

The change keeps observer isolation intact, adds a bounded warning through `auto-reply/reply-dispatcher`, and makes the idle wrapper run both callbacks sequentially.

## Evidence

Base-red (`origin/main` plus the new regression tests): both cases fail because no warning is emitted, and the idle failure skips `onSettled`.

Head-green:

```text

src/auto-reply/reply/reply-flow.test.ts                  17 passed
```

prs.title: fix(sessions): apply archive retention without cron
prs.body:
Closes #181976

## What Problem This Solves

A configured archive-retention window was silently ignored when cron was disabled. Expired reset/deleted transcript archives and their SQLite rows stayed on disk indefinitely. The regular transcript maintenance pass now applies that retention without requiring cron.

- Problem: `session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention` was only read by the cron session reaper, and only when that reaper deleted a cron-run session. With `cron.enabled: false`, no pass ever aged out `.deleted.*` / `.reset.*` archives.
- Solution: resolve the retention from the current runtime config and apply it in the existing periodic transcript-maintenance owner, using the existing file cleanup and archive-row pruning helpers.
- What changed: the maintenance owner now runs when cold storage is enabled **or** archive retention is configured; the sweep applies both `deleted` and `reset` rules across configured agent stores.
- What did NOT change: cron reaper behavior, cold-storage archiving, archive publication, config schema, and the `null`/`false` keep-forever behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Archive cleanup was implemented as a side effect of cron-run deletion, while the periodic transcript-maintenance owner was gated solely on cold-storage enablement. Keeping retention inside that existing 60-second owner makes the policy independent of cron without adding a new scheduler or command.

- Best fix: apply the existing archive-age policy through the session maintenance owner, as the issue's review recommended.
- Alternative: a startup warning was rejected because it documents the gap but still lets archives grow without bound.
- Risk / non-goals: no new CLI command and no change to the cron reaper or pagination internals. A failed file cleanup leaves the row in place for the next pass rather than hiding the failure.

## User Impact

Operators who disable cron now get the archive retention they configured. Operators who leave `resetArchiveRetention` unset or `false` keep the current keep-until-disk-budget behavior.

## Evidence

Runtime reproduction through the production maintenance function with cold storage disabled and `resetArchiveRetention: "1h"` (one archive two hours old, one fresh):

```text
before: { rows: 2, expiredFile: true, freshFile: true }
after: {
  rows: [ { archive_name: 'fresh.jsonl.deleted.2026-10-24T00-34-02.081Z' } ],
  expiredExists: false,
  freshExists: true
}
RESULT: PASS — expired archive removed, fresh archive retained
```

The same script on unmodified `main` retains both rows and both files:

```text
after: {
  rows: [
    { archive_name: 'expired.jsonl.deleted.2026-10-23T22-35-05.753Z' },
    { archive_name: 'fresh.jsonl.deleted.2026-10-24T00-35-05.753Z' }
  ],
  expiredExists: true,
  freshExists: true
}
Error: retention sweep did not remove only the expired archive
```

Focused regression tests:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/config/sessions/session-cold-storage.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       21 passed (21)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/session-cold-storage-maintenance.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       8 passed (8)
```

The new regression test fails on unmodified `main` with the expired row still present, and passes with the fix. What was not tested: a multi-hour wall-clock run and a production Gateway with a pre-existing archive backlog; the isolated run exercises the same production function and SQLite archive tables.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used `git grep`, `git log -S`, `node --import tsx`, and `vitest` to trace the cron-only retention path, reproduce the stale archive, and implement the maintenance sweep. The implementer understands the code: archive files are removed first, then rows whose files are gone are pruned, so an unexpired or still-published archive is never deleted. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(codex): preserve protected scheduled continuations
prs.body:
## Problem

A same-session scheduled or internal continuation can arrive while its retained Codex thread is still protected by native/background work. If the current dynamic-tool surface or producer-owned turn context differs, warm reuse can fall through to cold replacement and fail with:

```
Codex thread ... is claimed by active work; stop it first.
```

## What changed

- Recover the accepted native tool catalog only for a verified local protected binding.
- Rebuild executors from the current turn and bind only definitions whose names, schemas, and descriptions exactly match the accepted contract, so current authority remains decisive at tool I/O.
- Mark producer-owned conversation context as turn-local and relay it outside immutable thread identity.
- Annotate the direct cron delivery prompt path that was missing from #174900.
- Keep compaction/plan restoration distinct from transient developer handoff context.
- Pass the exact admitted session workspace to existing media-root validation; sibling/shared workspace access remains excluded.

## Safety boundaries

- Genuine immutable policy, provider, runtime, MCP, and plugin changes still rotate or reject.
- Genuine simultaneous claimed ownership is still rejected; this is not a concurrent claim-takeover mechanism.
- Direct/no-relay connections remain fail-closed: handoffs supplement creation policy, and changed protected context without a safe relay still refuses.
- Accepted catalogs restore declarations only. Executors and execution-policy checks are rebuilt from the current admitted turn.
- This intentionally avoids the broader persisted-catalog and completion-ownership architecture in #174900.

## ClawSweeper remediation evidence

| Concern | Evidence added |
|---|---|
| Allowed current owner | Retained declarations execute through freshly prepared current executors. |
| Identityless/private completion | Owner-only effects remain unavailable without current admitted authority. |
| Authority revoked before tool I/O | Revocation is asserted before executor invocation; no second executor call occurs. |
| Scheduled context delivery | Producer-to-harness and direct cron delivery paths are covered. |
| Post-compaction context | Current transient context is restored separately from compacted native history. |
| Existing stored data | A concrete v2026.10.6 stored binding is decoded and recovered without schema migration. |
| No-relay behavior | Documented and tested as fail-closed for changed protected context. |
| Consumer regressions | History, skill, attribution, subscription, and context-budget assertions now distinguish the exact conversation handoff while preserving their original semantics. |
| Provider mocks and protected hook | Real runtime exports are preserved and native metadata is seeded from the actual accepted declaration. |
| Media isolation | Exact session workspace is authorized; shared and sibling roots remain excluded. |

## Relationship to existing work

- Supersedes #176177 while retaining its verified native-catalog/current-executor repair and Stronggenetics attribution.
- Selectively incorporates the safe transient-context portion of #174900, with Ricardo Almeida and Paul Bohm attribution preserved.

## Validation

- Focused repaired consumer suites: 107 tests passed.
- Direct cron/session and turn-context suites: 21 tests passed.
- Final targeted rerun after lint repairs: 54 tests passed.
- Independent review reran 104 tests across 12 files and found no P0–P2 issues.
- Core/core-test/extension/extension-test type checks, formatting, ratchets, core/scripts lint, import-cycle checks, and changed-extension lint passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- The local host lacks a Codex CLI/authenticated native lane and Docker, so the proof is deterministic runner/native integration coverage rather than a live external Codex reproduction. Hosted CI is the final full-environment check.

## Remediation revision

The follow-up commit is intentionally narrow: 191 additions and 54 deletions across tests, fixtures, documentation, and one production-line correction. It also removes two obsolete full-mock exceptions.

prs.title: docs: add release manager and owner lifecycles
prs.body:
Closes #182071

## What Problem This Solves

Release owners depend on long kickoff and takeover prompts to preserve their mission, and there is no separate skill mode for coordinating releases and shared hotfixes across channels.

## User Impact

Maintainers can use short release-management requests or a compact generated brief. Beta management includes validated publication unless held; stable and extended-stable management require publication approval unless already granted. Explicit prepare-only requests, prior approvals, signed tags, and enforced workflow gates remain authoritative. No runtime, publisher, or workflow code changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Distills recurring lessons from 12 historical kickoff/handoff prompts into two linked roles within the existing release skill:

- A manager coordinates owner sessions, briefs, cross-channel hotfix dispositions, approval communication, and handoffs without becoming a second branch writer or publisher.
- An owner follows one lifecycle through preparation, failure/repair cycles, publication, verification, retrospective, and closeout.

Adds patch/feature lineage for all three channels, bounded recent-incident discovery, explicit late-hotfix intake and requalification, and takeover records that preserve authority and exact evidence. Corrects preparation's unconditional main-cut assumption and documents the stable controller's explicit cut selection. Existing phase references still own commands and detailed gates; no parallel orchestration service or prompt catalog is introduced.

Historical tag-replacement, blanket preflight-skipping, and bot-score instructions are deliberately not carried forward. Private prompt contents and operational credentials are not included.

## Evidence

- Read and compared all 12 source prompts with the current skill, release policy, and relevant phase references.
- Scenario review: beta patch/feature, stable patch/promotion, extended-stable patch/refresh, late hotfix intake, approved credential handoff, concurrent same-train owners, and closeout. Addressed the missing recent-open-issue/PR readiness pass.
- AutoReview: scoped-clean at P0/P1 before the two final focused documentation adjustments; those adjustments received a source/scenario review.
- Source-checked stable controller cut selection and confirmation against `scripts/lib/release-stable-phases.mts` and `scripts/release-stable.mts`.
- `pnpm docs:list`, targeted `pnpm dlx oxfmt@0.72.0 --check` on all seven changed files, 54 relative file/heading references, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Simplification pass: extends the existing skill and handoff rather than adding another skill, state system, or executable. Documentation-only: 389 lines added / 16 removed; production and test code unchanged.

The local commit hook could not use the shared tooling owner because its formatter version differs from the required 0.72.0. Exact-version isolated formatting passed; the documented separate-formatting-proof commit route was used without changing shared dependencies.

No release was dispatched or published; live release execution is outside this documentation PR's scope.

prs.title: fix: include nested PostgreSQL bridges in memory diagnostics
prs.body:
Related: #181432

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway memory diagnostics omitted PostgreSQL bridge isolates created inside other workers. A quiet Gateway could retain a substantial bridge footprint while its worker census and pressure reports hid those isolates.

## User Impact

`diagnostics.lanes`, memory samples, pressure warnings and exported diagnostic bundles now include `postgresBridgeCount` for direct and nested bridges. Direct bridges also participate in the existing worker/heap census. They overlap `workerCount`; nested heaps remain outside its direct-worker heap totals, as documented.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing worker registry owns one shared atomic direct-bridge counter per isolate. Its existing memory channel propagates counter descriptors recursively through registered parents, deduplicated by native thread ID. Bridge starts/exits update the counter; descriptor messages are needed only when descendants register or exit. Native parent exit retires its subtree, and self/unchanged descriptors do not echo. Store and lease-heartbeat parents attach the same diagnostic channel.

Plain Worker construction, PostgreSQL transport, SQL, locks and pool topology stay unchanged. GC-storm reporting remains in its existing lazy profile owner, and shared diagnostic types live in the existing leaf type module. No configuration option or competing registry is added.

## Evidence

The real-Worker regression is red on the base and green with this change. It covers direct/deeply nested bridges, late descendants, shared-buffer clone deduplication, subtree exit and root exit. A real Gateway completed eight turns and 185 seconds quiet: all nine reported counts matched the passive native census through four levels of workers; stable lanes were 65/65 and memory pressure 66/66. All child processes exited. The final commit only adjusts a GC test's measurement scope; production hashes match this verified clean runtime build.

Focused worker/census/inventory and GC checks, affected TSRS lanes, lint/format, zero-cycle architecture check, full runtime build, pr-simplify and independent P0–P3 autoreview passed. CI-discovered type-cycle, descriptor-echo and transfer-list defects were repaired; the GC cadence assertion retains its expected four messages while observing only its owned GC envelopes.

Final-head CI run [40047711007](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40047711007) actually executed all three PostgreSQL conformance shards: **1143 passed, 37 existing skips**. Security-fast passed. The aggregate gate remains red for three unrelated jobs: one-second `chat.send` timeout (reproduced identically on pristine main, with five sibling cases passing), plus eight mocked-browser cases in UI shards 2/9 and 6/9 (Files, sidebar roster and operator scopes). Personally inspected source and fixture inputs are identical between the actual CI main base and merge; those browser flows do not execute the PG bridge. These failures remain recorded and use the native inherited-failure route; no failed check is relabeled green. No timeout/assertion was weakened to qualify them.

The companion expiry change is #182048: three-minute cache expiry reduced the matched final quiet-minute PG RSS by 107.8 MiB and live bridges from 20 to 14, with identical warm requests/trips/statements and no extra warm bridge launches. That timing experiment does not establish a latency improvement.

prs.title: fix(discord): keep the gateway READY wait deadline on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Discord monitor's bounded wait for the gateway READY event keeps polling past its configured timeout when the system wall clock steps backward during the wait, so a Discord account that never reaches READY stalls in "connecting" for the length of the step instead of timing out and reconnecting with backoff.

## User Impact

User impact: a Discord channel whose gateway connection never becomes READY now always moves on to the reconnect-with-backoff path after `DISCORD_GATEWAY_READY_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 15s) of real elapsed time, regardless of NTP corrections or VM/laptop resume. Startup and recovery no longer hang on a wall-clock-inflated wait, and status keeps reporting the recovering lifecycle promptly.

## Why This Change Was Made

`waitForGatewayReady`'s inner `waitUntilReady` seeds `deadlineAt = Date.now() + gatewayReadyTimeoutMs` and checks `Date.now() >= deadlineAt` between 250ms polls armed with monotonic `setTimeout`. A backward wall-clock step during the wait inflates the remaining budget by the step, so the monitor polls for `15s + step` before logging the READY timeout and reconnecting; a forward step gives up early.

The deadline now lives on `performance.now()` — seed and expiry check — which is monotonic and unaffected by wall-clock adjustments. Status timestamps (`lastEventAt`, transport activity) stay on `Date.now()` because they are absolute wall-clock facts. This is the same cross-clock-domain pattern already fixed for command process-group teardown in #174151 and the orphaned-process reap grace deadline in #181335; the Discord READY wait is the sibling site left on the wall clock.

Related but separate open PRs touch the same file's outer recovery behavior: #162377 bounds the number of consecutive READY recovery attempts, #124162 adds a runtime disconnection watchdog, and #138441 fixes voice bridge selection. This change only moves the per-attempt wait deadline to the monotonic clock and composes with those.

No configuration, protocol, or status-shape change; the env override semantics (a duration in ms) are untouched, and behavior on a clock that never steps is identical.

## Evidence

**Pre-fix RED** — stock main (`97d96e53d22f`), regression test only. Fake timers advance 15s of monotonic time past the READY timeout while `vi.setSystemTime` rewinds the wall clock 60s mid-wait; the timeout never fires, so no error is logged and no reconnect happens:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/provider.lifecycle.test.ts -t monotonic
 × times the READY wait out on the monotonic clock when the wall clock rewinds
   → expected "…" to be called with stringContaining("gateway READY wait timed out after 15000ms")
```

**Post-fix GREEN** — the READY wait times out at its 15s monotonic bound, logs the timeout, and reconnects:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/provider.lifecycle.test.ts
      Tests  16 passed (16)
```

**Behavior matrix** (gateway never READY, wall clock rewound 60s mid-wait, 15s default timeout):

```text
clock during READY wait     => timeout + reconnect        => result
normal (no step)            => after 15s                  => bounded
wall rewind 60s (pre-fix)   => after 15s + 60s (polling)  => inflated by step
wall rewind 60s (post-fix)  => after 15s                  => bounded
```

Also verified on the changed tree: `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm lint`, and the extensions typecheck entry. The regression drives the real `runDiscordGatewayLifecycle` through the existing test harness (mocked gateway/supervisor, real lifecycle state machine); the local bundled-gateway proof path is not runnable on this Windows contributor box and was not used as evidence.

When a task needs a new credential, default guidance does not identify an admitted masked-entry tool, including when its schema is deferred.

The published revision preserves the intentional credential policy from #143238 and #157447 by omitting an unconditional chat prohibition. At head 143dcebc4472827580370d04c10249fb34f12926:

- Source validation includes 84 focused tests, including prefix stability and affected prompt consumers; 67 supporting question/store/tool boundary tests; production typecheck, scoped lint, formatting and canonical snapshot checks. The v05 run uses the Gateway's internal question-prompt callback; it does not claim real Discord/Telegram delivery or browser rendering. It uses a restricted direct tool surface, while v04 preserves separate native catalog-discovery evidence. prs.title: fix(codex): preserve owner threads after subagent completions
prs.body:
Closes #181580
Related: #143386

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Codex loses the owner's native thread or misses the child's result after a restricted subagent completion.

## User Impact

User impact: the next owner turn resumes its original Codex thread with the unseen completion input and answer as quoted context. Completion restrictions and the child's persistent restrictions remain enforced. No configuration changes or migrations are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Treat verified completions' inherited restrictions as turn-scoped so the existing temporary-thread handling preserves the owner's durable binding. When that owner resumes, exclude history belonging to its own native thread rather than excluding all Codex-mirrored history. Keep the existing coverage cutoff and quoted-context renderer, so a successful owner turn consumes the unseen completion delta without replaying it on later turns.

Host-admitted user rows do not always carry a native thread identity. Keep fresh, unqualified rows rather than silently discarding them: an earlier accepted but failed turn can consequently appear again as quoted context. This recoverable duplication is preferable to losing a completion result; no new state or ownership mechanism is introduced.

## Evidence

- Policy regression: the restricted-completion case fails on the base with expected `turn`, received `conversation`, and passes with the fix; unrestricted completions and persistent child policy retain their scope.
- ClawSweeper's missing-result finding reproduced with both native-mirror and host-admitted transcript writers. Both cases failed on the previous history filter because the actual resumed-owner `turn/start` input omitted the unique child result.
- New four-attempt regressions use the production Codex attempt lifecycle and real SQLite transcripts with a mocked app-server transport: the temporary completion leaves the owner binding unchanged; the owner resumes its original thread and receives the child input and answer; its subsequent turn does not replay that delta or old owner history.
- 74 focused tests passed on the repaired tree: Codex durable/bounded/restricted continuity and transcript admission (36), requester policy (30), and prompt-prefix stability (8).
- Focused TypeScript, targeted lint (zero warnings/errors), formatting, documentation MDX validation, and `git diff --check` passed. Fresh independent Auto Review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.

- @Marvinthebored supplied an [authenticated live Gateway/Codex A/B replay](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181591#issuecomment-6367793360), with [pinned proof and artifacts](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/6f89f479d5f678071271efe393ec2bf220448c9f/PROOF.md): two fresh targeted runs per revision, comparing merge base `648528a15470451db1d6b89ad35a829630372ec3` with this PR head `b5803a09ccaad014d0a9c693f628e037d0be102c`. On the patched head, both five-turn sequences are `A,A,B,A,A` instead of stock `A,A,B,C,C`; the original owner binding survives the restricted completion, the resumed owner recalls its result, restrictions remain enforced, and the fifth ordinary turn does not inject the completion context again.
- In those live runs, the recall turn records 28,670 / 28,784 and 28,667 / 28,780 cached / input tokens, versus 0 / 28,462 in each stock run. Supplied turn inputs, policy logs, binding hashes, and artifact checksums were inspected against the reported outcomes.

**Validation scope:** the authenticated replay was run locally by @Marvinthebored on isolated macOS Gateways with Node 26.12.1, Codex CLI 0.159.2, API-key authentication, and an observation-only policy logger. It was not independently rerun by Roboclaw; the committed lifecycle regression still uses a mocked app-server transport. The token figures are native usage observations from these runs, not a billing benchmark or a guarantee for other environments. The unrestricted control still rotates threads on both revisions; the reporter attributes that separate catalog-description issue to #167277, outside this restricted-completion fix.

Reported and reproduced by @Marvinthebored.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/63f60f4b-1fbc-4c84-81b6-2ae4391c3951)

## Worked on by

- @Marvinthebored

prs.title: fix: release PostgreSQL bridges after three idle minutes
prs.body:
Related: #181432, #181687

## What Problem This Solves

Quiet PostgreSQL Gateways retain unused bridge worker isolates and their backend connections indefinitely, even after the logical database handles close.

## User Impact

Unused cached PostgreSQL connections now close after three idle minutes. Bursts still reuse them, and a checked-out connection is never expired by the cache. A connection opened after that quiet interval pays the normal bridge startup cost. No configuration, pool topology, schema, or durability change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing four-entry per-isolate cache already owns exclusive transport reuse and teardown. Its entries now own unreferenced timers; taking, replacing, evicting, or draining an entry cancels its timer. Expiry uses the same clean close path. The measured warm fixture reused every cached bridge within 19.7 seconds, leaving ample headroom under the three-minute limit.

## Evidence

Acceptance was recorded before measurement: at least 64 MiB less quiet PG RSS, fewer live bridges, identical warm requests/trips/statements and no additional warm bridge launches, and no failed turns.

Paired four-agent, sixteen-session Gateway measurement at base `539fefd280f1`, candidate `237575a74607` (Node 26.12.1, PostgreSQL 17, 48-turn workload per cell):

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Idle RSS in first minute after warmup | 4103.4 MiB | 4020.3 MiB |
| RSS in final minute of ten-minute quiet interval | 2240.3 MiB | 2132.5 MiB |
| Live bridges after ten minutes quiet | 20 | 14 |
| Cached idle bridges after ten minutes quiet | 7 | 1 |
| Warm requests/trips/statements, each turn | 12/34/43, 11/33/42, 11/33/42 | identical |
| Warm bridge launches, each turn | 0, 0, 0 | 0, 0, 0 |

The quiet RSS reduction is **107.8 MiB**, with six fewer live bridge isolates. Both memory arms completed 48/48 turns with no failures and clean child shutdown. Both traced and full-window counts match exactly, with no failed census turn or shutdown. All 203 baseline and 204 candidate warm cache reuses were within 19.7 seconds. The SQLite control completed 48 turns without failure: 1545.9 MiB after ten minutes quiet, with zero bridges. The remaining PG gap to SQLite is 586.6 MiB in this workload; expiry addresses part of the standing footprint. The local C64 pair completed 320/320 stress turns per arm with no errors or timeouts. Throughput was 4.039 → 3.892 turns/s and p95 17.156 → 20.910 seconds on the shared host. Both stress windows had four bridge starts, zero exits, 392 connects and 388 cache reuses. They ended within 101 seconds of Gateway startup, before any three-minute expiry could fire. This rules out expiry-driven churn, but the timing pair does not establish a latency or throughput improvement; acceptance is the quiet footprint reduction and unchanged warm work/launch counts. The requested Testbox lease queued and was stopped before a workload ran; no remote timing claim is made.

The real PostgreSQL regression fails on the base because the backend survives the idle deadline. It passes with the fix and also checks burst reuse, survival while borrowed beyond the old deadline, and clean reopen after expiry. All 10 connection-reuse tests pass. Core and infra-test type checks, targeted lint and formatting pass. Independent Codex review is clean through P2. Final-head PostgreSQL conformance passed all three shards at `237575a74607`: 1,142 tests passed with 39 existing skips. Initial attempts with missing or extra database extensions were corrected and the affected shards rerun; no source or snapshot waiver was used.

Scope: production +17 net lines for timer ownership, test +24 net lines; the old unbounded idle lifetime is removed without a second cache or cleanup owner.

CI run 40046063004 also reports three UI end-to-end timeouts (file download, Files filter, and a stale directory response). Their complete UI/test/tooling/dependency inputs are identical between the actual CI base and tested merge, and all three cases replace Gateway traffic with a browser mock. They do not execute the changed PostgreSQL cache. The failures remain recorded; no UI timeout or assertion was changed. Their exact timing cause is unresolved, and no matching failed scheduled-main run or baseline UI reproduction is claimed. The scoped inherited-failure landing exception is supported by this source inspection.

prs.title: fix: Control UI and TUI ignore an agent's own verboseDefault in chat history
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/182058

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: chat history ignores an agent's own `verboseDefault` and reports the global default for that agent's sessions, so Control UI and the TUI fall back to the global level while replies and `/status` use the agent's.

## User Impact

User impact: an agent's own `verboseDefault` now reaches chat history, matching what replies and `/status` already use. With the agent's default at `full` (global `off`), Control UI now auto-expands tool calls for that agent. With it at `on` or `full`, the TUI now shows tool activity and reports that level instead of verbose off. Agents without their own default still inherit the global one, and a session override set with `/verbose` still wins.

## Why This Change Was Made

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177613 made replies, `/verbose`, `/status` and `openclaw agent` use the agent's own `verboseDefault`. The two chat-history readers (the Gateway `chat.history` handler and the local TUI backend) still read `agents.defaults.verboseDefault` directly, while `thinkingDefault` in the same response is already resolved per agent. Both now use one small helper next to `resolveAgentConfig`: session override, then the agent's `verboseDefault`, then the global default.

## Evidence

Tested at `26c3b712e4a` (base `upstream/main` `3ac1e62c3603`).

Built Gateway (`pnpm build`) on Linux, Node 24, started on loopback in an isolated state directory with no outside network and no provider keys. Config: `agents.defaults.verboseDefault: "off"`, agent `ops` with `verboseDefault: "full"` and `thinkingDefault: "high"`, agent `main` with no own defaults. Steps on both sides: `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes`, `openclaw gateway run`, then `openclaw gateway call chat.history --params '{"sessionKey":"<key>"}' --json` for both agents' main sessions.

Before (base `3ac1e62c3603`):

```text
agent:ops:main: verboseLevel=off sessionInfo.verboseLevel=off sessionInfo.thinkingDefault=high thinkingLevel=high
agent:main:main: verboseLevel=off sessionInfo.verboseLevel=off sessionInfo.thinkingDefault=undefined thinkingLevel=undefined
```

After (this PR):

```text
agent:ops:main: verboseLevel=full sessionInfo.verboseLevel=full sessionInfo.thinkingDefault=high thinkingLevel=high
agent:main:main: verboseLevel=off sessionInfo.verboseLevel=off sessionInfo.thinkingDefault=undefined thinkingLevel=undefined
```

Observed result: the `ops` session reports its own `full` at the top level and in `sessionInfo`; `main` still inherits the global `off`; the per-agent `thinkingDefault` control is unchanged on both sides.

Checks: the touched tests (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, wall time per file in the table below) and `pnpm check:changed` (typecheck, lint, format and guards pass; its dead-export scan fails only on exports already unused on the base, none in this diff); the broad suites run in this PR's CI. The new `chat.history` test fails on the base (`expected 'off' to be 'full'`) and passes here; for the TUI history test, the same assertion failed on the base before it moved into the history test-support file.

`pr-simplify`: the two global-only reads are gone; the remaining growth is the three-line helper, which keeps each reader to one line so neither over-cap file grows. Production +11/−8 lines, tests +48, against the merge base.

| Test file | `--maxWorkers=1` wall |
| --- | --- |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-handler.test.ts` | 42.3 s (cold compile cache) |
| `src/tui/embedded-backend.test.ts` (registers `embedded-backend.history.test-support.ts`) | 8.3 s (warm cache) |

Not changed on purpose: the last-resort global fallback for tool events in `src/gateway/server-chat.ts` (used only when a run carries no verbose level; runs now carry the agent's level) and the placeholder level in `src/tui/tui.ts` that the history load replaces.

Not covered: the TUI site was checked with the backend's own `loadHistory` unit test, not by driving `openclaw tui --local` interactively; Control UI rendering was not captured, only the `chat.history` payload it reads.

prs.title: fix(gateway): config.patch hangs after a superseded reload until another config change lands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A persisted `config.patch` / `config.apply` can leave its RPC waiting indefinitely after an in-process Gateway restart. Retained reload candidates were not always rescheduled. Real Gateway verification also exposed a second cause: the effective-unchanged path compared a resolved secrets snapshot with an unresolved SecretRef candidate, classified the permanent mismatch as supersession, and kept retrying it.

## User Impact

Provisioning and other source-equivalent config writes receive their application acknowledgment without an unrelated follow-up edit. Existing credential activation, publication ownership, and rollback checks remain in force. No config option, schema, dependency, or protocol change.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Schedule another attempt whenever a superseded write candidate is retained, including candidates retained by either inner catch.
- When the candidate differs from the active resolved snapshot only by canonical SecretRefs, use the existing hot-reload owner to materialize and publish it. Compare through the existing canonicalization helper so an already-owned restart's unapplied non-secret settings keep their restart publication path.

The complete PR adds nine net production lines, reusing existing activation and canonicalization owners rather than introducing a second resolver, state, or weaker guards.

## Evidence

### Exact-head real Gateway recovery: `b8c13e0f9263549628b1c1a3c8d1ba550501d625`

<!-- pr177823-real-gateway-repair-b8c13e0 -->

The previously stalling workload now completes on the final fixed full Gateway: **437 ms server / 439 ms client**, after a real SIGUSR2 in-process restart and concurrent synthetic credential refresh, with **no later config edit**.

Important distinction: this final run logged **zero supersessions**. The repair prevents the permanent resolved-value/SecretRef mismatch that produced them on the older head. This is not presented as a new-head trace that throws a supersession and then succeeds.

#### Comparable real-runtime controls

| Source | Same restart + file-credential-refresh workload | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Direct parent `08d04a9d7b97e50849ba089c3837d2e1c3c4f7fd` | One supersession, credential restored, no additional config write | Original patch still pending at the 30 s client deadline. It answered UNAVAILABLE only during shutdown, at 50,016 ms. **FAIL** |
| Initial PR head `ebfffd5599a7ee7c6d793718b96f923107b27691` | Eight supersessions before credential restoration; retries continued afterward | Original patch still pending at 30 s; 482 supersessions were recorded before task-owned forced cleanup. **FAIL** |
| First repair `c337231afc47e7cf137f0273a9051daab79b71ae` | Identical public-RPC/file workload | Original patch answered in **308 ms**, but broader CI exposed a restart-reapply regression. This is prior-head runtime evidence, not the final candidate. |
| Final head `b8c13e0f9263549628b1c1a3c8d1ba550501d625` | Identical public-RPC/file workload | Original patch answered successfully in **439 ms**, before the credential-restoration step. Clean Gateway shutdown. **PASS** |

All runs used OpenClaw 2026.10.5, Node v26.8.1, macOS arm64, independently owned dependencies, isolated synthetic HOME/state/config/workspace, and distinct free loopback ports between control families. The final build and runtime-postbuild stamps both identify exact `b8c13e0f9263549628b1c1a3c8d1ba550501d625` with `inputsClean:true`.

No mocked hot-reload callback, injected exception, fake clock, manually settled receipt, inference call, live Mattermost traffic, operator Gateway change, or TEST/PROD mutation was used in these real Gateway runs.

#### Executed workload

prs.title: fix(sessions): align reply barrier extension deadline with monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The extendable reply-barrier settlement budget is seeded with `Date.now()` and consumed with `Date.now()` elapsed while feeding a monotonic `setTimeout`, so a wall-clock jump makes a healthy run either hang past its hard budget (clock stepped back) or finish early (clock stepped forward). Seed and consume now both use `performance.now()`, so the bounded retry envelope settles on its monotonic budget regardless of wall-clock jumps.

- Problem: `waitForReplyBarrierSettlement`'s object-timeout branch mixed clock domains — it measured the elapsed budget with `Date.now()` but delivered the deadline to a monotonic `setTimeout`. A backward wall-clock jump inflated the remaining budget (settlement hangs past `maxTimeoutMs`); a forward jump forced an early finish (a still-active barrier is misjudged as timed out).
- Solution: measure both the seed and the elapsed with `performance.now()`, the same monotonic domain the timer consumes, so `remainingMs` stays correct across wall-clock jumps.
- What changed: two lines in `src/sessions/session-controller.settlement.ts` (`Date.now()` → `performance.now()` for the seed and the elapsed subtraction), plus a new sibling regression test `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.settlement-deadline.test.ts` that flips the wall clock in both directions and asserts the barrier settles exactly on its monotonic budget.
- What did NOT change: the number-timeout path, the default `REPLY_RUN_IDLE_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_MS`, extension policy, or any public signature. Production line count is unchanged (+2/−2).

## Why This Change Was Made

The object-timeout branch of `waitForReplyBarrierSettlement` (`ReplyFollowupAdmissionBarrierTimeoutPolicy` with `shouldExtend`) seeded `startedAt = Date.now()` and computed `remainingMs = maxTimeoutMs - (Date.now() - startedAt)`, then fed that value to a monotonic `setTimeout`. Mixing the wall-clock domain (`Date.now`) with the monotonic domain (`setTimeout`) is the same wall-clock-remaining-budget anti-pattern fixed across this codebase's settlement/timer family. Both the seed and the consume must live in one clock domain; `performance.now()` is the correct monotonic source on both sides, so elapsed time is immune to wall-clock jumps (NTP steps, manual clock changes, VM suspend/resume).

- Best fix: switch both the seed and the elapsed to `performance.now()` — the smallest change that puts the deadline computation in the same monotonic domain the timer consumes.
- Alternative: recompute the wall-clock-based deadline by converting to monotonic at schedule time, or track the deadline as an absolute `performance.now()` timestamp once. Those add state/indirection without benefit; the two-line domain fix is equivalent and simpler.
- Risk: `performance.now()` is a valid Node global (Node 16+). The value is only ever used as a `setTimeout` delay, so its sub-millisecond float precision is irrelevant. The affected policy is currently exercised by tests; the production resolver leaves it undefined by default, so this is a latent-but-correct owner fix that matches the established family.

## User Impact

Reply-barrier settlement now resolves on its monotonic budget regardless of wall-clock jumps, so a healthy follow-up reply is no longer cut off early (or left hanging) when the host clock changes (NTP correction, manual set, or VM suspend/resume). No behavior change for runs that never see a wall-clock jump — the monotonic and wall-clock elapsed times are identical in steady state.

## Evidence

Regression test that flips the wall clock in both directions and asserts the extendable barrier settles exactly once on its monotonic budget, not on the wall-clock jump:

```console
$ vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.settlement-deadline.test.ts
 ✓ |auto-reply| ... > settles an extendable barrier on its monotonic budget despite a wall-clock jump of -1 interval 188ms
 ✓ |auto-reply| ... > settles an extendable barrier on its monotonic budget despite a wall-clock jump of 1 interval 5ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

Behavior matrix (extendable barrier, `maxTimeoutMs = 3 * interval`, `shouldExtend` always true):

```text
wall-clock jump      => pre-fix (Date.now)   => post-fix (performance.now)
clock steps back -1  => hangs past budget    => settles exactly at budget (2 passed)
clock steps forward  => settles early        => settles exactly at budget (2 passed)
```

Pre-fix RED (production source reverted to `Date.now()`, test kept):

```console
 FAIL  > settles an extendable barrier on its monotonic budget despite a wall-clock jump of -1 interval
 AssertionError: expected "settled" to be called once, but got 0 times   (settlement hung)
 FAIL  > settles an extendable barrier on its monotonic budget despite a wall-clock jump of 1 interval
 AssertionError: expected "settled" not to be called at all, but been called 1 times  (early finish)
```

Post-fix GREEN, the owner suite also passes:

```console
$ vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  69 passed (69)
```

- What was not tested: a real live Gateway turn with a wall-clock jump — the affected policy is off by default in production and only exercised by tests, so the fix is proven at the unit level against the exact clock-domain mixing. No timing-dependent live harness was spun up for this latent path.
- Open PR collision check: searched open PR topics (settlement deadline / monotonic / wall-clock) and scanned the changed-file lists of open PRs for `session-controller.settlement.ts` and the new test file; no open PR touches either. The bug is still present on latest `main` and is fixed by this branch.

prs.title: fix(ollama): web search ignores configured maxResults and timeoutSeconds
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/182051

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Ollama Web Search always asks for 5 results and waits up to 15 seconds when `tools.web.search.maxResults` or `tools.web.search.timeoutSeconds` is set.

## User Impact

User impact: with `tools.web.search.provider: "ollama"`, a search without `count` now returns the configured number of results, and a slow or stuck Ollama host is cut off at the configured deadline. An explicit `count` still wins, and with the settings unset the provider keeps its 5-result and 15-second defaults.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Ollama provider never read `tools.web.search`: the request body used its default count of 5 and every attempt used a fixed 15,000 ms timeout. The other web search providers already honor both settings; this follows the shape of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180115 (Tavily, Firecrawl, DuckDuckGo) and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173467 (SearXNG). The tool's `count` falls back to `searchConfig.maxResults` through the existing `resolveSearchCount` (same 1–10 range), and the deadline is `resolveTimeoutSeconds(searchConfig.timeoutSeconds, 15)`, so the provider's own 15-second default stays instead of the shared 30-second one. The Ollama web search docs now name both settings.

## Evidence

Tested at `09719789803` (base `upstream/main` `3ac1e62c360`).

Real Gateway: the built Gateway on each side (Node 24.22.1, Ubuntu 22.04) in a fresh HOME, state directory and config, with the network off except loopback, a synthetic Gateway token and no provider keys. `plugins.entries.ollama.config.webSearch.baseUrl` points at a local Ollama stub that records each request body, returns ten results, and never answers the query `hang`. Two `web_search` calls without `count` go through `POST /tools/invoke`: `openclaw`, then `hang`. Elapsed is the wall time of each HTTP call.

Before (base `3ac1e62c360`), `tools.web.search` with `maxResults: 2`, `timeoutSeconds: 2`:

```text
search: http=200 elapsed=1.4s
  ok: True | result count: 5
hang: http=200 elapsed=15.8s
  kind: error | provider_error: Search timed out. Try again later or choose another provider.
stub received:
   /api/experimental/web_search {"query": "openclaw", "max_results": 5}
   /api/experimental/web_search {"query": "hang", "max_results": 5}
```

After (this PR), same settings:

```text
search: http=200 elapsed=1.3s
  ok: True | result count: 2
hang: http=200 elapsed=2.8s
  kind: error | provider_error: Search timed out. Try again later or choose another provider.
stub received:
   /api/experimental/web_search {"query": "openclaw", "max_results": 2}
   /api/experimental/web_search {"query": "hang", "max_results": 2}
```

Observed result: with the settings, the request now asks for 2 results and the unanswered search ends after about 2 seconds instead of about 15. Without `maxResults` and `timeoutSeconds`, both sides give the same `max_results`, result count and timeout: `max_results: 5`, 5 results, timeout after 15.7–15.8 s.

Regression test: `extensions/ollama/src/web-search-provider.test.ts` creates the tool with `searchConfig: { maxResults: 2, timeoutSeconds: 2 }` and checks the guarded request: `max_results: 2` and `timeoutMs: 2000` without `count`, and `max_results: 7` with `count: 7`. It fails on the base (`expected '{"query":"openclaw","max_results":5}'`) and passes with this PR; the 14 other tests in the file, including the default 5-result and 15,000 ms request, pass on both.

Checks: `pnpm test extensions/ollama/src/web-search-provider.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`; `pnpm check:changed` (typecheck, lint, format and plugin boundaries pass; untracked local scratch files made it run every lane, and its dead export scan then failed only on files this PR does not touch). The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

| Test file | `--maxWorkers=1` wall |
| --- | --- |
| `extensions/ollama/src/web-search-provider.test.ts` | 33 s (15 tests) |

Simplify pass: no new helper or state; the fix reuses the shared `resolveSearchCount` and `resolveTimeoutSeconds` and replaces the fixed millisecond constant with a seconds default. Against the merge base: production +15/−3, tests +16/−2 (one test added to the existing suite), docs +5.

Not covered: the hosted `https://ollama.com` path and the Ollama Cloud fallback attempt (same request body and timeout code, not run here), and a real Ollama daemon (the stub stands in for its web search endpoint).

prs.title: fix(memory-wiki): ChatGPT import drops messages that mention "dalle" or start with pasted JSON
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw wiki chatgpt import` silently leaves messages out of the imported transcript when they contain the word "dalle", which Italian uses all the time ("dalle 9 alle 18"), or when they start with a pasted JSON object.

## User Impact

User impact: imported ChatGPT conversations keep every message of the active branch, including Italian text and questions that start with pasted JSON, so the wiki pages, labels and preference signals built from them see the whole conversation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The message cleaner treated any part longer than 40 characters that contained `dalle`, `asset_pointer` or `file_service` as an image part, and any part over 80 characters that started with `{` and contained `:` as a serialized part object, and dropped both unless the object had a `text` field. Real prose matched these substring checks. Now only a part that starts with `{` and names a `content_type` or `asset_pointer` is handled as a serialized part; its handling is unchanged. Everything else is kept as written.

## Evidence

Shipped CLI from this checkout (Node 24.22.1, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `node scripts/run-node.mjs`): `openclaw wiki init` in an isolated vault, then `openclaw wiki chatgpt import --export <dir>` with one conversation of four messages (two Italian ones that contain "dalle", one user message that starts with a JSON object, one English reply). The active-branch count and transcript of the imported source page:

```text
main (fa7e822d)
- Active-branch messages: 1
## Active Branch Transcript
### Assistant
Yes, the object matches the Saturday hours.

this branch (23bca1ad)
- Active-branch messages: 4
## Active Branch Transcript
### User
Il negozio è aperto dalle 9 alle 18 dal lunedì al venerdì?
### Assistant
Sì, il negozio è aperto dalle 9 alle 18, il sabato invece dalle 10 alle 14.
### User
{"day": "saturday", "open": "10:00", "close": "14:00", "note": "holiday hours"}
Is this JSON right for Saturday?
### Assistant
Yes, the object matches the Saturday hours.
```

- New `chatgpt-import-text.test.ts`: "keeps messages that mention dalle or start with pasted JSON" (fails on main) and "still drops serialized image parts and reads serialized text parts" (passes on both, pins the unchanged handling).
- `pnpm test:extension memory-wiki`: 51 files, 390 tests passed (1 skipped).
- `tsgo` for `tsconfig.extensions.json` and `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json`, oxfmt, oxlint and the line-cap ratchet: passed.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Fixes the Create Agent form sitting left of center inside a wider, partly empty modal. At 1024px the unused right-hand strip is 100px; at 320px it wastes 24px of available form width.

## User Impact
The dialog is centered on desktop and uses the available mobile width. No configuration, migration, Gateway, submission, or provider behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made
The native modal owns the intended 440px width, and the form fills that shell instead of independently sizing a second box. Native focus, dismissal, and submission behavior are unchanged.

Context: [Control UI Focus Week](https://community.openclaw.ai/t/focus-week-oct-19th-25th-2026-control-ui/183). Source-reproduced bug; no matching existing issue or open PR found in fresh searches.

## Evidence — built Control UI, real sidebar entry point
Pinned head: `9c40587534a9e943b69944fd3498f847982d7e61`.

- Built the production Vite app using `buildProductionControlUiE2e`, served it through `startBuiltControlUiE2eServer`, installed synthetic `installMockGateway` before navigation, opened **New Session → mobile sidebar drawer (320px) → agent card → Create new agent**. No component mounting shortcut, live Gateway, real credentials, provider call, agent creation, or avatar generation.
- **Chromium + WebKit**, each at **320×768 and 1024×768**, before and after. All eight screenshots below were inspected and contain synthetic content only.

prs.title: feat: let plugins attach presentation to embedded final replies
prs.body:
Related: #179709

## What Problem This Solves

Plugins cannot currently return typed presentation content alongside the ordinary final answer selected by the embedded runner.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can return an optional `finalPresentation` from `before_agent_finalize` when the event advertises support. Existing channel adapters retain rendering, text fallback and delivery. Plugins that do not use the field keep their current behavior; no configuration, dependency or stored-data migration is required.

This is a bounded first implementation, not completion of #179709. Support is embedded ordinary-final only. Tool-prepared attempt identity, actual destination capabilities, native Codex relay, Copilot and settled-tool finalization remain outside this PR. No live channel or Teams-client qualification is claimed.

## Public Contract

This intentionally extends the public plugin contract with optional fields: `supportsFinalPresentation?: true` on `PluginHookBeforeAgentFinalizeEvent` and `finalPresentation?: ReplyPayload["presentation"]` on its result. `EmbeddedAgentRunPayload` also declares optional `presentation`, `interactive` and `btw` fields using the existing reply-payload types. Existing exports remain available; no hook is renamed and no new SDK subpath or required parameter is introduced. Existing plugins remain compatible, but acceptance of these new extension fields requires maintainer review.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Maintainer Review Focus

- Is extending `before_agent_finalize` with optional support/result fields the right public API for candidate-local presentation, without a new hook or SDK subpath?
- Does the candidate identity/lifetime boundary correctly retain native ownership across revision, cancellation and final selection, including first-producer precedence?
- Is the bounded embedded-only support declaration clear enough for plugins to avoid promising preparation on unsupported runtimes? It is not destination-capability detection.
- Does residual delivery preserve unsent media and existing payload hooks without replaying streamed prose or creating a separate send?

Plugins may independently refresh their presentation preferences or authoring guidance through supported configuration and hooks. This PR supplies final attachment, not a configuration-refresh engine. Dynamic tool discovery, tool-prepared attempt identity and actual sink capabilities remain separate contracts; no hot-reload or complete cross-runtime integration claim is made. Maintainer guidance on those boundaries is welcome without widening this first PR.

Reuse the existing finalization hook and terminal reply owner rather than add a tool, staging store or finalization manager. The presentation is computed from this hook invocation's candidate and bound to that exact assistant. Revision, cancellation, retry and non-ordinary completion cannot reuse a rejected candidate's presentation.

The first producer in hook priority order wins; existing force-finalize/revise precedence stays intact. Attachment preserves payload metadata and media, leaves existing structured envelopes alone, and emits a presentation residual alongside any eligible unsent media if ordinary prose already streamed, without replaying that prose. Existing payload hooks still transform or cancel delivery.

The support flag describes this finalization path, not a destination's rendering capabilities. The wider issue remains open so execution identity and sink contracts can be coordinated with related upstream work rather than duplicated here.

## Evidence

- Core production typecheck passed on Windows with Node 24.19.0 and the pinned dependency install.
- Focused proof covers 193 tests across six files. The initial five-file run passed 170 tests; after the final helper extractions and fixture completion, 121 terminal/settlement/hook tests passed again at `8592765311b5`. Unchanged candidate-lifetime and result-assembly inputs retain their earlier passing proof.
- Agent, harness and plugin-platform test typechecks passed. Core production typecheck and changed-file lint passed again after the helper extraction and additive result-payload typing repair. Formatting and whitespace checks passed.
- Independent review completed with no actionable P0-P2 findings before behavior-preserving helper extractions and optional result-carrier type completion; those final repairs were manually checked and passed the focused rerun. Markdown lint and the line-growth ratchet pass. The Windows commit hook could not launch `pnpm` (`ENOENT`); its selected checks were run directly using the documented equivalent-validation commit route.
- Simplification: extend existing owners with optional fields and candidate-local state; no new public subpath, core tool, manager or store. Necessary production growth carries the candidate to the existing terminal-selection boundary; regression tests cover selection and rejection paths.
- Whole change against the pinned base: 19 files, +639/-96; production +273/-94, tests/support +337/-2, documentation +29/-0. Existing finalize types and merge code move to sibling modules, retaining public exports, and the terminal owner calls a small result decorator to satisfy existing line-growth budgets.
- Review repairs at `73b9631612be`: all 67 terminal-resolution tests pass (546.84 seconds wrapper wall time); the real preparation/resolution regression first failed with unsent media on the old implementation, then passed with the repair. The shared fixture repair separately passed all 48 provider-error, transport and settled-turn tests (398.50 seconds). These are scoped runs, not a rerun of the entire earlier suite.
- Fresh independent Codex review of the three-file repair was scoped-clean with no actionable P0-P2 findings. Core and agent-test typechecks, changed-file lint, formatting, whitespace and the line-growth ratchet pass. The normal commit hook passed for this repair.
- [ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179763#issuecomment-6327648066) of exact head `73b9631612be` confirms both previous findings resolved and no new actionable findings: ready for maintainer review. This is advisory review, not human acceptance of the public contract or live-channel qualification.
- Exact-head [CI run 39707431413](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39707431413) completed successfully: 54 jobs passed, 28 scope-selected skips, including passing agent-test shards, production/test types, lint, build, both UI E2E shards and the CI gate job. Automatic [security-review follow-up 39708326743](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39708326743) also passed; the combined `openclaw/ci-gate`, dependency-review and security-sensitive-review commit statuses are all successful.
- No authenticated live Gateway/channel/client proof was run. Hosted CI remains the broad proof.

## CI Follow-up

Historical CI run [39648112504](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39648112504) failed on head `8592765311b5`; the new-head run above passes:

- Two agent-test jobs exposed five failures from a shared settled-turn test fixture missing the new internal `getFinalPresentation` getter. The provider-error failure was reproduced locally before editing. The one-line fixture completion is included in `73b9631612be` and passes the 48 affected tests above. The retained local tooling lock is resolved; lint is no longer blocked.
- ClawSweeper identified a second P2: after ordinary text streamed, remaining unsent media prevented the presentation residual. The repair preserves eligible media payload objects and appends the presentation, while retaining protected-payload, pending-delivery and message-tool exclusions. The misleading independently prepopulated replacement test was removed; actual candidate-lifetime coverage remains in `attempt-stream-prepare.test.ts`. Both repairs are now confirmed by fresh CI and ClawSweeper re-review above.
- The UI E2E failure is also present on scheduled main CI: [main job 119376935880](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39644558400/job/119376935880), at main commit `d5621d9084887432c7637774d85de692ba8c5445`, has matching failure annotations with [PR job 119390002595](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39648112504/job/119390002595). Both mobile and desktop cases time out after 30000ms locating the `Retry now` button, with the same locators and stack at `ui/src/e2e/gateway-module-boundaries.test-support.ts:62`. No UI files change in this PR. The initial classifier reported unknown because shard names differed (`1/9` on main versus `1/2` on the PR); the subsequent annotation comparison establishes matching baseline failures. This is inherited failure evidence, not a passing check or authorization to bypass CI.
