prs.title: fix(agents): describe sessions_spawn agentId allowed targets in the tool description
prs.body:
Fixes #149550

## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_spawn` never said which `agentId` targets are allowed, so models only learned by being rejected.

## User Impact

User impact: the tool description lists the targets the spawn path accepts, for native subagents and ACP. Text only. Lists are capped at 20 ids, so a large roster cannot bloat every turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

The text is built from the real admission rules: ACP ids go through the ACP resolver and `acp.allowedAgents`, and `requireAgentId` is honored. Callers pass the requester's already-resolved subagent status, so building the tool reads no session store. One helper resolves `allowAgents` and `requireAgentId` for all four callers.

Native and ACP lists share one renderer (`describeTargetIdList`, built on `summarizeStringEntries`). It lists the first 20 sorted ids, then `(+N). Only the first 20 ids are listed.` Agent ids are at most 64 chars, so the count cap also bounds bytes (about 1.4 KB per list). The overflow text does not assume `agents_list` exists.

It lives in the tool description, not the `agentId` schema property. Codex drops every schema description once a tool schema passes 5,000 bytes (first pass of `compact_large_tool_schema`), and `sessions_spawn` is already at 5,045 on `main`. The schema is unchanged; the tool description is kept.

Tests: the metadata-only suite that imported the full spawn runtime is deleted. Policy and cap cases live in the target-policy and ACP target tests. One registration assertion and the prepared-requester regression (never a store read) sit in the existing `sessions-spawn-tool.test.ts`.

## Evidence

Shipped entry point: `pnpm openclaw agent --local --agent main --message hi` against an isolated state dir and a local OpenAI-compatible mock that records the model request. Agents `main` and `planner`, `tools.toolSearch: false`. `sessions_spawn.description` in the captured request:

| Config | `main` (base) | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No allowlist | no `agentId` text | `` `agentId` targets: Only the requester agent is allowed as a target; no other agentId is configured. Omit to keep the requester agent ("main"). `` |
| `agents.entries.main.subagents.allowAgents: ["planner"]` | no `agentId` text | `` `agentId` targets: Configured agent to target: planner. Omit to keep the requester agent ("main"). `` |

The schema `agentId` stays `{"type":"string"}` in both.

ACP, through the Gateway with a backend enabled: an isolated `pnpm openclaw gateway run` (own state dir, loopback port) with `acp.enabled`, `acp.backend: "acpx"`, `acp.defaultAgent: "codex"`, `acp.allowedAgents: ["codex","claude"]`, agents `main` and `planner`, and `main.subagents.allowAgents: ["planner"]`. The Gateway logs `embedded acpx runtime backend registered lazily`. `pnpm openclaw agent --agent main --message hi` then sent this `sessions_spawn.description` fragment (head `02c4032`) to the local OpenAI-compatible mock (full text, nothing truncated, no secrets):

```
`agentId` targets: With runtime="subagent" (default): Configured agent to target: planner. Omit to keep the requester agent ("main"). With runtime="acp": ACP harness id from: claude, codex. Omit to use the configured ACP default ("codex").
```

The captured `agentId` schema is still `{"type":"string"}`.

Real output, config with `main`, `planner`, `acp.defaultAgent: codex`:

```
description: `agentId` targets a configured agent; ... `sandbox` inherit|require. `agentId` targets: With runtime="subagent" (default): Only the requester agent is allowed as a target; no other agentId is configured. Omit to keep the requester agent ("main"). With runtime="acp": ACP harness id, for exam...
schema agentId: {"type":"string"}
acp agentId=codex:     accepted
acp agentId=main:      rejected: agentId "main" is an OpenClaw config agent, not an ACP harness
acp agentId=(omitted): accepted
requireAgentId=true:   ... agentId is required; the requester agent is "main".
```

Codex fixture, `sessions_spawn`: schema 5,045 bytes on both `main` and this branch (byte-identical); tool description 2,805 to 2,884. Checked against `openai/codex` at `064c6b8c`, `codex-rs/tools/src/json_schema/compaction.rs`. A local Codex checkout was not available, and Codex's own normalized byte count was not measured.

The existing `agents_list` rewrite of `configured agent;` still applies (`agent-tools.deferred-followup-guidance.test.ts`).

Cap regressions: exactly 20 ids has no overflow text, 21 ids does, and 5,000 allowed ids render under 1,000 chars (native); 25 ACP ids are capped for both the allowlist and example forms.

Main merged; prompt snapshots regenerated with `pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen`. Focused tests, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, `tsgo:core`, changed `tsgo:core:test` graphs and `prompt:snapshots:check` pass.

Test wall (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, measured on this head):

| File | Wall |
| --- | --- |
| `subagent-target-policy.test.ts` (16 tests) | 3.4s |
| `acp-spawn-target.test.ts` (22 tests) | 20s |
| `sessions-spawn-tool.test.ts` (74 tests, existing suite) | 31s warm; the 2 added cases take 5ms and 51ms |
| removed `sessions-spawn-tool.agent-target-description.test.ts` | was ~74s cold |

CI on `02c4032` (main at `12a91e0919` when it ran), all in files this PR does not touch:

| Red | Same on base? |
| --- | --- |
| `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` (wrapper inventory) | Yes. Fails on pure `main` `12a91e0919` and `08005517c4` locally, and on unrelated PRs in the same window. |
| `src/gateway/server.visible-spawn-fallback.product-proof.test.ts` (session storage) | Yes. Fails 2 cases on pure `main` `12a91e0919` locally (`Session patch failed unexpectedly`). |
| `ui/src/e2e/chat-mention-search.e2e.test.ts` (UI) | Not reproduced locally (no browser here). No UI file is touched; unrelated PRs fail other UI e2e cases in the same window. |

Touched tests, `tsgo:core` and `prompt:snapshots:check` pass on this head.


## Maintainer follow-up (b636aaa)

- Single-agent setups without ACP (the requester is the only configured agent, no `requireAgentId`, no collect default) now get no `agentId` guidance, since there is no target to choose. The prompt snapshots match `main` again, so the PR no longer touches them.
- Tests slimmed: the native description cases are now a table, the 5,000-id and ACP cap cases are dropped (the shared renderer's 20/21 test covers the cap), duplicate empty-config and sender-restricted cases are merged, and a lone-agent test checks that no guidance is added.
- Local: the touched tests pass (36 + 78), plus `tsgo:core`, oxlint/oxfmt and the prompt snapshot regeneration.

prs.title: fix: prevent queued followup replies after session reset
prs.body:
Closes #181877

## What Problem This Solves

A completed queued follow-up can enter durable delivery custody after its first outbound connection fails, then replay its old answer after the user successfully resets the session. Ordinary follow-up routing did not retain the original session generation with the unsent reply.

## What Changed

Follow-up delivery captures its admitted session generation before handing off custody. Both raw and prepared reply routes forward that scope to the existing durable sender and generation validator. Recovery refuses a generation revoked by reset instead of adopting the replacement session. The added structured-send argument is internal, not a plugin-SDK export.

Thanks @HermanZeng for the repair and regressions. Existing retry policy, cancellation, ambiguous-send reconciliation, credentials, SDK surface and persisted format are unchanged. The queue guide now describes reset-safe recovery.

## Evidence

Built Linux Gateway on Node 24.22.1. Main `22a311919bab0057bde6ee941466af743c21efab` reproduced the stale replay twice; candidate `9a180bed77b173d849d9f28fd368fa3311d0ed39` ran the same reset and no-reset controls.

### Built Gateway, native webhook and real HTTP refusal

Local application configuration came from shipped config commands. Telegram's supported apiRoot pointed to an owned Bot API fixture; model selection explicitly used a local OpenAI Responses fixture. Ordinary A and B arrived through the native authenticated webhook route with followup queue mode configured. B arrived while A's finite HTTP response was continuously producing text. Neither a tool nor a provider request was held, and no private queue insertion was used.

After A was delivered, the Bot API listener was closed before B's final connection. Native logs recorded ECONNREFUSED and `followup queue: route-reply remains pending`. Read-only queue inspection confirmed B in pending custody with retryCount 1 and platform dispatch attemptCount 0. No Bot API endpoint had accepted B.

The public sessions.reset RPC completed before restoring the listener. Reset advanced lifecycleRevision; the physical sessionId remained unchanged in these cases, so the oracle checks the actual generation rather than assuming a new UUID. Then the Gateway recovered, restarted a second time, and processed a fresh C.

| Case | A accepted | Old B after recovery | Fresh C accepted |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main reset, run 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Main reset, run 2 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Main without reset | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Candidate reset | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| Candidate without reset | 1 | 1 | 1 |

Main's recovered B text was byte-identical to the retained payload and sent during the first recovery, before C. Candidate custody retained the original generation; recovery logged the literal SESSION_DELIVERY_GENERATION_REVOKED code, retired that attempt, and did not send B across either recovery. Without reset, B still delivered exactly once. Every final passing control executed each marked model request only once.

### Telegram Test Server confirmation

The exact candidate also ran through the maintained Convex-leased Telegram userbot workflow with a real QA user and SUT bot. An owned loopback forwarder was stopped only after the observer received A and B's finite model stream had started. B's first send received native ECONNREFUSED before reaching Telegram, entered real durable custody with its generation, and the configured-target public sessions.reset command succeeded before the forwarder was restored.

Both real Gateway restarts and their read-only retirement checkpoints completed. Raw TDLib message records show A once, no B, and fresh C once; the recording completed. The native Gateway logged SESSION_DELIVERY_GENERATION_REVOKED and the old attempt was no longer pending after each recovery. The provider records contain exactly one marked A, B and C conversation. No queue or session row was seeded or edited.

Native fixture/receipt corrections are retained separately: an initial URL-override credential check prevented reset, and the successful run's supervisor initially looked for text in the text-redacted summary timeline. Corrected read-only analysis uses the original raw NDJSON, confirms A1/B0/C1 and every checkpoint, and did not repeat successful native actions. The lease, credential scratch, native consumer and proxy were cleaned up.

Full main/candidate builds, 98 focused regressions across five files, and focused formatting/lint passed. A separate real OpenAI gpt-5-mini CLI turn completed with exit 0 and no fallback; its key was removed afterward.

## Simplification

The repair retains the existing generation, durable-custody and recovery owners; no replacement queue, cache, retention rule or SDK shim is introduced. The small scope record is captured once before asynchronous delivery and reused for the routed payloads. Production +38/-6, tests +282, docs +5. The growth carries existing authority metadata through the two internal send paths and protects the reset/no-reset boundary.

## Merge Risk

Code rollback is reversible; already queued records retain whichever generation scope they were authored with. No schema migration is needed. Blast radius is ordinary follow-up routing and its durable recovery scope. Replies already accepted by a channel are not retracted, and existing ambiguous-send reconciliation is unchanged.

prs.title: fix: preserve updates after read-only SQLite probes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes updates from published stable stopping in post-activation Doctor with `SQLite migration source changed after update capture.` after a read-only SQLite probe, even though the captured database contents are unchanged.

## User Impact

Read-only probes no longer prevent the candidate from migrating preserved SQLite state. Changed database contents or write evidence still refuse migration and automatic restoration. This is a candidate-side repair, so an older installed updater can benefit without a new handoff protocol.

## Why This Change Was Made

Opening a cold WAL database can create a zero-write shared-memory index; closing its last writable reader can remove it. The candidate now recognizes only those two equivalent observations, bound to the same file identity and committed content, before acquiring native exclusion. Legacy fingerprints stay byte-for-byte compatible, and exclusive handles, postimages, and native close keep their strict checks.

## Evidence

The two real SQLite regressions fail on unchanged main and exercise migration plus close attribution with the fix. Additional checks cover retained exclusive custody and reject outside commits, including a write followed by restoration of the original value. The migration suite passes all 12 tests; the generation suite passes all 21 tests. Core and infra-test typechecks and independent review are clean.

The real published 2026.10.6 updater now completes against the packed candidate in an isolated npm prefix: exit 0, durable run status `succeeded`, all three agents migrate from schema 25 to 32 and shared state from 20 to 31, and memory/cache table hashes remain identical. The replay restores the failed run’s stable pre-activation backup; isolated paths and update-ledger rows differ. The latest published stable has no PostgreSQL state support, so this is a stable-created SQLite upgrade.

All three final-head PostgreSQL CI shards actually ran and passed (1,143 tests, 37 existing skips); local shards 1 and 2 also passed. [CI run 40044349319](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40044349319) has three unrelated UI failures, each reproduced with the same test and selector on unchanged base `a69cf566`: directory-race folder navigation, downloads second-file selection, and file-link “Show in Files” filter selection. The update-only diff does not change their inputs. These remain recorded as inherited failures.

Release-note context: the next candidate must contain this repair for updates from 2026.10.6; it fixes the candidate-side migration check while retaining the shipped updater’s fingerprint and handoff protocol.

The shared observation owner adds 40 net production lines; regression coverage adds 104 lines and the update contract adds seven. No protocol, configuration, or schema was added.

prs.title: fix(update): release owned agent-database holders before package Doctor
prs.body:
Refs #181958. Thanks @RockhopperBot for the detailed update diagnostics.

## What Problem This Solves

A macOS package update can finish stopping a LaunchAgent while its verified serving Gateway child still owns agent databases, allowing package Doctor to encounter the updater's own unfinished cleanup.

## User Impact

Updates wait for the admitted serving process to finish cleanup before proceeding. An unloaded launchd job or a released listener no longer proves stop completion by itself. Pending cleanup produces a warning and uses the existing bounded service-stop deadline. The updater performing the stop must contain this fix; a candidate cannot change an older driver's shutdown sequence.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restart-intent admission already recognizes a serving child beneath the native launchd PID and verifies its membership. Stop completion discarded that distinction and waited only for native PIDs observed through launchctl. Retain the admitted serving PID in that existing wait, including the shipped file-lock ownership path. Process exit also joins its worker threads and database handles. Foreign processes retain Doctor's existing actionable maintenance refusal.

This is a reproduced shutdown-owner defect related to the reported symptom, not proof of the historical holder's exact identity. The saved report does not establish that process tree, so this PR deliberately references the issue without closing it. Current main already preserves an exit-1 Doctor maintenance refusal as the primary error; secondary schema-mismatch errors are generated only while activation is otherwise successful. No presentation change is needed for that path.

## Evidence

- Node 26.12.1 regression with two real processes and an SQLite write transaction: base returned `stopped-before-database-close`; fixed stop waited, then returned only after child exit and committed data remained intact.
- Final owner suite: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/daemon/launchd-update-intent.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 24 passed; 28.48 s wall, about 5.4 s tests, most remaining time compiler preparation.
- Direct and one-barrel consumers selected with `rg`: 517 tests passed across 21 files on Node. Existing Doctor advisory/report suites also passed 64 tests.
- Native `launchd.integration.e2e.test.ts` did not pass: deleted-plist recovery timed out at 120115 ms; co-located node-host/Gateway recovery timed out at 90008 ms. These cases use ordinary service control, where the retained PID set and all awaited operations are unchanged. The underlying host/native-suite stall remains undiagnosed; the lane-owned run was stopped after the repeated timeout. All three task-created service labels were verified absent afterward. No timeout/retry/baseline change was made.
- Real isolated Gateway API proof, without mocks: own HOME/state, loopback port 63625, `/readyz` 200, agent database lease held by the Gateway PID; graceful close exited 0, clean-close receipt written, remaining agent leases 0. Real `doctorCommand(..., { nonInteractive: true })` on the same state exited 0 without maintenance refusal. Doctor's expected health warning named the stopped fixture's port. Exact live commands: `node .artifacts/live-gateway-proof.mjs`, spawning `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .artifacts/live-server.mts 63625` and `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .artifacts/live-doctor.mts` with HOME, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, config path, service label, and port pinned to the fixture. This is lifecycle/maintenance proof, not an npm 2026.10.3-to-2026.10.6 replay.
- The source CLI setup initially refused runtime-artifact publication because it could not establish offline service state; no override was used. Public Gateway/Doctor APIs provided the isolated runtime proof without rebuilding shared artifacts. An initial fixture omitted its dynamic port, causing an authentication refusal at the default health endpoint; the final proof pins both config and environment to its own port.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services.json --incremental`, touched-file `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services.json` and `oxfmt --check`, `git diff --check`, and Madge (0 cycles) passed. Full `check:changed`, including the slow SQLite inventory step, was not run under the campaign's local-gate budget.
- Independent autoreview could not start: sandbox rejected its temporary-directory location even with temporary-directory environment overrides unset. No clean review verdict is claimed; lead review of this head remains necessary.

Simplification: reuse the existing lifecycle wait and existing admission facts; no new retry owner, schema, dependency, or setting. Production LOC +20/-3; test LOC +81/-2; docs +7.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep MCP request timeout budget exact across human-input holds when the wall clock steps
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an MCP request with a human-input pause can hang far past its request timeout, or lose part of its budget, when the system wall clock steps during the request — the timeout deadline, the human-input hold accounting, and the re-armed timer all live on the wall clock while the actual waiting happens on the monotonic clock.

## User Impact

User impact: a session MCP tool request that pauses for a human decision (approval/question) always resumes with its exact remaining execution budget, regardless of NTP corrections or VM/laptop resume. Requests no longer hang open for the length of a backward clock step, and no longer time out early after a forward step.

## Why This Change Was Made

`createMcpRequestLifecycle.run` seeds `deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs`, records `humanInputStartedAt = Date.now()` when the first human-input hold begins, and re-arms the timeout with `expiresAt - Date.now()`. All of this is wall-clock arithmetic, but the budget is consumed by monotonic `setTimeout` waits. A backward wall-clock step between the seed and a hold inflates the re-armed pause window by the step (a 60s rewind turns a 5s+60s hold budget into a 125s armed timer), and a step during a hold makes `elapsed` negative, shrinking the deadline while inflating the remaining human-input budget.

The deadline, hold elapsed measurement, and re-arm computation now live entirely on `performance.now()` — monotonic and unaffected by wall-clock adjustments. This is the same cross-clock-domain pattern already fixed for command process-group teardown in #174151 and the orphaned-process reap grace deadline in #181335; the MCP request lifecycle is the sibling site left on the wall clock.

No public API, configuration, or `didTimeout` contract change; the `SdkError` timeout object and AbortSignal behavior are untouched; behavior on a clock that never steps is identical.

## Evidence

**Pre-fix RED** — stock main (`97d96e53d22f`), regression test only. The request holds for human input while the wall clock rewinds 60s during execution; after 20s of monotonic time the request has not been timed out (its re-armed timer sits at 65s instead of 5s):

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/mcp-client-lifecycle.test.ts -t monotonic
 × fires the request timeout on the monotonic clock when the wall clock rewinds across a human-input hold
   → expected 'still-pending' to be 'rejected'
```

**Post-fix GREEN** — the same request is aborted with `RequestTimeout` inside its budget and `didTimeout` classifies it:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/mcp-client-lifecycle.test.ts
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

**Behavior matrix** (requestTimeoutMs=5s, first human-input hold takes 5s of real time, wall clock rewinds 60s during execution):

```text
clock during request          => post-release timeout armed => result
normal (no step)              => 5s                        => budget exact
wall rewind 60s (pre-fix)     => 65s                       => request hangs past bound
wall rewind 60s (post-fix)    => 5s                        => budget exact
```

Also verified on the changed tree: `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm lint`, and `pnpm tsgo:core` typecheck. The regression test drives the real `createMcpRequestLifecycle` with no transport mocks (the request callback and its hold/release protocol run for real); the local bundled-gateway proof path is not runnable on this Windows contributor box and was not used as evidence.

prs.title: feat(knowledge): bundle the Knowledge memory plugin
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Knowledge, the evidence-backed memory plugin, ships separately from OpenClaw, so it can drift from core and users have to install and load it themselves.

## User Impact

User impact: Knowledge ships with OpenClaw as a bundled plugin, off by default. Setting `plugins.slots.memory: "knowledge"` turns it on. Existing stores keep working: the bundled build opened a copy of a real standalone-Knowledge store without a migration step.

People who installed the standalone plugin need a manual switch, because an installed copy takes precedence over the bundled one. `openclaw plugins uninstall knowledge` also clears `plugins.entries.knowledge.config`, including `stores`. The [Knowledge guide](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/openclaw-ef3/bundle-knowledge/docs/plugins/knowledge.md) lists a safe save, uninstall, enable and restore order. No vault data is touched.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin moves into `extensions/knowledge` and now follows the repository rules for bundled plugins:
- Its tests run under vitest.
- It passes repo lint, type and file-size gates. Large files are split; assertions are justified or removed.
- Workers, the default ontology and the sample vault load from the runtime entry and ship as static assets.
- SQLite access uses the plugin SDK's worker helpers, Kysely builders and immediate transactions.
- A new `knowledge_attach_file` tool attaches a file from the agent's workspace by path, reusing the durable chunked-upload path, so the model no longer copies attachment bytes through its context.

**One part needs maintainer review:** keyword search keeps its SQLite FTS5 index. `scripts/database-dialect-inventory.mts` now excludes `fts5`, `temp-schema` and `rowid` in `extensions/knowledge/src/retrieval.ts` only, through the same mechanism as the existing SQLite-only exclusions. The reasons:
- The index is a cache rebuilt from the vault.
- It lives only in each store's private `state.sqlite` and is never opened through the PostgreSQL-capable database layer.
- Moving it behind a shared SDK text-index API would need core to own plugin database files, which it doesn't today.

`docs/reference/database-schemas/storage-changes.md` documents the exclusion. Tests prove that other constructs in that file, and `fts5` anywhere else, still fail the ratchet. If this exclusion isn't acceptable, the fallback is scoring search in TypeScript inside Knowledge.

The config-surface baseline grows by 28 entries. They are Knowledge's own config schema (`stores`, write and read policy, maintenance), now part of the bundled inventory.

## Evidence

- **Upgrade on real data.** I took a consistent copy (SQLite online backup) of a live standalone-Knowledge state directory: 487 MB, 2 stores, about 76k state pages. An isolated Gateway built from this branch opened it on port 19390 with Knowledge as the memory slot:
  - `status`: the store is `ready` and live watching is on.
  - Keyword search: the FTS index is `ready` and returns ranked hits.
  - Record read, exact lookup, `records`, `timeline`, `history` (git `committed`) and `connections` all succeed.
  - A temporary, uncommitted test opened the same copied store through `createKnowledgeService` and saved a claim with `remember`. The receipt came back `published`, the claim count went from 1,097 to 1,098, and keyword search found the new claim.
- **Authority at the final effect, bundled Gateway.** An isolated Gateway built from this branch, plus the memory-audience fixes (#181359), with a real model and agents `main`/`fm-know`. Probe sessions saved claims with `knowledge_remember`, and the vault path shows the partition:
  - Owner-private permitted: owner dashboard turn, owner turn started by `sessions_send`, and owner cross-agent `sessions_spawn` child all published to `stores/<id>/vault/private/claims/…`.
  - Conversation caller denied private content: a non-admin turn wrote only to `vault/conversations/<sessionId>/claims/…`. The same `knowledge_grep` query returned `no hits` for it and the three private probe claims for the owner. A non-admin `knowledge_record` on a private claim's exact ID returned not found.
  - Operator surfaces on a Gateway with two people: the Knowledge page (`agent_query status`) and `memory.search` refuse `operator.read`/`operator.write` and succeed for `operator.admin`.
  - Revocation before publication (reset, reassignment, retired service) is covered at the worker and publication boundary, not live: `storage-worker.test.ts` (authority revoked mid-operation publishes nothing), `stores.test.ts` (the cutover fences old-assignment access), `live-state.test.ts` (in-flight operations leave no accepted write), `session-activity.test.ts` (revoked authority fails delivery). Gap: there is no live trace of a reset racing a queued write.
- **`knowledge_attach_file` through a bundled Gateway.** An isolated Gateway ran this branch's `dist` at `46415c3e63c` with Knowledge as the memory slot and `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`. The turn ran in a direct session created with `sessions.create`, which the host granted an owner-private memory audience. The agent workspace held `proof/notes.md` (87 bytes); `outside/secret.txt` sat next to the workspace, with a symlink to it at `proof/link-out.txt`. Tool calls and results from the session transcript:

  ```text
  knowledge_attach_file {"filePath":"../outside/secret.txt"}       -> ERROR Source file must be a readable regular file inside the authorized workspace without aliases.
  knowledge_attach_file {"filePath":"proof/link-out.txt"}          -> ERROR Source file must be a readable regular file inside the authorized workspace without aliases.
  knowledge_attach_file {"filePath":"<proof>/outside/secret.txt"}  -> ERROR Source file must be a readable regular file inside the authorized workspace without aliases.
  knowledge_attach_file {"filePath":"proof/notes.md"}              -> {"state":"complete","receivedBytes":87,"evidence":{"path":"artifacts/e5807468-543e-463c-83aa-184e98ccc4fc/notes.md","sha256":"6efbc2b0345f03f0c62b955a866600d1aa6f3397759f322c2cf316c85c1619d9","size":87}}
  ```

  The retained `vault/private/artifacts/e5807468-…/notes.md` is byte-identical to the workspace original (same SHA-256). Neither `secret.txt` nor its marker text appears anywhere under the Knowledge state directory. The agent's first attempt at the allowed file passed `expectedVaultId: ""`, copied from the status of a store that did not exist yet, and the input schema rejected it; the retry omitted the field.
- **Review fixes, now on head `e7c62d534a2`** (rebased onto `main` `93a374a9c95`, which includes #181359; the core commits it carried were dropped as identical to the merged code; the only conflicts were the generated config baseline and worker inventory, regenerated with their generators). Each regression test fails without its fix and passes with it:
  - *Live operator policy:* plugin session actions get host-owned `allowsAgent()` and `isSharedGateway()` checks (#181359). Knowledge calls them each time it re-resolves the principal. `real-vault.test.ts > a role or roster change after admission refuses the operator read before disclosure` admits under the old policy and is refused at the recheck before records are returned.
  - *Pinned memory index:* the rendered index is pinned per agent, session incarnation, store binding and cutoff, while authority is still checked live each turn. `memory-index-hook.test.ts > keeps the rendered index byte-stable when a record is renamed mid-session` fails without the pin. A Gateway restart re-renders once (accepted).
  - *Recycled-inode admission:* found while running the full suite. Since `74f001f8ec1`, state databases were admitted once per `device:inode`, so a recreated or restored database on a recycled inode skipped schema creation (`no such table`). Admitted inodes must now also carry the current schema stamp. `storage-schema.test.ts > a legacy database written into an already admitted inode is admitted again` reproduces it deterministically by rewriting an admitted file in place.
  - *Missing-audience assertions* updated to the new diagnostic; flush-plan prompt-wording assertions trimmed.
  - Full `extensions/knowledge` suite: 51 files, 405 tests pass. Plugin contract, host-hook and memory-provider tests pass; `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:core`, `config:docs:check` and `db:worker-inventory:check` pass.
- **Registry sentinel recovery.** `2ac79915156` completes an empty `registry.id` from the verified registry ID before comparing it. Its regression test, `stores.test.ts > an interrupted sentinel write is completed; a sentinel naming another registry is refused`, fails with the previous `store-registry.ts` (1 failed / 24) and passes with the fix (24 / 24).
- **Build.** `pnpm build` passes, and Knowledge loads from `dist` with origin `bundled`.
- **Rebased onto current `main`** (`0843b940a56`, which includes #180466). Two real conflicts: `main` added a v31 `rowid` exclusion to `scripts/database-dialect-inventory.mts` and its test in the same spots as this PR's FTS5 exclusion, so both exclusions are kept and the test covers both files. The config baseline and worker inventory were regenerated with their generators. On head `64a8959f4cb`: the dialect ratchet (against `0843b940a56`), its 39 tests, the worker-inventory, config-baseline, plugin-inventory and skill-reference checks, `tsgo:extensions`, Knowledge oxlint, the import-cycle check and `pnpm build` all pass.
- **Tests.** Under Node (the CI runtime), `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test:extension knowledge` passed on `3a28571f0ae` (the rebase before the attachment commits): 48 files, 385 tests, in 13m7s. On head `64a8959f4cb` (49 files, 391 tests), 390 passed. The one failure was `publication.test.ts > cross-process publishers fence competing edits and never lose the winner`, which saw revision 4 instead of 2 while the winner's hash was correct. It passed 3 of 3 runs alone, and passed in the earlier full run. The attachment commits don't touch publication, so I'm treating it as a rare timing-sensitive failure under load, tracked as a follow-up, not a regression from this head.
  - `fix(knowledge): bound Markdown block runs before link lexing` fixes the Bun-only slowness in `record-capacity.test.ts > near-limit records…`: JavaScriptCore gave up on `marked`'s paragraph regexp after ~49K lines and fell back to line-by-line lexing. CI runs Node, so CI wasn't affected.
- **Control UI.** Screenshots from an isolated Gateway on this build (origin `bundled`), seeded with the synthetic sample vault. Knowledge is a new page, so there's no "before".

  ![Knowledge Recent view](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff1e59e3-07f9-48c7-b121-6e6e89dc4ee3)
  ![Knowledge Browse view](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b1dfee30-839d-4fcd-80ba-13bee055fa1a)
  ![Knowledge record view](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/39a802af-b106-4bfd-bf3b-e478e1be373c)
- **Gates.** `pnpm check:changed` passes every gate that covers Knowledge, including typecheck, the dialect, worker and assertion ratchets, and import cycles. The dead-export scan flagged two of this PR's re-exports. I removed them, and the scan is now clean. Three gates fail only on files this PR doesn't touch:
  - lint, for line caps in `ui/`, `src/` and `extensions/{telegram,crabbox}`
  - the `max-lines` suppression ratchet, for `ui/` files
  - the core test-shard root budget
- **Review.** Autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, branch mode, P0 threshold) returned `scoped-clean` across 5 passes.
- **Simplify.** `pr-simplify` removed a test-only `Publisher` rename alias and two unused `MAX_ENTRIES` re-exports. Two things remain by design:
  - The `includeMetadata` tool input stays, because agents already use it with the published plugin.
  - Raw prepared statements stay where the SDK database rules allow them.

Diff against the merge base: about 53.7k lines added. Roughly 26.5k is production TypeScript and 3.3k CSS. The rest is tests (14.7k), docs (8.1k) and fixtures, ontology and skills.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Internal one-consumer helpers and private type synonyms add indirection to their owning paths.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior, configuration, CLI, protocol, or Plugin SDK change. Validation, authorization, ordering, retries, shutdown settlement, and lazy-import boundaries stay in place.

## What Changed

Keep one-use image preparation and video-mode selection with their callers. Put private sole-use structural types directly at their annotations. Shared/public names and the standalone session memory backend remain unchanged.

Net production reduction: **112 lines across 28 paths** (188 additions / 300 deletions against the branch base). Tests, fixtures, generated files, and .d.ts files are unchanged. Moved implementation is not counted as removed code.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

No rare-failure guard is removed and no new best-effort behavior compromise is introduced. Runtime decisions and exact structural types remain at their existing owner.

## CI Repair and Attribution

Under the campaign withdrawal rule, only the 15 reachable changed paths were withdrawn, now byte-identical to protected main cb2dbda93738f84f6b25c974c6d0b2d50698b76b. The original full head is preserved without a PR on deslop/z25-parked-ci150-ui-20261015. The other 28 cuts are unchanged. No tests, retries, skips, timeouts, or baselines were altered to address these failures. A new exact-head CI run is the broad proof after the repair push.

Repaired head 687a67fe80de065a84d6a6676802928c576e5143, CI run 40044817245:

| --- | --- | --- |

The test and determining progress-card handlers are unchanged from main parent f79d1b through the new CI base 24adbb81 and actual tested merge fb2c6ec5. Existing focused owner/consumer tests, native targeted typechecks, typed lint, format/parity, line-cap and assertion ratchets, lint-suppression checks, wrapper/eager-import closure, prompt-prefix stability, import cycles, and relevant UI guards passed before publication. prs.title: fix(sessions): use monotonic clock for mailbox debounce deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The session-controller mailbox debounce deadline is seeded with wall-clock `Date.now()` but consumed by monotonic `setTimeout`, so a wall-clock rollback between enqueue and pump inflates the debounce delay by the rollback delta (e.g. a 90 s NTP correction turns a 500 ms debounce into a 90.5 s stall), and a forward jump collapses it to 0 ms via `Math.max(0, …)`, causing premature dispatch. All seed and consume points now use `performance.now()`.

- **Problem**: `lastEnqueuedAt` was written with `Date.now()` at three seed points (enqueue, drain retry, prepare-failure catch) and the remaining budget was computed with `Date.now()` at the consume point, then handed to `setTimeout` (monotonic). This cross-clock-domain mismatch means clock skew directly distorts debounce timing.
- **Solution**: Replace all four `Date.now()` references on the `lastEnqueuedAt` field with `performance.now()`, aligning seed and consume to the same monotonic clock domain as `setTimeout`.
- **What changed**:
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/queue/enqueue.ts:162` — seed `Date.now()` → `performance.now()`
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/queue/drain.ts:269` — seed `Date.now()` → `performance.now()`
  - `src/sessions/session-controller.mailbox-dispatch.ts:157` — consume `Date.now()` → `performance.now()`
  - `src/sessions/session-controller.mailbox-dispatch.ts:232` — seed `Date.now()` → `performance.now()`
  - `src/sessions/session-controller.mailbox.test.ts` — new regression test (BUG-217 counter model)
- **What did NOT change**: `disposeSessionControllerMailbox` (L301, `recentSources.expires`) is a separate cross-clock concern seeded in `enqueue.ts:186` with `Date.now() + TTL`; it is not part of this fix. `waitForQueueDebounce` in `queue-helpers.ts` operates on a different queue object (`pendingQueue` in the TUI layer) and is also out of scope.

## Why This Change Was Made

`lastEnqueuedAt` is a purely in-memory field (initialized to 0, never persisted, never crosses process boundaries), so it is safe to switch entirely to the monotonic clock. The fix is a mechanical clock-source alignment — no new branches, guards, or parsers — which eliminates the cross-clock-domain mismatch at its root.

The initial analysis identified only the consume point (L157) and one seed point (L232) in `mailbox-dispatch.ts`. During implementation, two additional seed points were discovered in `enqueue.ts:162` and `drain.ts:269`: `enqueueFollowupRun` sets `queue.lastEnqueuedAt = Date.now()` on every enqueue, and `executeClaim` sets it on retry-source requeue. Omitting either would leave the seed in wall-clock while the consume reads monotonic, producing a multi-trillion-millisecond delay (wall epoch ~1.79 × 10¹² vs `performance.now()` ~10⁴) that hangs the mailbox. All four points must be in the same clock domain.

## User Impact

Follow-up messages queued behind a non-zero debounce window now dispatch after exactly `debounceMs` regardless of wall-clock adjustments (NTP corrections, manual time changes). Previously, a wall-clock rollback could stall message delivery for the rollback duration, and a forward jump could bypass the debounce entirely.

## Evidence

**Pre-fix RED** (code reverted via `git stash`, test kept): the counter model simulates a 90 000 ms wall-clock rollback between seed and consume. Pre-fix, the delay inflates to 90 500 ms; `vi.advanceTimersByTime(500)` does not fire the wake callback.

```console
$ npx vitest run src/sessions/session-controller.mailbox.test.ts -t "BUG-217"
 FAIL  |unit| src/sessions/session-controller.mailbox.test.ts > controller mailbox scheduling > uses monotonic clock for debounce delay to survive wall-clock rollback (BUG-217)
AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called once, but got 0 times
      Tests  1 failed | 29 skipped (30)
```

**Post-fix GREEN**: after switching all four `Date.now()` to `performance.now()`, the delay is exactly `debounceMs` (500 ms); `vi.advanceTimersByTime(499)` does not wake, `+1` does.

```console
$ npx vitest run src/sessions/session-controller.mailbox.test.ts -t "BUG-217"
 ✓ |unit| src/sessions/session-controller.mailbox.test.ts > controller mailbox scheduling > uses monotonic clock for debounce delay to survive wall-clock rollback (BUG-217) 11ms
      Tests  1 passed | 29 skipped (30)
```

**Full mailbox test suite** (30 tests, no regressions):

```console
$ npx vitest run src/sessions/session-controller.mailbox.test.ts
 ✓ |unit| src/sessions/session-controller.mailbox.test.ts > controller mailbox scheduling > uses monotonic clock for debounce delay to survive wall-clock rollback (BUG-217) 9ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  30 passed (30)
```

**queue.collect.test.ts** (91 tests, includes debounce-stamp assertions — no regressions):

```console
$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/queue.collect.test.ts
 ✓ |infra| src/auto-reply/reply/queue.collect.test.ts > followup queue collect routing > does not advance debounce stamp when overflow rejects an incoming message 7ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  91 passed (91)
```

**Behavior matrix**:

```text
wall-clock state        => pre-fix delay   => post-fix delay
no skew                 => 500 ms          => 500 ms
90 s rollback           => 90 500 ms       => 500 ms
90 s forward jump       => 0 ms (clamped)  => 500 ms
```

**What was not tested**: production NTP correction scenarios — the counter model provides an equivalent semantic proof by separating `Date.now()` and `performance.now()` return values across seed and consume calls. The `waitForQueueDebounce` path in `queue-helpers.ts` (TUI `pendingQueue`) was verified as a separate consumer on a different queue object and is not affected.

**Open PR collision check**: searched all open PRs by changed-file list for `session-controller.mailbox-dispatch.ts`, `session-controller.mailbox.test.ts`, `reply/queue/enqueue.ts`, `reply/queue/drain.ts`; no open PR touched any of these files. Also searched open PRs by keywords "mailbox debounce monotonic", "lastEnqueuedAt", "session-controller mailbox clock" — zero hits.

prs.title: perf(doctor): compute runtime tool schemas once per effective tool set
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor spends part of a large fleet's maintenance window rebuilding identical plugin inventories for agents with different workspaces.

Refs #180690. Thanks @609NFT for the fleet measurements and phase profile.

## User Impact

Runtime tool schema inspection has lower overhead for large agent fleets while still constructing and validating each agent's actual runtime tools, including workspace-local differences.

## Why This Change Was Made

The workspace snapshot cache holds 64 entries. A larger fleet repeatedly evicts those snapshots across Doctor's preparation and inspection sweeps, rebuilding the same installed inventory, normalized manifests, and owner indexes.

Reuse those immutable facts in the existing plugin metadata generation, keyed by actual discovery, install records, host compatibility, environment, and policy. Workspace and capture-time views remain separate. Mutable management inputs retain owned copies; receipt reconciliation copies records before writing. Per-agent tool factories and schema normalization still run for every agent.

The remaining growth is generation-owned sharing and the ownership boundary needed to reuse frozen inventories: production **+157/-29 (net +128)**, regression tests **+183/-22 (net +161)**, and the rerunnable measurement script **+87** lines. There is no new cache manager, config/CLI surface, dependency, or database schema.

## Evidence

Acceptance: identical effective discovery inputs must have constant expensive inventory/owner builds across a fleet, a workspace-local variant must remain independent, and findings plus agent factory contexts must remain identical. Measure the real standalone Doctor phase in fresh Node processes, with five serial interleaved baseline/candidate pairs; elapsed-time tails and peak RSS must hold or improve.

Committed workload, with 200 distinct workspaces, bundled plugins enabled, an offline configured model, isolated state, and cleanup:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/doctor-tool-schemas-measure.ts
```

Node **26.12.1**, baseline `afd591f79f7fe5a5d473114ae166fa6136fc11fe`, candidate `52a7188e94e219a56ebc190dde9a1e6b682626d8`, five samples each:

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Phase median | 27.59 s | 18.09 s |
| Observed p95 (maximum of five) | 30.81 s | 18.92 s |
| Phase range | 25.51–30.81 s | 15.26–18.92 s |
| Median peak RSS | 1715 MiB | 1561 MiB |
| Peak RSS range | 1675–1762 MiB | 1452–1576 MiB |
| Inventory clones per phase | 603 | 2 |
| Findings | 0 | 0 |

Median phase time improved **34%** and median peak RSS **9%**. One-minute host load ranged from 6.1 to 12.2; no concurrent test/build/check jobs from this worktree ran during the samples. A local CPU profile identified repeated inventory/manifest construction and snapshot cloning. These memory numbers cover runtime schema inspection; write-config/final-validation peaks remain a separate follow-up.

The production-path regression uses 200 distinct workspaces and a workspace-local plugin at one agent. The base is red with **1203** provider-owner index builds; the candidate has **5** owner builds, **2** actual installed-inventory builds for the two discovery sets, and **3** index clones. All 200 factories receive their own agent/workspace context, and only the differing agent's two malformed schemas produce findings. Host-version separation, caller metadata ownership, and persisted source-admission reconciliation also pass.

Live CLI against a separate isolated 200-agent config and free port:

```sh
pnpm openclaw --profile upd-l1874-proof doctor --lint --only core/doctor/runtime-tool-schemas --json
```

```json
{"schemaVersion":1,"ok":true,"checksRun":1,"checksSkipped":68,"findings":[]}
```

Exit 0. HOME, OPENCLAW_HOME, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, and OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH pointed to the synthetic fixture. The CLI used the repository's pinned runtime; the measurement above used Node explicitly.

Targeted core/scripts/test-leaf tsgo, oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and madge pass (zero import cycles). All eight prompt-prefix stability cases pass. The requested consumer scan selected 555 paths: the normal runner reported **8228 passed, 8 failed, 31 skipped** across 30 shards. Its live-provider opt-in file was excluded by classification. Seven failures reproduce identically on the untouched base; the eighth was a missing UI-build prerequisite and its unchanged two-case replay passes after `pnpm ui:build`.

The full `check:changed` SQLite inventory was omitted under the requested local gate budget. Independent Codex review could not authenticate, so no independent review verdict was obtained; maintainer review is pending.

<details>
<summary>Inherited failures, setup recovery, and slow-test follow-ups</summary>

The four failing plugin files were replayed on the untouched baseline with:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/plugins/cli-config-lifetime.test.ts \
  src/plugins/plugin-bundled-reload.test.ts \
  src/plugins/plugin-module-generation.sdk.test.ts \
  src/plugins/plugin-sdk-deprecated-imports.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Result: **7 failed, 22 passed**, with the same seven case names and errors as the candidate consumer run. The two CLI config-lifetime cases encounter ESM syntax through the source loader; the two bundled-reload cases fail source capture/CJS file-URL resolution; three legacy-loader cases deliberately remove `Module.registerHooks` while the current Node resolver always selects hooks. These four files were unchanged; no retries, skips, timeout increases, or baselines were added.

The built-CLI Doctor E2E initially hit its 30-second command deadline while building absent Control UI assets. After preparing the runtime and UI through their existing build owners, the unchanged file passed **2/2** tests (53.91 s reported by Vitest, approximately 30 s test time; the complete command took 248.56 s including runtime/compiler preparation). The timed-out UI build's retained artifact lock was recovered only after its owner and associated build processes were verified stopped.

Existing slow suites encountered in the required consumer run:

| File/case | Test time | Observed cost |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `update-command-original-service.test.ts` | 265.0 s/file | Repeated real split-root update/rollback and fresh-state workers |
| `update-command-lease.test.ts` | 204.2 s/file | Repeated continuation and fresh-process Doctor/finalization cycles |
| `doctor-config-preflight.plugin-deferral.test.ts` | 127.1 s/file | Repeated Doctor repair/retry against fresh plugin states |
| Candidate-authority process, healthy case | 35.2 s | Real candidate plus Doctor child-process flow; runtime fixture is prepared once |
| Discord transcript capture E2E | 68.4 s | Cold Gateway/model preparation; startup reached 44.1 s before server initialization completed |
| Recovery-install E2E | 42.4 s | Six scenarios with two fresh CLI boots each |
| Status degradation ownership E2E | 32.5 s | Gateway plus independent status processes |

These are recorded follow-ups under the existing-slow-suite policy. The new fleet regression took 10.1 s of test time in the consumer run.

</details>

prs.title: fix(gateway): reclaim dead legacy locks without a process namespace
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #181993: Windows updates and dev Gateway startup refuse an old lock without `processNamespace`, even when its PID has exited and its heartbeat is weeks old. Thanks @asswwwsa for the report.

## User Impact

Stale legacy Windows file locks recover automatically only when native PID inspection or a recorded process start-time mismatch proves that their owner stopped. Live, unknown, fresh, null, malformed, and foreign owners remain protected. Confirmed recovery also refuses a legacy Windows owner that cannot be proven dead.

## Why This Change Was Made

The file-lock classifier now owns the narrow legacy-record decision and receives the complete holder. It returns `dead` only after the existing 90-second heartbeat threshold and existing process-identity proof; a missing namespace never becomes `same` or grants local maintenance authority. Strict inspection, historical projections, state ownership, and recovery consume that decision. SQLite lease namespace policy stays unchanged.

The namespace field arrived in 99fccf43358c (#164236) and is present in stable v2026.10.1. This is ownership safety for persisted upgrade input rather than config normalization: Doctor cannot manufacture the missing host/namespace evidence. The runtime holding the file-lock reader needs this fix; a candidate cannot patch an already-running older reader. No options, schemas, or dependencies change.

## Evidence

- Explicit Node 26.12.1 (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`): all three touched test files pass, 69 tests, 53.31 s wall (about 7 s test execution; the remainder is compiler/setup work). The exited/reused strict-inspection regressions fail on unchanged base source at the reported `GatewayLockError` guard; that baseline replay used the repository's default pinned Bun runtime.
- The regressions exercise strict inspection and real file-lock acquisition across the process owner and both historical projections, plus confirmed recovery and live/unknown/fresh refusal.
- Core typecheck, touched-file oxlint/oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and Madge (0 cycles) pass.
- Full `check:changed` SQLite inventory omitted under the campaign's local gate budget; PR CI supplies broad proof.
- Isolated autoreview could not launch: its preflight rejected this host's shared temporary-directory setup even with TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP unset. No clean review is claimed; lead review remains required.
- Live macOS proof from the committed head, with isolated HOME/state and a claimed free loopback port: real `pnpm openclaw gateway recover-lock --json` inspected three synthetic legacy records, the printed confirmation returned `{"recovered":true,"removed":3}`, and `pnpm openclaw gateway run --allow-unconfigured --auth none --bind loopback --port <claimed-port>` reached ready in 11.49 s. Direct `/healthz` returned HTTP 200 / `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}`; SIGTERM clean shutdown completed in 357 ms. No real Windows machine was used; Windows identity observations are supplied by the Node regressions. The one-off proof helper waited for an obsolete listening-log string, so readiness was verified directly by HTTP and the lane-owned process group was stopped and joined.
- Simplification: the existing file-lock classifier absorbs the decision; no Doctor rewrite, parallel ownership state, or local-authority fallback. Production +42/-19 LOC; tests +95/-3; docs +2/-2.
- Existing slow consumer: `src/gateway/update-recovery-cleanup.authority.integration.test.ts`, “fences real cleanup RPC deletion by authenticated scope, owner identity, and mid-removal device revocation,” passed in 64.753 s. It cold-starts a real Gateway inside the single test, then creates paired clients and exercises cleanup/revocation. Preserved under the campaign’s pre-existing slow-suite exception; no timeout/retry/assertion changes.
- Required 151-file consumer selector completed on the repository's pinned Bun runtime: 142 files passed, 2 failed, 7 skipped; 2,214 tests passed, 2 failed, 67 skipped; 2,054.56 s wall. Both failures reproduce identically with all changed production files replaced by unchanged parent source at `8c9fb121e8cd98c6f2b5c43c06282e35695492c5`; the committed fix was then restored byte-for-byte. This run is not claimed green.
- Additional existing slow file: `src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.process.test.ts` accumulated 144.031 s of reported test-case execution. It starts separate CLI processes for invalid-config cases and composes Doctor, Gateway startup, and status for readiness cases; it does not perform one warm in-process fixture run. Preserved under the pre-existing slow-suite exception.
- Inherited host failures: `doctor-maintenance.continuation-scope.test.ts` (cached writer false) rejects a group-writable, non-sticky external-volume ancestor (0775), followed by a synthetic service-restoration refusal after capture aborts. `codex-node-exec-server.e2e.test.ts` connects and approves its node but observes `sessionHost: false`; a direct real worker-workspace admission probe rejects that same ancestor, and `runtime.ts` disables worker hosting on this refusal. The E2E case took 172.580 s in the consumer scan and again failed on parent source (139.90 s file wall). These are setup/host limitations, not Windows lock-reclamation failures. Volume permissions and guard assertions were not changed.

prs.title: perf(cron): avoid roster allocation in availability checks
prs.body:
**Hold for performance: do not merge this candidate.** Owner allocation falls sharply and all availability boundaries remain intact, but two valid serial whole-turn comparisons show adverse total GC and maximum pauses. A concurrent swapped-slot comparison was unavailable after the bounded 15-minute wait. Final-head CI completed red on four UI E2E jobs; their inherited status is unverified. The lane owner will not merge.

## What Problem This Solves

Scheduled operator continuations repeatedly rebuild the full agent roster and resolve the state database path while checking cron owner availability. Each assertion asks about one agent, but temporary allocation grows with the configured fleet.

## Change and User Impact

Both cron adapters use a roster-owned membership lookup. Canonical keyed entries use a direct own/enumerable lookup; legacy lists, raw ID normalization, malformed roster handling and absent-versus-empty roster behavior remain supported. A state-bound admission reader reads live refusal publications and the current preparation scope. Canonical agent IDs return unchanged before normalization, avoiding repeated lowercasing. The strict normalization API is unchanged.

Availability assertions remain at every existing boundary: agent removal, deletion blocking, refusal changes and expired preparation scopes still revoke work at the next check. No cache, retained roster, configuration, schema or migration changes.

Production delta is **+41 lines**: +34 for direct membership with raw-roster compatibility and shared roster selection, +7 for the fixed-state live reader, +4 for canonical normalization, +1 existing-barrel export, and −5 in cron adapters. Each addition replaces repeated work; no unrelated deletion offsets the count. This removes work rather than retaining prepared objects, but it is not a net-LOC deletion.

## Measurement

Five samples per side for each of six cells, 20,000 checks per sample (100,000 per side/cell), alternating baseline/candidate process order. Original baseline source: `f8d9d253e1c4bf4433d32f9827d5f078fa377112`; final owner implementation is unchanged by the latest-main rebase. Check timing did not require a whole-Gateway A/B. The attempted extra controlled comparison could not obtain a slot; the reverse-order serial repeat retained the GC concern.

## Proof

Focused local checks used Node 26.12.1 and one worker:

- `src/agents/agent-scope-config.test.ts`: 35 passed; the no-projection regression fails on the original membership implementation.
- `src/state/agent-database-admission.test.ts`: 14 passed, including live replacement/clearing, fixed state scope and escaped preparation revocation.
- `src/gateway/server-cron.test.ts`: 85 passed.
- `src/cron/store/run-receipt-store.test.ts`, `src/cron/session-reaper.test.ts`, `src/cron/service/store.test.ts`, `src/cron/service.manual-delivery.test.ts`: 50 passed.
- `packages/normalization-core/src/agent-id.test.ts`: 19 passed.
- `test/scripts/gateway-bench-profile.test.ts`: 14 passed.
- `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts`, `test/scripts/pr-wrapper-source-closure.test.ts`: 22 passed; export-name collision guard passed.
- Changed-file formatting/lint, targeted core typecheck using tsrs and `git diff --check`: passed. PR CI owns broad proof; no Testbox/Crabbox lease used.
- `src/gateway/server.chat-abort-settlement.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/progress-card-refresh.integration.test.ts`, `src/gateway/tools-invoke-authorization.test.ts`: 38 tests passed under pinned Bun after the CI fixture repairs.
- `test/scripts/type-suppression-inventory.test.ts`: 4 passed. Its single added entry explicitly records the deliberately malformed JavaScript roster fixture; production types and the runtime assertion stay strict.
- **Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable):** no remaining actionable P0/P1/P2 findings. Autoreview preflight rejected a provider/config mismatch; operator configuration was not changed.

CI repairs are preserved, with no reruns to chase green:

- Initial run 40037948466 exposed the scheduler fixture's missing canary-model allowlist entry; the synthetic model is now explicitly permitted. The local attempt was stopped when it requested a full package build; subsequent PR CI supplies its execution proof.
- Run 40041422303 exposed a malformed-array fixture typing error. It is now an explicit negative-input test; run 40042657398 passed all five core test typecheck shards. Its expected-error inventory entry is recorded explicitly, rather than widening production types.
- After rebasing onto upstream's asynchronous chat ACK change, progress-refresh and accepted-injection abort fixtures assumed ACK meant admission had already completed. Both now wait for real injection acceptance before exercising their original assertions. The progress test reproduced red locally before repair; all three affected fixture files passed under pinned Bun afterward.
- A tools-invoke fixture saw an HTTP reset followed by a stale one-shot mock result in the next case. Mocks now reset between cases and fixture requests close their connections. The precise initial reset cause remains unproven; no production network behavior, retry or authorization assertion changed.

Final reviewed source head: `27d9c4e5399ef6e239bddcec045e3181db468f36`. [Final-head CI run 40043692738](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40043692738) completed with all changed Node test shards, core test typechecks, lint, and all three PostgreSQL conformance jobs passing. Four UI E2E jobs failed, leaving the aggregate CI gate red:

|Job|Failing files/signature|
|---|---|
|[UI 2/9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40043692738/job/120720961123)|`chat-workspace-directory-race.e2e.test.ts`: reports button timeout; `sidebar-complete-roster.e2e.test.ts`: four missing child-toggle cases.|
|[UI 3/9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40043692738/job/120720961152)|`chat-file-links.e2e.test.ts`: Files filter button timeout.|
|[UI 6/9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40043692738/job/120720961116)|`session-management.operator-scopes.e2e.test.ts`: SESSION_WRITE organization assertion, expected 1, received 0.|
|[UI 7/9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40043692738/job/120720961175)|`chat-workspace-downloads.e2e.test.ts`: large.txt button timeout.|

No UI files changed in this PR. Each failed job's log was fetched once. The latest scheduled-main result available during the investigation was [40040034138](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40040034138), source `2a7d1994c2a1477483661bc4af5cc90e4d76e8df`, which predates subsequent UI changes and has no matching UI signatures. **Inherited attribution remains unverified; these failures are not dismissed or rerun for green.** The performance hold already prevents landing; final CI is not claimed green.

## Deployment Signal and Limits

During scheduled operator continuations, roster projection and repeated state-path resolution should disappear below availability checks; canonical normalization should no longer allocate there. Assertion frequency and next-check revocation should remain unchanged. Windows without these jobs need not show a measurable difference. The owner benchmark measures successful last-entry checks; raw compatibility and removal/refusal behavior are covered by tests. The synthetic turn uses a small fixture and does not establish production capacity.

**Lead handoff: keep this candidate unmerged because of the repeated GC concern.** The requested owner and authenticated continuation evidence is complete; the concurrent comparison was unavailable. Production growth (+41 lines), small whole-turn fixture, serial host exposure and unresolved GC causality are explicit limitations. Final-head CI is complete with the four UI E2E jobs above still red. Inherited attribution and GC causality remain open; no merge is authorized by this handoff.

prs.title: fix(update): keep upgrade CI compatible with automatic recovery cleanup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes main upgrade and dependency CI after automatic recovery cleanup landed in #181033 and no-op plugin repair landed in #181025. Related: #181195.

## User Impact

No production behavior change: successful updates keep automatic cleanup enabled, while CI verifies the original archive before retirement and the imported content afterward.

## Why This Change Was Made

The survivor still required intentionally retired originals. Its external pre-start observer now records the actual archive bytes; disposed originals must have a matching completed receipt, matching size/digest, and no recreated archive. Pending-delivery, session/history, and rollback checks remain intact. The already-current oracle also accepts exactly one verified recovery-cleanup outcome without accepting package/service mutations. Two internal-only exports are removed.

A direct main repair push was attempted after local proof and independent review, as the red-main policy requires. GitHub rejected it with `GH013: Changes must be made through a pull request`, so this PR is the required fallback.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the archive failure through real migration and terminal automatic cleanup: original absent, producer receipt disposed, 2 files / 400 bytes removed.
- Production-path regression now passes and rejects missing receipts, wrong digests, absent observations, and recreated originals.
- Two no-op cleanup acceptance cases failed before the oracle repair and pass afterward.
- 139 focused tests pass across the six affected/consumer suites (`--maxWorkers=1`), including pending delivery, schema expectations, retirement performance, and configured-plugin no-op repair.
- Core, commands/Doctor tests, script tests, and scripts typechecks pass; touched-file lint/format, shell syntax, and diff checks pass.
- Knip before/after removes only `RecoveryCleanupProgress` and `recordMatchesBundledPackage`; no new findings. Unrelated inherited findings are not changed.
- Independent API-only read-only review: no actionable P0–P2 findings; whole-file test audit completed.
- Real Docker **openclaw@2026.10.5 → 2026.10.6, legacy-operator-state, auto-auth** passes, including managed restart, exact archive observation, pending delivery, schema checks, no-op cleanup, candidate agent turn, final Doctor, and backup rollback. The 596-byte original was observed before cleanup and matched SHA-256 `fc5ce14d10c0d7c8d6cbe7a7a85094a5d28de0b7e8448251f4629e794cfc1f45`.
- Historical 2026.9.4/manual variant remains blocked by an unrelated pending Codex assignment migration: it retained original sources, produced no archive move, and cleanup removed zero files. Its assertions were not weakened.

Baseline main CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40040034138 (first scheduled run including #181195). Its known archive/export failures are the scope here; unrelated architecture, packaging, sessions-list, Bun-stall, Windows, and other main failures are not repaired or rerun by this change.

Focused test wall time was about 59 seconds including wrapper setup/compilation; the new behavioral regression itself took about 1.5 seconds. CI timing remains pending.

prs.title: fix(ui): recover panel reads without inline notices
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session Details and its related panels mix content with loading, empty-state, access-error, and Retry notices. This removes those auxiliary messages and the proposed shared feedback footer. Explicit action failures use the existing toast.

## User Impact

Typed transient read failures recover without inserting notices into the content. Valid same-scope results stay visible during recoverable refresh failures; explicit access denial retires protected results. Stop, sharing, progress refresh and other explicit actions retain failure feedback without automatic replay.

The integration preserves main's native read receipts, clipboard helper, Files selection/scroll/preview lifecycle, Outputs navigation intent and Review request ownership. It removes overlapping presentation adapters rather than restoring retired owners. The remaining delta supplies quiet presentation, missing recovery and action toasts. Existing healthy polling and Dashboard retry policy remain unchanged.

## Diff breakdown

Compared with the integrated base `333b38de8778e13447410eecae53333c49dfd9e3` (not current main):

| Area | Added | Removed | Net |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Production | +2,794 | −3,616 | -822 |
| Unit / component tests | +2,931 | −661 | +2,270 |
| Browser / E2E tests | +39 | −53 | -14 |
| Test support / fixtures | +101 | −2 | +99 |
| **Total** | **+5,865** | **−4,332** | **+1,533** |

The recovery follow-up adds 113 net production lines and 290 net test lines. Test audit removed redundant backoff steps and obsolete output-state fixture mutations; distinct recovery, authority and concurrency contracts remain covered. Production remains net-negative, but the complete PR does not.

## Risk and coverage

This changes UI presentation and read recovery, not Gateway endpoints or Team server configuration. Recovery starts at 30 seconds, backs off to five minutes, preserves server minimum waits and pauses for hidden consumers. Scope replacement retires old work. Files and artifact reads now require visible demand, including initial admission and follow-up reads started by a completed request. Closing the panel or hiding the document retains pending invalidation and accepted data; reopening admits one catch-up without bypassing an existing retry deadline. Validation uses fake clocks and the real UI with a synthetic Gateway; it is not a production load test.

### Recovery follow-up — 2026-10-23

Published head: `c835524d928ae31efea307b06ece24a6df98ffe1`, tree `731ce3612ceeb3054e06a5964935dc249c0ee8c8`. This update preserves the previous PR history. Conflicts with newer main remain; it has not been rebased or merged.

- **Subagents:** transient list failures retain the last valid rows and metrics. Failed reads do not trigger child-history fan-out or immediate pagination loops. Successful recovery resumes the saved next page. Scope retirement and authority errors still clear inaccessible data. Explicit Archive receives a visible read error instead of silently cancelling when discovery is unavailable.
- **Environment:** a typed `FORBIDDEN` clears the current retained change counts, including a copied presentation sharing the loader. Temporary unavailability still preserves them.
- **Context:** closing/reopening preserves the scoped server retry deadline and backoff as numeric facts. Each mounted view keeps its own scheduler; hidden views do not read. Session, identity and connection changes isolate the state. Expired unrelated records are lazily removed; no component callbacks or DOM references are retained. A successful older request cannot erase a newer failure, including one with a shorter requested wait.

**Observed application behavior:** Chromium with the same synthetic Gateway, comparing published `307af84` against this correction. A Gateway session-change event followed by `UNAVAILABLE` changed Subagents from one row to zero before; afterward the row remained. `FORBIDDEN` previously left Environment counts visible on desktop and mobile; afterward those counts cleared. A complete Context sequence of initial open, five reopenings and document hide/show made **8 reads before and 1 afterward** during the 120-second cooldown. Document visibility was controlled by the harness; this is not native macOS suspension or a live production Gateway test.

The three original regressions failed on `307af84`. Additional regression cases protect pagination recovery, Archive error delivery, independent consumers and late success/failure ordering discovered while reviewing the correction; those are not all claimed as defects in the previous published head.

**Validation:** 101 focused tests across eight files passed on the published head in 2.61 seconds Vitest time. UI-chat and UI-components compiler gates passed; final changed-scope lint and whitespace checks passed. Fresh independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issue. The prior CPU, heap and repeated open/close measurements below belong to `307af84`; the new numeric retry retention is validated by scoped lifecycle/concurrency tests and request counts, not a new heap campaign. GitHub CI status is separate from these local results.

These crops show the changed rendered states. Before is the previously published PR head `307af84`, not main; after is this recovery correction. The earlier main comparisons are retained below.

![Recovery follow-up: Subagents retains rows during unavailability; Environment clears denied counts on desktop and mobile](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d0c168e2-08db-4bbd-9662-9a2f4e51a344)

### Visible-only read follow-up

- Fixed three hidden-read paths: delayed artifact refresh after the last consumer closes, directory fan-out after a root listing completes while hidden, and terminal-event refreshes while the document is hidden. These gaps also exist in current main; they were not introduced by the quiet-error presentation changes.
- Same Chromium application flow and synthetic Gateway, comparing pre-fix `dc02e6b997e0a87e9476f913dda458e6e247c26d` with this candidate: closing Files before the held artifact response produced **1 → 0** additional artifact requests; closing before the held root response produced **1 → 0** additional directory requests. Three terminal events while hidden produced **3 → 0** artifact requests and **6 → 0** file-list requests. Reopening completed the deferred work without duplicate requests.
- Twenty additional open/close cycles produced **zero** file or artifact requests. Browser listener count stayed at 983 after cycles 10 and 20 and fell to 950 after final close; DOM nodes did not grow. A separate 50-cycle owner regression leaves zero timers and balances visibility listeners. These are bounded lifecycle observations, not a full heap/CPU or production-load assessment. Document-hidden behavior was exercised through a controlled visibility override; native background-tab suspension was not established by headless Chromium.
- **146 focused tests across six files passed on the published head in 4.79 seconds.** The three hidden-read regressions fail on the pre-fix source for the expected request-count differences. Forced invalidation, independent artifact roles, retry deadlines, and access-denial clearing remain covered.
- UI-chat TypeScript compiler gate passed. Scoped type-aware lint passed with zero errors and one unchanged reactivity warning in an import-only caller; formatting and diff checks passed. Independent final review found no actionable issue. The existing workspace publication helper moved to the model owner to stay within the file-size limit; all callers use that single owner.

### Earlier integration validation

- Integrated owner/sibling validation: 276 tests across 15 files passed in 5.42 seconds Vitest / 6.79 seconds command wall. Six existing browser tests passed in 5.27 seconds, covering Review navigation/focus/mobile controls and Files scroll/search retention.
- Review's retained-row regression failed before the repair and passes afterward: typed transient refresh failures preserve the same DOM row, consecutive retries receive fresh receipts, offline scope replacement hides retired data, and typed denial clears it. The pre-integration branch already hid cached Review content on failure; that defect is not attributed to the main refactor.
- Independent full-delta review completed two passes and found one P2: automatic Context usage updates could bypass recovery deadlines. The fix keeps usage-only updates behind the existing deadline while manual refresh and scope changes remain explicit admissions. Both 30-second and 600-second cases failed before repair; all eight Context tests then passed in 0.689 seconds Vitest / 2.32 seconds wall. An independent focused review found no actionable P0–P2 issue in that fix.
- All 29 core test type graphs and UI types passed on the integrated candidate. Final UI and UI-chat test types passed after the repairs. Scoped lint passed on 137 source/test files with zero errors and eight callback-tracking warnings. Formatting, line-cap, controller and i18n checks passed.
- The full changed-check command is not green: it reports three unchanged max-lines suppressions, two unchanged test-root budget violations, and unused exports outside this UI delta. Exact blob comparisons are retained with the gate output; no baseline allowance or suppression was added. Both new line-cap violations were resolved by moving coherent presentation/state helpers into their existing owner modules, with all callers migrated. Review extraction validation passed 41 unit/browser cases; its independent focused review found no P0–P2 issues. The workspace selection/focus regression also passed after its helper move.
- A fresh full-delta review of the published commit completed two passes. Its only additional report was rejected: the existing `result.computing` guard returns before clearing the pending computation timer. The existing owner-boundary regression passed on the published head (1 test, 4.25 seconds Vitest / 5.77 seconds wall), proving the 500 ms follow-up, retained results, and demand/checkout retirement. No source change was needed.
- The earlier test audit removed 181 net lines from its pre-integration candidate. Its counts are historical, not additional reductions from the table above.

Earlier visible-only validation source: 307af84ddb559a31393da2241ab619b97cb07629 (tree b01b47b0b2af50090f4c2ec4bf367b1720c8bc1c). This update preserves the existing PR history and integrates main 333b38de8778e13447410eecae53333c49dfd9e3. The PR remains open for review, with auto-merge disabled.

## Integrated screenshots

Before is exact main 333b38de8778e13447410eecae53333c49dfd9e3; After was captured at tree 08adedc23452c9e8cabb3670278990d60193435c. Four real UI scenarios passed. The subsequent Context scheduling fix and behavior-preserving helper extraction preserve these rendered states.
