prs.title: fix(update): enable process-tree termination and signal forwarding in runUpdateStep
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a CLI-driven update step (`runUpdateStep` in `src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:213`) spawns a package-manager child tree (such as `npm i --prefix <stage-dir> openclaw@<version>`) that hangs in `ep_poll` and ignores `SIGTERM`, timeout or abort cancellation previously did not enable `killProcessTree: true` and `runStep` (`src/infra/update-runner-command.ts:65`) did not forward `signal?: AbortSignal` to the underlying command runner. Unlike `buildUpdateCommandRunner` (`src/infra/update-runner-command.ts:223`), which already sets `killProcessTree: true`, `runUpdateStep` left `SIGTERM`-ignoring child and descendant processes alive instead of escalating through `createCommandTerminationController` (`src/process/exec-termination.ts:22`) to force-kill the process group and wait for descendant settlement.

### Root Cause & Architectural Fix

- **Architectural owner**: `src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts` (`runUpdateStep`) and `src/infra/update-runner-command.ts` (`runStep`).
- **Canonical fix**:
  - Enable `killProcessTree: true` in `runUpdateStep` (`src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:232`) so timed-out or aborted update steps escalate from graceful `SIGTERM` to forced process-tree termination after the grace window (`COMMAND_PROCESS_TREE_KILL_GRACE_MS`) and wait for process-group extinction.
  - Accept and forward `signal?: AbortSignal` across `RunStepOptions` (`src/infra/update-runner-types.ts:98`), `runStep` (`src/infra/update-runner-command.ts:96`), `PackageUpdateStepRunner` (`src/infra/package-update-lifecycle.ts:32`), and `runUpdateStep` (`src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:220`).
  - Per ClawSweeper review feedback, I removed the staging-directory activity watchdog (`withStageActivityWatchdog`) and npm fetch-timeout env overrides (`applyNpmFetchTimeoutEnv`) so existing `.npmrc` preferences and unbounded default install work are preserved unchanged.
- **Production LOC delta**: Net `-3` lines across 4 production files (`+15 / -18`), plus `+69` lines in `src/cli/update-cli/shared.command-runner.test.ts`.

## Evidence

### Real-Process Cancellation & Descendant-Settlement Regression Test

I replaced the mock-only assertion in `src/cli/update-cli/shared.command-runner.test.ts:749` with a real child-process tree regression test using the actual `runCommandWithTimeout` implementation (`vi.importActual("../../process/exec.js")`). It spawns a real Node parent process that ignores `SIGTERM` and spawns a child process that also ignores `SIGTERM`, verifies both PIDs are alive, aborts `runUpdateStep`, and verifies that `runUpdateStep` settles with `termination: "signal"` and both parent and descendant PIDs are dead (`waitForPidToExit` -> `true`):

prs.title: fix(plugins): keep plugin service stop budgets on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A wall-clock correction during a plugin reload or a one-shot diagnostics stop can stall plugin service cleanup well past its budget, or reject healthy cleanup early. When the system clock is stepped (NTP correction or VM resume), the stop budget is measured on the wall clock (`Date.now()`) but consumed by a monotonic `setTimeout`, so the two diverge: a backward step stretches the budget (the stop hangs far beyond its 5s limit), and a forward step can kill a healthy in-flight cleanup.

- Problem: `runBeforeDeadline` computed `remaining = deadline - Date.now()` and seeded deadlines with `Date.now() + timeout`, while the consuming `setTimeout` runs on the monotonic clock — a cross-clock-domain bug.
- Solution: measure the whole stop/startup budget chain on the monotonic clock (`performance.now()`). A caller-supplied wall-clock deadline is converted once at the `stop()` boundary.
- What changed: `src/plugins/services.ts` (6 seed/read sites to `performance.now()`, plus a single boundary conversion), `src/plugins/service-lifecycle.types.ts` (documents `deadlineAtMs` as a wall-clock epoch), and a regression test in `src/plugins/services.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: the public `stop({ deadlineAtMs })` contract stays a wall-clock epoch, and the two Gateway call sites in `src/gateway/server-plugin-reload-cleanup.ts` are untouched — this is the seam #175639 explicitly left open ("The separate plugin-service API keeps its existing absolute-deadline contract").

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin-service stop chain (producers → diagnostic drain → exporter cleanup) shares deadlines across awaited phases, so a wall-clock step inside that window must not stretch or shrink the remaining monotonic budget. Converting the caller's wall-clock epoch once at the `stop()` boundary keeps the external contract stable while every internal seed and read uses the same clock as the consuming timers.

- **Best fix**: yes. Option B (boundary conversion, unchanged contract) is the smallest closure of the seam left by the already-merged monotonic drain fix (#175639); it needs no Gateway changes and no config or API migration.
- **Alternative**: redefining `deadlineAtMs` as a monotonic value would require touching the two Gateway call sites and several test seeds, and would contradict the absolute-deadline contract #175639 preserves — rejected as broader churn with no behavior gain.
- **Risk**: a caller-supplied deadline that is already expired converts to `Math.max(0, ...)` = immediate timeout, which is the correct fail-closed behavior; a forward clock step yields the same safe clamp. This is an in-process, non-persisted deadline, so no serialization or reporting surface is affected.

## User Impact

Plugin reloads and one-shot diagnostics keep their existing elapsed-time budgets regardless of wall-clock corrections. No configuration, CLI, or migration changes are required, and the plugin-service `stop` API keeps its documented contract.

## Evidence

Validated on head `754d0d97827a` with the shipped `openclaw.mjs` entry. The isolated proof plugin registers a real `diagnostics-otel` service, steps the wall clock back one hour during `stop()`, and leaves cleanup pending for 120s so the deadline domain is observable. It is loaded locally only; no credentials or external services are involved.

**Before/after**

| Shipped entry | Pre-fix | Current head |
|---|---|---|
| `openclaw plugins reload diagnostics-otel --json` through a real Gateway | still pending after `45005ms`, no timeout marker | service budget fired at `4855.55ms` |
| `openclaw agent --local ... --json` | n/a: one exporter cannot create the cross-phase step | agent returned `proof ok`; diagnostics budget fired at `9999.45ms` |
| Targeted `vitest.plugins.config.ts` regression | covered by the existing RED output below | `2 passed`, `25 skipped`, exit 0 |

The service budget settling does not cancel the deliberately retained exporter work; the outer process can remain alive until that work ends. This is intentional ownership behavior and the specific invariant under test is the observation deadline, not cancellation.

### Raw terminal output (inline, current head 754d0d97827a)

```console
# pre-fix source, real Gateway + shipped reload CLI
[proof-plugin] stop begin wallOffsetMs=-3600000 hangMs=120000
[reload-proof] stopMarker=null elapsedMs=45005 cli=timeout
[reload-proof] VERDICT=STILL-PENDING-AFTER-45S

# current head, same shipped entries
[proof-plugin] stop begin wallOffsetMs=-3600000 hangMs=120000
[plugins] plugin service degraded ... stop timed out after 4855.555632000003ms
[reload-proof] VERDICT=BOUNDED
[proof-plugin] service start pid=487025
"finalAssistantVisibleText": "proof ok"
[proof-plugin] stop begin wallOffsetMs=-3600000 hangMs=120000
[plugins] one-shot diagnostics shutdown failed: ... stop timed out after 9999.451649000002ms
[oneshot-proof] sawSuccess=true stopObserved=true
[oneshot-proof] VERDICT=BOUNDED
```

Regression test (existing `services.test.ts` suite, no new file):

```console
$ vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.plugins.config.ts src/plugins/services.test.ts -t "keeps the"
✓ keeps the caller deadline on the monotonic clock across a wall-clock correction
✓ keeps the one-shot stop budget on the monotonic clock across a wall-clock correction
Test Files 1 passed (1)
Tests 2 passed | 25 skipped (27)
```

Pre-fix, the same cases fail with `expected 'pending' to be 'stopping'`.

- **What was not tested**: a real remote exporter with a network socket that remains open after its promise budget expires. The proof uses a local service to isolate the clock-domain invariant.
- **Open PR collision check**: no open PR touches `src/plugins/services.ts`, `src/plugins/service-lifecycle.types.ts`, or `src/plugins/services.test.ts`; related monotonic-clock PRs (#175639, #181360, #180622, #180599) touch different owners.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep CLI final text in peer-result transcripts
prs.body:
Closes #177093

## What Problem This Solves

A `claude-cli` peer-result turn using `message_tool_only` sent two progress messages through the `message` tool, then ended with a distinct final answer. Each progress send already had its own delivery-mirror row, but command fallback also persisted the joined sends as the turn's assistant row, duplicating progress and losing the CLI's final answer.

## User Impact

Chat history and transcript-based reseeding now retain the CLI's authored final answer once. Progress sends remain delivery-owned rows and are not repeated in a joined fallback row. If the CLI produced no final text, no visible assistant row is invented.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveCliTranscriptReplyText` returned an empty fallback for any result carrying `sourceReplyTranscriptMirror` metadata. The real optional peer-result producer demonstrates that progress-only sends also carry mirrors, so that guard suppressed the authored answer entirely.

The resolver now:

- treats an explicit `sourceReplyFinal: true` mirror as delivery-owned;
- for progress-only mirrors, uses `finalAssistantMessageRawText` (then `finalAssistantRawText`) only when that text is not already represented by the mirror rows;
- preserves the existing no-mirror behavior, including receipt-only external delivery.

The usage-only fallback row is emitted only when no authored fallback text remains, so a real final answer is visible instead of hidden.

## Evidence

### Real producer path

The regression runs the real `prepareCliRunTerminalReply` and `buildCliRunResult` producer with `sourceReplyDeliveryMode: "message_tool_only"` and `terminalReplyExpectation: "optional"`. It verifies that both delivered payloads carry transcript mirrors marked non-final, while the result separately retains the authored message.

```text
payloads: 2 source-reply mirrors
sourceReplyFinal: false, false
finalAssistantVisibleText: "Starting.\n\nStill working."
finalAssistantRawText: "Still working."
finalAssistantMessageRawText: "The worker result is ready."
resolved fallback: "The worker result is ready."
```

The persistence assertion then verifies exactly one assistant row with the authored final text. A second regression covers an explicit final mirror and confirms it remains delivery-owned with no duplicate row.

### Base-red and head-green

```text
Base d415cdd4:
expected '' to be 'The worker result is ready.'

Head f968d88f:
✓ persists the CLI answer instead of delivered progress sends for an optional peer-result turn
✓ keeps an explicit final source reply mirror delivery-owned
Tests 8 passed (8)
```

### Validation

- Focused suite: `transcript-persistence.test.ts`, 8/8 passed.
- Consumer suites: `attempt-execution.cli.test.ts` (64) and `cli-runner.reliability.test.ts` (90), 154/154 passed; 162 including the focused suite.
- Core typecheck fallback passes with no diagnostics.
- `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Proof uses the shipped CLI result producer and persistence owner; it does not invoke a live `claude-cli` provider.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted implementation and validation under user direction. The issue, real producer metadata, transcript ownership, and consumer suites were reviewed; the reported base-red behavior was reproduced before applying the fix.

prs.title: fix: expose saved dashboards in session inventory
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: authorized session cleanup cannot distinguish sessions without saved dashboards from unknown dashboard state because the agent-facing inventory omits existing Gateway metadata.

## User Impact

Agents can filter visible sessions by saved-dashboard presence without reading dashboard contents. Missing metadata stays unknown, never empty. Existing session visibility, sharing, incognito exclusions, archival permissions, and pagination bounds are unchanged; there is no migration or new configuration.

Deployment requires a build containing this change and a fresh tool-definition turn/session. No deployment, restart, or live archival is performed by this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already owns the boolean `hasBoard` and its pre-pagination filter. This patch passes those existing contracts through `sessions_list` instead of adding a dashboard reader, new database state, or broader access. A saved tab counts even without widgets; a saved dashboard face alone does not.

Existing timestamps, run metadata, permitted history/search, and live PR state are sufficient for conservative qualification. Documentation requires completed-work evidence, preserving active/queued or ambiguous work and refreshing candidates before archival. Inventory observations are not atomic archive preconditions.

Simplification review retained the existing owner: production +6/−2 lines, tests +75/−1, documentation +4. Remaining growth exposes one existing fact and protects tool projection, visibility, pagination, and stored-tab behavior; no parallel machinery was introduced.

## Evidence

- Regression-first check: three expected failures on the original implementation.
- Focused inventory/query/projection/privacy/description tests passed (103.26s command wall time).
- Real agent-tool `→` Gateway handler `→` stored/resident-row proof passed over 3,474 rows, including a saved tab with no widgets, explicit no-board rows, both filters, and pagination. Gateway test body: 5.327s.
- Final Gateway/query/prefix-stability command passed (126.41s wall time, including cold compilation); prefix stability 8/8 passed.
- Targeted TypeScript, production/test lint, formatting, docs MDX, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Codex Auto Review completed with no P0–P2 findings. CI runtime is not yet available; no full-suite/full-build claim.
- Live model-driven cleanup and deployed tool verification remain pending redeploy. No real sessions were archived.

### Deployment and verification

After normal review/CI and merge, deploy a release containing the merged commit through the authorized deployment owner; do not change permissions. In a fresh tool-definition turn/session, confirm `sessions_list` accepts `hasBoard` and returns explicit booleans. Query `hasBoard: true` and `hasBoard: false` with small pages, then follow `nextOffset` with identical filters; check a known saved-tab session remains in the true set. Confirm active/queued sessions retain their run state and hidden/incognito sessions stay omitted.

Resume cleanup from a fresh deduplicated inventory, not the old audit as an execution plan: require explicit false, last activity older than 24 hours, completed PR-associated work evidenced by permitted history, and live merged PR state. Preserve pinned, current/main/channel/automation, running/queued, active-descendant, pending-input, or ambiguous sessions. Refresh immediately before each manageable archive batch, pass each listed `sessionId` as `expectedSessionId`, inspect per-item outcomes, and verify preserved sessions remain. Any actual authorization refusal remains a blocker; never use raw state as a workaround.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): add localized abort triggers
prs.body:
## Summary

Resubmission of #61075 (and test-only #61067), rebased on current `main` with the review findings fixed.

- Problem: abort detection recognized stop/interrupt commands mostly in English and a few other languages, so users speaking Spanish, French, Hindi, or Arabic could not reliably halt a run in an emergency.
- Why it matters: safety and accessibility. Users need to stop agent execution in their native language.
- What changed: added localized stop/interrupt phrases to the shared `ABORT_TRIGGERS` set in `src/auto-reply/reply/abort-trigger-text.ts`, and matching positive/negative cases in `src/auto-reply/reply/abort.detection.cases.ts`.
- What did NOT change: the matching logic. It is still an exact match after lowercase/whitespace/trailing-punctuation normalization, and `/stop` handling is untouched.

### Review findings addressed

- French: replaced the source/test mismatch. `"avorter"` is not used; French now uses the computing terms `"abandonner"` and `"interrompre"` in both source and tests.
- Test coverage: every added trigger has a positive assertion, and all 66 entries in `ABORT_TRIGGERS` are covered by the positives list, including capitalization and punctuation normalization through `isAbortRequestText`.
- False positives: added negative assertions showing that multi-word uses of the new words do not match (`"para ti"`, `"no lo hagas ahora"`, `"basta de esto"`, `"alto el fuego"`, `"cancel that meeting"`).
- Trailing whitespace removed from the Hindi test lines; `git diff --check` passes.
- Rebased onto current `main` (the trigger set moved to `abort-trigger-text.ts` since the original PR).

## What Problem This Solves

Abort detection only recognized stop/interrupt words in English plus a few languages, so a Spanish, French, Hindi, or Arabic speaker could not reliably halt an active run by typing a stop command. This PR adds the missing standalone phrases to the shared trigger set so those users can abort in their native language.

## Evidence

Focused test on this head:

```text
$ pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/abort.test.ts -t "isAbortTrigger matches standalone abort trigger phrases" --maxWorkers=1
Test Files  1 passed (1)
```

`git diff --check` passes.

Current head running from source with an isolated config/state, the real Gateway `chat.send` ingress, and a real model request (`opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`). Token and API key omitted.


prs.title: fix(text): settle ownership after completed paragraphs
prs.body:
Fixes #181696

## What Problem This Solves

A streamed reply that began with a completed leaked plain-text tool call and then a paragraph re-projected the entire retained reply on every later delta. Visible output remained correct, but a 32 KB reply blocked the Gateway thread for roughly 12 seconds locally.

## User Impact

Completed tool calls now settle at the blank-line boundary, so ordinary prose after them streams with bounded work. The 32 KB repro drops from 12.3 s to 0.38 s and output remains identical to the canonical sanitizer. Nonblank LF and CRLF continuations retain the ownership cache instead of reintroducing repeated parsing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The checkpoint ownership cache reused parsed ownership across a newly created blank line. The cached `retainStart` still pointed at the completed tool call, so `findTextCheckpoint()` kept returning the opening line and `projectPlainTextToolCallBlocks()` rescanned the whole reply for every delta.

The checkpoint now refreshes ownership on a genuine blank-line completion, treating a CRLF split across chunks as one line ending and ignoring ordinary nonblank lines. The shared reuse predicate remains stable, so settled XML output does not rescan the cumulative reply after each paragraph.

## Evidence

### Shipped Gateway proof

A temporary E2E harness exercised the real Gateway `agent` / `agent.wait` path and reconstructed the `chat` subscriber stream. It used a mock OpenAI-compatible provider that emitted 4-character deltas. The completed-tool-call case sent `[tool:read] {}\n\n` followed by 29,717 characters of ordinary prose; the Gateway subscriber received the exact 29,701-character visible reply in 4,445 ms, with `containsToolCall: false` and the expected trailing `Done.`.

```text
GATEWAY_STREAM_PROOF {"label":"tool-call-prose","elapsedMs":4445,"deltaEvents":45,"inputCharacters":29717,"outputCharacters":29701,"outputSha256":"68486157a2e817c71dff9748a3ceeb7c417bb995bbefef4eddf08f52eacc719b","outputPrefix":"Answer paragraph with ordinary prose and no tool markers. Answer paragraph with ","outputSuffix":"no tool markers. Answer paragraph with ordinary prose and no tool markers. Done.","containsRuntimeMarker":false,"containsToolCall":false}
```

The same run also streamed 262,144 ordinary characters with exact output and exercised a split runtime marker; the marker was stripped. The temporary proof harness was removed after capture.

### Regression and work bounds

The original P2 finding is fixed at `14e30dd4`. A follow-up P2 showed that putting the blank-line invalidation in the shared predicate also disabled settled XML reuse; that is fixed at `8804f3ee` by refreshing only the checkpoint ownership cache. Production-projector assertions cover nonblank multiline tool-call continuations for both LF and CRLF.

```text
Base 9fae: LF 18671 ms -> expected 2 to be >= 512
Base 9fae: CRLF 16661 ms -> expected 2 to be >= 512
Base 9fae: reusable LF 7303 ms -> expected 512 to be +0
Base 9fae: reusable CRLF 7006 ms -> expected 512 to be +0
Base 9fae: split CRLF -> expected false to be true
Head 14e30dd4: 5 passed, 25 skipped
Head: LF 196 ms, CRLF 159 ms, reusable LF 21 ms, reusable CRLF 17 ms, split CRLF 2 ms
```

XML work bound, `<tool_call>{}</tool_call>\n\n` followed by 512 blank-line-separated paragraphs in 4-character deltas:

```text
pre-fix 14e30dd4: 512 rejected ownership-reuse checks
fixed 8804f3ee: <16 rejected ownership-reuse checks
```

Deterministic work bound through `createAssistantVisibleStreamText("final_answer")`, 4-character deltas:

```text
base: 114,261,817 projected characters (budget 120,916)
head: 257,000 projected characters
```

Same-host shipping-path timings (Node 24.22.1, fresh process per data point):

| Payload | Base `e65af3ab` | This head |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 16 KB `[tool:read] {}` | 3,088 ms | 198 ms |
| 32 KB `[tool:read] {}` | 12,258 ms | 382 ms |
| 16 KB `[tool:read]` + JSON | 3,181 ms | 194 ms |
| 32 KB `[tool:read]` + JSON | 12,319 ms | 309 ms |

Validation: 297 tests pass across `src/shared/text` and `packages/tool-call-repair`, including the new XML blank-line regression and the existing plain-tool-call bound; `tsc`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` pass.

## AI Assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance under contributor direction and review.

Chat color previews crowd the surrounding prose, and the hexadecimal value is difficult to distinguish at a glance.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the inline swatch treatment, add `0.2em` of outer spacing, and raise normal hexadecimal text from weight 400 to 500. Preserve the existing swatch-to-text gap, color detection, copied text, accessibility, and adjacent mentions and links.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(ui): keep fitting Environment branch names readable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The branch name in Details → Environment fades at its end even when the complete name fits.

## User Impact

Branch names that fit remain fully readable. Longer names keep the existing fade at the available text boundary, with the Worktree label, tooltip, and actions preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the unconditional branch mask so the existing measured text-overflow owner decides when fading is needed. The change removes one CSS declaration and does not change row widths, spacing, or markup.

## Evidence

Captured the real Details → Environment flow from two production builds: baseline `098e991549b` and PR head `af8bf253e1a`. The production difference is the removed CSS declaration; all project and branch data below are synthetic.

Each grid shows all four combinations: a fitting short branch and an overflowing long branch, each with and without the Worktree indicator. Left is before; right is after. Measurements are browser `scrollWidth` and `clientWidth`, in CSS pixels.

**Desktop — 1600 × 1000**

![Before and after: desktop, short and long branch names, with and without Worktree](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5f8a8b7b-29dc-48a6-8197-5f7628463a92)

**Narrow desktop — 1000 × 1000**

![Before and after: narrow desktop, short and long branch names, with and without Worktree](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/32e0ba70-980c-49b8-8c3b-717667d9dc88)

The short branch measures 136/136 px and now has no mask. The long branch measures 510/234 px without Worktree and 510/173 px with Worktree; both retain the overflow fade. Label, row, and badge bounds and the 8 px row gap are identical before and after. The two desktop viewports retain the same native Details column width.

**Mobile — 390 × 1000**

![Before and after: mobile, short and long branch names, with and without Worktree](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/06620362-aa9f-4904-afb9-587ea3bea90d)

Mobile uses its existing separate layout: long names wrap onto multiple lines, without a fade. All four mobile states retain identical geometry and masks. `scrollWidth` equals `clientWidth` here because the text wraps within the label.

- Fresh visual matrix: 12 scenarios per build passed (26.13 s before, 22.94 s after). Opened Details through its native control, verified complete branch text, Worktree presence/absence, desktop overflow and full-name tooltip, and captured settled screenshots with no page errors. Earlier proof additionally covered light theme and read-only access.
- Existing Details and text-overflow browser tests: 14 passed (1.94 s), including width changes, both text directions, adjacent controls, hover, focus, and disclosure behavior.
- Control UI build, scoped CSS formatting/stylelint, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Codex reviews of the CSS change and test follow-up: clean for P0–P2 findings.
- Updated the existing Environment/PR row browser test after initial CI exposed an outdated unconditional-fade expectation. It now checks the three fitting-label fixtures and one genuinely overflowing branch, preserving geometry, publication actions, and the complete title. The revised assertions fail with the original unconditional mask and pass with the fix.
- Changed test file: `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-pull-requests.browser.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1` — 10 passed; 9.91 s wall, 5.986 s test time (new overflow case: 0.799 s). In CI, this file took 14.383 s; the new overflowing-branch scenario took 1.256 s.
- The test-only follow-up leaves production byte-identical to the build shown in the screenshots above.
- [CI run 40023774417](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40023774417) and `openclaw/ci-gate` passed at `af8bf253e1a`.

**Risk and coverage:** This only removes the branch-specific unconditional fade. The shared overflow measurement and CSS remain responsible for clipped labels. No data, permission, API, or layout contract changes.

prs.title: perf(workers): reduce unused imports and duplicate admission maps
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Git and skill-discovery workers retain execution or preview modules their task paths never execute. Plugin preparation also retains the transferred admission maps after copying their entries into the admission owner.

## User Impact

Reduces avoidable worker memory while preserving Git results, plugin publication and custody, and skill discovery. No configuration, schema, or public API changes. Code Mode was audited and remains unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Load process execution at the existing asynchronous execution boundaries; worker-side Git continues delegating execution to its host. Load skill preview validation only when preview is requested. Plugin preparation keeps the admission owner's maps, imports the transfer entries without allocating entry tuples, and clears the consumed transfer maps retained by the capture command. Resource retirement stays with the existing owners.

Runtime source delta is **+1 line** (15 added, 14 removed): the Git asynchronous imports add two lines and releasing consumed admission maps removes one. Keeping each existing async execution API callable on the host requires its local import; authority checks remain after the awaited import and before the effect. There is no second runtime path or new cache. The larger overall diff adds a reusable worker measurement driver, its documentation, and focused import/test coverage.

## Measurement method and decision

Concurrent baseline/candidate source workers ran under an exclusive sandbox slot, with interleaved physical cores and swapped placement in pair 2. Both sides used identical dependencies, URLs, source transformation, fixtures, and start deadlines; only the five import/admission owners differed. One isolate per side. Baseline owner bytes remained unchanged through the final rebase. Heap is collected isolate-local retained heap; file modules are unique debugger script URLs. Warm snapshots are outside the timing window. Worker and whole-process GC/promotion are separately attributed from V8 traces. No production state was read or changed by the workload.

Acceptance rule recorded before measurement: mean paired adverse delta ≥20%, or ≥10% in both original swapped pairs, rejects latency, total GC/request, promotion/request, and eligible loop tails. p99 requires ≥1,000 samples/side; p95 ≥200. Opposite signs or >5× baseline differences require absolute deltas and a third pair for a gating metric; that metric is then decided on its absolute mean. A third pair does not erase an already consistent rejection. GC pause-percentile mean shifts below 1 ms are context, and major percentiles below 50 collections are context. Maximum pause must not exceed max(50 ms, twice baseline maximum). Guard-interrupted measurements are discarded.

The fixture is four workspaces with eight skills each and admission facts for 100 roots/5,000 files. Git exercises uncached branch requests through real host Git, verifies an added branch, and covers affected Git siblings in tests. Plugin resolve verifies captured bytes and close releases all resources. Discovery verifies four workspace results with eight skill entries each. Code Mode completes fresh contexts and verifies results. This is **worker-boundary proof, not a full Gateway/team-shape load test**. Main-isolate heap and total allocated bytes are not measured; no fleet-wide allocation or deployed-memory improvement is claimed.

### Accepted Git and discovery results

Values below are arithmetic means across three paired runs; relative decision values use the prespecified paired rule rather than silently choosing favorable pairs. Each side completed 1,200 requests per pair, making request p95/p99 eligible.

| Worker | Retained heap, baseline → candidate | File modules | Mean latency | Request p95 | Request p99 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Git | 22.071 → 18.812 MiB (**−3.258 MiB, −14.76%**) | 630 → 415 (−215) | 11.334 → 10.743 ms (−0.591) | 17.296 → 16.532 ms | 22.684 → 21.246 ms |
| Discovery | 56.509 → 51.026 MiB (**−5.483 MiB, −9.70%**) | 2,265 → 1,581 (−684) | 3.670 → 3.677 ms (+0.007) | 4.089 → 4.167 ms | 4.941 → 5.068 ms |

| Worker | Worker GC observer ms/request | Worker traced GC ms/request | Whole-process traced GC ms/request | Worker promotion bytes/request | Whole-process promotion bytes/request | Loop p99 ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Git | 0.03630 → 0.02983 | 0.01450 → 0.01570 | 0.05753 → 0.06511 | 40.19 → 36.04 | 49,223.82 → 56,174.78 | 2.819 → 2.798 |
| Discovery | 0.07017 → 0.07914 | 0.05571 → 0.06435 | 0.05751 → 0.06581 | 8,680.13 → 8,045.76 | 9,275.85 → 8,462.84 | 4.749 → 4.837 |

Tradeoffs remain visible: Git whole-process promotion rises **+6,950.96 bytes/request** (+14.74% mean paired relative; original pairs +25.99%, +6.70%, so neither rejection condition). Git worker/whole-process traced GC had opposite original signs; third-pair absolute mean changes are +0.00120/+0.00758 ms/request, equivalent to +8.27%/+13.17% against mean baselines. Discovery worker trace GC original deltas are +9.63%/+11.09% (not both ≥10%); three-pair mean relative is +18.95%, below 20%. Its observer/whole-process mean relative GC changes are +14.52%/+17.71%. These are memory wins, not general allocation or GC wins.

Eligible opposite-sign metrics were resolved with the third pair: Git loop p99 absolute mean −0.021 ms; discovery latency mean +0.007 ms, p95 +0.078 ms, worker promotion −634.37 bytes/request, and loop p99 +0.089 ms. Discovery p99 mean paired relative +2.56%. No accepted worker breaches its applicable gate.

| Worker/pair | Loop samples B/C | Minor collections B/C | Major collections B/C | Maximum worker pause B/C, ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Git 1 | 17,139 / 15,347 | 76 / 79 | 0 / 0 | 9.432 / 5.881 |
| Git 2 | 8,455 / 8,184 | 75 / 79 | 0 / 0 | 1.856 / 1.687 |
| Git 3 | 9,078 / 9,749 | 77 / 79 | 0 / 0 | 2.648 / 5.206 |
| Discovery 1 | 1,380 / 1,412 | 375 / 386 | 3 / 3 | 11.429 / 9.050 |
| Discovery 2 | 1,343 / 1,346 | 374 / 375 | 3 / 3 | 2.827 / 2.996 |
| Discovery 3 | 1,348 / 1,350 | 373 / 375 | 3 / 3 | 3.189 / 2.737 |

Git collection percentiles lack enough samples. Discovery minor p95 mean shift is only +0.056 ms (context under the 1 ms rule); minor p99 and major percentiles lack required counts. Every maximum is below the maximum-pause bound.

### Plugin replacement

The owner-map copy-and-clear replacement passes. Three pairs completed **100,000 requests per side**. Retained heap is 37.489 → 37.358 MiB (**−0.130 MiB, −0.35%**), with the same 973 modules. Snapshots show exactly one populated admission owner and cleared transferred maps: duplicate table storage falls by 236,208 bytes. Net heap savings are smaller because total heap includes other objects and strings; the table-byte reduction is not substituted for measured heap.

Latency mean is 0.02561 → 0.02601 ms (+0.00039); p95 0.03164 → 0.03239 ms (+0.00075), p99 0.09651 → 0.09860 ms (+0.00210). All have 100,000 samples/side/pair and opposite original paired signs; the third-pair absolute means correspond to +1.54%, +2.37%, and +2.17% against mean baselines.

Worker GC observer mean rises approximately 0.000057 ms/request (+6.30% mean paired relative), worker traced GC +0.000067 ms/request (+10.88%), and whole-process traced GC +0.000070 ms/request (+10.64%). The original worker-trace pair deltas are +18.28%/+7.15%, whole-process +17.51%/+7.55%; neither consistently exceeds 10%, and means remain below 20%.

Promotion is specifically decided under v5.2: original worker absolute deltas **+37.3584/−36.7774 bytes/request** (+172.73%/−68.55%) require the third pair (+8.7850 bytes). The three-pair absolute mean is **+3.1220 bytes/request**, 33.3701 → 36.4921 (+9.36% against mean baseline). Whole-process deltas +37.3552/−36.7604/+8.7846 bytes produce mean **+3.1265 bytes/request**, 61.4908 → 64.6173 (+5.08%). The large mean of relative percentages is not used. Loop p99 is 1.115 → 1.094 ms (−0.021).

| Pair | Loop samples B/C | Minor collections B/C | Major collections B/C | Maximum worker pause B/C, ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 2,415 / 2,427 | 1,052 / 917 | 5 / 4 | 6.627 / 6.880 |
| 2 | 2,818 / 2,811 | 923 / 1,072 | 4 / 5 | 3.252 / 4.587 |
| 3 | 2,468 / 2,573 | 961 / 947 | 5 / 5 | 2.110 / 1.931 |

Minor p95 mean shifts −0.0022 ms, context under v5.3; minor p99 lacks 1,000 collections on every side and major tails lack 50. Maximum-pause bounds pass. This is a small retained-memory simplification, with GC/promotion costs reported above, not a throughput claim.

The original map-adoption variant was rejected: worker promotion +50.86%/+17.58%, whole-process promotion +25.27%/+10.98%, and whole-process traced GC +12.76%/+16.90% across the two corrected 100,000-request pairs. Replacing owner maps is not retained in the final implementation.

### Code Mode audit and measurement limitation

No change: every cold/warm/retained inventory has the same 325 file modules, none of the five modified owners is loaded, and every run returns to one native context and zero detached contexts. Collected heap stays 17.095 MiB. No abandoned-context leak was demonstrated.

The corrected unchanged A/A control **fails the short-burst total-GC rule**: its first two 12,000-request pairs show worker GC +16.14%/+14.05% (trace +16.41%/+14.97%). The third pair, requested for other opposite-sign metrics, does not erase that failure. This is an unresolved control/measurement limitation, not a demonstrated regression attributable to changed source and not a passing four-worker campaign. Code Mode is left unchanged and no Code Mode performance improvement is claimed. Request p99 changes were +0.071/+0.091/+0.242 ms; 12,000 samples per side. Loop counts were 4,352/4,335, 4,373/4,396, 4,342/4,275; loop p99 changed +0.504/+0.172/−0.410 ms. Minor/major collection counts were 41/39→45/41, 44/40→45/40, 45/38→31/45. Maximum pauses were 20.143→23.629, 4.167→4.526, 4.571→4.152 ms. GC percentiles are context by sample count.

Earlier non-Git runs had a driver confound: unconditional parent Git imports differed even for unrelated workers. Those timing/GC results are excluded; the committed driver imports that host graph only for Git. Non-Git results above use the corrected driver. Git used the prior driver, whose Git path is unchanged. Heap snapshots corroborate the unused module graphs and duplicated admission backing tables; snapshot shallow-category sizes are not presented as retained-byte attribution.

## Evidence

Focused Git, plugin-generation, plugin-skill-read, discovery-import and status-Git-probe files passed. The discovery import guard fails on the original source and passes the candidate. Core typecheck, changed-file lint/format, export-name collision guard, both closure files (22 tests), and diff checks passed. The replacement plugin file passes all 14 focused tests (86.31 seconds including wrapper). Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable) found no actionable source findings; it also independently audited the paired decisions and retained the failed Code Mode control limitation. No Testbox/Crabbox allocation. PR CI supplies broad proof.

Previous CI exposed a concurrent manual-mock problem in `status.git-probe.test.ts`: after lazy import, siblings bypassed the Vitest factory and invoked real Git. A namespace function spy preserves every assertion and passes all 11 cases. Earlier install-warning CI failures were independently reproduced on baseline and candidate (1 failed/30 passed), not rerun to chase green. Previous head `4be70de7d66ec500b837778dbeb437e25b0c4fcd`, run 40041644158, is **green** (65 successful jobs, 27 skipped). Final head `2e480c8ad983879afb98f90b6bb99c26b238cf48` passes CI run 40043049755: **65 successful jobs, 27 skipped, no failures**. Replacement measurements are complete and independently checked. The PR evidence checker also caught a renamed heading; restoring the required `Evidence` section passed its local policy check. The latest rebase changes none of the five measured owners or their recorded worker module inventories.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Feishu was the only preview-capable bundled channel that did not use the shared progress-draft compositor. It rendered a single replaceable tool status line that could only attach to an already-started answer card (when no streaming session existed, `renderMode !== "card"` dropped it), and it ignored `onItemEvent` / `onPlanUpdate` / `onApprovalEvent` / `onCommandOutput` / `onPatchSummary`. Mid-turn, a Feishu DM stayed visually silent until the final answer began streaming (#147895).

This adopts the same engine the Telegram/Discord/Slack/Mattermost/MS Teams progress drafts use (`createChannelProgressDraftCompositor`) and completes the alignment based on live-gateway validation:

- **Lazy draft creation**: the streaming card starts on the first work event (tool, plan, approval) or streamed text, replacing the eager `onReplyStart` placeholder card. Quick Q&A turns no longer flash an empty card.
- **Progress ownership declaration**: `suppressDefaultToolProgressMessages: true` while the preview is active. Core only forwards the quiet progress callbacks (`onToolStart`, `onItemEvent`, `onPlanUpdate`, `onCommandOutput`, compaction) to channels that declare ownership of progress display when tool summaries are hidden — without this flag the draft receives no events at all (verified live: zero callbacks before the flag, rolling tool lines after).
- **Draft rendering**: rolling tool lines, the plan checklist, approval lines, command-output ends, and patch summaries render through the shared compact progress formatter into the card's status slot.
- **Finalization**: the finalized card keeps only the committed answer by default (`streaming.finalize: "overwrite"`), matching the other draft channels. `streaming.finalize: "append"` opts into retaining the rolling tool lines above the final answer behind a `· · ·` separator; the rotating status label ("Working" and friends) is dropped either way since it marks an in-flight turn.
- **Lifecycle guards**: a committed final stops the draft so late events cannot spawn a phantom card, while a mid-turn retraction (`deleteCurrent`) keeps the draft armed for continued work. Progress callbacks stay unregistered when preview streaming is suppressed (outbound bot mentions, `renderMode: "raw"`, modifying hooks) — unchanged.
- Includes the block-streaming policy fix from #147897 (an unset `channels.feishu.streaming.block` follows `agents.defaults.blockStreamingDefault` instead of being hard-disabled), since mid-turn visibility needs both paths. Supersedes #147897.

## Config

New key `channels.feishu.streaming.finalize`: `"overwrite"` (default) | `"append"`. Documented in `docs/channels/feishu/advanced-configuration.md`; schema in `extensions/feishu/src/config-schema.ts`. The key raises the channel config-surface budget from 3730 to 3732 (`docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json`), raised consciously per the config-surface bar: it is the first Feishu-side control for retaining mid-turn progress on the finalized card and mirrors the retention question raised for the other draft channels.

## Evidence

- `vitest run -c test/vitest/vitest.extension-feishu.config.ts`: 2089 passed. The one failure in `setup-surface.test.ts` ("prompts over SecretRef appId/appSecret config objects") reproduces on the base commit without these changes.
- Delivery-level tests in `reply-dispatcher.test.ts`: the card starts on the first tool event and rolls progress text; plan checklist steps render; **no placeholder card is created on reply start**; **append finalize keeps the tool lines above the answer behind a separator**; final close carries the answer only and stops the draft (a late tool event spawns no phantom card); the no-visible-reply fallback still fires after an empty card close under the lazy model; modifying hooks keep all progress callbacks unregistered.
- **Visual evidence** (real Feishu DM screenshots from the validating deployment):

- Before (stock `2026.9.4`): eager placeholder card stays empty for the whole turn — [screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Decent9967/openclaw/pr-assets-148176/assets/148176/feishu-before-empty-card.png)
- After (this PR): multi-tool turn finalizing with rolling progress retained above the `· · ·` separator and the answer below — [screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Decent9967/openclaw/pr-assets-148176/assets/148176/feishu-after-final-card.png)
- Live-text contrast: the same model turn renders live in CLI consumers while channels historically stayed silent — tracked with diagnostics in #132615 (text-only reference; the earlier screenshot attachment was dropped for exposing operational details)

Live validation on a production gateway (2 users, real multi-minute tasks): lazy creation confirmed (card first appears at the first tool event, ~69s into one turn), tool lines stream during execution, append finalize retains progress, final answer lands in the card.

## Notes for reviewers

- The shard16 startup-error test was flaky-red on #147897 while passing locally and on unrelated PRs; control-ui-performance sits ~66B over its bundle budget with zero UI files in the diff. Both reproduce independently of this change.
- Known upstream limitation (not addressed here): on the embedded agent runtime with the zai provider, text partials never reach channel callbacks even with this PR — tool/plan/approval events stream fine, text lands at turn end. Filing separately with the diagnostic trail.



# Production acceptance-recovery drill (2026-09-15, live gateway + real DM turn)
# Timeline (operator-controlled DNS/egress outage via iptables REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset):
11:21:00  POST /cardkit/v1/cards -> card created (cardId=<card-1>)  [Started streaming]
11:21:13  OUTAGE START (all resolved open.feishu.cn addresses rejected, 32 addrs)
2026-09-15T11:21:41.275+08:00  PUT /cardkit/.../elements/content/content -> Update failed: TypeError: fetch failed
2026-09-15T11:21:41.283+08:00  PUT /cardkit/.../elements/content/content -> Update failed: TypeError: fetch failed
2026-09-15T11:21:41.442+08:00  PUT /cardkit/.../elements/content/content -> Update failed: TypeError: fetch failed
11:21:43  OUTAGE END (rules removed)
11:21:5x  Card content writes resume; card closes with the full answer  [Closed streaming: cardId=<card-1>]
11:22:27  Final reply delivered to the DM (delivered message observed via im/v1/messages)

## Raw session log lines (redacted: host, trace ids, file paths)
feishu[default]: dispatch complete (queuedFinal=true, replies=1)
feishu[default]: dispatch complete (queuedFinal=true, replies=1)
feishu[default] Started streaming: cardId=<card-1>, messageId=<om-1>
feishu[default] Update failed: TypeError: fetch failed
feishu[default] Update failed: TypeError: fetch failed
feishu[default] Update failed: TypeError: fetch failed
feishu[default] Closed streaming: cardId=<card-1>
feishu[default]: dispatch complete (queuedFinal=true, replies=1)

## Evidence notes

The acceptance-recovery path is covered three ways: the wire-level golden `recovered-content-rejection.trace.jsonl` (real dispatcher wiring, replayed in CI), dispatcher/session regression tests (rejected-write retry, coalescing, observer ordering), and the production drill above (a genuine 30s egress outage against the live gateway; the card content writes were rejected mid-stream and the card still closed with the full answer).

# Live mid-turn block drill (2026-09-15, real DM turns per config state; restored after)

- **Inherited-on emits mid-turn messages.** `streaming.mode="off"` (preview off), channel block key unset, `agents.defaults.blockStreamingDefault="on"`: a plan-first narration turn (message tools forbidden in the prompt) delivered the model's pre-tool-call plan as its own mid-turn `🛠` message alongside the final — chat timestamps `16:26:25` (final) / `16:26:27` (block); on the deployed v2026.9.4 core the progress flush coalesces to turn end, so the block lands ~2s after the final while carrying text authored before the tool call.
- **Explicit-off kept emitting — real gap caught by this drill, fixed in 047513ebc.** With `streaming.block.enabled=false` the `🛠` mid-turn message still arrived (`16:30:40` for the `16:29:29` turn): with preview off, nothing declared ownership of mid-turn progress. `c4f0ed77` first targeted `suppressDefaultToolProgressMessages`, but that flag only governs quiet progress-callback forwarding; verbose progress messages are gated by `suppressToolProgressMessages` (`dispatch-from-config.choose-route.ts:100-102`). `047513ebc` sets `suppressToolProgressMessages: !previewStreamingEnabled && !blockStreamingEnabled` with two regressions pinning the flag; extension suite 202/202.
- **Version-skew note:** the post-merge branch requires the matching core build — rebuilt against v2026.9.4 the Feishu WebSocket fails at connect (newer SDK runtime symbol), so the live drill ran on the pre-merge extension build that carries the same block-policy wiring this PR finalizes.
- **Matching-core drill (main @ `ed264cc3c` + this branch's extension build):** inherited-on with verbose progress emits the 💬 commentary message and 🛠️ tool line mid-turn, before the final card (chat timestamps 23:44:22 inbound → 💬 23:44:31 → 🛠️ 23:44:32 → final 23:44:40); with verbose off (the default) three real turns produced exactly one final message each — no upgrade-time message spray. Explicit-off did **not** suppress the verbose lane on the live gateway (💬+🛠️ still preceded the final under `block.enabled=false`) on either core generation: the lane delivering these messages in real turns is not gated by channel `replyOptions` — see the drill comment for the full matrix and what that means for the commentary owner decision.
- Full timeline and methodology (including the first round discarded because the model reported steps through its own message tool, which bypasses channel policy): see the drill comment thread.

prs.title: fix(ui): improve contrast between the active spinner and pending tasks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In Task progress, the pending icon looked stronger and slightly larger than the active spinner.

## User Impact

The active step is easier to identify. Pending icons are subtly softer and their visible circles match the active spinner in width and height.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the active spinner in the existing text color, reduce only the pending icon to 90% opacity, and compensate for the dashed SVG circle’s internal padding. Text, row spacing, the marker’s layout slot, and spinner animation stay unchanged.

## Evidence

- The real Control UI with a synthetic Gateway passed before and after in dark/light themes with normal/reduced motion. Completed, active, and pending steps render together.
- Painted geometry: the pending circle changed from 13.44px to 13.00px in both axes, matching the 13px active spinner. The SVG’s outer box differs because of its internal padding; the comparison measures the painted contour.
- The pending marker keeps its 16×20px layout slot, remains decorative and outside keyboard focus, and keeps the existing text color. Active rotation remains 1.6 seconds and reduced motion disables rotation.
- Keyboard focus on the card summary passed; the pending icon remains `aria-hidden` and has no tab stop.
- The comparative production build budget passed: total CSS −138 bytes raw and +58 bytes gzip, within the 64-byte growth allowances.
- Targeted formatting, stylelint, and diff checks passed. Independent Codex review found no actionable issues. No permanent tests were added for this small visual adjustment.

prs.title: fix: typing filters an open assignment menu
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes typing closing an open **Assign to** submenu instead of filtering its people and agents.

## User Impact

Users can hover **Assign to** and immediately type to filter, then use Escape to clear the search or Arrow Down and Enter to select an owner. Ordinary shortcuts in menus without an active search remain available. There is no visual layout change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The active searchable submenu now receives printable keys before parent-menu shortcuts and chat-composer focus handling. This preserves native text insertion rather than copying keystrokes into a second input path.

Requested and co-authored by @steipete.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/61d7884c-a920-4239-a994-3456bcfaed5c)

## Evidence

- Reproduced in the bundled Control UI before the fix: hovering **Assign to** and typing **carol** invoked Copy link, closed the menu, and sent the remaining text to the composer.
- 32 Chromium checks passed: 29 menu/navigation/people-search tests, two bundled-app sidebar/header regressions, and the existing compact archive-shortcut regression.
- The bundled-app regressions verify empty results, Escape clearing, filtering without clicking search, focus, and the actual owner-assignment request after Arrow Down/Enter.
- UI and component/E2E TypeScript checks, focused formatting/lint, documentation formatting, controller guardrails, and diff whitespace checks passed. Focused lint reports two existing warnings in unchanged code.
- Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- [Current-head WebKit CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40040134846/job/120709464817): 648 tests across 66 files, including assignment, compact assignment, and members-search keyboard tests at 60 and 101 entries. Local proxy startup remains a separately investigated environment limitation; it did not prevent the CI WebKit run.

## Worked on by

- @steipete

prs.title: fix(agents): retain requester selection for returned peer replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A returned legacy peer result may need the original requester's personal-tool selection after the originating tool invocation has ended. The existing continuation retains operator source authority but deliberately removes its ambient tool caller. Reconstructing a fresh caller later can select the wrong requester or reject valid return work.

This is the personal-requester proposal extracted from [#177698](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177698), presented separately so its authority decision does not hold up the lifecycle consolidation.

## Proposed Behavior

Capture the requester selection while the originating caller is live. Only the legacy `replyMode: peer` return flow opts into re-entering that selection under its existing retained operator source. Completion custody follows its existing path; peer messages retain separate turns. The ended invocation's receipt and operational-run instance are not restored.

The retained source's device/Gateway lifetime, release and operator-policy checks remain. The selected person's authority is intersected with the existing caller's scopes. No schema, configuration option, dependency, storage migration or native Codex change is introduced.

## Current upstream conflict repair (2026-10-22)

Current head `615876add6b9448d661e73d9f3ae597f5f9d349f` integrates pinned upstream `52df852cd5be3b3691ef27d0942a4db7b2258eb1` into this standalone requester-selection proposal. Upstream’s accepted-steering custody suite and regular continuation behavior are preserved. Only legacy returned-peer work without a completion owner opts into the captured selected-requester path; completion-owned work retains its existing custody. The requester remains Bob when Alice selected Bob, while upstream’s initiating-creator provenance remains Alice. The ended invocation’s receipt, operational run and full-permission flags are not restored.

The conflict repair also adopts the upstream `AgentStepSession` type owner. One stale test expectation exposed upstream’s new delegated-creator field; the tests now assert both Bob’s selected identity and Alice’s original creator field, including the actual reply-flow composition. This requires no production permission change or new fallback.

The final affected suites pass **20 checks**: four real reply-flow compositions, eight retained-source/accepted-steering custody cases, and eight AgentStep siblings (25.74 seconds through the canonical wrapper). The production-identical regular continuation suite separately passes 13 cases (12.05 seconds file duration). Core production types, the bounded four-file owning test type graph, scoped production/test typed lint, six-file formatting, and whitespace checks pass. The earlier integrated run correctly exposed the stale creator expectation; its failure is retained as the reason for this test-only repair. Broad exact-head CI remains pending publication.

Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the final candidate against the pinned base returns `scoped-clean`, with no actionable findings. Both passes complete: one metadata/context pass explicitly records its limited implementation coverage, and the second reviews the actual patch with frozen authority context. This is a source assessment; the reviewer did not execute project code and does not supply owner approval or a new runtime capture.

The simplify pass keeps selection capture and source re-entry in the existing continuation owner; no second authority store or recipient-permission owner is introduced. The two test groups protect different boundaries: accepted queue custody and retained selected-human identity. Existing compositions additionally protect return delivery, source revocation and requester-session replacement. Net changes against pinned upstream are production +81/−20 lines, tests +640/−3, and one test-planner line. The test growth is retained focused proof from this standalone proposal; this repair adds only explicit initiating-creator expectations and preserves upstream cases.

The security/session-owner decision below remains explicitly open; this PR is ready for that review. Historical authenticated returned-peer, canonical revocation, and personal-tool final-effect captures remain qualified to their recorded `9600c93` source. Their satisfied proof requests are not reopened by this integration; they are also not new runtime executions of the repaired head. Source reassignment, native Codex personal-tool effects, and owner approval remain unclaimed. No operator Gateway was changed or restarted.

## Local deployment checkpoint (2026-10-20)

The operator explicitly opted into a combined local deployment containing main consolidation `7605b4fc8c28a628cd4d6b9a3e63bc9f1304ce10`, reply-obligation candidate `66eea4b4ef10f196ba1640398d186884d5557cdd`, reconnect candidate `de1dfafe07c8f0762b9e5fc16d4dfc6b36a3fbeb`, and selected-requester candidate `9600c93d45bbdb867ff738d258f25ea94a7f2f45`, alongside existing local integrations and the separately restored saved-attempt UI work. The resulting local build is `764886a56987d82f3a3934e2dd7d6a2416ef98da`.

Operational readback confirms the exact loaded build, readiness, health, Node 24, unchanged service environment, and all 25 previously active plugins. This is a combined integration deployment, not standalone validation of each PR or security/session-owner acceptance of any extracted policy. No new business-message, native-effect, revocation or reassignment proof is inferred from operational health. The earlier isolated traces below retain their recorded revisions, scenarios and failed-collector qualifications.

## Maintainer Decision

Should accepted returned peer work be allowed to re-enter the originally selected personal-tool requester under its retained, live-checked source authority? This is a policy proposal, not inferred approval from matching profiles or session identifiers. It does not authorize reviving the ended invocation or replacing recipient execution permissions.

Recommendation: permit this bounded return path only with the original selection, live checks and the full-flow/final-effect proof below. Review it independently of #177698; that consolidation excludes this machinery.

## Evidence

### Actual returned-peer personal-tool effects

An isolated Gateway built at `9600c93d45bbdb867ff738d258f25ea94a7f2f45` completed the genuine public `sessions_send` return using the built-in OpenClaw runtime and scripted inference. Configured trusted-proxy authentication established distinct synthetic Alice and Bob profiles. Bob's explicit human steering was actually accepted into Alice's original execution before the provider selected Bob through the advertised tool. The original invocation and peer ended normally. The returned result then started a distinct execution in the original Gateway session, retaining Bob and the original read/write ceiling without the ended invocation's receipt, operational run or full-permission flag.

The returned execution made three actual advertised `personal_instructions` calls: get and set on Bob's permitted agent succeeded and matched Bob's authenticated canonical readback; set on an agent permitted to Alice but forbidden to Bob returned the exact current-role error. Canonical history attributes all three tool results to that returned execution, with two successes and one error. Alice's own-file readbacks on both agents and five confined filesystem observations remained unchanged; no Bob file appeared on the forbidden agent. The returned execution ended normally with one visible final, one attributed forwarded peer row and an empty pending-input queue. Four main provider requests covered this returned tool/final cycle; background utility requests are counted separately.

The collector exited **0, qualified=true** without timeout or forced containment. Raw facts retain stale initializer fields (`status=UNRUN-unqualified`, `pass=false`); the final `bodyQualified=true` and `passed=true`, exercised assertions and joined exit0 determine qualification. Raw records were not rewritten. The Gateway exited0, all eight observed task processes exited0 and were absent afterward, clients/proxy/provider joined, and task/bootstrap state was removed. The allowlisted trace below uses fixed aliases and relative timing; raw identifiers and state remain private.

**Scope and retained failures:** the API is self-only. This proves a personal effect on an Alice-permitted/Bob-forbidden **agent**, not a foreign-profile file target API or every recipient permission. This is built-in runtime/scripted-provider evidence, not native Codex or real-model inference. Profile reassignment and source revocation are not exercised by this effect case; the separate revoked-source trace retains its own scope. No owner/security approval is inferred. Three prior effect captures remain unqualified setup failures (multi-agent ownership marker, missing private workspace, then the implicit QA workspace suffix); none reached a provider or personal-effect call. Each was preserved and corrected through the supported fixture contract, without changing production guards or permissions.

### Actual authenticated returned-peer and revocation boundaries

At source `9600c93d45bbdb867ff738d258f25ea94a7f2f45`, an isolated authenticated Gateway and the built-in OpenClaw runtime exercised genuine public selection: Alice and Bob became real participants; Alice selected Bob in `sessions_send`; the original and peer runs completed normally before the separate returned execution. The observed requester remained Bob with the original read/write intersection, without borrowing the ended receipt, run, or full permission. One returned main-execution request and one attributed peer history entry produced a normal final. The original positive collector exited **1** because it incorrectly required a user-role history row; the canonical display projection returns that forwarded entry as assistant. The saved raw observations were audited after the run; this is not a whole-collector pass.

A separate revoked-source capture exited **0**. A metadata-only pause held the actual prepared result before its unchanged consumer; the revocation record timestamp was 49 ms after the hold; the successful RPC confirmed persistence by 52 ms, before resumption/source refusal at 54 ms. There were zero returned main-execution requests and zero attributed peer entries. Auxiliary label inference is distinct: two positive and one revoked-case label requests also contained peer text, so this evidence makes no global zero-model-I/O claim. Gateway, provider, proxy, task state and bootstrap cleanup joined without forced containment in both captures.

This uses a scripted local provider with actual loopback provider I/O and disclosed in-memory observation of original owner code, not native Codex. Personal-tool effects, recipient execution permissions and reassignment remain unproved by these captures. Earlier failed collectors remain preserved.


The original positive collector's final history-role assertion remains a failed collector result. The factory now takes requester origin from the existing canonical selected-operator resolver, with its required-origin check, while retaining the original caller's agent/session bindings. The proof fixtures above are synthetic. No operator Gateway or business session was changed, restarted or deployed to collect them.

## Remaining Merge Gates

- Security/session-owner acceptance of the bounded requester re-entry policy remains required. Passing checks do not grant that approval.
- Source reassignment and native Codex personal-tool effects are not claimed; the canonical source-revocation capture exercises the requested revocation alternative.
- Hosted CI and any security-sensitive-change approval remain subject to the repository's normal maintainer gates.

This PR is ready for security/session-owner review of its extracted authority-policy proposal, independently of the lifecycle consolidation.

prs.title: fix: preserve native CLI sessions across completion turns
prs.body:
Related: #178982
Supersedes the temporary main-branch workaround in #178955.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native CLI conversations losing context or rebuilding their tool/prompt prefix when an attached-client or owner turn is followed by a completion turn.

## User Impact

The conversation keeps a stable tool catalog across those turns. Tools still require the current caller’s authority, client capabilities, and delivery context to execute; a visible declaration grants no permission. This applies to shared runtime and plugin tools, not only Claude CLI.

No schema or configuration migration is added. Upgrading from the #178955 hotfix can cause one native-session reset because the full catalog is fingerprinted again. Saved OpenClaw history remains intact, but automatic replay into a replacement native session still depends on the existing history-account boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Remove #178955’s four-name fingerprint exemption and its documentation; replace its regression with stable-catalog/prompt/reuse proof plus configured-tool-removal invalidation.
- Keep names, descriptions, and schemas stable. Reuse the existing execution gate for client capabilities, task delivery, session controls, and owner-only Codex tools.
- Preserve the same declarations through plugin discovery and wrapping, including class-backed/lazy descriptors. The callback adapter is extracted from the existing plugin wrapper, not a second implementation.
- Distinguish declared process support from currently callable process support, so exec’s schema stays stable without enabling detached execution.
- Settle accepted completion bindings through the existing owner instead of suppressing their persistence. Genuine configuration/catalog changes still invalidate native reuse.

Integrated main at `d1db2f3298050` to resolve the hotfix/test overlap and current widget/plugin changes. Retained main’s scheduled-widget routing and plugin metadata validation. No release-branch changes.

## Evidence

Current candidate: `46f025590788b2a256d9a51c519caea1ddfc44e9`.

- Focused integration batches: **326 tests passed in 12 files**, covering CLI preparation/settlement, prompt-prefix stability, client/plugin gates, sandbox session authority, widgets, and exec continuation. Runner wall times: 104.80s and 112.37s; these are local times, not CI seconds. The final consolidated completion suite also passes all 30 tests (47.43s runner wall time; not added again to the total).
- Full production build (including all 157 SDK subpath checks), core production typecheck, affected agents test-typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, complete changed-file formatting, and whitespace checks passed.
- Negative control: retaining main’s #178955 fingerprint implementation makes the consolidated regression fail on configured tool removal (`system-prompt` instead of `prompt-tools`); removing the exemption passes. The control restored the exact tested candidate bytes afterward.
- Full-candidate independent AutoReview: **scoped-clean through P2**, with no actionable findings. Review was source-only; the later test-only consolidation preserves the same assertions. An additional independent plugin/Codex source pass also found no actionable issue.
- Simplification: one execution gate, one descriptor-preserving callback adapter, no tool-name exceptions or new persistence. Against pinned main: production/tooling +391/-291; tests +802/-267; docs +25/-12. The retained growth covers the same declaration/execution contract across existing core, plugin, and native-tool consumers; no new manager or state format.
- The first integration typecheck caught a removed presenter lookup still needed by scheduled routing; it was restored before the passing tests. A lint line-limit finding led to folding the configured-tool-removal assertion into the existing turn sequence, without weakening it.

### Retained live and upgrade evidence

- [Authenticated Claude continuity](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179363#issuecomment-6316094871): contributor’s Control UI → real child completion → Control UI flow retained one native session on `2edffaf5d811`; the base control reset.
- [Authority and stable-upgrade checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179363#issuecomment-6331081185): denied callers did not reach protected handlers; token rotation rejected an outstanding read result; stable-state upgrade preserved messages and settings. Both base and head had a one-time initial native reset.
- [Fork interruption](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179363#issuecomment-6344815555): on `c19837bc3077`, abort/reset during awaited fork preparation produced no fork dispatch or binding write, while the allowed control succeeded. This is outcome evidence; it does not isolate the specific authority assertion, prove prevention of already-issued reads, or cover every revocation timing.

These are contributor-run, prior-head results, not new exact-head live runs. Earlier exact-head CI and ClawSweeper results remain historical. Current-head CI and a fresh ClawSweeper review are pending; this update does not claim merge readiness yet. The prior formal SDK comparison found one added export (`tool-plugin.gateAgentToolExecution`), no removed exports/entrypoints, and no schema or stored-format change.

## Worked on by

Adapted from @Marvinthebored’s [recovery branch](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/tree/fix/178982-stable-tool-declarations), retaining the original contribution and follow-up fixes.

- [Original implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/16662a3f-9198-4c14-b09e-c08323bfd5a4)
