prs.title: fix(windows): launch terminal shims with versioned Node runtimes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Windows terminal sessions reject npm-installed CLIs when OpenClaw is already running under a supported versioned Node executable such as `node24.exe`.

## User Impact

User impact: users whose supported Node installation uses a versioned executable name can launch npm shim-backed terminal CLIs without also placing a separate `node.exe` on `PATH`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The terminal shim path had its own exact `node.exe` check even though the runtime owner now recognizes `node`, `nodejs`, and versioned Node names. Reusing `isNodeRuntime` for the current executable keeps that policy with its owner; non-Node hosts still use the existing `PATH` lookup and fail closed when it is unresolved.

## Evidence

### 2026-10-24 CI integration and lease investigation

- Product head `40e371bf70f4b6a7dcf6ddf337dca2dcc599b76f` integrates frozen main `2a7d1994c2a1477483661bc4af5cc90e4d76e8df`. This is a fast-forwardable merge preserving the original author commits, not a history rewrite. The complete pending diff remains exactly two files, +29/-4. No lease implementation, timeout, assertion, retry policy or retired heartbeat fixture is added to this PR.
- Main contains the specific repairs for the other historical leaves: [retained-custody owner comparison (#160288)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160288), [authority fixture using process.execPath](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8b549de1e0c7559756178ddf328d3f6c6aad06ba), and the heartbeat admission barrier. The heartbeat executor and its old failing test were subsequently [retired by #180192](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180192); this is retirement, not a current pass of that deleted test.
- The historical lease abort originates in the native expiry timer, which creates a stored error later thrown by `assertActive`. The printed stack after `records:` does not establish first-abort timing or implicate the index transaction. [#167467](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167467) changes that same owner site to `scheduleAbsoluteDeadline`, which rechecks the selected `Date.now` clock before expiry. Current main therefore removes the old unconditional real-timer expiry mechanism, but its long-delay regression is not causal proof of the original 1,000 ms renewal ordering.
- A single new [secretless original-order observation](https://github.com/ly85206559/openclaw/actions/runs/40039905824) used controller `1029f8aef73bf47d50378e8e1bb75014748d77f4` and original tested merge `4be713527fbc5f6eb815294cd525f934404516a0`, Node 24.19.0 / pnpm 12.5.1, max workers 2, concurrency 1, and the original six ordered groups (9/1/26/6/6/2 files). All six invocations completed with exit 0. The decoded 4,435-byte group payload retained SHA-256 `aca5296864d1ceef08fb6ace79024cfe55dfaec0875ce1dbd150439da8d2cfcc`.
- I inspected raw logs, source/overlay receipts and both bounded child traces. `observationComplete=true`, no events dropped, both `firstAborts=[]`. The named case passed (7,401 ms); alpha and beta completed before their real expiry callbacks or renewal events were observed. Classification: **NON_REPRODUCING_NOT_A_REPAIR**. This hosted-Linux observation does not reconstruct the historical Blacksmith timing, prove a same-root RED/GREEN repair, or override original upstream CI.
- Normal commit checks, canonical `node scripts/run-format.mts --check src/process/terminal-pty.ts src/process/terminal-pty.test.ts`, targeted `oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json` on both files, and `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed. The locked formatter/linter and canonical lint plugin ran from a separate trusted-main tool environment; contributor product code was not run locally. Fresh product tests/typechecking remain upstream-CI work.
- Complete-range branch-mode P0–P3 autoreview at `40e371bf70f4b6a7dcf6ddf337dca2dcc599b76f`, actual base `origin/main`, supplied `src/daemon/runtime-binary.ts` owner context: `scoped-clean`, `findings=[]`, no priority-filtered findings, confidence 0.96. A 19,815-file / 3,663,252-byte ordinary snapshot was stopped at its first 15-second progress report; the detached non-cone sparse snapshot retained all changed files, owner and instruction context (6 tracked files, about 63 KB), while the full branch bundle remained 2,536 bytes. No paths were filtered from the semantic PR diff.
- GitHub initially retained the old September base record after synchronization and displayed a contradictory large diff. Reasserting the unchanged target branch `main` once refreshed that record without closing/reopening, retargeting to another branch, changing source, or force-pushing. Fresh API readback confirms **2 files, +29/-4, 3 commits**, at unchanged reviewed head `40e371bf70f4b6a7dcf6ddf337dca2dcc599b76f`.
- Fresh exact-head [upstream CI run 40042320220](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40042320220) **completed successfully: 42 jobs passed, 30 planned skips, no failed jobs**. The required [openclaw/ci-gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40042320220/job/120718380940) is SUCCESS at reviewed product head `40e371bf70f4b6a7dcf6ddf337dca2dcc599b76f`; its generated merge `d484d02f584d058165bce65f5c376f5f5fd60687` has main parent `f31da849888b17c221b3081420f112f5eea8dbf5` and that head. Production/test typechecks and lint passed remotely. Fresh live readback is MERGEABLE/CLEAN with no unresolved inline review threads. ClawSweeper exact-head re-review was requested once ([comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/151009#issuecomment-6377183722)); maintainer review/acceptance is still separate. The real Windows npm-shim trace below remains prior-head evidence, not a new Windows execution, and green current CI does not prove the historical lease failure's complete timing.

<details>
<summary>Historical proof and CI investigation (prior heads; latest status above supersedes old next steps)</summary>

### 2026-10-04 measured single-worker cost

- Exact product head `d2efd0713ff5cfd0ee8e3076f24924b33c1e02f4`, clean frozen install, Node 26.8.2 / pnpm 12.5.1 in a secretless Ubuntu 24.04 container: [focused proof job](https://github.com/ly85206559/openclaw/actions/runs/37196754393/job/111420140517) passed.
- Command: `pnpm test src/process/terminal-pty.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --retry=0`, with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1` and `OPENCLAW_TEST_PROJECTS_PARALLEL=1`. Result: 17 passed, 6 platform-specific tests skipped; one file; Vitest duration 1.61 s. The enclosing command measured `/usr/bin/time` wall **3.29 s**, user **4.38 s**, system **0.62 s**, exit 0. No retries were used.
- This is current-head Linux test-cost evidence, not a new Windows PTY execution or a before/after performance claim. The earlier Windows real-shim trace remains explicitly prior-head evidence. Upstream CI remains red as attributed below; this fork proof does not override its gate.

- Real Windows behavior proof on Node `v24.13.1`: copied the installed Node binary under the supported versioned name `node24.exe`, set `PATH` to a proof directory containing that executable but no `node.exe`, and invoked the production `spawnTerminalPty` path against a real npm-style `.cmd` shim using the installed `@lydell/node-pty`. The child reported the actual executable name and preserved arguments, then emitted PTY exit code 0:

  ```text
  OPENCLAW_PROOF {"execBase":"node24.exe","argv":["--","literal"]}
  OPENCLAW_PROOF_EXIT {"exitCode":0}
  ```

- Current-main red proof: the new Windows regression failed before the production change with `A Node executable is required to launch this Windows npm wrapper; add node.exe to PATH.`
- Green proof: the focused versioned-Node test passes and verifies that `node24.exe` launches the resolved npm JavaScript entrypoint with argv preserved.
- Full file on this Windows host: 22 tests passed and 1 non-Windows test skipped; one pre-existing PATH-node fixture was blocked by host policy with `EPERM` while creating a hard link to the installed Node binary. The failure is outside the changed path and reproduces on both D: and the Node binary's F: volume.
- Formatting and static checks: `oxfmt`, direct `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: conflict markers, line/max-lines/assertion ratchets, attribution, ownership/export, duplicate coverage, dependency pins, and formatting passed. The later config-doc stage could not load current `@openclaw/fs-safe` exports from the intentionally reused, stale main-worktree `node_modules`; no dependency install was run in this worktree.
- Exact-head autoreview at `23b1a3ce156`, with `src/daemon/runtime-binary.ts` supplied as owner evidence: no P0-P3 findings; patch-correct confidence 0.98. The reviewer confirmed `node24.exe` / `node-24.exe` acceptance and preservation of the unresolved-`node` rejection.
- Hosted clean-install type, lint, security, and relevant test checks passed. One unrelated compact shard failed `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.global-row-observation.test.ts` after 6,769/6,770 tests passed; this PR does not touch UI or session sidebar code. GitHub refused a failed-job rerun because fork PR authors do not have upstream repository admin rights.

### 2026-09-28 current-main conflict refresh

- Exact head `d2efd0713ff5cfd0ee8e3076f24924b33c1e02f4` merges `origin/main` `ff8c752d852f5d01da5a8a5e6abb7546c1328e83`. The only conflict was the import block in `src/process/terminal-pty.ts`: main had removed the unused `IPty` type while this PR needs the canonical `isNodeRuntime` helper. The result keeps the helper and main's removal; the complete pending diff remains two files, +29/-4, with no Bun/non-Node fallback change.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed. The focused `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/terminal-pty.test.ts` attempt did not collect: the reused Windows `node_modules` lacks the current repository tooling dependencies, and host Node v24.13.1 is below the source floor. No install or dependency reconciliation was run in the shared worktree. The earlier real Windows npm-shim proof remains prior-head behavioral evidence, not a current-head test pass.
- Complete pending-range P0-P3 autoreview used a detached non-cone sparse snapshot (218 files, 2,381,324 bytes; complete branch bundle 2,532 bytes), with `src/daemon/runtime-binary.ts` supplied as owner context. Result: `findings=[]`, no filtered findings, patch correct, confidence 0.96. Fresh exact-head upstream CI is the remaining executable gate; no green or merge-readiness claim is made.

### 2026-09-29 exact-head CI attribution

- At unchanged head `d2efd0713ff5cfd0ee8e3076f24924b33c1e02f4`, upstream CI run `36394331485` finished red in four compact shards. The failed tests were `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-convergence-authority.test.ts` (2), `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.skips-busy-session-lane.test.ts` (1), `src/daemon/service-operation-lock.retained-custody.test.ts` (4), and `src/plugins/plugin-lifecycle-lease.test.ts` (1). This PR changes only `src/process/terminal-pty.ts` and its test, so these failures are outside the PR diff; their root causes and current-main reproducibility are not yet proven. The derived `openclaw/ci-gate` is red. This is not a green-CI or landable claim, and no rerun or push was made just to change the signal.

### 2026-10-04 source-attributed CI follow-up

The source is unchanged at `d2efd0713ff5cfd0ee8e3076f24924b33c1e02f4`; upstream run `36394331485` and its required gate remain red. Three failed test roots now have specific fixes on main, verified in frozen main `4d2617d425ab247a2f55a18523da8cc6a483746c` and absent from this PR head:

- Retained-custody assertions: [#160288](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160288) fixes the mutation owner to compare the stored owner, payload bytes, and timestamp before decoding a changed lease. It restores the existing `release=false` contract. The intermediate test-only expected-throw adjustment is not the proposed repair.
- Post-core authority fixture: [8b549de1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8b549de1e0c7559756178ddf328d3f6c6aad06ba) uses `process.execPath` instead of assuming `/usr/bin/node`, preserving the real refusal and completion assertions.
- Empty-heartbeat replacement fixture: [6d1826f1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6d1826f1ad1f7993a252e94b60b2da3469747186) awaits the existing database-release/admission barrier before creating the successor. Its recorded paired proof is 39/40 before, 40/40 after, plus 665 sibling tests.

The fourth leaf, `plugin-lifecycle-lease.test.ts > reloads install records after waiting for another process`, still lacks a proven same-root repair: it loses the Node lease after acquisition. A different serialization-test repair or a Bun-only lease repair does not establish a fix for this failure.

Next author step is an isolated main integration, fresh focused checks for these exact four files and the terminal owner, complete pending-diff review, and renewed exact-head CI; the remaining lease failure must be investigated if it persists. No blind rerun, all-green claim, or new Windows execution claim is made here.


### 2026-10-07 original-order lease-failure investigation

- Author head is still `d2efd0713ff5cfd0ee8e3076f24924b33c1e02f4`. Both required gate results remain FAILURE ([original aggregate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36394331485/job/108844475301), [derived gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36396650335)). No rerun or push was used to change that signal.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Empty session panels start at inconsistent heights, use different typography, and show mismatched action buttons. Some mobile panels move their content vertically when a description or action is absent.

## User Impact

Full-page empty states now begin consistently below each panel's controls, with the same messages and necessary actions. Mobile content starts 64 px below those controls; desktop content starts 140 px below them, including the existing 12 px host inset. Browser and Terminal use the same existing button appearance.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse PanelEmptyState across the session panels and full-page mobile Details views. Group only the content that is present, remove duplicate wrapper spacing, and keep compact notices, loading, errors, permission restrictions, and unavailable content distinct. Consumers without an explicit session presentation retain their previous layout.

## Evidence

- CI and the CI gate passed for `295e42935b658ef9e6df6ef6e0a4a190911a1b6a`: [completed run 40024356071](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40024356071).
- Test-only CI follow-up at `295e42935b658ef9e6df6ef6e0a4a190911a1b6a`: run 40022142962 exposed a stale `.bp-btn` selector in the stopped-browser routing test. The unchanged Start button now uses the shared `.btn` style. Replaced that selector with the button's accessible role/name, retaining the click-to-start, screenshot recovery, and no-historical-focus assertions. Reproduced the original failure locally; all 13 routing tests and 6 startup/recovery sibling tests pass. The changed file took **4.57 seconds wall time** (1.10 seconds reported by Vitest); the corrected case passed in **0.213 seconds in CI** (run 40024356071). No new test cases or production changes.
- Production UI builds, UI typecheck, targeted CSS lint, formatting, and diff checks passed.

- Fixed the actual CI failure in run 40016876675: the generic cold-open classifier began recognizing Subagents as an empty state after its migration and incorrectly required a button. The test now checks its exact informational title, explanation, and absence of an action; actionable panels retain the enabled-action assertion.
- Compiled app: 46 matched scenarios per side with desktop/mobile and dark/light captures for every applicable panel below. Terminal's empty Sessions picker was opened through its visible control. Browser and Terminal buttons both measure 38.14 px tall, with 8 × 14 px padding, the same radius, background, foreground, and font.
- Six mobile Details pages mount through the real ChatDetails owner and lazy mobile host, with native CSS, synthetic properties/Gateway responses, and a 390 × 844 viewport for each capture. Optional-content combinations and long text at 280 px width/220 px content height retain reachable actions without horizontal overflow. The default presentation's measured geometry is unchanged. These are not claimed as passing lint.

prs.title: fix(test): make WebKit tests selectable in isolated runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: WebKit browser tests cannot be selected through the secretless isolated launcher, which does not forward the package config's environment opt-in and intentionally rejects --project.

## User Impact

No end-user UI change. Developers can select the existing scoped WebKit suite in a network-isolated runner without changing host proxy policy, browser versions, test timeouts, or the launcher's environment allowlist.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a standalone entrypoint that reuses the canonical WebKit configuration factory, extend native discovery coverage to WebKit, and document the image and pinned native pnpm prerequisites. No duplicate browser policy or new CLI flags.

## Evidence

- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40042626261) passes on 6dd9f828f0daf6029e555bb4c0d631ebf80811d9, including openclaw/ci-gate.
- New discovery case fails without the entrypoint; the full owning config suite passes: 7 tests, 46.53 seconds locally. The WebKit case takes 9.66 seconds because it resolves native standalone, embedded, and explicit-root projects. CI timing is not yet available.
- Pinned Playwright 1.64.0 / WebKit 27.2 in the official matching image, with network disabled: all 23 existing menu-navigation tests pass (4.15 seconds test time).
- Independent source-app startup proof in the same secretless isolation: visible mocked history, ready/routeReady/rosterReady true, Gateway connected, native search and actual app composer input accepted, zero page errors. Temporary proof fixtures are not committed.
- Targeted root-test typecheck, lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. Independent P0–P2 review completed with no actionable findings.
- **Local infrastructure gap:** both isolated test bodies passed, but the wrapper later exited 2 when Podman post-test container inspection exceeded its existing 30-second command deadline. Both owned containers were subsequently confirmed absent. This is not reported as a fully green wrapper invocation.

The original host failure was traced to inherited authenticated proxy routing: WebKit's initial document receives HTTP 400 and its loopback WebSocket cannot connect. This change uses the existing network-none runner rather than bypassing or expanding that proxy policy. No live Gateway or shared browser installation was changed.

Requested by @steipete.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @steipete](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/61d7884c-a920-4239-a994-3456bcfaed5c)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/9413d6c4-31ee-439e-abb9-7f2a00c99677)

## Worked on by

- @steipete

prs.title: fix(test): live ACP bind lane fails after raw harness sessions moved to the requesting agent
prs.body:
Related: #178944, #181959

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the live ACP bind lane always fails at the bind step with `expected 'agent:main:acp:…' to match /^agent:claude:acp:/` when spawning a raw harness such as `claude` or `codex`.

## User Impact

No product change. The live ACP bind lane passes again on main, so release validation can catch real ACP regressions. That includes the intermittent `Session storage changed while starting work` conflict from #178944, which #181959 makes self-diagnosing and which needs this lane working to capture.

## Why This Change Was Made

#168989 intentionally made `/acp spawn <raw harness>` keep the session owned by the requesting configured agent, unless the harness id is itself a configured agent (`src/auto-reply/reply/commands-acp/lifecycle.ts`). This live test was not updated and still asserts the pre-#168989 key `agent:<harness>:acp:`, so the lane fails at the bind step on every run.

The lane always spawns from the `main` session, so the assertion now expects `agent:main:acp:`.

Accepted edge case: a personal live config that defines an agent named after the harness (for example an agent called `claude`) would keep that agent's namespace, and this assertion would fail. The inline comment names this. The lane's own config never defines such an agent.

The test file is already over its line cap, and the pre-commit ratchet blocks growth, so the change is a one-line assertion plus a comment rather than a reimplementation of the ownership rule.

## Evidence

Real live lane, the same command on both sides:

```
OPENCLAW_LIVE_USE_REAL_HOME=1 OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$(mktemp -d)" OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 \
OPENCLAW_LIVE_ACP_BIND=1 OPENCLAW_LIVE_ACP_BIND_AGENT=claude OPENCLAW_LIVE_ACP_BIND_CLAUDE_AUTH=subscription \
pnpm test:live -- src/gateway/gateway-acp-bind.live.test.ts
```

It starts a real Gateway and a real Claude ACP agent (Claude Code subscription auth), with OpenClaw state in a fresh temp directory.

**main**

```
[live-acp-bind] gateway websocket connected
[live-acp-bind] bind command completed
× gateway live (ACP bind) > binds a synthetic Slack DM conversation to a live ACP session and reroutes the next turn
AssertionError: expected 'agent:main:acp:95b51786-…' to match /^agent:claude:acp:/
 ❯ src/gateway/gateway-acp-bind.live.test.ts:773:35
Tests  1 failed | 7 passed (8)
```

**This PR (committed assertion)**

The committed assertion (`/^agent:main:acp:/`, a diff identical to this PR) passed 5 consecutive live runs. Each was `Tests 8 passed (8)`, with the bind to `agent:main:acp:…` and 6 bound-session turns. These runs were on a local branch combining this change with #181959. Run 5:

```
[live-acp-bind] gateway websocket connected
[live-acp-bind] bind command completed
[live-acp-bind] binding announced for session agent:main:acp:c562bcab-858e-4006-ab4e-e070059618ae
[live-acp-bind] follow-up turn completed (attempt 1)
[live-acp-bind] memory recall turn completed (attempt 1)
[live-acp-bind] bound session transcript retained the previous token
[live-acp-bind] memory marker turn completed (attempt 1)
[live-acp-bind] bound session transcript contains the final marker token
[live-acp-bind] image turn completed (attempt 1)
[live-acp-bind] bound session classified the probe image
✓ gateway live (ACP bind) > binds a synthetic Slack DM conversation to a live ACP session and reroutes the next turn
Tests  8 passed (8)
```

An earlier run on this branch with a draft of the assertion (`listAgentIds(nextCfg).includes(liveAgent) ? liveAgent : "main"`, which resolves to the same `main` owner) also passed 8/8, binding `agent:main:acp:7265064c-658d-4861-bfcd-5e3fc9ef6ce5`. The committed one-liner was reduced to satisfy the file's line-cap ratchet.

**Control:** the bind itself, the rerouted follow-up turns, transcript retention, the image probe, and the cron MCP probe's existing non-fatal fallback ("cron mcp job … not observed; continuing after bind/image verification") all behave as before. Only the session-key assertion changed.

**Checks:** `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, and the pre-commit line-cap ratchet are clean.

**Note for #181959:** no `Session storage changed while starting work` refusal appeared across any of these full bound-session runs, consistent with #178944 being rare rather than caused by ordinary bound-session traffic.

Production delta +0/-0; test delta +3/-1.

**Merge risk:** none for runtime. This is a live-only test assertion aligned with the existing `/acp spawn` ownership contract from #168989.

prs.title: fix(plugins): read mixed-case plugin policy from canonical lowercase entries
prs.body:
Fixes #180071

## What Problem This Solves

Reinstalling or updating a plugin whose manifest id is mixed case (for example `MyPlug`) ignored the settings stored under its canonical lowercase policy key (`plugins.entries.myplug`). The install printed "requires configuration first", wrote a second raw-case entry (`MyPlug: { enabled: false }`), and the loader, which resolves the lowercase key, then treated the plugin as disabled. A configured, enabled plugin ended up disabled after a reinstall.

## Why This Change Was Made

#164683 moved the loader, config validation, and `plugins enable`/`disable` onto the normalized plugin id, but install persistence still looked up policy by the raw manifest id in four places. They now use the same `normalizePluginId` / `normalizePluginsConfig` identity:

- `plugin-config-enablement.ts`: the required-settings check reads `config` from the canonical entry.
- `enable.ts` `prepareConfigForDisabledInstall`: stages the disabled install through `setPluginEnabledInConfig`, the helper `plugins disable` uses. The entry lands on the canonical key and folds any aliases, keeping existing policy minus `config`.
- `install-persistence.ts`: the denylist removal and the explicit-disable check compare canonical ids.

Lowercase ids are unaffected, because `normalizePluginId` returns them unchanged. This follows the approach in @yetval's closed #177672.

Accepted edge case (unchanged, as the issue proposes): configs already damaged by an affected build still carry a raw-case `MyPlug: { enabled: false }` alias. Nothing deletes it automatically, since it can't be told apart from a disable an operator wrote. `openclaw plugins enable MyPlug` collapses it.

## User Impact

Reinstalling or updating a mixed-case plugin keeps its settings and enabled/disabled state, shows no false "requires configuration" warning, and writes no duplicate keys.

## Evidence

**Contributor-supplied regression and CLI evidence:**

**Regression tests:** two new tests in `src/plugins/install-persistence.test.ts`. Both fail on `main` and pass with the fix:
- A configured mixed-case reinstall stays enabled, an explicit lowercase `enabled: false` is preserved, and no duplicate key is written.
- A mixed-case install with missing settings is staged disabled under the lowercase key, and its lowercase `deny` entry is cleared.

**Tests and checks:**
- `pnpm test src/plugins/install-persistence.test.ts src/plugins/enable.test.ts src/plugins/management-service.workspace-inventory.test.ts`: passed.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-plugins.install.test.ts`: 18/18 passed.
- Changed-file lint (oxlint), format, every core typecheck shard, and `git diff --check` pass.
- The core test shard root budget check fails, but it fails on `main` too.

**Real CLI** (`pnpm openclaw`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`). Two local plugins, `MyPlug` and `OtherPlug`, each with a configSchema requiring `token`. Settings are under the lowercase keys; MyPlug is enabled and OtherPlug disabled. Then both are reinstalled:

```
# BEFORE (main)
Installed plugin "MyPlug" without enabling it because it requires configuration first. ...
Installed plugin "OtherPlug" without enabling it because it requires configuration first. ...
plugins.entries: {"myplug":{"enabled":true,"config":{"token":"abc"}},"otherplug":{"enabled":false,"config":{"token":"xyz"}},"MyPlug":{"enabled":false},"OtherPlug":{"enabled":false}}
  MyPlug: disabled
  OtherPlug: disabled

# AFTER (this branch)
Installed plugin: MyPlug
Installed plugin: OtherPlug
plugins.entries: {"otherplug":{"enabled":false,"config":{"token":"xyz"}},"myplug":{"enabled":true,"config":{"token":"abc"}}}
  MyPlug: enabled
  OtherPlug: disabled
```

**Upgrade from current stable `openclaw@2026.10.6`, plus existing-data compatibility.** Each scenario starts from a fresh isolated state seeded only with the published 2026.10.6 CLI:
- `MyPlug`: installed, `config set plugins.entries.myplug.config.token abc`, then `plugins enable MyPlug`.
- `OtherPlug`: installed, `config set plugins.entries.otherplug.config.token xyz`, then `plugins disable OtherPlug`.

The branch then runs `doctor --fix --non-interactive` and `plugins install --force` for both plugins. Effective status comes from `plugins list --json`.

```
# A. BEFORE: reinstall on 2026.10.6
Installed plugin "MyPlug" without enabling it because it requires configuration first. ...
Installed plugin "OtherPlug" without enabling it because it requires configuration first. ...
plugins.entries: {"myplug":{"enabled":true,"config":{"token":"abc"}},"otherplug":{"enabled":false,"config":{"token":"xyz"}},"MyPlug":{"enabled":false},"OtherPlug":{"enabled":false}}
status: MyPlug: disabled, OtherPlug: disabled

# B. UPGRADE: 2026.10.6 state -> this branch
existing data, read by the branch before any write:
plugins.entries: {"myplug":{"enabled":true,"config":{"token":"abc"}},"otherplug":{"enabled":false,"config":{"token":"xyz"}}}
Installed plugin: MyPlug
Installed plugin: OtherPlug
plugins.entries: {"otherplug":{"enabled":false,"config":{"token":"xyz"}},"myplug":{"enabled":true,"config":{"token":"abc"}}}
status: MyPlug: loaded, OtherPlug: disabled

# C. EXISTING DAMAGED DATA: state already reinstalled on 2026.10.6 (raw-case aliases) -> this branch
plugins.entries before: {"myplug":{"enabled":true,"config":{"token":"abc"}},"otherplug":{"enabled":false,"config":{"token":"xyz"}},"MyPlug":{"enabled":false},"OtherPlug":{"enabled":false}}
Installed plugin: MyPlug
Installed plugin: OtherPlug
plugins.entries after reinstall: unchanged (settings intact, no new keys)
$ openclaw plugins enable MyPlug   # documented recovery, collapses the alias
Installed plugin: MyPlug
Installed plugin: OtherPlug
plugins.entries: {"otherplug":{"enabled":false,"config":{"token":"xyz"}},"OtherPlug":{"enabled":false},"myplug":{"enabled":true,"config":{"token":"abc"}}}
status: MyPlug: loaded, OtherPlug: disabled
```

Both settings and both preferences survive the upgrade (B). Data already damaged by 2026.10.6 still loads, and reinstalls neither lose settings nor add keys (C). The leftover `OtherPlug: {enabled:false}` alias matches the canonical disabled preference and is left in place by design (see the accepted edge case above).

**Doctor on 2026.10.6 state (pre-existing, unchanged by this PR).** `doctor --fix --non-interactive` on this seeded state reports `Plugin "myplug" data/settings upgrade is unfinished: The migration owner is unavailable`, and `plugins.entries.otherplug.config.token: invalid config: must have required property 'token'` ("config fixes were not applied"). The branch parent `f5a4d6157d`, without this change, prints the identical output on the same seed. Current `main` (`d85f1a04b5`) prints the same migration warning. Doctor's migration code does not import any file this PR changes. Doctor keeps the data in every case, and the reinstalls above run after it.

**Gaps:**
- The contributor reported an isolated review authentication failure; the maintainer review result is recorded below.
- No credentials, IPs or endpoints appear above; tokens are placeholders.

### Maintainer review

**VERDICT: LAND-AS-IS** at `1a9024b57c2a8e45897ebc501dcfcd026d533c6c`. The contributor's patch and commit by @anmol0b are retained unchanged, including the credit to @yetval above. The simplification review found that the existing canonical policy and toggle owners provide the complete fix without new helpers or a migration.

Confirmed against fresh main `b389baf8895b209dbc5252487bc672c0e0c45aba`: the defect remains at [`plugin-config-enablement.ts:20`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b389baf8895b209dbc5252487bc672c0e0c45aba/src/plugins/plugin-config-enablement.ts#L20), where `MyPlug` misses `myplug.config`, followed by raw-case disabled staging at `enable.ts:29` and raw deny/disable checks at `install-persistence.ts:63` and `:346`. prs.title: feat(channels): follow filtered channel logs
prs.body:
Closes #130198

## What Problem This Solves

Operators currently have to repeat channel log snapshots or manually filter the general log stream to watch one channel.

## User Impact

`openclaw channels logs --channel slack --follow` prints the initial tail and then new matching records, with the same channel filtering and secret redaction. `--interval <ms>` controls polling; Ctrl-C stops the command. Existing one-shot text and JSON output stay unchanged.

`--follow --json` emits newline-delimited `meta`, `log`, and `notice` records, consistent with the general logs stream. This remains bounded diagnostics, not archival delivery: polls may omit backlog beyond 5,000 matching records or 1 MB, with notices. Shrinking files and changed rolling paths reset the cursor; same-path replacement without shrink retains the shared reader's existing limitation. No config, migration, Gateway RPC, or provider access is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the configured log reader's cursor, parser, redaction, and bounds within the channel command. Shared Gateway/UI reader behavior is unchanged; the parsed reader only gains the optional cursor type already supported underneath.

## Evidence

- [Untouched-base actual CLI baseline](https://github.com/ly85206559/openclaw/actions/runs/39970922742): `pnpm --silent openclaw channels logs --channel slack --follow --interval 50 --json` exits 1 with `OpenClaw does not recognize option "--follow".` and the matching structured `cli_error`; configuration and source unchanged, cleanup confirmed. This diagnostic success demonstrates the missing feature, not a product pass. Earlier run 39968909470 failed a controller assertion expecting raw Commander wording and is not counted as passing.
- [Actual supported CLI proof](https://github.com/ly85206559/openclaw/actions/runs/40040390038/job/120709831544) on `f67de3a4e6bb10f9a924c8110c01729d85d1aab6`: canonical `pnpm build:runtime`, one-shot text/JSON, follow text/JSON, matching-channel append batches, UTF-8, a partial record held until its newline, configured secret redaction, file shrink/reset, no replay, and real SIGINT all passed. Snapshot commands exit 0; follow commands exit 130 after SIGINT. All four actual CLI stderr files are empty; configuration/source integrity and strict process/scratch cleanup are confirmed in the receipt. Raw stdout, stderr, six fixture generations, and receipt are in the job artifact.
- Final candidate `5767f1464940f1d19fb5d277a4e846fd3f57e12e` differs from that runtime-proved head only by canonical formatting of one test expression. All production, CLI, reader, and documentation bytes are identical, so the runtime proof is reused rather than replayed. [Final-head focused checks](https://github.com/ly85206559/openclaw/actions/runs/40041232491/job/120712540632) passed: 52/52 tests across command/CLI/shared-reader suites, zero skip/todo, core production and command-test types, touched typed lint, format including oxfmt/Bun parity, and tracked-source integrity. The full channel-command test file took 3.39s (test bodies about 1.25s); the three shards including cold worker preparation took 49.81s. Fresh complete-candidate P0–P3 source review found no actionable findings.

Actual follow JSON message order was `initial`, `appended é follow…7890`, `partial`, `batch one`, `batch two`, `rotated`; the other-channel and omitted initial records did not appear. The stream also emitted the initial truncation notice and the file-reset notice. No duplicate message was emitted during idle polling.

Earlier candidate runs 39974523831 and 40040390038 remain overall failures because of authored lint/format errors. Their successful runtime jobs are separate evidence, not an all-green claim; the lint and formatter corrections are included in the final candidate.

Upstream CI is **not green**: [READY run 40041801093](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40041801093) passed 36 jobs but `checks-node-changed-compact-small-14` failed in the Bun Gateway configuration suite after 300,000 ms without output. Its automatic failure table says `unknown` because the packed job name has no main counterpart. Independent log comparison found [scheduled main run 40034030350 / job 120689332895](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40034030350/job/120689332895) had already stalled in the same `server.config-patch.test.ts` flow after the same last completed case, with the same timeout and Bun policy; the test, Gateway fixture, and Vitest config blobs match. This establishes that the primary stall also exists on main, not its root cause. This PR run additionally could not verify process-group cleanup; that secondary difference is not claimed to be proven inherited. The required gate remains failed. No CI rerun or gate bypass was requested.

prs.title: improve(gateway): name which session identity changed when chat.send refuses stale storage
prs.body:
Related: #178944, #182005

## What Problem This Solves

When chat.send refuses work with "Session storage changed while starting work. Retry.", the error doesn't say what changed, so intermittent failures like the Docker live ACP bind lane in #178944 can't be diagnosed.

## User Impact

User impact: the refusal now reads "Session storage changed while starting work (agent | store key | store source). Retry.", so operators and release validation can see which session identity changed. Nothing else changes: the same requests are refused or accepted as before, and no keys or paths are exposed.

## Why This Change Was Made

#178944 describes the failure as a benign concurrent session write and asks whether to retry. The check doesn't look at row contents. It compares only the resolved agent, the store key, and the physical store identity (path, database identity, birth time). Retrying or loosening the check without knowing which identity changed could hide a routing bug, so this change makes the next occurrence explain itself instead. The check and the refused requests are unchanged; only the message names the first dimension that differs.

## Evidence

**1. Real incident path: live ACP bind lane, 5 consecutive runs on this change**

The #178944 failure came from the live ACP bind lane. That lane was itself broken on main by a stale assertion (fixed separately in #182005), so these runs use this PR's head `6e5b03e` with #182005's one-line test fix applied locally.

```
OPENCLAW_LIVE_USE_REAL_HOME=1 OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$(mktemp -d)" OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 \
OPENCLAW_LIVE_ACP_BIND=1 OPENCLAW_LIVE_ACP_BIND_AGENT=claude OPENCLAW_LIVE_ACP_BIND_CLAUDE_AUTH=subscription \
pnpm test:live -- src/gateway/gateway-acp-bind.live.test.ts
```

It starts a real Gateway and a real Claude ACP agent, with OpenClaw state in a fresh temp directory. Results:

| Run | Bind to `agent:main:acp:…` | Bound-session turns completed | Storage conflicts | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ✅ | 6 | 0 | 8 passed (8) |
| 2 | ✅ | 6 | 0 | 8 passed (8) |
| 3 | ✅ | 6 | 0 | 8 passed (8) |
| 4 | ✅ | 6 | 0 | 8 passed (8) |
| 5 | ✅ | 6 | 0 | 8 passed (8) |

Run 5:

```
[live-acp-bind] gateway websocket connected
[live-acp-bind] bind command completed
[live-acp-bind] binding announced for session agent:main:acp:c562bcab-858e-4006-ab4e-e070059618ae
[live-acp-bind] follow-up turn completed (attempt 1)
[live-acp-bind] memory recall turn completed (attempt 1)
[live-acp-bind] bound session transcript retained the previous token
[live-acp-bind] memory marker turn completed (attempt 1)
[live-acp-bind] bound session transcript contains the final marker token
[live-acp-bind] image turn completed (attempt 1)
[live-acp-bind] bound session classified the probe image
[live-acp-bind] cron mcp turn completed (attempt 1)
[live-acp-bind] cron mcp turn completed (attempt 2)
[live-acp-bind] cron mcp job live-mcp-714ce0 not observed; continuing after bind/image verification
✓ gateway live (ACP bind) > binds a synthetic Slack DM conversation to a live ACP session and reroutes the next turn
Tests  8 passed (8)
```

Every chat.send in these runs went through the changed admission check on the exact path where #178944 failed, and none was refused. The conflict did not recur. That matches the source: ordinary bound-session traffic changes rows, not the agent, store key, or physical store the check compares.

**2. Why a real conflict can't be produced on demand**

- **Agent:** the latest row is loaded through the prepared target's own agent, so this dimension compares equal to itself in normal flow.
- **Store source:** a replaced database file is caught first by an earlier guard ("Qualified session source changed during consumption").
- **Store key:** needs a session row to move from an alias key to its canonical key between preparation and admission, which only a concurrent Doctor migration of a legacy row does.
- A real Gateway with 30 `chat.send` calls each racing 4 concurrent `sessions.patch` writes produced 0 conflicts.

So the refusal is reachable only through rare interleavings like the original release-validation flake. This PR makes that next occurrence name its cause, rather than staging one artificially.

**3. Regression test** (`chat-send-admission.reads.test.ts`, run on current main)

- **Without this change:** fails. Expected `…(store key). Retry.`, received `"Error: Session storage changed while starting work. Retry."`.
- **With this change:** passes, 24/24 in the file.

**4. Control: real Gateway, no conflict path**

With this change, 15/15 `chat.send` calls (control) and 15/15 calls racing concurrent `sessions.patch` writes were accepted, with 0 conflicts and 0 conflict lines in the Gateway log. Main gives the same result with the same script (30/30).

**Checks:** `oxfmt`, `oxlint` (the file stays under its 700-line limit), `pnpm tsgo:core`, and `git diff --check` are clean.

Production delta +7/-7; test delta +24/-0.

**Merge risk:** low. Only the refusal message text changes, and nothing in the repo matches on it.

prs.title: fix: managed files open as links instead of previews
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes managed files opening as a generated Markdown link instead of their existing reader when selected from Files or Outputs.

## User Impact

Users can read supported text, Markdown, HTML, SVG and PDF files and play supported audio/video through the native file viewers. Files opened from the catalog start with navigation collapsed; the native toggle remains available. Desktop file metadata no longer forces a working preview into the download-only fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

Routes managed download grants into the existing readers and retains their permissions, cancellation, expiry and connection scope. The media owner adopts the freshly authorized grant, avoiding a second authorization request on first open. Unknown formats retain the download fallback; no new renderers or external SVG access are added.

Depends on #181903 for the shared artifact read/cancellation boundary. Files and Outputs share this reader owner.

## Evidence

- Real compiled UI, mocked Gateway: reproduced the generated-link failure through Files and Outputs before the fix; verified CSV through both entry points, mobile CSV, Markdown, HTML, JSON, SVG, PDF, MP4 and WAV afterward. PDF proof includes a visibly rendered page, not only an iframe.
- On PDF/MP4/WAV first open, the measured requests fell from two artifact authorizations plus one media GET to one authorization plus one GET. All three final compiled scenarios passed.
- 59 focused tests passed in 3.12 seconds wall time, covering close/cancellation, original download bytes, desktop/mobile routing, grant expiry, connection isolation, newer denial/pending requests, resource replacement and bounded retention. Scoped production/test types and formatting passed; lint has zero errors and two unchanged warnings.
- Independent native Codex review completed: no actionable P0–P2 findings. The reviewer inspected the frozen diff and supplied owner context; it did not rerun tests.

### Earlier Markdown timeout

[CI run 40024704510](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40024704510), `checks-ui (1/3)`, failed because the existing `markdown-streaming.test.ts` chunked-prefix parity case took 71.306 seconds against its 60-second limit; 7,880 tests passed and one was skipped. The cause of that historical timeout remains unresolved.

On Tempbook, Node 24/jsdom/forks passed the whole file (19/19; parity case 2.510 seconds) and the five-file sequence preceding it in the CI worker (94/94; parity case 2.989 seconds). These are limited comparisons, not a reproduction of the custom Bun/Linux environment. The same test passed in the Details PR CI on the same custom Bun version in 19.912 seconds. The test and relevant Markdown blobs match; the one differing relative dependency only inlines a helper. No cause or cure is established by those passing runs.

Main already contains #181856, which removes the incremental Markdown pipeline after profiling. It was not imported merely to obtain a green run. No timeout, coverage, or source change was made for this failure; no CI rerun or empty push was used. This PR remains ready for code review with this explicit CI qualification.

### Before and after

All six before captures show clean production source at main baseline `b39247716c4064ac1b478f4e3458371d5598740d`. CSV captures are from the initial baseline run; PDF, MP4, WAV and SVG were recaptured in an isolated worktree at that same commit. ### Risk and coverage

The eager text path remains limited to known sizes up to 256 KiB. Larger or unknown-size text keeps the existing reader, excerpt and download behavior; the PDF reader retains its 16 MiB limit. Playback depends on browser codec support; MP4 and WAV fixtures do not establish support for every codec. Verification uses synthetic Gateway data rather than a live user session. No full-suite or production performance benchmark claim. The temporary multi-format visual harness was used for proof and is not added to recurring CI.


### Files navigation default

Inherits the shared catalog-to-reader default from the PNG parent. Opening a file from Files collapses its tree, including after returning to the catalog with reader tabs retained. Explicit toggles remain unchanged during reader-to-reader navigation.

Six compiled UI scenarios passed with synthetic Gateway responses: PNG and CSV through Outputs, desktop Files and mobile Files. Each also returned to the catalog and opened a second file with existing tabs retained; desktop cases exercised the explicit tree toggle. The shared owner regression covers direct/preview entries, toggles and catalog reentry (50 MCP/file-panel tests, 5.62 s runner wall after the follow-up below). Independent native Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. The earlier broader consumer run passed 82 tests in 17.91 seconds runner wall across file-panel, workspace and managed-artifact suites. Production/test scoped typechecks and scoped lint passed. New-head CI timing is pending.

![Mobile second reader after catalog return](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f0825978-a14d-4d09-a5d1-a36bcb8932cb)

Before: 8ffafd62057. After: that readers head plus the exact shared default change in parent commit 4a77597e083; no reader implementation changed during this default adjustment. The earlier gallery above covers the original managed-reader repair.


### Final navigation and MCP verification

The shared default is limited to native file readers. MCP app tabs keep their existing action-retirement lifecycle. Native readers now fill their existing per-tab navigation snapshot after direct opens, so returning through a retained tab restores the saved tree choice, including an explicit open choice.

[PNG CI 40038173427](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40038173427) and [readers CI 40038228535](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40038228535) exposed the MCP sibling regression (`chat-pane-mcp-app.test.ts`, retirement called five times instead of once). It reproduced locally before the scope repair. The retained direct-tab case also failed before its navigation-snapshot repair. Afterward, all 50 MCP/file-panel tests passed in 5.62 seconds runner wall; production/test scoped types, scoped lint (zero warnings/errors), formatting and fresh independent Codex review passed. The existing MCP test was preserved. These changes do not alter the reader rendering shown in the screenshots above.

### Managed-grant HTTP authority proof

The earlier review requested proof beyond browser cache tests. A focused isolated fixture now exercised the production `artifacts.download` dispatcher and managed-media HTTP handler with synthetic profiles and ingress contexts. The same issued URL produced the following results, for both canonical and legacy artifact IDs and both full and thumbnail routes (four URL variants per row):

| Authority change | Issuing ingress | Different ingress principal | Issuing ingress again | After revocation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Session visibility | 200 | 404 | 200 | 404 |
| Profile role | 200 | 404 | 200 | 404 |

Successful full responses matched the fixture bytes. Denied responses contained only `not found`. No new authorization request was inserted between the different-principal rejection and the successful reuse of the original URL. Revocation was checked after issuance, including after the WebSocket disconnected. The test took 3.547 seconds; cold runner setup brought wall time to 83.92 seconds.

The [HTTP owner checks the current ingress against the issuing principal](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d69c018e2a6d599eb2ab0d427779d7341777dee8/src/gateway/managed-image-attachments.ts#L1256) before media lookup and revalidates the retained authority before serving bytes. The UI's prepared-grant adoption reuses the issued URL and does not replace this server check. This is issuer/HTTP-owner proof with a managed PNG fixture, not a claim that a browser or every media codec ran in that server fixture; the compiled browser reader scenarios remain the separate presentation proof above. The temporary scenario extends the existing `artifacts.prepared.test.ts` fixture and is not added to recurring CI. Tickets, private endpoints and personal data are omitted from this trace.

### Stack integration

The PNG parent is merged as `d25ac789c15a36aa89614abc5bc84e8504ecb4a8`. This PR now targets `main`; head `22f23472bbb0163730047bb851c872a6e5e8c35e` replays only the original reader delta over that squash. The stable patch ID is unchanged (`26b3ebd0f8aeee17e95fbe092ea75260c2cefc00`). The previous head's CI completed successfully; the new head has its own CI run. The navigation repair is already in the parent, and the inspected screenshots and focused proof above remain applicable.

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep public reads available during session updates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes intermittent HTTP 503 responses when a public conversation changes while an anonymous reader is loading it.

## User Impact

Readers receive the current published conversation without retrying the page. Publication revocation, transcript rewrites, conditional responses, rate limits, and concurrency limits retain their existing checks. HTML, preview cards, and shared media use the same admission owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

A committed session metadata update removed an in-flight rendered representation. The admission owner treated that invalidation as service unavailability even when the session remained public. A second invalidation window existed during the final readiness wait.

The existing admission owner now rebuilds invalidated work and owns consumption through the final synchronous publication check. Concurrent readers still share rendering; a disconnected initiator cannot cancel surviving readers. Shutdown, request cancellation, and oversized results stop work rather than rebuilding indefinitely. No schema, configuration, or dependency changes.

Production LOC delta: +40. The growth preserves current-content and publication-authority checks across both asynchronous boundaries while retaining one shared admission/cache owner; simply removing those checks would serve superseded content.

## Evidence

- Unchanged main `491b03c8751a`: the original X publication composition test failed with HTTP 503 on attempt 2 under both Node 26.12.1 and pinned Bun 1.4.4-canary.1.
- Two deterministic HTTP regressions failed with 503 on unchanged production code and pass with this repair: metadata changes during rendering and immediately before response publication.
- Focused public HTTP, chat, media, cache, reader, and admission tests pass. Admission coverage includes twenty coalesced readers, rate/capacity bounds, revocation, cancellation, and surviving a disconnected initiator. The new two-reader cancellation regression was red before its repair and is green afterward.
- Changed-file formatting/lint and `git diff --check` pass. [Exact-head CI run 40038616728](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40038616728) is green, including `checks-node-changed` (6m 06s) and `openclaw/ci-gate`. No Testbox/Crabbox lease was used.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): one cancellation finding fixed; final P0/P1/P2 review clean.
- Original X publication composition E2E: **Node 26.12.1: 50/50 passed; pinned Bun 1.4.4-canary.1: 50/50 passed**, serial shell loops on reviewed head `bf1aa6118bb8959d10c79ec299d4d4da3ada367b`. Zero failed attempts or retries; the original E2E assertion is unchanged.

This is synthetic source-composition and HTTP-boundary proof. It does not establish how often deployed Gateways encountered the error. No performance speedup is claimed.

prs.title: perf(ui): defer optional root English copy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI startup loads route subtitles, automation validation/outcome copy, and command responses before the corresponding features use them.

## User Impact

The same English copy remains available on first use while startup, Chat, and New Session transfer less JavaScript. Requests and CSS are unchanged; no new loading state, configuration, permission, or migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move 84 strings into the existing cold English registrars: 50 route subtitles, 31 automation labels/errors/outcomes, and three command responses. Each consumer registers fallback copy synchronously before translating. The canonical catalog preserves all 11,350 ordered entries and namespace object identity. No domain owner or duplicate catalog is added.

## Evidence

Prior measured head: `d457b771b0334522305577ab1dfb0d7135e60665`; measured base: `bf93c438e2fc20a5e97f4502a3b2c1220e0c1ba3`. Main was merged without replaying commits; the sole conflict was the performance budget, resolved by preserving main's tighter caps and then ratcheting from the newly measured savings.

Two production builds on the same machine use Node 24.22.1, identical fixed build metadata, and the same 29 hash-pinned plugin inputs. These are shipped sidecar bytes, not summed module diagnostics.

| Surface | JS raw bytes | JS gzip bytes | JS Brotli bytes | JS requests |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Startup | 878,044 → 873,453 | 282,747 → 281,233 (−1,514) | 257,318 → 255,928 | 7 → 7 |
| Chat | 4,102,756 → 4,098,211 | 1,269,817 → 1,268,099 (−1,718) | 1,127,193 → 1,125,842 | 20 → 20 |
| New Session | 2,491,156 → 2,486,611 | 763,598 → 761,956 (−1,642) | 683,286 → 682,081 | 16 → 16 |

CSS is identical: startup 40,195 B/1 request; Chat 137,169 B/3; New Session 100,662 B/3. The strict performance check has no warnings or violations. Startup baseline is officially ratcheted to 281,233 B; Chat/New caps preserve the previous relative headroom at 1,357,842/797,395 B. No cap is loosened.

### Cold-load proof

The predeclared rule is ten strictly alternating baseline/candidate cold-cache pairs using the committed real-Gateway workload, gzip, 240 synthetic messages, and no profiling. Both readiness medians must be ≤1.05× baseline and neither p95 may worsen. All 20 observations are retained; no extra batch was needed.

prs.title: fix: keep restored sessions unpinned unless archive is undone
prs.body:
Closes #181719

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes personal session pins reappearing when a user restores an archived session later.

## User Impact

Archiving takes effect immediately and removes the current profile's personal pin. The toast's explicit **Undo** restores both the session and its previous personal pin. Once the toast is gone, **Restore session** on the Archived page restores the session unpinned, using the existing selected sort.

## Why This Change Was Made

Personal navigation references are independent of shared session pin metadata. Confirmed archive actions remove the reference; only the Undo callback retains the previous personal pin. Its restore operation adds pins only for successful, current-profile restorations and preserves newer manual pin changes.

Other profiles, rail shortcuts, shared-pin behavior, and sorting remain unchanged. No archive delay, new persistent state, or retrospective preference rewrite is introduced.

## Evidence

- Real Control UI with the repository's mocked Gateway: header and Sessions-page Undo restore the personal pin; after the toast expires, Restore from the Archived page leaves it unpinned.
- Both Undo browser cases failed on the preceding implementation and passed with the correction. The original main reproduction of ordinary restoration re-pinning the session remains documented below.
- Owner suites: 68 passed (5.75s combined wall). The final archive-owner file passed 14 tests in 5.42s wall; it covers rejected restore, profile retirement, newer manual pin/unpin, preserved rail references, and partial batch Undo.
- Browser suite: all ten cases passed across full and focused runs. The final Archived-page case took 2.201s test time and 35.47s wall including the shared production build.
- UI and affected test typechecks, targeted lint and formatting passed. Independent review found no additional P0–P2 defects in the working-tree correction.
- Broad CI is bound to the pushed head. The earlier full local changed-check was not green because of unused exports in unchanged scripts; no baselines were changed.

Main before the fix: ordinary restoration brings the session back under Pinned.

![Main before: ordinary restore re-pins](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/512410e0-4770-474e-9781-b0f95edff050)

After: restoration from Archived after the toast expires leaves the session unpinned.

![After: later Restore stays unpinned](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/38e3b0b8-b712-4f84-a6b6-e2bf456feb52)

Explicit Undo before this correction (original PR head `d3b7850c58f3`): the personal pin was lost.

![Before: Undo lost the personal pin](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f5a341c9-735d-4d03-aa7a-26e8ca2885d5)

Explicit Undo after this correction restores the personal pin.

![After: Undo restores the pin](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff185779-c6f2-4949-b57d-bbe05e9f3c81)

prs.title: fix(doctor): bound the state content-version wait and restart the Gateway Doctor stopped
prs.body:
Refs #181490

## What Problem This Solves

Follow-up `openclaw doctor --fix` can spend hours preserving original state without a total capture budget after stopping the managed Gateway, and an interrupted restoration failure can omit the command needed to bring it back.

## User Impact

Standalone Doctor cancels its original-state capture after ten minutes, waits for that work to settle, and continues through the existing warning path with backup and retry advice. Repair-specific migration backups still apply. When restoring a Gateway Doctor stopped fails, Doctor prints the failure and `openclaw gateway start` recovery instructions before releasing its exit gate.

## Why This Change Was Made

The 2026.10.6 (`fe06181`) call chain is `createUpdateRunAdmissionReader` → `readCurrentOpenClawStateDatabaseContentVersion` → `readAdmittedStateContentVersion` → `readSqliteSourceContentVersionSync` → the `content-version` child. The equality check selects cached ledger rows; it does not poll until a revision matches or until a WAL checkpoint completes. The hash includes the DB, WAL and rollback journal; SHM is excluded. A stable non-empty WAL does not itself make the hash unstable.

Repeated per-path capture admission checks can launch a new hashing child each time in that release. Main already fixes the repeated work in [770caeb414f7 / #169905](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/770caeb414f77741ac71df389e94d64997e9b923) (retain the repair scope) and [206f1f1fdf97 / #170934](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/206f1f1fdf97ebcdc22651e148b39be9404b2fd8) (reuse the hash while DB/WAL/journal metadata is unchanged). Both fixes are absent from the 10.6 ancestry. The process samples alone do not establish an infinite convergence loop.

This change adds the missing total capture budget at its existing owner, `preserveDoctorOriginalState`. The budget uses the existing slow-hardware Doctor measurement (258 seconds, doubled and rounded up), with synchronous deadline checks as well as an abort signal for awaited workers. It does not race cleanup against a timeout promise. Main already restores on capture interruption in the synthetic service proof; this PR also guarantees visible recovery advice when that restoration throws. The older restoration mechanism is present in 10.6 too; the exact native launchd failure from the report remains unreproduced. No change to launchd authority or activation policy is claimed.

For affected 10.6 users: interrupt the stalled follow-up Doctor, run `openclaw gateway start`, and defer that follow-up pass until using a version containing the main fixes. Keep the databases, WALs and retained recovery evidence intact.

Thanks @kenrohde for the process samples and the separate interrupted-Gateway report.

## Evidence

- Node 26.12.1. Deadline regression failed before the fix because no timeout warning was returned; interrupted restart-failure regression failed because stderr contained only the interruption notice and no start command.
- Final frozen Node run: both changed files passed all 49 tests, with 226 ms of settlement tests and 1,548 ms of capture tests. The original single-file wall times were 34.22 seconds for settlement and 24.79 seconds for capture; shared transform/build preparation dominated. Both synchronous-admission and awaited-worker deadline cases pass, along with successful and failed SIGINT restoration.
- Isolated live state and HOME, named profile and free port: `pnpm openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` started with a crash-retained 4,152-byte WAL and completed with exit 0 in 166.18 seconds including runtime build and artifact-lock waits. The row committed in the WAL remained readable afterward. The runtime build reported 78.7 seconds.
- Live proof warnings: this host's group-writable volume ancestor prevents original-capture staging; the synthetic installation has no configured model context. Doctor reported both warnings and completed. Native launchd restart is covered by service-boundary fixtures, not by changing an operator service.
- Pre-change baseline `doctor-maintenance.continuation-scope.test.ts` also fails at the volume's SQLite staging-ancestor policy, followed by the fixture's non-default-home restoration refusal. No filesystem permissions or safety guards were changed.
- Final Codex autoreview: scoped clean at P0–P2. Core and Doctor test typechecks, touched-file oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Madge: zero import cycles.
- Full `check:changed` SQLite inventory skipped under the campaign's local gate budget; PR CI remains the broad proof. No remote lease was used.

Final importer selection: 60 basename matches, 58 unique files, run on Node with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <selected files> --maxWorkers=1` and isolated HOME/state. Frozen source verification completed: **646 passed, 10 failed, 7 skipped**, 1,214.89 seconds wall including preparation. The changed files account for 49 passing tests. The broader run is not green.

Observed failures outside this diff:

- `doctor-health.fleet-preflight.test.ts` (2), `doctor-maintenance.continuation-scope.test.ts` (1), `doctor-migration-preservation.test.ts` (1), and `doctor-rehearsal-capture.test.ts` (1): original capture is unavailable because the volume ancestor is group-writable. The continuation-scope failure was reproduced before editing.
- `openclaw-state-maintenance-resources.test.ts` (2): the final response has `dataText: ""` instead of `"finite capture response"`. Both Doctor and the plain Gateway-lock producer fail; the latter bypasses the changed Doctor code. The likely separate race is that the unchanged response-capture owner can finalize a pending clone before the fixture's EOF notification has published the body.
- `install.definition-repair.test.ts` (3): unchanged service owners return `ServiceInspectionError` instead of `service-authority-revoked/recovery-pending`, and retain LaunchAgent values 20/1 instead of expected 330/10. These cases call the unchanged service repair/restoration owners directly.

Pre-existing slow case: `doctor.runs-legacy-state-migrations-yes-mode-without.e2e.test.ts` → `runs legacy state migrations in yes mode without prompting`: 37.698 seconds; full file 63.649 seconds of tests. Its fixture resets modules and prepares the full real Doctor contribution graph before each case, then runs Doctor. Recorded for the existing tooling/fixture follow-up; no test timeout, retry, skip, assertion or baseline was changed. PR CI remains the broad authority.

Simplification: the capture and restoration owners remain unchanged; no new manager, worker protocol, config, CLI option, schema or dependency. Production +35/-11 lines (net +24), tests +65/-1 (net +64), docs +7.

prs.title: fix(codex): queue inference roots at capacity instead of failing turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With the Codex app-server harness, a Gateway running many agent turns at once failed them outright: `Codex parent-local inference root limit reached`, logged as "Codex agent harness failed; not falling back to embedded OpenClaw backend". One physical inference transport allows 64 active inference roots. When subagent fleets pushed concurrent Codex turns past that, every extra turn failed immediately. Parents saw failed children and had to spend replacement attempts on them, and fleets with a tight replacement budget ended incomplete. A capacity spike became task failure.

## User Impact

Additional Codex turns wait in arrival order when all 64 inference roots are active and start when capacity is released. Cancellation and transport shutdown end waiting turns. The resource limit stays at 64; no new configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Root cause

`createCodexInferenceContext().register()` (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/inference-context.ts`) threw synchronously when a new thread arrived and `roots.size >= MAX_ACTIVE_ROOTS`. Roots are not leaked: normal turn cleanup, startup cleanup and abort all release them, and a parent that yields with `sessions_yield` completes its turn and frees its root while children run. So the failures were pure concurrency against a bound that was enforced by failing, not by waiting.

### Fix

Registration (and side-question `fork`) is now async and queues FIFO at capacity. `release()` drains waiters into freed roots, and admission re-validates the transport, the turn's abort signal and turn ownership at admit time. An aborted waiter leaves the queue without taking a root, and closing the transport rejects every waiter. `MAX_ACTIVE_ROOTS` stays as the resource bound, with no new config. A debug log names the limit and the queue depth so a long wait is diagnosable. The two production callers await registration. The Codex harness doc describes the behavior.

Accepted edge case: a turn that waits in-turn for its own children (for example, Swarm collection inside one Code Mode script) keeps its root while it waits. If 64 such turns held every root while their children all queued, the children would wait until run timeouts or aborts free a root. Yielding parents don't hold roots, and this shape needs 64 simultaneous in-turn orchestrators on one transport, so it isn't coded around.

## Evidence

- New `inference-context.capacity.test.ts`, red on base (5 failed with `Codex parent-local inference root limit reached`) and green with the fix (5 passed, twice): at capacity the next registration waits and proceeds when a root releases, an aborted waiter leaves without consuming a root, and a closed transport rejects waiters. The Codex inference-context, inference-proxy (http, model-policy, capacity, native), shared-client, run-attempt, settlement, side-question and provider-review suites pass: 418 and 263 tests across two groups.
- Live A/B on a Crabbox AWS host with the Codex app-server harness (Codex, `agentRuntime.id: "codex"`), 12 concurrent fleet parents × 8 children on one Gateway:
  - main: 33 child turns failed with the root-limit error (33 lane errors). Parents recovered only by spending replacements.
  - this branch: 0 root-limit failures, 0 lane errors. 12/12 fleets finished every module in the same 442 s window.
- The worker's targeted tsgo typecheck could not run locally because generated SDK declarations were missing, so PR CI covers typecheck.
- Landing follow-up: the first CI run found two typed-lint errors in the new promise rejections. Commit `0e19056165f` uses the existing SDK `toErrorObject` helper to preserve Error instances and normalize other rejection values. Targeted typed lint and all five capacity tests pass after the repair; independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.

prs.title: fix: open generated images directly from Outputs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes generated images opening as a Markdown heading and an “Open artifact” link when selected in Outputs or Files.

## User Impact

Images open directly in the existing image viewer, with Copy, Download and expansion. Files opened from the catalog start with Files navigation collapsed; the toggle remains available and explicit choices persist while file tabs remain open. Closing or replacing a pending preview cancels its image transfer; retained background tabs can finish loading.

## Why This Change Was Made

Managed image downloads return an authorized media URL. The workspace reader handled inline bytes but treated that URL as a generic link. It now reads the image through the existing media owner before selecting the existing image renderer. Each explicit download still reauthorizes access before using cached bytes; the preview retains image data rather than an expiring grant.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the incorrect Markdown screen on main `b39247716c4` through the compiled Control UI and its real Outputs action, using synthetic Gateway responses and an actual PNG.
- The same compiled flow passes with decoded image content, byte-identical download, native lightbox, denied download after access revocation, and cancellation when closing the tab during a held image fetch. Test time: **2.27 s**. CI timing pending.
- **50 focused tests passed** (7.82 s runner wall); the final artifact suite passed **11 tests** (2.85 s runner wall). The cancellation regression fails without the owner signal. Retained background loading, existing text/binary handling and source identity remain covered.
- UI-chat typecheck, scoped lint, formatting and independent Codex review passed (no P0–P2 findings).
- Simplification: reuse the existing image loader/viewer and workspace lifecycle; no new renderer, URL fetch policy or cache. Production delta: +71/−14; test delta: +222/−1.

**Risk and coverage:** the original long delay was not reproduced. Local synthetic cold openings were 327 ms for the incorrect screen and 258–344 ms for the decoded image; these observations are not a speedup claim. This proof uses a mocked Gateway with the real compiled UI, not the original private session. Other file-format reader defects are tracked separately.

Before:

![Before: generated image opens as a Markdown link](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f081c5f0-f79b-4277-8c19-9b88cfc70fdf)

After:

![After: generated image opens in the native image viewer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fc2ba6ac-5ef2-4c0f-8a54-18ee1d0467db)


### File navigation default

The shared preview owner collapses the tree when entering a reader from the catalog, retaining the catalog navigation for returning to Files. It preserves explicit toggles across later file opens without introducing another preference or renderer.

- Regression failed before the change because the first reader kept the tree open. Both preview and direct-open cases now pass, including explicit toggles, return to the catalog and opening another file with tabs retained; 50 MCP/file-panel tests passed in 5.62 seconds runner wall after the follow-up below. New-head CI timing is pending.
- Real compiled Control UI with synthetic Gateway data: PNG opens through desktop Outputs, desktop Files and mobile Files. Desktop readers start collapsed and the native toggle reveals the tree.
- Independent native Codex review of the default change completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. Production/test scoped typechecks and scoped lint passed on the existing readers checkout with the identical shared patch; the newly created PNG checkout uses linked dependencies and was not used to claim those static checks.
- Six compiled scenarios across PNG/CSV, Outputs/Files and desktop/mobile also proved returning to the catalog and opening a second file with tabs retained. The earlier broader consumer run passed 82 tests in 17.91 seconds runner wall across file-panel, workspace and managed-artifact suites.

| First image open | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Outputs | ![Before: Files navigation open](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/87aaf3ca-722e-4d26-b7c8-70a0a969c217) | ![After: image reader with Files navigation collapsed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/957c8d13-94ec-43fe-bcf3-401450221e23) |

The before capture uses child head 8ffafd62057, which includes the unchanged PNG fix; the after capture uses that readers head plus the exact shared default change in PNG commit 4a77597e083. The earlier image-reader gallery above demonstrates the original generated-link fix.


### Final navigation and MCP verification

The shared default is limited to native file readers. MCP app tabs keep their existing action-retirement lifecycle. Native readers now fill their existing per-tab navigation snapshot after direct opens, so returning through a retained tab restores the saved tree choice, including an explicit open choice.

[PNG CI 40038173427](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40038173427) and [readers CI 40038228535](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40038228535) exposed the MCP sibling regression (`chat-pane-mcp-app.test.ts`, retirement called five times instead of once). It reproduced locally before the scope repair. The retained direct-tab case also failed before its navigation-snapshot repair. Afterward, all 50 MCP/file-panel tests passed in 5.62 seconds runner wall; production/test scoped types, scoped lint (zero warnings/errors), formatting and fresh independent Codex review passed. The existing MCP test was preserved. These changes do not alter the reader rendering shown in the screenshots above.

prs.title: fix(agents): creating an agent fails with UNAVAILABLE on PostgreSQL state
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Creating an agent through a Gateway whose shared `state` family uses PostgreSQL fails with `UNAVAILABLE: PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker; only synchronous admission, migrations, and CLI one-shots may run on the main thread`. The same operation succeeds with SQLite state.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the current recovery-hold recheck inside the existing synchronous engine admission and reuse it for agent creation and workspace-file mutations. Filesystem effects remain outside that admission. Move PostgreSQL cron-owner/schema inspection into the existing cron read worker, reusing its current schema assertion and Doctor inventory query instead of opening PostgreSQL on the Gateway thread.

## User Impact

A PostgreSQL-state Gateway can create an agent normally. Recovery holds still block unsafe publication, unrelated Gateway-thread SQL remains refused, and SQLite behavior stays supported. No schema, migration, storage-format, configuration-default, or plugin-SDK changes.

## Evidence

Built and installed separate current-main and candidate Linux packages. Provisioned disposable PostgreSQL 18.6 with `vector` 0.8.7, `unaccent` 1.1, and `pg_trgm` 1.6 on a task-only Docker network. The Gateway uses an ordinary non-superuser runtime role. Each fresh profile selects PostgreSQL only for `database.families.state`, with SQLite as the default for other families and a unique PostgreSQL schema prefix.

Persisted config through shipped `config set` commands, initialized application state with shipped `setup` and `doctor --fix --non-interactive`, then called public `gateway call agents.create` with `onboarding:false` and an isolated helper workspace. No application SQL inserts, injected recovery receipts, held SQL locks, or model calls in this operator-flow proof.

Main reproduced twice: `agents.create` returns the PostgreSQL main-thread `UNAVAILABLE`; config bytes remain unchanged; no helper workspace or agent directory appears; `agents.list` after a Gateway restart still has no helper. The SQLite baseline control creates helper and retains it across restart.

Candidate reproduced twice: creation returns `ok:true`, creates the helper workspace/agent directory, publishes the generated config entry, and lists helper after a stop/start of the built Gateway. Both SQLite controls also create and retain helper. [Inspectable CLI/RPC receipts, config hashes, filesystem checks, and restart rosters](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181676#issuecomment-6376528320).

Focused checks passed: four PostgreSQL/SQLite hold/cron-owner boundary regressions and 62 direct agent-create, workspace-worker, integration, and cron-schema tests. Oxfmt/Oxlint passed. The conformance test preflight required its administrative test connection for `track_functions`; the public Gateway proof continued to use the restricted runtime role.

Simplification retains one recovery predicate owner and one cron worker. Owner inspection preserves the independently authoritative SQL `agent_id` even when legacy JSON omits it; generic job inventory does not return that column. Distinct schema-only and owner requests preserve those existing contracts without a duplicate query owner. Production +78/-14; tests/support +282/-0; test registration tooling +6/-0; docs +6/-0.

An existing `Cron maintenance failed: Agent database resources are closing` warning appears in the baseline SQLite control as well as the candidate PostgreSQL flow; it is not claimed fixed here.

Merge danger: two-way door; a revert restores the admission failure without changing database formats. Agents created successfully remain ordinary configured agents after a revert. Blast radius is recovery-hold rechecks around agent/workspace publication and PostgreSQL cron read placement.
