prs.title: fix(database): rebuild memory indexes before agent ports return
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #181859. Porting an agent store discarded its embedding cache and left the memory index empty, so the first search rebuilt the corpus and repeated embedding calls. Thanks @etzelm for the report.

## User Impact

Agent-family ports preserve cached embeddings and rebuild memory before returning, while the Gateway remains stopped. Text output and `--json` report each agent's result. A failed rebuild warns with `openclaw memory index --agent <id>` and leaves the published port successful. Unchanged cached chunks need no embedding calls; new or uncached content retains normal indexing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing docs explicitly reserved this post-port hook. The port now retains the cache's provider/model/provider_key/hash identities and binary payload, then releases port custody before acquiring a fresh configured `memory.cli` owner. The selected memory plugin owns indexing. Fresh config loading avoids the pre-port runtime snapshot, and per-agent secret resolution prevents an unavailable peer credential from blocking healthy agents. Retained stores outside active configuration receive recovery guidance rather than opening a different store.

No new CLI options, configuration, SDK contract, schema, or Gateway-startup rebuild is introduced. Both pending-hook documentation passages are updated.

## Evidence

Baseline pin: `ddbf65c9215087e7e1d10164021d8bcad7514cad`, including #181860 and #181957. The local deterministic provider uses no paid API. The fixture contains 4,857 chunks (1,000 memory / 3,857 sessions), 60 sources and a full 1,536-dimensional embedding cache.

On main, the first PostgreSQL search took 23.778s and embedded 4,857 corpus chunks plus its query; the next search took 3.634s and embedded only its query. Both port directions dropped the cache; rebuilding reproduced identical cache identities and bytes. A cached full PostgreSQL rebuild still took 20.158s with zero embedding calls and 4,001 top-level statements / 12.984s server execution. This does not reproduce or partition the reporter's historical 1,376.9s latency.

The cache round-trip regression is red under main's omission policy and green with this fix. All 15 focused command tests, source and touched-test TSRS checks, lint, the native line-cap guard, docs sanity, and independent P0–P3 review pass. Tests cover fresh post-port ownership/configuration, custody through close, isolated rebuild/close/dirty-state failures, retained-path selection and per-agent SecretRefs.

Clean-tree real CLI replay passes the pre-registered acceptance rule on `cf88eb38a3637f2af4198ae8d1c52ddb96ec6d7c`:

prs.title: fix(claude-cli): subagent completions reset the Claude session and lose context
prs.body:
Closes #178953

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a `claude-cli` session started from the Control UI loses its native session, and most of its context, whenever a subagent completion or a channel turn runs in it.

## User Impact

Agents that delegate to subagents keep their Claude session across completion announcements and the client turns that follow, instead of being reseeded from saved history each time. Other tool-name changes still start a fresh session, as before.

Upgrade caveat: an existing binding can reset once when its tool fingerprint changes. The latest-stable-to-development-head test below preserved saved messages and settings, but native context was not transferred automatically; the original conversation remained readable through the history tool.

## Why This Change Was Made

`screen`, `show_widget`, `suggest_task` and `dismiss_task` exist only when the turn's client provides them (Control UI caps, gateway task delivery). Turns with no client drop them, and since #176577 that changes `promptToolNamesHash` and invalidates session reuse with `prompt-tools`. These four names are now left out of that hash.

The stale-catalog problem #176577 guards against does not return for these tools. They are still listed in the system prompt, so a change restarts a warm process through the live fingerprint's system prompt hash. A resumed Claude CLI process then lists the current MCP tools (see Evidence). A call to one of them on a turn that doesn't serve it gets `Tool not available` from the loopback bridge, because each turn's grant still filters `tools/list` and `tools/call`.

The docs for `prompt-tools` resets now name the excluded tools.

## Evidence

### Real Gateway + Claude CLI flow (stock versus this head)

[Redacted native stdout, reset events, upgrade transcript, and test setup](https://gist.github.com/Marvinthebored/fca5ca0aaa94e34912564dfce6a775fb). Real Anthropic calls through Claude Code 2.1.305; no mocked provider. A signed Control UI WebSocket client supplied `ui-commands,inline-widgets`, native `sessions_spawn` created real children, and real child settlement delivered completion turns. This validates the server/runtime flow, not browser rendering.

| Build | Control UI → real child completion → Control UI | Actual current catalog |
|---|---|---|
| Stock parent `fd8cd75f96d` | `e68f6fd9…` → `47e65689…` → `e68f6fd9…` | 48 → 46 → 48 tools |
| PR head `6cb5f16fe18` | `84306e78…` → `84306e78…` → `84306e78…` | 48 → 46 → 48 tools |

- Stock logs `cli session reset: provider=claude-cli reason=prompt-tools` on completion. Its returning UI turn remembers the initial nonce but explicitly cannot see the child completion: native context is split across the two sessions.
- Patched: the real completion recalls the original `SATURN-CEDAR-178955`; the final UI turn recalls it without tools/history. All three phases retain the exact same native session UUID.
- Actual Claude initialization records show `screen` and `show_widget` present on UI turns, absent on completion, and restored afterward. Thus the resumed process receives the current catalog; this is not just a model self-report.
- Separate fresh scratch states, canonical temporary paths, distinct port, `env -i`, and launchd label `ai.openclaw.scratchproof`. Production launchd PID remained unchanged before/after. Both runtime builds exited 0.

### Latest-stable persisted-data compatibility

- Installed exact latest-stable npm package `openclaw@2026.10.6` (`fe06181`), created a real Claude conversation and assistant reply, and saved a session label and `low` thinking setting.
- Stopped stable and upgraded the **same state directory** to this PR head. Standard `doctor --fix` performed the intervening upstream migrations (state schema 20→29; agent schema 25→31), with automatic pre-migration backups. This patch adds no schema migration.
- The original session ID, both pre-upgrade messages, label, and thinking setting loaded. A real Claude `sessions_history` call retrieved the pre-upgrade nonce and returned `QUARTZ-ORBIT-178955`.
- **Limit:** this proves persisted-data loading and use, not uninterrupted native identity across upgrade. The first upgraded turn reset with `prompt-tools`; automatic old-nonce recall failed when native-auth history reseeding was unavailable. Saved history remained intact and tool-readable. The attached transcript includes the failed automatic-recall turn as well as successful history recovery.

### Focused regression and existing checks

- `keeps the Claude session across Control UI turns and caller-less completion turns` in `prepare.completion-tools.test.ts` fails on main with `prompt-tools` and passes patched. It also asserts that exactly the four excluded caller-surface tools differ and that the system prompt still changes.
- Touched suites: `prepare.completion-tools`, `prepare.existing-session`, `prepare`, `cli-session`, and `prepare.configured-mcp`: 187 passed in 5 files.
- Previously recorded targeted production typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed; exact-head CI is green.
- Earlier separate stdio MCP resume checks also observed new tools after resume, including deferred `ToolSearch`. The Gateway trace above now exercises the actual changed flow.

This change was written with AI assistance (Claude Code) and adversarially reviewed by two models (Claude and Codex) before filing.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: fix: recognize retained updater exports in dead-code analysis
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes CI dead-code analysis reporting a published updater recovery export as unused even though the canonical compatibility inventory still consumes that exact source surface.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible or runtime change. Maintainers can keep enforcing zero unexplained exports without deleting a binding that supported upgrades still need or exempting unrelated findings. Inventory contents, updater recovery behavior, package and SDK surfaces, dependencies, and configuration semantics remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing root-manifest JSON compiler already owns analyzer-only consumers that package metadata cannot express directly. It now reads the validated updater compatibility inventory, deduplicates its recorded source bindings, and uses the existing module graph to distinguish real named exports from private imported lexical bindings.

Real recorded named surfaces become exact named imports from their recorded modules with deterministic unique aliases. Private imported bindings are accepted only when their real source import resolves to a current named declaration owner; they do not become fabricated imports. Unknown or ambiguous source shapes continue to fail configuration. One native parser and module graph serve each compilation and are disposed on both success and error.

The focused config test covers the retained recovery facade, duplicate exported names, all current private-binding controls, and rejection of an unresolved recorded binding. Existing updater external-binding tests continue to protect the published recovery path.

## Evidence

The exact candidate tree passed remote changed-file formatting and lint, every selected type graph, the changed config suite (15/15, measured with one worker), and the updater external-binding controls (20/20).

`pnpm deadcode:exports` no longer reports any recorded updater surface, including the recovery facade. It still exits nonzero and reports every unrelated hard-zero finding: 6 script, 15 production, and 12 full-tree rows. This demonstrates a precise analyzer edge rather than a whole-file root, ignore rule, or false green scan.

The unchanged inventory's registry-freshness command separately reports newly published versions that are not present in this frozen source snapshot. This PR does not update release inventory; canonical inventory parsing and the analyzer behavior above passed.

Exact-head hosted CI passed the required gate and all selected analyzer, changed-test, lint, type, source-contract, boundary, guard, security, package, and baseline-ratchet rows. Full calibrated review concluded clean and called this the best fix. Separate canonical Codex autoreview completed both intact-context passes through P2 with no findings.

## What Problem This Solves

Installed native plugin interfaces still require a separate Labs opt-in even though the same infrastructure already serves bundled plugins.

## User Impact

Enabled user-installed plugins can show native UI by default, without a Labs detour. Existing explicit `gateway.controlUi.experimental.customPlugins: false` values remain off; there is no new configuration key or migration.

**Upgrade behavior:** when the key is omitted, already-enabled plugins may begin loading their native browser UI after upgrading. Native UI is trusted, unsandboxed code running with each signed-in viewer's Gateway permissions. Existing authentication, scope, provenance, asset grants, and lifecycle checks remain unchanged.

Install surfaces explain that plugins may include browser code; installed details and existing enable reviews identify native UI from the inspected manifest. No extra modal, checkbox, or permission gate is added. All plugin APIs retain their existing experimental API-stability policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move browser-execution disclosure to ordinary plugin installation and enablement instead of hiding the whole capability behind Labs. Keep the existing advanced opt-out for compatibility, and share the effective default between admission and browser refresh notifications. prs.title: ci: qualify PostgreSQL 17 daily on main
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL 17 conformance is path-selected in PR CI and skipped on main pushes. A change outside those paths can break the integrated PostgreSQL behavior without a daily signal; the existing weekly qualification covers only PostgreSQL 16 and 18.

## User Impact

Maintainers get daily PostgreSQL 17 qualification on main. Failed scheduled jobs are visible in Actions, with no new notifications or secrets. PR CI selection is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing workflow as PostgreSQL Scheduled Qualification: PG17 at 07:17 UTC daily, the existing PG16/18 run at 06:43 UTC Monday, and manual `versions=all|pg16|pg17|pg18` (default `all`). Reuse the shared conformance action and PR CI's pinned PG17 image. Keep the main/repository guard, three shards, max-parallel 3, fail-fast false, and 50-minute timeout rationale.

Expected added daily cost: 3 shards × approximately 25 minutes = approximately 75 hosted runner-minutes. The weekly run remains six jobs. A short matrix expression avoids adding another workflow or planning job; removing the static include rows prevents unselected versions from creating extra jobs.

## Evidence

- The regression failed against the original workflow because it lacked the daily trigger, then passed with the fix.
- All 32 PostgreSQL workflow selection tests passed, covering both schedules, all four manual choices, main-only admission, shard preservation, and image selection/parity.
- Repository workflow lint passed, including pinned actionlint, zizmor, and workflow guards; `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Codex autoreview: clean through P2.
- Broader workflow structure tests passed: 793 passed, 8 skipped across the planning and guard suites (306.37s wall time). Focused lint and the tooling test typecheck passed.
- Rebased onto current main. Required PR CI passed on `a192a14a1815e7d381c50a4ec628a03a67e5b128` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40034485973)); its path-selected PG job was skipped.
- The initial unsharded local run hit PostgreSQL's default 100-connection ceiling in a Doctor rollback case and a memory-suite cleanup timeout. The CI-layout local attempt then encountered PostgreSQL server-side `Interrupted system call` file-open failures across unrelated tests and was stopped. No connection limit or assertions were relaxed. Full conformance passed on an isolated Linux Blacksmith Testbox with the exact pinned PG17 image: 1,143 tests passed, 37 skipped across all eight groups; test runtime 19m18s, total remote runtime 22m11s ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40036279160), wrapper exit 0). The lease was stopped. The local host failures remain recorded; no product fix is claimed for them. After merge, manual `versions=pg17` dispatch [40038700528](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40038700528) passed on merge commit `b3e994d25865d4cce44f76e48da61aa9d2f7e331`: shard 1/3 19m05s, shard 2/3 16m25s, shard 3/3 11m22s (46m52s combined job time). Exactly three PG17 jobs ran; no PG16/18 jobs were added.

Scope: 3 files; workflow +13/-8 lines, documentation +9/-5, tests +47/-11. The necessary growth adds trigger selection and protects its behavior in the existing test owner.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A completed answer can show only “Worked” above its activity while still showing “Done in 13 seconds” below the answer after session metadata advances to another run.

## User Impact

The existing Worked disclosure keeps the known duration for its own run. The footer keeps output tokens without repeating that duration; answers without a matching Worked disclosure retain their footer timing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the terminal recap already associated with the answer's run when the session no longer carries that run's timing. This changes presentation only: no transcript rewriting, timestamp estimates, new state, or grouping changes. Production delta: +26 lines; tests add 73 lines for the lifecycle boundary, token display, and zero-runtime case.

## Evidence

- Reproduced in the compiled Control UI against synthetic Gateway events on main d90c4d0e729: the regression fails with “Worked”; the candidate preserves “Worked for 13 seconds”, keeps 42 output tokens, and survives reload.
- Chat lifecycle browser suite: 16/16 passed, 44.16 seconds; the changed scenario took 1.816 seconds. After the final zero-runtime guard, the affected browser scenario passed again (19.91 seconds including setup). This exercises actual WebSocket delivery, session reconciliation, rendering, and reload. CI timing is pending.
- Duration, message, and recap tests: 62/62 passed, 1.56 seconds, including unavailable metadata, independent runs, and session/agent/connection changes.
- UI and chat E2E TypeScript checks, focused lint/format, and diff checks passed. Independent Codex review completed. The zero-runtime finding is fixed and protected by an 87 ms regression; no other P0–P2 findings.

Before (main, same synthetic scenario):

![Before: Worked has no duration; the footer shows 42 output tokens and Done in 13 seconds](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bf3ec07a-67df-4b0a-a281-9ce78f2a54a7)

After (0303124763d):

![After: Worked for 13 seconds; the footer retains 42 output tokens](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f3c30862-fd9c-41ca-8970-37a9caf98ba9)

## Risk and coverage

Historical work without matching lifecycle facts remains untimed. Zero runtime keeps the existing footer duration because Worked cannot format it. prs.title: fix(gateway): add restart guidance to replayed settle wakes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a Gateway restart interrupted a requester's settle-wake turn (the cohort wake after `sessions_yield`), recovery replayed the owed wake, which is correct because the turn never finished. But the replay carried none of the restart guidance that other recovered turns get ("Your previous turn was interrupted by a gateway restart … Verify what happened before repeating an action"). Models saw the identical settle input again with no explanation; on the Codex runtime it came after Codex's own `<turn_aborted> The user interrupted the previous turn on purpose`. They reported "duplicate completion deliveries" and had nothing telling them to verify side effects before repeating them.

On the Codex runtime, these replays also logged `failed to mirror codex app-server prompt at turn start error="native prompt annotation conflicts with recorded provenance"`, so the replayed wake prompt was not mirrored into the OpenClaw transcript.

## User Impact

Interrupted settle wakes now explain the Gateway restart and tell the agent to verify previous actions before repeating them. Codex replay prompts are mirrored into the OpenClaw transcript while the admitted input and replay identity stay unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Root cause

1. The wake dispatcher reuses the stable `announce:requester-settle:…` run ID and sets `settleWakeReplay` on both the initial dispatch and the replay. Nothing on that path recorded whether this exact input had outlived its Gateway execution, so preparation had no fact to attach a notice from.
2. A replay starts a new native Codex turn for the same admitted input. The transcript annotation owner (`src/sessions/user-turn-transcript-annotation-message.ts`) rejected the new native turn ID as conflicting with the previous attempt's annotation, even though run, origin and content were identical.

### Fix

- The pending-input owner (`session-accessor.pending-inputs.ts`) now reports `interruptedByRestart` on the staged receipt when the input was staged by an earlier Gateway lifecycle, was committed by an attempt that never recorded an outcome, or previously stopped for a restart. Gateway turn preparation (`agent-run-user-turn.ts`) reads that fact for a settle-wake replay and adds the canonical `RESTART_RECOVERY_INTERRUPTION_NOTE` as a turn-local runtime-instruction fragment. That keeps it out of the system prompt and the provider prefix, and leaves the settle content and replay identity unchanged. Embedded and Codex both consume that runtime context.
- The annotation owner allows a validated replacement of its own previous attempt: same run, same mirror origin, matching content fingerprint. All other conflicts still throw.
- `docs/gateway/restart-recovery.md` documents both behaviors.

Accepted edge case: a same-lifecycle re-dispatch of the same idempotency key without a recorded outcome would also be labeled restart-interrupted. Retry wakes use distinct keys, so this is not coded around.

## Evidence

- Regressions, red on base and green twice with the fix: a real Gateway restart replay through the server settle-replay harness (base: 1 failed / 18 passed; fixed: 19 passed), input recovery (2 failed / 14 → 16 passed), and Codex transcript mirroring (1 failed / 4 → 5 passed). Normal (non-restart) settle wakes get no notice. The main-session recovery (193), child recovery (85) and `agent-tools.prefix-stability` (8) suites pass.
- Live on a Crabbox AWS host with the Codex app-server harness and real OpenAI models. Nested fleets (director → 2 leads → 4 sub-leads → 8 workers), with the Gateway killed `-9` at +120 s while sub-lead settle wakes were running:
  - main: 0 of the interrupted settle-wake replays carried a restart notice; 8–12 mirror-conflict warnings per run; directors reported "duplicate completion deliveries".
  - this branch, 2 runs × 3 fleets: 16 of 16 interrupted settle-wake rollouts carry the restart notice after the abort, 0 mirror conflicts, all 6 fleets 35/35, 0 lane errors. Directors now report "Gateway-restart completion replays recovered without repeated mutations".
  - The first version of this fix passed its fixtures but did not take effect live because it keyed off session-entry status. That's why the decision now comes from the pending-input owner's own record.

prs.title: refactor: consolidate measured error and plugin clone owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Measured clone clusters still repeated small error envelopes, cleanup loops, diagnostic preparation, and type vocabularies across production owners. Those copies could drift independently.

## What changed

Consolidate the matching paths at their existing owners: Gateway error responses and forbidden-session errors; synchronous cleanup failure collection; session interruption error envelopes; execution observation fields and media-kind vocabulary; read-only reader registration; Doctor and CLI diagnostics; and plugin-local Feishu, Google Meet, xAI, and Teams operations.

All bundled-plugin sharing stays inside each plugin. No new Plugin SDK contract, persisted shape, config option, protocol field, dependency, or feature is introduced. Phase E is untouched. Existing security checks, cancellation authority, FIFO ordering, cleanup settlement, error identities/messages, and lazy boundaries remain in place.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None newly introduced. This cut consolidates implementations without removing guards or changing supported behavior. Error stacks may include the shared helper frames.

## Size

153 net production lines removed across 35 production files against the fixed branch base. Four test files add 107 net lines for distinct cleanup, diagnostic-redaction, complete-ID-versus-capped-summary contracts, and the existing host-link repair warning. Other existing coverage remains unchanged.

## Evidence

Focused module and consumer tests, targeted native typechecking, lint, and formatting passed for each cut. Latest session slice: 29 lifecycle, 30 Stop, 1 Stop-authority, 8 agent-admission, and 8 error-owner cases; lint-suppressions: 14 passed. Teams: 16 attachment and 8 inbound-media cases passed. Google Meet: 34 CLI cases passed; xAI: 20 video-provider cases passed.

All local test/typecheck commands ran serially at low priority with isolated state. The latest session commands took 35.3s, 11.2s, 13.8s, 7.7s, and 2.2s respectively, predominantly transformation/setup. The changed Teams test command took 11.2s (8.51s Vitest); Meet took 30.0s (26.04s Vitest). Hosted CI on this exact head owns broad/platform proof; no live provider calls or broad local build/E2E claim.

Independent P0–P2 reviews are clean for the individual cuts and the complete candidate. The cumulative review found no actionable findings. Wrapper import-closure passed (3 cases); runtime and static import-cycle checks both reported zero cycles. No new lint suppressions.

Initial CI exposed an additional eager-wrapper inventory requirement for the transcript-version comparison extraction. Those four files are restored to the fixed base; the five-line extraction is parked on `deslop/z33-parked-transcript-version-comparison-20261015` because it requires adding a protected wrapper entry, not a shrink-only inventory edit. The two failed eager-import inventory cases now pass locally. The media-facts assertion baseline is reduced from 14 to 10, as required by the removed assertions.

The installer warning failure also reproduces on clean main `de41c8622d2d4b9859732d52c495451e81da0932`. The successful repair warning was intentionally added in #181140 for the human report #180903. Production repair/reporting is unchanged; the stale test now requires the repair warning for a copied host and no warnings for an unchanged host. Both focused cases pass (26.5s command, 22.76s Vitest, about 1.92s test execution). No retries, skips, timeout increases, or weakened link checks.

Repair checks pass: targeted native test types, one-file lint/format, assertion-safety ratchet, and 14 lint-suppression cases. Fresh independent P0–P2 reviews of both repairs are clean. Initial CI also reported a Mermaid mock-Gateway browser reload `ERR_ABORTED`; its six scheduled-main comparisons do not establish a matching signature, so it is not being labelled inherited. No UI or browser fixture changes are included. Current exact-head hosted CI remains the broad gate for this repaired candidate.

prs.title: fix(webchat): acknowledge pending input before steering admission
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes chat messages staying in “sending” for minutes when steering waits behind an older queued input during an active turn. Two observed requests took 437,831 ms and 137,522 ms and were acknowledged together.

## User Impact

Chat sends acknowledge saved input custody promptly. Steering or followup execution continues in reservation order and reports its outcome through the existing lifecycle. The existing `started` response means admitted input, not native runtime consumption.

## Why This Change Was Made

The request's `replyContext` timing also covered steering startup, including the mailbox predecessor wait. Input was already durable, but the ACK waited for runtime admission. Detached dispatch now owns that wait and native settlement. The controller retains FIFO, cancellation, live authority, and uncertain-outcome custody; there is no timeout-driven replay or second delivery path. Terminal collaborative-steering refusal is recorded before fallible workspace preparation.

The pre-ACK steering branch is removed. Quoted reply previews retain their existing durable-admission hydration contract. No schema or configuration changes.

## Evidence

- Real WebSocket regression: baseline times out at the one-second ACK boundary with an older reservation held; candidate acknowledges both sends before release, verifies durable pending inputs, then exactly two FIFO injections. All six isolated-Gateway cases pass.
- Focused checks passed: six isolated-Gateway cases; 138 directive/reply-context and prestart cases; 20 cross-client/collaboration/commit-authority custody cases; the ordering file. Core typecheck passed. Focused lint and formatting checked changed files. Isolated Gateway launcher 38.91 s; directive/prestart files 41.70 s; custody launcher 66.76 s (including 24.2 s worker preparation). PR CI supplies broad proof.
- First PR CI passed lint/typecheck but exposed six profile-steering tests that treated ACK as native settlement. Updated them to verify the earlier ACK, captured-owner fences, terminal errors, retained original-profile input, and zero fallback/injection on revocation. All 10 focused profile-steering cases passed, and CI then passed on `8b81822b0054`. The subsequent authority-window extension also passes: 12 cases, 25.94 s launcher; changed-file lint, formatting, and independent review pass. No runtime change was needed. Final CI passed on `07c128476b30` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40033072188)).
- Deferred-admission authority proof: the production request handler acknowledges while an older reservation still holds the real mailbox predecessor. The unchanged-profile control reaches native execution once. Reassigning the caller through the real profile owner before releasing the predecessor yields a terminal source-identity error with zero native entry, enqueue, or fallback dispatch, retaining the admitted input under its original profile. This is in-process request/authority/storage proof; the separate isolated Gateway regression supplies the WebSocket boundary.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): one actionable refusal-ordering finding corrected; updated diff has no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Runtime production code: net 81 lines removed. The requested committed active-run workload adds 200 tooling lines plus 14 README lines; the non-test/non-docs stat includes that tooling and is +133 overall. This growth supplies a rerunnable wire ACK/terminal/history measurement, while the runtime itself shrinks.

## Paired active-run measurements

Two completed concurrent pairs on interleaved slot-A CPUs, swapped in pair two; 63 measured rounds per side after warmup. Each side had **1,008 active ACK samples**, **2,016 total user sends**, and **1,512 extra inputs verified consumed exactly once**. All 2,016 candidate active ACKs arrived before the 1,500 ms primary-release timer; baseline was 1,008/1,008 in pair one and 992/1,008 in pair two.

Baseline → candidate; deltas are candidate minus baseline. Main-isolate GC and promotion are normalized per user send. Inconclusive means no improvement or adverse claim under v5.2.

| Metric | Pair 1 | Pair 2 | Paired mean / decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| active ACK p50 ms | 151.48 → 122.75; Δ -28.73 (-18.96%); n=1,008/1,008 | 190.49 → 150.02; Δ -40.47 (-21.24%); n=1,008/1,008 | Δ -34.60 (-20.10%); within-threshold |
| active ACK p99 ms | 633.96 → 372.92; Δ -261.04 (-41.18%); n=1,008/1,008 | 4,662.52 → 838.66; Δ -3823.86 (-82.01%); n=1,008/1,008 | Δ -2042.45 (-61.59%); inconclusive |
| total GC ms per user send | 32.39 → 26.42; Δ -5.97 (-18.44%) | 30.77 → 32.01; Δ +1.24 (+4.01%) | Δ -2.37 (-7.21%); inconclusive |
| Promotion MB per user send | 27.70 → 18.55; Δ -9.14 (-33.01%) | 18.65 → 18.69; Δ +0.04 (+0.21%) | Δ -4.55 (-16.40%); inconclusive |
| main-thread CPU ms per user send | 254.44 → 237.15; Δ -17.29 (-6.79%) | 269.04 → 278.68; Δ +9.64 (+3.58%) | Δ -3.82 (-1.61%); inconclusive |
| process CPU ms per user send | 583.79 → 548.46; Δ -35.33 (-6.05%) | 597.40 → 649.62; Δ +52.22 (+8.74%) | Δ +8.44 (+1.34%); inconclusive |
| minor GC p95 ms | 7.67 → 7.23; Δ -0.44 (-5.79%); n=10,172/8,790 | 9.40 → 9.49; Δ +0.09 (+0.95%); n=8,922/8,916 | Δ -0.18 (-2.42%); context: absolute mean <1 ms (v5.3) |
| minor GC p99 ms | 14.26 → 11.19; Δ -3.07 (-21.56%); n=10,172/8,790 | 17.48 → 16.68; Δ -0.80 (-4.60%); n=8,922/8,916 | Δ -1.94 (-13.08%); within-threshold |
| major GC p95 ms | 158.06 → 137.75; Δ -20.31 (-12.85%); n=114/115 | 166.66 → 159.50; Δ -7.16 (-4.30%); n=99/133 | Δ -13.74 (-8.57%); context: insufficient tail samples |
| major GC p99 ms | 249.71 → 158.42; Δ -91.29 (-36.56%); n=114/115 | 318.14 → 236.61; Δ -81.53 (-25.63%); n=99/133 | Δ -86.41 (-31.09%); context: insufficient tail samples |

**Max single GC pause:** pair one 1,736.290 → 167.334 ms; pair two 318.137 → 312.521 ms. Both pass `max(50 ms, 2 × baseline max)`. ACK maxima were 984.6 → 1,013.8 ms and 5,334.1 → 883.5 ms; this is not a claim that every stressed ACK is below one second.

**Event-loop tails:** pooled p99 is unavailable because the owner retains per-round summaries only. Per-round p99/count ranges (context, every window below 1,000 samples):

- Pair 1: baseline 60.88–266.99 ms, n=328–601 per window (24,712 total); candidate 64.26–147.72 ms, n=326–527 per window (23,922 total).
- Pair 2: baseline 60.78–243.01 ms, n=355–736 per window (26,852 total); candidate 63.73–246.02 ms, n=340–869 per window (26,791 total).

**Decision:** no metric crossed the v5 adverse thresholds and neither max-pause clause triggered. P99 is inconclusive because baseline spread is 7.35×; resource metrics with opposing signs are also inconclusive, not improvements. None would provisionally trigger rejection, so no third-pair gate applies. This requested bug fix and runtime simplification can land without a threshold-level adverse result; its held-predecessor wire regression proves the original hang independently of this steady active-run workload.

**Host context:** the shared guard completed both pairs without interruption. It logged one pressure sample in pair one (load 72.38, Dirty 4,907,952 KiB) and two nonconsecutive samples in pair two (Dirty 4,815,084 KiB; later load 66.07, Dirty 6,000,176 KiB). CPU affinity was checked directly, and mpstat captured outside utilization. No stricter guard or post-hoc discard was applied.

**Revision scope:** measurements compare `2d8d8ad39dc9` against `4de1807ff7e2`, with identical workload tooling on both sides. SHA-256 checks verified all four runtime files and the tooling. The runtime files are byte-identical on final reviewed/CI head `07c128476b30`; later commits add consumer and authority-window tests.

**Sandbox signal:** neither candidate run emitted a `stage=request` slow-send line with `replyContext > 1 s` (zero candidate request-stage slow lines). This is sandbox evidence, not a post-deployment production claim.

Production deployment is outside this PR; post-deployment absence of request-stage replyContext stalls remains to be checked by the deployment owner.

prs.title: fix: MCP relay runs abort after submission succeeds
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

MCP relay submissions leave their 15-second request deadline armed after returning a successful conversation/run ID. The accepted run retains that signal, so a reply that keeps making progress can be cancelled near 15 seconds even when the MCP client requests a longer observation window and remains connected.

## Changes

Use the existing clearable SDK timeout helper in the relay's request wrapper and clean up the deadline when that RPC settles. The original 15-second deadline still bounds a request that has not returned acceptance. `agent.wait` retains its separate observation timeout, and grant revocation/relay disconnect still cancel owned work.

@crwohlfeil's commit and regressions are retained. Whole-diff simplification keeps the one existing request owner rather than adding another lifecycle abstraction: production **+7/-1**, tests **+70/-1**. No SDK export/type, configuration, scope, grant, or storage-policy change.

## Evidence

Built main `a6067465a8a281270d74a3183df3103b6158b72e` and candidate `59232c876d2bd35b5e5885320fbe1622907f8a98` on Node 24.22.1 in isolated Docker state.

The actual MCP SDK v2 Client calls tools over loopback Streamable HTTP. The owned external relay fixture forwards ordinary request/response frames over the shipped plugin's real outbound WebSocket. It verifies the Gateway's Ed25519 challenge signature, completes hello/ready, responds to keepalive pings, and consumes a code issued by the shipped `mcp-relay pair` command through normal `grant.create`. No private grant table or principal-bound Gateway request helper is substituted.

The local OpenAI-compatible Responses endpoint sends visible text approximately once per second for 30 seconds. There is no held tool, exec timer, silent provider pause, or system-clock change. Public Gateway assistant events independently record the progress. `send_message` returns an accepted run ID with `waitMs: 0`; the real SDK client then calls `get_reply` with `waitMs: 18000`, followed by the supported `50000` window when still running.

| Submission path | Main outcome / elapsed from submission | Candidate at first observation | Candidate completion / elapsed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| New conversation, run 1 | failed / 15.05 s | running after 18.95 s from acceptance | completed / 33.48 s |
| Existing conversation, run 1 | failed / 15.08 s | running after 18.18 s | completed / 31.60 s |
| New conversation, run 2 | failed / 15.38 s | running after 18.47 s | completed / 31.91 s |
| Existing conversation, run 2 | failed / 15.08 s | running after 18.17 s | completed / 31.81 s |

Each definitive run has exactly one primary HTTP inference request. Main records continuing provider/public assistant progress before native `agent.wait` ends with an RPC cancellation; no completion marker arrives. Candidate records all 30 progress steps and 31 public assistant progress events over approximately 31 seconds, then returns the exact complete text and per-run completion marker through both the MCP reply and native terminal snapshot.

Controls:

- Short reply: both arms complete normally in about 2.7 seconds through the same MCP client.
- Shipped grant revoke, triggered after observed streaming progress: both arms abort the active provider stream and native run; the revoked grant is refused.
- Actual relay peer disconnect/reconnect during streaming: both arms cancel the old owned run. Normal handshake/keepalive behavior is preserved.
- A never-accepted request still reaches its original 15-second limit in the focused regression fixture. Both accepted-run regressions fail on main because the signal becomes aborted after settlement, and pass on candidate.

**84 tests across three focused suites pass**, including operation, service and state ownership cases. Targeted formatting and package-boundary-aware extension lint pass. A separate real OpenAI `gpt-5-mini` shipped-agent check returns `RELAY_DEADLINE_LIVE_OK`.

### Proof limits

The relay endpoint and streaming model are owned local fixtures, not a hosted connected-app tenant or a ChatGPT/Claude application UI. The MCP SDK, Gateway relay plugin, pairing/grant path, principal-bound execution, cancellation and public run observation are actual production components. The real-provider check is separate from the deterministic relay comparison.

Early setup attempts are excluded from the definitive table: CJS WebSocket import interop and misclassified incidental session-title inference contaminated initial fixture timelines. The final fixture demultiplexes the observed title envelope and answers metadata requests separately; all counted assistant runs have one real, steadily streaming request. The initial core-project lint command was also corrected to the plugin's package-boundary-aware configuration without changing or suppressing the logging expression it mis-typed.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the prior timer behavior without migration. Blast radius is accepted MCP relay run lifetime; submission timeouts, observation limits, grant authority and disconnect/revocation cancellation remain unchanged.

prs.title: feat: let agents participate selectively in group conversations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agents in groups need to recognize invitations and useful opportunities without replying to every message when mention gating is disabled.

## User Impact

With Decision assistance enabled and an effective Decision Model, eligible unmentioned group messages receive a pre-generation participation assessment. An invitation or useful opportunity takes the ordinary agent reply path, including its normal permissions, tools, streaming, and delivery. A negative assessment records the message without starting a primary agent run. Explicit mentions, commands, ambient room events, and generic CLI backends retain their existing paths. Unavailable assessments and unassessable media fall back to ordinary replies.

The existing default-off Labs flag opts into current and future Decision Model consumers, including on upgrades with an already-saved enabled preference. No separate participation setting is added. Hosted evaluations receive bounded conversation evidence and may incur provider charges. Opt-out invalidates pending participation judgments; ordinary cancellation and current-turn authority continue to govern execution.

## Why This Change Was Made

Deciding before generation avoids unnecessary agent runs and keeps sent-message history accurate. There is no private draft generation, post-generation review, revision loop, or special publication queue. Accepted-input and configuration changes invalidate stale preflight decisions before generation.

## Evidence

Updated October 23, 2026. Evidence is scoped to the tested inputs; this is not a merge-ready claim.

- **Earlier published tree:** head `60becc8feacd3aa5d4d7eb149470e25d8cce97b6` has tree `214f54dc7f68c057f47bd66bee5a6a26a6db541c`. Isolated validation of that tree passed **149 tests across nine files**, full `pnpm build`, configuration-doc generation, and generated-file drift checking. The overall run failed `check:changed` on a stale max-lines baseline entry; it was not an all-green run.
- **Saved configuration:** the built CLI accepted fixtures with Decision assistance absent, false, and true, with no warnings and identical before/after configuration SHA-256 values. This proves parsing and byte preservation, **not** runtime rollout, fresh installation, or version-upgrade behavior.
- **Actual-provider rubric smoke:** four bounded TypeSafe calls using synthetic conversations returned the expected invitation, opportunity, chatter, and resolved-conversation categories (`jev-1.13.0`). These used the installed evaluation tool, not the candidate's exact provider adapter or Telegram path; they are a small semantic smoke set, not a reliability guarantee.
- **Telegram prerequisite:** the canonical Test Server doctor now exits 0 with Convex credentials, isolated TDLib state, authorized Test Server user, and verified SUT bot. This was a DM authentication/readiness check, **not** selective group-participation proof. Actual candidate group scenarios remain pending.
- **Current-main rebase (published):** head `73edfa2d43da3f86d5f27621b2497843c4a31d29` integrates main `c6facd08e4b5aa14c4424a716f097388537f52ae` using Git’s merge-preserving rebase. All 15 original logical PR commits are retained. The preceding 14 commit IDs are unchanged; only the final integration commit was recreated, preserving its original author, author date, and message. Its complete tree is `d4fe891304f55ec637b23d1bf573c406add897d9`, identical to the previously validated candidate. That unchanged tree passed the full build, core/extension typechecks, affected messaging/plugin test typechecks, focused participation/Decision/transcript/queued-turn suites, all 230 reply entry-point tests, and all 8 prompt-prefix stability tests. Targeted lint, formatting, line-cap/max-lines/mock-export ratchets, configuration-doc generation checks, and documentation links passed. The prior static review reported no actionable P0–P2 finding; it did not execute project code. Validation and review are reused based on exact complete-tree equality. Exact-head GitHub CI remains pending.

Still required: full changed-file CI checks; runtime saved-config and persisted-session upgrade proof; actual candidate real-Decision-provider Telegram group send/silence cases; exact-head CI verification. The isolated real-provider tests still need a task-scoped TypeSafe credential or ready local Kev endpoint. No gate is waived and no merge is authorized.

The ClawSweeper review of the preceding published head `60becc8feacd` reported no actionable introduced code/security finding, but retained rollout, real-provider, integration, and compatibility verification work.

prs.title: fix(oc-path): find misses children of quoted array indexes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`path find` returns no children when a wildcard follows a quoted numeric array index, while `path resolve` accepts the same concrete address. This affects JSON/JSONC, JSONL and YAML arrays.

## What Changed

Both existing array walkers now pass the key through the existing unquoteSeg helper before the existing array-index validator, matching concrete resolution. Returned paths retain their original quoted spelling. No new path grammar, configuration, dependency, persisted format or SDK surface is introduced.

Thanks @LinzeShi for the two-line repair and consolidated regressions. The README now describes quoted array-index behavior.

## Evidence

Built Linux CLI, Node 24.22.1, bundled oc-path enabled through shipped config commands in fresh isolated state. Main `a6067465a8a281270d74a3183df3103b6158b72e` ran twice; candidate `70c7c37b0995d27884ef658927274fa0099496ef` ran the same matrix. Input documents are external read-only fixtures, not handwritten OpenClaw state.

For an array containing `{"name":"old"}`, the actual shipped commands include:

```sh
openclaw path resolve 'oc://array.jsonc/"0"/name' --file array.jsonc --json
openclaw path find 'oc://array.jsonc/"0"/*' --file array.jsonc --json
```

Equivalent JSON, JSONC-with-comment, JSONL and block-YAML inputs were exercised. JSONL uses its normal L1 line selector before the array index.

| Format | Main resolve, both runs | Main quoted find, both runs | Candidate quoted find |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JSON | resolves old, exit 0 | count 0, exit 1 | count 1, old, exit 0 |
| JSONC | resolves old, exit 0 | count 0, exit 1 | count 1, old, exit 0 |
| JSONL | resolves old, exit 0 | count 0, exit 1 | count 1, old, exit 0 |
| YAML | resolves old, exit 0 | count 0, exit 1 | count 1, old, exit 0 |

Captured candidate paths retain the quotes:

```text
oc://array.json/"0"/name
oc://array.jsonc/"0"/name
oc://array.jsonl/L1/"0"/name
oc://array.yaml/"0"/name
```

Every candidate match was independently passed to the public resolve command and returned the identical match object with valueText old. Unquoted-index controls work in all arms. Empty arrays, empty quoted indexes, quoted literal $first and out-of-range quoted 9 retain count 0 / exit 1 rather than acquiring selector behavior. SHA-256 readback confirms all eight input files remain byte-identical in every arm.

Full main/candidate builds, all 70 focused CLI regressions, and focused lint/format passed. A separate real OpenAI gpt-5-mini CLI turn completed successfully, exit 0 and no fallback.

## Simplification

The production change is two substitutions in the existing JSONC/JSONL and YAML adapters: +2/-2, no growth or new helper. Tests reuse one existing table-driven case across formats (+25/-9); docs +4. The original spelling is retained by the existing path formatter rather than reconstructed or special-cased.

## Merge Risk

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous search behavior without rewriting input documents or state. Blast radius is array-key lookup during structured-file path searches; invalid-index validation and concrete resolver behavior are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(gateway): skip eager install discovery when startup update checks are disabled
prs.body:
# Gateway start runs `git rev-parse` / `npm root -g` even when `update.checkOnStart: false`

Closes #158099

## What Problem This Solves

The Gateway post-attach startup step called `updateCheck.initialize()`
unconditionally. That eager initialization resolves the install status,
which spawns `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (and `npm root -g` for
non-git installs) on every start — even when the operator opted out with
`update.checkOnStart: false` or `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1`. On machines
without the Command Line Tools installed this triggers the macOS CLT
install dialog on every Gateway start.

The existing `checkOnStart` gate lives inside
`runGatewayUpdateCheckOwned` (`src/infra/update-startup.ts`), which only
runs on the `owner.start()` scheduled path — the eager initialize call in
`src/gateway/server-startup-update-check.ts` bypassed it entirely.

## Fix

Gate the eager `updateCheck.initialize()` call at the gateway owner layer
(`createDeferredGatewayUpdateCheck`): skip it when
`update.checkOnStart === false` or `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE` is truthy
(reusing `isTruthyEnvValue`), matching the gate the scheduled loop
already applies. `owner.start()` still runs — its internal gate decides
whether scheduled checks happen.

Explicit update-status request paths are unaffected: the RPC handlers
(`update-effective-channel`, `update-admission`) call the memoized
`lifecycle.initialize()` directly and still get lazy install discovery,
which is exactly why the gate must live at the eager startup call site
and not inside the lifecycle.

## Evidence

Pre-fix failing tests (both added in
`src/gateway/server-startup-update-check.test.ts`):

- `skips eager install discovery when startup update checks are disabled`
  — with `getConfig: () => ({ update: { checkOnStart: false } })`,
  asserted `initialize` is not called while `start` still runs. Red on
  the pre-fix tree (`initialize` was called unconditionally).
- `skips eager install discovery when auto-update is disabled by
  environment` — same shape with `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1`. Red on the
  pre-fix tree.

Post-fix: both green, plus the 4 pre-existing cases in the file and the
full `src/infra/update-startup.test.ts` regression file pass. Real spawn
behavior is exercised indirectly through the owner contract: the test
asserts on the production `createDeferredGatewayUpdateCheck` code path,
so skipping `initialize` means `resolveStartupInstallStatus →
checkUpdateStatus → resolveUpdateInstallKind` (the actual git/npm spawn
chain) never runs at startup.

### Round 2: real-process startup proof (head e3638596bb6)

Real-behavior proof at the changed owner boundary, with real git child
processes observed (no mocks anywhere in the chain):

- Harness: `git` on `PATH` is a wrapper script that timestamps and forwards
  every invocation to the real `/usr/bin/git` (the production spawn path
  resolves `git` through `PATH`). The production owner pair is driven in a
  real Node process from this branch's source: `createDeferredGatewayUpdateCheck`
  (the exact function this PR changes, `src/gateway/server-startup-update-check.ts`)
  wired to the real `createGatewayUpdateCheck` from `src/infra/update-startup.ts`,
  with a real on-disk config file (`{ "gateway": { "mode": "local" }, "update":
  { "checkOnStart": true|false } }`) and an isolated state dir. `start()` is
  called and the process is given 20s of real wall time before `stop()`.
- `checkOnStart: true` (after-fix, controls): **23 real git child processes**
  spawned during startup — `rev-parse --show-toplevel`, `rev-parse --abbrev-ref
  HEAD`, `describe --tags --exact-match`, `rev-parse HEAD`, `show -s --format=%ct`,
  `status --porcelain`, branch `config --get`/`--get-all`, upstream
  `rev-parse --symbolic-full-name`, `merge-base`, `remote get-url`, and
  `fetch --quiet ... origin refs/heads/main`.
- `checkOnStart: false` (after-fix): **0 git invocations** during the same
  20s window — the eager `initialize()` (install discovery) is skipped, so the
  whole git probe chain above never spawns. The owner still starts and its
  scheduled/catalog work runs (`remote model catalog refresh failed` logged,
  i.e. the scheduler itself is alive — only install discovery is skipped).
- `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` with `checkOnStart: true` (after-fix): **0 git
  invocations**, same as the config opt-out.
- Pre-fix behavior reference: calling the real owner's `initialize()`
  unconditionally (what current main does at this boundary) spawns **12 git
  child processes** even with the opt-outs set — measured with the same probe
  harness against `resolveStartupInstallStatus` on this checkout.
- Honest scope note: a full `openclaw gateway run` from source via tsx in this
  sandbox stalls before the deferred post-attach update chain (same
  tsx-direct-run limitation family previously seen with gateway startup
  promotion), so the trace above drives the exact changed boundary
  (`createDeferredGatewayUpdateCheck.start()` → gate → eager `initialize`)
  in a real process instead of a full server; nothing in the chain is mocked
  and every probe line is a real spawned child of the proof process.

Measured cost of the new tests (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run
src/gateway/server-startup-update-check.test.ts --pool=forks --maxWorkers=1`):
6 tests (2 new + 4 pre-existing), one-worker wall time 95.0s on this machine,
the two new cases assert on the mocked-owner contract and add no child
processes (in-run test time ~0.1s each).

prs.title: docs(i18n): expand Russian glossary (250 entries) and add ru navigation (12 tabs / 55 groups)
prs.body:
## What

Russian docs localization is wired up but nearly empty: `docs/.i18n/glossary.ru.json` was 21 entries (1.2 KB) against 107 KB for `zh-CN`, and `ru-navigation.json` did not exist at all, so the Russian sidebar fell back to English while the pages themselves were already 75% translated.

This PR fills in the two files that drive the Russian locale:

- `glossary.ru.json`: **21 → 250 entries** (1.2 KB → 18.6 KB). Existing entries and their order are preserved; 6 target terms were corrected for consistency with the pages: Compaction → Сжатие контекста, Gateway → Шлюз, Node → Нода, Plugin → Плагин, Skills → Скиллы, Webhook → Вебхук. Deliberately kept in English: Active Memory, Cron, Dreaming, Heartbeat, Loopback, Markdown, Self-hosted.
- `ru-navigation.json`: **created from scratch — 12 tabs, 55 groups** (8.6 KB), mirroring the English navigation structure.

No page content, no build scripts, no English strings touched: two data files only.

## Verification

- Every path in `ru-navigation.json` was checked against the repository tree (1,385 `.md` files): 0 broken links, 55 unique anchors.
- Rendered through the real `composeDocsConfig()` from `scripts/docs-sync-publish.mjs`: 12/12 Russian tabs, 55/55 groups, pages resolve as `ru/index…`.
- `glossary.ru.json` parses as valid JSON and keeps the original key order (`json.load` round-trip diff on the untouched prefix).
- Note: `check-docs-i18n-glossary.mts` only validates `zh-CN` today, so this file is not CI-gated — I verified it manually as described above.

## Why

The Russian locale is the largest non-English audience for OpenClaw docs and currently has English headings over Russian text. These two files are the smallest, highest-leverage change: no translation work, but the sidebar and the inline glossary switch to Russian immediately.

## Visual proof

Rendered through the real `composeDocsConfig()` from `scripts/docs-sync-publish.mjs`, locale `ru`, same tree, only `docs/.i18n/ru-navigation.json` added.

| Before (`main` — no ru overlay) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adamant064/openclaw/docs/ru-i18n-proof/proof/ru-sidebar-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adamant064/openclaw/docs/ru-i18n-proof/proof/ru-sidebar-after.png) |

Behavioural comparison of the two composed configs:

```
before: tabs 12, groups 55, pages 308
after : tabs 12, groups 55, pages 308      # page inventory identical
before tabs: Get started | Install | Channels | Agents | Capabilities | Models |
             Platforms | Gateway & Ops | Reference | Releases | Contributing | Help
after  tabs: Начало работы | Установка | Каналы | Агенты | Возможности | Модели |
             Платформы | Шлюз и эксплуатация | Справочник | Релизы | Участие в разработке | Помощь
```

Only labels change; every route and its order is preserved, which is the guarantee the overlay functions (`applyLocaleNavLabelOverlay`) are supposed to give. Screenshots are generated from the composed `docs.json` (sidebar label tree), not from a live docs host, so nothing is redacted and no endpoint is involved.

prs.title: fix(openai): restore Azure realtime Talk on GA deployments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Azure Realtime Talk defaults to a preview-only connection that fails for GA-only Azure deployments. Input transcription can also fail when its separately deployed model has a non-default name. This PR defaults to the GA URL and matching session payload, accepts a configurable transcription deployment, and preserves explicitly selected preview protocols.

## User Impact

Azure users whose Realtime deployment only supports GA can connect without an explicit preview selector. Transcription can use its own Azure deployment, and existing users who explicitly selected a preview API version keep that protocol until they remove the setting.

## Why This Change Was Made

The previous Azure default built a preview-only URL, while input transcription assumed a fixed deployment name. The bridge now pairs each Azure URL with the corresponding session payload, keeping the explicitly selected preview route, and passes the configured transcription deployment to session creation.

## Evidence

- Current branch after integrating `main`: focused bridge connection suite **25/25 passed** (12.20 seconds on current head after removing two unrelated restored tests), including GA default, explicit preview, Azure transcription override, and browser Gateway relay; extension production typecheck passed; touched-file lint/format and docs config-example validation passed. The earlier pre-integration bridge suite passed 37/37. Full `pnpm build` under Node 26.12.1 completed successfully (12m 49s) at the unchanged production head.
- Live Azure GA WebSocket proof (2026-10-07), using synthetic speech: both the separate-transcription-deployment configuration and the existing default-transcription behavior produced an accepted session, nonempty input transcription, completed response, and assistant audio (74,400 and 88,800 bytes respectively). Redacted output is included below; private endpoint, credentials, utterance, transcript, and audio are omitted.
- Microsoft Learn's [Preview-to-GA migration guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/realtime-audio-preview-api-migration-guide) states that the preview API was deprecated April 30, 2026 and directs migration to GA. It specifies `/openai/v1` with no API-version parameter and describes the GA session/event format changes.

## Summary

- add `inputTranscriptionModel` to the OpenAI realtime provider config
- use it for GA realtime input transcription and Azure deployment session payloads
- preserve existing defaults (`gpt-4o-mini-transcribe` for GA; `whisper-1` for Azure when the override is unset)
- route Azure Realtime through GA by default; preserve explicit preview selection and its matching session payload
- send the GA `session.update` shape required by the GA endpoint
- use Azure `api-key` auth for Azure realtime connections, including the preview route
- document the Talk config knob for Azure transcription deployments

## Azure protocol compatibility

With no `azureApiVersion`, Azure Realtime uses the GA `/openai/v1/realtime` route and GA session/event payload. If a user explicitly selects an Azure API version, the existing preview URL and matching preview session updates are preserved; remove `azureApiVersion` to migrate to GA. This avoids silently changing a shipped configuration selector while fixing GA-only resources. Microsoft [deprecated the Preview Realtime API on April 30, 2026](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/realtime-audio-preview-api-migration-guide), recommends GA migration, and documents the changed route and session format. The current PR does not remove the opt-in preview contract.

## Why

Azure realtime Talk has two independent deployment requirements: its Realtime conversation endpoint must use the currently available GA route, and input transcription can use a separate Azure deployment from the conversation model. The preview URL and preview session payload do not work against resources offering only GA; explicit preview configurations still use that protocol for compatibility. The session transcription model must also name an Azure deployment that exists in the resource.

## Released Gateway/Talk upgrade evidence (isolated, 2026-10-23)

I compared the **published npm `openclaw@2026.10.6` artifact** (tarball SHA-256 `b13fc9f1221e185451573a435ff31bdeb8c5875f569e6f41008198708ca2359f`; SHA-512 matched npm registry `dist.integrity`) against production head `fe7464cb8d` (identical production code at current test-only head `0636f68232`), using Node 26.12.1. Each launched its own compiled `dist/index.js gateway` with separate temporary HOME/state/config/workspace and loopback ports. An operator Gateway client invoked `talk.session.create` (`provider=openai`, `transport=gateway-relay`, `mode=realtime`); a loopback synthetic Azure WebSocket peer recorded the bridge URL, headers and `session.update`. The same synthetic provider settings were applied to both versions, without touching an installed/running Gateway or using a live Azure credential.

```text
Config common to both: azureEndpoint=http://127.0.0.1:<ephemeral-port>/,
  azureDeployment=realtime-prod; synthetic key used (value omitted); version override omitted unless shown
v2026.10.6, no version: /openai/realtime?api-version=2024-10-01-preview&deployment=realtime-prod
  preview session; transcription=whisper-1
PR head, no version: /openai/v1/realtime?model=realtime-prod
  GA session; transcription=whisper-1
v2026.10.6, inputTranscriptionModel=transcribe-prod: preview session; transcription=whisper-1
PR head, inputTranscriptionModel=transcribe-prod: GA session; transcription=transcribe-prod
v2026.10.6, azureApiVersion=2024-10-01-preview: /openai/realtime?api-version=2024-10-01-preview&deployment=realtime-prod
PR head, azureApiVersion=2024-10-01-preview: same preview URL and preview session;
  configured transcription=transcribe-prod
All six: talk.session.create=OK; one stub WebSocket connection/session.update;
  api-key matched synthetic fixture; no Authorization header.
```

A second identical comparison with `azureEndpoint` **ending `/openai/`** also passed Talk creation and protocol checks, but revealed a path normalization difference: released v2026.10.6 appends `/openai/realtime` to that base and sends `/openai/openai/realtime`; this PR removes the duplicate segment, sending `/openai/realtime` for explicit preview. Thus explicit preview *selection and payload* are preserved, but the pathname is not byte-for-byte preserved for an endpoint already suffixed with `/openai/`. This is disclosed for owner review, not hidden as identical upgrade behavior.

**Limits:** These Gateway/Talk tests use a permissive synthetic WebSocket peer. They prove shipped-entry-point config routing and wire shape, **not** Azure acceptance, real microphone/audio playback or actual transcription. The separate October 7 live Azure WebSocket results below demonstrate GA acceptance, transcription and assistant audio, but did not run through a shipped Gateway/Talk entry point. The released artifact was installed with production dependencies in a temp directory (optional dependencies/lifecycle scripts omitted); its exercised Gateway/Talk route ran. No live cloud usage or Gateway restart occurred.

## Maintainer decision requested

Azure Realtime area owner: please approve or reject (1) making GA the default when `azureApiVersion` is omitted and (2) adding optional `inputTranscriptionModel` as a supported provider setting. Explicit preview version selection remains available; the `/openai/`-suffixed endpoint path normalization above is also visible for review. This PR does not presume owner acceptance.

## Existing upstream work

[#79130](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/79130) migrated direct OpenAI Realtime to GA but deliberately kept Azure on its deployment-compatible preview transport. [#165632](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165632) added a custom `baseUrl`, which cannot be combined with Azure deployment settings and does not select an independent transcription deployment. Neither fix resolves these Azure-specific reports.

## Issues

Fixes #166773
Fixes #166776

## Live Azure proof (2026-10-07)

Manual end-to-end run against the existing Azure resource using short synthetic English speech. Private endpoint and credentials were redacted; the utterance, transcript contents, and audio payloads were not included in the evidence.

**Separate deployments, configured transcription override**

```text
provider: Azure OpenAI Realtime (endpoint redacted)
GA endpoint: /openai/v1/realtime?model=<redacted>
conversation deployment: <redacted>
transcription deployment: <redacted>
deploymentsAreDistinct: true
sessionAccepted: true
inputTranscriptReceived: true
inputTranscriptNonEmpty: true
assistantAudioEvents: 4
assistantAudioBytes: 74400
responseDone: true
responseStatus: completed
responseErrorCode: null
result: PASS
```

**Existing/default behavior, transcription override omitted**

```text
provider: Azure OpenAI Realtime (endpoint redacted)
GA endpoint: /openai/v1/realtime?model=<redacted>
conversation deployment: <redacted>
transcription deployment: <redacted>
deploymentsAreDistinct: true
sessionAccepted: true
inputTranscriptReceived: true
inputTranscriptNonEmpty: true
assistantAudioEvents: 5
assistantAudioBytes: 88800
responseDone: true
responseStatus: completed
responseErrorCode: null
result: PASS
```

No stored-data format changes.

prs.title: feat(ui): dismiss completed processes from Details
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Completed processes accumulate in Details, where users cannot dismiss them and hovering a row repeats its command and status in a tooltip.

## User Impact

Completed rows now have a small, muted X using the existing Stop hover/focus pattern. Dismissing a row keeps it hidden from desktop and mobile Details after reopening or reloading, while it remains available in the Processes tab's Finished section. Row tooltips are removed; the action tooltips are “Dismiss process” and “Stop process.”

## Why This Change Was Made

One Details-only projection applies a preference stored by the existing UI settings owner, scoped to this browser, Gateway, viewer, agent, and session. The process observation, full collection, output, and Gateway APIs are unchanged. The control waits for viewer identity to resolve before applying or saving a preference.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the original tooltip and missing dismissal on main `d90c4d0e729` through the real Control UI with a mocked Gateway and synthetic running/completed processes.
- Chromium, light and dark: hover, keyboard focus/activation, reload, switching to mobile, reopening Details, and the dismissed row remaining in Finished. WebKit passed the same flow using macOS Option-Tab.
- 41 focused tests passed. The new integration regression failed against the original source. Measured wrapper wall time: process panel suite **2.98 s** (9 tests); settings suite **1.59 s** (32 tests). [CI run 40014875165](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40014875165) completed successfully on `a743b7da86da7fab6a6b6dc72e6fee6fa27bb4e8`.
- UI typecheck, targeted lint, stylesheet lint, formatting, i18n baseline, controller guard, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent Codex review: no actionable P0–P2 findings after resolving the viewer-identity issue.

### CSS budget verification

The CSS-budget follow-up in `a743b7da86d` consolidates the existing process action styles without changing the approved appearance. No budget, baseline, or exception changed.

The native performance comparator rebuilt the CI merge source (`c8779885caf`) plus this repair against its exact base (`98d8c5cefd9367de12c8aeb3204498bcca53befb`):

| Metric | Base | Candidate | Difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Total CSS raw | 1,596,850 B | 1,596,625 B | −225 B |
| Total CSS gzip | 302,804 B | 302,830 B | +26 B (64 B allowed) |

The gate passed; boot CSS sizes and request counts stayed unchanged. After settling the actual tooltip surface, **20/20 before/after crops were byte-identical**, and **20/20 computed-style snapshots matched** across light/dark, pointer/touch, reduced motion, rest, row/action hover, focus, and long-command truncation. Chromium and WebKit flows, 9 focused component tests, targeted lint/stylelint, and an independent P0–P2 review passed. The screenshots below remain representative of the unchanged visuals.

| Theme | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dark | ![Before: completed row tooltip, no dismiss action](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1639b4d5-ec1c-48a8-bea8-953b77127e34) | ![After: muted X with Dismiss process tooltip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/174b911c-5296-4f1c-897e-193ad77eec74) |
| Light | ![Before: completed process in Details](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7578d739-8c5a-4320-b719-a415745567ae) | ![After: completed process dismiss action](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2610286d-d4e9-4dcb-8eb7-e0008ca9074e) |

<details>
<summary>Full context, Stop tooltip, and mobile persistence</summary>

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Full desktop context before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5dc8a189-5caf-480f-b580-314e99a6a73d) | ![Full desktop context after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/489af978-fb91-47cd-9c53-36911b76a7a6) |
| ![Mobile Details before dismissal](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cfb95914-b2a2-44e8-a05a-4e4a92e544a5) | ![Mobile Details after dismissal and reload](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff0a439c-f819-4849-a44a-7e618e484a2d) |

![Stop tooltip contains only Stop process](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/66de8883-dcba-437a-a96c-9a3a16e419f3)

![Dismissed git merge remains in the Processes Finished section](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c62bec93-e898-4bab-a6d6-e9c1abbbf5cf)

</details>

### Risk and coverage

This is a browser-local presentation preference; clearing browser storage restores the rows. It does not delete output or change process retention, cancellation, access, or other viewers' preferences. Only `completed` rows can be dismissed. prs.title: perf(media): remove redundant upload collision check
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Attachment uploads perform an unnecessary synchronous destination check before `chat.send` can acknowledge durable media custody, and the ACK benchmark cannot distinguish async durability waits from main-thread filesystem stalls.

## User Impact

Uploads keep the same durability, authority, collision rejection, and cleanup behavior while doing one fewer filesystem lookup. This is a small simplification; it does not claim to fix the previously observed multi-second ACK tail.

## Why This Change Was Made

The pinned fs-safe atomic move already owns no-overwrite publication, including its fallback. Remove the caller's duplicate `lstatSync` while preserving `assertPublicationAllowed`, file sync, and directory sync. The new test proves an existing destination survives a collision and the temporary upload is removed.

Extend the existing synthetic filesystem probe with opt-in inbound-media operation timings and equal file/directory sync delay injection. Add whole-workload ACK diagnostics so event-loop and GC tails have valid sample counts; omit those acceptance metrics from profiling runs that force GC. Document settled synthetic runs to avoid startup recovery overwhelming the fixture.

Runtime production code: **+1/-13, net -12 lines**. The prescribed non-test/non-doc diff is **net +160** because the requested operation-attribution and whole-workload sample-count tooling adds 172 lines. Test: net +17; docs: +23. That growth supplies the requested measurement contract, not another runtime path or cache. No fs-safe internals, schema, product config, or public API changes.

## Evidence

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean. The autoreview helper refused the configured provider route before inference; no configuration was changed.

Focused `src/media/store.read-scope.test.ts`: 18/18 on the original base, 19/19 with collision coverage on the base, and 19/19 with the deletion. This is a preservation test, not a claimed red-to-green bug reproduction. Changed-file source/test and script lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. PR CI supplies broad validation; no remote validation leases were used.

Synthetic Linux attribution uses 5,000 sessions, 6,000 settled retained runs, 4 KiB text attachments, and a 50 ms delay added to each real inbound sync. Among 200 measured ACKs, attachment preparation averaged 131.7 ms, of which the required file and directory syncs averaged 55.2 and 55.6 ms. ACK p50 was 214.2 ms; p99 327.0 ms is context only at N=200. JavaScript main-thread fsyncSync: zero measured calls, zero recorded blocking time. The probe cannot observe synchronization inside native code or workers, so this is not a claim of zero total main-thread blocking.

Source and probe attribution found no attachment content hash, pixel decode/thumbnail, or re-read-after-write verification on this text path. Preparation and store MIME sniffs inspect different prefix lengths; they are retained. SQLite message custody occurs in the subsequent pre-ACK persistence phase. Optional audio/video metadata probing is unchanged.

**Acceptance: neutral latency, no rejection gate.** Three concurrent pairs measured 1,000 ACKs per side per pair (3,000 per side total), with matching synthetic fixtures and sync injection. Pairs 1–2 swapped even/odd CPUs 96–127 under one exclusive slot; the third used even/odd CPUs 64–95 under the other exclusive slot. Every pair used the same shared guard, 24 GiB per side, and recorded CPU-load context. No completed pair was interrupted by the guard. Detailed operation logging was disabled for comparisons.

The third pair was required because median ACK and promotion deltas changed sign. It also exposed a 5.78× p99 baseline difference and an opposite-sign p99 delta. Therefore use the **three-pair absolute mean**, not the mean of percentages: ACK p99 775.821 → 750.825 ms (−24.996 ms, −3.22% of mean baseline), median −1.756 ms, and p95 +13.104 ms (+5.04%). This does not establish a repeatable speedup. The deletion qualifies as a neutral simplification; the historical multi-second attachment stall remains unproven.

Other three-pair absolute means: main-thread CPU −2.672 ms/ACK, event-loop p99 +0.546 ms, total GC −0.551 ms/ACK, promotion −0.850 MB/ACK. No eligible metric crosses a 20% adverse mean or a 10% adverse change in both original swapped pairs. CPU and GC include completed turns and inter-cohort diagnostics, not just the ACK path. All six valid runs have zero diagnostic errors/drops, matching raw main-isolate GC counts/promotion, and **zero measured JavaScript synchronous fsync calls (0 ms recorded fsync blocking)**; native synchronization and other synchronous operations are outside that probe's visibility.

The pair-2 minor GC maximum is real: 17.385 → 71.738 ms (raw main-isolate pause 71.567 ms). Conservatively apply the max-pause clause to restore p95 gate eligibility: minor p95's three-pair mean is −0.053 ms, below the rejection thresholds. Minor p99's +0.480 ms is sub-millisecond context. Major-GC p95/p99 are context because each pair has fewer than 200/1,000 collections per side, respectively. No observation was discarded to improve the result.
