prs.title: fix(agents): release restart-recovery fences for killed runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A stopped conversation can reject every new turn when an unfinished restart-recovery fence survives without a recovery cycle or delivery owner. #181801 only handles fences already recorded terminal, so it does not cover the exact stored row reported in #181952.

Fixes #181952. Thanks @najef1979-code for evaluating the earlier fix against the preserved session and identifying the missing state.

## User Impact

Killed conversations accept new turns in the same session, preserving history. Active runs, session work, pending final deliveries, harness completion, reservations, foreground claims, and restart tombstones retain their existing custody. No schema, dependency, configuration, or CLI changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recovery lifecycle producer requires an exact run/generation fence match. A current lifecycle owner's terminal event could therefore be suppressed when its own fence still named an older generation. It now consumes that same run's fence when the current generation and authoritative lifecycle owner both match; another owner's event and older-generation events cannot use this exception.

For already-persisted killed rows, the existing startup and pre-admission recovery owner can release fence-only custody. It checks the live run registry and session controller and revalidates those owners before committing. It releases the stopped work rather than replaying it. The reporter's row alone cannot establish the historical cancellation ordering; the mismatched-generation producer failure and the exact stored-row deadlock are independently reproduced.

## Evidence

- Node 26.12.1 regressions: the exact killed, cycle-free row retains its unfinished fence on the base; current-owner end/error events against an old-generation fence are suppressed on the base. Both pass with the fix.
- Real Gateway regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.chat-first-turn-binding.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes, including the exact dangling-fence seed, subsequent completed turns, unchanged session ID, and preserved earlier transcript events. Fixed test time 15.476 s; file wall time 21.09 s. The base stalled at `agent.wait` and failed its existing 30 s request deadline (81.53 s file wall time).
- Focused ownership and persisted recovery files: 24 tests pass; the new stored-row/ownership controls take 924 ms. The unit-file run took 30.31 s wall time, dominated by transform/import work. Controls cover live registry and controller owners, pending delivery, harness completion, reservations, foreground claims, and tombstones.
- Independent live proof: isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, config, and loopback port 64000; seeded the reported row before starting the dev Gateway. `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .artifacts/live-proof.mts` drove real WebSocket `chat.history`, `chat.send`, and `agent.wait` through the real agent runtime and a synthetic local Responses provider. Output: `chat.send {"runId":"killed-fence-proof-turn","status":"started","messageSeq":1}`, `agent.wait` status `ok`, same session ID, stale fence absent, exactly one provider request, clean Gateway shutdown. This proves local execution and admission, not an external provider or package upgrade.
- Cross-lane importer proof on Node: all 406 tests in 24 direct-import files pass (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <direct-import files in discovery order> --maxWorkers=1`, 574.96 s wall time). All 251 tests in nine additional recovery-barrel import files pass (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <barrel-import files in discovery order> --maxWorkers=1`). Together with the Gateway regression: 658 tests across 34 unique files pass.
- Existing slow suite: `src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts` reports 237.348 s cumulative case time. Its existing `beforeEach` creates fresh state and `afterEach` drains/closes/removes SQLite state per case. No timeout, retry, assertion, or baseline changes; recorded under the campaign ruling that pre-existing slow suites do not block publication.
- Core tsgo and the agents-sessions/gateway-server test typecheck leaves pass. Touched-file oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and Madge pass (0 cycles). Full `check:changed`, including the SQLite inventory step, was omitted under the campaign local gate budget; PR CI is the broad proof.
- Independent autoreview: no accepted/actionable P0/P1 findings. Simplification keeps the existing lifecycle/recovery writer and its authority checks; no new cleanup owner or operator repair command.

Production delta: +40/-7 lines. Test delta: +175/-2 lines. Documentation delta: +3/-1 lines. Necessary growth is the producer fix, shared fence-only selection, and the regression/safety controls.

prs.title: fix: keep shared-state writers available during update progress checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes shared-state writes being blocked throughout full database integrity scans when update progress is recorded.

## User Impact

Other writers can proceed while ordinary update bookkeeping prepares its integrity check. Corruption, ownership changes, schema drift, and failed native cleanup still prevent unsafe writes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ordinary existing-state admission prepares integrity on its native handle in a query-only read snapshot. It consumes that result inside the managed write transaction only when the same connection reports an unchanged data version. A peer commit requires transactional revalidation. Repair and existing-runtime schema scopes retain their current validation.

The correction uses the current transaction, maintenance and failed-close owners. It preserves file identity, schema, external ownership and original-error checks. It does not restore the retired coordination-file APIs. The scan remains synchronous; this reduces writer exclusion, not scan duration, and a busy store can require a second scan under write admission.

## Evidence

The published head remains `e720e434d9035ab3d10e3becedbd74a95f98b7f7`. The unpublished correction is `bd96fa01b76fc03512808428aac04b6d144e7051`, containing canonical `7db874d10a7b215a81806a6c97203fe133c8dff8` through normal ancestry-preserving merges. Its parent `04bdb963` native invocation was stopped during build after pinned pnpm rewrote redundant package-manager lock metadata. A no-op script reproduced the write; the normalized same-fixture control left the lock unchanged. The generated 25-line correction leaves the entire application dependency document byte-identical and passed independent P0–P2 review. Exit 130 and incomplete builds do not count as passing gates. Publication, full exact-head gates, hosted checks, ClawSweeper review and verified merge remain pending.

The correction now uses canonical #162599 for checkpoint-stable database generations. The obsolete unpublished checkpoint callbacks, successor tracking and removal module have been removed. A real native-close fault and same-owner retry succeeded on unchanged canonical code locally and on Windows. Independent Windows acceptance passed normal restore and foreign-writer refusal. Both committed 4,152-byte WALs were observed before restore; separate processes then read baseline rows, displaced candidate rows and the update-run ID. This is API acceptance, not packaged-updater or Windows service proof.

https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_d7432b2e288072da0609ac12c3ee9f17

Browser cleanup tests retain canonical test movement and awaited database closure. Their improved oracle rejects an actual no-op cleanup that falsely passed the earlier test; deferred waits now observe premature operation settlement. All 44 browser cases, typed lint and formatting passed on the preceding composition. The newer canonical dependency and SDK changes are incorporated and the frozen install passed. All 58 CI-planner and 17 restore cases pass on the current composition, including both retained native-reader refusal and successful retry cases. Scoped lint, formatting, independent full-file audits and API reviews pass. Full required gates remain outstanding.

The supplier results below are historical and retain their original candidate identities.

The earlier supplier candidate `f8d82080` passed all seven selected cases on Windows Server 2022, Node 24.20.0 and SQLite 3.53.4. [Native run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_cdc53be5c87b35aa5d288c51b5ab38ec). The same seven local cases, scoped type-aware lint and formatting pass. The final two-line correction review is P0-P2 clean at 0.94 confidence. All 18 restore cases and their complete fixture were audited without weakened assertions, skips or timeouts. Earlier API review 12884 retained a P2 finding; actual ordinary-read/write refusal under retained maintenance authority falsified it, and its disposition remains recorded rather than relabeled clean.

Independent source-blind acceptance on that supplier candidate now passes all three clauses. A bounded external-fixture pause let the validator directly inspect both 4,152-byte WALs, their complete committed frames and actual candidate rows before restore. Both WALs remained unchanged after the readers closed. Separate fresh readers after restore confirmed baseline rows, recoverable displaced candidate rows and the exact update-run ID. Earlier checks also confirmed foreign-write refusal without displacement and independent witnesses in distinct private roots. This qualifies the old supplier candidate, not the pending canonical composition, service lifecycle or packaged updater.

The preceding exact `e736b1d3` native build failed at `update-database-restore.ts:322` with TS2322; check and tests did not start. The generation reader already validates the exact inventory and string-or-null values. Consuming its validated singleton avoids an unchecked indexed lookup without a duplicate guard or widened type. The same native base-declaration lane passed on the corrected source in 93.491 seconds. That scoped result is not a full build/check/test pass. The new canonical composition preserves 64 authored-only and 207 canonical-only file contents; its sole merged maintenance fixture retains all eight cases and both the canonical mock relocation and timer cleanup.

The following paragraphs retain earlier candidate evidence. Their failed or incomplete runs do not count as current-head gate success.

The preceding `145e9147` native run passed the full build in 13m 10.2s, then failed only the 1,000-line lint cap in `session-tab-registry.sqlite.test.ts`, at 1,036 counted lines. Full tests did not start. That file matched fresh canonical main. The current fixture refactor shares repeated session/profile inputs and stored-row reads, uses the existing deferred helper, and always releases and joins the paused sweep during cleanup. All 28 original cases and assertions remain. The same focused lint command fails before and passes after; the whole file passes before and after in 54.55s and 30.53s. Typed lint, formatting and independent P0–P2 review pass. The shorter second run reused compiler outputs, so it is not a measured test-speed improvement. Required full gates for the current commit remain pending.

A follow-up fixture audit separated malformed-field validation from the existing wrong-key case, propagates early sweep settlement to the waiting test, and awaits worker retirement before reset and temporary-directory cleanup. The final two-file refinement preserves all 28 cases, 93 assertions and the line cap. All 44 cases across its three fixture consumers pass on the exact final source in 52.58s; typed lint, formatting and independent P0–P2 review also pass. This improves test isolation and coverage; the audit did not establish a historical resource leak.

The current candidate adds two reviewed test prerequisites. The shared child-readiness fixture now uses the existing Vitest cancellation signal: the original timeout-race check fails before the repair and passes afterward, and both existing real-child cleanup/refusal cases pass. The explicit Gateway-port prerequisite preserves the reviewed socket reservation, startup, rejected-close and cleanup behavior. Its three files exactly match the credited supplier; 51 passing cases and the independent source review are reused after checking the relevant inputs. Scoped type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks pass. All touched test files were audited, with no weakened assertions, skips or timeouts.

The credited missing-scope UI import is also present identically on canonical main as `03137c1d729e25edbdb4dc482730aed74a6c2427`. The reviewed Kysely/package and updater presentation prerequisites landed in PR #162464 as `3a3d68111cc8ace6f257acddfe79913bf5ebcab1` and are adopted here with their original credit. Lint prepares the generated database types, packaged hooks retain their import closure, and the updater keeps its final renderer until terminal publication while stopping polling at the inner return. The latter use simulated service boundaries and prove phase order, not per-line latency. Final API review is scoped-clean P0-P2, confidence 0.89. The seven integration conflicts were resolved and the entire touched test files audited. The merge preserves canonical test pruning, deterministic fixture release, joined child cleanup and private Git routing. The focused native run passed 207 tests across nine files, with one existing platform skip, in 273.637 seconds. Review found an inherited Git environment gap in the new foreign-repository sentinel. The complete `52f20898` integration API review finished both passes with no P0-P2 findings, confidence 0.68. Scoped type-aware lint, formatting, diff checks, assertion checks and line limits passed. Normal commit hooks preserved the reviewed tree. The retired artificial MCP file-order wrapper remains covered by canonical direct runtime-retirement and requester-lease tests; the original historical timeout remains unexplained. The TUI unit shard found one OSC8 terminator assertion mismatch. The PTY shard found 37 rejections of `CSI 16 t` and one more terminator assertion mismatch. The independently reproduced test correction landed in #158748 at `e91fd2ed975aff1260beabea73e9f67e74f0c7b5`. It preserves production rendering and strict control rejection. The same run hit the 180-second outer timeout in `agent-bundle-mcp-retention.test.ts`, before its retention assertion. The cancellation-cleanup repair landed separately in #158767 at `8d9179bca949ca20bfd6ee01c82a5b16739220f9`; it is not a proven performance fix. A lower-concurrency run on scanner candidate `77defc7a` passed the MCP case in 147.621 s and its containing shard with 1,938 tests passed and five existing skips. That run used two project shards and two Vitest workers, unlike the ledger run's ten project shards and one worker. The original normal timeout remains unclassified. None of these observations is claimed as the cause of the original Mac lockup, and none has been hidden by skips, weakened assertions, retries, or increased timeouts.

The run also reported a native `SIGSEGV` in one 138-file `unit-src` group. It emitted case output from 123 files before stopping; the other four source groups completed. The scheduler stopped admitting new shards. An independent native replay of the exact group reproduced SIGSEGV 139 after 448.196 s, ending after a different test file. The remaining three groups were then cancelled through the native supervisor. Across 24 completed shard summaries, 50,265 tests passed and 44 failed; the other 639 planned shards did not complete. The exact file and cause remain unknown. Interleaved state-test output is not crash attribution, and no successful full-gate result is claimed.

A dedicated worker completed three bounded LLDB comparisons of the same 138-file inventory. Each passed 130 files and 1,843 tests, with eight existing skipped files and 103 skipped tests. All 123 original observed file positions matched.

Sampled compiler inputs and all four loaded native libraries kept stable hashes and file identities during the final control. The original deleted dependency graph was unavailable for a direct binary comparison. Two earlier diagnostic setups were rejected for changed compiler-input metadata and a cached test-order mismatch; neither counts as crash evidence. The successful comparisons still differ from the two raw crashes in debugger timing and background load. There is no reproduced canonical fault or originating native stack to justify a crash patch or assign its cause. Integrated candidate `aa244113` still requires native gates; these focused passes do not replace them.

prs.title: fix: bound stalled session archive and reconciliation work
prs.body:
Related: #176080

## What Problem This Solves

Stuck archive work can hold its FIFO indefinitely, and timed-out archive or transcript-reconciliation workers can retain native/database custody forever if termination never finishes. This completes the reporter's requested bounded retirement and recovery through the existing Gateway service lifecycle.

## User Impact

Archive admission is bounded to 128 outstanding claims. Active archive and reconciliation tasks request retirement after 180000ms. FIFO and database ownership remain held until physical settlement; expiration never admits overlapping replacement work.

If native settlement remains pending after the existing 5000ms retirement grace, the Gateway recovery owner verifies its live native service and Node command, then requests forced fresh-process recovery through the existing shutdown and hard-exit path. Required fresh-process recovery cannot fall back to an in-process restart. Concurrent requests coalesce and a worker that settles during verification cancels recovery. Unmanaged, external-supervisor, embedded, disabled-respawn or unavailable-native-service instances remain report-only.

The accepted native recovery records and awaits the existing boot-lifecycle completion before shutdown watchdogs or teardown. That native reason survives forced process death, so a successor with another stuck worker within five minutes remains report-only. The existing consumed boot ID prevents a later generic shutdown deadline overwriting the native reason.

Native systemd capability is prepared before workers start: lazy dependency initialization otherwise calls Node's diagnostic-report API, which waits for the stuck worker and deadlocks recovery. Actual service/Node verification remains live at recovery time.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair reuses the archive FIFO, scoped archive worker, reconciliation WorkerTaskPool and Gateway process lifecycle. Schemas, canonical transcript bytes, retention and final archive-publication rules are unchanged. Whole-process death may leave an unreferenced staging artifact; no new orphan-cleanup policy is introduced. Existing best-effort boot-history persistence policy is preserved.

## Evidence

Final source and actual runtime build: `989b30680025e029885e77e6aeefb3c1cc7626a5`.

[Immutable evidence index, complete logs, drivers, receipts, hashes and limitations](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/1dfe0de7623a8ef25ed67a11dbbb807a90382f23/README.md).

- **Permanent archive recovery:** real native fsync remains blocked through the unchanged 180-second budget and five-second grace. FIFO/native/staging custody remains held. The service replaces PID 629111 with 632652 without releasing the fault; both archive retries match exact canonical rows, retained history is readable and SQLite integrity passes.
- **Forced-death cooldown RED/GREEN:** the pre-repair production baseline kills its successor again 225.2 seconds after the first death and queues another service restart. Final head records the native planned-restart row durably while the old process is still alive. After its physical death, the successor holds a second permanent native fsync for 205.125 seconds without restarting, logs the five-minute report-only cooldown, and retains native custody and canonical rows. [Baseline failure](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/1dfe0de7623a8ef25ed67a11dbbb807a90382f23/cooldown-upgrade/native-baseline/cooldown-successor.json), [pre-kill durable row](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/1dfe0de7623a8ef25ed67a11dbbb807a90382f23/cooldown-upgrade/native-archive/durable-native-recovery-before-kill.json), [successor result](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/1dfe0de7623a8ef25ed67a11dbbb807a90382f23/cooldown-upgrade/native-archive/cooldown-successor.json).
- **Permanent reconciliation recovery:** startup SQLite pread stays blocked, and the durable lease/canonical rows remain held without cleanup overlap. After physical death, PID 629566 is replaced by 632844; the dead lease is reclaimed, successor reconciliation and authenticated history rebuild the index, and canonical rows and SQLite integrity remain intact. A separate pre-fault credential migration restart is explicitly distinguished in the receipts.
- **Official stable upgrade:** verified npm `2026.10.6` creates two conversations/four canonical rows and non-default settings. Candidate Doctor succeeds. Both candidate boots retain every original JSON/compressed transcript byte and selected settings; authenticated history works, and a third conversation's two new rows survive another clean restart. [Stable package identity](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/1dfe0de7623a8ef25ed67a11dbbb807a90382f23/cooldown-upgrade/stable-install/install.receipt.json), [upgrade/restart receipt](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/1dfe0de7623a8ef25ed67a11dbbb807a90382f23/cooldown-upgrade/stable-upgrade/upgrade-v2.receipt.json), [final settings/history/integrity](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/1dfe0de7623a8ef25ed67a11dbbb807a90382f23/cooldown-upgrade/stable-upgrade/candidate-restart-v2-integrity.json).
- The new ordering regression fails before the repair and passes after; all six runtime-unavailable cases pass. Scoped type-aware core lint, config-cli types, formatting and diff checks pass. Independent P0-P2 review of the final delta is scoped-clean, with its context/execution limitations retained. Earlier custody, retirement, FIFO, import-closure and service-recovery validation remains linked in the evidence index.
- Failed fixture admission, a lint prerequisite timeout, and the first upgrade comparison's null-prototype-object mismatch are retained and explained. The corrected upgrade comparison normalizes representation while still comparing every original byte; no product code or expected data was changed for that proof correction. Final native scenarios use unchanged production timeouts and never release injected faults to obtain a passing result.

The actual main merge conflict is resolved using exact current-main hook-fixture bytes; that fixture is no longer part of this PR's diff. The final cooldown repair adds 10 production lines and 48 test lines. Permanent recovery and its cooldown remain one coherent availability repair.

## Maintainer Decision

The contributor recommends bounded admission, retirement and verified-service recovery. Upstream acceptance of the fixed limits and automatic escalation remains outstanding: overload can be rejected and slow healthy work can be retired. This PR does not claim authority to grant that owner decision.

The incident's underlying memory-growth cause is not established by this availability repair. Final-head CI and ClawSweeper's verdict remain separate gates, not implied by evidence publication.

prs.title: fix: avoid false startup status during observed chat progress
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes “Waiting for turn to start…” appearing while the Control UI is already displaying progress from a run started by another client, including after that progress moves into history.

## User Impact

The active claw stays visible while work continues. The misleading startup label disappears once that run has shown activity. A new turn can still show its initial wait, and explicit model-wait and recovery statuses remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing known-run identities when choosing the startup label, recognize received activity items, and carry the observed activity into the same run when history adopts it. Connection and run cleanup are unchanged; no timer or additional state store is introduced.

## Evidence

Reproduced in the compiled Control UI on `2f5cb8110d7` through synthetic Gateway events: an existing session receives a remote run and completed progress item before the browser adopts that run. The regression also covers persisted progress with a compact history response, completion, the next turn, and a late event from the previous run.

| ![Progress shown with an incorrect startup wait](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/517422bc-dce3-4afd-bca7-ac14c4424a9f) | ![Progress shown with the active claw and no incorrect startup wait](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8c027dc8-5447-4424-8c64-4081956ac812) |

- Compiled UI E2E: **4/4** pass; `pnpm test ui/src/e2e/chat-startup-progress.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` took **28.79 s** wall time.
- Recovery, model-wait, and tool/approval checks: **35/35** pass. The changed recovery file took **2.26 s** wall time for **6 tests**.
- UI typecheck, targeted lint/format, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Production change: **+12 net lines**; tests: **+136 lines**. CI passed on this head ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40012989254)). In CI, the four browser scenarios took **3.407 s**, including **0.955 s** for the new regression.

**Risk and coverage:** This proves a supported observer flow, not the exact original browser event sequence, which was not captured. No Gateway runtime, provider, or persisted-data behavior changes.

prs.title: fix(discord): Doctor warns recovery coverage is unknown for a disposable cache
prs.body:
Closes #180960

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Doctor warns that Discord migration recovery coverage is unknown, though the migration only discards a rebuildable cache.

## User Impact

Doctor no longer shows this warning for Discord.

## Why This Change Was Made

The migration now declares an empty backup inventory, as Matrix, Microsoft Teams, and Nostr do for migrations with no data to retain.

## Evidence

Real `pnpm openclaw doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive` on the same tree, with and without the one-line declaration. Isolated `HOME` and state dir, Discord enabled, legacy `discord/command-deploy-cache.json` present.

Both runs, raw output:
```
[state-migrations] Auto-migrated legacy state:
- Removed Discord command deployment cache legacy source (state/discord/command-deploy-cache.json)
...
└  Doctor complete.
exit=0
```

Plugin ids under `warnings` (`undeclared-migration-resources`) in the recovery capture `manifest.json`:
```
before: discord line matrix memory-lancedb zalouser
after:  line matrix memory-lancedb zalouser
```

The warning that goes away:
```
discord migration recovery coverage is unknown: no backup inventory was declared. Update the plugin to a version with migration backup support. ...
```

`channels.discord` is identical before and after the run (`enabled`, `token`), and `state/discord/` is empty in both. The other four warnings are unchanged.

- `src/plugins/doctor-migration-resources.test.ts`: red without the fix, 18 pass with it.
- Doctor contract declaration guards, format, and core test typecheck pass.
- Upgrade from the published release: state written by `openclaw@2026.10.6` (Discord enabled), legacy cache file added, then this PR's `doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive`. Isolated `HOME`, output (config values and paths shortened):
```
$ ls ~/.openclaw/discord
command-deploy-cache.json
$ pnpm openclaw doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive
[state-migrations] Auto-migrated legacy state:
- Removed Discord command deployment cache legacy source (~/.openclaw/discord/command-deploy-cache.json)
...
└  Doctor complete.
exit=0
$ ls ~/.openclaw/discord
(empty)
channels.discord before: {"enabled": true, "token": "<redacted>"}
channels.discord after:  {"enabled": true, "token": "<redacted>"}
manifest.json warnings (pluginId): line matrix memory-lancedb zalouser
```
Discord is absent from the warnings, the other four remain, and only the cache file left the state dir. `openclaw@2026.10.6` itself records no recovery warnings.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep Details stable while sections load
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Details growing and shrinking while its pull-request renderer loads, and Outputs waiting for the Details module before starting its data read.

## User Impact

Known pull requests keep the same row height through loading, while People and other Details controls remain usable. Outputs loads alongside the Details module after the initial chat paint, releases its demand when closed, and preserves explicit mobile access during history loading.

## Why This Change Was Made

The pending and final PR rows share one projection, including recovered publication receipts. The existing session admission owner controls automatic Outputs reads; connection replacement retires only the Details-owned demand before checkout reset can replay it. Files keeps its independent demand. No timer, polling, cache, or Gateway contract was added.

Depends on #181855. That parent fixes publication receipt settlement; this PR fixes the remaining module-loading geometry and Outputs acquisition lifecycle.

## Evidence

The screenshots compare **parent #181855** with this candidate, with the same PR module held pending. Both use sanitized synthetic data in the production UI.

| Before: parent #181855 | After: this PR |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: five loading rows for one known PR](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c91d6ac6-5208-45aa-a94d-d6dda20ba84c) | ![After: one loading row matching the known PR](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0ec4338d-8386-4d00-9234-b101adf0f5c1) |

- PR loading body: **179 → 32 px**; final PR body: **32 px**. Multiple PRs and an unmatched recovered receipt also preserve height. People remains interactive, mounted, expanded, and focused when the module arrives.
- Desktop Outputs: no read while offline or while initial history is pending; one read after history settles, including failure, while the Details module is still held. Closing, receiving an update while hidden, and reopening produces one catch-up read.
- Two direct connected-client replacements preserve Files demand and release stale Details demand; repeated old cleanup callbacks remain harmless. Explicit mobile access works during pending history and stops while hidden.
- Regressions reject the old behavior: **147 px** loading-height mismatch, missing parallel Outputs read, premature offline demand, and stale demand replay on connection replacement.
- Focused tests, UI/test types, and asset budgets pass. One pre-existing Solid reactivity warning remains on an unchanged expression in `chat-pane-runtime-view.tsx`. Fresh native Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 issue. It inspected the supplied full admission, hydration, field projection, connection replacement, Outputs binding, workspace-demand and mobile-retention owners against the delta; surrounding runtime wiring and test infrastructure were not audited, and it did not rerun tests.

Risk and coverage: this is not a claim of faster boot or removal of every network-dependent section arrival. Five paired timing samples include a slower shell maximum and one extra pinned-session lookup burst; attribution remains limited. Context is outside this change. Proof uses a synthetic Gateway, not private live sessions.

<details>
<summary>Performance measurements and test cost</summary>

Five alternating parent/candidate pairs used the same production build settings and workload: 390 sessions, 30 pins, 120 people, 24 transcript messages, 12 inline widgets, and 35 ms synthetic RPC latency. HTTP cache was warm, CPU unthrottled, tracing disabled. Host load average was 9.2–9.7.

| Metric, ms | Parent median [min–max] | Candidate median [min–max] |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Shell interactive | 208.4 [204.2–262.5] | 213.1 [204.6–325.0] |
| Composer enabled | 289.2 [243.1–350.0] | 301.2 [292.7–325.0] |
| Transcript visible | 306.1 [288.7–350.4] | 301.6 [293.0–325.3] |

At five samples, nearest-rank p95 equals the maximum. The shell maximum is 23.8% higher, so this does not establish a boot speed improvement. Parent long tasks: four at 77–84 ms and one run with none; candidate: five at 64–84 ms. Parent RPC totals were 51/51/51/52/51; candidate 79/51/51/51/51. The 28 extra requests describe distinct pinned sessions through the unchanged sidebar owner after the shell appears; they are not repeated Outputs requests. Outputs itself made exactly one request after startup in all five candidate runs.

One separate profiled diagnostic pair recorded 60 pane projections in both builds: 37.6/35.2 ms total synchronous render time, 0.1/0.5 ms total Outputs projection time, and 0.9/0.9 ms applying three Gateway snapshots. Those methods first ran after the shell milestone. The fallback adds no request; its helper stays in an existing Chat chunk. Profiled timings are not pooled with the untraced samples.

Final build: initial CSS remains 236,734 raw / 40,195 gzip bytes in one request; Chat CSS remains 857,068 raw / 137,169 gzip bytes in three requests. Chat JavaScript stays at 21 requests; raw bytes change by +1,159 and gzip by +949. Asset budgets pass; no budget was changed.

Focused validation: 70 distinct unit/component cases across the PR, Outputs, hydration, connection lifecycle and mobile suites; 22 browser component cases; four new production E2E scenarios. Measured wall time: 4.22 s for the 64-case owner batch, 3.09 s for the 27-case mobile/lifecycle batch (shared cases counted once above), and 26.10 s for the two warm-reload E2E cases including the production build. Individual new E2E cases cost 1.959 / 0.848 / 2.612 / 2.579 s. The new connection regressions stay in the existing lifecycle suite. CI [run 40024025144](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40024025144) passed on `2cc36a9339b7f35f28649b8528eddc67f0d5aa18`. The four new E2E cases took 8.551 s as a file (individual cases: 1.550 / 1.501 / 2.747 / 2.601 s). The two added lifecycle cases took 0.668 s combined (mobile: 0.589 s; connection retirement: 0.079 s), within the 22-case lifecycle file at 1.974 s. The modified nine-case PR browser file took 34.339 s. These are CI-reported test execution durations, not full job wall times.

The warm-reload fixture initially failed before reaching the product boundary because its default authentication did not persist a boot record; it now uses the existing trusted-proxy fixture contract. A lifecycle setup assertion was corrected to await the actual asynchronous startup request. No timeout, retry, or assertion weakening was added.

</details>

prs.title: fix: keep PR publication progress accurate and rows stable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a misleading **Retry** warning during an accepted PR publication and a temporary tall card in Details while PR metadata is loading.

## User Impact

Details keeps showing **Creating…** while publication is pending. A confirmed PR immediately has a compact, usable link and action menu; its title and checks arrive in the same row without losing keyboard focus.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Environment trigger now shares the publication status projection used by the recovery details. Confirmed publication receipts join the existing PR list by their URL, and the same row/menu renders before and after metadata arrives. Only the corresponding PR can acknowledge that receipt when hidden. Unavailable reads, failed publication, unknown outcomes, and confirmation remain distinct.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through the compiled Control UI on `main` at `c9b30315e27`: accepted publication displayed Retry; the confirmed receipt row was 58 px tall and became 32 px after metadata arrived.
- The corrected row stays **32 → 32 px**. Link, menu trigger, and focused Hide item survive metadata arrival. An unrelated PR neither hides the confirmed receipt nor acknowledges it when dismissed.
- The flow emits one publication request, one status read, and no confirmation request. Existing personal/shared/guest recovery, idempotent retry, account selection, and permission scenarios pass.
- **38 browser E2E tests and 59 component tests passed.** Final lifecycle suite was rerun after removing capture instrumentation: 6/6 passed. UI typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 issues.

| Stage | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accepted publication, between requests | ![Before: accepted publication incorrectly offers Retry](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/133e479d-ddcf-4873-aa77-c833b5a6fb06) | ![After: accepted publication remains Creating](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/590bd0bd-5fb2-4581-b011-3954b548dd56) |
| Confirmed URL, metadata still pending | ![Before: temporary repository and branch card](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5a5b3bcf-b126-45bd-ba0b-546a95aaff3e) | ![After: compact confirmed PR link and stable action menu](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0bf56a4c-f5f5-4aa8-949d-b7a2e8d10446) |

The captures use the same synthetic scenario. The height measurement is for the PR row, not the entire Details panel.

### Risk and coverage

This changes presentation only. Publication admission, receipt ownership, idempotency, the Gateway protocol, and refresh scheduling keep their existing owners. PR status and checks are shown only when supplied by metadata. Validation uses the real compiled UI with synthetic delayed Gateway responses; it does not recreate a historical browser trace or make a live GitHub publication through the product. Chromium was exercised locally; broader CI, including other browser coverage where selected, is pending.

Focused test cost (`--maxWorkers=1`, repository wrappers): the three browser suites took 84.16 s wall including their shared production build. The final lifecycle file took 29.86 s wall / 10.07 s test time; its two new regressions took 1.55 s and 1.43 s. The existing publication and guest files took 48.51 s and 5.60 s test time. The three component files took 1.89 s wrapper wall / 1.25 s runner wall. CI seconds are pending. Browser proof protects compiled rendering, focus, geometry, and actual Gateway request counts that a component mock cannot establish.

Simplification pass: no new state owner, cache, timer, or request path. Production changes add 66 net lines; test changes add 138 net lines. The additional menu guards keep metadata-dependent CI controls absent until their real data exists. Lint emitted seven warnings at unchanged Solid control-registration lines; the copy-fixture diagnostics were also reproduced with the base component.

prs.title: perf(gateway): move preference and cookie snapshot flushes off main
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Slow storage can stall unrelated Gateway requests when a TTS preference update flushes its JSON file or browser cookie import creates a synchronous SQLite snapshot.

## User Impact

TTS RPC, slash-command, and CLI preference updates await durable persistence off the main thread. Concurrent updates preserve unrelated fields and their order. Browser cookie import prepares and disposes its coherent snapshot through the existing asynchronous SQLite owner, including committed WAL content.

No schema, file format, configuration, permission, retention, or dependency changes. Public synchronous Plugin SDK setters retain their contract. Browser cookie querying/decryption remains on main; this change moves snapshot work only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The current private-file store's async path still synchronizes native descriptors synchronously. TTS therefore uses one serial worker to invoke the existing private mutation kernel, with lifecycle drainage before pool closure. Published synchronous SDK setters join that same FIFO worker through the existing retained-operation wait support. Async callers use ordinary queue completion; only synchronous SDK calls retain a task handle for their blocking wait. The worker owns the complete read/merge/publish mutation, so sync and async callers cannot overwrite one another’s changes. Browser import deletes its local `VACUUM INTO` and scratch ownership, reusing the existing snapshot operation and joining cleanup on success and failure.

Runtime production LOC is **+91 net** (+167/−76). The requested non-test/non-doc stat is **+553 net** (+630/−77); it also includes 463 lines of benchmark code/documentation and one removed mock-baseline entry. The growth preserves durable private-file publication and the synchronous SDK contract while the dependency fix awaits release; browser snapshot ownership shrinks by nine lines. No new cache or database owner is introduced.

Dependency follow-up: [fs-safe #1031](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/1031) replaces POSIX native staged-file flushes with async `fs.fsync` on retained descriptors. OpenClaw currently uses fs-safe 0.26.11. Its `durable:false` option is unsuitable for retained workspace files, so this PR does not disable workspace durability or add an override. That dependency PR is merged as `c0aa03b408d25d0d26988b92da011f0e7e4fe239`; package version remains 0.26.11 and requires a separately approved release before an OpenClaw dependency update; Windows native flushes are outside its change. TTS JSON remains runtime state that should eventually move to the existing SQLite state owner through a separately approved schema migration.

Related: #181928.

## Evidence

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no remaining actionable P0–P2 runtime or measurement-instrumentation findings. Automated PR review identified a real overlap between synchronous SDK setters and worker mutations; both now use the same worker queue. A new independent review checked FIFO, failure settlement, and native-owner shutdown; its shared-buffer type correction is included. The configured autoreview provider failed preflight because it did not match operator configuration; no configuration changed.

The TTS regression invokes the real `tts.enable` handler and verifies persisted bytes, private modes, zero main-thread synchronous fsync calls, concurrent patch preservation, and malformed-file refusal. The original handler fails with **two** main-thread fsync calls; the candidate passes with **zero**. An additional regression fails on the first PR head, then proves that a synchronous SDK setter waits for two accepted async updates, retains their unrelated fields, and durably applies last. The browser regression fails on the original main-thread `VACUUM`, then passes with a fresh cookie committed only to an active WAL; it also prohibits main-thread snapshot `COMMIT` and verifies failed-preparation cleanup.

Focused TTS/config/RPC/command/CLI and browser tests pass. The core typecheck, changed-file lint/format, export-name collision guard, and import/source-closure tests (22/22) pass. PR CI exposed three newly added mocks without real-export pass-through; they now preserve the real exports. The affected RPC/CLI/slash files pass (127 tests). The mock baseline generator removed its one retired allowlist entry (7130 → 7129); no new exception was added. The malformed-preference slash test additionally checks the real async writer’s specific error so an unrelated exception cannot satisfy it. The repaired queue also passes its 6 preference, 16 config, 37 runtime sibling, and 22 source-closure tests. Broad validation is delegated to PR CI; no remote test lease was allocated. A source-stamp failure caused by concurrent formatting was corrected by rerunning the affected command test on frozen inputs.

[Pre-rebase CI run 40031943298](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40031943298/job/120682797136), like the first PR run, failed `src/flows/doctor-health.deletion-recovery.test.ts` (“refreshes supplied missing-history discovery after maintenance admits a newer configured store”) with `SqliteWorkerError: Shared-state admission requires the host broker`. This is inherited: [main run 40020064421, job 120642282363](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40020064421/job/120642282363) fails the same test with the same error and stack, before the PR run. The test, Doctor health flow, broker guard, and thread-pool configuration are byte-identical between that main head and the pre-rebase PR parent. All checks on pre-rebase head `b9dba114474c9d81c32f3cc860c2122753c64d9f` completed: the Doctor shard is the only failed test job, and the CI gate reflects that failure. Typecheck, lint, other test jobs, dependency review, and security-sensitive review passed. No CI rerun was requested to chase green.

### Paired measurement acceptance

The committed workload uses real isolated Gateway WebSocket `tts.enable`/`tts.disable` requests and verifies preference bytes after each response: 120 paced mutations over 60 seconds, with 50 ms injected per synchronous fsync on both main and worker threads. Two concurrent pairs use disjoint interleaved 16-CPU sets, swapped for the second pair, under one exclusive slot and the shared production guard. Interrupted pairs are discarded.

Required result: main-thread fsync calls/blocked time reach zero without dropping durable work. Report process CPU, all-isolate total GC and promotion, main event-loop p99, sample counts, and baseline/candidate maximum GC pauses. Apply v5.1–v5.3: eligible regressions gate at paired mean ≥20% adverse or ≥10% in both pairs; opposite signs or >5× baseline spread require a third pair if gating. GC pause percentile shifts below 1 ms are context. The first implementation was rejected: process CPU rose 30.79%/38.74% across the two pairs (+34.77% paired mean). Async calls now avoid unnecessary retained-task custody while sharing the same FIFO pool with synchronous setters. The rejected results are not acceptance evidence. The current implementation has two valid swapped pairs, reported below.

Cookie import is macOS-only; Linux Gateway measurements cover TTS. The synthetic macOS cookie-owner test proves snapshot behavior, not end-to-end Chrome/Keychain import latency.


### Current paired results — accepted by maintainer decision

The predeclared steady-workload gates used whole-process CPU, total GC and promotion, plus main event-loop p99. Those metrics pass v5–v5.3. The maintainer explicitly accepted this change on 2026-10-23: **whole-process promotion +2.38% passes; main-isolate promotion +111.49% (+4.16 MB) is context for this change**, given the small absolute increase and removal of a user-visible main-thread stall class. Both promotion measurements are valid; the main-isolate result is neither sample-ineligible nor outside the measurement interval. This is an explicit scoped acceptance decision, not a change to the reported data or a general promotion-gate exemption.

| Metric | Pair 1 baseline → candidate | Pair 2 baseline → candidate | Paired mean change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Main sync flushes | 240 → 0 | 240 → 0 | −100% |
| Total durable flushes | 240 → 240 | 240 → 240 | unchanged |
| Main blocked time, ms/min | 12,868.886 → 0 | 12,381.431 → 0 | −12,625.159 ms/min |
| Event-loop p99, ms | 108.265 → 10.904; n=4,726/5,962 | 108.134 → 10.977; n=4,769/5,957 | −97.260 ms; −89.89% |
| Whole-process CPU, ms | 2,267.486 → 2,719.395 (+19.93%) | 2,518.353 → 2,740.849 (+8.83%) | +337.203 ms; +14.38% |
| Whole-process GC, ms | 167.212 → 166.978 (−0.234 ms; −0.14%) | 180.297 → 187.760 (+7.463 ms; +4.14%) | +3.614 ms; +2.00%; opposite signs: inconclusive |
| Whole-process promotion, bytes | 176,321,400 → 184,140,200 (+7,818,800; +4.43%) | 176,585,120 → 177,145,528 (+560,408; +0.32%) | +4,189,604 bytes; +2.38% |
| Main-isolate promotion, bytes | 3,730,088 → 11,829,112 (+8,099,024; +217.13%) | 3,664,192 → 3,878,568 (+214,376; +5.85%) | +4,156,700 bytes; +111.49% |
| Maximum single GC pause, ms | 18.183 → 17.730 | 20.867 → 18.253 | Both candidates below the 50 ms floor |
| Cold first write, ms; n=1 per side | 40.116 → 573.134 | 41.856 → 779.504 | +635.333 ms |

Main CPU is also inconclusive: +102.540 ms/+20.64% and −37.682 ms/−6.14%. Minor GC counts are 135→167 and 133→201; major counts are 16→17 and 17→17. Neither GC percentile has enough samples on both sides to gate, and maximum pauses remain below the v5.1 limit. Warm RPC mean latency is effectively unchanged (109.545→109.376 ms and 105.658→105.720 ms); its n=120 per side does not support a gating p95/p99. No guard interrupted either pair.

Cold latency was measured before injection, outside the predeclared steady interval. The exclusion follows that interval definition, not an exemption for low sample counts: the extra 533/738 ms is a real source-mode worker-startup cost. Whole-Gateway midpoint RSS also rose 202/106 MiB; this includes source-loader overhead and is not a retained TTS heap measurement. Production-build cold startup has not been measured.

The common source archive is `02e5fd188e88` plus the candidate overlay. SHA256 checks match current-head TTS owners, handler and instrumentation. The measured process manifest differs from the latest main only by an unrelated automatic-update cleanup registration; its TTS entry is identical. This is controlled source-mode TTS evidence, not a measurement of every file on the latest PR head. Raw traces, source hashes, and both paired distribution summaries were inspected before acceptance, including the rejected first attempt; task scratch was removed after merge. Independent raw-trace parsing reproduced the main-isolate promotion result; the first two measured collections account for most of its pair-1 increase and are correctly included.


### Final conflict repair and simplification

Rebased onto `c6facd08e4b5aa14c4424a716f097388537f52ae`; final head `3644bc60823e7db601d09a0d69dc87c5dbe7b0f4`. The only conflict was independent appended sections in `scripts/perf/README.md`; both sections were preserved. Runtime code and tests are unchanged from the independently reviewed, measured head. Diff whitespace and the resolved README formatter checks pass. [Exact-head CI run 40035625531](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40035625531) passed, including all test jobs and its aggregate CI check. Dependency and security-sensitive reviews passed. The rebase picked up #181964, which fixes the formerly inherited Doctor test, so no inherited-failure exception is needed for this head. Prior-head failures above are historical attribution evidence. No CI rerun was requested.

A second simplification pass found no worthwhile safe deletion. The old main-thread read/merge/write path is removed completely. Existing Promise-based queue helpers cannot progress while a synchronous SDK caller waits, while the shared worker pool already owns FIFO order. The small synchronous adapter is required by the published SDK contract; it is not a second mutation implementation. Runtime remains **+91 LOC**; removing a single redundant idle-timeout default would not simplify the ownership model.

### Cold-write visibility and existing UI acknowledgement

The Control UI has no direct TTS preference-RPC toggle: its TTS settings editor uses the separate `config.set`/`config.apply` path. `/tts` is sent through normal chat, which already acknowledges input before preference persistence. The UI clears the composer and retains the queued row before sending (`ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send-submit.ts`), and the Gateway responds with `status: "started"` before calling `startChatDispatch` (`src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-input-dispatch.ts`). Thus the initial UI acknowledgement does not wait for the cold TTS worker.

The extra **533–738 ms is still visible in the final command confirmation and setting effect**, and direct RPC/CLI completion also waits. It can recur after the writer's 60-second idle retirement. Final success remains after durable persistence so malformed-file/disk errors reach the caller and immediate read-after-write remains valid. The in-memory worker queue drains on orderly shutdown; acknowledging that the preference was saved merely after enqueue would not establish crash durability. The existing early chat acknowledgement already provides the requested prompt UI response without weakening the final persistence result. No UI code or visual layout changed. Production-build cold startup remains unmeasured.

prs.title: feat(cron): give scheduled runs their parent conversation's memory audience
prs.body:
Builds on #179011 (merged), #178933, #179834 and #178965 (all merged). It uses #179011's per-run registry. Rebased onto main; the conflict with #181359's cross-agent memory lineage was additive, and both `resolveAgentStorePath` and `scheduledParent` are kept.

Related: #178812
Related: #178811

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a scheduled run created from a conversation reads an empty memory store. The memory audience is resolved from the cron run's own session row. That row is neither a direct-chat root nor a spawned child with lineage receipts, so the native memory provider gets no audience. For example, a knowledge-ingest automation created in the owner's direct chat finds no knowledge.

## User Impact

User impact: an automation linked to the exact conversation that created it now gets that conversation's memory audience on each run.
- A child of the owner's direct chat gets owner-private memory when this occurrence's requester check confirms owner status.
- A child of a group, channel or non-owner conversation gets that conversation's memory.
- A requester who has lost owner status loses the private partition on the next run, and no spawn receipt anywhere in the parent's lineage can restore it.
- An automation that runs inside its linked conversation keeps that conversation's audience. It also gets the occurrence's owner bit instead of the scheduler's missing sender bit.
- Jobs without a conversation link (operator- or CLI-created) and jobs that store only a session key resolve memory from their run row, as today.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **One owner for audiences.** `resolveMemoryAudienceFromEntry` in `src/plugins/memory-audience.ts` still mints every audience. It now accepts an optional `scheduledParent`: the exact parent incarnation and owner bit from the run's execution context (#178933). This plays the role a spawn receipt plays for subagents, as the first lineage hop:
  - the run row and the parent each hold a session generation lease;
  - the parent must still be the linked incarnation;
  - the root chat type picks the partition;
  - a later parent reset revokes the grant before provider I/O.

  A link that recorded no lifecycle revision proves only the session id, matching the pause check in #178965.
  A parent already reset when the occurrence is admitted does not pause the job (#178965): the context builds that occurrence as an unbound parent, so it resolves memory from its own run row, as before this PR.
- **The occurrence caps owner status.** Whenever a scheduled parent is supplied, this occurrence's requester result is an upper bound for the whole lineage walk. A spawned parent's receipt, or a spawned session the run executes in, cannot grant owner-private memory after the requester check failed.
- **Who can name the parent.** The link is host-stamped at creation: an agent caller's job records the caller's own session (`captureCronCreatorSession`). Only trusted operator clients without a caller scope can name another session. A model in a group cannot point a job at another conversation's memory. A job restored from a Control UI operator source is parent-linked by design (#178933) and takes its owner bit from the restored operator authority.
- **In-session runs.** When the parent is the run's own session, the resolver checks that the admitted row is still the linked incarnation and applies the occurrence's owner bit. It does not hop to itself.
- **Wiring.** The execution-context registry from #179011 exposes the parent for the admitted run. The embedded attempt and the CLI loopback grant both resolve through `resolveEmbeddedAttemptMemoryAudience`, which now takes the run's own inputs as one object and reads the parent itself. That keeps the embedded dispatch file under its line cap.
- **Codex harness.** Core resolves the attempt's memory audience in `run-attempt-dispatch.ts` before any harness runs and passes it to Codex as `memoryAudience`, so Codex scheduled runs get the parent audience too.
- **Not covered here:** the memory-flush path during compaction.

## Evidence

- **End to end through both runtimes** (`src/cron/execution-context-memory-audience.test.ts`): a real occurrence admission and run admission bind the context; the embedded resolver and the CLI loopback resolver each mint the run's audience; a provider is bound to it with the host's `bindMemoryProvider`. Session rows and generation leases come from the shared fake session owner used by the resolver tests.
  - An owner's direct-chat child gets owner-private memory on both runtimes, and the bound provider is reached.
  - A non-owner requester, and a group parent, get only the conversation's memory.
  - A parent reset mid-run refuses provider I/O on both runtimes before the provider is called.
  - A requester who loses owner status gets only the conversation's memory on the next run.
  - A key-only job and a job with no recorded requester never reach the parent's private memory.
  - With the registry's parent hop removed (the base behavior), the five grant and revocation tests fail.
- **Resolver tests** (`src/plugins/memory-audience.test.ts`): scheduled child grants, stale links, session-id-only links and in-session runs; the owner cap holds through a spawned parent's lineage, for an in-session run on a spawned row, and for a run on a spawned session other than its linked parent. Removing the cap fails the cap tests.
- **Rebased onto `main` with #181916**, which fixed the scheduled requester owner check for channel (Discord) requesters. The mocked scheduled-parent passthrough case in `attempt-memory-audience.test.ts` was dropped, as ClawSweeper suggested; the cron composition suite covers that path end to end.
- **Related suites** (memory audience, attempt memory audience, CLI MCP memory audience, MCP HTTP and tool-resolution memory audience, cron execution context): pass.
- **QA lab:** the bundled QA lab has no native memory provider, so the live proof below uses a local proof plugin and scenarios that are not part of this PR.
- **Static replay on a real Gateway's state copy:** the three exact-parent jobs (two child runs and one in-session knowledge-ingest job) gain the parent memory audience, as intended. Every other job keeps resolving from its run row. Nothing is lost, gained unexpectedly or paused.
- **Checks:** `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` are clean; type-aware oxlint and oxfmt are clean; the line-cap and mock-export ratchets pass.
- **Autoreview (Codex, P0–P2):** two P1 findings about owner status through spawned lineage were fixed with tests. A later P2 assumed jobs restored from a Control UI operator source should not inherit; that contradicts the #178933 design, where such jobs are parent-linked, so it was declined.

### Live behavior proof (real Gateway, head `d5ef50d0b65`)

A scratch build of this head adds a native memory provider (`kind: "native"`) that logs the host-minted audience for every `open`, `search` and probe call. QA scenarios then create jobs through the Gateway and force-run them (`mock-openai`, real Gateway child process). The scenarios and plugin are local proof tooling only.

| Scenario | This PR | `main` without this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Embedded: operator-chat parent → owner-private memory | pass | denied (`no host-minted memory audience`) |
| Embedded: channel DM job without an authenticated requester → that conversation only | pass | denied |
| Embedded: group parent → that group's conversation only | pass | denied |
| Embedded: parent reset mid-run → provider refuses before I/O | pass (0 opens/searches after reset) | n/a |
| CLI loopback: operator-chat parent → owner-private | pass | denied |
| CLI loopback: group parent → that group only | pass | denied |
| CLI loopback: parent reset mid-run → refused | pass | n/a |
| Upgrade from v2026.10.6 | jobs and settings intact | — |
| Embedded, Discord owner DM job: owner → owner-private; requester removed from `commands.ownerAllowFrom` → next occurrence gets that DM conversation only | pass | — |
| CLI loopback, same Discord owner DM job flow (`provider=qa-memory-cli`) | pass | — |

<details><summary>Provider audience log (embedded, redacted)</summary>

```text
op=probe  run=agent:qa:qa-channel:direct:dm:qa-operator  audience=owner-private            OWNER-PRIVATE-NOTE   (baseline: owner DM itself)
op=probe  run=agent:qa:cron:e7feb612…                    audience=owner-private            OWNER-PRIVATE-NOTE   (operator-chat parent)
op=probe  run=agent:qa:cron:fcec7d86…                    audience=conversation:<owner DM>  CONVERSATION-NOTE    (DM job, no authenticated requester)
op=probe  run=agent:qa:cron:ed38fd05…                    audience=conversation:<group>     CONVERSATION-NOTE    (group parent)
op=probe  run=agent:qa:cron:fbc0b993…                    audience=owner-private            OWNER-PRIVATE-NOTE   (before reset)
op=probe  run=agent:qa:cron:fbc0b993…                    current=rejected  "memory audience is no longer current"  (after parent reset)
```

CLI loopback produced the same pattern: owner-private → group conversation only → `rejected` after reset. On `main` the same scenarios log `audience=null` and the probe is denied with `no host-minted memory audience`.
</details>

<details><summary>Requester revocation, Discord (crabline local provider, redacted)</summary>

The job is created by the agent from a Discord owner DM, so the host records the authenticated Discord requester. It is force-run, then `commands.ownerAllowFrom` is replaced so it no longer names that sender, and the same job is force-run again. Provider `open` calls:

```text
embedded  occurrence 1  run=agent:qa:cron:efa01f6f…:run:6645c187…  audience=owner-private                         OWNER-PRIVATE-NOTE
embedded  occurrence 2  run=agent:qa:cron:efa01f6f…:run:885d96bb…  audience=conversation:<discord owner DM>       CONVERSATION-NOTE
cli       occurrence 1  run=agent:qa:cron:7cc1dbdb…:run:df522597…  audience=owner-private                         OWNER-PRIVATE-NOTE
cli       occurrence 2  run=agent:qa:cron:7cc1dbdb…:run:9e7f6c19…  audience=conversation:<discord owner DM>       CONVERSATION-NOTE
```

No owner-private `open`, `search` or probe follows the revocation on either runtime.
</details>

**Upgrade.** v2026.10.6 created a parent conversation and two jobs (one linked, one unlinked) on isolated state. This build then ran `doctor --fix` and started on the same state. Both jobs came through with their schedule, payload, delivery and parent link unchanged; the only job diff is doctor's existing migration of the built-in heartbeat job. Both Gateways report `2026.10.6` because this branch does not bump the package version; the second one ran from this PR's source.

### Known limitation (outside this PR; fails closed)

- **Older operator chats.** Parents created on v2026.10.6 or earlier have no stored chat type. #181359 stamps it only on new operator chats and has no doctor backfill, so jobs linked to those parents still get no memory audience after upgrade. That matches pre-PR behavior and leaks nothing. Tracked separately.

prs.title: fix(docker): preserve SDK imports for bundled plugin helpers
prs.body:
Closes #181950

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the shipped 1Password SecretRef resolver failing at startup with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` in Docker because it cannot import `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*`.

## User Impact

Bundled plugin helpers can resolve the host SDK from their packaged locations in the Docker image. Omitted plugins are still removed, and npm package exclusions are unchanged.

This fixes SDK module resolution. The separate root-owned interpreter admission issue in #134446 remains unchanged; this PR does not claim that all default Docker SecretRef setup paths are repaired.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root package excludes `dist/extensions/node_modules/**` from npm artifacts. The shared collector mistakenly classified that dependency directory as an omitted plugin, so Docker pruning deleted the generated SDK alias used by plugin-scoped scripts. Exclude that reserved directory from plugin IDs at the existing collector. No Dockerfile workaround, per-plugin import fallback, new alias generator, or dependency is needed.

This follows the same repair proposed in the closed, unmerged [#157206](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157206) by [xydigitLybnnnn](https://github.com/xydigitLybnnnn), with additional runtime evidence for the 1Password report.

## Evidence

- **Main fails:** [owner regression baseline](https://github.com/grootbro/openclaw-contributions/actions/runs/40029945121/job/120675430675) uses production code from `74cb12dd2c7597f0d9a388b94bb2b776cac6db25`. The collector returns `node_modules` as an omitted plugin; actual pruning followed by a real Node ESM import fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. Both new regressions fail; 19 existing tests pass.
- **Main Docker:** [official Dockerfile baseline](https://github.com/grootbro/openclaw-contributions/actions/runs/40029945121/job/120675430975) builds successfully, then the unbundled resolver fails with `Cannot find package 'openclaw' imported from /app/dist/extensions/onepassword/onepassword-secret-ref-resolver.js`. Node 24.22.1, default image user `node` (UID 1000), no network.
- **Fixed Docker:** [final Docker acceptance](https://github.com/grootbro/openclaw-contributions/actions/runs/40032196994/job/120682913888) succeeds on public [`proof/docker-plugin-sdk-alias@65067ed0`](https://github.com/grootbro/openclaw-contributions/tree/65067ed08d2ce07f79b7c34b1cca803c3fb33949): exit 0, two verified `op` calls, SDK alias present, failure output redacted, npm dependency-exclusion declaration retained.
- **Final-head checks:** [77 tests passed across seven owner/consumer suites](https://github.com/grootbro/openclaw-contributions/actions/runs/40033973435/job/120688813997), with one existing macOS-only voice-rpath case skipped on Linux. Formatting, type-aware lint and the actual `test.root.scripts` typecheck all pass. Public proof revision [`b3ea99d3`](https://github.com/grootbro/openclaw-contributions/tree/b3ea99d3f9a3c0fac020cdda5ec69aaeb668f350) matches all three final PR files. Upstream [test-types-core-3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40033923689/job/120689663291) also passes after repairing the regression fixture to use the typed `{cwd}` API.

The Docker proof builds the repository's actual Dockerfile with `OPENCLAW_EXTENSIONS=onepassword` and runs the final image as its default unprivileged UID 1000, with networking and capabilities disabled. It invokes the shipped, unbundled resolver. Only the `op` process and token are synthetic; exact arguments and resolver results are verified. The failure case also exercises the dynamic security SDK import and checks token/secret redaction. Executable ownership and private token-file checks remain enabled.

This is direct resolver-process proof, not a live 1Password account or full Gateway credential-setup proof. The synthetic executable and its interpreter are current-user-owned private fixtures. No real credentials are used, no system executable ownership checks are changed, and no root package symlink is installed to make the proof pass.

The larger Docker fixture and fork-only workflows remain on public proof branches, outside this PR. Final production bytes match the successful Docker proof; the later change only uses a real package.json fixture in the collector test. The complete final diff matches the separate final-head checks above.

Test cost on the final regression revision: the two touched files took 840 ms and 35 ms of test time; the new import regression took 34 ms. All seven suites took 57.8 seconds Vitest wall time (62 seconds step; complete quality job 250 seconds). Docker build and acceptance took 417 seconds, with the resolver scenario completing in about two seconds.

The upstream diff is three files: production +2/-1 and regression tests +63. The existing collector keeps ownership; no new runtime machinery or metadata is introduced. Independent read-only cloud-agent review found no P0–P2 findings.

The earlier fixed-image job [120676755113](https://github.com/grootbro/openclaw-contributions/actions/runs/40030340912/job/120676755113) passed all resolver/security assertions, then timed out in an auxiliary `npm pack --dry-run` inventory scan after 120 seconds. That job remains failed. Full image npm inventory equality is unverified; the final acceptance checks the retained exclusion declaration, not an npm file-list comparison. `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and the Dockerfile are unchanged.

## Upstream CI

[CI on final head `09420029`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40033923689) has completed: 32 jobs pass, including build artifacts, lint and all test typecheck lanes. The compact tooling shard fails in two pre-existing `tsdown-config.test.ts` relocated fs-safe cases: missing `p-map` at runtime and a rejected `worker-chunk` import. [A separate unchanged-main run](https://github.com/grootbro/openclaw-contributions/actions/runs/40033973435/job/120688813830) at `74cb12dd` reproduces both exact errors with Node 24.22.1. That baseline job and the overall proof workflow remain red; the final-head focused job linked above is green. The aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` is therefore red. These failures are not waived or claimed fixed by this PR.

The separate [Auto response failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40034582238/job/120690801773) is a Barnacle `owner`-read TypeError in the upstream workflow.
