prs.title: perf(gateway): retain task PR lineage across row updates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session PR subscriptions repeat task-lineage selection and target preparation when unrelated session display or activity updates publish the shared row revision. The lineage stays unchanged, but its cache becomes cold.

## User Impact and Change

The existing row owner now publishes a task-lineage revision for identity, parent, removal, topology, configuration, and uncertain-metadata changes. Lineage retains compact identities; current rows are reused only within their sharing revision. Retained PR targets validate their own source facts and live viewer authority. Obsolete display graphs can be collected, and own-profile targets retain their existing creator/binding validation path. No configuration or schema changes.

Production delta: **85 lines added, 25 removed, net +60**. This growth separates lineage, current-row, and source-readiness lifetimes within the existing owner. It removes the global-revision rebuild of retained PR targets without adding a competing selection implementation. The row cache is necessary: the first candidate saved allocation but regressed subscription mean latency 27.19% and was rejected. The final revision below fixes that regression to within the predeclared acceptance limits.

## Measurement

Accepted after two concurrent, swapped pairs on an isolated Linux sandbox: baseline `40172b9e4ff2f2f47def87b8105370d915a669b1`, candidate `41c993116647248d034a2c87abc9cfab5649e82d`. One exclusive slot, interleaved CPUs, identical separate synthetic state, synchronized starts, shared load/dirty-page/event-loop guard; both valid pairs completed without interruption. Both sides used 16 logical CPUs. Preparation used a separate CPU range and low scheduling weights.

Workload: 5,000 sessions, 4,000 settled retained runs, eight clients watching 50 targets, 256 subscriptions, 1,000 unrelated category patches at 100 ms intervals, and a sidebar list every eight patches. Each side processed 2,000 canonical notifications. PR frames stayed at 400 and initial/final snapshots matched across all four runs. Parent selections fell **250,755 → 0** and **250,255 → 0**; most eliminated selections were attributed to background `other` work, not the explicit `control-ui-pr` task label. No selection reset occurred.

Notification allocation, CPU, GC, promotion, and event-loop metrics were collected under allocation sampling; CPU includes profile setup/materialization. Subscription timing precedes sampling. These numbers do not establish unprofiled CPU savings. Decimal MB/KB units; paired change is the mean of per-pair deltas, not a ratio of pooled totals.

| Metric | Pair 1 baseline → candidate | Pair 2 baseline → candidate | Paired mean change | Tail samples (baseline/candidate) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Allocated MB/operation | 22.080 → 10.475 | 22.073 → 10.444 | -52.62% (-11.617) | — |
| PR-family KB/tab notification | 1194.357 → 479.756 | 1195.390 → 480.319 | -59.83% (-714.836) | — |
| Instrumented main CPU ms/operation | 27.555 → 16.335 | 27.159 → 16.921 | -39.21% (-10.729) | — |
| Total GC ms/operation | 1.475 → 0.536 | 1.469 → 0.562 | -62.70% (-0.923) | — |
| Promoted KB/operation | 886.453 → 195.641 | 881.020 → 184.064 | -78.52% (-693.883) | — |
| Subscription mean ms | 5.124 → 5.251 | 5.714 → 6.210 | +5.58% (+0.312) | — |
| Subscription p95 ms | 8.584 → 8.961 | 8.144 → 9.065 | +7.85% (+0.649) | 256/256 each pair |
| Notification RPC mean ms | 8.543 → 8.353 | 8.656 → 8.643 | -1.19% (-0.102) | — |
| Notification RPC p95 ms | 10.907 → 10.995 | 11.271 → 11.321 | +0.62% (+0.069) | 1,000/1,000 each pair |
| Notification RPC p99 ms | 19.158 → 14.866 | 20.605 → 16.147 | -22.02% (-4.374) | 1,000/1,000 each pair |
| Notification settlement mean ms | 28.841 → 18.222 | 28.494 → 19.143 | -34.82% (-9.985) | — |
| Notification settlement p95 ms | 43.995 → 31.248 | 42.984 → 32.825 | -26.30% (-11.453) | 1,000/1,000 each pair |
| Notification settlement p99 ms | 51.477 → 36.178 | 53.881 → 40.767 | -27.03% (-14.206) | 1,000/1,000 each pair |
| Event-loop p99 ms | 40.993 → 31.326 | 39.551 → 31.080 | -22.50% (-9.069) | 4,658/4,865; 4,695/4,865 |
| Sidebar list mean ms | 35.235 → 23.650 | 35.127 → 25.185 | -30.59% (-10.763) | — |

The small subscription increase is explicit: mean **+0.312 ms / +5.58%**, p95 **+0.649 ms / +7.85%** (256 samples/side/pair). Neither reaches the predeclared rejection rule: >=20% adverse paired mean, or >=10% adverse in both pairs. Qualified gating metrics have consistent signs and baseline scales below 5×. No third pair is required.

Context-only metrics, including all opposite-sign cases:

| Context-only metric | Pair 1 delta | Pair 2 delta | Paired absolute / relative mean | Samples baseline/candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Subscription p99 ms | -2.135 ms (-16.42%) | +1.002 ms (+10.41%) | -0.567 ms / -3.01% | 256/256 each pair |
| Minor GC p95 ms | -0.664 ms (-26.80%) | -0.472 ms (-20.22%) | -0.568 ms / -23.51% | 744/352; 743/350 |
| Minor GC p99 ms | -0.448 ms (-13.67%) | +0.544 ms (+17.81%) | +0.048 ms / +2.07% | 744/352; 743/350 |
| Major GC p95 ms | -2.944 ms (-17.69%) | +8.640 ms (+59.48%) | +2.848 ms / +20.89% | 12/5; 13/5 |
| Major GC p99 ms | -5.120 ms (-27.21%) | +7.360 ms (+46.56%) | +1.120 ms / +9.68% | 12/5; 13/5 |
| Event-loop maximum ms | -30.278 ms (-37.99%) | +5.865 ms (+10.04%) | -12.206 ms / -13.97% | one maximum per side/pair |
| Sidebar list p95 ms | -12.817 ms (-31.73%) | -11.352 ms (-27.72%) | -12.085 ms / -29.73% | 125/125 each pair |
| Sidebar list p99 ms | -17.050 ms (-33.08%) | -25.077 ms (-42.71%) | -21.063 ms / -37.90% | 125/125 each pair |

Subscription p99, list tails, and minor-GC p99 lack the required samples (p99: 1,000; p95: 200). Major GC has fewer than 50 collections/side. Minor-GC percentile absolute mean changes are below 1 ms, and collection counts fell over 50% while total GC time fell. Opposite-sign context metrics are inconclusive rather than adverse. Event-loop maximum is context; its p99 carries the gate. Maximum single GC pause was **18.786 → 13.671 ms** and **15.754 → 23.049 ms**; both candidate maxima are below `max(50 ms, 2 × baseline max)`.

Heap deltas were +51.76 → −2.92 MB and +64.15 → −17.20 MB; RSS deltas +228.60 → +73.34 MB and +228.90 → +93.77 MB. These are context only: the harness does not provide absolute/peak memory or a retention soak. CPU sampling includes benchmark activity and cannot isolate outside utilization.

Setup failures yielded no measurements: an active-run fixture hit worker capacity before readiness; settled fixtures resolved that. After rebasing, old synthetic schema-31 fixtures required repair, so both were regenerated equivalently with the current fixture owner; baseline and candidate readiness passed before the valid pairs. No manual schema edit. Remote task sandbox and processes have been removed. No production deployment or production load test occurred.

## Proof and Review

The lineage regression fails against the original owner (11 selections versus expected 8 after harmless updates). The row-capture regression fails on the first candidate (12 captures versus expected 4), then passes with the final revision. Repository-deletion coverage verifies immediate source invalidation before background preparation. Locally, the four focused suites passed 63 cases with one existing platform skip; the two revised files passed again (48 cases and one skip). Core tsrs, changed-file lint/format, and `git diff --check` passed. No Testbox lease was used.

Current-head [CI run 40028846041](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40028846041) verifies 63 passing cases in the four affected PR suites, plus projection siblings for topology, invalidation, retention, visibility, accepted facts, and runtime ownership. [Task PR tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40028846041/job/120672346658), [access tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40028846041/job/120672346724), [own-profile tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40028846041/job/120672346586), and [host tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40028846041/job/120672346726) have inspected passing output. Build, typing, lint, security, documentation, and selected UI checks passed. CI performance, real-Gateway UI E2E, Windows/macOS, and Node 24 compatibility lanes were skipped; the real Gateway performance proof is the separate workload above.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean after resolving source-readiness and retained-root lifetime findings. Autoreview preflight refused the requested provider because it did not match operator configuration; no configuration was changed. Current-head GitHub code review also completed with no findings.

## Inherited CI Failure

The only failing test job is [checks-node-changed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40028846041/job/120672346711), with the aggregate CI gate failing downstream. `x-publication-owner-composition.e2e.test.ts:944:63` intermittently returns HTTP 503 instead of 200: “This conversation is temporarily unavailable. Please retry.” The exact unchanged baseline `40172b9e4ff2f2f47def87b8105370d915a669b1` reproduced the same assertion on attempt 3 after two passes, using CI's pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+ef37c31de`. Repetitions stopped at the matching failure; CI was not rerun.

prs.title: fix(telegram): sibling bot's deleted stream previews corrupt group history
prs.body:
Closes #164958

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in a group running two OpenClaw bots, one bot's streamed reasoning preview (the 🧠 draft) is recorded into the other bot's persistent message cache as an ordinary message. Telegram never delivers message deletions to other bots, so when the streaming side deletes the superseded preview, every sibling cache keeps its copy. From then on, each group turn's history window carries that foreign reasoning text, and Anthropic rejects the whole turn with `reasoning_extraction`. The issue's live capture shows the orphaned preview surviving in cache long after it disappeared from Telegram.

## User Impact

User impact: multi-bot Telegram groups stop breaking on streamed reasoning previews. Once a preview is confirmed deleted, every account's history cache drops it, so later turns no longer inherit dead draft text from a sibling bot. No config change or migration needed; previews orphaned before this fix age out through normal retention.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix tracks previews precisely instead of classifying by content, which is the direction the review discussion on the issue called for. The draft stream is the one component that knows the exact message id of a superseded preview, and it already waits for Telegram to confirm the delete. It now reports that id through a new `onPreviewRetired` callback, and the dispatch layer fans the retirement out to every configured account's message cache, including the sender's own (its cache recorded the preview too). Each cache drops the entry from the live map and the persisted store: retained group history through a compare-and-delete loop, bounded private-chat history through a map delete plus store delete. Nothing keys on message text, prefixes, or usernames, so ordinary bot messages are never misclassified. If Telegram rejects or never confirms the delete, nothing is retired, because the preview may still be visible and its history copies are then still honest.

## Evidence

- New `preview-retirement.test.ts`: two accounts each holding the same preview id in group (retained) and private (bounded) history, fan-out retires it from both and keeps neighboring messages; a single-account config with no `channels.telegram` section still covers the implicit default account.
- New cache tests: `retireMessage` evicts from the live map and the persisted store, a reopened bucket does not resurrect the entry, repeat retirement returns false, non-native ids are rejected, and other chats with the same message id are untouched.
- New draft-stream tests: `onPreviewRetired` fires exactly once after a confirmed supersede delete, and never fires when the delete is rejected or returns unconfirmed.
- Review round 4 follow-ups (head 8e35a3e79d5, rebased onto current main a134038ad7f): retirement fan-out now keys on the Bot API chat type carried from the inbound message instead of the `-100` id prefix, so a basic group whose id was recycled into the supergroup space stays account-local; `record()` and `retireMessage` serialize per cache key through one writer chain, so a record in flight while retirement lands can no longer write the preview back; the persisted tombstone settles before retirement reports done, keeping the fence across restarts. New regression tests cover the recycled-id basic group, channel fan-out, unknown chat type staying local, and both store paths racing retirement mid-write.
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/telegram/src/preview-retirement.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/message-cache.retained.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 24 passed. Same command over `message-cache.test.ts` + `draft-stream.test.ts` → 64 passed. oxfmt and oxlint clean on the five touched files.

Gap I want to be explicit about: I could not stage the live two-bot Anthropic reproduction locally, so the end-to-end proof rides on the issue's live capture for the failure side and on the cache/draft-layer tests above for the fix side. The retirement path itself is covered at every layer it touches; a maintainer with two bots can confirm in one group turn by watching the sibling's cache stay empty after the preview is deleted.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): hide features unavailable to limited operators
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Limited-scope Control UI connections advertise the full RPC catalog, but several optional surfaces treated advertisement or connectivity as permission. Opening chat caused rejected session previews, MCP discovery, Side Chat hydration, observer visibility, and plugin catalog requests; refreshes could repeat the same work.

## User Impact

Unavailable Side Chat and MCP surfaces stay hidden. Session links retain their ordinary labels, and an unavailable plugin catalog completes empty without an error. Allowed chat reads continue to work. No configuration changes or server authorization changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing client capability helper and the connection's granted hello scopes at each owning caller. Side Chat presentation uses the same permission for its launcher, shortcut, and saved layout. Plugin connection ownership now excludes a connection that cannot load its catalog. MCP discovery requires general write permission rather than session-only write permission. No denial cache, retry mechanism, or parallel authorization policy is added.

## Evidence

The standalone `scripts/perf/control-ui-forbidden-rpc-measure.ts` records real WebSocket requests and responses against an isolated synthetic Gateway with `operator.sessions.write`. The workload waits for the synthetic transcript, keeps the connection open for one minute, and records screenshots and successful chat reads. Acceptance: zero calls to the five unavailable RPCs, with chat still readable.

Two concurrent, guarded one-minute pairs used the same pinned headless Chromium and synthetic state, with interleaved CPU sets swapped for pair 2. Each side had one connection per pair, granted only `operator.sessions.write`.

| Pair | Baseline FORBIDDEN | Candidate FORBIDDEN | Baseline connection-min | Candidate connection-min | Baseline / candidate rate per connection-min |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 5 | 0 | 1.070383 | 1.070667 | 4.671224 / 0 |
| 2 (CPU sets swapped) | 5 | 0 | 1.009817 | 1.010150 | 4.951394 / 0 |

Mean paired rate: **4.811309 → 0 (-100%)**. Totals: **10 → 0**, across 2.080200 / 2.080817 connection-min (two connections per side). Each baseline called all five affected RPCs once; every candidate omitted all five. `chat.startup` and `sessions.list` succeeded, and all four pages had zero page errors. Both guard checks passed without interruption. An earlier attempt was discarded because the system browser launcher forced both processes into one profile; the pinned browser passed concurrent launch verification before the valid pairs.

Baseline source was `1ba6f92d4074`; all eight candidate runtime UI files match final PR head `245b20d2747f` byte for byte. This proves request admission and retained chat reads; no latency, GC, or model-turn claim is made. The isolated fixture deliberately has no model runtime. Final before/after screenshots below are synthetic-only and were inspected in full.

Live signal before deployment: 133 matching FORBIDDEN responses in the 30-minute journal window ending 2026-10-23 22:03:19 UTC (46 previews, 42 MCP discovery, 21 companion state, 12 observer visibility, 12 plugin catalogs). That is 4.43/min aggregate; the live connection denominator is unavailable. Production was not changed, so there is no post-deployment claim.

Focused regression coverage reproduced repeated preview/catalog calls on the baseline, and the MCP scope regression is red on the baseline and green with the fix. Focused UI tests, the targeted UI typecheck, export-name collision check, and 22 source-closure tests pass. Changed-file formatting passes. Changed-file lint has one inherited failure: `bootstrap.ts` exceeds its 700-line limit on both baseline (732) and candidate (731; reduced); all other touched-file lint checks pass.

The header menu also uses the shared panel availability flag; the scope-downgrade regression passed after failing on the prior header implementation. Initial CI exposed incomplete permission/method fixtures in sibling UI tests and a partial-context cast in the new MCP regression. The fixture corrections retain existing behavioral assertions and scope grants. Focused replays pass (135 plugin/sidebar tests, 24 MCP tests, 27 forwarded-attribution tests, and 11 mock-Gateway tests); E2E browser replay is delegated to PR CI.

Review: independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable), no actionable findings. Final-head CI run [40034534327](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40034534327) passed, including the UI and browser E2E shards. The first CI run exposed the fixture/cast issues described above; they were repaired and the new head passed without a CI rerun. No Testbox/Crabbox lease was allocated under the lane's local-check policy.

Runtime LOC: +36 lines across the eight UI owners. The missing admission/presentation checks require that growth; existing scope policy is reused. The standalone measurement script adds 140 lines, and its README adds 24 (the requested non-test/non-docs-directory diff is +203 total, including 3 fixture-helper lines).

![Before: limited operator is offered unavailable Side Chat](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/afeb7b4d-90ab-4637-89ab-8a2f5c9d1f5a)

![After: unavailable Side Chat is hidden and readable chat remains](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/03484a80-6355-4d1b-9fe4-c51f66234bba)

prs.title: fix(config): clobber snapshots skipped silently when the lock is not released
prs.body:
Related: #153482

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: config clobber snapshots are skipped with no log when the snapshot lock cannot be removed.

## User Impact

Operators see a warning naming the stuck lock and the 30s stale window.

## Why This Change Was Made

Lock release now warns on any error except ENOENT. It never throws. Snapshots still wait for the lock to go stale.

## Evidence

- `src/config/io.clobber-snapshot.test.ts`: red on base, 6 pass with the fix (sync and async, EPERM warns, ENOENT does not).
- `io.observe-recovery.test.ts` 32 pass; core tsgo, test tsgo, oxlint and format clean.
- Gap: release failure is injected, not reproduced on a real filesystem.


## Proof

Real CLI (`openclaw sessions`) on a throwaway HOME: clobbered `openclaw.json` plus a good `.bak`. A second process adds a file to the lock dir while it is held (the dir holds 100k empty files to widen the race), so the real `rmdir` fails with ENOTEMPTY. No mocks. Base 94cee2a vs this PR.

Before (base):
```
Config auto-restored from backup: ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json (gateway-mode-missing-vs-last-good)
$ ls ~/.openclaw | grep clobber
openclaw.json.clobbered.2026-10-23T16-42-23-841Z
openclaw.json.clobber.lock
# same again within 30s
Config backup recovery deferred: ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json; original config snapshot could not be saved. Retry recovery.
```

After (this PR):
```
Config clobber snapshot lock ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json.clobber.lock could not be released (ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rmdir '~/.openclaw/openclaw.json.clobber.lock'); snapshots are skipped until it goes stale (30s).
Config auto-restored from backup: ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json (gateway-mode-missing-vs-last-good)
$ ls ~/.openclaw | grep clobber
openclaw.json.clobbered.2026-10-23T16-45-09-862Z
openclaw.json.clobber.lock
# same again within 30s
Config backup recovery deferred: ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json; original config snapshot could not be saved. Retry recovery.
```

Async path, calling `recoverConfigFromJsonRootSuffix` (the function Doctor uses; not run via `doctor --fix`), after:
```
Config clobber snapshot lock ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json.clobber.lock could not be released (ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rmdir '~/.openclaw/openclaw.json.clobber.lock'); snapshots are skipped until it goes stale (30s).
Config auto-stripped non-JSON prefix: ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json (original saved as ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json.clobbered.2026-10-23T16-45-24-744Z)
recoverConfigFromJsonRootSuffix -> true
```

The config is restored and the snapshot saved in both runs. The only change is that the stuck lock is now reported.

prs.title: feat(learn): /learn can save lessons to the selected memory plugin
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`/learn` can only save lessons as Skill Workshop skills. Facts, preferences, decisions and knowledge about a person or project have nowhere to go, and Workshop's own rules tell the agent not to save those as skills. Agents without Skill Workshop can't use `/learn` at all.

## User Impact

No change for current installs: with no memory plugin opting in, `/learn` sends the same prompt as today and gives the same reply when unavailable.

When the plugin that owns the memory slot opts in, `/learn` sends repeatable procedures to Skill Workshop and other lessons to that plugin's memory. It also works on agents where only memory is available. If neither can write, the reply now names both instead of only Skill Workshop.

Plugin developers get two optional fields on `registerMemoryCapability`: `learnToolNames` and `learnGuidanceBuilder`. This adds to the public plugin SDK, so it needs SDK owner review.

## Why This Change Was Made

The memory plugin knows how its memory should be written, but not which of its tools the current turn's policy allows. So the plugin declares its write tools, and core runs those names, tagged with the plugin's id, through the same final tool-policy composition and runtime allowlist used for `skill_workshop`, so plugin-ID and `group:plugins` entries apply as they do to the real tools. Core then passes the surviving names to the plugin, which returns a few lines of guidance, or nothing if those tools aren't enough. Core splices the guidance into the `/learn` turn's user message, so the cached prompt prefix is unchanged.

Memory plugins that don't own the memory slot (for example Memory Core running as a dreaming sidecar) have both fields removed at registration, the same treatment `recallToolNames` already gets. `/learn` adds no new authority: the turn calls the plugin's tools under the access it already had. Undo is still Workshop-only.

## Evidence

- Focused tests pass: `commands-learn` (memory-only, combined, neither available, plugin-ID and `group:plugins` allow/deny, plus the existing policy and undo cases; the plugin-wide policy case fails without the fix), `memory-state`, `registry.dual-kind-memory-gate` (an unselected sidecar can't contribute the learning fields), `memory-provider-registration`, `tool-policy-diagnostic` and `tool-policy-pipeline`.
- `agent-tools.prefix-stability` test: 8 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` are clean.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check`: no unauthorized removals against the shipped SDK (v2026.10.5).
- Independent review (autoreview, branch mode against `origin/main`, P0–P1): scoped-clean.
- **Gap:** no plugin on `main` uses the new fields yet, so this PR doesn't change runtime behavior, and the memory path has unit-test proof only. The first user is the Knowledge plugin, landing separately. `/learn` with a participating plugin has not yet been run end to end through a real Gateway; that proof belongs with the Knowledge change. Merging should wait for an SDK owner's review and that proof.

<details><summary>Memory Core</summary>

Memory Core doesn't opt in here. It could declare its file tools (`read`, `write`, `edit`) and return a line telling the agent which topic file under `memory/` each lesson goes in. Note that a `write` grant isn't limited to memory files, so that rule would be a prompt convention, not an enforced restriction.
</details>

prs.title: fix(memory-wiki): percent-encoded Markdown links are reported as broken and get no backlinks
prs.body:
Related: #181380

## What Problem This Solves

`wiki lint` treats valid percent-encoded local Markdown destinations as literal filenames, reporting existing targets as broken. The same unresolved path prevents compile from generating the target page's Referenced By backlink.

## What Changed

The shared Markdown link extractor percent-decodes local URL paths after stripping query/fragment syntax and before existing path normalization. Lint and backlink generation consume that same result. Malformed percent escapes retain their previous literal behavior; Obsidian wikilinks, remote-link filtering and authored link text are unchanged.

Thanks @L4XB for the focused decoder repair. No SDK, configuration, dependency or persisted-format change. The README now describes the link semantics.

## Evidence

Built Linux CLI, Node 24.22.1, fresh isolated state, bundled memory-wiki enabled through shipped config commands with Obsidian rendering and official Obsidian CLI actions disabled. Main `a339211296bca56476a5455e9901b44f13d88580` ran twice; candidate `34ced32414e89df1a35f968dc561978cbe703a30` ran the same operations.

All vault/config state was created by shipped commands, not direct vault writes or renamed fixtures:

```sh
openclaw wiki init --json
openclaw wiki apply synthesis Target --source-id proof-source --body 'Target body' --json
openclaw wiki apply synthesis Meeting --source-id proof-source --body '[Target](%74arget.md)' --json
openclaw wiki apply synthesis Plain --source-id proof-source --body '[Target](target.md)' --json
openclaw wiki apply synthesis Malformed --source-id proof-source --body '[Missing](malformed100%.md)' --json
openclaw wiki lint --json
openclaw wiki compile --json
openclaw wiki get syntheses/target.md --json
```

The mutation results confirmed the generated paths, including syntheses/target.md and syntheses/meeting.md. Each page was read through `wiki get`; the generated lint report and page files were also read independently from disk without mutation.

| Observation | Main run 1 | Main run 2 | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Meeting's valid encoded target reported broken | Yes | Yes | No |
| Meeting included in Target's Referenced By | No | No | Yes |
| Plain target works and its backlink is present | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Malformed percent escape stays a non-crashing literal broken target | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Complete lint issue count | 2 | 2 | 1 |

Both main runs report `syntheses/%74arget.md` as a broken target. The remaining candidate warning is the intentional missing `syntheses/malformed100%.md` control. Full issue arrays and raw reports were retained; no provenance warning was suppressed (this fixture emitted none).

Main's Target page contains only Plain in the Referenced By section. Candidate's independently read generated section is:

```md
### Referenced By

- [[syntheses/meeting|Meeting]]
- [[syntheses/plain|Plain]]
```

The oracle examines this section specifically, not another Related Pages entry caused by shared source ids. Meeting's authored body still contains `[Target](%74arget.md)` after compile.

Full main/candidate builds, 31 focused tests across the Markdown and lint suites, and focused formatting/lint passed. The regressions also cover space-encoded names, UTF-8 and malformed escape preservation. A separate real OpenAI gpt-5-mini CLI turn completed successfully with a nonempty response, exit 0 and no fallback.

One decoder at the existing shared extraction boundary fixes both consumers; no separate lint/backlink workaround, cache or writer was added. Production +12/-1, tests +36, docs +4. The small private helper is retained because malformed encodings must remain literal rather than aborting the scan.

## Merge Risk

Two-way door: revert and compile rebuild the generated backlinks using the prior behavior; no schema migration is involved. Blast radius is local Markdown link resolution for wiki lint and generated related/backlink blocks. Authored page links and unrelated provenance diagnostics are not rewritten or suppressed.

prs.title: perf(gateway): share session event delivery variants
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session-event fanout repeatedly constructs equivalent payloads for viewers with the same audience, capabilities, and delivered-row history.

## User Impact

Session events preserve their existing wire bytes and per-viewer permissions while reducing repeated projection work. There is no protocol or configuration change. Performance acceptance remains pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepare one complete delivery plan and its wire variants per synchronous publication, then reuse it after each recipient's live authority check. Every socket still commits only its own accepted handoff.

The connection row owner records a bare history token covering both ordered retention maps, byte accounting, ancestor certificates, and wire versions. Shared invalidation preserves equal histories through one operation-scoped transition map. Independent legacy roster reads can rejoin the canonical empty history only when no wire version has ever been committed and no ancestors remain. Sockets retain no publication, message graph, plan, or transition map.

This removes the baseline-ID map, JSON cache keys, layered payload caches, and per-recipient delivery closures. Runtime code changes by +23 lines; the history transition rules account for the growth and prevent unsafe reuse across differing baselines. Benchmark tooling adds 49 lines and its documentation 20 lines. The requested non-test diff is +92 lines overall.

## Status

Updated head: `816750c3150fa83a327e6ef0ea8e7c3f39edee44`, based on `673b3ecef9ee694d3a999a67e3f87b5fde0a8658`. **Performance acceptance is pending. Do not merge yet; the lane lead owns merging.** CI passed on this exact head, including `openclaw/ci-gate`: [run 40013970251](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40013970251).

The real parent-update regression failed on the original candidate with 12 row encodings where at most 4 were expected. Independent legacy roster reads also reproduced 6 payload encodings where at most 3 were expected. Both pass with the repairs, and the counted publication must send exactly once to every intended viewer. A subsequent automated review found that staggered legacy listeners still split after delivery of ancestor-free rows: the regression observed two encodings instead of one. Delivery now canonicalizes truly empty final history as well; nonempty and nonzero-version histories retain their reentry guard.

## Evidence

All 58 tests in nine focused files pass, including nine unchanged wire goldens, event/list parity, different contents at equal numeric versions, retention limits, per-connection handoff failures, and live authority changes:

- `src/gateway/session-row-delta-audiences.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/session-row-publication-authority.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/session-row-event-parity.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/session-ancestor-references.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/session-row-delta-retention.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/session-row-delta-delivery.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/server-broadcast.serialization.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/server-broadcast.transport.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/server-connection-state.test.ts`

The final production snapshot passed all 58 tests in the nine-file run in 69.22 s wall time. The new staggered-admission regression failed on the preceding head with two envelope encodings versus one, then passed with the repair. Changed-file formatting and lint pass. The initial candidate passed one core typecheck; current-head production and test typechecks, changed-code tests, build and PostgreSQL conformance all passed in PR CI.

Initial runtime and benchmark reviews were clean. All three repairs received **independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable)** after the helper refused the requested provider route before inference. No operator config was changed. The final review found and resolved one test false-green risk from stale mock frames; there are no remaining actionable P0–P2 findings. Review and test results are not performance acceptance.

## Repair owner counts

The completed original-versus-shared-invalidation-repair diagnostic uses 8 measured rounds, 64 turns and 16 resets per side, with the same mixed-capability cohort and active roster polling. It counts actual construction sites and is excluded from allocation measurements.

| Event / construction | Original plans or variants per publication | Invalidation repair | Eligible deliveries per publication |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| sessions.changed / delta plan | 20 | 4 | 20 |
| session.message / delta plan | 20 | 4 | 20 |
| sessions.changed / field-reference variant | 10 | 3 | 10 |
| session.message / field-reference variant | 10 | 3.988 | 10 |
| sessions.changed / legacy plan | 10.001 | 9.571 | ~10 |
| session.message / legacy plan | 10 | 9.676 | 10 |

Delta reuse is restored to five deliveries per plan. Legacy reuse still fragments during polling in this intermediate repair; the follow-on comparison below measures the final canonical-empty repair. Original/repaired publication counts are 719/715 for sessions.changed and 259/259 for session.message, so the table normalizes by each side's publications. Cohort receipts are 29,340/29,220. Each side has one extra observed legacy projection at a cohort boundary. No allocation or latency conclusion is drawn from these diagnostic hooks.

### Empty-history invalidation repair (superseded candidate)

On the refreshed common runtime, the intermediate repair and candidate `de43272a95de` each completed 8 measured rounds, 64 turns and 16 resets. Delta plans remain exactly 3 per publication on both sides; field-reference variants remain 3 for sessions.changed and about 3.988 for session.message. This comparison isolates the four-line empty-history repair.

| Legacy construction | Intermediate repair | Candidate de432 | Change | Publications, before / after | Eligible deliveries, before / after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| sessions.changed plans/publication | 10 | 6.835 | −31.65% | 722 / 716 | 7,220 / 7,160 |
| session.message plans/publication | 10 | 7.625 | −23.75% | 255 / 259 | 2,550 / 2,590 |

The de432 legacy miss counts are 4,894 and 1,975. These are full-window results; legacy reuse remains partial. Raw counters were independently aggregated, with matching rounds, turns and resets. Cohort receipts were 29,310 / 29,250. Allocation, promotion and latency acceptance still require the normal paired captures.

### Delivery-time empty-history repair (current head)

On common runtime `673b3ecef9ee`, the preceding `de43272a95de` candidate and current `816750c3150f` each completed eight measured rounds, 64 turns, 16 resets, and 29,220 received session events. Actual construction counters were independently aggregated from raw results.

| Legacy construction | Previous candidate | Current head | Change | Publications per side | Misses, before / after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| sessions.changed plans/publication | 6.959 | 5.352 | −23.09% | 715 | 4,976 / 3,827 |
| session.message plans/publication | 7.656 | 6.865 | −10.34% | 259 | 1,983 / 1,778 |

Delta plans remain exactly 3 per publication; field-reference variants remain 3 for sessions.changed and 3.988 for session.message. Current-head legacy changed projections include one cohort-boundary extra lookup (7,151 versus 7,150); received event totals match. Legacy reuse is still partial. These counters prove less construction, not allocation or promotion acceptance.

## Current-main baseline sharing

Synthetic fixtures contain 5,000 sessions and 6,000 retained runs. The count probes use 30 viewers across three capability cohorts (legacy, row delta, row delta plus field references), with five exact and five roster viewers in each cohort. Both probes completed 64 measured turns, eight measured/ten total cohorts, 16 resets, and 29,640 received session events.

The diagnostic hook counts distinct combinations of audience, ancestor delivery key, current-row wire versions, and baseline object identities for the 20 delta-capable viewers. It does not count complete retained histories. The hook is excluded from all allocation and acceptance captures.

| Polling | Event | Publications | Eligible delta deliveries | Distinct touched-row plans | Plans/publication | Deliveries/plan |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Active | sessions.changed | 726 | 14,520 | 2,904 | 4 | 5.00 |
| Active | session.message | 262 | 5,240 | 1,048 | 4 | 5.00 |
| Disabled | sessions.changed | 726 | 14,520 | 2,178 | 3 | 6.67 |
| Disabled | session.message | 262 | 5,240 | 786 | 3 | 6.67 |

Polling adds one touched-row plan per publication while preserving five-way reuse. This provides a concrete sharing opportunity on the current implementation.

## Baseline allocation attribution

A separate capture disabled TurboFan and Maglev inlining, included collected objects, and sampled at 256 KiB. It completed 64 turns and 30,840 continuous-window session-event deliveries (29,640 within individual cohort counters). Total sampled allocation was 13,915,761,912 bytes across 52,465 samples. The raw profile hash and independently recomputed totals match the analysis.

| Allocation owner | B/delivery | Allocation samples |
|---|---:|---:|
| Projection subtree | 27,851.15 | 3,273 |
| Recipient callback subtree | 25,844.65 | 3,037 |
| Callback self | 10,824.00 | — |
| Row preparation subtree | 4,414.25 | — |
| Ancestor preparation subtree | 2,193.74 | — |

| Audience-key subtree | 1,420.76 | — |

Projection accounts for 6.17% of sampled main-isolate allocation in this diagnostic. Disabling inlining changes execution; these are attribution results, not acceptance numbers or a production extrapolation.

## Original candidate: rejected

Two normal-inlining, collected-object sampled, swapped concurrent pairs on Node 26.12.1 completed with matching 640 turns, 100 total rounds and 40 resets per side. The original candidate increased projection allocation by 56.06% paired mean. Raw tree totals, owner sample membership and main-isolate GC trace accounting were independently verified for both pairs.

| Metric | Pair 1 baseline → candidate | Pair 2 baseline → candidate | Mean paired change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Projection B/delivery | 26,756.11 → 43,734.84 | 29,309.99 → 43,573.98 | +56.06% |
| Projection allocation samples | 15,581 → 25,470 | 17,071 → 25,374 | — |
| Whole allocation MB/turn | 217.169 → 229.484 | 217.089 → 228.312 | +5.42% |
| All allocation samples | 262,535 → 277,509 | 262,404 → 276,051 | — |
| Promotion MB/turn | 40.588 → 42.203 | 40.512 → 40.793 | +2.34% |

| Maximum GC pause ms | 67.680 → 80.833 | 96.599 → 133.999 | No bound breach |

The original result is retained and will not be replaced by repaired-candidate data. Pair 1's small receipt variation was uniform across all viewers and attributable to complete publications around measurement/cohort windows. Pair 2 had equal total receipts, with small uniform differences between event kinds. Diagnostics recorded no dropped events or collection errors. Raw GC kinds, tail counts, absolute deltas, timing and work audits are retained with the measurement evidence. Some RPC/turn p95 signs disagree and remain inconclusive; no third pair is spent on the already-rejected original candidate.

## Corrected pair 1: preliminary, swapped pair pending

The first final-candidate pair completed on the common runtime with matching 640 measured turns, 80 measured / 100 total rounds, and 40 resets per side. Baseline used the even CPUs and candidate the odd CPUs within one interleaved slot. The shared guard did not interrupt it, frozen hashes matched, and raw allocation-tree totals and main-isolate GC accounting were independently reconstructed.

The frozen analyzer applies the maximum-pause gate to the overall maximum and separately reports per-kind breaches for lead review; the overall bound was not breached. This distinction does not dismiss the minor-pause observation. The 60% owner-allocation reduction target was also missed in this first pair.

Minor-GC p95/p99 were 5.822/9.086 → 6.110/9.214 ms (4,912/4,871 collections); major-GC p95/p99 were 55.294/74.750 → 53.502/71.678 ms (149/148 collections, below percentile sample floors). Chat p95/p99 were 1.465/1.877 → 1.453/1.855 ms (19,200 observations per side). Sessions.list p95/p99 were 44.650/75.076 → 42.679/73.899 ms (7,149/7,202 observations). Earlier owner-count comparisons are preserved above. The initial normal-inlining de432 capture was stopped before results after the independently reproduced staggered-legacy defect was fixed; its partial artifacts are retained as superseded, not used for acceptance. The second pair swaps interleaved CPU sides. Inputs are hashed, fixtures are synthetic, the shared guard is unchanged, and rounds, turns and reset boundaries must match. prs.title: fix(agents): renew Sign-in-with-ChatGPT credentials for each model request
prs.body:
Closes #175801

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Sign-in-with-ChatGPT model requests keep sending the access credential captured at attempt preparation, so an expired or rotated token fails every subsequent request and the attempt ends in a terminal auth failure after settled tool work.

## User Impact

User impact: SIWC (chatgpt-token-sharing) sessions now carry the owner's current access credential on every model request and recover from a single `token_expired` 401 with one forced re-acquisition and one retried request, instead of dying at the first credential expiry mid-turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stream wrapper previously captured the resolved API key once at creation and replayed it for the lifetime of the attempt, and the renewal trigger matched prose on thrown errors — which never fired because the Responses client surfaces provider 401s as projected stream terminals, not rejections. The fix:

- `createRenewableRequestApiKeyResolver` (in `run/auth-store.ts`, owned by the auth controller) re-resolves the selected seat's current access through the canonical `getApiKeyForModelCore` owner with `lockedProfile: true` on every call, reading the live auth state rather than a static snapshot. No production code is mocked or injected; the refresh queue, rotation fences, and pre-expiry margin come from the real owner.
- `wrapEmbeddedAgentStreamApiKey` calls the resolver before each request; the live resolution leads the captured key and any static override, and non-renewable credentials keep the captured-key-first contract.
- `createRenewalGuardedStream` (new `stream-renewal-guard.ts`) buffers a provider stream until its first output event. A terminal `error` event carrying a structured 401 token-expiry before any output triggers exactly one `forceRefresh: true` re-acquisition and one retried request. The 401 fact is read only from deterministic projection fields: `errorCode === "401"` or the projection's status prefix (the colon form the local projection adds, and the SDK form that already embeds the status, e.g. `"401 The authentication token is expired"`). The expiry fact comes from structured codes (`token_expired` / `expired_token` in `errorCode`/`errorType`) or a bounded regex over `errorMessage`/`errorBody`; prose alone never classifies. The final commit closes a real gap the reviewer proof exposed: the actual OpenAI Responses client projects a 401 whose message keeps the SDK's status-embedded prefix without the colon and whose provider code shadows the HTTP status (`errorCode=token_expired`), which the earlier colon-only gate missed.
- The renewal budget is per source stream: a replacement stream's terminals pass through untouched, so a revoked grant surfaces once without looping, and a 401 that arrives after output was forwarded is never retried (no replay of settled tool work or partial output).

The resolver is created in `auth-controller.ts` (the lifecycle owner with live state access) and threaded through the existing runtime → dispatch → stream-settle path; the stream wrapper only receives the resolver, so per-request logic stays out of the dispatch file.

## Evidence

**Focused tests (44/44 pass, standalone vitest, 1 worker, re-verified after the SDK-401 classification commit):**

```
 src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/stream-renewable-api-key.test.ts  29 tests  PASS
 src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-store.test.ts            9 tests  PASS
 src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/stream-resolution.test.ts         6 tests  PASS
```

The 29-test file exercises the real `AssistantMessageEventStream` objects, real `CodexApiError` instances with `projectProviderError` projections (the exact production terminal shape — including the real SDK `APIError` shape whose message keeps the status-embedded `"401 "` prefix and whose provider code shadows the HTTP status), and the canonical `getApiKeyForModelCore` owner against a fresh isolated state dir (`withOpenClawTestState`) — including externally renewed seats picked up on the next request and unrenewable expired seats keeping the captured credential. No production code is mocked in the renewal path.

**Gates (all clean on the changed files):** oxfmt format, oxlint, import-cycle check (0). TypeScript: the scoped `tsc -p` over the changed files reports 0 errors, including after the final SDK-401 classification commit.

**Real-transport authority chain (local Responses endpoint, production client):** the production `createOpenAIResponsesTransportStreamFn` client (`createResponsesTransportExecutor` → `failTransportStream` terminal) runs against a local `node:http` endpoint that emulates the incident wire behavior, wrapped by the branch's real `selectEmbeddedAgentStream` / `wrapApiKey` / guard — 3/3 checks:

```
=== Real-transport authority chain (local Responses endpoint) ===
PASS  C1: allowed selected-account request is admitted through the real transport  (bearers: ["siwc-access-A"], terminal: done)
PASS  C2: post-settlement wire 401 token_expired recovers via one forced reacquisition  (terminal: done, refreshCalls=1, bearers: ["siwc-access-A","siwc-access-A","siwc-access-B"])
PASS  C3: revoked account is rejected once, terminally, with the structured 401 projection  (requests: 1, reacquireAttempts: 0, refreshCalls: 0, terminal: token_expired/invalid_request_error)
```

C1 is the allowed selected-account request: the server observes the owner-resolved bearer and returns 200; the stream completes. C2 is the incident: the first request settles, the server then expires the captured access (HTTP 401 `token_expired` on the wire for the next request), and the guard's one forced re-acquisition rotates the bearer so the single retried request completes — exactly one unauthorized request, no replay of settled work. C3 is the revoked account: the owner hands out no current access, the captured key leads, the request fails once with the projected 401 `token_expired` terminal, and nothing loops or retries. The pre-fix classifier missed exactly this wire shape (its 401 gate only accepted the colon prefix or `errorCode === "401"`, while the real client projects `errorCode=token_expired` with the status embedded in the message) — C2 failing on the pre-fix code and passing after the classification commit is what closed that gap.

**Issue-prescribed proof** (extracted-function harness: synthetic credential owner, virtual clock, fake transport; Phase A uses the published `openclaw@2026.10.5` wrappers extracted verbatim from dist, Phase B uses the branch code with the real guard, real `AssistantMessageEventStream` terminals, and real `CodexApiError` projections; Part B8 drives the real resolver against the canonical `getApiKeyForModelCore` owner on a temp state dir) — 12/12 checks:

```
=== Phase A: published openclaw@2026.10.5 (pre-fix) ===
PASS  A1 (bug): captured A is still used after the owner renewed to B  (key used: siwc-access-A, owner access: siwc-access-B)
PASS  A2 (bug): 401 token_expired surfaces terminally with no request retry  (inner calls after 401: 1)

=== Phase B: branch fix/siwc-request-credential-renewal (post-fix) ===
PASS  B1: each request carries the owner's current access (externally renewed B is picked up)  (keys: ["siwc-access-A","siwc-access-B"])
PASS  B2: expiry after settled work recovers via one forced reacquisition  (delivered=true, refreshCalls=1, final key=siwc-access-B)
PASS  B3: one unauthorized request + one retried request (no loop, no replay of settled work)  (keys: ["siwc-access-A","siwc-access-A","siwc-access-B"])
PASS  B4: 401 after output is surfaced once without retry or a second turn  (inner calls: 1, events: start,text_start,text_delta,error)
PASS  B5: non-token-expired 401 surfaces once without renewal  (inner calls: 1)
PASS  B6: revoked grant surfaces once without looping  (inner calls: 1, refreshCalls: 1)
PASS  B7: static credentials keep the captured-key-first contract  (key: static-K)

=== Part B8: real resolver + canonical owner (temp state) ===
PASS  B8a: real owner resolves the seat's current access
PASS  B8b: externally renewed seat is picked up on the next request
PASS  B8c: unrenewable expired seat keeps the captured credential
```

**Shipped-entry live proof (running source-mode gateway, fake OpenAI Responses endpoint, real `agent` RPC):** the gateway boots and accepts the turn through the real `agent`/`agent.wait` RPCs with the new wrapper wired end-to-end. Gap to note: the proof host's free memory stayed under the 4 GB guardrail budget (user applications), and the cold source-mode turn did not settle within the wait window on the final attempt, so the model request could not be observed on the wire; the provider-level per-request behavior is covered by the Phase A/B proof above, which drives the real `selectEmbeddedAgentStream` / `wrapEmbeddedAgentStreamApiKey` / `createRenewalGuardedStream` code with the real stream terminal types.

**Data-model compatibility:** no persisted schema, config key, or auth-store file format changes; the auth store file shape is untouched. The change is additive in-memory state access only.

**Upgrade from published stable:** Phase A of the proof runs against the published `openclaw@2026.10.5` package (installed from npm) to demonstrate the pre-fix behavior; the upgrade path is purely in-process behavior with no stored-state migration.

## What Problem This Solves

The maintained full-tree dead-code scan reports `scripts/perf/async-context-probe.cjs` as unused even though the performance guide provides a concrete wrapper that loads this diagnostic before the Gateway entrypoint. Because that wrapper is created and selected by path, static import analysis cannot discover the probe on its own.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible runtime change. Maintainers can keep the documented async-context census workflow without its preload being misclassified as obsolete, while production and full-tree analyzer scopes, the diagnostic's private Node runtime contract, and all unrelated findings remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Knip configuration already owns package-, workflow-, and documentation-invoked programs in `repositoryScriptEntries`. Adding the exact probe path there models its real consumer without inventing a static import, package script, ignore, or suppression. The full-tree configuration imports this root list and only removes the production scripts exclusion, so the same owner correctly serves both scans.

## Evidence

On the accepted baseline, the production unused-file scan reported zero entries and the full-tree scan's sole residual was this probe. On the exact candidate tree:

- changed-config formatting and lint passed;
- all selected canonical type graphs passed;
- the existing dead-code reporting, unused-file, and export owner suites passed 30/30; and
- `pnpm deadcode:unused-files` no longer reported `scripts/perf/async-context-probe.cjs`.

The prepared proof base predates five analyzer roots that are already present on `main`, so that scan still exited `1` for those inherited rows; they remained visible and were not suppressed. The diagnostic, benchmark, Node runtime, PostgreSQL, UI, and live Gateway were not executed because their behavior did not change.

Two separate exact-head reviews found no defects: the full calibrated engineering review used the retained scan output, and the source-complete canonical review inspected the complete owner, profile, preload, harness, and child-argument files. Exact-head CI preflight, security, source-contract, changed-boundary, and related static rows were also green at final qualification; broader rows remained pending with no failures.

prs.title: fix(minimax): treat the documented MiniMax-M3.1-Flash id as M3.1
prs.body:
Closes #177387

## What Problem This Solves

The bundled MiniMax integration keys every M3.1 behavior on the exact string `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview`. MiniMax's current API documentation lists the model as `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` (the `-Preview` spelling no longer appears on any reference page). Configuring the documented id silently:

1. falls back to the two-level `off`/`adaptive` M3 thinking profile instead of the five-level `low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max` profile (default `max`),
2. skips the M3.1 stream payload patch (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`, `output_config.effort`, `max_tokens` clamp), and
3. has no bundled catalog row, so a bare config entry resolves the inherited 128k text-only profile instead of the documented 1M multimodal one with `codeMode: "preferred"`.

## Fix

Treat both spellings as the same model, give the documented id the bundled catalog row, and price it at MiniMax's published launch rates:

- `extensions/minimax/thinking.ts` — `isMinimaxM31ModelId` now matches the id stem, accepting exactly `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` and `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview` (case-insensitive, anchored). New export `MINIMAX_M31_FLASH_MODEL_ID`.
- `extensions/minimax/provider-models.ts` — `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` added to `MINIMAX_TEXT_MODEL_ORDER` and `MINIMAX_TEXT_MODEL_CATALOG` with the same profile as the preview id (1M context, `text`+`image`, `reasoning`, `codeMode: "preferred"`). The preview id stays in the catalog so existing configs keep working.
- `extensions/minimax/model-definitions.ts` — the launch id gets the rates MiniMax publishes for it ($0.15 input / $0.60 output / $0.015 cache read per million, from the MiniMax pricing page); the preview id keeps the zero fields because its per-token pricing is still unavailable (the zero fields on the earlier map entry were the preview's, carried over when the launch id was added).

Runtime selection is unchanged: `resolveThinkingProfile`, `resolveDynamicModel`, the static catalog, and the `wrapStreamFn` payload patch all key off the same two spellings.

## Evidence

### Before/after through the real extension modules (source, tsx)

```
# BASE (origin/main 9b9364cfed0)
MiniMax-M3.1-Flash: m31=false catalog=false levels=[off,adaptive] default=adaptive contextWindow=204800 input=text codeMode=- cost={"input":0.6,"output":2.4,"cacheRead":0.12,"cacheWrite":0}
MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview: m31=true catalog=true levels=[low,medium,high,xhigh,max] default=max contextWindow=1000000 input=text+image codeMode=preferred cost={"input":0,"output":0,"cacheRead":0,"cacheWrite":0}

# THIS PR
MiniMax-M3.1-Flash: m31=true catalog=true levels=[low,medium,high,xhigh,max] default=max contextWindow=1000000 input=text+image codeMode=preferred cost={"input":0.15,"output":0.6,"cacheRead":0.015,"cacheWrite":0}
MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview: m31=true catalog=true levels=[low,medium,high,xhigh,max] default=max contextWindow=1000000 input=text+image codeMode=preferred cost={"input":0,"output":0,"cacheRead":0,"cacheWrite":0}
```

### Wire-level: real registered provider `wrapStreamFn`, captured Anthropic request payload

The hook is driven through the real plugin registration (`registerProviderPlugin` + `provider.wrapStreamFn`), with the request captured via `onPayload` before any network I/O.

```
# BASE — official id bypasses the M3.1 patch; preview keeps it
--- MiniMax-M3.1-Flash ---
{ "model": "MiniMax-M3.1-Flash",
  "thinking": { "type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 8192, "display": "summarized" },
  "max_tokens": 10192 }                      # no output_config, no adaptive thinking
--- MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview ---
{ "model": "MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview",
  "thinking": { "type": "adaptive" },
  "output_config": { "effort": "medium" },
  "max_tokens": 2000 }

# THIS PR — both spellings carry the M3.1 patch
--- MiniMax-M3.1-Flash ---
{ "model": "MiniMax-M3.1-Flash",
  "thinking": { "type": "adaptive" },
  "output_config": { "effort": "medium" },
  "max_tokens": 2000 }
--- MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview ---
{ "model": "MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview",
  "thinking": { "type": "adaptive" },
  "output_config": { "effort": "medium" },
  "max_tokens": 2000 }
```

### CLI (shipped entry, isolated state, synthetic key)

`openclaw models list --all --json` with `models.providers.minimax-portal.models: [{ "id": "MiniMax-M3.1-Flash", ... }]`:

```
"key": "minimax-portal/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash", "name": "MiniMax M3.1 Flash", "available": true
```

The bundled static-catalog rows (the `minimax/*` and `minimax-portal/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview`-style rows) come from `staticCatalog.run` → `buildMinimaxProvider` — exercised directly by the discovery test below, which asserts the official id's row (1M context, `text`+`image`, `codeMode: "preferred"`, hosted cost) on both provider routes.

### Completed production turn (reviewer-required): real plugin, real transport, wire capture

The registered provider's real `wrapStreamFn` (the shipped `wrapMinimaxProviderStream`) is driven end to end with the production Anthropic transport as the underlying stream function — no fetch override, the real client performs the HTTP I/O against a loopback fixture that speaks the MiniMax Anthropic-compatible SSE contract. The fixture records the exact outgoing request payload; the turn completes (`done` + assistant text) on every selected effort:

```
=== PR head (fix/minimax-m31-flash-id, 2d3c27bc6ec2) ===
PASS  turn low: completed with the corrected profile and outgoing effort low  (failed=-, text=OK, requests=1, thinking={"type":"adaptive"}, output_config={"effort":"low"})
PASS  turn medium: completed with the corrected profile and outgoing effort medium  (failed=-, text=OK, requests=1, thinking={"type":"adaptive"}, output_config={"effort":"medium"})
PASS  turn high: completed with the corrected profile and outgoing effort high  (failed=-, text=OK, requests=1, thinking={"type":"adaptive"}, output_config={"effort":"high"})
PASS  turn xhigh: completed with the corrected profile and outgoing effort xhigh  (failed=-, text=OK, requests=1, thinking={"type":"adaptive"}, output_config={"effort":"xhigh"})
PASS  turn max: completed with the corrected profile and outgoing effort max  (failed=-, text=OK, requests=1, thinking={"type":"adaptive"}, output_config={"effort":"max"})
PASS  discovery: launch id priced at the published API rates  (cost={"input":0.15,"output":0.6,"cacheRead":0.015,"cacheWrite":0})
PASS  discovery: preview id keeps its zero fields  (cost={"input":0,"output":0,"cacheRead":0,"cacheWrite":0})
```

The `onPayload` trace above stopped at the request boundary; the completed turns above show the same selected effort arriving on a finished production turn for each level.

### Latest-stable upgrade behavior (published `openclaw@2026.10.6` from npm)

The published package's bundled MiniMax plugin (verbatim `node_modules/openclaw/dist`) is registered against the published package's own API surface and driven through the same real transport and loopback contract with the user's existing selection and settings (`models.providers.minimax.models: [{ "id": "MiniMax-M3.1-Flash", "reasoning": true }]`, baseUrl + key):

```
=== published openclaw@2026.10.6 ===
PASS  stable 2026.10.6: existing MiniMax-M3.1-Flash selection still completes a turn  (failed=-, text=OK, requests=1)
PASS  stable 2026.10.6 (bug): launch id gets no adaptive thinking or output_config.effort  (thinking={"type":"disabled"}, output_config=null)
PASS  stable 2026.10.6 (bug): discovery has no M3.1 catalog entry for the launch id  (launch id not discovered)
```

Existing selections and settings stay intact across the upgrade — the launch-id selection still turns on the published stable (that is the reported workaround behavior: the model answers, without the M3.1 controls). Upgrading to this head restores the five-level profile, the outgoing effort, and the 1M multimodal catalog row without any config change; the only persisted-data touch is none — the change is in-memory catalog and stream-shaping only, so no state migration is required. No production credentials or external endpoints were used in either harness; the bearer is a fixture secret that is never printed.

### Tests (focused, maxWorkers=1)

- `extensions/minimax/index.test.ts`, `provider-catalog.test.ts`, `model-definitions.test.ts`, `provider-discovery.contract.test.ts`: **40 passed** on this head (the two default-only rows the expanded discovery case already covers are removed, per review).
- Base-failing run (same test file against `origin/main` implementation): **7 failed | 26 passed** — the two new thinking-default cases, the discovery case for `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`, and all four M3.1 stream-payload cases.
- New/changed assertions:
  - `defaults minimax(/minimax-portal)/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash thinking to max`
  - discovery test parameterized over both spellings: catalog row, five-level profile (default `max`), the published rates on the launch id (zero fields on the preview id), and `resolveDynamicModel` → `anthropic-messages`
  - M3.1 effort stream test now runs for both spellings (payload asserts `thinking.adaptive`, `output_config.effort`, clamped `max_tokens`, no `budget_tokens`)

### Gates

- oxfmt: clean on all changed files (re-verified after the pricing commit)
- oxlint: clean on all changed files (re-verified after the pricing commit)
- tsgo (`-p extensions/minimax/tsconfig.json --noEmit`): clean
- line-cap ratchet: OK (no new violations or over-cap growth)
- max-lines ratchet: reports 3 pre-existing `ui/` suppressions that are byte-identical to `origin/main` (untouched by this PR); no minimax file is over cap

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On main, Context is a section inside Details. Inspecting its report means expanding content inside that narrow popover.

This stack moves context inspection into a dedicated panel. The parent, #179225, provides the composer entry point and shared report; this PR implements the panel's page. The screenshots compare main with the complete code at this PR's head, including its parent.

## User Impact

Open **View context** from the composer to inspect usage in the Context tab. Usage, Refresh and Compact share one header. Open one category at a time; lists above 20 items initially show eight, with **Show all** and local search.

Bar and category highlights follow pointer and keyboard focus. Escape closes the category and returns focus. Background refresh preserves the open category, search and scroll. Short bottom docks scroll the whole page so the header cannot hide the list.

## Validation

- Historical full CI passed on 16558bfe65fb9218d69a03b0b2b0e52ba8357d2d (run 39730813401).
- Integrated validation: 190 focused unit tests, UI/UI-chat/E2E test types, i18n, scoped lint and CSS checks passed. Native desktop/mobile flows passed (2 cases, 24.59s).
- Independent review completed; the identified billing-test mismatch was corrected while preserving cost coverage.
- These new screenshots were captured through the real application entry points: two main scenarios and two PR scenarios passed, using the same synthetic session, report and 1440 × 1100 viewport in light and dark appearances.

### Current-main integration (October 23)

Current head: `9d794db5951536e59dfb2248594352979163408d`, integrated with main `0e1123fbfca8`. Latest-head CI is pending. The preceding run failed the total-CSS growth policy; the approved cleanup below does not eliminate that blocker.

Preserves main's lazy panel loading and lazy English catalogs, local lazy-load recovery, and Environment branch publication. The removed import registry was not restored. Saved Context tabs stay cold until presented; the shared report owner still gates reads on visible demand and retains its connection/session fences.

Validation: 30 focused unit/component tests; bundled desktop and mobile Context flows (2 cases, 9.52 s test time); UI and UI-chat types; i18n; scoped lint; independent P0–P2 review. Updated recovery coverage follows the appropriate renderer in each stack layer, including failure, retry, loading, and an accepted report. No provider visibility, quota policy, Gateway method, or schema changes were added during integration.

[Matched current-main/final-head desktop and mobile screenshots, plus measured CSS gate details](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180332#issuecomment-6368204368). The older gallery below remains explicitly historical.

### Approved CSS cleanup (proposals 2 and 3)

Only redundant declarations, shared label truncation and equal-specificity loading selectors were consolidated. Complete-stack production CSS shrank **481 raw bytes / 28 gzip bytes** (parent contribution: 30 raw / 10 gzip, already included). Eighteen before/after screenshots and four computed-style snapshots are byte-identical; four candidate desktop/mobile E2E cases passed. [Measurements, exact heads, screenshot hashes and proof limitations](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180332#issuecomment-6368204368). No budget or design change; no merge or auto-merge.

## Risk and coverage

The page uses the shared report store introduced by the parent. Its requests, scope checks, retry policy, token calculations and compaction command remain unchanged by this layer. No schema, endpoint, report field or polling was added.

Transient refresh failures retain accepted data; disconnects and authenticated-scope changes still clear it at the report owner. Compact uses the native action/optimistic-state pattern. Its callback cannot reliably provide a successful before/after token delta, so the page does not display a “tokens freed” badge.

Proof uses synthetic Gateway data in the real application, not a live model run. The narrow-layout proof uses the native mobile sheet and the same renderer; desktop retains its 480px minimum.

prs.title: feat(ui): move context breakdown into the composer popover
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Context inspection currently takes space inside Details and nests contributor lists and management actions there. This change moves the compact report to the existing composer context ring and opens the full report in one native Context panel.

Closes #179147.

## User Impact

- Context is removed from desktop and mobile Details. The composer ring keeps its existing size and warning colors.
- Its popover shows the five context categories, latest-run tokens and cost when available, and compact provider quota rows. **View context** opens the existing Context panel; Refresh and Compact stay in that panel.
- The panel preserves contributor groups, deferred tool information, scroll position, and the unsent draft. Unverified sizes remain marked and deferred schemas remain outside current usage totals.

## Internal Behavior

The popover and retained Context tab share one session/model/provider-scoped report and in-flight request. Usage changes refresh the shared result without clearing accepted content. Transient read failures use the existing Gateway retry owner, with no healthy polling; hidden views pause the pending deadline and server retry hints remain respected. Retired requests cannot replace current results or produce a toast for a newer connection. Explicit Refresh failures use the existing toast messages.

## Validation

- Shared report and rendered adapter: 10 tests passed, 1.45 s native-runner wall. Regression cases failed before the corresponding fixes: duplicate reads after a session rename, an immediate retry bypassing a 600-second server hint, and a stale manual refresh displaying a newer connection's failure.
- Composer browser geometry and palette: 8 tests passed, 1.85 s Vitest duration.
- Production-bundle visual matrix: 32 scenarios passed, 50.17 s test time; three themes, light/dark, two/three quota windows, high usage, cost, long email, loading, offline/missing report, estimates and credits.
- Final-source desktop and mobile Context flow: 2 tests passed, 7.27 s tests / 15.92 s Vitest duration including the production build, including one report read across the popover-to-panel handoff, compaction, draft retention and the full skills catalog.
- Existing Details coverage migrated after review: 14 unit cases passed (1.61 s runner), 2 geometry/navigation E2E cases passed (14.30 s tests / 22.31 s duration), and session-event-to-painted-ring E2E passed (0.89 s test / 9.36 s duration). Removed assertions for the retired Details Context disclosure; retained dynamic percentage, freshness, warning colors, privacy and keyboard navigation coverage.
- UI types, controller guards, changed CSS stylelint, i18n verification and changed-document MDX checks passed. Final scoped type-aware lint also passed. Fresh native `codex review --uncommitted` returned no actionable regressions after the test cutover corrections; its 21 focused tests also passed.

### Integration validation

Completed the remaining test cutover: removed the retired Context arrival/disclosure test and its private helper (57 fewer lines), and stopped the Progress recovery E2E from waiting for the removed Context meter. Outputs/Environment sibling tests and both desktop/mobile Progress recovery cases pass, preserving request counts, 30/60-second backoff and zero write calls. Formatting and focused review passed.

Updated onto main at 0d0df35. This preserves main's lazy English catalogs, Details lifecycle and layout, automation observation, and Outputs behavior. Removed the redundant Details props wrapper and the retired Context disclosure. The popover and shared report behavior are unchanged.

Existing tests now follow the compact quota/cost presentation while retaining provider scoping, reset values, billing breakdown and navigation checks. The compaction regression now uses the native Context panel and still verifies busy state, duplicate-click prevention and the current callback.
