prs.title: perf(workspace): reuse admitted child directory membership
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Managed sandbox turn startup repeats directory enumeration after its canonical workspace scan has already accepted the directory's children.

Timing-only attribution from slow-start diagnostics puts substantial time in this path: one 33.640 s sandbox preparation spent 22.638 s synchronizing the canonical workspace and 6.144 s synchronizing its projection. In the selected slow-log population, canonical synchronization reached 26.263 s and projection synchronization reached 14.624 s. These are diagnostic samples, not population latency estimates. Other preparations contained up to 50.802 s without a named subspan, so this bounded change does not explain or fix the entire reported startup delay.

## User Impact

Removes filesystem work from managed workspace synchronization while preserving the selected files and directory membership. No configuration, schema, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scan already joins children before parents. Carry each accepted child's direct parent instead of reopening the directory to rediscover that it contains an accepted child. Directories without accepted children retain their empty/derived-only classification; that scan stops once a derived entry determines the result. File containment, symlink, cancellation, and inventory limits remain intact.

The existing workspace computation driver gains a `startup` case with 32 files per directory. It repeatedly calls the actual managed-workspace preparation owner, validates reconciled contents and settled recovery state, and reports CPU, memory, GC and event-loop measurements.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule recorded before measurement: two concurrent baseline/candidate pairs under one guarded quiet-slot lock, swapping interleaved 16-CPU assignments; 10,000 tracked synthetic files, one changed guest file per reuse, ten warm measured samples per side per pair. Decide on paired mean deltas. Reject at >=20% adverse mean or >=10% adverse in both pairs; opposite signs or >5x baseline spread require another pair for a gating metric. p95 needs 200 samples and p99 1,000; smaller tails are context. GC pause shifts below 1 ms are context; total GC, promotion and event-loop delay retain their gates, including max-pause limits.

The directory-membership regression fails on the original code for unnecessary directory reads and passes with the change. All 43 focused scanner/manifest tests pass (3 files; 34.10 s wrapper wall time). Changed-file formatting/lint and core typechecking pass. Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable) found no actionable P0/P1/P2 findings; the final simplification was also reviewed clean.

Production delta: -7 lines. Benchmark and documentation additions make the workload rerunnable.

The initial two concurrent pairs completed successfully under the shared production guard, with CPU placement swapped for pair 2. A third pair using the original placement resolved the mixed-sign total-GC gate. Ten measured preparations per side per pair; identical synthetic Git workspaces with 10,000 files in 32-file directories and one guest edit per preparation. The benchmark exercises the real managed-workspace preparation owner and verifies reconciled contents and settled state. No guard interruption, request failure, or content mismatch occurred.

| Metric (baseline → candidate) | Pair 1 | Pair 2 | Mean paired delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Preparation mean | 1,448.29 → 1,412.65 ms | 1,492.25 → 1,453.44 ms | -2.53%; -37.22 ms |
| Preparation p50 (n=10/side/pair) | 968.90 → 914.86 ms | 1,005.90 → 977.03 ms | -4.22%; -41.46 ms |
| Process CPU per preparation | 1,592.06 → 1,528.51 ms | 1,590.39 → 1,499.97 ms | -4.84%; -76.98 ms |
| Main-isolate promotion per preparation | 1,553,833 → 1,420,962 bytes | 1,409,685 → 1,279,080 bytes | -8.91%; -131,738 bytes |
| Main-isolate total GC per preparation | 3.463 → 3.588 ms (+3.63%; +0.126 ms) | 3.440 → 2.554 ms (-25.75%; -0.886 ms) | Inconclusive: mixed signs; mean -0.380 ms |
| Mean external peak RSS | 1,707.94 → 1,733.92 MB (+1.52%; +25.98 MB) | 1,759.24 → 1,741.08 MB (-1.03%; -18.16 MB) | Inconclusive: mixed signs; mean +3.91 MB |

The third pair measured preparation mean 1,408.19 → 1,429.05 ms (+1.48%; +20.86 ms), process CPU 1,524.93 → 1,505.94 ms (-1.25%; -18.99 ms), main-isolate total GC 4.250 → 3.433 ms (-19.23%; -0.817 ms), and promotion 1,291,974 → 1,425,392 bytes (+10.33%; +133,418 bytes) per preparation.

Under the three-pair absolute-mean rule, total GC changed by -0.526 ms/preparation (3.718 → 3.192 ms; -14.14% of the baseline mean). Wall time changed by -17.86 ms (-1.23%), CPU by -57.65 ms (-3.67%), promotion by -43,353 bytes (-3.06%), and mean external peak RSS by +5.48 MB (+0.32%). These ratios describe the absolute means; they are not a new balanced placement comparison. No adverse threshold is reached, including the promotion increase in only one pair. The wall-time and promotion signs reverse in pair 3, so the result is treated as roughly neutral latency with reduced CPU work, not a robust latency or promotion win. Landing follows the rule that a net code deletion may land with neutral, non-regressing measurements.

Tail/count context:

- Preparation p95/p99: 5,848.58 → 5,795.41 ms in pair 1; 5,915.95 → 5,830.86 ms in pair 2 (only n=10/side/pair, so both percentiles are context-only).
- Mean of per-preparation event-loop p99 values: 28.069 → 27.360 ms in pair 1 (-2.53%; -0.709 ms; 66–556 / 64–552 samples per histogram); 30.135 → 30.183 ms in pair 2 (+0.16%; +0.048 ms; 64–560 / 64–552 samples). These are not pooled p99 values; every histogram is below 1,000 samples and the mixed signs are inconclusive.
- Maximum single main-isolate GC pause: 5.142 → 5.222 ms in pair 1; 5.585 → 3.732 ms in pair 2. Total collections: 29 → 28 and 29 → 26. Minor collections: 25 → 24 and 25 → 25. Major collections: 2 → 2 and 2 → 0; major and per-collection percentile evidence is below the required counts. GC/promotion diagnostics exclude worker isolates; process CPU and RSS include workers.
- Pair 3 preparation p50: 920.94 → 945.74 ms; p95/p99: 5,819.33 → 5,792.98 ms (n=10/side, tails context-only). Mean per-preparation event-loop p99: 28.053 → 28.588 ms (63–555 / 68–549 samples per histogram, context-only). Maximum GC pause: 18.822 → 5.876 ms; total collections 28 → 28, minor 26 → 24, major 1 → 2. No candidate maximum exceeds the max-pause threshold.

Load context: timed `mpstat` samples averaged 14.59% / 12.20% busy on even/odd CPUs in pair 1 and 13.52% / 13.84% in pair 2 (these include benchmark work). The third pair lacks timed per-CPU samples; the shared guard admitted it at load 7.22, dirty pages 478,348 KiB and production loop max 100.5 ms, and did not interrupt it. Outside load is context, not a run-invalidating gate.

Both fixtures used the same archived base `c537658285b7906c5de296b7c4b379f57d835157`, identical benchmark instrumentation, and only the candidate scanner patch differed. The PR was rebased onto `40172b9e4ff2`; the affected scanner/workspace owner paths were unchanged upstream. Full PR CI passed on exact head `fb2bce5e97497329e1ec5232aa5057108896d274` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40028612752)), including the aggregate gate. Automated Codex review on that head also completed without findings.

Scope: workspace reuse is only part of chat startup. This change does not establish an end-to-end time-to-first-model-request improvement, eliminate container provisioning or queue waits, or claim to fix every observed long startup. No production Gateway was modified.

Admission audit: commands that require a separate turn deliberately wait for the session controller, and pending inputs have a queued presentation path. There is no hard overall admission deadline for a healthy active run; watchdog checks occur while waiting. The long admission sample is consistent with this path, but its journal lacks the controller phase needed to identify the blocker. No lost wakeup was established. A final `stage=queued` label also does not prove that the entire preceding prepared-reply span was queue time. Those waits remain separate follow-up attribution work.

prs.title: fix(github): keep uncaptured publication failures readable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A shared GitHub publication can fail before capturing its workspace snapshot. Reading its options still discovered pull requests even though that failure has no accepted tree to compare, adding unnecessary Git/HTTP work and potentially hiding the failed receipt behind a discovery error.

## User Impact

`sessions.github.options` keeps these failed receipts readable when PR discovery is unavailable. Failures with a captured tree retain the existing published-history reconciliation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The relevance owner now checks its existing tree prerequisite before acquiring PR history. The lazy source carries the original target-bound authority guard through subsequent GitHub reads; the handler still checks session authority before responding. No new cache, configuration, schema, or publication-write behavior.

Production LOC: +6 (35 added / 29 removed). The small growth introduces the lazy acquisition contract and retains the source's authority guard, avoiding a duplicated eligibility guard or a second discovery implementation.

## Evidence

- Regression failed on original production code: unavailable PR discovery returned `FORBIDDEN` instead of the existing failed receipt. It passes with the change and verifies zero PR-owner reads.
- Focused three-file validation: 51 tests passed; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-github-read.test.ts src/gateway/github-publication-relevance.test.ts src/gateway/control-ui-session-prs-publication.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` completed in 96.59 seconds including cold compilation. Exact-head [CI run 40017284393](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40017284393) passed (57 checks passed, 62 skipped); run elapsed time was 827 seconds, including scheduling and all parallel jobs. Per-file CI time was not isolated.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. The configured review provider did not match the helper's requested route; configuration was unchanged.
- Changed-file formatting, lint, and whitespace checks passed.

### Guarded paired measurements

Two concurrent baseline/candidate pairs, with interleaved CPU placement swapped for pair 2, completed with both process and production-guard exits 0. Baseline source: `3f5d04f8ebc9`; candidate overlays the two reviewed production files. The affected owners did not change between that baseline and the PR's rebased parent. Node 26.12.1; isolated synthetic state with 5,000 sessions and 6,000 retained runs; identical two-minute mixed workloads, 32 completed turns per side per pair. No production state or real GitHub credentials were used.

The real options preflight required the failed null-tree receipt on every response and proved eight baseline PR-owner reads versus zero candidate reads before each timed window. The source-entry harness includes instrumentation and first-use module/worker initialization; cold milliseconds are not a prediction for packaged production latency.

| Handler metric | Pair 1: baseline → candidate | Pair 2: baseline → candidate | Mean paired change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cold burst mean, ms (n=8 each side/pair) | 824.769 → 306.140 | 846.752 → 307.246 | −529.067 ms; −63.30% |
| Measured-window mean, ms | 32.200 → 31.020 (n=151 each) | 35.187 → 30.765 (n=152 each) | −2.801 ms; −8.12% |
| Measured-window p99, ms | 134.355 → 135.186 (n=151 each) | 159.822 → 155.801 (n=152 each) | Context only; below 1,000 samples |
| PR-owner reads / options call | 1 → 0 | 1 → 0 | Removed |
| Successful Git launches / cold options call | 0.25 → 0 (2 → 0 across 8 calls) | 0.25 → 0 (2 → 0 across 8 calls) | Removed |

The warm p99 deltas have opposite signs: +0.831 ms (+0.62%) and −4.020 ms (−2.52%), so they are also inconclusive under v5.2. Canonical successful-launch instrumentation covers broker and local processes. Cold burst-window and direct handler attribution agree on 2→0 Git launches. Warm handler-attributed launches were zero on both sides; the entire mixed workload launched 48 Git processes per side in each pair. Setup-wide or mixed-workload counts are not presented as per-options-call counts.

| Resource metric | Pair 1: baseline → candidate | Pair 2: baseline → candidate | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total GC, ms/turn | 45.834 → 48.001 | 46.358 → 47.555 | Paired +1.682 ms / +3.65%; below gate |
| Promotion, MB/turn | 41.563 → 40.927 | 41.054 → 42.966 | Inconclusive: −0.637 MB (−1.53%), +1.913 MB (+4.66%); neither otherwise gates |
| Event-loop p99, ms | 39.322 → 41.288 (n=5,791 each) | 40.600 → 41.714 (n=5,762 each) | Paired +1.540 ms / +3.87%; below gate |
| Minor GC p95, ms | 6.046 → 6.462 (n=287/292) | 6.558 → 6.846 (n=295/291) | Paired +0.352 ms; context under v5.3 |
| Minor GC p99, ms | 9.214 → 10.494 (n=287/292) | 8.830 → 9.662 (n=295/291) | Context: below 1,000 samples |
| Major GC p95, ms | 52.990 → 59.646 (n=15/15) | 61.950 → 61.438 (n=13/15) | Context: below 50 collections |
| Major GC p99, ms | 59.902 → 61.694 (n=15/15) | 75.262 → 62.974 (n=13/15) | Context: below 50 collections |
| Maximum single GC pause, ms | 59.900 → 61.678 | 74.791 → 62.952 | Neither exceeds max(50 ms, 2× baseline max) |

Major-tail deltas are also opposite-sign context: p95 +6.656 ms (+12.56%) / −0.512 ms (−0.83%); p99 +1.792 ms (+2.99%) / −12.288 ms (−16.33%). No metric crossed v5 thresholds, and no third pair was required by v5.2.

Both sides of pair 2 retained a roughly 2.75-second shared-receipt-read outlier. This is a targeted receipt-availability fix with avoided cold discovery work and a modest warm mean improvement; it does not establish a fix for aggregate production options p99. Earlier observer/fixture failures and an unaffected session-only-scope pair were excluded from the decision.

prs.title: feat(update): show recovery disk use and retire selected untracked copies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Recovery copies can consume substantial disk space without appearing in status, and old unregistered migration originals or orphan update captures have no supported retirement command. A space-rejected original-state capture also needs an unmistakable warning when the update continues.

**Dependency #181033 is merged** as `fb9e117745a74a0f65c098bd1392d15daffd76e0` (2026-10-23). This branch now incorporates that main commit; its 31-file diff is only the reviewed recovery-visibility delta. PR #181025 and Doctor capture reuse remain separately owned.

Related: #174253 #162622 #179789.

## User Impact

- `openclaw status` / `--json`, normal read-only Doctor, and `doctor --lint` report local logical bytes and counts by recovery-copy kind and eligibility.
- `openclaw update cleanup --include-unmanifested <path>` explicitly selects one known unregistered migration original or orphan update capture. Repeat it for additional exact paths. Preview shows bytes, modification age, and irreversible consequences; applying still requires offline ownership and separate consent.
- Insufficient measured capture space produces a prominent **NO ORIGINAL-STATE SNAPSHOT** warning with needed/available bytes in stderr, final text/JSON, and durable run steps. The update can still succeed.

**No total-size cap and no byte-budget-driven deletion.** Unmanifested/orphan originals are never automatically selected. Retirement permanently loses those selected originals; maintain an independent backup when that recovery history is still needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing recovery inventory and retirement custody rather than introduce another retention owner. Status bounds directory entries, metadata reads, and elapsed scan time; limits only return an incomplete observed-byte estimate. A large shared history database is not copied just to render status, and unknown eligibility stays protected. Logical bytes are not physical allocation or a promise of reclaimed space.

Explicit retirement refuses pending/retained recovery references (including aliases), configured live databases and sidecars, symlinks/hardlinks/nonregular files, changed identities, and paths outside the existing recovery inventory. Current config, references, and custody are checked again before removal; files are unlinked individually instead of recursively removing an uninspected tree. Existing automatic eligibility rules are unchanged.

Space measurements survive the existing worker diagnostic transport; they do not create an update failure gate or remove old copies to make room. Installed-updater behavior requires an updater containing this change; staging a candidate cannot retrofit an older running driver's initial capture warning.

Simplification: shared inventory/projection serves both status forms and Doctor; no new cache, database schema, persistent inventory, or retention policy. The necessary growth is the exact-path safety/identity checks, bounded diagnostic scan, and behavioral refusal/transport coverage across the three requested outcomes.

prs.title: fix: Ask OpenClaw rejects implicit Bedrock SDK inference
prs.body:
Related: #138584

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Ask OpenClaw rejecting a successful Bedrock Converse inference check when authentication implicitly uses the AWS SDK and the exact credential is observable.

## User Impact

A working, unpinned Bedrock SDK connection can pass the verified-owner gate without requiring an explicit provider auth override. Missing proof or actual credential rotation still rejects the binding. No configuration migration or new options.

This fixes a reproduced code defect, **not a demonstrated fix for every persistent failure after changing models**. A reported symptom persisted across retries and recovered after restart; that full process/reload scenario has not been reproduced or established as fixed here.

## Why This Change Was Made

Execution supplies the successful model ID and API to auth resolution. The runtime-owner check dropped both, even though implicit SDK selection requires `modelApi === "bedrock-converse-stream"`. It could therefore re-resolve the same connection as API-key auth and reject the successful SDK owner's fingerprint.

Both binding creation and later reuse now forward the recorded model facts, require them for SDK verification, and disable profile fallback when execution did not select a profile. Pinned-profile checks and fingerprint comparison stay fail-closed.

The existing runtime-owner resolver and Bedrock tests move into focused sibling files because the original modules are at their enforced size-growth limits. CLI/plugin-harness behavior is unchanged. No cache resets, reload changes, source-label hash changes, or endpoint-alias changes are included. The earlier credential-resolution-source fix in #142877 does not repair this SDK branch.

## Evidence

- On unmodified production source at `bdeca1661473fa73194a55df2bcfc1b3b64e9501`, the regression's implicit-SDK case fails at binding creation with `The successful inference credential is no longer the active route owner.`
- Final candidate: **63 tests passed across 4 files** (verified binding, Bedrock binding, setup turn, execution fingerprint).
- Regression uses the real provider auth resolver and fingerprint functions with synthetic AWS environment values. It checks implicit and explicit SDK selection, initial binding and later reuse, missing model facts, token rotation before binding/reuse, credential removal, and the existing refusal of unobservable SDK principals.
- Complete changed-code checks passed: production/test types, lint, formatting, module-size guards, dead exports, import cycles, and selected repository guards.
- Independent canonical autoreview: scoped-clean at P0–P2 for the final candidate. This is supporting code review, not maintainer/security approval.
- Measured with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: Bedrock file **6.35 s wall**, 3 tests; existing verified-binding file **7.05 s wall**, 36 tests. Vitest durations 4.71 s / 5.53 s including transform/import/setup. No real timers, live AWS requests, Gateway boots, or persistent state in the new cases. Hosted CI duration is not available at submission.

Commands:
```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/system-agent/verified-inference.test.ts src/system-agent/verified-inference.bedrock.test.ts src/system-agent/setup-inference-turn.test.ts src/agents/execution-auth-binding.test.ts
node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base bdeca1661473fa73194a55df2bcfc1b3b64e9501 --timed -- src/system-agent/verified-inference.ts src/system-agent/verified-inference-runtime-owner.ts src/system-agent/verified-inference.test.ts src/system-agent/verified-inference.bedrock.test.ts
```

Not claimed: live Bedrock inference, full Gateway/UI end-to-end verification, or the full build/test suite. The installed Gateway and its configuration were not changed. Allow edits by maintainers is enabled.

prs.title: fix(doctor): reuse verified captures across healthy repair runs
prs.body:
Refs #173564 #174253
Related: #173564, #174253

## What Problem This Solves

Repeated standalone `doctor --fix` runs on healthy, unchanged state retained another full original-state capture each time. Avoiding a copy was not enough: Doctor itself dirtied schema metadata and plugin lease/index pages, and WAL-mode source headers differ from the retained single-file images.

This PR is scoped to **reuse a verified capture when state is unchanged**. Deferring the first capture until the first actual mutation is a separate follow-up below. The existing eager pre-repair safety boundary stays intact.

## User Impact

Three consecutive healthy standalone repair runs now retain **one** original capture. A real config, database, filesystem, or declared-resource change still requires a fresh capture. No equivalence checks are replaced with timestamps or logical-row comparisons.

Update-associated originals, Docker activation markers, retention, pending-recovery protection, full-integrity capture semantics, and free-space checks remain intact. No live deployment or release is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Verify the newest eligible sealed standalone original, every retained payload, and the complete rediscovered config/includes, database owners, plugin declarations, files, directories, missing paths, symlinks, permissions and SHA-256 content.
- Use the existing fresh-capture database owner for discovery and canonical SQLite images rather than a parallel discovery path. WAL-mode normalization changes header bytes even without data changes; compare **complete canonical-image digests**, preserving source fingerprints across preparation, not masked headers or selected rows. Nonempty WAL/journal data still refuses reuse.
- Keep healthy schema version/header metadata idempotent. Full repair still runs and performs real recognized repairs.
- Plan plugin registry and configured-install repair against fresh read-only metadata before acquiring a durable lease. Empty work must not insert/delete lease rows: deleted-cell bytes alone break exact reuse. Actual work is replanned under the original lease and effect guards. Bundled-record planning is shared with the existing repair owner rather than duplicated.

Reuse still streams retained payloads and prepares temporary SQLite images, then removes those images. This avoids additional **retained** full originals, not all I/O or temporary space. Incomplete or unprovable comparison, PostgreSQL, and unknown plugin coverage fall back to fresh capture. Verification limits are cache misses, never update failure policy.

## Conflict repair for authorized landing — October 23, 2026

Updated head: `e4ed2faffae76d54d4e01c6b90de9a6355783128`; integrated `origin/main` at `74cb12dd2c7597f0d9a388b94bb2b776cac6db25` because GitHub reported a merge conflict. Last passing head/run: `9b02f8104463aadcd118319736787e6d8ec3bbfc`, CI `39874891637` attempt 1.

- Re-read all three conflicted files in full. Combined verified capture reuse with main's 600-second capture deadline and awaited cancellation settlement; retained both registry owners/imports and main's stale-generation repair. Kept behavior-specific migration preview and first completed receipt assertions, not a fragile schema-tail inventory.
- Fresh affected proof: **108 tests in 5 files passed**, 235.77s total. The actual Doctor regression still produces **1 → 1 → 1** captures for three healthy runs, then **2** after a real config change while preserving the first. Capture timeout, registry repair, exact reuse/cancellation, and migration suites pass.
- Core, commands-Doctor-test, and infra-test typechecks passed. Targeted lint: **0 errors/warnings**; formatting and PR-delta whitespace check pass. Private HOME/state/TMPDIR and verified private handoff store; no live state or service operations. Compiler proof used a task-local physical dependency graph with the shared pnpm package store after the normal global graph correctly refused checkout containment.
- Fresh independent API-only review of exact head `e4ed2faffae76d54d4e01c6b90de9a6355783128` completed: **no substantiated P0–P2 code or test-quality findings**, after all 12 PR diffs, complete changed production files, all three touched/new test files and relevant owner tests/contracts.
- Fresh exact-head CI run `40030580717` has one inherited failure: job `120678164724`, `src/flows/doctor-health.deletion-recovery.test.ts` / “refreshes supplied missing-history discovery after maintenance admits a newer configured store”, with `SqliteWorkerError: Shared-state admission requires the host broker`. The same case fails on the clean main parent `74cb12dd2c7597f0d9a388b94bb2b776cac6db25` without PR changes (1 failed / 1 passed), and on this PR in a four-file reproduction (1 failed / 52 passed / 4 platform-skipped). The failing test/support and stack owner files are unchanged between CI base `1ba6f92d40748765de3b7bf325ee24b4d08f483f` and tested merge `5fe31ed647b3d174b2e33bf0a80ff25e0545e50f`. This is independently attributed baseline failure, **not green CI**. All 92 CI jobs finished: 63 successful, 27 intentionally skipped, and 2 failures (the single inherited test shard plus its aggregate gate). Native inherited-failure landing admission verified the exact head, source/evidence identities, independent security/review and the writer’s existing CI-only ruleset bypass. Merged as `1d99689ccf817eed5526f20576920841751cfc6c`; ancestry on `origin/main` verified.
- Exact-head CI independently passes the real Doctor repeat/change regression in **41.267s**. No CI rerun or synthetic push was used to chase green.

## Prior-head evidence

Candidate: `9b02f8104463aadcd118319736787e6d8ec3bbfc`; merge base `a39dd6d4968891599257cca778d2530ceba5d037`. No relevant owner drift or merge conflict required a rebase at preparation.

- **Permanent real-Doctor regression, red then green:** after first-install initialization, run actual `doctorCommand(..., {repair:true, nonInteractive:true})` three times with real maintenance, repair, snapshot, comparison and retention. Prior published `0bb1d49b` produced capture counts **1, 2, 3** and changed SQLite bytes each run. The final implementation produces **1, 1, 1**, with the entire healthy shared SQLite file byte-identical after every run. A subsequent real config change produces a second capture and preserves the first. No repair or capture owner is mocked; only installation-root selection is redirected to a disposable fixture. Private HOME/config/state/TMPDIR and external service-repair policy are enforced.
- Repeat suite: **1 test passed, 52.763s test time / 55.68s wall time**. It intentionally performs six real Doctor invocations (two first-install preparation runs, three healthy runs, one changed run). A helper-only test missed the original incident, so this composition is retained despite its cost.
- Capture suite: **9 tests passed, 68.28s wall time** including compiler preparation. Covers exact inventory/content, retained seals, WAL/journal refusal, 257 MiB payloads, verification-bound fallback, successful 65 MiB WAL-mode reuse, and cancellation/settled cleanup during selection, discovery, and canonical-image preparation.
- **Production-identical `f40c9526` aggregate: 250 tests passed across 14 files, 179.65s wall time** (89 unit, 123 infra, 38 commands). Includes all affected schema/snapshot suites, missing-plugin repair, registry, original capture, rehearsal capture, retention, repeat-Doctor and reuse tests. One earlier registry-test failure was inherited `OPENCLAW_PROFILE=odin` leaking into expected CLI wording; rerunning with that profile unset passed, without changing production or test expectations.
- Core, commands-test and infra-test typechecks passed. Targeted lint: **0 warnings/errors**. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Documentation audit: **15,831 links, 0 broken**.
- Full-file audit of both touched/new test suites completed. Tests assert observable captures, exact bytes, preserved originals and settled work; no source-text mirrors or fake repair results.
- **Final-head CI repair proof:** `f40c9526` CI found a fixture lifetime bug: per-case cleanup removed a cached native broker's Unix socket. Reproduced locally with a short private TMPDIR (same two initial-capture failures), then joined retained readers and the broker before fixture removal. The complete capture suite and complete migration suite pass in order: **70 tests, 2 files, 111.10s wall time**. The second CI failure was a pre-existing hardcoded migration-preview inventory omitting v30/v31; the test now asserts its specific audit migration and first completed schema receipt while preserving exact event/owner/version data checks. ## Follow-up: capture at first mutation

Prior isolated production-path probes established why empty repair reports are not safe admission to defer capture:

- Current shared schema v31 can return `needsOpenClawStateDatabaseSchemaRepair(..., "doctor") === false` and `{changes: [], warnings: []}`, while full Doctor repair updates `schema_meta.updated_at`. With a recognized retired `database_verifications` table, the same signals occur while that table is actually dropped.
- A real on-disk channel plugin with only `doctor.runConfigSequence` returns no config-repair preview, yet its first sequence call repairs a file and its second is genuinely a no-op. That callback has no complete planning contract.

This PR fixes recurring healthy schema/index bookkeeping and needless plugin leases. It does not skip full schema repair based on version detectors or empty reports: actual retired-table removal, opaque plugin callbacks, and post-scope service changes remain reasons to retain eager capture.

prs.title: refactor: fold single-consumer parsers and private frames
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Internal one-consumer helpers and modules split responsibility away from the code that actually uses it.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior, configuration, CLI, protocol, SDK, or stored-data changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep private callbacks and annotations at their existing point of use. Fold the patch-preview parser into its sole view owner and the runtime-parity Markdown renderer into its report owner. Shared algorithms remain shared; lazy loading, input validation, live authority, FIFO ordering, cleanup, scrollback limits, and cache identity remain intact. No markup or styles change.

Net removal: **178 production lines across 16 production paths**. Tests add **23 lines** by extending an existing public Team Reports case to cover case-insensitive work-session lookup, no leakage between active members, and quiet-member links. Counts exclude tests, fixtures, generated files, and declarations; moved bodies are credited only by the actual net diff. The retired parser's assertion-baseline entry is removed; its existing regex-backed assertion now documents its invariant at the new owner rather than moving the allowance.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

No defensive guard is removed. The private provider-filter, route-transition, and existing-push-subscription wrappers' extra promise-adoption continuations are not retained as timing contracts. Their actual menu/navigation/subscription awaits, cancellation/current-authority checks, ordering and cleanup remain. The helpers came from the completed ownership work in #164153, #122713, #129348 and #179517; this does not remove those features or their guarantees.

Internal Web Push client method lookup may occur after subscription JSON validation instead of before it; side-effectful property getters on the internal typed client are not a supported contract. Malformed browser subscriptions are still rejected before an external request.

## Evidence

Focused touched-owner tests passed serially with one worker, including 32 parser/diff cases and seven selected public tool-card cases; 29 selected ChatLog/event cases; 14 model-picker cases; 20 route/browser/native-ingress cases; and the existing Signal, request timing, lineage, Web Push, report, theme and stream-assembler boundaries. Targeted native typechecks, typed lint, format and line caps passed for each packet. Every parser/input/stat bound, malformed structured-to-text fallback, hunk coordinate rule, and tool-view cache invalidation is retained.

The changed Team Reports file passed all 16 existing cases both before and after the production fold; the head focused command took 3.1 seconds including runner startup. This is refactor-under-green proof, not a claim that a bug was reproduced. Hosted CI seconds are not available yet.

Fresh isolated review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. All 11 final structural guards passed, including zero runtime/static cycles, suppression/assertion/mock ratchets, wrapper/eager closure, frozen updater bindings, prompt-prefix stability, line caps, UI guards and keyless i18n verification. Exact-head PR CI supplies the broad build and suite proof. No broad local builds, whole-graph typechecks, or Gateway E2Es were run under the shared-host CPU budget. This refactor makes no live-provider, live-device, screenshot, or visual-layout claim.

prs.title: refactor: trim private bundled plugin overrides
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Bundled plugins carry private override arguments that no production caller supplies, plus alternate branches exercised only by those overrides in tests.

## User impact

No user-visible change or migration is intended. Supported defaults, features and external contracts stay intact.

## What changed

Use the existing production defaults for private catalog, approval, lifecycle, polling, storage-wrapper and QA helpers. Tests select the same behavior through scoped dependency spies, configuration and clock controls. Public plugin SDK options, configuration, CLI flags, protocol fields, stored data and lower cancellation/authorization contracts remain intact.

This is the bundled-plugin slice of one 112-production-line cleanup, split by area to keep each PR below 80 files. This slice removes 46 net production lines and 31 net test/support lines across 41 files.

Paired core slice: #181851.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- The private Telegram polling-lease wait override had no production supplier. Its zero-wait and oversized-input branches were synthetic override cases, not serving behavior; handoff keeps the existing fixed five-second wait and all abort, identity and replacement checks.

Fixes an unused-export failure in dependency validation when the session-row metrics implementation type is exported even though no supported consumer imports that name.

prs.body:
Related: #181794 (merged), which made the wiki read percent-encoded link paths; this is the writing side.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in native render mode, `openclaw wiki compile` writes links to pages whose file names contain a space, such as `[Meeting notes](sources/meeting notes.md)`, which Markdown viewers and the wiki's own parser show as plain text instead of a link, in `index.md`, the dashboards and the generated related blocks.

## User Impact

User impact: in native vaults, generated index, dashboard and backlink entries for pages with spaces in their file names are clickable links again.

## Why This Change Was Made

CommonMark does not allow a space in a bare link destination; the destination has to be in angle brackets. `formatWikiLink` now writes destinations that contain spaces, parentheses or angle brackets as `<...>`, with `<` and `>` escaped. Other destinations, and Obsidian render mode, are unchanged. The wiki's link reader already resolves `<...>` destinations (#181380). The README now says so next to the paragraph #181794 added.

## Evidence

Shipped CLI from this checkout (Node 24.22.1, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `node scripts/run-node.mjs`) on an isolated vault created with `openclaw wiki init` (`vault.renderMode: native`), with `entities/plan.md` and `sources/meeting notes.md` (which links `[Plan](../entities/plan.md)`), then `openclaw wiki compile`. The generated lines, and the link nodes `mdast-util-from-markdown` (the parser memory-wiki uses) finds in each file:

```text

entities/plan.md:  - [Meeting notes](../sources/meeting notes.md)

```

prs.title: perf(memory): avoid duplicate cosine evaluation in PostgreSQL search
prs.body:
Related: #181922 (original candidate and measurements; GitHub refused reopening after the rebased branch update).

## What Problem This Solves

Exact PostgreSQL memory searches evaluate cosine distance twice per eligible row because the selected distance and ORDER BY use separately bound expressions.

## User Impact

Vector and hybrid memory searches do less database work while preserving exact IDs, ordering, scores, zero-vector eligibility and limits. No schema, configuration, ranking, writer or scheduling change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Order by the selected `dist` alias. This one-line plugin-owner change reduces a 20k-row search from 40,000 to 20,000 cosine evaluations. The norm predicate and ID tie-break remain unchanged. PostgreSQL never executes the supplied scope-count builder, so no COUNT scan is removed.

The committed benchmark exercises production PostgreSQL retrieval/merge and file-backed SQLite KNN with the deterministic PGMEMSTORE fixture, without model calls. It records every search statement and EXPLAIN ANALYZE/BUFFERS plan. The additional source is reproducible proof tooling; the production delta is +1/-1.

## Evidence

Owner acceptance (coordinator, 2026-10-23): ordering by the selected distance removes the duplicate cosine evaluation (40k → 20k distance computations per 20k-chunk search) with identical result hashes and counts; local 20k/50k gates and concurrency passed, and the single Testbox p95 block gain (23.111 ms) sat 0.1 ms inside its spread. Accepted under the standing direction that every removed unit of work counts.

The original preregistered wall-time gate remains recorded: 100 AB/BA pairs per flow/corpus after five warmups per arm, five blocks of 20. The final local campaign passed both sizes; the single Testbox campaign missed the 20k vector p95 spread criterion by 0.113 ms. The coordinator explicitly accepts deterministic work removal instead. No samples were excluded and no replacement Testbox campaign was run. The earlier failed 50k hybrid campaign also remains in the evidence.

Final-source local paired results at `6313d608d8f2bed2f1a36a94562f7344b1922be7`:

| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |

|20k|hybrid|258.368 / 262.896|201.731 / 205.105|
|50k|vector|807.041 / 827.934|660.457 / 689.025|
|50k|hybrid|831.838 / 871.760|687.533 / 716.000|

All sampled hashes and six boundary pairs per corpus matched byte-for-byte; SQL counts stayed vector 1 / keyword 1 / hybrid 2, with no keyword or narrow-scope regression beyond spread. SQLite KNN references: 20k 63.437/72.836ms and 50k 111.507/119.465ms p50/p95.

Final-source Testbox A/B ([run 40022866391](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40022866391)):

prs.title: fix: confirm objective replacement when a session already has a goal
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated Goal submissions in the Control UI, including when the agent is already executing the current goal.

## User Impact

Submitting another `/goal <objective>` (including creation aliases) or using the Goal composer offers **Cancel** and **Replace objective** instead of a creation error or an ambiguous Stop action.

- Cancel or Escape preserves the proposed draft and leaves the running turn untouched.
- Confirming during an executing goal interrupts that exact turn, waits for its work to settle, pauses and edits the same goal, then resumes through normal continuation admission.
- Goal identity, accounting, budget, history, and timer are retained. An exhausted budget is not reset to force a restart.
- Idle and paused replacements remain status-preserving edits. Completed-goal restrictions, explicit management commands, first creation, and textual CLI/TUI behavior are unchanged.

A failed or unverified stage does not automatically resume. The draft and original recovery request remain available. If interrupted output cannot be saved, replacement stops before editing or resuming and tells the operator to preserve visible text.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both submission forms share the established confirmation and async recovery UI. The running case uses one lifecycle-owned operation rather than a blind sequence of browser RPCs: existing Stop, Goal mutation, and normal Resume owners retain authority, physical settlement, and durable retry behavior.

The decision is tied to the original session, goal revision, and executing run. Stale decisions cannot stop a newer run, concurrent controls cannot be overwritten, and the admission fence does not cancel unrelated queued work.

## Evidence

- Copy-only refinement on `6504be6f…`: both replacement confirmations now use one clear sentence. The complete 34-test replacement suite and both production-built Chromium flows pass; production UI/E2E-chat types, focused lint/formatting and i18n verification pass. Fresh independent review of the two-file copy/assertion diff found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Runtime behavior is unchanged.
- 121 focused UI tests pass, plus two production-built Chromium flows covering literal and structured submissions, running confirmation, Cancel/Escape, and resumed-run presentation.
- All 42 Goal Gateway tests pass, including 13 replacement cases: exact-run interruption, physical settlement, same-ID replay, partial-stage recovery, stale/concurrent changes, unrelated pending admissions, interrupted-history warnings, allowed/denied session access, and real role revocation during settlement, pause, edit, Resume admission, and recovery. The admission-isolation and warning regressions were demonstrated red before their repairs.
- Latest-stable 2026.10.6 install-over proof preserves the complete original Goal, accounting/timers, both durable operation receipts, all 26 original transcript events and 18 readable messages. Exact old edit replay is idempotent.
- The installed candidate replaces an actually executing goal on one persistent read/write operator connection: the original model stream closes 436 ms before replacement inference begins. Same Goal/budget/accounting baseline retained; interrupt/pause/edit/resume receipts occur once. Cold-process replay changes neither inference count, 43 events, 10 receipts nor 24 history messages. This uses a synthetic loopback model, not live-provider inference.
- The stale restart-safe Goal test caller identified by PR CI is migrated; its complete 32-test suite, both affected strict test-type graphs, and the required failed-CI test selection pass locally.
- Focused Stop, worker inference, budget-policy, prompt-prefix, archive, and compaction consumer checks pass. Production/test types, lint, formatting, i18n, documentation, assertion/timeout/line and SQLite-worker ratchets, and production build are checked separately.
- Fresh canonical independent reviews of the implementation and final test-only CI/authority repair found no actionable P0–P2 defects after earlier findings were repaired. Hosted review and exact-head PR CI remain separately reported.

- Hosted ClawSweeper review completed on `78f955a5ef7af50cfe6091b0ae79353672bc3085`: **no findings**, security concern cleared, ready for maintainer review ([review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181688#issuecomment-6367421480)).

**Current-head CI recovered:** [run 40017700073, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40017700073/attempts/2) completed successfully on unchanged `6504be6f…`: **89 successful jobs, 20 skipped**. Following the documented one-time failed-job infrastructure-recovery route after the Android SDK extraction failure, all three selected failed leaves now pass, including packaged Android native execution and both previously failing Vitest shards. The native CI CheckRun (`120683774920`) and protected Security Review commit status (`57137193413`, [publisher](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40032479939)) are both successful. No source rewrite, full-CI redispatch or check bypass was used. Original attempt-1 failures and the exact-merge/main controls are retained; passing recovery supplies missing hosted coverage, not proof that the original causes were repaired or that the tests are flaky.

The failure is “Subagent terminal execution changed” in the inline child follow-up timeout case. The hosted failure was not reproduced, not fixed or relabeled green. prs.title: perf(sqlite): batch database page-cache progress
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Periodic Linux database page-cache warming sends a progress request through the Gateway for every session and message batch, even when each read touches very few bytes. Large session stores consequently create thousands of main-isolate request envelopes, launch comparisons, file inspections, and transfer handshakes during maintenance.

## User Impact

The warmer reports progress in roughly 1 MiB chunks while preserving its hot-page selection, byte budget, pacing, cancellation, and read-only process ownership. Requests whose caller owns the deadline also stop calculating an unused file-size-based timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

The database payloads already stay in a separate process. Coalescing progress at that owner removes unnecessary main-thread work without another cache, worker, configuration option, or schema change. Progress replies remain independent snapshots and every bounded read still checks the pass budget.

Runtime LOC: +7 net. The added byte counter and condition preserve the existing pacing/budget contract while suppressing per-session replies; the small timeout branch preserves default deadlines for other callers. Test LOC: -6 net. The standalone measurement tools are not runtime code.

## Evidence

- The unused-budget regression fails on the original code and passes with the fix; all 12 session-owner tests pass.
- The focused Gateway family-routing tests pass. The two Linux-only warmer tests skip on macOS and are covered by the successful Linux PR CI; they preserve exact payload coverage, WAL checkpoint freedom, reader retirement, and the byte budget while bounding progress calls.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no remaining actionable findings. The review caught and fixed a harness cancellation check before measurement.
- Guarded Linux comparisons completed successfully, without guard interruptions. The fixture has 5,000 synthetic sessions, 6,000 settled runs, a 407 MiB agent database, and an 11 MiB shared-state database; it is generated sequentially, without production data.

### Measurement acceptance, recorded before the first run

Exercise the actual maintenance owner with the Gateway spawn broker and read-only process pool. Count requests, main-thread stats, useful warming bytes/messages, main-isolate allocation, main/process/child CPU, GC time/promotion, and loop p99/max. Keep allocation/CPU profiles separate from unprofiled timing gates. Compare at least two concurrent pairs with swapped interleaved CPU placement under the shared production guard. Interrupted pairs are discarded.

Reject a mean adverse change of at least 20%, or at least 10% in both pairs. Opposite signs or baselines differing by more than 5× require absolute deltas and a third pair for a gating metric. p99 requires 1,000 samples per side; p95 requires 200; major GC requires 50 collections. Sub-millisecond absolute paired-mean GC percentile changes are context; fewer collections with non-increasing total GC also make per-collection tails context. Report each side's max pause and retain the max-pause exception. Resident and cold-file cases are separate. Production deployment is outside this change, so no deployed effect is claimed.

### Results

Each cold timing pair contains three passes per side; placement swaps for pair 2. Allocation is measured in separate profiled pairs. The change column is the mean of the two within-pair percentage changes, not a ratio of pooled means.

| Metric per cold pass | Baseline mean | Candidate mean | Mean paired change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sampled main-isolate allocation | 612.33 MiB | 11.33 MiB | -98.15% (-600.99 MiB) |
| Progress requests | 6,916 | 113.83 | -98.35% |
| Main-thread file stats | 34,569 | 110 | -99.68% |
| Main CPU | 1,534.96 ms | 162.29 ms | -89.45% (-1,372.68 ms) |
| Parent process CPU | 1,881.91 ms | 189.45 ms | -89.93% |
| Broker/reader CPU | 5,305.00 ms | 3,458.33 ms | -34.70% |
| Total main GC | 81.41 ms | 4.86 ms | -94.01% (-76.55 ms) |
| Promoted bytes | 1,954,793 | 55,480 | -97.16% (-1,899,313 bytes) |
| Mean of per-pass loop p99 | 1.860 ms | 1.641 ms | -12.04% (-0.218 ms) |
| Wall time | 21.22 s | 12.80 s | -39.65% |

Cold pair 1/2 main CPU changes were -89.29%/-89.61%; total GC -94.15%/-93.87%; promotion -97.11%/-97.21%; loop p99 -7.00%/-17.07% (-0.138/-0.299 ms). Allocation pairs were 613.60→11.71 MiB and 611.05→10.96 MiB. No eligible gate regressed or required a third pair.

Every paired pass warmed exactly the same payload byte/message count on both sides. Across timing passes this was 33,809,483–33,816,769 bytes and 1,813–1,815 messages; agent disk reads were about 168 MB per pass. All runs completed without hitting the byte limit. The slight variation between passes comes from the existing time-based hot-session selection.

### Loop tails and GC pause context

Loop p99 is eligible in every timing/resident pass. The table reports baseline→candidate values; maxima are observations, not claims about exact uninterrupted CPU slices.

| Cold pair/pass | Loop samples | Loop p99 ms | Loop max ms | Minor GC count | Major GC count | Max single GC ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1/1 | 20959→11772 | 2.275→2.114 | 16.310→7.643 | 23→0 | 1→0 | 7.891→0.000 |

GC pause percentiles are context-only: minor collections are 0–23 per pass, major 0–1. Minor p95/p99 ranges were 4.309–5.465/4.310–6.189 ms on baseline (n=22–23), versus 0.662–1.059 ms for both on candidate passes with collections (n=14–15); two candidate passes had none. Baseline major p95/p99 were 7.891 and 3.721 ms (n=1 each), and candidate had no major collections. Pair-level maximum single GC was 7.891→1.059 ms and 4.532→0.753 ms. The max-pause exception—candidate maximum exceeding max(50 ms, 2× baseline maximum)—is not triggered. Separate allocation-profile pairs had maximum GC 7.326→0.532 ms and 9.794→0 ms (minor counts 22→15 and 22→0; major 1→0 in each).

### Is a memory-locked database redundant work?

A task-owned locker held all four synthetic database files resident (855,048 KiB locked, matching their page-rounded sizes). Both baseline and candidate owners reported 100% residency, zero disk bytes, and zero payload bytes/messages warmed. The existing residency/query capability check already skips warming in this case: four requests on both sides, with main stats reduced from 20 to 4. Main CPU was 31.049→28.223 ms and 19.350→18.533 ms; GC and promotion were zero on both sides.

Resident loop p99 was 2.527→2.206 ms (n=2,917→3,054) and 1.152→1.105 ms (n=1,890→1,874); loop maxima were 6.939→7.492 ms and 6.107→2.986 ms (+0.553/-3.121 ms, +7.97%/-51.11%; mixed signs, inconclusive context). Resident wall time (+155.237/-18.128 ms, +4.83%/-0.91%) and child CPU (+50/-30 ms, +1.82%/-1.53%) have opposite signs and are inconclusive context under v5.2; no speedup is claimed there. The cold case proves that deleting warming globally would remove useful disk/payload warming.

### Proof and limits

[Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40030178585) passed: 49 jobs succeeded, 27 skipped, no failures or reruns. Focused local tests, changed-file lint/format, and independent review are complete.

This exercises the actual Gateway maintenance owner, spawn broker, and read-only pool, rather than a full Gateway boot or a 15-minute scheduler soak. The synthetic agent DB is 407 MiB, not the production-sized tens-of-GiB database; its 5,000 sessions reproduce the repeated-request allocation. Allocation is sampled and remains about 11 MiB/pass, not literally zero. Candidate unprofiled loop maxima were 1.995–7.643 ms; exact longest main-thread execution slices were not measured. No production deployment/restart was performed, so disappearance of deployed 15-minute spikes remains a post-deployment observation.

prs.title: fix: restore Doctor deletion recovery CI coverage
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the Doctor deletion-recovery regression being scheduled in a generic Worker lane, where the real shared-state SQLite owner correctly refuses access because the host broker is unavailable.

Once the file reaches its proper owner, its first case also needs to assert the current test-harness contract: Doctor refreshes the supplied stale discovery and hands both configured database targets to the existing mocked migration owner before that deliberately isolated harness reports its expected incomplete-migration refusal.

## User Impact

There is no production behavior change. CI now executes both existing Doctor deletion-recovery cases with the required host-owned broker, preserving the schema-19 fixtures, byte-for-byte database checks, cleanup, timeouts, and the unchanged quarantine case.

The corrected first case observes the real same-invocation handoff instead of inferring success from a later registry, hold-list, count, or log postcondition.

## Why This Change Was Made

`databaseWorkerCoreTestFiles` already owns tests that require physical admission and descriptor custody from the application host. The infra Vitest project consumes that registry with forked processes, while generic projects exclude its entries. Adding this exact file reuses that established routing mechanism.

The initial discovery intentionally knows only `main`. A case-local spy wraps the already mocked config-flow owner without replacing its implementation, then verifies Doctor calls it once with configured `main` and newly added `late` targets. A stale handoff has no active targets, so it cannot satisfy the assertion. The spy is restored in the existing cleanup path.

## Evidence

- The existing scheduled CI failure reached `Shared-state admission requires the host broker` in the first case before this routing repair.
- The maintained planner selected the Doctor file exactly once under `vitest.infra.config.ts`, excluded it from the prior generic Worker lane, and passed the existing routing/planner consumers: 424 tests.
- Remote changed-file formatting and lint passed.
- Every selected affected type graph passed.
- The complete `src/flows/doctor-health.deletion-recovery.test.ts` file passed both cases under infra forks.
- The exact published head passed the reviewer-requested three-file command: registry 11/11, scoped Vitest config 22/22, and Doctor deletion recovery 2/2.
- Full calibrated independent review concluded clean after that command.
- Canonical P2 autoreview completed three source-context passes with no actionable findings.
- The committed tree is identical to the remotely validated tree.

Hosted PR CI and the required ClawSweeper review continue on this published head.

prs.title: perf(gateway): avoid reclassifying prepared session rows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Warm `sessions.list` reads normalize every durable page key again when entering a prepared read view, after the placement preparation owner already classified the same selection.

## User Impact

Removes one redundant per-row pass without changing filtering, ordering, returned rows, or private-session access. Two swapped pairs measured **4.00% less allocation** (57,972 bytes/RPC) and **1.82% less main-thread CPU/RPC**. Process CPU rose 1.40%, below the adverse thresholds.

## Why This Change Was Made

The selection owner already recomputes `hasPrivateQueries` with `preparedQueries` after readiness waits and uses it to decide whether memory-actor preparation is needed. Pass an empty private-preparation query list for durable-only selections. Consumers still receive the full selection; mixed/private reads retain preparation, live authority, cancellation, and synchronous-view lifetime checks.

Gateway runtime LOC delta: **0** (one line replaced). The duplicate durable-key classification pass disappears without new state, cache, option, or helper; the existing loop remains necessary for private-session preparation. Non-test code grows by **one line** in the opt-in benchmark hook to load this owner for repeatable A/B proof. The README gains one net line to list all eight required files; tests gain 14 net lines. Remaining filter/sort and row-presentation allocations are outside this bounded change.

## Evidence

- Both existing durable lifecycle variants fail on the old code: one prepared key resolution becomes two during consumption. Both pass with the fix. The three focused placement/prepared-read files passed **51 tests**; no new test cases or production test seams were added.
- Changed-file formatting and repository lint passed; `pnpm tsgo:core` passed using the native typechecker. The README follow-up passed formatting and `git diff --check`. No Testbox/Crabbox lease was used.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable P0/P1/P2 findings, including a fresh review of current head `8e2f0fafb4b2b018bcf8c0174d6eaf4c9fde6a82`. The helper refused its provider/configuration mismatch; configuration was not changed.
- Real isolated Gateways produced **20 byte-identical normalized response goldens** covering pagination, all three sorts, archive selection, search, pinning, owner ordering, and scope/exclusion filters. Each capture is 1,645,138 bytes; SHA256 `11b24199234fb6de4a62fbc3d0379469e7219fb8cc162f2e8679bd7831f8c1b6`. Session/lifecycle identities and fixture timestamps remain exact. Normalization is limited to envelope `ts`, projection `snapshotAt`, process-local `rowsRevision`, sandbox paths, and the harness main root's adoption `updatedAt` clock.

## Measurement

**Performance decision: accept; no adverse gate crossed.** Current-head [CI run 40029507491](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40029507491) completed with the inherited public-read failure documented below; all other planned jobs passed, including `security-fast`.

Synthetic fixture: 5,000 metadata sessions, 6,000 settled runs, 200 approvals, 100 cron jobs, no projects or transcript payloads. Each side made 10,000 warm `sessions.list` sidebar calls (limit 100, one client), after 250 warmup calls. CPU and allocation campaigns each used two concurrent pairs with swapped, interleaved 16-CPU placements under the shared exclusive lock and production guard. All eight sides completed; none was guard-interrupted. Heap sampling interval: 524,288 bytes. Node 26.12.1, pinned fs-safe 0.26.11.

Measurements and goldens use base `f74efc3695f8` and the runtime patch originally published as `6f238caa37fc`. The documentation follow-up required a rebase onto `74cb12dd2c75`; `git range-diff` confirms the runtime patch is identical. The placement/prepared-read owners, key normalizer, focused test files, preload, and dependency lock are unchanged upstream. Adjacent main changes include child-controller presentation and agent schema metadata, so these numbers are explicitly measurements on the recorded base, not a new measurement of current main. Fresh review and current-head CI cover the refreshed integration.

Allocation improved in both pairs (-3.71%, -4.29%). Its promotion mean rose 6.02% (individual pairs +4.33%, +7.72%), below the >=20% mean or >=10% in both-pairs gates. CPU-pass process CPU rose 1.40%; its mixed-sign total-GC, promotion, and RPC-tail results are **inconclusive**, not adverse. Allocation-pass total GC also has mixed signs and is inconclusive. None of these inconclusive results would cross an adverse threshold, so no third pair was required.

Event-loop p99 is context-only for both CPU pairs and allocation pair 2 because at least one side has fewer than 1,000 samples. Minor-GC p99 is undersampled; minor-GC p95 paired-mean shifts are below 1 ms and context-only under v5.3. Major-GC percentiles are context-only (3–5 collections per side). Every raw maximum-pause check passes `candidate <= max(50 ms, 2 × baseline)`; both raw and observer maxima are reported below. No paired-mean gate has a baseline ratio above 5×. Allocation-pass observer maxima do differ by more than 5× across baselines and remain context; maximum pauses are assessed per pair, never averaged. prs.title: perf(memory): batch PostgreSQL full-index publication
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL full memory reindex publishes each source separately even though the existing writer can batch chunk rows across sources. A 20,000-chunk / 2,000-source publication issues 6,000 chunk, recall-metadata, and provenance INSERT statements instead of 471.

## User Impact

Full reindex performs 5,529 fewer SQL statements and bridge round trips with identical search and stored data. SQLite, schemas, scheduling, advisory locking, and commit authority are unchanged. No migration or operator action is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route PostgreSQL source groups and staged full publication through `MemorySourceIndexKernel.replaceGroup`. Reuse its existing 128-row bound, conflict-key deduplication, and repeated-source ordering. The spool still streams one source at a time inside the admitted publication transaction.

Owner acceptance (coordinator, 2026-10-23): this change deterministically removes 5,529 statements and round trips per 20k-chunk full reindex with identical search and storage hashes; paired wall time improved within run-to-run spread (median 97.3 → 92.0 s, spread 19.4 s) and incremental latency improved. Accepted under the standing direction that every removed statement counts.

## Evidence

Three serial interleaved A/B pairs on base `b1967334895d55c70b68aa1ee27449a39b9d6bc3`, with the same decoder, 20,000 chunks, 2,000 sources, and 1,536 dimensions. Fixture SHA-256: `a853dd3d074eafe596de2d1e3811c30af11ad6c18a2bff77244764faf802257a`. Host load was recorded for every phase. No paid embedding calls.

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Full reindex pair 1 | 111.800 s | 91.997 s |
| Full reindex pair 2 | 95.046 s | 91.028 s |
| Full reindex pair 3 | 97.331 s | 93.690 s |
| Full reindex median | 97.331 s | 91.997 s |
| Full reindex SQL statements | 50,159 | 44,630 |
| Full reindex bridge trips | 42,155 | 36,626 |
| Initial publication median | 22.767 s | 22.538 s |
| Initial publication SQL / trips | 7,404 / 7,203 | 7,404 / 7,203 |
| Incremental median (15 samples/arm) | 49.229 ms | 45.687 ms |
| Incremental p95 | 77.793 ms | 54.386 ms |

The full-reindex median gain is 5.334 s against a combined within-arm range of 19.416 s; this is not a statistically resolved wall-time improvement. All vector, keyword, hybrid, and storage hashes matched across all arms. Full-reindex one-minute host loads before A/B were 16.63/7.73, 5.50/6.84, and 7.73/7.07.

Restored on current main `34c95cb9e0017b061942cb6df4b3801f7cc53e9e`. The production delta is the same retained and measured patch. A real PostgreSQL binder regression checks one INSERT per row family across ten sources, exact persisted content/metadata/vectors and keyword results, private staging, rollback, and one revision advance. It fails on current main and passes with the change.

Validation: 28 focused PostgreSQL tests passed (publication, source-index kernel, duplicate chunks; 48.12 s Vitest / 51.72 s including runner). The new grouped/staged cases took 197/135 ms; the owning publication file passed in 2.481 s reported test time. Targeted lint/format and source/test TSRS passed; final-head PostgreSQL conformance passed all three shards at `76b91e572863c491d89e52a43f60ae9e5ee5a9cd`: 1,141 passed, 39 existing skips, zero failures (341.524 / 420.771 / 251.734 s). Fresh isolated P0–P3 autoreview is clean. CI run [40029993005](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40029993005) passed on the same head, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards. All required checks are green. CI PostgreSQL jobs completed in 1,140 / 1,258 / 970 seconds including setup.

`pr-simplify`: removes the per-source writer dispatch in favor of the existing bounded owner; no new state or abstraction. Production +37/-30 (net +7), tests +175/-0, total net +182 lines.

prs.title: fix(agents): refuse empty recreation of retained PostgreSQL stores
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With PostgreSQL agent storage, retain an agent's local database anchor, lose its logical PostgreSQL namespace, then run `agents add` for that agent again. Ordinary creation can provision a fresh empty namespace under the retained identity instead of reporting the missing store, making the prior history appear empty.

## User Impact

Agent creation now refuses an unavailable or mismatched retained PostgreSQL store before changing the workspace or publishing its configuration. Restore the matching PostgreSQL namespace before retrying. An already-written anchor with an uninitialized namespace is ambiguous, including an interrupted first creation, so it also refuses; truly fresh and unanchored files retain ordinary creation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing schema-inspection and execution owners admit retained anchors through their existing-only path before creation effects. The preflight validates the agent identity and schema metadata, retains the creation authority checks, and awaits reader/execution cleanup. Existing held-store recovery is unchanged. There are no new flags, schemas, or recovery journals.

## Maintainer Decision

Please confirm the conservative recovery policy: an anchor committed during a failed first creation also blocks ordinary retries until operator recovery, because it is indistinguishable from an anchor whose prior PostgreSQL history was lost. The live proof now demonstrates this actual failed-first-creation case. The recommendation is to retain the refusal; this PR does not claim maintainer approval of that tradeoff.

## Evidence

- [Real PostgreSQL + disposable Gateway qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181951#issuecomment-6375623438) on exact head `accc05c79cd25f9edc560bf99cacd8b4e070a167`: **PASS**. The unchanged parent `4e26493aafd06079dc94195f03b871bba6c3c618` reproduced false success through both offline `agents add` and Gateway `agents.create`; the fix refused both before namespace/workspace creation or configuration publication, preserving anchor bytes and identity.
- Positive live controls passed: fresh CLI/RPC creation, a zero-byte unanchored file, valid retained-store registration with unchanged UUID/namespace, and exact session-history preservation after registration and a full Gateway restart. Node 24.22.1, pinned pnpm 12.15.0, PostgreSQL 18.6. Final fixture harnesses exited 0; zero fixture namespaces remained and the disposable database/Gateways were cleaned up.
- Parent-to-head existing-data upgrade: **PASS**. Parent-created configuration/anchor bytes, store UUID/namespace, session ID and complete messages survived startup on the PR runtime; a new write, retained-store re-registration, and another Gateway start also passed. Details are in the linked proof.
- Actual failed-first-creation retry: **PASS** for the stated refusal policy. A real public CLI attempt failed with `ECONNREFUSED` after writing its Native anchor but before namespace initialization; after connectivity was restored, the retry refused without changing config/anchor bytes or creating the retry workspace/namespace.
- Focused `createAgent` boundary suite: four intended failures and 24 passes on unchanged upstream; **28/28 pass** with the fix. Controls cover missing-store errors, wrong agent identity, existing-only refusal, and fresh/unanchored/valid stores. Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-create.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Scoped production/test type checks, type-aware lint, three-file formatting, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Current-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40028846775) and [CI/dependency/security guard statuses](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40029740282): green. The separate Barnacle auto-response workflow has an `undefined.owner` exception; details are in the proof comment.
- Canonical independent review: complete, scoped-clean for P0–P2 findings.

The live proof exercised the source-built public CLI and real Gateway WebSocket RPCs against actual PostgreSQL, including an exact parent-to-head upgrade with existing data. No model/provider call, published-package installation, or published-stable-to-candidate upgrade was part of this storage qualification. The focused unit suite uses synthetic external-store I/O facts and complements that live proof.

prs.title: fix: name the last tool in the fallback shown when a tool run ends without a summary
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent turn ends after only calling tools and the tool-free summary pass returns nothing (both attempts), the user sees a fixed placeholder: "The tool run finished, but no final summary was produced. I did not repeat any completed actions." The message gives no hint of what ran last or whether the last step worked, so users and operators cannot tell a harmless silent finish from a failed final step without opening the transcript.

## User Impact

The fallback keeps its existing sentence verbatim and appends a short digest:

| Last tool result | Appended digest |
|---|---|
| `isError === false` | `Tool calls: N; last: <tool> (succeeded).` |
| `isError === true` | `Tool calls: N; last: <tool> (failed).` |
| `isError` absent or `undefined` | `Tool calls: N; last: <tool> (outcome unknown).` |

Example (interactive turn: `read`, then `exec`, then two empty summary attempts):

- Before: `The tool run finished, but no final summary was produced. I did not repeat any completed actions.`
- After: `The tool run finished, but no final summary was produced. I did not repeat any completed actions. Tool calls: 2; last: exec (succeeded).`

Unchanged: cron and other silent runs stay silent, and failed or timed-out turns keep their original outcome.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runner already holds the settled tool batch (`toolMetas`) when it builds the placeholder, so the digest is derived locally with no extra model call, no new setting and no new flag.

- Only the last tool name (truncated to 64 characters), the call count and the outcome are used. Arguments, results and tool metadata are never echoed, so the fallback cannot leak command lines or output.
- An absent `isError` is reported as "outcome unknown" and never as success. This follows the existing "outcome unknown" style and the producer contract that leaves the field absent for unknown terminal outcomes (this was the P2 finding from the automated review on the first revision, now fixed in the second commit).
- The change lives in the shared finalization owner (`settled-turn-finalization.ts`, new exported `buildSettledToolFallbackText`), so every channel that shows this fallback gets the same text.

Compatibility note: any consumer that matches the old fallback text exactly would need a prefix or substring match. I found one such assertion (`embedded-agent-runner.run-embedded-agent.finalization-scope.test.ts`) and relaxed it to `stringContaining`; the qa-lab e2e only checks `not.toContain`, and `chat.directive-tags` uses a fixture string.

## Evidence

Verified:

- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/settled-turn-finalization.test.ts`: 23 of 23 pass locally. New tests cover no tools (plain placeholder), last tool succeeded and failed with call count, an omitted `isError` and an explicit `undefined` (both "outcome unknown"), and that tool metadata is not echoed. Existing fallback assertions were updated.
- In CI the same test file passes in the shard that runs it (32 of 33 tests in that shard pass, including the new "reports an unknown outcome when isError is absent" test).
- oxfmt and oxlint are clean on the touched files.

## Runtime proof (added after the first review)

One real agent turn through the locally built `openclaw agent` command (embedded runner, Windows, Node 24), run against the PR head. A credential-free local stub that speaks the OpenAI chat-completions wire format answered as follows: request 1 returned a single `read` tool call; every later request (the tool follow-up and both tool-free summary attempts) returned empty text. This is the exact path the PR changes.

Stub request log (one line per model request):

```
{"request":1,"stream":true,"tools":11,"hasToolResult":false,"respond":"tool_call:read"}
{"request":2,"stream":true,"tools":11,"hasToolResult":true,"respond":"empty-text"}
{"request":3,"stream":true,"tools":0,"hasToolResult":true,"respond":"empty-text"}
{"request":4,"stream":true,"tools":0,"hasToolResult":true,"respond":"empty-text"}
```

Gateway log lines from the same run (ids shortened):

```
settled post-tool turn lacked a final answer: runId=3527b60a... provider=stub/stub-1 - running isolated finalization
settled-turn finalization completed without a visible answer: ... - retrying 1/1 with tools disabled
settled-turn finalization completed without a visible answer: ... attempts=2/2 - using terminal fallback reply
```

Reply delivered by the run (`final` and the single payload of the JSON output):

```
The tool run finished, but no final summary was produced. I did not repeat any completed actions. Tool calls: 1; last: read (succeeded).
```

Run summary from the same output: `toolSummary: {calls: 1, tools: ["read"], failures: 0}`, `assistantTurns: 4`, `status: ok`.

Limits, stated plainly:

- The "before" text in the table above is the unchanged placeholder from the base branch; I did not capture a second run on base.
- This was the embedded agent command, not a Telegram or other channel run, so no Telegram Test Server output is attached.
- The stub is a few lines of Node I can attach or turn into a committed e2e scenario if maintainers want it.

Known CI failure, not caused by this diff:

- `settled-turn-finalization.unavailable.test.ts` ("preserves a failed cron turn and its transcript when finalization is unavailable") fails at the `assistantTranscriptOwned` assertion (`expected undefined to be true`). That test does not assert the digest text. It fails the same way locally with this PR's four original files reverted to base `a7b8ae74`, and the main run is also red across many shards. I have not root-caused it.

Not verified, stated plainly:

- `finalization-scope.test.ts` fails 8 of 8 in my local Windows environment with and without this change ("Runtime config is not prepared"), so my one-line edit to that file is unverified locally and relies on CI.
- `pnpm check` stopped at two preflight guards unrelated to this diff, and I could not complete a full `pnpm build` locally.

Offer: I can commit the stub scenario as a test if wanted.

## Maintainer decision

The automated review marks this as a product preference that needs an owner decision: should the conservative missing-summary fallback include a tool count, last tool name and known or unknown outcome? I think it is a small, safe diagnostic gain, but I am happy to adjust wording, drop the docs sentence, or close the PR if the existing message is intentional.

AI-assisted PR (written with Claude); the author owns the change and will address review feedback.
