prs.title: fix: streamed replies no longer re-run the runtime-context scrub per delta
prs.body:
Fixes #181682

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary final-answer prose activates the streaming runtime-context scrub on its first `o`/`O`. Every later delta can then rescan the growing reply even though it contains no runtime-context carrier. Long answers consume avoidable Gateway CPU.

## Changes

Keep ordinary text on the existing append/identity path. Probe the complete incoming delta plus a bounded, whitespace-normalized overlap for real runtime-context carriers. Retain partial line-delimiter withholding, replacement reset, and canonical stripping after activation; the canonical privacy grammar is unchanged.

JasonBuildAI's commits and regression coverage are retained. The simplification removes the per-character JavaScript whitespace classifier/concatenation loop and normalizes the overlap and delta together. Compared with the adopted revision, this removes 23 lines and adds 7. The dedicated partial-line hold remains necessary: simply calling the whole-text conditional transform on every possible delimiter prefix would bring back growing-reply work at ordinary paragraph starts. Whole diff against main: production **+142/-12**, tests **+316/-0**. No SDK, configuration, or storage changes.

## Evidence

Built main `4c7b43d17b080f1f6f307291f33162a6f2d6d446` and candidate `f944a10c1d794d48b5606b32a92828e515d08a7f` on Node 24.22.1 in isolated Docker state. Setup used shipped CLI commands, turns used public `chat.send` and `agent.wait`, and completion/history came from the actual built Gateway.

The local OpenAI-compatible Responses endpoint emits unique English prose containing ordinary `o` characters, no brackets/runtime markers/tool markup, and no repeated paragraphs. Each size is delivered in four-character deltas, twice per arm. The Responses message carries the normal `final_answer` phase, selecting the actual final-answer sanitizer. Gateway CPU comes from `/proc/<pid>/stat`, sampled outside that process; event-loop delay uses Node's built-in `monitorEventLoopDelay`, not a sanitizer helper or mocked cost counter.

| Output | Provider deltas | Main CPU seconds, runs 1 / 2 | Candidate CPU seconds, runs 1 / 2 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 32 KiB | 8,192 | 1.52 / 0.98 | 1.80 / 0.81 |
| 64 KiB | 16,384 | 3.16 / 2.40 | 2.56 / 2.13 |
| 128 KiB | 32,768 | 7.06 / 6.57 | 5.50 / 5.04 |
| 256 KiB | 65,536 | 21.55 / 21.88 | 16.78 / 16.18 |

At 256 KiB this removes **22–26% of measured Gateway CPU**; the measured streaming/completion window falls from **23.30 / 23.91 seconds** to **18.41 / 17.72 seconds**. The cold 32 KiB sample is noisy and not an improvement claim. Full public streaming-delta hashes match the expected output and each other in all eight comparisons. Terminal snapshots match between arms and intentionally cap long text at 4,096 characters; their truncation is not used as a full-output oracle.

Seven separate real Gateway controls pass on both arms: coalesced blocks, one-character split delimiters, indented CRLF delimiters, a private block larger than the probe window inside one delta, wide-whitespace carriers, Unicode-whitespace carriers, and marker-free replacement text. Private block content never appears in the captured preview stream, and each final visible answer is `Visible reply.`. The short marker-free replacement control costs 0.03 seconds on main and 0.02 on candidate.

Additional checks:

- **99 tests across five focused suites pass**, including ordinary-text cost guards, subscriber composition, canonical runtime-context behavior, partial delimiter holds, coalesced chunks, replacements, and whitespace parity.
- Reverting the production owner makes the subscriber cost regression fail: 134,231,904 cumulative characters reach the runtime scrub instead of zero. Restoring the candidate makes it pass. Unit cost assertions supplement, not replace, the built-Gateway measurements above.
- Targeted formatting and lint pass.
- A separate real OpenAI `gpt-5-mini` shipped-agent check returns `STREAM_CONTEXT_LIVE_OK`.

### Controlled latency follow-up

The [requested five-pair ABAB comparison and full table](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181692#issuecomment-6375637901) use the same container, identical 256 KiB stream, immutable main/candidate builds, and fresh isolated Gateways with no other active container workload. Whole-workload `monitorEventLoopDelay` histograms were reset before stream release and stopped after public completion, without the periodic logger or RSS sampler.

| Median over five runs | Main | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Gateway CPU | 24.45 s | 18.72 s |
| Event-loop p50 | 18.61 ms | 18.61 ms |
| Event-loop p95 | 25.28 ms | 25.20 ms |
| Event-loop p99 | 34.87 ms | 32.96 ms |
| Event-loop maximum | 63.11 ms | 59.77 ms |

Candidate p99 was lower in all five pairs; p95 and maximum were higher in only one pair each, within overlapping run-to-run ranges. The initial two-sample maximum increase did not persist. All ten full-stream hashes match, and CPU is lower in every pair. No production code changed for this comparison.

### Measurement limits

This removes the runtime-scrub cost, **not every source of nonlinear Gateway work**. Total Gateway CPU still grows superlinearly. A separate diagnostic CPU profile of the built candidate attributes 44.8% of self time to the unchanged `createStreamingReplyResolver`; that independent directive-resolution work is outside this patch. The initial two-sample maximum figures (main 56.7 / 50.2 ms, candidate 75.6 / 62.0 ms) prompted the controlled follow-up above; its larger alternating comparison does not show a consistent latency regression. No memory improvement or universal per-sample latency win is claimed.

The first fixture omitted the Responses final-answer phase and exercised the intentionally raw branch; it is retained as a setup/control observation, not counted as the performance baseline. The phase-correct baseline above is the corrected shipped-entry-point reproduction. No system clock changes, private state writes, private sanitizer imports, or paid-provider failure injection were used.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: a revert fully restores the prior behavior without migration. Blast radius is streaming final-answer text projection. Privacy-sensitive carrier handling remains owned by canonical stripping and is protected by the split/coalesced/whitespace controls; non-streaming sanitization is unchanged.

prs.title: feat(mxc): move the MXC sandbox plugin to MXC SDK 1.0
prs.body:
<!--
Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
Use a parenthesized scope only when it adds clarity:
fix(auth): login redirect loops when session cookie is expired

Types: feat, fix, improve, refactor, docs, chore.
For fixes, describe the user-visible symptom and trigger:
fix: task list fails to load when user has no environments
Avoid implementation details such as:
fix: add null check to task query

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.
-->

## What Problem This Solves

The MXC sandbox plugin still uses the preview SDK 0.8 request and process APIs, which are incompatible with the released MXC SDK 1.0 runtime.

## User Impact

MXC sandboxed agents keep the same workspace, network, environment, timeout, and cleanup behavior on SDK 1.0.

Operators need to account for three compatibility changes:

- Windows requires Node.js `>=24.21.0 <25` or `>=26.8.0`. The plugin fails activation with a remediation message on older releases.
- `mxcBinaryPath` must select an SDK 1.0 architecture directory containing both `wxc-exec.exe` and `mxc_ffi.dll`. Invalid or incomplete overrides fail closed instead of falling back to bundled native components.
- SDK 1.0 cannot request LPAC. The `appcontainer-dacl` and `appcontainer-bfs` tiers use a regular AppContainer and can reach resources granted to `ALL APPLICATION PACKAGES`. `base-container` is unchanged. The selected tier and boundary are logged and documented. Chaz accepted this boundary and the upgrade requirements for this migration.

Ordinary sandboxed exec remains non-PTY. The retained SDK PTY path owns its deadline, kills the sandbox on timeout, returns `124`, and writes the timeout notice.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin now builds an SDK 1.0 `ContainerRequest`, uses `spawn` or `spawnWithPty`, and pins `wxc-exec.exe` plus `mxc_ffi.dll` from one validated release directory. Launcher stream errors, backpressure, cancellation, timeout, and cleanup are explicitly owned so a failed stream cannot be reported as exit `0`.

The dependency closure also pins `node-gyp@11.4.2` for `node-pty@1.1.0` source builds on platforms without a prebuild. The packed dependency scanner records the reviewed `node-pty` maintainer-script findings; they are not install-time or runtime paths.

## Evidence

Current branch head `0cbf9b5481de42e1ea4207c1b27fd50441e51c0b` includes a test-only restoration of sandbox-policy admission coverage. Its parent merge `0722b5d9cf4b5c7612bc142b6e68ee90f3333aa7` integrates upstream `061f22646cf6eb3c199f7f776ea6bdb1b92d971a`.

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` on Node.js 24.22.1: passed, including the 1,878-entry supply-chain policy check.
- `pnpm test extensions/mxc/test/sandbox-policy-loader.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: passed 11 tests in 14.15 seconds.
- `pnpm test:extension mxc`: passed 14 files and 121 tests in 234.32 seconds.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: passed.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/mxc/src/mxc-backend.ts extensions/mxc/src/mxc-container-config.ts`: passed.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-mock-exports.mts --staged --base upstream/main`: passed with 7,136 grandfathered factories.

The accepted Windows runtime proof is bound to candidate `6e69db30aa6bbbbb2454258a6b1f0b0008f86c52` (tree `dff5db0a2d539c550f70dc63d203198b83a7c78b`). The current-main merge only reconciles upstream owner/localization refactors and tests; it does not intentionally change the validated SDK 1.0 behavior. No candidate source changes arose from the runtime harness work.

- Windows 26700.1001 x64, `base-container`, existing Crabbox `harbor-prawn` lease.
- Run `run_fbef3881c610ceafd3624e5e429dcb80`, duration 48m29.9s.

prs.title: feat(trajectory): configurable runtime event retention thresholds
prs.body:
Closes #173184

## What Problem This Solves

Trajectory runtime events (the `trajectory_runtime_events` store holding raw tool-call data) are only pruned by hardcoded sweep thresholds: 14 days of age and a 512 MiB global byte cap. Operators with high-volume or sensitive workloads cannot tune retention, and there is no way to force a cleanup sooner than the periodic sweep.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can now configure retention for trajectory runtime events via `session.maintenance.trajectoryRetention` (`maxAge` and `maxBytes`) instead of relying on the fixed 14-day / 512 MiB defaults, and the recorder respects those bounds for both SQLite and in-memory stores. Missing or invalid values keep the existing defaults, so existing configurations behave exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retention thresholds were hardcoded constants (`RETENTION_MAX_AGE_MS` / `GLOBAL_MAX_BYTES`) used directly by the SQLite retention owner and duplicated in the memory store and the gateway worker live-event path. This change:

- Adds a `session.maintenance.trajectoryRetention` config block (`maxAge` as a positive duration, `maxBytes` as a byte size) to the session config schema.
- Adds shared constants in `src/trajectory/paths.ts` and threads the configured values through the runtime recorder (`src/trajectory/runtime.ts`), both store owners, and the gateway worker environment startup path.
- Resolves the config through `resolveTrajectoryRetentionConfigFromMaintenance` in `store-maintenance.ts`, falling back to the previous defaults for missing or non-positive values so behavior is unchanged for existing configs.
- Documents the new config keys and the actual retention semantics (see Evidence).

This is a conservative, additive change: cleanup remains best-effort and append-triggered (rate-limited to at most once per hour), with the triggering session's rolling window always protected, exactly as before.

## Evidence

- **Real behavior proof (production owner, un-mocked):** `src/trajectory/runtime-retention.sqlite.test.ts` drives the actual SQLite retention owner against a real temp SQLite store and now includes two config-driven scenarios:
  - *Shorter than default:* `maxAge: 7d` removes a 10-day-old run from another session while keeping the triggering session's runs (fails under the old fixed 14-day policy).
  - *Longer than default:* `maxAge: 21d` retains a 16-day-old run that the old fixed 14-day policy would remove (fails under the old policy).
  - **Red on base / green on head:** checked out the base production files (no `TRAJECTORY_RUNTIME_RETENTION_MAX_AGE_MS`/`MAX_BYTES` constants, no `maxAgeMs` threading); the config-driven tests cannot even build against base (`MISSING_EXPORT`), while the head passes 26/26 in the same file.
- New and updated unit tests, all passing locally: `zod-schema.gateway-auth.test.ts` (schema accepts a valid block, rejects an invalid byte size), `store.pruning.test.ts` (resolver defaults / configured values / fallback on invalid input). The previously-added mocked sink-forwarding test in `runtime.test.ts` was removed: it only asserted internal argument copying and could pass even if production persistence ignored the thresholds; the SQLite tests above now prove the real behavior.
- `pnpm config:docs:check` passes; config baseline regenerated (`core` 2558 鈫?2561, +3 keys).
- `pnpm lint:docs` reports 0 issues; `pnpm check:docs:content`'s config-examples check passes.
- `oxfmt --check` clean on all changed files; `oxlint --type-aware` reports no findings in any changed file; core typecheck (`tsgo:core`) passes.
- `check:bundled-channel-config-metadata` passes (no generated output change).

### Honest limitations of the evidence

- **No full model-backed Gateway run was performed.** This environment has no provider credentials, so a live agent run generating real trajectory events is not possible here. The storage-boundary behavior above exercises the real production retention owner end to end with real SQLite; a maintainer with credentials can reproduce it via `openclaw` with `session.maintenance.trajectoryRetention` set.
- Full `check:changed` and the src test typecheck `gateway-root` shard were not fully green on this Windows host due to pre-existing environment gaps unrelated to this change (missing ripgrep in the DB worker ratchet, a frozen `CHANGELOG/` record tripping the attributions check, and a missing `libdeflate` module in `ui/vite.config.ts`); none overlap with the files changed here, and the CI on Linux passes all `checks-node-changed-*`, `check-lint-core-*`, `check-test-types*`, `check-prod-types`, `check-guards`, and `check-bundled-channel-config-metadata` jobs.
- The `auto-response` check fails due to a Barnacle infra bug (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'owner')`), unrelated to this PR.

## Data-model compatibility

This is a purely additive, optional configuration change. No schema or state migration is required:
- The `trajectory_runtime_events` table is unchanged.
- Existing configs without `trajectoryRetention` load unchanged and use the same internal defaults (covered by the resolver defaults test).
- Existing stored rows are unaffected until a sweep runs; a sweep under configured thresholds uses the same whole-run deletion, byte accounting, and triggering-session protection as before.
- **Existing-data read path covered:** the shorter-than-default age test asserts the pre-sweep row loads through the production reader before the configured sweep evicts it, confirming existing rows are read and swept by the same owner.

## Scope Boundary

- Only trajectory runtime event retention is configurable; the fixed defaults remain for any other store and remain the fallback when the new config is absent.
- No schema/state migration is required: the new config keys are optional and defaulted at read time.
- Documentation covers the new keys and their actual semantics (`docs/gateway/config-agents/sessions.md`, `docs/tools/trajectory.md`).

## Maintainer decision requested

Per the review, converting the deliberately internal retention thresholds into a public configuration surface is an owner decision. The linked issue (#173184) is an explicit operator request for exactly this capability (configurable thresholds with the existing sweep mechanics), and this PR preserves the defaults and existing behavior when the settings are absent. A maintainer decision is requested to confirm this should become supported public configuration.

prs.title: refactor: localize single-consumer read rendering and plugin annotations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Several internal helpers and annotation names have one consumer, leaving call frames, exported seams, and a renderer utility module without separate ownership.

## What changed

Keep read rendering in its actual tool owner, remove the orphan render-utils production module, and prove its visible output through the public renderer callbacks. Retain the existing small Windows test target and move its home-display source watch to the new owner. Inline sole-use result preparation, regular-file error construction, and installed/bundled duplicate-warning frames at their existing branches. Localize exact single-use plugin, logging and channel-list annotations and Discord's empty legacy-rule constant.

No UI text, features, public contracts, persisted shapes, dependencies, lazy imports, or Phase E memory code change.

Net production reduction: **99 lines across 12 production paths**. Tests grow by 82 lines while replacing direct private-helper assertions with public rendering proof. The CI routing companion has no net line change. This is the retained slice of the original 172-line candidate after the campaign's CI-attribution rule withdrew five reachable files; the smaller residual lands under that rule, not a deletion quota.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- The retired text-output utility no longer accepts an undefined internal result. Its only caller requires a result and already reads its details. The old optional generic helper contract is not a public contract; the required public renderer shape remains checked by types and tests.
- Home-path rendering no longer repeats a non-string check after the existing string/nullish boundary has prepared that value. The generic guard originated in runtime internalization (#85341); the actual renderer still rejects non-string input at its existing boundary and preserves the incomplete-path placeholder.
- Private helper stack-frame names disappear. No security, durability, concurrency, recovery, or user-facing guard is removed. In particular, directory-error normalization remains in its existing helper after direct catch inlining failed the caught-error lint rule; no suppression or altered error contract was introduced.

## Evidence

Focused tests run serially with one worker in isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG state; targeted native typechecks, typed lint, formatting and line caps pass for the touched graphs. Original read/image/public-renderer coverage: 34 passed, with the unchanged Windows-only real home-casing case skipped on macOS. Windows scope routing: 27 passed. Logging/provider diagnostics: 42 passed. Existing plugin-manifest, Slack, Discord, Anthropic and channel-list proofs also pass. No full local build, broad suite, or whole-graph typecheck was run; exact-head PR CI is the broad gate.

The first CI head (`4652fd808a78a479d941354ef1d11d22c821c254`, run 40027571368) exposed a boundary-guard failure caused by the migrated test's direct `../extensions/types.js` import. The unchanged guard reproduces red before repair and passes after the fixture derives its type from the public renderer callback. No guard or baseline is weakened.

The same run's UI E2E shard 5 failed the landscape collapsed-question case (`question-footer.test-support.ts:124`, expected composer count 0, received 1). The flake registry and six completed scheduled-main runs provide no matching failure. Local E2E is outside the assigned proof budget, so the cause remains unsettled. Static and literal-dynamic import tracing reaches five changed files: server-prefs-reconcile, app-sidebar-child-session-data, chat/commands, chat-command-executor, and fetch-timeout. All five were returned byte-for-byte to the captured protected-main version; no other family was dropped. Original head 4652fd8 is retained on `deslop/z25-parked-question-footer-20261015` for those five hunks only. This is not an inherited-failure exception or a claim the question bug is fixed. Native Windows execution is not claimed from macOS proof.

After repair: the unchanged boundary case passes (red before fix, green afterward); the renderer suite passes 34 cases with its existing Windows-only skip. Targeted native types, typed lint and formatting pass. All eleven final structural checks pass, including 14 suppression cases, wrapper/eager closure, frozen updater bindings, eight prompt-prefix cases, zero runtime/static cycles, and line caps. Fresh isolated review of the staged repaired candidate is clean through P2; its sole earlier index-only finding was resolved by staging the already-proven type repair.

Final structural guards pass: assertion/mock/suppression ratchets, wrapper/eager-import closure, frozen updater bindings, prompt-prefix stability, zero runtime and static import cycles, line caps, UI controller ratchets, and keyless i18n verification. Independent isolated review is scoped-clean through P2 with no actionable findings.

prs.title: improve(memory): avoid repeated cosine work in PostgreSQL search
prs.body:
Continued in #181961 under explicit coordinator owner acceptance. This original PR remains closed and unmerged; its original failed-gate evidence is preserved below.

**Closed, unmerged:** the candidate failed its preregistered Testbox acceptance gate. No production change landed.

## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL memory searches evaluate cosine distance twice per eligible row because the selected distance and ORDER BY use separate bound expressions.

## User Impact

The candidate preserves exact vector and hybrid search IDs, ordering, scores, eligibility and limits, without a schema or configuration change. Its measured latency improvement did not satisfy every preregistered gate, so it remains unmerged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Order by the already selected `dist` alias. The production change is one line; a 20k-row function-count diagnostic drops cosine evaluations from 40,000 to 20,000. The existing norm eligibility check remains. PostgreSQL does not execute the supplied scope-count query, so no COUNT scan is removed.

The committed benchmark reproduces production PostgreSQL retrieval/merge and file-backed SQLite KNN using the deterministic PGMEMSTORE fixture, without model calls. It captures all search statements and EXPLAIN ANALYZE/BUFFERS plans.

## Evidence

**Not qualified for landing.** The single final-source Testbox campaign fails the preregistered 20k vector p95 gate: median block improvement 23.111 ms is below the 23.224 ms paired spread. All result hashes/counts match; the rule is not relaxed and no repeat will run.

Preregistered acceptance: 100 AB/BA pairs per flow and corpus after five warmups per arm, five 20-query blocks; median block p50/p95 gain must exceed maximum absolute block deviation at both 20k and 50k. Require exact result hashes, no increased SQL count, and no keyword or narrow-scope regression. An initial 50k hybrid campaign failed its spread gate and is retained; no sample was removed. The final-source workload releases its synthetic in-memory corpus before timing. One final local campaign and one Testbox campaign were registered before execution.

Final-source local results at `6313d608d8f2bed2f1a36a94562f7344b1922be7`:

| Chunks | Flow | Before p50/p95 ms | After p50/p95 ms |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
|20k|vector|246.402 / 249.646|191.336 / 195.364|
|20k|hybrid|258.368 / 262.896|201.731 / 205.105|
|50k|vector|807.041 / 827.934|660.457 / 689.025|
|50k|hybrid|831.838 / 871.760|687.533 / 716.000|

Both corpus gates pass; all 600 sampled results per corpus compare byte-identically by pair, plus six scope-boundary pairs. Statement counts remain vector 1 / keyword 1 / hybrid 2. Keyword movement is within spread. Candidate-ID and missing-model diagnostics show no regression. SQLite 20k reference: 63.437/72.836ms.

The existing regression is red on the original expression and green on the alias: one statement with one cosine expression. All 15 PostgreSQL memory-search tests, targeted repository typecheck, script syntax/lint and independent P0–P3 autoreview pass. Both runtime builds pass. Production delta: +1/-1; remaining additions are the requested reproducible benchmark/fixture and its documentation.

Final-source Testbox A/B ([run 40022866391](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40022866391)):

| Chunks | Flow | Before p50/p95 ms | After p50/p95 ms |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
|20k|vector|225.404 / 291.024|204.744 / 259.465|
|20k|hybrid|211.883 / 273.038|187.800 / 251.225|
|50k|vector|499.801 / 568.300|425.980 / 492.546|
|50k|hybrid|586.557 / 640.621|518.979 / 581.937|

The other vector/hybrid gates pass, and keyword changes are within spread. The failed 20k vector p95 gate prevents landing despite the aggregate improvements. Local SQLite 50k reference: 111.507/119.465 ms.

The original frozen Gateway controls fail before warm turns on both baseline and candidate: retired heartbeat/model fixture keys cause SQLite account setup failure and a PostgreSQL configuration-read admission failure. No R/T/S or C64 success is claimed. All three final-head local PostgreSQL conformance shards ran; results are recorded below. No corrected control or search campaign ran after the acceptance failure.

## Final-head PostgreSQL conformance

All three local shards actually ran at `6313d608d8f2bed2f1a36a94562f7344b1922be7` against PostgreSQL 17/pgvector 0.8.7 with the default pinned Bun runtime and internal-disk HOME/TMPDIR. All exited 1: 158 files passed, 5 failed, 3 skipped; 1,119 tests passed, 13 failed, 39 skipped. CI 40024300560 was cancelled when the rejected PR returned to draft; its PostgreSQL jobs are not passing evidence.

Eleven failures were caused by child processes selecting unsupported Node 26 from inherited PATH despite the outer command using Node 24.22.1. A single bounded qualification of exactly those 11 CLI cases verified the production resolver selected Node 24.22.1 before execution: all 11 passed (3 files; 5 nonselected Gateway tests skipped by the test-name filter). The original failed shard results remain part of the evidence; this qualification does not make the full conformance run green.

Two product-flow failures remain unresolved and are not attributed to baseline or rerun: inherited-auth startup reports an unavailable isolated state database through `listOpenClawRegisteredAgentDatabasesAsync`; the lexical memory/transcript scope test in `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.postgres.test.ts:249` returns `[]` instead of the expected `sessions/main/source-decoy.jsonl`.

The owned Testbox and local PostgreSQL instance are stopped, and all task proof slots are released. No production change landed. Exact result hashes and statement counts passed, but the failed latency gate and the unresolved conformance failures remain recorded without a rerun or baseline attribution.

prs.title: fix(gateway): deleting an account stalls and reconnects siblings
prs.body:
Related: #142193

## What Problem This Solves

Deleting one channel account can wait behind unrelated Gateway requests and reconnect healthy sibling accounts.

## User Impact

Removing a proven isolated, non-default named account stops only that account, including an account already stopped for migration. Siblings keep their connections. Shared settings, `accounts.default`, ambiguous or unproven identities, unresolvable surviving accounts, and plugins without the opt-in keep whole-channel handling.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reload planner matches authored keys to plugin-listed runtime IDs using the previous and candidate snapshots. Removal uses the channel manager's captured teardown, waits for that account's work, and retires its runtime state without starting a replacement. Failed or unfinished teardown retains its cleanup owner and requests recovery.

This proposes extending the published `accountScopedRestart` capability to isolated named-account removal. **Maintainer acceptance of that contract extension and current-head security approval are still required.**

## Evidence — October 23

Candidate **`27193149bc2bfa1438b617035637323a522f1009`** merges conflicting upstream **`c537658285b7906c5de296b7c4b379f57d835157`** into the previously published head `68b9e541b1d5a6a02f2440138d3ffbeb43e23598`. The repair preserves upstream's removal of the planner test hook and its current publication, credential and teardown ownership. The resulting PR has 19 changed files, +743/-173.

- **Regression control:** the eight account-identity cases ran against the current upstream planner: four failed and four passed, exposing removal/canonical-identity and dotted-key classification differences. The candidate passes them.
- **Affected owners:** all **482 tests in ten suites passed**; Vitest 255.87 seconds, maintained-wrapper wall time 265.36 seconds. This includes running/stopped account removal during unrelated work, canonical/raw identities, pending startup/task/stop-hook work, failed cleanup recovery, inactive credentials, secrets reload and model publication.
- **Types:** `core-test-gateway-root` passed in 18.9 seconds; `core-test-gateway-server` passed in 16.5 seconds.
- **Static checks:** targeted lint for all changed TypeScript files, formatting of all 19 changed files, and diff whitespace checks passed.
- **Local review:** the canonical isolated autoreview helper reported no actionable P0–P2 findings in the selected diff. Its assessment was limited to supplied diff/context and did not execute tests.
- **Shipped runtime:** the full maintained `pnpm build` passed in **6m 58.5s**. The clean checkout's built CLI removed running/already-stopped accounts in **255/130 ms** while an independently admitted 45-second Gateway request remained pending. Departing sockets closed and runtime accounts disappeared; the sibling delivered **four actual IRC status replies on its original socket, with zero reconnects through the full observation**. Driver exit 0 and child cleanup were verified.
- **CI:** [Exact-head CI is running](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40028756475), with CodeQL and the other PR workflows attached to `27193149bc2bfa1438b617035637323a522f1009`. GitHub reports no merge conflicts, and maintainer edits are enabled. The current-head [security guard requires maintainer approval](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167431#issuecomment-6068444877) and currently fails until that approval is supplied. No current-head hosted CI pass or merge is claimed. Previous-head CI is identified separately below.

Reproduce the focused checks:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/config-reload-plan.test.ts src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-channel-restart.test.ts src/gateway/server-aux-handlers.test.ts src/gateway/server-channels.account-lifetime.test.ts src/gateway/server-secrets-reload.model-runtime.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-model-runtime-scope.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-channel-restart.inactive-accounts.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --ci-graphs-json '["core-test-gateway-root","core-test-gateway-server"]'
```

<details>
<summary>Fresh shipped-CLI / real-ngIRCd trace and reproduction</summary>

The [public driver and ngIRCd configuration](https://gist.github.com/ceckert/a62e6702bb3f27671c7395b9dbcd7e22) were reused with one fixture-only update: omit the retired `agents.defaults.heartbeat` key from the fresh configuration. All behavioral assertions are unchanged. Original driver SHA256: `2a964b9fab3e7b9d8a9a08b61bfa16c0ffd5321126381d40fe630cbc96a71213`; updated driver SHA256: `2c9fcab889b4a7d0f1465dbdb0a09ba9b1c727b94664ee008d5a03790bdae600`.

Apply this single-line patch to the public driver before reproducing:

```diff
-  agents: { defaults: { workspace: path.join(out, 'workspace'), heartbeat: { every: '0m' } } },
+  agents: { defaults: { workspace: path.join(out, 'workspace') } },
```

Node **v24.22.1**, pnpm **12.15.0**, macOS arm64 Gateway; real ngIRCd **26.1**, Debian package `26.1-1+deb12u1`, in a task-owned Linux AMD64 container with only a loopback host port. The maintained full build exited 0; tracked checkout was clean before and after the proof. Embedded build commit was `27193149bc2bfa1438b617035637323a522f1009` (OpenClaw `2026.10.6`). Build-info SHA256: `265a44dad614bbf15b5eec0f08a2e24dfcc27dfe6eefbd87b48e2e7eb1f80e2c`. Complete trace SHA256: `8cf27b05b7e5b0d3889b4db1c203f04ed262f3d3dc47c64f04eff3c098cfff0d`.

The driver launches `openclaw.mjs gateway run --allow-unconfigured` with a temporary HOME, state and workspace, a sanitized environment, synthetic accounts and loopback endpoints. A transparent TCP observer records connections to real ngIRCd; an independent IRC client receives actual sibling status replies.

{"event":"unrelated_request_active","pending":true,"counts":{"rootRequests":1,"cronRuns":0,"sessionMutations":0,"terminalPersistence":0,"lifecycleWrites":0}}
{"event":"removal_complete","authoredKey":"Root","runtimeAccountId":"root","alreadyStopped":false,"configApplyMs":255,"unrelatedRequestStillPending":true,"departingSocketClosed":true,"removedAccountAbsent":true,"siblingOriginalSocketOpen":true,"siblingConnectionCount":1}

Driver exited 0 after joining its Gateway child. Process inspection found neither the driver nor Gateway child remaining. The task-owned IRC container and its task-specific image tag were removed.

```sh

pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

# Start real ngIRCd using the public configuration on a loopback-only port.
node /path/to/proof.mjs /path/to/clean-checkout LOOPBACK_IRC_PORT /path/to/new-isolated-output
```

</details>

## Maintainer Decisions Still Required

- Accept the extension of `accountScopedRestart` to isolated non-default named-account removal. The previous public contract excluded removal.
- Supply the enforced security-sensitive approval for this exact head after the guard notice updates. The secrets-reload changes pass existing in-memory snapshots to the planner; they add no I/O, logs or RPC fields and preserve preparation, publication, revision checks and rollback.

## Limits and Previous Evidence

The initial October 23 runtime attempt exited 78 before Gateway startup: the old driver's `agents.defaults.heartbeat` field is now rejected as retired configuration. No removal case ran in that attempt. The single-line fixture update above was made before the successful replay; it changes no production source or behavioral assertion.

The new full build exited 0. Its current Control UI startup JS was 276.1 KiB gzip against an enforced 276.5 KiB limit. This is the new build's result, not a claim that this PR repaired the earlier size advisory.

This proves the two removal paths through a local macOS arm64 Gateway and a real Linux IRC service; it does not establish Linux Gateway execution, all-channel behavior, external model/provider behavior, a full repository `pnpm check`, or hosted CI acceptance.

The [October 20 evidence](https://gist.github.com/ceckert/265774b3d6b7232d0d5fb6c2d2a0e7c1) and [earlier author update](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167431#issuecomment-6115046820) retain prior environment/setup failures, restricted-loopback stalls, build-size advisory, and historical UI/export audit results. prs.title: fix: human messages queue behind runs with older recovery claims
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Human steering can incorrectly fall back to the queue when a new execution is admitted beside an unresolved recovery-delivery claim from a different source.

## User Impact

Human input can join the admitted execution without clearing, replacing, or settling the retained claim. Existing terminal-delivery, execution-settings, and current-authority checks remain in place. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture the retained claim tuple with the existing execution selection and let the prepared delivery owner compare it with the current tuple. A missing source ID uses the captured claim rather than adopting a replacement row's source. Terminal-send ownership and settlement remain unchanged; this adds no schema, public SDK surface, or peer-delivery policy.

The existing unavailable-steering regression now checks that the expected input actually enters followup custody, preserving its no-injection and no-model-start assertions. It no longer requires a particular queue helper call.

## Evidence

**Real Control UI → Gateway → native-worker proof completed on candidate `ed9b83ddacc3ab82b4cc8e165d3878b439c93e7c`, compared with base `b19bade1d3ad29533784228947e7a729c70a0961`.** [Correlated runtime records, screenshots, and sanitized artifacts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181768#issuecomment-6375217911).

| Case | Observed behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Base, unchanged unresolved predecessor claim | `reply-owner-ended` → `followup-queued`; correction executes afterward in a separately mapped native task. |
| Candidate, unchanged claim | `active_run_injected`; correction and successful effect occur within the original native task before completion. |
| Candidate, claim replaced after admission | Steering is rejected and followup custody recorded; original native task does not consume the correction. |

These are constructed cases using isolated AWS state, the rendered Debug `agent` form for initial work, and the real composer for the correction on the same authenticated connection. A task-only public-SDK fixture sets the claim; production admission and native execution remain real. The replacement cell retains an **incomplete harness status** because a post-completion assertion incorrectly rejected legitimate queue-drain claim acquisition; its refusal and original-task nonconsumption were independently verified. The full base followup mapping and candidate original-task effect are separately verified. Native version is 0.162.1, versus the incident's reported 0.163.0.

**The historical production incident's cause remains unresolved.** Missing admission/rejection tuples cannot be reconstructed from later rows. This proof does not establish that incident's cause or uninterrupted claim custody between observed endpoints. Diagnostic instrumentation remains separate from this PR.

- The matched retained-predecessor regression failed on the base (`deferred`, expected `prepared`) and passed with the four-file production repair; #181766's exact-run Stop change was held constant. [Matched AWS proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_10312f477fa853fe20bba4634217a933).
- Existing message-join/handoff and adjacent checks remain valid. Additional evidence-only controls cover claim replacement/restoration, terminal-pending state after preparation, incumbent cancellation, and actual completion; none permitted backend injection.
- The runner-test repair passed independent review, owning typecheck, targeted lint/formatting, whitespace, line-cap, and assertion-safety checks. No new test, timer, retry, timeout, or mock was added.
- [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40018857925) passed, including all 230 runner tests and `openclaw/ci-gate`. The separately diagnosed [Barnacle auto-response failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40018901986) reads missing `context.repo.owner` in unchanged automation code.

<details>
<summary>Measured validation costs and proof limitations</summary>

The corrected test took 2.339s in its body, 57.41s in Vitest, and 310.099s command wall including the supported e2e build on AWS. In CI it took 0.121s; the 230-test suite took 97.38s Vitest / 98.85s runner wall, within a 448s job. These are observed durations, not incremental costs.

The live comparison's base/positive/replacement attempts took 60.155s / 53.611s / 55.350s. All nine setup, failed, and proof attempts total 483.619s; the two runtime builds took 245.551s separately. Returned usage across eight distinct native threads was 523,151 total tokens (520,551 input, including 379,701 cached; 2,600 output, including 565 reasoning). Counters are counted once per thread and are not billing. No per-PR CI tests were added for this proof.

Native/Gateway task, thread, and call IDs plus the harmless effect establish consumption; screenshots or transcript persistence alone do not. Error events and a failed-tool indicator are preserved, and not every operation is claimed successful. The replacement cell lacks the later followup's complete Gateway/thread binding; its original-task nonconsumption is established, and the base cell independently supplies the full queued-execution mapping. This is not a new live preparation-to-injection race. Existing deterministic race proof remains applicable. Owned processes settled and the AWS lease was released.

</details>

<details>
<summary>LoC churn against the pinned base</summary>

| Category | Files | Added | Removed | Churn |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Production | 4 | 50 | 13 | 63 |
| Tests | 2 | 71 | 16 | 87 |
| Total | 6 | 121 | 29 | 150 |

The test-only correction accounts for +15/-15. The evidence update changes no source or tests.

</details>

prs.title: fix: automatically retire old recovery copies after successful updates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Recovery copies accumulated indefinitely even after later successful updates made them eligible for the existing `openclaw update cleanup` retirement. Operators had to remember to run cleanup manually.

Related: #174253 #162622 #173564

## User Impact

Successful updates automatically retire superseded recovery copies, while retaining the just-finished update's rollback generation. Cleanup failures leave the update successful and surface advisory diagnostics in output/JSON and update history. Manual cleanup remains available.

## Why This Change Was Made

- CLI terminal publication invokes cleanup **after durable success and executor settlement**, using the existing local-state-owner router. A stopped state gets exclusive offline custody; a running Gateway receives an owner-bound admin request and runs the same retirement in a worker with live owner checks before effects. Cleanup never stops/restarts the Gateway or bypasses the manual command's offline lock.
- Gateway-owned restart completion invokes the same operation after success, including later observation of managed completion. The macOS app already uses these CLI paths; `--no-restart` does not imply ownership.
- The existing eligibility, dependency, manifest, and identity checks remain authoritative. Current-generation, pending-recovery, unfinished, unresolved-failed/rolled-back, orphan/unmanifested, and blocked artifacts remain protected under those rules. If any retained historical reference lacks artifact proof, automatic cleanup conservatively defers migration-original disposal as a group because dependency edges may span manifests. This uses underlying references, not final classification, so already-protected/incomplete originals cannot hide missing proof. Independently eligible captures still retire; manual cleanup retains its existing verification/classification. Doctor retention is unchanged.
- Post-success cleanup diagnostics may extend a terminal record but cannot change its outcome. No config switch, new retention schema, or new scheduler is introduced. The prewritten update report artifact remains the settled update report; late cleanup diagnostics are included in terminal output/JSON and update status.

## Evidence

Validated head: `393a60efa2496ae129a585c07d9954cff2611736`, clean merge of current main `9418ace887e21bff48459f3be6ffe5ad086f6d6c` into the previously reviewed head. The resulting tree exactly matches Git's merge-tree; no implementation edits or conflict resolutions were added. The prior independent API-only review through P2 and full touched-test audit remain applicable to the carried cleanup change; fresh composition checks below cover the new base.

- Focused: **66 tests / 5 files**, including real authenticated Gateway-worker cleanup/revocation, terminal authority/recording, already-current behavior, and all 13 automatic-cleanup cases.
- Affected: **102 tests / 7 files**, including manual retirement, ledger/restart, and the upstream hooks regression.
- Consumers: **47 tests / 4 files**, including progress, protocol descriptor, and recovery-inventory/manifest behavior.
- Synthetic-package restart outcome: **19 tests**. Total **234 tests** across the distinct commands.
- Targeted lint: **27 files, zero warnings/errors**; changed-file formatting, protocol registry and diff checks passed.
- Canonical production typecheck, all **29 core-test graphs**, and core declaration-boundary check passed on the isolated Linux checkout. The local global pnpm graph was refused by the physical declaration-containment guard, so these gates ran on the already-built Linux checkout's contained dependency graph; no boundary was bypassed.
- The optional full local changed gate completed all stages. Broad core/scripts lint and remaining guards passed; aggregate exit remained 1 for the local declaration-layout refusals above and an unrelated full-tree dead-export scan (12 pre-existing symbol paths, 11 whole files identical to the captured main; the retirement progress type and its test-only consumer are also unchanged). No findings were hidden or baselines changed.



### Real-install runtime acceptance

Dedicated **AWS Crabbox Linux x64**, Node **24.22.1**, isolated npm prefix/HOME/state/TMPDIR and systemd profile on loopback port 28333. The actual managed-handoff resolver was asserted inside the task-private temporary tree; the shared handoff store was absent. Live Odin was never touched.

Two independent fresh `openclaw@2026.10.6` installations were seeded through released Doctor with a real legacy session (two transcript events). Both supported first-hop updates to the exact final-head package succeeded and verified the final serving build/health (**423.24 s** and **416.22 s**), retaining their capture and both eligible `.bak` originals. Each automatically removed two imported originals / **512 logical bytes**.

The second-update fixture uses the same compiled final-head package and opaque build ID, stamped with the repository's `stampFixtureVersion` helper to force a real repeated installation rather than an already-current shortcut. Tarball comparison proved the only changes were `package.json`, `dist/build-info.json`, and its matching postinstall inventory digest; no production code or schema was modified.

| Case | Result | Automatic retirement | Latest generation retained | Total state + capture logical bytes before → after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Second update, Gateway **running** | exit 0; durable `succeeded`; exact build healthy/ready | prior capture **3,572,418 B** + agent/shared `.bak` **675,840 + 2,936,832 B** = **7,185,090 B** | **3,749,156 B** capture | **30,473,274 → 27,132,021 B** |
| Independent second update, Gateway **stopped**, `--no-restart` | exit 0; durable `succeeded`; systemd PID remained 0/inactive | prior capture **3,572,422 B** + agent/shared `.bak` **675,840 + 2,936,832 B** = **7,185,094 B** | **3,749,156 B** capture | **13,607,285 → 10,019,142 B** |

`update cleanup --dry-run --json` inventories and logical-file-size inventories were captured before and after every update. The three superseded artifacts disappeared, the triggering generation and Doctor capture remained, and update JSON plus `update status --json` reported the exact cleanup counts/bytes. Totals include mutable SQLite WAL/diagnostic data and are **not physical disk reclamation claims**.

Both same-head second updates also reported a **post-plugin Doctor source-generation refusal** as an advisory. They nevertheless finished succeeded, and the running case passed full Gateway readiness. No native diagnostic SQLite reads ran during either update; the running case's raw family/loader observations were saved separately. The advisory's writer/cause is not established, and it is not attributed to this cleanup PR. The two fresh stable-to-final first hops did not reproduce the original failure. A later control investigation separately identified the original failing run's native-read observer confound; no source-generation safeguard was weakened here.

**Injected cleanup failure:** a real ext4 immutable flag (`chattr +i`) on the previous capture's manifest denied retirement; no production/mock code was changed. The next same-head install exited **0**, durable status stayed **succeeded**, and both terminal JSON and `update status --json` showed `update-capture-retirement-failed` (the filesystem removal helper surfaced `ENOTDIR` while handling the denied manifest removal). The old manifest and latest **3,810,596 B** capture remained; cleanup reported **0 files / 0 logical bytes**. Total logical state/capture bytes: **10,019,253 → 13,862,296 B**. The immutable flag was removed after verification. This same-head update also carried the separately disclosed post-plugin Doctor advisory.

Final copied-database checks: both integrity checks `ok`, schema 31; the seeded session and its two transcript events survived all updates.

### Exact-head CI and review

All **189** check/status entries on `393a60efa2496ae129a585c07d9954cff2611736` are terminal: **136 SUCCESS, 52 SKIPPED, 1 NEUTRAL**, no failures/pending. Required `openclaw/ci-gate`, `openclaw/dependency-review`, and `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` statuses pass. [CI run 39894584305](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39894584305), attempt **1**, completed successfully on this exact SHA; no CI reruns were needed.

The clean-merge review reuse is explicit, not a claim of a fresh substantive-code review: the previous API-only review was clean through P2, and this pass added no implementation changes. The final merge tree is `bfe4b65be234a64b6d20ac96ab8fa730f52e3deb`.

prs.title: perf(plugins): carry input recovery in invocation frames
prs.body:
## Decision: rejected; not merged

The real-Gateway comparison crosses the predeclared v5 total-GC/work gate in both swapped pairs: **+61.24% and +93.34% (paired mean +77.29%, +38.735 µs/RPC)**. Allocation improves, but it does not override this regression. Close without merging. All exact-head CI and security statuses passed, and independent reviews found no actionable code findings. The proposed production delta is −3 lines; zero production lines are landed.

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin calls install a separate native async-context map for input recovery even though the plugin invocation frame already owns the same request lifetime. This adds allocation and GC work to every Gateway-scoped plugin callback.

Related: #181428, #181771.

## User Impact

Reduces plugin-call allocation while preserving per-agent recovery admission, saved-before-fresh input ordering, mutable request isolation, and plugin lifecycle checks. No configuration, schema, or public SDK change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the exact recovery source in the existing invocation frame and remove its separate AsyncLocalStorage. Generation-only scopes preserve the original source even when they copy or mutate the Gateway view; explicit Gateway scope entry rebinds it. Recovery still resolves the live owner on each check.

The access-policy callback remains dynamic: registration metadata cannot replace a revocable authorization decision. Nested plugin calls retain their independent mutable Gateway views. The implementation removes one native store and its get/enter helpers, with a net production delta of −3 lines (+35/−38).

## Evidence

67 focused tests pass across Gateway scope/import, plugin invocation, tool callbacks, reply-source recovery, and channel recovery. The store-count regression fails before the change (two native installs instead of one) and passes afterward. Export-name collision and closure guards pass (22 closure tests). Changed-file formatting/lint, `git diff --check`, and the targeted core typecheck (tsrs) pass. Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable) found no actionable P2-or-higher findings; the runtime change and subsequent type-only repair were independently reviewed.

CI exposed a type-import cycle through the recovery context module. The repair moves the unchanged recovery contracts into a dependency-free leaf and migrates all consumers. The affected 24 consumer tests, export guard, changed-file core lint, and closure checks pass. A stale local `fs-safe` install initially failed three closure checks; reconciling the existing install to the rebased frozen lock resolved all three (19/19 tests in that file). The type extraction emits identical runtime code.

**Final performance decision: reject under v5.** The completed real-Gateway pairs below cross the total-GC/work gate. This PR is not eligible to merge despite green CI.

Acceptance rule, recorded before candidate measurements: run identical workloads in concurrent pairs under the shared production guard and one exclusive measurement lock. Use interleaved 16-CPU placements and swap sides for pair two. Reject a ≥20% adverse paired mean or ≥10% adverse in both pairs. Opposite signs or baselines differing by more than 5× are inconclusive; eligible gating metrics get a third pair, decided on the absolute mean. A p95 requires 200 samples per side; p99 requires 1,000. Major-GC tails are context below 50 collections. GC-pause percentile shifts below 1 ms are context, as are higher tails with ≥20% fewer collections and no increase in total GC. Always compare maximum pauses against max(50 ms, 2× baseline maximum). Guard-interrupted pairs are discarded.

The existing `scripts/perf/plugin-gateway-scope-measure.ts` workload exercises 4,000 synthetic turns × 33 registered plugin callbacks = 132,000 callbacks per side. Allocation sampling includes collected objects; CPU/GC runs separately. A complementary real Gateway `plugin.scope` RPC workload uses synthetic 5,000-session/6,000-settled-run state with separate ports, state, and allocation/CPU passes.

### Historical comparison motivating this fix

Exact source snapshots `b7a1b32848fd` and `5369cfd439b8`, Node 26.12.1, same registered-plugin workload. These numbers compare the two baseline revisions, **not this PR's candidate**. Source inspection distinguishes the changes: #181428 introduced recovery scope after the older revision; #181771 reduced that overhead but retained a separate store. A completed same-revision rollback control confirms that #181771 reduced allocation; it did not cause the normalized allocation increase.

| Metric | Pair 1 older → newer | Pair 2, swapped | Mean paired delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Allocated B/callback | 7,969.7 → 10,262.5 | 7,859.8 → 10,296.9 | +29.89%, +2,365.0 B |
| GC µs/callback | 0.606 → 0.814 | 0.651 → 0.714 | +22.06%, +0.136 µs |
| Promoted B/callback | 373.73 → 460.38 | 375.68 → 436.75 | +19.72%, +73.86 B; >10% adverse in both |
| CPU µs/callback | 12.787 → 15.085 | 13.459 → 13.400 | +8.77%, +1.120 µs; mixed signs, inconclusive |
| Turn p99 ms (4,000 samples/side/pair) | 0.247 → 0.400 | 0.267 → 0.305 | +37.92%, +0.095 ms |
| Loop p99 ms (3,999 samples/side/pair) | 1.641 → 1.723 | 1.635 → 1.543 | −0.32%, −0.005 ms; mixed signs, inconclusive |

Minor/major collection counts: 55/5 → 103/5 and 55/5 → 73/5. Minor maximum pauses: 1.831 → 2.106 ms and 1.983 → 2.353 ms. Major maxima: 4.329 → 7.008 ms and 4.872 → 6.059 ms. GC tails are context at these collection counts; no maximum-pause gate is crossed. Both runs verified identical factory, prepare, execute, and authority-check counts. Scope-store installs doubled from 50 to 100 per synthetic turn, or one to two for a direct instance call.

These are source-owner measurements, not a compiled-build or whole-Gateway latency claim. The candidate owner and completed transport results are recorded below. The pre-push rebase includes #181780; final candidate measurements will use that updated baseline, because its async-context consolidation changes native map-copy cost. The five changed production owners are unchanged by the rebase.

### Candidate owner result

Pinned parent `a8aee07e3870` versus candidate `12ca8118a209`, three valid concurrent pairs, alternating interleaved CPU placement. Each side executes 132,000 callbacks per pair; all factory, prepare, execute, and authority-check counts match. Pair three was required because CPU, total GC, and turn p99 had mixed signs. These metrics are decided on absolute paired means, not the relative average. No v5–v5.3 rejection gate is crossed.

| Metric | Pair 1 parent → candidate | Pair 2, swapped | Pair 3 | Mean paired change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Allocated B/callback | 10,190.66 → 7,974.09 | 10,194.59 → 7,978.38 | 10,342.79 → 7,965.83 | −22.16%; −2,269.91 B |
| Promoted B/callback | 435.53 → 393.62 | 434.70 → 398.95 | 432.65 → 381.75 | −9.87%; −42.85 B |
| CPU µs/callback | 13.735 → 12.971 | 13.419 → 13.936 | 14.497 → 13.365 | −0.460 µs; −3.31% of mean baseline |
| GC µs/callback | 0.670 → 0.650 | 0.678 → 0.713 | 0.841 → 0.680 | −0.049 µs; −6.72% of mean baseline |
| Turn p95 ms (4,000 samples/side/pair) | 0.260 → 0.206 | 0.224 → 0.212 | 0.272 → 0.228 | −0.0365 ms; −14.04% |
| Turn p99 ms (4,000 samples/side/pair) | 0.320 → 0.301 | 0.322 → 0.344 | 0.380 → 0.386 | +0.0030 ms; +0.89% of mean baseline |
| Loop p99 ms (3,999 samples/side/pair) | 1.463 → 1.556 | 1.503 → 1.734 | 1.793 → 1.904 | +0.1447 ms; +9.29% |

The loop tail rises in all three pairs, but neither the ≥20% mean nor ≥10% in both initial pairs gate is crossed (+6.37%, +15.33%, +6.17%). Minor collection counts are 74→56, 104→55, and 72→57; major counts are 5→4, 5→5, and 5→4. Minor maximum pauses are 1.628→2.383, 2.170→2.176, and 3.625→2.925 ms. Major maxima are 5.482→6.407, 5.312→5.104, and 6.984→4.808 ms. No max-pause gate is crossed. GC percentile sample counts remain below eligibility, and absolute mean pause shifts are below 1 ms.

Native heap-profile attribution for the first two pairs narrows the win to the explicit Node `enterWith → Map` family under plugin Gateway scope: 2,656.68→877.38 and 2,642.49→873.14 B/callback, a mean **66.97% reduction** (−1,774.33 B/callback). Other native allocations remain roughly flat. Native store installations halve from 100→50 per synthetic turn, 2→1 per direct instance call, and 4→2 for nested calls. This is the intended post-deployment signal, normalized per invocation; no production deployment is claimed.

The required pre-push rebase leaves the measured scope owners, owner harness, fixture generator, and dependency lock unchanged. The reviewed type-only extraction emits identical runtime code. Whole-Gateway results, when available, remain corroborating evidence at their pinned revisions rather than an exact-final-head throughput claim. Initial control/Gateway setup attempts failed before useful comparison (unsupported loader mode; omitted UI import closure; a newer diagnostics preload on the old revision). These attempts were discarded, and the setups were repaired without modifying historical production code. Historical owner runs have guard evidence but no per-core load artifact; the candidate and subsequent runs capture `mpstat` context.

### Attribution control for #181771

Holding revision `5369cfd439b8` and the workload fixed, replacing only the two production owners with their pre-#181771 versions gives 11,979.27→10,209.38 and 12,057.24→10,248.07 B/callback for pre→post, a paired mean **−14.89% (−1,789.53 B/callback)**. Each side executed 132,000 callbacks with identical work and authority-check counts. Native scope installs fell 150→100 per synthetic turn (3→2 per direct invocation). Reverting #181771 would increase allocation; the current patch removes its remaining recovery store.

Control context, not candidate acceptance evidence: CPU changes +9.84%/+12.98% (+1.467 µs/callback mean), and loop p99 +3.31%/+3.60% (+0.0538 ms; 3,999 samples/side/pair). Total GC, promotion, and turn p99 have mixed signs and remain inconclusive in this attribution-only control. Minor counts87→106 and124→103; major5→5 both pairs. Minor maxima1.323→2.035 and1.797→2.148 ms; major maxima6.552→6.385 and6.626→7.997 ms. No max-pause gate is crossed. The candidate's separate three-pair acceptance results are above.

### Decisive real-Gateway comparison

Pinned parent `a8aee07e3870` versus candidate `12ca8118a209`, Node 26.12.1, identical synthetic 5,000-session/6,000-settled-run state, 1,000 validated `plugin.scope` RPCs per side per pass at approximately 453 requests/minute. Allocation and natural CPU/GC use separate passes. Both concurrent pairs completed successfully under the shared guard, with CPU placement swapped for pair two. Work is normalized by validated RPC, not an inferred count of internal plugin callbacks.

| Metric | Pair 1 parent → candidate | Pair 2, swapped | Paired result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Allocated B/RPC | 143,214.59 → 138,457.37 | 140,485.82 → 136,456.14 | −3.10%; −4,393.45 B |
| Total GC µs/RPC | 55.101 → 88.845 | 46.847 → 90.573 | **+77.29%; +38.735 µs; reject** |
| Main CPU µs/RPC | 1,136.674 → 1,083.301 | 1,171.770 → 1,186.769 | Mixed signs; −19.187 µs mean; inconclusive |
| Process CPU µs/RPC | 4,462.127 → 4,072.123 | 4,537.572 → 4,580.483 | Mixed signs; −173.546 µs mean; inconclusive |
| Promoted B/RPC | 26,359.03 → 25,557.55 | 16,399.20 → 25,472.82 | Mixed signs; +4,136.07 B mean; inconclusive |
| RPC p95 ms (1,000 samples/side/pair) | 1.401 → 1.349 | 1.387 → 1.308 | −4.70%; −0.0654 ms |
| RPC p99 ms (1,000 samples/side/pair) | 1.916 → 1.730 | 1.499 → 1.427 | −7.27%; −0.1291 ms |
| Loop p99 ms (6,599/6,602 samples parent/candidate in each pair) | 20.824 → 20.906 | 20.693 → 20.660 | Mixed signs; +0.0246 ms mean; inconclusive |

Minor collections: 16→77 and 21→64. Major collections: 1→0 and 1→1. Minor maximum pauses: 3.577→5.190 ms and 2.494→3.855 ms. Major maxima: 16.928 ms→no collection, and 14.402→13.849 ms. No maximum-pause clause is crossed. GC percentile tails lack eligible collection counts; the rejection is **total GC time per work**, not a sub-millisecond pause percentile shift.

Main-isolate trace inspection shows smaller candidate young-generation capacity before the first capture (2 MiB versus 32 MiB), followed by more frequent, smaller allocation-failure scavenges. Both processes had pre-capture memory-reducing collections; capture starts differ by only 0.091 ms. This explains the observed count pattern but does not establish independence from the candidate and does not waive the gate.

A third CPU pass had been selected for other mixed-sign metrics; it was stopped once the independent, consistently adverse GC gate was confirmed. The supplemental historical Gateway campaign was also stopped. Neither partial run is counted. The two historical owner pairs and the separate #181771 attribution control remain complete; historical whole-Gateway numbers are not claimed. No deployment or production runtime changes were made.

prs.title: fix(update): show new releases without waiting for a second daily check
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a new stable release reaches `update.status`, the sidebar update card and the Control UI inbox up to two days after it was published, while `openclaw update status` reports it right away, when the Gateway runs the `stable` channel without automatic updates.

## User Impact

User impact: the Gateway update notice shows a new stable release within an hour of the daily telemetry check that found it, instead of waiting for the update check's own next daily run.

Affected: every package install on the default `stable` channel with `update.auto.enabled` off (the default) and update checks on (the default). The same applies with auto-update on when an external supervisor owns updates, because that path also takes the version from telemetry. Auto-update, `beta`, `extended-stable` and `dev` keep their npm lookups, throttles and rollout delays unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two daily timers run independently and the notice needs both:

1. Gateway maintenance pings `telemetry.openclaw.ai/api/latest-version` and caches the answer for 24 h (`telemetry.updateCheck`, `src/infra/telemetry.ts`, re-run every 5–10 min in `src/gateway/server-maintenance.ts`, effective once per day). CLI runs refresh the same cache.
2. The Gateway update check (`runGatewayUpdateCheck`, `src/infra/update-startup.ts`) reads that cache only when its own task runs: at startup and then every 24 h (`resolveCheckIntervalMs`), and it returns early when its last check (`update.checkState.lastCheckedAt`) is less than 24 h old. For stable without auto-update the version comes only from the cache (`version: telemetryUpdate?.version`).

So a release found by the maintenance ping waits until the update check's next daily run, and a Gateway restart in between skips the check on the throttle. The seam is between the telemetry cache owner and the update-check owner; this change lets the update check follow the cache:

- stable package installs re-read the local cache hourly (the interval auto-update already uses). This reads local state only; the telemetry request count does not change because the cache keeps its 24 h lifetime;
- a cached release newer than the one already published (or than the installed version) bypasses the 24 h throttle once. After it is published, `lastAvailableVersion` matches and the throttle applies again.

| | Lines |
|---|---|
| Production (`src/infra/update-startup.ts`) | +15 / −3 |
| Tests (`src/infra/update-startup-cached.test.ts`) | +132 / −2 |
| Docs (`docs/gateway/telemetry.md`) | +3 / −1 |

No new scheduler, no new state, no change to the telemetry request or its consent rules.

## Evidence

**Production timeline (2026.10.5 installed, stable, auto-update off):**

| Time (UTC) | Event |
|---|---|
| 2026-10-22 12:44:56 | 2026.10.6 published on npm `latest` |
| 2026-10-22 16:36:36 | Gateway update check runs, telemetry cache still holds 2026.10.5 → `update.checkState` `{"lastCheckedAt":"2026-10-22T16:36:36.554Z","lastNotifiedVersion":"2026.10.5"}`, no `lastAvailableVersion` |
| 2026-10-22 21:16:40 | Gateway restart; update check skipped by the 24 h throttle |
| 2026-10-23 02:43:39 | shared telemetry cache refreshed: `{"lastPingAt":1792723419731,"latestVersion":"2026.10.6"}` |
| 2026-10-23 15:45 | `update.status` → `updateAvailable: null`; inbox shows nothing; `openclaw update status` shows 2026.10.6 |
| 2026-10-23 21:17:44 | next scheduled update check (24 h after the restart): first notice, ~32.5 h after release and ~18.5 h after the Gateway already had the version cached. Observed at 21:30: `update.checkState` `{"lastCheckedAt":"2026-10-23T21:17:44.423Z","lastNotifiedVersion":"2026.10.6","lastAvailableVersion":"2026.10.6"}`, `update.status` → `updateAvailable: {"currentVersion":"2026.10.5","latestVersion":"2026.10.6","channel":"latest"}` |

The worst case is close to 48 h: a ping just before the release keeps the old version for 24 h, and the update check can run just before that cache expires.

**Live before/after on an isolated Gateway** (loopback, own state, package copy without `.git` so the install is detected as `package`, `OPENCLAW_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT` pointed at a local stub that answers with the installed version). Same script for both builds:

1. start once so the Gateway creates its state, stop;
2. write the production situation into the state DB: update check 1 h ago without a finding, telemetry cache refreshed 30 min ago with `2026.10.7`;
3. restart and read `update.status`.

| Build | `update.status.updateAvailable` after restart | `update.checkState` after restart |
|---|---|---|
| base `7845dd3eb29` | `null` (17:00:17Z) | unchanged, `lastCheckedAt` 1 h old |
| fix `fce5dc4dbe3` | `{"currentVersion":"2026.10.6","latestVersion":"2026.10.7","channel":"latest"}` (17:16:03Z) | `lastAvailableVersion: "2026.10.7"`, `lastNotifiedVersion: "2026.10.7"` |

No telemetry request reached the stub during step 3 in either run; both builds used the cached value.

<details><summary>Fix run, step 3 (excerpt)</summary>

```text
--- 2026-10-23T17:16:03Z update.status
{
 "updateAvailable": {
  "currentVersion": "2026.10.6",
  "latestVersion": "2026.10.7",
  "channel": "latest"
 },
 "effectiveChannel": "stable",
 "schedule": {
  "channel": "stable",
  "autoEnabled": false,
  "install": { "kind": "package" },
  "target": { "kind": "package", "version": "2026.10.7" }
 }
}
--- Telemetry requests at the stub during step 3:
--- Log lines 'update available':
2026-10-23T19:15:56.586+02:00 update available (latest): v2026.10.7 (current v2026.10.6). Run: openclaw update
```

</details>

**Tests** (Linux, Node 24.22.1, `--maxWorkers=1`):

- `src/infra/update-startup-cached.test.ts`: 9 passed, 64 s. New cases run the real `runGatewayUpdateCheck` / `createGatewayUpdateCheck` owners against the state DB with the scheduler test clock (no sleeps or timers): cached release published within the throttle (new, and newer than an already published one); throttle kept when the cached release is already published or not newer; auto-update throttle unchanged (no npm lookup); hourly scheduled re-read publishes a refreshed cache one hour later.
- Counter-check: without the production change 3 of the new cases fail; with only the throttle bypass (daily interval kept) the scheduled case still fails, so both parts are needed.
- All tests that use the changed owner: 17 files (`src/infra/update-startup*.test.ts`, `src/infra/telemetry*.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-startup-update-check.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/update-*.test.ts`, `src/cli/update-cli.candidate-activation.test.ts`, …), 322 passed, 724 s.
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint --type-aware` on changed files, `check-test-mock-exports`: clean.

Gap: the hourly re-read was not observed live (it needs an hour of wall-clock time per run); it is covered by the scheduler-clock test above.

Context: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/64807 reported the same class (dashboard uses a throttled Gateway cache, CLI checks live) before the telemetry cache existed; it was closed by the reporter without a code change. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/128424 introduced the daily telemetry ping that added the second 24 h layer.

prs.title: fix: Skill workshop reader stays short as the skill list grows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the selected skill's instructions stop at a viewport-based height while a longer Skill workshop list keeps growing.

## User Impact

Instructions and supporting-file readers now fill the space alongside the skill list. Narrow screens retain a bounded, scrollable reader. No configuration changes or migrations.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stretch the two panels together and let the detail body own the available reading height, rather than independently capping each document. This stays CSS-only, with no JavaScript measurements or new state.

## Evidence

- Real Chromium regression: red on the base, green with the fix; covers list growth, supporting-file scrolling, and mobile stacking.
- Existing workshop page suite: 12 tests passed.
- Control UI production and test typechecks, targeted oxlint/stylelint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed.
- Fresh independent Auto Review returned no findings at its P0-only scope on the CSS budget repair.
- Unchanged UI performance comparison passed: total CSS raw +60 B (64 B allowed), gzip +23 B (64 B allowed), and startup CSS unchanged. No budgets or baselines were relaxed.
- The CSS simplification is pixel-identical to the previously published implementation at 1440px desktop and 390px mobile, so the existing inspected screenshots remain current.
- Built Control UI exercised through the actual `/skills/workshop` route with synthetic Gateway data. Before: detail panel 1465.09px beside a 2034.25px list. After: both panels 2034.25px, with the reader scrolling internally.

**Before**

![Skill workshop before: the instructions reader stops while the skill list continues](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e3289644-3b9e-4f5c-98c6-bbb375e918cd)

**After**

![Skill workshop after: the instructions reader expands alongside the skill list](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e195638c-0e59-4ec7-ac94-25fc7e1c0f67)

<details>
<summary>Verification and scope notes</summary>

- New regression command: `pnpm test ui/src/pages/skill-workshop/skill-workshop-layout.browser.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1` — 1.95s command wall time, 66ms test execution. CI seconds: pending GitHub CI.
- Performance command: `pnpm ui:check-performance:base ec58b6924b9a5b69764d95dff1c5c49ce00e7806` (exit 0). CSS raw 1,596,956 → 1,597,016 B; gzip 302,824 → 302,847 B. [Exact-head hosted performance CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40008147451/job/120602036833) on `86d5c8b07008857a414edad0c0f208566e37af6d`, confirming the same +60 B raw / +23 B gzip deltas.
- Existing page suite: 11.62s command wall time. Final production UI capture/build scenario passed (39.29s build, 41.83s total).
- An existing Solid development warning in unchanged `detail.tsx` is emitted by the support-file fixture; all assertions pass.
- Simplification: remove the independent document height caps; preserve existing document formatting and horizontal overflow. Production delta: +16/-6 CSS lines. Test delta: +88 lines in one real-browser regression. No new runtime owner or state.

</details>
