prs.title: perf(github): overlap pull request comment reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening a pull request's discussion waits for discussion comments and inline review comments sequentially, adding an unnecessary upstream round trip.

## User Impact

The discussion section and full `github_read` documents fetch both independent comment collections concurrently. Comments, ordering, partial-result markers, credential checks, and final public-repository checks are preserved. This does not change hover previews or claim to fix their reported tail latency.

## Why This Change Was Made

Overlap the existing reads at the document owner; no cache, transport owner, or configuration is added. Validate both comment counts before starting either request. If one request immediately exhausts quota, the other may already be in flight; subsequent requests still honor the existing cooldown. Production runtime change: 15 additions / 17 deletions, net -2 lines. The separate 139-line benchmark is committed measurement support; it does not run in the product.

## Evidence

The regression fails on the baseline: two synthetic 100 ms reads take 200 ms. It covers success and a partial discussion failure. Candidate focused checks: `detail.test.ts` and `detail-checks.test.ts`, 67 tests passed (13.50 s wrapper wall time; test work approximately 0.2 s). Final changed-file lint/format passed; the final regression rerun passed all 50 tests. Export collision and both required source-closure guards passed (22 tests). Broad PR CI passed on exact head `5e92faba5dd3d49851e15b5d1545be16fedf6685`: [CI gate, run 40016236045](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40016236045/job/120632621229). No CI reruns or Testbox lease used.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable P0–P2 findings. An independent audit of all six raw GC traces and the final threshold arithmetic also passed. The configured autoreview route was rejected because it did not match the operator configuration; configuration was not changed.

Measurement acceptance, recorded before running: synthetic cold authenticated discussion reads through the production plugin API, 20 ms per upstream response, 20 discussion + 20 review comments, 1,000 samples per side at concurrency 2. Two concurrent CPU-interleaved pairs, placements swapped, exclusive slot and shared production guard. Require latency improvement with unchanged successful request count and no qualifying regression in CPU/work, RSS, total GC/work, promotion/work or event-loop p99. A mean adverse change of at least 20%, or at least 10% in both pairs, gates. Opposite signs or baselines over 5x apart are inconclusive and require a third pair for gating metrics; p99 requires 1,000 samples, p95 200, major GC tails 50 collections. Sub-millisecond paired-mean GC percentile changes are context; max pause must not exceed max(50 ms, twice baseline). GC percentiles also become context when counts fall at least 20% without increased total GC time.

Measurement passed the declared thresholds. Three concurrent pairs completed without guard interruption; pair 2 swapped placements, pair 3 repeated pair 1 placements to resolve mixed-sign promotion. Each side completed 1,000 reads and 5,000 synthetic HTTP requests. Node 26.12.1, same bundled baseline/candidate artifacts throughout; 16 interleaved CPUs and 4 GiB memory limit per side. Baseline retains sequential comment reads; candidate overlaps them, with all other source and dependencies held identical.

Mean latency fell 100.971 → 80.921 ms (−19.86%); mean of per-run p99 values fell 102.738 → 82.511 ms (−19.69%). CPU/read fell 2.329 → 2.083 ms (−10.61% mean paired change, −10.54% change of absolute means). GC pause time/read fell 0.089367 → 0.081450 ms (−8.93% mean paired).

Promotion was initially inconclusive: +37.24% and −9.18%, followed by −10.58% in the required third pair. Applying v5.2 to absolute means gives +2.024 KB/read, 42.490 → 44.514 KB/read (+4.76%); no boundary collection was discarded. Peak RSS absolute means rose 7.293 MiB (+1.55%); final RSS fell 10.186 MiB (−2.43%). Event-loop p99 rose 0.088405 ms (+6.04% mean paired), below the declared rejection thresholds. No qualifying adverse gate fired.

GC per-collection tails are context: all distributions are below the 200/1,000 percentile sample floors, and every major-GC side has fewer than 50 collections. Minor p95/p99 absolute mean shifts are also below 1 ms. Overall baseline → candidate maximum GC pauses were 11.954 → 14.818 ms, 13.203 → 13.813 ms, and 13.628 → 13.843 ms; none crosses max(50 ms, twice baseline max). Total GC pause time and promotion remain included in the gate.

The tables retain every pair, absolute and relative deltas, and sample counts. Paired percentile means are means of run percentiles, not pooled percentiles; each latency percentile uses n=1,000 per side per pair, and event-loop percentile sample counts are listed in each pair. All comments, ordering and successful request counts remain unchanged. Reproduce with `node --trace-gc-nvp --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/github-reader-measure.ts 1000 2`; inspect GC/promotion records between `BENCH_START` and `BENCH_END`. This measures the production reader owner with synthetic HTTP responses, not Gateway transport, real GitHub, or credential-store latency.


<details>
<summary>Full paired measurement results</summary>

### Pair 1

prs.title: perf(memory): speed up PostgreSQL full reindex staging
prs.body:
## Disposition: not landing

The local bulk result passed, but the required remote A/B did not hold incremental latency. On the 4-CPU/16-GiB Testbox, full reindex improved 126.738→108.247 s and removed the expected 2,000 trips, while incremental median rose 57.047→153.717 ms and p95/max rose 66.901→268.225 ms (five per arm). The p95 increase exceeds that pair’s combined sample ranges. These observations are retained; the local 90/arm control does not override the failed remote criterion. This candidate is closed without landing.

The first remote setup failed before benchmarking. The recovery completed both arms and their within-arm search-hash checks, then automatic host cleanup ran; complete raw remote receipt retrieval was not completed before shutdown. Console phase/statement/function receipts are retained. All three final-head local PostgreSQL conformance shards passed (345.7 s, 457.2 s, 256.3 s). Source correctness review remains clean; this is a performance-acceptance rejection.

Related: #181860

## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL full memory reindex scans each staged source again immediately after copying it into the publication spool.

## User Impact

Full reindex is faster on PostgreSQL. Three interleaved 20,000-chunk pairs reduced median storage-owner time from **96.315 s to 83.557 s**, with identical search results. SQLite behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing copy now returns the source completion flag in the same statement. The integer aggregate preserves the exact `last = 1` condition, including empty input. Source checks, ordered fragments, the eager outer advisory lock, commit authority, rollback and separate COMMIT remain with their existing owners.

## Evidence

Same base `b1967334895d`, 20,000 prepared chunks / 2,000 sources / 1,536 dimensions, decoder version 2 in both arms, three serial interleaved pairs. Fixture SHA-256: `a853dd3d074eafe596de2d1e3811c30af11ad6c18a2bff77244764faf802257a`. Zero paid embedding calls. The workload exercises cache/source owners, bounded spool staging and atomic publication through the real PostgreSQL bridge.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Full reindex median | 96.315 s | 83.557 s |
| Full outer SQL statements | 50,159 | 48,159 |
| Full query trips | 42,155 | 40,155 |
| Initial publication median | 23.167 s | 23.255 s |
| Primary incremental median, 15/arm | 45.451 ms | 48.313 ms |
| Primary incremental p95 | 65.648 ms | 115.673 ms |
| Supplemental incremental median, 90/arm | 47.939 ms | 48.872 ms |
| Supplemental incremental p95 | 74.374 ms | 61.539 ms |

Acceptance was registered before edits: deterministic trip reduction, bulk median gain beyond combined within-arm ranges, identical search hashes, and initial/incremental latency holding within measured spread. The 12.758 s bulk gain exceeds the 9.491 s combined range. All vector/keyword/hybrid hashes match across all six arms. Host load and every sample are retained.

The primary incremental p95 worsened and is retained. Its slow samples executed zero changed CTEs; cost was distributed across unchanged operations. The increase is within the registered 96.697 ms combined incremental range. The separate 90/arm control used two valid 20,000-chunk stores, an untimed checkpoint, and three interleaved 30-update groups with bindings reopened; canonical/vector/search hashes all match. This does not claim every metric or cold sample improves.

The real-binder regression is red on the base at one redundant SELECT per source and green with this change. It covers complete/empty staged sources, refused final append and retry, refused publication and retry, exact text/vector results and revision. All 17 publication tests pass (25.6 s total including compilation, about 2 s test time). Production and extension-test TSRS, targeted lint, formatting and independent P0–P3 review pass.

This PR will not be landed because of the remote incremental result above.

Net LOC: production +4; tests +110; total +114. The existing long publication case moved into a test helper to preserve the test file's 1,000-line limit while adding the missing empty/refusal coverage. No new runtime state or cache.

The composer documentation does not distinguish source-supported video preparation paths from the device, audio, and mixed-track compatibility evidence that is still missing.

## User Impact

Readers can distinguish MP4/H.264/AAC and WebM/VP9/Opus preparation, unchanged pass-through, actual conversion, disclosed loss, refusal, and untested or blocked qualification. The docs include a proposed device runbook without advertising new compatibility.

No codec support, upload limits, mixed-track policy, or runtime behavior changes. ## What Problem This Solves

Several internal preparation and projection operations still route through private helpers, a sole-instance cache factory, or named annotations with only one consumer.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Public SDK, protocol, configuration and CLI contracts remain unchanged, as do lazy imports, security checks, persistence, and the standalone session memory backend.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move those private frames into the existing operations that consume them. This includes chat grouping's singleton cache, archive and launcher preparation, hosted catalog snapshot fallback, skill discovery, diagnostic formatting, and AI transport annotations. Keep cache keys and retirement, containment, signatures, expiry, resource cleanup, output bytes and settlement behavior intact.

Net production reduction: **151 lines** across 22 production paths, including one retired internal module. No tests, generated files, configuration, schemas or dependencies change.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

No defensive guard is removed. Private stack frames and one internal snapshot-result promise hop disappear; the same actual parser await remains inside the fallback catch. The route forwarding alias stays because a broader inline changed generic inference in targeted typechecking.

## Evidence

Focused native typechecks, typed lint and formatting pass for every touched cohort. Existing suites pass for chat grouping (57), routes (5), CLI launcher (17; five existing native-Windows skips), archive preparation (39), Google projection (58), hosted catalog (44), AI annotations (154), compatibility/schema consumers (85), Tailscale status (20), CLI diagnostics (19), and update consumers (79). prs.title: feat(models): expose canonical model family in models.list and the requester catalog
prs.body:
## What

Model catalog rows can now carry an optional, additive `family`: the developer lineage of the model, taken only from provider or catalog metadata. It reaches `models.list` rows and the plugin requester catalog from #180283 (`runtimeContext.models.list()`). Hosts that support it advertise the runtime capability `requester-model-family-v1`.

The same model reports the same family on every route. `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`, `github-copilot/claude-opus-5.5` and ClawRouter's `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` are all `anthropic`. When the host does not know a row's family, the field is absent. It is never inferred from a model id or name. No credential or route fields are added.

This answers the maintainers' question in the pstack v2 plan ("Should the catalog carry a canonical model `family`?"). Plugins can now check a different-family requirement against host facts instead of guessing from names.

## Field contract

- **Name:** `family?: string`. It appears on `models.list` `ModelChoice` rows and on `PluginRequesterModelCatalog.models[]`.
- **Value:** a lowercase, hyphen-separated token (`^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$`, at most 64 characters). It is the provider id of the developer's own catalog: `anthropic`, `openai`, `google`, `xai`, `mistral`, `deepseek`, `cohere`, `moonshot`, `meta`, `zai`, `xiaomi`, `stepfun` or `tencent`.
- **Meaning:** compare it only for equality. Absent means unknown, never "different". A host without `requester-model-family-v1` carries no family at all.
- **Protocol:** `ModelChoiceSchema` gains `family: Type.Optional(ModelFamilyString)`. The schema rejects malformed values; the host drops them before projection.

## Where a family comes from

- **Bundled manifests**
  - **Provider level:** `modelCatalog.providers.<id>.family` is declared only for catalogs where one developer makes every model: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI, Mistral, DeepSeek, Cohere, Moonshot (`moonshot` and `kimi`), Meta, Z.AI, Xiaomi, StepFun and Tencent. Rows inherit it the same way they inherit `api`.
  - **Row level:** `models[].family` is for hosts that serve several developers' models. The GitHub Copilot catalog declares one per row.
  - **Not declared:** hosts such as Qwen (which also serves GLM, Kimi and MiniMax), OpenRouter or Venice declare nothing. Their rows stay unknown.
- **GitHub Copilot discovery:** a fixed table maps Copilot's `/models` `vendor` labels (Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Google, xAI, Moonshot AI) to families. With no vendor, or one not in the table, the row falls back to the bundled row for the same exact id, else stays unknown.
- **ClawRouter discovery:** a routed row takes the family of the bundled first-party row with the same exact upstream id and wire API. This reuses the existing exact-match identity-facts resolver. ClawRouter's `google-gemini` catalog is mapped to the bundled `google` provider. Unknown upstreams, unknown ids and other wire APIs get nothing.
- **Route binding:** the family follows the same rule as `parameterCount` and other catalog facts.
  - A configured model that moves to another API or endpoint drops the catalog family, because that endpoint may serve a different model under the same id.
  - A route overlay that moves a row drops it too.
  - A managed OpenAI route projection keeps the model's identity, family included.
- **Hosted catalog overlay:** its strict schema has no `family`, so it keeps the bundled row's family for the same id.
- **Live rows:** discovered rows keep a family only when they match a manifest row exactly. A newly listed id that is not in the manifest stays unknown until the manifest declares it.
- **Persisted catalogs:** `models.json` normalizes the family when it is read. A malformed value drops only that fact, never the catalog.

## Tests

Unless noted, every run below is on exact head `6cc834ad`, on main `53227198`.

- **E2E, real isolated Gateway:** a new test builds `dist`, starts a Gateway with the real bundled plugins and reads `runtimeContext.models.list()` from a plugin command.
  - Kimi Code's bundled catalog row `kimi/k3` reports `moonshot`.
  - A custom config provider reports no family.
  - Configured ClawRouter refs named `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` and `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` report no family, because no catalog describes them. Nothing is inferred from the vendor-looking ids.
  - The existing #180283 E2E still passes.
- **Routing providers:**
  - ClawRouter's real discovery projection, checked against the shipped Anthropic, OpenAI and Google catalogs: routed `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` → `anthropic`, `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` → `openai`, and `google-gemini/gemini-3.5-flash` → `google`. An unknown id, another wire API and an unknown upstream (`acme/claude-opus-5-5`) report nothing.
  - Copilot `/models` fetch:
    - The `Anthropic`, `Azure OpenAI` and `Moonshot AI` vendors map to families.
    - A row without a vendor falls back to the bundled row for its id.
    - An unknown vendor with an id the catalog lacks reports nothing.
  - Contract test with the real bundled resolver: `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` and `github-copilot/claude-opus-5.5` are both `anthropic`, and Copilot's GPT and Gemini rows match the OpenAI and Google catalogs. Qwen's GLM row reports nothing.
- **Pipeline:**
  - Registry rows → prepared catalog snapshot (entries and route variants).
  - Manifest provider and row inheritance (normalization, raw manifest, effective manifest, augmentation).
  - Hosted overlay.
  - Config merge and configured-catalog route rules, overlay route change, and managed route projection.
  - `models.json` normalization.
- **Config and hosted catalog stay valid:**
  - Onboarding writes catalog rows to config without `family`. Strict config validation accepts the written models and rejects the same rows with `family`.
  - The hosted catalog publisher strips the family, which the strict v1/v2/v3 hosted schemas do not allow.
- **Reader and protocol:**
  - `models.list` through the real handler passes `Check(ModelsListResultSchema)`, and the requester reader equals the projected Gateway result. A declared family is present; an undeclared or malformed one is absent.
  - Protocol schema accepts canonical tokens and rejects `""`, `Anthropic`, `open ai`, `-anthropic`, 65 characters and non-strings.
  - Runtime capabilities include `requester-model-family-v1`.
- **Upgrade/rollback data compatibility (`ea388bff`, the same change, vs its base `cee236c9`):** each checkout wrote three artifacts with its own code: a `models.json` with native, bundled and routed rows; a replace-mode Kimi onboarding config; and the v1 and v2 hosted bundles. The other checkout read them with its own code.
  - The old registry loads the new `models.json` (all 16 rows; extra properties are accepted).
  - Strict config validation accepts both configs. Neither carries `family`.
  - Both versions parse both bundles. Neither carries `family`.
  - The new reader keeps the families it wrote and reports none for old data.
- **Focused (`6cc834ad`):** every touched test file, the publisher tests, the onboarding test, both E2Es, the Gateway lifecycle test and `chat-boot-render-storm`. 13 shards, 27 files, 349 tests passed.
- **Affected (`6cc834ad`):** 21 shards, 854 files, 9,711 tests passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed. Coverage:
  - `src/agents/sessions`, `src/model-catalog`, `src/plugin-sdk` and `src/plugins/contracts`.
  - `packages/model-catalog-core` and `packages/gateway-protocol`.
  - Every extension whose manifest or code changed: ClawRouter, GitHub Copilot, Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI, Mistral, DeepSeek, Cohere, Moonshot, Kimi Code, Meta, Z.AI, Xiaomi, StepFun and Tencent.
  - Every model-catalog, model-selection, models-config, prepared-model-runtime and bundled-model test in `src/agents`.
  - The models-list, requester and chat-metadata Gateway method tests, and the provider-catalog and provider-discovery plugin tests.
- **Fail-before** (on `594f679e`, the same change before rebase): with only the production TypeScript reverted (tests and manifests kept), every new test fails. That is 19 in-process tests plus the E2E (`kimi/k3` reports no family). Without the onboarding change, the onboarding test fails.
- **Typecheck:** `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions` pass.
- **`pnpm check:changed`:** every lane passes: format, typecheck (core, core tests, extensions, extension tests, test root), lint (core, extensions, scripts, test root), runtime import cycles, line-cap and max-lines ratchets, assertion SAFETY ratchet, plugin boundaries and the remaining guards. The aggregate exits 1 only because the dead-export scan lists 25 unused exports, none in files this PR touches (Telegram, X, `scripts/control-ui-*` and others).
- **Line cap:** to avoid growing an over-cap file, `ModelRegistry.createRuntimeModel` moved unchanged, apart from `family`, into `src/agents/sessions/model-registry-runtime-model.ts`. The assertion baseline for `model-registry.ts` shrank from 5 to 3; the two moved assertions carry SAFETY invariants.
- **`checks-ui-e2e (8/9)`:** `ui/src/e2e/chat-boot-render-storm.e2e.test.ts` failed on base `cee236c9` too, with the same "Search people…" timeout. The fix, #181798, has since merged; on this head the test passes.
- **First CI run:** `src/gateway/server-plugins.lifecycle.channels.test.ts` failed on the earlier base `792b48a3`. That base fails it without this change too ("gateway starting; retry shortly"), and on current main it passes.

## Docs

- `docs/plugins/manifest/models.md`: new provider and model `family` fields and a "Model family" section. The section also says `family` is catalog metadata, not a config field.
- `docs/plugins/sdk-runtime/models.md`: the field and the `requester-model-family-v1` capability. This replaces "no canonical family is exposed".
- `docs/gateway/protocol/rpc-system-and-channels.md`: the `models.list` row field.

## Risks

- **Authored families:** the families are hand-authored. A contract test checks that every bundled value is canonical, and that every row-level value is one some developer's own catalog also declares.
- **New models:** a model added to a first-party API before the manifest lists it reports no family until the manifest is updated. This is deliberate: there is no name inference.
- **ClawRouter in a real Gateway:** routed discovery could not be exercised in a real Gateway. A loopback ClawRouter endpoint is a custom endpoint, so the plugin's discovered inventory is (correctly) not used. Routed families are proved by the plugin's real discovery projection against the shipped bundled catalogs, then the registry-to-published-catalog pipeline, then the requester reader.

prs.title: fix(database): port refuses upgraded state and agent stores
prs.body:
Closes #181875 Related: #178230, #178005 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: `openclaw database port` refuses upgraded shared-state and agent stores when they have not used every feature that adds a column on first use. ## User Impact User impact: operators can port upgraded agent and shared-state stores to PostgreSQL without first exercising every feature. The live SQLite stores are not modified, and the destination gets the complete current layout. ## Why This Change Was Made Both schema owners allow these columns to be absent until their feature first writes them. The port's strict layout check rejected the absence anyway: the agent port never reported such columns as pending, and the state port knew only the single column that #178005 added and #178230 reported as pending. This change applies the #178005/#178230 design to every first-use column in both families. Port inspection reports each one as pending when its table exists, and port preparation adds it to the private copy before verification and staging. Each family keeps its own column list, and one shared check reads both. Any other missing or unknown column is still refused. Schema versions, schema shapes and public contracts are unchanged. Accepted edge case: the agent column `standing_intents.creator_sender` is not covered. Maintenance admission also allows it to be absent, but it is outside the first-use list and carries a CHECK constraint, and only its standing-intents owner adds it. A store whose `standing_intents` table predates that column would still be refused. None of the 11 real agent stores below hits this; all have the column. No follow-up is planned: all 11 real stores already have it, and only its feature adds it. ## Evidence **Published-stable upgrade proof: v2026.10.6 → this PR → PostgreSQL.** This follows the published-stable upgrade qualification lane in `docs/gateway/postgresql.md`. I installed the published `openclaw@2026.10.6` (`fe06181`) in an isolated npm global prefix, with `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` all set to one scratch directory. I onboarded it on SQLite and seeded the data listed below. I made a verified backup, then used the installed 10.6 updater to update to a package packed from `f5d7013`. The installed `dist/build-info.json` then reported commit `f5d701312d4f…` (`2026.10.6-f5d701312d4f-2026-10-23T19-21-41.310Z`). Both packages report version 2026.10.6, so I compared build identity instead. Next I ported to PostgreSQL 17.11 (scratch role and database `openclaw_ci`, DSN from a file SecretRef with `mode: "singleValue"`) and ran a foreground Gateway on loopback with token auth. No service was installed. The updater reported `service management skipped: non-default state dir or config path`. Data seeded on 10.6 before the upgrade: - **Agents:** `main` plus `ops`, with its own workspace and an identity name. - **Settings:** `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds=420`, `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault=low`, `session.dmScope=per-channel-peer`, and the gateway port/bind/auth. - **Memory:** `MEMORY.md` and a daily note in each workspace, indexed with `openclaw memory index --force`. - **Sessions:** one per agent, each created by a real Gateway turn. - **Automations:** two disabled cron jobs (an agent job and a command job), plus the two jobs the Gateway manages itself. Live provider turns were skipped because the local provider was unavailable. The sessions were created by real Gateway turns against a loopback stub OpenAI-compatible endpoint that returns a fixed reply. **Result: 10.6-created stores do not reproduce the refusal.** A fresh 10.6 install creates agent stores that already include every agent first-use column (`sqlite pragma table_info`, both before and after the upgrade migrated agent schema 25 → 31). In the shared-state store, `agent_deletion_journal.phase` is absent, but current main already treats that column as pending (#178230). `user_profile_identities` does not exist yet, so its column is not pending either. On this upgraded state, current main and this branch give the same port preflight result. So this run shows upgrade and data compatibility with the change. It does not show the refusal. The refusal evidence is the long-lived real install in **Real-data before/after** below, whose stores predate these columns. | Step | Build | Result | Time | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `npm install -g --prefix openclaw@2026.10.6` | published 10.6 `fe06181` | exit 0 | 12.5 s | | `onboard --non-interactive` (SQLite, loopback, token auth) | 10.6 | exit 0 | 2.7 s | | foreground `gateway run`, two agent turns, `cron add` ×2 | 10.6 | ready in 6.7 s. Both turns `terminalDisposition: visible`. Jobs created. | 0.4–3.0 s each | | `backup create --verify` | 10.6 | exit 0, `verified: true` | 1.8 s | | `update --tag --yes --no-restart --json` | 10.6 updater | exit 0, `status: succeeded`. The candidate doctor, doctor lint, gateway startup and post-update verification steps all completed. Build `fe06181` → `f5d7013`. | 216.2 s | | `database port --to postgres --dry-run` | main `93a374a` | exit 0: 3 stores, `1 stores need private migration` (state). SQLite checksums unchanged. | 8.2 s | | `database port --to postgres --dry-run` | branch `f5d7013` | exit 0: same 3 stores, `1 stores need private migration` | 7.4 s | | `database port --to postgres` | branch `f5d7013` | exit 0: `phase: complete`, `engine: postgres`. State plus 2 agent stores. 2 local-only stores stay on SQLite. | 20.5 s | | `doctor --lint --json` | branch `f5d7013` | state, `main` and `ops`: `observed: postgres`, schema 31/31, pending 0, no store issues. Exit 1 comes only from two config warnings: plaintext token/API key in the scratch config, and the legacy browser-relay auth default. | 8.5 s | | `memory status --agent main` | branch `f5d7013` | `Indexed: 0/3 files`, `index metadata is missing (metadata_missing)`. This is the documented rebuild after a port (#181859). | 2.6 s | | `memory index`, then `memory status` | branch `f5d7013` | main 3 files / 12 chunks and ops 2 files / 11 chunks, the same as the upgraded SQLite index before the port | 3.5 s + 2.7 s | | foreground `gateway run` on PostgreSQL, then `health --json` | branch `f5d7013` | ready in 11.3 s. `ok: true`. | 1.1 s | | `agent --session-key agent:main:proof-thread` (existing session) | branch `f5d7013` | exit 0. The same `sessionId` continues, and PostgreSQL `transcript_events` for `main` goes from 6 to 10. | 3.4 s |
Data-model compatibility: 10.6 data after upgrade and port ```text ## first-use columns (sqlite pragma table_info on the stores 10.6 created; same after the update) agent stores (main, ops): session_nodes.owner_actor_type/_id, owner_assigned_by_type/_id, owner_assigned_at, legacy_acp_migration_json, session_key_contract.canonical_ready: PRESENT state store: agent_deletion_journal.phase: absent | user_profile_identities: table absent | the other 17 state first-use columns: PRESENT schema: agent user_version 25 (10.6) -> 31 (after update); state 20 -> 31 ## listings, 10.6 (before update) vs f5d7013 on PostgreSQL (after port) agents list: equal [main (default, workspace), ops ("Ops Proof Agent", ws-ops)], model stubllm/stub-echo sessions --all-agents: equal agent:main:proof-thread 5e2965b1-…, agent:ops:ops-thread 80e73874-… (status done) cron list --all (Gateway on PostgreSQL): equal 4 jobs, same ids, names, enabled flags, schedules and agents memory search "blue heron ledger" (main) -> MEMORY.md:2 "PR181876 sentinel: the blue heron ledger lives in drawer seven." memory search "quartz lantern" (main) -> memory/2026-10-23.md memory search "copper kettle" (ops) -> MEMORY.md:2 "Ops sentinel: the copper kettle rotation runs every Thursday." workspace/memory markdown sha256: unchanged (11 files) ## settings: openclaw.json in the verified 10.6 backup vs after port timeoutSeconds 420, thinkingDefault low, session.dmScope per-channel-peer, ops identity name, default model, workspaces, gateway port/bind/auth mode/token: SAME added by port: database.engine; added by me before the port: database.postgres (file SecretRef, schemaPrefix), secrets.providers.pgdsn changed by the update's Doctor (already in the port's pre-port config capture): agents.defaults.heartbeat.agentId removed (it was the default, main); messages.queue.allowCollaborativeSteering=false added ## catalog: PostgreSQL (BEGIN READ ONLY) vs the port's SQLite original captures operation complete/ported; every target schema 31->31, ownerAdmitted true agent main/ops: all 7 first-use columns present in both; 13 non-empty canonical tables, row counts equal (session_nodes 1/1, transcript_events 6/6, session_windows 1/1, ...) state: agent_deletion_journal.phase original=absent postgres=present; original capture still lacks it 17 of 20 non-empty tables equal (cron_jobs 4/4, audit_events 4/4, update_runs 2/2, ...). The other three changed only after the port, through the post-port Doctor and memory runs: diagnostic_events 11/12, plugin_state_entries 8/14 (memory-core events and recall), agent_databases 2/4 (see note). ```
Note: after the port, the first `doctor` run added a second `agent_databases` row for each agent, keyed by the absolute store path, next to the ported relative-path rows. `agents list` and Doctor still show exactly two healthy agents. This PR does not change that code. I have not filed it separately. Logs: each step has its own log, and the first line of each log names the build. The run ended with the scratch PostgreSQL schemas dropped (only `public` remains) and no listener on the scratch Gateway or stub ports. **Focused tests.** Every new assertion fails on the merge base production code and passes on this branch: - `agent-port-descriptor.test.ts`, "completes absent first-use columns in the private current-schema copy". A schema-31 store missing `session_nodes.legacy_acp_migration_json` and `session_key_contract.canonical_ready` reports both as pending and passes layout inspection. An extra unknown column, or a missing non-first-use column (`session_nodes.project_id`), is still refused and is not reported as pending. The private copy is completed and the source bytes stay unchanged. Base result: `expected {} to deeply equal {…}`. - `agent-port.postgres.test.ts`, "ports lazy raw and compressed predicates and absent first-use columns through the verified command …". This drives `doctorDatabasePort` end to end on a store missing both agent columns. The PostgreSQL namespace has both columns, and the captured original still lacks them. Base result: `Unknown or missing columns in session_key_contract`. - `port-command.integration.test.ts`, "privately adds absent first-use columns when porting a current-schema shared state". This extends the case from #178230 with `worker_workspace_pending_results.repository_workspace_id` on a second table. The unrelated extra column is still refused, the PostgreSQL namespace has the column, and the original lacks it. Base result: `Unknown or missing columns in worker_workspace_pending_results`. **Per-file wall times (`--maxWorkers=1`).** `agent-port-descriptor.test.ts`: 16 s. `port-command.integration.test.ts` (SQLite lanes): 18 s. The extended PostgreSQL cases: 11.1 s (state, in `port-command.integration.test.ts`) and 4.2 s (agent, in `agent-port.postgres.test.ts`). **Commands (Node 24.22.1).** The PostgreSQL lanes ran against a dedicated scratch database (role and database `openclaw_ci`; extensions unaccent, pg_trgm, vector). - `pnpm test src/infra/database-engine/{agent-port-descriptor,agent-port,state-port,diagnostics,port-command.integration}.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 22 passed. The 17 skips are the PostgreSQL lanes, which ran next. - PostgreSQL conformance for `agent-port.postgres.test.ts`, `agent-opening-refusal.conformance.test.ts`, `port-command.integration.test.ts` and `state-port.postgres.test.ts`: 34 passed, 1 failed. I ran it as the `test-projects.mts` child of `scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs` with its conformance preload. The script's own `generate-postgres-schema --check-connection` preflight could not run because it executes `SET track_functions`, which this role is not granted. - The one failure is `reconnects after a committed PostgreSQL transaction loses its reply …` (`preflight: … observed database validation or I/O failure`). It fails the same way on the unmodified merge base `d75915ee883` against this database, so it comes from this environment and not from this change. - Exact-head CI: pending. - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.core.json `: 0 warnings, 0 errors. `pnpm format:check `: clean. - `pnpm tsgo:core` and `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.infra.json`: clean. - `pnpm build`: passed. **Real-data before/after (the refusal).** These stores come from a long-lived real install and predate the first-use columns, so this is the run that reproduces the refusal on main. The commands ran on a stopped-Gateway copy of a real install, restored from a verified `openclaw backup create` archive. The agent run used installed main `93a374a` before and branch head `e4442cd` after. `f5d7013` keeps that agent logic unchanged and only moves the pending check into the shared helper; the agent run was not repeated. The state run used main `93a374a` before and `f5d7013` after, and each `state-*` log records its build in its first line. Before the state run, the retained `fleet_cells` table was removed from the scratch copy because it blocks the state port separately (#181857). | Step | Build | Result | Time | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | agent port `--dry-run` | main 93a374a | exit 1: `Unknown or missing columns in session_nodes` (dev-go) | 17.5 s | | agent port `--dry-run` | branch e4442cd | exit 0: 11 stores need private migration | 35.7 s | | agent port | branch e4442cd | exit 0: `complete (postgres); 11 database stores` | 164.4 s | | state port `--dry-run` | main 93a374a | exit 1: `Unknown or missing columns in worker_workspace_pending_results` | 15.3 s | | state port `--dry-run` | branch f5d7013 | exit 0: 1 store needs private migration | 15.4 s | | state port | branch f5d7013 | exit 0: `complete (postgres); 1 database stores` | 40.1 s | | `doctor --lint --json` | branch f5d7013 | state and all 11 agent stores `observed: postgres`, schema 31/31, pending 0, no store issues (exit 1 only from two unrelated config warnings) | 24.1 s | | `memory status --agent dev-go` | branch e4442cd | exit 0. It reports missing index metadata, which is expected: the port omits rebuildable memory indexes and a reindex is required (#181859). | 4.6 s |
Read-only catalog checks (psql in BEGIN READ ONLY; SQLite opened read-only) ```text ## state: first-use columns present in PostgreSQL namespace agent_deletion_journal.phase user_profile_identities.verified_email_json worker_workspace_pending_results.repository_workspace_id ## state row counts: table sqlite_original postgres worker_workspace_pending_results 0 0 agent_deletion_journal 4 4 user_profile_identities 1 1 task_runs 1205 1205 subagent_runs 867 867 session_groups 2 2 cron_jobs 29 29 audit_events 99575 99575 ## state original capture columns agent_deletion_journal.phase present=0 user_profile_identities.verified_email_json present=0 worker_workspace_pending_results.repository_workspace_id present=0 ## agent: agent session_nodes_pg legacy_acp_col canonical_ready_col troubleshooter 83 1 1 dev-go 1 1 1 wb-review 13 1 1 wb-dev2 36 1 1 dev 652 1 1 main 504 1 1 wb-dev 52 1 1 researcher 42 1 1 wb-triage 10 1 1 dev-react 1 1 1 wiki-maint 11 1 1 ## agent original.sqlite captures: session_nodes_rows legacy_acp_col 1 0 | 1 0 | 652 0 | 504 0 | 42 0 | 83 0 | 52 0 | 36 0 | 13 0 | 10 0 | 11 0 ```
Simplification pass (pr-simplify) - **Defect:** the ports treat first-use columns as missing even though the schema owners allow them to be absent. **Invariant:** such a column is valid when absent and is completed only in the port's private copy. **Smallest fix:** one shared check reports absent first-use columns from each family's existing list, and each family's existing private-copy migration adds them. - **Removed or reused:** The hard-coded `agent_deletion_journal.phase` inspection and migration branch (added by #178005, reported as pending since #178230) is gone. The state port now uses the existing state first-use list and the existing `ensureFirstUseAdditiveStateColumnsForStrictMigration` owner, whose comment now names the port as a second caller. The agent port uses the existing agent first-use list. The one new helper is the shared pending check that replaces the per-family logic. No new export beyond it, no new module, no new option. - **Not moved into schema ensure:** startup and Doctor still leave first-use columns absent. - **Tests:** each case has a named failure: refused current store, widened pending set, uncompleted copy, or modified source. The PostgreSQL cases extend the existing owner suites instead of adding new scaffolding. - **Delta vs merge base:** production +51/−22, tests +94/−4.
Independent review (autoreview) `autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P2` with the Claude engine (Codex CLI is not available on this host), on head `f5d7013`: scoped-clean, "patch is correct (0.72)", no P0–P2 findings.
Out of scope, filed separately: the shared-state refusal caused by the retained `fleet_cells` table (#181857), and port-created PostgreSQL schemas named `port_` instead of using `schemaPrefix` (#181858).

prs.title: fix: resume stopped conversations with terminal recovery residue
prs.body:
Fixes #181770

## What Problem This Solves

A stopped conversation with leftover, fully terminal restart-recovery records can accept a new message and then fail to start the reply. Refreshing the conversation does not remove those records.

## User Impact

The next message can continue the same conversation, preserving its session ID, transcript, and model override. Existing stuck rows in this state recover at dispatch without a reset.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pre-admission reconciliation selected failed or running rows but skipped killed rows. Once a new chat input added its own delivery claim, the existing terminal-only cleanup no longer recognized the old records as settled. Include proven-terminal residue in the existing recovery owner's reconciliation candidates before accepting new input. Live owners, unfinished fences, reservations, and pending delivery keep their existing protections.

Thanks @najef1979-code for reporting the stuck-conversation behavior.

## Evidence

- Real isolated Gateway and fake OpenAI-compatible Responses provider: stream a reply, Stop, resume the same session, seed killed/abortedLastRun=false with terminal recovery records from an older generation, and send two further turns. The assertions preserve the old transcript and session ID and require actual provider requests and successful agent.wait outcomes.
- On base c99f01afc757, the terminal-residue variant stalled before the provider and agent.wait timed out after 30 seconds (61.29 seconds test time, 98.09 seconds wrapper wall time). Ordinary Stop/resume and a killed row alone were healthy. The reporter's original triggering transition and full stored recovery metadata are unavailable; the regression seeds this specific stale-state variant through the session owner.
- Node 26.12.1: all 175 tests in the affected Gateway regression and nine direct importer files pass (4 shards, 256.60 seconds wrapper wall). The Gateway regression took 27.656 seconds of test time.
- Pinned Bun fork: the same real Gateway regression passes (10.846 seconds test time, 21.27 seconds Vitest duration, 24.65 seconds wrapper wall).
- Production tsgo, all 29 selected test-type graphs, targeted oxlint and oxfmt, git diff --check, and madge (0 cycles) pass.
- Independent Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2; no actionable findings.
- Full check:changed was not run under the campaign's local gate budget for the slow SQLite inventory. The targeted checks above ran directly; PR CI supplies broad proof.

Production: +4/-2 lines. Tests: +48/-1 lines. Docs: +3 lines. No schema, dependency, or configuration changes.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and validation commands</summary>

All runtime commands used isolated HOME, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, and TMPDIR beneath this worktree's .artifacts directory.

```sh
export HOME="$PWD/.artifacts/home"
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$PWD/.artifacts/state"
export TMPDIR="$PWD/.artifacts/tmp"
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/gateway/server.chat-first-turn-binding.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/restart-recovery-claim.lifecycle.test.ts \
  src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-recovery-store.test.ts \
  src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-recovery-state.terminal-residue.test.ts \
```

Fixes #181875
Supersedes #181876

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes database port refusing valid upgraded agent and shared-state stores whose feature-owned first-use columns are still absent.

## User Impact

Operators can inspect these stores and prepare complete private port copies without exercising each feature first. Existing rows gain NULL values for the absent nullable columns; the original SQLite bytes remain unchanged. Unknown extra columns still refuse the port. Thanks @etzelm for the report and first-use contract analysis.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both family descriptors now consume their schema owner's canonical first-use definitions. One shared inspection helper identifies pending columns, the agent's existing private migration completes its definitions, and the state port reuses the existing state completion owner. This removes the state port's independent phase-only policy while preserving normal lazy admission and strict copy verification.

This is an independently implemented replacement: #181876 was read only as a diff reference; its fork was neither checked out nor executed. Mitchell Etzel is credited in the commit.

Stacked on #181882, currently unmerged, at `210c200b86aa16734cc04b4b48656c371435f780`. This PR targets its branch so the diff contains only this repair; it can target main after #181882 lands. The task delta against that base is production +48/-26 (net +22), tests +66/-0, docs +4/-0. The simplify pass retained the existing migration callbacks and descriptor fingerprints and removed the special-case phase handling.

## Evidence

- Node 26.12.1, `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`: both new command-worker regressions failed before the production fix on the original #181882 base (2 failed; 4.08 s test time, 47.87 s wrapper wall). They now pass, exercising agent and state inspection, private preparation, retained rows with NULL first-use values, verification, unchanged original bytes, and rejection of unknown extra columns.
- Final focused run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/database-engine/port-command.test.ts src/infra/database-engine/port-command.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed: 22 tests passed, 17 PostgreSQL cases skipped; 70.30 s Vitest / 74.21 s wrapper wall. This includes native custody, capture/rollback, and the adjacent retained-table behavior.
- All 27 directly importing / one-barrel consumer files were selected in repository order on Node. The regular configurations passed 189 tests and skipped 69 PostgreSQL/opt-in cases. Their invocation ended with a selection error for the live-only consumer because its ordinary config excludes live files; running that file through `test/vitest/vitest.live.config.ts` collected it correctly and skipped its 7 existing opt-in provider stress cases. No assertion failures. Regular invocation: 192.48 s wall; dedicated live config: 49.74 s Vitest, dominated by preparation. No test exceeded 30 s.
- Unmocked live command-handler proof on isolated, populated schema-31 stores: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .artifacts/l1873/live-port.ts` invoked `doctorDatabasePort({ family, to: 'sqlite', dryRun: true })` for agent and state. Both exited successfully at preflight, found their registered store, and reported `1 stores need private migration; copy and privilege probe not performed`. No Gateway was stopped, restarted, or used.
- Core and infra-test tsgo, changed-file oxlint, oxfmt, docs inventory, `git diff --check`, and Madge (0 cycles) passed. The full `check:changed` SQLite inventory was omitted under the campaign's local gate budget.

That build failure is outside this diff; dependencies and guards were left intact. The unmocked command-handler run above proves offline inventory and inspection, while the Node worker regressions prove private completion and retained rows. A latest-stable installation upgrade was not run.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Transcript history workers retain provider transport and schema-compiler modules while formatting already-recorded messages. Three shared-barrel imports bring those modules into each affected isolate even though the worker needs only the fallback text and overflow/TLS classifiers.

## Change and User Impact

Import the existing canonical leaves at all three entry edges. History output and error classification remain unchanged; no cache, configuration, schema, protocol, or public API change. Production LOC: **−2** (4 additions, 6 deletions); regression test: +5 lines.

The heap snapshots show the removed functions retained through `ModuleLoader → LoadCache → ModuleJob → SourceTextModule`. Provider stream/request helpers disappear from the candidate snapshot, and loaded script count falls **1,856 → 1,692**. This addresses unused module retention, not the entire transcript-worker working set; no duplicated-data or cache-lifecycle change is claimed.

## Evidence

Two concurrent pairs, then swapped interleaved CPU placement, under the shared quiet lock and production guard. Compiled workers on Node 26.12.1; separate synthetic 5,000-session/6,000-run databases; 128 warmup requests and 16,000 measured requests per side (4,000 history + 12,000 stats across 32 active sessions). No production state or Gateway was modified. Builds share base `3483558acbfd`; the three candidate production files match this PR head exactly. No TypeScript loader runs in the measured worker.

Separate heap-snapshot diagnostics: **40,227,296 → 39,039,064 bytes**, a **1.13 MiB / 2.95%** reduction per warmed isolate. The two paired warmed heaps average **40,238,948 → 39,057,652 bytes (−2.94%)**. After measured work and idle settling, heap averages **55,316,432 → 53,975,292 bytes (−2.43%)**.

Baseline → candidate; timing values in milliseconds:

| Metric | Pair 1 | Pair 2 | Mean paired change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Worker total GC per 16,000 requests | 148.054 → 146.484 | 155.750 → 142.314 | −4.84%; −7.503 ms |
| Whole-process promotion, bytes | 135,325,680 → 134,107,480 | 136,928,544 → 135,250,416 | −1.06%; −1,448,164 bytes |
| Worker CPU | 4,548.450 → 4,476.105 | 4,898.081 → 4,889.482 | −0.88% |
| History p99, n=4,000 each side | 1.670239 → 1.675547 | 1.824340 → 1.831100 | +0.34%; +0.006034 ms |
| Stats p99, n=12,000 each side | 0.323666 → 0.306380 | 0.322464 → 0.311979 | −4.30%; −0.013886 ms |
| Loop p99, n=32,215→32,137 / 32,162→32,193 | 1.952767 → 1.944575 | 2.107391 → 2.129919 | Inconclusive: −0.008192 ms (−0.42%) / +0.022528 ms (+1.07%) |
| Mixed-request p99, n=16,000 each side | 1.273262 → 1.217148 | 1.357949 → 1.471540 | Inconclusive: −0.056114 ms (−4.41%) / +0.113591 ms (+8.36%) |
| Maximum worker GC pause | 2.363 → 2.209 | 2.487 → 2.530 | Both below 50 ms max-pause gate |

Minor GC counts are 151→150 / 153→152; major counts are 27→27 in both pairs. Minor p95/p99 and major GC are context-only under the sample-count rules; all their absolute paired-mean pause shifts are below 1 ms. No eligible metric crosses the v5 adverse thresholds. Opposite-signed loop and mixed-request tails are inconclusive under v5.2, not evidence of either improvement or regression; they do not trigger a third pair. This is a small memory reduction and net simplification with neutral request performance, not a large latency win.

Promotion covers all process isolates, including the controller. The initial parser did not recognize Node's JSON GC trace format; totals above were recomputed from the original measured-window logs. Cross-fixture hashes differ only in generation/source identifiers and mutation timestamps. Captured baseline/candidate responses on the same fixture are byte-identical; replaying each fixture's 128-response cycle reproduces every 16,000-request measurement digest exactly. All cross-fixture differences were checked against those four specific metadata fields, including decoded cursor contents.

## Validation and Limits

- Cold-import regression fails on the old imports because display projection loads provider stream parsing. Focused cold-import, classification, and context-overflow tests: **28 passed**.
- Changed-file oxfmt/oxlint and `pnpm tsgo:core` passed. No broad local suite or Testbox allocation.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep exec approval followup observation deadline on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the post-approval exec followup observation window grows past its configured bound when the system wall clock steps backward during observation, so a turn whose followup run is accepted but unreachable keeps retrying `agent.wait` for the length of the step instead of ending observation at its deadline.

## User Impact

User impact: after a human approves an exec tool call, the followup observation window always ends after `AGENT_FOLLOWUP_OBSERVATION_TIMEOUT_MS` of real elapsed time, regardless of NTP corrections or VM/laptop resume. A turn whose accepted followup run cannot be reached stops observing at its bound instead of hanging on to a wall-clock-inflated window, and no direct-delivery race is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

`waitForAgentFollowupRun` seeds `observationDeadline` with `Date.now()` and computes `remainingMs` and the transport-retry `retryDelayMs` against the wall clock, while the budget is actually consumed by gateway round-trips and `sleepWithAbort` on the monotonic clock. A backward wall-clock step inflates every remaining-budget computation by the step length, so the loop keeps observing `6m + step` instead of `6m`; a forward step can end it early.

The deadline now lives entirely on `performance.now()` — seed, loop-top remaining check, and retry-delay clamp — which is monotonic and unaffected by wall-clock adjustments. This is the same cross-clock-domain pattern already fixed for command process-group teardown in #174151 and the orphaned-process reap grace deadline in #181335; the exec approval followup observation window is the sibling site left on the wall clock. Node 16+ exposes a global `performance`, so no import is required.

The pre-existing deadline test drove the deadline by mocking `Date.now`; it now advances monotonic time with fake timers, preserving its original assertion that the deadline ends observation without competing direct delivery.

No parser, policy branch, configuration surface, or gateway protocol change; behavior on a clock that never steps is identical.

## Evidence

**Pre-fix RED** — stock main (`97d96e53d22f`), regression test only. Fake timers advance monotonic time 6m10s while `vi.setSystemTime` rewinds the wall clock 1h mid-observation (same two-clock separation as #181335/#174151); the observation loop is still pending after its entire budget:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-approval-followup.test.ts -t rewinds
 × exec approval followup > ends observation at its monotonic deadline when the wall clock rewinds  420ms
   → expected 'still-pending' to be 'settled'
      Tests  1 failed | 17 skipped (18)
```

**Post-fix GREEN** — same test with the fix settles inside the window, and the full affected file passes through the agents-core vitest project:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-approval-followup.test.ts
 ✓ ends observation at its monotonic deadline when the wall clock rewinds
      Tests  18 passed (18)
```

**Behavior matrix** (accepted followup run, gateway unreachable, wall clock rewound 1h mid-observation):

```text
clock during observation       => observation ends            => result
normal (no step)                => after 6m budget            => bounded
wall rewind 1h (pre-fix)        => after 6m + 1h (retries on) => inflated by step
wall rewind 1h (post-fix)       => after 6m budget            => bounded
```

Also verified: `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm lint`, and `pnpm tsgo:core` typecheck pass on the changed tree. Regression test drives the real `sendExecApprovalFollowup` → `waitForAgentFollowupRun` path with only the gateway transport mocked (the same boundary the existing suite mocks); the local bundled-gateway proof path is not runnable on this Windows contributor box and was not used as evidence.

prs.title: fix(subagents): parent turns never settle after an inline child reply
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a parent's turn never fully settles when it waits inline on a `sessions_send` reply from its own native child and that child's run ends during the wait.

## User Impact

User impact: parents that talk to their own children through `sessions_send` no longer leave the child run stuck as an unfinished descendant, so later turns, descendant-settlement waits, and run cleanup complete normally. There is no configuration or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a child run ends while the requester's inline wait still claims it, cleanup is deferred to that claim. Acknowledging the inline result then marked the result delivered and retired the requester obligation without re-entering cleanup, so the run never got `cleanupCompletedAt`. The acknowledgement now resumes the run after its write commits when the run has already ended, the same step completion delivery already takes after committing its own publication.

## Evidence

- **Regression:** the existing "consumes an inline child follow-up result" case now ends the child while the parent waits inline and asserts `cleanupCompletedAt` is set and the requester has no pending descendants. It fails without the fix (`cleanupCompletedAt` is `undefined`) and passes with it (30/30 in the file).
- **Real behavior (AWS Crabbox, real Gateway, `openai/gpt-5.4`):** this defect was found while proving #181117, whose opt-in live test hung in descendant settlement right after an inline child reply ([failed run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_9f3292124f7a)). The same live test with this commit applied on the #181117 head passed every phase in 82 s, exit 0 ([run_4eec342e5810](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_4eec342e5810)). The touched files are identical on `main` and that head.
- **Focused suites on this branch:** child coordination, `sessions-send-followup`, `agent-step`, `sessions-send-owner-continuation`, and Gateway `agent.followup-owner` pass. `tsconfig.core.json` and the agents-root test typecheck pass.
- **Review:** independent autoreview of the branch is scoped-clean through P1.
- The test file was at its line cap, so one existing reply helper moved into the shared test-support module; no lint or line-limit gate was relaxed.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions-send-child-coordination.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-send-followup.test.ts src/agents/tools/agent-step.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-send-owner-continuation.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.followup-owner.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

</details>

prs.title: perf(sessions): reuse checkout facts in uncommitted diffs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reviewing uncommitted changes repeats checkout discovery and untracked-file enumeration when a session started with pre-existing edits.

## User Impact

The same filtered diff requires less Git work. Four concurrent `sessions.diff` WebSocket pairs with a populated baseline used **12 subprocesses instead of 15**, with identical response hashes. Paired main-thread CPU fell **8.1%** and sampled allocation fell **8.1%**. Handler mean rose **2.8% (+3.88 ms)** and handler p99 was unchanged in the CPU passes: this is a resource/work reduction, not a latency win. This applies to fresh uncommitted diffs whose paths overlap the session baseline; unchanged cache hits and all-changes diffs are not the target.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the already resolved checkout and bounded untracked paths into baseline filtering. Keep the default branch-relative tracked comparison: a branch-added file is modified relative to HEAD but added relative to the baseline base, including when Review uses an accepted managed base. Raw fingerprints, file limits, hardlink/containment checks, and authorization remain intact. There is no new cache or stored-shape change.

Production delta: **23 additions / 16 deletions, net +7 lines**. The extra arguments preserve the existing contract between initial baseline capture (which needs an independent inventory) and display filtering (which already has one), while deleting three subprocess launches per affected recomputation.

## Evidence

- Focused baseline-file and Gateway diff tests: **42 passed** on the rebased head; 54.47 seconds including compilation. The expanded preservation test also passed on the original implementation. It covers pre-session branch-added and untracked edits, both with and without an explicit review base.
- Changed-file format/lint and targeted `tsgo:core` passed before the patch-identical rebase; PR CI owns broad validation on the current head.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): scoped clean, no actionable P2-or-higher findings.
- Functional RPC fixture: 5,000 sessions, 6,000 settled runs, a managed linked worktree with 5,000 unchanged files, 32 tracked changes, 32 untracked files, and 32 captured baseline paths. Actual Git trace2 starts establish 15 → 12 subprocesses; response SHA-256 matches. Single-request smoke timings are not performance evidence.

**Acceptance passed on the exact PR source.** Four completed pairs (two CPU, two allocation), 1,000 RPCs per side each, passed the declared v5/v5.1/v5.2/v5.3 rules. No guard interruption and no eligible metric requiring a third pair. The benchmark now seeds dirty baselines, invalidates freshness with identical-byte writes, substitutes baseline/candidate source symmetrically inside Git workers, verifies worker-load receipts, counts actual subprocesses, and starts CPU/profile capture after a warmed start barrier.


### CPU pairs

Each pair used 1,000 RPCs and 1,000 handler samples per side. Placements were concurrent interleaved 16-CPU sets, swapped for pair 2. Both pairs returned the same response SHA-256 (`cd1d1218347c9e52b891b50848dbbff1a626b464a6857e8968704c562e2864d0`) and measured exactly 15 versus 12 Git starts per RPC.

| Metric | Pair 1 baseline → candidate | Pair 2 baseline → candidate | Mean paired delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Handler mean | 139.369 → 142.508 ms | 141.607 → 146.220 ms | +3.877 ms / +2.76% |
| Handler p95 (n=1,000/side/pair) | 149.502 → 152.574 ms | 157.694 → 160.766 ms | +3.072 ms / +2.00% |
| Handler p99 (n=1,000/side/pair) | 158.718 → 158.718 ms | 169.982 → 169.982 ms | 0 ms / 0% |
| RPC mean | 140.069 → 143.203 ms | 142.369 → 146.921 ms | +3.843 ms / +2.72% |
| RPC p99 (n=1,000/side/pair) | 159.247 → 158.960 ms | 170.496 → 170.294 ms | −0.244 ms / −0.15% |
| Main-thread CPU / RPC | 14.615 → 13.376 ms | 15.339 → 14.160 ms | −1.209 ms / −8.08% |
| Process CPU / RPC | 45.635 → 43.881 ms | 46.417 → 44.321 ms | −1.925 ms / −4.18% |
| Total GC / RPC | 0.609 → 0.537 ms | 0.594 → 0.513 ms | −0.077 ms / −12.76% |
| Event-loop p99 | 21.266 → 21.201 ms (n=7,013/7,164) | 21.250 → 21.250 ms (n=7,119/7,348) | −0.033 ms / −0.15% |

These are work/CPU/GC savings, **not a latency win**. The small handler-mean increase is below the agreed adverse thresholds; handler p99 is unchanged. No eligible CPU-pass metric has opposite-sign deltas or baselines over 5× apart, so no third CPU pair was required.


### Allocation pairs

Separate profiling passes used the same fixture, 1,000 RPCs per side per pair, and swapped placements. Allocation and promotion figures cover the Gateway main isolate; worker allocation is not included. CPU numbers above are from the separate CPU passes.

| Metric | Pair 1 baseline → candidate | Pair 2 baseline → candidate | Mean paired delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Allocated bytes / RPC | 4,467,773 → 4,093,666 | 4,464,401 → 4,116,008 | −361,250 / −8.09% |
| Promoted bytes / RPC | 487,408 → 436,060 | 480,782 → 432,287 | −49,922 / −10.31% |
| Total GC / RPC | 0.680 → 0.631 ms | 0.641 → 0.517 ms | −0.086 ms / −13.26% |
| Handler mean | 156.035 → 159.633 ms | 138.397 → 141.900 ms | +3.551 ms / +2.42% |
| Handler p95 (n=1,000/side/pair) | 208.894 → 210.942 ms | 150.526 → 151.550 ms | +1.536 ms / +0.83% |
| Handler p99 (n=1,000/side/pair) | 239.614 → 233.470 ms | 157.694 → 157.694 ms | −3.072 ms / −1.28% |
| Event-loop p99 | 21.152 → 21.119 ms (n=7,833/8,008) | 21.561 → 21.119 ms (n=6,949/7,122) | −0.238 ms / −1.10% |

No eligible metric in either pass had opposite-sign deltas or baseline values over 5× apart. No mean reached 20% adverse and no eligible metric was at least 10% adverse in both pairs. Resource reductions were consistent across placements; latency is neutral under the agreed acceptance thresholds.

<details>
<summary>GC counts, tails, and maximum-pause gate</summary>

All values below are baseline → candidate. GC pause tails are context: minor counts are below 200 per side, major counts are below 50, and minor-pause paired absolute mean shifts are below 1 ms. The sparse major-GC p95/p99 increase in allocation pair 1 is reported rather than treated as a regression gate. Every maximum pause is below max(50 ms, twice that pair's baseline maximum).

| Pass / pair | Total collections | Maximum pause (ms) | Minor n | Minor p95 / p99 (ms) | Major n | Major p95 / p99 (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | --- |
| cpu 1 | 192 → 176 | 21.931 → 24.439 | 184 → 168 | 3.294/4.014 → 3.406/3.966 | 4 → 4 | 22.014/22.014 → 24.446/24.446 |
| cpu 2 | 188 → 172 | 21.251 → 22.918 | 180 → 165 | 3.566/4.126 → 3.182/3.486 | 4 → 3 | 21.374/21.374 → 23.038/23.038 |
| allocations 1 | 193 → 200 | 16.916 → 46.579 | 181 → 188 | 4.158/4.766 → 3.646/3.966 | 6 → 6 | 17.022/17.022 → 46.590/46.590 |
| allocations 2 | 194 → 174 | 15.729 → 17.418 | 180 → 166 | 3.646/4.158 → 3.278/3.742 | 7 → 4 | 15.742/15.742 → 17.534/17.534 |

</details>

### Reproduction and proof

The existing performance driver runs an isolated Gateway from `src/entry.ts`, with synthetic state and a real managed worktree. Baseline is the parent implementation at `a8aee07e3870`; candidate is `88aff11c225c`. Both use the same rebased source/dependencies, symmetric source substitution, and recorded Git-worker load receipts. Each pair holds the shared quiet slot, runs both sides concurrently on interleaved 16-CPU sets, then swaps placements. External CPU activity was recorded for context. The shared production guard passed every run; production state was untouched.

```text
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/history-diff-measure.ts 
  --state-dir <synthetic-state> --entry src/entry.ts 
  --scenario diff-uncommitted-full --mutate --clients 1 --operations 1000 
  --rounds 1 --warmup-cohorts 2 --start-file <barrier> 
  --diff-source <baseline-or-candidate-source> --port <loopback-port> 
  --output <artifact-directory> [--allocations]
```

All eight sides completed successfully. A runner cleanup error occurred after the first CPU pair had written complete reports and both sides exited 0; it was repaired before resuming the campaign. No measured pair was guard-interrupted or discarded. The unchanged all-changes path is covered by focused Gateway tests; no separate all-changes performance campaign was run.

[Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40020203708): **33 passing jobs, no failures**. The 42 focused tests passed again after rebase; changed-file lint/format and the targeted core typecheck passed. GitHub code review and ClawSweeper found no introduced code defect; ClawSweeper's pending request was completion of these measurements.

Scope: this removes redundant work on fresh uncommitted diffs with overlapping pre-session baseline paths. It does not establish an improvement for every production `sessions.diff` request, cache hits, or other diff scopes, and it does not claim a production deployment.

<details>
<summary>Paired measurement acceptance rule</summary>

Use concurrent baseline/candidate processes with separate synthetic state and loopback ports under one exclusive quiet slot and the shared production guard. Swap interleaved 16-CPU placements for the second pair. Collect 1,000 RPCs per side, handler latency, subprocesses, main-thread/process CPU per call, allocated bytes, total GC time and promotion per call, and event-loop tails. Compare response hashes.

Decide on paired means: reject an adverse mean of at least 20%, or at least 10% adverse in both pairs. Opposite-signed deltas or baselines over 5× apart are inconclusive; report absolute deltas and obtain a third pair for gating metrics. p95 requires 200 samples per side; p99 requires 1,000. Major GC tails are context below 50 collections. GC pause-percentile paired absolute mean changes below 1 ms are context, as are increased pause percentiles when collection count falls at least 20% without increased total GC time. Report both maximum pauses; the candidate exceeding max(50 ms, twice the baseline maximum) retains its gate. Discard guard-interrupted pairs.

</details>

prs.title: feat(skills): review background learning as drafts with Skill Workshop propose mode
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161057#issuecomment-6361144325

## What Problem This Solves

Since #161057, background learning either changes skills on its own (`auto`) or does nothing (`off`). Users who reviewed proposals before they applied lost that workflow, and Doctor silently switched their `propose` config to `off`.

## User Impact

User impact: set `skills.workshop.autonomous.mode` to `"propose"` (or pick **Propose** in the Control UI) and background reviews save drafts instead of changing skills. `/learn drafts` reviews all waiting drafts together, saves the good parts as normal versioned and undoable changes, and discards the rest.

- Configs that still say `mode: "propose"` keep working; Doctor no longer rewrites them to `"off"`. Legacy `autonomous.enabled: true` now maps to `"propose"` instead of `"off"`.
- Proposals that Doctor already exported to `workshop-skills/.archive/.retired-proposals/` move into `workshop-skills/.drafts/` on the next Doctor run, so `/learn drafts` finds them. New exports go straight to `.drafts/`.
- Users already migrated to `"off"` must opt in again; Doctor cannot tell them apart from users who chose `"off"`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Drafts are plain directories (`.drafts/<id>/SKILL.md` plus an optional `.reason`), in the same shape Doctor already exported. There is no SQLite table, status, approval flow or rollback. The review stays one change per run; in `propose` mode the `skill_workshop` tool refuses its live writes and takes `action=draft` instead. Judging drafts happens in one foreground `/learn drafts` turn, where the model can compare them globally. Up to 50 drafts wait per agent; past that, reviews save nothing new. Drafts are not announced, and unused-skill cleanup stays `auto`-only.

**Protocol change (needs an owner decision):** `skills.workshop.list` result `mode` gains the literal `"propose"`. Only the bundled Control UI and the CLI read it; the CLI prints the string and the Control UI reads the mode from config, so an older peer degrades to showing `propose` as text. No native app consumes it.

**Update behavior:** Doctor's existing Skill Workshop final step now also renames earlier exports into `.drafts/` (never overwriting an existing draft, skipped in update rehearsals). A failure there throws like any other filesystem error in that step; nothing is deleted.

## Evidence

- UI before/after screenshots (mock Control UI): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181747#issuecomment-6369430306
- `src/agents/tools/skill-workshop-tool.test.ts`: in `propose` mode a review's `patch` is refused, `draft` saves, the live skill and change feed stay unchanged, the review cannot discard; a foreground run lists, views and discards the draft. An aborted run cannot discard a draft: `discard` rechecks caller authority right before deletion (this case fails without the fix).
- `src/commands/doctor-skill-workshop-retire-proposals.test.ts`: exports land in `.drafts/`; earlier `.retired-proposals/` exports move there without overwriting.
- `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.skills.test.ts`: `propose` is kept; `enabled: true` → `propose`.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-learn.test.ts`, `src/skills/workshop/experience-review-scheduler.test.ts`, `ui/src/pages/skill-workshop/skill-workshop-page.test.tsx`: `/learn drafts` rewrite, reviews still queue in `propose`, the UI switch writes `mode: "propose"`.
- Focused runs of those files plus `experience-review.test.ts` pass locally; changed-file oxlint and `ui:i18n:verify` pass. Other UI locales get the three new strings from the post-merge locale refresh.
- Not run locally: full typecheck and broad suites (hosted CI), and a live background review with a real model.

<details><summary>Simplify pass</summary>

- Removed: the `propose -> off` config migration (the value is valid again), the draft read-back after save, and a nested parameter branch in the tool.
- Kept on purpose: the `.reason` file (the `/learn drafts` turn has no source conversation, so the reason is its only evidence), the 50-draft cap (bounds an unread inbox), the symlink boundary check on `.drafts/`, and the Doctor move of earlier exports (already-upgraded users would otherwise never see them).
- Whole-change delta against `origin/main`: production +361/-73 (including the new `drafts.ts`, about 170 lines), tests +78/-25, docs +85/-46. The growth is the new mode; no new owner, table or config key.

</details>
