prs.title: fix: model setup loses authorization while sign-in continues
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes model setup failing with “Gateway caller authority is no longer active” when sign-in, verification, or activation continues after the initiating request returns.

## User Impact

Setup retains its original authorization across asynchronous work and reconnects without changing saved credentials or working model defaults. Early revocation cases rejected the original grant before provider or activation effects. After an originally authorized configuration write had persisted, the observed late-revocation path transiently applied the candidate, then restored the original configuration and active credential through compensation; zero transient visibility is not established. Cancellation remains effective; connection-bound provider login keeps its existing disconnect behavior. No config, credential-format, dependency, schema, or protocol migration is introduced.

**Deployment qualification remains open:** native/live-provider and real install-over acceptance, current-head PR CI and applicable owner review, then an independent security audit of the final immutable deployment artifact. This PR is not deployment clearance; the final audit must remain last before deployment.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture the original operator through the existing continuation owner before acknowledging setup, and run the wizard in that retained scope. Keep caller-specific checks, forward the source assertion into actual inference-probe admission, and release custody after runner settlement, including deferred recovery. Retry admission still checks the new caller before cancelling an earlier attempt.

## Evidence

### Production-path authority evidence (2026-10-23)

The following runs exercised the real token-authenticated Gateway setup RPC, wizard, activation, embedded inference execution, HTTP/SSE transport, credential/configuration owners, and production config-reload watcher. Activation, authority, execution, stores, and application claim/settlement were not mocked. The provider and exec-secret backend were owned deterministic local services with synthetic credentials: this is production-path evidence, **not live OpenAI/ChatGPT/native-provider qualification**.

Source binding: published head b5eb9861ef59f99f23f781baad16f5c263ac28d8; complete working candidate tree 06c63c96530ad45be99a543c6cfa2ccf4e6e01a4; eight feature-file hashes unchanged. Official Node 26.12.1 and integrity-pinned pnpm 12.15.0 were used. Normal frozen install and required canonical source runtime build exited 0 with dependency-policy inputs unchanged. The source build retains the original-base build stamp (42c0d5a…, version 2026.10.5), not a fabricated clean published-head stamp; source/tree equivalence was verified separately. This is not upgrade qualification.

| Scenario | Observed production-boundary outcome |
|---|---|
| Allowed completion after reconnect | Start response returned, original socket closed, replacement client authenticated, real HTTP POST/SSE completed; the inactive saved credential became active/static and the new primary/profile binding persisted. |
| Original-device revocation before effects | Revoked through public device.token.revoke at the natural API-key prompt. Cumulative provider requests stayed 1→1; config hash, primary and existing credential summaries were unchanged. Wizard rejected the original continuation authority. |
| Revocation while provider response was held | A genuine second HTTP response was held after authorized inactive staging. Revoked the original device, then released the response. Wizard rejected completion; original config/active credential remained unchanged and the attempted replacement stayed inactive. |
| Allowed deferred application | The actual config watcher hot-reloaded and accepted the revision. Wizard completed; public configRevisionHash equaled appliedConfigHash and the credential was active/static. No synthetic application claimant/settler was used. |
| Revocation after application claim | A same-action exec-secret control succeeded first. A real exec-secret resolution then held candidate application after persistence and watcher preparation. Revoking the original device and releasing the resolver produced an authority error and real compensating recovery: original raw config hash, primary, applied/persisted revision and active credential were restored; the attempted credential remained inactive. |

**Important late-window limitation:** the candidate hot reload occurred after revocation and before compensation restored the original state. This is evidence of recovery, **not proof of zero transient application or prevention of every post-revocation effect**. No concurrent inference was attempted during that transient window. Review is still needed on whether this commit/recovery behavior is sufficient or whether runtime publication must recheck the original grant before exposing the candidate. This packet does not claim security clearance.

<details>
<summary>Redacted late-window trace and reproducible observation method</summary>

P1 and P4 are display aliases for observed synthetic profiles; they were not seeded expected state.

~~~text
16:09:07.537 UTC  Real watcher evaluates candidate P1 (after application.prepare in source order).
16:09:07.596      Actual exec-secret request #5 held; candidate primary already persisted.
16:09:07.606      Public config.get: persisted revision != applied revision.
16:09:07.607      Public wizard.status: running.
16:09:07.616      Public device.token.revoke receipt for the original operator device.
                 Owned resolver response released.
16:09:07.654      Candidate hot reload applied.
16:09:07.657      Candidate source revision accepted.
16:09:07.759      Watcher evaluates compensating configuration.
16:09:07.882      Actual exec-secret request sees restored original primary P4.
16:09:07.917      Recovery hot reload applied.
16:09:07.923      Recovery source revision accepted.
16:09:07.933      Wizard error: Gateway continuation authority is no longer active.
16:09:07.971      Owner reads: original config/primary restored, P4 static, P1 inactive.
16:09:08.338      Owned Gateway closed with SIGTERM; both owned HTTP servers closed.
~~~

The matched candidate-specific watcher log occurs after await application.prepare in the unchanged config-reload owner. Its managed-write listener synchronously claims the attached application receipt. The held request came from real secrets/runtime preparation, corroborated by public pending-revision and running-wizard reads. No public claimed=true field or fake application status was invented.

~~~ts
// Redacted excerpts of executed production-facing requests.
c.request("openclaw.setup.activate.start", {
  sessionId, kind: "api-key", authChoice: "openai-api-key",
  apiKey: "[synthetic-value-redacted]",
  modelRef: "openai/gpt-5.4-mini", nativeSessionCatalogsEnabled: false,
});
await control.client.request("device.token.revoke", {
  deviceId: original.identity.deviceId, role: "operator",
});
await control.client.request("config.get", {});
await control.client.request("models.authStatus", { agentId: "main" });
~~~

The barrier used the documented exec-secret provider with an owned resolver, trusted executable directory, normal path/mode checks and unchanged default timeout. All runs used isolated HOME/state/config/workspaces and per-client credential stores. The late run explicitly scoped logging.file inside its private run directory. Earlier runs used the default temporary log destination; that logging-isolation limit is retained, and no outside-workspace log was read or deleted for cleanup. Exact command receipts and hashes remain in the linked implementation session. Matrix, dedicated application, and the combined same-action exec-secret control/late-negative command exited 0. Owned Gateway/provider/secret-backend processes were stopped and checked absent.

Evidence integrity: production-results.json SHA-256 81f1d759446231c1b0495ab66095a0ef5f3a20e8a073cb30c353239dc5ebcfdb; redacted late observations SHA-256 89aa33a3daea6876799446e55d17b0430f5a0544015d995388aea32260431059; parent-readable proof SHA-256 aea49b6e23e134fc1dd40471480a2eb8af79aaee9331c0ce019009c7aefedb8a. These are trace identities, not a substitute for the observations above.

</details>

Earlier test and baseline-install evidence follows; it is not relabeled as new-head CI or live qualification.

- The real authenticated Gateway reproduction fails on the original base with the reported error. The six-scenario regression passes start-response, reconnect, sign-in and revocation-before/after-capture cases; later authentication cannot revive the original revoked grant.
- Focused unit, Gateway, activation/credential-preservation, remote-CLI and browser cases passed on the original-base implementation. Browser evidence includes a real browser/HTTPS Gateway flow and cancelled/stale callback rejection. External identity/model responses remain fixtures, not live-account qualification.
- The eight-file implementation was independently reviewed on base `42c0d5a8f9d00e113c48090c3d259977e67b5b5a`, candidate tree `06c63c96530ad45be99a543c6cfa2ccf4e6e01a4`: scoped-clean, no P0–P2 findings. The helper reported source-context limitations across its evidence batches; the reviewer did not independently rerun tests. This is bounded code review, not the final security audit.
- Separately, the byte-identical eight feature files passed 199 tests, focused type/lint/format checks and a full canonical source build after integration onto base `7d31fe01b636c6b7bf2e3a4cb362658f4b52e5b0`. That separate candidate is supporting integration evidence, not full-tree/current-head CI for this published original-base branch.
- The new real-Gateway regression shares one server across six scenarios because helper-only tests missed the request-completion/reconnect boundary. Retained latest run: 21.1 seconds test time; about 137 seconds command wall time including cold preparation. CI timing is not yet available.
- Released 2026.10.6 was installed in an isolated prefix and its published build identity/lifecycle verified. Real working-state install-over remains unrun. Local packaging stopped at the unchanged dependency-age policy; no package archive or global policy change resulted.

Reported by Sedrak Hovhannisyan. Publication requested by Ayaan.

## Worked on by

- @Sedrak-Hovhannisyan

prs.title: fix: exclude zero-scale hidden text from web fetch
prs.body:
Closes #105438.

## What Problem This Solves

`web_fetch` includes text hidden by inline zero-axis CSS transforms such as `scale(0,0)`, `scale3d(0,0,0)`, and `scaleX(0)`. That violates its existing hidden-content cleanup behavior and can feed text into an agent that is not visible on the page.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing visibility sanitizer's transform check to recognize valid zero X/Y scales, validating function arity and numeric arguments first. Keep the existing offscreen-translation behavior. A zero Z axis alone, nonzero scales, and malformed transforms remain visible. No fetch permission, provider, dependency, configuration default, or SDK surface change.

## User Impact

Basic HTML cleanup and bundled Readability extraction omit zero-X/Y-scale content in both markdown and text modes while retaining visible article text and controls. JavaScript is still not executed.

## Evidence

Built and installed separate current-main and candidate Linux packages in secretless Docker. Created fresh profiles/config/session state through shipped commands and public Gateway RPC. Served a local HTTP article with unique hidden/visible markers and admitted only its exact host through `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy.allowedHostnames`.

Invoked the real `web_fetch` tool through the authenticated built Gateway's `POST /tools/invoke`, twice in markdown and text modes for each extraction path: basic HTML fallback with the bundled extractor disabled, and bundled Readability enabled. Captured the full HTTP tool responses and their native `extractor` metadata (`raw-html` / `readability`); no private helper invocation or DNS/mock override.

[Inspectable captured Gateway HTTP responses](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181785#issuecomment-6374774774) include the complete `result.details` objects for main/candidate, both extractors, and both modes. The duplicate content rendering is omitted and the synthetic fixture address is redacted; the extracted text and marker outcomes are retained.

Main reproduces in all eight invocations: all six zero-X/Y hidden markers leak into extracted output, while all eight visible controls remain present. Cases cover two-axis/3D scales, X/Y functions, signed zero, zero percentages, and exponent zero. Visible controls cover scale(1), nonzero scales, Z-only zero, malformed values, and invalid arity.

Candidate passes all eight invocations: zero hidden markers returned, all eight visible controls preserved, HTTP 200 throughout. Both `raw-html` and `readability` metadata confirm the intended extraction paths. All 92 focused tests pass; the two real-tool zero-scale regressions fail on main. Focused Oxfmt/Oxlint checks pass.

Simplification keeps one visibility owner and removes an unnecessary axis-array copy. Existing unit cases cover valid/invalid numeric and arity boundaries, and real-tool tests cover both output modes.

Whole-change delta: production +29/-1, tests +42/-0, docs +4/-0. The small production growth replaces the scalar-only transform test with validated X/Y-axis handling; no parallel extraction path or persistent state is added.

Merge danger: two-way door; reverting restores the former extraction behavior without migrating stored state. Blast radius is HTML text extraction for content carrying inline scale transforms; fetch authorization and provider selection are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(tts): accept model as an alias for modelId in ElevenLabs provider config
prs.body:
Closes #161914

## What Problem This Solves

Older TTS docs and examples configured the ElevenLabs provider with a `model` key, but synthesis reads only `modelId`. A `model`-only config was silently ignored and the default `eleven_multilingual_v2` was used on the wire — confirmed against the published `openclaw@2026.10.3` package in the upgrade proof below.

## Approach: Doctor migration, not a runtime alias

An earlier revision of this PR added a runtime `model` fallback. Review pointed out (per `VISION.md`/`AGENTS.md` policy) that long-lived runtime aliases are rejected and legacy config repair belongs in the owning plugin's Doctor contract. This revision implements that:

- `migrateElevenLabsModelConfig` (in `config-compat.ts`) moves `model` → `modelId` across root, per-agent, persona, channel/account, and Talk provider blocks. An existing `modelId` wins and the obsolete `model` key is removed; non-string/empty values are dropped with an actionable change report. Idempotent.

issues.title: web_search (ddgs): ambiguous failures look like empty results

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### Bug Description

With the default search provider (DuckDuckGo, no API key), consecutive web_search calls in the same turn fail with an error that reads like an empty result set:
  Error: DuckDuckGo search failed (No results found.)

The original report observed that spacing the same distinct queries correlated with recovery. Follow-up diagnostics on the original host observed an explicit Mojeek HTTP 403 refusal, then intentionally stopped the remaining requests. These observations do not establish that every `No results found` exception is rate limiting, or that retry/backoff is the root-cause fix. ddgs can hide upstream refusal, empty parsing and aggregation failures behind that generic exception. The agreed nanobot-side resolution is to report search unavailability and uncertainty honestly, rather than interpret the exception as a completed search with zero matches.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Keep the default provider (tools.web.search.provider = "duckduckgo", empty api_key), no proxy.
2. In one turn, issue several distinct web_search calls with no pause between them (a normal multi-query research turn does this).
3. Observe that a subset of the calls fail with the "No results found" error; repeating the same queries with a pause succeeds.

Isolated library repro (no nanobot involved), same host:
  from ddgs import DDGS
  qs = ["capa galaxy a12 preco", "fone bluetooth barato", "notebook i5 usado", "cadeira gamer preco",
        "tenis corrida promocao", "panela eletrica preco", "mochila escolar", "lampada led preco"]
  d = DDGS(timeout=15)
  # no pause -> 0/8 results, all DDGSException: No results found
  # 3 s pause between queries -> 8/8 results

### Agreed acceptance criteria

- Return ambiguous ddgs failures as tool errors that explicitly say no usable search result was obtained and the cause is unknown. Do not present them as confirmed zero matches or infer rate limiting from `No results found`.
- Distinguish the tool's waiting deadline from a timeout reported by ddgs.
- Preserve successful result formatting, the configured network route, cancellation and existing diagnostic privacy behavior.
- Verify through a normal public entrypoint with a real model: live search succeeds and uses returned sources; controlled refusal and timeout cases report the failed lookup without claiming that matching pages do not exist or inventing sources.

### Outside this issue

- Removing upstream rate limits, IP restrictions or anti-automation blocks.
- Adding automatic retry, backoff or pacing configuration. These are not required for this issue's resolution.
- Recovering HTTP refusal/rate-limit facts already discarded by ddgs. Upstream error preservation and any later nanobot integration are separate follow-up work. Related upstream report: https://github.com/deedy5/ddgs/issues/478.

### Resolution

PR #6409 resolves the agreed nanobot-side scope when merged. This scope supersedes the original retry-based proposal; the original reproduction steps, measurements and environment are retained in this issue as reported evidence, not proof that every failure has the same cause.

### Relevant Logs

```shell
Two calls issued in the same second, then the failure (Telegram turn, 17/10/2026):
2026-10-17 21:32:33 | INFO  | - | Tool call: web_search({"query": "REDACTED_QUERY", "count": 8})
2026-10-17 21:32:33 | INFO  | - | Tool call: web_search({"query": "REDACTED_QUERY", "count": 8})
2026-10-17 21:32:44 | INFO  | - | Tool call: web_search({"count": 6, "query": "REDACTED_QUERY"})
2026-10-17 21:32:50 | WARNING | - | DuckDuckGo search failed: No results found.
2026-10-17 21:32:54 | INFO  | - | Tool call: web_search({"count": 6, "query": "REDACTED_QUERY"})
2026-10-17 21:33:40 | WARNING | - | DuckDuckGo search failed: No results found.
2026-10-17 21:33:51 | WARNING | - | DuckDuckGo search failed: No results found.

Additional measurements
- 8 distinct queries with no pause: 0/8 returned results (all DDGSException: No results found).
- The same 8 queries with a 3 s pause: 8/8 succeeded.
- The host recovers after idling, and a second host on a different IP served results while the first was failing — transient and rate/IP dependent, not a permanent block.
- exclusive=True only keeps DuckDuckGo out of the parallel batch; it does not pace calls, so consecutive searches still go out immediately.
- The per-turn guard in utils/runtime.py (_MAX_REPEAT_EXTERNAL_LOOKUPS = 2) only blocks repeating the same query or URL, so it does not help with distinct queries.
- ddgs 9.16.0 itself has no retry/backoff (checked its sources).
- Checked todays `main`: _search_duckduckgo is unchanged there.
```

### nanobot Version

0.3.5

### Python Version

3.14.4

### Operating System

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, aarch64 (Oracle Cloud VM, kernel 7.0.0-1013-oracle)

### Channel / Platform

Telegram (headless, systemd service)

### LLM Provider

opencode

### Model

deepseek-v4.1-flash

### Browser

N/A — headless VPS, no browser involved

### Connection

Direct outbound HTTPS from the host, no proxy (tools.web.proxy unset), datacenter IP

### Configuration (Optional)

```yaml

```

### Additional Context

_No response_

issues.title: DeepSeek Responses: full-history reasoning replay uses output_text instead of documented reasoning_text
issues.body:
## Problem

Checked HKUDS/nanobot main at `0254bf121736bf02bbcd9e988a2c1b3fc265f8d9` against the current DeepSeek documentation.

DeepSeek's [Responses API reference](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/api/create-response) documents `reasoning` input items with `content` blocks of type `reasoning_text`. nanobot's full-history conversion instead serializes assistant `reasoning_content` as `output_text` inside a `reasoning` item:

```json
{"type":"reasoning","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"think first"}]}
```

This is a request-schema mismatch on the built-in DeepSeek Responses path, not a request to implement an optional API feature.

## Reproduction (no API request)

```python
from nanobot.providers.openai_compat_provider import OpenAICompatProvider
from nanobot.providers.registry import find_by_name

provider = OpenAICompatProvider(
    default_model="deepseek-flash",
    spec=find_by_name("deepseek"),
)
assert provider._should_use_responses_api("deepseek-flash", None)
body = provider._build_responses_body(
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "hi"},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": "hello", "reasoning_content": "think first"},
        {"role": "user", "content": "next"},
    ],
    tools=None,
    model="deepseek-flash",
    max_tokens=8192,
    temperature=0.7,
    reasoning_effort="high",
    tool_choice=None,
)
print(next(item for item in body["input"] if item.get("type") == "reasoning"))
```

Actual output is the JSON shown above. The documented shape uses `"type": "reasoning_text"` for that content block.

## Reachability and evidence

- [nanobot/providers/registry.py:631–673](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/0254bf121736bf02bbcd9e988a2c1b3fc265f8d9/nanobot/providers/registry.py#L631-L673): built-in DeepSeek declares Responses support and plaintext reasoning replay, including `deepseek-flash` on the official endpoint.
- [nanobot/providers/openai_compat_provider.py:1250–1257](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/0254bf121736bf02bbcd9e988a2c1b3fc265f8d9/nanobot/providers/openai_compat_provider.py#L1250-L1257): enables plaintext reasoning preservation for this request.
- [nanobot/providers/openai_responses/state.py:55–64](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/0254bf121736bf02bbcd9e988a2c1b3fc265f8d9/nanobot/providers/openai_responses/state.py#L55-L64): uses the full-history converter when opaque Responses state is absent or incompatible.
- [nanobot/providers/openai_responses/converters.py:41–48](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/0254bf121736bf02bbcd9e988a2c1b3fc265f8d9/nanobot/providers/openai_responses/converters.py#L41-L48): emits `output_text` for the reasoning block.

## Impact and limits

When nanobot reconstructs a Responses request from Chat-format history containing assistant reasoning, the replayed reasoning is not encoded with DeepSeek's documented reasoning content type. This affects the full-history/fallback conversion path; it does not establish that exact replay of prior raw Responses output items is broken.

The actual request builder was exercised locally. No live/paid API request was made, so whether DeepSeek rejects, ignores, or tolerates the undocumented block type is **not verified**. This report is specifically about the reproducible schema conflict, not a confirmed production 400 or confirmed reasoning loss.

Could you align plaintext reasoning conversion with the documented `reasoning_text` shape and update the corresponding DeepSeek request-body regression tests?

issues.title: Idle compaction can archive a session whose turn is still running through the direct entry point
issues.body:
I think the idle-compaction guard misses turns that arrive through process_direct, and I reproduced it on Linux with Python 3.12 against main at cdb6210.

_check_expired_sessions_if_due passes active_session_keys=self._pending_queues.keys() and check_expired skips those keys, but the only writer of _pending_queues is _enqueue_session_message, the bus path. process_direct never registers there; that is what the API server, the SDK and single-shot CLI use.

The scan reads updated_at from the session jsonl metadata line, and during a direct turn it stays frozen at turn start, because runtime checkpoints go to the sidecar via save_runtime_checkpoint and the main jsonl is not rewritten until the turn ends. The freeze held with and without tool calls.

So a direct turn outliving the idle threshold looks idle. With sessionTtlMinutes at its default of 15, a longer turn gets archival scheduled while still running, and I then watched compact_idle_session commit a summary checkpoint (last_archived 0 to 3) that the live turn's final save overwrites (back to 0, summary gone). No messages are lost, but the compaction is wasted.

Repro: an AgentLoop whose chat_stream_with_retry blocks, process_direct, then while it blocks confirm loop._pending_queues is empty and the metadata updated_at is unchanged seconds later, shrink auto_compact._ttl, and call check_expired with active_session_keys=loop._pending_queues.keys() (one archive scheduled).

Uncertainty boundary: I did not run the documented two-service setup end to end, so how the gateway and API service share a sessions directory is unverified. I compressed the TTL to seconds instead of 15 minutes, so only wall clock is simulated, and in the archive-discarded step I stubbed the summarizer while the reload, the checkpoint commit and both saves are real. Whether the fix belongs in the active set or elsewhere is only a suggestion.

If this is known, or a second guard exists that I missed, point me at it.

issues.title: Idle compaction can run immediately after a long direct turn without a fresh idle interval
issues.body:
## Problem

An idle-compaction candidate can be selected while a long `process_direct()` turn is running, then execute immediately after that turn completes without a fresh idle interval.

The original concurrent transcript/checkpoint overwrite reported in #6214 is resolved by merged PR #6221: scheduled idle archives and turns share the per-session lock, so summary generation and persistence wait for the running turn to finish. This follow-up tracks only the remaining idle-eligibility problem.

## Current behavior

1. Idle compaction is enabled, with a 15-minute threshold for example. A persistent direct turn starts and continues for 20 minutes while the same AgentLoop also runs its idle scanner.
2. The scanner only excludes `_pending_queues`, which does not include direct calls. The persisted activity timestamp makes this session appear expired, so an idle archive is scheduled.
3. The archive waits for the session lock held by the active turn.
4. The turn completes and saves its new reply and activity timestamp.
5. The queued archive obtains the lock and immediately summarizes the session without rechecking its updated idle eligibility.

The archive is serialized correctly, but it runs before the session has actually been idle for the configured interval. A subsequent same-session request can also wait behind that summary operation if the archive obtains the lock first.

## Reachability and user impact

The direct call and idle scanner must coexist in the same runtime. The retained built-in path is a gateway heartbeat task running longer than the idle threshold. Heartbeat uses its own internal `heartbeat` session; its idle compaction does not compact the user's conversation or send a compaction notice to that conversation. No ordinary-chat user-visible regression has been established from this path.

Normal WebUI, TUI and channel messages use the bus and already have pending-queue activity exclusion. Stock single-shot CLI, standalone `nanobot serve`, and ordinary SDK calls do not start the idle scanner themselves. A custom integration running direct business-session calls together with the scanner can expose premature context summarization to that session's next request.

This issue does not establish a cross-process shared-storage failure, message loss, or increased total model-call volume.

## Verification so far

A controlled probe used a real isolated AgentLoop and SQLite session owner, a persistent direct turn, stubbed model/summary responses, and an advanced idle-scanner clock. An archive was scheduled during the blocked turn, summary generation remained blocked until the turn finished, and then one summary was generated immediately. Both the completed reply and summary remained persisted. The probe is not a real-provider or live-user deployment test.

The probe used main at `06f3981962ccfa37e9d8edda583cad4b651a6054`; the affected runtime, session and entrypoint paths are unchanged at audited main `d045285ced7c9d15ba7b7a346d70fb2394988d26`. PR #6221's merge commit is an ancestor of that main snapshot.

## Expected behavior / acceptance criteria

- An idle archive delayed by an active turn must use the session's latest settled activity when deciding whether it is still eligible. It must not summarize immediately after a fresh turn merely because its pre-wait timestamp was expired.
- After the session really remains idle for the full configured interval, automatic compaction still runs normally.
- Preserve serialization between compaction and turns, completed replies and summaries, and independent progress on other session keys.
- Keep explicit/manual and context-pressure compaction behavior unchanged. Cross-process activity coordination is outside this follow-up.
- Cover the delayed-archive/fresh-activity ordering and later genuine-idle behavior with a controlled clock and deterministic task coordination, without relying on long sleeps.

Related proposals: #6215, #6230, #6405. Their changes should be evaluated against this remaining scope rather than the already-fixed overwrite race.

issues.title: Allow agents to observe group messages without always replying

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: priority: p2
labels.description: Normal backlog: minor bug, enhancement, docs, cleanup, edge case, or unvalidated proposal.

issues.body:
### Problem / Motivation

In group chats, there is an important distinction between:

1. receiving/observing a message,
2. deciding whether the message is relevant to the agent,
3. processing it with the main agent,
4. deciding whether a response should actually be sent.

Today, group message handling is mainly based on whether a bot should be triggered by a message at all, for example through mention-based or open group handling.

For multi-agent group chats this is limiting.

Example:

A Telegram group contains several specialized agents:

- a calendar / personal assistant
- a project management agent
- an information/archive agent

A user writes:

> I will be on vacation next Thursday.

This information may be useful context for multiple agents, but only one of them may have something useful to say.

Ideally:

- the calendar agent may handle the message and respond
- the project management agent may observe it as useful context but remain silent
- the archive agent may ignore it entirely

Without such a distinction, users either have to explicitly mention every relevant bot or allow multiple bots to respond to messages where they have nothing useful to contribute.

This becomes especially noisy in groups with multiple agents.

### Proposed Solution

Introduce an optional contribution policy for incoming group messages that separates message observation from response delivery.

Conceptually, an incoming message could pass through the following stages:

```text
Incoming group message
        |
        v
Contribution decision
        |
        +--> IGNORE
        |
        +--> OBSERVE / CONTEXT_ONLY
        |
        +--> HANDLE
                 |
                 v
             Main agent
                 |
                 v
          Delivery decision
                 |
          +------+------+
          |             |
       SUPPRESS       DELIVER
```
The exact API/configuration is open for discussion, but an opt-in policy could conceptually look like:
```json
{
  "channels": {
    "telegram": {
      "groupPolicy": "open",
      "contributionPolicy": "relevant"
    }
  }
```
The important behavior would be:
- IGNORE: do not invoke the main agent
- OBSERVE / CONTEXT_ONLY: retain the message as conversation context without generating a response
- HANDLE: invoke the normal agent
- after agent execution, optionally allow the resulting response to be suppressed instead of requiring every successful agent run to produce a user-visible message
The contribution and delivery decisions could use a lightweight configurable evaluator rather than the agent's main model.
Explicit mentions should probably bypass the contribution gate and continue to trigger the addressed agent directly.
Existing group behavior should remain unchanged unless the new policy is explicitly enabled.

### Alternatives Considered

### Mention-only group handling

This avoids unwanted responses, but the bot does not get useful context from messages where it was not explicitly mentioned.

It also requires the user to know in advance which agent may need a piece of information.

### Open group handling

This gives agents access to the whole conversation, but can cause every agent to react to every message.

In a multi-agent group this quickly becomes noisy and can also cause unnecessary LLM calls.

### Prompt the main agent to return something like `NO_REPLY`

This could suppress some responses, but the expensive main agent has already been invoked.

It also makes "no user-visible response" a special text convention instead of an explicit runtime behavior.

### Only add a post-run delivery evaluator

This would solve unwanted responses, but would not avoid unnecessary main-agent invocations for clearly irrelevant messages.

A pre-run contribution decision and a post-run delivery decision solve different problems and could therefore be useful independently.

### Related Component

Channel (WeChat, Feishu, Telegram, etc.)

### Additional Context

A similar separation already exists conceptually in the heartbeat flow:

- work is performed internally
- the resulting response is evaluated
- only relevant results are delivered to the user

The proposed group-chat behavior could reuse or generalize this idea, while additionally introducing a lightweight pre-run contribution decision to avoid unnecessary main-agent executions.

This would be particularly useful for groups containing multiple specialized bots, where all agents can share conversational context but should only speak when they have something relevant to contribute.

The evaluator implementation should not necessarily depend on a specific model or provider. A configurable model preset, deterministic policy, or another lightweight decision mechanism could be supported by the underlying abstraction.

prs.title: fix(agent): keep idle scans away from in-flight direct turns
prs.body:
## Summary
- Idle scans only excluded sessions that had a `_pending_queues` entry, but `process_direct` (used by the API server, SDK, and single-shot CLI) installs no queue, so a long direct turn looked idle once it outlived `sessionTtlMinutes`
- The scheduled `compact_idle_session` then committed a summary checkpoint mid-turn that the live turn's final save overwrote (`last_archived` reverting), wasting the compaction — exactly as diagnosed in #6214
- Register in-flight direct turns in a refcounted active set (`_direct_turns`) consulted alongside `_pending_queues` in `_check_expired_sessions_if_due`, so direct turns are skipped until they finish; concurrent direct calls and lock-waiting turns are covered by counting before the session lock is awaited

## Test plan

prs.title: Refactor: Replace `message_id` with generic `metadata` in tool contexts
prs.body:
## 描述
本 PR 重构了从 `AgentLoop` 向底层工具（`MessageTool`、`CronTool`、`SpawnTool`）传递消息上下文的方式。

之前，代码仅显式提取了 `message_id` 并传递给工具。当我们需要特定平台的其他扩展信息或路由配置时，这种硬编码的方式极大地限制了扩展性。本次更新改为传递完整的 `metadata` 字典，确保各个工具（尤其是 `MessageTool`）能够获取到输入消息的所有上下文信息。

## 主要更改
* **`agent/loop.py`**: 更新了 `_set_tool_context` 方法，现在接收并传递 `metadata: dict`，而不是特定的 `message_id`。
* **`agent/tools/message.py`**: 
  * 更新了 `__init__` 和 `set_context` 方法，使用 `metadata` 替代了 `default_message_id` 参数。
  * 现在构建 `OutboundMessage` 时会附带完整的 `metadata`，保留了所有的原始上下文（其中自然也包含了原本的 `message_id`，并且为未来支持诸如 thread ID、UI 状态等扩展留出了空间）。
* **`agent/tools/cron.py` & `agent/tools/spawn.py`**: 更新了 `set_context` 方法的签名，增加了 `**kwargs` 参数以对齐新的通用接口，提升了代码的向前兼容性。

## 影响范围
* **扩展性提升**: 未来如果需要在消息的元数据中增加任何新字段，它们都会自动流转到各个工具和发出的消息中，无需再频繁修改 `AgentLoop` 的方法签名。
* **非破坏性更新**: 原有的 `message_id` 依然会被成功传递，因为它现在被完整保留在了 `metadata` 字典内。原有功能不受影响。

---

## Description
This PR refactors how message context is passed from the `AgentLoop` to the underlying tools (`MessageTool`, `CronTool`, `SpawnTool`). 

Previously, only `message_id` was explicitly extracted from the incoming message and passed to the tools. This limits extensibility when other platform-specific metadata or routing information is required. This update passes the entire `metadata` dictionary, ensuring that tools (especially `MessageTool`) have access to all context from the incoming message.

## Key Changes
* **`agent/loop.py`**: Updated `_set_tool_context` to accept and pass `metadata: dict` instead of a specific `message_id`.
* **`agent/tools/message.py`**: 
  * Updated `__init__` and `set_context` to manage `metadata` instead of `default_message_id`.
  * Now attaches the full `metadata` payload to the `OutboundMessage`, preserving all original context (which naturally includes `message_id` but allows for future additions like thread IDs, UI states, etc.).
* **`agent/tools/cron.py` & `agent/tools/spawn.py`**: Updated the `set_context` method signatures to accept `**kwargs`, aligning with the new generic interface and improving forward compatibility.

## Impact
* **Extensibility**: Any new fields added to a message's metadata will now automatically flow through to the tools and outbound messages without requiring changes to the `AgentLoop` signature.
* **Non-breaking**: The `message_id` is still successfully propagated because it is preserved inside the `metadata` dict.

prs.title: fix(agent): recheck idle eligibility after the session-lock wait so a queued archive cannot summarize a freshly active session (#6410)
prs.body:
## Summary

- `AutoCompact.check_expired` decides idle eligibility from the persisted `updated_at` it reads during the scan, then schedules `_archive` in the background. The archive queues behind the per-session lock — which a long `process_direct()` turn can hold well past the TTL — and then summarizes unconditionally, using a decision made from the pre-wait timestamp (#6410).
- `check_expired` now passes the timestamp it observed (`scanned_updated_at`) to `_archive`. Once the archive holds the session lock, it re-reads the session: if settled activity advanced past the scan's observation and the session is not idle-expired by that latest activity, the archive skips. The session becomes eligible again only after a full idle interval, when a later scan archives it normally.
- If activity advanced but the session is *still* idle-expired by its latest timestamp (e.g. the archive itself was delayed), compaction proceeds — the recheck compares settled activity, not lock timing.
- Explicit archival is unchanged: direct `_archive` calls pass no scan observation and are not TTL-gated (the contract `test_session_can_be_compacted_again_after_new_messages` documents), and manual/context-pressure compaction through `Consolidator.compact_idle_session` (slash command, SDK) never goes through `_archive`.

Fixes #6410.

## Root cause

Eligibility was computed once, at scan time, from `list_sessions()` metadata, but the decision was consumed later, after an unbounded wait on the session lock. Nothing re-validated it against the session's latest settled `updated_at`, which a turn commits when it finishes. PR #6221 serialized the archive against turns (no more overwrite race), and #6405 proposes excluding in-flight direct turns at scan time; neither re-decides eligibility for an archive that was already queued when the turn settled — the remaining scope #6410 tracks. This change composes with both: whatever schedules the archive, the decision is re-made under the lock from settled state.

## Test plan

- [x] New `TestArchiveRechecksEligibility` in `tests/agent/test_autocompact_unit.py` — deterministic lock coordination, no sleeps: an archive queued behind a held session lock skips when the "turn" settles fresh activity first, and still compacts when no activity arrives. The skip test fails on unpatched code (`compact_idle_session` awaited once); the guard test accompanies the new `scanned_updated_at` parameter.
- [x] `tests/agent/test_compaction_serialization.py`, `scheduled_idle` parameter: now asserts the #6410 outcome end-to-end through the SDK facade — the queued archive produces no summary after the turn settles, the reply is preserved, and a later genuine-idle scan archives the session with the settled reply included (fails on unpatched code). The schedule helper gained an `exclude` option because the follow-up scan would otherwise also schedule the `sdk:other` session. `TestCheckExpired::test_runtime_is_captured_before_background_starts` restores the idle timestamp after `_add_turns` (adding messages bumps `updated_at`; the recheck reads the settled value).
- [x] Full suites: `tests/agent` — 1984 passed; `tests/test_nanobot_facade.py` — 69 passed; `tests/command/test_compact_command.py` — 20 passed. The recheck + serialization tests pass 5/5 repeat runs.
- [x] `ruff check` on all changed files — clean. No `ruff format` (per AGENTS.md).

## Notes for reviewers

- `_activity_advanced` treats an unparseable/missing timestamp as "cannot prove advancement", mirroring `_is_expired`'s tolerance for raw persisted metadata: the scan's decision then stands rather than the archive crashing or silently never running.
- No behavior change when the archive is not delayed: with no settled activity after the scan, the timestamps are equal and compaction proceeds exactly as before (covered by the existing suites, unchanged).

prs.title: fix(agent): budget oversized tool-result delta after compaction so large read_file rounds no longer abort the turn
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #5879: a tool round of large `read_file` results can abort the turn even when history summarization succeeds. `read_file` is exempt from the ingest-time tool-result budget (deliberately — the exemption prevents persist→read→persist loops, #4155), so its results enter the post-acceptance delta unbounded. Compaction preserves the delta unchanged, so when the delta alone exceeds the input budget, `ensure_request_fits` raises `ContextWindowExceededError` after a successful summary and the turn ends `started -> failed`.

## Change (`nanobot/agent/context_governance.py`)

- In `_compact_request_history`, if the post-compaction request still doesn't fit, the delta's tool results are admitted under the standard budget on the model-facing copy as a last resort, and the fit check runs again. The context guard is unchanged: a request that still doesn't fit after budgeting is refused exactly as before.
- The budgeting reuses the existing machinery — `apply_tool_result_budget` / `normalize_tool_result` gain an `include_exempt` flag that lifts the offload exemption for this pass only. With a workspace, oversized results are persisted in full and replaced by the usual reference + preview, so the model can read the persisted result back in slices; the raw transcript is never modified. The ingest-time exemption itself is untouched, so the #4155 loop cannot return.

## Tests

Two regression tests in `tests/agent/test_runner_governance.py`, using the issue's scenario (three 80,000-char `read_file` results, `max_tool_result_chars=16000`, byte-fallback estimator forced for determinism):

- `test_oversized_read_file_delta_is_budgeted_after_summarization` — compaction emits `started -> succeeded`, the prepared tool results are shrunk, and the raw transcript keeps its full contents. Fails on the unpatched code with the issue's exact error (`240507/190784 via heuristic`).
- `test_oversized_delta_still_rejected_when_budgeted_delta_cannot_fit` — 30 oversized reads still raise `ContextWindowExceededError` after budgeting, locking the guard in place.

## Verification

- The issue's own reproduction probe: unpatched aborts with `ContextWindowExceededError` and `['started', 'failed']`; patched completes with `['started', 'succeeded']`.
- Repo test suite: full `tests/agent` run passes — 1980 tests (1978 pre-existing + the 2 new ones); the pre-existing oversized-delta refusal tests pass unchanged.
- `ruff check` clean on both changed files.

prs.title: fix(agent): recheck idle expiry after acquiring session lock
prs.body:
This PR fixes [issue #6410](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/issues/6410).

An idle archive can be selected during a long persistent direct turn, wait for the session lock, then summarize immediately after that turn saves its reply. Reload the persisted session header after acquiring the existing lock and recheck the full idle interval before compacting. A freshly settled turn defers the archive; a genuinely idle session still compacts normally. Explicit/manual and context-pressure compaction routes stay unchanged.

This addresses the remaining idle-eligibility issue, not the transcript-overwrite race from #6214 already fixed by #6221. It complements the scan-time activity exclusions proposed in #6215, #6230 and #6405, and also covers the ordering where an archive was already queued before the direct turn began, which scan-time exclusion cannot prevent. The stock retained path is a long gateway heartbeat; custom integrations combining persistent direct calls with the scanner can also reach it. This does not establish ordinary-chat message loss, cross-process coordination or extra total model-call volume.

Tests use deterministic clocks and task coordination with real session storage and stubbed provider responses. Existing direct idle-archive fixtures now explicitly satisfy their idle precondition. The scheduled SDK test now expects deferral after a fresh reply, as requested by #6410, then checks a later idle summary and restart persistence. Its later target-specific scan excludes `sdk:other` through the existing active-key argument only as a test-scope exclusion; that is not a claim of a real concurrent turn. Actual independent progress on that key is checked earlier. The idle command fixture enables its private TTL before backdating activity; the manual command and explicit SDK assertions remain unchanged.

Validation at `3c022ada6ac6`, Docker Linux amd64 / Python 3.12.12, offline with core dependencies:

- The two new regression cases and the changed scheduled SDK expectation fail at their intended assertions on unmodified production code and pass with the fix. The four changed test modules otherwise pass on base (124 passed, 3 intended failures), in both plugin modes.
- Wider scope: `tests/agent`, `tests/session` and all 25 compaction-related test modules. Isolated plugins: 951 passed, 1 baseline-common failure, 5 skipped. Default plugins: 2,559 passed, 1 baseline-common failure, 5 skipped. No introduced or changed failures.
- Full configured Python Ruff scopes pass on base and candidate.
- Full configured strict basedpyright analyzed 444 files on each tree: 1,599 identical errors, including 58 missing-import errors, with no candidate-only diagnostics and none in `autocompact.py`. **This check did not pass** in the core-only environment; optional/channel dependencies were not recreated. Tests are excluded by the upstream type-check configuration.

The common failing dream test exits at `git config --file` in the container; its cause is not verified. Five native update tests require uv 0.11.16 and were skipped. Tests beyond the stated scope, all optional/channel dependency combinations, real-provider calls and upstream CI have not been run locally. This is not a full CI pass.

prs.title: refactor(webui): replace idle polling with gateway invalidations
prs.body:
Related: [NAN-339](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-339)

## Why

Keeping WebUI tabs open repeatedly reads unchanged pairing requests, channel status, automations, usage, and remote connections. Let the gateway notify clients when those resources may have changed, so idle tabs avoid unnecessary snapshot requests while changes still refresh the existing authoritative HTTP snapshots.

## Changes

- Deliver invalidations on the existing trusted WebSocket. Notifications contain only fixed resource names; remote-directory notifications remain local-only. The gateway owns filesystem watches, expiration deadlines, committed usage observation, channel-runtime sampling, and shared remote-health sampling.
- Use one event-driven refresh lifecycle for six consumers: pairing, Channels, global automations, session automations, Overview usage, and the remote-instance directory. Subscribe before the first snapshot, serialize/coalesce reads, reconcile after foreground return and reconnect, abort old lifetimes, ignore stale results, and bound transient retries.
- Follow the paired-release product contract: WebUI and its corresponding Gateway are used together. Remove this PR's old-host polling fallback, optional state-event capability, dynamic polling parameters, browser-side duplicate health debounce, and compatibility-only fixtures. Existing core protocol and authorization mechanisms are outside this narrowing.
- Preserve pairing countdowns despite client/server clock skew; use the grouping timezone in the usage snapshot rather than a potentially older settings snapshot. Cached remote health prevents extra tabs or directory reads from multiplying probes. Profile changes retain loaded frames/drafts, and a restarted remote requires explicit reconnect before identity replacement.
- Handle supported native-watch interruptions and SQLite connection replacement. Recognize known automation data-directory signals for a newly published first record, while excluding lock/staging-file activity to avoid refresh loops. WebSocket tests wait for the actual listener rather than guessing startup delay.
- Document ownership, access, and recovery in [the developer contract](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3d9b9541a291c430457c4fe9a7162b69a3887b06/docs/webui-state-events.md).

## Scope and limits

WebUI core protocol 1, mutation authorization, domain locking/persistence, agent execution ownership, and session storage remain unchanged. This does not automatically reconnect or replace remote identity, remove backend runtime/health timers, or change OAuth/QR/update-job tracking. The paired state-refresh implementation does not maintain a new-WebUI/old-Gateway combination.

Native filesystem notification registration must succeed before the WebSocket/WebUI listener opens. Unusual or network-mounted filesystems still require deployment validation. This removes repeated browser snapshot polling, not all periodic work; no CPU, memory, energy, model latency, or cost improvement has been benchmarked.

## Verification

Candidate: `3d9b9541a291c430457c4fe9a7162b69a3887b06`; PR base: `5ae49a43e7990f021b8d7dd1d8a53bf8cb443c95`. Runtime/test evidence below was obtained at `cae2c5e2b32cdfb41996446fa0e940d2f60eeb6b` and carried forward over a README-only follow-up removing the stale older-host promise and fixing its section link; production code, tests, dependencies/config, and built assets are unchanged. Main has advanced separately; local evidence is not a claim that the latest main has been incorporated or verified. GitHub PR CI checks its generated merge ref, associated with the recorded PR head.

- Narrowed frontend/test content: **3,322 tests passed in 188 files**, coverage thresholds passed. TypeScript, ESLint, production build, and client import boundaries passed; import-boundary harness: **41 passed, 1 platform-specific skip**. The final gallery example-only correction was subsequently typechecked, linted, and built.
- Affected Python checks: **284 passed** across state events, remote instances, settings API, and client contract; Ruff and Python import boundaries passed. Broader Python evidence from the previous candidate remains historical, not a fresh run of the entire suite on this commit.
- Controlled browser event-delivery check: **2 passed**, desktop and narrow viewport. The complete local browser run had **261 passed, 1 failed**: `prompt-rail.spec.ts:61` did not observe the expected next-page request after a wheel gesture. Its isolated rerun on the unchanged candidate passed; that does not establish the cause or turn the original run into an all-green result. No prompt/history code or test was changed to suppress it.
- Fresh isolated real-Gateway/production-browser acceptance at `cae2c5e2b` (inherited over the README-only follow-up): **8 local checks and 5 remote/two-tab checks passed**, with gateway logs confirming loaded watchfiles **1.3.0**. Covers external committed changes across the consumers, first-run-record directory notifications, real eight-second pairing expiry, 60-second automation/empty-queue idle with no additional resource GETs/events, real WebSocket reconnect and draft retention, 80 remote-directory reads with no extra health probes, shared sampling (3 probes in 16 seconds), external rename preserving iframe/drafts, offline isolation, and explicit reconnect before remote identity replacement. It does not include the removed older-host combination.
- Final-head [CI run 40009495576](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/40009495576) completed with **failure; this candidate is not ready**. [Windows native acceptance](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/40009495576/job/120606006414) failed while building its test wheel: `TUI release file has an invalid size: nanobot-tui-win32-x64.exe`; the required gate failed as a result. No TUI size/integrity guard or browser assertion was weakened, and unrelated TUI packaging/history changes were not added. prs.title: fix(agent): preserve goal continuation lifecycle
prs.body:
## Why

Long `/goal` runs could be reported as finished at an internal iteration-budget boundary even though work continued. This reset the WebUI transcript sequence for the same public turn and could make loading earlier history fail with `Could not place earlier history` despite successful HTTP responses.

`/goal` replaces the inbound message and copies its metadata. The continuation helper wrote its pending flag onto that replacement, while dispatch checked the original message. Keep this execution state on the shared delivery instead of using message metadata as a side channel.

Related: [NAN-348](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-348).

## What changed

- Record the successful continuation handoff on the per-slice `TurnDelivery`; completion, failure and idle all consult that same result.
- Clear the handoff when the session worker is cancelled, so Stop still ends the visible run if a continuation was queued just before persistence was interrupted.
- Exercise the real `/goal` rewrite in the existing continuation lifecycle regression, and add the reachable Stop-after-enqueue regression for both ordinary goal messages and `/goal`.

## Scope

This is the causal prevention fix for newly executed goal continuations. It does not change the wire protocol, frontend reconciliation, database format, dependencies or user data. It does not disable live-history protection or add automatic refresh as a workaround.

**Existing history that already contains duplicate public turn/sequence identities is not repaired by this PR.** Physical records are not keyed by those logical identities, so they were not overwritten, but older/latest reconciliation can still collide. Non-destructive legacy read-side compatibility remains open under NAN-348. This prevention fix is ready for review independently of that remaining work; NAN-348 is not being marked Done. No production database has been rewritten.

## Tradeoffs

A delivery-owned result survives command replacement and remains available to exception/finally handling if persistence fails after enqueue. Expanding only `_process_message`'s return value would not cover that failure path; copying the flag back into another metadata dictionary would retain two state owners.

## Blast Radius

The common continuation completion path affects WebUI and other goal-capable channels. The new cancellation regression protects the narrow handoff/persistence window. Python recovery, inbox, delivery and channel regressions were included in the complete local suite; live browser acceptance used an isolated Gateway and synthetic sessions. These checks do not establish exhaustive platform compatibility, production deployment, or repair of pre-existing collisions.

## Verification

All results below apply to head `32c19d3c911c2d4ce3e1ca45fb10bc96c4f2f4b4`.

- Red/green: the `/goal` case produced an extra intermediate `idle` before the lifecycle fix; the Stop-after-enqueue cases produced only `running` before the cancellation correction. Both ordinary and `/goal` cases pass with this change.
- Local Python: **11,151 passed, 97 skipped** across the full parallel suite and the four separate serial CLI files; combined coverage **85.93%**, above the 75% gate. Dependencies and channel manifests were installed in a private verification environment; shared runtime dependencies were not changed.
- `ruff check` for the five changed files, scoped BasedPyright for the three changed Python runtime files, `python -m scripts.check_import_boundaries` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local WebUI: **3,292 tests / 185 files passed**, with coverage thresholds satisfied (94.14% statements/lines, 88.77% branches, 91.69% functions). `bun run build` passed. Existing React act/KaTeX test warnings and Vite chunk-size warnings remain.
- Isolated real Gateway + Chromium: `/goal` executed four distinct stream slices at an iteration budget of one. While held at the fourth slice, desktop (1400×1000) and narrow (390×844) clients accepted earlier history, retained the live tail, and reloaded while still active. Completion produced one `turn_end` and one idle; persisted projection sequences increased across slices without collisions (19 retained identities, spanning 1–28). Completed-history reload also passed.
- The narrow client disconnected and reconnected its own WebSocket during continuation: the active turn was preserved, without intermediate completion; final content rendered with one final `turn_end` and idle.
- Additional real-browser scenarios passed: Stop during `/goal` continuation, Stop during ordinary-input continuation of an already active goal, ordinary-input completion, and a deliberate provider failure followed by a new input. Stop retired the owner without reviving or replaying the cancelled turn; completion/failure emitted one final `turn_end` and idle. All four scenarios retained unique, increasing sequence identities, retired the backend owner, and had no page errors. The active ordinary-input goal was established through `/goal` and Stop, not by bypassing opt-in or writing session metadata.
- Remote Test Suite [40006206033](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/40006206033) completed successfully on this exact head: Linux Python 3.11/3.14 with coverage, Windows Python/process checks, both TUI platforms, Docker, WebUI checks/build/browser and `CI required` passed. Native-package and Windows-installer checks were skipped by the workflow's scope selection.

Owned verification Gateway/provider/browser resources were cleaned up; the isolated Gateway ports were released. No daily or third-party instance was restarted. No formal GitHub review, merge or deployment is included.

prs.title: fix(providers): support Kimi K3.1 Pro request parameters
prs.body:
## Why

Switching a Moonshot preset to `kimi-k3.1-pro` or `kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed` currently sends a configurable temperature (default `0.1`) even though the API fixes it at `1.0`. The WebUI also offers unsupported `medium` reasoning and omits `max`. The existing K3 adaptation only recognizes the exact `kimi-k3` ID.

Fixes [NAN-347](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-347).

## What changed

- Share the three documented K3-family model IDs between the provider adapter and model settings.
- Apply existing K3 behavior to both K3.1 variants: omit fixed temperature, send the configured output budget as `max_completion_tokens`, and preserve supported or normalize legacy reasoning presets.
- Extend existing provider regressions and check the actual settings payload for default / `low` / `high` / `max` choices.

## Scope

Moonshot's OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions path and existing WebUI settings metadata only. No new provider, Agent-core changes, dependency changes, user-config migration, enlarged token budgets, Kimi Coding changes, or Responses-specific features. The deprecated `max_tokens` field is replaced without claiming that upstream already rejects it.

The official [K3.1 Pro guide](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/guide/kimi-k3-1-pro-quickstart.md), [model parameter reference](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api/models-overview.md), and [Chat Completions schema](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api/chat.md) document the shared parameter contract.

## Blast Radius

Known K3-family IDs use the same request rules and settings choices, including the adapter's existing model-slug handling. K2.x and other model families keep their previous rules. The immutable ID set lives in provider metadata; no new WebUI wire fields or protocol requirements are introduced.

## Verification

- Regression-first: before the fix, the scoped K3 checks had **16 failures / 8 passes**; after the fix, **24 passed**.
- `PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$PWD/tests" python -m pytest tests/providers tests/webui/test_settings_api.py tests/webui/test_settings_models.py -q`: **1,634 passed**; two Pydantic serializer warnings from the existing Mistral streaming fixtures.
- Ruff on the five changed files: passed. BasedPyright 1.39.0 on the three changed product modules: **0 errors, 0 warnings**.
- `python -m scripts.check_import_boundaries`: passed (13 rules, 217 files). `git diff --check`: passed.
- An isolated loopback HTTP fixture exercised the real provider factory and OpenAI SDK **2.29.0** for all three model IDs: **12 requests passed**, covering default parameters, streamed reasoning/tool calls, legacy `medium` normalization, supported effort, disabled-preset compatibility, and preservation of reasoning/tool history on continuation. Clients and the fixture listener were closed afterward.

No paid Kimi API calls were made. The loopback fixture validates SDK serialization and local handling, not live-provider availability, account entitlement, or upstream acceptance. No daily instance, real credentials, or existing user configuration was changed.

## Why

Restoring a waiting message also restored its automatic execution eligibility. Loading an old completed turn could therefore start a new agent run without fresh user confirmation.

## What changed

- Scope automatic sending to the live page that queued the message. Legacy drafts and drafts from another page restore as manual input without losing text, attachments, quotes or session targets.
- Revoke eligibility on `pagehide` and document `freeze`; retain it across topic/component remounts and short reconnects. Keep Stop and failed sends manual.
- Add regression coverage, five browser cases, and document the changed restore behavior.

## Scope

Frontend waiting-message authorization only. Backend scheduling, admission, recovery, protocol and the existing merged-message behavior are unchanged.

## Tradeoffs

Reloading, reopening or leaving the page now requires **Send now** or editing and sending the restored content. A live hidden tab or a disconnected socket alone retains eligibility; no elapsed-time cutoff is introduced. Browser suspension is handled when the browser reports `freeze` or creates a new document.

## Blast Radius

All Composer variants and their waiting messages. The existing localStorage key and v1 array shape remain; an optional page identifier cannot authorize execution in a different document.

## Verification

### After resolving the main conflict (`79c37cdcb`)

Merged `main@169062be1` with an ordinary merge commit. The only conflict was in `docs/webui.md`; this keeps main's concise guide and the restored-draft safety guidance. The queued-send implementation and its regression fixtures are unchanged.

- Current merge: **333 focused tests**, **5 Chromium browser regressions**, full typecheck, lint, import-boundary check and production build passed.

- Chromium browser regressions: **5 passed**, one worker and zero retries; includes desktop/narrow reload, live topic switching, browser back navigation and complete legacy payload preservation.
- Real isolated gateway with production assets and a deterministic loopback provider: frozen-base build reproduced an unsolicited admission, model request and real file write after restoring the old queue shape. The candidate produced **zero admissions/model calls/tool effects from the restored draft**; explicit Send now admitted it once and executed the file tool. Live topic navigation and a byte-preserving WebSocket outage each released fresh waiting input exactly once. Stop retained the queue for manual delivery, which then completed once.

The first default-worker coverage run timed out in the unchanged Tailwind-scan test; the initial import-rule run had six child-process timeouts. prs.body:
## Why

Resolves #6285. ddgs can collapse upstream refusal, empty parsing and aggregation failures into `DDGSException("No results found.")`. That exception does not establish that a search completed with zero matches. This PR implements the agreed nanobot-side resolution: report the uncertainty accurately to the model without guessing a cause or retrying the search.

## What changed

- Report generic ddgs failures as search unavailable with an unknown cause, explicitly preserving uncertainty about matching pages.
- Distinguish the tool's waiting deadline from a timeout reported by ddgs. Keep the existing error status, cancellation behavior, diagnostic logging and unexpected-exception path.
- Exercise the released Wikipedia parser and ddgs aggregator with offline responses, checking the next model request's actual tool message and error event for empty parsing, HTTP 403, HTTP 429 and library timeout. Strengthen the existing outer-timeout check.

## Scope

This PR resolves the agreed nanobot-side scope of #6285: report ambiguous ddgs failures honestly as search unavailable with an unknown cause. Preserving precise underlying HTTP refusal/rate-limit facts requires an upstream public contract and is tracked independently (related upstream report: https://github.com/deedy5/ddgs/issues/478). This PR does not claim to recover HTTP 403/429 from `No results found`.

No automatic retry, pacing configuration, dependency/backend changes, production hooks into ddgs internals, Agent core changes or frontend changes. Existing successful search formatting and proxy routing remain unchanged.

## Verification

- Red/green: the four model-input cases and existing tool-deadline case fail against the frozen parent because of the misleading or empty error message, then pass with the fix.
- `uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests/agent/test_runner_web_search_errors.py tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py tests/tools/test_private_tool_logging.py tests/agent/test_runner_errors.py -q --tb=short` — 149 passed with ddgs 9.11.4.
- The same search/model-input/privacy scope under `uv run --no-sync --with ddgs==9.16.0` — 134 passed. These are controlled offline library/runner checks, not a new VPS or live-model acceptance run.
- Full-project Ruff and Python import boundaries — passed.
- `uv run --no-sync basedpyright` — **FAIL**, four `BaseFileLock`/`FileLock` return-type diagnostics in unchanged `mcp_oauth.py`, `gateway/runtime.py`, `process_runtime.py` and `xai_oauth.py`. The identical environment against the frozen parent `06f398196` reproduces the same four diagnostics; they remain failures and are outside this change.
- `uv run --no-sync python -m pytest -n 3 --dist loadfile -q --tb=short` — **FAIL**, 1 failed, 11,020 passed, 186 skipped in 23m12s. The failure is `tests/gateway/test_runtime.py::test_competing_foreground_claim_preserves_the_live_gateway`: its first child did not publish the claim marker within the existing deadline. The isolated case passes on both this candidate and the frozen parent; the original full-suite failure remains unattributed, not cleared by those isolated passes.

Subsequent published-head CI and real-model black-box acceptance have passed. The original local failures remain documented above; no unrelated gateway tests, timeouts or type annotations were changed to make checks pass.


## Black-box acceptance

Completed through the normal CLI entrypoint in separate processes with isolated homes/configs/workspaces, a real DeepSeek `deepseek-v4-flash` model and ddgs 9.16.0. No scripted model responses or production hooks. All four cases used the same one-search request; persisted tool messages and the real final assistant responses were inspected.

| Case | Network condition | Observed result |
|---|---|---|
| Live search | Real search through the existing configured Web proxy | ddgs returned the official Python asyncio documentation; the model explained asyncio and cited the returned official URL. PASS (13.0s). |
| Refused connection | Task-owned proxy returned HTTP 403 to CONNECT; it did not contact search engines | Tool reported unavailable / cause unknown; the model reported the failed lookup and explicitly distinguished it from no matching pages, without inventing source links or a rate-limit diagnosis. PASS (7.2s). |
| Tool deadline | Controlled proxy held the connection beyond the configured one-second tool waiting deadline | Tool and real model reported the waiting timeout; no fabricated search-based answer or source. PASS (7.9s). |
| Library timeout | Controlled proxy held the connection; the tool's 100-second waiting budget allowed ddgs's existing request timeout to finish first | Tool identified a timeout reported by ddgs; the model reported the failed lookup and declined to invent a source link. PASS (47.1s). |

Each case made exactly one `web_search` tool call. The refusal and timeout conditions are synthetic network faults, not a claim to reproduce the original VPS rejection. Task processes and fixture listeners exited, fixture ports were released, the source instance's configuration was unchanged, and no provider keys were persisted in the verification files.

[CI run 39893174211](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39893174211) completed successfully for this published head, including the required gate, Python 3.11, Python 3.14 + coverage, Windows, Windows process compatibility and Docker. Path-unrelated checks were skipped. The original local failures above remain recorded; they were not reclassified as passing.

prs.title: ci: reuse isolated pip seeds and parallelize native acceptance
prs.body:
## Summary

Reduce repeated integration preparation and the native serial critical path while retaining per-test isolation and the complete acceptance workload. This is an experimental Draft: the final matched-source full run is green, but current-main PR integration still exposes two timing-sensitive Windows failures.

## Changes

- Keep stdlib venv responsible for creating each independent test prefix. Reuse the current interpreter's exact ensurepip wheels through virtualenv's offline app-data seeder only; copy packages and regenerate prefix-specific console scripts without virtualenv creation/import hooks. Real pip installation, updates and recovery remain exercised.
- Split native acceptance into two independent controller lanes, retaining all nine scenarios and fifteen journeys per OS. Each lane installs its own dependencies once and owns its venv, HOME/config/data/cache/temp, locks and processes. Recovery and the following upgrade stay ordered within the same lane; target wheel identity and complete report coverage are checked before merging results.
- Try doubled workers: Linux pytest 2→4, ordinary Windows pytest 3→6, browser 1→2 and native 1→2. The heavy Windows update6/installer8 trials failed, so these lanes retain their original 3/4 budgets. Serial CLI/process checks, platform/Python matrix, coverage gates, original test assertions/parameterization, retries and existing deadlines are unchanged.
- Retain controller-tree ownership after the controller exits: reuse the existing suspended-spawn Windows Job Object owner; unconditionally clear the owned POSIX process group before private-config gateway cleanup. Public native artifacts remain restricted to explicit safe result/report JSON paths, excluding credential-bearing raw logs.

The dev extra adds virtualenv rather than hand-building pip or copying a live relocatable venv. Its current dependency constraints resolve dev filelock to 3.32.7 instead of 4.2.4; production dependency constraints and the application version are unchanged. Native parallelism pays for a second independent dependency installation.

## Snapshot-bound measurement

Frozen product baseline: `bc5c58d23941b1bcca8980c4a0ebfc4d1d783bf2`. Final head: `d8a1fbd0b8402273c57d39f7126893f8eb9aeeb5`. Ancestry and unchanged production/browser workload were checked. Main advanced by five commits during the experiment; PR synthetic-merge timings are excluded from this performance comparison.

Two frozen-source control runs: [39748961300](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39748961300) and [39765369473](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39765369473). Final matched-source candidate: [39765207434](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39765207434), **SUCCESS, 21m28s total**. The following ranges use only successful, equivalent stages; the browser has one completed control.

| Stage, excluding job queue | Frozen baseline | Final candidate | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Windows native upgrade/recovery | 16:32–22:23 | 10:03 | 39–55% |
| Linux native upgrade/recovery | 9:28–11:13 | 5:07 | 46–54% |
| Linux coverage main tests | 8:33–8:41 | 5:19 | 38–39% |
| Linux minimum main tests | 8:29–10:16 | 7:32 | 11–27% |
| Windows isolated update tests, still 3 workers | 6:11–7:08 | 5:23 | 13–25% |
| Windows ordinary main tests, successful control only | 9:15 | 8:20 | 10% |
| Browser test step, same 223 cases | 8:13 | 6:28 | 21% |

Whole Windows native job: 23:29–28:52→20:59 (11–27%); build, clean installation and other setup limit the end-to-end benefit. Whole Linux native job: 11:42–13:47→7:03 (40–49%). Installer4 has **no established gain**: its successful test steps ranged 13:28–16:44 in controls and took 16:39 in the final candidate.

Original Python node IDs were retained with unchanged outcomes against the successful repeat-control stages: Linux main 10,937→10,952 and Windows main 10,696→10,711 add fifteen infrastructure regression cases; update86, installer80, serialCLI253, process59 and coordination25 are unchanged. Both native reports retain exactly 9 scenarios/15 journeys with identical outcome facts. Browser223 passed in the completed control and candidate, with zero retries.

The first control overall failed with a Settings API `httpx.ReadTimeout`. The repeat control's Python/native/installer jobs passed, but browser installation took 577s and the browser job hit its unchanged 15-minute limit before completing tests. Queueing reached 364s in that repeat and is reported separately from execution. Thus there is no all-green-before/all-green-after whole-workflow comparison. Observed runner-seconds were 7,299/6,847 for the incomplete controls and 5,656 for the successful candidate; these are recorded, not presented as a proven full-workflow cost reduction.

## Verification and remaining blockers

- [Final current-main PR integration 39765214057](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39765214057) tested merge `284a936ed60f174a581da8920c1a21bd0e34d84e` with target `254f94b068bd0338396b71ac6ec244812b79e1c8`. Native, Linux, installer, browser228 and the isolated Windows update suite passed. Windows main had two failures, so the required gate remains red:
  - `test_graphql_rate_limit_error_is_retryable`: its live-clock 60-second reset was created before setup; the test took 12.68s and then asserted at least 50s remained, observing 47.32s. This is an existing wall-clock-sensitive test exposed in the six-worker run; the effect of worker count has not been isolated.
  - `test_settings_api_returns_safe_subset_and_updates_whitelist`: `httpx.ReadTimeout`, the same failure observed in the first frozen control at three workers. The endpoint root cause remains outside this optimization's verified results.
- Initial six-update/eight-installer worker trials failed in two independent runs ([matched](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39753831920), [PR](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39753834636)). Restoring update3 did not immediately eliminate an intermittent supervisor timeout in a matched run, while that head's PR run passed it. Final stdlib-created environments passed update86 in both matched and PR runs; this does not establish the cause of the earlier timeout. No deadline or retry was increased.
- Real exited-controller descendant-listener regression demonstrated red→green; verifier/seed/lifecycle selection: 31 passed with two workers. Final direct seed/supervisor selection: 2 passed; exact seed isolation also passed under Python 3.11.12. Original 83 installation/update test function ASTs, including decorators and parameterization, are unchanged.
- Hosted final Linux lint, import boundaries, BasedPyright and coverage passed. Local Windows BasedPyright still reports two optional setproctitle diagnostics, reproduced on the exact archived baseline under the same interpreter/dependencies.
- Full local WebUI typecheck/lint/import scan passed; browser223 passed with two workers. Import-checker tests initially had 39 pass/3 timeout; one unchanged-command rerun passed42 without increasing deadlines. Initial prototype-only local covered timing (291.19→170.79s, identical4,411 executed production lines) is retained as earlier evidence, not attributed to final source.

Keep Draft pending Windows stability work. No formal review, merge, tracker change or shared-runtime modification was performed.
