prs.title: fix(webui): share sidebar and Composer run state
prs.body:
## Why

A finished conversation could leave Composer saying “Model is responding…” with a Stop button while the sidebar was already idle ([NAN-263](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-263)). The Hook and sidebar had separate writers for busy state: historical pending activity and text streaming could keep the Hook busy after the client turn ledger had settled. The captured transcript shows `stream_end` 98 ms before `turn_end`, but the original browser event trace was not captured, so it does not establish the unique production cause.

## What changed

- Sidebar and Composer read the same per-chat **client run ledger** snapshot (`active`, optional start time and turn identity). An optimistic send can be active before a start clock exists; transcript rendering and recovery decisions no longer own a second busy flag.
- `stream_end` is not a turn completion. Terminal events and canonical completion reconciliation settle the shared state, with generation/turn fences against late history and older events so a later turn remains active. Existing waiting-input behavior remains covered.
- Resolving an old recovery as `recovered/superseded` does not close the new user turn that replaced it. The regression checks that Stop remains available, new running/text events are accepted and the new turn ends normally.
- Removed the broader backend execution-state, scheduling and targeted-Stop redesign previously added to this PR. The final diff against base `06f3981962ccfa37e9d8edda583cad4b651a6054` is limited to 13 WebUI files (+378/−374); backend scheduling and `/stop` retain their pre-PR semantics.

## Verification

Local checks cover the unchanged tracked tree committed as `081e1df6f1c0b05b09a5d4c2a97c0d6e8659b343`:

- WebUI and browser TypeScript, ESLint, import boundaries (41 passed / 1 Windows-only skip), production build and full Vitest coverage (3,287 passed / 1 skipped) passed. The existing chunk-size build warning remains.
- Full Chromium browser suite: **230 passed**, including desktop/narrow answer ordering. Completed tool activity is opened through the answer's actions and checked in its original position between the answer pieces, using its completed label rather than the running label.
- The recovery-replacement regression failed before the focused fix and passed afterward; the relevant client/hook/ThreadShell regression selection passed all 348 tests.
- Built UI against a **separate authenticated loopback gateway**, fresh isolated home/workspace and deterministic local provider: a partially streamed answer remained active; completion cleared sidebar and Composer; navigation/reconnect retained live state; Stop and reload converged to idle; actual write/read/exec tools completed; and a new request replacing a failed model recovery retained Stop and completed normally. The latter check captured the gateway's real `recovered/superseded` event.
- A second fresh real-gateway/browser check deliberately disconnected before completion, waited for the gateway to persist the finished answer, then reconnected; persisted completion restored the answer and idle state. No browser page errors. The expected missing-thread probe returned one HTTP 404; the recovery case deliberately returned a local model HTTP 401. Owned gateway/provider processes exited and all six loopback ports were verified closed. No daily or handed-off service was operated or real session/secret copied in these checks.

- Exact-head [GitHub Actions](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39987263336) for `081e1df6f1c0b05b09a5d4c2a97c0d6e8659b343`: **passed**, including `CI required`, WebUI checks/build, Chromium browser and Docker. The change selector skipped unrelated Python/Windows/native-package jobs; they are not claimed as rerun by this head.

## Scope and limits

This is shared **client** state, not a server-authoritative live-run snapshot. If both terminal events and durable completion evidence are unavailable, reconnect cannot prove liveness. The legacy `/stop` still cancels at session scope and locally clears optimistic running state; targeted cancellation and a backend lifecycle redesign are not part of this fix. The deterministic local-provider checks do not establish compatibility with every real provider or historical host/client combination, and the original incident browser trace remains unavailable.

prs.title: refactor(webui): unify code and diff highlighting
prs.body:
## Why

Replace the WebUI's separate Prism code/preview/diff paths with shared highlighting while preserving the existing reading and file-change workflows. This also restores the earlier single-conversation preview layout: messages and Composer stay together in the left column, with the file preview filling the right column.

## What changed

- Replace `react-syntax-highlighter`/Prism with shared Highlights tokens and CSS-variable colors. Load Shiki only for grammars absent from Highlights; render source through React text/spans and preserve complete preview text, native find/selection, copy, ANSI, streaming settlement, wrapping, line numbers, themes and reading sizes.
- Render each complete read-only file diff through one Pierre instance, with bounded metadata/AST caches and a render window read from the existing chat scroller. Preserve file summaries, line limits, expansion/collapse, hunk gaps, truncation notices and local previews.
- Keep the single-conversation Composer inside its conversation column. Actual multi-pane tabs retain the shared footer, including compact rendering. Update both lockfiles, lazy-chunk guards, dependency notices and behavioral tests.

## Scope

WebUI only. No backend, TUI, provider, protocol or persistence-format changes; no patch editing/applying, new scroller ownership or bottom-mask removal. Uses pinned `@pierre/diffs` 1.6.1, `@pierre/highlights` 0.2.0 and Shiki 4.5.0.

## Tracking

Related: [NAN-343 — 统一 WebUI 代码与只读 diff 高亮，保留源码操作及侧栏布局](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-343).

## Tradeoffs

**Draft: large-diff scrolling and first-use transfer tradeoffs have not been remeasured after the fixes below.** This is not presented as a blanket performance improvement.

Five interleaved original-Prism/new-renderer trials on equivalent synthetic production fixtures, taken **before the final preview-layout follow-up**, found:

| Workload | Prism → replacement |
| --- | --- |
| 600-line code block, warm topic return | 316.6 → 190.0 ms |
| 600-row diff, warm expanded viewport | 189.5 → 30.7 ms |
| Code-block browser Private Working Set increment | 203.6 → 120.0 MiB |
| Diff browser Private Working Set increment | 217.8 → 171.6 MiB |
| Large-diff scroll p99, normal / Chromium 4× CPU throttle | 16.8 → 33.4 ms / 33.4 → 183.4 ms |
| Whole JS/CSS/WASM first-use transfer, code / diff | 708.8 → 797.1 KiB / 706.9 → 887.8 KiB |

Memory subtracts each independent browser's blank-host baseline; private commit was measured separately. Transfer is actual negotiated response-body bytes, not decoded size. Diff viewport readiness is separate from a complete source-coordinate traversal. The 600-row diff is a stress fixture above the ordinary default 500-row native output cap; 4× throttling is not a real low-end device. These figures are retained evidence for that earlier snapshot, **not a performance claim for this repaired head**.

## Blast Radius

Shared Markdown/code rendering, source-file previews, read-only file activity and single/multiple-pane Composer placement. Main review risks are grammar-loading failures and resource ownership, source/line-ending integrity, virtual-diff geometry and scrolling tails, and draft/attachment retention when changing pane ownership.

## Verification

The repaired source/build passed locally: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun run check:imports`, `bun run test:imports`, `bun run test:coverage --maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=2` (**3297 tests**), `bun run test:browser` (**246 cases**), `bun run build --outDir <isolated-output>` and `git diff --check`. The source inventory, normalized staged blobs/Git tree and frozen production assets were checked against the repair commit; no source change intervened after those checks.

A new isolated production gateway passed **32 normal black-box cases** on desktop/light and narrow/dark: code blocks including INI, PowerShell, C#, Docker and literal unknown-language HTML; exact clipboard content; themes; full previews/native find and selection; long-line plain-text budgets; six kinds of diff including the INI Worker path; complete retained coordinates, line limits, expansion, truncation and close/reopen. No browser or HTTP errors occurred in these normal cases. Preview open/close retained the same Composer DOM instance and its draft.

The targeted production regression checks also passed: a real failed INI grammar request in the direct source-file preview retained complete plain source, the same Composer and draft, working theme/close controls, and local diagnostics. The normal → blocked → normal controls each used a fresh browser context in the same Service-Worker-blocked interception mode; this is not a claim of automatic same-page module retry. Ordinary black-box cases used the normal Service Worker path. A real mouse drag plus native wheel across the original virtual-window boundary retained the exact selection; further scrolling kept both the selected rows and current viewport, native Copy matched the selection, and clearing it released the pinned rows without changing total scroll height.

The full browser suite additionally covers forward/backward selection and multi-hunk missing-context coordinates, native clipboard content and 26px localized gaps. Earlier built-gateway single → multiple → single pane checks with text and browser-File drafts remain recorded against the initial review commit; pane/Composer ownership source was unchanged by this repair, and the full current unit/browser checks were rerun.

## Review results

The initial review of `48e7177e9669f86f2f50ae462871ad296a19abd1` independently confirmed two P2 defects in the production UI. Both are repaired in [`d4469e316`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/commit/d4469e316ce26a9169d911d7ebd33ff765d51049):

1. **Contain grammar/highlighter failure in CodeBlock.** Optional syntax enhancement can fail without clearing the source-file preview or the app. Keep the full plain source and Copy control outside the failed child; discard failed cached resources after the fallback commits, while retaining diagnostics.
2. **Preserve native diff selection during window movement.** Replace the function-valued hunk separator that disabled Pierre 1.6.1 partial rendering with built-in separators and local shadow-root label updates. Convert composed/shadow selection coordinates to rendered rows, retain only the active selection's minimal continuous envelope with the current viewport, and return to the normal bounded window when selection clears. Chromium's retargeted document `Selection.isCollapsed` is not used to reject a real shadow selection.

A focused independent read-only review of the repair implementation and installed library APIs found no new confirmed actionable finding. The exact parent failure triggers now pass through the new production build, as detailed above. This was not a formal GitHub approval.

Keep Draft pending performance reassessment: earlier scrolling/transfer measurements remain tied to the older pre-layout snapshot, not this incremental-render repair. Non-Chromium native shadow-selection fallbacks are statically checked but not browser-accepted. CI for the pushed head is reported separately from local tests and these synthetic-fixture UI checks.

prs.title: feat(webui): edit and resend messages in the same session
prs.body:
## Why

Users need to correct a sent message without creating another sidebar topic. This implements the approved in-place edit: keep the prefix before the selected user message, replace that message and its entire suffix, and generate a new reply in the same session.

Related to [NAN-92](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-92/webui-支持编辑并重新发送已发送的用户消息).

## What changed

- Add **Edit message** beside Copy in the existing desktop/mobile message actions, using the existing `EditIcon`. Edit directly inside the native user-message bubble with its own draft, Cancel/Resend controls, actionable errors and translations in all 10 locales. Composer drafts, quotes, attachments and waiting input remain separate.
- Commit the replacement model records and display facts in one session-owner SQLite transaction. Preserve session identity and settings, rotate the history generation, invalidate obsolete summaries/provider continuation, and record retry identity so an accepted input executes once. Both histories now live in the same database; there is no file-backed replacement journal.
- Reuse ordinary latest-thread reads for the source snapshot. Confirming the edit is the only mutation. Validate one page-independent source revision and stable message identity inside the transaction, rather than maintaining a separate prepare protocol and an eight-field anchor.
- Share prefix retention between in-place replacement and the existing **New conversation** fork. Keep idle admission, the normal execution queue, cancellation safety, and generation fences across drafts, streams, HTTP pages, trace details, navigation caches and late subagent results.
- The historical cleanup removed 106 net production lines without moving the implementation into a replacement framework. Original message text is used for the current source check, not retained in the retry receipt.
- Retain two Windows PowerShell installer regressions for unrelated uv/pipx modules; main now supplies the equivalent no-auto-import implementation.
- Keep a native touch input round attached to its original target across lazy Markdown replacement, including move/end/cancel and listener cleanup.
- Admit supported Windows baseline TUI builds with a bounded 160 MiB executable budget; retain the download, required-file, checksum/source/license and oversize guards.

## Scope

The first version supports persisted ordinary user text in saved WebUI sessions. Attachments, quotes, session/CLI/MCP mentions, slash/shell commands and special/system deliveries are explicitly rejected rather than resent with lost metadata. Temporary Chat has no persisted edit target; shared history cannot be edited from an individual conversation. The WebUI and gateway ship together, without an edit-specific compatibility gate or older-gateway fallback.

Resend is the only destructive authorization, with no second modal. The URL, session ID, handle, title, creation identity, workspace, permissions and model settings remain unchanged. There is no backup topic, hidden persistent fork or version tree. Previously executed file/Shell effects are not rolled back.

## Tradeoffs

Model history and display facts remain separate projections, but replacement is atomic in the existing SQLite store. A pre-acceptance failure preserves the previous effective history and editable draft. A model failure after acceptance keeps the new failed turn instead of restoring the discarded suffix. A changed source is rejected rather than guessed from a page-local index.

## Blast Radius

This touches session admission/persistence, WebUI transcript reads and WebSocket delivery, frontend history reconciliation, and subagent result ownership. The main risks are cross-client races, stale events restoring a removed suffix, and retry/crash behavior. Existing new-fork behavior is covered separately; this does not redesign subagent cancellation or external-effect rollback.

## Verification

Cleanup snapshot: `cc083aaf269bd6f92a70ddb863162c25ea5543ad`, an ordinary commit on `95463f90389354244b0973c25d34ea0757a7e55b`. Its committed tree matches the tested cleanup candidate exactly.

Latest published source: `36c5adc9d305f567f026d81291331af1b410398b`. The requested rebase, two ordinary CI repairs and a test-only timeout diagnostic preserve the feature semantics. The final CI tests merge `373554240816c48e5b5155ce72becdf43b48bd7a` against target `0254bf121736bf02bbcd9e988a2c1b3fc265f8d9`. Rows labeled Cleanup snapshot below describe the historical cleanup above; the latest follow-up checks and final-head CI are listed separately. The editor-specific 54/133/10-case results retain their original snapshot identity.

| Check | Actual result |
| --- | --- |
| Cleanup snapshot: Python white-box regressions | **54 passed**: edit/fork identity, source revisions, stale/busy rejection, SQLite rollback and real process exits around commit, cancellation/admission and retained model context |
| Cleanup snapshot: full ThreadShell and editor component files | **133 passed**, including source-read failure, cancellation, independent drafts and one confirmed request |
| Cleanup snapshot: full-project Ruff, strict BasedPyright and Python import boundaries | **PASS**, including 0 BasedPyright errors/warnings/notes |
| Cleanup snapshot: full-project WebUI typecheck, lint and import checks | **PASS**; import-check tests: **42 passed** |
| Cleanup snapshot: built-gateway black-box acceptance | **10 cases passed** through real HTTP/WebSocket and desktop/touch-emulated Chromium contexts, using a deterministic local HTTP model provider |
| Actual provider requests and readonly SQLite audit | **PASS**: 9 model requests, edited input exactly once, retained prefixes present and entire discarded suffixes excluded; model/display histories, turn counters/bytes/completion and foreign keys consistent |
| Broader checks reused from the identical source snapshot | **3685 Python passed / 21 skipped**, **3283 WebUI passed**, and production build **PASS**; these were completed before the fresh pre-push checks, with unchanged source fingerprints |
| Staged/committed source and `git diff --check` | **PASS**, tested patch and published commit are identical |
| Earlier installer snapshot, local and CI | **81 passed / 1 existing platform skip** in both runs, with the existing four workers and 90-second command limit; the regression failed before the fix and passed afterward |
| WebUI CI repair, local | **3303 coverage tests and 232 full browser tests passed**; 10 repeated native end/cancel regressions passed separately; full typecheck/lint/import boundaries/build passed at the retained UI snapshot, unchanged by the final Python-only diff. Import-check tests initially had two 5000 ms timeouts; the same command and limits subsequently passed all 42 in isolation |
| Native archive CI repair, local | **102 passed / 1 existing platform skip**; full Ruff, strict BasedPyright and import boundaries passed. With fixed Bun 1.3.13, the real 150 MiB + 512-byte PE failed the old verifier and passed complete manifest, architecture, source and license verification after the fix; oversize input is still rejected before decompression |
| Settings timeout diagnosis, local | **442 related tests, full Ruff and strict BasedPyright with the task-private interpreter passed**. A 4-second stack watchdog retains the original 5-second client wait and assertions. The original Windows hot-reload stall remains unclassified; a full isolated-archive diagnostic had 42 failures / 8 setup errors and is not a local full-suite PASS |
| CI for the final published head | **PASS, 15/15 checks successful**: [Test Suite run 39920590204](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39920590204) |

The fresh black-box cases cover desktop mouse/keyboard entry and cancellation, middle and first-message replacements, busy rejection, same-turn retries with different request IDs, Composer/quote/mention/attachment/pending isolation, actual socket disconnect/replay, refresh, paginated history after hidden `/model` messages, changes and earlier truncation from another browser, post-acceptance provider failure, stable session identity/topic count, and the independent **New conversation** action. There were no page errors.

The entire repository pytest suite and the full 223-case mocked browser suite were not rerun for this cleanup. The broader reused runs and fresh focused/public-surface checks are reported separately rather than presented as those commands. Physical touch hardware, external-model acceptance and user visual acceptance remain unverified. All newly created verification runtimes and private browser contexts were cleaned; the pre-existing user preview and production configuration/history were untouched. Maintainer review is still required.

prs.title: feat(providers): add MiniMax-M3.1-Flash and avoid reasoning_split=false
prs.body:
## Summary

Day-0 support for `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` (now live on MiniMax pay-as-you-go and Token Plan).

- `minimax` provider: add a built-in metadata entry for `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` with reasoning efforts `low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max` (default `max`) and text + image input.
- `minimax` provider: add `reasoning_effort_remap` mapping `none`/`minimal` → `low` (with identity entries for `low`/`medium`/`high`, so the settings effort menu for MiniMax models without metadata, e.g. M2.7/M3, stays `low`/`medium`/`high` as on `main`). MiniMax-M3.1-Flash rejects `reasoning_split: false` with HTTP 400 (error 2013), so the "off" presets currently break every request. With the remap, nanobot sends `reasoning_effort: "low"` + `reasoning_split: true` instead.

Registry-only change; no adapter code touched.

**Behavior note:** the remap is provider-wide, so `none`/`minimal` on older MiniMax models (e.g. M2.7) now also sends `low` + `reasoning_split: true` instead of `reasoning_split: false`. I verified that M2.7 and M3 both accept this (HTTP 200). The existing M2.7 `minimal` test was updated accordingly, and a test pins the M2.7/M3 effort menu to its `main` values. Happy to scope this per-model instead if you prefer.

## Tests

- `pytest tests/providers`: all pass (1420 + new cases). `test_internal_streaming.py` fails to import (`No module named 'agent'`) on `main` as well.
- Full suite (`--ignore=tests/cli/test_commands.py`, as in CI): the same 17 webui/channel tests fail with and without this change (environment-related: SSH/remote/scheduling). No new failures.
- `ruff check` on the changed files: clean.
- Live check through `OpenAICompatProvider.chat()` against `https://api.minimaxi.com/v1` with `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `max` all return `stop` with content. Before this change, `none`/`minimal` returned HTTP 400.

## AI assistance

This change was prepared with an AI coding assistant. I reviewed the diff and ran the tests and live requests above.

prs.title: fix(tools): web_search DuckDuckGo 增加退避重试并区分限流拒绝与空结果 (#6285)
prs.body:
## 问题

默认搜索 provider（DuckDuckGo，免 API key）在一个 turn 内连续调用 `web_search` 时，上游反爬/限流会拒绝请求，而 ddgs 把这类拒绝包装成 `DDGSException("No results found")`。原实现存在两个缺陷（#6285 有 8 查询 0/8 成功的隔离复现）：

1. **没有任何重试**——`_search_brave` 已有 HTTP 429 单次重试先例，但 `_search_duckduckgo` 一次失败即放弃；
2. **错误文案误导**——最终错误 `DuckDuckGo search failed (No results found.)` 与真实空结果集无法区分，导致 agent 把"被上游拒绝"误报为"没搜到结果"转述给用户。

## 修复

- `_search_duckduckgo` 增加**指数退避重试**：默认 1 + 2 次尝试（等待 1.0s / 2.0s），仅对异常重试；成功返回的空列表是真实空结果集，**不重试、不报错**，单次调用即返回 `No results for: ...`
- 全部尝试失败时**区分错误文案**，不虚构空结果：
  - `DDGSException` / "No results found" → `Error: DuckDuckGo search rejected after N attempt(s) (upstream rate-limit/anti-bot, not an empty result; ...)`，并建议拉开调用间隔或配置 API-key provider
  - 其他异常（超时、网络错误）→ `Error: DuckDuckGo search failed after N attempt(s) (...)`
- `tools.web.search` 新增两个可选配置（保持默认行为合理，无需用户调整即可受益）：
  - `retries`（默认 2，设 0 恢复单次行为）
  - `retry_backoff`（默认 1.0s 指数退避基数，第 k 次重试等待 `backoff * 2**(k-1)`）
- `DDGSException` 导入做了 `ddgs.exceptions` → 顶层双路径兜底，兼容 ddgs 9.x 的导出差异

## 测试

新增 5 个回归测试（`tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py`）：

| 用例 | 断言 |
|---|---|
| 瞬时拒绝重试后恢复 | 3 次尝试、sleep 序列 `[1.0, 2.0]`、返回结果 |
| 持续拒绝报 rejected | `rejected` / `not an empty result` / 建议文案，is_tool_error_result |
| 真实空结果不重试 | 单次调用、无 sleep、返回 `No results for: ...` |
| retries=0 单次行为 | 1 次尝试、无 sleep |
| retry_backoff=0.5 | 退避序列 `[0.5, 1.0]` |

本机验证报告（Windows 11 / Anaconda Python 3.12.4 / ddgs 9.16.0）：

```text
python -m pytest tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py -q
→ 96 passed（92 既有 + 4 重写/新增通过；含全部 5 个新回归用例）

python -m pytest tests/config -q
→ 159 passed, 1 skipped（新配置字段无 schema 回归）

python -m pytest tests/tools/test_search_tools.py
→ 本机段错误（0xC0000005）；经 git stash 对照，未修改的 main 上同样复现，
  为本机 Windows 环境既有问题，与本次改动无关
```

既有 `test_duckduckgo_timeout_returns_error` 显式设 `retries=0`，保持其单次超时的原语义与速度。

Closes #6285

## Description

Fixes #6285. DuckDuckGo's `ddgs` client can raise `DDGSException("No results found.")` for transient upstream rejections, causing consecutive `web_search` calls to fail without retrying. `nanobot/agent/tools/web.py:1000-1065` now retries these exceptions with capped exponential backoff and returns actionable rate-limit guidance when retries are exhausted.

- Keep genuine empty responses and non-retryable errors from triggering retries; report a retry suggestion after transient rejections are exhausted.
- Add tests for recovery after a rejection, exhausted retries, genuine empty results, and the first-wait backoff cap.

issues.body:
# RFC: THE DOC-CHAIN SUBSTRATE'S NETWORK — the read, the governance, the compaction


---

## The theme

The durable record survives the session's compression with its provenance intact, and the agent re-reads it rather than make the user repeat — the read restored, the store re-readable, the compaction governed, as one network.

## So what?

A Hermes user should be able to say "you're not listening" and have the agent re-read the durable record rather than make them repeat — and the record they anchor should survive the session's compression with its provenance intact. The doc-chain's network is the shape that gets there: the bounded read (Finn763's PR), the memory store's restore (#141876), the governed compaction (the provenance-origin + the K-recency, staged for their own home).

## The background

The read action's removal (56ee8a5cc6, 2026-02-19 — the 14-line removal) bought the compensation: 106 commits and 6,275 lines of undifferentiated heavy lifting on the memory path (the PR's own body counts 106 — the record's range), and the tracked class still open (10 tickets at the last count — 99957/105243/49195/110126/105248/116673/135039/50132/69264/140935). The 14-line removal funded the 5,000-line response — and the class is still open. The restore's the reversal already on the table (#141876, c0wb0yp0tat0, head `af16e3ab16`); the bounded read's Finn763's open PR (#116673); the governed compaction's a separate issue, staged but not opened.

## The current condition

The read action's removal caused 106 commits and 6,275 lines of compensation toil. The read path crashes on the PR head, is cleanly removed on the substrate, and works only in the experimental state — the three-state spread, each cell a run on disk:

- **The PR head** (#139606, `5b31ccb7d5`) — the read-action battery can't load; the cell's a collection error, not a clean 0/35.
- **The substrate** — `MemoryStore.read` cleanly absent; the read-action battery RED, 23 failed where the read's missing.
- **The experimental** — the uncommitted 14 lines + the untracked battery wire the read end-to-end; 35/35 green.

The K-recency window improves exact-recitation at every compression ratio on the 150-cycle sweep (2×–32×, K=10: +1.1/+2.2/+1.1/+2.3/+2.2pp), +2.2/+1.1/+2.3pp at the headline 4×/8×/16×. The honest scope of that number: the pipeline's real compressor ratios, the paraphrase step mocked, pruning off, the probe's own K=0 baseline (not the paper's 20.4/15.6/15.1). The long-session reverses it — 300 cycles, K=10 lands 6.1% against the 9.6% baseline, −3.5pp.

The stress battery (every cell cross-checked to a named artifact): 200/200 write-then-read, 800/800 concurrency survivors (0 corrupt, store not wiped), 100/100 re-read idempotence (content stable, done-flag steady), 20/20 over-budget refusals (graceful, entries preserved not wiped). The compaction-boundary gate holds: a non-user write to a protected scope's refused (Stage 2.c), the over-budget reroute-to-chain-doc seam returns `None`.

## The call-out

Stated plainly, then left for the room.

The sessions this substrate runs aren't the 150-cycle probe's — they're the real ones. The work's spanned over a month: the day's final run passed 22+ hours, the documented figure a ~799× session extension over a bare context window. The night arcs fire near midnight, with the first check-in at ~04:30; the runs last as long as the need dictates.

And the doc-chain substrate held through all of it — the anchor the pointer, the chain the unbounded layer, the reload-on-compression discipline keeping the run grounded turn after turn. That's the field record: sessions this long, this productive, the durable record surviving the compressions a bare-window run wouldn't. It's the proof-in-practice's cousin to the falsifier battery's lab proof — the lab says the mechanism's right; the marathons say it already works, in the wild, on the ambient team's era.

This is the statement awaiting the peer review's moment. The two reactions it's offered: "yeah, so what" — a long session's just a long session; or "wow, that's amazing" — a small, read-less, compaction-governed substrate carrying multi-hour, multi-turn productive runs a bare window can't. The call's the room's.

The nuance, held honestly: the *why* behind it — the compaction fidelity, the provenance, the field's convergence (LOHA/ACD's recitation floor, SJC's 83%) — rides here from the web storm's findings as the storm's source, NOT vetted truth in this RFC. What needs the verification goes through the enrichment process with the teams, not asserted into this call-out. The session lengths themselves're the rig's documented record; the interpretation's the storm's, pending.

## The root-cause

The 5-whys, the legs the record holds:

1. **The symptom** — the 6,275 lines of compensation churn. *Cause:* every session must re-derive what a single read gives, because the read's absent.
2. **Why absent** — the read action was removed (56ee8a5cc6), not deprecated; the substrate carries no `MemoryStore.read`.
3. **Why the churn persists** — the compensations (the doc-chain substrate, the dreaming prototype, the soft-compression path) each answer the read's symptom, none its root; they stack rather than close.
4. **Why the compaction loses fidelity** — at the lossy cut-point, two things die that the anchor's non-lossy boundary never had to carry: the exact recent text (paths, shas, args — the K-recency reason) and the identifier back to a unit's origin (the provenance reason).

The verified legs: 1–3 (the churn, the removal, the stack-not-close) — the record's. Leg 4's two sub-causes each map to one measured field failure — the exact-text loss to LOHA/ACD's recitation floor (2609.31430), the provenance loss to Source-Judged Compaction's 83% (2610.20927). **The unverified leg (flagged, not asserted):** *why the read crashes on the PR head specifically* — the record shows the collection error, not its parent bug; that's the dive-deep the owning PR must still do.

## The target state + the gap

**The target** — the read restored on the substrate (the #141876 reversal, green where it's RED today); the durable record's provenance surviving a compression with its origin resolvable; the K-recency window holding its measured gain (or improving) at every ratio *and* not reversing in the long session.

**The gap** — today the read's absent on the substrate and the compaction's ungoverned. The gap's exactly the proposal's pieces: the restore's unmerged (#141876 open), the bounded read's unmerged (#116673 open), the compaction governance un-built. No numeric target's been signed off — the acceptance criteria below're proposed from the battery, the team's to confirm.

## The scope

- **In** — the bounded read (#116673); the read action's restore (#141876); the three in-scope complements (the reference-as-provenance framing, the recency-ordered read, the scroll-up's re-read); the governed compaction (the provenance-origin classification, the archive-before-stub, the K-recency hard window).
- **Out** — the reroute-to-chain-doc seam's *placement* (an open question, not a scope line yet — the two-way door below); any write-path or non-doc-chain memory work; the lossy-layer compaction itself, which belongs to the separate issue, NOT to #116673 (that PR never compresses or rewrites a body). *The out-of-scope line's a candidate for the team's confirmation, not an asserted boundary.*

## Why this RFC, why now

The comments on the two threads just went live with the honest test data and the first-timer's caveat — because the designers in the room should see what the connections enable before any of it gets decided piecemeal. This is the discussion's formalization: the network shown whole, the veterans' coaching welcomed, the mechanisms judged by the evidence on the record. And the field's reading the same terrain — the ecosystem's radar names memory governance the next competitive battleground, both projects moving from "memory storage" to "memory governance" (trust, budget, audit, access pipeline), the middleware window opening (big_model_radar's report). The discussion's timely, and the evidence's on the record.

## The proposal

The network, each piece in its home — and the connections between them, the way the threads framed it: the bounded read is the anchor the whole thing hangs from; the restore is the retrieval the listening mechanism rides on; the dreaming prototype (the quiet-hours consolidation, the session preservation cycle) and the compression work (the K-recency and provenance on the compaction path) live in their own homes, never stretching the anchor's scope; and the scroll-up's re-read is the read action's second life — a correction triggers a re-read, not a request to scroll up and dig it out, the agent scrolling up itself instead of asking twice. One network, each piece in its place, the connections load-bearing.

1. **The bounded read** (#116673 — owner: Finn763) — the chain-doc reference + the read/patch semantics, as scoped.
2. **The read action's restore** (#141876 — owner: c0wb0yp0tat0) — the retrieval the listening mechanism rides on; the 14-line reversal of 56ee8a5cc6.
3. **The three in-scope complements** — the reference-as-provenance framing, the recency-ordered read, the scroll-up's re-read.
4. **The governed compaction** (the separate issue — relates to #116564, the parent gap) — the provenance-origin classification, the archive-before-stub, the K-recency hard window.

## The acceptance criteria

Proposed from the battery on disk; the team's to sign off the thresholds:

- [x] The read-action battery goes RED→GREEN at the restore (the verified flip: 23 failed → 35 passed) — the sandbox's run verified it end-to-end.
- [x] The stress battery's floors hold after the restore: 200/200 write-then-read, 800/800 concurrency survivors (0 corrupt), 100/100 re-read idempotence, 20/20 over-budget refusals — the runs on disk.
- [x] The K-recency window's falsifier: it measurably improves exact-recitation at the 4×/8×/16× headline ratios (the +2.2/+1.1/+2.3pp held) — the gain's on the runs.
- [x] The long-session hard gate — PASS/FAIL, not an open question. At 300+ agent cycles the K-recency window's exact-recitation must sit ≥ 0pp vs the K=0 baseline — never below — measured at the compression ratios production sessions actually run (4×–8×), evaluated across the whole run, not at the headline ratio alone. Any single measured point in the 300+ band below baseline at any ratio in 4×–8× fails the gate. This is the field's bar (3oltan-seo): a multi-hour production contour does not ship on a short-session extrapolation.
  - Status today: FAIL. The current data does not clear it — 300-cycle, K=10 landed 6.1% vs the 9.6% baseline (−3.5pp), below the line. The 150-cycle falsifier passing is necessary but not sufficient.
  - The honest caveat — the ruler's broken, the gate's not waived. The −3.5pp isn't the final word, and it isn't grounds to waive the gate. Across the runs the 300-cycle delta was non-reproducible (−9.2 to +10.2pp), root tracing to a scope bug in the probe itself — the measurement, not the window, was confounded. Under mock-forced paraphrase the window held stable at +1.1pp. So today's result is a broken ruler, not a reading: it can't certify the window safe, nor broken. Both the −3.5pp headline and the +1.1pp mock-stable are disqualified as certifying evidence until the probe's fixed. The gate stands — the Governance Decay reproduction (recency eviction → 100% violation, arXiv 2606.22528, DeepSeek-V4) is exactly the tail a soft gate lets through.
  - Measurement protocol: (1) fix the probe's scope bug first, no certifying run on the old probe; (2) sweep to and past 300 cycles to the field's longest contour, fixed K=10; (3) report per-cycle/per-bin Δ at every ratio in 4×–8× plus the headline ratios — the whole curve, not the endpoint; (4) baseline named and fixed; (5) paraphrase real, not mocked, for the certifying run (mock +1.1pp is a sanity check only); (6) judged on the worst case, not the mean — pass only if minimum Δ over all cycles ≥300 is ≥0pp at every 4×–8× ratio; one sub-zero point = FAIL.
- [x] Provenance survives the compression: a compacted unit carries a resolvable origin back to its archived original (the SJC 83% guard) — the governed-compaction leg, staged in its own home.

## The open questions

- Does the K-recency window scale with the session length? (The long-session reversal's a real finding: −3.5pp at 300 turns — the window must scale.)
- Should the caller's provenance default to "unknown" at the pipeline's definition, not just the call site?
- Where does the reroute-to-chain-doc seam land — this pipeline's follow-up or the governed compaction's home?

## The invited reviewers

The people I'm grateful for — the ones who engaged with me on GitHub as I'm new to the surface and have learned so much from every single interaction. This is a thank you, and a come-join-the-talk: the door's open to the room, and the invitations themselves go in the opening comment when this posts, where the @-mentions notify. This section is the record:

- @Finn763 — the bounded read's author ([#116673](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/116673)), the thread's owner
- @uni5592427 — the acceptance pipeline's author ([#135039](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/135039))
- @jimy-r · @RemanenetSpy — the thread's designers
- @alt-glitch · @teknium1 — the engaged, the field's voices
- @whyyagswhy — the restore's verifier, the RFC's referrer
- @xngg1021 — the one-shot bug work's helper, the classes' checks, the early-on confirmation that I was on the right track — a special thank you
- @binhnt92 — the early gut instinct of calling it out, the thread's first nudge — a special thank you
- @binhnt92 · @George-RD · @Enough1122 · @area51tazz · @xlionjuan · @3oltan-seo · @icegs · @GottZ · @liuhao1024 · @kvnloo · @jfugalde — the direct network's members and engagers
- @ZacharyThomasStone · @Im4EverDead — the trust circle

The invitation's the general engagement's — never the VIP treatment, never the exclusion — the door's open to the room.

## The two-way doors

Each decision's stated reversible with the available data; the direction's the room's:

1. **The K-recency window's size-and-scaling** — reversible (a window's a parameter; scale it with the session or fix it and re-measure). The −3.5pp@300-turn finding makes this the live one.
2. **The provenance default = "unknown" at the pipeline definition** — reversible (a default's a line change).
3. **The reroute-to-chain-doc seam's placement** — reversible (follow-up vs. compaction home; the open question above).
4. **The three complements' framing** (reference-as-provenance, recency-ordered read, scroll-up re-read) — reversible with the available data.

**The one-way door, flagged so it's not missed:** the archive-before-stub's *archive* side's cheap to reverse (the original's on disk); the *stub* side, once a working copy's replaced, leans on the archive's resolvability. Keep the archive-before the stub, always — that ordering's the only part that isn't freely reversible.

## The ownership

- The bounded read (#116673) — **Finn763**.
- The read action's restore (#141876) — **c0wb0yp0tat0**.
- The governed compaction (the separate issue, relates #116564) — staged in the pivot draft; the issue's to be opened by its author.

## The follow-up

The enrichment process with the teams follows the discussion's decision. The verification leg: the RED→GREEN re-run on the substrate, the stress battery's re-tally post-restore, the K-recency falsifier at the signed-off ratios, the long-session scaling probe, the provenance-survival end-to-end on the compaction issue.

## The no-blame note

This is a review of the system's state, not the actors'. The removal was a decision made in good faith (56ee8a5cc6, @teknium1); the 6,275 lines of compensation were the class's best effort at a root the decision didn't name. The design's elegance deserves the naming: the read's absence at the memory-store level, the fewer hops, the streamlined system — the 14 lines that would have been the amplifier it was designed to be. And the same class, done by hand on a single machine — a headless workstation that peaked during the Obama administration — the teams and the silicon that made it happen — the same amplifier, the same gift. The field's own version of the same class: $19K of tokens → $1.8M of value (Teknium1's refactoring post).

And the honest note, stated plainly: this is my first time running one of these — the process's etiquette is as new to me as the open-source rhythm was — so the direct feedback is the gift, and the door stays open either way.

issues.title: pre_tool_call shell hook with fail_closed: false still blocks every tool for 60s after one timeout (dispatcher wrapper fails closed, ignores matcher)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: comp/plugins
labels.description: Plugin system and bundled plugins

labels.name: area/config
labels.description: Config system, migrations, profiles

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
## Summary

A `pre_tool_call` **shell hook** configured `fail_closed: false` with a `matcher` can still block **every** tool call, of every type, for 60 s after a single timeout. The plugin dispatcher wraps the shell hook in its own bounded callback. That wrapper times out at the same 30 s and then applies its own fail-closed policy for `pre_tool_call`. The shell hook's `fail_closed: false` and its `matcher` never get a say.

Version: `Hermes Agent v0.21.5+5778.g0a374d1 (2026.9.24)` on Windows 11.

## Configuration

```yaml
hooks:
  pre_tool_call:
    - matcher: terminal|execute_code
      command: python <HERMES_HOME>/agent-hooks/require-command-purpose.py
      timeout: 30
      fail_closed: false
```

`plugins.hook_callback_timeout` is unset, so it takes the default of 30 s.

## What happened

One invocation of the hook stalled. The cause is unknown; normally it returns in well under a second. Two cron agent runs were in flight:

```
05:05:45,961 WARNING hermes_cli.plugins: Hook 'pre_tool_call' callback shell_hook[pre_tool_call:python …/require-command-purpose.py] timed out after 30s — skipping
05:05:46,222 WARNING agent.shell_hooks: shell hook timed out after 30.27s (event=pre_tool_call command=python …/require-command-purpose.py)
05:05:48,456 WARNING hermes_cli.plugins: Hook 'pre_tool_call' callback shell_hook[…] skipped after previous timeout or while still running
05:05:54,101 WARNING agent.tool_executor: Tool read_file returned error (0.02s): {"error": "pre_tool_call plugin callback timed out or is still running"}
05:05:59,470 WARNING agent.tool_executor: Tool search_files returned error (0.02s): {"error": "pre_tool_call plugin callback timed out or is still running"}
05:06:05,696 WARNING agent.tool_executor: Tool write_file returned error (0.02s): {"error": "pre_tool_call plugin callback timed out or is still running"}
```

From 05:05:46 until both runs gave up at 05:06:11, every tool call was refused: `terminal` (even `echo ok`), `read_file`, `search_files` and `write_file`. That's 16 refusals in total. Both runs ended having done nothing.

## Why (as read in `hermes_cli/plugins_dispatch.py` at this version)

1. The shell hook is registered as an ordinary plugin `pre_tool_call` callback. `invoke_hook` runs it through `_run_hook_callback_bounded` with `plugins.hook_callback_timeout`, which defaults to 30 s, the **same** value as the hook's own `timeout: 30`.
2. The dispatcher's wait expires first: 45.961 vs the shell layer's 46.222. It returns `_HOOK_SKIPPED`, and since `pre_tool_call` is in `_HOOK_TIMEOUT_FAIL_CLOSED_HOOKS`, it appends `{"action": "block", "message": _PRE_TOOL_CALL_TIMEOUT_BLOCK_MESSAGE}` (lines ~229-234). The shell hook's own `fail_closed: false` handling in `agent/shell_hooks.py` never gets to return its fail-open result.
3. The timeout also sets `_hook_timeout_suppressed_until` for `_HOOK_TIMEOUT_SUPPRESSION_SECONDS = 60`. For the next 60 s, every `pre_tool_call` dispatch skips the callback and blocks (lines ~282-289).
4. The callback is skipped **before** the shell hook's matcher is evaluated, so tools outside `matcher: terminal|execute_code` are blocked too.

## Expected

- **Respect `fail_closed: false`:** a shell hook with `fail_closed: false` should fail **open** however it times out. That covers the dispatcher's wrapper too, and the suppression window after a timeout.
- **Respect the matcher:** tools that don't match the hook's `matcher` should never be gated by that hook's timeout or suppression state.
- **Don't race the two timeouts:** the dispatcher's timeout for a shell-hook callback should be longer than the shell hook's own `timeout`, so the shell layer's decision is the one that counts. Alternatively, the dispatcher shouldn't double-wrap shell hooks at all.

## Workaround

Set `plugins.hook_callback_timeout` above the shell hook's `timeout` (for example 45 with `timeout: 30`). Then the shell layer times out first and its `fail_closed: false` applies. The matcher problem (point 4) remains whenever the dispatcher's timeout does fire.

## Related

- #131857 covers a different way shell hooks hang (helper processes keeping pipes open).
- #100942 is about blocking hooks failing **open** under a non-TTY gateway. This is the opposite direction.

issues.title: Plugin admission fails for any plugin with Python deps: core uv.lock cannot be re-resolved for the sys_platform == 'android' split

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: area/install-update
labels.description: Installer, updater, packaging, wheels, doctor

issues.body:
## Summary

Any plugin with Python dependencies (for example the official `homeassistant` catalog plugin, which needs `aiohttp`) gets refused at admission:

```
Plugin 'homeassistant' conflicts with the dependencies pinned by Hermes core or an enabled plugin, so it was not admitted. Resolver: uv lock exited 1: for split (markers: python_full_version == '3.14.*' and sys_platform == 'android')
  cause: Because playwright==1.62.0 has no `python_full_version >= '3.14'`-compatible wheels and hermes-agent[google-meet] depends on playwright==1.62.0, we can conclude that hermes-agent[google-meet]'s requirements are unsatisfiable.
         And because your workspace requires hermes-agent[google-meet], we can conclude that your workspace's requirements are unsatisfiable.
```

The plugin did not cause this. Core's own lock cannot be re-resolved.

## Root cause

- `[tool.uv] environments = ["python_version >= '3.14'"]` includes Android. Because of the `psutil` Android marker, uv forks an `android` split.
- The committed `uv.lock` only passes `uv lock --check` because uv reuses it as-is.
- `pm/workspace.py::_generate_pyproject` adds workspace members and drops `exclude-newer` (`_without_release_age`), which forces a full re-resolve ("Resolving despite existing lockfile due to removal of global exclude newer").
- uv resolves every extra of every workspace member universally. In the Android split, some extras have no compatible wheels:
  - `google-meet` → `playwright==1.62.0` (no Android wheels)
  - `stt-whisper` → `faster-whisper` → `onnxruntime` (no cp314 Android wheels). This one shows up after `google-meet` is marked out.
  - There may be more.

## Reproduction (no plugin needed)

Tested on `7ac2c6dc29` with uv 0.13.5, CPython 3.14.7, linux aarch64. `origin/main` as of 2026-10-23 has the same `environments` and `google-meet` lines.

```bash
cp pyproject.toml uv.lock /tmp/repro/ && cd /tmp/repro
uv lock --check                     # OK: "Resolved 328 packages"
sed -i '/^exclude-newer/d' pyproject.toml
uv lock                             # FAILS: same playwright / android-split error
```

Adding a workspace member such as `members/ha` (a pyproject with `aiohttp>=3.9,<4`) fails the same way, even when `exclude-newer` is kept.

## Workaround that works

```toml
[tool.uv]
environments = ["python_version >= '3.14' and sys_platform != 'android'"]
```

With this change the workspace resolves ("Added hermes-homeassistant v2.0.1"), and `hermes plugins enable homeassistant` succeeds.

## Possible fixes

1. Exclude Android from `tool.uv.environments`, if Termux/Android doesn't need a locked PM environment.
2. Or add `sys_platform != 'android'` markers to every extra that has no Android wheels (`google-meet`, `stt-whisper`, and probably others), plus a CI job that runs a fresh `uv lock` without `exclude-newer` and with a dummy workspace member. That catches the case where the committed lock only works because uv reuses it.

issues.title: [Feature]: Quote-and-Ask — select generated content, add it to a task, and get anchored annotations (like Codex desktop)
issues.body: ### Problem or Use Case Hermes responses are often long and structured — multi-step plans with rules, exclusions and rollback schemes, or step-by-step annotated code walkthroughs. In practice, users frequently want to drill into **one specific sentence** of such a response, either to ask a follow-up about it or to turn it into an annotated, actionable item. For example: - "Why does this step require a restart? Can we avoid it?" - "What does this config flag actually do?" - "Why was this item added to the exclusion list?" **Reference behavior (prior art):** the OpenAI **Codex desktop app** already supports exactly this pattern — the user selects a portion of the generated content, can choose **"add to task"**, and the system then **outputs an annotation anchored to that selection**. This makes long agent outputs far easier to review and act on. In Hermes, the only workflow today is to manually copy the sentence and paste it into the next prompt wrapped in quotes. This has several problems: 1. **Loss of positional context** — in a 20-step plan, the model cannot reliably tell *which* step is being referenced, leading to ambiguous or generic answers. 2. **Tedious and error-prone** — especially in the terminal or on mobile, where text selection and copy/paste are awkward. 3. **Breaks after context compression** — manually re-pasted quotes lose their linkage to the original message, so session retrieval (SQLite) and MEMORY.md cannot resolve exactly what was referenced. ### Proposed Solution Implement a Codex-desktop-style **"select → attach → annotate"** workflow: 1. **Selection in the response viewer (Desktop/Web UI):** allow selecting any text (or clicking a per-paragraph / per-sentence "quote" icon). 2. **Two actions from the selection:** - **Ask about it** — opens an inline input pre-filled with the selection as a blockquote, for a targeted follow-up question. - **Add to task** — attaches the selection as an item to the current task/plan (to-do, review comment, or follow-up), and the agent **outputs an annotation** (a short explanation/comment) anchored to the selected content. 3. **Anchor metadata:** store the follow-up/annotation with a reference to the source message ID + text offsets (or step/line number). This lets the agent resolve exactly which sentence is referenced, and lets SQLite session retrieval recover the anchor even after context compression. 4. **Rendering:** display annotations and quoted references above the reply (or inline in the plan view), clickable to scroll back to the original sentence. 5. **CLI equivalent:** a command such as `/quote ` (or a `#:` prefix), so terminal users get the same workflow. This would compose naturally with Hermes' existing strengths — the three-layer memory architecture and temporary-agent plan output are exactly the kind of long, structured responses where sentence-level anchoring pays off the most. ### Alternatives Considered - **Manual copy-paste with quotation marks:** works today, but no anchoring, ambiguous in long outputs, and clunky on mobile/terminal. - **Asking the model to re-print the relevant section first:** doubles tokens and latency; compressed sessions may paraphrase and lose exact wording. - **Referencing earlier messages via session retrieval:** message-level granularity only, and it doesn't cover the live-conversation case. - **Implementing as a fork/plugin on the open-source Web UI:** technically possible (MIT license), but native support would ensure consistent anchoring across Desktop / Web / CLI and keep the quote/annotation data model maintained upstream. ### Feature Type New tool ### Scope Medium (few files, < 300 lines) ### Contribution - [x] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR ### Debug Report (optional) ```shell ```

issues.body:
**Verified during a line-by-line audit (2026-10-14).** Three chained issues in pm/ where lock/state file values are used as path/env components without shape validation:

1. **HIGH — arbitrary directory deletion** (`pm/store.py:379-388`, `pm/install.py:289-292`): `lock.json` artifact `sha256` is concatenated into `fetch-{sha}` entry names with no `^[a-f0-9]{64}$ ` validation. A value like `../../../x` normalizes outside the store root; both `fetch_many`'s `shutil.rmtree(entry)` and `_remove_downloads` will then recursively delete attacker-chosen paths. Reproduced that normalization escapes the store root. Fix: fail-closed regex validation at `Lockfile.artifacts()`, and assert entry names are single path components before any remove.

2. **MEDIUM — process env injection** (`pm/lock.py:225-229`): `facts.json` `entry`/`env` used without the validation that `refresh_digests` applies — `entry` can traverse, and arbitrary `env` keys (LD_PRELOAD / DYLD_* / PATH) flow into every PM subprocess via `compose_env`. Fix: reuse the entry charset check and deny loader/path-class env keys.

3. **MEDIUM — https-only/loopback gate bypass** (`pm/downloader.py:49,62,293`): the loopback check is a string prefix test — `http://127.0.0.1:@evil.com/payload` passes (verified `startswith=True` while the real host is evil.com), allowing plaintext fetches to remote hosts. Fix: parse with `urllib.parse.urlsplit`, require scheme https and hostname in {127.0.0.1, ::1, localhost}, and reject userinfo.

Lower-severity siblings (filename traversal in `store.py:387`, generation parsing in `runtime.py:147-156`, `pm update --npm` missing `--ignore-scripts` in `cli.py:652`, publish race in `store.py:415-434`, `hash_url` scheme in `store.py:168-191`) can ride along in the same fix.

issues.title: [Bug] shared-metrics store: recurring SQLite header mangling with intact body + no self-heal on NOTADB (traceback spam at every tool dispatch)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
### Summary

The shared-metrics store (telemetry/shared_metrics/metrics.sqlite3) can end up with a mangled SQLite header while its body stays intact, and SharedMetricsStore has **no recovery path** — every metrics touch then raises sqlite3.DatabaseError (file is not a database) with a full traceback, spamming logs at each tool dispatch and silently losing all telemetry counters.

### Reproduction / evidence (local install, 2026-10-24)

Second occurrence in 11 days on the same install (previous instance quarantined by hand on 2026-10-13):

- metrics.sqlite3 (1,040,384 bytes) and metrics.sqlite3.corrupt_20261013 (1,978,368 bytes) both fail sqlite3 with "file is not a database".
- Byte-probe of the first 16 bytes (both files):

  current:  [83,81,76,105,116,23,3,3,0,19,168,163,171,14,255,206]
  expected: [83,81,76,105,116,101,32,102,111,114,109,97,116,32,51,0] ("SQLite format 3\0")
  20261013: [83,81,76,105,116,23,3,3,0,19,49,241,40,56,63,8]

  Note the identical 10-byte prefix ("SQLit" + 23,3,3,0,19) in both damaged files, then divergent bytes — deterministic-looking mangling, not random torn-write noise.
- Body is intact: page 2 (offset 4096) starts with 0x0d (valid leaf table page), "CREATE TABLE" x5 and the schema table names (telemetry_state, counter_aggregates, ...) survive inside page 1. Only the header region is toast.
- All sibling databases (state.db, kanban.db, shared-state.db, projects.db) have correct magic — the damage is specific to this one file.
- A freshly created store via SharedMetricsStore writes the correct magic, so the writer itself is fine; something external mangles the head afterwards. Filesystem is clean (no ext4/IO errors in journal), so not disk-level corruption.
- Environment: Linux x86_64, Python 3.14.9 (pm-managed runtime), SQLite 3.53.1, tree at 5894e750c3. The install runs a heavily-patched tree, but no local patch touches this store or any VFS layer.

### Impact

1. Telemetry silently stops (all counter writes fail).
2. A multi-line traceback is emitted at essentially every tool dispatch (six dumps in one small probe run) — log spam and wasted work on a hot path.
3. It never self-heals: the corrupt file stays in place forever until a human quarantines it by hand.

### Suggested fix

1. Self-heal on init: when _ensure_schema (or the first open) hits a DatabaseError whose message matches "file is not a database" / "database disk image is malformed", quarantine the file (rename to metrics.sqlite3.corrupt_<timestamp>, keep the newest N for forensics) and rebuild the schema once, then continue.
2. Root cause is still open — the identical 10-byte damaged prefix across two files 11 days apart suggests a deterministic writer rather than a torn write. Happy to collect more forensics (fs snapshots, strace on candidate writers) if someone has a hypothesis to test.

### Local mitigation already applied (for reference)

We shipped the self-heal locally (quarantine + rebuild + cap 5 quarantines, logging at WARNING). Verified live: init on the damaged file now quarantines it to metrics.sqlite3.corrupt_20261024T031246Z, rebuilds a healthy 5-table store, and the gateway's writes flow again immediately. The 128 tests in tests/hermes_cli/test_shared_metrics_signals.py + test_shared_metrics_sender.py + test_shared_metrics_send_wiring.py stay green with the change.

issues.body:
### Bug Description

On Windows, `hermes backup` reports a partial archive and exits 1 on every run while the wake-word microphone lease is live, because `$HERMES_HOME/runtime/wake-word.lock` is held with a **1-byte byte-range lock** and a byte-range-locked file cannot be *read* by another handle at all.

`tools/wake_word.py` takes a machine-wide lease on the mic: `_acquire_machine_lock()` opens the lock file `a+b`, writes a single `\0` byte if empty, and `_flock()` (Windows branch) calls `msvcrt.locking(fileno, LK_NBLCK, 1)` — i.e. an exclusive lock over **1 byte starting at offset 0**. On Windows, `LockFile`-style byte-range locks are mandatory: any other process reading that range gets `ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION`, which CPython surfaces as `PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied`. Python's `zipfile.write()` therefore cannot even open the member for reading, `_write_zip_entries()` appends it to `errors`, `run_backup()` returns `False`, and `cmd_backup()` exits 1.

`runtime/` is not a policy exclusion (`_EXCLUDED_ROOT_DIRS` = `{"models", "runtimes", "node"}`; `_EXCLUDED_NAMES` = `{".backup.lock", "gateway.pid", "cron.pid"}`), so `runtime/*.lock` is selected for archiving even though it is machine-local state that no restore would ever want.

This is the same exit-status problem as #118062 and #93374, but with a different, *deterministic* trigger: not a file vanishing mid-archive, but a file that is permanently unreadable for as long as the lease holder runs. It is not intermittent — with `wake_word.enabled: true` it fires every night. Consequences seen here: a wrapper that treats exit 1 as "backup failed" aborted before copying the archive off-machine (4 nights without an off-site copy), and `--keep` pruning is skipped because it is gated on `not errors`.

### Steps to Reproduce

Windows 11, git install, `wake_word.enabled: true` in `config.yaml`, gateway running (it holds the lease).

1. Confirm the lease is held and the file is unreadable. In Python:
   `python -c "open(r'%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\runtime\wake-word.lock','rb').read()"`
   → `PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied`
   (git-bash `cat` on the same path: `cat: ...: Device or resource busy`.)
2. Run a full backup:
   `hermes backup -o E:\Backups\hermes\test.zip -k 0`
3. Observe the summary and the shell exit status.

Root cause is visible in one line: `tools/wake_word.py` `_flock()` takes `msvcrt.locking(..., LK_NBLCK, 1)` over 1 byte, and Windows enforces byte-range locks against readers too. Only the lease holder (the gateway process) can release it, and it does so only when the wake-word detector stops.

### Expected Behavior

Runtime lock/pid files that live only on the source machine are policy exclusions (like `gateway.pid` / `cron.pid` / `.backup.lock`) and are never selected, so the run reports `Backup complete` and exits 0. The archive is provably complete in this case: 2761 members, `ZipFile.testzip()` returns `None`, and `config.yaml`, `.env`, `state.db` (exact root member), `SOUL.md`, `memories/MEMORY.md`, `cron/jobs.json` are all present.

Suggested fix, in order of preference:

1. Exclude it as policy: add `"wake-word.lock"` to `_EXCLUDED_NAMES` in `hermes_cli/backup.py` (minimal), or more generally skip `*.lock` / `*.pid` files directly under a root `runtime/` directory — deterministic and race-free.
2. Optionally also treat `PermissionError` on members under `runtime/` as a benign skip instead of an incomplete archive, as a belt-and-braces measure.

### Actual Behavior

```
  Archive kept, but 1 file(s) could not be added:
  runtime\wake-word.lock: [Errno 13] Permission denied
```

Exit status `1`. `Backup incomplete:` is printed although the only excluded member is a 1-byte runtime lock file. On this host nightly cron output for 2026-10-21, 2026-10-22, 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-24 is identical to the above; the same message shows intermittently in earlier runs (2026-10-07, -08, -14, -15), i.e. whenever a wake-word listener was active at midnight.

Environment: Hermes Agent v0.22.0+119.g0e427d7 (2026.9.24) · stable · git install · Windows 11 · Python 3.11 (bundled venv).

**What changed**

Since recent main (seen on 0.22.4+222, commit 7ac2c6dc29), `admit_api_turn` in `gateway/session_api_turn.py` refuses any API turn whose target session's `source` is not `api_server` or `bot_room`:

    if existing is not None and existing['source'] not in ('api_server', 'bot_room'):
        raise RuntimeStoreError('permission_denied')

Earlier builds (e.g. d94b70f675) accepted `POST /v1/runs` with `session_id` set to a session started in the desktop app, and the turn ran normally.

**Why it matters**

A self-hosted API client (a phone front end on the same machine and profile, using the server's own API key) lets the user pick up any of their sessions and keep going. Now every session started in the desktop app, CLI or a messaging platform is read-only from the API, and the client only sees a generic 409 `permission_denied`.

**Request**

An opt-in config setting, for example `api_server.allow_foreign_session_turns: true` (default off), that skips this check for the authenticated API key. Turns would still go through the normal session FIFO, so they queue behind a live desktop turn rather than racing it.

If the restriction is meant to stay, a more specific error code (e.g. `foreign_session_source`) would let clients explain it to the user.

Happy to test a branch.

labels.name: type/bug

labels.description: Plugin system and bundled plugins

labels.name: P2

issues.body:
## Summary

In Discord, the `/model` picker's confirmation embed is overwritten with **"⏱ Selection expired — no model change."** about two minutes after a *successful* switch. The model change itself is real (asking the agent which model it is on confirms it), but the visible record of what was selected is replaced with a message saying nothing changed.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In a Discord channel, run `/model`, pick a provider, then pick a model.
2. The embed correctly changes to the green "Model Switched" confirmation.
3. Wait ~120s after the last click.
4. The embed is edited to "⏱ Selection expired — no model change."

Cancelling the picker has the same problem: the "cancelled" embed is later overwritten with "expired".

## Cause

`ModelPickerView` (`plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py`) is created with `timeout=120`.

- `_switch_selected_model` sets `self.resolved = True`, clears the items and edits the message with `view=None`, but never calls `self.stop()`. discord.py's view timeout therefore keeps running.
- `on_timeout` doesn't check `self.resolved`. It sets `resolved = True` itself and then unconditionally `msg.edit(...)`s the original message with the `picker.expired` embed.
- `_on_cancel` has the same omission.

`ChoicePickerView` (used by `/reasoning` and `/fast`) already does this correctly: it calls `self.stop()` on selection, and its `on_timeout` begins with `if self.resolved: return`.

## Fix

- `ModelPickerView.on_timeout`: return early if `self.resolved` (before the existing `self.resolved = True` line).
- Call `self.stop()` at the end of `_switch_selected_model` and `_on_cancel`.

I have this working locally with regression tests (timeout after a completed switch, timeout after cancel, and a guard that an untouched picker still expires). The shared `_FakeView` in `tests/gateway/conftest.py` needed `stop()`/`is_finished()` to match discord.py. Happy to open a PR if that's useful.

<details><summary>Diff</summary>

```diff
diff --git a/plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py b/plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py
index f5d39af68d..b1a1289cd7 100644
--- a/plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py
+++ b/plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py
@@ -6742,6 +6742,7 @@ def _define_discord_view_classes() -> None:
                 embed=self._config_embed(result_text, title=t("platform.discord.picker.switched_title"), color=discord.Color.green()),
                 view=None,
             )
+            self.stop()  # cancel the timeout so on_timeout can't overwrite the confirmation
 
         async def _on_model_selected(self, interaction: discord.Interaction):
             if not await self._gate(interaction, resolved_msg=t("platform.discord.picker.already_resolved"), unauth_msg=_unauthorized()):
@@ -6783,8 +6784,11 @@ def _define_discord_view_classes() -> None:
             self.resolved = True
             self.clear_items()
             await self._edit(interaction, t("platform.discord.picker.cancelled"), color=discord.Color.greyple())
+            self.stop()
 
         async def on_timeout(self):
+            if self.resolved:
+                return  # already switched or cancelled; keep that message
             self.resolved = True
             self.clear_items()
             msg = self._message
```

</details>

Observed on Hermes 0.22.5 (`bf0203a7`), Linux, Discord adapter.

issues.title: Slack: handle agent_session_stopped — the native stop button does nothing today

labels.name: type/bug

issues.body:
Slack shows a native stop button while an agent session has the `processing` status. The Slack adapter does not subscribe to the `agent_session_stopped` event. A search of `main` at `c47f0b4590e6` returns no match for `agent_session_stopped`.

Slack states: "All apps that manage agent sessions must handle this event". Support for stop is not optional.

## Why this affects every Slack deployment

The adapter enables native streaming by default, with no configuration gate (`plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py`, the `_native_stream_unsupported` path). Slack's compatibility bridge states that apps which use the streaming methods "participate in the sessions UX without code changes by automatically creating sessions".

As a result, any Hermes Slack app with AI features enabled already has agent sessions and already shows a stop button. This is not limited to apps that use `agent_view`.

## What happens today

When a user clicks stop, three results occur:

1. The agent continues to run. No work stops.
2. The session status stays at `processing`. Slack does not change it.
3. The status clears one hour later, at the Slack timeout.

The user sees a control that has no effect. The gateway continues to spend tokens on a turn that the user stopped.

## Event payload

```json
{
  "type": "agent_session_stopped",
  "channel": "C123ABC456",
  "thread_ts": "1782234671.392669",
  "message_ts": "1782234987.693923",
  "user": "U123ABC456",
  "team_id": "T0123ABC456",
  "event_ts": "1783536983.783769"
}
```

## Suggested change

1. Subscribe to `agent_session_stopped` in the Slack adapter.
2. Stop the work in progress for the `channel` and `thread_ts` in the payload.
3. Send the session out of `processing` with `agents.sessions.setStatus` or `chat.stopStream`.
4. Tell the user that the work stopped.
5. Use the cancellation path of the `/stop` command. Do not add a second path.

## Note

Slack does not change the session status when the user clicks stop. The app must change it.

## Related

The adapter still calls the legacy `assistant.threads.setStatus` (`adapter.py:3442`, `:3523`) and `assistant.threads.setTitle` (`:5105`). Slack replaces these with `agents.sessions.setStatus` and `agents.sessions.rename`, and deprecates the Assistant messaging experience in February 2027. A compatibility bridge covers them until then. The two changes touch the same call sites, so one pull request can carry both.

This fits the Slack Feature Parity campaign (#79772), whose stated goal is alignment with the official Slack platform. No lane covers agent sessions today.

## References

- [`agent_session_stopped`](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/events/agent_session_stopped)
- [Stopping a session](https://docs.slack.dev/ai/agent-sessions#stopping)
- [Migrating to the Agent messaging experience](https://docs.slack.dev/ai/migrating-to-agent-messaging/)

issues.body:
## Problem or Use Case

When running Hermes in CLI mode (`hermes --tui`), there is currently no way to detach from the interactive session while letting the agent continue processing in the background.

Existing related commands don't cover this use case:

- **`/background` (`/bg`)** — Runs a prompt in a separate background session, but the user stays in the current TUI. The original session is still occupied.
- **`/branch` (`/fork`)** — Forks the current session into a new one, but both the original and the forked session are still within the same interactive TUI.
- **`/btw`** — Ephemeral side-question, no background execution.

**Real-world scenario:** A user kicks off a long-running task (e.g., a large code refactor, data processing pipeline, or multi-step research task) and wants to close the terminal without losing progress. Currently the only option is to keep the terminal open, or use external tools like `tmux`/`screen` manually.

## Proposed Solution

Add a new `/detach` slash command that:

1. **On invocation:** The current agent session transitions to a background process (daemon/detached mode). The agent continues executing whatever task it was given.
2. **CLI exits cleanly:** The TUI/interactive shell returns to the system prompt, freeing the terminal.
3. **Re-attach later:** Optionally, a way to re-attach to the detached session later (e.g., `hermes attach` or `hermes chat --resume`).

**Suggested behavior:**

```
hermes> /detach
Detaching session abc123...
Agent is running in background.
Use `hermes attach abc123` or `hermes chat --resume abc123` to re-attach.
```

**Implementation ideas:**

- On `/detach`, spawn the agent loop as a detached child process (using `start_new_session=True` or similar), persisting the session ID and state to `~/.hermes/sessions/`.
- The TUI process exits normally after handing off to the background process.
- A new CLI subcommand `hermes attach <session-id>` (or extending `hermes chat --resume`) reconnects to the running background session.
- Alternatively, integrate with tmux/screen under the hood — create a detached tmux session running `hermes chat --resume <id>` and inform the user how to re-attach (`tmux attach -t hermes-abc123`).

**Re-attach via messaging platforms:** If the user has gateway/messaging integrations (Telegram, Discord, WeChat) configured, the detached session could continue communicating through those channels. The user would receive responses and could interact with the agent via their messaging platform without needing to re-attach to the CLI at all.

## Alternatives Considered

1. **Tell users to use `tmux`/`screen` manually** — Works but is not user-friendly and requires external tool knowledge. A built-in `/detach` would provide a seamless experience.
2. **Use `/background` + close terminal** — `/bg` spawns a separate session but doesn't cleanly detach the TUI. Killing the terminal would also kill the background process since they share the same process group.
3. **systemd user service** — Overkill for interactive sessions; doesn't fit the ad-hoc nature of chat sessions.
4. **`nohup hermes --tui &`** — Clunky, loses the interactive nature. The whole point is to detach mid-session, not start in detached mode.

## Feature Type

CLI improvement

## Scope

Medium (few files, < 300 lines)

## Additional Context

This feature is inspired by the `tmux detach` pattern and would bring Hermes CLI closer to a true daemon-mode experience. It complements the existing `/background` command:

| Command | Stays in TUI? | Agent keeps running? | Use case |
|---------|:---:|:---:|----------|
| `/background` | Yes | Yes (child session) | Multitask within one TUI |
| `/branch` | Yes | Yes (forked session) | Explore alternate paths |
| **`/detach`** | **No** | **Yes (same session)** | **Free terminal, keep agent running** |

The `/detach` command would be particularly useful for:
- Long-running tasks that don't need interactive monitoring
- Users who switch between CLI and messaging platforms
- Server/remote environments where keeping an SSH session open is impractical
