prs.title: fix(auth): recover expired Codex sessions without restarting
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A long-running Codex session can keep failing with HTTP 401 after Hermes has recovered a valid token from the Codex CLI or another process. The singleton guard compares bearer strings, so it rejects a rotated token even when both JWTs identify the same ChatGPT account and subject. Starting a new session works because it reads the recovered token.

Allow the existing one-shot 401 recovery to adopt that token when the original bearer is expired, the replacement has a known expiry beyond the refresh window, both principal claims match, the route is unchanged, and the replacement comes from the Hermes singleton. The shared client and client kwargs are rebuilt together, and the pool entry ID is rebound to the adopted bearer so a later 401 refreshes the correct grant. Adopting an already-live token avoids spending another single-use refresh token.

## Related Issue

Related: #142473 (long-lived Codex credential failures). This addresses the client adoption gap after singleton recovery; #143304 handles refreshing entries during unmatched pool rotation. #136695 covers following an explicit re-auth onto another account at a turn boundary.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Changes Made

- `agent/client_lifecycle.py`: retain principal and route isolation while allowing an expired Codex session to use a fresh same-principal singleton.
- `tests/agent/test_codex_rotated_session_credentials.py`: three behavior contracts cover actual store/CLI recovery and the SDK's outgoing bearer, one-shot retry, refusals for unrelated principals, routes, pool-only rows and unusable replacements, and correct grant attribution on a subsequent 401.

## How to Test

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_codex_rotated_session_credentials.py
python scripts/check --base 5894e750c3
```

- On base `5894e750c3`: 3 recovery/grant-attribution cases fail, 8 isolation cases pass.
- With this change: 11/11 regression cases pass.
- Related client lifecycle, Codex/xAI recovery, replay recovery, singleton isolation, route settings, fallback restoration and auth-store suites: 152 passed across 11 files.
- `scripts/check`: all 12 checks pass, including the code-health ratchet.
- Tested on Linux/WSL, Python 3.14.7. Auth-store resolution and SDK request construction are real; tests use synthetic tokens and `httpx.MockTransport`, without live OAuth grants. Native Windows/macOS and the complete test suite were not run.

## Checklist

- [x] Read the contributing guide; conventional commit; focused change.
- [x] Searched existing issues and PRs; checked the related work above.
- [x] Added regression tests and proved recovery fails on the base.
- [x] Focused test suites and all local blocking checks pass.
- [x] Considered profiles, account/workspace isolation and route binding.
- [x] No configuration, dependency, tool schema or user documentation changes required.

Implemented with Codex. Independently reviewed by a fresh Codex before submission; validation details are listed above.

prs.title: fix(anthropic): replay DeepSeek's own signed thinking blocks on /anthropic
prs.body:
fix(anthropic): DeepSeek /anthropic signs its own thinking blocks and requires them back

## What

On `https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic`, keep prior-turn `thinking` blocks on the
wire (signed or unsigned) and drop only `redacted_thinking`. Relays fronting a
DeepSeek model keep the existing strip-signed / keep-unsigned policy unchanged.

## Why

`_manage_thinking_signatures` treats any thinking block with a truthy `signature`
as Anthropic-proprietary and strips it on the DeepSeek route, assuming DeepSeek
cannot validate it. That assumption is wrong in the direction that breaks the
request: DeepSeek signs its **own** blocks (the signature is a UUID, e.g.
`76aef10f-3f0b-4e0b-a3ab-9656acd4b622` — observed in Hermes' own session store)
and REQUIRES them replayed when thinking mode is on. Stripping the block makes
the next call fail with HTTP 400:

    The `content[].thinking` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API.

Because that 400 classifies as `FailoverReason.format_error` (not retryable), the
turn silently falls back to another provider — or dies when no fallback is
reachable. Every multi-step tool loop on a DeepSeek thinking model is affected,
not just long conversations.

## Measured (live, against api.deepseek.com/anthropic, tool-loop shape)

| request | result |
|---|---|
| thinking present, unsigned | 200 |
| thinking present, signed (UUID) | 200 |
| thinking present, empty text + signature | 200 |
| thinking present + `cache_control` | 200 |
| **thinking absent** (what Hermes sent) | **400 `content[].thinking must be passed back`** |
| `redacted_thinking` | 422 `unknown variant \`redacted_thinking\`` |

And end-to-end through Hermes' own converter, replaying the canonical messages of
a real failing session (8 messages: user → assistant+tool_use → 4 tool results →
assistant → tool):

| converter | thinking blocks on the wire | result |
|---|---|---|
| before | 0 | HTTP 400 (the error above) |
| after | 2 (both signed) | HTTP 200 |

## Changes

- `agent/anthropic_message_convert.py`: on the `deepseek` route, branch on the
  endpoint. Real `api.deepseek.com/anthropic` keeps `thinking` and drops only
  `redacted_thinking`; a third-party relay carrying a DeepSeek id keeps the
  strip-signed / keep-unsigned policy of #17510 (a relay cannot verify
  Anthropic signatures).
- `tests/agent/test_deepseek_anthropic_thinking.py`: replaces the test that
  froze the old behaviour (`test_signed_anthropic_thinking_block_is_stripped`)
  with `test_presigned_deepseek_thinking_block_is_replayed`, and adds coverage
  for `redacted_thinking` being dropped and for the relay policy staying put.

## Tests

`scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_deepseek_anthropic_thinking.py tests/agent/test_anthropic_adapter.py tests/agent/test_anthropic_kimi_signed_thinking_replay.py tests/agent/test_kimi_coding_anthropic_thinking.py tests/agent/test_anthropic_thinking_block_order.py`

    5 files, 125 tests passed, 0 failed

## Context

- Real-world case: a daily 07:00 cron job on `deepseek-flash` (many tool turns)
  failed at the same point every day for 11 days straight — first silently via
  provider fallback, then fatally when the fallback was unavailable. The job
  still reported success, so nothing surfaced.
- Related: #17992 (same effect, root cause partly attributed to Anthropic-signed
  blocks), #29607 / #26774 (relays stripping blocks), #47685. #17991 proposed the
  same preservation for this endpoint and was closed without merge; #17510 fixed
  the unsigned half of the original #16748 report.

prs.title: fix(tools): stand down the own-tab preamble when browser-harness isolates natively
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Stops `browser_exec` from creating a redundant second tab for every named session on current `browser-harness` releases. Hermes' `_OWN_TAB_PREAMBLE` (#86924) pinned named sessions to their own tab because the stock harness attached named daemons to the first shared page; one day later browser-harness 0.1.9 shipped native named-daemon tab isolation (browser-use/browser-harness#618). With both layers active, the harness creates its dedicated tab AND the preamble creates a second target — one extra Chrome renderer (~8-11 Linux cgroup tasks) per named session, materially accelerating PID-cgroup exhaustion under parallel sessions (#91522).

The fix detects harness ≥ 0.1.9 inside the preamble itself (leading-numeric parse of `importlib.metadata.version("browser-harness")`) and returns before creating any target. The check lives in the preamble rather than in Hermes because the browser-harness package is installed in the CLI's environment, not necessarily in the gateway process. Pre-0.1.9 harnesses keep the compatibility pin; an unresolvable version falls back to the pin (pre-fix behavior is safe); private provider browsers keep skipping the preamble entirely, as before.

## Related Issue

Fixes #91522

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `tools/browser_use_cli.py`: Add `_NATIVE_TAB_ISOLATION_SINCE = (0, 1, 9)` (with a comment tying it to the embedded gate) and the `_parse_version_prefix` helper documenting the leading-numeric parse algorithm. Embed the version gate at the top of `_OWN_TAB_PREAMBLE::_hermes_ensure_own_tab`: on harness ≥ 0.1.9, return before any `Target.createTarget`; on parse failure, fall through to the pin.
- `tests/tools/test_browser_use_cli.py`: In `TestOwnTabPreamble`, add `test_preamble_stands_down_on_native_tab_isolation` (AST structural assertion: the gate's return precedes the createTarget call, and the embedded threshold matches the module constant) and `test_version_prefix_parser` (pure parser coverage: `0.1.9rc1` → gate, `0.1.8` → no gate, short/pre-release forms).

## How to Test

1. With browser-use 0.13.8+ (browser-harness 0.1.9+), start a fresh named `browser_exec` session against a shared CDP Chrome and diff `http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/list` before/after
2. Before the fix two page targets are created for one named session; after the fix exactly one is created and the named session's isolated current tab is preserved (matches the issue's patched live E2E: one target, isolation intact, target removed on idle cleanup)
3. With a pre-0.1.9 browser-harness, the compatibility pin still runs (Observed result: `test_version_prefix_parser` asserts `0.1.8 < threshold`)
4. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_browser_use_cli.py -q` → should pass except the pre-existing environment-dependent timeout test (Observed result: 93 passed, 1 failed — `test_timeout_returns_actionable_error` fails identically on unpatched main)

## What does this PR do?

With `display.tool_progress: "off"` and `display.streaming: true`, the CLI still prints `preparing tool_call…`, `preparing tool_describe…`, `preparing skill_view…`, and other tool names. The streaming setup registers `_on_tool_gen_start`, whose status output bypasses the configured progress mode.

prs.title: fix(kanban): a lost receipt is requeued, not booked as a crash
prs.body:
## Problem

`hermes_cli/kanban_worker_client.py::_submit_claim` raised `GatewayClientError('Kanban execution unknown; retained by owner')` the moment `prompt.receipt` answered `unknown` — **before** it ever read `worker_result()` back from the board.

`unknown` only says the receipt's answer was lost (an owner restart fences the admission that way). The board is a second ledger: when the worker settled before the fence, the attempt's terminal result is already there.

Real incident (local card t_0b026e13, 2026-10-22): run 27 finished its work and recorded `worker_result exit_code=0`; the review-lane submitters then polled `unknown` across an owner handoff, exited 1, and the dead-worker sweep booked `crashed`. Two retries later the card hit `failure_limit` and gave up — the work was done, the board said "blocked".

## Fix (two halves, both minimal)

1. `_submit_claim`: on `unknown`, read the board back first. A recorded `worker_result` under the same run + claim is returned as-is (exit 0 → the clean-exit class, i.e. the bounded protocol-violation path, not a crash).
2. Nothing on the board: exit the new sentinel `KANBAN_RECEIPT_UNKNOWN_EXIT_CODE` (79) instead of a bare rc=1. The dead-worker sweep maps it to a new `receipt_unknown` exit kind / run outcome and requeues the card to its source phase **without** touching `consecutive_failures` — the same neutral channel as the quota wall (`KANBAN_RATE_LIMIT_EXIT_CODE`/75) — reports it on `DispatchResult.receipt_unknown`, and skips it in the protocol-violation streak.

## Tests

New `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_receipt_unknown.py` (8 tests, all passing):

- settled exit 0 across a lost receipt → the client returns 0 (the incident shape)
- settled nonzero → returned as recorded (a real failure stays a failure)
- another claim's result is not adopted → `KanbanReceiptLost`
- `_submit()` exits 79; `main()` writes the exit trailer
- sweep: trailer 79 → event/outcome `receipt_unknown`, `consecutive_failures == 0`, card `ready`, own tick channel
- five consecutive lost receipts never trip a `failure_limit=2` breaker
- owner-recorded exit 0 → booked as the protocol violation (clean-exit class), not a crash

No existing kanban behavior changes: the `tests/hermes_cli -k kanban` selection shows the identical 38 pre-existing environment failures with and without this patch (verified by stashing the change and re-running).

prs.title: fix(dashboard): only the default gateway's standalone reason reaches /api/status
prs.body:
## Problem
The dashboard shows "Your gateway serves only one profile. Not served: ops ... this profile is standalone (gateway.standalone: true)" at every login, even though ops runs its own gateway unit and `/api/status` reports `gateway_mode: "multiple"`. The banner contradicts its own data and recommends a real topology migration.

## Cause
`_collect_profile_gateway_topology()` loops over every profile with its own gateway and assigned the host-level `standalone_reason` from any profile's runtime `multiplex_standalone_reason`. The multiplex flag right above is guarded by `name == "default"`; this assignment was not. A secondary profile being standalone is a normal per-profile state, but its reason leaked into `/api/status`.

## Fix
Guard the assignment with `name == "default"`. Banner template, i18n keys and the real warning path are untouched: a guard refusal recorded by the default gateway still surfaces.

## Tests
Two regression tests in `test_web_server_gateway_topology.py`:
1. default serving itself + standalone secondary with a recorded reason -> `multiplex_standalone_reason is None`
2. default runtime carries a guard reason (and a secondary carries a different one) -> default's reason returned verbatim

Both fail on current main (arm 2 also fails there because the later secondary overwrites the default's reason) and pass with the fix. Related topology/multiplex test files: 49 passed.

prs.title: feat(webapp): serve the Desktop workspace from the gateway
prs.body:
## What this does

The gateway serves the browser-hosted Desktop workspace (the Webapp) from its own listener. With
`webapp.enabled: true` in the config, `hermes webapp` opens it. Chats run on the profile's gateway, the
process that already serves the CLI, the native Desktop and messaging, so every surface sees one
conversation with one queue.

This follows teknium's direction on #93508
(https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/93508#issuecomment-6259130824): the gateway hosts the
Webapp, with no separate Webapp server and no relay. It carries @BearHuddleston's work from #93508 under
his authorship: the browser renderer and bridge, the browser terminal, staged uploads, file tickets,
the Webapp routes and the bundle build, plus two fixes from #93508's review rounds. The relay and the
profile-incarnation fence stay out; carried code follows main's named-profile rule and refuses a
missing or deleted profile home. #93508 stays open.

@IAvecilla's #142220 adds Settings → Web Access to native Desktop: one place to serve the Webapp on the
network or at your own URL, behind Nous sign-in.

## How it works

- **Config.** `webapp: {enabled, host, port, public_url}`, off by default, `127.0.0.1:9120` when on.
  A wildcard host (`0.0.0.0` / `::`) or a `webapp.public_url` engages the dashboard sign-in gate; any
  other non-loopback host keeps the Webapp off and `hermes webapp` says why. `dashboard.public_url`
  describes `hermes dashboard` and never applies to the Webapp's listener.
- **Listener.** With the Webapp on, the gateway binds its API listener to the Webapp's address and
  serves the bundle there; native clients keep dialing loopback. With it off, the listener is main's.
  When the Webapp's listener cannot start (port taken, the sign-in gate refusing with no provider),
  the gateway keeps main's private loopback listener for native clients, replaces the browser
  credential (someone else may hold the port), and `hermes webapp` says why. A Webapp with no built
  bundle, or one `hermes update` could not rebuild, reports as unavailable and says to run
  `hermes webapp`. On Windows the gateway holds the fixed port exclusively.
- **Sign-in on this machine.** The gateway keeps the browser credential in a user-only file in its
  home, so open tabs stay signed in across a gateway restart. `hermes webapp` asks the gateway for a
  one-use link (60 s) over its private control socket, which answers same-user peers only. On Linux
  and Windows the server checks who redeems the link and the command opens it. Elsewhere (macOS, the
  BSDs, illumos) the command prints the one-use link and never opens it. The secret redactor masks the
  credential and launch tickets in Webapp links that reach a transcript. Each browser socket,
  including each voice stream, opens with a one-use ticket named for that socket, so no socket URL
  carries the credential.
- **Sign-in from other machines.** Behind the sign-in gate, `hermes webapp` opens the Webapp's
  address (`webapp.public_url` when set; on the LAN, the address Web Access registered Nous sign-in
  for) and the user signs in there with a password or Nous account. Each login is bound to the browser
  credential by an HttpOnly cookie named for the gateway, so two gateways on one hostname keep their
  sign-ins apart. A write that carries the sign-in cookie has to come from the Webapp's own origin
  (Sec-Fetch-Site, else Origin). On the Webapp's listener a provider token works on its own (as a
  bearer token or on the native refresh route) only if a native app's sign-in received it there; a
  browser login's tokens work only inside its cookies.
- **Sign-out.** `hermes webapp --sign-out` replaces the credential. Every tab and every login behind
  the gate is signed out, and the account tokens those logins held stop working on the Webapp; the
  sockets, host terminals, screen viewers and media links they opened close or stop working, and the
  command reports how many connections closed. Native apps that signed in with their own sign-in stay
  signed in. With no gateway running it replaces the stored credential and says so.
- **Web Access (native Desktop).** Settings → Web Access serves the Webapp on the network or at your
  own URL, behind Nous sign-in (sign in to Nous under Providers first). Start builds the bundle, writes
  the `webapp:` block of the config, registers the Nous Portal callback when it changed (saving the
  client id as `HERMES_DASHBOARD_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` in `.env`), and restarts the gateway. A running chat
  refuses the restart: the settings are saved, the pane shows Restart needed, and they apply at the
  next restart. Only the native app or the loopback credential can call these routes. `hermes update`
  rebuilds the bundle for any home that serves the Webapp.
- **Profiles.** `hermes -p work webapp` opens the default gateway's Webapp on `work`. A standalone
  profile's own gateway serves its own Webapp when its config turns it on. Profile export and
  `--clone-all` leave the browser credential out.
- **Files.** One shared parser reads `file:` URLs (drive letter, UNC, POSIX) on every surface, decodes
  them once, and refuses one that encodes a separator or a dot-segment. Dropping files onto a terminal
  types their paths as a paste, and a path with a control character is skipped with a warning.
  Sessions and the terminal start in the profile's home unless its `terminal.cwd` names another
  folder. On a profile whose workspace is an SSH machine, images picked in the browser are read from
  the gateway's staged uploads.

## Commits

1. `feat(webapp)`, `feat(desktop)`: carried server pieces and browser host renderer (BearHuddleston)
2. `feat(gateway)`: serve the Webapp from the gateway's own listener
3. `feat(cli)`: `hermes webapp`
4. `feat(desktop)`: sign-in view for a signed-out tab
5. `test(webapp)`, `docs(webapp)`: e2e spec, smoke script, configuration, CLI reference, Desktop guide
6. Ported from #93508's review rounds (BearHuddleston): refuse cookie-authenticated writes from another
   origin; read `file:` URLs with one shared parser. Each has a gateway-side test.
7. Fixes from the review of #93508 and live runs on this branch, one per commit.
8. Web Access API, pane and docs (IAvecilla, #142220).
9. Fixes from this PR's reviews (teknium, unsupportedpastels, Greptile, yoniebans), one per commit,
   each with a test that fails without it.
10. `fix(desktop)`: the bots avatar escapes a bot's name in its face markup (from @bakon11's audit
    checks; main's code, reachable from the Webapp's origin).
11. `fix(desktop)` (yoniebans' review): carried renderer changes that only the browser needs are gated
    to the browser, so native Desktop keeps main's behaviour for each, with a native test.

### Native-only commits

These change native Desktop, TUI or CLI behaviour. Each is its own commit with a test.

- `6c9a8a8711d` `hermes sessions adopt` (new here) prints one line on an old or locked state.db
  instead of a traceback. The Webapp doesn't need it.
- `b3ba8906605` Native Desktop on a remote SSH-backend profile reads cached images while the SSH
  host is down. The Webapp's paste read-back uses the same rule.
- `6ec3b1f8372` + `5caf2b647df` + `534454e726e` Reattach replay on slow links for the dashboard `/chat`
  tab and the Webapp host terminal; a replay that timed out keeps the smaller size for the rest of
  the session. Native Desktop's terminal is node-pty and is unaffected.
- `23747ee47bd` + `b97f6169ea7` Native Desktop's remote default folder and the Webapp's start folder:
  the profile's `terminal.cwd`, else its home.
- `1440790ca57`, `ccd1da7adce` Put Electron's clipboard writes and native ticket fallback back to
  main's behaviour after the carried renderer changed them. Keep them, or Electron regresses.
- `82974d567d0` + `a11d787b1f8` Electron's media protocol and previews read `file:` URLs with the
  shared parser; a bare `%` in a file name is escaped first, so that media plays.
- `56c04c4d770` Terminal file drop: the control-character and paste handling applies to Electron too.
- `b265e3837f8` Native file attach: host files of any size are copied in chunks; inline data URLs
  stay at Electron's 256 MiB reader cap.
- `14cd7f862ce` Bot avatars escape the bot's name in their markup, in native Desktop as well.

### Changes to main's behaviour

Native Desktop:

- A pane on a collapsed layout side reads as hidden: the statusbar terminal button and terminal
  keybinds treat it as closed, and its toggle shows it on the first press (`e1e70f6beb0`, test
  `d61ec54f55b`).
- "Open image" on a remote gateway's generated image saves through the save dialog instead of handing
  the system browser a URL that carries the connection token (`e1e70f6beb0`, test `8791b570b8a`).
- `file:` URLs with a drive letter or UNC host open the Windows path in previews, media links and
  Electron's media protocol; a URL that encodes a path separator is refused. Remote audio and video
  send their file URIs to the gateway unconverted (`82974d567d0`).
- When the clipboard IPC write throws, copy buttons fall back to the renderer's clipboard API instead
  of reporting a failure (`1440790ca57`).
- "Open HTML artifact in browser" percent-encodes its `file:` URL, so a path containing `#`, `%` or
  `?` opens (`e1e70f6beb0`).
- Restored terminal scrollback finishes writing before the new shell starts, and terminal query
  replies inside the replay are no longer sent to the shell (`e1e70f6beb0`).
- Queued composer focus retries no longer take focus back from audio or video controls the user just
  focused, which completes main's #135228 (`e1e70f6beb0`, test `floating-target-media.test.ts`).
- Terminal file drop skips paths with control characters (`56c04c4d770`).

Once, after upgrading: browsers behind sign-in sign in again (the sign-in cookie now carries the
gateway's name), and native apps that signed in on a gated Webapp before this change sign in again.

## Testing

- Every fix from this PR's reviews has a test that fails without it. For each module they changed,
  the fixes ran its test files; every failure left also fails on main (`db1fa153fe2`) on this Windows
  machine (POSIX-only fixtures, symlinks, the space in the home path).
- `scripts/check` passes all 12 checks, code health included.
- Renderer: typecheck, lint (no errors), the i18n key check and the touched vitest files pass. A full
  Python and vitest comparison against main at the new base is running; the numbers follow in a
  comment.
- Live, Windows, headless Edge, isolated homes (earlier rounds): cold launch, single-use link, chat, CLI
  and browser on one session, host terminal and its tickets, reload, gateway restart keeps the tab
  signed in, sign-out closing open sockets and showing the sign-in view within about 2 s, Webapp off,
  named profile, terminal file drop, the default folder, Windows file URLs, the gated fallback with
  and without a password provider, sign-out behind the password gate (real gateway), and raw
  WebSocket upgrades with a foreign `Host` (all refused). A live gateway confirmed the stale-bundle
  report after a failed update.
- E2E: CI runs the desktop and Python e2e suites only on release or manual runs. Manual run at this
  head: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/40003439648

Not yet verified: a real Mac (the macOS launch path runs simulated on every host), a real Nous OAuth
sign-in, and the in-app gateway restart from Web Access.

## Known gaps

- Portal: whether any Nous account can authorize a self-hosted client, and whether registering a new
  callback replaces or adds a redirect URI on the shared dashboard client. If it replaces, Web Access
  and `hermes dashboard` cannot both use Nous sign-in on one client.
- Native apps signed in on the Webapp's listener stay signed in at sign-out. The bundled password
  provider cannot revoke their tokens; they end when the user signs out in that app or changes the
  provider's credentials.
- Where the printed link has no peer check (macOS, the BSDs, illumos), a local user who reads it first
  can redeem it within its 60 s; the owner then sees that it was already used.
- A reattach replay that timed out stays at the smaller size for that session, so a fast viewer after
  a slow one gets the shorter replay with the "output was trimmed" notice.
- A second profile that turns on Web Access without its own `webapp.port` finds 9120 taken and shows
  that reason; there is no automatic port choice.
- On macOS, `SO_REUSEADDR` stays on so a restart can rebind during TIME_WAIT.
- As on main, `dashboard.public_url` with no sign-in provider stops the gateway: hosted sign-in
  relies on that setting gating the gateway's own listener. Web Access never writes it.
- The other SSH file routes (`/api/fs/list`, `read-text`, `git-root`, `default-cwd`) still answer 500
  when the host is down; only the image route checks the cache first.
- On an SSH workspace, browser audio and video stream from the gateway host, as remote native
  Desktop's do; downloads come from the SSH machine.
- The browser attaches images up to 16 MiB; native Desktop takes 25 MiB.
- The Webapp page sends no Content-Security-Policy yet; the sign-in handoff pages do.
- Host shells survive sign-out for their 15-minute retention; their sockets close at sign-out.
- Unchanged from main: reloading mid-reply drops the text streamed so far, and the hermes-bots plugin
  keeps polling `/api/profiles` from a signed-out tab.

prs.title: plugin-catalog: update operations to 0.3.5
prs.body:
Re-pins `plugin-catalog/operations.yaml` from `61ffdaa` (0.3.3) to `5a12f81` (0.3.5), covering two
releases. `requires_hermes` is unchanged. The description gains a disclosure block for what 0.4.0
collects and writes, and the first known issue is rewritten because 0.3.5 makes it no longer true.

## What changed since 0.3.3

- **0.3.5 — the plugin stands alone.** It used to read hermes-metrics-dash's `metrics.db` as its
  only metrics source, so a stopped dashboard meant an empty page. It now runs its own stdlib
  collector over the same local sources (offset-tracked, read-only) into its own store,
  `<hermes root>/metrics/operations.db`, which only this plugin writes. The fleet DB is a
  read-only fallback while the own store is empty; every metrics payload names its source.
- **Retention is a user decision with real numbers**: `metrics_retention_days` (30/60/90/forever,
  default 30), with a page section showing current store size, per-table MB, and the projected
  size at each option.
- **Alerts no longer depend on kanban**: when no dispatcher tick arrives, a single daemon timer
  runs the sweep and the page shows "heartbeat: own timer".
- **Recognition instead of collision**: a cached probe of the metrics dashboard's `/api/about`
  (which now advertises its capabilities) makes Operations link to it rather than duplicate it.
- **0.3.5 — failed model calls explain themselves**: each failure group is classified with the
  host app's own error classifier and shown with a plain-language cause — naming *which* provider
  account is out of credit, after a real incident where a funded portal hid an empty one — plus
  the prefilled remedy commands (`hermes cron edit/run`, `hermes auth add`).

## Disclosures (rule 13) — what is new since 0.3.3

- **New reads (all read-only, offset-tracked tails):** `<hermes root>/metrics/requests.jsonl`,
  `moa-refs.jsonl`, guardrail lines in `logs/agent.log`, `logs/model-router-requests.jsonl`,
  `clientgate/clientgate-usage.jsonl`.
- **New write:** `<hermes root>/metrics/operations.db` (this plugin is its only writer; pruned to
  the retention setting). The `metrics_retention_days` setting is written through Hermes'
  plugin-settings writer. New probe: the local metrics dashboard `/api/about`
  (`METRICS_DASH_URL`, default `http://127.0.0.1:8899`, cached 5 minutes).
- **Background line changed**: was "nothing beyond the gateway's dispatch-tick hook" — now also a
  single daemon timer that only runs the alert sweep when no tick has arrived.
- Everything else is as the 0.3.3 entry stated; no other network calls, credentials, or stores.

## Disclosures (rule 13) — carried forward, still accurate

- **Network:** GitLab REST API (the `gitlab_host` setting or `GITLAB_HOST`, with the `gitlab_token` secret or `GITLAB_TOKEN`; it reads no other tool's login); the model router's status endpoint (the `model_router_token` setting or `MODEL_ROUTER_TOKEN`); and LM Studio's local server (`LMSTUDIO_URL`, default `http://127.0.0.1:1234`) to list loaded models.
- **Reads outside its own data (read-only):** hermes-metrics-dash's `<hermes root>/metrics/metrics.db` (fallback only since 0.4.0), the kanban database, `<hermes root>/plugin-data/gitlab-mr/device-aliases.json`, profile `config.yaml` files (to show where the plugin is enabled), and git-tracked files in the projects it checks.
- **Shell commands:** `git status`, `git rev-parse` and `git ls-files` in checked project folders. Nothing else.
- **Model calls (opt-in or on click):** Activity summaries send activity entries to the model set for the auxiliary task (off by default). "Explain" on a Trace sends that session's call facts (models, hosts, timings, token counts, error text) to the same task's model, only when clicked and only with Activity summaries on; nothing is stored.
- **Messages (opt-in):** Discord alerts go through Hermes' own `send_message` tool to the `alert_target` you set. Empty by default.
- **Writes:** kanban cards through Hermes' kanban functions; a merge request proposing a rule (never to main); its own files under `<hermes root>/plugin-data/operations/`; its own metrics store (above); and, only when the Connect GitLab step is used, this plugin's own settings — `gitlab_host` through Hermes' plugin-settings writer and `gitlab_token` through Hermes' `.env` credential route.
- **Model roles (on click):** for a router role with no loaded model, it opens a new Desktop chat with a drafted brief (the user reviews and sends it) or files a kanban card, for a profile whose config has rolectl-mcp with writes on (`ROLECTL_MCP_ALLOW_WRITE=1`). The plugin itself only reads LM Studio and the router; any change is the agent's, under Hermes' approvals. When no profile qualifies **and rolectl-mcp is present on this machine**, a once-a-day toast offers a chat that adds it to this profile's config, or the lines to copy. Without rolectl-mcp it says nothing.
- **Fix this (on click):** on an attention item, incident or error group it files a kanban card, or opens a new Desktop chat with a drafted prompt that the user reviews and sends.
- **Starting work:** handing a card to a profile runs one Hermes dispatcher tick so its worker starts at once, under the same config limits and approvals as `hermes kanban dispatch`. Automatic fix cards are off by default (`drift_action: button`).
- **Background:** the gateway's dispatch-tick hook, plus the single fallback timer described above. No telemetry.

## Surfaces used

- `desktop/plugin.js` (Desktop plugin SDK only)
- dashboard backend routes at `/api/plugins/operations/`
- hook: `on_kanban_dispatch_tick` (scheduled cards, optional Discord alerts, optional automatic fix cards)
- one auxiliary model task, "Operations activity summaries" (off by default)
- no tools, no middleware, no Python dependencies

`hermes plugins validate plugins/operations` passes, including the security scan, desktop surface and
no-core-override checks. The plugin's own suite (283 tests) and its syntax / no-personal-data /
version gates are green, and both image URLs return 200 at the pinned sha.

prs.title: fix(dingtalk): ship python-socks so the stream websocket can use a SOCKS proxy
prs.body:
Fixes #135646

dingtalk-stream opens its websocket with a plain `websockets.connect(uri)`, so websockets picks the proxy from `urllib.request.getproxies()`. On macOS with Clash/Surge-style system proxies that dict includes a SOCKS entry, and websockets prefers SOCKS over HTTPS for wss. Dialing it needs `python-socks`, which none of our extras install, so every attempt fails with "python-socks is required to use a SOCKS proxy". The SDK swallows that in its own retry loop, so the gateway says it's connected but no messages ever arrive.

Two changes:

- Add `python-socks==2.8.2` to the `dingtalk` extra. It's already in uv.lock (aiohttp-socks pulls it in for matrix), so the lock diff is just the extras metadata. I added it to `feishu` too since lark-oapi dials its event websocket the same way. That's separate from the Windows bare `socks://` issue in #67244.
- If the ImportError still shows up (e.g. an install that hasn't re-synced the extra), the adapter now treats it like the existing #24851 case: one clear non-retryable fatal error that says how to fix it, not an endless 3s loop.

Repro without network (port 9 is closed):

```python
import asyncio, os, websockets
os.environ["socks_proxy"] = "socks5h://127.0.0.1:9"
async def main():
    try:
        async with websockets.connect("wss://wss-open-connection.dingtalk.com/connect", open_timeout=3): pass
    except Exception as e: print(type(e).__name__, e)
asyncio.run(main())
```

Without python-socks you get the ImportError from the issue. With it you get `ProxyConnectionError`, which means it's actually going through the proxy now.

Testing: the new `tests/gateway/test_dingtalk_socks_proxy_runtime.py` fails on main and passes here. The existing dingtalk, feishu and pm extras tests pass, and so do `python scripts/check` and `pm.build_env --check-lock`. I tested on Linux with Python 3.14. I haven't tested on a real macOS system proxy.

prs.title: feat(mcp): per-server result_filter to drop opaque prefixed values
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds an opt-in, per-server `result_filter` for MCP tool results: `mcp_servers.<name>.result_filter.drop_string_prefixes` removes object entries and list items whose string value starts with a listed prefix, in the JSON text block and in `structuredContent`, before the result reaches the model.

Motivating case: gbrain stamps every `search`/`query` hit with `id: gbrain-page:v1:<base64url of [source_id, slug]>` (up to ~150 chars). A large `query` result carries dozens of them, and OpenRouter rejected the whole request:

```
403 Request blocked: prompt injection patterns detected
metadata: {"patterns": ["base64_encoded_injection"]}
```

Hermes then fell back to the next provider for the rest of the turn. The hits keep `slug` and `source_id`, and gbrain's `fetch` accepts a plain slug in place of the encoded id, so dropping the id loses nothing the model needs:

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  gbrain:
    result_filter:
      drop_string_prefixes: ["gbrain-page:v1:"]
```

Why a value-prefix filter rather than dropping a key name: other tools on the same server use `id` for things that matter (jobs, takes), so dropping every `id` would be lossy. Without the config key the rendered result is returned unchanged; non-JSON text, `_meta` and error results are never touched.

## Related Issue

No existing issue. Searched open PRs: #124210 adds `transform_mcp_servers` (server *config* transforms), which does not cover tool *results*.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `tools/mcp_result_filter.py` (new): `apply_result_filter(rendered, server_config)`; pure, no I/O.
- `tools/mcp_tool_handlers.py`: `_make_tool_handler` applies it to `_render_call_tool_result(...)` with the server's `_config`.
- `tests/tools/test_mcp_result_filter.py` (new): one invariant test (configured prefixes are dropped from text and `structuredContent`, everything else survives) and one for the unconfigured pass-through.
- `website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md`: `result_filter` row in the server-keys table.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_mcp_result_filter.py tests/tools/test_mcp_tool*.py`: 131 passed. The new test fails on `main` (module absent).
2. Live: gbrain 0.60.32.0 over Streamable HTTP with the config above. Before, a `query` returning 28 KB of hits made the next OpenRouter request fail with the 403 above; with the filter, the result carries no `gbrain-page:v1:` values.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)

prs.title: fix(desktop,gateway): tell clients a quiet turn is still running (turn.alive)
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

It adds the backend half of the fix on top of #128401 (merged as `77e2992020`). The gateway now tells clients that a quiet turn is still running, so the client no longer has to guess.

This replaces #128480, which I closed: the same change, squashed into one commit on current `main` (`94f3f170d4`), with the review follow-ups folded in. #128480 carried #128401's commits until it merged; the merged commit is byte-identical to them, so nothing of #128401 is repeated here.

### Why the backend half

The gateway emits nothing between `tool.start` and `tool.complete`. On `main`, the Desktop reads a 45 s gap as a dropped connection (#122416, #125306). #128401 makes the client ask `session.active_list` every time a turn goes quiet. That fixes the false card, but the client is still guessing, and the backend already knows the answer.

Field report from today (macOS, Desktop at `16c59d0e`, window unfocused): a `terminal` call ran 71.7 s (`agent.log` 23:11:25 → 23:12:37). The card appeared 45 s in, while the agent kept working for minutes. That turn was opening PRs, so Retry would have sent the same instructions twice.

A second report from the same machine an hour later (Desktop `16c59d0e`, hosted Codex model, ~470k-token context, window unfocused while the user worked in another app) shows it is not only tool calls:
- 00:04: a `terminal` call running `git rebase origin/main` for 3 min 17 s. The card appeared, and the tool row showed "Result unavailable" until `tool.complete` landed later with `exit 0`.
- 00:07: a provider wait. Below 60 s of silence the agent only calls `_touch_activity` (`agent/chat_completion_nonstream.py`); its first client-visible wait notice ("provider stream open; 60s without substantive model progress") comes at 60 s, after the Desktop's 45 s window. The backend's own watchdog for that request was 300 s.
- 00:19: a `terminal` call that ran 180 s (`agent.log` 00:17:02 → 00:20:02).

The agent kept working through all three (API calls #113–#129 follow in `agent.log`), and Retry would have re-sent a turn that was running dozens of subagents.

### 1. `turn.alive` (gateway)

`tui_gateway/turn_alive.py` ticks every 5 s.
- **When it fires:** a session's live status is `working` or `starting` (the same `_session_live_status` that `session.active_list` reports), a client can hear it (`_session_has_live_transport`), and the session has had no frame for 15 s. The gateway then emits:

  ```json
  {"type": "turn.alive", "session_id": "…",
   "payload": {"status": "working", "quiet_s": 15.0,
               "activity": "waiting for stream response (60s, prefill)", "activity_age_s": 12.3}}
  ```

- **No extra frames for busy turns:** `server.write_json` records every frame it routes to a session's client. That covers `_emit` events and also the two paths that bypass `_emit`: a compute host's relayed frames (`_relay_compute_host_rpc`) and server→client requests. A turn that streams or runs tools gets no heartbeat, isolated or not.
- **Only to a client that can hear it:** a closed window's running turn stays on `_detached_ws_transport`, a drop sink that is not `None`. The ticker skips it, and closed sockets, via `_session_has_live_transport` (the same predicate the transport code uses for fan-out peers).
- **A dropped frame is retried once per interval.** The attempt restarts the quiet clock whether or not the peer took the frame, so a failing write is not repeated on every 5 s tick.
- **`activity` / `activity_age_s`:** for a local turn, the agent's own `_touch_activity` label and its age. For a turn isolated in a compute host, only the age of the host's mirrored `_compute_host_activity_ns` stamp (the clock the ws-orphan reaper reads). The label stays in the host, and the parent's local agent is not the one running the turn.
- **Ephemeral:** `event_replay` neither sequences nor keeps it. A 10-minute quiet tool call would otherwise push 40 frames through the session's 512-event replay ring. A reconnecting client never replays stale liveness.
- **Advertised:** the WS `gateway.ready` frame carries `turn_alive_s: 15`. The interval is a fixed 15 s, not a setting (no `HERMES_*` env var, per the repository's config rules): the frame after a lost one (2 × 15 + 5 s tick = 35 s) still lands inside the Desktop's hardcoded 45 s window, and clients don't read `turn_alive_s`.
- **Contracts:** `TurnAlivePayload` is declared in `tui_gateway/contracts/events.py`, and `gateway-contract.generated.ts` / `.openrpc.json` are regenerated.
- **Old clients** ignore it: Ink has no exhaustive switch on event types, and `ui-tui` and `web` both typecheck against the regenerated union.
- **It also fixes Desktop builds that do not know the event.** `resolveGatewayEventSessionId` never drops an event with an explicit `session_id`, and the dispatcher's `finally` calls `noteSessionEvent` for any attributed event, handled or not. With the `status.ts` handler reverted to `main`, `turn-alive-event.test.tsx` still passes. So the gateway half can ship on its own, and already-installed Desktops stop showing the false card after a backend update.

### 2. Desktop

- **`turn.alive`** is consumed as a no-op event. The dispatcher's `finally` already counts any attributed event, so a quiet turn on a current backend keeps resetting its silence clock and is never checked at all (0 `session.active_list` requests over a 10-minute quiet tool call in the test). On an older backend, or when a turn truly stops emitting, #128401's check still decides.
- **A turn the backend has not accepted yet is not ended.** This is a gap #128401 inherits from #122417 (@Enough1122's blocker 2 there):
  - After submit, before `message.start` or the `running=true` edge, the backend honestly lists the session `idle`. `rehydrateLiveSessionStatuses` keeps such a turn busy for exactly this reason (`awaitingResponse && !sawAssistantPayload`).
  - `liveTurnVerdict` read the same answer as `ended`, so the turn settled with a `no_reply` Retry card while the first submit could still start.
  - Such a turn is now asked again next window, like an unanswered check, for up to two windows (`UNACCEPTED_TURN_GRACE_MS`, counted from the optimistic arm, like the #86795 pre-start gate). Once accepted (`turnLive`), the same answer ends it as before; past the grace, `idle` ends it too.
- **Traceable `no_reply` card.** The surface carries the runtime id, and "Copy error details" prints a `session:` line, so a pasted blob maps to `agent.log`. This comes from #127447.

### Also fixes: the turn clock stuck under a finished reply

Seen on a live install running this branch: a turn finished (`agent.log`: `tui turn finished … status=complete` at 01:49:09, session idle from then on, no reconnect), the reply rendered with its footer, and the running-turn row (pulse + elapsed clock) stayed under it, counting past 18 minutes.

- **Desktop, root cause:** the not-yet-accepted hold above had no bound. A busy arm with `awaitingResponse` and no `turnLive`/payload is also kept by `rehydrateLiveSessionStatuses`, so once the hold answered every `idle` with "ask again", nothing could end it. On `main` the silence check settled that state at 45 s; the hold made it permanent. It is now bounded (above). Separately, and also on `main`: only an event armed the silence window, so busy re-armed with no event after it was never checked at all. Every live publish now arms the window if none is running.
- **Gateway, hardening:** `running` outlives `message.complete` (goal judge, loop hooks, follow-up scheduling), so the ticker could send `turn.alive` for a turn the client had just settled, or race the terminal frame. `write_json` now marks the turn ended before writing `message.complete`; `message.start` (or the ticker seeing the session idle) clears it, and the ticker re-checks right before each write. Current Desktops already ignore such a frame (it changes no state), but nothing should follow a turn's terminal frame on the wire.
- **Tests:** `test_turn_alive.py` (no frame after `message.complete`; none when the turn finishes mid-tick), `session-watchdog.test.ts` (a re-arm the backend never takes up settles after the grace and stays settled 18 min later), `turn-alive-event.test.tsx` (a late `turn.alive` after `message.complete` leaves the turn settled, with no status check). The first three fail without the fix.

## Related Issue

Follow-up to #128401 (merged), which fixed #122416; this closes the remaining gateway half. Fixes #125306.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `tui_gateway/turn_alive.py` (new): the ticker, `note_emit`, `note_frame` (no frames after `message.complete`), and the fixed 15 s interval.
- `tui_gateway/server.py`: `write_json` records every frame it delivers to a session's transport for `turn_alive`, and passes turn boundaries to `note_frame` before writing; `_emit` is unchanged from `main`.
- `tui_gateway/event_replay.py`: `turn.alive` is not sequenced or kept.
- `tui_gateway/ws.py`: `turn_alive_s` in `gateway.ready`; starts the ticker next to the backend heartbeat refresher.
- `tui_gateway/contracts/events.py`, `apps/shared/src/gateway-contract.generated.ts`, `…openrpc.json`: the `turn.alive` contract and the ready field.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event/status.ts`: the no-op `turn.alive` handler.
- `apps/desktop/src/store/session-states.ts`: bounded `awaitingAcceptance` in `onEventSilence`; a silence window armed on every live publish; `session` on the `no_reply` surface.
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/error-surface.ts`: `ErrorSurface.session` and its diagnostics line.
- `tests/tui_gateway/conftest.py`: an autouse fixture keeps `handle_ws` tests from starting the process-wide ticker.

## How to Test

```
python -m pytest tests/tui_gateway/test_turn_alive.py tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_ws.py tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_event_replay.py tests/tui_gateway/contracts
cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --project ui src/store/session-watchdog.test.ts src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/turn-alive-event.test.tsx
```

`tests/tui_gateway/test_turn_alive.py` (12 tests):
- one frame per 15 s of quiet, and the frame itself restarts the clock;
- any other event defers it;
- idle, `waiting`, finalized, closed-socket and detached sessions get nothing, the detached one on the real `_detached_ws_transport`, and nothing is even attempted for them; an agent build counts as `starting`;
- a frame the peer drops is retried once per interval, not on every tick;
- a compute host's relayed frame defers it like any other event;
- the local agent's activity and its age ride along; an isolated turn reports the host's activity age and no label, even when the parent holds a local agent with an old stamp;
- 39 frames over a 10-minute quiet call leave the replay ring with only `message.start`, and no frame carries `seq`;
- a later turn counts its quiet afresh;
- the payload validates against the contract under `HERMES_TEST_ISOLATION`.

`test_tui_gateway_ws.py` asserts `turn_alive_s` in `gateway.ready`.

Desktop:
- `turn-alive-event.test.tsx`: through the real dispatcher, 40 `turn.alive` frames keep a quiet turn live with **zero** status checks and no state change. When the frames stop, the check fires once at 45 s.
- `session-watchdog.test.ts`: a submitted, not-yet-accepted turn answered `idle` stays and is asked again, and ends once accepted; the `no_reply` card carries `session` and the diagnostics print it.

Results on macOS (`main` `7cadfaa6` + the same change, before the rebase):
- `npx vitest run --project ui`: 9780 passed; 2 failed in `src/store/voice-prefs.test.ts`, which fails the same 2 on clean `main`.
- `python -m pytest tests/tui_gateway`: 2268 passed, 11 skipped; 6 failed in `test_profiles_list_{canonical_session,session_field_cache,ui_meta_cache}.py`, which fail the same 6 on clean `main`. `test_hosted_room_two_gateway_scoped.py` was not collected (no `aiohttp` in this venv).
- The four gateway tests added in the last commit fail on the commit before it and pass on it.
- `tsc --noEmit` is clean for `apps/desktop`, `apps/shared`, `ui-tui` and `web`.
- eslint on the changed desktop files: 0 errors.
- `ruff`, `check-windows-footguns --all`, `check_bash_shebangs`, `check_no_tmp_literals`, `check_config_yaml_writers` and `check_os_marker_fakes` are clean.
- `scripts/gen_gateway_contracts.py` regenerates the committed files byte-for-byte.

On `94f3f170d4` (this branch): the gateway tests above plus `tests/tui_gateway/contracts` (39 passed), the three desktop files above (32 passed), `tsc --noEmit` for `apps/desktop` clean, and the contract generator still byte-for-byte.

## Checklist

- [x] Conventional Commits
- [x] Only changes for this fix
- [x] Tests added
- [x] Tested on macOS
- [x] Contracts regenerated

## Acknowledgements

- Builds on @jquesnelle's #128401 (owner-routed backend check, the settle without `interrupted`, write-through, `no_reply`).
- Based on work by @rodricksz4h5 (#122417, probe-before-settle; report #122416), @liuhao1024 (#125352, `starting` as liveness) and @edward670216-collab (#127447, honest client-raised copy and the session id in diagnostics). The first two are already co-authors on #128401's commit, and @edward670216-collab is a co-author on the desktop commit here.
- Thanks to @mecworks for #125306, to @Enough1122 for the reviews on #122417 and #125352 (the cold-start settle closed here was their blocker 2), to @whyyagswhy for verifying #122417, to @alt-glitch for triaging the overlap, and to @DavidMetcalfe for the review that caught the uncapped `HERMES_TURN_ALIVE_S` (co-author on the follow-up commit), and to @ehz0ah for the review that removed that env override entirely.

**If this gets salvaged:** please keep the authorship credit, either by cherry-picking the commits or by adding these trailers to the salvage commit:
```

Co-authored-by: David Metcalfe <80915+DavidMetcalfe@users.noreply.github.com>
```

prs.title: feat(telegram): show live status for running subagents
prs.body:
## Problem

Hermes already emits subagent lifecycle events through `_ChildProgressRelay`, but Telegram does not show that activity after a parent turn finishes while detached subagents continue. Users cannot distinguish active detached work from abandoned work.

This adds a live, per-turn status view for direct subagents and implements #90608 without changing delegation execution or completion delivery.

## Change

Show one compact Telegram message that follows the subagents launched by a turn:

~~~text
🔀 Subagents · 1/3 done
├ #1 ✅ done · 42s · 4 tools
├ #2 ⚙️ working · ~4m · 2 tools
└ #3 💭 thinking · ~7m
~~~

- Introduces `SubagentActivityBoard`, a projection of the existing `subagent.*` event stream.
- Tracks every direct subagent launched by one parent turn, including several delegation waves, while excluding nested grandchildren.
- Keeps accepting late events through the originating turn's captured callback and delivery target after the foreground turn ends.
- Renders only ordinal, phase, elapsed time, and tool count. Goals, arguments, output, errors, model names, and session IDs never enter the status text.
- Recomputes running age on each observed lifecycle event and uses the existing 30-second delegation heartbeat during quiet work. Live age is approximate, rounding to the nearest minute after the initial `<30s` and `<1m` bands. Terminal rows freeze the child's authoritative duration and retain seconds for sub-hour work.
- Coalesces bursts behind a three-second update floor.
- Sends the status once and applies later changes to that same message. Ambiguous initial delivery is abandoned rather than risking duplicate messages; update failures use bounded retries and never fall back to a second send.
- Marks the status as an interim send so relay delivery cannot seal an answer stream.
- Requires a concrete edit implementation. Relay destinations must negotiate both `supports_edit` and the `edit` operation.
- Adds `display.platforms.telegram.subagent_activity_board: false` as an opt-out. Other platforms default off.

`TurnRunner.progress_callback()` contains one early `observe_subagent_activity(...)` call before its foreground-generation gate. State projection, rendering, pacing, delivery, and message ownership live in `gateway/subagent_activity_board.py`.

## Validation

The tests exercise the feature at its observable boundaries:

- lifecycle projection across concurrent and sequential delegation waves, nested-child filtering, terminal-state immutability, tool counts, and elapsed-time rounding;
- detached updates after foreground ownership ends, using the real child-progress relay callback;
- stable message ownership, paced burst coalescing, bounded update retries, ambiguous initial delivery, and shutdown behavior;
- Telegram forum routing, including independent turns in different topics of the same chat updating only their own messages;
- adapter capability and per-platform configuration gates, including relay-backed Telegram routes; and
- privacy checks with secret-bearing event payloads to ensure only structural fields reach rendered text.

Timing and pacing tests use deterministic clocks and controlled publisher blocking rather than wall-clock sleeps. The focused activity, wire-contract, Telegram-routing, and delegation suites pass on current upstream `main` at `3ba5602b62` (**179 passed**), along with the required Ruff check and `git diff --check`.

Live validation on `telegramalpha` at `af7058c33c` exercised two independent Telegram forum topics. Each turn maintained its own subagent status message and updated independently in the correct topic. The final candidate differs only by registering the existing `subagent.heartbeat` event in the TUI wire contract and regenerating its committed artifacts; gateway runtime behavior is unchanged.

## Further work

- Offer the same live status on other messaging channels whose adapters can preserve the originating route and update a stable message.
- Include background process activity in the turn's status view.

Closes #90608

## What does this PR do?

Fixes remote Desktop downloads of `MEDIA:` files produced inside a Docker terminal sandbox. The dashboard received the container path such as `/workspace/report.mp4`, but resolved it only on the gateway host and returned 404 even though the bind-mounted file existed.

## Related Issue

- `hermes_cli/web_server_files.py` — translate a missing Docker container path to its existing host bind mount before the managed read-path checks.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server_files.py` — cover download, stream, and read access to a `/workspace` artifact through a Docker volume mapping.

## How to Test

Run `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server_files.py -k managed_file_reads_translate_docker_container_paths` — 1 passed.

## Evidence

- BEFORE RED: the focused command above failed with 404 from download, stream, and read for `/workspace/report.mp4`.
- AFTER GREEN: the same focused command passed (1 passed); broker-bound publication evidence is recorded for `ad477da5bf2dc94f2f2d0ad741a6028a838ab030`.
- CONTROL: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server_files.py -k 'not git_branch_decodes_utf8_under_a_gbk_default_codec'` passed 21 tests, and `ruff check hermes_cli/web_server_files.py tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server_files.py` passed.

## Checklist

- [x] Code: the read-path fallback reuses the established Docker mount resolver.
- [x] Code: mapped paths still pass the managed-root boundary check.
- [x] Code: mapped paths still pass the sensitive-path denylist.
- [x] Tests: added a regression for remote Docker MEDIA paths.
- [x] Tests: demonstrated the focused failure before the repair.
- [x] Tests: ran the focused repair test after the change.
- [x] Verification: ran ruff on both changed Python files.
- [x] Housekeeping: did not change dependencies, lockfiles, or generated artifacts.

## Review follow-up

The unfiltered test file has one existing environment blocker: `test_git_branch_decodes_utf8_under_a_gbk_default_codec` invokes `git init`, which this controlled sandbox rejects before the test can run. It is unrelated to this change; all remaining 21 tests passed.

prs.title: feat(catalog): add opt-in Adaptive Inference routing plugin
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds the opt-in Adaptive Inference routing plugin to the community catalog, pinned to [reviewed source commit d6f4e201](https://github.com/midhatn/adaptive-inference/tree/d6f4e201ba28602189872746922e527c58ed0cbd/plugins/hermes). It lets host-known delegated/background work share a configured gateway with interactive requests while keeping the chosen model, messages, tools, output settings and provider authentication unchanged.

The plugin uses public `llm_request` middleware and child/compaction lifecycle hooks. Newer SDKs can additionally supply public cron execution identity; the retained 0.21.5 SDK lacks that optional capability. Explicit caller classification wins, and the plugin is disabled unless the profile opts in. It does not infer priority from prompt text or change endpoint selection.

## Changes made and disclosure

- Adds only `plugin-catalog/adaptive-inference-routing.yaml`; no Hermes core or bundled-plugin changes.

prs.title: Desktop Settings › Storage frees space from inactive sessions and opens with /storage (Cowork-inspired, salvage #141551)
prs.body:
Settings › Storage in Hermes Desktop can now free disk space: it counts the ended sessions you have not used in 30/90/180/365 days, and after you confirm, the running Hermes service deletes them. Typing `/storage` in the composer opens the page.

Builds on @AGI-Junkie's read-only Storage page (#141551, commit cherry-picked with authorship intact). If #141551 lands first, this PR reduces to the two commits on top.

## Inspiration: Claude Cowork

Claude desktop [v3.1623.0 (Oct 20, 2026)](https://claude.com/docs/cowork/changelog#v3-1623-0), General:

> Added Storage to Settings. It shows the disk space Claude uses and lets you free up space by removing inactive Cowork tasks and Code sessions; a low disk space warning opens it, and so does typing `/storage` in Cowork and Code.

[v3.6556.1 (Oct 22)](https://claude.com/docs/cowork/changelog#v3-6556-1) widened it to deleting inactive chats too. #141551 already ports the "shows the disk space" half. This PR adds the other two pieces: freeing space and `/storage`. Cowork shows a breakdown and also lets you act on it. Hermes users with a big `state.db` had no Desktop way to do the second part, and the CLI path (`hermes sessions prune`) is out of reach for non-developers.

## Changes

- **Free up space card** (`apps/desktop/src/app/settings/storage-cleanup.tsx`), shown under the breakdown at the top level:
  - The count comes from the read-only dry run of `POST /api/sessions/prune` (`older_than_days`, `dry_run: true`, the viewed profile). It opens `state.db` read-only, so it works alongside the live gateway.
  - Delete opens a destructive confirm naming the profile and the last-used range, then calls the owner's `session.prune` RPC with the same filters (`older_than_days`, `archived: false`). This is the path `hermes sessions prune` already takes under a running gateway. The REST delete path takes the exclusive-maintenance lock, and a running gateway always holds that lock, so it would 409.
  - Pinned and still-running sessions are kept: prune excludes them by default, and the owner skips guarded rows.
  - A footnote explains that `state.db` reuses the freed pages and that `hermes sessions optimize` (Hermes closed) shrinks the file.
  - The card is hidden on a remote connection, because the breakdown above it measures this machine.
- **`/storage`**: a Desktop action that routes to `#/settings?tab=storage`.
- **`gateway/session_controls.py`**: `session.prune` joins `_PROFILE_IMPLICIT`. Desktop's shared-primary socket adds `profile` to every RPC for a non-primary local profile. Before this change, naming the owner's own home reached the strict contract as an unknown key, and the prune was refused with `invalid_params (fields: ['profile'])`. `session.mutate` and `session.stats` were already in that set. A profile-bound ticket naming a *different* profile is still a `profile_mismatch`.
- Docs: `website/docs/user-guide/desktop.md` Storage section. i18n: new keys in `en_storage_section.ts`, gaps recorded in `overlay-gaps.json`, `_keys.desktop.json` regenerated.

## Validation

**Live repro (native Electron 44 under Xvnc, real `hermes gateway run` from this tree, sandbox HOME seeded with aged sessions):**

| Leg | Profile | Gateway tree | Result | state.db readback |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| head | default (primary) | this PR | toast "Deleted 3 sessions." | `fresh-chat`, `old-pinned` kept; 3 old gone |
| base | `work` (non-primary) | `origin/main` `session_controls.py` | toast "Could not delete inactive sessions · invalid_params" | all 5 `work` rows still present |
| head | `work` (non-primary) | this PR | toast "Deleted 3 sessions." | `work-fresh`, `work-pinned` kept; default store untouched |

`/storage` typed into the real composer landed on `#/settings?tab=storage` in every leg.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_sessions_prune_via_owner.py::test_owner_prune_accepts_its_own_profile_param` | red on `origin/main` (`invalid_params`, `fields: ['profile']`), green on head; file 4/4 |
| `storage-cleanup.test.tsx` (preview is a dry run; decline deletes nothing; confirm → `session.prune` with the previewed filters) | pass |
| vitest `src/i18n` + storage + slash-command suites | 108/108 |
| `npm run typecheck`, eslint on touched files, `scripts/check --only health` | clean |

### Screenshots

1. Settings › Storage, reached with `/storage`: breakdown and the new card
   ![storage page](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/e1065037e0c5ad2153d66f044340a7c9/raw/1-storage-page.png)
2. Free up space card with the preview count
   ![card](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/e1065037e0c5ad2153d66f044340a7c9/raw/2-free-up-space-card.png)
3. Destructive confirm naming the profile and the last-used range
   ![confirm](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/e1065037e0c5ad2153d66f044340a7c9/raw/3-confirm.png)
4. After delete: success toast; the card re-counts to zero
   ![after](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/e1065037e0c5ad2153d66f044340a7c9/raw/4-after-delete.png)
5. Base leg: the same click on a non-primary profile against `origin/main`'s gateway is refused with `invalid_params`
   ![base](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/e1065037e0c5ad2153d66f044340a7c9/raw/5-base-named-profile-refused.png)

## Not covered

- No low-disk-warning → Storage deep link. Cowork has one, but Hermes' low-disk notice is the `/autoprune` question (`hermes_cli/prune_advisor.py`), and a route action on that backend-sent notice needs a payload field. That is a separate change.
- Space freed inside `state.db` reaches the disk only after a VACUUM, and the owner has no VACUUM verb. Under the always-on gateway, `hermes sessions optimize` refuses while the store is held. The footnote says this plainly instead of claiming the file shrinks.
- macOS/Windows not exercised live. The card is renderer-only and the backend change is platform-neutral.

## Infographic

![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aaf9abe/BdkRmvwRY2AQj971OLwcH_iqY9Lrqb.png)

prs.title: fix(kanban): keep a dispatcher-owned worker running when the whole skill set is missing (#54088)
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A dispatcher-owned Kanban worker whose **entire** requested skill set fails to resolve no
longer crashes at init. It logs a clear warning and keeps running the task, so the card is
not left stranded as `running` until a human reclaims it. Direct CLI invocations keep the
strict behavior: a fully-missing set still raises `ValueError`.

Rebuilt on current `main` (commit `018009bc` moved the missing-skill handling into
`HermesCLI.finalize_preloaded_skills`, where a mixed valid/invalid set already warns and
continues for everyone). The remaining delta is the fully-missing case: outside workers it
still fails loudly, while a worker with `HERMES_KANBAN_DB` pinned (set by the dispatcher)
warns and continues without preloaded skills. Independent reproductions in the issue
(@rumoii's Windows report and @lwwjsdf's production evidence) both hit exactly this
all-missing path: `Error: Unknown skill(s): ...` at worker startup, retries exhausted, card
blocked/running and unnoticed.

## Related Issue

Fixes #54088

- `cli.py` (`HermesCLI.finalize_preloaded_skills`): a fully-missing skill set raises only
  when `HERMES_KANBAN_DB` is not pinned; inside a dispatcher-owned worker it logs a
  "Kanban worker: no requested skill resolved ... continuing without preloaded skills"
  warning instead. The mixed valid/invalid warning is unchanged.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_preloaded_skills.py`: new regression tests covering the three
  branches — all-missing in a kanban worker (warn + continue), all-missing on the direct
  CLI (still raises), mixed set in a kanban worker (continues with the loaded skill).

prs.title: fix(desktop): prevent false persistent NVIDIA SwiftShader recovery
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Prevents a second Desktop launch or an intentional shutdown from leaving a false NVIDIA boot-failure witness that forces SwiftShader on the next launch. Recovery records now identify the artifact and driver that actually attempted the GPU probe, so a source rebuild reporting the same `0.0.0` version can retry hardware rendering.

Automatic NVIDIA recovery no longer appends `--use-angle=swiftshader` to relaunch arguments. The persisted witness selects the fallback instead, avoiding an automatic flag being forwarded through later update relaunches. Explicit user launch arguments remain intact.

## Related Issue

Related work: #131067 and #134903, both currently open drafts. This adapts the lock-owned marker writer and build-identity approach from Konstantin Khlopkov (kokhlo) in #131067. It extends NVIDIA recovery to qualify interrupted-boot records, clean up intentional exits, honor runtime exclusions, and test persisted process lifecycle. It also incorporates the Electron `launch-failed` correction identified in #134903 using the SDK's reason type. Consolidation with those drafts should be considered before merging.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Security fix
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `launch-marker-writer.ts` defers startup recovery writes until the process owns the single-instance lock. All four existing startup marker writers use it.
- `launch-build-identity.ts` identifies stamped builds, including same-version rebuilds. NVIDIA records include that identity and the full driver version.
- `linux-nvidia-egl-recovery.ts` owns persistence, healthy boot, clean exit, and bounded GPU-death recovery. Runtime handling respects explicit opt-outs, WSL, remote-display exclusions, and teardown.
- `main.ts` wires those lifecycle transitions into the existing coalesced recovery handler, preserving sandbox precedence and avoiding two relaunches for one GPU event. Startup and recovery decisions reach the Desktop log.
- Regression tests cover legacy/stale records, interrupted and successful boots, updates, second launches, opt-outs, and genuine same-build failures. Existing legitimate fallback remains sticky for the same artifact and driver.

## How to Test

From `apps/desktop`, using the locked workspace dependencies and prepared Electron runtime:

1. Run `node ../../node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --project electron electron/linux-nvidia-egl-fallback.test.ts electron/linux-nvidia-egl-recovery.test.ts electron/launch-marker-writer.test.ts electron/launch-build-identity.test.ts electron/linux-nvidia-egl-recovery.native.test.ts --maxWorkers 4`.
2. Run the sibling regressions with `node ../../node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --project electron electron/linux-gpu-fallback.test.ts electron/windows-sandbox-fallback.test.ts --maxWorkers 4`.
3. From the repository root, run `npm run typecheck --workspace apps/desktop`, `npm run lint --workspace apps/desktop`, and `python scripts/check --only health --base origin/main`.

Executed on Windows with Node 26.12.1, npm 12.0.2, Electron 44.9.3, and the committed lockfile. Results: 55 focused tests and 43 sibling regressions passed. Four of the focused tests launch real isolated Electron processes, exercise the actual single-instance lock, and replace one stamped fixture artifact with another at the same app version. They test Linux recovery policy with synthetic driver facts and do not create windows or a backend.

Red/green proof: reverting the production NVIDIA decision module to the base makes four new witness/update assertions fail. They pass with this change.

Remaining validation: actual Linux NVIDIA rendering, observed CPU usage, and the full installer/updater transaction have not been exercised on this Windows host. Legacy unqualified boot records deliberately get one fresh probe because their original cause cannot be recovered. A genuine failure of the new qualified probe retains fallback. Unstamped development builds retain version-based behavior when no stronger identity exists. An old process already carrying `--use-angle=swiftshader` can still forward it during its first update restart. That requires a fresh launch without that argument, since this change deliberately does not strip explicit user arguments.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] I searched for existing PRs. Relevant overlap and attribution are described above.
- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this fix
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass. Not run for this TypeScript-only change.
- [ ] `python scripts/check` passes. The applicable TypeScript code-health lane was run, not the complete Python guard set.
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows, with the native-process and rendering limitations described above

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation or N/A. Owning code comments document the marker transition and recovery boundary.
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` or N/A. No configuration keys changed.
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` or N/A. No development workflow changed.
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact. Shared startup writes are lock-owned, and Windows sandbox recovery retains its existing path.
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas or N/A. No tool interface changed.

## Screenshots / Logs

Desktop typechecking passes. ESLint completes with zero errors and existing advisory warnings outside the changed files. Code health reports zero blocking or advisory findings. Formatting passes for the changed helpers and tests. The remaining whole-file formatting differences in `main.ts` match the pristine base exactly, so this PR leaves that unrelated formatting unchanged.

prs.title: fix(gateway): convert HEIC/HEIF images to JPEG when caching inbound media
prs.body:
## Problem
iPhone photos and macOS/iOS screenshots arrive as HEIC. `cache_image_from_bytes` (gateway/platforms/base.py) only accepts PNG/JPEG/GIF/BMP/WebP magic bytes, so HEIC uploads are refused as "non-image data" **before** `agent/image_routing.py`'s HEIC→PNG transcode can ever run. The agent never sees the image.

On Slack it's worse: `_describe_slack_download_failure` maps "non-image data" to *"Slack returned an HTML/login or non-media response. This usually means a scope, auth, or file-permission problem."* Users go chasing Slack app scopes while the bot has `files:read` and PNG/JPG uploads work fine.

Observed in production on a Slack gateway: every failing attachment was `.heic`; PNG/JPEG in the same channels routed natively.

## Fix
- `gateway/platforms/base.py`: detect ISO-BMFF HEIF brands, re-encode to JPEG with `pillow-heif` (already a core dependency), applying EXIF orientation, and cache as `.jpg`. This applies to every adapter using `cache_image_from_bytes` (Slack, Telegram, Signal, Matrix, Mattermost, email, ...).
- If conversion fails, raise a format-specific error instead of "non-image data".
- `plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py`: give that error its own notice so it isn't reported as a scope/auth problem.

## Tests
- `test_converts_heic_to_jpeg`: a real HEIF encoded via pillow-heif is cached as a valid JPEG.
- `test_undecodable_heic_raises_format_error`: an undecodable HEIC raises the format error, not "non-image data".
- Both fail on `main` and pass with this change. `tests/gateway/test_media_download_retry.py`, `test_async_media_cache.py`, `test_slack.py`, `test_document_cache.py` all pass.
- Manual: a macOS `sips`-produced HEIC (1290×2796) caches as a valid JPEG.

prs.title: plugin-catalog: add session-find 1.0.0
prs.body:
Adds `session-find`, a desktop plugin that puts a search window over the session history.

## What it does

`Cmd+Option+F` (or the command palette, or the glyph in the bottom bar whose hover
shows the chord) opens a window that finds a past session by what you remember of it:

- **Keyword search** over message text, tool output and tool arguments, through the
  gateway's own SQLite full text index (`messages_fts`). No index to build.
- **Meaning search** when a `session-find` service answers on `127.0.0.1:8474` or on
  `SESSION_FIND_URL`; the agent half proxies to it and says so on `/status`.
- **Typed filters** mirrored as chips: `in:`, `-in:`, `after:`, `before:`, `me:`,
  `repo:`, and quoted phrases.
- **A preview pane** with the matching message and its neighbours, so two similar
  sessions can be told apart before opening one.
- Pinned then recent sessions on the empty box, and the round trip in the footer
  (`30 sessions · 27 ms`) for the list on screen.

## What it needs

Nothing. No credentials, no environment variables, no network calls of its own. The
session database is opened read only. `capabilities` are all empty and the plugin
registers no agent tools, hooks or middleware.

The window half ships off by default, as a unified package's desktop half does, and
is switched on in the app's plugin inventory.

One deliberate design point worth a reviewer's eye: `/status` reports which backend is
live and whether it can rank by meaning. On a machine with no service the window keeps
the keyword half on, greys the meaning glyph and says on its hover why, instead of
failing a new user's first search with an error about a service they have never heard
of. A meaning-only query on that backend is refused with a sentence rather than an
empty list that would read as "no such session".

## Verification, at the pinned commit

- `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` on this entry: `OK: 1 file(s) valid`. The full
  directory still validates (762 files).
- `scripts/scan_plugin_payloads.py <plugin dir>`: exit 0, no findings.
- `node --test tests/plugin.test.mjs`: 20 of 20 pass. The suite is the gate a plugin
  with no compiler has: no third argument to `jsx()`, only `@hermes/plugin-sdk`,
  `react` and `react/jsx-runtime` imported, no em dash or emoji in the file, no keybind
  colliding with a built-in default, and the pure helpers behind the chips, keys, rows
  and footer behave.
- Installed from the pin: `hermes plugins install djmango/session-find --ref
  caf185c59e62c56a6e4377b8fb08a0ce0e574301` reports `Installed`, and the file the app
  loads (the materialised desktop half) and the agent half both hash-match the pinned
  tree byte for byte.
- Desktop half: inside the plugin SDK surface. No `eval`, no `new Function`, no
  `import()` beyond the allowlist, no prototype patching of renderer or browser
  objects, no reaching into the app's internals or its markup.

## Pin

`sha: caf185c59e62c56a6e4377b8fb08a0ce0e574301`, read back from the pushed `v1.0.0`
tag in `djmango/session-find` (tag object `717b61455a6a870905a5fc61aa6d5481826d2fcf`).
There is no self-updater: updates arrive as a SHA bump here.

Submitted by the plugin repository's owner, per rule 5.

`requires_hermes: ">=0.22"` is the version this was developed and tested against; I have
not verified the SDK surface it uses on earlier releases, so the constraint is stated
rather than guessed.

This PR is from a fork, so its workflow runs wait on a maintainer to approve them. I ran
the gates above locally; nothing here is claimed green.
