prs.title: fix(cli): add-mount --rw, so a read-write mount is expressible (--ro is currently a no-op)
prs.body:
Fixes #3690.

## The bug, plus one part #3690 doesn't mention

`ncl groups config add-mount` cannot create a read-write mount — and **`--ro` is currently a no-op**.

The handler stores `readonly: true` when `--ro` is passed and **omits the key otherwise** (`src/cli/resources/groups.ts`). `validateMount` computes `requestedReadWrite = mount.readonly === false` and starts from `effectiveReadonly = true` (`src/modules/mount-security/index.ts`), so an *absent* key is a read-only request. The two shapes the CLI can produce are therefore identical at spawn time: passing `--ro` and omitting it do the same thing, and no CLI-created mount can ever be read-write — even when the matched allowlist root has `allowReadWrite: true`.

The help text points the other way: `[--ro]` reads as "read-write by default, opt out", the inverse of what the validator does.

**There is no sanctioned path to a read-write mount today.** `/manage-mounts` manages only the allowlist and never attaches a mount to a group; templates cannot declare mounts; the setup wizard doesn't write them. What remains is hand-editing `container.json` before a `container_configs` row exists, or raw SQL into that table — which `docs/skill-guidelines.md` calls "a smell, not a workaround". So an operator can grant `allowReadWrite: true` on a root and still have no supported way to use it.

## The change

Keep the conservative default exactly as it is and add an explicit opt-in.

```ts
const readWrite = args.rw === true || args.readonly === false;
const readOnly = args.ro === true || args.readonly === true;
if (readWrite && readOnly) throw new Error('--ro and --rw are mutually exclusive');
...(readWrite ? { readonly: false } : args.ro || args.readonly ? { readonly: true } : {}),
```

- **No default changes.** With neither flag, no `readonly` key is stored — byte-for-byte today's behaviour.
- `mount-security` is untouched. The two-gate design stays: the allowlist root is the operator's standing policy, the per-mount flag is the caller's request, and requiring both still stops a caller inheriting write access from a permissive root by accident. The bug was only that the CLI couldn't express one of the two gates.
- Help text now documents `[--ro | --rw]` and states that `--rw` is granted only when the matched root also has `allowReadWrite: true`.

### Deliberately different from the issue's first suggestion

#3690 proposes storing `readonly: false` by default when `--ro` is absent. That fixes the same breakage but flips the default to read-write, which changes behaviour for every existing caller and for hand-edited configs. An explicit `--rw` fixes it with no default change. Happy to switch if maintainers prefer the other shape.

### On the issue's second suggestion (echo the effective mode)

Not done, deliberately. Knowing the effective mode at add time means calling `validateMount()`, which loads the allowlist and `realpathSync`es the host path. That would make a pure DB-write handler fail (or report "read-only") for a path that doesn't exist yet but will by restart time, and would read a possibly-stale module-cached allowlist. Both are snapshots that can be wrong by spawn — a confidently wrong answer. Instead the `--rw` path returns a `note` naming the remaining gate, alongside `added`, which already shows what was stored.

## Why this is safe

`add-mount` is `hostOnly`, and `src/cli/guard.ts` denies `hostOnly` commands **before** scope and **before** approval, at any `cli_scope`. There is also no mount surface in the agent-side tool set — `container/agent-runner/src/mcp-tools/` has `install_packages` and `add_mcp_server` only — and `config update` handles scalars, so there's no back door to `additional_mounts`. Worst case is an operator writing a mount to a directory they have already marked `allowReadWrite: true` in a file that lives outside the project root precisely so containers can't reach it.

## Tests

Four new cases in `src/cli/resources/groups.test.ts`: `--rw` ⇒ `readonly: false`; neither flag ⇒ **no `readonly` key at all** (asserted with `'readonly' in mount === false`, which is what actually pins the default — the existing test only ever passed `ro: true`); `--ro` ⇒ `readonly: true`; `--ro` + `--rw` ⇒ rejected with nothing written.

`vitest run src/cli/resources/groups.test.ts src/modules/mount-security` → 2 files, 20 passed. `tsc --noEmit` clean, eslint clean on both changed files.

Note: `docs/SECURITY.md` does not pass `prettier --check`, but that is pre-existing on unmodified `main` — I left the formatting alone rather than balloon the diff. Also left alone as out of scope: `--ro false` parses as the truthy string `"false"` and still sets read-only. `--rw` is unaffected, being checked with `=== true`.

prs.title: feat: add AgentMail email channel adapter
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds `/add-agentmail`: an email channel on an AgentMail-hosted inbox, so an agent gets its own address without touching the operator's domain MX records.

- **Adapter**: native (no Chat SDK bridge exists for AgentMail). One messaging group per correspondent (`agentmail:<address>`), same flattened model as Resend. Can originate threads (`messages.send`) and reply in-thread (`messages.reply`).
- **Modes**: cron-scheduled polling (default; no public endpoint) or webhook (Svix-verified, on the shared webhook server).
- **Sender allowlist**: optional `AGENTMAIL_INBOUND_ALLOW` (addresses and `@domain`s). Unlisted mail stays in the inbox and raises no approval card, so a public inbox doesn't flood the operator with spam cards.
- **Agent-facing text**: a header (from, subject, thread/message ids, attachments) plus AgentMail's `extracted_text` (quoted history stripped).
- **Restart safety**: poll cursor, recent ids, and reply targets persist to `data/agentmail-state.json`; resume is capped at 3 days back.
- **Channel defaults**: declared (`dm-only` mentions, `request_approval` for unknown senders).
- **Out of scope**: an agent-side mail tool (reading the inbox, attachments, cold sends with subjects). That will be a separate `/add-agentmail-tool` PR.

This PR was rebuilt as one commit on current `main` (the earlier history conflicted).

## Related work

No issue. #287 is an older AgentMail skill PR (Feb 2026, pre-v2 channel model); this one targets the current registry-branch / `ChannelDefaults` shape.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm run build` -> passes
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/channels/agentmail-registration.test.ts src/channels/agentmail-format.test.ts` -> 5/5 pass (registry entry via real barrel; allowlist matching incl. `owner@example.com.evil.com` rejected; header formatting)
- `pnpm exec prettier --check src/channels/agentmail*.ts` -> clean
- `pnpm test` -> 3563 pass, 1 fail in `src/group-skills.test.ts` ("resolves the legacy shape…"), which fails identically on clean `main`
- Manual: running on a live install (Raspberry Pi, polling every 2 min, allowlist set, agent-shared wiring into a Telegram session) since 2026-10-10
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
New /add-agentmail skill: give an agent its own email inbox via AgentMail (polling or webhook), with an optional inbound sender allowlist.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- New untrusted input: inbound email. Webhook payloads are Svix-signature-verified before parsing; unsigned/invalid requests get 401.
- `AGENTMAIL_INBOUND_ALLOW` narrows who reaches the agent; when unset, the normal unknown-sender policy (`request_approval`) applies.

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Approval cards on Telegram, Discord and WhatsApp Cloud now show the whole request. A card too long for one message posts its full text first, then a short card with the buttons. Slack and Google Chat approval card text shows as typed.

- **Problem**: these channels show a card as one message with a length cap (Telegram 4,096 characters after formatting, a Discord embed 4,096, a WhatsApp Cloud card 1,024 with a 60-character title) and cut or reject text past it.

Transcript rotation now runs between completed turns in warm queries, so recurring tasks cannot keep an oversized session alive indefinitely.

- Check transcript limits without moving the file while Claude is running. Wait for the SDK's idle state, including background shell and subagent work, before closing the warm query.

prs.title: fix(container-config): write container.json without following a symlink
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

`materializeContainerJson` writes a group's `container.json` on every spawn, by path. While a container runs, `container.json` is mounted read-only over the group folder, so the agent cannot swap that leaf then; the reachable window is before the mount exists — an old or legacy group folder, between runs, or a second mount of the group folder without that read-only layer. This is defense in depth for that window.

- **Problem**: the write used `fs.writeFileSync(path, …)`, which follows a symlink at the leaf and blocks on a reader-less FIFO.
- **Fix**: open the leaf with a no-follow, non-blocking open. A regular file is truncated in place (same inode, so a running container's read-only mount still sees the config live, as before); a symlink or FIFO is unlinked and replaced with a fresh regular file; a planted directory is left in place and the spawn fails, as it did before, rather than being removed.
- **Out of scope / residuals**: the startup backfill read (separate PR); the unlink/create window on the replace path (a sibling replacing the name between operations); and the bind-source resolution — Docker resolves `container.json` as a mount source later, at container-create time, and follows a symlink itself, with other steps (`initGroupFilesystem`, project-doc compose) in between, so this writer does not close that path. All tracked with the other mount-source residuals.

## Related work

No linked issue. Maintainer hardening; the diff and its tests are the review surface.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [x] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/container-config-materialize.test.ts` -> 5 passed: fresh create; in-place rewrite keeps the same inode; a planted symlink is replaced without touching its target; a planted FIFO is replaced without blocking; a planted directory fails the spawn and deletes nothing outside the group.
- Full `vitest run`, `tsc --noEmit`, `lint` (0 errors), `format:check` -> clean apart from load-dependent integration timeouts that pass in isolation.
- Behavior confirmed on Linux + Docker: an in-place truncate keeps a running container's bind-mounted config live; a no-follow open refuses a planted symlink.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [x] No user-visible behavior change
- [ ] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
```

## Security and trust boundaries

Host write of a file inside the container-writable group folder, at spawn time. No change to what the container itself can do. One rare new failure mode: the replace path's exclusive create can fail a spawn with `EEXIST` if a second host process creates `container.json` at the same instant — it fails closed, and is rare.

prs.title: fix(codex): make Responses transport configurable
prs.body:
I created this patch because of reliability issues with the Websockets transport protocol behind a proxy.

Similar to

https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/2672

See my issue

https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/issues/3338


## Summary
- ~Forces~ Re-routes Codex Responses traffic through HTTP/SSE instead of WebSockets to avoid stalled turns hidden behind retry, if parameter `NANOCLAW_CODEX_TRANSPORT` (i.e. is set to `http`).

```
# head -1 nanoclaw/.env
NANOCLAW_CODEX_TRANSPORT=http
```
- if variable is not set, Codex traffic keeps using Websockets (which is the codex default)

---

  > Backward-compatible, opt-in transport configuration. Native Codex transport remains the default; HTTP/SSE can be selected for environments where WebSockets are unreliable.


  Adds a OneCLI-compatible custom provider with supports_websockets = false, preserving authentication and
  conversation continuity. Includes focused regression tests.

  Related: #3338 and #2672.

prs.title: ci: cut the PR gate from 7.5 to 2.5 minutes with sharded tests and a cached image
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Cuts the wait for a pull request's required checks from about 7.5 minutes to about 2.5, without taking anything off the PR path.
- **Problem**: the skills gate ran 22 skill jobs four at a time, and each provider skill built the agent image twice (once per install of its add-remove-add proof); the host suite ran as one 85-second job per Node version.
- **CI workflow**: static checks, host tests and container tests get their own jobs; the host suite runs in four vitest shards per Node version, every file in exactly one shard. Gate: 165 s -> 80 s.
- **Skills gate**: no parallel cap; provider skill jobs build the image through a buildx builder with a layer cache kept by `actions/cache` (written back only on a miss) and never load it, since nothing runs the image there. Gate: 448 s -> 146 s.
- **Skill test**: the second install of the round trip skips its `build` and `test` effects; the byte-for-byte snapshot already proves it identical to the first.
- **Skills gate, continued**: the skill matrix is written into the workflow so every skill job starts with the run; discovery stays as a guard that fails when the matrix and the skill directories differ, and a skill whose registry source is missing skips itself. The legacy-provider refresh runs one job per provider plus one with both in the same tree (the two skills edit the same provider barrels), each with its own image cache key; the payload switch is its own job. The host build is incremental, so the verifier's rebuild takes a second.
- **Cursor probe**: the gateway probe behind the HTTP/2 refusal test asks the SDK not to retry the refused transport (1, 2, 4, 8 s backoffs), which it paid twice per install. Production behaviour unchanged.
- **Trade**: skill jobs now resolve the providers and channels commits themselves instead of taking one pinned pair from discovery, so a push to those branches during a run can reach some jobs and not others; promotion dispatches still pin through their inputs.
- **Out of scope**: the two provider skill jobs sit at about 110 s each (setup, the skill's own build and tests, the contract verifier, a cached image build, remove and re-add), and about 30 s of the gate's wall clock is the chain of two small verdict jobs after them.

## Related work

No issue. CI-only change; the runs on this PR are the evidence.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [x] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- CI runs on this PR: gate green in 70–86 s depending on the runner; shards 31–47 s, checks and container tests about 40 s.
- Registry skills run 39841976193, attempt 2 (warm caches): registry gate green in 146 s; add-cursor 114 s, add-codex 112 s, legacy refresh 100 s and 74 s, every other skill under 70 s. Cold caches (attempt 1): 159 s.
- Registry skills run 39844018530 (with the combined legacy job): green in 155 s; combined legacy refresh 111 s, add-cursor 136 s on a slower runner.
- `pnpm exec tsx scripts/test-registry-skills.ts --old-provider-refresh 99283f3e… add-opencode` locally -> PASS in 87 s.
- `pnpm exec tsx scripts/test-registry-skills.ts add-cursor` locally -> PASS in 106 s; the cursor proxy suite 18.8 s -> 2.2 s.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --shard=N/4` for N in 1..4, locally -> 312 test files, 4166 tests, each file in one shard; same two macOS-only failures as on main.
- `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/test-registry-skills.test.ts` -> 7 passed.
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`, `prettier --check` on the changed script, `shellcheck` on the new script -> clean.

Workflows only. `actions/cache` is pinned by commit. The new script runs in the skills gate with the job's existing permissions and only changes how `container/build.sh` reaches docker. No new secrets or permissions.

## Summary

Setup refuses a display name that is too long for the agent's folder, says why, and asks again.

## Summary

Setup's verify step now says why a Slack install failed, turns green after a good re-run, and reports when no owner can approve new chats.

prs.title: fix(onecli): warn when a remote gateway points agents at their own machine
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Setup now warns, with the exact fix, when a OneCLI gateway on another machine would send agents to their own machine.

- **Problem**: OneCLI tells agents to use the proxy at `GATEWAY_BASE_URL`, default `host.docker.internal:10255`. With a remote gateway that's the agent's own host, so every model call retries forever and the agent never replies, with no error.
- **Fix**: after setting up or reusing a remote gateway, `check-proxy.ts` reads the proxy address OneCLI hands an existing agent (`/v1/container-config`, which never creates an agent). If it points at the agent's own machine (loopback, `host.docker.internal`, or an address of the agent's host such as its docker bridge), the wizard shows a note. The note's command:
  - sets `GATEWAY_BASE_URL=<gateway-host>:<port>` in place in `~/.onecli/.env`, swapping the file atomically;
  - recreates only `onecli`, keeping the running image, bind address and ports, and refusing an unpinned `latest`;
  - reads the value back with `docker exec`, and fails with the one-line compose change on 1.42-era compose files that don't load that `.env`.

  "Is this machine" also counts a Docker bridge that is down, so a local bridge-bound gateway is never called remote.
- **Out of scope**: the docs.nanoclaw.dev pages (separate docs PR); this PR's SKILL.md only adds the step.

## Related work

No issue; found in the OneCLI 1.45 two-machine test (gateway and NanoClaw on separate LXCs).

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `vitest run .claude/skills/add-onecli/`: 126 pass. The recreate command runs under real `sh` against a stub `docker`. It keeps the published ports, keeps a digest pin, refuses `latest`, and replaces the line where it stands. It leaves `.env` untouched when it can't read it or the final rename fails, and fails loudly when the value doesn't reach the container.
- Live:
  - The two-machine 1.45 setup reproduced the hang.
  - Throwaway 1.42 gateways warned before the fix and stayed quiet after, with no agents created.
  - A Windows WSL install with a bridge-bound local gateway showed no false warning. An earlier run had one, which is the down-bridge fix above.
  - The command against a real 1.42.0 compose on a test VM:
    - the value arrived in the container, and a re-run kept one line;
    - an older-layout compose failed with the message;
    - an unreadable `.env` was left as it was;
    - after a restore, the agent replied.
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact


prs.title: fix(skills): resolve channel ids without jq
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

The Slack, Discord, Telegram, Teams and Dial setup steps no longer need jq, which stock Ubuntu and WSL don't ship.

- **Problem**: these skills pipe `curl` into `jq`, and nothing declares, checks or installs it. On WSL, Slack setup died at "Resolve your DM channel" with `jq: command not found`, which then left a failed install job and no owner.
- **Fix**: simple fields use the engine's `capture:var=.path` (as Mattermost did in #3809). Steps that build a prefix, pick from a list or write a file use a `node -e` one-liner. A good reply gives the same value as before. A bad one now fails where jq let it through: a revoked Slack token, a missing `im:write`, a refused Discord DM.
- **Out of scope**: `add-dial-tool` and `add-dial-number` still use jq. They are optional and run after setup.

## Related work

No issue; found in an OSS user's WSL setup report. The guard test below keeps jq out of every skill setup applies.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `setup/channels/channel-skills-no-jq.test.ts` (44 tests) runs each changed step through the engine on a PATH with Node and no jq, against fixture API replies (good and error shapes). A guard fails if any skill's `nc:run` step pipes through jq (it doesn't read the scripts those steps call).
- The related skill and setup suites pass (251 tests). Putting back the old Slack file fails the new tests.
- Not run against the real Slack, Discord, Teams or Dial APIs.

```release-note
Slack, Discord, Telegram, Teams and Dial setup no longer need jq, so they work on a stock Ubuntu or WSL install. The optional Dial tool still needs jq.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

The Dial default-sender pin now writes its temp file as 0600 (before, the default umask applied). Untrusted API replies are only parsed, never executed.

prs.title: fix(setup): reach Docker from the user service when the docker group was just added
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

When setup has just added the user to the docker group, the background user service can now reach Docker on the first run.

- **Problem**: the systemd user manager keeps the groups it had at login, and setup's linger keeps it alive, so logging out doesn't help. Setup's `setfacl` workaround needs the `acl` package, which stock Ubuntu and WSL lack. The service crash-loops on `docker.sock`, the first chat is skipped, and the printed fix (`sudo setfacl …`) can't run.
- **Fix**: in the service step, install `acl` non-interactively (`sudo -n`, apt only) when `setfacl` is missing. Then apply the socket ACL and re-check from the user manager before starting the service. When it still can't reach Docker, the wizard prints commands that work. That means the acl install only when needed, the setfacl line, clearing the crash backoff, and `systemctl --user restart <unit>`, plus that a reboot (on WSL, `wsl --shutdown`) makes the group stick. If the ACL was applied and the service still can't reach Docker, it points at `systemctl --user status` / `journalctl` instead of repeating setfacl.
- **Out of scope**: the ACL resets when Docker restarts; the reboot note covers the lasting fix.

## Related work

Refs #2006
<!-- Merges cleanly with the sudo up-front PR in either order: this one keeps its platform checks inside setup/lib/docker-access-hint.ts. -->

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `vitest run setup/service setup/lib/docker-access-hint.test.ts setup/auto`: 65 pass (14 Linux-only skipped on macOS). They cover acl install → ACL → re-check before the restart, no cached sudo ticket, ACL applied but still no access, no apt, and group not stale.
- Live, with a user whose sudo needs a password and no Docker or acl:
  - On exe.dev, the first run without this fix reproduced the crash loop. With it, the log says `Installing acl for the socket workaround` → `Applied temporary ACL…`, and the agent replies.
  - Same on Windows 11 WSL / Ubuntu 24.04 with Docker Engine.
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
When setup has just added you to the docker group, it now gives NanoClaw's background service access to Docker itself (when your sudo password is still cached). Otherwise it prints commands that work; before, the first chat failed and the suggested fix needed a tool that isn't installed.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

Installs the `acl` package with `sudo -n` (no prompt) and grants the current user read/write on `docker.sock` by ACL, the same access the docker group membership setup just added.

prs.title: fix(setup): ask for the sudo password up front on Linux, and give WSL the right docker-group hint
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

On Linux and WSL, setup now asks for the sudo password once, in the open, before the progress spinner hides it.

- **Problem**: `nanoclaw.sh` runs the Node bootstrap under a spinner, and the container step installs or starts Docker inside a windowed step. sudo's prompt lands under that output, the user never sees it, and it times out (#2025).
- **Fix**: a pre-flight in `nanoclaw.sh` (`setup/lib/sudo-preflight.sh`) says what it will install, then runs `sudo -v` in the foreground. It asks only when setup will really use sudo: it follows `setup/lib/node-version.sh` (the #4183 minimums, uvx, version-manager Node), so an unpatched apt Node 22 asks and a patched or nvm-managed one doesn't. The container step asks again only if that answer has expired. When Docker runs but the socket refuses the user, the reason reads "add you to the docker group". On WSL, the docker-group hint says to run `wsl --shutdown`, since logging out doesn't refresh groups there.
- **Out of scope**: the service-side docker-group fix (separate PR).

## Related work

Closes #2025
Refs #2006

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `vitest run setup/lib/sudo-preflight-shell.test.ts setup/lib/sudo-preflight.test.ts setup/auto.container-sudo.test.ts setup/lib/node-version.test.ts`: 72 pass. They cover Node missing or below the minimum (apt vs a version manager), patched Node off PATH, uvx, root, passwordless sudo, no TTY, `--skip container`, and refused sudo. A scripted run of setup.sh's real path with a fake `sudo` agreed with the pre-flight on 19 machine shapes.
- Live, with a user whose sudo needs a password and no Node or Docker:
  - exe.dev Ubuntu 24.04 and Windows 11 WSL 3.0.3 / Ubuntu 24.04 with Docker Engine: exactly one prompt, before the spinner.
  - The same WSL run on main showed the prompt after "Installing the basics…".
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Setup on Linux and WSL asks for your password before it starts installing (usually once), instead of hiding the sudo prompt behind the progress spinner. On WSL, the docker-group message now tells you to run `wsl --shutdown`.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

`sudo -v` runs in the foreground only when setup is about to install or update Node, install or start Docker, or add the user to the docker group; no new privileged command.

prs.title: feat(context-preview): revive the context-preview tool on main
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Revives `scripts/context-preview.ts` (the "see what the agent sees" tool) on today's main, so a maintainer or an e2e run can print the exact context an agent reads without spawning a container.

- **Problem**: the tool lived on `context-preview-tool` (#3004, closed unmerged), 717 commits behind; four of its seams were gone and its host half predates the async DB boundary, the provider contracts, and the flat composed project document.
- **Fix**: port both halves to the current code paths (`initTestDb`, `resolveProviderContribution` + `buildMounts`, `createScheduledTask`, `createProvider('claude')`) and re-add the seams it imports instead of copying strings: `ClaudeProvider.buildQueryOptions()`, `formatMessagesWithCommands` (now exported), `listRegisteredTools()`, `setTestConfig()`.
- **Not re-added**: `taskPromptWithLog` — the task contract now lives in the system prompt's task mode (`buildSystemPromptAddendum`), which the tool renders through the same path `index.ts` uses.
- **New flags**: `--persona-file` stages standing instructions through `stageGroupPersona`; `--replay <jsonl> [--turn <seq|a-b>]` stages real inbound rows, routing, destinations and the stored continuation from a mailbox-format session dump, so a real turn's exact prompt renders (with the SDK `resume` it ran with).
- **No more mirror**: the Bun half reads the tool-module list from the MCP barrel file instead of duplicating it, so an installed or removed tool module shows up on the next run.
- **Out of scope**: a central-DB target other than the in-memory SQLite sandbox (a Postgres-only deployment migration cannot run there), and a container-config override for the synthetic group.

Design and maintenance seams: `docs/context-preview.md`. Background: the hub page [NanoClaw context-preview — see what the agent sees](https://team-metabase.tailc2ca02.ts.net/htmlit/p/engineering/tools/nanoclaw-context-preview) (tailnet).

## Related work

Supersedes #3004. No issue: the production diff is four small exports plus one extract-method refactor (`query()` now calls `buildQueryOptions()`), all covered by the existing provider and poll-loop suites.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` and `pnpm exec tsc -p container/agent-runner/tsconfig.json --noEmit` → clean; both new scripts also typecheck under an ad-hoc tsconfig that includes them.
- `pnpm exec vitest run` → the new `scripts/context-preview.test.ts` runs `first-message --json` end to end with the Bun half and asserts the five surfaces are non-empty. Its first CI run failed on Linux: the composed doc was located as "first read-only file mount in the group dir", which is `container.json` there; macOS masked it because mount paths are realpaths (`/private/var`) and never matched. Fixed by matching the provider contract's project-doc file name (the name `buildMounts` uses), and the test now runs with a realpath'd `TMPDIR` so macOS reproduces Linux (old code: `container.json`, 0 sections; new: `CLAUDE.md`, 9 sections). Re-verified on the branch merged onto current `main`: both typechecks clean, smoke test passes, all seven scenarios run.
- `cd container/agent-runner && bun test` → 429 pass, 0 fail.
- All seven scenarios run and print every surface (`first-message`, `followup`, `accumulate`, `task-fire`, `on-wake`, `a2a`, `subagent`), plus `--json` and `--section claude-md`; nine `mcp__nanoclaw__*` tools listed on trunk.
- Replay of a real session dump (a k3s e2e lane, Claude provider): the connect-nudge turn renders with the dump's stored continuation as `resume`, the session's real destination in `from=` and in the addendum, and the `Persona` section byte-identical to the persona the deployment's composer staged. Run on a copy of that deployment's host tree, the tool composes the tree's own module and skill sections (canvas, rooms, nanoco-gw, slack-construct) and lists its twelve tools.
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [x] No user-visible behavior change
- [ ] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
```

## Security and trust boundaries

The tool never touches the live install read-write: the whole run happens in a throwaway sandbox with an in-memory central DB; `--group` opens `data/v2.db` read-only. Only `ASSISTANT_NAME`, `ASSISTANT_HAS_OWN_NUMBER`, `TZ` and `DEFAULT_AGENT_PROVIDER` are copied from `.env` into the sandbox (never credentials); per-MCP-server env values are redacted in the output; `CLAUDE_*` host-shell overrides are stripped from the Bun half's env. No workflow or container changes.

issues.title: [申诉] LobsterAI 账号被误封，未恶意使用却被封禁（18811912020 / 13043620160）
issues.body:
## 账号信息
- 账号 1：18811912020
- 账号 2：13043620160
- GitHub 账号（申诉人）：https://github.com/7597qqme

## 问题现象
两个 LobsterAI（有道龙虾）账号近期无法登录/使用，系统提示账号已被封禁或异常。
本人声明：**两个账号均未进行过恶意使用、未刷接口、未批量调用**，封禁认定疑似误判。

## 补充说明（可能的误判来源）
我曾在本地第三方 DSH 插件（dsh-comprehensive-platform / our-free-model）中配置过 LobsterAI 账号凭据，用于调用有道模型服务。
该插件存在自动化流量：
1. 每日自动签到（每天 1 次，模拟正常 App 行为）；
2. 之前版本的模型目录自动刷新间隔为 5 分钟，会带真实账号凭据轮询 `GET /api/models/available`，每渠道每天产生约 288 次带凭据请求。

我已意识到这可能被上游风控系统判定为“异常活动（unusual activity）”，导致账号被封。**现已从本地彻底移除相关 LobsterAI 凭据，且修复了刷新间隔（已改为默认 6 小时 + 抖动 + 无已登录账号时零请求），不会再产生自动化流量。**

## 诉求
1. 查明封禁原因，并告知两个账号的封禁时长；
2. 若确认为误判，请解除封禁，恢复正常使用；
3. 若无法解封，请提供可申诉的客服联系方式或申诉入口。

## 时间线
- 发现封禁：约 2026-10-23 起
- 已移除本地凭据：2026-10-24
- GitHub 申诉提交：2026-10-24

---

感谢配合。

issues.title: [Feature] 增加“退出前不再确认”设置项，跳过 Cmd+Q 退出二次确认
issues.body:
## Problem Statement

每次通过 Cmd+Q、应用菜单、Dock 或托盘退出 LobsterAI 时，都会弹出原生“确认退出”对话框，且没有任何设置项可以关闭。对于把客户端当作常驻工具的 user，一天多次启停时这是纯摩擦。

代码位置：`dist-electron/main/libs/appQuitConfirmation.js`。`before-quit` 对所有用户发起的退出统一调用 `showAppQuitConfirmation`，只有更新安装、应用重启、系统关机/注销会走 bypass。

## Proposed Solution

在「设置」中增加一个开关，例如“退出前需要确认”，默认开启：

1. 开启时保持现有行为，弹原生确认框。
2. 关闭后，用户发起的退出直接执行现有清理流程 `runAppCleanupAndExit`，不再弹框。
3. 安全兜底：仍存在未保存的 Markdown / Office 编辑时，无论开关状态都保留确认或提示保存，避免数据丢失。
4. 该设置持久化到本地 store，与 `auto_launch_enabled`、`prevent_sleep_enabled` 等现有应用设置一致。

## Alternatives Considered

1. 用 `kill -TERM` 退出：可绕过弹窗且会走清理，但普通用户不友好，也容易误伤正在运行的任务。
2. 本地修改 `app.asar`：会破坏 ASAR 完整性校验和代码签名，且每次更新失效，不可持续。

## Additional Context

- 客户端版本：2026.10.16（macOS arm64）
- 场景：常驻使用，频繁启停客户端
- 建议保留“有未保存编辑时强制确认”的兜底逻辑

issues.title: [Bug] stdio MCP server 静默丢弃 NODE_OPTIONS，导致 TLS 拦截环境下 MCP 工具全部 fetch failed
issues.body:
### Bug Description

在 2026.10.16 版本中，LobsterAI 的 MCP 运行时会静默丢弃 stdio 型 MCP server 的 `NODE_OPTIONS` 环境变量，导致所有依赖系统根证书的 MCP 服务不可用。

具体表现：配置好的 GitHub MCP server 能正常启动，`tools/list` 也正常返回 26 个工具，但任何实际调用都失败：

```
github__search_repositories failed: MCP error -32603: fetch failed
```

日志中只有一条 warn 级提示，UI 上完全没有反馈：

```
[bundle-mcp] server "GitHub": env "NODE_OPTIONS" is blocked for stdio startup safety and was ignored.
```

影响面不止 GitHub：凡是运行在企业 MITM 代理或本机 TLS 拦截（Steam++/SteamTools、Zscaler、Netskope 等）环境下的 Node.js 型 stdio MCP server，都会因为 Node 不信任系统根证书库而全部 `fetch failed`。而此前唯一可行的规避手段就是 `NODE_OPTIONS=--use-system-ca`，现在被这条安全策略取消了。

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Windows 11 (10.0.26200)，安装并启用带 hosts/证书拦截的加速器（本例为 Steam++：`C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts` 中把 `api.github.com` 等指向 `127.0.0.1`，并把 `CN=SteamTools Certificate` 根证书装入 `LocalMachine\Root`）。
2. 在 LobsterAI 中配置 GitHub MCP server（`@modelcontextprotocol/server-github`），并在 `mcp.servers.GitHub.env` 中加入 `NODE_OPTIONS: "--use-system-ca"`。
3. 重启 LobsterAI，让模型调用任意 GitHub MCP 工具，例如 `search_repositories`。
4. 观察结果：工具调用报 `MCP error -32603: fetch failed`。

### Expected Behavior

期望在以下任一方式下 MCP 可用：

1. `NODE_OPTIONS=--use-system-ca` 不再被静默丢弃（或至少针对性地放行 `--use-system-ca` 这一无害参数）；
2. 或为 stdio MCP server 提供与 HTTP 传输对齐的自定义 CA 能力（目前 `sslVerify` 只在 HTTP/SSE 传输上生效，stdio 没有对应选项）；
3. 或至少把该 warn 提示暴露到 UI（MCP 设置页或工具报错详情），而不是只写日志。

### Actual Behavior

- `NODE_OPTIONS` 命中 `blockedEverywhereKeys` 被丢弃，只在 gateway 日志留一条 warn；
- MCP server 自身进程完全正常：手工用同一份配置拉起 stdio 会话，`initialize` 成功、`tools/list` 返回 26 个工具（create_or_update_file、search_repositories 等），说明配置、路径、PAT 都没问题；
- 去掉 `NODE_OPTIONS` 后，Node 的 undici 不信任系统根证书库，与被拦截的 `api.github.com` 握手时证书校验失败，最终表现为 `fetch failed`；
- 改为 `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` 指向拦截方根证书 PEM 后立即可用（见下方实测对照），但该 key 属于 `blockedOverrideOnlyKeys`，只是恰好对 stdio env 放行，用户无从得知，也无法在 UI 中配置。

### Environment

```
- OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26200.9457)
- LobsterAI Version: 2026.10.16
- Node.js Version: v22.22.2 (C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe)
- Bundled openclaw runtime: 2026.8.1 (dsh 0.1.5-rc.3)
```

### Logs

启动期日志（`%APPDATA%\LobsterAI\openclaw\logs\gateway-2026-10-20.log`）：

```
[bundle-mcp] server "GitHub": env "NODE_OPTIONS" is blocked for stdio startup safety and was ignored.
```

工具调用日志（`gateway-2026-10-17.log`）：

```
[tools] github__search_repositories failed: MCP error -32603: fetch failed raw_params={"query":"openclaw","perPage":3}
[security] blocked URL fetch (url-fetch) targetOrigin=https://api.github.com reason=Blocked: resolves to private/internal/special-use IP address
```

（第二条来自 hosts 指向 127.0.0.1 的拦截，是同一根因在 URL 抓取侧的另一个表现。）

### 定位结论

策略源码位置（安装目录内，只读查看）：

- `resources\cfmind\dist\mcp-stdio-fN-LPfO8.js`：`toMcpEnvRecord()` 用 `isDangerousMcpStdioEnvVarName()` 过滤 env，命中即丢弃；
- `resources\cfmind\dist\host-env-security-*.js`：`NODE_OPTIONS` 位于 `blockedEverywhereKeys`（无条件丢弃），`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` 位于 `blockedOverrideOnlyKeys`（仅拦宿主 exec 覆盖，stdio MCP env 放行）。

实测对照（同一份 config，仅替换 env 一项）：

| stdio env | 结果 |
| --- | --- |
| `NODE_OPTIONS=--use-system-ca` | 被丢弃 → `fetch failed` |
| `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=<拦截方根证书 PEM>` | 保留生效 → `search_repositories` 返回 `total_count: 74702` |

### 建议修复方向

1. 在 `blockedEverywhereKeys` 过滤之后，对 MCP stdio env 额外放行白名单参数（例如仅允许 `--use-system-ca`，拒绝 `--require`/`--import` 等可执行注入项）；
2. 或给 stdio 传输补上与 HTTP 一致的 `sslVerify` / `ca` 配置项，并在 MCP 设置界面提供入口；
3. 以上任一种之外，当前这条“静默丢弃”至少要在 UI 上可见，否则用户只能看到无解释的 `fetch failed`，排查成本很高。

---

*本 issue 由用户环境实测整理，Token 等敏感信息已移除。*

## Summary

Contribute the current **Lynxce (灵策智算)** expert sources, existing avatars, and brand attribution for maintainer review: **43 desktop presets, 53 expert teams (328 member/lead roles), and 783 WorkBuddy experts**, totaling **879 catalog entries**.

The content lives entirely under `contributions/lynxce-experts/`. Start with its README and `index.json`. WorkBuddy packages include their complete latest local agent/skill/reference/script deliveries, deduplicated by slug; source revision selection and 27 same-version prompt conflicts are recorded.

**Disclosure:** I work on Lynxce. The original WorkBuddy metadata includes commercial distribution flags and some external Lynxce services. The contribution preserves those facts; it does not claim free access to services or WorkBuddy approval.

## Changes Made

- Add complete desktop preset/team definitions, existing local SVG avatar mappings, 783 WorkBuddy source packages and their existing portraits.
- Reference the separate Lynxce brand mark and `灵策智算 LynxceAI` attribution on every contributed entry. Portraits are retained without painting new marks onto them.
- Inventory another **215 third-party imported experts** with origin and hashes only. Their prompts, packages and original portraits are excluded because whole-package redistribution permission is unconfirmed.
- Preserve source package notices, author metadata, dependency declarations and distribution flags; include SHA-256/size integrity records and a standard-library, read-only verifier.

## Integration and review boundaries

This PR proposes **content**, not automatic runtime registration or live-store publication. LobsterAI currently publishes its expert catalog remotely. Maintainers can select entries, host approved assets on the existing CDN, map to `ExpertCatalog`, validate, and publish through that existing process. No Electron, IPC, agent storage, CDN allowlist or production configuration changes are included. It is independent of #2874/#2875.

- The 43 desktop presets declare 17 skill IDs; their desktop skill bodies are not included and require mapping to upstream equivalents.
- WorkBuddy bundled skill bodies are included. Its plugin conventions require conversion before installation in LobsterAI.
- 397 WorkBuddy entries declare MCP dependencies, 98 appear in the local CPS inventory, and 309 retain `needEncrypt` source metadata. External services, purchases, credentials and platform review states were not exercised or asserted.
- Team portrait hint IDs are preserved, with real local SVG fallback assets supplied; they are not represented as bundled remote photos.
- The snapshot contains 5,457 files, mostly resource/package content. All WorkBuddy delivery files are retained byte for byte apart from excluding four Python cache files. Historical blank lines at EOF in original package text are preserved.

## Testing

- `python3 contributions/lynxce-experts/verify.py`: **passed**; 879 entries, all 5,457 files, image formats/paths, package references, branding, source hashes and file integrity checked.
- Independent full-file comparison of **all 783 selected WorkBuddy packages**, including **311 ZIP sources**: matched the selected local source deliveries; no missing package references or relative Markdown links.
- Additional private-key, token, credential-assignment and personal absolute-path scans: no actual credentials or machine paths found.
- `git -c core.whitespace=-blank-at-eof diff --cached --check`: passed; only historical EOF blank lines in verbatim source imports are exempted.
- Runtime build/tests were not run because application code is unchanged. Individual expert workflows and external integrations have not all been executed.

## Type of Change

- [x] Other: expert content and asset contribution for catalog review
- [x] Documentation update

## Electron-Specific Changes

- [x] None

The source attribution and third-party boundary are documented in the contribution README. Validation establishes content completeness and consistency, not upstream acceptance or live marketplace availability.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): stop restarting the gateway right after it starts
prs.body:
## Summary

User logs (Windows, 2026.10.16) show the gateway starting **twice on every launch**: it boots once, and as soon as it is ready `ensureRunning:config-confirm` hard-restarts it. All 7 launches in the logs reproduce it. The second boot adds 100–280s to every launch.

### Root cause
1. **Trigger:** `runStartupCacheWarmup` cached `/api/models/available` without the derived `presetContextWindows`, but `loadAvailableServerModels` adds them. So the renderer's first `getModels` always reported `metadataChanged=true`, and the rendered `models` gained `contextWindows`/`contextWindowDefault` while the gateway was still starting.
2. **Escalation:** a starting gateway owns its config file, so the change was deferred. `executeDeferredGatewayRestart` always synced with `restartGatewayIfRunning: true` + `expectedImpact: Restart`. Because the target can't be persisted during startup, `configChanged` stayed true, which re-armed a respawn demand on the generation that was still booting. The sync also re-ran every 3s while the gateway was starting (35 runs, ~18s of main-process CPU in one launch).
3. **Restart:** once the gateway was ready, `ensureRunning:config-confirm` saw the pending respawn and hard-restarted it (6s shutdown timeout → SIGKILL → ~8s prep → ~90s boot). A model-list change only needs a hot `config.apply`.

### Changes
- **Model metadata:** new `updateServerModelMetadataFromResponse()` in `claudeSettings.ts`, used by both the startup warmup and `loadAvailableServerModels`, so an identical response is treated as unchanged and no startup config sync happens.
- **Deferred restart:** the deferred state now records whether a respawn was actually requested.
  - A change deferred because the gateway is not running, and that asks for no respawn itself, is only reapplied once the gateway is up (via the existing `config-confirm` / gateway-ready reconcile).
  - Deferred polls skip while the engine phase is `starting`.
  - Real restart demands (env, bindings, plugin impact, explicit IM restart, deferrals while busy) keep their previous behavior.
- **Startup prep:** an enabled `nsp-clawguard` forces the pre-spawn compatibility helpers only when a supported payload exists under `third-party-extensions` (the only case its install repair acts on). An unsupported (e.g. 2.5.8) or removed package now uses the existing startup-prep marker instead of rerunning both helpers (~8–9s) on every gateway start.

### Electron / OpenClaw behavior changes
- OpenClaw config/restart: model-list changes that arrive while the gateway is starting are hot-applied after ready instead of triggering a gateway respawn.
- No IPC, storage, or UI changes.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm test` (7929 passed before rebase; targeted suites re-run after rebasing onto the latest `release/2026.10.19`)
- [x] New regression test: a startup-warmed cache stays unchanged for the same `/api/models/available` response (fails on the old warmup code)
- [x] New tests for preset context window derivation and for nsp-clawguard startup-prep gating (supported / unsupported / missing payload)
- [x] `npx eslint --max-warnings 0` on touched files, `npm run compile:electron`
- [ ] Manual: cold start in `npm run electron:dev` while logged in. Expect a single `gateway process spawned`, no `HARD RESTART EXECUTING. reason=ensureRunning:config-confirm`, and `server model metadata unchanged, skipping config sync` on the renderer's model fetch

prs.title: fix(desktop-companion): keep orb clicks from activating the main window on macOS
prs.body:
## Summary

On macOS, clicking the desktop companion orb while the LobsterAI main window was on screen but covered by another app could bring the main window to the front instead of opening the quick input panel. With the main window minimized, the panel opened normally. The expected behavior is that clicking the orb always opens only the quick input panel, whatever state the main window is in.

### Root cause

Electron's `type: 'panel'` on macOS only emulates a nonactivating panel; AppKit logs `NSWindow does not support nonactivating panel styleMask 0x80`. A real click on the non-focusable orb half-activates the app: WindowServer treats LobsterAI as frontmost, but no window keeps key status. The quick panel lost key focus about 40 ms after showing, the macOS focus watcher dismissed it about 250 ms later, and key focus could fall to the main window. Whether it failed depended on which app was in front; native apps and Claude reproduced it reliably.

### Changes

- **Orb is key-capable on macOS** (`desktopCompanionManager.showOrb`). A click then hands key focus over cleanly without activating the app, the same way the composer panel already does. Windows and Linux are unchanged.
- **Orb ignores `close` unless the manager is disposing.** Once the orb can be key, the default app menu's Cmd+W would otherwise close it. This uses the same pattern as the composer panel; quit runs `dispose()` first, so quitting is unaffected.
- **Dock restore uses `restore()` for a minimized main window** (`app.on('activate')`). `show()` on a minimized window draws it at full size for one frame before the Dock animation, which looked like a flash. This flash predates this PR.

## Verification

Verified on macOS 15.1 with real OS-level clicks (CGEvent), tracing window focus events, companion IPC and the on-screen window order:

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main window covered by another app (native app, Claude, Calculator), click orb | Panel lost focus and closed; main window could take focus | Panel stays open and focused; main window untouched |
| Main window minimized, click orb | Inconsistent | Panel stays open and focused; main window not restored |
| Click Dock icon with main window minimized | Full-size frame flashes before the Dock animation | Animates straight out of the Dock, then takes focus |
| Orb focused, press Cmd+W | — | Orb stays |

- `tsc --noEmit` passes for the Electron project.
- ESLint is clean on both changed files.
- `vitest run src/main/desktopCompanion` passes (300 tests).

## Electron behavior notes

- **Windowing:** on macOS the orb can become the key window. After the quick panel closes, keyboard focus stays on the orb rather than returning to the previous app. Before this change, keystrokes at that point went nowhere.
- **Not reproduced:** a report that a first orb click sometimes made the panel vanish and needed a second click. It did not reproduce in a traced hands-on session or in 30+ replays after this change.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): keep tool payloads unmasked in transcripts for cache replay
prs.body:
## Summary
Users reported much faster credit use after upgrading. Follow-ups on heavy code-reading sessions read only about 15% of their prompt from the provider cache. OpenClaw v2026.8.1 masks secret-shaped text only in the persisted transcript copy, and the bare AWS secret pattern also matches 40-character relative paths. The next turn therefore replays different bytes than the previous request and loses the prefix cache from the first masked string onward.

## Changes Made
- Add `openclaw-tool-payload-transcript-fidelity.patch`, backporting the agents half of upstream OpenClaw #169063 (`f956a18741`). Tool arguments, tool results and conversation text are persisted and emitted as live tool events exactly as the model saw them. Logging, diagnostic, telemetry and config redaction, image payload stripping and persisted detail size caps are kept.
- Add a strong apply validator, README notes with verification and removal conditions, and patch contract tests.
- Add log-only TokenProxy prompt-prefix diagnostics: each model request is fingerprinted by hashes and compared with the previous request of the same session. The log line reports the first changed component, the stable prefix bytes and the cached tokens. It carries no message text.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Testing
- [x] OpenClaw: 35 related test files, 1301 tests passed. The new 40-character path regression fails without the source change.
- [x] The official patch script reapplies all 73 patches from a clean tag, and the result matches the tested tree byte for byte.
- [x] LobsterAI: `npm test -- openclawPatches openclawReplay patch` (149 tests) and the TokenProxy/diagnostics tests (71 tests) passed. Changed-file ESLint is clean.
- [x] Rebuilt the runtime and ran the scheduled-task audit task plus follow-ups (external account, deepseek-flash). Every follow-up's first request was a clean `change=append` with 99–100% cached tokens, and completed follow-up turns hit 98.6–99.6% cache overall.
- OpenClaw core tsgo reports existing errors only in three untracked files from other patches; the files changed here are clean.
- The server returned intermittent `500` errors during the check (serverTrace `0336c125`, `185d1115`, `300cee7a` and others). They are unrelated to this change; the server team should look into them.

## Electron-Specific Changes
- OpenClaw runtime patch: the runtime must be rebuilt (`npm run openclaw:runtime:host`) for the change to take effect.
- Behavior: secrets read by tools are now stored unmasked in local transcripts and live tool events, matching what was already sent to the model. Logs stay masked. Transcripts written before the upgrade keep their masked text, so the first follow-up after upgrading misses the cache once.
- The diagnostic adds one log line of about 320 bytes per model request (routine steps at debug level). Memory is bounded at 64 sessions × 4 lineages.

prs.title: fix(subscription-trial): hide popup for subscribed and enterprise accounts
prs.body:
## Summary
Signed-in subscribers and enterprise accounts could see the one-cent trial popup, including when a previously open popup reappeared after another dialog closed. Require fresh subscription and enterprise identity checks before each new or restored display, and keep the popup hidden when either refresh fails.

## Changes Made
- Wait for authentication and subscription readiness; suppress known subscribed and enterprise accounts.
- Allow signed-in display only after a fresh free subscription result and a successful personal-account context refresh. Revoke display approval while hidden and discard responses after account or visibility changes.
- Preserve anonymous behavior, existing activity checks, device-level weekly frequency, and the three-dismissal limit. Restoring a popup preserves its existing frequency record.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Testing
- [x] Changed-file ESLint passed: `npx eslint --ext ts,tsx --report-unused-disable-directives --max-warnings 0 src/renderer/components/SubscriptionTrialCampaign.tsx`.
- [x] `npm run build` passed with Node.js 24.22.1.
- [x] `git diff --check` passed.
- Full `npm run lint` remains blocked by 51 existing import/export sorting errors across 49 unrelated files and one existing unused-variable warning in `src/scheduledTask/integration.test.ts:9`. Diagnostics match the pre-change baseline; the changed file is clean.
- No automated tests or manual UI/browser validation were run; validation was limited to lint and build as requested.

## Checklist
- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines.
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code.
- [x] I have commented the visibility invalidation and refresh failure handling.
- [x] The changed file introduces no ESLint errors or warnings.

## Electron-Specific Changes
Renderer display gating calls the existing `auth.getQuota()` and `enterpriseAccount.getContext()` IPC APIs. The explicit enterprise refresh success check is necessary because `getQuota()` can return a cached enterprise context after a refresh failure. IPC contracts and local popup frequency storage remain unchanged.

prs.title: fix(image-editor): prevent preview flicker and selection crashes
prs.body:
## Summary
Fix image editor flicker and selection crashes reported in the 10.19 feedback (rows 6, 7, and 10). Previews remain stable at fractional viewport sizes, and releasing a selection drag no longer causes `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'start')`.

## Related Issue
10.19 feedback: rows 6, 7, and 10. No linked GitHub issue.

## Changes Made
- Preserve fractional viewport dimensions from `ResizeObserver.contentRect` and skip unchanged measurements. This prevents zoom rounding from repeatedly toggling scrollbars and resizing the preview in local-edit, aspect-ratio, and erase flows.
- Capture the drag origin before scheduling the React selection update, so the updater remains valid after pointer release clears the drag state.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Manual testing performed

Validation on Windows with a real Electron client driven through Playwright/CDP:
- Reproduced preview oscillation before the fix (114–121 size changes in 2 seconds); the same cases stabilized after the fix.
- Passed 36 image/mode/window-and-zoom combinations and 150 rapid selection drags without renderer errors.
- Completed two real erase tasks against the test environment and verified stable previews through submission and completion.
- Checked drawing, text, undo/redo, save-copy, pan/zoom, reset-to-fit, and adding a selection to the conversation draft.
- Changed-file ESLint and `git diff --check` passed.
- `npm test -- imageEditing imageEditDrafts imageText`: 7 files, 33 tests passed.
- `npm run build` passed with existing build warnings.

## Screenshots (if applicable)
Screenshots, logs, recordings, and the detailed acceptance report remain local as requested; no acceptance files are uploaded in this PR.

## Checklist
- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented the non-obvious resize behavior
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] Relevant existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

No product documentation changes are needed. Regression evidence for these browser scheduling/layout issues is retained in the local Electron acceptance materials.

## Electron-Specific Changes
- [x] None of the main process, preload, IPC, storage, runtime, or window-management contracts change; this is a renderer-only fix.

## Additional Notes
Row 2 (intermittent Windows unresponsiveness) was investigated using the existing feedback. It was not reproduced in either the development or production renderer, including CPU-throttled and scaled-window runs, and is not claimed as fixed by this PR.

prs.title: feat(cowork): refactor prompt input with structured composer
prs.body: ## 为什么要做这次优化 这次改动不只是补一个 `@` 或 `/` 功能，而是对 Cowork 输入框做一次输入内核重构。 当前 Cowork 输入区虽然已经支持附件、技能和快捷操作，但底层仍然是围绕 `textarea + 字符串拼接` 演进出来的实现，已经开始限制体验和后续扩展： 1. 资源“已附带”和“正文中显式引用”没有被统一到一个更顺手的输入体验里，用户很难像 Cursor 这类产品那样在一句话里自然表达“这条指令明确引用了哪些资源”。 2. `@` 和 `/` 的发现成本较高，尤其是在复杂任务里，用户需要频繁在外部胶囊栏、技能栏、快捷操作区之间切换。 3. 现有实现对“文件引用”“技能引用”“快捷操作”“后续更多结构化 token”缺少统一输入模型，每增加一种交互都需要继续在字符串层叠补丁，维护成本和回归风险会持续变高。 4. 如果继续沿用原有输入内核，很难稳定承接后续更丰富的 composer 能力，例如更多类型的 `@资源`、更复杂的 `/操作`、结构化片段混排、节点级删除/替换，以及更稳定的 IME 和键盘导航交互。 这次改动的目标是： - 先把 Cowork 输入区升级成可扩展的结构化 composer 内核，为后续演进打基础。 - 在不破坏原有附件胶囊栏、技能激活栏和快捷操作栏的前提下，引入结构化 inline composer 体验。 - 让用户只在自己显式 `@` 引用或 `/` 选择时，输入框才体现结构化意图，从而实现更接近 Cursor 一类产品的输入交互。 - 保持发送链路仍然兼容现有 `prompt: string` 主路径，降低对主流程的侵入和回归风险。 ## 方案设计 ### 核心思路 在 `CoworkPromptInput` 内部引入轻量结构化 composer，但严格区分三类状态： - 已附带资源：继续走原有胶囊栏语义 - 已激活技能：继续走原有技能栏语义 - 正文显式引用：仅当用户通过 `@` 选择时，才插入 inline token 这样既能提供结构化输入体验，又不会把原本的附件/技能主路径改坏。 更重要的是，这次把输入框从“字符串编辑器”升级成了“结构化节点编辑器 + 序列化层”的模式。后续再引入新的 token 类型或 suggestion 源时，可以沿用同一套扩展点，而不需要继续在 `textarea` 的字符串规则上叠补丁。 ### 架构分层 ```text CoworkPromptInput # 输入区主控，保留原有附件/技能/发送主路径 composer/resourceMention.tsx # @ 资源引用节点与 suggestion 接入 composer/slashCommand.ts # / 快捷操作 suggestion 接入 composer/suggestionPopup.ts # suggestion 浮层渲染、定位、键盘滚动联动 composer/promptSerializer.ts # 结构化 doc -> 兼容字符串 prompt 的序列化 composer/ResourceMentionView.tsx # inline token 视图层 composer/types.ts # token / suggestion / serializer 类型抽象 ``` ### 设计要点 - 低侵入：发送链路不改 `prompt: string` 契约，结构化能力只存在于输入端和序列化层。 - 主路径兼容：上传/粘贴/拖拽附件仍然只进入原胶囊栏；点击技能按钮仍然只激活技能；不会自动往正文里塞 token。 - 显式引用优先：只有用户通过 `@` 选择资源或技能时，正文里才出现结构化 inline token。 - 快捷操作回归语义：`/` 只负责快速选中 quick action / prompt，不直接把模板正文灌进输入框。 - PromptPanel 保持原有“纯替换输入框”语义：用户通过 prompt 面板选择模板时，不会保留旧的 `@` 引用残留。 - 交互细节补齐：浮层支持视口内自适应定位、最大高度收缩，以及键盘上下选择时的滚动跟随。 - 扩展性优先：资源节点、slash item、序列化逻辑和浮层渲染都已模块化，后续新增 provider 或 token 类型时不需要重做整套输入框。 ### Prompt / 数据 / 交互策略 - `@` 与 `/` 的职责边界： - `@` 表示“把某个资源显式引用进这句话里”，解决的是上下文指向问题。 - `/` 表示“快速选择一种预设操作或模板入口”，解决的是任务起手式和动作发现问题。 - 前者会在正文里留下结构化引用 token；后者只更新快捷操作选中态，不直接把模板正文灌进输入框。 - Prompt 策略： - 正文中的 `@attachment` / `@skill` 会序列化成兼容现有链路的文本协议。 - 技能引用在正文和“技能引用”段都统一使用 `@token` 形式，避免附件和技能表现不一致。 - 数据策略： - “已附带附件”与“正文已引用附件”拆成两套状态，避免胶囊栏和正文互相污染。 - 已引用文件不会重复出现在 `输入文件` 段，减少冗余提示词。 - 交互策略： - `@` suggestion 同时支持文件和技能资源。 - `/` suggestion 复用现有 quick action 数据源和选中态，不重造模板系统。 ## 改动内容 ### 新增文件 - `src/renderer/components/cowork/composer/resourceMention.tsx`：定义 `@` 资源引用节点和 suggestion 插件。 - `src/renderer/components/cowork/composer/slashCommand.ts`：定义 `/` 快捷操作 suggestion 插件。 - `src/renderer/components/cowork/composer/suggestionPopup.ts`：统一 suggestion 浮层渲染、定位与键盘导航表现。 - `src/renderer/components/cowork/composer/promptSerializer.ts`：将结构化 editor 状态序列化成兼容旧链路的 prompt。 - `src/renderer/components/cowork/composer/ResourceMentionView.tsx`：渲染正文内的结构化 inline token。 - `src/renderer/components/cowork/composer/types.ts`：composer 资源、slash item、序列化结果等类型定义。 ### 修改文件 - `src/renderer/components/cowork/CoworkPromptInput.tsx`：接入结构化 composer，同时恢复并保留原附件胶囊栏、技能激活栏和发送主路径语义。 - `src/renderer/services/i18n.ts`：补齐 composer / suggestion 相关中英文文案。 - `package.json`：引入结构化 composer 所需的 Tiptap 相关依赖： - `@tiptap/core` - `@tiptap/pm` - `@tiptap/react` - `@tiptap/starter-kit` - `@tiptap/suggestion` - `@tiptap/extension-placeholder` - `/Users/yujiayu/code/ai/lobsterai-development-guides/04-development-execution-checklist.md`：补充了本次使用的 Electron + CDP 运行态验证方式，供后续迭代复用。 ### 关联 commit - `6d13c70`：refactor cowork input into a structured composer while preserving existing main flows. ## 测试验证 1. 使用 `nvm` 切到 Node 24 环境。 2. 对本次相关文件运行 ESLint。 3. 运行 `npm run build`，确认 renderer / main / preload 构建通过。 4. 通过 Electron + CDP 冷启动验证首屏不崩。 5. 验证附件主路径： - 拖拽 / 粘贴 / 上传文件后，只出现在上方胶囊栏，不会自动插入正文。 - 删除胶囊后，对应正文引用也会被同步清理。 6. 验证技能主路径： - 点击技能按钮后，只激活技能栏，不会自动插入正文。 - 仅在用户通过 `@` 选择技能时，正文里才出现 skill token。 7. 验证 `@` suggestion： - 文件和技能都能在同一个 suggestion 浮层里被发现。 - 选中后正文出现结构化 inline token。 8. 验证 `/` suggestion： - 浮层在视口边缘时仍可见，支持高度收缩和位置自适应。 - 键盘上下选择时，滚动条会自动跟随高亮项。 - 选中后只更新快捷操作选中态，不把模板正文直接灌进输入框。 9. 自动化回归补充： - 通过独立 reviewer 检出了 `PromptPanel -> setValue` 的回归风险。 - 修复后补充了 prompt 面板“纯替换输入框”主路径回归验证，确认不会残留旧 `@` 引用。 ## 截图 - 胶囊栏与正文输入解耦：上传附件和激活技能继续保留原有外部胶囊/技能栏语义，不会自动污染正文。 - `@` 统一资源 suggestion：用户在正文里输入 `@` 时，可以在同一个浮层里发现文件和技能资源。 - `/` 浮层支持滚动与自适应：键盘下移时滚动条会自动跟随，高亮项不会丢；浮层会根据视口空间调整显示高度。 - `/` 只联动快捷操作状态，不灌正文：slash 选择后的结果与手动点击 quick action / prompt 对齐，输入框保持干净。 - 输入过程中可随时穿插 `@` 与 `/`：用户可以在连续输入中自然地边写边引用资源、边触发快捷操作，而不需要跳出输入上下文。

prs.title: feat(cowork): 消息书签/收藏系统 + 全局书签视图
prs.body: ## 背景 现有的 Cowork 界面没有办法**保存和回顾重要消息**。用户在进行长对话或多个会话时，经常会丢失对话历史中的关键决策、代码片段或重要指令。本 PR 添加了完整的书签/收藏系统，让用户可以标记、整理并快速导航回重要消息。 ## 设计 ### 两级架构： - **会话级别**：每条消息上的内联书签按钮 + 会话头部浮动面板 - **全局级别**：侧边栏独立视图，按会话分组展示所有书签，支持跨会话跳转 ### 新增文件（3个）： | 文件 | 用途 | |---|---| | `bookmark.ts` | 书签服务 — KV 持久化存储，全局索引（`bookmarks:__index`），内存缓存，发布/订阅机制 | | `BookmarkComponents.tsx` | `BookmarkButton`（消息行内按钮）和 `BookmarksPanel`（会话级浮动面板，支持跳转到消息） | | `BookmarksView.tsx` | 全局书签视图 — 整页展示，按会话分组，包含消息预览和会话标题 | ### 修改文件（6个）： - `CoworkSessionDetail.tsx` — 在用户/助手消息的复制按钮旁集成书签按钮；头部添加书签面板开关；监听 `cowork:jump-to-message` 自定义事件实现跨会话导航 - `Sidebar.tsx` — 添加书签导航入口，支持激活状态高亮 - `App.tsx` — 在视图切换器中注册 `bookmarks` 视图；添加 `handleNavigateToBookmark` 跨会话跳转处理 - `index.ts` — 导出 `BookmarksView` 组件 - `i18n.ts` — 添加 10 条书签相关的国际化翻译（中文 + 英文） - `index.css` — 添加 `bookmark-flash` 关键帧动画用于跳转高亮 ### 关键设计要点： - **零数据库迁移**：使用现有 KV 存储（`bookmarks:{sessionId}` + `bookmarks:__index`），无需新建数据表 - **渐进增强**：书签按钮悬停时显示，已收藏消息显示持久图标 — 不影响现有 UI - **跨会话导航**：全局视图点击 → `coworkService.loadSession()` → 自定义事件 → `scrollIntoView` + 闪烁高亮动画 - **响应式更新**：行内按钮使用 `useSyncExternalStore`；面板/视图使用发布/订阅 — 所有状态保持同步 - **完整国际化**：中文和英文各 10 条翻译 - **暗色模式**：全部组件完整支持明暗主题 ### UI截图

prs.title: perf(cowork): 为 MarkdownContent 添加 React.memo 避免流式输出时历史消息重复解析
prs.body:
## 改动内容

为 `MarkdownContent` 组件包裹 `React.memo`，使其在 props 未变化时跳过渲染。

## 背景

Cowork 流式输出时，每个 streaming chunk 会触发 Redux 状态更新，导致 `CoworkSessionDetail` 整个组件树重渲染。由于 `AssistantMessageItem` 没有 `React.memo`，**所有历史 assistant 消息**的 `MarkdownContent` 都会被重新执行，触发完整的 markdown AST 解析 + remark-gfm + remark-math + rehype-katex 插件链。

## 效果

加上 `React.memo` 后，历史消息的 `content`、`className`、`resolveLocalFilePath` 三个 prop 在流式期间均保持引用稳定（`resolveLocalFilePath` 由 `useCallback([currentSession?.cwd])` 保证），浅比较通过即跳过渲染。

- 20 条历史消息的会话中，每个 streaming chunk 的 markdown 解析次数从 20 次降为 1 次（仅当前流式消息）
- 会话中历史消息越多，优化效果越明显
- 改动极小（3 行），零风险

prs.title: fix(user_plugins): persist OpenClaw entry hooks across sync (#2654)
prs.body:
## Summary

- Persist `plugins.entries.*.hooks` in SQLite and rewrite them on `syncToDisk` so gateway restarts no longer drop OpenClaw entry hook config.
- Aligns store / sync / plugin manager paths so hooks survive the same round-trip as other plugin entry fields.
- Fixes https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/issues/2654

## Test plan

- [x] Confirm unit coverage in `src/main/libs/openclawConfigSync.runtime.test.ts` (added in this branch) covers hooks rewrite on sync
- [ ] Manual: set entry hooks -> sync to disk -> restart gateway -> hooks still present
- [ ] Manual: sync without hooks still succeeds (no regression on hook-less entries)
- [ ] Re-run local automated suite if maintainers ask

## Notes

- Branch tip: `6709dc69` (rebased onto `main` 2026-09-22)
- Author GitHub: FOWEPJF255

releases.name: LobsterAI 2026.10.23
releases.body:
This release brings image editing into your conversations, makes remote tools easier to connect, and gives you clearer visibility into usage. It also improves startup reliability, browser tasks, and account recovery.

## ✨ Highlights

### Edit images without leaving your conversation

Annotate images with drawings, arrows, shapes, and text, or select an area and describe what you want to change. With a compatible image model, you can remove backgrounds, erase objects, and expand images to a new aspect ratio.

Save annotated copies or send your edits to AI. Conversation snapshots preserve the source image, selections, and annotations so you can revisit your instructions.

[#2907](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2907)

### Connect remote tools with less setup

Install remote MCP connectors from the marketplace and connect through browser-based OAuth or guided credential forms. Supporting services can now be authorized without manually copying API keys.

[#2905](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2905) · [#2909](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2909)

### More options for custom models

Custom providers now support OpenAI Responses and Gemini native APIs. Built-in model lists and default selections have also been refreshed, while compatibility with existing model configurations is preserved.

[#2897](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2897) · [#2904](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2904)

## Improvements

- Show per-turn credit usage and model presets for conversations started through messaging channels and scheduled tasks. Personal accounts can open the corresponding usage details directly. [#2903](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2903) · [#2915](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2915)
- Add Help & Feedback for bug reports, feature suggestions, and AI content reports, with screenshot attachments and optional diagnostic logs. [#2901](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2901) · [#2926](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2926)
- Use the in-app browser by default, keeping browsing tasks inside LobsterAI. The external browser option remains available in Settings. [#2913](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2913)
- Improve image and video generation progress indicators. Video confirmation now shows estimated credit costs when available and lets you refresh an expired confirmation while the request is retained. [#2918](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2918) · [#2924](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2924)
- Refresh Kits, Skills, and Connectors management pages, refine sidebar menu transitions, and improve typography across Settings. [#2911](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2911) · [#2920](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2920) · [#2931](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2931)
- Add “Close Other Tabs” and “Close Tabs to the Right” to file previews. [#2907](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2907)
- Add a “Confirm Before Quitting” setting. Document changes at risk of being lost still trigger a warning when this setting is off. [#2931](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2931)
- Preserve supported custom OpenClaw overrides in `openclaw.user.json` across configuration syncs and restarts, with controls to enable, apply, and inspect their status. [#2896](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2896)

## Fixes

- Prevent the AI engine from restarting again immediately after startup. [#2932](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2932)
- Limit disk usage from runtime caches, repair backups, and old configuration snapshots. Background cleanup runs in batches and pauses on battery power. [#2893](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2893) · [#2931](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2931)
- Recover account data after an offline startup and show clearer account connection and model loading states. [#2914](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2914) · [#2923](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2923)
- Stop showing subscription trial popups to actively subscribed users and enterprise accounts. [#2928](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2928)
- Improve browser recovery, background screenshots, and web fetching through proxy connections. [#2922](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2922)
- Fix image preview flicker and crashes when selecting image regions. [#2927](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2927)
- Restore online kit catalogs after temporary network failures. [#2892](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2892)
- Improve MCP OAuth cleanup and authorization status refresh, and use system certificates for compatible Node.js-based MCP servers. [#2908](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2908) · [#2912](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2912)
- Fix desktop companion quick-answer model selection and wait for the AI engine before starting tasks. [#2917](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2917) · [#2919](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2919)
- Prevent companion orb clicks from unexpectedly activating the main window on macOS, and keep companion windows out of the Windows taskbar. [#2930](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2930) · [#2910](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2910)
- Fix Windows auto-launch queries when executable paths contain spaces. [#2902](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2902)
- Allow managed workspaces to follow updated directory links. [#2899](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2899)

<details>
<summary>Internal improvements</summary>

- Remove the legacy OpenAI compatibility proxy and consolidate model request routing. [#2898](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2898)
- Preserve tool payloads in conversation transcripts for faithful cache replay. [#2929](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2929)
- Make repair cleanup tests independent of the system clock. [#2900](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2900)

</details>

## Contributors

Thanks to @fisherdaddy, @btc69m979y-dotcom, and @Mind-Hand for their contributions, and to everyone who shared feedback and reported issues.

**Full Changelog:** [2026.10.16 → 2026.10.23](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/compare/2026.10.16...2026.10.23)

prs.title: fix(providers): correct DeepSeek thinking tests and refresh Z.AI models
prs.body:
## Summary
- Correct the live reasoning contract: simple DeepSeek tool calls can return zero reasoning tokens even with thinking enabled. Verify lossless parsing of the returned stream and successful tool-result replay; preserve explicit empty reasoning in both completion parsing and request serialization. Offline tests still require exact nonempty reasoning replay.
- Use production provider registration in the DeepSeek and Z.AI live suites. DeepSeek previously constructed a bare adapter, so its thinking test bypassed the DeepSeek policy and did not send the explicit thinking toggle or replay policy.
- Promote the documented `deepseek-flash` alias, retain supported legacy IDs, and add GLM-5.3/Flash/FlashX and GLM-5.2. Correct context, vision, and reasoning capabilities and update configuration/docs.
- Align effort mapping with low/high/max and preserve reasoning on preceding assistant answers as well as tool turns. Offline HTTP tests cover the registered request fields, both Z.AI namespaces, and all effort levels.
- Preserve underlying streaming transport causes and timeout/connect flags while removing the request URL. The Z.AI failure was a transport error, not a model-not-found response; GLM-4.5-Flash is still supported but its free pool returned explicit 429 quota/overload errors. Behavioral tests now exercise GLM-5.3-Flash; the old free model remains in catalog health reporting. No new retry or skip workaround is added.
- Beads: `moltis-f5n`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Test[Live and offline tests] --> Registry[Production provider registry]
    Registry --> Policy[Model capabilities and reasoning policy]
    Policy --> Request[Thinking toggle + supported effort + reasoning replay]
    Request --> API[DeepSeek or Z.AI]
    API --> Result[Completion or streaming events]
```

issues.title: [Bug] Agent 间调用会话被静默取消（CancelledError）：同秒成对、产物归零，且取消不记录发起方与原因
issues.body:
## 环境
| 项 | 值 |
|---|---|
| 客户端 | QwenPaw Desktop（Windows 10 AMD64） |
| 版本 | **2.2.1**（`qwenpaw --version`） |
| 场景 | 多 agent 舰队（Orchestrator / Reasoner / Executor / Reviewer / Defender）+ 一个飞书通道入口；agent 之间通过 `ChatWithAgent` 互相调用 |
| 涉及代码位置 | `qwenpaw/hooks/error/error_hook.py:90`、`qwenpaw/runtime/runtime.py:297,379`、`qwenpaw/app/routers/tool_calls.py:91`、`qwenpaw/app/channels/base.py:589` |

## 现象（Actual）
1. **跨 agent 调用会话被静默取消**：日志落 `cancel_cleanup: cancelled (session=<A>:to:<B>:<epoch>:<hash>): CancelledError`，并伴随 `cancel-save: persisted interrupted turn` 与 `cancel-save: ... closed 1 dangling tool call(s)`。被取消的会话**没有 result、没有产物**。
2. **成对出现**：多为**同一秒**两条一起被取消（形如 `f-orchestrator:to:f-executor:*` + `f-reasoner:to:f-orchestrator:*`）。
3. **系统性**：本地主日志 3 天内共 **19 次**（10-12: 6 次、10-13: 7 次、10-14: 6 次）；**全部**为 `A:to:B` 跨 agent 会话，未见到单机/用户直连会话被同样取消。
4. **不可溯源**：日志**只**记录 `CancelledError`，**不记录取消的发起方与原因** ⇒ 使用者无法判断属于"框架回收 / 超时 / 上游断开 / 路由错配"中的哪一种。

### 单个实例（逐条可复核的原文形态）
| 时刻 | 日志原文（截断） |
|---|---|
| 11:52:23 | 本地派发台账行：`task_id=<任务号>, agent=f-executor` |
| 11:52:29 | `legion-guard: cb pass task=<任务号> agent=f-executor attempt=1`（本地插件，仅登记、无取消能力） |
| 11:52:29 / 11:52:30 | `Auto-registered new chat` → `builder: built agent for session=...85c3f2e3 agent=f-executor` |
| 11:52:32–35 | 一连串 `Read` / `Bash` 放行（**只读巡检，无写无删**） |
| **11:55:56** | **`cancel_cleanup: cancelled (session=f-orchestrator:to:f-executor:...85c3f2e3): CancelledError`** |
| 11:55:56 | `cancel-save: persisted interrupted turn` + `cancel-save: ... closed 1 dangling tool call(s)` |
| 11:55:56 | **同一秒**另一条：`cancel_cleanup: cancelled (session=f-reasoner:to:f-orchestrator:...ccd46635): CancelledError` |
| 之后 | **零 result、零产物**；该会话上下文仅 2 条（末条为 Executor 自述"我先读权威状态机"）⇒ **刚开工即被掐** |

## 已逐项排除的原因（本地只读取证）
1. **审批（approval）** — 取消时刻**无任何** `app/approvals` 行；对照：另一次取消伴随 `Cancelled 1 pending approval(s) for root session ...`，与本例形态不同。
2. **本地插件 / 自定义守卫** — 本地守卫插件源码中无 `cancel` / `interrupt` / `terminate` / `stop_session` 任何关键词（不具备取消能力）；取消时刻亦无任何插件日志行。
3. **危险命令触发** — 被取消的会话上无删除类或命令行写文件类命令（被取消的 Executor 会话刚进入只读阶段）。
4. **保存配置触发的"零停机热重载"**（即 #8225 所述机制）— 四次取消时刻（10-13 11:20:07 / 10-13 14:28:31 / 10-14 09:37:27 / 10-14 11:55:56）**均无** `config.json` 或任一 `agent.json` 的写入（mtime 逐一核对）；日志亦无 reload / restart / `feishu channel started` 标记。⇒ **与 #8225 不是同一机制**。

## 与 `session_id mismatch` 的时间相关（因果假设，未闭合）
- 10-13 `22:24:43` 落 `qwenpaw/app/routers/tool_calls.py:91` 的 `session_id mismatch`（`url=<调用方会话>` vs `backend=1791895062459-d82gki8`）；
- **10-13 `22:29:16`**：该 `backend` 会话被 `cancel_cleanup: cancelled`。
- 另见 `qwenpaw/app/channels/base.py:589 Message ignored (task already running)`（框架对"同一会话重复投递"的护栏）⇒ 佐证该**投递 / 回执通道确有重复与错配**。
- **保留**：因框架不记录取消发起方，因果链**未 100% 闭合**；本条的重点不只在错配，更在于**取消本身不可溯源**。

## 影响
单次取消 = 该子任务**会话死亡、零产物、需人工决策重派**；对多 agent 舰队属**可用性级**损失。并且，由于 `CancelledError` 与"agent 自身失败/超时"在日志上无法区分，本地只能靠人工逐条复核（本例即花了一轮人工取证才定性）。

## 期望
1. **让取消可溯源**：取消时至少落一条含 **发起方 / 原因 / 目标会话** 的日志（以区分：框架回收 / 超时 / 上游断开 / 路由错配）。
2. 确认上文「mismatch + 高频重投」路径**是否会导致会话级联取消**。
3. 若"同一秒成对取消"属**既定回收语义**（例如父会话结束回收子会话、收尾回收），请在文档或日志中明示。
4. 提供**可观测手段**（日志字段 / 接口 / 指标），以便本地自动区分"被取消"与"agent 失败"，无需人工复核。

## 最小复现建议
短时间内成批发起跨 agent 调用（同一调用方 → 多个被调方），观察数分钟后是否出现**同秒成对**的 `cancel_cleanup`；本地侧只读日志即可复核。可复跑聚合：以工具调用 id（`tc`）为主键，统计同一 `tc` 在 ≤120 秒窗口内的重复条数与 `session_id mismatch` 计数（正常段为 1，收尾段显著大于 1）。

## 相关 issue（可串联）
- **#8225**（保存 agent 配置触发的"零停机热重载"会取消正在运行的 cron 任务）— 机制不同，本条已显式排除配置保存。
- **#6608**（长命令绕过 `shell_command_timeout`、取消时留孤儿子进程、飞书会话被无限阻塞）
- **#7011**（Console 停止请求可取消活跃飞书会话；已 closed）

issues.body: Summary The Console file preview drawer supports only images, PDF, MD/MDX, HTML and CSV. Office documents produced by agents every day (.docx, .xlsx, .pptx) show "Preview is unavailable. Metadata and download remain available.", so the user has to leave the chat and open the file externally. **Current behavior (verified in v2.2.2)** In the bundled console/assets/FilePreview-*.js the preview-type dispatcher is: const exts = new Set(["png","jpg","jpeg","gif","webp","svg","ico","bmp"]); // image → , pdf → , md/mdx → react-markdown, // html/htm → sanitized iframe, csv → table, everything else → "none" There is no branch for doc(x), xls(x), ppt(x), and no mammoth.js / SheetJS / PDF-conversion fallback anywhere in the bundle. **Expected behavior** Opening a .docx/.xlsx/.pptx sent in chat shows a readable preview in the drawer instead of "Preview is unavailable". **Why it matters** Agents routinely deliver final results as Office files (reports, dossiers, spreadsheets — the built-in skills are literally named "PDF, Office, ..."). The current flow breaks the loop: agent produces the file → user must download → open another app → switch back. Current workaround: the agent converts everything to PDF via LibreOffice and sends both files. It works, but adds a conversion dependency and doubles attachments. **Suggested approaches (any of these would help)** - Client-side (lightest): bundle mammoth.js (docx → sanitized HTML, reuse the existing HTML preview path) and SheetJS (xlsx → reuse the existing CSV table path). For pptx, fall back to "download only" or slide thumbnails. - Server-side fallback: for Office MIME types, auto-convert to PDF server-side (e.g. libreoffice --headless) and render via the existing PDF embed path. Could be an optional setting for users without LibreOffice. - Minimal UX fix: at least replace the dead-end message with an actionable one: "No preview for Office files — download, or ask the agent for a PDF copy", with a one-click "Convert to PDF" button that sends the request back to the agent. - **Environment** QwenPaw 2.2.2, Linux (Nobara/Fedora 44), Console in Chromium/Firefox Affects: Console chat file drawer and file previews generally
