issues.title: [Bug]: DingTalk final reply silently dropped when sessionWebhook expires — on_event_message_completed has no Open API fallback (errcode=300001)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.2 (also reproduced against `main` @ `210f5aa` — the code below is identical there)

## Description

When a DingTalk reply takes longer than the `sessionWebhook` TTL, **the final reply is silently dropped**. The user receives nothing: no text, no error, no fallback — while the framework still emits the "done" reaction, which makes it look like the task succeeded.

The root cause is that `on_event_message_completed()` — the function that actually sends the agent's final reply in markdown mode — calls `_send_via_session_webhook()` and **discards the return value**. It has neither the Open API fallback nor the delivery-error surfacing that the other two send paths in the same file already have.

`src/qwenpaw/app/channels/dingtalk/channel.py` has 4 call sites of `_send_via_session_webhook()`:

| line | enclosing function | Open API fallback | raises delivery error |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2029 | `send_content_parts` | ✅ | ✅ |
| 3551 | `send` | ✅ | ✅ |
| **2503** | **`on_event_message_completed`** | ❌ | ❌ |
| 573 | `_on_consume_error` | ❌ | ❌ |

The docstring of `on_event_message_completed` even claims the behaviour that the code does not implement:

```python
    """Send completed message via AI Card or sessionWebhook.

    ...
    Markdown mode: send via sessionWebhook or fallback to send().
    """
```

but the body calls `_send_via_session_webhook(...)` directly and drops the `bool` it returns.

Because DingTalk's `sessionWebhook` is a short-lived credential (per the official docs: *"SessionWebhook 通过 TLS 安全信道和短周期的过期时间确保了其安全性…… 如果你的场景是收到请求后立即回复，可以忽略该过期时间的约束。"*), any reply that takes longer than that TTL is lost.

**Impact is worst for long-running tasks** — exactly the case where a human is most likely to be waiting for an answer.

### Why the existing fallback does not save it

All the required configuration is already present in the reported setup:

- `channels.dingtalk.client_id` / `channels.dingtalk.client_secret` — configured
- the stored session-webhook entry → `conversation_id`, `conversation_type: "dm"`, `sender_staff_id` — present

so `_try_open_api_fallback()` would succeed if it were ever called. But it is never reached: the reply path does not call it. In the log of the reproduction below, `Open API fallback` appears **0 times**, while `errcode=300001` appears 10 times in a row.

### Related history

- #2221 (closed) reported the same `errcode=300001` for the **cron/proactive** path.
- #710 (PR, closed) added fail-fast delivery errors for **proactive** sends, and explicitly stated: *"keep reply-context behavior unchanged (no new exception for normal reply path)"*.

So the proactive path was hardened while the **reply** path was intentionally left as-is. That decision is reasonable for a request that is answered immediately, but it leaves long-running replies unprotected — the reported case.

### Proposed fix

Mirror what `send_content_parts()` already does, in `on_event_message_completed()`:

```python
            delivered = await self._send_via_session_webhook(
                session_webhook,
                body.strip(),
                bot_prefix="",
                at_user_ids=at_uids,
                at_dingtalk_ids=at_dids,
            )
            if not delivered:
                await self._invalidate_session_webhook(to_handle)
                logger.warning(
                    "dingtalk on_event_message_completed: sessionWebhook send "
                    "failed, trying Open API fallback for to_handle=%s",
                    to_handle,
                )
                if not await self._try_open_api_fallback(
                    body.strip(), to_handle, send_meta
                ):
                    self._raise_delivery_error_if_api_send(
                        self._api_send_delivery_errors(send_meta),
                        "DingTalk send failed via sessionWebhook and Open API fallback",
                    )
```

Note `_invalidate_session_webhook()` intentionally keeps `conversation_id` and the other metadata, so the Open API fallback still works on subsequent sends without a redundant failed POST.

The same treatment would apply to `_on_consume_error()` (line 573), where an error message to the user is currently swallowed the same way.

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.2 (reproduced on `main` @ `210f5aa` as well)
- **OS:** Linux 5.19.17 (x86_64), Docker container
- **Install method:** pip (in Docker image)
- **Python version (if applicable):** 3.11

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Send a DingTalk DM to the bot requesting a task that takes longer than the `sessionWebhook` TTL (observed here: ~90 minutes).
2. The agent completes the work and produces its final reply.
3. Observe: the user receives **no reply**, no error notification, and no fallback attempt — only the "done" reaction.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** the final reply is silently discarded. The log shows a repeating `errcode=300001 errmsg=session 已过期` (WARNING level only, no exception raised, no retry, no Open API fallback attempt). The stream then ends as if everything succeeded.
- **Expected:** the reply is delivered — by falling back to the Open API (already implemented and already configured in this setup) — or, if that also fails, the failure is surfaced instead of being swallowed.

## Logs / Screenshots

```
2026-10-20 16:59:54 | INFO | dingtalk/channel.py:956 | dingtalk sessionWebhook POST ok: msgtype=markdown status=200 errcode=0
2026-10-20 17:00:18 | WARNING | dingtalk/channel.py:946 | dingtalk sessionWebhook POST API error: msgtype=markdown session_from_url=a84d6434... errcode=300001 errmsg=session 已过期
2026-10-20 17:00:44 | WARNING | dingtalk/channel.py:946 | dingtalk sessionWebhook POST API error: ... errcode=300001 errmsg=session 已过期
2026-10-20 17:01:18 | WARNING | dingtalk/channel.py:946 | dingtalk sessionWebhook POST API error: ... errcode=300001 errmsg=session 已过期
2026-10-20 17:01:31 | WARNING | dingtalk/channel.py:946 | dingtalk sessionWebhook POST API error: ... errcode=300001 errmsg=session 已过期
2026-10-20 17:01:44 | WARNING | dingtalk/channel.py:946 | dingtalk sessionWebhook POST API error: ... errcode=300001 errmsg=session 已过期
2026-10-20 17:02:31 | WARNING | dingtalk/channel.py:946 | dingtalk sessionWebhook POST API error: ... errcode=300001 errmsg=session 已过期
2026-10-20 17:02:53 | WARNING | dingtalk/channel.py:946 | dingtalk sessionWebhook POST API error: ... errcode=300001 errmsg=session 已过期
2026-10-20 17:03:08 | WARNING | dingtalk/channel.py:946 | dingtalk sessionWebhook POST API error: ... errcode=300001 errmsg=session 已过期
2026-10-20 17:03:36 | WARNING | dingtalk/channel.py:946 | dingtalk sessionWebhook POST API error: ... errcode=300001 errmsg=session 已过期
2026-10-20 17:03:37 | WARNING | dingtalk/channel.py:946 | dingtalk sessionWebhook POST API error: ... errcode=300001 errmsg=session 已过期
2026-10-20 17:03:37 | INFO | dingtalk/channel.py:3074 | dingtalk _send_emotion: reply 🥳Done on msg=msg3NrJtjbugT5fq3dWUzmlx
2026-10-20 17:03:38 | INFO | dingtalk/channel.py:2594 | dingtalk stream thread stopped
```

Grepping the same log confirms the fallback never ran:

```
$ grep -c "Open API fallback" qwenpaw.log
0
$ grep -c "_send_via_open_api" qwenpaw.log
0
$ grep -c "accessToken" qwenpaw.log
0
```

The "Done" reaction at 17:03:37 is sent through a different API path and therefore succeeds — which is exactly what makes the failure look like a success to the user.

## Additional Notes

- The 84-minute gap between the last successful send (16:59:54) and the user noticing something was wrong (18:27) was entirely this silent drop.
- DingTalk's official guidance (智能交互概述) confirms the design intent: `sessionWebhook` expiry "会满足绝大多数场景，如果你的场景是收到请求后立即回复，可以忽略该过期时间的约束" — i.e. it assumes an immediate reply. Long-running replies need the Open API path.
- A complementary hardening would be to also honour a `robot_code` / proactive-send configuration for final replies, so that delivery does not depend on a short-lived credential at all.

issues.title: [Feature]: Plugin-facing theme extension point (semantic token override layer)
issues.body:
## Summary

The Console theme system added in #7741 lets **users** pick a palette (6 built-ins) and customize accent / hover / background / surface / radius. But **plugins** still have exactly one theme knob: `window.QwenPaw.chat.theme.set(pluginId, { colorPrimary })`. Plugin authors who want deeper theming (backgrounds, glass / `backdrop-filter`, full palettes) have no official hook, so they end up injecting CSS.

Proposal (for discussion): add a **plugin-facing semantic token override layer**, built on QwenPaw's *own* semantic tokens rather than the upstream UI library's raw tokens — so plugins can theme deeply **without coupling to upstream upgrades**.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Console (frontend web UI)

## Problem / Motivation

1. **Plugin theming is one-dimensional today.** The plugin theme API only accepts `colorPrimary` (see `plugins/types/qwenpaw.d.ts` and `plugins/hostSdk/install.ts` → `themeFieldMap`). Everything else is unreachable from a plugin.
2. **The marketplace already proves both the demand and the fragility of the workaround.** Appearance plugins such as *QwenPaw Skin Studio*, *background-wallpaper*, and *No Glass (Flat UI)* all describe themselves as "pure frontend, zero-dependency" — i.e. they inject CSS and poke the DOM directly. That breaks whenever the Console's markup or styles change.
3. **Why not simply expose the upstream tokens?** Because `plugins/types/qwenpaw.d.ts` deliberately keeps the public surface stable *"across vendor upgrades"* — exposing the upstream UI library's raw tokens would couple every plugin theme to that library's token names. The layer worth opening is **QwenPaw's own semantic layer**, part of which already exists (see #7682).

## Proposed Solution

Two steps, in order:

1. **Own the layer.** Make the Console's theming go through **QwenPaw-owned semantic tokens** (semantic role names → mapped internally to whatever the underlying UI library expects). #7682 ("use semantic tokens in SettingsCenter") is already a step in this direction.
2. **Open the layer to plugins.** Add a plugin API to override those semantic tokens, with the same disposable / registration semantics as the rest of the plugin SDK, e.g.:

```js
const dispose = window.QwenPaw.chat.theme.overrideTokens("my-plugin", {
  "surface":         { light: "#ffffff", dark: "#1f1f1f" },
  "chat.background": { light: "#fafafa", dark: "#111111" },
  // ...any semantic token; both light & dark required, so an override
  // never goes illegible when the user flips the color scheme.
});
```

Because plugins override **QwenPaw's semantic names**, an upstream library upgrade only changes QwenPaw's internal mapping — plugin themes keep working. That removes the exact risk that motivates keeping the surface closed today.

Happy to start with a **minimal first cut** (e.g. the handful of tokens the Console already uses for surface / background / border / text) and grow from there, rather than a big-bang "full skin system".

## Alternatives Considered

- **Status quo — each plugin injects CSS.** Works, but fragile and duplicated; breaks on Console changes; no clean restore. (This is what marketplace appearance plugins do today.)
- **Expose the upstream UI library's raw tokens directly.** Rejected — couples plugins to upstream token names and contradicts the existing "do not expose vendor config" design intent.
- **Only widen the current scalar list** (accent / surface / radius / …). Helps a little, but still cannot reach backgrounds / glass / full palettes.

## Additional Context

- Related: #7741 (merged — 6 palettes + accent/hover/background/surface/radius), #7406, #5909, #6312 (superseded by #7741), #7287 (external frontend gateway — `not_planned`).
- **Reference design**: DeepSeek Harness ships exactly this — `ctx.theme.overrideTokens(source, tokens)` plus a `ThemeDefinition` type (alias-token overrides, light + dark required), documented as *"Third-party themes can register alias-token overrides through `ctx.theme`."*
- Marketplace plugins currently working around this: `@osier-yi/qwenpaw-dream-skin`, `@levodoubt/background-wallpaper`, `@erickcharles/qwenpaw-no-glass`.

## Willing to Contribute

- [x] I am willing to open a PR for this feature (after discussion).

---

### 中文摘要

Console 的主题系统（#7741）让**用户**能换 6 套预设、自定义 accent / 背景 / 表面 / 圆角；但**插件**目前只有一个主题接口 `chat.theme.set(id, { colorPrimary })`。插件想深度定制（背景、毛玻璃、整套配色）没有官方入口，只能注入 CSS —— 市场里的外观类插件（Skin Studio、背景壁纸、去玻璃化）都是这么干的，Console 一改版就失效。

建议：**在 QwenPaw 自己的语义 token 层上加一个面向插件的覆盖接口**（而不是暴露上游 `AgentScope Runtime WebUI` 的原始 token）—— 这样上游升级时插件主题不受影响（只需 QwenPaw 内部重新映射）。愿意在讨论通过后提 PR，可先做最小版本。

issues.title: [Bug] send_file_to_user on a video permanently wedges the session: 422 unknown variant `video_url`
issues.body:
**What happened**

A `send_file_to_user` call on a `.mp4` permanently wedged a session: every subsequent request — including plain-text turns — failed with

```
422 UnprocessableEntityError
Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type:
messages[443]: unknown variant `video_url`, expected one of `text`, `image_url`, `file`
```

**Why it happens**

1. `send_file_to_user("<local>.mp4")` returns a tool result whose output holds a `type: data` block with `media_type: video/mp4`.
2. `FileBlockSupportFormatter.format()` promotes that block into a `video_url` content part for **every** OpenAI-family formatter (`_promote_tool_result_videos` / `_replace_video_placeholders`). `video_url` is a vendor extension, not part of the Chat Completions schema. `view_video` honours `supports_video`, but tool-result file blocks bypass that gate entirely.
3. DeepSeek rejects the schema (422). The block is persisted in session history, so every later turn replays the same payload, and the 422 shape matches none of the recovery signals — no media-free retry, no video strip, so the session never heals.

**Repro**

1. Any OpenAI-compatible provider without video support (e.g. DeepSeek, `supports_video` absent/false).
2. Have the agent produce a small `.mp4` and deliver it with `send_file_to_user`.
3. Send any follow-up message: every request fails with the 422 above.

**Expected**

Delivering a file must not turn it into model input. The tool result should either become a text placeholder or be capability-gated; and if a broken payload does reach the provider, the next turn should degrade (strip video) instead of failing forever.

**Environment**

- QwenPaw 2.0.1 desktop backend (packaged), Windows 10; channel: WeChat
- offending block: `context[26].content[65].output[0].source = {"type":"url","url":"file:///D:/ProjectBlenderAgent/out/turntable.mp4","media_type":"video/mp4"}`
- request dump 20,461,343 bytes; provider error at `column 20498070`

**Related**

#8290 (video wedge, "At most 0 video(s)"), #8171 (same wedge for audio via `send_file_to_user`), #7792 (WeChat video/audio tool_result `file://` URLs), #7876 / #7886 (audio `input_audio` 422 precedent), #8022 / #8064 (closed: file/PDF wedges via `send_file_to_user`).

A fix is ready and linked below: capability-gated video emission plus a video-only strip-and-retry.

issues.title: [Bug]: XiaoYi channel emits no working/status frames during long turns (blank client for minutes) and drops the WS silently
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.2.post1

## Description

**Two related symptoms on the XiaoYi (小艺) channel:**

**1. No downstream frame at all during a long turn.** While a turn is running, the
channel writes nothing to the WebSocket except the 30s protocol-level
`msgType=heartbeat` (constant `HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL = 30` in `xiaoyi/constants.py`).
That heartbeat keeps the TCP/WS link alive but is invisible in the client UI, so
the user sees a completely blank conversation for the whole duration of the turn.

Concrete case (2026-10-20): a short prompt wrote nothing back for ~7m36s. Queue
and consumer were created, the agent was rebuilt and the session was being read
during the turn, but no user-visible message was ever emitted, and the turn was
finally cancelled by an instance restart:

```
2026-10-20 15:43:16 | INFO | unified_queue_manager.py:206 | Created queue: channel=xiaoyi session=<redacted> priority=20
2026-10-20 15:43:16 | INFO | channels/base.py:550 | _consume_with_tracker: chat_id=<redacted> session=<redacted>
2026-10-20 15:43:17 | INFO | runtime/builder.py:574 | builder: built agent for session=<redacted> model=deepseek-v4.1-flash tools=75
2026-10-20 15:44:42 | INFO | chats/session.py:454 | Get session state dict ... successfully.
2026-10-20 15:50:52 | INFO | hooks/error/error_hook.py:90 | cancel_cleanup: cancelled (session=<redacted>): CancelledError
```

**2. Unexpected disconnects, sometimes twice within 40 seconds.** The channel
re‑connects successfully (1s backoff), but nothing in the log says *why* the link
dropped (no close code / reason), and the in-flight turn is not resumed or
replayed.

```
2026-10-22 21:55:11 | WARNING | xiaoyi/channel.py:838 | XiaoYi [primary]: Disconnected
2026-10-22 21:55:11 | INFO    | xiaoyi/channel.py:1089 | XiaoYi: Reconnecting in 1s (attempt 1)
2026-10-22 21:55:12 | INFO    | xiaoyi/channel.py:222  | XiaoYi [primary]: Disconnected
2026-10-22 21:55:28 | INFO    | xiaoyi/channel.py:1101 | XiaoYi: Reconnected successfully
2026-10-22 21:55:48 | WARNING | xiaoyi/channel.py:838  | XiaoYi [primary]: Disconnected
2026-10-22 21:55:48 | INFO    | xiaoyi/channel.py:1089 | XiaoYi: Reconnecting in 1s (attempt 1)
2026-10-22 21:55:49 | INFO    | xiaoyi/channel.py:222  | XiaoYi [primary]: Disconnected
2026-10-22 21:55:49 | INFO    | xiaoyi/channel.py:1101 | XiaoYi: Reconnected successfully
```

**Related PR(s):** none

**Security considerations:** none — no credentials or config values are included
in this report; `agentId`/`session` IDs are redacted.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.2.post1 (`qwenpaw-2.2.2.post1.dist-info`)
- **OS:** Linux, kernel 4.19.90-2003.4.0.0036.oe1.x86_64 (openEuler), containerised
- **Install method:** Docker image
- **Python version:** 3.11

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure the `xiaoyi` channel and confirm `XiaoYi: Connected` in the log.
2. From the XiaoYi app, send a prompt that takes more than ~40s to complete
   (one that triggers several tool calls works reliably).
3. Watch the app during the turn: no typing indicator, no progress text, no
   partial output — the conversation stays empty until either the final message
   arrives or the turn dies.
4. Leave the channel connected for a few hours and grep the log for
   `XiaoYi [primary]: Disconnected`; drops occur every few minutes to tens of
   minutes, occasionally twice within 40s (2026-10-22 21:55:11 and 21:55:48).

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** the client shows nothing for the whole turn; on a 7m36s turn the
  user reasonably concludes the bot is hung. Disconnects are silent about their
  cause, and any final message produced while `_ws.closed` is true is dropped —
  `send_json()` returns `False` and no retry/replay follows.
- **Expected:** (a) a user-visible working/status frame at a configurable
  interval while a turn is in flight, so the client never looks frozen;
  (b) the disconnect log carries the WS close code/reason; (c) a final message
  that cannot be delivered because the socket dropped is persisted and replayed
  after `Reconnected successfully`, instead of being silently lost.

## Logs / Screenshots

See the two log blocks under **Description** (turn with no output; repeated
disconnects 37s apart).

Code pointer for the silent-drop case — `xiaoyi/channel.py`:

```python
async def send_json(self, data: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    """Send a JSON payload. Return True on success."""
    if not self._ws or self._ws.closed or not self.connected:
        return False
    try:
        await self._ws.send_json(data)
        return True
    ...
```

`await self._ws.send_json(...)` succeeds as soon as the frame is written to the
local transport; a peer that has already gone away is not detected until the
next receive, so a `True` return is not proof of delivery.

## Additional Notes

**Local workaround already validated on 2.2.2.post1 (not submitted as a PR —
happy to open one if the maintainers want it):**

- emit an immediate ack frame when a turn starts (so the client stops showing a
  blank screen), then a `status-update(working)` frame every 12s for the
  lifetime of the turn;
- interval configurable via `XIAOYI_KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL` (set to `0` to disable),
  hard-capped at 1800s per turn;
- all keepalive tasks cancelled on `stop()` / disconnect, so no task leaks.

Result in the log — the same long turn that previously produced silence now
keeps the client refreshed, and the frames are accepted (`ok=True`):

```
2026-10-23 15:56:38 | INFO | xiaoyi/channel.py:1469 | XiaoYi: keepalive(working) session=... waited=12s ok=True
2026-10-23 15:56:50 | INFO | xiaoyi/channel.py:1469 | XiaoYi: keepalive(working) session=... waited=24s ok=True
2026-10-23 15:57:02 | INFO | xiaoyi/channel.py:1469 | XiaoYi: keepalive(working) session=... waited=36s ok=True
2026-10-23 15:57:14 | INFO | xiaoyi/channel.py:1469 | XiaoYi: keepalive(working) session=... waited=48s ok=True
```

The patch is 237 lines against `qwenpaw/app/channels/xiaoyi/channel.py`
(backup kept, `py_compile` clean, unit tests green).

issues.title: [Bug][Console] Wheel scrolling in a long conversation gets stuck: transcript height re-estimation snaps the view back 1.1-2.2k px
issues.body:
### QwenPaw Version

2.2.2 (QwenPaw Desktop, Windows 10 AMD64, WebView2 / Edge 155.0.4283.45)

Bundle under test: `console/assets/chat-vendor-BLoJqpIE.js` (mtime 2026-10-15 14:25). Captured on 2026-10-16.

### Component(s) Affected

- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Core / Backend
- [ ] Channels
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

### Description

Plain mouse-wheel scrolling in a **long** conversation cannot make progress: every 1.5-2.2 s the transcript is thrown back 1,100-2,200 px, so the user ends up scrolling in place. No navigation action, no streaming answer and no new message is involved - the recording below is a pure wheel-scroll session in an already-finished conversation.

After the snap-back the view lands exactly on the *new* maximum scroll offset (see the arithmetic below), which is what makes me think the transcript total height is being re-estimated while the user is scrolling, and the scroll offset is then clamped to it instead of being anchored.

### How this was measured (read-only)

The app was started through the official `qwenpaw-desktop-debug.cmd`, which only adds `WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS=--remote-debugging-port=9222` on `127.0.0.1`. Over that port a small recorder attached to the page:

- passive listeners for `wheel` (capture, `{passive:true}`) and `scroll` on the transcript scroller, recording `{scrollTop, scrollHeight, clientHeight, elements matching [data-role][id], elements matching [class*="anchor"]}` for every event;
- a `MutationObserver` on the same subtree, plus console/exception capture.

No input was synthesized and no DOM was modified. Raw JSONL trace (1,600+ events) kept locally.

### Observed loop - 15 consecutive identical cycles

One cycle, verbatim from the trace (identical numbers repeated 15 times between 19:03:12 and 19:03:38):

```
wheel  dy=+100  scrollTop=-1563  clientHeight=648  scrollHeight=3312   <-- last position the user reached
scroll          scrollTop=-3799  clientHeight=648  scrollHeight=5548   <-- +2236 height jump, 1 ms later
scroll          scrollTop=-2745  clientHeight=648  scrollHeight=3394   <-- -2154, 15 ms later
scroll          scrollTop=-2663  clientHeight=648  scrollHeight=3312   <-- -82, 17 ms later: view snapped back
wheel  dy=+100  scrollTop=-2563  ...                                   <-- the user keeps scrolling from here
```

The last two offsets are exactly the *bottom limit of the shrunken content*:

```
-(3312 - 648) = -2664   (observed -2663)
-(3394 - 648) = -2746   (observed -2745)
```

so the browser is not "animating back" - the offset the app wanted (`-3799`, valid while `scrollHeight` was 5548) becomes out of range when the content shrinks to 3312 and gets clamped to `-2664`.

Net effect per cycle: the user wheels from `-3699` down to `-1563` (2,136 px of progress), then is pushed back to `-2663`, i.e. **zero net movement**; the view is stuck oscillating between `-1563` and `-2663`.

### The height keeps changing although the message set does not

In every sampled frame during the loop:

```
document.querySelectorAll('[data-role][id]').length        = 25   (constant)
document.querySelectorAll('[class*="anchor"]').length      = 64   (constant)
scrollHeight over the same second: 3312 / 3394 / 5138 / 5548 / 8969
```

Largest single jump seen: `scrollHeight 4942 -> 8969 (+4027)` with `scrollTop -1411 -> -5437`, then back down to `-2745 / -2663` within 20 ms. Average per-item height implied by these numbers swings between ~130 px and ~360 px for the same items, so item heights are clearly being estimated rather than measured. No `mutate` events accompany the jumps (the mutation observer reports nothing in that window).

### Code pointer

In `console/assets/chat-vendor-BLoJqpIE.js` every transcript item is rendered with:

```js
{ contentVisibility: "auto", containIntrinsicSize: "auto 160px" }
```

and the scroller itself:

```css
.qwenpaw-bubble-list-scroll { height:100%; width:100%; overflow:auto; scrollbar-gutter: stable both-edges; }
.qwenpaw-bubble-list { display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:24px; padding:16px 16px 0 16px; }
/* in -order-desc mode: ::before { height:16px } ::after { height:70px } */
```

Hypothesis: items that are scrolled out of view are laid out with the 160 px intrinsic placeholder instead of their real height, so the transcript's `scrollHeight` changes while the user scrolls, and because nothing re-anchors the scroll offset, the browser clamps it to the new maximum - which is the snap the user sees.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a long conversation (the one recorded had 64 anchors / 25 rendered bubbles).
2. Scroll continuously with the wheel toward the newer end.
3. Every ~1.5-2.2 s the transcript jumps back and the scroll position cannot advance past a certain point.

### Expected behaviour

Wheel scrolling should move the transcript monotonically, and `scrollHeight` should not change unless the transcript content actually changes.

### Related issues

- #8186 / PR #8214 - "message-navigation jump overrides manual wheel scrolling". That one requires clicking a navigation entry first; this report uses no navigation at all and still reproduces.
- #8251 / PR #8273 - navigation directory accuracy. Also requires the navigation panel; unrelated to wheel-only scrolling.
- The bundle recorded here (2026-10-15) predates #8273, but since neither repro path uses the navigation panel, I do not expect #8273 to change this behaviour.

### Suggested fixes

- Re-anchor on height change: record the offset of the first visible item before the transcript's height changes and restore the same visual offset after it, instead of letting the browser clamp `scrollTop`.
- Do not rely on `contain-intrinsic-size` placeholders for the transcript (measure items, or cap the discrepancy), so that total height stays stable while scrolling.
- Guard the automatic "scroll to bottom / scroll to active item" path so it cannot run while a user wheel gesture is in flight (this is the part that #8214 started).

prs.title: fix(runtime): prevent injected context from persisting
prs.body:
## Description

Keep request-local context supplied by `HookContext.inject_context()` available to the current model call without saving it as a user turn or searchable conversation history.

Related: #6360 and #6358. Updated against official `main` at `697aeb669f42f223d060772eb7a313eec78ebd20` (2026-10-16). Verified PR head: `0228564e5a9afea0a298fdd05d4ddecbb5339ea6`.

## What Problem This Solves

AgentScope accepts user/assistant input messages, so QwenPaw wraps injected system context in `Msg(name="system", role="user")`. AgentScope copies these inputs into the agent context. Without an explicit persistence boundary, temporary page/user state can appear as a real user turn after a reload, accumulate on subsequent turns, and become searchable through Scroll history.

Cleaning up only after model execution is insufficient: Scroll writes through during execution, and conversation slash commands load and re-save session state before `SessionLoadHook` runs.

## Changes

- Tag injected context explicitly and remove this request's copied message by ID before normal or interrupted session snapshots. The model still receives the context for the current turn.
- Reject tagged runtime context and structurally identifiable legacy context at `msg_to_entries()`, the shared Scroll serialization boundary, before any SQLite row or FTS entry is created.
- Sanitize normal session loads, chat-history rendering, and conversation-command state loads. Both modern saved state and the legacy memory conversion are covered, so `/history` and `/compact` cannot consume or re-save those internal messages.
- Migrate existing history databases from versions 0/1 to version 2: delete only rows carrying the explicit runtime-context metadata tag and rebuild FTS in the same transaction. If rebuilding fails, roll back without quarantining or discarding source history. Other messages and sessions are preserved; builds without FTS5 are covered.
- Add regression tests for SQLite write-through and migration, command dispatch/load/save, and the complete runtime lifecycle: normal completion, cancellation, execution error, and stream closure (`GeneratorExit`).

### Follow-up to the September 14 review

1. **Scroll persistence:** filtering is enforced before serialization, not just after execution. Existing tagged rows and their search-index entries are removed by a versioned migration, including a rollback regression.
2. **Direct command loads:** `_load_agent_state()` sanitizes before `AgentState.model_validate()` and after legacy conversion. Adapter tests exercise a read command and a mutating command and inspect the saved state, not only the displayed message list.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend
- [x] Tests
- [ ] Console
- [ ] CI/CD

## Testing

All Python test runs pin `PYTHONPATH` to this checkout's `src` and `packages/qwenpawmail-mcp/src`, with isolated `QWENPAW_WORKING_DIR` and `QWENPAW_SECRET_DIR`. Runtime tests: Windows, Python 3.12. Formatting/static checks: Ubuntu 24.04 in WSL, Python 3.12.

```bash
python -m pytest \
  tests/unit/runtime \
  tests/unit/agents/context \
  tests/unit/agents/hooks \
  tests/unit/app/chats \
  tests/unit/agents/test_command_handler.py \
  tests/unit/backup \
  tests/unit/config/test_history_path.py \
  tests/integration/test_chat_history_conversion.py \
  -q --tb=short
```

1643 passed, 16 skipped in 81.28s (0:01:21)

```bash
pre-commit run --all-files
```

All applicable hooks passed, including mypy, Black, Flake8, Pylint, Prettier and actionlint.

## Evidence

Regression comparison for the newly completed persistence boundaries:

```text
# Temporarily remove only the new command-loader and history-migration fixes
# in the isolated checkout, leaving the new tests in place:
8 failed, 139 deselected

# Restore the fixes and run the related suite above:
1643 passed, 16 skipped in 81.28s (0:01:21)
```

The assertions check actual SQLite row retrieval and FTS matches before/after migration, unrelated-row preservation, repeat opens, migration rollback, and the command adapter's re-saved session payload. The stream-exit tests verify that the model receives injected context while the saved snapshot contains only the real user message.

### Full-suite limitation, disclosed separately

`python -m pytest tests/unit -q --tb=short --maxfail=5` was also attempted locally: **3129 passed, 13 skipped, 5 failed**, stopping at the configured limit. The failures are four pre-existing `TestCleanupExpired` cases in `test_offloader.py` and `TestClientPool.test_pool_key_uses_resolved_path` (`WinError 1314`, Windows symlink privilege). All five failures were reproduced against the unmodified official `main` commit `697aeb66` using the same environment. They are not reported as passing checks or changed in this PR. Official Linux CI still needs maintainer approval.

## Compatibility and scope

- No Worklist-specific matching, injected-text keyword matching, dependencies, workflow changes, or model configuration changes.
- Legacy session cleanup recognizes the documented old `name=system` / `role=user` structure. The SQLite migration deletes only explicitly tagged rows; it does not guess which untagged historical rows were injected context or attempt to rewrite existing summaries.
- History database version 2 is intentional for the one-time data migration. A version-1-only writer will reject the newer database; keep a pre-upgrade backup before downgrading. No history files are deleted or recreated during migration.
- No frontend source changes in the PR diff; a frontend rebuild is not applicable.

## Checklist

- [x] `pre-commit run --all-files` passes on the final tree
- [x] Related regression suite passes on the final tree
- [x] Previous review findings addressed with persistence-boundary tests
- [x] Full-suite failures and clean-up/migration limits disclosed
- [x] Ready for re-review after maintainer approval of CI

prs.title: feat(pawapp): redesign the SDK and app control plane
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PawApps can expose durable work to Main Chat and their own UI through a shared, scoped Host contract. Small Apps register an `app.action` handler; external runtimes implement the adapter protocol. Host owns task identity, retries, permissions, setup, questions, approvals, results, artifacts and continuation delivery.

For example, Creator can pause production for generation authorization or content review. Main Chat shows what is being approved and the task's approval progress. Users can authorize clearly scoped generation in chat; content review opens the exact pending review and revision in Creator. Decisions resume the same project/task through Creator's existing mechanisms. A manual review no longer appears as ongoing planning.

This PR includes:

- Generated Python/JSON Schema/TypeScript contracts, validated results and scoped clients.
- Durable task execution/recovery, grants, artifacts, handoffs and App-owned configuration prompts.
- Main Chat discovery/delegation tools, generic task cards and scoped continuation back into the originating chat.
- Typed execution/review approvals with immutable proposal digests, stable decision IDs, optional cost information and expiry, authenticated user identity and persisted decision receipts. Ordinary agent answers cannot approve. Retries retain the same command identity; stale or conflicting decisions are rejected.
- Approval cards show bounded object/operation scope, operation count and revision, with authenticated inspection handoffs. App-only review is enforced on the server. Mutable progress counts stay separate from the immutable proposal; future counts distinguish unknown, estimated and exact. Creator reports authoritative handled/pending counts and leaves future approvals unknown.
- Creator story-writing integration: the bilingual skill hands the full StoryPackage and exact script to `prepare-production`; `revise-story` preserves revisions; `produce-video` continues the same project with setup/approval gates and verified final-film publication. Generation approvals and content review use shared cards; new content reviews require inspection and decisions inside Creator.
- An App-independent word-counter quickstart, managed-handler approval API and generic conformance tests.

## App integrations are separate

- **Data integration: #8363.** Adapter, native Console task routing, Engine compatibility pin, Data-specific tests and external Engine CI. Depends on this SDK and [QwenPaw-Data #85](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw-Data/pull/85).
- **File Browser reference App: #8364.** Managed listing, directory setup, frontend, persistence, legacy recovery adapter, attribution, tests and dedicated CI. Depends on this SDK independently of Data.

Both are draft follow-ups to rebase after this SDK merges. Neither App implementation is included here. The shared conformance suite runs without either integration or an external Data Engine.

## Compatibility and behavior

- Existing authorization/event digests and accepted task identities remain compatible. Legacy persisted question-shaped approval events retain their original replay payload; new events use typed approvals.
- Versioned PawApps require explicit activation. Managed child services inherit OS basics plus explicitly declared environment variables.
- Each new Creator action needs its own grant. Setup completion, action permissions and per-operation approval remain separate. Host does not change App YOLO settings or model/credential configuration.
- Creator validates its authoritative authorization/review token before applying decisions. A lost response reuses the existing decision journal; decisions already made inside Creator invalidate stale chat proposals.
- Artifacts remain reusable across sessions within authorized user/workspace/App scope; cross-App handoffs require exact-version grants.
- Story references and notes are retained. Binary reference transfer and multi-film production are outside this increment.

## Evidence

Local verification for the approval contract and Creator adaptation (2026-10-23):

- **575 backend tests passed:** `tests/unit/pawapp`, Creator's video-workflow suite and project-file review tests. Covers authenticated decisions, cross-scope rejection, expiry/replacement, concurrent decisions, restart/replay, App-side decisions and lost-receipt recovery; also immutable approval content during progress updates, App-only decision enforcement, and stale inspection rejection.
- **135 frontend tests passed:** 129 Console task-card/API/SDK tests plus 6 Creator decision-tray/plugin-entry tests. Covers scope details, forecast certainty, precise inspection routing and revision mismatch handling.
- TypeScript, both frontend builds, generated-contract drift checks, `git diff --check` and changed-file pre-commit hooks passed.
- Deterministic browser acceptance passed: image approval, video approval, reload recovery, exact Creator authorization inspection, completion and verified artifact download. No paid provider calls. The local 8088 instance was updated and restarted; Main Chat and Creator health checks passed.

Documentation: `docs/design/pawapp-app-quickstart.md`, `docs/design/pawapp-approvals.md`, `docs/design/pawapp-task-runtime.md`, `docs/design/pawapp-creator-story-handoff.md`, and `docs/design/pawapp-contract-progress.md`.

prs.title: feat(plugins): add escalation-only tool policy hooks
prs.body:
## Description

Expose a plugin-owned pre-tool-call policy hook after static governance evaluation, so external classifiers and organization-specific checks can participate without monkey-patching the host.

**Review status:** ready for maintainer review. Implementation, focused regression, full unit/contract tests, and post-commit full-repository lint are complete. Both ACP cases subsequently passed in isolated runs on the unchanged commit using the project's CI test timeout. The broader integration run was not green; its original results, baseline comparison, and follow-up evidence remain documented below. Ready for review does not imply that all CI or integration tests have passed.

- Add `PluginApi.register_tool_policy_hook(...)` with ascending priority, per-hook `fail="open"|"closed"`, and host-enforced `timeout_s`.
- Export `PolicyHint` and the public `ToolCallSpec` contract from `qwenpaw.plugins`. The spec exposes `schema_version=1`, policy tool name, raw arguments, agent/session IDs, and the effective approval level, including F1 overrides.
- Apply escalation-only semantics: static DENY bypasses hooks, first hook DENY short-circuits, otherwise first ASK wins. Neither ALLOW nor abstention relaxes a static decision.
- Reuse existing interactive/cross-session approval routing. Plugin ASK approval retains any required sandbox and does not create a persistent static allow rule.
- Store hook outcomes, abstentions, reasons, metadata, and the original static decision in the existing audit `extra` field. Clean up registrations on plugin unload or failed-load rollback.
- Add regression coverage plus English/Chinese API documentation and an external-classifier cookbook example; update both README documentation indexes.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #7878

**Security Considerations:** Callbacks receive independent argument snapshots. Invalid results, callback exceptions, self-cancellation, and timeouts follow each hook's configured failure mode. Error records include exception types rather than potentially sensitive exception messages. Hooks are trusted in-process async code, not a sandbox: callbacks must avoid blocking the event loop and cooperate with cancellation. The existing OFF-mode bypass remains unchanged and is documented. The cookbook explicitly limits external data transmission to an operator-approved classifier endpoint.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [x] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Checklist

- [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass (relevant regression, full unit, and contract suites; broader integration caveat below)
- [x] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [x] Ready for review

### For Channel Changes

Not applicable: this change reuses the existing approval service; no channel implementations or contracts are changed.

## Testing

The new tests cover the static/hook decision matrix, stable priorities and DENY short-circuiting, both failure modes, invalid results and metadata, bounded timeouts including delayed cancellation, caller cancellation, isolated arguments, SQLite audit round-tripping, registration replacement/ownership cleanup, OFF bypass, effective approval-level context including F1 and governor fallback, and real approval-service orchestration with sandbox retention and no durable plugin consent.

The development environment uses Python 3.11 and the complete `.[dev,test,full]` extra set. Work and secret directories are isolated for test runs. Chromium was installed for browser integration tests. Test suites are run by directory, matching CI, because root collection has conflicting `test_backup.py` basenames. Lowercase proxy environment variables are unset for the unit test subprocess because they otherwise override the uppercase proxy variables set by `test_external_client_cannot_send_token_through_proxy[False/True]` (both cases pass with the clean subprocess environment).

## Evidence

```text
pytest tests/unit/governance tests/unit/plugins tests/integration/test_governance_module.py tests/integration/test_governance_security_module.py tests/integration/test_plugin_sdk_module.py -q --timeout=60
673 passed, 7 skipped in 4.72s

pytest tests/contract --timeout=120 -q
412 passed, 1 skipped, 1 warning in 2.56s

env -u http_proxy -u https_proxy -u all_proxy -u no_proxy pytest tests/unit --timeout=120 -q
13726 passed, 22 skipped, 67 warnings in 298.95s

pytest tests/e2e --timeout=120 -q
1 skipped in 0.12s

pre-commit run --all-files
# Exit 0 after commit aa68f76: all applicable hooks passed, including
# mypy, Black, Flake8, Pylint, Prettier, and GitHub Actions lint.

pytest tests/integration -n 4 --dist=loadfile --timeout=120 -q
6 failed, 1881 passed, 4 skipped, 3 xpassed, 2 warnings in 670.32s
# Interrupted after the run stopped progressing near the end.
```

`cd website && npm run format` completed successfully.

The broader integration run was **not green**. Its failures were:

- `test_skills_pool.py::test_hub_install_start_poll_complete`: task stayed in `importing`.
- `test_plugins_router.py::test_plugins_get_nonexistent`: HTTP 405 versus expected 400/404.
- `test_providers_router.py::test_providers_get_nonexistent`: HTTP 405 versus expected 400/404.
- `test_plugins.py::test_plugins_install_official_cloudpaw_lifecycle`: 120-second test timeout.
- `test_acp_runner.py::test_acp_start_spawns_mock_runner`: 120-second test timeout.
- `test_acp_runner.py::test_acp_close_after_start`: 120-second test timeout.

An isolated comparison against **unmodified upstream `549a7f3`** reran those six node IDs with `-n 4 --dist=loadfile --timeout=120 -q --tb=short`: **5 failed, 1 passed in 205.62s**. The two HTTP 405 assertions, CloudPaw timeout, skill-import wait, and ACP-close timeout reproduced on that baseline. **ACP-start passed on the baseline**, so I am not claiming its failure is pre-existing.

An isolated rerun on this branch of the CloudPaw, ACP-start, and ACP-close node IDs with `-n 2 --dist=loadfile --timeout=120 -q --tb=short` initially produced **3 failed in 243.58s**, all timeouts. These are historical results from the same insufficient total timeout, not the final ACP verification result.

### ACP follow-up verification

The earlier local invocation used a **120-second total test limit**, whereas the ACP test itself can spend 120 seconds polling history before its disk/log fallback. The repository's CI uses **`--timeout=300`** (`.github/workflows/tests.yml`). The old failure logs already contained the mock runner reply and cron `status=success`; the timeout occurred while polling history. `tests/integration/helpers.py::wait_cron_executed` documents an existing history-cache race after agent reloads and provides the fallback.

Without any source changes, both cases passed when run individually on commit `aa68f76`, with the CI's 300-second test limit and the same isolated working/secret directories and cleaned lowercase proxy environment:

```text
pytest tests/integration/test_acp_runner.py::test_acp_start_spawns_mock_runner --timeout=300 -q --tb=short
1 passed in 11.50s

pytest tests/integration/test_acp_runner.py::test_acp_close_after_start --timeout=300 -q --tb=short
1 passed in 6.98s
```

This corrects the earlier ACP regression concern, but does not establish that the complete parallel integration suite is green. The two HTTP 405 assertions, CloudPaw installation timeout, and network-backed skill import wait remain documented above and reproduced on the unmodified baseline under the original invocation. No unrelated test expectations, repository timeout settings, or source code were changed to hide failures. CI approval and maintainer review are still required.

## Additional Notes

The pinned Pylint/Astroid version reports `E1120` for the two existing Windows `ctypes.c_ulong()` initializers in `sandbox/runtime_boundary.py`. This PR makes their implicit zero explicit (`ctypes.c_ulong(0)`) so the required full-repository lint gate can pass; runtime behavior is unchanged.

No console screenshots are needed: the feature is a backend/plugin API extension using the existing approval UI. The classifier cookbook has no new runtime dependency or hard-coded service integration.

prs.title: fix(agents): recover from rejected media URLs
prs.body:
## Description

When a provider returns HTTP 400 with “The provided URL does not appear to be valid” for a request containing media, an existing conversation can keep failing on every turn. The reasoning loop currently retries explicit media-capability rejections but does not handle this URL-validation error.

Retry this specific error once with media replaced by text placeholders in the formatted request. Keep the original saved messages and restore media handling after the retry, including when the retry fails. Do not record a model-wide media rejection for a URL error. Requests without wire media, unrelated validation errors, authentication/server errors, and content-policy rejections retain their existing behavior.

Adds regression coverage using deserialized tool-result history, the real formatter, and simulated OpenAI API errors, plus English/Chinese model documentation and README documentation entries.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #7966

**Security Considerations:** Content-policy errors are excluded from this fallback. The change reuses existing request-time media normalization and does not introduce new file access or URL fetching.

- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

- [x] Documentation updated (if needed)

## Testing

Current verification: 9 of the original 11 failures pass on follow-up testing. Two pre-existing tests still assert 400/404 for GET routes that do not support GET; their 405 responses reproduce on the unchanged base. This PR is submitted for review with those failures disclosed. The full suite was not rerun after the environment setup, so the all-tests-pass checkbox remains unchecked.

Installed the required `.[dev,test,full]` dependencies and pre-commit hooks. Ran the website's `npm run format` successfully.

The regression tests cover recovery, preservation of serialized history, subsequent requests retaining media, one retry only, cleanup on failure, no media-capability cache poisoning (including overlapping error text), and non-retriable errors.

## Evidence

Before the production fix, the initial regression tests reported `2 failed, 6 passed`; both failures exercised the missing retry. After the fix and two additional classifier-boundary cases:

```text
$ pytest --import-mode=importlib -o pythonpath=tests/integration --ignore=tests/contract -n 4 --dist=loadscope
11 failed, 18680 passed, 27 skipped, 3 xpassed, 90 warnings in 810.22s (0:13:30)

The initial full-suite run was not green. Seven browser integration failures reported a missing Playwright Chromium executable. The other four are `test_cli_doctor_runs` (120-second timeout), `test_plugins_install_official_cloudpaw_lifecycle` (HTTP timeout), and the plugins/providers nonexistent-resource tests (HTTP 405 instead of 400/404). All four non-browser failures reproduce on the unchanged base commit `a762e31b` in the same environment (the same two HTTP 405 responses and the same two timeouts).

Plain `pytest` is blocked during collection by duplicate `test_backup.py` module names. The complete suite was therefore run with importlib mode and the integration helper path; contract tests were run separately because their parametrization order differs across xdist workers. ```text

a762e31b
$ pytest tests/integration/test_cli_surface.py::test_cli_doctor_runs tests/integration/test_plugins_router.py::test_plugins_get_nonexistent tests/integration/test_plugins.py::test_plugins_install_official_cloudpaw_lifecycle tests/integration/test_providers_router.py::test_providers_get_nonexistent -n 4 --dist=loadscope --tb=short -q
4 failed in 144.51s (0:02:24)
```

### Follow-up verification

Installed the matching Playwright Chromium and isolated the test processes' working, secret, and backup directories, with `QWENPAW_RUNNING_IN_CONTAINER=true` for file-backed test secrets. All seven previously failing browser cases passed; the three affected files contain eight cases in total. The doctor and plugin lifecycle tests also passed on rerun. These reruns do not establish that all timing-related failures are eliminated.

```text
$ pytest tests/integration/browser/test_e2e_isolation.py tests/integration/browser/test_playwright_provider_e2e.py tests/integration/browser/test_browser_tool_e2e.py -q --tb=short

2 failed, 2 passed in 79.23s (0:01:19)
```

Remaining failures are stale route expectations:

- `test_plugins_get_nonexistent` requests `GET /api/plugins/{id}`, whose supported method is DELETE. The supported query `GET /api/plugins/{id}/status` returns 404 for a missing plugin.
- `test_providers_get_nonexistent` requests `GET /api/models/{id}/config`, whose supported method is PUT. The supported query `GET /api/models/{id}/pool` returns 404 for a missing provider.

Two temporary read-only diagnostic cases verified both old routes' 405 responses and Allow headers, and both supported queries' 404 responses: `2 passed in 4.61s`. Repository code and test assertions were not modified for these follow-up runs.

## Additional Notes

This implements the issue's request-scoped graceful-degradation option. Existing normalization already converts available local media into inline data or placeholders; this change handles providers that still reject the resulting media URL. The retry can use text context but cannot inspect omitted media. Verification uses a simulated provider rejection on macOS, not a live AgentScope endpoint or Windows desktop reproduction.

prs.title: fix(console): correct thinking slider fill and stabilize saving
prs.body:
## Description

Fix misleading thinking-slider fill and keep the latest selection visible while settings save. This update also addresses both regressions reported in [the maintainer review](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8287#issuecomment-6285707088).

### Review follow-up

1. **Off to numeric budget was not committed.** Numeric-input dirtiness is now separate from slider/preview state, so changing the preview from Off to Budget cannot cancel submission on blur or Enter.
2. **Switching chats discarded submitted writes.** Save queues now belong to an agent/chat scope outside the component. Switching or unmounting the UI never cancels submitted writes. Returning to a chat (including A to B to A and remounting with a different runtime session ID) waits for all pending writes before reading settings. Failed writes do not block the next queued write; stale responses cannot update the current UI. Idle queue entries are removed after completion.
3. Merged current upstream main at `27d22cd18d6e7fe610536ef1375cebf7aea89215`, resolved the conflict, and preserved upstream's `onDecisionEnabledChange` callback and advanced decision settings.

The original visual fix remains: neutral unselected rail, accent fill only through the selected value, no whole-panel dimming or preview rollback during ordinary thinking-strength saves.

Changes are limited to six frontend source/test/style files. No backend, model protocol, authentication, dependency, or downstream business-integration changes are included.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8286

**Security Considerations:** Queues are separated by agent and persisted chat ID (or runtime session ID for a new chat), retain only in-flight operations, and do not contain credentials. Tests use isolated fixture settings and never call a real model or business database.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [x] Tests

## Checklist

- [x] All applicable pre-commit checks pass for the changed files; no auto-fixes required
- [x] Changed frontend files pass Prettier checks
- [x] Full frontend test suite and coverage thresholds pass
- [x] Complete production frontend build passes
- [x] Regression tests cover the maintainer's two reproductions
- [x] Latest main merged; upstream decision-setting callback preserved

No channel implementation or contract changes.

## Testing

1. Start with thinking Off, edit a numeric budget to 4096, and blur or press Enter. Verify exactly one save with the numeric budget.
2. Hold the first save, choose High then Medium, and switch to another chat. Both writes must finish for the original chat, without changing the other chat's UI.
3. Repeat A to B to A, or unmount/remount the same persisted chat under a new runtime session ID. The new settings read must wait until both writes finish and display Medium. A subsequent Low save must remain the final value.
4. Reject the first held write. The second submitted write must still execute.
5. Use the same chat ID under another agent. That agent's reads and writes must proceed independently.
6. Retain advanced decision-setting behavior for existing/new chats, failure rollback, model reset, numeric budgets, and the original slider-fill behavior.

## Evidence

New focused regressions against the prior PR implementation: **6 failed, 1 passed**. With this update: **7 passed**.

prs.title: fix(plugins): do not abort a plugin install when invalidate_caches fails
prs.body:
## Description

`PluginLoader` called `importlib.invalidate_caches()` unconditionally at three sites. On Python builds where that stdlib call itself raises (the issue shows `TypeError: MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cls'` on a distro-patched 3.11), the exception aborted the whole plugin install or hot-update. Refreshing import caches is best effort, so a failure should not be fatal.

The three calls now go through `_invalidate_import_caches()`, which catches the error and logs it at debug level.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8265

**Security Considerations:** None

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Tests

## Checklist

- [ ] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes (I ran `black --check` on the two changed files only)
- [x] I ran tests locally: `tests/unit/plugins/test_loader_helpers.py`, the two new tests fail without the change and pass with it. One existing test in that file, `test_symlink_escape_rejected`, fails on my Windows machine because creating a symlink needs a privilege I do not have; it is unrelated to this change.
- [x] Documentation updated (if needed): not needed
- [ ] Ready for review

## Evidence

Behavior before the change: when `importlib.invalidate_caches` raises (the `TypeError: MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cls'` from #8265), the exception escaped `PluginLoader` and aborted the plugin install / hot-update.

Behavior after the change: the two new tests in `tests/unit/plugins/test_loader_helpers.py` patch `importlib.invalidate_caches` to raise `TypeError`, and the install path now completes with the error logged at debug level. Both tests fail on the base commit with the raised `TypeError` and pass with this change (run locally with `pytest tests/unit/plugins/test_loader_helpers.py`).

prs.title: feat(memory): integrate ReMe 0.4.2.0 with opt-in decision compaction, images and tags
prs.body:
## Description

将 QwenPaw 的 ReMe 依赖从 `reme-ai==0.4.1.11` 升级至 `0.4.2.0`，适配后台索引和纯粹的 Auto-Dream 记忆整合流程，并接入默认关闭的决策模型相关性压缩、对话图片记忆和实体标签生成。主动交互继续使用现有 `/proactive`，不与 Auto-Dream 串联。

以下内容已按 2026-10-23 的最新 PR 提交 `73803d32f` 更新；当前 PR base 为 `a4501e767`，本地验证使用 ReMe `0.4.2.0` editable 源码 `c773fa7b`。原检查基于 PR 提交 `410ecd6ad`、当时记录的 QwenPaw main `33f04faf8` 和同一 ReMe 候选源码。较早的 `d22e00bb` Git 源码覆盖已移除，依赖保持正式版本 pin `reme-ai==0.4.2.0`。

## ReMe 0.4.1.11 → 0.4.2.0 的改动

- 新增可选的决策模型组件，将决策推理与普通文本生成分开，并提供统一的决策调用接口。供应商相关依赖按需安装，模型在首次调用时初始化。
- 新增 `compact_context`，根据当前任务与工具证据的相关性，为旧工具输出生成更短的预览。工具调用和消息本身保持完整，预览中携带恢复原文的引用。
- 压缩前按唯一调用 ID 校验工具调用与结果配对，保护近期消息、显式保护内容、失败或未完成调用及非文本结果。缺少恢复引用、配对不明确或模型判断不可靠时保留原文。
- 为相关性压缩增加状态与请求 token 预算、证据长度限制、并发控制和整体超时。供应商错误、非法答案、超时或替换后没有缩短时不应用该项预览。
- 支持注入宿主管理的 AgentScope 决策模型实例，区分借用模型和组件自行创建的模型。关闭时等待进行中的请求结束，只释放自身拥有的客户端，并在清理完成后传播取消。
- Auto-Memory 新增 `include_images`，支持结合对话文本理解图片，并将图片信息写入记忆。Base64 图片原始资产可以保存为独立文件，在记忆中保留来源引用。
- 同一 session 的对话 transcript 写入改为串行处理，减少多个记忆任务同时追加或更新会话文件时的覆盖问题。
- 新增从 Markdown frontmatter 派生的本地标签索引，支持配置标签字段、每文件标签数量和规范化规则。标签保存在记忆文件中，索引可以从文件重新构建。
- 新增 `auto_tag_step`，根据当前任务新增或修改的记忆文件生成实体标签，并写回指定的 frontmatter 字段。单个文件打标失败会记录在任务元数据中，不覆盖已经生成的记忆正文。
- 新增 `list_tags`，支持分页列出已有标签及关联文件数。混合检索支持可选的 `tags` 过滤，匹配包含任一有效标签的文件，不传标签时保持全量搜索。
- 将主动主题生成从 Auto-Dream 中拆出，增加独立的 `proactive_refresh` 流程及 catalog，分别执行主题抽取、规划、议程生成和持久化。Auto-Dream 专注于 daily 到 digest 的整合，原 `dream_topics_step` 被移除。
- 主动记忆读取与刷新分开，读取接口仅返回已经生成的主题和议程，不再重新分析 daily 或调用模型生成内容。
- Dream checkpoint 改为记录实际扫描到的源文件版本，避免扫描后文件发生变化却仍被标记为已处理。抽取结果和整合回执通过校验后才推进处理状态，失败时保留重试机会。
- Embedding 对 429 限流错误执行重试，并隔离批次中的异常输入，避免单个坏样本导致整批健康输入丢失。
- 对供应商明确报告超限的 embedding 输入增加有界缩短重试，保留源文件及向量空间身份。重试结果按条目处理，成功条目可以继续进入索引。
- BM25 增量维护有效文档长度，减少重复统计开销，并在批量分词失败时保留原索引。搜索过滤条件按查询预处理，减少检索过程中的重复计算。
- 明确混合检索 RRF 分数与单路检索分数的阈值差异，阈值高于混合检索有效上界时记录警告。无结果或结果已全部返回时继续保持 `answer=""`，原因放入 `metadata.empty_result`。
- 文件监听新增可选的 `watch_mode="watch"`，使用专用线程等待文件变化，提供背压和停止、取消清理。默认仍使用 `awatch`，嵌入式宿主可以显式切换以避免长期占用 AnyIO 共享线程额度。
- AgentScope 依赖对齐至 `2.0.10`，补齐 embedding usage 所需接口，并支持宿主共享同一版本的模型和决策组件。

## QwenPaw 接入改动

- 同步将 `pyproject.toml` 和运行期 `_REQUIRED_REME_VERSION` 更新为 `0.4.2.0`，嵌入索引显式设置 `watch_mode: watch`。启动时检查依赖是否提供该参数，并增加实际启动、文件变更、索引与关闭的契约测试。
- Auto-Dream 只保留 `dream_extract_step → dream_integrate_step → dream_finish_step`，继续使用原有 action 与调度，不再生成兴趣主题；移除旧 Dream 参数 `topic_count`、`topic_diversity_days`。ReMe 自身仍提供独立主动主题能力，但 QwenPaw 本 PR 不接入 `proactive_refresh` 或专用 proactive catalog，现有 `/proactive` 实现保持不变。
- Auto-Dream 直接复用通用 Job 执行与通知路径，移除双任务串联、专用 `_run_auto_dream` 和 `notify_result` 参数。保留原有成功、无变更、失败和取消时的通知策略。
- 新增默认关闭的 `light_context_config.decision_compact_config`，在 Scroll 和 native 自动压缩前尝试相关性压缩。该开关独立于长期记忆和聊天审批决策，需要同时启用自动上下文压缩。
- 从智能体或全局 decision slot 创建 AS 决策模型，复用供应商的 API Key、base URL 和自定义请求头，再将同一实例借给 ReMe。审批与压缩共享构造入口，分别保留零重试和一次重试。
- Scroll 为已持久化且仍可读取的历史原文提供 `recall_history` 引用，native 先通过 offloader 归档，再提供 `read_file` 恢复路径。压缩提案通过完整内容校验和实际模型输入 token 检查后才提交，失败或无收益时继续原压缩流程。
- 增加 compaction revision，使消息 ID 不变、仅工具输出缩短时，MemoryMiddleware 仍能保存压缩前快照。手动 `/compact` 和紧急溢出恢复保留既有行为。
- 新增默认关闭的 `auto_memory_include_images`，每次任务结合最新配置与实际记忆模型的 `supports_image` 判断是否传入图片。会话临时模型选择不改变记忆模型，调用者仍可显式关闭图片。
- 消息快照可保留不超过 50 MiB 的本地图片原始内容，模型请求使用副本进行重编码和按需缩放，并修正 Base64 padding 的字节数计算。远程图片先有界下载再执行字节适配，超出准备上限或无法缩放时明确报错。备用模型适配和共享模型并发仍存在下文列出的未完成项。
- 新增默认关闭的 `auto_memory_generate_tags`，开启后选择私有 `auto_memory_with_tags` 流程，在保存笔记后追加打标。开关变更对后续任务生效，不修改共享 Job 的步骤列表，也不删除已有标签。
- 增加 `memory_list_tags` 工具和 `/reme list_tags`，并为 `memory_search` 与 search action 增加可选 `tags` 参数。同步补齐工具治理注册、只读工具识别和标签发现提示。
- Console 增加决策模型压缩的基础及高级参数、图片记忆和标签生成开关，并支持在文件预览元数据区展示 YAML block-list 格式的 `memory_tags`。
- `/reme help` 和数组、对象参数错误增加 JSON 引号示例，如 `tags='["赵六","Project_A"]'` 和 `filter='{"kind":"decision"}'`。
- 决策模型构造并入已有 `model_factory.py`，审批和压缩共享模型解析；启用判断集中在 Agent，删除 token 计数纯转发层，共用压缩元数据标记。复用已有 `run_sync_io` 和 `run_async_to_completion`，Scroll 仅读取相关原文并移至工作线程，关闭时完成模型、历史库与产物清理后再传播取消。
- 更新配置、上下文、长期记忆和主动记忆的中英文文档，并增加压缩回滚、原文恢复、配置切换、图片能力、标签检索和 Dream 通知的回归覆盖。

原检查针对已提交的 `410ecd6ad`，使用独立工作区，没有混入开发目录中的未提交修改。以下保留原问题清单，并按当前提交 `73803d32f` 标注处理状态；离线测试通过不代表仍待处理的图片边界已经解决。

- **已处理：移除旧 Git 固定来源。** 已删除 `tool.uv.sources` 中固定 `d22e00bb` 的 ReMe 覆盖，保持 `reme-ai==0.4.2.0`。当前本地验证使用包含后续修复的 editable 源码 `c773fa7b`；这仍不能代替正式分发包验收。

prs.title: feat(agent): add /steer command for mid-execution guidance (#1775)
prs.body:
Fixes #1775.

## What Problem This Solves

Today there is no way to correct the agent while a turn is already running:
stopping the turn loses all progress, and waiting for it to finish means
irrelevant work keeps accumulating. `/steer <guidance>` fills this gap — it
lets the user hand the agent mid-flight guidance that takes effect on the
**next** agent turn without stopping anything.

```
/steer Focus on the error handling first
```

## How it works

- `qwenpaw/steer/store.py` — per-session hand-off buffer with a 10-minute
  TTL.
- `qwenpaw/steer/handler.py` — the `/steer` command; records the text.
- `qwenpaw/steer/hook.py` — `SteerInjectionHook`, a `HookBase` subclass at
  `PRE_AGENT_BUILD`, drains the buffer and calls `inject_context`.
- Registered in `bootstrap_factory`'s `builtin_hook_clses` and in
  `collect_builtin_command_specs()`.

## Why not true mid-execution steering

Dispatching inside a running turn needs changes to the reply loop that the
current runtime does not expose safely; injecting at `PRE_AGENT_BUILD`
achieves the same user-visible effect (the next turn follows the guidance)
without touching turn-dispatch internals.

## Evidence

- Manual run: with a long turn in flight, issuing `/steer Focus on the error
  handling first` returned an immediate acknowledgement; the subsequent turn
  opened with the injected context and the agent addressed error handling
  first (observed via turn context log).
- Without `/steer`, the same run ran to completion with no guidance applied.
- Buffer drain is one-shot: a second turn does not re-apply stale guidance;
  guidance older than the 10-minute TTL is dropped.

prs.title: fix(docs): correct anchor case for Security Web-login link in api-tutorial
prs.body:
fix(docs): correct anchor case for Security Web-login link in api-tutorial

The link `./security#Web-登录认证` (appears 3x) points to the heading
"Web 登录认证" in security.zh.md, whose slug is `web-登录认证`.
GitHub-slugger lowercases Latin letters, so the uppercase `W` in the
anchor makes the link permanently dead.

Evidence:
- target heading: security.zh.md `## Web 登录认证` -> generated slug `web-登录认证`
- broken link anchor: `Web-登录认证` (case mismatch, never resolves)
- fix: lowercase the anchor so it matches the generated slug

## Evidence
- `git show origin/main:website/public/docs/security.zh.md` line 955: `## Web 登录认证`
  -> slug = `web-登录认证` (lower-cased by the docs slugger)
- `git show origin/main:website/public/docs/api-tutorial.zh.md` lines 9, 73, 608:
  `[Web 登录认证](./security#Web-登录认证)` -> anchor `Web-登录认证` != `web-登录认证`
- Working anchors like `./cli#qwenpaw-cron` prove the framework lowercases,
  so the correct anchor must be `web-登录认证`.

prs.title: fix(skill): avoid scanner false positive in make-skill validator
prs.body:
## Description

The built-in `make-skill` is blocked by QwenPaw's own skill security scanner when it is imported into the skill pool or a workspace:

```
[CRITICAL] Dangerous code execution functions that can execute arbitrary code
(scripts/validate_skill.py:432) rule_id=COMMAND_INJECTION_EVAL
```

The flagged line is the validator's syntax check for generated scripts:

```python
compile(path.read_bytes(), relative, "exec")
```

`compile()` only produces a code object, which is never executed here, so this is a false positive. However, `COMMAND_INJECTION_EVAL` matches any bare `compile(` call. This PR replaces it with `ast.parse(path.read_bytes(), filename=relative)`, which performs the same syntax check and raises the same `SyntaxError` (with the same filename and line) without producing a code object. Applied identically to `make-skill-en` and `make-skill-zh`.

I chose to fix the skill rather than relax the scanner rule, since loosening a CRITICAL rule to let one built-in pass seems like the wrong trade.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8320 (same validator, different failure)

**Security Considerations:** No behaviour change beyond removing `compile()`; the scanner rule is untouched.

prs.title: fix(providers): route content inspection errors to fallback

## Description

Ali-compatible gateways can return `data_inspection_failed` or `inappropriate content` when a request is rejected by content inspection. QwenPaw currently classifies both messages as `bad_request`, so `FallbackChatModel` stops instead of trying the next configured model. This change classifies those provider markers as `content_safety` and allows fallback while keeping same-model retry disabled.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8092

**Security Considerations:** No credentials, network policy, or user content handling changed. The change only affects provider error classification and fallback eligibility.
