prs.title: feat(creator): release 2.0.3 with skills, narration, scratch and script import
prs.body:
## Description

This PR releases QwenPaw Creator **2.0.1 → 2.0.3**, carrying only the plugin work completed **after the previous upstream release**. That release landed as `878bf4535` on 2026-10-13; its fork head was `a5db0ade6`. The plugin trees at those two commits were re-verified byte-identical (`git diff a5db0ade6 878bf4535 -- plugins/apps/qwenpaw-creator/` is empty) before reconnecting their ancestry. Everything below is the delta from that baseline, not a repetition of the 2.0.1 release notes.

**Scope and baseline.** This PR is opened directly from **`xuanrui-L:dev/creator`**, not a detached release branch. The integration branch contains the recorded upstream baseline `7c757a8e8`, with the previous squash explicitly connected through a content-equivalent merge. The resulting diff is **88 files under `plugins/apps/qwenpaw-creator/` (+13,459 / −222)**. No host application, Console, other plugin, or general release-workflow file is contributed by this PR; the only non-plugin file included in the previous release (`.github/workflows/creator-app-tests.yml`) is unchanged in this delta. The single non-`backend/`-`ui/` path touched is the plugin's own `scripts/dev.sh` hot-install helper.

**Release composition.** `9b0a1d6f8` prepared 2.0.2 (skills panel + narration safety, fork PRs [#212](https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/212) and [#218](https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/218)). Three further fork PRs then merged into the same branch and `6fc5f7043` bumped the plugin to **2.0.3** ([#228](https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/228)):

| Fork PR | Commit | Theme |
|---|---|---|
| [#212](https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/212) | `6e44d30c9` | User-managed skills panel, ZIP/URL import, bounded archive extraction |
| [#218](https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/218) | `0db1089b4` | Single-voice narration gate, legacy self-heal, recovery/ETag consistency |
| [#219](https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/219) | `ff290ec68` | Task-scratch reclamation, storage profile, narration/subtitle prompt corrections |
| [#222](https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/222) | `9924219d8` | Unsupported-temperature handling (kimi-k3 seed + runtime capability learning) |
| [#225](https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/225) | `50129e5d6` | Script direct-landing import, script attachment at project creation, harvest hardening |
| [#228](https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/228) | `6fc5f7043` | Version bump to 2.0.3 |

### What's new since 2.0.1

- **User-managed skills configuration panel.** A new "Skills" pane in the model-configuration modal lets users list, create, edit, toggle, delete, preview, and import custom SKILL.md skills. Builtin skills are shown read-only alongside user skills. The panel supports three import channels: hand-authoring in a modal editor, uploading a ZIP bundle, and importing from a Skills Hub URL. The URL import reuses the host QwenPaw Skill Pool's fetch-and-normalise step (`_prepare_install_payload`), so all market schemes, package size caps, and path sanitising come from the host; nothing networks on its own, and no new SSRF surface is added. Duplicate-name and builtin-shadowing rules apply uniformly across all three channels. ZIP imports use a dedicated extraction budget (32 MiB expansion, 256 members, 1 MiB per document) enforced against bytes actually written, not declared sizes; oversized uploads are refused on Content-Length before the multipart reader spools to a temporary file. Skill writes are serialized under a module-wide RLock; the editor freezes its body and name while a save is in flight so late completions cannot silently drop edits; and dialogs are centered consistently.

- **Single-voice narration overlap gate and legacy project healing.** Projects now reject two enabled narration Elements on the same timeline span at write time, preventing the "switched the voice but both play" double-narration defect. Re-voicing a segment must rebind or delete the original narration Element instead of stacking a second one. A non-destructive load-time repair heals pre-gate projects by keeping only the newest take (by `source_asset_version_id` `created_at`) and muting older overlapping narrations; role-less legacy audio de-conflicts to SFX. Audio-role stamping now walks elements in stable `(start_tick, element_id)` order so one ETag yields exactly one mix. TTS agent guidance instructs rebinding on re-voice. Recovery and commit now carry `diff_semantics` (SOURCE vs MIGRATED) so cross-version journal replays use the correct base/latest representation, fixing crash-recovery bricking after the load-time repair lands as a tracked change. The commit pipeline threads the source document through ProjectSnapshot so transaction "before" snapshots use one authoritative representation, and the three-way merge stays consistent. Protected-pointer user-edit diffs run on the migrated model_dump while base.json/latest.json persist the verbatim source as the recovery ETag anchor, fixing phantom protected-pointer rejections on legacy saves.

- **Task-scratch reclamation and a read-only storage profile.** Task work used to accumulate until nothing read it and nobody cleaned it — the motivating case was a 1.1 GB project holding 607 MB of task-work, 444 MB of it byte-identical to the Artifacts it had been copied from. Stored Artifacts are now **linked** into `task-work/<task>/inputs` instead of copied (`AssetFileStore.resolve_verified_path` keeps the size + sha256 verification), and scratch is released at three points: the provider output on publication, the render predecessor when a step supersedes it (premix, preloud), and every remaining media file once a Task turns terminal. `ProjectExecutionStore` grew an `on_task_terminal` seam so transition, attempt-head replay and quarantine share one choke point. The startup sweep only collects what a killed process left behind, gated by a per-project `runtime/.storage-baseline.json` so pre-upgrade bytes stay put as the before/after reference; `QUARANTINED` work dirs are never touched. Transaction snapshots (base/candidate/latest/final) now land in a gzip container read back by magic sniffing — same filenames, plain history still loads, and ETags are unchanged because the checksum covers the canonical value. `GET /storage/profile` reports the footprint split new vs legacy, read-only and mounted outside the model-config dependency so it survives invalid model settings, with reclaimable bytes counted as the media a release would actually take. Deletion walks a chain of directory handles opened with `O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW` and never resolves a path, so a `runtime/task-work` redirected out of the data root — before or after any check — cannot send the unlink elsewhere; a platform that cannot pin a directory refuses to release scratch, leaving reclamation dormant there until a Windows equivalent lands. Emergency switch: `CREATOR_SCRATCH_RELEASE_ENABLED=false`, which stops every deletion including the render pipeline's own superseded-step release.

- **Script direct-landing import and script attachment at project creation.** A user's finished script can now become the selected `timeline_script` version without material understanding or a model round-trip. `POST .../timelines/{tid}/script-import` plus the shared `publish_script_import` service is content-addressed, idempotent, and written through the existing commit boundary, so `production_stage` still asks for script confirmation and the review policy is not bypassed. A mainline-only `import_script_asset` agent tool (never exposed to specialists) lets the agent register an already-ingested text/DOCX/PDF asset as the script instead of re-drafting it. DOCX/PDF text-layer extraction refuses to land scanned or image-only pages rather than silently dropping the script body, including pages whose text was outlined to vector curves (转曲) in both the many-glyph-path and merged-single-path forms, while a genuinely blank page stays unreported. `script_version_id` is now scoped by `project_id`, so the same content imported into two projects' `timeline:main` no longer collides and 503s on media read; `DEFAULT_MAX_PROJECT_JSON_BYTES` rose from 8 MB to 32 MB for larger scripts. In the UI, script import moved into the creation composer: attachments are sniffed asynchronously, `AttachmentChip` offers a script/material two-way toggle with a Script badge, one script is kept per launch, and `handleLaunch` imports it via `importTimelineScript` (Idempotency-Key) before the first agent message, falling back to material on failure. Import idempotency now verifies a committed-transaction replay's body against the content-addressed version that transaction actually selected — a same-key/different-body retry is rejected with `SCRIPT_IMPORT_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` rather than fabricating a success — and an identical re-import while a `REQUIRE_REVIEW` commit is still pending restores the pending review id so the caller reports 待审阅 instead of claiming the body landed.

- **Observation harvest and background batching hardening.** Harvest-all accepts optional `taskIds`, and a bounded harvest reports overflow instead of dropping paid work, now exposing a `harvestOffset` pagination cursor so a Run that submitted more observations than one harvest bound can reach every task without tracking ids. Discovery is ordered by immutable `created_at` rather than `updated_at`, so awaiting a page to a terminal state cannot reshuffle the cursor into repeating harvested tasks and skipping the rest. Driver and prompt reminders tell the agent to submit independent observations with `background=true` across consecutive rounds (one tool call per round); `creator_agent` and `source_intelligence_agent` prompts were updated to match, including backfilling an empty synopsis from an imported script body before requesting confirmation.

- **Unsupported-temperature handling: kimi-k3 seed plus runtime capability learning.** DashScope rejects the hard-coded `temperature=0.2` for kimi-k3 ("Parameter 'temperature'=0.2 is not supported for kimi-k3 model"), which had paused auto-creation behind a generic retry hint that hid the real cause. `models/config.chat_temperature()` now drops the field for seeded or learned models through the shared `ModelCapabilityCache`, and temperature is omitted in `text_model._call_openai`, `vlm_model._call_openai_vlm` and the DashScope path of `model_client._build_chat_model`. On a refusal the text path learns it, drops the field and retries once so the same turn self-heals; the AgentScope agent path additionally drops the cached model/configuration so the next rebuilt turn omits temperature (`_configured_model()` keyed only on the connection tuple, which the capability flip does not change). The whole Kimi K2/K3 family is seeded by prefix and Moonshot's "invalid temperature" wording is classified on both backend and UI, where `AgentDock.simplifyErrorMessage` surfaces a sanitized, actionable message with new zh/en locale keys. The classifier requires `invalid` to sit adjacent to `temperature` — `not supported`/`unsupported` stay trusted — so a generic `invalid_request_error` 400 whose body merely echoes `temperature` cannot permanently mark a model as rejecting it.

- **Narration, dialogue-duration and burned-in-subtitle prompt corrections.** Dialogue overruns are now caught by an immediate recomputation of characters-per-speaking-second at the `video_prompt` compile point and in the pre-commit self-check (Chinese 3–4 chars/s, English 2–3 words/s, action pauses deducted first); over budget, the only allowed remedies are trimming the line or lengthening the generation unit — never asking the model to speed up or truncate. The prompts no longer overstate what the code gate does: `_validate_narration_overlap` catches s2v-vs-narration and narration-vs-narration only, not R2V native speech, so that case is stated as a creative invariant the agent must keep itself. Finished videos are explicitly required not to burn in subtitles, dialogue text or on-screen text (dialogue is audio-only), in both the `video_prompt` compile section and `professional-media-prompts` section E. Narration sourcing defaults to the video model's native voice because TTS-synthesised narration measured worse; narration and dialogue are written verbatim into `creation.narrative`/`video_prompt` instead of getting a separate track, with only two exceptions kept — a user-uploaded voice sample for timbre cloning, and carriers that do not emit sound on their own (`motion_clip`, edits of existing footage, s2v that needs a driving audio track). A prompt contract test locks the new default.

- **Parameterized archive extraction budgets.** `archive.py` extraction is refactored from module-wide constants to a caller-supplied `ArchiveLimits` tuple, with bytes counted chunk-by-chunk against the budget as they are written rather than trusted from declared sizes. Project import retains its existing 16 GiB headroom; skill import passes its own tight budget. A partial file is removed on any failure.

- **Dev hot-install fix.** `scripts/dev.sh` staged `plugin.json`/`requirements.txt`/`__init__.py`/`backend`/`ui-dist` but not the plugin-root `templates/`, which the backend reads at import time (`templates/cat-launch/template.json` via `parents[3]`). Because hot-install replaces the target directory, the omission deleted the installed copy's `templates/` and failed the plugin load while `plugin install` still exited 0 and dev.sh printed "Installed" — a silent, destructive miss. The staging is now guarded with `[ -d ]`, so branches without `templates/` are unaffected.

Skill ZIP import inherits the existing archive path-traversal, symlink and zip-bomb guards, with a dedicated extraction budget (32 MiB / 256 members / 1 MiB per document) enforced against bytes actually written. URL import reuses the host's existing Skills Hub fetch/sanitise pipeline (`_prepare_install_payload`); no new network surface is added, and credential-bearing URLs are refused before any request. Script import writes through the existing commit boundary, so review policy and `production_stage` confirmation are not bypassed; its idempotency key rejects a same-key/different-body replay instead of reporting a false success, and text extraction refuses scanned or vector-outlined pages rather than landing an empty script. prs.title: test(security): keep the sips preflight cases platform-neutral
prs.body:
> **Submitted by**: 墨子·BEUnit@QPQAT

## What

Two independent test-side defects made the sips preflight cases fail on
`windows-latest` while passing on ubuntu and macos. Neither is a product
defect: `sips` is a macOS-only binary and the product treats an
unidentifiable output as "unknown" (`None`) by design, so the cases were
asking the Windows runner to exercise a code path that cannot exist there.

## Defect 1 — Windows path shape makes the preflight return `None`

The command strings were rendered with plain f-string interpolation of
`WindowsPath` objects, which yields backslashes. `_sips_output_exists()`
splits the command with `shlex.split()`, and shlex runs in **POSIX mode**, so
every backslash is consumed as an escape character. The `--out` token came out
as `C:Usersrunneradmin...small.jpg` with no separators at all, `os.path.isabs()`
then returned `False` for that drive-relative form, and the function returned
`None`:

- `test_sips_existing_output_requires_approval_without_decision_model`
  expected the "output already exists" preflight reason, but the call fell
  through to the provider instead;
- `test_sips_new_output_supplies_verified_fact` expected
  `state["verified_facts"]`, which is only populated when the output is
  identified as absent, so the key was missing entirely.

Rendering both paths with `as_posix()` removes the platform difference instead
of skipping the cases. On POSIX `str(p) == p.as_posix()`, so it is an identity
transform there and the tokens are verbatim identical — no regression. The
whole path has to be converted: replacing only the last segment leaves the
earlier backslashes to be eaten the same way.

## Defect 2 — the guard stubs never executed, so their assertions always passed

The guard stubs were declared `async def unexpected(*args):` while the product
calls the provider with keywords only:

```python
await provider.evaluate(state=state, questions=_QUESTIONS, model=model)
```

So the `TypeError` is raised **during argument binding and the stub body never
runs**. The product's `except (TypeSafeEvaluationError, ValueError, TypeError)`
then swallows it and returns the fail-closed fallback
`DecisionModelAssessment(True, "Decision model assessment unavailable; approval
required", "TypeError", ...)`. Because that fallback also sets
`needs_approval=True`, **`assert result.needs_approval` passed
unconditionally** — the guard this case claims to enforce ("a verified
overwrite must not call the decision model") was already broken and the
assertion could not see it. The only assertion that actually went red was the
`reason` one, which is a consequence of defect 1, not the guard.

A corollary worth stating for anyone writing probes here: because the exception
is raised at binding time, any counter or in-body instrumentation inside the
stub is structurally blind to it. The observed message is verbatim
`unexpected() got an unexpected keyword argument 'state'` while an in-body call
counter reads `0`.

Note that `evaluate` is declared keyword-only (`self, *, state, questions,
model, timeout`), so an `(*args)` stand-in can never receive any argument at
all. The mismatch — and therefore the blindness of all six guards — is
structural, not incidental to how the call happens to be written.

Adding `**kwargs` to the signature makes the same situation raise
`AssertionError`, which is **not** in that `except` clause, so it propagates
through the product layer and the test really goes red. The guard regains
detection power. (Verified separately that `AssertionError` is not caught by
that clause, so the positive control is not self-proving.)

## Re-verified on this base, not carried over from an older one

Both defects were originally demonstrated against an earlier commit. Since then
`150598da` (#8360) rewrote 109 lines of `decision_model.py` and 204 lines of
`typesafe_provider.py`, so the evidence was re-taken on this base:

- `pytest tests/unit/security/test_decision_model.py` -> **21 passed**
- the neighbouring suites `tests/unit/security/ tests/unit/providers/` ->
  **1718 passed, 1 skipped**, i.e. no regression from this change
- a five-leg positive control for defect 2, using the real product function and
  the real autouse fixture (never a reconstruction), with every observation
  point **outside** the stub body:

| Leg | Door | Stub signature | Guard assertion | Stub body ran | `error_type` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C control | intact | bare `(*args)` | PASS (the door rejects the target) | 0 | None |
| **A** | **broken** | bare `(*args)` | **PASS — false green** | **0** | **TypeError** |
| **B** | **broken** | `(*args, **kwargs)` | **AssertionError escapes into the test** | 1 | None |
| A2 | broken | bare `(*args)` | PASS — the second case is false green too | 0 | TypeError |
| B2 | broken | `(*args, **kwargs)` | escapes | 1 | None |

Leg A produces the product's own warning line, verbatim
`Decision model assessment unavailable (TypeError)`. A separate leg confirms the
clause is `except (TypeSafeEvaluationError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:` and
does not mention `AssertionError`, so leg B is not self-proving.

- for defect 1, the Windows-shaped command yields the `--out` token
  `C:UsersrunneradminAppDataLocalTemppytest-of-runneradminsmall.jpg` with no
  separator left, `ntpath.isabs` returns `False`, and the real
  `_sips_output_exists` returns `None`; on POSIX the same function returns
  `True` for an existing output and `False` for a missing one, and `as_posix()`
  is an identity transform (`str(p) == p.as_posix()`). That probe carries its
  own positive control — a missing parent directory, a glob character and a
  non-sips tool all return `None`, so the three outcomes are discriminable and
  the `True`/`False` legs above are not vacuous.

## 🔴 Blast radius: six stubs, two of which are false-green *today*

The same `async def unexpected(*args):` shape appears six times in this file.
Split by the polarity of the enclosing test's assertions:

| Stub line | Test | Assertion polarity | Blind spot |
|---|---|---|---|
| L198 | `test_read_only_listing_skips_model_but_not_existing_ask` | includes `assert not result.needs_approval` | Masked — still goes red, but the message points at the fallback reason and misleads triage |
| L240 | `test_target_free_builtin_read_skips_model_but_not_existing_ask` | three `.needs_approval` assertions | Masked |
| L305 | `test_declared_local_media_read_skips_decision_model` | includes `assert not (...).needs_approval` | Masked |
| **L351** | **`test_sips_existing_output_requires_approval_without_decision_model`** | **only `assert result.needs_approval`** | **Exposed — the guard passes unconditionally** |
| **L498** | **`test_literal_secret_is_not_sent_to_decision_model`** | **only `assert result.needs_approval`** | **Exposed — latent false green, currently PASSED** |
| **L508** | **`test_sensitive_target_never_reaches_service`** | **only `assert result.needs_approval`** | **Exposed — latent false green, currently PASSED** |

The last two are the point of this change. `test_literal_secret_is_not_sent_to_
decision_model` and `test_sensitive_target_never_reaches_service` are
**currently passing on ubuntu, macos and windows alike**, yet their guard
assertions are structurally identical to the L351 one. If the product ever did
send a literal secret or a sensitive target to the decision service, **both
tests would still pass**: the fallback path also returns `needs_approval=True`
and the `AssertionError` is swallowed. These two cases claim to guard a safety
property — sensitive content must not leave the process — and today they do not
guard it. That is worth fixing precisely because a red test gets read and a
false-green test does not.

All six are fixed here; leaving half of a single failure surface in place would
keep the blind spot alive.

## Why this is not a product defect

1. `sips` is macOS-only — the product accepts exactly `{"sips",
   "/usr/bin/sips"}`, so on Windows the preflight cannot apply at all.
2. Returning `None` is the documented fail-safe: *"None means we could not
   safely identify the output, not that it is new."*
3. The `except` clause fails closed — any exception means `needs_approval=True`,
   i.e. ask a human. Conservative and harmless.
4. So the defect is in the tests: a macOS-only path was exercised with a Windows
   `tmp_path`, i.e. the carrier did not match the platform of the code under
   test.

## One suggestion, not part of this PR

That `except` clause including `TypeError` is broad. It is broad in the
fail-closed direction, so it is **not** a defect, but it also swallows plain
programming errors — a mistyped stub signature — and reports them as "decision
service unavailable", which is exactly what blinded the six guards above.
Narrowing the clause, or at least logging `TypeError` with its stack, would make
this class of mistake visible. Left to the maintainers; this PR touches no
product code.

---

## About the windows failures in this PR's CI

The windows leg of this PR shows a number of failures under `tests/unit/plugins/`.
**They are not introduced by this PR.** Evidence:

- We ran a control job on the base commit `0db9a8e625e73917a0d113e255b3147134022db8`
  **without any change from this PR** (branch `beunit/baseline-0db9a8e62-for-comparison`,
  run `39752852521`, windows unit job `119737435528`):
  `= 38 failed, 18265 passed, 166 skipped, 1 xfailed, 93 warnings in 3328.62s (0:55:28) =`,
  of which `tests/unit/plugins/` accounts for **23 test names / 34 parametrised instances**.
- This PR touches **no file** under `tests/unit/plugins/`, `src/qwenpaw/plugins/`,
  and no `conftest.py`. `git rev-parse beunit/fix-win-unit-decision-model-sips-and-stub-signature:tests/unit/plugins` is
  `60bac011a9042674c63daadc432150576ef19ba2` on both base and this branch.

**To be equally explicit: this failure set is partly non-deterministic.** Across four runs

prs.title: test(unit): make advisor listing and tui drain assertions platform-stable
prs.body:
> **Submitted by**: 墨子·BEUnit@QPQAT

## What

Fixes three failures on the `Unit Tests - py3.11 - windows-latest` leg of the
nightly run. All three are test-side defects; no product behaviour is wrong.

## tests/unit/modes/test_advisor_middleware.py (2 failures)

`_workspace_listing()` reports each file size as `entry.stat().st_size`, so it
faithfully reports whatever the filesystem holds. The two tests built their
fixtures with `Path.write_text()`, which passes `newline=None` to `io.open`:
every `"\n"` written is translated to `os.linesep`. On Windows that is
`"\r\n"`, so `"a,b\n1,2\n"` lands as 10 bytes instead of 8 and `"print(1)\n"`
as 10 instead of 9, while `"hi"` — which has no newline — stays 2 bytes and
passed. The tests asserted the POSIX byte counts, so they were encoding a
platform detail of the fixture rather than behaviour of the listing.

Writing the fixtures with `write_bytes()` keeps their size identical on every
platform. The assertions are unchanged: they still pin the exact byte count the
listing reports, including the 2-byte `README.md` case that shows a file
without a trailing newline is reported verbatim.

Reproduced locally: with the original fixtures the two tests fail under a
forced CRLF newline translation with messages identical to the CI output, and
pass under LF; with `write_bytes` they pass under both.

## tests/unit/cli/tui/test_app.py (1 failure)

`test_messages_queue_while_busy_and_drain_on_turn_end` left the `run_test()`
block while the `_consume` worker still had events to dispatch. Textual then
tore the screen down and the worker mounted into a tree without
`#transcript`, surfacing as `WorkerFailed(NoMatches)` at `__aexit__`.

`FakeTransport.send()` appends to `transport.sent` **before** it pushes that
turn's four events, and the test used `transport.sent == [...]` as the drain
predicate. That flag can therefore be satisfied while the turn is still in
flight — the same shape the resume test in this file already documents for
`transport.loaded`. Poll the observable state instead: two tool panels mounted
and the turn no longer busy, which the worker can only reach after dispatching
that turn's last event. The iteration bound is raised from 10 to 60 because a
slow event loop needs more pauses to get there, and an explicit `pytest.fail`
reports exhaustion instead of silently exiting with events pending.

## Why this is not a loosened threshold

The `transport.sent` / `app._queued` / `QueuedMessage` assertions are unchanged
verbatim. Only the "when may we stop waiting" predicate changed — from a flag
that is set *before* the events are dispatched, to a state that can only hold
*after* they are. The bound 10 → 60 is headroom for a slow loop, and exhausting
it now fails explicitly where it previously broke out of the loop silently.

---

## About the windows failures in this PR's CI

The windows leg of this PR shows a number of failures under `tests/unit/plugins/`.
**They are not introduced by this PR.** Evidence:

- We ran a control job on the base commit `0db9a8e625e73917a0d113e255b3147134022db8`
  **without any change from this PR** (branch `beunit/baseline-0db9a8e62-for-comparison`,

  `= 38 failed, 18265 passed, 166 skipped, 1 xfailed, 93 warnings in 3328.62s (0:55:28) =`,

- This PR touches **no file** under `tests/unit/plugins/`, `src/qwenpaw/plugins/`,
  and no `conftest.py`. `git rev-parse beunit/fix-win-unit-advisor-crlf-and-tui-drain:tests/unit/plugins` is
  `60bac011a9042674c63daadc432150576ef19ba2` on both base and this branch.
- Those files were added by `0db9a8e6` (#7565) itself.

**To be equally explicit: this failure set is partly non-deterministic.** Across four runs
(base / this PR / two sibling branches) the sets of failing plugins test names differ
(23 / 23 / 21 / 25; intersection 21, union 25), and
`test_tool_deadline_cancels_work_and_reports_public_error` plus

prs.title: test(pawapp): answer the sidecar probe with a raw socket
prs.body:
> **Submitted by**: 墨子·BEUnit@QPQAT

## What

Fixes two failures on the `Unit Tests - py3.11 - macos-latest` leg of the
nightly run, both `TimeoutError: managed service 'lifecycle' did not become
healthy within 10s` (params `[False]` / `[True]`). Test-side defect; the
product is not wrong.

## Why it fails only on macOS

The lifecycle probe served its health response through
`http.server.HTTPServer`, whose `server_bind()` calls `socket.getfqdn()` — a
reverse DNS lookup — **between** `bind()` and `listen()`. On GitHub macOS
runners that lookup blocks for tens of seconds
(actions/runner-images#6383), so the child spends the whole 10s
`startup_timeout` bound but not yet listening, and the supervisor reports a
service that is bound and healthy as never having started.

Measured on macos-latest: `getfqdn` 35.02s, `bind` 0.0012s, both parameters
failing at 10.68s / 10.70s across two rounds; ubuntu 0.36s and windows 5.39s
pass in the same run.

## Fix

`tests/unit/pawapp/test_app_contract.py` already documents this exact trap and
answers with a raw socket for the same reason, so this follows that precedent
instead of widening `startup_timeout`.

## Why this is not a widened timeout

- `startup_timeout` is unchanged verbatim: still 10s.
- Every assertion is unchanged: the probe still reports its pid, the granted
  and withheld environment, its `sys.path` and its `argv`, so the test still
  proves the sidecar keeps the supervised pid, inherits only the granted

prs.title: fix(desktop): speed up cold start and recover frozen WebView
prs.body:
## Description

Addresses the desktop cold-start / degraded-view / frozen-window reports in #8115 (the `desktop.log` rotation item is handled in a separate PR).

**1. Cold start blocked by session-sync (Symptom 1)**
`_sync_scroll_history_on_startup()` ran inside lifespan before `Server ready`, so uvicorn served nothing (the console stayed on the splash) until it finished. On cold boots the first `HistoryStore` open runs `PRAGMA quick_check` over the whole `history.db` (336 MB in the report), and every session file opened a `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` write transaction via `claim_session`, even files skipped by the manifest.
- Run the backfill as a background task right after `Server ready`. It is idempotent against concurrent live writes (`ux_dedup`), and failures were already non-fatal. Shutdown cancels and awaits it; backup restore waits for it (shielded) before swapping workspace directories, since Windows cannot rename the open DB.
- New `HistoryStore.unowned_session_ids()` (one indexed read via `ch_agent`); `claim_session` now runs only for sessions that actually have unowned rows, so typical boots perform no write transactions.

**2. "Degraded view" while background startup runs (Symptom 2)**
`/api/healthz` already existed but the console never consulted it, and `startup_ready` is set after core agents while phase-2 plugins/providers keep loading.
- `app.state.startup_phase` (`plugins` → `agents` → `finalizing` → `complete` / `failed`) is reported as `phase` in `/api/healthz` (status codes unchanged).
- New `StartupProgressBanner` in `MainLayout` polls `/healthz` once per second (capped at 2 min) and shows a non-blocking info banner until loading completes; renders nothing for backends without `phase` or on probe failure. Strings added for all 7 locales.

**3. WebView frozen while backend stays alive (Symptom 3)**
`webview_recovery.rs` only handled `BrowserProcessExited` with `FAILED`. A crashed or hung *render* process leaves the browser process alive, so nothing recovered and the window froze.
- Register `ICoreWebView2::add_ProcessFailed`: `RENDER_PROCESS_EXITED` → reload; `RENDER_PROCESS_UNRESPONSIVE` → wait once (could be a long script), reload if it repeats within 60s; a further failure within 60s of a reload → full rebuild via the existing `recreate` path.

**4. Single instance + window state (follow-up comment)**
- `tauri-plugin-single-instance`: a second launch focuses the existing window. Previously it started another backend whose `reconcile_singleton_backend` killed the running one.
- `tauri-plugin-window-state` with `SIZE | POSITION | MAXIMIZED` (not `VISIBLE`, so quitting while hidden in the tray never restarts hidden). The `Cargo.lock` growth is the single-instance plugin's Linux-only D-Bus (`zbus`) deps; no existing versions changed.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8115

**Security Considerations:** None. `/api/healthz` gains one non-sensitive field; the banner uses existing auth headers.

prs.title: 🚀 Shared daemon for desktop: independent windows and coordinated updates
prs.body:
## Description

The desktop window currently owns the backend it starts. Opening multiple desktop instances can create competing runtimes, and closing or updating one instance can disrupt another. This PR moves shared runtime ownership into a detached native daemon and makes desktop windows independently connected clients.

### Shared daemon and client lifecycle

- Discover and reuse one `shared` runtime per data directory. OS file locks serialize startup, and private instance tokens authenticate lifecycle controls.
- Keep the runtime alive after the last client disconnects. Each connection owns its registration and optional Computer Use endpoint; disconnecting releases only that client's resources.
- Supervise unexpected backend exits with bounded restart retries. Explicit shutdown records stop intent so it does not trigger a restart.
- Close a window directly when other clients remain. The last client chooses **Run in background** or **Quit completely**, with an optional remembered preference. Complete shutdown rechecks active clients and refuses to interrupt another connection.
- Keep the tray to **Show Window** and **Quit App**, using the same close flow. Intentional shutdown no longer displays a misleading connection/retry notice.

Runtime modes remain explicit and separate:

| Mode | Ownership and lifetime |
| --- | --- |
| `shared` | Reusable, supervised runtime; stays alive until explicitly stopped |
| `standalone` | Foreground `qwenpaw app`, owned by its invoker |
| `stdio` | Existing `qwenpaw acp` transport and host-owned lifetime |
| `hub` | Hub-managed instances, excluded from shared discovery |

### Coordinated desktop updates

Updates coordinate windows and daemons belonging to the same installation, including windows using different data directories. Downloads remain in the background. After verification, the user confirms closing the installation's windows and interrupting running tasks; cancellation keeps the downloaded package.

Installation blocks new clients, waits for other windows and the supervised backends to exit, and holds runtime launch locks during replacement. Clients outside this installation must disconnect first. Windows hands the installation barrier to NSIS using the installer's process identity. A failed in-process installation attempts to restore the initiating window's runtime connection. Reconnecting clients wait while an update holds the admission lock and retry automatically if the update is cancelled or fails, instead of treating maintenance as a connection error.

### Persistent local desktop UI

The console is bundled with the desktop shell instead of being loaded by navigating to the backend's HTTP origin. The loading UI appears while Python initializes; the workbench still waits for backend readiness and authentication. A connection snapshot plus revisioned native events lets the existing document reconnect across backend restarts, preserving unsent drafts.

The shell and console share one theme state, with remote theme loading deferred until connection readiness. File-drop navigation is blocked without disabling text drag-and-drop.

### Future direction: one daemon, multiple clients

This establishes a foundation for a VS Code extension, alternative desktop shells, and other local clients to attach to the same `shared` runtime. A user could move between the desktop app and their editor without starting a separate backend for each interface, while each client manages its own connection and UI lifetime.

Those integrations are future work, not included here. Supporting them will require a documented, versioned client protocol and explicit capabilities. The snapshot/event mechanism in this PR describes native connection status; it is not an Agent-session snapshot and ordered-event synchronization protocol.

**Scope:** this changes desktop process ownership, connection lifecycle, and update coordination. Agent execution, conversation storage, existing HTTP APIs, ACP transport, and Hub provisioning retain their existing architecture. App/ACP/Hub entry points receive explicit mode tags.

## Type of Change

- [x] Refactoring
- [x] Bug fix

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- Tauri desktop lifecycle, daemon supervision, and updater
- Shared runtime registration and shutdown controls

## Testing

- Shared lifecycle changes: 212 relevant existing Python tests passed; 9 platform-dependent tests skipped. Update-specific validation subsequently passed 69 relevant Python tests and 39 existing frontend update-context tests.
- 15 Rust library tests passed; macOS debug native build and release `cargo check` passed.
- [External packaged build verification at `8f6f9fd29`](https://github.com/wangfei010313/QwenPaw/actions/runs/39787732820): macOS packaging, launch/readiness, and the browser-based UI verifier passed; Windows packaging and silent installation passed, with startup verification failing as described below.
- Follow-up fixes passed 15 Rust library tests, macOS release checking, four temporary reconnect-control scenarios, an isolated Windows spawn-code cross-compilation check, PowerShell syntax parsing, workflow lint, and the full console format check. Temporary verification code is excluded from the PR.
- Latest frontend fixes: 31 existing theme/settings tests, TypeScript, desktop and browser production builds, targeted ESLint/Prettier, and changed-file commit hooks passed. Existing lint and bundle-size/circular-chunk warnings remain.
- macOS native checks covered concurrent startup into one runtime, independent window closure, zero-client background retention, reuse on reopening, backend crash recovery with an unsent draft retained, last-client close choices, and explicit shutdown without supervisor restart. A client attaching after the close prompt opened correctly prevented shutdown.
- macOS update fixtures covered two-window confirmation/cancellation, direct and cached installation entry points, peer-window exit, external-client refusal, and runtime recovery after an intentionally invalid archive failed installation. A temporary cross-process harness checked installation admission and registration cleanup; it is not included in this PR.
- The Windows installer handoff module passed an isolated `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` cross-compilation check. This does not constitute a full Windows application build or native installation test.

prs.title: test(e2e): re-anchor thirteen nightly cases and remove two silent-skip fallbacks
prs.body:
> **Submitted by**: 李时珍·E2E@QPQAT

## Description

Thirteen `nightly` e2e cases had been failing for consecutive nights. Triage shows **zero product defects**: 3 of them were already fixed upstream by #8247, and the remaining 10 were **stale test-side anchors, missing waits, and one tautological assertion** left behind by upstream UI redesigns (#7899 model-selector rework, #8130 settings-header rework, #7502 session-list rework, #8128 hub-as-builtin-plugin).

This PR re-anchors those 10 cases and, importantly, **removes two silent-skip fallbacks** that had been masking real failures — the same failure mode as the gate blind spots previously fixed in #6686 (42 unmarked cases silently skipped) and #6727 (Windows path separators skipped 66 cases while CI still reported green).

Two further cases that are red on upstream `main` today are **deliberately out of scope** and will be fixed in a separate PR (see *Additional Notes*).

### What changed, per family

| Family | Cases | Root cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| A-1..A-4 | `test_model_switch_and_skill_invocation`, `test_model_switch_and_chat_continuity`, `test_security_config_affects_chat`, `test_workspace_file_and_chat_qa` | #7899 moved the model selector out of the chat header into `SessionThinking`, and swapped the antd Dropdown for a Popover — both old anchor layers are gone | Re-anchor to the new component; add a **fourth terminal state** so a picker that opens with rendered provider headers but `models=0` returns normally instead of burning the 8 s budget and failing |
| A-5 | `test_skill_to_agent_to_chat` | Agents page switched from a table to a card gallery | Re-anchor |
| A-6 | `test_long_conversation_compression` | **Two layers.** (1) The bubble list renders **in reverse** (`REVERSE_MESSAGE_SCROLL_SELECTOR` carries `bubble-list-order-desc`; newest is index 0) and compaction *empties the oldest bubble*, so `get_last_ai_message() == get_ai_messages()[-1]` read an **emptied bubble** and returned `''`. (2) The assertion `assert "1" in response_text` was **tautological**: every bubble permanently contains `Completed 1 steps` and a timestamp such as `12:24:41`, both of which contain the character `1` | (1) Read the answer from the **newest bubble born after the send**, not from the DOM end. (2) Add `extract_answer_body()`, which strips `Completed N steps`, `Canceled · N steps`, timestamps, the brand name and `Thinking`/`Loading`, and asserts on the **answer body only**; an empty body now fails independently |
| C-1 / C-2 | `test_market_compat_tags_render`, `test_incompatible_install_warning_modal` | The three plugin tabs share one set of CSS-module classes (`InstalledPluginList.tsx` imports `MarketPluginList.module.less`), and antd `Tabs` keeps inactive panes in the DOM with `display:none`, so a global `.first` always resolved to a **hidden Installed card** (`123 x locator resolved to hidden`) | Anchor the market pane by its stable rc-tabs pane id (`[id$="panel-market"]`) instead of the `-active` class, which drifts during the ~90 ms React commit window; **remove the silent `except: pass` fallback** around the view toggle so a failure is loud |
| SESS-003 | `test_session_edit_name_and_save` | `open()` only proves the table *container* exists; rows arrive later via async `GET /api/chats`, so counting raced the fetch | `settle_rows_against_server()` in `wait_for_page_loaded()` |
| SESS-004 | `test_session_batch_delete` | Same zero-wait race, **plus a second layer**: after settling, the DOM can still read empty while the server already has rows ("false empty"), and the old code turned that into `pytest.skip` | Cross-check the server first; if the server has rows but the table does not, re-read (6 x 1.5 s, worst case ~10 s against a 480 s ceiling). A false empty that never resolves now **FAILs and reports both counts** instead of skipping. A genuinely empty table still skips; an unreachable server is reported as unknown |

### Why the A-6 assertion hardening matters

Before this PR, `test_long_conversation_compression` could pass **without the feature under test working at all**. A mechanical check over 27 sampled runs showed the assertion held in 27/27 regardless of the answer body. After the fix, four counterfactual groups were replayed against **real log strings** (not synthesised ones): genuine answers 5/5 still pass (no false red), counterfactuals 3/3 now fail, scaffold-only text 3/3 now raise, and cancelled rounds now raise — **0 mismatches**. The green light now carries information.

## Type of Change

- [x] Test only — **no production code is modified by this PR**

## Component(s) Affected

`e2e/` (Playwright page objects and specs) only:

- `e2e/pages/chat_page.py`
- `e2e/pages/plugin_page.py`
- `e2e/pages/sessions_page.py`
- `e2e/tests/test_chat.py`
- `e2e/tests/test_context_scroll.py`
- `e2e/tests/test_cross_module.py`
- `e2e/tests/test_plugins.py`
- `e2e/tests/test_sessions.py`
- `e2e/tests/test_agent_stats.py`, `e2e/tests/test_backups.py` (conflicts resolved in favour of upstream #8247 during rebase)

No `console/` or `src/` changes.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added/updated to cover the change (this PR **is** the test change)
- [x] No new `pytest.skip` introduced; two pre-existing silent-skip fallbacks **removed**
- [x] No assertion weakened — the only assertion rewrite (A-6) is **strengthened**, verified by counterfactual replay
- [x] `Pre-commit Checks` and `NPM Format` green on the branch head
- [x] All commit messages in English, signed off

## Testing

Verified on fork CI against a head that **includes** upstream #8332 (`ce748971`, base of this branch), i.e. on 2.3.0b1 real runners:

| Leg | Marker | Summary line (verbatim from job logs) | Conclusion |
|---|---|---|---|
| run 39898107473 | `-m "p0"` | `1 failed, 66 passed, 4 skipped, 165 deselected, 2 xpassed, 1 rerun in 668.20s` | 13-case scope clean |
| run 39898159191 | `-m "p0"` | `1 failed, 66 passed, 4 skipped, 165 deselected, 2 xpassed, 1 rerun in 709.11s` | 13-case scope clean |
| run 39898165171 | `-m "p0"` | `1 failed, 65 passed, 5 skipped, 165 deselected, 2 xpassed, 1 rerun in 658.57s` | 13-case scope clean |
| run 39898156078 | `-m "p1"` | `1 failed, 105 passed, 2 skipped, 127 deselected, 3 xpassed, 1 rerun in 1777.36s` | 13-case scope clean |
| run 39898162067 | `-m "p1"` | `1 failed, 105 passed, 2 skipped, 127 deselected, 3 xpassed, 1 rerun in 1716.03s` | 13-case scope clean |
| run 39898167964 | `-m "p1"` | `1 failed, 105 passed, 2 skipped, 127 deselected, 3 xpassed, 1 rerun in 1770.00s` | 13-case scope clean |

**Result matrix, 13 cases x 3 rounds on a single head (`ed4eb64d`):** 12 cases passed in all 3 rounds; `test_session_batch_delete` passed in all 3 rounds (it had been skipping on the previous base); `test_session_edit_name_and_save` passed in rounds 1-2 and skipped in round 3 (`No operable sessions`) — a **pre-existing data-dependent flake**, not a regression and not a failure.

**The single `failed` in each leg is outside this PR's scope** and identical across all three rounds: `test_approval_toggle_renders_and_switches` (p0) and `test_cronjob_edit_and_update` (p1). Both are pre-existing red on upstream `main` — see *Additional Notes*.

**`--reruns` accounting.** The e2e job always runs with `--reruns=1` (`_e2e-job.yml:247/249`), so a "first run red, retry green" can look green. In all six runs `failed == rerun == 1`, and the rerun line resolves to the two out-of-scope cases named above. **None of the 13 cases in scope was rescued by a retry.**

## Evidence

```
# 13 in-scope cases, 3 rounds, single head ed4eb64d — all passed
p0: 66 passed / 66 passed / 65 passed (+1 pre-existing flake skipped in round 3)
p1: 105 passed / 105 passed / 105 passed

# A-6 hardened assertion actually carrying information (round-3 p1 log):
[read_ai] get_last_ai_message: idx=0 why='fresh_after_send' count=26 \
  text='QwenPaw\nCompleted 1 steps\n\nThe first number you asked me to count to was 1.\n\n06:24:56'
answer_body='The first number you asked me to count to was 1.'

# Counterfactual replay of extract_answer_body() against real log strings:
#   genuine answers        5/5 pass   (no false red)
#   counterfactual text    3/3 fail
#   scaffold-only text     3/3 raise AssertionError
#   cancelled round        raises AssertionError
#   mismatches: 0
```

Three of the 13 cases (`test_session_rename_pin_delete_switch`, `test_agent_stats_page_load_and_cards`, `test_backup_page_load_and_display`) were fixed upstream by #8247 while this branch was in flight; during the rebase those hunks were resolved **in favour of upstream**, so this PR carries no competing changes for them.

## Additional Notes

**Out of scope, will be a separate PR.** Two cases are red on upstream `main` right now and are *not* touched here:

1. `tests/test_chat.py::TestToolApproval::test_approval_toggle_renders_and_switches` — `expected 4 approval levels, got 5`. #8283 added a fifth level, `JEV` ("decision model" mode). The fix is to assert 5, keep the level-by-level click loop at the 4 selectable levels, and add an explicit "JEV is visible but disabled" assertion. It is intentionally kept out of this PR because it would require editing `APPROVAL_LEVELS` in `chat_page.py`, which is the shared carrier of the other 12 cases — touching it would invalidate the 3-round verification reported above.
2. `tests/test_cronjobs.py::TestCronjobEditAndUpdate::test_cronjob_edit_and_update` — `Updated job not found`. Re-triaged: `5a1b52bd` (#8249/#8349) removed `useAutoSave` from `JobDrawer`, so editing now requires an explicit **Save** instead of saving on drawer close, while the test still only clicks Close. The older #7502 attribution cannot produce this signature (the failure frame carries `url='.../cron-jobs'`, i.e. no navigation ever happened).

Both are **test-side** issues; no product defect is claimed and no Aone ticket is warranted.

**Not touched here.** The cron-job 409 case (`tests/integration/test_provider_switching.py::test_persistent_5xx_eventually_fails`, Windows-only) is tracked separately.

**Note on `e2e-smoke`.** This PR touches `e2e/**`, so the smoke workflow will trigger. It selects `-m "ui_smoke"` only, and none of the files changed here carry that marker, so this PR's edits are not selected by it. That check is also documented in the workflow as not part of the required-check set.

**Base drift.** This branch is rebased onto `ce748971` (which includes the large console refactor #8332) and is `ahead 11 / behind 0` at the time of writing. The verification above was run on a head that already contains #8332.

prs.title: fix(desktop): let desktop.log rotate by sharing one file handle
prs.body:
## Description

The Tauri sidecar opened `~/.qwenpaw/desktop.log` **twice**:

1. `install_sidecar_logging` kept a raw `open("a")` handle for the whole process lifetime (stdout/stderr tee + `faulthandler`);
2. `add_project_file_handler` attached a `_SafeRotatingFileHandler` (5 MiB × 3) to the same path.

Consequences:

- **Windows**: the long-lived handle makes `os.rename` in `doRollover()` raise `PermissionError`. `_SafeRotatingFileHandler` swallows it and reopens the same file, so rotation never happens and the log grows without bound (the reporter has a 230 MB `desktop.log`).
- **macOS / Linux**: the rename succeeds, but the raw handle keeps writing to the renamed — and eventually deleted — file. Teed stdout/stderr and native crash traces after the first rotation are **silently lost**. Reproduced on the unmodified source: after rotation, a marker printed to stdout appears in none of `desktop.log{,.1,.2}`.

Fix:

- Teed stdio now writes through the rotating handler's own stream (under the handler lock, with a size-based rollover check), so only **one** handle on `desktop.log` exists and rotation works on every platform. Write failures (incl. unencodable text) never break stdio.
- `faulthandler` holds its fd for the whole process lifetime, so it cannot share the rotating `desktop.log` (rotation would leave it pointing at a closed/reused fd). Native crash traces now go to a separate `desktop-crash.log` that uses the **same rotation policy** as the other logs (size limit, backup count, `.N` naming, `QWENPAW_LOG_MAX_SIZE` / `QWENPAW_LOG_MAX_BACKUPS`), but is only checked at startup. The rotating handler is closed right after writing the startup header, and faulthandler gets a raw `os.open()` descriptor instead: `uvicorn.Config` runs `logging.config.dictConfig`, which closes *every* logging handler ever created (attached or not), so a handler-owned stream would be closed under faulthandler. Its path is logged at startup.
- Small refactor in `utils/logging.py`: `create_rotating_file_handler()` is extracted from `add_project_file_handler()` and reused for the crash log; `add_project_file_handler` now returns the handler it created/reused (previously `None`; existing callers ignore the return value).

Why not the alternatives for crash traces:
- *Write them into `desktop.log` and re-point faulthandler after each rollover*: faulthandler caches the fd number, so between close and re-registration a crash could be written into whatever file/socket reused that fd; traces would also age out with ~20 MiB of regular logs.
- *Write them to the sidecar's stderr (captured by Tauri)*: the Tauri log uses tauri-plugin-log defaults (40 KB, `KeepOne` = delete on overflow), and all Python log lines flow through stderr too, so traces would be wiped quickly.

Existing oversized logs need no migration: the first write after upgrade rolls the big file to `desktop.log.1`, and it ages out with later rotations.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8115

**Security Considerations:** None.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Checklist

- [ ] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [ ] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [ ] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [ ] Ready for review

## Testing

New tests in `tests/unit/tauri/test_sidecar_logging.py`:

- rotation happens with teed output, file size stays bounded, and output after rotation lands in the fresh `desktop.log` (not the renamed backup) — this fails on the old code;
- unencodable text is replaced instead of raising;
- an oversized crash log is rotated to `desktop-crash.log.1` at startup and faulthandler receives a descriptor for the fresh file;
- a subprocess test that follows the real desktop startup order (`install_sidecar_logging` → `uvicorn.Config` → native segfault) asserts the crash trace is written to `desktop-crash.log` and that `desktop.log` still receives both logging records and teed stdout after uvicorn's `dictConfig`. This test fails on the previous revision of this PR (crash log only contained the startup header).

Also verified end to end with a real segfault (`faulthandler._sigsegv()`): a pre-existing 6 MB crash log was rotated to `.1` and the new `desktop-crash.log` contains the startup header followed by the `Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault` trace.

Still needs a manual smoke test on **Windows** Desktop to confirm the rollover rename now succeeds there.

## Evidence

```bash
pytest -q tests/unit/tauri tests/unit/utils/test_logging.py tests/unit/app/test_provider_startup_offload.py
# 106 passed in 11.63s
```

Lint on changed files: `black --line-length=79 --check` clean, `flake8` clean, `mypy` no issues, `pylint` (repo hook disables) 10.00/10. Full `pre-commit run` could not complete locally because fetching the actionlint hook environment failed (HTTP 502).

## Additional Notes

Follow-up (out of scope here): `uvicorn.Config`'s `dictConfig` also closes the `desktop.log` handler created before it. Logging keeps working only because `FileHandler.emit` (and `_HandlerStream.write`) lazily reopen a closed stream — standard-library behaviour that predates this PR and is now covered by the subprocess test. Avoiding the reset altogether would mean passing uvicorn a custom `log_config` (or `None` and configuring its loggers ourselves), which changes access-log formatting/routing and deserves its own issue.


Native crash traces move from `desktop.log` to `desktop-crash.log`; troubleshooting docs that point to `desktop.log` for crash stacks should mention the new file.

prs.title: feat(deploy): add offline image variant with Office/PDF toolchain
prs.body:
## Description

Adds `deploy/Dockerfile.offline`, a variant of `deploy/Dockerfile` that bakes the
Office/PDF toolchain into the image, plus a short section in `scripts/README.md`
explaining how to build it.

The default image intentionally stays lean: the `docx`, `pptx`, `xlsx`, and `pdf`
skills resolve their prerequisites at task time (`apt-get`/`npm`/`pip`), which
fails in air-gapped or offline deployments and is slow for document-heavy
workloads. This variant preinstalls:

- **System:** `libreoffice-{writer,calc,impress,draw}`, `pandoc`, `poppler-utils`,
  `qpdf`, `tesseract-ocr` (+ `eng`, `chi-sim`, `chi-tra` traineddata)
- **npm (global):** `docx`, `pptxgenjs`, `pdf-lib`, `pdfjs-dist`, `react-icons`,
  `react`, `react-dom`, `sharp`, with `NODE_PATH=/usr/local/lib/node_modules`
- **Python (venv):** `pypdf`, `pdfplumber`, `reportlab`, `openpyxl`, `xlrd`,
  `pandas`, `python-docx`, `python-pptx`, `markitdown[docx,pptx,xlsx,xls,pdf]`,
  `pdf2image`, `pytesseract`, `lxml`, `defusedxml`

The Python libraries are installed **before** the app so that the app's own pins
win in the final resolve (`markitdown`'s `magika` pulls `onnxruntime`, and the app
pins `onnxruntime<1.24`). The `uv` binary is therefore copied earlier in the
offline file than in the default one.

`scripts/docker_build.sh` already honours the `DOCKERFILE` env var, so no script
change was needed:

```bash
DOCKERFILE=deploy/Dockerfile.offline bash scripts/docker_build.sh qwenpaw:offline
```

Trade-off: the image grows by roughly 2 GB and duplicates the shared parts of
`deploy/Dockerfile`. The alternative — an opt-in build arg in the default
`Dockerfile` — was avoided so the default image and its build cache are
unaffected. If the duplication becomes a maintenance burden, collapsing to a
build arg is the natural follow-up.

**Related Issue:** N/A

**Security Considerations:** None. No new ports, credentials, or network
services; the added `tesseract`/`pandoc`/`libreoffice` packages are invoked
headless by the existing skills.

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD

## Checklist

- [ ] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [ ] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [x] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [ ] Ready for review

## Testing

Not yet executed end-to-end — this is a draft to get direction on the approach
(separate Dockerfile vs. build arg) before spending a full multi-GB image build.

Verification done:

```bash

# libraries land in the venv before the app is installed).
$ diff deploy/Dockerfile deploy/Dockerfile.offline | grep -c '^<'
2      # both are the relocated uv COPY lines

prs.title: fix(providers): honor OpenAI-compatible input limits and cap Qwen catalogs
prs.body:
## Description

OpenAI-compatible model discovery reads total context metadata but ignores a separately reported `max_input_tokens`. This can overstate the usable input budget. Read the explicit input limit as API capability metadata so existing resolution caps discovered windows and user context overrides. Reject invalid input-limit values and retain existing behavior when no input limit is reported.

Several Qwen models also have a 1,000,000-token context window but accept at most 983,616 input tokens in thinking mode. Add that conservative `input_token_limit` to documented Qwen entries in DashScope and domestic/international Coding Plan and Token Plan catalogs:

- qwen3.8-max and the DashScope qwen3.8-max-0902 snapshot
- qwen3.8-flash
- qwen3.7-max, qwen3.7-plus, qwen3.7-flash
- qwen3.6-plus, qwen3.6-flash
- qwen3.5-plus

Mark limit provenance as documentation so remote metadata refreshes preserve it. Regenerate the catalog index and checksums. Smaller overrides remain effective. Both thinking and non-thinking modes use the conservative catalog cap; no new user settings are introduced.

Each modified model card links its official specification, e.g. https://help.aliyun.com/zh/model-studio/qwen3-7-plus and https://help.aliyun.com/zh/model-studio/qwen3-8-max. Other vendors' catalog limits are unchanged: OpenAI compatibility alone does not establish an independent input cap.

prs.title: fix(agents): retry without video when providers reject video input
prs.body:
Fixes #8298

## Description

A video returned by `send_file_to_user` can remain in conversation history and be included in later requests. If the provider rejects the video content part, even a subsequent text-only turn fails with the same error. For example, DeepSeek returns HTTP 422 with `unknown variant video_url`.

Add a video-specific recovery path alongside the existing audio fallback. When the failed wire request contains video and the error identifies a video rejection, remove video from the request copy and retry once. Preserve images, audio, and stored conversation history.

## Changes

- Recognize rejected `video_url` / `input_video` parts, unsupported video input, and `At most N videos` limits. Require video in the actual wire request before attempting recovery.
- Keep the existing media-free retry for errors that also identify other media types, such as `This model does not support video or image input`. Schema errors listing accepted alternatives still use the video-specific retry.
- Filter video from message content and tool-result output before reading or encoding media, and track video parts in the formatted request.
- After a successful retry for an unsupported video capability or a zero-video limit, cache `rejects_video` for the provider/model using the existing 30-minute TTL. Subsequent requests omit video while that entry remains valid.
- Treat positive video-count limits as request-specific: retry without video without caching a capability rejection. Failed retries do not create a cache entry.
- Apply cached audio and video filtering together and clear temporary formatter flags after success or failure.

## Validation

- **187 tests passed** across the suites touched by this change (agent media/audio recovery, request normalization, formatter normalization, video capping, capability cache) — exact command in Evidence below.
- Regression coverage uses real `send_file_to_user` output and formatter processing with the OpenAI SDK against a mocked HTTP transport. It covers schema and zero-limit rejections, positive limits, mixed image/video and audio/video rejections, failed retries, history preservation, image/audio preservation, cache expiry and model isolation, and formatter flag cleanup.
- Formatter coverage includes OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic and Gemini. The change itself is formatter-agnostic: video is removed in the request normalizer, before any formatter runs.
- Tests are kept in existing test files. `pre-commit` checks and `git diff --check` pass.

## Evidence

Reproduction of the failure this fixes (a real WeChat session):

- stored block: `context[26].content[65].output[0].source =`
  `{"type":"url","url":"file:///D:/ProjectBlenderAgent/out/turntable.mp4",`
  `"media_type":"video/mp4"}`
- request dump: 20,461,343 bytes; provider reply
  `422 … messages[443]: unknown variant 'video_url', expected one of`
  `'text', 'image_url', 'file'`
- every later turn, text-only included, failed identically until that stored
  block was replaced with a text placeholder.

Tests, run on this branch (`PYTHONPATH=<worktree>/src`, Windows host):

```
$ pytest tests/unit/agents/test_react_agent_media_strip.py \
    tests/unit/agents/test_message_request_normalizer.py \
    tests/unit/agents/test_model_factory_message_normalization.py \
    tests/unit/agents/test_model_factory_video_capping.py \
    tests/unit/providers/test_model_capability_cache.py -q
187 passed in 3.90s
```

```
$ pytest tests/unit/agents -q
4 failed, 3983 passed, 18 skipped in 64.78s
```

The 4 failures are the pre-existing `test_offloader.py` retention tests: they
fail identically on a clean `origin/main` worktree on this machine
(file-mtime behavior) and are unrelated to this change.

The recovery tests drive the real `send_file_to_user` tool output through the
formatter and the OpenAI SDK with a mocked HTTP transport (`httpx.MockTransport`),
so they exercise the wire payload without network access. They assert, among
other things, that:

- after a video rejection the retry succeeds and the **next** turn sends no
  video part (`test_video_rejection_recovers_and_next_turn_skips_video`);
- a mixed image+video rejection still falls back to the existing media-free
  retry (`test_mixed_media_rejection_uses_media_free_retry`);
- a positive "at most N videos" limit is not learned as a capability loss
  (`test_positive_video_limit_does_not_disable_next_valid_input`);
- a failed retry neither caches a rejection nor mutates stored history
  (`test_failed_video_retry_does_not_learn_or_mutate_history`);
- a video-shaped error on a request that carried no video is not retried as a
  video problem (`test_schema_error_without_wire_video_does_not_retry`);
- learned audio/video flags are cleared by an unrelated failure
  (`test_cached_audio_and_video_flags_clear_after_unrelated_failure`).

prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #8372.

Raise the Hub model gateway default timeout from 120 to 600 seconds and expose **Gateway timeout (seconds)** beside the default model in Hub settings. Reuse the existing administrator-only, revision-checked model policy to validate and persist a whole number of at least 60 seconds.

New requests use the saved value for HTTP I/O and streaming/non-streaming response handling without restarting Hub. Each in-flight request retains its original timeout. Dispatch atomically persists a conservative recovery deadline in the existing Hub settings table; lowering the policy cannot shorten recovery protection, including across repeated restarts. Normal settlement clears the deadline when no requests remain dispatched. Reuse existing UI controls, contextual help, theme tokens, and responsive layout.

Upstream HTTP errors now retain their status and sanitized message/type/code, with a Hub request ID. Both SDK error fields and the existing console detail contract receive the same diagnostics. Streaming and HTTP-200 in-band errors are inspected before protocol translation; transport failures get readable messages and timeouts return 504. Error reads are bounded, and the actual provider key plus credential patterns are redacted.

prs.title: chore(deps): replace GPL-licensed html2text with stdlib converter
prs.body:
## Description Remove the `html2text` dependency. `html2text` is licensed under **GPL-3.0**, which is incompatible with QwenPaw's Apache-2.0 license. It was only used in one place: `web_fetch` (`src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/web_search.py`) to convert fetched HTML into Markdown. This PR replaces it with a small stdlib (`html.parser`) based converter in `src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/_html_to_markdown.py` — **no new dependency is added**. The converter mirrors the previous html2text configuration (links kept, images dropped, no line wrapping) and handles headings, paragraphs, bold/italic/strikethrough, inline code and fenced `
` blocks (whitespace preserved, also inside blockquotes), nested ordered/unordered lists, blockquotes, simple tables, `
`/`
` and HTML entities. The `` prepending logic in `_html_to_text` is unchanged.

Design notes:
- Only `script`, `style`, `title` and `iframe` are dropped with their content. `HTMLParser`, like browsers, reads these as raw text, so nothing nests inside them and an unclosed `template`/`svg`/`select`/`noscript` or a missing `</head>` can never hide the rest of the page. Like html2text, the text of those other elements is kept (`select` options go on separate lines).
- Line breaks are written lazily: block elements only *request* breaks, which are flushed before the next text. Empty elements therefore leave no blank lines, empty list items (e.g. icon-only footer links) vanish with contiguous ordered numbering, `<li><p>…</p></li>` stays on the marker line, and no global whitespace tidy pass is needed (so `<pre>` content is never touched).
- Links, emphasis and blockquotes are captured and wrapped on close: emphasis markers hug the text (`A<b> bold </b>text` → `A **bold** text`; italics use `*` so they also work right after a word), inline code containing a backtick uses a double-backtick fence, card-style links wrapping headings/paragraphs are flattened into a single-line link, code blocks are never wrapped in links/emphasis, and mis-nested tags are closed together.
- `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `data:` and `#...` links are rendered as plain text (case-insensitive, leading whitespace ignored). Parentheses and spaces in link destinations are escaped so the full target survives.
- Code fences (fenced `<pre>` blocks and inline code) are longer than any backtick run in the code, so Markdown examples inside `<pre>` stay intact.
- Paragraphs inside table cells stay on their row, and cells are closed implicitly at the next cell/row/table end (`</td>`/`</th>` are optional in HTML); `<ol start>` is honored.

Known differences from html2text (acceptable for `web_fetch`, whose goal is readable page content for the model):
- Tables are rendered as `| A | B |` rows without the `| --- |` separator row (not strict GFM).
- Complex structures (nested tables, definition lists) degrade to plain text.

Also removes the now-unneeded `html2text` stub module in `tests/unit/agents/test_tool_result_pruning_middleware.py`.

**Related Issue:** N/A

**Security Considerations:** N/A — pure text transformation, no network/config changes.

## Description

- Add provider-configurable Realtime Voice chats with speech input, playback, interruption, and model selection in the existing Chat UI.

Two-layer split — provider-neutral vendor layer vs. application orchestration:

- `providers/realtime_voice/` — vendor-neutral contracts (`RealtimeProviderSession`, `ProviderEvent`, `RealtimeSessionConfig`) plus the DashScope adapter. No application dependencies.
- `app/realtime_voice/` — orchestration: `VoiceCoordinator`, `VoiceTaskBridge`, `SpokenTurnCommitter`, `PresentationQueue`. Pure prompt building lives in `prompts.py`; user-facing text and ordinals in `labels.py`.
- `app/routers/realtime_voice.py` — HTTP/WS boundary only, no business logic.

| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |

- The E2E verifier passed, and all nine changed source/test files matched their pre-E2E hashes. Test instrumentation stayed outside the repository and was disabled/closed afterward.

Playback was muted and input was synthesized, so this is not a physical-microphone acceptance result. prs.title: fix(console): scope chat input drafts to the conversation
prs.body:
## Description

The Console composer saved unsent text under one localStorage key per agent (`qwenpaw_chat_input_draft_<agentId>`), so a draft typed in one conversation came back in every other conversation of the same agent.

This PR keys the draft by agent **and** session:

- A conversation with a session id stores its draft under its own key. It never reads the old per-agent key, so a stale legacy value can't resurface in a session.
- A chat that has no session id yet gets its own pre-creation slot (`..._pending_<composerId>`, id kept in sessionStorage) instead of one shared `__pending` slot per agent. Opening **New Chat** (from the sidebar or from another page) starts a fresh slot, so two brand-new chats don't see each other's text.
- When the first message allocates a session, only the active pre-creation draft is handed to the new `/chat/<id>` route.
- Sending clears only the current conversation's draft. Leaving the chat page and coming back still restores the draft (the #4774 behaviour).

The cases from the reporter's comment on the issue are covered by tests, all with the same agent: A to B shows B's draft; A to another page and back restores A; two new chats don't share text; send clears only the sent conversation; drafts don't leak across agents. A desktop-style `/console/chat/<id>` path is covered as well.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8351

**Security Considerations:** None. Frontend-only change to localStorage/sessionStorage keys; no new data is stored.

prs.title: fix(providers): honor thinking defaults and declared wire controls
prs.body:
## Description

Fix a mismatch between the thinking setting displayed by the Console and the parameters sent by OpenAI-compatible providers.

For a custom Chat Completions model declaring native effort control (`low`, `medium`, `xhigh`, supports off), saving the model default as off (`thinking_enabled=false`) currently has two effects:

1. An inherited request omits the default altogether, although the Console displays off.
2. An explicit off preference is incorrectly routed to compatibility flags because `_uses_compat_thinking_controls()` treats the presence of `thinking_enabled` as a protocol declaration. Changing a default must not change the wire protocol.

An explicit session preference also leaves stale `extra_body.chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking/reasoning_effort` values behind. A serving engine such as vLLM can give these template arguments precedence over the new request setting.

### Changes

- Apply the existing model-default hook before agent/session preferences.
- Serialize configured OpenAI model defaults through the same declared-control mapper used by explicit preferences.
- Share model-default interpretation between the display and provider construction paths; include configured budgets and nested chat-template settings.
- Honor an explicit model/provider wire declaration before the legacy compatibility fallback.
- Replace conflicting nested template controls when applying a higher-priority preference, preserving unrelated JSON and the original provider/model state.
- Add SDK-boundary regression tests for native and compatibility protocols, inherited defaults, reset/reload, and request isolation.

No model-name matching, global default change, frontend change, or database migration is introduced. Unsupported effort labels are not silently renamed.

**Related Issue:** No matching backend issue identified.

**Security Considerations:** Settings are resolved into request-local dictionaries. Tests verify that shared provider/model configuration is unchanged.

prs.title: feat(agents): stop replaying media the model no longer needs
prs.body:
## Description

Every request re-uploaded every image and video block stored in history. A screenshot-heavy WeChat session reached a **48.9 MB** request body; the endpoint rejected it with

```
openai.APIStatusError: Failed to buffer the request body: length limit exceeded
```

and because the block lives in `agent.state.context`, every later turn failed the same way — the session stayed wedged until the file was edited by hand.

### Why the existing guards miss it

- `CappingFormatterMixin` caps **each block** at 2 MB. All 43 blocks in that session were below the cap, so nothing tripped.
- Context compaction triggers on **tokens** (`trigger_ratio * context_size`), and image tokens are cheap while their bytes are not — the log showed `outcome=at_or_below_trigger` at a 48 MB body.
- Prompt caching does not help either: a cache hit lowers the *price* of replaying the prefix (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash bills cached tokens at ~10% of input), but it **never removes the upload**.

### What this changes

Two rules, applied **only to the per-request copy** (stored history and channel delivery are untouched — `_normalize_messages_for_formatter` already deep-copies):

1. **Delivery is not context.** Media returned by `send_file_to_user` is never model input: the channel ships the file, so the model gets a reference instead of the bytes.
2. **Consumed media is not re-sent.** Media belonging to a completed turn (an assistant message with text and no tool calls, followed by something newer) has already been turned into text by the model, so it becomes a reference:

```
[image not re-sent to the model: slide_v_zh_00002_.png (image/png, 0.74 MB)
 at D:\...\slide_v_zh_00002_.png — call view_image again if another look is needed]
```

Only the **current turn's** media stays inline. That keeps the newest message working, including a top-level `view_audio` / `view_image` data block stored in an assistant message. A second look now costs one tool call instead of re-uploading megabytes on every turn.

Properties worth noting:

- **Deterministic** for a given history, and the boundary only moves forward, so prefix-cache churn is confined to the turn boundary rather than rewriting the conversation each request.
- Runs **before** `_prepare_media_sources`, so elided media is never read from disk or base64-encoded.
- **Kill switch:** `QWENPAW_DISABLE_MEDIA_ELISION=1`; extra delivery tools via `QWENPAW_DELIVERY_ONLY_TOOL_RESULTS=a,b`.

## Evidence

- Session in the report: 43 media blocks, 35.4 MB decoded (`view_image` 24 / 17.39 MB, `send_file_to_user` 14 / 11.50 MB, `desktop_screenshot` 5 / 6.51 MB); request dump 48.9 MB.
- With these rules only the current turn's media is inlined (typically 0–3 blocks); everything older becomes a one-line reference. Delivery is unaffected because channels render the tool-result block, not the formatter output.
- `pytest tests/unit/agents/test_media_turn_scoped_elision.py` → 11 passed (including a test that the stored `Msg` list is not mutated, and one that a current-turn `view_audio` block stays inline).
- `pytest tests/unit/{agents,channels,app}` → 9065 passed, 22 skipped, 4 failed. The 4 are the pre-existing `test_offloader.py` retention failures (they fail on a clean `origin/main` worktree on this Windows host as well).
- `black --line-length=79`, `flake8`, `mypy` (0 errors) and `pylint` (10.00/10) clean on the changed files.

## Not in this PR (deliberate)

- **No aggregate byte budget.** One turn that views many large images can still exceed an endpoint limit; that case would still need a manual session repair. A byte budget (and a retry on `length limit exceeded` / 413) is the natural follow-up, but it adds config surface and is better discussed separately.
- **No storage-side change.** Media still lives in the session as base64; this PR only stops replaying it. Storing `{path, sha256, dims}` instead is the longer-term direction (see #8335).

## Related

- **#8335** — design discussion: 48 MB bodies, permanent wedges, the two cost bills
  (tokens vs bytes), and the roadmap for media-by-reference.
- This PR implements the **S1 + S2** slice of that design. The aggregate byte
  budget and the oversized-body retry described there are intentionally left
  out, so **#8335 should stay open** to track them.

> Note for reviewers: this PR is intentionally *not* a closing reference. GitHub
> only auto-links an issue when the body says `Fixes #n` / `Closes #n`; this one
> is a partial implementation, so link it manually from the sidebar ("Link an
> issue") if a sidebar link is preferred.
