prs.title: fix(channels/telegram): withdraw the ack reaction when a reply finishes
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:** `TelegramChannel` adds an acknowledgement reaction when an update arrives (`try_add_ack_reaction_nonblocking`), but it never overrode the `Channel::remove_reaction` hook, so the trait's default no-op ran when the orchestrator withdrew the ack. The bot's ack emoji therefore stayed on the user's message forever. This PR implements `remove_reaction` for Telegram so the ack is cleared when the reply finishes.
- **Scope boundary:** Only `crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/telegram.rs`. The ack-add task now tracks in-flight acknowledgements and can perform a deferred clear. The orchestrator call sites, the `Channel` trait defaults, `TELEGRAM_ACK_REACTIONS`, and every other channel are unchanged. `add_reaction` is deliberately left as the trait no-op (see below).
- **Blast radius:** Telegram only. Because `remove_reaction` now really sends `setMessageReaction`, the `reaction` tool's `remove` action also starts working on Telegram (it was a silent no-op before), and the ack path gains one outbound API call per finished reply. No other channel or subsystem is affected.
- **Linked issue(s):** None. A bug fix is ordinary work under the RFC rules (`docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md`: "a new channel, a new provider, a new tool, and a bug fix are all ordinary work") and does not cross an RFC trigger, so no issue or RFC was filed.

### What this does, simply

When a message arrives, the Telegram channel drops an "I saw this" reaction (👀 or a random pick from `TELEGRAM_ACK_REACTIONS`) on the user's own message. When the reply is finished, the orchestrator asks the channel to withdraw that reaction and then add a done reaction (✅ on success, ⚠️ on error). On Telegram both of those calls fell through to the `Channel` trait's default no-op, so the ack emoji never went away — the user's message kept the bot's reaction permanently.

This PR implements `remove_reaction` for Telegram. A Telegram bot has a single reaction slot per message, so withdrawing means sending `setMessageReaction` with an empty `reaction` list; the method ignores the `emoji` argument because the slot is cleared by position, not by emoji (which also means it clears whichever emoji the ack path happened to pick). A message id that is not in the `telegram_{chat_id}_{message_id}` shape is treated as "nothing to withdraw" and returns `Ok(())` without a network call.

`add_reaction` is intentionally **not** implemented. The generic acknowledgement callers pass 👀 (which Telegram's own ack path already set) or ✅/⚠️, and the latter two are not in Telegram's allowed reaction set, so a real implementation would either overwrite the emoji the channel already chose or silently drop the done emoji. Leaving it a no-op keeps the existing visible behavior and keeps this a minimal bug fix. This is why the ack emoji is withdrawn rather than swapped for a done emoji on Telegram. Explicit additions through the reaction tool also remain a no-op.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes` — the fix is user-visible in a real Telegram chat and there is no CI substitute for the live client.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel: telegram` (no `web` / `tui` / `cli` surface; this is a messaging-channel integration).
- **Setup / preconditions:** A Telegram bot token wired to a `telegram` channel alias, and an account allowed to talk to that bot.
- **Steps to run:** On `master` and on this branch, send the bot a message that produces a short reply and watch the reaction on your own message.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The ack reaction appears when the bot starts working, then disappears once the reply is delivered.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The ack reaction stays on your message indefinitely.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Rust Quality Gate` (`cargo fmt` + workspace clippy + provider dispatch gate) and the `zeroclaw-channels` unit tests cover the changed surface. I also ran the workspace clippy locally with `-D warnings`, which is stricter than the gate's default `-D clippy::correctness`.
- **Current regression coverage and remaining gap:** The current head includes mock-server tests for the outgoing clear request, delayed acknowledgement ordering, bounded cleanup waits, deferred clearing after a wait timeout, and failed cleanup. Live Telegram client behavior has not been verified. The local command results below remain evidence for the originally tested revision.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean (no output), exit 0.

  `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets -- -D warnings` — exit 0:
  ```
      Checking zeroclaw-channels v0.8.5 (/app/crates/zeroclaw-channels)
      Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 3m 41s
  ```

  `./scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh` — exit 0:
  ```
  ==> rust quality: cargo fmt --all -- --check
  ==> rust quality: cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets -- -D clippy::correctness
      Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 2m 44s
  ==> rust quality: provider dispatch gate (no direct ModelProvider method calls outside ProviderDispatch)
  ==> rust quality: provider dispatch gate clean
  ```

  `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- telegram_clear_reaction_request_shape parse_telegram_message_id remove_reaction_skips_unparseable_message_id` — exit 0:
  ```
  running 4 tests
  test telegram::tests::parse_telegram_message_id_rejects_unrecognised_ids ... ok
  test telegram::tests::parse_telegram_message_id_reads_the_numeric_suffix ... ok
  test telegram::tests::telegram_clear_reaction_request_shape ... ok
  test telegram::tests::remove_reaction_skips_unparseable_message_id ... ok

  test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1974 filtered out; finished in 0.00s
  ```

  `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib telegram::` — exit 0:
  ```
  test result: ok. 375 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 1601 filtered out; finished in 8.23s
  ```

  `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib` — one failure, unrelated and pre-existing:
  ```
  ---- tts::tests::edge_tts_removes_temp_output_when_read_fails stdout ----
  thread 'tts::tests::edge_tts_removes_temp_output_when_read_fails' (9885) panicked at crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/tts.rs:2132:14:
  called `Result::unwrap_err()` on an `Ok` value: []

  test result: FAILED. 1975 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 12.54s
  ```
  I confirmed this failure is not caused by this change: with the change stashed, the same test fails on unmodified `master` (`test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; ... 1973 filtered out`). It is an Edge TTS temp-file test unrelated to reactions.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I verified the id parser against the exact shapes the channel produces (`telegram_-100200300_42`, `telegram_1234_7`) and against ids it never produces (`telegram_1234`, `slack_1234_42`, `telegram_1234_abc`), and that an unparseable id returns before any HTTP call. I did **not** verify against a live Telegram bot; the live behavior is left to the reviewer recipe above.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` — the only user-visible surface is the Telegram client's rendering of the bot's reaction, which cannot be captured from this repository or CI without a live bot. The change is verified at the API-request boundary instead (request body + id parsing unit tests).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** commit `d35b943599b70224f2fa88f87a86d2b260938a90`, `channel: telegram`; evidence is the local `cargo`/`scripts/ci` output pasted above (no screenshot path).
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** exact command output pasted under "Commands run and tail output" above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** When a reply finishes, the orchestrator calls `remove_reaction`; on this branch the channel now POSTs `setMessageReaction` with `{"chat_id": <chat>, "message_id": <id>, "reaction": []}`, clearing the bot's ack reaction. Unit tests assert that body shape and that unrecognised message ids are a no-op.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** I did not run the full-workspace `cargo test`; `docs/book/src/contributing/how-to.md` accepts focused crate tests as evidence for a change of this surface, and the changed crate's tests plus the workspace clippy gate cover it. Required CI runs the full suite.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (`No`)
- New external network calls? (`Yes`) — `remove_reaction` now issues one `setMessageReaction` request to the configured Telegram API base per finished reply, where it was previously a no-op. It reuses the existing channel HTTP client, proxy policy, and bot token, and adds no new host or endpoint.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (`No`)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (`No`) — tests use synthetic ids and a fake token.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (`No`)
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: The only `Yes` is the new outbound call. Risk is bounded to the channel the operator already configured: the request goes to the same Telegram bot API base and credentials the ack-add path already uses, carries only the chat id and message id already present in the inbound message, and is best-effort (the orchestrator ignores its result).

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? (`No`)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? (`No`)
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

This is ordinary behavioral work (`risk:medium`).

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert d35b943599b70224f2fa88f87a86d2b260938a90` and redeploy; the ack reaction simply stops being withdrawn again.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `channels.telegram.<alias>.ack_reactions = false` disables the Telegram ack path entirely (it stops the add as well), so no reaction is set and there is nothing to withdraw. There is no separate toggle for the withdrawal alone.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A Telegram API error on the clear surfaces as `Telegram setMessageReaction (clear) failed (<status>): <body>` from the `reaction` tool result; the ack path itself ignores the result, so the visible symptom of a regression would be reactions once again lingering on user messages. Grep the `reaction` tool output and the Telegram channel logs for `setMessageReaction`.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A — this PR does not supersede another PR.

---

**Labels** live in the GitHub label UI, not in the body. The PR path labeler owns path/scope labels from `.github/labeler.yml`, and the PR size labeler owns canonical `size:*` labels. Maintainers and reviewers with label permissions still set `risk:*` and any missing manual labels via the sidebar. Contributors without label permission can note obvious label mismatches in a comment. Canonical colon-scoped labels use no-space spelling; during migration, copy exact live label spelling from the GitHub UI.

**Do not add bot/AI attribution footers** such as `Co-authored-by: Claude ...`
or `Created with Claude Code` to the PR body or commit-message tail. Human
co-author trailers are appropriate only for incorporated contributor work under
the supersede-attribution section and privacy contract.

**Privacy contract** (`docs/book/src/contributing/privacy.md`) is a merge gate. Never commit real identities, secrets, personal emails, or PII in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs.

prs.title: fix(providers): project JPEG admission without copying the input
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `projected_allocation` now routes `image::ImageFormat::Jpeg` to a new
    `projected_jpeg_allocation`, which projects the decode peak from the SOF
    (`jpeg_frame_header`) on the borrowed `&[u8]`.
  - `image` 0.25.10's `JpegDecoder::new` copies the whole encoded input and
    walks retained metadata before `Limits` apply, so the previous admission
    path allocated in proportion to the input before the 64 MiB per-image cap
    or the aggregate budget could refuse the image.
  - PNG / GIF / WebP keep the existing `into_decoder()` header-only path.
- **Scope boundary:** Admission projection only. The decode path, both caps,
  and aggregate-budget accounting are unchanged. One-component grayscale JPEGs charge 1 B/px (L8); multi-component charge
  3 B/px. Decode-time input/metadata copies remain in the projection — see
  Compatibility. No config, CLI, or dependency change.
- **Blast radius:** Multimodal image admission (`validate_within_budget` /
  `projected_allocation`) for image attachments across providers; the
  projection also charges the shared aggregate decode budget.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11654

### What this does, simply

Before decoding an image, ZeroClaw estimates how much memory the decode will need so it can refuse one that would exceed the per-image or per-request caps. For JPEG that estimate used the decoder's own header parse, which copies the whole encoded file first, so an image that was about to be refused had already paid for a copy of itself. This change reads the JPEG frame header (SOF) straight from the bytes already in memory, so refusal precedes any allocation proportional to the encoded input.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — no interactive path; admission is
  covered by unit tests and CI.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI Required Gate` passes on `ad5a32e12`, including `Format`, `Lint`, `Check *`, `Test`, and `Test (Landlock)`. The change is confined to `zeroclaw-providers`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No allocator-wide assertion that admission
  avoids constructing `JpegDecoder` (optional Greptile P2). Evidence for the
  no-copy claim remains the borrowed-byte walk itself; APP0 desync is covered
  by a focused admission regression.
- **Commands run and results (revision `ad5a32e12`):**
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers --lib app0_length_six_cannot_hide` → ok
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers --lib grayscale_jpeg_near_cap` → ok
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Marker walk uses
  `zune_jpeg_segment_overread` (APP0 length-6); one-component frames charge
  1 B/px; `projected_jpeg_allocation` also charges decode-time
  `bytes.len() * 2` plus retained metadata so #11637 terms are not dropped.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` — no user-visible interface.
- **Tested revision:** `ad5a32e12ae007cc1d29f59c1131e10ca17d4ab0`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- Note: image bytes are untrusted input. The SOF walk is bounds-checked and
  models zune-jpeg's APP0 length-6 one-byte over-read; a fake SOF hidden behind
  that segment fails closed as `CorruptImage` before decode (regression:
  `app0_length_six_cannot_hide_a_larger_jpeg_frame_from_admission`). Other
  headers it cannot project are also refused before decode.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for ordinary admission outcomes. One-component
  grayscale JPEGs again charge 1 B/px (L8), matching the decoder path
  (`grayscale_jpeg_near_cap_keeps_one_byte_output_charge`). Decode-time
  input/metadata copies are still charged so totals stay conservative vs the
  real `JpegDecoder` peak.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- Exact upgrade steps for existing users: none.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR (or `git revert` the two commits on the branch).
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** New decode-memory refusals for JPEG
  attachments — `corrupt_image` / "decoded canvas … exceeds per-image limit"
  in provider logs for images previously accepted.

prs.title: fix(cron): prevent shell diagnostics from leaking to channels
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** A scheduled shell command (`cron` with `job_type = "shell"`) forwarded the raw `status/stdout/stderr` envelope to the delivery channel. A failing command — or a successful one that prints to stderr — could therefore leak command text, file paths, and stderr diagnostics to the end user. This closes that leak.
- **What changed and why (mechanics):** `run_job_command_with_runtime_and_timeout` now returns bare stdout on success (logging any stderr internally at WARN after a full-text `crate::security::scrub` followed by `sanitize_api_error`'s provider/URL sanitization and 500-byte bounding), and on failure returns the wrapped envelope only to a new `render_job_output` helper, which replaces it with a localized user-safe message and logs the sanitized failure. `execute_job_now_with_runtime` and `execute_and_persist_job` route their results through `render_job_output` inside the job attribution span, so both the channel and the persisted run history see only safe text. `cron run`'s tool-level policy rejection is likewise localized.
- **Scope boundary:** Shell jobs only. Agent jobs and non-shell outputs pass through unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** Cron shell job result rendering. No change to scheduling, retry, delivery routing, or command execution itself.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

A cron shell job that prints `internal-warning` to stderr and `public-output` to stdout now delivers only `public-output` to the channel; the stderr is recorded in the server log. A cron shell job that fails no longer sends its `status=`/`stdout:`/`stderr:` dump to the channel — the operator sees "The scheduled command failed. Check the server logs for details." while the sanitized details are logged server-side.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`; output-rendering change covered by unit tests and required CI.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required hosted CI covers the changed `zeroclaw-runtime` surface via `Test`, `Lint`, `Format`, and `Parallel Runtime Test`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The executor and emitted-attribute tests cover output rendering and credential scrubbing. No live channel delivery or separate failure-attribution capture evidence is supplied.

- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(no output; formatting clean)

$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 4m 42s
(no warnings)

$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib cron::
test result: ok. 228 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5224 filtered out

$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib cron_run
test result: ok. 20 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5432 filtered out

$ git diff --check
(no output)
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** `execute_job_now_hides_shell_failure_diagnostics` and `execute_job_now_shell_success_returns_only_stdout` drive the real `execute_job_now` entry point and assert the failure output is the localized message (with no `wecom-leak-repro`, `status=`, or `stderr:` substring) and the success output is exactly `public-output`. The emitted-attribute regression (`shell_success_logs_credential_scrubbed_stderr`) captures this job's `cron.shell.command_warning` by unique ID and error key, requires the `diagnostic` field, and asserts the `[REDACTED` marker is present while no leading 12-character slice of the secret survives — so the truncate-then-scrub order would fail it.
- **Visual interface changed?** Yes — cron shell failure/block messages are now localized; success output is bare stdout.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes. Shell diagnostics, including successful stderr that Raw mode previously discarded, now enter operator logs after full-text credential scrubbing, provider/URL sanitization, and bounding.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No — this *reduces* what untrusted command output can reach the channel

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No for shell result formatting. Successful `Wrapped` jobs now return bare stdout, failures in either mode return a localized message, and empty successful `Raw` output becomes a completion message. Agent-job output is unchanged.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No new fields or flags. `shell_output_format` remains accepted but no longer changes execution output; its documentation remains a follow-up.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

High-risk privacy change: revert the merged commit to restore the previous behavior, including its raw-diagnostic exposure.

- No disable toggle: removing the localization returns raw shell diagnostics to the channel, so revert rather than toggling.
- Watch for: raw diagnostics re-appearing in delivered cron results, or missing failure diagnostics in the server logs (the sanitized failure is logged at WARN).

prs.title: fix(zerocode): answer dropped elicitations and record them in the transcript
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A pending `ask_user` / `poll` prompt could be cleared on the client with no reply. The daemon then waited out the tool's own timeout (600 s for `ask_user`) while the user saw nothing. Every clear that isn't the user's answer now goes through `withdraw_pending_elicitation`. `Chat::answer_withdrawn_elicitations` (run each transport tick, after the resync drain) sends the `cancel` and notes it in the transcript.
  - A modal that outlives its turn is closed on `TurnComplete` and recorded as expired.
  - The `ask_user` / `poll` tool card now leads with `question:` and lists the choices. Before, the collapsed card showed the first 120 bytes of key-sorted input JSON, so `channel` and `choices` came first and the question was cut off. The card is the one record of the question.
  - The card's `result:` is the record of the outcome. For `ask_user` / `poll`, the pick (or the `DISMISSED` marker from #11815) is shown in the warn colour the old outcome line used. An outcome line (answered, dismissed, withdrawn, expired) is written only when no matching `ask_user` / `poll` card is on screen, such as an older history or a card that never arrived. In dogfooding, a line under the card repeated its `result:`.
- **Scope boundary:** Client only (`apps/zerocode`). No daemon or wire change. Overlay placement and the sidebar needs-input dot are unchanged; the dot already exists (`ChatState::sidebar_status`). Free-form `ask_user` on the Code tab is still unsupported.
- **Blast radius:** The ZeroCode Code and Chat panes' elicitation path, and how the `ask_user` / `poll` tool cards render. A dropped prompt now gets a `cancel` reply where before it got none. The daemon already handles `cancel` (`Ok(None)` → "user cancelled").
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11623. Related #11117 (durable human-question primitive; it scopes ACP elicitation out). Companion #11815 makes `ask_user` return a `DISMISSED` result rather than an error when the user presses Esc, so the card's `result:` reads as a dismissal.

### What this does, simply

When an agent asks you a multiple-choice question in ZeroCode, a box pops up with the options. If the pane reloaded while that box was up (which happens when the client falls behind the live stream) or you started a new session in place, the box disappeared and nobody told the agent. The agent sat waiting for up to ten minutes and then failed with a timeout. Nothing about the question stayed on screen either, so afterwards you couldn't tell what had been asked.

Now the agent is told "cancelled" right away whenever the box goes away without your answer. The `ask_user` tool card shows the question, its options and what happened. A separate note appears only if the card isn't on screen.

**Why the record is client-side.** The prompt asked whether the record belongs in the daemon so it survives reload. It already partly does: the daemon persists the `ask_user` tool call with its full input, and with this change that card shows the question and choices. So after a reload the question is still on screen. The card's `result:` carries the answer or the cancel, and it is persisted with the card. Making the outcome durable means a new daemon event and storage, which is the job of the #11117 durable-question primitive. I kept this PR to the client.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The failing path needs a notification-lag reload to land while a prompt is up, which is hard to trigger by hand. The regression test drives it directly.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui` (ZeroCode Code pane)

### How I tested

All through the remote wrapper (`scripts/zc-cargo`) on the build host.

- `zc-cargo test -p zerocode elicitation` → `test result: ok. 19 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1410 filtered out` (at the third commit)
- `zc-cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → `Finished `dev` profile`, no warnings
- `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check apps/zerocode/src/chat.rs` → clean
- Full `zc-cargo test -p zerocode` → `1426 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored` at the second and third commits (first commit: 1425/1). The one failure is `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` ("SIGINT was swallowed while the insecure-TLS prompt was blocked", `main.rs`). It fails the same way on unmodified `origin/master` 05f9fe95d4 on the same host (`0 passed; 1 failed; 1422 filtered out`), so it's environmental on that host, not this change.

**Mutation check, third commit.** `elicitation_question_choices_and_answer_are_recorded` now applies the card's result and asserts no outcome line; `elicitation_with_a_card_adds_no_outcome_line` (renamed from `elicitation_outcome_sits_under_its_card_inside_the_agent_turn`) asserts the entries stay `agent, tool:ask_user, tool:shell` after Esc and the browse cursor is untouched. Writing the line even when a card exists: `17 passed; 2 failed`, both tests. Restored → 19 passed.

prs.title: fix(android): restore the aarch64-linux-android build
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `zeroclaw-runtime` has not compiled for `aarch64-linux-android` since #10236 (f46e6736e5, 2026-09-16): `error[E0425]: cannot find value DESKTOP_READINESS_FRAME_MAX_BYTES` at `service/mod.rs:727`. The constant is gated to `linux`/`macos`/`windows`/`test`, but the desktop handshake helpers that read it (`desktop_handshake_frame`, `desktop_error_frame`, `emit_desktop_*`, `handle_desktop_preflight`, `desktop_log_path`, `desktop_config_dir`) were left ungated. On Android, `run_desktop_daemon` is the stub that bails, so those helpers are unreachable there. Each one now carries its callers' gate. Making the constant unconditional instead would only trade the error for dead code on Android.
  - Fixing the error lets rustc reach its dead-code pass on Android, which reports the rest of the same drift in `service/mod.rs`. The `Duration`/`Instant` and `resolve_runtime_dirs` imports now carry their users' gates, and `open_private_desktop_subdir` goes from `any(unix, windows)` to its callers' gate. `SERVICE_STOP_TIMEOUT` gets back the `linux`/`macos`/`all(test, unix)` gate that #10931 dropped. That last one also clears the `constant SERVICE_STOP_TIMEOUT is never used` warning that the Windows check job prints on master today.
  - The same Android build log carries dead-code warnings from two other crates. In `zeroclaw-tools` (`browser_open`), the launch timeout and launcher helpers are only called from the macOS, Linux and Windows branches plus unix tests. In `zeroclaw-config` (`platform/native`), `first_available` and the unix `shell_is_available` are unused because the Android default-shell path returns `/system/bin/sh` directly.
  - #10236 also broke Android *test* builds of `zeroclaw-runtime`. `use tokio::process::Child` is gated `any(linux, macos, all(test, not(unix)))`, but the unix child helpers that use it are gated `any(macos, linux, all(test, unix))`. So `cargo check --all-targets --target aarch64-linux-android` failed with `cannot find type Child` at 3 sites. The import now carries the union of its users' gates, `any(linux, macos, test)`.
  - Only `cfg` attributes change. Linux and macOS compile exactly the same items as before. Windows only stops compiling the unused `SERVICE_STOP_TIMEOUT`.
- **Scope boundary:** No behavior changes on any target. Nothing becomes reachable on Android that wasn't before: the desktop daemon runner still bails there, `browser_open` still reports "not supported on this OS", and the default shell is still `/system/bin/sh`. This PR does not:
  - touch the release or Cross-Platform Build workflows, or promote the experimental Android release leg.
  - fix the unrelated Windows-only warnings (`resolved_launcher`, `resolved_shell`, `manager_from_snapshot`).
- **Blast radius:** Compile-time only, in `zeroclaw-runtime` `service/mod.rs`, `zeroclaw-tools` `browser_open.rs`, and `zeroclaw-config` `platform/native.rs`. Other non-desktop targets (for example FreeBSD) hit the same E0425 and get the same fix, but I have not verified them.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11306 (its Cross-Platform Build evidence run 37408271392 surfaced the break). No tracking issue exists.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw ships an experimental Android binary with each release. A desktop-app change in mid-September added some helper code that only makes sense on Linux, macOS and Windows, but forgot to mark it that way. Android builds then failed to compile. Nobody noticed because no pull-request check builds Android: only the manual Cross-Platform Build and the release workflow do, and the release workflow lets the Android leg fail without blocking. The next release would have shipped without an Android download. This PR marks those helpers, and a few similar leftovers, as desktop-only so Android compiles again, with no warnings from workspace crates. It also fixes one import that kept Android test builds from compiling. Nothing changes for Linux, macOS or Windows users.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. No PR check builds Android, so dispatching the manual build is the only CI evidence for this change.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** None at runtime. This is a compile-time change to the `aarch64-linux-android` release target.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Push access to dispatch `workflow_dispatch` on `zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw`.
- **Steps to run:** Run **Cross-Platform Build** (`cross-platform-build-manual.yml`) on this branch, for example `gh workflow run cross-platform-build-manual.yml --ref fix/runtime-android-desktop-cfg`. Then open the `Build dist / aarch64-linux-android` job.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The Android job compiles `zeroclaw-runtime` and finishes the dist build, with no warnings from `zeroclaw-runtime`, `zeroclaw-tools` or `zeroclaw-config`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The same job fails with `error[E0425]: cannot find value DESKTOP_READINESS_FRAME_MAX_BYTES` at `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/service/mod.rs:727:29`, as in run 37408271392.

### How I tested

There is no Android NDK on the test machine, so I ran the Android and Windows checks with a check-only C compiler stand-in. A wrapper (`CC_<target>`) passes cc-rs compiler detection through to Homebrew clang and compiles every C/asm unit as an empty object for the target, and `llvm-ar` archives them. That is enough for C build scripts (`ring`, `libsqlite3-sys`) to finish. `cargo check` never links, so every Rust diagnostic below is real rustc output for the target. As a control, on unmodified master the stand-in reproduces the CI failure exactly: the same error, the same `Instant` warning, and the same five warnings in `zeroclaw-config` and `zeroclaw-tools` as run 37408271392.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required `Lint` (fmt, clippy `--workspace --all-targets --features ci-all -D warnings`, comment hygiene), `Test`, and the Linux/macOS/Windows `Check` rows. They cover the desktop targets, where every gated item still compiles.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** PR CI (`ci.yml`) builds no Android target. Its matrix is x86_64 Linux, aarch64 macOS and x86_64 Windows, plus an i686 Linux check. `aarch64-linux-android` is built only by the manual **Cross-Platform Build** (`cross-platform-build-manual.yml`, `workflow_dispatch` only) and by **Release Stable** (`release-stable-manual.yml`). There the Android leg is `experimental` with `continue-on-error`, and its asset is excluded from `required_assets`. That is how this break went unnoticed. No workflow compiles Android test targets either; the local all-targets check below covers them.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  Reproduction on master `e654b4b73f` (Android, stubbed C compilers, rustc 1.98.0). The three touched files are unchanged between that commit and `05f9fe95d4`, this branch's base, so the failure is the same on current master:
  ```text
  $ cargo +1.98.0 check -p zeroclaw-runtime --target aarch64-linux-android
  error[E0425]: cannot find value `DESKTOP_READINESS_FRAME_MAX_BYTES` in this scope
     --> crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/service/mod.rs:727:29
  warning: unused import: `Instant`
    --> crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/service/mod.rs:24:27
  error: could not compile `zeroclaw-runtime` (lib) due to 1 previous error; 1 warning emitted
  ```

  This branch, with the CI Android leg's profile, `--locked`, features and target, as `cargo check` rather than `cargo build` (`dist` features resolved by `xtask generate features --selection dist --target aarch64-linux-android`):
  ```text
  $ cargo +1.98.0 check --release --locked --no-default-features --features "acp-bridge,agent-runtime,channel-acp-server,channel-discord,channel-email,channel-filesystem,channel-git,channel-lark,channel-matrix,channel-telegram,channel-webhook,gateway,observability-prometheus,schema-export" --target aarch64-linux-android
      Checking zeroclaw-gateway v0.8.5
      Finished `release` profile [optimized] target(s) in 3m 18s
  # exit 0, 0 warnings, 0 errors; the root `zeroclaw` crate was re-checked in this run
  ```

  Android, all targets (unit tests, integration tests, examples) of the touched crates, A/B against master:
  ```text
  $ cargo +1.98.0 check --locked --all-targets -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-config --target aarch64-linux-android
  master:      error[E0425]: cannot find value `DESKTOP_READINESS_FRAME_MAX_BYTES` in this scope   (lib)
               error[E0425]: cannot find type `Child` in this scope   (x3, lib test)
               plus the 6 dead-code / unused-import warnings
  this branch: Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 40s   # exit 0, 0 warnings, 0 errors
  ```

  Windows, all targets of the touched crates (stubbed C compilers, rustc 1.97.1), A/B against master:
  ```text
  master:      warning: constant `SERVICE_STOP_TIMEOUT` is never used  (lib and lib test)
  this branch: (gone); the remaining Windows warnings are identical on both and in untouched code
  ```

  Host (aarch64-apple-darwin, rustc 1.98.0):
  ```text
  $ cargo +1.98.0 fmt --all -- --check                      # exit 0
  $ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                 # Comment hygiene gate passed.
  $ cargo +1.98.0 check -p zeroclaw-runtime                 # Finished, no warnings
  $ cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-config --all-targets -- -D warnings
      Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 56s
  $ cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib service::
  test result: ok. 99 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored; 0 measured; 5538 filtered out; finished in 0.18s
  $ cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib browser_open
  test result: ok. 26 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 2051 filtered out; finished in 0.03s
  $ cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-config --lib platform::native
  test result: ok. 37 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1734 filtered out; finished in 0.01s
  ```
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** For each newly gated item, I checked that its gate equals the union of its callers' gates (including test-only callers), and that Linux and macOS compile exactly the same item set as before. I did not run a real NDK build, link or run the Android binary, or check other non-desktop targets.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (no user-visible interface state changed)
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** All "this branch" results above are from the branch head on top of master `05f9fe95d4`. The "master" A/B runs used `e654b4b73f`, and none of the 8 commits between those two touch the three changed files. Evidence is the compiler output above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No real NDK or MSVC builds: neither toolchain is installed locally. The dispatch requested above covers the NDK build. I ran per-crate clippy for the touched crates instead of the full-workspace `ci-all` clippy, which the required `Lint` job runs.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: `git revert <sha>` is the plan.

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`. Reverting restores the Android compile error but changes nothing on Linux, macOS or Windows.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A gate that is too narrow fails compilation on the affected target (`cannot find value` or `cannot find function` in `service/mod.rs`, `browser_open.rs` or `platform/native.rs`). A gate that is too wide shows up as `never used` warnings on that target. There are no runtime symptoms.

prs.title: fix(channels): classify telegram transcription failures and bound transient retries
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Every error from `manager.transcribe` in the Telegram voice path became `UpdateDisposition::RetryTransient`, so a terminally rejected voice update pinned the long-poll offset and head-of-line blocked every later message until an operator intervened (#10863; production incident reported in #10640, where an ASR endpoint's persistent HTTP 413 wedged the channel for ~8 minutes and survived restarts).
  - Transcription providers now classify failures: substantiated payload-specific terminal rejections (HTTP 413/415, plus local pre-flight byte-cap and format rejections) are `Permanent`; credential (401/403), rate-limit, 5xx, transport, and unrecognised failures stay `Transient` — the same conservative philosophy as the `getFile` classifier (#9314/#9315): retrying a recoverable failure is safe, skipping a recoverable one loses a message.
  - The Telegram voice parser acknowledges terminal rejections with a new sender notice (`VoiceDropReason::TranscriptionRejected`, Fluent key added in en/es/fr/ja/zh-CN) instead of retrying forever — the same contract as the existing duration and file-lookup drops.
  - A bounded transient budget (10 consecutive attempts per update) acknowledges a persistently failing update with a loud ERROR (update id + attempt count) instead of retrying it forever, so failures that can never be classified as permanent but never recover either (e.g. an endpoint returning 500 for one corrupted file) cannot wedge the channel indefinitely. Giving up is explicit and observable, never silent.
- Deepgram, AssemblyAI (upload step), and Google STT now check `!status.is_success()` before JSON deserialization, so a proxy/gateway 413/415 with a plain-text or HTML body classifies as `Permanent` instead of falling into an untyped JSON-parse failure (misread as retryable `Transient`). Error bodies are read as text, extracting the vendor JSON message when present. AssemblyAI `create`/`poll` carry no audio bytes, so their non-success statuses stay explicitly `Transient` instead of masquerading as a payload rejection.
- **Scope boundary:** media-group batch retry machinery unchanged; `getFile`/download classification unchanged; other channels' transcription call sites unchanged (they do not acknowledge vendor offsets); no config, CLI, or schema changes; `TranscriptionProvider` trait signature unchanged (classification rides inside the `anyhow` chain).
- **Blast radius:** Telegram channel update-disposition path (voice parse + single-update retry gate); transcription error construction sites in `zeroclaw-channels/src/transcription.rs`; one new Fluent key in runtime locale catalogs.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10863. Related #10640, #9314, #9315.

### What this does, simply

When someone sends a voice note, the Telegram channel downloads the audio and hands it to a transcription endpoint. If that call fails, the channel used to retry the update forever — including failures that could never succeed, like the endpoint rejecting the recording as too long. Because Telegram redelivers unacknowledged updates first, one poisoned voice note blocked every message behind it, for every chat of the bot, and restarts did not help.

This PR makes the failure handling distinguish two cases. If the endpoint rejected *this recording* (too large, unsupported format), retrying is pointless: the channel now tells the sender why their voice note was dropped and moves on — the same way it already handles over-duration recordings and expired files. If the failure might recover (endpoint down, rate limit, bad credentials awaiting an operator fix), the update is still retried as before. As a safety net for failures that claim to be recoverable but never actually recover, an update is given up loudly after 10 consecutive attempts: an ERROR log names the update id and attempt count, so the message loss is explicit and observable rather than silent — which is the recovery policy the issue asks for.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — the behavior boundary is covered by new wiremock-driven listener tests that replay the production incident shape (persistent 413) and the recovery shape (500 then 200); no manual Telegram setup adds signal beyond them.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` = `telegram` (voice transcription path)
- **Setup / preconditions:** N/A
- **Steps to run:** N/A
- **Expected on this branch (after):** N/A
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** N/A

### How I tested

New focused tests, all at the real behavior boundary:

- `listen_terminally_rejected_transcription_does_not_block_later_updates` — the incident replay: voice update, ASR endpoint consistently answers 413 `audio duration exceeds limit`; the voice update is acknowledged with exactly one sender notice, and the text update behind it is delivered with the offset advancing past both.
- `listen_recoverable_transcription_failure_retries_and_delivers` — 500 once, then 200: the same update is retried at the same offset and delivered as `[Voice] recovered words`.
- `process_update_acknowledges_update_after_transient_budget_exhausted` — the transient budget gate: an update at the attempt cap is acknowledged with no further I/O; below the cap or for a different update id, routing is unchanged.
- `try_parse_voice_message_terminally_rejected_transcription_notifies_sender` — the sender notice carries the new dedicated wording to the right chat.
- `transcription.rs` unit tests: status classification (only 413/415 permanent; 400/401/403/408/409/422/425/429/451/5xx transient), local validation rejections classified permanent, `failure_kind` recovery through `anyhow` context layers and its transient default, and a wiremock pass over the Groq provider proving 413 → permanent while 500/429 → transient.
- Provider-path regressions (wiremock, added with the review fix): `deepgram_non_json_413_is_classified_permanent` (HTML 413 body → `Permanent`; vendor-JSON 413 keeps the readable message), `assemblyai_upload_413_is_permanent_but_metadata_413_stays_transient` (upload-step 413 → `Permanent`; create-step 413 → `Transient`), `google_stt_non_json_413_is_classified_permanent`.

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-telegram
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** workspace `fmt` / `clippy` / test jobs cover `zeroclaw-channels` and the locale catalogs; the new tests run in the standard channels suite.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** 5 `link_enricher` tests fail in this Windows/localhost/VPN environment — pre-existing on clean `master` (localhost networking restriction), unrelated to this diff. CI (Linux) is expected green.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` → clean (after one `cargo fmt --all` normalization pass over the new tests).
  - `cargo +1.98.0 clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-telegram --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` → `Finished dev profile` (no lints in the crate; `--no-deps` because path-dependency `zeroclaw-config` trips pre-existing Windows-only `collapsible_if` lints on this host that Linux CI never compiles).
  - `cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-telegram` → `test result: FAILED. 1958 passed; 5 failed` — the 5 failures are the pre-existing `link_enricher` localhost cases above; every telegram/transcription test passes.
  - Filtered re-runs of the 9 new tests (`terminally_rejected`, `recoverable_transcription`, `transient_budget`, `failure_kind`, `http_status_classification`, `local_validation`, `whisper_style_http`) → all `ok`.
  - Review-fix round at `19293ef9a` (rebased onto master `4e82ce46e`): `cargo fmt --all -- --check` → clean; `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` → clean; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib transcription` → 82 passed / 0 failed; the 3 provider-path regression tests re-run after the rebase → all `ok`.
  - `cargo fluent check` → all catalogs `ok`, including the 5 edited `cli.ftl` files.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The classification mirrors the existing `FileLookupError::classify` philosophy and the voice-drop notice plumbing (`notify_voice_drop`, bounded notice timeout) is shared with the three existing drop reasons. Not verified: a live Telegram bot end-to-end run (covered instead by the wiremock listener tests at the same boundary the existing offset tests use).
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` — no user-visible interface state changed; the only new user-facing string is a chat notice delivered through the existing `sendMessage` path, asserted by exact text in tests.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(acp): surface plan persistence failures
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Add a typed runtime `plan_persistence` session update so ACP plan load/write storage failures are visible to RPC clients instead of looking like an empty saved plan.
  - Keep TodoWrite plan durability best-effort: session restore, prompt completion, transcript recovery, and the live in-memory plan continue when the ACP plan projection cannot be loaded or saved.
  - Add the matching direct ACP custom notification and ZeroCode system notice, plus SQLite read/write, join-failure, and later-refresh recovery coverage.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not make TodoWrite plan persistence authoritative or required; conversation history and transcript recovery behavior are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** ACP session resume/load and prompt plan persistence, runtime RPC session updates, direct ACP notifications, and ZeroCode TodoWrite status messaging.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11020.

### What this does, simply

TodoWrite plans are a client-facing tracker projection, not the durable authority for the conversation. When the ACP store cannot load or save that projection, the session still restores or completes from the transcript, but clients now receive a stable unavailable status. That makes a storage problem distinguishable from a legitimately empty saved plan, and a later successful TodoWrite refresh can still reconcile the in-memory and durable state.

prs.title: fix(web): keep the in-flight prompt when chat hydration replaces local state
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - The gateway commits a turn's user prompt only when the turn finishes, so a chat transcript fetched while a detached turn is still running does not contain the prompt the browser already showed. Hydration replaced the local transcript with that snapshot and the mirror effect then overwrote `localStorage`, so the prompt disappeared on reload (and on a round trip to another conversation) while the turn kept running.
  - Hydration now keeps the uncommitted tail of *this conversation's* browser copy: it starts at the earliest pending prompt the browser composed itself (`local: true`) and runs to the end of the copy. A prompt is pending when it occurs more often in the browser copy, up to and including itself, than in the snapshot; the gateway commits turns in order, so the committed occurrences are the earliest ones. Counting occurrences, rather than testing presence, keeps a repeated prompt such as "continue" from being mistaken for one the snapshot already holds. Earlier pending prompts are included only while no finished turn lies between them (a turn that already has its final answer, an agent reply that is not a tool call, is not pending), so a second prompt queued behind a running turn does not displace the first one.
  - The browser copy is read from `localStorage` for the conversation being hydrated, before the mirror effect can overwrite it. A session switch empties the in-memory transcript, so reading it from state lost the prompt on A → B → A.
  - The comparison lives in a new pure helper (`chatHydration.logic.ts`) that strips the runtime's `[CURRENT DATE & TIME: <date> <tz>]` prefix from the rows that came from the server before comparing, so a committed prompt is not shown twice. Rows the browser composed (`local: true`) are the user's verbatim input and are compared as they are, so a prompt the user typed with that prefix is not duplicated either.
- **Scope boundary:** this PR changes only how hydration reconciles the browser copy with the server snapshot. It does **not**: consult `GET /api/sessions/{id}/state` or keep the composer disabled while a turn runs (that is #9002); add `beforeunload` handling; recover the partial streamed response or add live replay (#7759); persist the prompt on the server when the turn is accepted (see *Server-side half*); restore tool, cron or error bubbles of finished turns (the server never persists them); strip the `[CURRENT DATE & TIME: …]` prefix from hydrated user bubbles for display (observed on `master`, separate finding). See *Known limits* below.
- **Blast radius:** `web/src/contexts/AgentContext.tsx` (the hydration effect and one import), a new `web/src/contexts/chatHydration.logic.ts`, tests, and the `test:contexts` script in `web/package.json`. No change to `chatHistoryStorage.ts`, the `localStorage` format, the API, config, or any Rust. #9002 (draft, not merged) also edits `AgentContext.tsx` (it adds `recoverDetachedTurn` and its import hunk is near the one here), so whichever lands second should rebase; this PR changes only the initial hydration effect.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11517. Related #9002.

### What this does, simply

With session persistence on (the default), reloading the dashboard while the agent is still working on a turn made the question you had just asked vanish, together with your browser's copy of it, even though the agent kept going. The server only stores a question once its answer is finished, so the page was rebuilding the chat from a copy of the server's record that did not have your question yet.

This change makes the page keep the question it already showed until the server's record contains it. If the server's record already has it (the turn finished), nothing extra is shown, so the question never appears twice. Switching to another conversation and back while a turn runs is covered the same way.

**Known limits (not addressed here; the root cause is server-side: there is no turn id or commit at accept time, so the client can only compare text):**

- A repeated prompt can still be dropped when the browser copy was truncated to its 100-bubble cap, or when another client already committed the same text and this browser's identical prompt is still running. This is not worse than `master`, which drops the in-flight prompt in every such case. Unit tests pin both (`known limit: …`).
- A local prompt that the gateway has already trimmed away (default cap of 50 whole turns, `max_history_messages`) can reappear and stays until the next locally composed prompt. By reading the server code (`history_trim.rs`, `kept_turns = max_turns.max(1)…`) the newest turn is always kept, so this needs 50+ later turns that did not go through this browser's copy, for example from another browser or device or the session message API. This is inferred from reading; it was not reproduced.
- A conversation deleted outside this browser (through the API or another client) brings back its last exchange when it is opened here again, and keeps it in the browser copy. `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages` answers 200 with no messages both for a session that no longer exists and for a turn that has not committed yet (`api.rs`, `handle_api_session_messages`), so the client cannot tell them apart. `GET /api/sessions/{id}/state` does answer 404 for a missing session, but consulting it is outside this PR and overlaps #9002. Only the last exchange comes back, not the whole cached chat, and `master` would show an empty chat in that case. A test pins it (`known limit: a conversation deleted elsewhere keeps its last exchange in this browser`).

### Server-side half (not part of this PR)

The limits above come from one cause on the server, which this PR does not change: the gateway writes a chat prompt to the session store only when the turn ends.

- At accept time the WebSocket handler marks the session `running` and does not write the transcript (`crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/ws.rs`, `// Set session state to running`). The only `.append(` of a chat message in the gateway is the REST handler (`api.rs`, `backend.append(&session_key, &message)`); there is none in `ws.rs` (searched with a pattern that matches the `api.rs` line).
- The prompt then lives only in the agent's in-memory history (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/agent.rs`, `append_streamed_user_message_to_history`) and reaches the store through `persist_agent_conversation_state` when the turn finishes (`ws.rs`, the success and the error branches).
- Observed with a real gateway in the manual A/B below: while `/state` was `running`, `GET /api/sessions/<S>/messages` returned `[]`, and the prompt row appeared with a `created_at` about 60 s after `turn_started_at`, 12 ms after the mock logged `stream finished`.

Making the prompt durable when the turn is accepted (for example by appending it before the session is marked `running`) would put it in the snapshot during the turn. From reading the helper in this PR (not tested), that would remove the first limit above in both variants, because the snapshot would already hold the prompt. It would not by itself remove the second limit, which also needs the client to stop merging its local copy, or a turn id; and a dashboard talking to an older gateway would still need the merge. By reading the code, it would also cover a gateway restart in the middle of a turn, which this PR cannot. I did not analyze how an earlier write interacts with the per-connection transcript watermark, nor how a transcript that ends in an unanswered user message should be re-seeded into the agent. This is context for reviewers, not a design proposal, and nothing here depends on it.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes (optional): the automated tests below cover the logic; a manual A/B shows the user-visible delta.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `web` (dashboard chat).
- **Setup / preconditions:** gateway running with the web dashboard served and `session_persistence = true` (the default), and a model provider that streams slowly enough to reload mid-turn (a local mock that emits chunks once per second is enough). `quickstart` needs a terminal, so a headless setup can use `zeroclaw config set` instead.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Open the dashboard chat and send a long prompt, for example "Write a 3000 word essay on the history of printing".
  2. While the turn is running, confirm `GET /api/sessions/<S>/state` is `running` and `GET /api/sessions/<S>/messages` does not contain the new prompt.
  3. Reload the page (F5) and check the chat and `localStorage › zeroclaw_chat_history_v1:<S>`.
  4. Repeat step 3 a second time before the turn ends.
  5. Wait until `/state` is `idle`, then reload once more.
  6. Variant: with the turn still running, switch to another conversation and back. (Covered by the automated tests only; I did not run this one in the real interface.)
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the prompt stays on screen and in `localStorage` after each reload (steps 3 and 4) and after the round trip (step 6); after the turn commits (step 5) the prompt and the answer appear once, with no duplicated prompt (the prompt still shows the raw `[CURRENT DATE & TIME: …]` prefix, as on `master`). Unchanged by this PR and visible in the screenshots: the composer stays enabled while `/state` is `running` (#9002), and the screen does not update when the turn ends until the next reload.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** after the reload the chat shows "Send a message to start the conversation", `localStorage` holds `{"messages":[]}`, and the composer is enabled while `/state` is still `running`. Observed twice with a built gateway, the real dashboard and Chrome, using a mock streaming provider (not a real model): on `master` at `74362c2d` (2026-10-01) and again on 2026-10-06 with the gateway built from this branch and the dashboard bundle built with the base `AgentContext.tsx` (see "How I tested").

### How I tested

Automated, on the branch head `5d69cdf84` (two commits on top of `f5f3b8d5c`, parent `e654b4b7`; as of 2026-10-06 `master` has moved on to `b9ec3e9a` without touching `web/` and a trial merge is clean). The regression tests are in `web/src/contexts/sessionLifecycle.test.ts` (harness already in the file) and in the new `web/src/contexts/chatHydration.logic.test.ts`.

- `F5 while a detached turn is still running keeps the prompt the browser already showed`: red on the unpatched `AgentContext.tsx` (`AssertionError: hydration must not drop a locally-sent prompt the server has not committed yet`), green on this branch.
- `an uncommitted prompt does not follow the operator into another conversation` (includes the return to the first conversation): red unpatched, green patched.
- `reloading twice while the same detached turn is still running keeps the prompt each time`: red unpatched, green patched.
- `a second prompt queued behind a running turn does not displace the first one on the next reload`: red on the previous head (`f5f3b8d5c`, which kept only the last prompt), green now.
- `known limit: a conversation deleted elsewhere keeps its last exchange in this browser`: green on both; it pins the behavior described under *Known limits*.
- `F5 after the detached turn committed shows the prompt once, with its answer` and `returning to a conversation whose turn committed meanwhile shows the prompt once`: green both ways; they guard against duplication. Their fixtures use the real prefix (`[CURRENT DATE & TIME: <date> <tz>]\n\n<prompt>`, `agent.rs` `enrich_user_message`) and the real row shape `{role, content, created_at}` (`api.rs` messages handler).
- Helper unit tests (13): prefix stripping, empty snapshot, already-committed prompt, only the last prompt and its tail, repeated prompts, server-rebuilt bubbles from an earlier reload, no local prompt, the two `known limit:` cases, and four added with the second commit (every pending prompt is kept, an earlier committed prompt is not brought back, answered turns are not brought back, a typed prefix is compared verbatim). Three of those four were red against the previous helper; the "answered turns" one guards against bringing back more than before.

How this maps to the criteria in the triage comment on #11517: the uncommitted prompt survives a reload (the first and third tests above, and the two-prompt test); no duplicates once the turn committed (the two guard tests); no cross-session carryover (the second test checks that the other conversation gets only its own snapshot and that returning keeps the first one's prompt); repeated prompts (`a repeated prompt is not mistaken for the committed one`, `server-rebuilt bubbles from an earlier reload count toward the local occurrences`, plus the two `known limit:` tests for the edges that remain); server-prefixed content (the guard tests use the real `[CURRENT DATE & TIME: …]` prefix and `strips the runtime date prefix the gateway persists on user rows` covers the helper).

The "red unpatched" runs used the `AgentContext.tsx` of the previous base (`3c8a6763`); `web/` is byte-identical between that commit and `e654b4b7`. The red runs for the second commit's tests used the helper of `f5f3b8d5c` (the previous head).

```sh
# Windows 11, Node v24.14.0, web/ (sessionLifecycle: 8 tests with includeChat=true also fail on a clean master here)
JITI_JSX=1 JITI_TSCONFIG_PATHS=1 npx jiti src/contexts/sessionLifecycle.test.ts
ℹ tests 26 / ℹ pass 18 / ℹ fail 8      # the same 8 fail on clean master (19 tests / 11 pass / 8 fail before this change's tests)

# Linux (WSL2 Ubuntu), Node 24, api-generated.ts regenerated with `cargo web check`
JITI_JSX=1 JITI_TSCONFIG_PATHS=1 npx jiti src/contexts/sessionLifecycle.test.ts
ℹ tests 26 / ℹ pass 26 / ℹ fail 0
npm run test:contexts            # pretest:contexts hook (8 + 14 + 26 tests) then the node --test files (45)
ℹ tests 45 / ℹ pass 45 / ℹ fail 0
npx tsc -b                       # exit 0
npm run build                    # exit 0 (only the chunk-size warning)
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Web Permission Tests` runs `npm run test:contexts` (`ci.yml`, `run: npm run test:contexts`), and npm runs the `pretest:contexts` hook first, which executes `sessionLifecycle.test.ts`; together with the new `chatHydration.logic.test.ts` registered in `test:contexts`, CI covers the regression tests. The checks on the current head `5d69cdf84` finished with no failures (checked on 2026-10-06): 47 succeeded and 7 were skipped, including `CI Required Gate` and `Web Permission Tests`. The previous head `f5f3b8d5c` also finished green.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none known. Note for reviewers on Windows: 8 tests of `sessionLifecycle.test.ts` fail on a clean `master` there (`useAgent must be used within AgentProvider`, only the tests that mount `AgentChatInner`); the cause was not established. They pass on Linux.
- **Commands run and tail output:** see the block above.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** An A/B end to end on 2026-10-06 with one gateway (built from this branch, WSL2) and two dashboard bundles, one built with the base `AgentContext.tsx` and one with the fix, driven by the same script in Chrome with a mock provider that streams 60 chunks at one per second. Without the fix, after a reload while `/state` was `running` the chat was empty and `localStorage` was `{"messages":[]}`, on two consecutive reloads. With the fix, the prompt stayed on screen and in `localStorage` (`"local":true`) after both reloads while `/messages` was still empty; after the turn finished, one more reload showed the prompt and the answer once. The first-ever run of the "before" side was discarded: the agent failed to start because the test config lacked a risk profile, so no turn was running. **Not verified:** the second commit in the real interface (the A/B above ran on `f5f3b8d5c` and was not repeated; the second commit is covered by the automated tests only); a real model provider; the conversation round trip in the real interface (only in the automated tests); two tabs or two devices on the same conversation; the second known limit beyond reading the server code; repeated runs (one run per side).
- **Visual interface evidence:** `Screenshot`
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** branch head `5d69cdf84` for the automated tests and `f5f3b8d5c` for the manual A/B and the screenshots (parent `e654b4b7`); interface `web` (dashboard chat), Chrome stable headless at 1280×800 on Windows against a gateway in WSL2; the gateway was built from a copy of this tree without `.git` (so `--version` prints `unknown`). Dimensions are recorded only because the screenshots are viewport captures.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** posted in [this comment](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11571#issuecomment-6020347025): `1-before-F5.png` (turn running just before the reload; the same in both runs), `before/2-after-F5.png` (empty chat after reload, without the fix), `after/2-after-F5.png` and `after/2b-after-second-F5-turn-running.png` (prompt kept after one and two reloads, with the fix), `after/4-reload-after-commit.png` (prompt and answer once after the turn committed). In the file names "after" means after the reload (F5), not after the fix; the captions in the comment say which run each one is.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** reload twice while a turn is running, then once after it finishes. Without the fix the prompt disappears from the screen and from `localStorage`; with the fix it stays on screen and in `localStorage` until the server has it, and appears once together with the answer after the commit. The composer is still enabled during the turn and the screen still does not refresh on its own when the turn ends; both are outside this PR.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy`, `cargo test --locked`, `./scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh` and `./dev/ci.sh all` were skipped because the diff touches only `web/` (no Rust). `cargo web check` was run (it regenerates the API types and runs `tsc -b`).

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No

prs.title: fix(providers): use the shared stream idle bound for Anthropic
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - The Anthropic streaming client hard-coded a 90-second byte-idle timeout. OpenAI Responses and OpenAI-compatible streams already use the shared 300-second floor that `timeout_secs` can raise (#10886); Anthropic was left on its own constant.
  - Anthropic's API sends `ping` events every ~30 s while it generates a long tool input, so 90 s was never hit there. Gateways that route Claude models to Bedrock send no pings: a probe writing a ~350-line file as one tool call saw 51 s of silence before the tool input arrived, and larger inputs crossed 90 s and failed the turn mid-stream.
  - The stream now uses `stream_idle_timeout(timeout_secs)`, the same bound as the other streaming providers. The `timeout_secs` field description (shown in the config editor) and the book pages now list Anthropic among the providers it applies to.
  - When a body read times out, the error names the bound ("no data from provider for 300s (stream idle timeout; raise timeout_secs ...)") instead of reqwest's bare "error decoding response body", which hid the cause.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to request bodies, auth, retry policy, or the non-streaming client timeout. No new config key.
- **Blast radius:** Anthropic-family streaming only. The idle bound goes from 90 s to 300 s (or `timeout_secs` if higher), so a stream that truly hangs is detected later.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10886, #10884.

### What this does, simply

When ZeroClaw streams a reply from a Claude model, it gives up if no data arrives for a while. For the Anthropic protocol that limit was 90 seconds, shorter than for every other provider. Anthropic's own servers send small keep-alive messages while the model is busy, so the limit was never reached there. Some gateways route the same models through Bedrock, which sends no keep-alives, and a model writing a large file in one go can go quiet for more than 90 seconds. ZeroClaw then cut the stream and the turn failed with a vague decoding error.

Anthropic streams now use the same 300-second limit as the other providers, raisable with `timeout_secs`, and a timeout says what happened.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`: the bound and the error text are covered by unit tests; reproducing needs a Bedrock-routed gateway.

### How I tested

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-config --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers --lib -- stream_idle sse_read_timeout_names_idle_bound
# test result: ok. 9 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1951 filtered out
```

- `stream_idle_bound_uses_shared_floor_and_timeout_secs`: default is 300 s, `timeout_secs = 900` raises it to 900 s.
- `sse_read_timeout_names_idle_bound`: a stream that goes silent after `message_start` yields an HTTP stream error naming the bound and the knob.
- The existing OpenAI and OpenAI-compatible idle-bound tests still pass.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Quality Gate (fmt, clippy, workspace tests) for both crates; Docs Style for the two changed doc pages.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Streamed the same large tool-call request through three routes with every SSE event timestamped. Anthropic direct: 2 pings, longest silence 30.0 s. A header-authenticated gateway pool: 2 pings, 30.1 s. Bedrock via gateway: 0 pings, 51.2 s. Not yet re-run on this branch against Bedrock.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`, no user-visible interface state changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** 107783d2 (on master e654b4b7), focused `--lib` tests above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace `cargo test`: CI runs it.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the merged commit (`git revert <squash-commit>`) to restore the fixed 90-second Anthropic stream-idle limit and previous error text.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** No new toggle. `timeout_secs` can raise the new idle bound but cannot lower it below 300 seconds.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A silent stream holds resources longer before failure, or a body timeout is reported with an incorrect bound. Reverting can restore the earlier long-tool-input timeout problem.
