prs.title: fix(providers): send configured extra_headers on Anthropic requests
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - The `anthropic` family accepted `extra_headers` in config (the schema documents it for every family) but never forwarded it: `AnthropicModelProviderConfig::create_provider` dropped `opts.extra_headers`, and the provider had nowhere to put them. Only the compatible, openai, hailo-ollama and opencode providers read the field. A gateway that authenticates with its own header and rejects `x-api-key` therefore answered every request with 401, with no warning that the configured header was ignored.
  - `AnthropicBuilder::extra_headers` validates the map once (invalid names or values are skipped with a warning, the same handling as the compatible provider) and marks values sensitive. The provider sends them as client default headers on both the buffered and the streaming client, so every request path picks them up without touching the five request sites. Clients that carry extra headers stop at a cross-host redirect (`opencode_session::redirect_policy`), and a failure to build such a client is returned as an error rather than replaced by a client without the headers.
  - Headers the provider sets on the request itself (`x-api-key`, `Authorization`, `anthropic-version`, `anthropic-beta`, `content-type`) keep the provider's value, because reqwest lets request headers replace client defaults. A configured `x-api-key` cannot override the real credential.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to auth selection, beta headers, request bodies or any other provider. No new config key: `extra_headers` already exists on `AnthropicModelProviderConfig`.
- **Blast radius:** Only anthropic-family entries that set `extra_headers`. With the map empty (every existing config that works today) the provider still uses the shared cached runtime client, so requests are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** None filed; found while pointing an anthropic entry at a gateway that authenticates with its own header.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw lets you add your own headers to requests sent to a model provider, for example a key that a company gateway asks for. For Claude models talking the Anthropic protocol, that setting was quietly ignored: the headers never left the machine, so a gateway that needed them refused every request.

Now those headers are sent on every request, streaming or not. ZeroClaw's own key and protocol headers still win if a configured header has the same name, and setups that do not use the setting behave exactly as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`: the wire behaviour is covered by capture-server tests on both request paths and through the factory.

### How I tested

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-providers --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers --lib -- extra_header apply_auth
# test result: ok. 26 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1941 filtered out
```

- Buffered and streaming requests carry the configured header, and a configured `x-api-key` does not replace the provider credential (exactly one `x-api-key` value on the wire).
- Invalid header names and values are skipped, valid ones kept, values marked sensitive.
- Redirects, buffered and streaming, through loopback servers: a same-host 307 is followed and the final hop gets the header; a 307 to another port stops and the other server receives no request; a 307 from `localhost:<port>` to `127.0.0.1:<same port>` stops and the origin records no request on the target path. The localhost cases run a same-host redirect first, so the stop cannot come from a failed `localhost` lookup.
- Client build failure (an invalid runtime proxy): the buffered call and the thinking-stream request both return an error, and no request reaches the server.
- Factory path: `AnthropicModelProviderConfig::create_provider` delivers `opts.extra_headers` to the wire.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Quality Gate (fmt, clippy, workspace tests) covers the touched crate.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None in CI.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Each new test fails with its fix taken out (local edits, not committed): without the redirect rule the redirect tests fail because the cross-host server gets a request; with the hostname comparison removed from the rule, the two same-port tests fail and the cross-port tests still pass; with a fallback to the shared client on build failure, the build-failure test fails because the request reaches the server. Before the fix, a live anthropic entry pointed at a header-authenticated gateway logged a 401 naming the missing header on every request and fell through to its fallback. A local build carrying this change (the same header, client and redirect code; it also carries #11544's stream idle bound) has run that entry since 2026-10-07. Streaming requests complete through the gateway with no 401, and a buffered request reached the gateway's per-model authorization (a 403 for a model the account may not use), which the gateway checks only after the configured header authenticates the caller.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`, no user-visible interface state changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** 745f0add (on master e654b4b7), focused `--lib` tests above and `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-providers --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace `cargo test`: CI runs it.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: configured header values, which can be credentials, now leave the machine on anthropic requests, as they already do on the other families. Values are marked sensitive so they are redacted from debug output, the warning for an invalid entry names the header and never the value, the provider's own credential headers cannot be overridden, and configured headers are not forwarded across a cross-host redirect.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the merged commit (`git revert <squash-commit>`). Before merge, drop this patch to restore the existing behavior in which native Anthropic requests ignore configured extra headers.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** No new toggle. Removing `extra_headers` restores the old request behavior for that entry but may prevent a header-authenticated gateway from accepting requests.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Header-authenticated gateways reject requests, or client initialization reports a transport setup failure. Credential-boundary concerns remain under review; rollback does not revoke or rotate any credentials already transmitted.

prs.title: fix(agent): restore cost attribution in AgentEnd usage annotations
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** The `AgentEnd` observability guard was dropping the accumulated turn cost and only emitting an annotation when input or output tokens were non-zero. Two defects followed: (1) a turn that billed cost but emitted no tokens produced no `AgentEnd` cost, and (2) the `cost_usd` field on the annotation was always `None`, so cost was never surfaced even when the annotation was emitted. This restores cost attribution.
- **What changed and why (mechanics):** Add `TurnUsage::is_zero()` to gate the `AgentEnd` annotation, carry the unpriced-token subset through the `TurnUsage` accumulator, and publish the turn cost through a new `TurnUsage::complete_cost()`: `None` whenever any token-bearing usage could not be priced, `Some(cost_usd)` otherwise (preserving `Some(0.0)` for fully priced, genuinely free usage). Applied at every call site in `zeroclaw-runtime` (`agent.rs`, `loop_.rs`) and the channel orchestrator.
- **Scope boundary:** This does not change token counting, pricing, settlement, or the `TurnTokenUsage` shape. It only fixes what is emitted into the `AgentEnd` event and when.
- **Blast radius:** Observability `AgentEnd` emission only. No permission, routing, or I/O boundary changes.
- **Linked issue(s):** `Fixes #8539` — restores the `cost_usd` field on `AgentEnd`, which is the remaining open half of that issue; the other half (channel lifecycle events) was already delivered by #8916.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw tracks per-turn token and cost usage and attaches an `AgentEnd` event at the end of each agent turn. That event previously attached only token counts, and only when at least one token was used. The empty-usage predicate now also retains a nonzero accumulated cost if token counts are zero. The current production recorder prices token-bearing usage; the cost-only case is covered by a constructed accumulator test, not a per-request billing path. This change treats "no tokens and no cost" as the only "empty usage" case, and it passes the recorded cost through so the `AgentEnd` event carries it — but only when pricing is complete: a turn with any unpriced usage reports `cost_usd: null` rather than a misleading partial or zero amount. The added unit regressions prove that token-only and cost-only turns are both treated as non-empty usage, and that known cost, free usage, missing pricing, and mixed pricing are distinguished at the emission boundary.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`; this is an internal observability fix exercised by a focused unit regression and required CI.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required hosted CI passes on `b7bdd47d0ed82e38bb9ac9fa26253a54e49ab570`. The [Test job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37879269599/job/113654936705) passed both `agent_end_cost_reflects_pricing_completeness` and `agent_turn_forwards_complete_cost_to_agent_end`. The latter drives a real turn through the recorder and guard and checks known, free, missing and partial pricing.

- **Earlier local commands and results, before the two observer regressions were added:**

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(no output; formatting clean)

$ cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Checking zeroclaw-eval v0.8.5
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 4m 48s
(no warnings; full workspace, all targets)

$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib agent::cost::
test result: ok. 37 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5415 filtered out
(includes the new turn_usage_is_zero_skips_empty_usage and
turn_usage_complete_cost_preserves_pricing_completeness regressions)

$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib
test result: FAILED. 5388 passed; 55 failed; 8 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --lib
test result: FAILED. 1961 passed; 6 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

$ git diff --check
(no output)
```

- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live-provider smoke was run. The earlier local runtime and channel suites above had 55 and 6 failures respectively; the author attributed them to environment differences, but this record does not establish a baseline for each failure. Required hosted CI passes on the current head.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Traced all five `set_usage` call sites (`agent.rs` ×2, `loop_.rs` ×2, orchestrator ×1) and confirmed each now forwards `complete_cost()` and gates on `is_zero()`. Did not run a live provider call.
- **Visual interface changed?** `N/A`; this changes observability event fields, not a rendered interface.

prs.title: fix(runtime): honor supplied capability boundaries
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`; Depends on #11187.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Make supplied tools the complete registry by default. Previously, supplying capabilities still constructed native tools before merging the supplied tools.
  - Add `ToolSource::uses_native_registry(&ToolRequest) -> bool`, defaulting to `false`. Application defaults explicitly request the existing native compatibility recipe.
  - Keep child capability binding, principal propagation, live config authority and scoped policy enforcement in their existing owners.
  - Add an independent real-turn consumer, a dependency/construction ratchet, lifecycle regressions and the implemented contract documentation.
- **Scope boundary:** Config schema3, the five capability kinds and gateway authority stay unchanged. Concrete dependencies remain for named compatibility owners. Channel/RPC starter migration and combined release validation remain separate work.
- **Blast radius:** Supplied-capability CLI turns, Agent construction, SOP/delegate targets and application default wiring; native registry integrations and daemon generation retirement.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10993 and #7432. Related #11174. Depends on #11187. Placement uses merged #11092; open #11090 remains design context.
- **Labels:** `docs`, `dependencies`, `core`, `agent`, `channel`, `cron`, `daemon`, `provider`, `runtime`, `skills`, `tests`, `channel:core`, `tool:delegate`, `tool:cron`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`, `cli`.

This implements the public runtime-composition boundary tracked by [#10993](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10993). “R1” is the release tracker’s label **Runtime API and ownership** in [#7432, Runtime gaps to close](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), corresponding to its Phase 2 D1 composition deliverable. It means applications can supply providers, tools, channels, memory and observers to the real runtime while preserving policy and lifecycle ownership.

The new work is the 19-file delta from `40499e30167abbcf08e3a2ef5508fb19ea73c49b` to the final head. The base remains `master` to preserve the existing fork PRs; their prerequisite changes remain visible until they land. Review the new boundary against #11187’s pinned head, and retain dependency-first merge order. This PR supplies local R1 boundary evidence; current-master integration, remaining channel/RPC migrations and release delivery are still separate.

### What this does, simply

An application that supplies its own tools can now run the real engine with exactly those tools. An empty supplied registry stays empty, even when native integrations are enabled in config. Provider or channel refusal is returned to the caller rather than triggering a native fallback.

CLI and daemon application defaults explicitly select the existing native recipe. They retain native tool precedence, integrations and permissions. The runtime still resolves and enforces policy for every supplied tool.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, use the independent consumer as an A/B construction check.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** Public agent capability API and the application caller shared by `surface=cli`, `channel=cli`; owning daemon capability entry.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Native GNU Rust toolchain and existing dependencies. The consumer supplies all five fake capabilities and needs no external provider or real credentials.
- **Steps to run:** `cargo test -p runtime-composition-consumer --lib --locked -- --nocapture`. For the prior behavior, use the retained original proof fixture with production restored to `40499e30`; the fixture did not exist on that base.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** A real `consumer_echo` tool round trip, two exact supplied-only catalogs, no native session database or peripheral construction, and the dependency ratchet passes.
- **Prior behavior (before):** The frozen proof on `40499e30` showed 50 native/source tools and a native session database; the construction ratchet failed. Production-only revert reproduced both failures with unchanged proof tests; exact restoration passed.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Quality Gate 37216745454](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37216745454) and its [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37216745454/job/111480707778) passed for head `fe069889`. The Test job actually ran the eight independent consumer cases, including constructor traps, supplied-only catalogs, refusal, cancellation and observer lifecycle; the required format, lint, plugin-feature, platform compile and parallel-runtime checks also passed.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** The reviewed combined CLI/release candidate and native platform/live acceptance remain pending. Hosted Apple/Windows compile checks do not establish their user-level runtime behavior. Hosted Test ran synthetic merge `59a45b72fb34cf4178a4aacb8ca4fedd147f8d8d` of the submitted head into master `77ff67da`; the separate source-bound native checks below retain their original signed-head scope.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Cargo selectors below ran natively on Linux GNU/Rust 1.98 with jobs2, dev/test debug0 and incremental compilation disabled. Source identity, actual artifact freshness, full command output and the production-only revert evidence were checked independently.

```text

```

Hosted Test output, preserved verbatim:

```text
Summary [  92.030s] 19121 tests run: 19121 passed (1 slow, 2 leaky), 39 skipped
```

The two passing `LEAK` results are `mcp_transport::tests::health_check_detects_direct_child_exit_with_inherited_stdout_open` and `connection_tests::spawned_daemon_exit_does_not_wait_for_inherited_stderr`. Their complete source files are unchanged from master baseline `e9ba`; the earlier green [#11187 Test job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37186811148/job/111390363437) reports the same two results. These fixtures deliberately retain inherited pipes in bounded descendants. The CI result does not establish leak-free process acceptance, and the 39 skipped cases remain skipped.

The final follow-up `fe069889852a926ae00663f74391188601dd32fb` changes only four owner/reason strings in the retained-dependency JSON. Every Rust file, edge, feature and constructor check is identical to reviewed `5d35`; the native ratchet was run on the signed follow-up:

```text
cargo test --locked -p runtime-composition-consumer --lib dependency::dependency_boundary -- --exact --nocapture
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 7 filtered out; finished in 0.02s
```

The filtered runtime run covers source propagation and refusal, provider switch/vision, delegates/subagents/peers/cron, real GNU execution and RPC dispatch, scoped native pipeline/filter/selector behavior, queued admission and channel/RPC drain, plus daemon startup and ordered shutdown. The plugin run covers collision-before-construction, reservations, live instance config/egress keys, discovery defaults and admission ceilings. These counts are scoped suites, not full-library totals.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Actual factory caller inputs and handle ownership; the canonical native factory body is unchanged. The consumer arms the native provider/tool controls, checks construction side effects independently of filtering, and exercises source refusal, cancellation during memory construction, observer flush and generation release. The manifest ratchet refuses new/stale edges and names active compatibility owners; its constructor check is a targeted lexical check of known generic builders, supported by the executable traps.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no presentation change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Full scoped gates on `5d35aa9135da1ded412e594c276aa6d372dbfe9e`, followed by the JSON-only ratchet on signed final `fe069889852a926ae00663f74391188601dd32fb`; `tests/fixtures/runtime-composition-consumer`, application `src/composition/mod.rs` tests, runtime scoped/factory/daemon tests and `docs/book/src/architecture/runtime-composition.md`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A; the relevant automated result tails are above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Frozen old production fails; the fix passes; production revert fails; exact restoration passes. An enabled pipeline also reproduced leakage into an empty supplied catalog before its separate minimal fix.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No full workspace, CLI artifact or release build; those belong to combined candidate acceptance. No Windows/macOS native execution. No generated localization churn for the English contract update.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No; the selector chooses construction within the existing tools kind and grants nothing.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No production prompt change; the consumer uses neutral synthetic tool inputs.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. Supplied tools retain the existing policy, approval and principal checks; no long-lived policy cache is added.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Application defaults and legacy adapters: yes. Custom `ToolSource` implementations that relied on implicit native extensions: no; their returned vector is now the complete supplied registry by default.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- **Exact upgrade steps:** A custom source that needs its previous native extension behavior implements `uses_native_registry(&self, _: &ToolRequest<'_>) -> bool { true }`. Supplied-only consumers need no extra method. `ToolRequest` fields are unchanged; the runtime compatibility adapter and application defaults opt in already.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Before squash, `git revert fe069889852a926ae00663f74391188601dd32fb 5d35aa9135da1ded412e594c276aa6d372dbfe9e 600b5b2a856e1142a5573eba38b383dab4220ab4`. After squash, revert the merged PR commit. Revert later dependent changes first.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None; recipe choice is through the tools source, not new config.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Missing expected tools in a custom source that has not opted in, `composition_cli_channel_missing` for a supplied interactive source without `cli`, or a native factory/observer lifecycle regression. The independent catalog/construction tests and application parity checks detect those boundaries.

prs.title: fix(runtime): settle session turns a killed process left marked running
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - **The bug (#11432).** A turn marks its session `running` when it starts and writes `idle` or `error` when it ends. A process killed in between never writes the second half, and nothing reset it, so `/api/sessions/running` and the RPC session state reported the turn as running for good.
  - **The fix, following @Audacity88's ruling on the issue.** The process that next takes ownership of the data directory settles those turns at startup, before it admits any turn of its own. Each is recorded as `error`, keeping its turn id and its messages. Nothing is restarted.
  - **Atomic in the session backend.** `SqliteSessionBackend::recover_abandoned_turns_at` is one `UPDATE` on the SQLite store (the only backend that tracks run state). It is a function on the store type, not a trait method: no backend handle exposes it, so no later holder of a store can settle live turns by mistake. The gateway and RPC handlers are untouched. The row it leaves is the row `set_session_state(key, "error", Some(turn_id))` already writes from both of them.
  - **Tied to the existing ownership boundary.** `ConfigOwnershipGuard::recover_abandoned_turns` settles the directory the guard itself locked, so it cannot be pointed at a store another process owns. The work is in `zeroclaw-infra`, beside the store (`recover_abandoned_session_turns`); the guard method only supplies the directory.
  - **Once per process.** The first time a process owns a data directory is the one moment it knows every `running` row belongs to a process that is gone. After that a `running` row may be its own, so the directory is recorded in a process-wide set, by resolved location, and every later call does nothing: on a guard carried across a reload, on a second acquisition in the same process, through another spelling of the path. Opening a backend never does it.
  - **Whatever backend is configured.** Run state only lives in the SQLite store, so that store is settled whenever it exists. A process that starts on JSONL and later reloads onto SQLite does not find turns from before it started.
  - **No store creation or migration at startup.** Recovery goes through a bare read-write connection: it creates no store, runs no schema or import step, and leaves a store from before run state existed alone.
  - **Errors are returned.** Both functions return `io::Result<usize>`. Startup paths call `recover_abandoned_turns_or_log`, which logs a failure at WARN and lets startup continue. In the daemon that call runs right after the runtime trace sink is initialised, still before any component starts, so what it settled is on record. A store whose existence cannot be checked is reported, not treated as absent.
- **Startup paths audited.** Every path that takes fresh ownership, and what it does now:

  | Path | Takes ownership | Recovery |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `zeroclaw daemon` (`src/main.rs`) | `ConfigOwnershipGuard::acquire` before the config load; guard carried across reload generations | Called once after the config load, data-directory check, and trace sink initialization, before the generation loop starts any component |
  | `zeroclaw agent`, `zeroclaw acp` (`src/main.rs`) | Same, standalone guard | Called before the authority is built |
  | Standalone gateway (`run_gateway`) | `LiveConfigAuthority::new_owned` | Inside `new_owned`, before the authority exists |
  | Standalone channels (`start_channels`, `start_channels_with_plugin_webhooks`) | `new_owned` | Same |
  | `daemon::run` (library entry) | `new_owned` | Same |
  | Offline alias CLI (`src/alias_cli`) | `acquire`, no turns admitted | None; the next daemon start settles them |

  The six places that open the session store (gateway, daemon RPC context, channels, session tools, alias CLI, one gateway test) all run after one of the rows above, or in a process that owns nothing and now changes nothing.
- **Scope boundary:** no change to how turns write their state, to the gateway or RPC handlers, or to the session schema. Not waiting on #10412 or #11412, as agreed on the issue.
- **Known limits:**
  - *One attempt.* If the store cannot be read or written at that moment, the error is returned once and the attempt is not repeated until the next process start. Retrying later could reset turns the process has since started.
  - *Placement.* What remains in `zeroclaw-runtime` is the thin guard method and the call in `new_owned`. The holding-crate exception for those two pieces is recorded by merged #11524.
  - *Not covered:* a turn whose task is force-aborted during a reload without writing its final state would stay `running` until the next process start. I did not confirm that this happens; if it does it wants a drop guard on the turn, which is a different fix.
  - *The two `src/main.rs` call sites have no direct test.* Everything behind them is tested; removing either line would not fail a test.
- **Blast radius:** every process start that owns a data directory with an existing SQLite session store runs one extra `UPDATE` before it starts work. A session left `running` by a crash now reads `error`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11432. Related #9736, #10412, #11412.

### What this does, simply

If the daemon is killed while it is answering, the chat was left flagged as "still working" forever, even after a restart. Now the next start notices those leftovers and marks them as failed, so clients stop showing work that is not happening. The conversation itself is kept.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, if you have a daemon to hand.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** gateway chat, `GET /api/sessions/running`.
- **Setup / preconditions:** a running daemon with gateway session persistence on.
- **Steps to run:** start a chat turn that takes a while, `kill -9` the daemon, start it again, then `GET /api/sessions/running`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the session is not listed; its state is `error` with the killed turn's id; its messages are intact; the log has one WARN "marked session turns left running by a previous process as failed".
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the session is listed, and stays listed.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Rust lint and test jobs cover `zeroclaw-infra`, `zeroclaw-runtime` and the binary; Docs Style covers the Markdown.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no CI test kills a real daemon; the tests drop the store handle and take ownership the way a new process does. A real kill-and-restart was run by hand on this head (result in the review thread): it found that the daemon's recovery WARN originally had no log sink, which `fb7eb5fd87` fixes.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (head `fb7eb5fd87` on base `e9ba349316`)

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                   # exit 0
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings   # exit 0
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-runtime   # exit 0
cargo test -p zeroclaw-infra --lib      # test result: ok. 319 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib    # test result: ok. 5447 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored
cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib    # test result: ok. 638 passed; 0 failed
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh # Comment hygiene gate passed.
```

The three cases asked for on the issue, in `live_config_authority`:

- **Killed daemon, then restart:** `fresh_owner_settles_turns_a_killed_process_left_running`. A store with a `running` turn is dropped; taking ownership leaves it `error` with its turn id and its message.
- **A competing process owner is refused:** `process_refused_ownership_settles_nothing`. While one owner runs a turn, a second `new_owned` on the same directory fails and the turn is still `running`.
- **Reload does not reset live state:** `reload_leaves_live_turns_running`. The guard is drained and transferred as the daemon does on reload, the next generation calls recovery again, and the turn is still `running`.

Others:

- `taking_ownership_again_in_the_same_process_settles_nothing`: a surface torn down and started again in one process leaves a detached, still-running turn alone.
- `fresh_owner_settles_the_sqlite_store_when_jsonl_is_configured`: a process configured for JSONL still settles an existing SQLite store.
- `unreadable_store_does_not_stop_startup_and_the_error_is_returned`: the guard method returns the error; `new_owned` on such a directory still succeeds.
- `recovery_reports_a_store_it_cannot_examine` (`zeroclaw-infra`): a permission error on the store directory is returned, not read as "no store".
- In `zeroclaw-infra`: `recovery_settles_what_a_killed_process_left_and_acts_once`; `recovery_claim_follows_the_directory_not_its_spelling` (a symlink and a `..` spelling settle nothing after the first claim); `failed_recovery_is_reported_and_not_retried`; `recovery_creates_no_store`; `recovery_settles_running_turns_and_nothing_else` (idle and error rows untouched, history kept); `opening_the_store_does_not_settle_running_turns`; `recovery_leaves_a_store_without_run_state_untouched` (no migration).

Checked against a broken build: with the once-per-process check disabled, the reload test fails; with the call removed from `new_owned`, the killed-daemon test fails.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Read every `ConfigOwnershipGuard::acquire` and `new_owned` / `new_with_ownership` call site and every `make_session_backend` call site (the table above); that the reload loop in `src/main.rs` carries the guard and never re-acquires; that readers of run state treat `turn_id` and `turn_started_at` as optional. A real daemon `kill -9` and restart was also verified on `fb7eb5fd87`, using a Linux x86_64 debug build, SQLite, gateway chat, and a stub model endpoint. The [result](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11523#issuecomment-6011959872) shows `error` state, an empty running list, preserved turn ID and history, and the recovery warning.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- `SessionBackend` is unchanged: recovery is a function on `SqliteSessionBackend`, not a trait method.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** revert the squash-merge commit on `master` with `git revert <squash-merge-sha>`. Rows already settled stay `error`, which is what a failed turn writes anyway; no migration, no persisted state of its own.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** the runtime trace WARN `could not settle session turns left running by a previous process` at startup when recovery fails; or sessions that read `error` after a restart when they should not (a live turn settled by a process that was not the sole owner).

prs.title: feat(zerocode): make Config save and cancel predictable
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Honor the resolved Save action in scalar and choice editors as well as multiline editors. Preserve Enter-to-save for scalar/choice and Enter-to-newline for multiline input.
  - Show resolved Save/Cancel controls and pending-edit state. Ask Stay/Discard before navigation replaces a changed draft; allow navigation that parks it.
  - Preserve personality content after Save and retain failed-write drafts for retry. Explain automatic import/save before launching the external personality or Skills editor, including when applying a personality template.
  - Route connection paste and remapped editor actions to the visible local editor. Persist connection candidates before replacing the in-memory saved value.
- **Scope boundary:** No persisted schema, RPC method, default shortcut, modifier migration, global navigation redesign, secret-handling change or Delete/Reset confirmation change.
- **Blast radius:** ZeroCode Config key, paste and mouse dispatch; personality/Skills editing; local connection draft writes. Existing persistence owners remain unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11486. Builds on #11460 (merged).
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `risk:medium`, `size:XL`, `zerocode`, `docs`.

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode Config lets you change daemon settings, personality files, Skills and the client's connection settings. Before this change, each editor had different save and cancel conventions. Moving away could lose typed work, and saving a personality file could clear the content of the still-open editor.

This PR makes the existing Save and Cancel actions visible and consistent. Enter still saves a single value, but still adds a newline when you are editing several lines. A changed draft shows that edits are pending. If navigation would throw it away, Config asks whether to stay or discard it. Switching to a pane that keeps the draft does not ask.

Saving a personality file leaves its content open. A failed save keeps your work so you can retry. External editors still import and save changed content after a successful exit, but Config explains that behavior before launch and lets you cancel there. When applying a personality template, it compares the edited result with the current file, or an empty baseline if the file does not exist. Config continues using the same files and daemon persistence calls.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

Four files, 1191 additions and 246 deletions against current `master`. The change stays inside the existing Config editor, ZeroCode connection pane, locale file and Config docs.

The interaction policy must cover keyboard, paste and mouse entry into the existing scalar, choice, multiline and composite editors. A footer-only change would still allow silent draft loss and the personality repeat-Save defect. The change keeps one Config owner, adds an original field snapshot where none existed, and derives pending state from existing draft baselines. It does not introduce a second configuration model or replace the editor. Much of the added code exercises real handler dispatch and existing persistence boundaries; future Config navigation should preserve this same departure policy.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for the visible controls and modal layout.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Config.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Use an existing non-sensitive agent and a matching-version daemon. Build ZeroCode from this head with `cargo build --locked -p zerocode --bin zerocode`, then launch `target/debug/zerocode --config-dir <your-existing-config-directory>` using your existing connection setup. An explicitly configured Cargo target changes the binary's location.
- **Steps to run:** Open Config, edit an ordinary scalar or choice and change its value without saving. Click an earlier breadcrumb or another daemon section. Cancel the dialog to keep editing, then use Save. Open an existing personality file, edit it inline, save twice, and confirm its text remains present. Return to the file list and invoke its existing external-editor action, then cancel the prelaunch dialog. Repeat that prelaunch check for an existing Skill if available.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The footer names the resolved Save/Cancel keys and pending state. Destructive navigation offers Stay/Discard without saving. Save retains personality content and failed writes remain editable. The external-editor dialog explains import/save after successful exit.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Scalar/choice editors use only Enter to save; draft loss on navigation is not deliberate; personality list refresh can clear the retained editor; no external-editor prelaunch explanation appears. Breadcrumb navigation itself came from #11460 and is already on `master`.

### How I tested

```text
# on 60f89750470d (master 4e82ce46e9c6 merged in)
cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode
test result: 1536 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored
  failing: connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint
  (fails identically on plain master 4e82ce46e9c6; unrelated to this change)

cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings
passed

rustfmt --edition 2024 --check (changed files)
passed

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.

git diff --check origin/master HEAD
passed
```

The suite exercises production Config handlers with scripted RPC responses. New cases check scalar/choice/array Save payloads under a remapped key, no writes on Cancel/Discard, filtered-choice cancellation, personality content after repeated Save, failed external personality import followed by inline retry, and keyboard/mouse departures. App-level connection cases verify paste reaches the visible editor, Save/Cancel remapped to Tab outrank section navigation, and a parked daemon draft stays untouched. Local connection tests use temporary real config files to check failure retention, successful retry and cancellation without a write. Existing Skills and breadcrumb-navigation tests also pass; Skills retention and payload compatibility were additionally source-reviewed rather than claimed as a new dedicated failure matrix.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Quality Gate passed on `efc9cfdb566c`; the run for `60f89750470d` (Greptile fixes) is in progress. Workspace Test and Lint provide broader compilation, test and lint coverage; Format and Zerocode RPC Boundary cover formatting and Config RPC isolation. Applicable cross-platform and MSRV checks also passed.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI and scripted handlers do not supply a human-operated TUI layout check.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source and dispatch review plus the automated tests above. I also ran the Config flows by hand on experiment build [20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d): a changed scalar draft followed by navigation, and the external-editor prelaunch dialog.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Two frames in [this comment](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11511#issuecomment-6232646371): the Stay/Discard dialog over a changed scalar draft, and the external-editor prelaunch explanation.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Automated evidence is for `60f89750470df86bc251e179530f7d2b13c0b7a5`; ZeroCode Config, English. The frames were captured on experiment build [20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d) (dogfood base `0341618f9d69`), which carries this PR's Config draft changes. It is not this exact head.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Scripted Save sends the expected persistence payload, Cancel/Discard send no write, personality Save preserves content across refresh, and failed connection Save keeps its draft until retry succeeds.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full local workspace tests and broad Clippy are delegated to current-head CI; the focused binary suite directly checks the edited dispatch paths without repeating that broader coverage.

### Visual evidence

Frames: see [this comment](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11511#issuecomment-6232646371).

Use this revision in a real 120-column by 40-row English terminal. The first frame should retain the editor's Save/Cancel/pending footer around the discard dialog. The second should show the explanation that a successful external-editor exit imports and saves changed content, with its launch and cancel actions. Expected visible result: readable explanation and controls without overlap or clipping. Observed result: readable dialog and controls, with no overlap or clipping. These frames check presentation; the handler and file tests establish save/cancel transitions.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- Risk and mitigation: The local connection candidate uses the existing config writer. External editors and daemon writes retain their existing access and persistence boundaries.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Existing defaults are retained and scalar/choice Enter remains a Save alias.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No schema, environment or CLI option changes. Config TUI interaction changes as described above.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: None. Existing keybindings continue to resolve through the current action registry.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the squash commit. It contains only this change; the navigation work from #11460 is already on `master` separately.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None; no new persisted controls.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Save does not persist the selected value, Cancel unexpectedly writes, navigation discards a changed draft without asking, or a saved personality editor becomes empty. Check the Config footer's localized save failure and pending status, then reopen the value to verify persistence.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A. No PR is superseded.

prs.title: fix(runtime): preserve container launcher environment
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Preserve `CONTAINER_HOST` and `DOCKER_HOST` for Docker runtime launchers after environment sanitization. A Podman-compatible `docker` launcher keeps the operator-selected host service instead of falling back to local Podman inside the ZeroClaw container.
  - Share the existing environment-name validation and restoration between shell and skill tools, so skills honor configured `shell_env_passthrough`.
  - Add subprocess regressions and document host-engine setup. Launcher connection settings are separate from guest environment forwarding.
- **Scope boundary:** Shell and skill execution through `DockerRuntime`; no new configuration, dependencies, guest forwarding, or resource-limit changes. Coding CLI execution and native-runtime Docker sandbox wrapping are outside this patch.
- **Blast radius:** Runtime adapter metadata and shell/skill environment preparation; native and shell-less adapters retain an empty launcher allowlist. Existing TUI environment overlays remain in place.
- **Linked issue(s):** Reported in community support; no issue-closing claim.
- **Labels:** `docs`, `config`, `runtime`, `tool:shell`, `size:M`, `risk:medium` (live snapshot).

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for Linux host-socket behavior.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=cli`, actual agent loop and skill tool execution.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Rootless Podman host with a mounted service socket, an Alpine client container with `docker` resolving to Podman, and a configured Python skill. Set `CONTAINER_HOST` to the mounted socket and `runtime.kind = "docker"`; keep memory/CPU/read-only limits enabled.
- **Steps to run:** Build the binary from the base and this branch; in each otherwise identical setup run `zeroclaw agent -a smoke -m 'Run the Python skill.'`. Repeat with `shell_env_passthrough = ["CONTAINER_HOST"]`. The skill command can be `python3 scripts/python_test.py`; configure the same provider, approval policy, and workspace in both cases.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Skill runs through the host service without a custom Docker wrapper. Guest connection variables are absent unless explicitly forwarded.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Connection variables are dropped. A local Podman launch can fail during cgroup setup; configured passthrough is also ignored by the skill executor.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Hosted CI has completed on this PR. Format, Docs Style, Semgrep, and 32-bit checks passed. Security is blocked by eight advisories against existing Wasmtime 48.0.3 packages ([job log](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37076400694/job/111067179902)); this patch changes no dependency manifests or lockfile. Local execution and focused gates are the functional evidence below; the required aggregate is blocked by that Security failure.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** Real nested Alpine/rootless-Podman service routing is covered by the manual actual-skill run below, beyond the fake-launcher unit guards.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
  passed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib tools::skill_tool::tests -- --test-threads=1
  43 passed; 0 failed (independently rerun after implementation)
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config platform::docker -- --test-threads=1
  16 passed; 0 failed (independently rerun)
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-runtime runtime_traits -- --test-threads=1
  16 passed; 0 failed
shell environment / passthrough / TUI / effective PATH-HOME checks
  3/3, 1/1, 4/4, 1/1 passed
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-api --all-targets -- -D warnings
  passed
scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh (temporary Node 22 on PATH)
  zero lint errors
scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
  6 collector tests passed; zero added links
```

  Standalone `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-api runtime_traits -- --test-threads=1` fails on both this branch and the clean base with `E0433` at unchanged `channel.rs:1389`: Tokio lacks the `time` feature. The combined package run above supplies the existing feature unification. No dependency change was included to mask this baseline defect. The docs gate's pinned linter requires Node >=20; the host Node 18 was replaced only for that invocation, without changing global configuration or tracked dependencies.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Baseline regressions failed on endpoint preservation and configured skill passthrough before production edits. Four targeted mutations each failed the intended assertion: endpoint allowlist, passthrough, environment clearing, and name validation. Every restore was SHA-256 identical. Native filtering excludes a synthetic API-key sentinel; Docker launcher settings do not add guest `--env` flags. Symbol graph data was unavailable without SCIP; crate dependencies and direct callers were inspected.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact plain-text output; this changes container execution, not presentation.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Signed commit `a9d6acaf981865ea67cb2ca921fef7bc347144d9`, whose source is byte-identical to the final tested diff on base `afc47d333c90211f92ca3eca80cd2293c72c5025`; CLI actual-skill output captured from a patched musl binary in Alpine 3.20 with rootless Podman 4.9.3, default `systemd`/cgroup v2. Only provider responses were stubbed over loopback to request the advertised skill; the agent loop, skill, Docker runtime, and containers were real.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Both default and configured-passthrough cases returned:

```text
alive
Python 3.12.13
PYTHON_PROBE_OK
GUEST_MEMORY_MAX=536870912
GUEST_CPU_MAX=100000 100000
LAUNCHER_ENV_NOT_FORWARDED
READ_ONLY_ROOTFS_OK
```

- **Action or changed state and observed result:** A real `SKILL.toml` shell tool launches successfully without a custom wrapper. Its effective 512 MiB/one-CPU limits remain enforced; a filesystem-root write returns `EROFS` and engine variables remain absent from the guest.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace tests were not repeated; scoped tests, combined clippy, and the actual runtime-boundary proof cover this change. Windows-specific execution was not manually tested.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No.**
- New external network calls? **No.** Existing engine selection is preserved.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes.** Skills now honor the same operator-configured passthrough as shell tools. Docker additionally retains two connection selectors for the launcher; filtering stays enabled, native defaults stay narrow, and connection settings are not automatically forwarded into guests. Synthetic-sentinel and mutation tests exercise those boundaries.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No.**

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes.** The runtime trait addition has an empty default.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes, behavior correction.** Existing `CONTAINER_HOST`, `DOCKER_HOST`, and `shell_env_passthrough` are respected for shell/skill launchers; no fields or flags were added.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- Exact upgrade steps: Rebuild/update the binary. Preserve the intended host socket mount and set its connection variable in the ZeroClaw process environment; a custom explicit-socket Docker wrapper is no longer required for this path.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this commit and rebuild the binary.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None added.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Engine connection errors or the return of `Failed to add conmon to cgroupfs sandbox cgroup` / `crun` cgroup setup failures. Inspect the selected host socket and launcher environment.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A — no PR is superseded and no external contributor implementation is carried forward.

prs.title: fix(providers): honor Ollama and llama.cpp thinking controls
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Ollama and llama.cpp collected the alias `think` setting and global `runtime.reasoning_enabled` switch but dropped them when constructing compatible requests. The factories now forward explicit on/off controls across text, tool, and streaming requests, including llama.cpp Responses.
- **Scope boundary:** This repairs forwarding and clarifies the existing settings. Models and templates must support an off mode for generation to stop.
- **Blast radius:** Local provider construction and config descriptions. Other compatible families keep their current behavior; regression tests check that boundary.
- **Linked issue(s):** No existing issue identified for this exact omission.
- **Labels:** `bug`, `docs`, `config`, `provider`, `distinguished contributor`, `risk:medium`, `size:L`.

### What this does, simply

Saving `think = false` on an Ollama or llama.cpp alias previously left the backend's mode unchanged. The alias now sends the backend's off request. When `think` is unset, these providers inherit the global runtime switch; when both switches are unset, backend defaults remain in effect.

Ollama receives `reasoning_effort`. llama.cpp Chat Completions also receives the boolean `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking`, while llama.cpp Responses receives `reasoning.effort`. An explicit alias setting wins over the global switch. Chat Completions overrides conflicting manual reasoning fields while preserving unrelated request options. For enabled thinking, effort is selected from `provider_extra.reasoning_effort`, then `provider_extra.reasoning.effort`, then `runtime.reasoning_effort`; the first non-empty, non-`none` string wins, otherwise `"medium"` is used. llama.cpp Responses uses that selected effort but does not forward other `provider_extra` fields or `chat_template_kwargs`.

The config descriptions distinguish these mode controls from native thinking budgets and Anthropic's display option. Disabling an added budget or leaving a display option unset does not disable a model's own reasoning.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for a live backend smoke check.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=cli`; provider HTTP requests. No messaging channel changes.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A test ZeroClaw instance and agent using llama.cpp with Gemma 4 26B A4B and its current chat template.
- **Steps to run:** Set the provider alias's `think = false`, rebuild, restart/reload the test instance, and start a fresh chat. Ask `What is 17 multiplied by 23? Reply with only the number.` Repeat with `think = true`, then unset the alias value and test `runtime.reasoning_enabled = false`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The off Chat request contains `reasoning_effort="none"` and `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false`. A supporting Gemma template generates the answer without a reasoning trace. The alias overrides the global switch.
- **Prior behavior on master (before):** The same boolean settings supply no off control to the compatible request.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The previous-head [CI run 37055617698](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37055617698) passed on `e6276f970389b84a6a12914e2f2dea6f94689054` on **2026-10-02 at 19:50:59 UTC**. That is historical evidence. The **2026-10-04** review fixes advance this PR to `ca582f75b26597e69d39e1097a3fb9e300d864c3`; new-head CI is pending and is not yet claimed as passing. Current-head local provider tests, scoped Clippy, formatting, and changed-docs gates pass. The provider tests exercise the real config/factory-to-HTTP boundary; dated live backend checks below cover the model/template behavior that fixtures cannot prove.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Live checks called the backend APIs directly with the control fields verified by the config-to-HTTP regressions; they were not a live rebuilt ZeroClaw CLI run. Generation suppression is confirmed for the tested Gemma/llama.cpp artifact and prompt. The tested Ollama/Qwen3 artifact continued generating reasoning under off controls.
- **Commands run and tail output:** The following checks ran on **2026-10-04 (UTC)** for review-fix head `ca582f75b26597e69d39e1097a3fb9e300d864c3`. The new nested-effort HTTP regression was first run against the unchanged resolver and failed with configured nested `"low"` overwritten by runtime `"high"`; it passes after the fix.

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
passed

cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-providers --lib local_thinking
9 passed; 0 failed

cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-providers --lib
1925 passed; 0 failed; 4 ignored

cargo clippy --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-providers --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
Finished dev profile
```

Dependency-inclusive Clippy was also attempted during the original **2026-10-02** validation. It fails on the unchanged `zeroclaw-infra/src/acp_session_store.rs:1648` expression with `clippy::nonminimal_bool` on Rust 1.96. The changed-package check passes; this PR does not include that separate cleanup.

On **2026-10-04**, `scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh` and `scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh` ran with `BASE_SHA=e6276f970389b84a6a12914e2f2dea6f94689054` and `DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/providers/configuration.md`. The quality gate found no blocking issues on changed lines. Full-file lint also identified an existing duplicate `See also` heading outside this patch; both headings are present on the parent revision. The links gate passed its six collector tests and found zero added links.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Original live verification on **2026-10-02 (UTC)**, repeated on **2026-10-04 (UTC)**. Both used the prompt `What is 17 multiplied by 23? Reply with only the number.` with temperature 0.

  **llama.cpp / Gemma:** Gemma 4 26B A4B instruction-tuned Q4_0 GGUF from ggml-org, with its original template, on llama.cpp commit `6f4f53f` and an RTX 3090. The downloaded GGUF was verified against its published SHA-256: `d208665ab1cd3a69f7a9a4bc59430e8448c8093d9b06334f566ac59d6d504a03`. The repeat used the same cached artifact and backend binary.

| Test date (UTC) | Thinking mode | Generated tokens | Reasoning characters | Final answer |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| 2026-10-02 | On | 157 | 280 | `391` |
| 2026-10-02 | Off | 4 | 0 | `391` |
| 2026-10-04 | On | 157 | 280 | `391` |

The answer-only content and four generated tokens confirm generation suppression for this case; an empty reasoning field alone would not establish that. This is one prompt, not a general quality or speed benchmark.

The **2026-10-04** repeat used an isolated Ollama server, the same cached model, and a 256-token cap:

| Request on 2026-10-04 (UTC) | Generated tokens | Separate reasoning characters | Ordinary content characters | Thinking generation disabled? |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Native `think=true` | 256 | 707 | 0 | No |
| Native `think=false` | 256 | 0 | 707 | No |
| Compatible `reasoning_effort="none"` | 256 | 0 | 707 | No |

  Both off requests produced identical visible reasoning and reached the token cap. The artifact's metadata advertises `thinking.values=[true]`, with `default=true`, and its stored template includes `<think>`. **Thinking was not disabled for this Ollama/Qwen3 artifact.** The PR repairs forwarding; it cannot guarantee generation suppression for a model/template without a working off mode. Temporary test servers were stopped after both checks.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No interface layout, styling, or interaction behavior changed; descriptions and documentation were clarified.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Review-fix head `ca582f75b26597e69d39e1097a3fb9e300d864c3`, **2026-10-04**. Config resolution and real factories were exercised against protocol-accurate HTTP fixtures for text, tools, streaming, and Responses. The live API checks above were captured for the original `e6276f9703` forwarding patch. The review fix changes enabled-thinking effort lookup and docs; explicit off still returns `"none"` before effort lookup, and current-head off regressions pass. The dated API checks remain model/template evidence, not a live rebuilt CLI run on this new head.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Current-head local test tails above; dated live comparisons above. The **2026-10-04** Gemma repeat again returned exactly `391` in off mode with four generated tokens and no reasoning. Ollama off mode still returned a reasoning paragraph in ordinary content.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Nine regressions cover alias/global precedence, manual-field conflicts, defaults, preserved unrelated Chat options, local model names, Gemma's template flag, and unaffected compatible families. The added regression checks nested-only effort, flat-versus-nested precedence, empty/`"none"`/non-string fallbacks, and explicit off across Ollama Chat, llama.cpp Chat, and llama.cpp Responses, including text, tools, and both streaming paths.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No duplicate full-workspace Cargo run: public Rust signatures are unchanged and the full provider package was exercised. `graph_changed` could not enumerate symbols because the fresh worktree has no SCIP index; factory callers were checked directly and crate impact was inspected.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No; existing requests gain control fields.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. Fixtures use synthetic messages, keys, model identifiers, and loopback endpoints.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. Mode selection comes from operator configuration; this patch adds no untrusted prompt text.
- If any Yes, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A.

## Compatibility (required)

- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: existing controls gain working behavior and clearer descriptions; no new keys or syntax.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.
